Plasma proteomics study comparing inflammatory and mitochondrial proteins in Neuro-PASC patients versus controls to identify potential biomarkers, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
A cross-sectional physiological study comparing autonomic and cerebrovascular phenotypes in Long COVID and ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls, without testing any treatment intervention.

Proteomic and metabolomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid comparing neuro-PASC patients to healthy controls and inflammatory neurological disease patients to identify biomarkers and pathogenic mechanisms.
Cross-sectional study comparing cortical thickness and inflammatory markers between healthy controls, COVID-19 survivors, and long-COVID patients with and without cognitive impairment.

Cross-sectional study using PET imaging to examine neuroinflammation in PASC patients and its correlation with vascular dysfunction markers, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Preclinical hamster study examining corticosteroid effects on SARS-CoV-2-induced anosmia and olfactory epithelium inflammation, not a human long COVID treatment trial.
RNA sequencing study comparing transcriptional profiles and immune cell patterns in long COVID patients with ME/CFS versus controls, identifying potential biomarkers and pathogenic mechanisms.

Experimental study using a mouse model of post-COVID syndrome to characterize acute and long-term neuropsychiatric and musculoskeletal sequelae, with focus on sex-dependent outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining cognitive performance and prefrontal haemodynamic patterns in undergraduate students with self-reported or objective cognitive impairment following COVID-19 infection, without testing any intervention.
Basic science study using Drosophila to investigate whether ACE2 downregulation contributes to neuromuscular manifestations of COVID-19, with no human patients or treatment intervention.
Experimental study in mice investigating whether SARS-CoV-2 spike protein alone can induce neuroinflammation and alpha-synuclein accumulation via multiple injection routes.

Clinical and preclinical study examining immunometabolic perturbations (IL-6, MAO dysregulation) in post-COVID neuropsychiatric syndromes, with therapeutic intervention via MAO inhibition in a mouse model.

Mechanistic study measuring kynurenine pathway metabolites in CSF and plasma of acute COVID-19 patients to understand neurological complications, with no intervention or treatment tested.
A multimodal MRI study correlating brain structure and function with depression and PTSD symptoms in COVID-19 survivors, without testing any intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between BMI, brain gray matter volume, and peripheral inflammatory markers in post-COVID patients.

Clinical evaluation comparing legacy pen-and-paper cognitive tests (ACE-III) with novel digital cognitive tests in 102 post-COVID patients with cognitive complaints, finding that digital tests detect impairments better than traditional tests.
Cross-sectional study comparing neurocognitive performance and olfactory dysfunction in COVID-19 recovered patients with and without anosmia versus uninfected controls.

Cross-sectional MRI and cognitive assessment study examining associations between persistent COVID-19 symptom load and brain structure changes in 43 survivors, without testing any intervention.

A cross-sectional MRI study comparing brain tissue microstructure and neurochemical profiles in long COVID patients, COVID-recovered individuals, and healthy controls—no treatment intervention tested.

In vitro study investigating potential interactions between SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein and FOXP3 transcription factor to understand mechanisms underlying COVID-19 coagulopathy.
Preclinical study evaluating Jing Si herbal tea's anti-inflammatory and stress-relieving effects in cell cultures and mouse models of long COVID-related symptoms.

An animal study investigating whether SARS-CoV-2 directly infects the brain and causes neuroinflammation in non-human primates, without testing any interventions or treatments.

Cross-sectional study investigating the association between IL1 genetics, EBV reactivation markers, and long COVID symptoms in a large cohort, without testing any intervention.

Mechanistic study using invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing to investigate the physiologic basis of post-COVID exertional intolerance, comparing 10 recovered COVID-19 patients to controls.
Mechanistic study investigating spike protein persistence at the brain-meninges axis in long COVID patients and experimental models, but not testing any treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional neuropsychological assessment of cognitive deficits in 100 elderly long COVID patients, finding high rates of impairment on cognitive tests.
Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of cardiovascular autonomic abnormalities in PASC patients using active stand testing, with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

Characterizes gut microbiome composition in long COVID patients and develops a machine learning model to predict symptom phenotypes based on microbial profiles, but does not test any treatment intervention.
Characterizes immune cell profiles and molecular signatures in peripheral blood of convalescent COVID-19 patients compared to controls using flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing.
Immunological study comparing T cell populations and chemokine receptor expression between long COVID patients and convalescent controls to identify immune dysregulation mechanisms.

Cross-sectional electrophysiological study comparing peripheral nerve and muscle function in long COVID patients with myopathic symptoms versus healthy controls, but does not test or evaluate any treatment.

High-dimensional immune profiling study comparing immune profiles in non-hospitalized COVID-19 cases with different symptom outcomes, identifying NK and T-cell subpopulations associated with asymptomatic infection and absence of long-term symptoms.

Investigates neurophysiological abnormalities and muscle pathology in long COVID patients using quantitative EMG, single-fiber EMG, and muscle biopsies to understand the physiological basis of fatigue.
A cross-sectional study comparing TMS-EEG measures of cortical motor activity between post-COVID fatigue patients and healthy controls, without any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional neurophysiological study comparing motor cortex excitability and inhibition in long COVID patients with cognitive impairment versus healthy controls, without testing any intervention.
Cross-sectional study examining associations between vitamin D levels, VDR genetic polymorphisms, and PASC severity in 123 pediatric patients.

A cross-sectional study using Raman spectroscopy to analyze serum samples from convalescent COVID-19 patients to identify potential biomarkers of infection and disease progression, but does not evaluate any therapeutic intervention.
Cross-sectional study measuring prevalence of sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity in post-COVID-19 individuals and their association with functional outcomes, with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing peripheral and central auditory function in 44 post-COVID-19 individuals without intervention.

Observational study comparing memory function between 209 COVID-19 survivors and 87 controls using online cognitive testing, without any intervention or treatment.

A multicohort observational study measuring circulating SARS-CoV-2 antigens in plasma/serum up to 14 months post-infection and associating antigen detection with PASC symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Network analysis of neural single-cell transcriptome data from COVID-19 patients to identify immune-related pathways and neuroimmune factors associated with neuronal dysfunction and long-term sequelae.

Cross-sectional study examining the frequency and persistence of post-COVID symptoms in healthcare workers and their association with renal, cardiac, and metabolic risk factors.

Cross-sectional study investigating whether SARS-CoV-2 infection induces specific autoantibodies and whether these autoantibodies are associated with long COVID.

Cross-sectional study investigating autoantibody profiles in long COVID patients with persistent olfactory impairment to understand immune-mediated mechanisms.

Basic research characterizing alterations in extracellular vesicles and their immunomodulatory effects on T cell function in long COVID convalescence, without testing any intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing enlarged perivascular spaces and glymphatic clearance markers in neuropsychiatric long-COVID patients versus healthy controls, without testing any intervention.

Untargeted lipidomic analysis of plasma samples from 147 post-COVID patients identifying lipid biomarkers and altered immune signatures, but no treatment intervention or trial design.

Bioinformatic analysis of RNA-seq data identifying differentially expressed genes in long COVID patients, with gender stratification but no intervention or treatment evaluation.
Machine learning study identifying early clinical biomarkers predictive of long COVID development, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study characterizing orthostatic intolerance in 86 long COVID patients using active standing tests and assessing clinical/endocrine features associated with OI.
Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive function (attention, memory, executive function) in post-COVID patients versus healthy controls using neuropsychological tests and experimental tasks.
RNA-seq analysis of cardiac tissue to identify gene expression changes and inflammatory pathways in SARS-CoV-2-infected cardiomyocytes.
Computational modeling study estimating the quality-adjusted life-year burden of long COVID in California by age group and symptom severity, not a treatment trial.

Observational study correlating COVID-19 severity with biomarker profiles and systemic sequelae in 226 participants followed for 6 months, identifying risk factors for long COVID symptoms but not testing any intervention.

A pre-post observational study of 10 mild COVID-19 patients examining brain temperature and free water changes as biomarkers of neuroinflammation using MRI, with findings linking these changes to chronic olfactory and cognitive dysfunction.
Develops a machine learning model using cytokine profiles to diagnose long COVID and differentiate it from chronic Lyme disease.
Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive function via Stroop task performance between long COVID patients, ME/CFS patients, and healthy controls.

Develops an HPLC-PDA analytical method to simultaneously quantify three drugs (Paracetamol, Dexketoprofen Trometamol, Rivaroxaban) used to treat post-COVID-19 symptoms, with greenness and whiteness assessment.

This study examines serum biomarkers (YKL-40 and MR-pro-ADM) in post-COVID patients with cognitive dysfunction, comparing their levels between groups with and without post-COVID syndrome, but does not test an intervention.
Cross-sectional study comparing resting-state brain functional connectivity and cognition between long COVID patients with and without cognitive impairment and healthy controls.

Metagenomic analysis comparing oral microbiome composition in COVID-19 patients versus healthy controls, with speculation about potential microbiome-based interventions but no actual treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study measuring heart rate variability parameters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls and CVD patients, finding altered autonomic regulation in COVID-19 but testing no intervention.
A cross-sectional study characterizing hippocampus-dependent memory impairment in COVID-19 survivors using cognitive testing in 1400+ participants, with no intervention or treatment evaluation.
Prospective study evaluating the effects of comprehensive inpatient rehabilitation on anxiety and depression symptoms in post-COVID patients, with biomarker analysis of BDNF and irisin levels.
Validates a computerized test (TAP) for detecting attentional deficits in post-COVID patients compared to healthy controls, but does not test any treatment or intervention.
A cross-sectional neuroimaging study comparing brain metabolic and electrophysiological patterns in post-COVID patients with cognitive decline versus healthy controls, using FDG-PET and EEG.
Mechanistic study demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 spike protein-induced inflammation causes cardiac arrhythmias in a mouse model, without testing any treatment intervention.

A pre-registered cross-sectional study comparing breathlessness perception during CO2 rebreathing between post-COVID patients and healthy controls, finding increased symptom perception despite normal breathing physiology.
In silico study examining HLA allele binding affinity to herpes virus and SARS-CoV-2 antigens to explain ME/CFS and long COVID pathogenesis, with no intervention or treatment evaluated.
Cross-sectional study characterizing cognitive profiles in Post-COVID-19 syndrome patients and identifying a severe cognitive impairment subgroup (7.5%) distinct from general post-illness effects.

Propensity-score matched cross-sectional study comparing inflammatory markers, gut integrity biomarkers, and endothelial function between COVID-19 positive and negative participants, with analysis of sex differences in long COVID.
Cross-sectional study examining relationships between pulmonary function and cognitive dysfunction in long COVID patients using imaging, pulmonary testing, and cognitive assessments.

A cross-sectional neuroscience study investigating neural mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction in post-COVID patients using EEG, diffusion MRI, and cognitive modeling, without testing any intervention.
Prospective cohort study developing an MRI-based machine learning approach to differentiate Post-COVID patients from unaffected controls using microstructural brain imaging metrics.
Cross-sectional MRI study comparing brain structural metrics and glymphatic function between children with acute mild COVID-19 and healthy controls.

In vitro study of vitamin B12's effects on peripheral blood biomarkers in long COVID patients with persistent visuoconstructive deficit, showing B12 normalizes inflammatory markers associated with cognitive impairment.

A case series evaluating epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT) as a treatment for long COVID by analyzing spatial transcriptomics and inflammatory markers in epipharyngeal tissue before and after intervention in 3 long COVID patients.

Exploratory neuroimaging study comparing brain intrinsic connectivity during cognitive task performance between long COVID patients and healthy controls, finding impaired network connectivity associated with cognitive dysfunction and illness duration.

A cross-sectional study comparing auditory brainstem responses between 37 long COVID patients and 45 healthy controls to identify objective electrophysiological markers of PASC-related cognitive fatigue.

Uses temporal topic modeling on EHR data from 14 million patients to identify clinical phenotypes and conditions increased after COVID-19 infection, but performs no treatment evaluation or intervention testing.
Develops and validates LATCH, a machine learning algorithm for identifying long COVID cases in electronic health records using limited labeled data.

Cross-sectional study comparing neuropsychological test performance in long COVID patients with neurologic symptoms versus non-PCS controls and healthy controls, finding impaired working memory, mental flexibility, and processing speed.
Develops a deep learning method (DLPE) to detect pulmonary lesions in CT scans of COVID-19 survivors, demonstrating radiomics predictive power for clinical outcomes and sequelae.
Mechanistic study showing SARS-CoV-2 triggers paracrine senescence and sustained inflammatory response in cultured cells and mice, with senolytic drug treatment reducing senescence markers.

Methodological paper applying a negative control-calibrated difference-in-difference approach to assess racial/ethnic disparities in post-COVID-19 health outcomes using electronic health records, but focuses on analytic method validation rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.
Proteomic study of acute kidney injury in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, focused on acute infection and post-discharge kidney function outcomes, not long COVID intervention.
Preclinical study in aged hamsters demonstrating that the senolytic drug ABT-263 reduces viral load and inflammation during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, not long COVID.

Cross-sectional mechanistic study comparing carotid chemoreflex sensitivity and breathing efficiency between long COVID patients and controls, identifying elevated carotid body responsiveness as a potential driver of symptoms but not testing any intervention.
Develops machine learning models to predict which acute COVID-19 patients will develop long COVID based on baseline clinical and immunologic factors.
Uses Google Trends data and statistical methods to forecast and monitor long COVID prevalence through search term analysis, without evaluating any treatment or intervention.
EHR-based machine learning study comparing symptom and condition patterns between PASC and ME/CFS patients using National COVID Cohort Collaborative data.
Mechanistic study identifying specific odor molecules that trigger parosmia (distorted smell) in post-COVID patients using gas chromatography, without testing any intervention.

Single-nucleus RNA sequencing study comparing cellular and molecular mechanisms of myocarditis in patients with non-COVID, post-COVID-19, and post-vaccination myocarditis, identifying distinct cytokine and immune cell patterns.
Mechanistic study using cell models and animal models to identify CCL2-mediated endothelial injury as a driver of cardiac dysfunction in long COVID, without testing a treatment intervention.
Genetic study using the Long COVID Host Genetics Initiative cohort to identify associations between thromboembolism-related variants and long COVID risk.
Develops and validates a hybrid NLP pipeline to extract post-acute COVID-19 symptoms from clinical notes across 11 health systems.
Bioinformatic analysis predicting long-term complications and comorbidities associated with COVID-19 based on multi-omics data, with no empirical treatment study or intervention evaluation.

Molecular study comparing DNA methylation and gene expression in nasal epithelial cells of acute COVID-19 patients vs controls, with follow-up transcriptome analysis at 3 and 12 months post-infection to investigate mechanisms underlying post-acute sequelae.

Targeted amino acid profiling comparing hospitalized COVID-19 patients and 1-month convalescent subjects to characterize metabolic disturbances during acute infection and early recovery.
Uses electronic nose technology to screen for long COVID in young adults via exhaled breath profiling, but does not test a treatment intervention.
Longitudinal proteomic analysis of lung tissue in Golden Syrian hamsters infected with SARS-CoV-2, identifying sex-specific protein changes persisting after viral clearance.
An endoscopy study of 46 IBD patients examining SARS-CoV-2 antigen persistence in gut tissue ~7 months post-infection and its association with postacute COVID-19 symptoms.
Describes development of a wearable device and AI system to monitor and predict long COVID patients' respiratory status in real-time, but reports no clinical outcomes or validation results.
A study evaluating whether aromatherapy with orange, thyme, clove, and frankincense essential oils improves energy levels and quality of life in female patients with post-COVID exhaustion.

A non-randomized controlled trial comparing comprehensive rehabilitation with and without micropolarization and transligual neurostimulation in 120 long COVID/post-COVID chronic fatigue syndrome patients, measuring outcomes via asthenia questionnaire, MMSE, sleep scales, and mood assessments.
Laboratory study comparing platelet activation and coagulation markers in convalescent plasma donors with mild COVID-19 history versus controls, finding no procoagulant phenotype.
Study examining elevated plasma biomarker concentrations in long COVID patients to investigate neuropathogenic mechanisms.

Data analysis examining the prevalence and distribution of persistent fatigue, cognitive problems, and respiratory symptoms in long COVID patients across hospitalized and non-hospitalized populations by gender.

Observational study using electron microscopy and flow cytometry to characterize blood cell and endothelial damage in mild COVID-19 survivors, finding persistent cellular abnormalities at discharge that may warrant long-term antithrombotic therapy.
Prospective cross-sectional study examining the incidence of persistent SARS-CoV-2 in gut tissues via endoscopic biopsy in post-COVID patients, with no treatment intervention.
A cross-sectional study comparing blood gas analysis and hematological parameters between long-COVID patients and healthy controls to characterize impaired red blood cell function.
A pilot study evaluating therapeutic apheresis to reduce agonistic autoantibodies and improve symptoms in 20 post-COVID patients with severe fatigue and post-exertional malaise.

A 3-year intervention study evaluating stress-controlled sensorimotor training and intensified cognitive behavioral therapy for post-COVID-19 fatigue and sensorimotor instability, integrated into a cross-sector management program.

An uncontrolled case series of 24 male patients from the MENA region treated with double filtration plasmapheresis to reduce lipids, inflammatory markers, and autoantibodies associated with long-COVID and chronic fatigue.
Develops and validates a pediatric-specific computable phenotype for identifying long COVID in EHR data through comparison with manual chart review.
Investigates the prevalence and long-term development of taste disorders following COVID-19 infection.
Cross-sectional study examining olfactory dysfunction in long-COVID patients approximately 9 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Cross-sectional study investigating the prevalence and long-term development of taste dysfunction following COVID-19 infection.
Investigates whether SARS-CoV-2 antigen persistence in the gastrointestinal tract is a mechanistic basis for long-COVID syndrome.
Cross-sectional study investigating the prevalence of sleep-related breathing disorders in long COVID patients months after SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence and extent of cardiac pathologies in long COVID patients using cardiac MRI.
Cross-sectional neuroimaging study examining cortical and subcortical grey matter volume alterations in patients with neuropsychiatric long-COVID syndrome.
Pilot study characterizing fibrosis-associated gene expression pathways in lung tissue from COVID-19 ARDS and long COVID patients with interstitial lung disease compared to ILD from other causes.
Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of chronic rhinosinusitis in long COVID patients.
Cross-sectional study investigating the frequency and severity of olfactory disorders in long COVID patients with fatigue symptoms.
Biomarker study comparing inflammatory and endothelial markers in long COVID patients versus controls, identifying microclotting and thrombotic endothelialitis as pathological mechanisms.
Investigative study examining the direct effects of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins on murine cochlear tissue in vitro, not a human clinical trial or treatment study.

Comparative cross-sectional study of biomarkers in the gut-liver axis between severe and mild COVID-19 patients at 9-10 months post-infection, identifying long-term alterations in microbial composition, serum metabolites, and immune function.
Cross-sectional study examining the frequency and characteristics of long COVID symptoms in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (CED).
Characterizes a phenotype of post-COVID-19 patients with dyspnea, identifying patterns of ventilatory dysfunction, neuromuscular disturbance, and chronic fatigue.
Cross-sectional electrophysiological study comparing neuromuscular junction function and muscle fiber conduction velocity between long COVID patients with and without fatigue and controls.
A German-language study examining whether hamsters are an appropriate animal model for post-acute respiratory sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection by investigating alveolar regeneration processes.
Describes a learning health system model for long COVID care and research in British Columbia, tracking patient outcomes and program metrics over 2 years without testing a specific intervention.

A mathematical model using ODEs to simulate long-term side effects in COVID-19 recovered populations, with numerical solutions and optimization methods but no empirical data or treatment intervention.
Identifies 140 candidate autoantigens from T-lymphoblasts that may contribute to autoimmune phenomena in post-COVID syndrome through proteome profiling and multi-omic comparison.

Analyzes electronic health records of COVID-19 patients to identify disease comorbidity patterns and molecular mechanisms of PASC through network and protein interaction analysis, without testing any specific intervention.
Longitudinal study characterizing SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ and CD4+ T cell responses and TCR repertoires in long COVID patients over 24 months post-infection and post-vaccination.
Mechanistic study investigating how SARS-CoV-2 S1 spike protein induces neuroinflammation and astrocyte dysfunction in long COVID, identifying TLR7 and p38 MAPK as potential therapeutic targets.
In vitro study using lung organoids to investigate SARS-CoV-2 entry mechanisms and pulmonary inflammatory responses, proposing surfactant and endocytosis blockers as potential adjunctive therapies.
Preclinical study modeling long COVID lung fibrosis in humanized mice and testing combined anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrosis treatment approaches.

Post hoc analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled trial of vortioxetine examining the relationship between fatigue and depressive symptoms in long COVID patients.

Autopsy and in vitro study characterizing SARS-CoV-2 brain infection, astrocyte damage, and neuronal dysfunction in severe COVID-19 and long COVID patients.
In silico molecular docking study proposing cannabidiol and cannabivarin as potential treatments for post-COVID neurodegeneration, but no experimental validation or clinical data.
Integrated network biology study identifying diseases associated with post-COVID syndrome through protein interaction networks and pathway analysis, not a treatment trial.

In silico molecular docking study evaluating phytochemical compounds from Citrus macroptera as potential inhibitors of post-COVID inflammatory proteins, with no experimental validation or clinical data.
Cross-sectional study comparing muscle oxygenation patterns during submaximal and maximal exercise tests in post-COVID-19 patients with pulmonary involvement.

Ecological momentary assessment study examining associations between long COVID diagnosis and real-world physical symptoms (aches/fatigue, respiratory) and their relationships with mental health and psychosocial functioning.
Cross-sectional study comparing prevalence and features of post-COVID syndrome symptoms in university students with mild-to-moderate acute illness versus recovered and never-infected controls.

Retrospective observational study examining associations between cognitive disengagement syndrome, mood, anxiety, and functional impairment in pediatric long COVID patients without testing an intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between post-COVID fatigue and cognitive complaints in 246 veterans, finding that subjective cognitive complaints correlate with fatigue rather than objective cognitive performance.
Latent class analysis identifying three PASC phenotypes differentiated by symptom burden over six months post-infection, comparing outcomes across vaccination status.
A cross-sectional experimental study examining anxiety responses to online health information searching about long COVID compared to imagery of illness in 60 participants.

A 4-week combined progressive rehabilitation program (12 sessions of respiratory and motor training) improved functional abilities, disability status, and quality of life in 18 COVID-19 recovered patients.

Cross-sectional study comparing oxidative stress and inflammatory biomarkers in blood samples from healthy controls, acute COVID-19 patients, and PASC patients to understand the role of OS in long COVID pathophysiology.
Economic analysis of Long COVID's impact on UK employment and labor supply using prevalence estimates and activity-limitation data.
In vitro study using C2C12 myoblasts to investigate spike protein effects on myogenic differentiation and protein metabolism, with FAK transfection as a potential intervention.

Cross-sectional assessment of psychological functioning in 43 long COVID patients using neuropsychological testing, finding elevated somatic preoccupation and depression but no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional neuropsychological assessment of 49 long COVID patients examining cognitive functioning, mood, and anxiety at 6 months post-infection, finding borderline cognitive performance but prominent psychological distress.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between performance validity test failure, fatigue, and psychological functioning in 175 Long COVID patients using standardized assessment instruments.

Multidimensional analysis of mood, cognition, sleep and circadian rhythms in long COVID patients to characterize the phenotype of PASC fatigue.
Economic analysis updating ME/CFS prevalence estimates and NIH funding implications post-COVID, without studying any treatments.
Experimental study showing that gut microbiota from post-COVID patients causes post-COVID-like symptoms in germ-free mice, suggesting the microbiota as a therapeutic target.
Observational study examining dysregulated microbial tryptophan metabolism in COVID-19 and long COVID patients, showing associations with inflammatory markers and immune dysfunction.
Cross-sectional study examining relationships between clinical and inflammatory markers and severity of fatigue and neuropsychiatric symptoms in post-acute COVID-19 survivors.

Case-control study identifying host genetic polymorphisms associated with long COVID development in COVID-19 patients.
Preliminary economic impact estimate of long COVID in the United States based on prevalence projections and ME/CFS cost models.

Metagenomics and metabolomics study of age-associated gut microbiota changes in a hamster COVID-19 model, correlating dysbiosis with acute disease severity and long-term sequelae, but not testing any treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of blood transcriptome data from 10,613 samples identifying mast cell activation and hub genes associated with poor health transitions in elderly COVID-19 patients with frailty.
Observational study measuring senescence markers in hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 3-month follow-up to investigate associations with pulmonary sequelae, not an intervention trial.
Multi-cohort study comparing interferon gene expression patterns across acute COVID-19, long COVID, and autoimmune disease patients to investigate cytokine exhaustion as a driver of long COVID.

In vitro study using human intestinal organoids to demonstrate that autophagy-enhancing drugs (MK-2206) limit SARS-CoV-2 infection and prevent barrier damage, with no human subjects or clinical trial component.
Cross-sectional study identifying distinct phenotypes of pediatric post-COVID condition through unsupervised clustering of exhaled metabolites and volatile organic compound biomarkers.
In vitro study of metabolic adaptation in skeletal muscle tissue exposed to sera from long COVID and ME/CFS patients, without testing any treatment intervention.
Retrospective study measuring podocyte-specific proteins in urine exosomes at 10 days, 6 months, and 12 months post-COVID to assess persistent renal injury in long COVID patients.
Cross-sectional study comparing cytokine profiles and immune pathway dysregulation in PASC patients versus healthy controls following in vitro TLR stimulation.
Cross-sectional study examining whether self-reported fatigue in long COVID patients correlates with EMG-derived muscle fatigue index; found no significant association.
Cross-sectional study examining prevalence of coronavirus anxiety and its associations with mood and cognitive symptoms in 72 PASC patients, with no intervention tested.
Exploratory analysis examining the relationship between health anxiety and cognitive performance in 19 PASC patients using neuropsychological testing, without testing any intervention.
Cross-sectional study characterizing cognitive functioning in neuro-PASC patients and examining associations with fatigue, depression, and hospitalization status.
A prospective follow-up study of 10 post-COVID patients examining exhaled breath condensate pH as a marker of residual alveolar inflammation at 3 and 6 months post-discharge.

Cross-sectional study measuring cytokine and chemokine profiles in SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals (symptomatic and asymptomatic) and their association with post-COVID-19 sequela symptoms 12 months post-infection.
A Mendelian randomization study examining bidirectional causal relationships between COVID-19 severity and thyroid dysfunction using genome-wide association data.
Cross-sectional study examining the association between insomnia symptoms and sustained attention deficits in long COVID patients seen at a PASC clinic.
Baseline neuropsychological assessment of 123 long COVID patients from an RCT (COVCOG) identifying three distinct cognitive profiles and characterizing cognitive, sleep, and fatigue symptoms.
Cross-sectional study examining symptom over-reporting, mood, and anxiety in long COVID patients undergoing neuropsychological evaluation, without any treatment intervention.
Integrated network analysis of biomedical data to identify genes associated with SARS-CoV-2 host response and long-term effects, with potential drug targets identified through computational methods.

Cross-sectional study examining how clinical variables, demographics, and comorbidities affect cognitive performance in 236 post-COVID patients compared to 148 controls using standardized neuropsychological testing.
Describes pyBiodatafuse, a bioinformatics tool for integrating omics databases and creating knowledge graphs, demonstrated on post-COVID syndrome gene expression data but not a treatment study.
Develops a Bernoulli mixture model with feature selection to identify long COVID subphenotypes and minimal diagnostic criteria using self-reported symptom data from the RECOVER-Adult cohort study.
Neuroimaging study comparing brain structural and functional alterations in post-COVID syndrome patients versus healthy controls, with correlation to cognitive dysfunction.
Cross-sectional neuroimaging study investigating early limbic inflammation as a potential mechanism underlying long COVID sequelae.
Investigates brain injury biomarkers (NfL, GFAP, tau) and dysregulated immune responses in COVID-19 patients followed at 4 months post-infection.

A 7T MRI study comparing brainstem abnormalities in 30 post-COVID patients versus 51 controls, finding persistent pathological changes in medullary and midbrain regions associated with acute disease severity and functional recovery.

Cross-sectional study examining cognitive impairment and structural brain abnormalities (cortical thinning, white matter changes) in 83 long COVID patients with persistent neurological symptoms compared to 22 COVID-recovered controls without neurological sequelae.
Cross-sectional mechanistic study comparing neurophysiological and autonomic function in 37 long COVID patients with fatigue versus 52 controls, without testing any intervention.
Cross-sectional study examining structural brain alterations and cognitive impairment in post-COVID patients 2 years post-infection, with correlations to blood biomarkers.
Comparative study examining dissociable impairments in short- vs long-term memory precision in individuals recovering from mild COVID-19 using a controlled experimental task.
Cross-sectional study comparing structural brain connectivity in post-COVID patients versus healthy controls, finding altered putamen connectivity associated with fatigue severity.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and neurobiological correlates of anosognosia (lack of awareness of cognitive impairment) in post-COVID syndrome patients, with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing cerebral blood flow dynamics during cognitive tasks in post-COVID-19 patients versus controls using functional near-infrared spectroscopy.

Cross-sectional study assessing olfactory function in COVID-19 survivors ~174 days post-infection using diagnostic testing and self-perception measures, finding subjective but not objective olfactory impairment.
Development and validation of patient-reported symptom and impact measurement tools for long COVID monitoring.

Cross-sectional study investigating the mechanisms and pathological basis of persistent taste dysfunction in long COVID patients using taste testing and taste papilla biopsies.

A thesis study examining cellular immunity from COVID-19 vaccination and inflammatory/immunological factors in long COVID patients over 24 months, but without testing or evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study characterizing persistent myeloid and lymphoid cell abnormalities in intestinal mucosa of post-COVID patients up to 10 months after infection, with detection of SARS-CoV-2 viral antigens in 33% of subjects.

Prospective observational study examining immune profiles and cardiac MRI abnormalities in long COVID patients with cardiac sequelae, identifying CD8 T cell dysfunction and elevated CCL7 as predictors of myocardial injury.

Cross-sectional study assessing subclinical left and right ventricular dysfunction in COVID-19 recovered patients 30-45 days post-infection using speckle tracking echocardiography, finding dysfunction in ~41-43% of patients.
Pilot study comparing endothelial function via RH-PAT imaging in 10 pediatric PIMS-TS patients versus age-matched controls at 6-month follow-up, finding no significant endothelial dysfunction.

A mechanistic study examining vascular dysfunction in post-COVID patients through tissue biopsy and laboratory assays, identifying Rho-kinase as a potential therapeutic target but not testing any intervention.
A cardiac rehabilitation program for acute COVID-19 patients during hospitalization, not focused on long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

Cross-sectional diagnostic study evaluating handheld ultrasound as a screening tool for cardiac abnormalities in asymptomatic patients one year post-COVID hospitalization, without testing any intervention or treatment.
Cross-sectional study comparing platelet activation status and microvascular dysfunction in long COVID patients at 6 months post-infection versus acute COVID-19 patients and healthy controls.
A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and diagnostic significance of novel ECG patterns following COVID-19 infection in 455 elite soccer players to detect cardiac inflammation.
Cross-sectional study comparing left and right ventricular strain on echocardiography in young adults with prior asymptomatic/mild SARS-CoV-2 infection versus healthy controls.
Cross-sectional study using speckle tracking echocardiography to detect subtle right ventricular systolic dysfunction in post-COVID syndrome patients compared to recovered and healthy controls.
Cross-sectional study evaluating cardiac autonomic function using heart rate variability indices in 50 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent symptoms.

Prospective study comparing cardiac structure and function between post-COVID patients and healthy controls using echocardiography and stress testing, finding biventricular dysfunction and pulmonary congestion in COVID survivors.
Cross-sectional study examining immune mechanisms and cardiac imaging abnormalities in post-COVID patients with cardiac involvement, but no treatment intervention evaluated.
Develops and validates multivariable prediction models for post-COVID-19 cardiovascular disease risk in the general population using electronic health records.
Observational case-control study comparing platelet function and inflammatory markers in COVID-19 convalescents versus matched controls at 2-15 weeks and 6-9 months post-infection.
Mechanistic study comparing carotid chemoreflex sensitivity between non-hospitalised long COVID patients and healthy controls to investigate dysregulated breathing and exercise intolerance.
Compares quantitative autonomic testing results in post-acute COVID-19 patients versus controls and neurogenic autonomic dysfunction patients to characterize cardiovascular dysfunction patterns.

A cross-sectional study developing a novel echocardiography parameter (pulmonary valve acceleration fraction) to assess exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension in long COVID patients, but it is a diagnostic/methodological study with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 204 long COVID patients examining associations between cardiorespiratory symptoms and lung function measurements including diffusion capacity and capillary volume.

Cross-sectional study comparing mitochondrial bioenergetic function in monocytes from post-COVID patients with heart failure symptoms versus matched controls, finding impaired respiratory capacity under oxidative stress conditions.

A 12-month longitudinal observational study of COVID-19 survivors developing an AI model to predict cardiovascular complications and long-term outcomes.

A cross-sectional study measuring endothelial and cardiac autonomic function in 63 young patients with post-COVID symptoms 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding no significant role for endothelial or autonomic dysfunction in cardiac symptom persistence.
A cross-sectional study comparing cytokine and inflammatory markers in long COVID patients with and without postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome versus healthy controls.
Italian national project assessing long COVID magnitude, healthcare service utilization, and care infrastructure with expert-developed clinical practice recommendations.
Diagnostic study comparing 24-hour ECG recordings in long COVID patients with and without POTS to identify autonomic dysfunction markers, with no treatment intervention.
A service evaluation of a 12-week virtual physical activity program for long COVID patients showing improvements in mental wellbeing and aerobic capacity.
Evaluates BioBeat wearable system for remote cardiovascular monitoring in acute COVID-19 patients and post-acute COVID patients, but does not test a treatment intervention.
Epidemiological study estimating the burden of long COVID symptom clusters in Ireland using modeled estimates from national surveillance data, not a treatment trial.

Economic analysis estimating the impact of long COVID on EU labour supply and productivity using survey data and prevalence estimates.

Ecological analysis comparing the epidemiological and economic impact of Long COVID in Italy and the United States among working-age individuals, estimating LC cases, QALY loss, and productivity loss.
Explores integration of Belgian national health data sources into the NEED database to assess unmet health needs for long COVID and other conditions, but does not study any treatment or intervention.
Uses Structural Equation Modeling on NHATS data to examine how severe COVID-19 increases dementia risk through cardiovascular disease as a mediating pathway.
A cross-sectional MRS imaging study comparing brain and muscle metabolites between ME/CFS patients, long-COVID patients, and healthy controls, with no treatment intervention tested.

A quantitative burden of disease study estimating years lived with disability (YLDs) and DALYs attributable to long COVID during the 2021-22 Omicron wave in Australia using previously published symptom prevalence and duration data.

Cross-sectional study measuring interferon-alpha autoantibody prevalence in long COVID patients and controls, finding low prevalence and suggesting these antibodies are unlikely drivers of long COVID symptoms.

Mouse model study examining neurobiological mechanisms of post-acute COVID-19 sequelae, identifying altered cytokines, kynurenine pathway metabolites, and microbiome changes associated with cognitive deficits.

Cross-sectional mechanistic study characterizing cardiopulmonary dysfunction, chronotropic incompetence, and inflammatory markers in long COVID patients compared to controls, without testing any intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing cerebrospinal fluid and plasma biomarkers in post-COVID patients with and without neurocognitive symptoms versus healthy controls, finding no evidence of ongoing viral infection or CNS inflammation.
Retrospective analysis of pre-pandemic metabolic biomarkers in people living with HIV to identify predictors of COVID-19 severity and Long COVID incidence, without testing any intervention.
A computational simulation model estimating the economic and health burden of long COVID in the United States, not a treatment intervention study.

Immunological study comparing immune phenotyping and cytokine profiles in 47 individuals with post-COVID syndrome versus 25 convalescent controls to identify biomarkers and mechanisms underlying persistent symptoms.
A cross-sectional study investigating the role of interferon signaling and autoimmune mechanisms in long COVID pathogenesis through serum biomarker analysis.

A case-control study comparing gene expression profiles in cerebrospinal fluid and blood between women with and without neuropsychiatric long COVID, identifying dysregulated stress response and metabolic pathways.

Develops distributed algorithms to quantify risk factors for PASC among children using EHR data from eight hospitals, but is a methodological paper analyzing existing data rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This study mines Reddit posts to identify and characterize long-COVID symptoms reported by patients, comparing symptom distributions with literature and analyzing temporal patterns, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
Describes development of standardized common data elements for long COVID research through community engagement, not a treatment study.

Develops and validates an XGBoost machine learning model for diagnosing long COVID using electronic health records data from the N3C database.

Develops and validates an NLP pipeline to identify Long COVID symptoms and functional impacts in pediatric EHR data by comparing prevalence of 25 clinical concepts between Long COVID and acute COVID cohorts.

This mechanistic study identifies autoantibodies targeting nervous system proteins in long COVID patients with neurological symptoms and demonstrates a causal link through passive transfer experiments in mice.

Demonstrates that macrophage peroxisome dysfunction contributes to post-COVID chronic lung pathology and fibrosis, and shows that pharmacologically enhancing peroxisome biogenesis mitigates both acute symptoms and chronic sequelae (PASC).
Preclinical study demonstrating that GLP-1 receptor agonists prevent pulmonary fibrosis in a type 2 diabetes mouse model of post-COVID syndrome by reprogramming macrophage responses.
Identifies spike-specific antibody epitopes as potential biomarkers for post-COVID syndrome through comparative analysis of PCS patients and convalescent controls.

This cross-sectional study uses flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing to characterize virus-specific T cell activation in long COVID patients, identifying immunological signatures but not evaluating any treatment intervention.

Mechanistic study examining epithelial-neuro-immune dynamics underlying dysgeusia in long-COVID patients through single-cell transcriptomics and immunological analysis, without testing any intervention.

Identifies an aberrant immune-epithelial niche driving post-viral fibrosis in PASC and demonstrates that neutralizing IFN-γ, TNF, or IL-1β improves pulmonary function in a clinically relevant mouse model.

Basic science study in mice demonstrating that antiviral CD8 T resident memory cells induce blood-brain barrier disruption and anxiety-like behavioral changes after viral clearance, modeling a putative long COVID mechanism.

Mechanistic study identifying age-exacerbated CD8+ T cell responses in post-viral pulmonary fibrosis using mouse models, with implications for understanding long-COVID pathophysiology but no treatment intervention tested.

This study uses Fine Needle Aspirate biopsies to compare germinal center B cell responses and antibody production between long COVID patients and healthy COVID-19 convalescents, finding impaired immune responses in LC patients.
Preclinical proof-of-concept study testing lipid nanoparticles carrying NET inhibitors in mouse models of COVID-19 lung injury, with no human treatment trial data.

Investigates the role of dysfunctional regulatory T cells (Tregs) and Notch4 expression in brain fog during long COVID through patient biomarkers, RNAseq analysis, and a post-viral infection mouse model.
RNA sequencing study comparing monocyte gene expression profiles in long COVID patients with pulmonary symptoms versus recovered and healthy controls to identify dysregulated inflammatory pathways.
Cross-sectional study comparing neutrophil dysregulation, NET formation, and inflammatory markers in PASC patients with pulmonary symptoms versus healthy and recovered controls.
Develops and pilots a computable phenotyping algorithm to identify children with postacute sequelae of COVID-19 and characterize their clinical epidemiology in a large healthcare network.
Mechanistic study investigating a genetic mutation (NACAD) associated with COVID-19 orchitis and its effects on ACE2 expression in testicular tissue, using siRNA knockdown in primary cells.
Prospective study examining associations between COVID-19 serology, humoral immunity, and laboratory test abnormalities including elevated HbA1c, without intervention or treatment focus.
Cross-sectional study examining the frequency and microbiological etiology of respiratory infections in long COVID patients, with analysis of associated clinical and radiological findings.

Cross-sectional study examining DNA damage and genetic instability in acute and chronic post-COVID groups using comet assay, finding no overall differences but gender-specific patterns in the acute phase.
Multi-omics study identifying distinct molecular signatures and biomarkers across long COVID symptom subgroups.

A cross-sectional study examining serotonin levels in hemodialysis patients with and without long COVID-associated cognitive symptoms, finding lower serotonin in the post-COVID phase among those with cognitive impairment.

Observational study examining the association between SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia at acute infection and development of post-acute sequelae, showing RNAemia predicts PASC independent of demographics and disease severity.

Uses machine learning to identify three distinct long COVID symptom phenotypes (sensory, fatigue/cognitive, respiratory) among 97 military beneficiaries with persistent symptoms at 6 months post-COVID.

Comparative study of glutathione levels, antioxidant activity, and DNA damage/repair markers in post-COVID patients versus controls, examining underlying pathophysiological mechanisms rather than testing a treatment intervention.
Machine learning analysis of blood transcriptome data to identify biomarkers predictive of long COVID development in military beneficiaries, but no treatment intervention tested.
Develops an elastic net regression algorithm to identify long COVID patients from population-level health administrative data in British Columbia, achieving high sensitivity and specificity.
An EHR-based study identifying and characterizing distinct clinical subphenotypes of pediatric long COVID using clustering methods on retrospectively identified patients from the RECOVER program.

Comparative antibody profiling study examining differences in humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 and endemic coronaviruses between PASC and non-PASC patients with pre-existing systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease.
Population-based outreach study characterizing the incidence and clinical characteristics of long COVID within a health system to assess care needs.

A Colombian clinic implemented a transdisciplinary care model for long COVID patients combining physiatry, physiotherapy, psychology, nutrition, and other specialties, reporting improvements in functionality and symptom resolution in 448 screened patients.

Investigates the role of type I interferon autoantibodies and IFN-stimulated gene activity in post-COVID-19 syndrome pathogenesis, finding limited evidence for IFN system impairment as a cause of PCS.
Retrospective cohort study evaluating treatment outcomes (IVIG, steroids, immunomodulators) in 126 children diagnosed with MIS-C at a tertiary care center between 2020-2022.
Cross-sectional study comparing plasma extracellular vesicle profiles between long COVID patients and COVID-recovered controls to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers.
Machine learning and transcriptomic analysis identifying distinct long COVID symptom phenotypes and their associated early gene expression signatures in military health system beneficiaries.
Cross-sectional study measuring PD-1 and PD-L1 serum levels in 108 children with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding significant correlation between PD-1 and PD-L1 concentrations.
A cross-sectional study examining mitochondrial dysfunction and altered cytokine responses in circulating immune cells of long COVID patients compared to healthy COVID-recovered controls.

A modeling study using a dynamic transmission model to estimate the potential impact of mRNA-1283 vaccine on preventing post-acute COVID-19 outcomes including long COVID, based on clinical trial data from vaccine efficacy trials rather than conducting a new treatment study.
A cross-sectional lipidomic study identifying sphingolipid and glycerophospholipid biomarkers that distinguish post-acute COVID-19 patients from healthy controls and COVID-19 patients without PASC.
Cross-sectional study of 35 long COVID patients examining the relationship between fatigue severity and neurological symptoms including depression and cognitive impairment.

Cross-sectional study characterizing cardiopulmonary structural and physiological changes in patients with persistent dyspnea following COVID-19 using imaging, cardiac testing, and pulmonary function assessments.

Quantitative analysis of environmental and cost benefits of consolidating pediatric long COVID subspecialty consultations into a single multidisciplinary clinic visit, with no treatment intervention or control group.
Machine learning study using wearable sensor data to develop models for detecting long COVID from acute infection metrics, without testing any intervention.
Uses NIH All of Us data to construct a long COVID phenotype risk score and examine associations between daily step counts and long COVID risk, but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.
Mechanistic study demonstrating SARS-CoV-2 can infect retinal pigment epithelium in mice and cell culture, causing inflammatory changes and barrier dysfunction similar to AMD pathology.

In vitro and animal model study investigating SARS-CoV-2-induced Tau phosphorylation and aggregation as a molecular mechanism underlying post-COVID neurological symptoms, without testing any treatment intervention.
A public health study using prevalence estimates and population data to predict the number of long COVID patients and inform service development in two UK health systems.

Phenome-wide Mendelian randomization study investigating genetic associations between COVID-19 and 2272 traits using FinnGen data, identifying causal effects on cardiovascular, respiratory, autoimmune, and metabolic outcomes.
Retrospective analysis of 254 pediatric long COVID patients identifying four distinct symptom clusters through multiple correspondence analysis to characterize disease heterogeneity.
Validates the C19-YRSm scale for measuring post-COVID-19 symptoms and functional disability in a prospective observational study of 369 long COVID patients and 426 controls.
Cross-sectional study assessing cardiac function (GLS) and heart rate variability in post-COVID patients to characterize long COVID-related cardiac involvement and dysautonomia.
A cross-sectional study analyzing EEG spectral density during sleep in COVID-19 survivors compared to pre-COVID controls, finding abnormal alpha frequencies and elevated REM density.

Comparative polysomnographic fractal analysis study examining differences in sleep signal patterns between long COVID patients with insomnia and matched controls with chronic insomnia, finding significant differences in abdominal and EEG fractal dimensions.
Pilot study comparing sleep quality, sleepiness, and neurocognitive function in post-COVID patients with OSA versus controls with OSA but without prior COVID infection.
Pilot study comparing sleep disturbances, cognitive function, and quality of life in PASC patients versus OSA controls without COVID history.
Preclinical rat study evaluating NLS-4 and modafinil effects on circadian rhythm impairment induced by experimental fatigue procedure.
Genome-wide association study identifying genetic risk loci and correlations for Long COVID, fatigue, and sleep disturbances using population-level genetic data and electronic health records.
Cross-sectional study evaluating the impact of sleep disruption on cognitive function and quality of life in 39 patients with neurologic manifestations of long COVID.
Comparative polysomnographic study of post-COVID-19 insomnia versus non-COVID chronic insomnia, finding subtle differences in REM sleep atonia and sleep continuity suggesting viral CNS involvement.
This study investigates nocturnal hypoxemia in people with long COVID using polysomnography to measure blood oxygen saturation during sleep.

Describes the diagnostic and monitoring utility of a cardiopulmonary coupling spectrogram device (SleepImage Ring) across various sleep disorders including long COVID and chronic fatigue syndrome, with data from over 500 patients.
Cross-sectional study comparing sleep architecture and neurocognitive function in long COVID patients versus controls using polysomnography and cognitive testing.
Cross-sectional study examining sleep quality, sleep efficiency, and their associations with depression, anxiety, PTSD, and fatigue in non-hospitalized individuals with PASC.
In vitro study of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein effects on bronchial epithelial cell gene expression, examining potential mechanisms underlying long COVID persistence.
In vitro study investigating NHE1's role in profibrotic activity in IPF and post-COVID lung fibrosis using fibroblast cell lines.

Cross-sectional study assessing autonomic nervous system function in collegiate athletes 2 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2 infection using beat-by-beat blood pressure, heart rate variability, and biochemical markers.
In vitro study testing whether angiotensin 1-7 administration restores endothelial-dependent vasodilation in isolated arterioles from post-COVID subjects compared to controls.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiac baroreflex sensitivity and heart rate variability between long COVID patients with and without persistent symptoms and healthy controls, with no intervention tested.
Cross-sectional study comparing cardiovascular and heart rate variability responses to acute exercise in previously symptomatic vs asymptomatic COVID-19 infected individuals and controls.
Case series measuring autonomic nervous system dysfunction in 6 PASC patients using physiological tracking algorithms, but reports no treatment intervention or therapeutic outcomes.
Preclinical mechanistic study using a hamster model to investigate SARS-CoV-2-induced neuropathy and pain hypersensitivity in long COVID, identifying transcriptional changes in dorsal root ganglia.
Conference abstract describing immune response mechanisms in COVID-19 and proposing patient-stratified treatment approaches, but no empirical trial or intervention study.
Basic science study examining how SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a protein disrupts autophagy and sphingolipid homeostasis in brain cells using mouse models and cell culture.
In vitro study using human cortical organoids to investigate SARS-CoV-2 infection and Spike protein-induced neurological pathology, not a treatment intervention study.

Cross-sectional study comparing brain MRI susceptibility-weighted imaging findings between 46 COVID-recovered patients and 30 healthy controls, showing brain abnormalities in frontal lobe and brain stem regions.
Examines red blood cell ultrastructural changes in heart failure patients with hypertension and long COVID using electron microscopy, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing blood pressure response to exercise between post-COVID patients with and without PTSD symptoms, finding exaggerated exercise BP response in PTSD group, particularly in women.
Develops machine learning models to predict Long COVID-19 development at 3 months post-discharge in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with improved accuracy in the hypertensive subgroup.

Observational case-control study comparing plasma ACE2 activity between SARS-CoV-2 recovered patients and uninfected controls, finding persistently elevated ACE2 in recovered patients but not testing any intervention.
Laboratory study examining SARS-CoV-2 S protein-induced endothelial dysfunction and senescence in cell cultures and isolated vessels, with testing of protective compounds (klotho, angiotensin-(1-7)).
Case series evaluating hyperbaric oxygen therapy for improving cognitive function, psychiatric symptoms, pain, and fatigue in post-COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study measuring endothelial vasodilator function via pulse wave response to salbutamol in previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients compared to controls, finding impaired β2-adrenergic endothelium-dependent vasodilation.
Case series evaluating pulmonary rehabilitation outcomes for dyspnea in long COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study assessing neuropsychological and cognitive impairment in nonhospitalized long COVID patients with subjective cognitive complaints, finding objective cognitive deficits in 69% of participants.
Mechanistic study investigating how SARS-CoV-2 N protein interacts with Nav1.7 ion channels to promote pathological pain in mouse models.

Cross-sectional comparison of cytokine profiles in children with long COVID, post-acute COVID controls, and healthy controls, identifying proinflammatory signatures including elevated Flt3L, CD5, uPA, CCL23, CD40, and TGFα.

Mechanistic study comparing anti-satellite glial cell IgG autoantibodies in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome and fibromyalgia syndrome patients using passive transfer experiments in mice, not a treatment trial.
Develops and applies novel statistical methods to analyze current status data on symptom resolution in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome from a University of Washington testing program.

A Mendelian randomization study investigating genetic evidence for causal association between COVID-19 susceptibility and chronic pancreatitis risk, not focused on long COVID or treatment of long COVID patients.

Describes a post-COVID care center model that provides comprehensive evaluation and multidisciplinary rehabilitation services to long COVID patients, with outcomes from 114 patients referred to various specialties.
Bioinformatic analysis of gene expression data identifying m7G methylation-related genes and constructing a predictive model for early LC identification, without testing any intervention.
Comparative study of two diagnostic tests (head-up tilt test vs NASA lean test) for assessing hemodynamic responses in young individuals with postacute COVID-19 syndrome.

A proof-of-concept cross-sectional study comparing [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging findings between long COVID patients with fatigue and myalgia and healthy controls, finding no significant quantitative differences.

Cross-sectional comparison of corneal endothelial cell parameters in COVID-19 patients with ocular symptoms versus controls, finding decreased endothelial cell density and hexagonality in COVID-19 patients.
Cross-sectional comparison of balance performance in post-acute COVID-19 patients versus COPD exacerbation patients and healthy controls, identifying balance deficits requiring physiotherapy.

Document analysis of implementing a multijurisdictional HIE-based academic-nonprofit partnership for Long COVID public health surveillance from 2022-2025, focusing on operational lessons learned rather than testing interventions.

A retrospective analysis of an occupational therapy fatigue management intervention for 60 post-COVID patients, showing significant improvements in fatigue, well-being, and health status after 2 weeks.
Compares clinical features and OPRM1 polymorphisms in post-COVID-19 chronic pain patients versus knee osteoarthritis patients and controls.
Mathematical modeling study analyzing uncertainty in PASC prevalence trajectories and the impact of variant transmission dynamics on long COVID forecasts.

Cross-sectional study using advanced imaging (HP Xe MRI) and computational modeling to characterize small airway functional impairment in long COVID patients with dyspnea, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
Observational study comparing PTPN22, TRAF-1, and IL-1β gene expression in rheumatoid arthritis patients versus controls following SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination.
Compares T cell assay methods for retrospectively determining SARS-CoV-2 infection to distinguish long COVID from other multi-syndromic diseases.
This paper describes an animal model study using BALB/c mice infected with SARS-CoV-2 B.1.351 variant to characterize neurological and respiratory pathophysiology, not a human treatment trial.

Describes the CUNY Recovery Corps virtual navigation service that connected COVID-affected New Yorkers to resources and Long COVID services, focusing on program implementation and quality improvement rather than testing a specific treatment intervention.
Mathematical modeling study examining long-term COVID-19 immuno-epidemiology and long COVID burden under various immunity and vaccination scenarios.

Mechanistic study in mice showing SARS-CoV-2 infection of substantia nigra induces miR-330-5p downregulation and neuroinflammation; proposes potential therapeutic target but does not study long COVID or any intervention in humans.
Theoretical epidemiological model examining how post-infection mortality from long COVID affects disease dynamics and epidemic cycling, without empirical treatment evaluation.
Comparative study of autoimmune antibody signatures in acute COVID-19 patients, long COVID convalescents, and pre-pandemic controls, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A randomized controlled mouse study evaluating whether ozone water enemas combined with fecal microbiota transplantation from COVID-19 patients can restore gut microbial balance and reduce post-viral inflammation through SIRT1-Nrf2/HO-1 pathway activation.
Mechanistic study of ryanodine receptor oxidation in COVID-19 tissues with ex-vivo drug testing, but no clinical trial or patient treatment data.

In vitro study of SARS-CoV-2-induced diarrheal mechanisms in human enteroid monolayers, demonstrating calcium-dependent inflammatory anion secretion involving viral uptake and cytokine-mediated ion channel activation.
Multi-omic longitudinal study of 140 COVID-19 patients identifying four distinct immunological recovery trajectories and predictive plasma protein panels for survival and recovery outcomes.
Longitudinal characterization of post-COVID-19 symptoms using machine learning analysis of 296,154 Twitter posts to track patient experiences and symptomatology over 150+ days.
Cross-sectional study characterizing small airways disease in post-COVID patients using pulmonary function tests and quantitative CT imaging across groups stratified by acute infection severity.
Immunological study documenting significant immune system differences between children who recovered from acute COVID-19 and those with post-acute sequelae (PASC).
Metabolomic analysis comparing plasma metabolite profiles in ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls to identify dysregulation of peroxisomal and lipid pathways.
Develops a comprehensive PASC symptom lexicon from electronic health records using NLP to identify and categorize post-COVID symptoms in 26,117 patients.
Observational study examining immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination in convalescent individuals, with mechanistic insights into long COVID but no active treatment intervention.
Characterizes distinct T cell and immunological responses in long COVID patients with neurologic symptoms compared to healthy COVID convalescents.
Immuno-proteomic study characterizing airway immune responses and epithelial injury in patients with prolonged post-COVID respiratory disease 3-6 months after hospitalization.

Cross-sectional study assessing depressive, anxious, and cognitive symptoms along with brain structure/function in 100 COVID-19 survivors ~3 months post-infection using questionnaires, neurocognitive testing, and neuroimaging.
Cross-sectional clinical assessment examining long COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms in 380 children and adolescents at a psychiatric outpatient clinic.
This retrospective cohort study identifies SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia at presentation as a predictor of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19, independent of demographic and disease severity factors.

Longitudinal profiling of immune responses in mild COVID-19 patients from early infection through >100 days post-symptom onset, identifying inflammatory signatures associated with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC).
Discovery study profiling IgG autoantibodies in SARS-CoV-2 positive healthcare workers to characterize autoimmune signatures associated with long COVID sequelae.
Develops machine learning models using EHR data to identify potential long COVID patients from a large COVID-19 cohort, not a treatment trial.
Immunologic and serological characterization identifying distinct inflammatory and quiescent PASC patient subsets with potential diagnostic biomarkers.
Postmortem neuropathological study comparing olfactory bulb deafferentation markers in COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 cases to understand mechanisms of post-acute neurological sequelae.

Transcriptome-wide investigation of acute COVID-19 patients followed into the post-acute period, identifying gene expression signatures and multiple molecular etiologies of long COVID sequelae involving plasma cells and antibody responses.
Animal and human tissue study characterizing persistent inflammation in olfactory tissues post-SARS-CoV-2 infection as a mechanism for long COVID symptoms.
Development and validation of the Symptom Burden Questionnaire for Long COVID (SBQ™-LC), a 17-scale patient-reported outcome measure to assess symptom burden in long COVID patients.

A cross-sectional study using trained sniffer dogs to detect volatile organic compounds in sweat samples as a potential diagnostic test for viral persistence in long COVID patients, with no treatment intervention.
Investigates HERV-W envelope protein expression in COVID-19 patients and post-mortem tissues as a potential pathogenic mechanism underlying acute and post-acute COVID symptoms.
Mechanistic study using mouse models and human tissue to identify neuroinflammatory pathways and cellular dysregulation underlying long COVID cognitive symptoms, without testing any intervention.
Bioinformatic and in vitro study identifying amyloidogenic peptides in SARS-CoV-2 proteome that may contribute to long COVID neurological symptoms through cytotoxic amyloid aggregates.
An imaging study using hyperpolarized xenon MRI to investigate pulmonary gas transfer abnormalities in long-COVID patients compared to controls and post-hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Comparative immunologic study of SARS-CoV-2-specific responses in people with and without HIV, measuring antibody and T cell responses in COVID-19 recovered individuals with and without PASC symptoms.

Observational study comparing SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell frequencies and inflammatory markers between pulmonary PASC patients and recovered COVID-19 controls, demonstrating associations with lung function impairment.

Prospective study comparing lung perfusion parameters via DCE-MRI in non-hospitalized post-COVID individuals with persistent dyspnea versus healthy controls, finding sex-specific perfusion disturbances.
A preclinical mouse model study testing antiviral (EIDD-2801) and anti-fibrotic (nintedanib) interventions for PASC-associated persistent lung disease.
Cross-sectional study examining childhood trauma as a risk factor for long COVID development in 338 participants.
Uses machine learning on electronic health records to identify four reproducible subphenotypes of post-acute SARS-CoV-2 infection based on co-occurring conditions and patient characteristics.

A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between acute COVID-19 severity markers and long COVID physio-affective symptoms through oxidative stress, antioxidant defenses, and inflammatory pathways.

Mechanistic study comparing fungal translocation markers (β-glucan) and inflammatory biomarkers in long COVID patients versus controls, identifying Dectin-1/NF-κB signaling as a potential targetable pathway.
RNA-seq and DNA methylation analysis of peripheral blood from recovered COVID-19 patients 3 months post-discharge to identify transcriptomic and epigenomic signatures associated with long COVID risk.
Observational study identifying naturally arising anti-chemokine antibodies in COVID-19 convalescents that correlate with favorable outcomes and absence of long COVID symptoms.

Investigates persistent smell loss in PASC patients through objective olfactory testing, single-cell sequencing, and histology of olfactory epithelium, revealing T cell-mediated inflammatory pathophysiology but no treatment intervention.
Serum proteome profiling study identifying inflammatory protein signatures in long COVID patients to define molecular subsets and potential therapeutic pathways.

Characterizes immune system changes in individuals recovered from mild COVID-19 using multimodal single-cell analysis and assesses their response to influenza vaccination, but does not test a treatment intervention for long COVID symptoms.
Develops a machine learning-based vocal biomarker to detect and monitor fatigue in COVID-19 and long COVID patients using voice recordings.
Uses machine learning on EHR data from NIH N3C and RECOVER to identify six distinct long COVID patient subtypes based on phenotypic abnormalities and their associations with outcomes.

In vitro study of SARS-CoV-2 infection of brain endothelial cells to understand mechanisms of BBB dysfunction and neuroinflammation in COVID-19/long COVID, with no treatment intervention or patient outcomes.

Cross-sectional study measuring elevated neurotoxic metabolites and inflammatory cytokines in serum of mild COVID-19 patients, proposing them as potential biomarkers for long-COVID cognitive symptoms.

Preclinical and human genetic study demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 spike protein induces TLR4-mediated cognitive impairment in mice and associating a TLR4 genetic variant with poor cognitive outcomes in post-COVID patients.
Longitudinal study of immune, metabolic, and inflammatory responses in 215 COVID-19 patients over one year to identify systemic recovery profiles and predictors of long COVID.

Identifies antibody epitopes associated with severe COVID-19 and long COVID through computational analysis of polyclonal antibody repertoires, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study comparing circulating spike protein and viral RNA levels in acute COVID-19 patients versus those with and without post-COVID symptoms, finding persistent viral components in PASC patients.
Systems serology study profiling antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2 and endemic pathogens in PASC patients with pre-existing rheumatic disease to characterize immunological mechanisms.

Observational cross-sectional study comparing cognitive and attention performance between long COVID, acute COVID, and no-COVID control groups using standardized behavioral tests and self-reported measures.
Preclinical study in a mouse model of SARS-CoV-2-induced brain inflammation demonstrating that donepezil improves symptoms by restoring cholinergic anti-inflammatory signaling.
Comparative study measuring plasma cytokine levels in long-COVID patients versus healthy controls to identify immune dysregulation patterns.

Prospective cohort study evaluating post-concussion assessment tools (symptom questionnaires, vestibular/neuropsychological tests, balance tasks) as diagnostic measures to differentiate long COVID patients from recovered controls, with implications for rehabilitation-based treatment approaches.
Laboratory study demonstrating elevated inflammatory molecules and microclots in long COVID patients' blood, suggesting thrombotic endotheliitis as a pathological mechanism.
In vitro study of SARS-CoV-2 infection mechanism in human neurons using iPSC-derived neural cells, demonstrating endosomal entry pathway and blockade by PIK5K inhibitors.

Cross-sectional study examining how inflammatory biomarkers from acute COVID-19 and subsequent neuro-immune/oxidative pathways predict quality of life, depression, anxiety, and fatigue severity in long COVID patients.

Systems serology study comparing humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses in serum and CSF of long COVID patients with neurological symptoms versus unaffected COVID-19 survivors.

Cross-sectional study examining immune activation patterns at 3 months post-hospitalization in COVID-19 patients, finding persistent T-cell activation in severe disease that correlates with long COVID symptoms.

Post-mortem brain tissue analysis examining transcriptional and cellular signatures in SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals compared to Alzheimer's disease, identifying shared neuroinflammatory mechanisms in neuro-PASC.
A neuroimaging study comparing susceptibility-weighted MRI brain alterations in COVID-recovered patients versus healthy controls, with correlation analysis of fatigue symptoms.

Post-mortem histopathological study of lung tissue from 12 patients who died with post-acute COVID-19, examining viral persistence and cellular damage including senescent alveolar type 2 cells and fibrosis.

A cross-sectional study characterizing pulmonary pathology, immune profiles, and radiologic abnormalities in 51 mild PASC patients via biopsy, imaging, and cytokine analysis without testing any treatment intervention.
