Cross-sectional study comparing immune responses and autoantibody profiles in 40 post-acute COVID-19 (PASC) patients versus 15 convalescent controls.

Investigates dysregulated alveolar regeneration in SARS-CoV-2-infected hamsters as a model for understanding respiratory PASC pathomechanisms, demonstrating incomplete alveolar restoration and senescence markers.
Uses NLP on social media posts to identify and characterize long COVID symptoms and patient-reported health outcomes, not a treatment intervention study.

Develops machine learning models to predict long COVID risk based on initial COVID-19 severity using NIH N3C data, identifying distinct predictive features for hospitalized versus non-hospitalized patients.

PhIP-Seq autoantibody profiling in 121 long COVID, 64 recovered COVID, and 57 pre-COVID controls found distinct post-infection autoreactive signatures but no autoreactive patterns distinguishing long COVID from recovery.
Computational analysis identifying G-protein coupled receptor genes and potential FDA drug alternatives as biomarkers for long COVID symptoms.
Applies Bayesian network inference to identify clinical variables and biomarkers associated with COVID-19 severity and long COVID outcomes using the BQC19 dataset, without testing any intervention.
Chart review study validating the accuracy and clinical utility of the ICD-10 U09.9 code for long COVID in 3 US healthcare systems.
Comparative serology study of IgG subtypes in post-COVID patients vs convalescent controls, finding reduced IgG2 but not elevated IgG4 levels.

In-depth analysis of skeletal muscle biopsies from 11 long COVID patients showing capillary alterations, macrophage infiltration, and distinct transcriptomic signatures compared to historical controls.
A longitudinal multi-omics study characterizing immunometabolic dysregulation and inflammatory activation in long COVID patients with chronic headache, without testing any intervention.
Preclinical study establishing a mouse model (MA10-infected BALB/c mice) that reproduces long COVID neuropathology including neuronal loss and microglial activation in the hippocampus.
Basic research study using mouse models and post-mortem tissues to investigate SARS-CoV-2 spike protein accumulation in the brain and its potential role in long-COVID neurological complications.
A phenotype genome-wide association study identifying shared genetic risk factors between COVID-19 and various diseases, biomarkers, and medications across multiple biobanks.

Compares autoantibody production in mild SARS-CoV-2 infected long COVID patients versus COVID convalescent controls, finding elevated SLE and inflammatory myopathy-associated autoantibodies in long COVID with persistent neurologic symptoms.
Pre-clinical study testing RAGE-Ig protein efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 variants in mouse and hamster models, not a human clinical trial or long COVID treatment study.
In vitro and in vivo studies investigating VE-cadherin cleavage by ACE2 as a mechanism for endothelial dysfunction in severe COVID-19 and potential contribution to long COVID development.

A cross-sectional metabolomic study comparing plasma metabolites in long COVID patients, acute COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls to identify dysregulated metabolic pathways and biomarkers associated with long COVID progression.

Develops a machine learning model to predict long COVID risk for clinical deployment, focusing on model selection, fairness, and deployment implications rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluates platelet function and thrombotic potential in long COVID patients compared to matched healthy controls, finding dysregulated platelet responses and coagulation abnormalities.
Animal model study in mice demonstrating post-acute immunological and behavioral sequelae after Omicron infection, with evidence that prior mRNA vaccination protects against these sequelae.

Large-scale blood proteome analysis of 719 long COVID patients identifying distinct inflammatory biomarker profiles associated with specific symptom clusters (cardiorespiratory, cognitive, GI, fatigue, anxiety/depression).
Cross-sectional study measuring plasma cytokine profiles in healthy, acutely infected, and MIS-C patients to identify biomarkers for COVID severity and long COVID risk.
Systematic analysis of UK Biobank health records identifying 679 diseases associated with severe COVID-19 and Long COVID risk, exploring comorbidity patterns and genetic susceptibility.

An uncontrolled case series evaluating polymerized type I collagen (PTIC) treatment in symptomatic COVID-19 outpatients, demonstrating reduced inflammatory markers, improved macrophage phenotype, and clinical symptom improvement including chronic fatigue.

A cross-sectional study investigating carotid chemoreflex sensitivity in long COVID participants compared to controls, proposing carotid body dysregulation as a mechanism for dysregulated breathing and exercise intolerance.
Characterizes shared biomarkers (fibronectin, natural IgM depletion, herpesvirus reactivation) in ME/CFS and long COVID patients to elucidate disease mechanisms.
Observational study using PET imaging to detect T cell activation and viral RNA persistence in long COVID patients up to 2.5 years post-infection, without testing any intervention.

Observational study examining cytokine profiles and microglial activation in COVID-19 patients with respiratory failure, analyzing post-mortem brain tissue and plasma samples without testing any intervention.
Uses machine learning on existing EHR data from the National COVID Cohort Collaborative to predict which COVID-19 patients will develop long COVID based on baseline characteristics.

Develops a single-particle detection assay (BARA) to detect SARS-CoV-2 antigens and RNA in saliva/nasopharyngeal samples, demonstrating long-term viral RNA persistence in extracellular vesicles of post-COVID patients.
Non-human primate study of metabolic dysfunction in long COVID, testing mRNA vaccine as a potential therapeutic intervention.

Post-mortem examination of non-human primate brain tissue showing persistent SARS-CoV-2 RNA and molecular changes relevant to understanding PASC neurological mechanisms, but no treatment intervention tested.
Comparative single-cell analysis of respiratory PASC identifying IFN-γ as a driver, with preclinical validation of IFN-γ neutralization in mouse models.
Single-cell RNA sequencing study characterizing myeloid cell transcriptomic profiles in blood from long COVID patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms versus healthy controls.
Chart review study evaluating the accuracy and utility of the ICD-10 U09.9 code for identifying long COVID patients across three healthcare systems using operationalized WHO and CDC definitions.

Preclinical mouse study demonstrating SARS-CoV-2 neurotropism causes anxiety/depression-like behaviors via microglial activation, with pharmacological microglial inhibition as a potential therapeutic approach.
Uses 3D digital holo-tomographic microscopy to characterize microclot structures in blood plasma of COVID-19 patients as a potential biomarker for long COVID risk.
PET imaging study comparing neuroinflammation in 12 PASC patients versus 43 healthy controls, finding increased brain neuroinflammation correlated with circulating vascular dysfunction markers.
Investigates blood plasma viscosity as a biomarker for COVID-19 and long COVID using Brillouin Light Scattering, but does not test or evaluate any treatment.

This study identifies complement dysregulation as a biomarker distinguishing long COVID patients from healthy convalescent controls, suggesting potential for complement inhibitor treatment, but does not test any intervention.

Mechanistic study of SARS-CoV-2-induced testicular injury and dysfunction in K18-hACE2 mice, examining inflammation, spermatogenesis disruption, and testosterone reduction during acute and post-acute phases.
Cross-sectional study identifying cognitive slowing as a potential biomarker in long COVID patients using web-based reaction time and vigilance tasks.
Describes reengineering a machine learning model to identify long COVID patients in clinical data across changing pandemic conditions, with no treatment intervention tested.
Mechanistic study using hamster model to investigate cardiac conduction system dysfunction in long COVID through innate immune activation and oxidative stress pathways.
Transcriptomic analysis comparing peripheral blood gene expression in long COVID patients with and without pneumonia history versus healthy controls to identify molecular mechanisms.

Single-cell RNA transcriptomics study of nasal biopsies from 33 post-COVID syndrome patients identifying epithelial dysfunction driven by TNFα and TGFβ signaling, with potential therapeutic implications but no treatment intervention tested.

Prospective study evaluating changes in symptoms and immune responses after COVID-19 vaccination in 16 vaccine-naïve long COVID patients, finding symptom improvement in 10 participants and identifying immune biomarkers associated with improvement.
Poisson regression analysis examining associations between accumulated COVID-19 cases and U.S. road deaths in 2021, finding increased road mortality linked to cumulative COVID-19 burden.
Blood transcriptomics study identifying persistent SARS-CoV-2 RNA and a 2-gene biomarker (FYN and antisense RNA) for Long COVID diagnosis with high sensitivity and specificity.
GWAS study of immune cell distributions in healthy individuals that uses polygenic risk scores for long COVID but does not test any treatment or intervention in long COVID patients.
Cross-sectional study correlating handgrip strength with symptom severity and disability in 144 post-COVID patients, finding distinct patterns in ME/CFS subtype.

Retrospective EHR analysis of 1.23 million participants from N3C identifying risk factors and developing machine learning models to predict long COVID development based on demographics and comorbidities.

A case-control study comparing immunological profiles and viral persistence markers in 121 severely affected long COVID patients versus convalescent controls, finding that restrained CD8+ T cell responses correlate with elevated IgG responses and viral antigen persistence.

Proteomic analysis of two long COVID cohorts showing that adjusted data does not support persistent complement system activation, instead identifying signatures of ongoing infection or sustained immune activation.

Post-hoc analysis of a randomized controlled trial evaluating vortioxetine's effect on cognitive function in post-COVID patients, examining the relative contributions of cognitive impairment and fatigue to quality of life.

Murine mechanistic study showing that activated CD8+ T cells in the brain contribute to post-infectious cognitive dysfunction in aged mice infected with respiratory coronavirus, using in vivo and primary cell culture models.

This study quantifies fibrinaloid microclots in platelet-poor plasma from Long COVID patients and controls, finding elevated microclot counts in Long COVID samples and suggesting microclots as a potential biomarker or treatment target.

Cross-sectional immunologic study comparing cytokine profiles and S1 protein persistence in post-vaccination individuals with PASC-like symptoms versus vaccinated controls, without testing any intervention.
Autopsy study examining neuroinflammatory changes (microgliosis, astrogliosis, AQP4 loss) in frontal cortex of COVID-19 patients with long-COVID symptoms.
Immunologic and proteomic study characterizing persistent inflammatory pathways in long COVID patients compared to controls, identifying potential therapeutic targets and biomarkers.

Mechanistic study in hamster models investigating persistent lung inflammation and alveolar-bronchiolization following SARS-CoV-2 infection, identifying Notch signaling dysregulation as a contributing factor.
Evaluates performance of an EHR-based case identification algorithm for pediatric long COVID by comparing algorithmic classification against manual chart review.
Genetic study using Long COVID Host Genetics Initiative data to identify thromboembolism-related genetic variants associated with long COVID risk.
Mouse study investigating persistent neurological dysfunction in PASC, testing whether early antiviral treatment (nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir) prevents long-term neurological abnormalities.

Preclinical mechanistic study in primates showing that kynurenic acid impairs prefrontal cortex cognition and suggesting KYNA-reducing agents as a potential therapeutic approach for cognitive deficits in long COVID.

Identifies diverse autoantibodies in long COVID patients that correlate with neurological symptoms, and demonstrates through animal models that patient-derived antibodies can induce pain, balance loss, and other neurological symptoms.
Preclinical study demonstrating that IgG from long COVID patients induces symptom-like phenotypes in mice, suggesting autoantibodies' role in disease pathogenesis.

Prospective cohort study characterizing PASC symptoms, comorbidities, and blood biomarkers in a diverse (52.5% Black) New Orleans population, finding 75% PASC prevalence and higher IL-6/TNF in PASC-positive patients.

Case-control study comparing autoimmune and inflammatory biomarkers in 90 long COVID patients versus 90 healthy controls to investigate the role of tight junction autoimmunity and HHV-6 reactivation in long COVID's physio-affective phenotype.
Multi-omic analysis of blood samples from acute infection through 12 months post-infection identifying sex-specific immune correlates of long COVID development and persistence.

This cross-sectional study uses MENSA technology to detect SARS-CoV-2 and herpes virus persistence in long-COVID patients compared to recovered controls, demonstrating ongoing viral inflammation in 60% of PASC patients.

This study investigates HERV-W ENV expression in B cells as a potential biomarker associated with COVID-19 severity and long COVID risk, demonstrating a novel ribosome readthrough mechanism for protein translation.
A cross-sectional study characterizing SARS-CoV-2 Persistent Intestinal Epithelial Syndrome (SPIES) in pediatric and young adult long COVID patients through endoscopy, histology, and RNA sequencing.

A mechanistic study examining how soluble IL-2R impairs mitochondrial function in long COVID patients with fatigue, using muscle biopsies and in vitro experiments rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.

Proteomics study in mice showing persistent basement membrane damage in lungs following resolution of influenza infection, with implications for long COVID pathophysiology but no treatment intervention tested.

Cross-sectional and longitudinal study characterizing inflammatory and neurology-related plasma protein profiles in long COVID patients compared to recovered and naive controls, with longitudinal analysis of immune responses to vaccination and breakthrough infection.

Prospective observational study investigating HIF-2α pathway inhibition as a therapeutic target for endothelial dysfunction in post-COVID syndrome, with in vitro validation of Belzutifan as a potential treatment.
Multi-ancestry genome-wide association study identifying genetic loci and shared genetic architecture between Long COVID and chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, and depression.
Laboratory study investigating how Nirmatrelvir-resistant SARS-CoV-2 mutations enhance immune evasion through NF-κB cleavage, with implications for long COVID pathogenesis.
Integrated transcriptomic analysis of NK cells and monocytes identifying potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for COVID-19 and long COVID, using existing datasets from the GEO repository.
Describes development of a mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 model to investigate post-acute sequelae mechanisms and potential interventions, but reports no actual treatment testing or results.

Uses imaging transcriptomics to measure ACE2, TMPRSS2, and HLA-DQA2 mRNA expression in brain gray matter across healthy pre-pandemic adults, finding significant sex differences that may explain disparities in post-COVID neurological symptoms.
Exploratory study examining serum spike protein persistence in post-COVID patients and healthy controls, with immunoadsorption treatment in a subset of spike-positive patients.

Longitudinal multi-omics study of 1,000+ hospitalized COVID-19 patients identifying immune subtypes associated with mortality, mechanical ventilation, and long COVID risk, but without testing any intervention.

Retrospective analysis of COVID-19 transmission and long COVID prevalence in California state prisons using individual-level infection timing and housing data, estimating 9,100–11,000 cases of long COVID with disproportionate impact on incarcerated Black and Indigenous populations.
Cross-sectional study investigating autoantibodies to EBV-mimicking sequences in post-COVID and ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls, without testing any intervention.

An animal model study using golden hamsters to investigate neuroinvasive mechanisms and neuropsychiatric/cognitive symptoms of long COVID, finding persistent viral RNA in the brainstem and evidence of neurodegeneration and altered neurotransmitter systems.
In-vitro mechanistic study examining autoantibody-induced cytokine responses in monocytes from post-COVID patients, without testing any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study examining molecular and immunological signatures (viral genes, mRNA, immunoglobulins, IDO-2 activity) in 72 participants (31 with suspected long COVID) to develop diagnostic and predictive models for long COVID.

A machine-learning study identifying potential gene targets for long COVID treatment through computational analysis of existing genomic datasets, without conducting original clinical trials or empirical testing.
A Mendelian randomization study examining potential causal relationships between long COVID and brain structure changes using GWAS and neuroimaging data.
Basic science study investigating how SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein alters chromatin structure at specific gene promoters linked to pathways dysregulated in severe COVID-19 and PASC.
Genome-wide association study identifying genetic variants associated with COVID-19 susceptibility and hospitalization that may contribute to long COVID risk through transcriptome-wide analysis.
Observational study of 977 LC patients revealing 55% prevalence of neuropathic symptoms with anti-ganglioside antibody involvement and pilot IVIG treatment response in 8 patients.

Machine learning analysis of multi-omics data from >500 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in the IMPACC cohort identifies a recovery factor that predicts long COVID risk at hospital admission and reveals inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers associated with long COVID development.

Observational study using continuous wearable heart rate variability monitoring to assess autonomic dysfunction and identify post-exertional malaise thresholds in 127 long COVID patients compared to 21 healthy controls.

Single-cell RNA sequencing study characterizing immune dysfunction in long COVID patients through analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, revealing altered T/NK cell proportions and signs of incomplete immune recovery.

Develops and validates TLDR, a machine learning framework for predicting post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection using longitudinal EHR data from 85,000+ patients in the Precision PASC Research Cohort.

This cross-sectional neuroimaging study compares brainstem and cerebellar peduncle volumes between long COVID patients and healthy controls using DTI and volumetric analysis, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Preclinical study using AC70 hACE2 transgenic mice infected with Omicron BA.1 to investigate pathophysiological mechanisms of long COVID neurological symptoms, examining blood-brain-barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, and coagulopathy.

A cross-sectional immunometabolic profiling study comparing long COVID patients, recovered COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls to characterize persistent immune dysregulation and metabolic alterations underlying long COVID symptoms.

Comparative study examining skeletal muscle properties and exercise responses in long COVID/ME-CFS patients versus healthy controls after 60-day bed rest, finding distinct muscle abnormalities not attributable to inactivity alone.

Establishes a validated mouse model of long COVID cognitive dysfunction using automated behavioral tracking and transcriptomic analysis to screen potential treatments, but reports no treatment results.

Transcriptional analysis of adipose tissue from Long COVID patients and controls, finding no persistent SARS-CoV-2 RNA and no consistent gene expression differences between Long COVID and indeterminate groups.

Mechanistic study demonstrating that persistent SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein in PBMCs triggers sustained type I interferon production via MAVS-dependent signaling, potentially explaining chronic inflammation and autoimmunity in post-COVID syndrome.
Transcriptomic analysis of public RNA-seq data identifying gene expression biomarkers and dysregulated pathways associated with brain fog in long COVID patients.
A cross-sectional study using sequential PET scans to evaluate neutrophil-mediated inflammation and tissue remodeling in the lungs of six long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea.
Deep phenotyping study comparing autonomic dysfunction in long COVID patients with POTS versus healthy controls, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A methodological paper describing challenges and solutions for conducting causal inference analyses using EHR data in long COVID research, using Long COVID as a running example rather than studying a specific intervention.
Preclinical mouse study of BA.5 Omicron pathogenesis and monoclonal antibody efficacy in preventing lung fibrosis; not a human clinical trial.
Plasma proteomics study identifying molecular alterations (oxidative stress, coagulation, glycolytic imbalance) in long COVID patients compared to controls, with no treatment intervention evaluated.
Describes a new geometrical method to measure baroreceptor sensitivity impairment in long COVID patients with POTS-like symptoms, but presents no intervention or treatment trial data.

In vitro study of SARS-CoV-2 infection and repair responses in human bronchial epithelial cultures from long COVID patients with pulmonary sequelae, examining age- and sex-dependent mechanisms of abnormal tissue repair.

Mechanistic study demonstrating that IgG immune complexes from ME/CFS and PASC patients induce mitochondrial dysfunction and alter inflammatory marker secretion in cell culture and PBMCs, without testing any treatment intervention.
Investigates pulsed speckle contrast optical spectroscopy as a non-invasive method to detect microclots in biofluids, a biomarker linked to long COVID symptoms.

Describes a transgenic mouse model (RAB/6N) that develops acute maladaptive immune responses and post-acute systemic disease syndromes mimicking PASC, with potential for testing therapeutic interventions in preclinical studies.
Characterizes immune dysfunction in children with long COVID through PBMC analysis, identifying myeloid CCR6 suppression as a key biomarker distinguishing long COVID from controls.
Large-scale validation study of the C19-YRSm patient-reported outcome measure using Rasch analysis in 1,278 long COVID patients, but no treatment intervention tested.
Prospective observational study comparing SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody responses, immune cell profiles, and cytokine levels in long COVID patients versus convalescent controls over 6 months.

A retrospective analysis of 25 long COVID patients to identify clinical features associated with diagnostic reliability, using Bayesian regression to determine which symptoms predict stable vs. unreliable diagnoses.

Integrative transcriptomic analysis of three RNA-seq datasets identifying molecular signatures distinguishing acute COVID-19 from post-acute sequelae, with potential biomarkers for precision diagnosis.
Mechanistic study in mice examining sex differences in acute COVID-19 and post-acute sequelae, focusing on viral persistence, inflammation, and cognitive outcomes.
Characterizes immunological profiles and biomarkers in long COVID patients versus post-infection controls, identifying patient symptom clusters and potential disease-driving mechanisms.
Develops machine learning models to predict long COVID and mortality outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients with substance use disorder using EHR data.
Develops TACO, a machine learning framework combining causal inference and foundation models for presymptomatic Long COVID detection using gene expression data.
A biomarker study investigating the association between persistent Spike antigenemia and post-COVID condition, comparing PCC patients, non-PCC individuals, and pre-pandemic controls.
Preclinical study identifying TCF4 as a therapeutic target for long COVID lung fibrosis via macrophage regeneration in mouse and human lung models.
Investigates whether IgG autoantibodies from long COVID patients with neurological symptoms can trigger pain-related symptoms in mice via passive transfer.

Single-cell multi-omics study comparing immune cell profiles in blood and airway samples from pulmonary long COVID patients versus controls, identifying T-cell dysregulation and autoantibodies as potential therapeutic targets.

This study identifies elevated mannose-positive extracellular vesicles in Long COVID plasma and demonstrates that GNA affinity resin can selectively remove these vesicles, potentially rebalancing immune and tissue-repair pathways.
This paper applies a machine-actionable framework to analyze the symptom space of DSM-5 disorders and Long COVID, comparing conceptual boundaries and redundancy between conditions.

Machine learning analysis of questionnaire data from four post-acute COVID cohorts identifies distinct symptom clusters, endotypes, and severity groups, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Uses machine learning models on acute-phase serological and symptom data from healthcare professionals to predict subsequent long COVID development, but is a retrospective analytical study without treatment intervention.
A review article explaining vascular pathology mechanisms in COVID-19, including endothelial injury and microischemia as potential causes of long COVID symptoms, based on autopsy and imaging studies.
Applies text mining and topic modeling to patient narratives about long COVID symptoms to identify shared clinical and psychological issues.
A machine learning study using questionnaire data to predict the effects of physical activity on COVID-19 survivors' recovery, without testing any intervention.
Describes an IoT-based wearable device system to monitor COVID-19 patients for cytokine storm risk, but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.
An NLP study using BERT models to detect long COVID symptoms from Twitter posts for health monitoring purposes, not a treatment intervention study.
Uses deep learning on EHR diagnosis codes from N3C to identify risk factors for Long COVID development, not a treatment study.

A machine learning study developing a predictive model for long COVID cardiovascular complications using demographic markers, but this is a methods/validation paper without clinical trial data or patient outcomes.
A machine learning study that builds predictive models to identify factors associated with developing long COVID using N3C clinical data, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Develops a machine learning model to prioritize long-COVID patients for specialist referrals based on clinical features, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Machine learning study using spatiotemporal attention networks to predict outcomes in long COVID patients from longitudinal clinical data.
Observational study using smartphone and smartwatch activity data to characterize COVID-19 recovery patterns and develop predictive models of recovery duration, with no intervention administered.
Uses big data mining and machine learning to predict long COVID risk based on demographic data and symptom groupings, but is not a treatment trial.
Describes the design and development of a mobile application to support long COVID patients based on elicited patient requirements, not a treatment intervention study.
Uses machine learning on EHR data from 7 million COVID patients to identify risk factors for long COVID, not a treatment study.
A glossary-based computational method for extracting and analyzing long COVID-related terms and trends from the LitCovid literature database using MeSH headings.
Develops a machine learning model to infer airway-to-lung ratio from cardiac CT scans to investigate relationships with PASC, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Uses machine learning algorithms to predict heart failure development in post-acute COVID-19 patients across racial and ethnic groups.

This study evaluates physical counterpressure manoeuvres as a treatment for orthostatic intolerance in long COVID patients, measuring blood pressure response and association with fatigue using surface electromyography.
A cross-sectional study comparing language and verbal fluency performance between 195 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients and 50 healthy controls using semantic and naming tasks.

Preliminary mechanistic study examining caspase expression patterns in COVID-19 and long COVID patients, proposing caspase inhibitors as a potential therapeutic strategy without clinical trial results.

Mechanistic study using murine models to investigate how aging impairs CD8+ T cell immunity in the brain, increasing severity of coronavirus infection and postinfectious cognitive impairment, rather than testing a treatment intervention in humans.

Describes an algorithm for measuring physical activity recovery in COVID-19 discharged patients using inertial measurement units, but presents only preliminary results without a treatment intervention or structured trial.
A case-control study comparing serum mast cell activation markers and inflammatory mediators in long COVID patients versus asymptomatic post-COVID and healthy controls.
Observational neuroimaging study examining the brain correlates of persistent olfactory dysfunction in post-COVID patients using MRI and perfusion analysis.

A cross-sectional study examining sex-related hormone levels in male COVID-19 patients during acute recovery, finding most hormones remain in normal ranges with no significant associations to disease severity or duration.
Comparative study of inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP, NT-proBNP) in post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MISC) in children versus Kawasaki disease patients to aid differential diagnosis.
Cross-sectional study measuring the prevalence of peripheral neuropathy and myopathy in post-COVID-19 patients via clinical examination and electrophysiological testing.

Prospective cohort study using unsupervised machine learning to identify post-COVID phenotypes based on laboratory parameters in patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, finding D-Dimer as a key discriminating marker for rehabilitation responsiveness.

Longitudinal study of critical COVID-19 survivors identifying microRNA signatures and molecular pathways associated with persistent lung dysfunction, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Compares retinal neurovascular coupling between 15 long COVID patients and 11 healthy controls using flicker light stimulation, finding no significant differences in vascular response.

A case-control study comparing EBV reactivation markers in long COVID patients with persistent fatigue versus recovered COVID-19 controls, finding higher frequency of EBV DNA in throat washings of long COVID patients.

In vitro study evaluating mesenchymal stem cell co-culture effects on airway basal stem cells from COVID-19 patients, demonstrating mitigation of inflammatory and fibrotic alterations relevant to long COVID respiratory sequelae.
Case series examining skeletal muscle histopathology and mitochondrial changes in 16 long COVID patients with fatigue and weakness, but no treatment intervention tested.

Observational study comparing plasma steroid concentrations during acute COVID-19 hospitalization and 5 months post-discharge, finding acute elevation in cortisol and testosterone depletion that normalize without correlation to post-COVID symptoms.
Cross-sectional study comparing myocardial blood flow and coronary vasodilator capacity between post-COVID-19 syndrome patients (n=23) and healthy controls (n=23) using PET/CT imaging.
Case series of 34 post-COVID patients with new-onset sleepiness showing that 35% have obstructive sleep apnea, with 6 patients treated and all reporting symptom resolution.
Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive function and brain imaging (olfactory bulb volume, cortical thickness) in COVID-19 patients with and without hyposmia versus healthy controls.
Cross-sectional study comparing tissue-specific autoantibody profiles in COVID-19 patients (acute and convalescent) versus non-COVID ITU controls.

Cross-sectional study of 170 post-COVID patients examining the relationship between subjective cognitive complaints (brain fog), objective cognitive performance, fatigue, and neuropsychiatric symptoms using neuropsychological testing and machine learning analysis.
Cross-sectional assessment of congruence between subjective cognitive complaints and objective neuropsychological test results in 46 long COVID patients with cognitive symptoms.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing small fiber neuropathy characteristics in post-COVID and ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls using quantitative sensory testing and corneal confocal microscopy.
Analyzes lectin pathway complement activation in long COVID patients versus healthy controls using MASP-2/C1Inh complexes and other complement markers to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers.

A computational/network pharmacology study investigating how bioactive compounds from functional foods may modulate genes associated with post-COVID cardiovascular, diabetic, and respiratory complications, without conducting clinical trials or human studies.

Single-cell molecular analysis of SARS-CoV-2-specific memory B cells in severe versus mild COVID-19 patients at 2-4 months post-symptom onset, revealing distinct activation signatures and immune trajectories in convalescence.

Neurophysiological and neuropsychological assessment comparing motor cortex physiology and executive cognitive function in 67 long COVID patients with fatigue/cognitive difficulties versus 22 healthy controls, finding altered M1 excitability and neurotransmission deficits.

Describes and evaluates a community-engaged approach to a long COVID research study using the 4PI Framework and Patient-Led Research Scorecards, focusing on methodology rather than treatment outcomes.
A cross-sectional study using DCE-MRI to investigate lung perfusion disturbances in nonhospitalized post-COVID patients with persistent dyspnea, finding sex-specific vascular abnormalities.
Mechanistic study demonstrating that circulating SARS-CoV-2 spike protein acts as a β-adrenergic receptor agonist and may contribute to cardiac sequelae in long COVID patients.

A cross-sectional study measuring peripheral microvascular oxygen delivery and tissue oxygenation in acute COVID-19 patients using diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and microscopy, hypothesizing that tissue hypoxia may contribute to long COVID symptoms.
Cross-sectional study characterizing persistent endothelial dysfunction and prothrombotic markers in long COVID patients at 68 days post-infection, without testing any treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional study comparing chronotropic responses and heart rate recovery during 6-minute walk test between women 3 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection and non-infected controls.

Study using submaximal cardiopulmonary exercise testing to assess exercise capacity and post-exertional symptom exacerbation in long COVID patients, demonstrating worsened physiological function 24 hours after exercise.

A case-control study comparing immune responses in pediatric long COVID patients versus convalescent controls, finding elevated SARS-CoV-2 reactive T cells with inflammatory cytokine production in those with post-acute sequelae.

Investigates vascular remodeling and correlations with lung function biomarkers in post-acute COVID-19 patients using CT imaging and functional assessments, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional comparison of muscle physiology and quality of life between long COVID patients with persistent fatigue and controls, finding symptoms persist despite absent pathophysiological mechanisms.
A cross-sectional diagnostic study using polarization-phase laser imaging to detect blood microstructure changes in long COVID patients, with no intervention or treatment component.
Cross-sectional study comparing neural responses to speech sounds in high school students with and without COVID history using EEG mismatch negativity paradigm.

Identifies persistent IFN-γ release from CD8+ T cells in long COVID patients as a potential biomarker and mechanistic driver, with symptom improvement correlating to normalization of IFN-γ production.
Multimodal proteomics study identifying dysregulated complement activation and thromboinflammatory markers as biomarkers in long COVID patients, with no intervention or treatment evaluated.
Demonstrates that pharmacologically enhancing peroxisome biogenesis in macrophages mitigates acute symptoms and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in animal models.
Describes a laser microscopy method to detect myocardial structural changes in deceased COVID-19 patients with long-term effects, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
Investigates peroxisome dysfunction in macrophages as a mechanism impairing lung repair after COVID-19 in a mouse model.
Characterizes immune signatures and pathophysiological traits in COVID-19 convalescents with chronic lung impairment, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
A mechanistic study characterizing neutrophil-associated immune signatures in patients with post-COVID pulmonary sequelae, comparing those with and without interstitial lung changes.
Preclinical mouse model study investigating PASC lung pathogenesis and testing antiviral (EIDD-2801) and antifibrotic (nintedanib) interventions.
Animal model study examining SARS-CoV-2-induced somatosensory abnormalities in hamsters using RNA sequencing and molecular analysis, not a human treatment trial.
Mechanistic study of mitochondrial gene expression changes during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection in rodent and human tissues, not focused on long COVID or treatment interventions.
Investigates persistent post-COVID smell loss through olfactory epithelial biopsies, revealing T cell-mediated inflammation and altered gene expression in long COVID patients compared to controls.
Cross-sectional PET imaging study of T cell activation and viral RNA persistence in post-acute COVID-19 patients, characterizing mechanisms rather than testing treatments.
Systems serology study comparing antibody profiles in SARD patients with and without PASC to identify immune markers associated with long COVID development.
Comparative study of systemic pathologies in hamsters and humans after SARS-CoV-2 infection, identifying persistent neuroinflammatory and tissue changes consistent with long COVID biology.
Multiomic analysis of blood samples from acute COVID-19 through 12 months post-infection identifying sex-specific immune correlates of Long COVID development and persistence.

Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing study in humans and mice identifying IFN-γ as a driver of respiratory sequelae in PASC, with functional validation that IFN-γ neutralization reduces lung inflammation and fibrosis in a mouse model.
Basic science study of SARS-CoV-2 infection mechanisms in human iPSC-derived neurons using cell culture models, not a clinical trial or treatment study.
Preclinical study developing a mouse model of post-acute lung fibrosis following SARS-CoV-2 BA.5 infection to enable investigation of potential therapeutic interventions.
Preclinical study in dwarf hamsters demonstrating SARS-CoV-2-induced chronic lung inflammation and testing antiviral treatment efficacy in an animal model.

Study demonstrates that SARS-CoV-2 spike protein expression causes coagulation abnormalities and systemic inflammation in mice similar to long COVID, with aspirin treatment reducing mortality and weight loss, and validates findings with elevated biomarkers (IGFBP-1, CXCL13) in long COVID patient serum samples.
Observational case-control study identifying ACE2-like enzymatic activity in antibodies from long COVID patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms, correlating with blood pressure dysregulation.

Cross-sectional immunological characterization of 49 COVID-19 convalescent individuals revealing NKT cell impairment and sustained immune alterations months after recovery, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

Mechanistic study identifying ORF3a as a driver of COVID-associated neuroinflammation in astrocytes and demonstrating that glibenclamide and glycyrrhizin mitigate ORF3a-induced neuropathological effects.
In vitro study of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein effects on respiratory epithelial cell mitochondrial and cytoskeletal function, comparing responses to influenza infection.
Mechanistic study showing how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein's RGD motif activates TGF-β signaling and suppresses interferon response in cell cultures.
Mechanistic study using mouse models to investigate how SARS-CoV-2-infected cells that survive acute infection contribute to inflammation and lung regeneration in post-acute sequelae.

Animal model study examining olfactory dysfunction and nasal tissue pathology in Syrian hamsters infected with different SARS-CoV-2 variants, focused on acute infection mechanisms rather than long COVID sequelae or treatment.
Reports therapeutic effects of high-dose gaseous nitric oxide inhalation in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients, proposing a mechanism involving NO-derived nitrosonium cations.
Observational study examining correlations between psychological symptoms and EEG parameters in depressive patients who recovered from COVID-19, without any treatment intervention.
Feasibility study evaluating personalized home-based computerized cognitive training to improve cognitive dysfunction in long COVID patients over 8 weeks.

Serum proteomic analysis comparing long-term persistent COVID-19 patients with persistent infection but no symptoms to healthy controls, identifying dysregulated proteins in coagulation and immune response pathways.
Animal study of blood chemistry changes in SARS-CoV-2-infected Syrian hamsters during acute infection and recovery, not a human long COVID treatment trial.
Development and psychometric validation of SBQ-LC, a 17-scale patient-reported outcome measure for quantifying long COVID symptom burden.
Cross-sectional study characterizing dysfunctional breathing patterns and cardiopulmonary exercise test findings in long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea, but no treatment intervention tested.

Cross-sectional assessment of 113 UK military personnel with post-COVID syndrome using cardiopulmonary exercise testing and imaging to identify diagnostic criteria for excluding clinically significant disease.

Cross-sectional study identifying three distinct clinical phenotypes of long COVID patients at 3-6 months post-infection using unsupervised clustering of patient characteristics, symptoms, and lung function data.
A cross-sectional diagnostic study assessing non-invasive electrodiagnostic techniques for detecting small fibre neuropathy in long COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study comparing 129Xe MRI ventilation defects between ever-hospitalised and never-hospitalised people with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome, finding worse ventilation abnormalities in the ever-hospitalised group.
Bioinformatic analysis of existing 16S rRNA datasets to identify bacterial dysbiosis (Prevotella and Pasteurellaceae) associated with IBD exacerbation in COVID-19 post-acute sequelae.
Population-level burden estimation of Long COVID symptom clusters in Ireland using Global Burden of Disease modeling framework, not a treatment trial.
Examines association between accumulated COVID-19 cases and US road deaths in 2021 using Poisson regression, suggesting lingering neurological effects of COVID-19 may increase accident risk.
Psychometric validation study of the C19-YRSm patient-reported outcome measure in 1,314 long COVID patients attending UK specialist clinics, evaluating reliability, validity, and responsiveness.
Evaluates cardiopulmonary exercise testing as a diagnostic tool to exclude significant cardiopulmonary disease in patients recovering from COVID-19, rather than testing a treatment intervention.
Feasibility study assessing the one-minute sit-to-stand test as a recovery measure in post-acute COVID-19 patients at follow-up clinics, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

Evaluation of a palliative care breathlessness service providing non-pharmacological symptom management (breathing techniques, relaxation, activity support, mindfulness) to 97 long COVID patients, with significant improvements in breathlessness severity, confidence, and fatigue.
Cross-sectional assessment of breathlessness sensations in COVID-19 patients post-discharge using the Multidimensional Dyspnoea Profile.
Mathematical modeling study using delay differential equations to analyze mechanisms of long COVID persistence through bifurcation and sensitivity analysis, not an empirical treatment trial.
Prospective comparative study of lung abnormalities detected via hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI in hospitalized vs non-hospitalized long COVID patients versus controls.
Uses natural language processing on clinical notes from outpatient encounters to identify and characterize patients with long-term COVID symptoms, achieving high recall for note-level prediction.
Observational study using hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI and CT imaging to characterize ventilation defects and airway disease in long COVID patients over one year of follow-up.

Experimental study examining how circulating extracellular vesicles from post-COVID patients affect endothelial function in mouse models under protein restriction, rather than testing a treatment in patients.

A prospective cross-sectional study comparing xenon-129 MRI and CT pulmonary vascular measurements in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients versus healthy controls to relate imaging findings to symptoms and exercise limitation.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiovascular and cerebral vascular function between females with PASC and age-matched controls, finding elevated blood pressure and arterial stiffness in the PASC group.
A case series of 136 long COVID patients who underwent post-COVID rehabilitation, showing significant improvement in health status measured by EQ-5D-5L index.

An animal study (ferrets) examining sex differences in myocardial stress responses and inflammation following SARS-CoV-2 infection, identifying potential mechanisms of cardiac injury in long COVID but not testing any treatment.
Comparative study of peripheral and cerebral vasodilator function in young adults with persistent post-COVID symptoms versus asymptomatic and control groups.

Preclinical study in a mouse model of long COVID demonstrating that B1 receptor blockade alleviates cardiac fibrosis, apoptosis, and inflammation associated with persistent post-infection cardiovascular complications.

Comparative gene expression analysis of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in post-COVID-19 patients with persistent vs resolved interstitial lung disease to identify immune mechanisms associated with pulmonary fibrosis.
Preclinical study examining ACE2 expression in lung fibroblasts from COPD and IPF patients as a potential risk factor for severe COVID-19, without investigating long COVID or testing any treatment.

Cross-sectional comparison of skeletal muscle structure and mitochondrial function in PASC patients versus controls, showing reduced exercise capacity and impaired mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in long COVID.

A cross-sectional study comparing cardiovascular, autonomic, and exercise parameters in 18 long COVID patients vs 19 controls ~2 years post-infection, finding persistent sympathetic overactivation, vascular impairment, and reduced aerobic capacity.
Cross-sectional comparison of central airway luminal areas between long COVID and acute COVID-19 patients using CT imaging, finding no significant differences between groups.

Observational study measuring ventilatory chemoreflex sensitivity and systemic inflammation in COVID-19 recovered individuals versus controls, with findings linking inflammation to altered breathing control.

A conference abstract describing mechanistic research on how viral infections (SARS-CoV-2, HIV, EBV) alter nonsense-mediated decay pathways and genomic responses, including observations in long COVID patients.
Autopsy study investigating TDP-43 microvasculopathy in brain tissue from COVID-19 and Alzheimer's disease patients, examining neurovascular unit dysfunction in Neuro-PASC.
Mechanistic study using spike protein-pseudotyped virus in obese mice to investigate how obesity exacerbates cardiac mitochondrial dysfunction in post-COVID cardiomyopathy.

Autopsy study examining TDP-43 microvasculopathy and blood-brain barrier disruption in Alzheimer's disease and COVID-19 brains, comparing post-mortem tissue from AD patients with and without COVID-19 comorbidity.

A mathematical modeling study using fractional-order differential equations to simulate immune responses and viral dynamics in COVID-19, including theoretical exploration of long COVID immune exhaustion phenomena.
An eight-week swimming intervention study evaluating effects on body composition and dietary intake in post-COVID-19 patients.
Network pharmacology and computational study predicting quercetin's mechanisms for asthma-pulmonary fibrosis overlap post-COVID, with animal model validation but no human clinical trial.
Methodological study proposing a supramaximal verification phase to accurately measure maximal aerobic capacity (VO2 max) in long COVID patients with respiratory symptoms.
A mechanistic study using Mendelian randomization and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify lactate metabolism as a key pathway in COVID-19-induced pulmonary fibrosis, without testing any treatment.
SeroNet pooling project examining COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness and immune responses in immunocompromised populations (cancer, transplant, autoimmune), including long COVID risk assessment.
A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between olfactory cleft length and persistent post-COVID olfactory dysfunction, comparing three groups without testing any treatment intervention.
Comparative study of gut microbiota composition and biochemical markers in post-COVID patients, recovered individuals, and healthy controls using 16S rRNA sequencing.
Secondary analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled trial examining associations between BMI and inflammatory biomarkers in adults with recent COVID-19 diagnosis.
Cross-sectional study of 116 long COVID patients examining inspiratory muscle dysfunction (reduced PImax) as a mechanism underlying dyspnea symptoms.
Cross-sectional study examining inspiratory muscle function impairment in 116 long COVID patients, finding reduced PImax strongly associated with dyspnea severity despite normal lung function tests.
Cross-sectional imaging study comparing cardiac structure, function, and myocardial energetics in PASC patients versus healthy controls, finding no significant abnormalities.
Cross-sectional study examining the impact of long COVID on reproductive health and assisted reproductive technology outcomes in women with infertility, without testing a specific intervention.
Case-control study measuring prothrombotic markers in long-COVID patients with mild acute infection compared to healthy controls, finding elevated platelet activation and thrombin generation.

Diagnostic study evaluating small fiber neuropathy in 18 long COVID patients with neuropathic pain using skin biopsy, QST, LEP, and ESC, finding high rates of abnormal results and modest symptomatic improvement at 6-month follow-up.

Observational study examining persistent kidney damage and inflammatory markers in COVID-19 patients at 10 days, 6 months, and 12 months post-infection, comparing podocyte protein markers between COVID and diabetic controls.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiovascular physiology (sympathetic nerve activity, endothelial function, aortic stiffness, exercise capacity) in COVID-19 survivors versus healthy controls at 6 months post-infection.

This cross-sectional study compares peripheral and cerebral vascular function between young adults with persistent post-COVID symptoms and asymptomatic controls, finding impaired peripheral vascular function but normal cerebral vasomotor reactivity in the symptomatic group.
Cross-sectional study comparing heart rate variability and orthostatic stress responses in post-COVID-19 recovered patients versus healthy controls using machine learning classification.
Cross-sectional study comparing microvascular endothelial function between PASC patients with and without POTS using pulse amplitude tonometry and cardiac MRI, with no treatment intervention.
Preclinical study developing acute and long-term mouse models of SARS-CoV-2 infection to investigate endothelial dysfunction mechanisms, with no human treatment intervention.

Retrospective evaluation of long COVID patients referred to Flow Therapy, quantifying disease severity using 6 validated assessment tools including PROMIS Fatigue, SAQ, DASI, 6MWT, RDS, and CCS angina class.

This is a conference abstract describing preliminary findings from a small cross-sectional study comparing fibrin/amyloid microclots in blood plasma between long COVID patients and healthy controls, with no treatment intervention tested.

Retrospective case series evaluating Enhanced External Counterpulsation (EECP) therapy for cognitive impairment in 51 long COVID patients, showing significant improvements in BrainCheck composite scores and multiple cognitive domains.

Retrospective study comparing myocardial perfusion reserve measured by stress CMR imaging in 30 long COVID patients with chest pain versus 13 controls, finding significantly reduced perfusion reserve in PASC patients.
Retrospective chart review examining whether abnormal left ventricular strain on echocardiography correlates with abnormal cardiac MRI findings in pediatric post-COVID patients.

Comprehensive physiological assessment of 30 long COVID patients with fatigue and breathlessness, examining cardiac function, autonomic responses, and exercise capacity without testing any intervention.
Immunohistochemical analysis of cardiac sympathetic innervation and ACE2 localization in autopsied hearts from COVID-19 and CVD patients to understand mechanisms of cardiac injury.
Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary blood flow and airway volumes in long COVID patients versus healthy controls using functional respiratory imaging analysis.

Descriptive case series of 28 POTS patients with pelvic venous compression who underwent diagnostic venography and intravascular ultrasound, with subsequent referral for angioplasty and stenting intervention.
Proteomics study identifying dysregulated chemokine pathways in long COVID patients compared to healthy controls, using blood samples from the Vienna POSTCOV Registry.
Cross-sectional study comparing plasma protein profiles in long COVID patients with and without POTS to healthy controls, identifying dysregulated cardiovascular and inflammatory pathways.
Characterizes cardiac, autonomic, and exercise physiology abnormalities in 21 long COVID patients using tilt testing, orthostatic challenge, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing.
Cross-sectional study comparing cardiac function via exercise stress echocardiography in 15 post-COVID patients versus historical controls, finding impaired left ventricular function during stress.
Case-control study comparing endothelial function, ADMA levels, and cardiovascular outcomes in long COVID patients versus uninfected controls and asymptomatic infected individuals.

A cross-sectional study examining persistent prothrombotic markers and their mediators (extracellular histones and immune complexes) in patients with mild acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and sustained PASC symptoms.

Cross-sectional study examining immune dysregulation (T cell-monocyte complexes and pro-inflammatory cytokines) in long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome compared to COVID-recovered controls.

Observational study comparing cardiovascular function, sympathetic nerve activity, and exercise capacity between severe COVID-19 survivors (~3 months post-discharge) and matched controls, finding evidence of sympathetic overdrive, vascular dysfunction, and reduced aerobic capacity in survivors.
Comparative study measuring blood volume in long COVID-POTS patients versus primary POTS patients and healthy controls to characterize hypovolemia.
Evaluates sensitivity and specificity of a wearable monitoring device (BioBeat Watch) in COVID-19 patients, including post-acute monitoring, but does not test a treatment intervention.

In vitro study of viral dsRNA-induced innate immune activation in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, examining mechanisms of COVID-19-related cardiac dysfunction without testing any intervention in patients.
In vitro study testing ATN-161 peptide's ability to prevent SARS-CoV-2-induced blood-brain barrier disruption in mouse brain endothelial cells.
Preclinical hamster model study testing mitochondrial antioxidant and JAK/STAT inhibitor treatments for COVID-19-induced cardiac arrhythmias and pulmonary dysfunction.
Observational study examining urinary exosomal podocyte proteins as biomarkers of renal injury in SARS-CoV-2 patients followed at 10 days, 6 months, and 12 months post-infection.
A thesis investigating mechanistic understanding of post-COVID breathlessness through sensorimotor processing and Bayesian brain models, without testing a treatment intervention.
Preclinical study investigating ATN-161 (α5 integrin inhibitor) as a potential therapeutic for SARS-CoV-2-induced neurological damage in cell culture and mouse models.

Preclinical mouse study investigating how MTHFR deficiency combined with SARS-CoV-2 infection causes cerebrovascular dysfunction and neurodegeneration through BBB disruption and dopaminergic system damage.
In vitro and electron microscopy study of microclot formation and erythrocyte interaction in long COVID patients versus healthy controls, demonstrating anomalous fibrin resistant to proteolysis.

Multimodal MRI study comparing brain morphology, microstructure, and functional connectivity between COVID-recovered patients and healthy controls, revealing focal atrophy in basal ganglia and limbic structures associated with infection severity.

A neuroimaging study comparing blood-brain barrier permeability and brain microstructure in older adults with neurological long COVID versus controls, examining modification by sex and Alzheimer's disease genetic risk.

A cross-sectional study of 86 COVID-19 patients evaluating persistent and new symptoms after resolution of acute infection, finding that 93% maintained symptoms including dyspnea, chest pain, fatigue, and cough.
Observational study examining cardiovascular recovery patterns in response to different body positions following exercise testing in long COVID patients, without testing any intervention.
Mouse model study examining pulmonary fibroproliferative response and chronic inflammation in aged mice surviving acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, without testing any interventions.

Prospective observational study identifying four symptom clusters (emotional, activity-limiting, gastrointestinal, pain) in 127 post-acute COVID-19 patients and their associations with quality of life impairments.

Retrospective chart review of 16 pediatric PASC patients showing improvements in 6-minute walk distance, dyspnea, and fatigue scores following pulmonary rehabilitation, with statistically significant improvement in fatigue (P=0.0431).
A conference abstract presenting preliminary results of advanced imaging and pulmonary function testing in COVID-19 survivors to detect long-term lung sequelae, with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing upper airway microbiome composition in 42 post-COVID patients versus 20 controls, finding significantly reduced nasal microbial diversity and altered bacterial taxa enrichment in post-COVID syndrome.
Case-control study comparing mitochondrial function in PBMCs between long COVID patients and healthy controls, finding ATP synthase dysfunction but no treatment intervention tested.
A cross-sectional study comparing exhaled breath metabolite profiles between long COVID patients, acute COVID patients, and various controls to develop a diagnostic test for long COVID.
Retrospective chart review identifying pulmonary-related predictors of sleep disturbance phenotypes in long COVID patients, but no treatment intervention studied.
Cross-sectional study comparing lung CT imaging and densitometry findings between individuals with long COVID presenting with dyspnea, fatigue, or exercise intolerance and healthy controls.

A computational study using density functional theory to analyze the SARS-CoV-2 envelope protein as a potential therapeutic target for long COVID, without any empirical testing or treatment evaluation.

In vitro study of airway basal stem cell dysfunction in acute COVID-19 patients, examining inflammatory signatures and differentiation impairment without testing any intervention or long COVID outcomes.
Mechanistic study of elevated fungal translocation markers and NF-κB signaling in long COVID patients compared to controls, with no treatment intervention.
Examines the association between oral microbiome composition and long COVID symptom duration in patients followed from acute infection to symptom resolution.
A mechanistic study using mouse models and human ICU survivors to investigate how impaired Apelin-APJ signaling contributes to Post-Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS), which is distinct from long COVID.
Investigates elevated fungal translocation markers and NF-κB signaling mechanisms in long COVID patients compared to controls, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.
Ex vivo study demonstrating that PD-1 blockade restores T cell function and anti-SARS-CoV-2 immune response in post-COVID-19 patients with immune exhaustion.
Proteome-wide autoantibody profiling comparing long COVID patients, recovered COVID patients, and pre-COVID controls to identify autoreactive signatures associated with long COVID.

This study investigates the mechanisms of cardiac arrhythmias in acute COVID-19 and long COVID using a hamster model, showing that innate immune activation and mitochondrial ROS induce persistent conduction system dysfunction.
Machine learning analysis of multiomics data from 500+ COVID-19 patients to identify biomarkers and recovery factors predictive of long COVID development.

Laboratory study analyzing plasma biomarkers and mechanistic pathways of bone loss in COVID-19 patients with pre-existing inflammatory diseases, using cell culture and proteomics rather than clinical trial data.
Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of orthostatic intolerance in 92 children with long COVID using bedside passive standing tests.
Non-randomized pilot study testing olfactory training with and without adjuvant therapies for post-COVID-19 olfactory dysfunction in 47 patients over 3 months.
Secondary analysis examining the relationship between fatigue and cognitive function in post-COVID-19 condition patients using cross-sectional assessment tools.

A bioinformatics and molecular docking study screening bioactive components from Andrographis paniculata herb for potential therapeutic mechanisms against COVID-19 and long-term sequelae, without conducting any clinical trials or treatment studies.
Pre-post study of 208 long COVID patients receiving psychoeducational rehabilitation, measuring cognitive and affective performance changes using standardized neuropsychological testing.
A transcriptomic-neuroimaging study examining associations between cerebral blood flow alterations, gene expression, and clinical symptoms in long COVID patients.
Integrated transcriptomic and network analysis identifying differentially expressed genes and inflammatory pathways associated with long COVID pathology, without testing any treatment intervention.
Case-control study comparing NK cell phenotypes in long COVID patients (N=21) versus recovered controls (N=14) to investigate immune dysregulation associated with persistent symptoms.

Proposes a machine learning algorithm (DA-ResBiGRU with ABER optimization) for predicting cardiovascular disease risk in long COVID patients, but presents only simulated results without clinical data or patient outcomes.
Pilot study comparing urine metabolite profiles in long COVID patients versus healthy controls and ME/CFS patients to identify dysregulated metabolic pathways.

A cross-sectional study investigating immune exhaustion gene expression in ME/CFS and long COVID patients compared to healthy controls, finding dysregulated immune signaling pathways in both conditions.
A case-control study comparing cerebral vasomotor reactivity measured by transcranial Doppler ultrasound in long COVID patients versus healthy controls to assess brain dysregulation.
Evaluates the psychometric properties of the DSQ-SF questionnaire for classifying Long COVID and ME/CFS patients using machine learning, but does not test a treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional study comparing platelet function and thrombotic potential in long COVID patients versus healthy controls 15 months post-infection.
A machine learning study using multi-label classification to predict long-COVID sequelae at one-year follow-up based on baseline and acute COVID-19 data from an Italian cohort.
Comparative neuroimaging study examining mid-term microstructural white matter alterations in COVID-19 recovered subjects with anosmia versus controls.

A case series evaluating a 7-week virtual psychology-led interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for post-COVID-19 syndrome, measuring health-related quality of life improvements via EQ-5D-5L in 76 participants.
Develops and characterizes a mouse model of long COVID that replicates hypercoagulability, endotheliopathy, and cognitive abnormalities persisting for months post-infection.
A cross-sectional study using 129Xe MRI to identify and characterize four distinct pulmonary phenotypes in long COVID patients, without testing any intervention.

Describes development and validation of PICUPS, a clinical screening tool for identifying rehabilitation needs in post-ICU patients (including some COVID-19 ICU survivors), not a long COVID-focused intervention study.
Retrospective medical record review developing and validating clinical diagnostic criteria for post-COVID syndrome based on central sensitization symptoms in 42 Mayo Clinic patients.

Mechanistic study comparing tissue factor and extracellular vesicles from PASC patients versus controls to demonstrate procoagulant effects and thrombosis risk, with no intervention or treatment tested.
Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between fatigue, dyspnea, respiratory function, and exercise capacity in 27 young adults 12+ weeks post-COVID-19.
Basic mechanistic study investigating how COVID-19 IgG antibodies activate endothelial cells and promote a procoagulant state in vitro, without testing any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional assessment of lung function and inspiratory muscle capacity in long COVID patients that proposes inspiratory muscle training as a potential therapeutic option but reports no actual treatment intervention or outcomes.

This paper develops an automated machine learning method to localize hemidiaphragms and segment lungs in portable chest X-ray images of COVID-19 patients for assessing diaphragmatic function during recovery.
Single-cell transcriptomic study of airway mucosa comparing pulmonary long COVID patients to controls, identifying neutrophil-driven inflammation and epithelial dysfunction.

Cross-sectional biomarker study examining endothelial cell activation and hypercoagulability in COVID-19 survivors up to two months post-symptom onset, proposing these markers as risk indicators for long COVID vascular complications.
A case series of 50 post-COVID patients evaluating the effectiveness of a supervised pulmonary rehabilitation program on functional capacity, lung function, and quality of life.
Cross-sectional study measuring symptoms, functional impact, and quality of life in 55 long COVID patients with dysfunctional breathing, using questionnaires and cardiopulmonary exercise testing.
A cross-sectional metabolomic analysis comparing saliva samples from post-COVID-19 patients (60+ days post-infection) to non-infected controls, identifying 19 significantly different metabolites.
Validates a modified Berlin Questionnaire for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnea in COVID-19 patients using polysomnography, but does not study long COVID or test any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional assessment of exercise tolerance and ventilatory efficiency using cardiopulmonary exercise testing in 20 long COVID patients at 15-month follow-up, without intervention or treatment.

Descriptive cross-sectional study identifying eight symptom clusters in 703 long COVID patients through factor analysis, examining associations with age, obesity, variant, and hospitalization history.

Prospective observational study comparing inflammatory profiles across recovery severity clusters in post-hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 5 months, identifying elevated proteins associated with persistent symptoms.
Observational study examining lymphocyte dysfunction and impaired cellular immune responses in COVID-19 convalescents at 3 and 6 months post-hospitalization, with no treatment intervention.
Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of nasal swabs from COVID-19 convalescents identifies impaired ciliated cell function and differentiation as a potential mechanism underlying persistent dyspnea.
Cross-sectional study characterizing dyspnea phenotype in 309 post-COVID patients using pulmonary function tests, blood work, and imaging to identify risk factors for post-COVID dyspnea.

A case series of 39 long COVID patients undergoing a 18-week pulmonary rehabilitation program (endurance, resistance training, education) showing significant improvements in dyspnea, fatigue, exercise tolerance, and quality of life.
Cross-sectional study identifying blood biomarkers (IL-1α, TGF-β) associated with lung fibrotic-like changes in post-COVID-19 patients.
Cross-sectional study comparing CPET ventilatory parameters across four breathing pattern groups in long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea, but no intervention or treatment tested.

Prospective study comparing objective sleep characteristics measured by polysomnography and wearable sensors between post-COVID syndrome patients and healthy controls, finding subjective sleep impairment and higher apnea-hypopnea index in PCS patients.
Cross-sectional study comparing SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell responses between long COVID patients with lung sequelae, recovered individuals, and controls at one year post-infection.
Describes early outcomes from the Your COVID Recovery digital rehabilitation programme for long COVID patients, showing improvements in quality of life and fatigue measures over 9 weeks.

A quasi-experimental pilot study evaluating a 40-day home-based exercise rehabilitation programme for reducing dyspnea and improving exercise tolerance and quality of life in patients with post-COVID-19 condition.
Descriptive cross-sectional study measuring pulmonary function and exercise capacity in 80 North African long COVID patients using spirometry and 6-minute walk testing.
Compares computerized lung SPECT-CT and HRCT imaging to quantify pulmonary vascular changes in post-COVID-19 patients.
Cross-sectional study comparing lung diffusing capacity for nitric oxide and carbon monoxide at rest and after exercise in 32 long COVID patients with dyspnea versus 20 controls.

A prospective case series evaluating the effects of a 6-week exercise-based COVID-19 rehabilitation programme on fatigue, exercise capacity, and post-exertional symptom exacerbation in 148 long COVID patients.
Evaluates the learning effect and test-retest variability of the 6-minute walk distance test in adults with long COVID.

Descriptive cross-sectional analysis of post-COVID-19 complications in hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients at 3-month follow-up, measuring pulmonary, cardiac, physical, and cognitive outcomes without testing any intervention.

Characterizes a distinct phenotype of post-COVID patients with complex ventilatory dysfunction, reduced respiratory muscle strength, and fatigue through pulmonary function testing and symptom assessment.
Comparative analysis of nasal epithelium inflammatory state and innate lymphoid cell function in long COVID patients versus healthy controls.
Genetic association study examining the relationship between HLA-G 14-bp variant and exercise-induced oxygen desaturation in post-COVID-19 patients.
Validates approximate entropy as an objective metric to identify dysfunctional breathing patterns in long COVID patients during cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

Characterizes invasive haemodynamic abnormalities in PASC patients with exertional intolerance using cardiopulmonary exercise testing, identifying distinct phenotypes including impaired oxygen extraction and HFpEF.
Cross-sectional study comparing virus-specific T-cell responses and immune profiles in long COVID patients versus recovered controls at 12 months post-infection.

A case-control study using targeted proteomics and machine learning to identify blood protein biomarkers that distinguish long-COVID patients from controls, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Prospective cohort study examining serum markers of inflammation and pulmonary damage in 235 long COVID patients over one year, finding reduced CC16 levels associated with fatigue and symptom burden.
Basic research study comparing TRPM3 ion channel function in NK cells from post-COVID and ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls, finding impaired channel activity in both patient groups.

Cross-sectional immunophenotyping study comparing B cell profiles in 17 long COVID patients with rheumatological symptoms versus 8 healthy controls, finding elevated DN B cells associated with symptom severity.
Temporal proteome analysis comparing plasma proteins during acute COVID-19 hospitalization and 6 months post-recovery to identify cardiovascular biomarkers, but no treatment intervention is tested.
Proteomic analysis of post-mortem lung tissue from fatal COVID-19 patients identifying inflammatory and tissue remodeling mechanisms, with only speculative mention of PASC.

Mechanistic study in mice demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein induces cognitive impairment through microglial senescence via glycolysis, with evidence that glycolysis inhibition and mitochondrial fission inhibition reverse the effect.

Cross-sectional study comparing PBMC apoptosis markers in elderly individuals with prior COVID-19 infection versus controls, finding elevated apoptotic signatures that may reflect persistent immune dysregulation.
Validates angiopoietin-1 and p-selectin as potential diagnostic biomarkers for post-COVID-19 condition using biobank data from 249 participants.
Observational study analyzing temporal changes in gut microbiota composition of hospitalized SARS-CoV-2-infected people with HIV and its correlation with COVID-19 severity and PASC development.
Prospective observational study comparing serological immune response to COVID-19 vaccination between PASC patients and recovered controls to characterize aberrant immune activation in long COVID.
Observational neuroimaging study comparing brain activity and functional connectivity in COVID-19 survivors at 6-month follow-up versus healthy controls, with no treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing ACE2 RNA expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells between severe COVID-19 patients and healthy controls to identify biomarkers associated with post-COVID-19 conditions.
Observational study of inflammatory cytokine profiles and endothelial dysfunction in 66 post-COVID syndrome patients, with no treatment intervention.
A proof-of-concept cross-sectional MRI study examining glymphatic system dysfunction and blood-brain barrier disruption as potential biomarkers for post-COVID neurocognitive impairment.
Psychometric validation study of the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale in elderly Iranian populations with post-COVID syndrome.
Longitudinal multi-omics analysis of blood samples from COVID-19 patients identifying pro-thrombotic and platelet activation biomarkers associated with PASC development.
Modelling study estimating the burden of long COVID and post-intensive care syndrome in Australia using disability-adjusted life years under different re-opening scenarios.
Burden of disease study estimating DALYs from COVID-19 in Belgium during 2020-2021, including post-acute symptoms but not testing any interventions.
Machine learning cluster analysis of 437 hospitalized COVID-19 patients identifying distinct long COVID symptom and social connectivity patterns at one-year follow-up.

Exploratory biomarker study comparing serum levels of tissue remodelling, wound healing, and neutrophil activity markers in COVID-19 patients three months post-discharge, with elevated markers in those who developed post-COVID ILD.
Hamster model study of SARS-CoV-2 distribution in tongue tissue during acute infection, investigating mechanism of taste disturbance.
Economic analysis projecting the production, healthcare, and pension costs of long COVID in Germany based on secondary data.
Develops and validates a predictive model to identify children at risk of long COVID symptoms 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 testing using baseline health and demographic factors.
Develops machine learning models using clinical hospitalization data to predict pulmonary long COVID sequelae in a cohort of 152 patients.
Mendelian randomization study investigating causal associations between genetic predisposition to COVID-19 and brain structural changes, not a treatment trial for long COVID.

Characterizes differences in oral and gut microbiomes and serum metabolites in long COVID patients with gastrointestinal symptoms versus healthy controls through prospective sampling and metagenomic analysis.

A cross-sectional study examining endothelial dysfunction and persistent inflammation in COVID-19 ARDS survivors six months post-ICU discharge, with mechanistic investigation using in vitro endothelial cell models.
