Develops and validates prediction models to identify children and young people at highest risk of persistent post-COVID-19 condition up to 24 months post-infection based on demographic and clinical factors.
Proteomic analysis of 171 individuals identifying VEGFA overexpression and sex-specific protein signatures associated with long COVID persistence.
Whole exome sequencing study identifying RTEL1 ultra-rare variants as predictive markers of acute COVID-19 severity and evolution to pulmonary fibrosis in the post-COVID phase.

A non-randomized trial testing two prototype 'Smell-Aids' devices to enhance olfactory function in 54 patients with olfactory loss, including 37 post-COVID long haulers, showing significant improvements in odor identification and detection thresholds.
Develops a machine learning model using CT radiomics and clinical features to predict post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis risk in COVID-19 patients.

Cross-sectional study comparing immune and inflammatory biomarkers in plasma samples from 51 patients with pulmonary sequelae, 31 with long COVID, and 31 recovered controls at 12 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Proteomics and microscopy study of persistent microclots and inflammatory markers in Long COVID plasma samples compared to controls, with no intervention or treatment tested.

A cross-sectional proteomic analysis of fibrin microclots in 99 long COVID patients versus controls, identifying entrapped pro-inflammatory molecules and failed fibrinolytic mechanisms but not testing any treatment intervention.

Preclinical study testing sequential nanoparticle therapy (DNase-I@PDA and Sivelestat@PLGA) to prevent neutrophil-induced pulmonary fibrosis in COVID-19 and PASC using murine models and isolated neutrophils from COVID-19 patients.
Validation study of fatigue measurement scales (FSS and SISQs) in patients recovering from COVID-19, without any treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional study comparing endothelial function and biomarkers in post-COVID patients with and without ME/CFS versus healthy controls.
Cross-sectional serological study examining autoimmune profiles in 100 post-COVID syndrome patients versus healthy controls, finding high rates of latent autoimmunity and polyautoimmunity.

Mechanistic study characterizing extracellular vesicles from long COVID patients and their effects on cellular stress responses and mitochondrial function in vitro, without testing any treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional comparison of cognitive impairment and neuropsychiatric symptoms between ME/CFS and post-COVID-19 patients to determine if they represent the same underlying pathology.

A cross-sectional study comparing plasma proteome profiles in long COVID patients versus acute COVID-19 patients and healthy controls to identify potential vascular and inflammatory mechanisms underlying long COVID symptoms.
Combinatorial genetic analysis identifying SNPs and genes associated with severe and fatigue-dominant long COVID phenotypes and their overlap with ME/CFS.

Observational study using spectral analysis to characterize cardiorespiratory control and baroreflex dysfunction in COVID-19 survivors 9 months post-hospitalization, stratified by ventilatory support severity.
Prospective cohort study analyzing gene expression patterns in post-COVID patients using bulk RNA sequencing to identify molecular mechanisms of persistent symptoms.
A metabolomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid identifying biomarkers to differentiate neuro-COVID from other CNS viral infections, with no treatment intervention tested.
Cross-sectional study comparing serum HDL and HDL subfractions in MIS-C patients versus healthy controls to evaluate their role as biomarkers of the condition.

Multi-omics analysis of 66 participants (22 healthy controls, 22 long COVID, 22 non-long COVID) identifies neutrophil activation subtypes in long COVID using transcriptomic and proteomic profiling, but does not test any intervention or treatment.
A cross-sectional neuroimaging study comparing functional brain connectivity patterns during cognitive fatigue between long COVID patients, ME/CFS patients, and healthy controls using 7 Tesla fMRI.

Cross-sectional study comparing serum inflammatory markers (NLRP3, caspase-1, cytokines) in 161 long COVID patients stratified by acute COVID-19 severity to identify immune pathways underlying neuropsychiatric and fatigue symptoms.
Genetic association study validating long COVID disease signatures across US and UK patient cohorts with diverse ancestries, identifying potential drug repurposing candidates.

Cross-sectional metabolomic study identifying a nine-metabolite signature that classifies long COVID patients and associates specific metabolites with cognitive, functional, and respiratory impairments.
Post-mortem brain tissue analysis examining neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease patients who survived COVID-19 infection.
Longitudinal PET imaging study in experimentally infected rhesus macaques demonstrating neuroinflammatory response post-SARS-CoV-2 infection via TSPO tracer uptake and postmortem analysis.

Retrospective analysis of cerebrospinal fluid profiles from 150 lumbar punctures in 127 COVID-19 patients with neurological involvement, characterizing blood-brain barrier dysfunction and inflammatory markers.

Characterizes ventilatory dynamics and exercise capacity in long-COVID patients using portable spirometry and six-minute walk testing, finding associations between airway disease and reduced exercise performance.

Observational study examining prolonged pro-inflammatory gene expression signatures in blood cells from COVID-19 patients up to 7 months post-infection, identifying potential mechanisms underlying long COVID development.
Observational study measuring persistent DNA methylation changes in blood one year after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with no treatment intervention.
Genome-wide DNA methylation study comparing post-COVID patients to healthy controls, identifying epigenetic changes and accelerated aging markers 6 months after infection.
In vitro mechanistic study of how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein S1 induces endolysosome dysfunction and cellular senescence in human astrocytes via TLR7 signaling.
Comparative epigenetic study identifying a unique DNA methylation signature in PACS patients versus controls and healthy COVID-19 convalescents.
Retrospective neuroimaging study comparing brain metabolic connectivity patterns in post-COVID patients versus healthy controls using 18F-FDG PET imaging.

Epigenome-wide association study examining DNA methylation patterns 7 months after mild/asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection in a household cohort, identifying CpG sites differentially methylated compared to controls.

Compares cardiopulmonary exercise testing performance and metabolic responses between post-COVID individuals with and without fatigue to assess the relationship between fatigue and physical exhaustion capacity.
Genetic association study showing APOE ε4 carriership associates with severe COVID-19, cerebral microhaemorrhages, and post-COVID mental fatigue in Finnish biobank, autopsy, and clinical cohort data.

Preclinical study using a bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis rat model to evaluate FGF/FGFR targeting with sildenafil and bosentan, with mention of post-COVID sequelae as a potential application but no human patient data.
Pilot serological study comparing biomarkers of neuronal damage and reactive gliosis in long COVID patients with persistent headache versus acute COVID-19 and controls.
Pilot study comparing cerebrospinal fluid markers of neuronal damage and glial activation in post-COVID-19 patients with persistent headache versus acute COVID-19 and control groups.

An in-depth analysis of skeletal muscle biopsies from 11 long COVID patients with exercise intolerance, comparing capillary structure and immune markers to historical controls to elucidate underlying mechanisms.
A Mendelian randomization study analyzing genetic data to assess causal relationships between COVID-19 and 86 diseases/traits, not focused on long COVID or treatment interventions.
In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein S1 activates connexin 43 hemichannels and affects intracellular calcium dynamics in cultured cells.
Develops and validates a prognostic model to identify COVID-19 patients at risk of developing long COVID symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional study examining neuropsychiatric symptom clustering patterns and phenotypes in long COVID patients infected during the Omicron wave, without evaluating any intervention or treatment.
Cross-sectional study comparing auditory and cognitive function (ABR and P300) in post-COVID patients versus controls, with no treatment intervention.
Develops and validates a prediction model for post-COVID-19 condition at 2 years post-infection using retrospective data from the CORFU study, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

An in silico study analyzing SARS-CoV-2 NSP6 protein interactions and downstream pathways in brain, heart, and lung tissues, identifying potential therapeutic targets and linking COVID-19 to cancer hallmarks.
Retrospective radiological study describing imaging findings of acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis complicating post-COVID-19 infection, not studying a treatment intervention.

Descriptive cross-sectional study assessing delayed verbal learning deficits in 17 post-intensive care COVID-19 patients using the SCIP-S cognitive test, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.
Descriptive cross-sectional study assessing verbal working memory performance in 17 post-ICU COVID-19 patients using standardized cognitive testing.
A cross-sectional study characterizing psychiatric and neuropsychological symptoms in long COVID patients using standardized assessments.

Cross-sectional study investigating interoceptive accuracy and body awareness in COVID-19 survivors at one month post-hospitalization, examining associations with anxiety, depression, and inflammatory markers.
Cross-sectional MRI study examining brain correlates of subjective cognitive impairment in COVID-19 survivors, with no treatment intervention tested.
Validation study of a COVID-19-specific patient-reported outcomes measure (MDASI-COVID) in cancer patients with acute COVID-19, focusing on symptom monitoring rather than treatment evaluation.
Cross-sectional study examining elevated cell adhesion molecules (VCAM-1) as a predictor of thrombotic risk in type 2 diabetes patients in the post-COVID period, with normal coagulation labs.
Cross-sectional study identifying inflammatory cytokine signatures associated with post-COVID depression in survivors, but no treatment intervention tested.
Evaluates which group therapeutic factors patients find most helpful in standardized acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) group treatments for long COVID.
Validates the Chinese translation of the modified COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale as a measurement tool for assessing post-COVID-19 rehabilitation status.

A cross-sectional biomarker study measuring plasma neurofilament and glial proteins in hospitalized COVID-19, post-hospitalized neuro-PASC, and nonhospitalized neuro-PASC patients to characterize CNS injury mechanisms.
Retrospective cross-sectional study measuring SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral and cellular immune responses in patients with postviral syndrome to investigate evidence of prior COVID-19 exposure.
An observational study characterizing neurologic symptoms and underlying autonomic/immune dysregulation in 12 long COVID patients at the NIH Clinical Center, comparing findings to healthy controls.
Cross-sectional study of lipid profiles and inflammatory markers in acute COVID-19 patients with 3-month post-discharge follow-up, not focused on long COVID or treatment interventions.
Characterizes autonomic symptoms and objective measures of autonomic function in post-COVID syndrome patients.
Cross-sectional analysis of 607 long COVID patients examining the relationship between neuropsychiatric symptoms and reduced work capacity.
Cross-sectional neuropsychological assessment of 452 long COVID patients examining whether different SARS-CoV-2 viral strains produce strain-specific cognitive impairment patterns.
Investigates molecular mimicry and neurofilament light chain as potential disease mechanisms underlying cognitive impairment in long COVID patients.
Methodological research note presenting a Sullivan method projection framework applied to modeling future long COVID burden in populations under various demographic scenarios.

Comparative study of body composition in COVID-19 survivors versus matched controls using DXA and BIA, finding no significant differences in muscle, fat, or bone composition 2-13 months post-infection.

Cross-sectional study comparing endogenous pain modulation mechanisms (conditioned pain modulation and exercise-induced hypoalgesia) in individuals with prior COVID-19 versus controls, finding impaired CPM in symptomatic COVID-19 patients.
Descriptive cross-sectional study exploring cognitive and behavioral features in COVID-19 patients within two months of hospital discharge.
Cross-sectional MRI study comparing gray matter atrophy and functional connectivity in long COVID patients with vs without anxiety/depression symptoms, without testing any treatment intervention.
Cross-sectional study comparing central blood pressure and wave reflection indices between long COVID patients and controls, finding increased arterial stiffness in post-COVID patients.

Cross-sectional assessment of cardiorespiratory fitness and exercise tolerance in college-aged adults with prior COVID-19 infection, finding no significant differences in VO2max but increased leg fatigue reports in those with multiple infections or recent recovery.

A feasibility study using PET imaging to measure neuroinflammatory response to acute exercise in 5 individuals with chronic multisymptom illness (including 3 with Long COVID), finding preliminary evidence that the imaging protocol is tolerable but presenting no treatment intervention or outcomes data.
Cross-sectional comparison of hemodynamic variables, arterial stiffness, and aerobic capacity between female long COVID patients with brain fog and healthy controls.

Comparative cross-sectional study measuring cardiopulmonary fitness, skeletal muscle oxidative capacity, and microvascular function in long COVID patients versus healthy controls, with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing central blood pressure and hemodynamic responses to high-intensity exercise between long-COVID patients with brain fog and controls, finding increased arterial stiffness in COVID group but similar exercise responses.

A non-randomized trial evaluating a 14-day inpatient physical rehabilitation program for 60 post-COVID patients with chronic fatigue and cognitive disorders, stratified by oxygen requirement during acute phase.

Comparative study of matrix metalloproteinase profiles in adult and pediatric COVID-19 patients, with assessment of anti-inflammatory treatment (glucocorticoids, tocilizumab, convalescent plasma) effects on MMP levels and implications for long-term consequences.

This study characterizes the trajectory of post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE) in individuals with ME/CFS and PASC over 7 days following a sub-maximal exercise task, finding variable symptom responses with greatest changes in the first 72 hours.

Uncontrolled case series of 103 post-COVID patients with musculoskeletal pain undergoing 14-day inpatient rehabilitation including physiotherapy, halotherapy, and electrotherapy, showing significant improvements in pain intensity and distribution.
Proposes an AI-based predictive system using deep learning to identify post-COVID patients at risk for heart disease, but does not study any treatment intervention.
Uncontrolled case series of 28 post-COVID patients who completed pulmonary rehabilitation, showing statistically significant increases in aerobic exercise capacity across all equipment types.

A cross-sectional study measuring 96 immune response proteins in serum samples from asymptomatic and mildly affected COVID-19 patients 40-60 days post-infection, finding persistent inflammatory response and mitochondrial stress markers.
A case-control study investigating the genetic association between SERPINE1 and IFNAR2 gene polymorphisms and post-COVID-19 respiratory syndrome symptoms in Indonesian patients.
Retrospective analysis of lost work days associated with long COVID symptoms among Mexican healthcare workers using disability claims data.
Cross-sectional comparison of endothelial dysfunction and kidney function markers in post-COVID patients versus controls, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A doctoral thesis evaluating the effects of a hybrid respiratory rehabilitation program (8 supervised sessions plus 24 home sessions over 12 weeks) on cardiovascular and respiratory function in long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea.

A non-randomized trial evaluating a multi-level rehabilitation approach combining cognitive-motivational correction and physiotherapeutic methods (magnetolaser therapy, blood irradiation, transcranial stimulation) for post-COVID cognitive impairment, showing improvements in cognition and mood after treatment.

Study examining skin microbiocenosis changes in patients with chronic dermatoses (psoriasis, atopic dermatitis) during COVID-19 infection. Findings show dysbiosis and increased S. aureus colonization in COVID-19 patients with dermatoses, but focuses on acute infection effects rather than long COVID sequelae.

This study evaluates a drug composition containing arginine for treating patients with coronary heart disease, post-COVID syndrome, and generalized periodontitis, using laser Doppler flowmetry to assess microcirculation. The treatment group showed significant improvements in periodontal tissue microcirculation and clinical outcomes compared to baseline measures.

This study investigates the role of T-cadherin in COVID-19 pathogenesis, endothelial dysfunction, and lung fibrosis through post-mortem lung analysis, cell culture experiments, and mouse models. While relevant to post-acute COVID mechanisms, it is a basic science study without any clinical treatment intervention or patient outcomes.

This cross-sectional study measured 13 salivary biomarkers in 105 saliva samples (49 from children with long COVID, 56 controls) to identify diagnostic and severity markers for pediatric long COVID. The study identified TOS, ADA2, total proteins, and AOPP as discriminatory biomarkers but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a laboratory study assessing low-intensity focused ultrasound for lysing amyloid microclots in a lab-on-chip model, motivated by microclots' association with Long COVID. The work demonstrates promising in vitro results but is a bench-top feasibility study with no human subjects or clinical application, representing early-stage therapeutic development rather than a treatment trial.

This paper applies principal component analysis to identify symptom clusters and correlations in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME), including those with post-COVID manifestations. It is a secondary statistical analysis of existing clinical data rather than a primary treatment intervention study or trial.

This study investigates how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein induces cellular senescence through Cdc42 upregulation and demonstrates that ML141, a Cdc42 inhibitor, reduces senescence and ameliorates lung injury in infected mice. The research provides mechanistic insights into long-COVID pathophysiology and identifies a potential therapeutic target for mitigating long-term post-COVID complications.

This study analyzes immune cell composition and spatial distribution in gastrointestinal tissues of 11 COVID-19 patients with persistent GI symptoms using imaging mass cytometry and gene coexpression analysis. The findings demonstrate that CD68+ macrophages and CD4+ T-cells contribute to local tissue inflammation in the GI tract, suggesting potential molecular targets for treating COVID-related GI symptoms, but no intervention or treatment is evaluated.

This cross-sectional study examined ACE2, ACE1, and TMPRSS2 gene expression levels in nasopharyngeal tissue from 102 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to explore molecular mechanisms linking initial symptoms (loss of taste/smell) to long-term cognitive dysfunction. The study found a negative correlation between ACE2 expression and ageusia but no associations with anosmia, and speculates on a bridge between acute symptoms and long-term neurological sequelae without testing any intervention or treatment.

This study evaluated a health nutrition rehabilitation program in 64 post-COVID syndrome patients with moderate manifestations, using fruits, vegetables, and spices with prophylactic properties. The program achieved functional recovery in 1.5-3.5 months depending on severity and comorbidity burden.

This prospective study compared ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) versus standard-dose CT (SDCT) chest imaging in 100 long COVID patients with respiratory dysfunction to assess diagnostic accuracy while reducing radiation exposure. ULDCT achieved comparable diagnostic accuracy to SDCT for detecting lung abnormalities in non-obese patients while reducing radiation dose by 94.8%, but the paper is a diagnostic imaging comparison study rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This study analyzes transcriptomic and DNA methylation changes in peripheral blood samples from 9 recovered COVID-19 patients 3 months post-discharge compared to healthy controls. While it identifies molecular signatures of long COVID including immune dysregulation and transposable element activation, it is an observational biomarker study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible as a clinical trial.

This study examined psychopathological manifestations in 129 post-COVID patients who received remote medical-psychological and psychiatric care combining cognitive-behavioral therapy with antidepressants and non-benzodiazepine tranquilizers over 10 months. The treatment demonstrated effectiveness in reducing stress, anxiety, and depression, with outcomes varying by COVID-19 severity and presence of comorbid bronchopulmonary pathology.

In vitro study evaluating the protective effects of N-acetylcysteine and Sulodexide on endothelial cells exposed to serum from post-COVID-19 patients (4 months post-infection). Both compounds reduced inflammatory markers and improved endothelial function, suggesting potential therapeutic roles in mitigating myocardial injury in post-COVID syndrome.

This pilot study investigates bacterial uremic metabolites (BUM) in 25 post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients compared to ME/CFS patients and healthy controls using urine metabolomic analysis. While the study identifies distinct metabolic patterns and elevated BUM concentrations in PCS patients, it is observational/diagnostic in nature and does not evaluate or test any treatment or intervention.

This study compares cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and endomyocardial biopsy findings in 32 patients with persistent cardiac symptoms post-COVID-19, 22 with classical myocarditis, and 16 healthy controls. The results show that COVID-19 patients exhibited mild and variable cardiac involvement without meeting acute myocarditis criteria, unlike the classical myocarditis group.

A cross-sectional case series examining coronary microvascular perfusion in 33 post-COVID patients using cardiac MRI stress perfusion imaging compared to healthy controls. Found significantly reduced stress myocardial blood flow in long-COVID patients, but this reduction was not associated with symptom presence or COVID-19 severity.

In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein affects endothelial barrier integrity by degrading junctional proteins in cultured cells and mouse arteries. While relevant to understanding potential vascular mechanisms in COVID-19, this is a basic mechanistic study without patient involvement or treatment evaluation, not a long COVID clinical trial.

A non-randomized trial evaluating antihistamine treatment (fexofenadine and famotidine) in 14 long-COVID patients with mast cell activation syndrome compared to 13 untreated controls. Treatment resulted in complete symptom resolution in 29% of patients and significant improvement in fatigue, brain fog, abdominal disorders, and heart rate across all treated patients versus no improvement in controls.

This paper characterizes CD169+ and HLA-DR+ extracellular vesicles (EVs) in blood plasma across acute COVID-19, long COVID, and healthy donors using flow cytometry and atomic force microscopy. The study identifies myeloid activation markers and inflammatory profiles that persist in long COVID, offering potential biomarkers for monitoring post-acute sequelae, but does not test or evaluate any therapeutic intervention.

This is a mechanistic study in transgenic mice investigating cardiac pathology in SARS-CoV-2 and Trypanosoma cruzi coinfection, focusing on immune and metabolic signaling. While it addresses post-COVID cardiac damage, it is an animal model study without human subjects and does not evaluate any treatment intervention in long COVID patients.

This study analyzes neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) degradation products in serum/plasma samples across multiple inflammatory conditions, including Post COVID Syndrome (PCS). It is a cross-sectional biomarker characterization study that does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study develops a multimodal mHealth self-management program targeting fibromyalgia and post-viral fibromyalgia-like syndromes using generative AI-based knowledge graphs to structure and illustrate digital therapeutic content. Results show that AI-generated knowledge graphs effectively organize self-management program content, with centralized themes around pain, sleep, and stress management.

This cross-sectional study examines cardiac autonomic function in 155 long COVID patients versus 94 COVID-free controls using heart rate variability analysis. The authors found reduced HRV and increased sympathetic modulation in long COVID patients, but this is an observational assessment study without any intervention or treatment component.

Genetic analysis of ACE2 SNP rs2106809 and its association with ACE2 expression variation across brain and artery tissues. Finds rs2106809*G allele shows protective effect against COVID-19 hospitalization and upregulates ACE2 transcriptional activity, with potential implications for understanding long COVID susceptibility.

A Mendelian randomization study investigating bidirectional causal relationships between autoimmune diseases (IBD, Crohn's, ulcerative colitis) and Long COVID using GWAS summary data. Finds evidence that inflammatory bowel diseases have causal effects on Long COVID risk, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigates the feasibility of using wearable device data (heart rate variability, activity, sleep) to predict next-day fatigue levels in 68 people with post-COVID fatigue via machine learning models. While demonstrating good predictive accuracy, it is a passive observational assessment study with no intervention or treatment provided to participants.

This paper conducts a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify genetic variants and biological pathways underlying COVID-19 severity and post-acute sequelae (PASC) in Indian populations. It is a secondary genomic analysis of existing datasets rather than a treatment intervention study.

This paper uses computational gene expression profiling to identify five compounds that reduce NRP1 surface expression in macrophages as a potential therapeutic strategy for PASC/long COVID. The work is a preclinical drug discovery study with in vitro validation only, containing no patient data or clinical trial results.

A Mendelian randomization study exploring the causal relationship between COVID-19 and sarcopenia-related traits using genetic data from the COVID-19 Host Genetic Initiative and UK Biobank. The study found insufficient evidence for a direct causal relationship between COVID-19 and sarcopenia, suggesting they may indirectly interact.

This study compared immune responses between COVID-19 infected and convalescent individuals, finding persistent immune abnormalities in severe COVID survivors including altered T cell populations, increased low-density neutrophils, and elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines. The paper identifies potential immune correlates of long COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study measured serum C5a levels in 32 hospitalized and 17 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients during hospitalization and up to three months post-discharge. Elevated C5a persisted in severe cases and was associated with long-term respiratory symptoms, suggesting a role for C5a in long COVID pathophysiology, but the study is purely observational with no treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigates immune dysfunction in mild/asymptomatic COVID-19 convalescents, examining neutrophil subsets and T-cell responses 3 months post-infection. The paper documents persistent immunosuppression characterized by elevated low-density neutrophils (LDNs/PMN-MDSCs) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigates the presence of SARS-CoV-2 S1 protein in monocyte subsets from 46 individuals (severe COVID-19 and PASC patients vs healthy controls). The analysis is primarily descriptive immunological characterization examining elevated monocyte levels and viral protein persistence; it does not test or evaluate any therapeutic intervention.

This cross-sectional study performed deep flow cytometry profiling of the immune system in 35 COVID-19 recovered individuals (12-305 days post-infection) compared to 16 healthy controls. The study found alterations in T-cell, B-cell, and innate cell subsets at 10 months post-infection, including increased cTfh1, plasmablasts, and follicular dendritic cells, suggesting potential prognostic markers for re-infection or long-term symptoms, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study characterizes immune profiles across the COVID-19 disease spectrum (healthy controls, mild-moderate, severe, and PASC patients) using flow cytometry and cytokine analysis in 224 individuals. The authors identify immune signatures and develop machine learning classifiers to predict disease severity and PASC chronicity, but this is an observational immunologic characterization study without any treatment intervention.

This paper investigates long and short non-coding RNAs (NEAT1, DANCR) and their association with inflammation and cholinergic signaling in COVID-19 infection using transcriptomic analyses of GTEx lung tissues and cultured cells. While the abstract mentions post-infection manifestations and long-term complications, it is fundamentally a molecular/mechanistic study focused on RNA expression patterns in acute COVID-19 and inflammation, not a study of long COVID-specific clinical features or treatments.

This study identifies circulating biomarkers in post-COVID-19 individuals using targeted proteomics, comparing 186 post-COVID patients with acute COVID-19 patients and healthy controls. While it characterizes proteomic signatures of long COVID, it is a secondary biomarker analysis without testing any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigates kynurenine as a biomarker for diagnosing acute, long-term, and post-COVID-19 in serum and saliva samples across 151 hospitalized COVID-19 patients and 302 controls. The authors found elevated kynurenine levels correlate with inflammatory markers in acute COVID and persist elevated in post-COVID patients, but this is a diagnostic biomarker study with no intervention tested.

Bioinformatic analysis of gene expression datasets to identify biomarkers associated with COVID-19-related chronic urticaria, using machine learning and network analysis. The study identifies three key genes (FCGR3A, TNF, CCL3) as potential biomarkers and proposes 84 therapeutic candidates, but does not involve clinical treatment evaluation or trial participation.

This paper investigates oxidative stress and inflammasome activation in CD14highCD16- monocytes from acute COVID-19 patients, comparing severe vs mild cases and healthy controls. It is a mechanistic immunology study of acute COVID-19 pathophysiology, not a long COVID study or treatment trial.

This study measured blood biomarkers of BBB disruption, neuronal damage, and systemic inflammation in COVID-19 patients with severe disease or neurological complications versus healthy controls. BBB disruption markers (MMP-9, GFAP) were elevated in COVID-19 patients, particularly in those with neurological manifestations, suggesting a potential link between BBB damage and long-term neurological complications.

This study investigates the presence of HERV-W ENV protein expression and anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody profiles in post-COVID-19 patients, hypothesizing that persistent HERV expression may contribute to long COVID pathogenesis. The authors found HERV-W ENV antigenemia in post-COVID patients and a strong negative correlation between elevated anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgE levels and physical function, suggesting these biomarkers warrant further investigation as potential therapeutic targets.

This paper uses proteomics to identify an autoantigen atlas from human lung fibroblasts and maps proteins altered in SARS-CoV-2 infection that may explain autoimmune and neurological manifestations of long COVID. It is a basic science/mechanistic study (not a treatment trial) presenting a molecular map for understanding autoimmune sequelae rather than testing an intervention.

This study examined immune responses 1 year after COVID-19 infection across patients with varying disease severity, measuring antibody titers, phagocytic capacity, and memory B- and T-cell responses. The findings show that immune response parameters at 1 year post-infection depend on prior COVID-19 severity, potentially informing tailored vaccination strategies.

This study investigates the role of the AIM2 inflammasome in long COVID-associated lung fibrosis by examining peripheral blood mononuclear cells from post-COVID patients. The findings show that AIM2 activation is associated with release of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrogenic cytokines in patients with radiological signs of lung fibrosis, but this is a mechanistic study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study compares monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (M-MDSC) and T-cell responses in SARS-CoV-2 recovered individuals 5 months post-infection versus uninfected controls. The research identifies M-MDSC as novel regulators of CoV-2 specific T-cell responses but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Multi-omics study comparing immune cell profiles in 14 COVID-19 convalescent individuals versus 15 healthy controls using single-cell RNA-sequencing, ATAC-sequencing, and DNA methylation. Findings show immune system largely recovers to baseline with only minor transcriptomic and epigenetic differences that do not affect functional cytokine responses.

This cross-sectional study compared immune parameters between Spanish individuals with long COVID (49 weeks post-infection) and those who recovered within 12 weeks, identifying cytotoxic immune markers as diagnostic biomarkers. Using a Random Forest algorithm, the researchers achieved 100% accuracy in predicting long COVID group assignment based on CD8+ TEMRA cells, CD8±TCRγδ+ cells, NK cells, CD4+ Tregs, PD-1 expression, and clinical features including lethargy, chest pain, and dermatological injuries.

This study compares antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and latent virus reactivation between ME/CFS patients and healthy donors following mild/asymptomatic COVID-19 infection. While it demonstrates altered anti-viral profiles in ME/CFS patients, it is a biomarker characterization study rather than a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional study measuring anti-SARS-CoV-2 and autoantibodies in plasma from 31 convalescent healthcare workers 8 months post-infection compared to 21 uninfected controls. Found persistent antibody responses and broad autoreactivity post-COVID-19, with anti-calprotectin antibodies associated with better clinical outcomes, but this is an observational biomarker study with no intervention tested.

Bioinformatics study identifying common gene networks and signaling pathways between long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome using databases and computational analysis. Predicted 10 potential therapeutic compounds but conducted no treatment trial or clinical validation.

This paper investigates whether SARS-CoV-2 proteins induce innate memory in human monocytes using in vitro experiments. The work is mechanistic/exploratory (not a treatment trial) and appears to be preliminary findings rather than a complete study with results.

This cross-sectional study uses NMR spectroscopy and flow cytometry to characterize metabolomic, lipoprotein, and cytokine profiles in long-term COVID-19 syndrome patients compared to acute COVID-19, recovered, and healthy controls. The study identifies distinct metabolite imbalances (lactate, pyruvate, amino acids) and lipoprotein alterations in LTCS patients that may serve as biomarkers for patient stratification.

This study measures inflammasome signaling proteins (caspase-1, ASC, IL-1β, IL-18) in blood plasma of COVID-19 patients during acute infection and after recovery to establish their utility as biomarkers of the inflammatory response. The findings show these proteins remain elevated for months post-infection and can reliably distinguish active COVID-19 and post-COVID inflammatory states, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study compares olfactory mucosa gene expression between COVID-19 patients with persistent, transient, or no olfactory symptoms and non-COVID controls. The findings show that persistent olfactory deficits are associated with altered inflammatory and zinc homeostasis gene expression patterns, but this is a mechanistic study rather than a treatment trial.

This study investigates NAD metabolism dysregulation in SARS-CoV-2 infection and PASC using mouse models and human lung tissue, proposing NAD pathway modulation as a therapeutic strategy. The authors test nicotinamide riboside and anti-NAMPT antibody treatments in infected mice, demonstrating effects on metabolite profiles, but this is preclinical research with no human clinical trial results.

This study compares virus-specific T cell and antibody responses between Neuro-PASC patients and healthy COVID convalescents to identify immunological signatures. While it characterizes immune dysfunction in long COVID, it is a secondary analysis examining biomarkers in existing patient groups rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This is a basic science study investigating the mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein affects microglial purinergic signaling in cultured cells and animal models. The paper demonstrates that spike protein modulates purinergic receptors on microglia and in hippocampal tissue, but does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention in long COVID patients.

This study examined serum autoantibody levels targeting vaso- and immunoregulatory receptors in 80 post-COVID syndrome patients (40 with ME/CFS criteria) compared to healthy and asymptomatic post-COVID controls. They identified dysregulated autoantibodies correlating with symptom severity, particularly fatigue and vasomotor symptoms, suggesting a pathophysiological mechanism involving autonomic nervous system dysregulation.

This study identifies circulating Reelin as a pro-inflammatory marker elevated in acute COVID-19 that returns to normal in long COVID patients, suggesting resolution of the hyperinflammatory state. The authors demonstrate that Reelin inhibition with an anti-Reelin antibody (CR-50) decreases mortality and disease severity in SARS-CoV-2-infected mice, identifying Reelin as a potential therapeutic target for severe COVID-19.

This study examines alterations in sphingolipid metabolism in lung tissue from COVID-19 patients and convalescents, finding increased SK1 expression and altered sphingolipid ratios associated with inflammatory damage. It is a mechanistic/pathophysiology study of post-COVID lung changes without testing any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared immune profiles of fatigued vs non-fatigued long COVID patients and healthy controls at 3-6 months post-discharge. While it identified associations between fatigue severity and monocyte activation markers, it is an observational characterization study without testing any intervention or treatment.

This study used RNA-seq and systems biology to identify mechanistic endotypes of long COVID by comparing gene expression trajectories in COVID-19 patients with and without post-COVID symptoms. Three distinct endotypes were identified and validated, with inflammatory and hemostatic gene signatures potentially useful for clinical stratification and personalized treatment approaches.

This study compared mannan-binding lectin (MBL) levels and lectin pathway activity in serum samples from long COVID patients with brain fog, patients with only hyposmia/hypogeusia, and healthy controls. The authors found significantly lower MBL levels in brain fog patients, suggesting MBL deficiency may contribute to long COVID-associated cognitive dysfunction.

This study investigates pentameric and monomeric C-reactive protein (CRP) isoforms as prognostic biomarkers in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection. The research focuses on acute COVID-19 severity prediction and does not address long COVID or any treatment interventions.

This cross-sectional study compares B cell and antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 antigens between convalescent individuals who developed post-COVID condition (PCC) and those who did not, stratified by sex. The findings show sex-related differences in anti-spike antibody responses in PCC patients, with females showing higher responses but no differences in B cell responses compared to males.

This study performed single-cell RNA sequencing on peripheral blood mononuclear cells from long COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms (PPASC) to characterize immune dysregulation. The analysis revealed increased myeloid-lineage cells with upregulation of fibrosis-related genes and downregulation of immune pathways compared to controls, suggesting a potential role in PPASC pathophysiology.

This cross-sectional study characterizes humoral and CD4+ T cell immune responses in long COVID patients, comparing seropositive and seronegative groups to recovered and uninfected controls. It identifies two distinct immune response patterns in long COVID but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Genetic analysis using GWAS and Mendelian randomization to identify shared genetic associations between COVID-19 and multi-site chronic pain. Identifies potential drug targets and biomarkers but conducts no treatment intervention or clinical trial.

This study examined monocyte proportions and functional responsiveness in convalescent COVID-19 patients compared to uninfected controls using flow cytometry and ELISA. Findings show persistent decreases in monocyte subsets and reduced proinflammatory cytokine production during the convalescent phase, suggesting dysregulation of immune response in long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study followed 29 acute COVID-19 patients for one year to identify biomarkers predictive of long COVID development. T cell apoptosis during acute infection was the only significant predictor, with higher apoptosis rates in patients who later developed long COVID, suggesting T lymphopenia may contribute to post-COVID sequelae.

This study investigates TRPM3 ion channel dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients and tests whether naltrexone hydrochloride (NTX) can restore TRPM3 function in natural killer cells using patch-clamp electrophysiology. The results show that NTX treatment significantly restored TRPM3 currents in NK cells from post-COVID patients, suggesting NTX as a potential therapeutic intervention with TRPM3 as a treatment biomarker.

This paper identifies dysregulated long noncoding RNAs in brain tissue from severe COVID-19 patients compared to controls, examining transcriptomic changes associated with cognitive impairment. It is a molecular/mechanistic study of acute severe COVID-19 brain changes, not a study of long COVID patients or any intervention/treatment.

This study identifies metabolomic and immune alterations in long COVID patients with ME/CFS compared to recovered, acute COVID, and healthy controls. It is a comparative biomarker study with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it observational research rather than a treatment trial.

Prospective cohort study following 494 COVID-19 patients to identify early immune signatures associated with PASC development. Found that early immune differences in double-negative B cells and autoantibodies were associated with later PASC onset, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

This study develops a murine (mouse) model of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 using K18-hACE2 mice infected with SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. The researchers document persistent neuropsychiatric and motor abnormalities, immune pathway activation, and neuronal dysfunction up to 4 months post-infection, providing mechanistic insights into long COVID pathogenesis rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This study identified three inflammatory clusters in 101 long COVID patients by analyzing plasma biomarker levels using unsupervised clustering and logistic regression. The inflammatory profiles were associated with clinical variables (age, BMI, vaccination status) but not individual symptoms, providing insights into immune dysregulation patterns in long COVID.

This paper investigates how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein directly activates NK cells through TLR2/TLR4 receptors in vitro, with mechanistic findings relevant to COVID-19 pathophysiology. While it mentions long COVID subjects in plasma samples, the study is fundamentally a basic immunology investigation of viral-immune cell interaction mechanisms, not a clinical trial or treatment intervention study for long COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study assessed plasma galectin-9 and artemin as biomarkers to differentiate long COVID patients with ME/CFS from recovered and healthy controls across two cohorts. The study found elevated galectin-9 correlated with inflammatory markers and cognitive failure scores, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study measures serum levels of IL-6 and related cytokines in long COVID convalescents (after mild infection) compared to acute COVID-19 patients and controls. It is a cross-sectional biomarker analysis that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This pilot study identified a blood-based mRNA signature (LILRB1 and LILRB2 downregulation) that distinguishes long COVID patients from COVID-recovered controls using RNA-Seq of peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The findings suggest a sustained pro-inflammatory state in long COVID but do not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper develops a mathematical model of immune response to vaccination and antiviral treatment in SARS-CoV-2 infection to understand mechanisms of long COVID. The model suggests vaccination and antivirals during acute infection prevent severe tissue damage but do not prevent persistent infection, and proposes combination therapy as a potential long COVID treatment—however, this is purely theoretical modeling without empirical data or clinical validation.

This study uses SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particles (VLPs) in apoE-targeted replacement mice to assess whether viral exposure affects behavioral and cognitive performance, with findings showing apoE isoform-dependent effects on activity levels and circadian body temperature. While it addresses long COVID pathophysiology, it is a preclinical animal model study without human intervention testing and therefore excluded from the treatment trial pipeline.

This case-control study characterizes the immunological signature of long COVID patients through deep immunophenotyping and functional assays, comparing LC, acute COVID-19, recovered, and healthy cohorts. While identifying persistent adaptive immune dysregulation (reduced T cell subsets and memory B cells) as a potential biomarker, the paper does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Computational study identifying common genes between EBV reactivation and long COVID using RNA-Seq analysis and molecular dynamics simulations. Predicts hub genes and natural bioflavonoid inhibitors as potential therapeutic targets, but presents no clinical trial or experimental validation of treatments.

This study identifies conserved SARS-CoV-2 spike peptide epitopes and tests their immunogenicity in animal models, finding that one region (stem helix/HR2) elicits autoreactive antibodies linked to autoimmune disorders. The work is mechanistic research on long COVID pathogenesis relevant to vaccine design, not a clinical treatment trial.

This case-control study measures neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) and macrophage activation markers in SARS-CoV-2-infected patients from two pandemic waves, comparing those with and without post-COVID complications. The study identifies alterations in inflammatory markers (NE, MPO, MRP, ChT, CCL18) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigates transcriptomic changes in peripheral blood cells of 111 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients compared to recovered individuals and healthy controls. While minimal overall gene expression changes were found, a subgroup of male PCC patients showed distinct erythrocyte-related gene expression patterns enriched in heme metabolism and gas exchange pathways.

This multicenter study investigates autoantibodies cross-reactive between SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein and spermatogenesis-related antigens in long COVID patients, hypothesizing that autoimmune responses may affect fertility. The work is primarily a mechanistic/immunological investigation of pathophysiology rather than an evaluation of a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines serum and CSF levels of renin-angiotensin system autoantibodies and neurofilament light chain in post-COVID patients with neurological symptoms versus controls. While the findings suggest AT1-receptor autoantibodies as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for cognitive deficits, this is a biomarker discovery study with no treatment intervention tested.

This study analyzes transcriptome profiles in PBMCs from 60 post-COVID patients and 50 controls at 28 months post-infection, identifying upregulation of JAK/STAT signaling and mitochondrial dysfunction markers. The findings support post-COVID as a chronic inflammatory condition but do not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional proteomic study measuring inflammatory protein signatures in COVID-19 patients and non-COVID controls to identify markers predicting long COVID risk. The study identifies distinct protein profiles associated with acute severe illness and long COVID development but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared CD4+ T helper cell subsets and their functionality in people with post-COVID condition versus individuals with acute COVID-19 to characterize immune dysregulation. The researchers found that post-COVID patients had skewed polarization of Th subsets with altered functionality more similar to severe acute COVID-19 than to recovered individuals, suggesting potential therapeutic targets for immune reprogramming but providing no actual treatment intervention or outcomes.

This case-control study characterizes CD4+ T cell subsets in patients with sarcoidosis who developed the condition after COVID-19 (within 12-24 weeks) compared to sarcoidosis patients without COVID-19 history. The study found significant immune imbalances in T-helper cells and effector memory cells in COVID-19 convalescent sarcoidosis patients, suggesting possible progression of chronic lung sarcoidosis post-COVID.

This exploratory study examines IgG autoantibody reactivity to EBV-derived peptides and homologous human proteins in post-COVID and ME/CFS patients. The findings suggest molecular mimicry may play a role in PCS/ME/CFS pathogenesis, but the study is a biomarker assessment without treatment intervention.

This study analyzes human endogenous retroviral (HERV) expression patterns in monocytes from 12 long COVID patients using scRNA-seq data, identifying three HERV loci expressed across all patients with amplified transcription. The findings suggest epigenetic remodeling of myeloid progenitors in long COVID pathogenesis but do not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study compares IgG autoantibody levels against neuronal and mitochondrial proteins in 45 long COVID patients versus 30 post-COVID controls to investigate whether these antibodies are associated with functional impairment and respiratory symptoms. The findings are correlative and exploratory, identifying potential biomarkers rather than testing any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared monocyte subpopulations in 32 PACS patients versus 22 healthy controls using flow cytometry, finding dysregulated monocyte homeostasis with increased intermediate and CD56+ monocytes in PACS patients. The study is not a treatment trial—it is a mechanistic biomarker study with no intervention tested.

This cross-sectional study compared autoantibody profiles in 237 long COVID patients, 54 recovered COVID-19 patients, and 220 pre-pandemic controls to assess whether circulating autoantibodies play a pathogenic role in long COVID. The findings showed no significant association between the evaluated autoantibodies and long COVID symptoms or disease severity, arguing against a primary pathogenic role for these autoantibodies.

Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of 73,110 PBMCs from healthy, exposed, infected, and hospitalized individuals examining immune cell communication networks and CD8+ T cell signatures in COVID-19 and Long COVID. Identifies memory CD8+ T cell exhaustion and seven gene biomarkers associated with chronic immune dysregulation, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines immune mechanisms in 60 COVID-19 patients four months post-infection, comparing those with and without prior ARDS to healthy controls. The research demonstrates that chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10 promote B cell differentiation into IgG-secreting plasma cells, linking chronic inflammation to prolonged lung impairment in long COVID patients with pulmonary sequelae.

This cross-sectional study measured acute-phase protein levels, particularly pentraxin 3 (PTX-3), in 141 COVID-19 convalescent patients 10 weeks post-infection compared to 98 non-infected controls, and performed genetic analysis in a subgroup. Findings showed significantly elevated PTX-3 levels in severe COVID-19 patients persisting up to 10 months post-infection, with a genetic variant (rs971145291) associated with higher PTX-3 levels in severe cases, suggesting PTX-3 as a potential biomarker for long-term immune activation and post-COVID-19 complications.

This is a preclinical/mechanistic study demonstrating that acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) disrupts SARS-CoV-2 spike protein glycosylation and impairs ACE2 binding in cell culture and transgenic mice. While motivated by long COVID pathophysiology, it does not evaluate ASA as a treatment in human patients or patient cohorts, and appears to be a basic science investigation rather than a clinical trial or observational study of treated patients.

This study analyzes immune cell transcriptomes in 44 long COVID patients versus 44 matched controls using single-cell RNA sequencing and validates findings with plasma cytokine measurements. It identifies downregulation of pro-inflammatory genes and dysregulation of monocyte differentiation in long COVID patients, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a Mendelian randomization study using genetic data to estimate causal associations between COVID-19 and cardiovascular conditions. It does not study long COVID specifically, does not test any treatment intervention, and uses only genetic/observational analysis without participant enrollment or outcome measurement.

A pilot study evaluating whether medical detection dogs trained on acute COVID-19 samples can identify long COVID patients through volatile organic compound detection. Dogs achieved high sensitivity (94.4%) and specificity (96.1%) when distinguishing long COVID samples from healthy controls, suggesting VOC patterns persist post-infection.

In vitro study examining how a luteolin-rich extract from Perilla frutescens seed meal inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation induced by SARS-CoV-2 spike S1 protein in lung epithelial cells. The extract shows dose-dependent anti-inflammatory effects by suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, IL-18) via JAK1/STAT3 pathway regulation, suggesting potential for preventing inflammation-related long-COVID, but no treatment was administered to human patients.

This cross-sectional study examined serum metabolic profiles in 75 long COVID patients 2 months post-discharge, finding elevated markers of coagulation (D-dimer, ferritin), inflammation (CRP, ESR), and protein dysregulation (low albumin/hemoglobin). While it identifies biomarkers suggestive of an inflammatory/hypercatabolic state, it is observational with no treatment intervention tested and therefore does not qualify as a treatment trial.

Bioinformatics study identifying potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for long COVID-associated inflammatory cardiomyopathy through analysis of gene expression datasets. No clinical trial or treatment evaluation conducted; primarily a computational analysis of differential gene expression.

This cross-sectional study assessed cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) findings in 46 athletes and physically active individuals with and without persistent symptoms >2 months post-COVID-19. Symptomatic participants showed more abnormalities in ventilatory and breathing parameters, though causality and clinical significance remain unclear without pre-infection baseline data.

This cross-sectional study measured plasma levels of inflammatory cytokines, angiogenic factors, and heat shock proteins in patients with osteoarthritis who had recovered from COVID-19, compared to healthy controls and OA-only patients. Results showed dysregulation of inflammatory and angiogenic markers in post-COVID patients with OA, suggesting systemic post-COVID inflammatory mechanisms.

This retrospective cohort study analyzes 4,752 Italian death certificates reporting post-COVID condition from October 2020 to December 2021, identifying underlying causes of death and calculating mortality rates. While demonstrating that post-COVID contributed to substantial mortality, the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention and therefore does not meet criteria for inclusion in a clinical trials meta-analysis.

This retrospective study evaluates U-Net-based CT quantification to predict fibrotic interstitial lung abnormalities at 3-month follow-up in COVID-19 patients. While it addresses post-COVID pulmonary sequelae, it is a diagnostic/prognostic study rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This study evaluates the 10-minute NASA Lean Test (NLT) as a diagnostic tool for orthostatic intolerance in long COVID and ME/CFS patients, comparing symptomatic and hemodynamic responses to healthy controls. The NLT provoked symptom worsening and objective abnormalities in patient groups but not controls, suggesting it can objectively confirm orthostatic intolerance and cognitive impairment in long COVID.

This paper describes the development and evaluation of a post-COVID syndrome curriculum for physician continuing medical education (CME), comparing in-person versus livestream delivery using flipped classroom methods. While about long COVID, it is not a treatment trial but rather an educational intervention study, and should be excluded as it does not test a clinical intervention for long COVID patients.

This study investigates serum decorin and biglycan as biomarkers for assessing COVID-19 severity and mortality risk in 240 patients followed for 2 months. While it mentions post-COVID lung fibrosis in the introduction, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 disease severity during the active infection phase, not on long COVID symptoms or post-acute sequelae.

This observational cohort study characterizes long-term pulmonary dysfunction in long-COVID patients using clinical testing, imaging, and serum proteome profiling at 4 and 12 months post-infection. The study identifies associations between pulmonary dysfunction and vascular inflammation pathways, metabolic syndrome, and impaired immune function, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This study compares anti-human adenovirus IgG levels in saliva samples from ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls, examining whether SARS-CoV-2 infection triggers reactivation of dormant adenovirus. The findings suggest COVID-19 reactivates latent adenovirus specifically in chronic fatigue patients with dysfunctional antiviral immunity, but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.

This study investigates autonomic nervous system dysfunction in post-COVID syndrome patients with prolonged cardiovascular symptoms, measuring heart rate variability and arterial pressure responses to head-up tilt testing. Findings show autonomic dysfunction with sympathetic predominance in PCS patients, with some improvement at 6-month reassessment, but indicate marked impairment of autonomic control despite clinical recovery trends.

This retrospective study analyzes 1,331 long COVID patients treated with Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) across three hospitals in China, developing machine learning models to predict which patients benefit from TCM treatment. The XGBoost model achieved 90.6% AUC in predicting TCM efficacy, with a nomogram created to assist clinical decision-making for TCM applications in long COVID management.

This cross-sectional study analyzes lung function test outcomes in 4,211 long COVID patients, with 80.46% showing positive bronchial provocation test results. While it identifies age, MEF50, and DLCOc SB as independent factors influencing BPT positivity, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention—only diagnostic and prognostic associations.

This prospective interrupted time-series study evaluated speleotherapy (cave air therapy) as a treatment for post-COVID-19 syndrome patients with persistent dyspnea, measuring lung diffusion capacity and symptoms across 46 rehabilitation patients. Speleotherapy showed no significant improvements in lung function parameters or symptom severity compared to control days.

This cross-sectional study investigates salivary innate immune molecules and their relationship to taste dysfunction in COVID-19 patients. While it addresses long COVID symptoms, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.

A Mendelian randomization study using GWAS summary statistics to investigate causal relationships between gut microbiota composition and Long COVID susceptibility. Identifies three causal associations (Parasutterella and Oscillospira increase risk; Eisenbergiella decreases risk) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study compares SARS-CoV-2-specific immune responses between 40 long COVID (PASC) patients and 15 healthy convalescent controls using flow cytometry and neutralizing assays. The researchers found that PASC patients have low-avidity, pro-inflammatory CD8+ T cells with TEMRA phenotype that may drive persistent inflammation, but no active treatment intervention was tested or evaluated.

This cross-sectional study compares plasma proteomics and metabolomics profiles in long COVID patients versus healthy controls and COVID-recovered patients to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers. The analysis reveals dysregulation in coagulation, immune response, and metabolic pathways in long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study uses machine learning and explainable AI to identify metabolic signatures distinguishing COVID-19, post-COVID-19, and control patients from 142 COVID, 48 post-COVID, and 38 controls. While it provides insights into metabolic anomalies in long COVID, it is a purely observational biomarker analysis without any treatment intervention or evaluation.

This paper describes the development and validation of an ELISA test for measuring neutrophil elastase (NE) as a potential biomarker of organ damage in post-COVID syndrome. The work demonstrates elevated NE levels in post-COVID patients with diabetic nephropathy but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared neuropsychological performance between 319 post-COVID patients and 109 healthy controls using a comprehensive cognitive battery. Post-COVID patients showed significant impairment in global cognition, memory, processing speed, and executive function, with Montreal Cognitive Assessment and digit symbol tests effectively distinguishing patients from controls.

This study uses a golden Syrian hamster model to investigate the biological mechanisms underlying post-COVID-19 condition, integrating virological, immunological, histopathological, and behavioral analyses from acute phase to 60 days post-inoculation. While it demonstrates persistent viral RNA and behavioral changes mirroring human PCC features, it is an animal model study rather than a human treatment trial and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive function in 40 patients during the subacute phase of COVID-19 using standardized neuropsychiatric tests. 72.5% of participants showed impairments in at least one cognitive domain, with executive function most frequently affected, but the study does not test any treatment intervention.

This in vitro study examines how prolonged exposure to TNF-α and IL-6 affects neural activity and function in human iPSC-derived neuron-astrocyte co-cultures. While relevant to long COVID pathophysiology, it is a mechanistic bench study without human subjects or patient treatment, thus excluded from the clinical trials pipeline.

This paper describes the adaptation of the UK Biobank brain MRI protocol for the C-MORE multi-organ study of COVID-19 survivors, including analysis pipeline development and imaging-derived phenotypes. It presents exploratory findings from 51 post-hospitalization COVID-19 patients and 25 controls, but is primarily a protocol/methods paper rather than a treatment intervention study.

Untargeted lipidomic analysis of post-COVID-19 patients two years after infection reveals dysregulation in lipid pathways including sterols, bile acids, and phosphatidylcholines compared to controls. The study identifies potential metabolic markers associated with persistent fatigue and musculoskeletal symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigates low-dose naltrexone (LDN) as a treatment for long COVID by examining its effect on TRPM3 ion channel function in natural killer cells from long COVID patients. Results demonstrate that LDN treatment restores TRPM3 ion channel function in long COVID patients to levels comparable with healthy controls, suggesting LDN may benefit long COVID patients by restoring calcium influx and cellular homeostasis.

This study compares brain microstructure and cognitive/fatigue outcomes in 56 COVID-19 patients versus 37 matched controls using MRI and neuropsychological testing at ~93 days post-diagnosis. While it demonstrates white matter microstructural changes correlating with fatigue in long COVID patients, it is an observational cross-sectional study without any treatment intervention.

This study evaluates motor fatigue in 29 non-hospitalized post-COVID patients using treadmill walking tests and the FSMC questionnaire. Despite severe subjective fatigue scores, only 2 subjects showed objective motor fatigability, suggesting functional capacity is better preserved than patients perceive.

This prospective study compared perivascular space (PVS) quantification on 7T MRI between 10 COVID-19 patients and controls to determine if PVS could serve as a biomarker of neuroinflammation. Results showed significantly elevated PVS count and altered white matter volume in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, though no correlation with symptom severity was observed.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 77 post-COVID patients using oculomotor, vestibular, reaction time, and cognitive (OVRT-C) testing via eye-tracking to identify objective neural deficits. While demonstrating feasibility of OVRT-C testing for screening neurological deficits post-COVID (88% sensitivity, 98% specificity), the study is purely diagnostic/observational with no treatment intervention tested.

This cross-sectional study evaluated vestibular function in 58 patients with persistent vertigo/dizziness 6 months after COVID-19 infection using comprehensive otoneurological assessment and videonystagmography. The findings demonstrate high prevalence of vestibular dysfunction (nystagmus, unilateral weakness, impaired tracking) suggesting COVID-19 can cause inner ear damage and post-infectious neuroinflammation, but the study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study evaluated cognitive deficits in 29 post-acute COVID-19 and post-vaccination syndrome patients and tested the efficacy of phosphatidylcholine and computer-assisted cognitive training for treatment. While all treatment groups showed cognitive improvement with positive trends, no statistically significant differences were found between groups, suggesting possible spontaneous remission of cognitive deficits.

A multimodal MRI study comparing 14 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment to 10 healthy controls, measuring blood-brain barrier permeability, brain metabolites, and white matter integrity at 3 and 12 months post-infection. PASC patients showed elevated blood-brain barrier permeability, elevated inflammation markers, reduced glutamate/glutamine levels, and white matter loss, with partial improvement at 12 months.

This cross-sectional study identified two neurocognitive domains in PASC patients using factor analysis: classic memory/concentration symptoms and sensory overload phenomena. The study characterizes symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared white matter microstructural integrity in 22 recovered COVID-19 patients versus 16 healthy controls using advanced MRI diffusion techniques (DTI, DKI, NODDI). Results showed reduced white matter structural complexity in certain regions of recovered COVID-19 patients, suggesting potential long-term neurological sequelae from COVID-19.

A bioinformatics study identifying co-expressed genes and molecular mechanisms linking post-COVID-19 and Guillain-Barre syndrome through analysis of GEO datasets and protein-protein interaction networks. The study identifies MMP9, CASP1, and CAMP as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) differences between 31 older adults with long-COVID and 31 unaffected controls, finding that the long-COVID group showed greater extreme CVR clusters in attention and executive function networks. The study links CVR abnormalities to cognitive symptoms and neuropsychological performance but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive functioning in 106 outpatients with neuro-PASC, comparing those with and without prior COVID-19 hospitalization. Findings showed subjective cognitive concerns were more pronounced than objective deficits and were primarily associated with fatigue and depression/mood symptoms rather than hospitalization status.

This case-control study compared brain structural MRI features between adolescents with long COVID headaches and those with primary headaches, using machine learning to distinguish between the two groups. While it identified distinct gray matter changes associated with long COVID headaches, it is a diagnostic/prognostic study rather than a treatment intervention study.

This cross-sectional study compared neurophysiological and cognitive function between 32 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent hyposmia and 16 controls using EEG/fNIRS during cognitive tasks and olfactory testing. The study found deficits in prefrontal function and olfactory performance in post-COVID patients but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines post-exertional malaise (PEM) in Long COVID by comparing self-reported PEM prevalence across cohorts and assessing symptom responses to standardized exercise testing (CPET). While the paper includes Long COVID patients undergoing exercise testing, it does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention—it is a descriptive/comparative assessment study without therapeutic intent or control groups receiving differential treatments.

This paper develops machine learning models trained on EEG data to detect PASC/ME using a wearable headband, achieving 93% accuracy with synthetic data augmentation. The study demonstrates a diagnostic tool for identifying PASC but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic outcome.

This exploratory cross-sectional study compared EEG neurodynamics during resting state and olfactory stimulation across three groups: severe COVID-19 patients, recovered moderate COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls. The study found differential patterns of cortical rigidity and neurodynamic adaptation in COVID-19 groups but explicitly notes the absence of behavioral or neuropsychological testing limits interpretations of cognitive status.

Cross-sectional study comparing memory consolidation and cognitive function in 42 long-COVID patients (with and without anosmia) versus 30 healthy controls. Found that long-COVID patients, particularly those with anosmia, show deficits in consolidation of declarative and procedural memories, suggesting limbic system dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study comparing cortical gray matter volume, thickness, and surface area between 33 COVID-19 patients with neurological symptoms and 33 healthy controls using MRI. Found reduced cortical volume in orbitofrontal, frontal, and cingulate regions in patients, with associations to CSF inflammatory biomarkers, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared brainstem volumes on 7T MRI between 10 ME/CFS patients, 8 long COVID patients, and 10 healthy controls. Both patient groups showed significantly enlarged brainstem regions (pons, whole brainstem) and correlations with symptom severity (pain, breathing difficulty), but this is observational research without any treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of skin biopsy samples from 31 long COVID patients comparing autonomic small fiber density (piloerector and sweat gland innervation) to healthy controls. Findings show significantly reduced nerve fiber density in long COVID patients, providing histological evidence of autonomic small fiber involvement independent of somatic nerve fiber loss.

This pilot study compares brain connectivity patterns during cognitive tasks between 10 long COVID patients and 13 healthy controls using 7 Tesla fMRI, finding altered connectivity in brainstem and default-mode network regions. The findings suggest brainstem circuit dysfunction may underlie cognitive and autonomic symptoms in long COVID, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined functional brain connectivity in non-hospitalized adults with post-COVID cognitive complaints using fMRI and neuropsychological testing. The findings showed preserved default mode network connectivity positively correlated with cognitive performance, providing neuroimaging evidence of brain function in individuals recovering from mild COVID.

This pilot study analyzes plasma fatty acid profiles in COVID-19 patients with varying disease severity and examines associations with post-acute sequelae (PASC). The paper reports observational findings linking fatty acid depletion to PASC development but appears to be a registered protocol without intervention or clinical trial results.

Cross-sectional study measuring serum tryptophan catabolites, inflammatory markers, and insulin resistance in 90 long COVID patients 3-10 months post-infection to identify biomarkers associated with chronic fatigue and affective symptoms. Identified three biomarkers (CRP, KYN/TRY ratio, insulin resistance) that explained ~40% of variance in physio-affective symptoms, suggesting inflammatory dysregulation from acute infection contributes to long COVID pathophysiology.

This metabolomics study compares serum metabolite profiles between COVID-19 patients with negative nucleic acid tests and healthy controls, identifying dysregulation in amino acid and lipid metabolism. Although the authors suggest metabolic changes could underlie long COVID pathophysiology, the study is a descriptive cross-sectional analysis with no intervention or treatment being tested.

This study describes acute SARS-CoV-2 infection symptoms and persistent symptoms 4-12 weeks post-infection in 2,001 children aged 0-17 years in Beijing. While it characterizes long COVID prevalence and symptom patterns, it is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study evaluates Qimai Feiluoping decoction (QM), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, for treating pulmonary fibrosis in COVID-19 convalescent patients through clinical observation and network pharmacology analysis. The work identifies active compounds in QM and demonstrates that it inhibits fibrosis progression by suppressing the TGF-β/Smad3 pathway and promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition reversal in cell culture models.

This is an in vitro mechanistic study investigating how histamine potentiates SARS-CoV-2 spike protein entry into endothelial cells and how the H2R blocker famotidine can block this effect. While relevant to long COVID pathophysiology, it is a basic science study without patient treatment or clinical outcomes, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This is a computational study identifying shared gene signatures between COVID-19 and major depressive disorder using machine learning and bioinformatics.
