It proposes trichostatin A as a potential therapeutic candidate through molecular docking simulations, but conducts no actual clinical or biological validation of treatment effects.

This paper analyzes publicly available data to investigate the effect of SARS-CoV-2 infection on mitochondrial non-coding RNA expression in COVID-19 recovery patients. The study is a secondary analysis of existing datasets examining molecular mechanisms rather than testing an intervention, and constitutes a review of published data rather than original research with patient cohorts.

This mechanistic study investigates how adenosine deaminase (ADA1) promotes endothelial inflammation in post-COVID syndrome through in vitro experiments using serum from post-COVID patients and human lung microvascular endothelial cells. The findings identify the ADA1-CD26 interaction as a key pathway in vascular dysfunction, but this is basic research with no patient treatment or intervention tested.

Experimental study in rats examining histological changes in reproductive tissues and hormone levels after exposure to SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein. While the authors speculate a link to post-COVID hypogonadism, the study is an animal model experiment with no human long COVID participants or treatment evaluation.

This paper develops a deep learning model using contrastive learning to differentiate post-COVID-19 patients from healthy controls and identify subtypes based on lung CT scans. It identifies two distinct post-COVID-19 phenotypes characterized by either small airways disease with air-trapping or airway-associated interstitial fibrotic patterns, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares pulmonary diffusing capacity measurements (DLCO and DLNO) between 37 long COVID patients and 37 symptom-free controls to characterize respiratory dysfunction in long COVID. The findings show significantly reduced DLCO, DLNO, pulmonary capillary blood volume, and alveolar volume in the long COVID group, suggesting impaired lung perfusion as a key mechanism.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiorespiratory fitness and running biomechanics between 14 female recreational runners who had recovered from COVID-19 and 14 healthy controls. Results showed that recovered COVID-19 runners had reduced running endurance, increased ground contact time, and weaker propulsion forces compared to controls.

This cross-sectional study examined the association between olfactory dysfunction and quality of life in 58 individuals with post-COVID olfactory symptoms. While it identifies correlations between smell impairment and daily life problems, it is not a treatment trial—it documents impairment without testing any intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated cognitive and neurological features in 406 COVID-19 patients at ~98 days post-symptom onset using neuropsychological tests and self-reported symptoms. The study found persistent cognitive alterations in 20.7% of patients, particularly in attention and working memory, associated with cardiovascular disease history, persistent fatigue, female sex, age, anxiety, and mental health stress.

This cross-sectional study compares maximal fat oxidation and exercise intensity at fat oxidation between endurance-trained and recreationally active subjects with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection. While the paper addresses long COVID-related exercise intolerance, it is a descriptive physiological comparison without testing any intervention or treatment.

This observational study evaluated sleep quality via wrist actigraphy and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index in 49 post-COVID-19 patients from the NAUTILUS Project, correlating objective sleep measures with cognitive performance. The study found divergent results between self-reported and objective sleep measures, with a trend toward reduced cognitive performance in those with lower sleep efficiency.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiovascular and autonomic nervous system responses to acute submaximal exercise in 27 individuals: 9 never infected (controls), 9 previously asymptomatic COVID-19 positive, and 9 previously symptomatic COVID-19 positive. Symptomatic COVID-19 survivors showed significantly reduced heart rate variability during exercise compared to controls and asymptomatic individuals, suggesting altered cardiovascular regulation.

This structural MRI pilot study examines differences in gray matter thickness and volume in cortical limbic and prefrontal regions between long COVID patients and healthy controls. The study found increased cortical thickness in specific brain regions (cingulate gyrus, middle frontal gyrus) and associations with cognitive and anxiety severity measures, but it is a cross-sectional observational study with no treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed IgG antibody levels and psychological measures in COVID-19 patients approximately 2 months post-diagnosis in Northern Cyprus. While it examines post-infection recovery, it does not focus on persistent long COVID symptoms (which typically manifest weeks to months after acute infection) and does not test any treatment intervention.

This pilot study assessed emotional, cognitive, and somatic concerns in 26 Long COVID patients using neuropsychological screening and the Personality Assessment Inventory. The study found elevated somatic and cognitive concerns in >50% of participants, but is descriptive and non-interventional, providing no treatment outcomes or comparative data.

This study validates the German version of the DSQ-PEM (DePaul Symptom Questionnaire for Post-Exertional Malaise) in a representative general population sample and a clinical post-COVID sample. It demonstrates the instrument's reliability and validity for measuring PEM in German-speaking populations but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines cognitive dysfunction in 41 long COVID patients using neuropsychological testing, psychiatric assessments, and inflammatory markers. The authors find that cognitive symptoms are more strongly associated with objective neuropsychological impairment than with depression, fatigue, or inflammatory cytokine levels.

A cross-sectional network analysis of 535 COVID-19 survivors 1 year post-hospitalization examining symptom-symptom interactions between mental distress (depression, anxiety, PTSD, sleep disturbance, fatigue) and quality of life. The study identifies key central and bridge symptoms (daytime dysfunction, fatigue) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This feasibility study evaluated an 8-week interprofessional group therapy program for post-COVID patients delivered in both face-to-face and online formats, targeting fatigue, stress intolerance, and symptom management. Among 57 participants (36 online, 21 face-to-face), the intervention was well-accepted and predominantly rated as helpful, with particular value in peer support, though the authors note that controlled studies are needed to formally evaluate efficacy.

This cross-sectional MRI study investigates sex-specific differences in gray matter volume alterations associated with cognitive impairment in long-COVID patients compared to healthy controls. The authors found that cognitive impairment manifests through sex-specific brain structural changes, with females showing more restricted alterations in frontal and limbic regions, while males displayed widespread neocortical involvement.

This study develops a machine learning model to predict post-COVID-19 syndrome development in 221 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors using pre-discharge and 1-month follow-up clinical data. It identifies early predictors of PCS (75% prevalence at 3 months) but does not test or evaluate a specific intervention or treatment.

Post-hoc analysis of the COMET-ICE trial examining health-related quality of life and predictors of long COVID development among patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The study identifies acute phase symptom severity and COPD as significant predictors of long COVID but does not test a long COVID treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared olfactory function, cognitive performance, and neuropsychiatric symptoms in 121 post-COVID patients versus 51 healthy controls. While it found significant cognitive and psychiatric sequelae in post-COVID patients, it is an observational study without any treatment intervention and therefore does not meet criteria for the clinical trials pipeline.

This study validates a German translation of the PAC-19QoL instrument, a quality-of-life measurement tool for long COVID patients. The instrument demonstrates good reliability and validity but this is a validation/psychometric study with no treatment intervention tested.

A multicentric cross-sectional study of 2,445 COVID-19 patients across LMICs assessing symptom persistence, depression, and chronic fatigue using validated instruments and deep learning models. Vaccinated individuals showed lower odds of prolonged symptoms and depression, and the study developed a predictive risk calculator for chronic fatigue and prolonged COVID-19 symptoms.

This paper describes the infrastructure, database, and biobank established at a major Brazilian academic health center to support COVID-19 research, including follow-up assessments of 700 hospitalized patients 6-11 months post-discharge. While it includes longitudinal follow-up of post-COVID patients, it is a descriptive paper about research systems and infrastructure rather than a treatment intervention study, and is excluded as a secondary/infrastructure analysis.

A cross-sectional analysis of 27,216 Reddit posts documenting long COVID patient experiences and symptom profiles using natural language processing and clustering. Identifies fatigue, pain, and neurological symptoms as most prevalent but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

The ECHOES dataset links national COVID-19 testing data with electronic health records for 44 million individuals in England to monitor health outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection. This is a descriptive epidemiological resource for investigating post-acute COVID-19 health conditions and mortality patterns, not a treatment trial or intervention study.

This study uses machine learning (random forest classification) on longitudinal cohort data from the UK's Understanding Society COVID-19 Study to identify risk factors for long COVID-19. The analysis identifies sociodemographic and health-related predictors including early pandemic infection timing, work hours, age, and financial insecurity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study evaluating a 12-session physiotherapy protocol in 42 post-COVID-19 patients over 4 weeks. The intervention improved lung function (FEV1 +7.16%, FVC +7.56%), exercise capacity (6-min walk +13%), and reduced post-COVID sequelae by ~50%, with improvements in psychoemotional status and handgrip strength.

This paper investigates potential autoimmune cross-reactivity of antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein with human self-antigens using Western blot and mass spectrometry in animal models (mice, rabbits, hamsters). The findings highlight differences in anti-N antibody responses across species and provide implications for vaccine design, but do not test or evaluate any treatment intervention in long COVID patients.

This paper develops a Fuzzy Cognitive Map Decision Support System to model causal relationships between post-COVID syndrome symptoms and recommend specialist referrals for speech-language pathology problems. It uses a systematic review of 19 studies to identify symptom prevalence and demonstrates preliminary validation on four case studies, but does not evaluate an intervention or treatment.

In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 PLpro impairs interferon-related genes in epithelial cells and testing hydroxytyrosol as a potential therapeutic agent. This is a basic science mechanistic study with no patient intervention or clinical trial component.

This cross-sectional study evaluates the test-retest reliability and minimal detectable change of two exercise tolerance tests (Chester Step Test and 1-Minute Sit-to-Stand) in 42 long COVID patients. While the tests show excellent reliability, this is a methodological validation study without evaluating any intervention outcomes, so it falls outside the treatment trial scope despite being directly relevant to long COVID assessment.

This cross-sectional study examined whether genetic variations in antioxidant enzymes (SOD2, GPX, GST, Nrf2, ACE2) are associated with neurological sequelae in long-COVID patients. Specific polymorphisms in GSTP1 and GSTO1 were found to independently or cumulatively affect the risk of developing long-COVID myalgia and brain fog, supporting genetic susceptibility as a factor in long-COVID manifestations.

This is a computational/in silico study using molecular dynamics simulations to predict the binding affinity and stability of apigenin and related flavonoids to the Nrf2 pathway as potential therapeutic candidates for long COVID. The study presents only molecular modeling results and predictions with no human participants, clinical trials, or experimental validation of therapeutic efficacy.

This prospective observational study validates an energy level diary tool for fatigue management in post-COVID syndrome patients across two German rehabilitation centers, using a codesign approach with feedback from participants. The diary effectively tracks daily energy fluctuations, correlates with the MFI-20 fatigue scale, and patients rated it as a useful tool for learning pacing strategies and adapting rehabilitation therapies.

A feasibility pilot study examining how secondary motor and cognitive tasks affect gait in 30 participants across six groups including long COVID patients, using wearable sensors to measure spatiotemporal parameters. The study found the incongruent dual-task condition most sensitive for differentiating clinical groups, with all participants completing the protocol successfully.

This cross-sectional study evaluates small airways dysfunction and lung hyperinflation in 33 long COVID patients using pulmonary function tests and nitrogen washout techniques. The study demonstrates associations between small airways impairment and persistent dyspnea but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper analyzes 1.2 million tweets about long COVID posted on Twitter between May 2020 and January 2023 using sentiment analysis and text mining techniques. It finds high tweet volume in 2022, mixed sentiment distribution (43% positive, 43% negative, 14% neutral), and that sadness was the most commonly expressed emotion.

This exploratory study compared chemosensory event-related potentials (CSERP) in 18 long COVID patients, 12 mild cognitive impairment patients, and 10 healthy controls to investigate shared neurobiological pathways. The study found reduced N1 amplitude and P3 latency abnormalities in long COVID patients, suggesting CSERPs could serve as biomarkers for cognitive and olfactory dysfunction, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This paper investigates sesamin's anti-inflammatory and anti-COVID-19 properties through in vitro cell line assays and in silico molecular docking analyses, not through clinical trials or patient treatment. While it mentions long COVID symptoms, it does not test any intervention on actual long COVID patients.

A pilot study examining whether dietary habits and vitamin levels predict long COVID development in mild COVID-19 cases. Found that higher symptom count and fatigue predicted long COVID, while certain nutrients (vitamin E, PUFAs, fiber, iron) were associated with lower symptom severity.

This cross-sectional immunoassay study investigates the presence of autoantibodies against vagal nucleus proteins in long-COVID patients, vaccinated subjects, and unvaccinated controls. The findings suggest molecular mimicry may contribute to neurovegetative symptoms in long COVID, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares red blood cell morphology, deformability, and aggregation between 30 long COVID patients and 30 controls to investigate the relationship between RBC abnormalities and fatigue. The study finds that LC patients have higher RBC aggregation, morphological abnormalities, and limited functional capacity to deform, which correlates with fatigue severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed heart rate variability, peripheral body temperature, and serum cytokine levels in 202 long COVID patients (stratified by symptom duration) compared to 95 healthy controls. The findings indicate reduced parasympathetic activation, elevated body temperature, and distinct inflammatory cytokine profiles (elevated IL-17/IL-2, low IL-4) in long COVID, suggesting potential treatment targets.

This paper investigates the role of toxin-like peptides produced by gut bacteria in long COVID patients, comparing plasma, urine, and fecal samples from COVID-19 and long COVID patients. The study is an in vitro proteomics analysis of bacterial cultures without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study comparing fecal microbiome composition and serum cytokine profiles in PASC and ME/CFS patients versus controls, using longitudinal databases and newly collected samples. Findings show significant dysbiosis and altered cytokine expression (elevated MIP-1β, reduced TARC) in PASC patients, with correlations to chronic fatigue symptoms.

This cross-sectional study examines inflammatory biomarkers and their relationship to depression and cognitive impairment in 101 COVID-19 survivors at one and three months post-infection. While it identifies sex-specific inflammatory pathways associated with neuropsychiatric outcomes, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper explores potential therapeutic approaches against long COVID by analyzing blood pH, temperature variations, and molecular interactions using NMR spectroscopy and computational modeling. The work proposes incretin mimetics as potential preventive agents but presents only in silico and in vitro experiments without any clinical trial data or patient outcomes.

This study compares brain source activity at rest using high-density EEG between 18 post-COVID patients with cognitive deficits/fatigue and 18 healthy controls. The findings show reduced delta activity in executive function regions in post-COVID patients, but this is a diagnostic/mechanistic study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This study investigates kidney pathology in mice infected with mouse hepatitis virus-1 (MHV-1) as a model for long COVID kidney injury, identifying elevated markers of fibrosis and inflammation. The authors test a synthetic peptide (SPIKENET) that reduces several pathogenic markers in the mouse model, suggesting potential therapeutic targets for COVID-associated kidney complications.

This cross-sectional study develops a metabolic fingerprinting approach using portable FT-MIR spectroscopy to differentiate long COVID from fibromyalgia based on blood samples. While it identifies distinct metabolic signatures between the two conditions, it is a diagnostic study, not a treatment intervention trial, and thus falls outside the scope of the screening criteria for intervention trials.

This study investigates abnormal immunological factors in autoimmune disease patients after COVID-19 recovery, comparing 11 patients with various autoimmune diseases and 16 SLE patients. It found increased follicular T helper cells and decreased regulatory T cells post-infection, but this is an observational cross-sectional study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials database.

This cross-sectional study measured adenine nucleotide levels in red blood cells and endothelial/microvascular function parameters in long COVID patients 12 weeks post-infection. The study found correlations between RBC ATP levels and vascular dysfunction markers but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compares immune cell profiles and checkpoint expression in post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (PCPF) patients versus idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and healthy controls. While the paper investigates long COVID sequelae, it is observational and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This prospective cohort study examined myokine levels (myostatin, agrin, irisin, myonectin) in post-COVID-19 patients undergoing comprehensive rehabilitation and their correlation with rehabilitation duration. Lower irisin and myonectin and higher myostatin levels correlated with longer rehabilitation time, suggesting baseline myokine profiles could predict recovery trajectory.

This study uses surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) combined with multivariate analysis to develop classification models that differentiate long COVID from fibromyalgia based on blood metabolite profiles. The research demonstrates the feasibility of identifying spectral biomarkers in blood samples with high accuracy (100% validation performance) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This proteomics study analyzes plasma samples from 28 COVID-19 patients with and without comorbidities to identify protein signatures and early diagnostic biomarkers. The research identifies alterations in coagulation, complement, and acute-phase response pathways, with potential relevance to long-COVID complications, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This study investigates the mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 spike protein induces α-synuclein aggregation in rodent models and neuronal cell cultures via microglia-mediated inflammation and mitochondrial ROS production. The authors evaluate metformin as a potential therapeutic intervention, finding it suppresses spike protein-induced inflammatory response and α-synucleinopathy in preclinical models.

This paper develops a machine learning clinical decision support system using fuzzy inference engines to predict dyspnea 12 months after acute COVID-19, based on retrospective patient data from the SeguiCovid database. The system is not a treatment trial but rather a diagnostic/predictive tool for identifying long COVID patients at risk of persistent dyspnea.

This cross-sectional study compared DNA methylation levels of the ACE2 promoter in 279 COVID-19 survivors who were hospitalized, stratified by presence or absence of post-COVID-19 pain symptoms. The study found no significant differences in ACE2 promoter methylation between those with and without post-COVID pain, failing to support the DNA methylation hypothesis for post-COVID pain development.

This study characterizes new-onset chronic musculoskeletal pain in post-COVID patients and assesses overlap with fibromyalgia syndrome using ACR 2010 criteria. Thirteen of eighteen patients (72.2%) met fibromyalgia criteria, suggesting FMS may develop as a long-term sequela of viral infection.

This study examines the effects of CSD peptide LTI-2355 on myeloid cell function in lung tissue from PASC-F patients, demonstrating that LTI-2355 improves phagocytic activity and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokine production. However, this is an in vitro mechanistic study using donor lung explant tissue rather than a clinical trial with human subjects receiving treatment.

This is a preclinical study using hamster and cell line models to investigate the mechanisms of muscle fatigue in long COVID, showing SARS-CoV-2 causes myofiber atrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction without direct viral invasion. The study does not test a treatment intervention on patients; it is mechanistic research in animal and cell models.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing leukocyte telomere length (LTL) and cognitive function in 256 post-COVID-19 subjects versus uninfected controls using MoCA and MMSE scales. Found decreased LTL in post-COVID subjects but no significant association between telomere length and cognitive impairment.

This cross-sectional study examines autonomic dysfunction and cardio-respiratory fitness in 192 subjects with post-COVID syndrome, comparing symptomatic and asymptomatic groups. While the paper characterizes autonomic abnormalities and their association with exercise capacity, it is not a treatment trial—it is a descriptive observational study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This paper uses bioinformatics and machine learning to identify common genes (CR1, TAP2) and immune mechanisms shared between COVID-19 and Sjögren's syndrome keratoconjunctivitis sicca (SS-KCS). It is a secondary analysis of transcriptomic data without any treatment intervention or original patient cohort.

This study develops an analytical method to measure cortisol in small saliva samples from COVID-19 recovering patients treated with CNS-active drugs. While it confirms elevated cortisol in post-COVID patients compared to controls, it is a methodological/biomarker study without testing a treatment intervention—the psychotropic drugs were already being used by patients, not assigned as part of the study design.

This cross-sectional study uses near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) to measure local oxygenation and deoxygenation dynamics in 100 post-COVID syndrome patients versus 50 controls during light exercise. PCS patients showed decreased deoxygenation peaks and a subgroup demonstrated association between severe fatigue and restricted oxygenation dynamics, suggesting NIRS as a potential diagnostic tool for microcirculation deficits.

This cross-sectional study examined brain metabolic changes in 14 long COVID patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction using [18F]-FDG PET imaging. The research identified hypometabolism in specific brain regions but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely a neuroimaging characterization study and should be excluded from a treatment trials analysis.

This cross-sectional study examined personality traits and their association with neuropsychiatric symptoms in 93 post-COVID syndrome patients compared to matched controls using the Big Five Structure Inventory. The study found that post-COVID patients had lower emotional stability and that personality traits predicted depression and anxiety levels, but this is an observational characterization study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This paper applies natural language processing techniques (LDA and BERTopic) to analyze Italian-language narratives about long COVID (PASC) versus general COVID-19 writings. It is a methodological study of text mining approaches rather than a clinical trial or treatment evaluation, and should be excluded as a computational linguistics/review paper.

This study evaluated a 6-month neurorehabilitation intervention for cognitive symptoms (memory, attention, executive functioning) in long COVID patients at a Mexican rehabilitation institute. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in memory and executive functioning scores on standardized neuropsychological tests (Neuropsi and BANFE-III).

This study analyzes blood biomarkers in post-COVID-19 patients stratified by disease severity and lung imaging findings to identify predictors of pulmonary fibrosis. Patients with lung fibrotic changes showed elevated IL-1α and TGF-β but lower IFN-β levels, which were associated with increased risk of fibrosis-like lung changes.

This study evaluated whether a virtual-reality oculomotor test system (VR-OTS) can distinguish post-COVID syndrome patients from healthy controls using machine learning, extracting 95 features related to stereopsis, gaze direction, and pupil diameter. The VR-OTS achieved an AUROC of 0.73 with pupil diameter features as the best discriminator, suggesting potential value as a diagnostic biomarker for objective PCS assessment.

A cross-sectional study of 14 long COVID patients examining the relationship between cerebral glucose metabolism (via PET imaging) and cognitive function on the same day. The study found hypermetabolism in the cerebellum correlated with cognitive impairment but is not a treatment trial—it is a diagnostic/mechanistic study without intervention or control group comparison.

This cross-sectional study used proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to examine cortical GABA levels in long COVID patients compared to matched controls. The PASC group showed significantly lower GABA+/water levels that correlated with depression and poor sleep quality, suggesting cortical hyperexcitability as a mechanism underlying long COVID neurocognitive dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study examining relationships between sensitization symptoms, mood disorders, sleep quality, and quality of life in 146 long COVID patients with post-COVID pain. Found that sleep quality mediates the effects of sensitization and mood disorders on quality of life, but this is an observational assessment study without treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzed circulating monocytes in 131 acute COVID-19 patients and 6-month post-COVID patients to identify biomarkers predicting severity and long-term sequelae. The authors found persistent chromatin modifications and altered gene expression in post-COVID monocytes, with early monocyte characteristics at admission predicting ICU admission or death risk.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive abilities, psychological symptoms, and quality of life in 57 long COVID patients versus 29 controls. Results showed significant differences in memory tasks, verbal fluency, and emotional impact (anxiety, depression, fatigue, sleep quality) between groups, but this is a descriptive comparison study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study compares immune biomarkers and inflammatory signatures between ME/CFS patients, long COVID patients, and healthy controls in 190 participants. Results show both conditions display comparable immune dysfunction patterns with reduced lymphocytes/CD8+ T cells/NK cells and elevated proinflammatory cytokines, with no significant differences between ME/CFS and long COVID groups.

Pilot study comparing brain perfusion metrics (cerebral blood flow and oxygen extraction fraction) in 7 COVID-19 ICU survivors versus 19 healthy controls using advanced MRI techniques. Found elevated oxygen extraction and reduced blood flow in the frontal lobe of survivors, suggesting microvascular damage but providing no intervention or treatment outcomes.

This cross-sectional study of 996 long COVID patients examines the relationship between gender, hospitalization duration, and psychiatric symptom severity. The research found that females had higher levels of psychopathology, depression, anxiety, and psychotropic medication use compared to males, with notable gender-specific correlations between hospitalization duration and agitated depression severity.

This Mendelian Randomisation study examined the potential causal relationship between COVID-19 phenotypes and vascular dementia risk using genome-wide association summary data. The analysis found no significant associations between COVID-19 infection and vascular dementia risk, suggesting vascular dementia is not a long-term sequela of COVID-19.

This exploratory study compared brain MRI/PET imaging outcomes in long COVID patients at different time points (≤6 months vs >6 months post-infection) and between fatigued vs non-fatigued individuals. The study found structural differences in brain volumes (putamen, pallidum, thalamus, frontal areas) associated with time since infection and fatigue severity, but no differences in brain glucose metabolism.

This cross-sectional study characterizes plasma biomarkers and neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicle proteins in 24 COVID-19 recovering individuals, comparing those with and without self-reported neurological symptoms. While it identifies elevated neuroinflammatory markers and neuronal dysfunction proteins in long COVID patients, it is a biomarker characterization study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study compares serum samples from post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients with and without ME/CFS to healthy controls, examining effects on endothelial cell function and autoantibody profiles in vitro. The research is a mechanistic bench study examining disease pathophysiology rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This study investigates neuro-axonal damage and blood-brain barrier integrity in acute COVID-19 patients with severe neurological symptoms, comparing biomarker levels across disease severity groups and recovery. While the paper measures neurological damage during acute infection, it does not address long COVID and does not test any treatment intervention.

This study analyzes how SARS-CoV-2 infection alters cytokine and chemokine levels in cancer patients under active treatment, comparing infected and uninfected cancer patients to healthy controls. While it mentions long COVID in passing, the paper's primary focus is on cancer progression and immune response in COVID-infected cancer patients, not on long COVID as a condition or its treatment.

This pilot fMRI study examines neural activation patterns during the Stroop cognitive task in six severe COVID-19 survivors at 9 months post-infection compared to 24 controls. While task performance was largely normal, patients showed distinct neural activation profiles suggesting different resilience patterns in underlying cognitive networks, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed exercise capacity and quality of life in 30 elderly participants (age >65) after SARS-CoV-2 infection using 6-minute walking tests and WHO QoL-BREF questionnaires. Results showed COVID-19 negatively impacted aerobic capacity and quality of life, with men showing worse sequelae than women, suggesting potential lung damage and physical deconditioning post-infection.

This study uses a mouse model (K18-hACE2) to investigate mechanisms of persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection, examining elevated B1 receptor expression and inflammatory markers in brain tissue. While it establishes a relevant animal model for long COVID research, it does not test any intervention or treatment in affected subjects and is therefore excluded from the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This study uses machine learning models to predict post-COVID condition incidence in hospitalised cancer patients using data from a longitudinal cohort study with follow-ups at 6 and 12 months. While it identifies risk factors for long COVID, it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is purely predictive modeling on existing cohort data.

This study uses RNA-sequencing to compare transcriptomic profiles of small airway cell cultures from IPF patients and post-COVID fibrosis patients, identifying distinct molecular signatures and signaling pathways between the two conditions. The research is a basic science investigation of cellular mechanisms rather than a treatment trial or clinical intervention study.

This case-control study compares blood markers and neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles between long COVID patients with neurological symptoms, asymptomatic COVID-19 survivors, and healthy controls. The study identifies elevated inflammatory markers and neurodegeneration-associated proteins in long COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This single-cell RNA sequencing study characterizes transcriptomic immune dysregulation in convalescent COVID-19 patients without comorbidities, identifying HIF1A as a severity-sensitive immunological marker in circulating monocytes. The research provides molecular correlates of COVID-19 recovery but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Bioinformatic analysis of published transcriptomic datasets from COVID-19 patients to identify type I interferon dysregulation signatures in olfactory networks and their association with Alzheimer's disease pathology. No primary data collection or treatment intervention; secondary analysis of existing genomic datasets.

This study compares immune markers including B cell subsets and Th2 cytokines in 63 long COVID patients versus 47 healthy COVID-recovered controls. The findings show altered B cell dynamics in long COVID patients but do not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigates the relationship between long COVID symptoms, neurological manifestations (brain fog, concentration difficulties), and anxiety using data from the COVID-19 Health and Mental Health Survey. The research explores anxiety as a potential mediator of the association between long COVID and neurological symptoms.

This paper describes a clinical qualification protocol for identifying genomic influences in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and long COVID, highlighting overlapping genetic variants and neuro-autonomic mechanisms. The authors note that further characterization of long COVID natural history will be necessary before these genetic findings can be translated into therapies, indicating this is a methodological/protocol paper rather than a treatment trial.

This case-control study compares plasma protein profiles and immune markers in 51 long COVID patients with neurological symptoms (nLongC), 35 recovered COVID-19 patients, and 51 healthy controls. The findings show persistent elevation of IL-1β, IL-8, GFAP, and hemopexin in long COVID patients, with a panel of four proteins plus age, BMI, and APOE4 status achieving 81% diagnostic accuracy for neurological long COVID.

A monocentric cross-sectional study of 28 children and adolescents with post-COVID-19 condition investigating immune risk factors, particularly atopy and elevated IgE levels. Found that 93% had aeroallergen sensitization and elevated IgE/IgG3/IgG4 levels, with variable recovery trajectories ranging from 5 to 30 months.

This paper retrospectively reanalyzed cognitive function data from 40 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at baseline and 6 months post-infection, developing a novel Cerebroviz brain mapping tool to visualize cognitive domain deficits. While it documents cognitive recovery patterns, it is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data without testing any new intervention or treatment.

This paper develops a machine learning case definition for Long COVID using LASSO regression to identify which symptoms best distinguish Long COVID patients from recovered controls. It is excluded as a methodological/diagnostic study rather than a treatment trial, focusing on case identification rather than evaluating therapeutic interventions.

This study evaluates the reliability and minimal detectable change of the 2-minute marching test (2MMT) for assessing cardiovascular response in youth with post-COVID-19 condition, comparing it with the 6-minute walk test. The 2MMT demonstrates good reliability (ICC=0.78) for clinical assessment, but the study is a validation/measurement study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study assessed neuropsychological, psychiatric, neurological, and olfactory deficits in 45 long COVID patients 8 months post-discharge, stratified by initial infection severity. Results showed cognitive deficits across all domains with severity-dependent phenotypes, including greater memory impairment and anosognosia in severe cases, emotion recognition deficits in moderate cases, and higher psychological distress in mild cases.

This study objectively characterized sleep-wake disturbances in 31 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients with fatigue and excessive daytime sleepiness using polysomnography, actigraphy, and questionnaires. Key findings include moderate sleep apnea (35.5%), increased arousal index (77.4%), elevated inactivity index (96.6%), but limited objective sleepiness on MSLT, highlighting a complex sleep phenotype in long COVID.

This cross-sectional study examines whether neurodivergent traits and personality characteristics predict long-term COVID-19 symptoms in 267 healthcare workers. While the paper is about long COVID, it does not study a treatment or intervention—it only investigates predictive associations between psychological/neurodevelopmental traits and symptom duration.

This cross-sectional study assessed neurocognitive deficits in 100 long COVID patients from Partinico Hospital using a standardized screening protocol, examining cognitive domains and correlating findings with neuroimaging abnormalities. The research documents gender differences in cognitive symptoms and reports an association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and new-onset diabetes diagnosis.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive impairments, neuroanatomical changes, and new-onset diabetes in 245 post-COVID patients between April 2021 and August 2023, finding cognitive dysfunction in 87% of participants with associated glial alterations on MRI. The study highlights a significant association between cognitive decline and new-onset diabetes in post-COVID patients, with notable gender differences in psychiatric symptoms and neuroimaging abnormalities.

This study evaluates functional impairments in post-COVID-19 patients in Romania using the ClinFIT COVID-19 assessment instrument across acute, post-acute, and long-term phases. The paper is descriptive/observational (no intervention tested) and focuses on characterizing impairments rather than evaluating a treatment.

This study examined morphological changes in myocardial tissue from 38 PASC patients using endomyocardial biopsy, immunohistochemistry, and morphometric analysis compared to pre-pandemic controls. Findings showed increased CD68+ macrophages in PASC myocardium but no evidence of coronavirus-associated myocarditis.

This study developed machine learning algorithms to predict which post-acute COVID-19 patients with pulmonary fibrosis would benefit from corticosteroid treatment, using data from 281 patients evaluated at baseline and 3 months post-treatment. Decision tree, Random Forest, and AdaBoost algorithms achieved 70-74% accuracy in identifying treatment responders, enabling personalized treatment selection.

This cross-sectional study used functional MRI with a cognitive task (modified Stroop test) to compare brain activation patterns in 30 post-COVID fatigue patients versus 20 healthy controls. Patients with post-COVID fatigue showed significant activation differences in brain regions associated with information processing, particularly in the supramarginal gyri, posterior cingulate cortex, and cerebellum.

This paper uses wearable laser Doppler flowmetry to assess microcirculation changes in COVID-19 patients during recovery and compares them to healthy controls. The study demonstrates persistent microcirculatory dysfunction and reduced cutaneous perfusion in the post-COVID period, suggesting microvascular involvement in long COVID pathophysiology.

This case-control study investigates epigenetic alterations in DNA methylation at the UGT1A1 locus in COVID-19 patients with persistent anosmia (smell loss) versus those with normal smell. The findings show significantly lower methylation levels in the anosmia group and suggest methylation status could serve as a biomarker for olfactory dysfunction post-COVID-19.

A cross-sectional study comparing blood levels of hormones and growth factors between 49 patients recovered from severe COVID-19 and matched uninfected controls. The study identified persistent reductions in growth hormone, IGF-1, BDNF, and PDGF at 6 and 15 months post-recovery, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study evaluated the effects of slow-paced breathing on cardiorespiratory dynamics in 49 COVID-19 survivors using photoplethysmographic and respiratory signal analysis. The results show that diaphragmatic breathing significantly improved cardiorespiratory coupling and vagal activity, suggesting relaxation techniques may help manage persistent post-COVID symptoms.

This is a preclinical mouse model study (MHV-1) investigating long COVID-like kidney pathology and testing SPIKENET (SPK) as a potential therapeutic intervention. The study demonstrates SPK's ability to reverse pro-fibrotic gene expression patterns in infected mice, but provides no human clinical trial data or results in actual long COVID patients.

This retrospective study used cardiac MRI with T1 and T2 mapping to characterize late-stage myocardial tissue changes in 25 COVID-19 patients (36-565 days post-infection) compared to non-COVID myocarditis and healthy controls. COVID-19 myocarditis patients showed persistently elevated T1 values and subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement, indicating residual myocardial injury weeks to months after infection.

A pilot study measuring serum NGF and BDNF levels in adolescents with long-COVID-19 compared to controls and post-infected asymptomatic individuals. Findings suggest NGF and BDNF may serve as early biomarkers for COVID-19 morbidity, with elevated BDNF in symptomatic and future long-COVID girls.

This study develops and validates the Post-COVID Cognitive Impairment Scale, a new measurement instrument for assessing cognitive deficits in long COVID patients. While directly relevant to long COVID, it is a psychometric validation study without any treatment intervention or clinical trial design.

This paper develops a fractional-order mathematical model to examine the relationship between COVID-19 and stroke as a long-term side effect, using real data from the United Kingdom. The study uses computational modeling and sensitivity analysis to explore how screening rates and population fear affect stroke development in the post-COVID community, rather than testing an actual treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between pain-related genetic polymorphisms (OPRM1, COMT, BDNF, HTR1B) and the presence of post-COVID pain in 293 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors. The authors found no significant associations between any of the four SNPs and the development or phenotypic features of post-COVID pain.

This cross-sectional study assessed the relationship between self-reported long-COVID symptoms and reaction times using a web-based visual detection task in 362 participants. The study found that cognitive and physical symptoms were predictive of slower reaction times, suggesting attention deficit disorder in long-COVID patients, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This secondary analysis examines the association between ApoE ε4 genotype and long COVID symptomatology in 287 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors. The study found no significant differences in long COVID symptoms based on ApoE genotype, suggesting that genetic predisposition via this marker does not explain long COVID development.

Cross-sectional study examining whether ACE2 and TMPRSS2 gene polymorphisms are associated with long COVID symptoms in 293 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors. Found no significant association between the four SNPs assessed and post-COVID symptom development, despite previous links to COVID-19 severity.

This study evaluated cardio-pulmonary rehabilitation in 25 post-COVID patients, assessing physical capacity via CPET, spirometry, and DLCO before and after 23±5 rehabilitation sessions combining interval training and resistance exercises. After rehabilitation, VO2 max and maximal workload improved by 18% and 26% respectively, with exercise hyperventilation reduced by 10%, demonstrating rehabilitation benefits for recovery of physical capacity in moderate-to-severe COVID-19.

This study validates the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) in long-term care facility residents, assessing post-COVID burden and symptoms three months after acute infection. The cross-sectional assessment found 70.9% of residents reported at least one complaint, with breathlessness, fatigue, and cognitive problems being most prevalent, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared acoustic voice and speech characteristics between 64 post-COVID-19 subjects (8.7 months post-infection) and 70 controls using voice recordings analyzed with PRAAT software. The study found significant differences in voice quality parameters (jitter, shimmer, HNR) between groups and sex-based differences in frequency parameters, suggesting voice acoustic features could serve as biomarkers for long-COVID voice disorders.

This study evaluates the effects of a 12-week pulmonary rehabilitation program combining aerobic and resistance exercises in 33 post-COVID-19 patients. The intervention improved lung function, lung mechanics, and reduced pulmonary and systemic inflammatory markers.

Retrospective analysis of 154 COVID-19 survivors with acute respiratory failure, clustering participants by exercise test response using six-minute walking test (6MWT) metrics. Study identifies two clusters with distinct physiological responses to exercise but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study measuring inflammatory and angiogenic mediators (IL-6, IL-12, IL-17, MIP-1A, VEGF-A, MMP-9) in 45 long COVID patients with normal versus abnormal spirometry. Found differential expression of these biomarkers associated with abnormal pulmonary function, hypertension, prior pneumonia, and disease severity.

This paper develops an AI framework to predict burnout, long COVID, and extended sick leave in healthcare workers using machine learning models trained on occupational health data from 1,244 Romanian professionals. While it addresses long COVID as one of three outcomes, it is fundamentally a predictive modeling study rather than a clinical trial or treatment intervention study, making it ineligible for the meta-analysis pipeline.

This prospective cohort study identified risk factors for long COVID among symptomatic US adults testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 at CVS Pharmacies, developing a predictive model with good performance (c-statistic 0.79). The study does not test any treatment or intervention, only observes symptom patterns and develops a risk prediction model.

This longitudinal study validated the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) in 79 Italian hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessed at 12 and 26 weeks post-infection. The C19-YRS demonstrated construct validity and moderate responsiveness for monitoring persistent post-COVID symptoms including fatigue, breathlessness, anxiety, depression, and mobility limitations.

This cross-sectional pilot study assessed objective olfactory function using the Sniffin' Sticks test in 20 COVID-19 patients who had not self-reported olfactory dysfunction, approximately 131 days post-infection. The study found that 45% of participants showed objective olfactory reduction despite not reporting symptoms, demonstrating that objective testing methods detect dysfunction at higher rates than patient self-reports.

This study compares inflammatory biomarkers and psychological symptoms in long COVID patients (n=93) versus controls three months post-discharge. It found persistent systemic inflammation and increased risk of somatization, depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbances in long COVID patients, with ferritin correlated to sleep disorders.

This study validates the psychometric properties of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) as a measurement tool in COVID-19 survivors with long COVID symptoms, assessing 1,969 previously hospitalized patients. While the paper confirms HADS has good reliability and validity for measuring anxiety and depression in this population, it is a methodological validation study rather than a treatment trial and should be excluded as it does not evaluate any intervention or treatment outcome.

Cross-sectional study examining how immune-inflammatory biomarkers from acute COVID-19 infection and neurotoxic pathways predict quality of life and affective symptoms in 86 long COVID patients versus 39 controls. Findings show that 70% of variance in health-related quality of life is explained by depression, anxiety, fibromyalgia-fatigue, and neuroinflammatory markers, with the effects of acute infection severity mediated through neuro-immune and oxidative stress pathways.

This study compares dual-task performance (balance + cognitive task) in 31 post-acute severe COVID-19 patients versus 30 healthy controls using stabilometry and Timed Up and Go testing. Findings show post-COVID patients exhibit executive function deficits during dual-tasking, prioritizing motor tasks over cognitive ones, suggesting rehabilitation programs should incorporate dual-task training.

This study evaluated the effect of COVID-19 on static balance performance in 12 professional handball players (6 infected, 6 uninfected controls) using pre/post balance assessments. Infected athletes showed significant balance deterioration while controls did not, suggesting COVID-19 impacts motor control, but the study is observational and does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compares the intestinal microbiota composition of Brazilian post-COVID-19 patients (1-8 months post-infection) to controls, finding significant dysbiosis with alterations in bacterial genera. While the authors hypothesize that microbiota modulation could be therapeutic, the paper is observational without testing any intervention.

Cross-sectional network analysis study comparing neurobehavioral symptom patterns in 650 Spanish-speakers with COVID-19 history versus 443 non-COVID controls. Identifies headache, frustration, hearing problems, and tension as central symptoms in the COVID+ network but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study uses cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to characterize dyspnea patterns in 120 symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients. The study identifies distinct limitation patterns (cardiac, pulmonary, deconditioning, breathing dysfunction) to guide differential diagnosis but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

This study validates the psychometric properties of the Functional Impairment Checklist (FIC), a disease-specific outcome measure for long-COVID patients in a multicenter cohort of 1,969 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors. The FIC demonstrates good internal consistency and construct validity, with women and older patients reporting greater functional limitations than men and younger patients.

This comparative study evaluates the effects of a 4-week exercise rehabilitation program on 38 long COVID patients compared to 38 coronary artery disease and 38 fibromyalgia patients, using cardiopulmonary exercise tests, handgrip strength, and heart rate variability as outcome measures. Exercise training significantly improved cardiorespiratory and muscular parameters across all three groups, confirming the benefits of personalized exercise rehabilitation in long COVID without exertional symptom worsening.

This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of a 4-week inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program in 47 long COVID patients with symptoms persisting >6 months post-infection. Significant improvements were observed across multiple outcomes including 6-minute walking distance, quality of life, fatigue, dyspnea, and psychological measures, with no adverse events reported and persistent symptom count reduced from 6 to 3 per patient on average.

This cross-sectional study identified five symptom clusters in 506 long COVID patients using latent class analysis and examined associations between psychological factors (personality, alexithymia, PTSD) and symptom profiles. The research explores psychological correlates of long COVID symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study evaluates inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation in 150 patients recovering from acute COVID-19, measuring spirometric improvements through aerobic, strength, and endurance exercises. While it shows statistically significant improvements in lung function parameters, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than persistent long COVID symptoms occurring weeks to months after infection.

This cross-sectional study evaluated functional capacity and pulmonary function in 60 post-COVID syndrome patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing, spirometry, impulse oscillometry, and lung ultrasound. The study found impaired oxygen consumption (VO2peak 18.4 mL/kg/min) correlated with age, BMI, and lung imaging abnormalities, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This study measures functional autoantibodies against G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCR-AAbs) and retinal microcirculation in 42 long COVID patients versus 6 controls using OCT-angiography. It reports impaired retinal vessel density in long COVID patients, particularly in those with GPCR-AAbs, suggesting a potential pathophysiological mechanism but no treatment intervention is tested.

This study evaluates Epipharyngeal Abrasive Therapy (EAT) as a treatment for chronic epipharyngitis, which the authors propose is linked to long COVID and other systemic inflammatory conditions. The results show that EAT significantly reduced IL-6 mRNA expression and TNFα in treated patients compared to untreated controls, suggesting an anti-inflammatory mechanism that may improve systemic symptoms in long COVID.

This paper uses network pharmacology and pharmacodynamics to analyze the molecular mechanism of NRICM101 (a traditional Chinese medicine formula) for COVID-19 and long COVID symptom treatment. It is a mechanistic/bioinformatics study with cell culture experiments, not a clinical trial or human treatment study, making it ineligible for the intervention trial database.

This cross-sectional study of 305 children who recovered from acute COVID-19 develops machine learning models to predict long COVID development using demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters. Among 265 children, 52% developed long COVID; the models identified obesity, allergic disorders, vitamin D deficiency, fever, symptom severity, and laboratory abnormalities (thrombocytosis, neutrophilia, prothrombin time alterations) as significant predictors.

This study develops and validates the Memorial Symptom Assessment Scale-Long COVID (MSAS-LC), a 45-item symptom assessment tool designed to measure symptom prevalence, frequency, severity, and distress in long COVID patients. Using a cross-sectional design with 261 participants (129 with long COVID, 131 controls), the authors demonstrate that the MSAS-LC can effectively differentiate long COVID symptom burden across multiple organ systems.

This study compares biological age acceleration and epigenetic markers (CpG methylation, ACE2 expression) between 117 post-COVID-19 survivors and 144 non-infected controls. The findings show accelerated biological aging in post-COVID patients (+10.45 years) but this is an observational biomarker study with no intervention or treatment tested.

This cross-sectional study examined the impact of post-COVID olfactory dysfunction (anosmia) on sexual function and orgasmic intensity in 138 sexually active participants. While it documents a long COVID symptom's effect on sexual wellbeing, it does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it an observational assessment rather than a treatment trial.

This prospective cross-sectional study investigates the association between chronic fatigue and retinal microcirculation in 173 post-COVID patients compared to 28 controls using OCT angiography. The study identifies impaired retinal vessel density as a potential objective biomarker for chronic fatigue in PCS, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper is a molecular biology study investigating potential mechanisms by which SARS-CoV-2 infection could cause long-lasting neuropsychiatric symptoms through alterations of the gut-brain axis, specifically examining ACE2 and neurotransmitter metabolism in infected intestinal cells. It presents bioinformatics analysis and RNA-seq data from infected organoids but does not test any treatment or intervention.

This is a mechanistic study using hACE2 mice to investigate SARS-CoV-2 persistence in adipose tissue and its role in long-term health complications. The research examines sex differences in viral loads and immune responses but does not study any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.

This proteomic study analyzed lymphocytes from COVID-19 and long-COVID patients to identify molecular mechanisms and biomarkers distinguishing the two conditions. The work identified iron dyshomeostasis and 5-lipoxygenase activation as key features but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzes blood coagulation, platelet aggregation, and plasma proteomics in AMI patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection, comparing them to healthy controls. The study identifies distinct hemostatic and proteomic signatures in post-COVID AMI patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein interacts with human nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) and exploring varenicline as a potential therapeutic agent. The paper is mechanistic research rather than a clinical trial—it uses electrophysiology in Xenopus oocytes to evaluate receptor binding, not patient treatment data.

Immunohistochemical analysis of lung tissue from COVID-19 decedents examining TGF-β signaling pathways and fibrosis markers compared to H1N1 and control groups. The study identifies dysregulated biomarkers associated with pulmonary fibrosis development and suggests TGF-β inhibitors as a potential preventive therapy for post-COVID pulmonary complications.

This study analyzes catalase activity of IgG antibodies from COVID-19 recovered patients, vaccine recipients, and controls. While it documents a biological finding related to post-COVID autoimmunity, it is a basic science characterization study with no treatment intervention or clinical outcomes.

This mouse model study investigates whether immune responses against SARS-CoV-2 protein epitopes can cause organ damage, a potential mechanism in long COVID development. The study found no significant inflammation or pathology in heart or other organs following immunization with viral peptides in autoimmune-susceptible mice.

This study evaluates a panel of serum biomarkers (cytokines and adipokines) in 108 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to assess disease severity, survival, and prediction of post-COVID lung sequelae. The authors identify inflammatory markers associated with disease progression and medium-term complications but do not test any treatment intervention.

This paper investigates the molecular mechanisms of endothelial damage in SARS-CoV-2 infection, specifically examining VE-cadherin cleavage by ACE2 as a potential mechanism underlying long COVID vascular complications. The authors present in vitro evidence and blood biomarker data from COVID-19 patients, but do not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares 16 long COVID patients with 13 non-long COVID controls to identify predictive factors and ACE-2 gene polymorphisms associated with long COVID susceptibility. Key findings include fatigue, myalgia, headache, and the A allele of rs2106806 as significant risk factors for developing long COVID.

This study investigates whether antioxidant genetic variants (SOD2, GPX1, GPX3, Nrf2) modify cardiac outcomes in 174 convalescent COVID-19 patients using echocardiography and genetic polymorphism analysis. It is a cross-sectional genetic association study, not a treatment trial, and represents a secondary analysis of cardiac imaging and biomarker data rather than evaluation of an intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined red blood cell aggregation in 52 COVID-19 pneumonia patients using dextran solutions to isolate cellular factors, finding that aggregates formed are denser and more compact. While the findings suggest potential mechanisms for post-COVID thrombotic complications, this is a mechanistic/pathophysiology study without treatment or intervention evaluation.

This computational study uses molecular docking and dynamics simulations to explore whether ivermectin can prevent SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binding to fibrinogen and reduce microclot formation in long COVID. The authors present in silico results suggesting ivermectin may bind to fibrinogen but explicitly state that additional in vitro and in vivo validation studies are needed, making this a methods/computational proposal rather than an empirical treatment evaluation.

This paper presents a computational pharmacogenomic and network pharmacology analysis of ivermectin combined with six antioxidants (EGCG, curcumin, sesamin, anthocyanins, quercetin, NAC) for long COVID treatment. The study identifies 12 interacting genes and associated pathways but explicitly states that further clinical trials are needed—it is a theoretical/in silico analysis, not an empirical treatment study.

Cross-sectional study comparing inflammatory and prothrombotic biomarkers (IL-6, vWF, D-Dimer, etc.) in recovered COVID-19 patients with and without long COVID symptoms. Found elevated immunothrombotic markers in long COVID patients, particularly those with metabolic syndrome, suggesting biomarker-based risk stratification.

This study compares muscle mitochondrial function and morphology in post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients versus healthy controls and chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) patients using high-resolution respirometry and electron microscopy. The findings show reduced complex I OXPHOS capacity in PCS and distinct morphological differences between PCS and CFS, suggesting virus-induced mitochondrial alterations in post-COVID patients.

This study uses microfluidic isolation to identify neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles and characterize neurological proteins in long COVID patients with cognitive complaints. The analysis reveals 11 proteins elevated and 2 decreased in long COVID, with some overlap in protein expression patterns with Alzheimer's disease and HIV infection, but this is a biomarker characterization study without intervention or treatment testing.

This cross-sectional study measures biological aging markers (DNA methylation age, telomere length) and physiological parameters in pauci- and asymptomatic COVID-19 healthcare workers one year post-infection. While it investigates long-term effects of COVID-19, it does not study long COVID (which involves persistent symptomatic illness) nor does it test any intervention or treatment.

This paper investigates SARS-CoV-2's ability to infect peripheral sensory and autonomic neurons and its role in CNS invasion using animal models and primary neuronal cultures. It provides mechanistic insights into neurological symptoms in COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between VEGF genetic polymorphisms (VEGF-936C/T, VEGF-634G/C, VEGF-2578C/A) and cardiac dysfunction in 67 long COVID patients, with assessments at baseline and six months. The study found that the VEGF-936C/T genotype was associated with changes in ejection fraction and predictive of augmentation index, suggesting genetic polymorphisms may influence cardiovascular outcomes in long COVID.

This is a computational drug-repurposing study that constructs a comorbidity network between COVID-19 and CNS disorders to identify potential drug candidates through network analysis and molecular dynamics simulations. It proposes pregnenolone and BRD-K87426499 as candidates but does not conduct any clinical trial or empirical treatment evaluation in patients.

This study investigates the mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein induces tau pathological changes in neurons and demonstrates that SUMO2 can counteract these effects. The work uses in vitro and in vivo models to elucidate a potential neurotoxic pathway relevant to COVID-19 neurological sequelae, rather than testing a therapeutic intervention in patients.

This study analyzes IgG N-glycome alterations in post-COVID-19 and post-vaccination patients using HILIC-UPLC with mass spectrometry. The findings show higher sialylation and afucosylation in post-COVID patients, further modified by vaccination in those previously infected, but this is an observational biomarker study with no intervention evaluation.

This cross-sectional study examined clinical, immunological, and metabolomic profiles in 51 COVID-19 survivors 7-19 months post-infection to identify risk factors for persistent post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). Patients with PACS showed elevated levels of specific immune markers (LDGs, IL-8) and metabolites (pyruvate, pseudouridine, cystine) at both acute infection and follow-up, suggesting these biomarkers could help predict who develops long COVID.

This study investigates associations between FAS and FASL gene polymorphisms, gene expression levels, and COVID-19 severity and long COVID occurrence in 116 severe, 254 non-severe COVID-19 patients, and 196 long COVID vs 67 non-long COVID individuals. The AA genotype of FAS rs1800682 and TT genotype of FASL rs763110 were associated with increased gene expression and higher inflammatory markers (IFN-γ), suggesting genetic factors influence susceptibility to long COVID through enhanced Fas-mediated T-cell death and inflammation.

This study investigates the role of mast cell carboxypeptidase A3 (CPA3) in pulmonary fibrosis development following COVID-19 infection. It demonstrates that increased CPA3+ mast cells correlate with fibrotic tissue development, but this is a mechanistic/pathophysiology study without any treatment intervention or clinical trial design.

This retrospective cohort study identifies serum autoantibody biomarkers (PITX2 and FBXO2) associated with long COVID through protein array screening and validation. The study distinguishes long COVID patients from non-PASC convalescents and healthy controls but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines genetic variants in lung function and interstitial lung disease genes and their association with severe COVID-19 outcomes and post-COVID-19 pulmonary function. It is an observational genetic association study without any treatment intervention, thus excluded from the trial screening pipeline.

This study evaluates polymerized type I collagen (PTIC) as a treatment for symptomatic COVID-19 outpatients, examining its mechanism through LAIR-1 receptor engagement and its effect on immune markers and long COVID symptoms. The treatment downregulated STAT-1 phosphorylation and inflammatory cytokines in monocytes, with improvements in dyspnea, chest pain, cough, and chronic fatigue in both acute and long-term phases of infection.

This study investigates the relationship between DNA methylation of the ACE2 promoter and five COVID-19-related genetic polymorphisms in 279 post-COVID-19 survivors. The analysis found no significant associations between genetic genotypes and ACE2 promoter methylation levels in this cohort.

This study compares mitochondrial function and mtDNA integrity in CD14++ monocytes from 14 long COVID patients with cardiovascular symptoms versus 10 age-matched controls. It is a mechanistic biomarker study investigating pathophysiology rather than testing a treatment intervention.

In vitro study using human brain microvascular endothelial cells to investigate SARS-CoV-2 replication and its effects on blood-brain barrier integrity via the ACE2/kallikrein-kinin system. Demonstrates a potential mechanism linking viral infection to BBB disruption and neurological long COVID symptoms, but does not test any treatment intervention.

This systems biology study uses genome-wide metabolic modeling to identify shared metabolic dysfunctions in ME/CFS and Long COVID muscle tissue, proposing LOLA (L-ornithine and L-aspartate) supplementation as a potential treatment candidate for future clinical trials. The work is computational/in silico analysis without any human subject intervention or clinical trial results.

This study compares DNA methylation patterns in peripheral blood from ME/CFS and Long COVID patients versus healthy controls using RRBS sequencing. While it identifies distinct epigenetic differences between the disease cohorts and controls, it is an observational biomarker study without any intervention, treatment, or therapeutic evaluation.

In vitro study demonstrating that cytokines (TNFα + IFNγ) secreted by SARS-CoV-2 S1-activated macrophages induce endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) in HUVECs, a mechanism implicated in long COVID microvascular damage. Baricitinib and infliximab successfully prevent or reverse EndMT by targeting JAK-STAT and TNFα pathways, respectively.

This is an in silico bioinformatic analysis of an SNP (rs9367106) associated with post-COVID condition, exploring how the risk allele alters molecular pathways and gene expression in lung and brain tissues. The paper does not study a treatment intervention, test therapeutic approaches, or involve any clinical or experimental data—it is purely a computational/theoretical analysis of genetic mechanisms.

This study investigates cytokine and immune mediator profiles in long COVID patients compared to healthy post-pandemic and pre-pandemic controls using multiplex analysis of 47 immune mediators. While it identifies distinct cytokine dysregulation patterns in long COVID (elevated IL-7, IL-8, IL-17F, IL-18 and decreased IL-4, IL-13, IL-22), it is observational research examining biomarkers rather than evaluating any treatment or intervention.

This genome-wide association study identifies genetic variants associated with long COVID using patient-reported symptoms from a 1-year cohort of 2,411 COVID-19 patients. The research maps protein-coding genes related to immune and nervous system dysfunction but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigates functional autoantibodies targeting G-protein-coupled receptors in 194 long-COVID patients and their association with specific clinical phenotypes. The findings show that certain GPCR-fAAbs are associated with distinct long-COVID symptoms, particularly the combination of M2- and β2-fAAbs with fatigue/PEM and cognitive dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between insomnia/depression and cognitive impairments, white matter changes, and serum biomarkers in 76 long COVID patients and 22 controls. Finds demyelination in specific brain regions correlates with insomnia and depression severity, with elevated myelin-specific autoantibodies in the insomnia group.

This study measures peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) mitochondrial respiration in COVID-19 patients and correlates these measurements with mortality and long COVID severity at three years post-hospitalization. The research identifies impaired mitochondrial respiration as a potential biomarker associated with COVID severity and long COVID symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined T cell dynamics and immune responses in 231 participants across acute COVID-19, convalescent, long COVID, and healthy control groups using flow cytometry and TREC assessment. The findings reveal distinct immune dysregulation in long COVID patients, including increased naïve CTLs, Th2 polarization, and reduced effector memory cells, suggesting ongoing immune dysfunction possibly driven by persistent antigen exposure or autoimmune mechanisms.

This is a preclinical mechanistic study in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice investigating how SARS-CoV-2 spike protein S1 induces ferroptosis-related alterations in brain regions relevant to post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms. The study does not test any treatment intervention on long COVID patients—it is an exploratory animal model study examining biological pathways, not a clinical or observational trial.

This study evaluates thermal nociception and inflammatory biomarkers in a female mouse model of post-COVID-19 condition following Omicron variant infection. The results showed only a trend toward lower heat nociceptive thresholds and slight systemic inflammation, with no significant alterations in neural inflammatory markers, suggesting the animal model does not fully reproduce the pain syndromes observed in human long COVID patients.

This pilot study evaluated cardiac and hepatic abnormalities in 97 patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (3-11 weeks post-infection) using echocardiography and liver elastography. Approximately one-third of patients showed pulmonary hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, increased liver stiffness and steatosis, with more severe findings in those with prior pulmonary injury.

This cross-sectional study examined 32 non-hospitalized post-COVID patients to identify cardiopulmonary causes of persistent dyspnea and fatigue through clinical examination, echocardiography, and exercise testing. The study identified chronotropic incompetence in 4 patients (12.5%) but did not test or evaluate any intervention—it was purely diagnostic/observational in nature.

This study evaluated a stepwise diagnostic approach for long COVID patients with cardiopulmonary symptoms, examining 231 reconvalescent COVID-19 patients to distinguish between actual organ damage and functional complaints. About 34.6% had suspicious findings on initial screening, with 44.4% of further-tested patients showing pathological findings on cardiopulmonary exercise testing and cardiac MRI, while others had functional long COVID without organ damage.

This cross-sectional study investigates the relationship between pain extent and sensory, cognitive, and psychological variables in 146 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain. The analysis found that pain extent was not significantly associated with sensitization, cognitive impairment, or psychological distress, though females reported higher pain intensity and anxiety than males.

Retrospective study comparing cardiopulmonary exercise testing and oxidative stress markers in COVID-19 ICU survivors, mild long COVID patients, and obese controls. While it documents exercise limitation in long COVID, it is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study characterizes brain fog in 108 long COVID patients through questionnaires, cognitive assessments, and physical performance tests. While providing valuable clinical insights into brain fog as a symptom cluster linked to fatigue, dizziness, and myalgia, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective analysis of 39 male long COVID patients examining the prevalence of late-onset hypogonadism (LOH) and its association with clinical symptoms. The study found that 48.7% of male patients met LOH criteria and that low testosterone correlated with increased fatigue, anxiety, cough, and hair loss, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This study objectively assessed physical activity patterns and sedentary behavior in 37 patients 3-6 months after COVID-19 hospitalization.
