Patients exhibited high levels of sedentary time (9.8 h/day) and moderate physical activity levels, with no significant differences across patient or disease severity subgroups.

This cross-sectional study examined vascular endothelium dysfunction in 22 frail elderly patients recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia (84+ days post-hospitalization) using passive leg movement testing, compared to matched controls. Results show significantly altered blood velocity and femoral blood flow in COVID-19 patients, suggesting vascular dysfunction may contribute to long COVID symptoms including fatigue and exercise intolerance.

This study examined 154 long COVID patients enrolled in a 7-week rehabilitation program, investigating how post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) and breathlessness interact to affect fatigue severity. Results showed a significant interaction between PTSS and breathlessness in predicting fatigue, with improvements in PTSS associated with fatigue improvement, supporting a biopsychosocial approach to long COVID rehabilitation.

This study compares immunological profiles across children with acute COVID-19, recovered from COVID-19, and with Long COVID, examining cytokine levels and immune cell subsets. The findings suggest Long COVID patients have impaired adaptive immune responses with reduced regulatory T cells and altered B cell compartments, but the study is observational without any intervention or treatment.

This study validates the hyperventilation provocation test (HPTest) and PETCO2 kinetics as a diagnostic tool for idiopathic hyperventilation syndrome in long-COVID patients. While it identifies a diagnostic threshold with high sensitivity/specificity, it is a diagnostic validation study, not a treatment intervention trial, and does not meet inclusion criteria for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study compared endothelial injury markers (CRP, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, E-selectin, syndecan-1) in COVID-19 convalescents versus healthy controls at least 6 months post-infection. The authors found only slight evidence of endothelial dysfunction in generally healthy convalescents without comorbidities.

Pilot study validating a free mobile application (RUNZI®) to measure aerobic capacity and endurance in post-COVID-19 patients using the 6-Minute Walking Test. The app showed excellent correlation with conventional 6MWT but no treatment intervention was tested; this is a diagnostic/measurement validation study only.

This study evaluated a 6-week multidisciplinary rehabilitation program (physical training, education, psychotherapy) in 97 long COVID-19 patients. The program significantly improved body composition, dyspnea, fatigue, and physical capacity, with no control group.

This cross-sectional study examined 86 long COVID patients and 39 healthy controls to identify biomarkers and immune pathways predicting chronic fatigue, depression, and anxiety symptoms. Results showed that 34.9% of patients had elevated neurotoxicity markers, with immune-inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways explaining 61.6% of symptom variance.

Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial examining minimal clinically important differences (MCID) in inspiratory muscle function variables after an 8-week respiratory muscle training program in long COVID patients. The study establishes MCID thresholds for MIP and IME and demonstrates that MIP has the best discriminative ability for assessing training efficacy.

This cross-sectional study compared oxidative stress biomarkers and mitochondrial regulatory proteins in post-COVID patients with and without long-term pulmonary complications. The study found elevated mitochondrial biomarkers (PINK1, DNM1L, MFN2) and inflammatory cytokines in patients with pulmonary sequelae, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study used cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to profile elite and recreational athletes with post-exertional malaise (PEM) after COVID-19 infection. The study found that most athletes with PEM did not meet ESC criteria for adequate cardiopulmonary response, with perturbed ventilation/CO2 ratio and O2 pulse plateauing being key markers of exercise limitation, but it is a diagnostic/assessment study with no treatment intervention.

This study analyzed electronic health records from 92,301 COVID-19 patients to identify predictive factors for PASC diagnoses using a Super Learner algorithm. The researchers developed a composite risk score with moderate discriminatory ability (AUC 0.66) to identify individuals at higher risk for long COVID, but the study does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares gait and functional mobility (Timed-Up and Go test) between 15 COVID-19 hospitalized patients and 15 healthy controls using inertial motion sensors. COVID-19 survivors showed significantly impaired mobility with 46% longer task completion time, reduced walking speed, and altered gait kinematics despite at least 8 weeks post-discharge recovery.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive performance in 25 post-COVID depression (PCD) patients compared to recovered COVID-19 controls and non-infected controls using neuropsychological testing. PCD patients showed gender-dependent cognitive impairment in memory, processing speed, and attention, but the study does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

This study uses machine learning on German primary care electronic medical records to predict which COVID-19 patients will develop long COVID based on pre-infection medical history and demographics. It is a retrospective analysis of existing data without any treatment intervention, focusing on risk factor identification rather than treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study measured serum NGAL levels in 146 COVID-19 patients three months post-infection to identify associations with disease severity and post-COVID symptoms. The authors found elevated NGAL levels associated with acute disease severity, prolonged dyspnea, and metabolic dysfunction, suggesting immune dysregulation persists in post-COVID syndrome.

This study uses quantitative muscle MRI (qMRI) to evaluate and characterize muscle involvement in various neuromuscular disorders, including post-COVID-19 myalgia, comparing findings across dystrophic, inflammatory, and metabolic myopathies versus healthy controls. qMRI metrics were found to correlate with clinical assessments and show distinct involvement patterns across different disease types, supporting their potential for monitoring neuromuscular conditions.

This study analyzes cytokine profiles in 294 acute COVID-19 and post-COVID patients to identify immune biomarkers associated with disease severity and post-COVID complications. It identifies distinct cytokine signatures that correlate with complications like hypertension and diabetes but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 144 post-COVID patients examining the relationship between hand grip strength and symptom severity, with 78 meeting ME/CFS criteria. Findings show impaired grip strength correlates with disability and physical dysfunction, particularly in ME/CFS patients, suggesting a common mechanism for muscle fatigue in this subtype.

This study measured aminothiol concentrations (cysteine, homocysteine, glutathione) in blood plasma of 212 COVID-19 convalescents using HPLC, stratified by sex, time since infection, and initial severity. While it addresses post-COVID pathophysiology and CVD risk factors, it is a descriptive biomarker study with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the intervention trials pipeline.

This cross-sectional study compared organ-dysfunction biomarkers (Lp-PLA2, S100, NGAL, NCAM-1, and others) in 215 mild-to-moderate COVID-19 convalescents versus 79 healthy controls at least 6 months post-infection. The study found lower Lp-PLA2 and NCAM-1 but elevated S100 in convalescents, suggesting low risk of lung fibrosis or chronic kidney disease, and no intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study compares cardiorespiratory function and exercise capacity in 42 long COVID patients versus 10 healthy controls using echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. The study identifies associations between impaired left and right ventricular performance and reduced exercise tolerance, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared brain myelination using MRI in 25 post-COVID depression patients versus 38 COVID-recovered controls without depression at ~13.5 months post-infection. The study identified extensive demyelination in white and grey matter structures in depressed patients, with inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus demyelination as a key biomarker for post-COVID depression.

Prospective controlled study comparing metabolic inflammation, long COVID, and systemic lupus erythematosus across 272 adults with varying BMI to identify differential diagnostic tools and inflammatory markers. Findings show BMI-dependent effects on inflammatory variables and mental health quality of life, but the study is observational/cross-sectional without testing any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzes blood samples from 97 post-COVID syndrome patients to investigate hypercoagulability and endothelial dysfunction through thrombin generation and von Willebrand factor/ADAMTS13 measurements. The study found elevated thrombin production and abnormal coagulation markers in a subset of patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares brain MRI findings between 23 post-COVID patients and 20 controls, using vessel wall imaging (VWI) and complementary MRI methods to assess neurological changes. The authors identified several radiological abnormalities in post-COVID patients including white matter changes, vessel thickening, and hippocampal/cortical atrophy, but this is a diagnostic imaging study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study examines reduced salivary gustin and statherin levels in long COVID patients with impaired taste dysfunction, comparing unstimulated whole saliva samples from long COVID cohort to pre-2019 controls. The research identifies salivary gustin as a potential biomarker for taste impairment but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study from the Nautilus Project examines personality traits and sleep quality in 599 post-COVID patients versus healthy controls, finding that neuroticism correlates with poor sleep quality more strongly in PCC patients. However, this is a secondary analysis of data from existing clinical trials (NCT05307549 and NCT05307575) rather than a primary treatment trial, and it does not test or evaluate an intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines the immunocytological profile of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid in 58 post-COVID patients with new-onset interstitial lung disease to identify biomarkers predictive of persistent lung disease. The authors found that elevated neutrophil counts, Th17 cell markers, and IL-8 levels are associated with worse prognosis in persistent PCS.

An exploratory pre-post study of 17 women with long COVID evaluated the effects of a 12-week non-aerobic motor control exercise program on body composition and fatigue. The intervention significantly reduced body fat and fatigue, improved pain perception, and increased physical activity, supporting structured exercise as part of long COVID rehabilitation.

This case-control study compares serum spike protein levels in 72 ME/CFS patients, 49 PCS patients without ME/CFS, and 69 controls (both pre-pandemic and post-COVID recovered) 4-31 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study evaluates immunoglobulin depletion as a potential treatment in 22 patients and finds that while spike protein is detectable in some patients, it does not correlate with ME/CFS severity or functional disability.

An 8-week unsupervised pulmonary rehabilitation program for 20 COVID-19 recovering patients, evaluating changes in cardiopulmonary function, exercise capacity, and body composition. The program significantly improved hemodynamic parameters, oxygen saturation, 6-minute walk distance, VO2 uptake, body composition, and sleep quality.

This economic modeling study estimates the workplace burden of COVID-19 including long COVID cases in the US and evaluates the health and economic benefits of workplace COVID-19 vaccination programs. While it addresses long COVID as a cost component in disease burden calculations, it is not a treatment trial but rather a health economic analysis of vaccination as a prevention strategy.

This study used machine learning algorithms to predict rehabilitation outcomes in 189 convalescent COVID-19 patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, with 6-minute walking test performance as the primary outcome. A random forest model achieved 83.7% accuracy in predicting three classes of rehabilitation improvement (low, medium, high).

This study compared pulmonary and cardiac function in patients with post-mild COVID-19 dyspnea to those with moderate/severe COVID-19 and unexplained dyspnea using exercise testing and imaging. The findings show that mild post-COVID dyspnea patients had normal cardiopulmonary exercise test results similar to controls, suggesting mechanisms other than physiologic limitation.

Cross-sectional assessment of 1,588 post-COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between persistent symptoms and suicide risk using standardized psychiatric interviews. Found that greater physical complaints and psychopathology during post-COVID syndrome were associated with elevated suicide risk, with psychotherapy suggested as a potential risk reduction strategy.

This study evaluated clinical features and paraclinical findings in 106 post-COVID-19 patients with pneumonia, with 26 patients enrolled in a pulmonary rehabilitation program. After 2 weeks of rehabilitation, approximately 50% of patients showed improvement in instrumental activities of daily living (eating, washing, dressing), demonstrating the impact of structured rehabilitation on functional recovery in long COVID patients.

This study evaluated a 14-day complex rehabilitation program in 39 post-COVID-19 patients, measuring clinical symptoms, laboratory biomarkers, and gut microbiota composition before and after the intervention. The program improved respiratory function and mood, though certain inflammatory markers and gut dysbiosis remained abnormal compared to healthy controls, suggesting personalized rehabilitation approaches may be needed.

This study investigates sleep patterns in pediatric post-COVID-19 patients using EEG recordings and parent-reported sleep quality questionnaires. The analysis focuses on sleep spindles in NREM2 sleep, comparing recordings within three months after infection to pre-infection baseline data; preliminary findings suggest increased slow spindle components in right-frontal leads.

A genetic association study examining SNP variants linked to COVID-19 outcomes and their association with neurological complications and long-term post-COVID symptoms in young adults. The study is observational (cross-sectional) and does not test any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the treatment trial screening pipeline.

This cross-sectional study investigates biological predictors and risk factors in post-COVID-19 syndrome among asthmatic patients with various comorbidities. The findings show elevated serum glucose, lactate dehydrogenase, and C-reactive protein in moderate-to-severe COVID-19 cases, with ALT activity and age identified as key variables distinguishing comorbidity profiles.

This cross-sectional study investigated associations between vitamin D receptor (VDR) genetic variants (ApaI, FokI, TaqI) and COVID-19 severity and long-COVID symptoms in 100 Jordanian patients. The study found significant associations between VDR TaqI polymorphisms and persistent fatigue, muscle pain, and shortness of breath lasting >4 weeks post-infection, but no intervention was tested.

This study examines SARS-CoV-2 presence in endothelial tissue and alterations in PROS1 plasma levels in COVID-19 patients with coagulopathies, comparing infected and non-infected cohorts. While mechanistic research relevant to long COVID complications, this is a descriptive pathophysiology study examining biomarkers rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study measured lung gas transfer (DLNO-DLCO) in 118 post-COVID-19 patients (4.6 months post-infection) and 28 healthy controls to characterize alveolo-capillary gas exchange disturbances. Patients across all severity groups showed impaired pulmonary diffusion capacity, reduced membrane conductance, and abnormal vascular capacitance, indicating persistent lung dysfunction in long COVID.

This study analyzes whole-genome sequencing data from 153 patients with persistent COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction to identify genetic factors associated with olfactory performance. The research found that ACE2 gene variants correlate with worse olfactory function, while IFI44 and NDUFAF4 variants correlate with better function, suggesting host genetic factors influence post-COVID olfactory dysfunction heterogeneity.

This study evaluates laboratory diagnostic tests (complete blood count, ESR, biochemical markers, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio) in 182 patients with COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCI) to compare diagnostic performance and identify risk factors. The study does not test any intervention or treatment, making it an observational diagnostic study rather than a treatment trial.

This study evaluated diaphragm muscle function in 46 post-COVID-19 patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation using ultrasonography and functional assessments. While it identified significant diaphragm atrophy (69.5%) and paralysis (6.5%) associated with exercise intolerance, it is a descriptive cross-sectional study without an intervention or control group, making it observational rather than a treatment trial.

This cross-sectional study assessed olfactory and taste dysfunction in 81 post-COVID patients using standardized tests (Sniffin' Sticks and Taste Strip). The results showed that post-COVID olfactory dysfunction was predominantly peripheral rather than central, but the paper describes the problem rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This study compared cognitive function (verbal working memory, divided attention, response inhibition) in 107 young adults across three groups: COVID-19-negative controls, COVID-19-recovered without PCC, and those with Post COVID-19 Condition. The PCC group showed significantly impaired cognitive performance and increased reaction times, indicating long-lasting cognitive slowing and dysfunction two years post-infection.

In vitro study using COVID-19 pseudovirus-infected cell model to simulate long COVID pathology, demonstrating ferrous ion accumulation and mitochondrial dysfunction. Tests nutritional interventions (lactoferrin, Q10, Echinacea purpurea extract) to reduce iron accumulation and oxidative stress in infected cells.

This paper proposes a path module correlation coefficient to analyze the correlation between SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID symptom manifestation using statistical analysis of gene networks. It identifies potential COVID-related genes like CTSC that may induce long-COVID symptoms but does not study any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between different levels and domains of physical activity and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, stress) in individuals who recovered from COVID-19. While the paper touches on post-COVID recovery, it is primarily an observational assessment of PA-mental health associations rather than a treatment trial—participants' activity levels were measured, not assigned.

This ex vivo study evaluates the effects of fucoidan, a marine polysaccharide with anti-inflammatory and immune-enhancing properties, on mitochondrial membrane potential in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from COVID-19 patients and recovered subjects. Findings show that SARS-CoV-2 infection induces mitochondrial dysfunction persisting 11 months post-infection, and fucoidan treatment promotes recovery of mitochondrial membrane potential in recovered subjects, suggesting potential therapeutic value for long-term COVID-19 sequelae.

This paper develops a qualitative phenomenological mathematical model exploring how vitamin D supplementation and degradation affect innate immune system response to SARS-CoV-2. The study identifies hysteretic phenomena when vitamin D influx is too low as potentially related to long COVID onset, but conducts no empirical treatment study or clinical trial.

This study compares cardiac autonomic function via heart rate variability (HRV) in 37 COVID-19 recovered individuals versus 37 healthy controls at rest and during a 6-minute walk test. It identifies significant differences in HRV measures between groups and after exercise, suggesting HRV analysis could monitor post-COVID cardiovascular recovery, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study examining serum IgE, immunoglobulin levels, and mast cell infiltration in 21 severe COVID-19 patients and 30 autopsies, finding elevated IgE and mast cell accumulation suggesting IgE-driven allergic mechanisms. While the study includes long COVID patients and discusses post-COVID immune dysregulation, it is a passive observational analysis without any intervention or treatment evaluation, so it does not meet the criteria for the intervention trials pipeline.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and predictors of dizziness and hearing loss in 209 long COVID patients. Found dizziness in 26% and hearing loss in 15.3% of participants, with female sex, fatigue severity, and acute neurological symptoms as significant predictors.

This study compares orthostatic symptoms, hemodynamic responses to head-up tilt, and cerebral blood flow reductions in long-haul COVID-19 patients versus ME/CFS patients and healthy controls. It is a descriptive cross-sectional comparison study with no treatment intervention, therefore excluded from the treatment trials pipeline.

This study examines the anti-inflammatory properties of luteolin-rich extract from Harrisonia perforata root against SARS-CoV-2 spike protein-induced lung inflammation in vitro. The work demonstrates dose-dependent reduction in inflammatory cytokines in cultured lung epithelial cells, but presents no human trial data or clinical outcomes for long COVID patients.

This paper develops a mechanistic differential equation model to investigate population-level dynamics of long COVID, incorporating COVID-19 transmission, vaccination, and long COVID progression. The work is a theoretical modeling study validated with US and UK data, not an empirical treatment trial or intervention study.

Longitudinal observational study comparing inflammatory biomarker profiles in long COVID patients versus controls at 3 and 6 months post-infection. Findings suggest immune exhaustion rather than elevated inflammation may characterize long COVID, with predictive models combining cytokine signatures and acute disease severity.

This study compares plasma metabolomic profiles of PASC patients (n=29), recovered COVID-19 patients (n=16), and healthy controls (n=30) to identify biomarkers of mitochondrial dysfunction. The findings show PASC patients have altered fatty acid metabolism and depleted tryptophan levels consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction, but no intervention or treatment is tested.

A prospective single-center study evaluated the effects of 6-week pulmonary rehabilitation on 46 long-COVID patients using pre/post measurements of respiratory function, exercise capacity, and psychological outcomes. The structured rehabilitation program showed significant improvements in functional capacity (6MWT distance, Sit-to-Stand test), pain (VAS scores), psychological measures (PHQ-9, GAD), and respiratory parameters.

This cross-sectional study compares salivary metabolite profiles in 30 long COVID patients versus 7 controls, measuring respiratory function and physical capacity. While it identifies biomarker differences (lower creatine, Gly Pro Lys, and calenduloside G), it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study develops a machine-learning model using metabolomic data to distinguish long COVID (PASC) from similar conditions like ME/CFS, Lyme disease, POTS, and IBS. The model achieves high diagnostic accuracy (AUC-ROC 0.8991) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or patient outcomes.

This paper evaluates the clinical performance of two neutralizing antibody tests (pseudovirus and surrogate virus neutralization tests) in a COVID-19 long-term follow-up cohort. It is a methods/validation study comparing diagnostic test sensitivity and specificity, not a treatment intervention trial.

This study investigates dermatologic changes in mice infected with murine hepatitis virus-1 (MHV-1) as an experimental model of long COVID, documenting skin damage across acute and chronic phases. The authors test treatment with a synthetic peptide (SPIKENET/SPK) designed to block Spike glycoprotein binding and demonstrate it restores hair follicles and repairs epidermal/dermal layers in infected mice.

This paper investigates the mechanism by which SARS-CoV-2 may interfere with hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and cause thrombocytopenia and thrombophilia in long COVID patients. It is an ex vivo mechanistic study using cell lines and primary CD34+ HSCs, not a clinical trial or treatment intervention study.

This is an in vitro mechanistic study examining how the SARS-CoV-2 S1 spike protein activates inflammatory signaling and cytokine production in human lung and intestinal epithelial cells cultured in the laboratory. It does not test any treatment or intervention on long COVID patients, making it a mechanistic research paper rather than a clinical trial or treatment study.

This study investigated the presence of SARS-CoV-2 microRNA-like small RNAs in serum samples from 24 COVID-19 patients, comparing those with and without PASC symptoms. The research found reduced small RNA positivity in PASC patients at later timepoints but found no significant differences in host target expression between groups.

This prospective longitudinal study examines predisposing and precipitating factors for ME/CFS development following infectious mononucleosis in college students, with planned inclusion of long COVID cases. The research identifies baseline and acute-phase predictors of non-recovery but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Analyzes the proteome of amyloid microclots found in long COVID and sepsis patients, identifying proteins that distinguish amyloid from normal clots. Identifies galectin-3-binding protein and thrombospondin-1 as potential biomarkers for amyloid-type clotting abnormalities in coagulopathies.

This study compared circulating microRNA (miRNA) expression patterns in plasma from long COVID patients with rheumatological symptoms, recovered COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls. The research identified differential miRNA expression and antibody-mediated hydrolysis activity associated with immune response pathways, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This computational and experimental study investigates how SARS-CoV-2 nucleoprotein binds neuropeptides and proposes mechanisms linking viral replication to long COVID symptoms through altered neurotransmission pathways. The work speculates on potential therapeutic targets but presents no clinical trial data or treatment outcomes in patients.

This pilot study compared cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) measured by breath-hold fMRI in 14 patients with neurological post-COVID syndrome (PCS) with fatigue/memory/concentration symptoms, 11 with PCS with myopathy/neuropathy symptoms, and 17 healthy controls. No significant differences in CVR or time-to-peak were found between groups, suggesting endothelial dysfunction may not be the primary pathomechanism of neurological PCS symptoms.

This study compares gut bacteriome composition, intestinal permeability, and inflammatory cytokine profiles between acute COVID-19 patients, post-COVID patients, and healthy controls using 16S sequencing and serological assays. The findings show dysbiosis and increased zonulin levels in infected groups, suggesting that gut dysbiosis may contribute to systemic inflammation, but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.

This exploratory study examines changes in appetite and eating behavior in 55 post-COVID-19 patients compared to controls, measuring appetite-related hormones and brain activity patterns. The findings show increased appetite hormone levels (NPY, ghrelin) persisting long after infection, correlating with specific activity in brain regions involved in appetite regulation.

This cross-sectional study examined associations between sensory, psychological, and cognitive variables in 149 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain using structural equation modeling. The analysis found that depressive symptoms were the strongest predictor of post-COVID pain, with psychological factors linked to central sensitization and sleep quality, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This secondary analysis compares serological biomarkers before and after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 76 ILD patients, with 79% developing post-COVID symptoms. CPK levels were significantly elevated in patients with post-COVID fatigue and dyspnea, but no other biomarkers showed significant changes.

This study investigates the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in 185 surveyed COVID-19 patients and examines the association between long COVID and Epstein-Barr virus reactivation in a subset of 68 patients. The findings show 30.3% long COVID prevalence and a significant association between long COVID symptoms and EBV reactivation markers, suggesting EBV reactivation may contribute to long COVID pathogenesis rather than SARS-CoV-2 directly.

In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 infection affects Wnt/β-catenin pathway components in human astrocytes derived from induced pluripotent stem cells. While relevant to Long COVID mechanisms, this is a basic mechanistic research study without any treatment intervention or clinical trial design.

This paper evaluates in vitro and ex vivo safety and efficacy of novel nasal nanoformulations containing lipid-soluble EGCG (EC16m) for potential long COVID treatment. The study demonstrates mucociliary safety and strong antiviral activity against coronavirus in laboratory models, but does not involve human subjects or clinical outcomes.

This study compares autonomic nervous system function in post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients versus ME/CFS patients and healthy controls using heart rate variability and blood pressure measurements. It finds similar patterns of dysautonomia and autonomic dysfunction in both PCC and ME/CFS groups but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigates nanocurcumin's anti-inflammatory effects on SARS-CoV-2 spike protein-induced inflammation in lung epithelial cells in vitro. While relevant to long COVID pathophysiology, it is an in vitro mechanistic study without any human participants or treatment evaluation, making it unsuitable for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This is a computational study using single-cell transcriptomics and network analysis to identify drug candidates for post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis, not a clinical trial testing treatments on patients. The paper performs drug repositioning via in silico methods without conducting any human intervention study or clinical evaluation.

Cross-sectional study comparing endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress biomarkers in 92 women across groups: controls, acute COVID-19, 12 months post-COVID, and asymptomatic COVID-19. Findings indicate persistent lipid peroxidation and free radical imbalance 12 months post-infection, suggesting oxidative stress contributes to long COVID pathogenesis, but no intervention or treatment is evaluated.

This paper proposes a novel liposomal drug delivery system for fluoroquinolones and antifibrotics (pirfenidone) designed to treat post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications including pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis. The work is a preclinical formulation study in mice demonstrating prolonged lung accumulation of moxifloxacin; no clinical trial or human data are presented.

This study develops a novel Jones-matrix theziography method to analyze optical anisotropy in blood plasma films as a diagnostic tool for long-term COVID-19 effects. The method demonstrates high accuracy in differentiating long COVID patients from healthy controls using multifractal analysis of birefringence patterns, but this is a diagnostic/biomarker study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

In vitro study examining luteolin's inhibitory effects on spike S1 glycoprotein-induced inflammation in THP-1 macrophage cells. While the abstract mentions long COVID in the background, the actual research is a cell-culture experiment with no human participants or patient populations—it tests a compound's mechanism of action at the cellular level, not a treatment intervention in long COVID patients.

The METAINFLAMATION study compared metabolic age and health-related quality of life across three inflammatory conditions (SLE, long COVID, and obesity/metabolic syndrome) in 232 participants stratified by weight status. The study found significant differences in biological age across disease groups and BMI categories, with implications for personalized monitoring and prevention of disease-related complications.

This paper uses machine learning (random forest) to predict ME/CFS development in COVID-19 patients based on early symptom profiles from the first two weeks of infection. While the study follows participants for ~6 months to assess later ME/CFS diagnosis, it is a secondary analysis identifying risk factors and predictive patterns rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Presents an AI-based home rehabilitation support system using machine learning to personalize monitoring of daily living activities (TUG and FTSTS tests) for post-COVID patients. The system achieves 100% accuracy in predicting patient conditions and difficulty areas while maintaining low computational footprint for unsupervised home use.

This proof-of-concept study uses video-oculography to measure eye movement alterations in 9 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 9 healthy controls. While it identifies significant differences in saccade latency and antisaccade performance, it is a diagnostic/observational study that does not test any treatment or intervention.

This study used multiparametric cardiac MRI to assess myocardial involvement in 65 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 50 matched controls, evaluating whether strain parameters could differentiate subclinical cardiac dysfunction. The findings showed that myocardial strain and strain rate were significantly reduced in patients with suspected myocarditis, suggesting MRI is useful for characterizing cardiac changes in PASC, but no treatment or intervention was tested.

This study compares SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell immunity between convalescent COVID-19 patients with short-duration symptoms versus those with prolonged symptoms lasting 18+ days. The findings show that persistent COVID-19 symptoms are not associated with dysregulated cellular immune responses, suggesting symptom duration minimally impacts T cell development.

This paper describes a novel multimodal physiological assessment methodology for evaluating neurocardiovascular and neuromuscular function in long COVID patients using simultaneous continuous monitoring. It presents proof-of-concept results demonstrating the technical feasibility of synchronized data collection from multiple biomedical sensors but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or compare outcomes across groups.

This study compares plasma acid sphingomyelinase levels in pregnant women with persistent taste/smell disorders >1 year post-COVID versus those without sensory disturbances. The research suggests elevated sphingomyelinase may indicate demyelination-related chemosensory dysfunction in long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper characterizes SARS-CoV-2-derived small RNAs and circulating miRNAs in plasma samples from active and convalescent COVID-19 patients using high-throughput sequencing. While it identifies viral-derived small RNAs with potential relevance to long COVID symptoms, it is a mechanistic biomarker study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Retrospective study comparing lung volumes in young long COVID patients (n=77) vs pre-COVID controls (n=77) using quantitative CT analysis. Found 10% reduction in total lung volume in post-COVID group despite negative inflammatory findings on standard imaging.

This study investigates post-acute SARS-CoV-2 infection in macaques, detecting persistent viral RNA and ongoing replication in multiple tissues weeks after initial infection. While relevant to understanding long-term COVID consequences, this is an animal model study with no human participants and no treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared heart rate variability between 30 long COVID patients and 20 controls using 24-hour ECG monitoring. The findings demonstrate impaired vagal activity and dysautonomia in long COVID patients, characterized by reduced heart rate variability components and elevated LF/HF ratio, suggesting autonomic nervous system dysfunction may explain persistent symptoms.

A case series of 58 long COVID patients treated with epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT), an anti-inflammatory treatment involving zinc chloride application to the epipharynx. EAT significantly reduced fatigue, headache, and attention disorder severity as measured by visual analog scale, suggesting potential as a novel long COVID treatment.

This study profiles peripheral blood immune cells in convalescent plasma donors at 2 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection using flow cytometry, comparing recovered donors to active COVID-19 patients and controls. While it documents persistent immune alterations in recovery, it is focused on acute post-infection immune dynamics and does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months later) or any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined correlations between two neuropathic pain questionnaires (S-LANSS and PainDETECT) in 146 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain, assessing their associations with pain intensity, anxiety, sensitization, and quality of life. The study found good convergent validity between the questionnaires, with S-LANSS more associated with symptom duration and PainDETECT more associated with sensitization and anxiety.

This study analyzes antibody responses in COVID-19 patients to characterize the autoimmune mechanisms underlying post-COVID symptoms, showing that IgG antibodies to nucleoprotein correlate with disease severity and long-term sequelae. The work identifies cross-reactivity patterns and HLA alleles associated with autoimmune complications but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study compares CD8+ T cell profiles in acute COVID-19 patients, convalescent subjects (post-COVID), and healthy controls using flow cytometry. The findings show abnormal CD8+ T cell maturation and polarization in convalescents, including lower effector cell frequencies and higher senescent markers, but this is an observational immunological study without any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared platelet mitochondrial bioenergy function and antioxidant levels in vaccinated vs unvaccinated long COVID patients and healthy controls. Vaccination protected mitochondrial respiration and energy production in long COVID patients, though it did not affect endogenous CoQ10 levels.

This study investigates SARS-CoV-2 infection of megakaryocytes in vitro using inhibitors AC-73 and syrosingopine targeting CD147 and MCT4. While relevant to COVID-19 and long COVID coagulation disorders, it is a mechanistic cell biology study without patient treatment or clinical outcomes.

A case series of 14 long COVID patients with fatigue undergoing a supervised exercise rehabilitation program, measuring response via 6-minute walk test and fatigue scales. 65% of patients showed improvement in walking distance and oxygen saturation, with biomarker differences (creatinine, protein levels) identified between responders and non-responders.

Cross-sectional study of 151 Brazilian post-COVID patients examining immunoglobulin profiles and symptom patterns across demographic groups. Found elevated IgA levels in long COVID patients, particularly in adult and elderly groups, suggesting IgA as a potential immunological signature for persistent post-COVID symptoms.

Feasibility study evaluating a saline-based nanoformulation containing EC16 (EGCG derivative) for intranasal delivery to treat long COVID by inactivating persistent SARS-CoV-2 in nasal epithelial cells. Study demonstrates in vitro antiviral activity and cell compatibility but is a preclinical development study without human participants or clinical outcomes.

This cross-sectional study analyzes IgG antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 spike and nucleocapsid proteins in 136 individuals with different COVID-19 clinical profiles, including those with long COVID. The results show that individuals with long COVID had significantly higher IgG responses compared to those with short-duration symptoms, suggesting antibody levels may be related to clinical evolution.

This study analyzed gut microbiome composition and serum cytokine profiles in 60 COVID-19 patients over one year using 16S rRNA sequencing and Milliplex analysis. The research identifies associations between pro-inflammatory microbial profiles, elevated cytokine levels, and post-COVID syndrome symptoms, suggesting the gut microbiota may play a mechanistic role in persistent post-COVID symptoms.

Retrospective analysis of German nationwide inpatient data identifying 29,808 post-COVID syndrome (PCS) cases hospitalized in 2019, with assessment of mortality, ICU usage, comorbidities, and direct healthcare costs (€136.6 million total). This is an observational study of hospitalized patients without any treatment intervention or trial design—it reports healthcare utilization patterns and costs rather than evaluating a specific treatment.

In vitro study examining how SARS-CoV-2 affects human brain microvascular endothelial cells to understand viral transmigration and BBB permeability in COVID-19 and long COVID. Found that viral exposure triggers endothelial activation via NF-κB pathway, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction, contributing to neuroinflammatory processes.

This study investigates histopathological changes in the small intestine following murine coronavirus (MHV-1) infection in mice, modeling both acute and long COVID phases. SPIKENET (SPK) treatment is tested as a potential therapeutic intervention to mitigate intestinal damage and inflammatory responses in this experimental model.

This paper proposes SPIKENET (SPK), a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide targeting SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, as a potential therapeutic for long COVID based on murine hepatitis virus-1 (MHV-1) model studies. The work demonstrates that SPK prevents viral attachment and reverses inflammation and tissue damage in mice, but presents only preclinical findings with no human clinical trial data or patient outcomes.

This study compares transcriptomic profiles of peripheral blood mononuclear cells in COVID-19 patients (with and without pneumonia) versus healthy controls at 1-year follow-up. The analysis identifies differentially expressed genes and long non-coding RNAs associated with disease severity and long-term inflammatory pathways, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study analyzes single-cell transcriptome data from peripheral blood samples of non-elderly female PASC patients to explore immune mechanisms underlying long COVID, identifying a CD14+STAT2high monocyte subset associated with type I interferonopathy. The work is a bioinformatic/mechanistic analysis of existing transcriptome data and does not involve a clinical intervention, patient treatment, or intervention trial.

Study comparing viral loads (EBV, HHV6, HCMV, HAdV, SARS-CoV-2) and anti-interferon autoantibodies in sputum samples from ME/CFS and long COVID patients versus healthy controls. Finds significantly elevated EBV in ME/CFS patients but no clear role for interferon autoantibodies in immune exhaustion.

This study analyzed long-term transcriptomic changes in blood immune cells of severe COVID-19 survivors one year post-infection, identifying persistent pro-oncogenic molecular signatures and cancer-associated pathways. The findings suggest severe COVID-19 may increase cancer risk, highlighting the need for prolonged oncological monitoring in these patients.

This experimental study uses a female hACE2 mouse model infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant to investigate cardiac tissue inflammation 28 days post-infection, measuring inflammatory biomarkers and tissue damage markers via Western blot. The study found elevated IL-6 and CD11d expression in infected mice, supporting persistent low-grade inflammation in post-COVID cardiac sequelae without severe tissue damage.

This is a cost-effectiveness modeling study using a Markov model to evaluate COVID-19 inactivated vaccines in preventing ischemic stroke after SARS-CoV-2 infection. It is not about long COVID treatments and uses secondary modeling analysis rather than primary research on patient cohorts.

This study examines morphological and immunohistochemical changes in liver tissue from post-COVID-19 patients compared to controls, finding increased portal and periportal inflammation and altered immune cell counts. It is a descriptive case-control study of disease pathology rather than an intervention trial, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

This study examines serum biomarkers (prolidase, MMP-1, MMP-7, TGF-β) and CT findings to predict pulmonary fibrosis in 68 moderate-to-severe COVID-19 patients. It is a cross-sectional biomarker analysis of acute COVID-19 complications, not a long COVID study, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study evaluates the clinical status and functional outcomes of post-COVID syndrome patients treated with rehabilitation combined with MDM therapy and interval hypoxic training. Results demonstrate that the combined approach improves rehabilitation effectiveness through synergistic functional potentiation effects.

This in vitro study evaluates anti-HIV prodrugs (tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and tenofovir alafenamide) for their antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 strains in cell cultures. While the authors discuss potential implications for long COVID treatment, no human subjects or clinical intervention was conducted—only laboratory testing of drug compounds.

This study evaluated the clinical status and functional outcomes of post-COVID syndrome patients receiving a rehabilitation program supplemented with MDM therapy and interval hypoxic training. The results demonstrated that the combined approach produced synergistic effects and improved rehabilitation effectiveness compared to standard methods.

This study examined hemostatic and inflammatory markers in post-COVID syndrome patients and evaluated non-drug treatments including standard therapy, hypoxic training, and mesodiencephalic modulation (MDM therapy). MDM therapy combined with hypoxic exposure showed significant normalizing effects on coagulation parameters and inflammatory markers.

This paper describes a cross-sectional survey and neuropsychological assessment of 1,200 Russian respondents experiencing post-COVID symptoms 4-12 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, identifying seven subphenotypes of long COVID manifestations including cognitive, psychiatric, and neurological sequelae. While focused on long COVID, the paper is observational and does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention, and appears to be a narrative overview rather than a primary research study with novel results.

This study evaluates the efficacy of low-frequency electrostatic field (LESF) and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), alone and in combination, for correcting carbohydrate and lipid metabolism disorders in post-COVID syndrome patients, including effects on inflammatory markers and depression. The combined treatment showed additive benefits in improving metabolic parameters, blood oxygen saturation, and reducing inflammatory activity in post-COVID patients.

This study develops a quantitative dose-response model characterizing the relationship between spike protein concentrations and long COVID symptoms in 12 patients, identifying key proinflammatory biomarkers (CXCL8, IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α) associated with symptom severity. The work provides a risk assessment strategy for early identification of long COVID susceptibility but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This study evaluates mesodiencephalic (MDM) therapy and normobaric hypoxia as non-drug interventions for post-COVID syndrome, analyzing their effects on carbohydrate and lipid metabolism. The combined use of both therapies produced enhanced therapeutic effects, improved insulin sensitivity, and reduced oxidative stress markers in post-COVID patients.

This study evaluated personalized sanatorium-resort treatment programs for 2,458 post-COVID patients with various manifestations of post-COVID syndrome using clinical observations and specialized research methods. The results showed that personalized spa treatment incorporating pathogenetically-justified physical factors based on clinical symptoms significantly improved rehabilitation effectiveness and quality of life in post-COVID patients.

This study examines oral hygiene and oral fluid parameters in 68 post-COVID syndrome patients (27-40 years) comparing different toothpastes, with a control group of COVID-uninfected individuals. Results show post-COVID patients had lower salivation rate, increased viscosity, and decreased antimicrobial markers, with moisturizing toothpaste (R.O.C.S.) improving these parameters more than chlorhexidine-containing toothpaste.

This paper identifies secondary metabolites in mango (Mangifera indica) leaves through qualitative phytochemical testing, finding phenols, tannins, flavonoids, and other compounds. The authors propose these constituents may have potential to treat post-COVID syndrome symptoms but acknowledge that quantification and characterization studies are needed—no actual treatment or clinical trial data is presented.

This study establishes normative reference data for the 10-minute Lean Test in 112 healthy controls without orthostatic intolerance or long COVID, measuring heart rate and blood pressure responses to standing. The data provides baseline values for interpreting Lean Test findings in younger patients with orthostatic dysfunction, potentially useful for managing dysautonomia in long COVID and other post-infection conditions.

This cross-sectional study examines endothelin-1 levels in blood and lung tissue of post-COVID-19 patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma compared to controls. While it documents long-term endothelial dysfunction in post-COVID patients, it is not a treatment study—it only measures biomarkers in patients with concurrent cancer, without testing or evaluating any intervention.

Retrospective chart review of 109 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining musculoskeletal symptoms and their correlation with inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, IL-10). Found no significant association between musculoskeletal manifestations and inflammatory levels, but identified correlations between post-COVID syndrome, fatigue, and duration of hospitalization/oxygen support.

This study evaluates a metabiotic supplement (Bactimunal®) containing Bacillus subtilis and FOS in long COVID patients with gastrointestinal symptoms and asthenia. Results show the supplement reduced GI complaints, asthenia, and dysbiotic changes in the gut microbiome.

This meta-transcriptomic study characterizes respiratory microbiome differences in 201 older adults with and without long COVID, identifying dysbiosis, increased pathogenic bacteria and fungi, and frequent viral detection in LC patients. The findings reveal altered microbial metabolism pathways, particularly in tryptophan-serotonin metabolism, suggesting a potential role for respiratory dysbiosis in long COVID pathogenesis.

A study of vinpocetine efficacy and tolerability in post-COVID syndrome patients with arterial hypertension and cerebrovascular insufficiency. Treatment showed decreased severity of physical and mental asthenia regardless of patient gender, age, post-COVID duration, or drug dose.

This study investigates altered glycan profiles in peripheral blood of post-infectious ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls, hypothesizing that changes in sialic acid and N-glycosylation patterns may serve as biomarkers for disease severity. Results show decreased sialylated glycans and increased pro-inflammatory terminal galactosylated glycans in ME/CFS patients, suggesting glycan-based biomarkers for immunological monitoring.

This cross-sectional study examines the frequency and nature of skin and mucous membrane changes in 106 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients in Gomel, Belarus from March to September 2023. The study identifies rash and skin dryness as leading dermatological manifestations, with prevalence increasing with age and more common in males six months post-infection, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining inflammatory markers and endothelial dysfunction parameters in 137 post-COVID-19 patients with and without persistent symptoms. Found elevated plasma NOx concentration significantly associated with long COVID symptoms, suggesting a potential objective biomarker for endothelial dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study examines plasma microparticles and procoagulant activity in 88 patients 1-4 months after COVID-19 recovery, comparing severe/moderate cases (n=54) to mild cases (n=34) against healthy controls. Findings show elevated platelet-derived microparticles persist in long COVID patients regardless of disease severity, with higher endothelial microparticles in severe cases; anticoagulant therapy appears to reduce procoagulant activity.

This paper analyzes long COVID diagnostic coding patterns across 58 million English primary care patient records using OpenSAFELY, reporting prevalence and variation in clinical coding practices. It is a secondary analysis of administrative health data documenting coding trends rather than an intervention trial or treatment study.

This study assessed emotional and psychological states in 50 post-COVID patients using standardized scales (HADS, MFI-20, SAN) to identify psychocorrectional targets. Results showed high anxiety and mental asthenia but low depression, with preserved motivation for treatment.

Retrospective analysis of 44 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining CT imaging patterns of post-COVID lung changes, with pneumofibrosis identified as the most common pattern (39%). The study documents staged progression of lung damage but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely diagnostic/observational imaging analysis without a therapeutic component.

A prospective study assessing cognitive impairments in 75 Bulgarian long COVID patients using the Cogstate Brief Battery to measure processing speed, attention, visual learning, and working memory. Results show executive functions and memory are predominantly affected, consistent with findings in other countries, with follow-up testing planned at six months.

Cross-sectional study of 125 COVID-19 patients 2-6 weeks post-infection examining mental health symptoms and psychological disorders. Describes clinical phenomenology of depression, anxiety, PTSD, and adjustment disorders but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A 3-month outpatient study of 47 post-COVID patients with respiratory syndrome treated with doxophylline (400 mg twice daily for 2-8 weeks). All patients showed significant reductions in cough intensity and improvements in spirometric respiratory parameters (FEV1, Tiffno index).

This study evaluates a complex therapeutic and preventive program (balanced nutrition, psychotherapy, hormone therapy, immunomodulators, vitamins, antioxidants) in 100 women with long COVID-related infertility, comparing 50 treated women to 50 untreated controls before assisted reproductive technology (ART) programs. The intervention group showed significant improvements in long COVID symptoms and substantially higher clinical pregnancy (36% vs 20%) and live birth rates (36% vs 16%) compared to controls.

This cross-sectional study compares hormonal profiles in 80 infertile women with long COVID symptoms to 40 controls without COVID history. The study documents neuro-endocrine abnormalities (elevated LH/FSH, hyperestrogenemia, elevated cortisol, decreased AMH) but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines somatic and cognitive disorders in 62 young adults (age ~20 years) who previously had COVID-19, using HRV measurements, neurodynamic tests, and the Long COVID Symptom Tool. The most common post-COVID symptoms were taste/smell disturbance and memory impairment, with worse CNS function and increased sympathetic activity in infected versus uninfected students, and symptom severity varying by time since infection.

This study evaluated psychotherapeutic interventions including cognitive training, cognitive behavioral therapy, art therapy, and psychoeducation in 75 long COVID patients with cognitive disorders. Treatment resulted in positive outcomes in 84.8% of men and 86.3% of women, with significant improvements in cognitive performance on the Addenbrooke's Scale.

A cross-sectional study examining pathopsychological features and mental health disorders in 167 post-COVID syndrome patients. Found high prevalence of depressive, anxiety, astheno-neurotic, and cognitive syndromes with specific symptom profiles on standardized psychometric scales.

This study proposes and applies a therapeutic exercise program to improve physical condition in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients, with two evaluations (initial and final) showing significant improvements. The program demonstrates that structured exercise can help patients recover functionality and quality of life following acute COVID-19 infection.

This cross-sectional study examined the immune status of post-COVID syndrome patients using flow cytometry analysis, specifically investigating T-lymphocyte populations during adaptive immunity formation. The paper characterizes immune abnormalities in long COVID patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluates herpesvirus reactivation (EBV, CMV, HIV) in long COVID patients as a potential contributing factor to persistent symptoms. The research examines viral reactivation patterns in well-characterized long COVID cohorts to understand mechanisms underlying prolonged COVID-19 sequelae.

This study investigates the frequency of newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus in patients recovering from SARS-CoV-2 infection at a tertiary care follow-up clinic. It examines a long-term post-COVID complication but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This retrospective study evaluated HRCT chest findings in COVID-19 patients 4-8 weeks after RT-PCR negativity to assess long-term lung sequelae including ground-glass opacities, fibrosis, and pleural effusion. The paper is descriptive imaging surveillance without testing any treatment intervention.

This study developed a multivariate regression model to predict adverse outcomes in 118 patients with acute coronary syndrome combined with post-COVID syndrome using clinical, laboratory, and genetic data. The model identified chronic heart failure, elevated soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1, hypokinesis zones, and ACE2 gene variants as significant predictors with 93.5% sensitivity and 76.6% accuracy.

This cross-sectional study of 181 long COVID patients investigates predictors of reduced exercise capacity using the incremental shuttle walk test, identifying sex, dyspnea perception, restrictive respiratory patterns, and peripheral muscle weakness as significant predictors. The study measures associations between exercise capacity and various clinical parameters but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Observational study examining chronic pain in 82 COVID-19 patients, documenting worsening of pre-existing musculoskeletal pain post-infection (68%) versus stable pain (32%). No treatment intervention is tested; this is a clinical observation of pain outcomes in long COVID patients.

A case series of 102 COVID-19 patients who received a 21-day sanatorium-based rehabilitation program including exercise training, breathing exercises, and psychological support. The treatment resulted in significant improvements in exercise tolerance (6-minute walk distance increased 14-21%), respiratory symptoms, anxiety/depression scores, and quality of life measures.

This prospective study evaluated SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibody status in individuals attending a post-COVID outpatient department at a tertiary care hospital in central India over a one-year period. The study found that IgG antibody positivity declined with time since infection, with no detectable antibodies beyond 18 months post-COVID, providing insights into long-term humoral immune response patterns.

This study evaluates multiple rehabilitation interventions (physiotherapy, haloinhalation, exercise therapy, hyperbaric oxygenation) in post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients at the ambulatory stage. The interventions were assessed for their effects on lung function, blood tests, CT findings, oxygen saturation, and dyspnea scores, with particular focus on hyperbaric oxygenation's impact on diffusion capacity.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 316 long-term COVID patients examining pulmonary gas exchange disorders using spirometry, plethysmography, and diffusion testing. Develops a logistic regression model to predict reduced DLCO based on CT severity, time since infection, and age, but does not test any treatment or intervention.

This study evaluated the effects of dry carbon dioxide baths and magnetotherapy on post-COVID patients (n=40, two treatment groups of 20 each) compared to healthy controls. Both interventions improved quality of life, reduced anxiety and depression, decreased dyspnea severity, and DCB significantly lowered C-reactive protein levels.

This study assessed diaphragm function in COPD patients who previously had COVID-19 compared to COPD-only controls using ultrasound imaging. While it documents respiratory muscle changes post-COVID, it is primarily a descriptive assessment study of COPD patients, not a long COVID intervention trial, as the focus is on COPD management rather than treating long COVID sequelae.

This cross-sectional study measures serum TRAIL and inflammatory markers in COPD patients 12 months post-COVID-19 versus COPD controls without COVID history. The study documents elevated biomarkers but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating comprehensive rehabilitation (respiratory exercises, chest massage, osteopathic adjustment) in 55 post-COVID-19 patients with impaired respiratory muscle strength. The program significantly improved respiratory function, muscle strength, oxygen saturation, and quality of life compared to baseline.

This cross-sectional study compares malondialdehyde and pro-BNP levels in 40 post-infarction chronic heart failure patients who had COVID-19 versus 20 controls without COVID-19 infection. The COVID-19 group showed significantly elevated oxidative stress markers and inflammation indicators, suggesting post-COVID syndrome may contribute to cardiovascular disease progression through oxidative stress mechanisms.

This study compares post-COVID arthritis (PCA) with rheumatoid arthritis in 160 patients divided into 4 groups based on COVID-19 severity and joint disease history. The analysis evaluates clinical symptoms, inflammatory markers, and response to anti-inflammatory and hormonal therapy to differentiate post-COVID arthritis from rheumatoid arthritis.

A study evaluating the effectiveness of a 30-day home-based respiratory gymnastics program with remote video monitoring in 50 post-COVID patients aged 24-72 years. Daily breathing exercises improved respiratory function and cognitive abilities, with 70-75% of patients under 60 years showing positive changes, though elderly patients showed less improvement.

Observational cross-sectional study comparing ambulatory blood pressure parameters and variability in 58 young adults with long COVID versus 57 healthy controls. Patients with long COVID showed significantly elevated blood pressure, increased variability, and abnormal nocturnal dipping patterns, suggesting increased cardiovascular risk.

This study evaluated a multi-modal health-resort treatment program (dietary, kinesiotherapy, balneotherapy, physical therapy, oxygen therapy) in 33 long COVID patients over 14-28 days. Treatment resulted in statistically significant improvements in clinical condition, with one-third of patients achieving complete symptom resolution and most others showing reduced symptom burden; physical capacity improved markedly, though VO2max changes were not statistically significant.

This study evaluates haloaerosoltherapy (dry salt aerosol inhalations) combined with physical exercises in 85 COVID-19 convalescents with persistent pneumonia manifestations across mild, moderate, and severe disease categories. The intervention improved ventilation, reduced inflammatory markers, enhanced cellular immunity, and produced clinical improvement, with greatest benefit observed in patients who had mild acute COVID-19.

This paper describes a rehabilitation program designed specifically for obese patients recovering from COVID-19, focusing on addressing physical deconditioning and post-COVID symptoms. The program aims to improve physical fitness, alleviate post-COVID symptoms, and promote better recovery outcomes in this higher-risk population.

This study evaluates a comprehensive rehabilitation program for asthenic syndrome (fatigue/weakness) in post-COVID-19 patients, measuring neuropsychological outcomes before and one month after intervention. Results show that patients completing the rehabilitation program experienced significant reduction in asthenic syndrome severity and disability duration compared to baseline.

This study evaluates treatment optimization for elderly patients with combined arterial hypertension and post-COVID syndrome, testing L-arginine and mebicar alongside standard antihypertensive therapy in 50 patients. Results showed significant improvements in blood pressure, anxiety, cholesterol levels, and clinical symptoms (headache, sleep) with faster symptom resolution.

This study conducted a comprehensive clinical-psychopathological examination of 115 post-COVID patients to characterize anxiety-depressive disorders in the context of post-COVID syndrome. The findings identified anxiety (36.7%), depressive (34.5%), astheno-hypochondriac (16.8%), and dysphoric (12.0%) variants as the main emotional disorder subtypes, with intrusive anxious thoughts and sleep disturbance being common features.

This paper analyzes social media posts from post-COVID patients in India to characterize symptom prevalence and emotional experiences, developing a predictive sentiment analysis model. It is a cross-sectional social media analysis study that does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study used functional MRI to characterize brain imaging patterns and stress phenotypes in 50 post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients one year post-infection, comparing them to 10 healthy controls. The study identified distinct temporal patterns of stress-related changes in brain networks and hypothalamic nuclei but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study evaluated complex psychotherapy interventions for mental disorders (anxiety, depression, PTSD, organic mental disorders) occurring after COVID-19 in 63 patients. Treatment combined pharmacotherapy (antidepressants, anxiolytics) with staged psychotherapy (CBT, NET, art therapy, family therapy), with 76.19% showing significant improvement.

This paper describes the reliability and validation of the ASIB neuro psychosomatic scale for assessing psychological impairments in post-COVID-19 patients. It is a measurement/validation study with no treatment intervention or outcome comparisons, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

A case series of 47 COVID-19 patients with auditory system disorders, documenting sensorineural and conductive hearing loss occurring weeks after infection. The study evaluates conservative therapy and surgical interventions (tympanopuncture) for post-COVID hearing impairment, finding that conductive disorders often require active intervention.

A cross-sectional study examining secretory otitis media in 38 COVID-19 patients using audiometry and impedance testing. The study documents hearing impairment as a post-COVID complication but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment, making it descriptive/observational rather than a treatment trial.

This paper describes the modeling and development of a plant-based phytocomposition designed as a functional food for post-COVID syndrome, outlining its recipe optimization and nutritional properties. The work focuses on composition design and organoleptic testing rather than clinical evaluation or outcome measurement in patients.

This study compares cytokine profiles and neurological manifestations across 30 post-COVID syndrome patients, 28 recovered COVID-19 patients, and 29 acute COVID-19 patients, measuring cognitive and affective function alongside serum biomarkers. The findings show elevated IFN-α, IL-6, and SARS-CoV-2 antibodies in PCS patients, with distinct IgG subclass patterns suggesting chronic inflammation in neurological dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study examines immune system alterations in 124 long COVID patients, comparing lymphocyte populations between those with and without HHV-6 reactivation using flow cytometry. The findings show dysregulation of T cells, B cells, and NK cells depending on HHV-6 status and COVID-19 severity, suggesting HHV-6 reactivation plays a role in immune dysfunction during long COVID.

This paper develops a point-of-care diagnostic test for detecting a long-COVID-associated SNP (rs17713054) in the LZTFL1 gene using Pyrococcus furiosus Argonaute. The study focuses on genetic risk stratification rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

Descriptive cross-sectional study examining olfactory dysfunction in 53 COVID-19 patients with persistent symptoms 2 weeks to 1.5 months after acute infection. Findings show anosmia, reduced sensitivity, or distorted smell in the majority, with endoscopic and anatomical assessment but no treatment intervention tested.

This experimental study evaluated the effectiveness of stacking deep breathing techniques on respiratory efficiency in 60 post-COVID-19 patients over 4 weeks. Results showed statistically significant improvements in respiratory rate and Post COVID-19 Functional Status Scale (PCFS) scores in the treatment group compared to control.

This study examines immunological parameters in children with bronchial asthma following COVID-19 infection. The paper focuses on immune response mechanisms in acute COVID-19 and potential long-term consequences, but does not study a treatment intervention for long COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study identifies the etiology of fungal infections in post-COVID patients at a tertiary care hospital, finding Mucor, Aspergillus, and Candida species among 578 samples. The paper does not evaluate any intervention or treatment, only characterizes the prevalence and types of fungal infections that occur post-COVID.

This cross-sectional study examined 100 long COVID patients to identify clinical and laboratory characteristics associated with post-COVID syndrome development. The paper describes symptoms and risk factors but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines immune system dysfunction in 18 lung cancer patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS), investigating phagocytosis impairment and altered NK/T cell populations. The findings suggest immune resistance disorders develop during PCS and propose that biotechnological interventions targeting co-stimulatory pathways may complement surgical cancer treatment.

This cross-sectional study examines immune dysfunction and DAMP fractions in 143 post-COVID patients presenting with urgent surgical pathology. The paper characterizes immunopathological patterns but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines immunoinflammatory markers and hemostasis system disorders in cardiac and vascular surgical patients during acute COVID-19 and post-COVID periods, measuring complement activation, cytokines, coagulation factors, and fibrinolytic activity. The research identifies predictors of thrombogenicity and endotheliitis but does not test or evaluate any therapeutic intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared lung function parameters between long COVID patients with varying dyspnea severity and healthy controls 12-16 weeks post-COVID pneumonia. The study identified reduced lung capillary blood volume and altered nitric oxide parameters as key physiological markers in symptomatic long COVID patients, suggesting mechanisms underlying respiratory dysfunction that standard spirometry would miss.

A case series of approximately 50 post-COVID-19 patients from an infectious disease institute who underwent pulmonary rehabilitation including respiratory kinesiotherapy and physical therapy. The paper describes clinical methodology for adapting rehabilitation programs to individual patients and reports that specific rehabilitative interventions are necessary and useful for managing respiratory sequelae in post-COVID cases.

This cross-sectional study examines cerebral hemodynamic characteristics in post-COVID syndrome patients using ultrasound imaging of head and neck vasculature. The paper describes clinical and hemodynamic findings but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This paper proposes a latent transfer learning model to integrate patient data across regions for improved prediction and personalization of PASC outcomes. It is a methodological/technical study describing a modeling approach rather than a clinical trial or treatment evaluation with results.

A prospective randomized study comparing remote monitoring of motor activity and rehabilitation outcomes in 80 patients: 42 with chronic coronary heart disease and 38 with long COVID undergoing sanatorium-based rehabilitation. Both groups showed improved cardiovascular hemodynamic load after rehabilitation, with the long COVID group demonstrating greater improvement (p<0.01).

This study evaluates a 12-week comprehensive physical rehabilitation program (cardiopulmonary training) in 128 cardiac patients with post-COVID syndrome across intervention, control, and comparative groups. Results show significant improvements in the intervention group including reduced dyspnea (mMCR 1.0 vs 2.0), increased exercise tolerance (VO2max +8.3%), normalized heart rate/blood pressure response, and greater 6-minute walk distance (688m vs 490m).

Study evaluates Mercurid, an immunomodulatory drug, in treating complications of COVID-19 with focus on immune dysfunction and chronic inflammatory manifestations. Reports 75.1% therapeutic efficacy in reducing severity of post-COVID complications through multi-target immune modulation.

This Mendelian randomization study investigates causal associations between genetic predisposition to COVID-19 and long COVID symptoms including pulmonary, neurological, and cardiac conditions. The study uses genetic data to establish causal links rather than testing any treatment intervention.

A non-randomized trial of 57 post-COVID patients treated with thiotriazoline (a drug with anticoagulant and endothelioprotective properties) combined with basic therapy for 30 days. Treatment resulted in increased endothelial NO-synthase, reduced D-dimer and normalized INR, with clinical improvements in palpitations and blood pressure.

This cross-sectional study investigates insulin resistance and immune disturbances in 168 subjects across three groups: active COVID-19, post-COVID with newly diagnosed carbohydrate disorders, and COVID-negative controls with metabolic syndrome. The findings demonstrate that insulin resistance persists in post-COVID patients and correlates with markers of immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and cellular hypoxia.

This study evaluated a 6-month home-based kinesitherapy (physical exercise) program for post-COVID syndrome patients, measuring changes in quality of life using the SF-36 questionnaire at baseline and end-of-study. The program improved functional status and functional independence, leading to enhanced quality of life in post-COVID patients.

This study validates the Turkish version of the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status (PCFS) scale in 100 long COVID patients through reliability and validity testing. The scale demonstrates excellent test-retest reliability (ICC=0.821) and moderate to weak correlations with other functional outcome measures, supporting its use for assessing functional limitations in long COVID patients.

This paper applies a multi-criterion decision analysis (TOPSIS) model integrated with Grey theory to prioritize follow-up care and preventive measures for post-COVID-19 syndrome patients in India. It is a methodological/decision-making paper rather than a clinical trial or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study compared physical fitness measures (handgrip strength, quadricep strength, 6MWT) across 105 young adults divided into three groups: those with long COVID, recovered COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls. Individuals with long COVID showed significantly lower handgrip strength and both post-COVID groups exhibited reduced exercise capacity and heightened physiological stress responses.

This cross-sectional study compares brain morphology between 316 recovered COVID-19 patients and 316 matched controls using MRI to identify imaging biomarkers of structural alterations. Results show statistically significant increases in cortical tortuosity and decreases in compactness in COVID-19 patients, suggesting gray matter atrophy potentially linked to neurodegenerative processes.
