A cross-sectional study investigating long-term chemosensory effects (smell, taste, trigeminal system) in participants approximately one year after COVID-19 infection. The study found persistent chemosensory dysfunction in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined neutrophil extracellular trap (NETosis) formation and miR-21-5p expression in post-COVID-19 patients 4 months after infection, comparing those who developed insulin resistance (IR) versus those without metabolic alterations. Patients with post-COVID IR showed significantly elevated basal NETosis and higher miR-21-5p expression compared to those without IR, suggesting a link between metabolic complications and innate immune dysfunction in long COVID.

This study examines autoantibody responses in long COVID patients (neuro-PASC) following mild SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing them to convalescent controls. It finds that neuro-PASC patients develop higher titers of autoantibodies associated with systemic lupus erythematosus and CNS disease, which correlate with cognitive impairment and symptom severity, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study examined the association between anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG levels, chemokines (CXCL9/CXCL10), and disease severity in 60 COVID-19 patients at 4 months post-infection. The findings show that IgG levels and proinflammatory chemokines correlate with COVID-19 severity and pulmonary sequelae, but this is a mechanistic immunology study without any treatment intervention.

This study investigates immune system perturbations in severe long COVID patients by analyzing blood samples from over 100 patients using proteomics, mass cytometry, and immunological assays. The findings show substantial clonal expansion of memory T cells, elevated IL-8 and circulating nucleosomes, indicating persistent neutrophil activation but no evidence of superantigen-mediated disease.

This cross-sectional study evaluates immunological biomarkers and immune pathways in individuals with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC/long COVID), comparing those with and without persistent symptoms. Findings show that PASC is associated with diminished antibody responses, elevated inflammation, gut dysbiosis, and elevated high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) as a predictive biomarker of poor immune recovery and viral inhibition capacity.

This study investigates epigenetic and transcriptomic changes in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPC) from severe COVID-19 patients, finding persistent inflammatory alterations months to a year post-infection. The authors demonstrate that anti-IL-6 blockade during acute COVID-19 can normalize these persistent phenotypes, suggesting IL-6's role in epigenetic memory development.

This study performed a 2-year longitudinal immune assessment in 110 PASC patients with respiratory symptoms, using spectral flow cytometry and machine learning to identify distinct respiratory phenotypes based on immune dysregulation patterns. The research characterized immune mechanisms (particularly T cell and innate immune abnormalities) associated with different severity levels of post-COVID respiratory disease, but did not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This study investigates temporal changes in memory T cell responses to latent viruses (EBV, CMV, HSV-1) and SARS-CoV-2 in 12 COVID-19 infected individuals, comparing those with and without persistent symptoms (PASC). It provides mechanistic insights into potential drivers of long COVID through longitudinal immune profiling rather than testing any intervention.

This study uses iPSC-derived human brain organoids to investigate how SARS-CoV-2 infection and Spike protein exposure affect central nervous system homeostasis and may drive long-COVID neurological symptoms. It is an in vitro mechanistic study with no treatment intervention or patient cohort.

This paper describes development of a humanized ACE2 mouse model for studying SARS-CoV-2 infection and mentions potential future use for long COVID research. The work is a preclinical animal model characterization study with no human subjects or treatment interventions.

This metabolomics study identifies key plasma metabolites that are altered in acute COVID-19 and persist abnormally in PASC patients but normalize in those who fully recover. The findings suggest a molecular pathway-level hypothesis for long COVID pathobiology and demonstrate that viral RNA can induce these metabolic alterations.

This study investigates inflammatory and immune response signatures associated with COVID-19 severity by comparing hospitalized and non-hospitalized cases at 3 months post-infection. The hospitalized cohort showed elevated inflammatory proteins and persistent symptoms including muscle pain, headache, fatigue, and shortness of breath, suggesting characteristic plasma proteome changes in long-term COVID-19 recovery.

This study screened neuronal-specific autoantibodies in serum and CSF samples from 60 post-COVID patients with neurocognitive symptoms using an OmicsArray containing 83 neuronal antigens. The authors identified 7 elevated anti-neuronal antibodies (including anti-CASPR2, anti-GAD65, anti-mGluR2) and validated their specificity, suggesting these autoantibodies may play a role in post-COVID neurological syndrome.

This study examines CD4+ T cell phenotypic changes in 17 individuals recovered from prolonged symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding that a subset with protracted symptoms showed CD4 downregulation and defective T cell activation that largely recovered over months. The work is an immunological characterization study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study measures antiviral and autoimmune antibody levels over 10-25 months in 7 SARS-CoV-2 infected subjects to assess long-term immunological consequences and vaccine response durability. The abstract indicates this is preliminary data from a small cohort with future work planned, presenting it as a study protocol/preliminary report rather than completed research with full results.

This paper describes a humanized ACE2 mouse model engineered to recapitulate COVID-19 immunopathogenesis, including long COVID-like symptoms in middle-aged male mice. While the model demonstrates persistent symptoms post-infection, this is a basic research/animal model study with no human intervention or treatment being tested.

This paper describes mechanistic research on tissue-resident helper T cells (TRH) in chronic lung disease following viral pneumonia, using mouse models of influenza and analysis of COVID-19 convalescents. The authors propose TRH blockade as a potential therapeutic target but present no clinical trial data or treatment outcomes in patients.

Single-cell proteomic analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells comparing pulmonary long COVID patients (with persistent dyspnea) to recovered controls 406 days post-infection. Study identifies altered immune landscape including increased double-positive T-cells and differential CD304/CD200R expression in long COVID patients, but is a cross-sectional observational study with no treatment intervention.

This study develops mouse models of SARS-CoV-2-induced long COVID to investigate neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits, identifying elevated CCL11 as a potential biomarker. The authors are evaluating therapeutic approaches targeting reactive microglia but present this as ongoing work without completed results.

This study evaluates the effectiveness and safety of aquatic exercises as part of a comprehensive rehabilitation program for long COVID patients with postural and gait impairments. Results showed statistically significant improvements in exercise tolerance (6-minute step test), postural control, and microcirculation with no serious adverse events reported.

This paper investigates mechanisms by which SARS-CoV-2 Nsp3 protein triggers cell death and exacerbates amyloid β42-mediated neurodegeneration in Drosophila and murine models. It is a mechanistic study of post-COVID neurodegeneration pathways, not a treatment intervention trial or clinical study.

This cross-sectional study compares lung diffusing capacity (DLCO, DLNO) and capillary blood volume in long COVID patients with and without persistent dyspnea 12-16 weeks post-discharge. The findings demonstrate that vascular abnormalities in lung diffusion persist despite radiological recovery, but no intervention or treatment is tested or evaluated.

This clinical report describes ROS (reactive oxygen species) production in long COVID patients and the effects of antioxidant therapy. Findings show enhanced ROS production across long COVID subjects and rapid improvement in ROS levels and clinical presentations following oral antioxidant treatment.

A prospective case series evaluating oral corticosteroids combined with olfactory training as treatment for post-COVID olfactory dysfunction in 78 patients. Results showed 90.4% recovery within 4 weeks, with the authors concluding this combination therapy is a safe and beneficial treatment option.

This is a preclinical study testing RAGE-Ig protein's antiviral and anti-inflammatory effects in K18-hACE2 mice and Syrian hamsters infected with SARS-CoV-2 variants. The work is conducted entirely in animal models and cell culture with no human patient data, clinical outcomes, or long COVID patient treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiopulmonary exercise parameters between 35 long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea and 35 healthy controls. The study identified predictive factors for persistent dyspnea (hospitalization days, symptom duration, CT severity score) but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series describing cardiac MRI findings in 43 patients assessed 3-6 weeks after recovering from COVID-19, with elevated T1/T2 mapping, late gadolinium enhancement, and impaired left ventricular function as common findings. This is a descriptive imaging study without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study examining serum biomarkers (D-dimer, ferritin, CRP, LDH, IL-6) in post-COVID patients to identify prognostic markers for complications and disease severity. Findings show elevated inflammatory markers persisting 3 months post-infection, with gender differences in marker levels, but this is observational characterization without any intervention or treatment.

A quasi-experimental study evaluating an educational intervention to increase awareness of post-COVID-19 syndrome among COVID-19 survivors. The 45-minute education program significantly improved awareness scores from 8.04 to 12.255, with 94.2% achieving good awareness post-intervention.

A pre-post interventional study evaluating the effectiveness of an 8-week pulmonary rehabilitation program (education, breathing exercises, aerobic and strength training) in 155 post-COVID patients. The intervention significantly improved six-minute walk distance, resting vital signs, and all domains of health-related quality of life.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function and brain involvement in 18 long COVID patients versus 15 healthy controls using neuropsychological tests. Patients showed significant impairments in verbal memory and executive function, suggesting hippocampal and frontal lobe involvement, though no treatment intervention was tested.

This paper reports a retrospective analysis of rehabilitation costs and outcomes in 27 critically ill COVID-19 survivors who required ICU care and mechanical ventilation during acute infection. While it documents rehabilitation therapy during acute critical illness recovery, it does not address long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and does not study a specific intervention trial.

This study validates the PASC-C screening checklist for assessing physical, psychological, and cognitive symptoms in long COVID patients through phone interviews. It describes symptom prevalence but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study compares serum Galectin-3 levels and periodontal clinical parameters in post-COVID-19 patients with periodontitis versus controls without COVID-19 history. The findings show elevated Gal-3 levels in post-COVID patients with periodontitis, suggesting a biomarker for understanding periodontal complications during recovery.

Cross-sectional study examining CD45+ and CD46+ expression on peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets in 72 post-COVID patients using flow cytometry. Findings show decreased CD46+ expression in T lymphocytes and cytotoxic T cells, suggesting potential SARS-CoV-2 effects on CD46 receptors that may contribute to long-COVID symptoms, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

This study characterizes persistent olfactory dysfunction in 34 post-COVID-19 patients using standardized olfactory tests (Sniffin' Stick Test) and self-assessment scales. Findings show that olfactory identification impairment (not just detection loss) correlates with quality of life impact and does not improve spontaneously over time.

This cross-sectional study investigates an integrative diagnostic index (IDP) based on neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and C-reactive protein to predict COVID-19 outcomes and development of post-COVID syndrome. The study examines blood samples from COVID-19 patients, those in early post-COVID period, and those with early post-COVID syndrome, finding elevated IDP levels correlate with chronic fatigue and cognitive impairment in post-COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study of 372 post-COVID patients investigates hematological and immunological markers (NLR, LMR, SII, PLR, immune response types) that correlate with long COVID severity using the PCFS functional status scale. The study identifies immune suppression and activation patterns across disease severity groups but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining immune system parameters in 78 patients 6 months post-COVID-19, measuring 50 immune markers including NK cells, T/B lymphocytes, and cortisol levels. Found marked NK cell depletion in >1/3 of patients, compensatory T cell elevation, and persistent high cortisol levels suggesting chronic immune dysregulation and stress.

This study evaluated mucosal immunity dynamics in 130 post-COVID patients (1-9 months post-infection) and tested interferon-alpha-2b (VIFERON gel) intranasally for 30 days in a subset. Treatment with IFNa2b significantly increased salivary and nasopharyngeal sIgA levels in patients treated within 3 months, whereas untreated controls showed persistent reduced mucosal immunity and higher rates of respiratory viral infections.

In vitro study examining the effects of recombinant interferon α2b on neutrophil phenotype and function in 45 post-COVID syndrome patients with herpesvirus coinfections. Results showed recIFNα2b improved deficient neutrophil phagocytic function and reduced excessive NADPH oxidase activity, suggesting potential for immunotherapy in treating PCS manifestations including fatigue and cognitive dysfunction.

This study examines phagocytic and bactericidal function of neutrophils in post-COVID syndrome patients stratified by degree of lung damage during acute infection. Results show statistically significant differences in innate immunity indexes between patients with varying levels of acute lung damage, suggesting a relationship between early lung injury and later immune dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study examines humoral immune response features in post-COVID syndrome patients with a history of allergies, comparing immune markers between affected and unaffected groups. The paper is excluded because it is observational without treatment intervention—it characterizes immune dysfunction rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining systemic inflammation markers in tuberculosis patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection, including those with post-COVID symptoms. Finds that tuberculosis infection independently drives low-grade systemic inflammation, with no significant additional contribution from COVID-19 exposure or post-COVID syndrome.

This paper describes an approach to comprehensive quality of life assessment in children with post-COVID syndrome, evaluating vegetative, psychoemotional, and cognitive functions through clinical and psychological testing. The study is a methodological/protocol paper aimed at establishing assessment criteria rather than testing a specific treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares biomarkers (HbA1c, triglycerides, cholesterol) between 50 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients and 50 controls. The study found significantly elevated HbA1c and triglycerides in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigates immune system abnormalities in post-COVID patients experiencing recurrent infections and exacerbations of chronic diseases 6+ months after acute infection. The researchers found that immune dysfunction severity correlates with clinical manifestations of post-COVID syndrome, particularly in patients with lung involvement during acute infection.

This study analyzes apoptosis and intercellular adhesion markers (CD95 and CD54) in healthy individuals and post-COVID patients treated with Mercureid, a drug intervention for post-COVID syndrome. The research examines immunological changes and cellular damage markers as a basis for understanding and treating long-term COVID-19 effects.

A case series of 49 long COVID patients with ophthalmic pathologies evaluating the immunomodulatory drug Mercureid, which showed corrective effects in 73.4% of patients and improved visual function in 50% of cases with retinal vascular damage. The study also examined immune marker changes (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD25, CD38, CD54, CD95) and their correlation with COVID-19-related chronic inflammatory manifestations.

This paper develops an automated deep learning approach (DeepLabv3+) to segment pathologically altered lung tissue on chest CT scans in post-COVID syndrome patients. It is a technical/methodological study demonstrating an imaging analysis tool rather than evaluating a treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study examines 131 post-COVID patients to assess the relationship between acute COVID-19 severity and post-COVID immune-mediated disorders, including autoimmune conditions, proliferative diseases, and allergopathology. While it provides important biomarker data on complement activation and immune dysfunction in long COVID, it is purely observational without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study examines quantitative and phenotypic changes in CD16+ neutrophil granulocyte subsets in 39 post-COVID syndrome patients compared to 30 pre-COVID controls, measuring interferon receptor expression and herpesvirus co-infection status. The authors propose recombinant interferon-2b combined with antioxidants as a potential therapeutic strategy to restore immune function and resolve post-COVID manifestations.

This study evaluates changes in immune markers (complement system, neutrophil phagocytic activity) in post-COVID syndrome patients with laboratory-confirmed herpes virus type 6 co-infection using immunological assays and statistical analysis. The findings show more pronounced immune system disorders in post-COVID patients with herpesvirus history, suggesting the need for individualized immunocorrection approaches, but this is a descriptive cross-sectional immunological assessment without a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated computed tomography characteristics of sinonasal structures in 130 patients with olfactory dysfunction following COVID-19. The study identified correlations between olfactory fossa morphology and severity of olfactory dysfunction but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This study examines immunological differences between patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who had prior COVID-19 infection and compares immune markers (TREC/KREC levels, lymphocyte subpopulations) between groups stratified by TREC status. The research identifies associations between reduced TREC levels and more severe clinical presentations, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Study of 414 patients examining IgG antibody levels and lymphocyte activation markers (CD25, CD54, CD95) in those who recovered from COVID-19, had acute respiratory infections, or were uninfected. Evaluated the immunotherapy drug Mercureid for correcting impaired immune homeostasis in post-COVID conditions, showing 75.6% therapeutic efficacy.

A case series of 30 long COVID patients treated with laser therapy and high-intensity electromagnetic stimulation for respiratory symptoms and chest pain. The treatment showed statistically significant improvements in chest pain, anxiety scores, and oxygen saturation levels.

Study of 49 patients with ophthalmic pathologies who previously had COVID-19, examining eye disorders to assess vascular and CNS effects and immunological responses post-infection. No specific treatment intervention tested; descriptive assessment of long COVID sequelae in ophthalmologic manifestations.

This retrospective study analyzes the correlation between circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants and chronic disease incidence in COVID-19 patients in the Dominican Republic (2020–2024). It examines genomic surveillance data and clinical records but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

This cross-sectional study used exploratory factor analysis to identify latent symptom dimensions in long COVID among 480 survey participants. The analysis revealed a three-factor model (General, PEM/Fatigue/Cognitive Dysfunction, and Psychological symptoms) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines immunological changes in 125 COVID-19 patients 1-4 months after recovery, measuring T-lymphocytes, B-lymphocytes, and circulating immune complexes using flow cytometry and ELISA. The study documents persistent immunological shifts post-COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective cross-sectional study compared endothelial function and inflammation markers in 109 recovered COVID-19 patients versus 50 healthy controls. The study found significantly lower flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) and elevated systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in post-COVID patients, suggesting persistent cardiovascular risk, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This paper proposes a 5-part classification system for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) based on a self-report survey dataset, distinguishing mild, moderate, and severe cases with overlap to ME/CFS criteria. It is a classification/consensus framework rather than an intervention trial or treatment evaluation.

This study examines age-dependent changes in immune markers in patients with comorbid post-COVID syndrome and gastric adenocarcinoma, exploring the inflammation-ageing-carcinogenesis pathway. The authors characterize dysregulation of innate immunity, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cascades in this patient population.

This retrospective study examined heart-type fatty acid binding protein (HFABP) as a predictor of myocardial injury severity and long-term cardiac function changes in COVID-19 patients over a two-year follow-up period. HFABP levels were significantly elevated in severe cases and predicted long-term cardiac dysfunction, suggesting it as a biomarker for COVID-related cardiac complications.

This cross-sectional study compared immune responses and post-COVID symptom development in 24 patients (unvaccinated, twice-vaccinated, and thrice-vaccinated) at 4 and 16 weeks following acute Omicron infection. The study found that vaccinated patients experienced prolonged disease and higher rates of post-COVID symptoms (60-78%) compared to unvaccinated patients (50%), with stronger autoantibody responses to G-protein coupled receptors correlating with POST-COVID risk.

This experimental study analyzes TNF-α and IFN-γ cytokine levels in monocytes from long COVID patients one month post-infection, comparing T2DM and non-T2DM groups. It is a mechanistic biomarker study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study compared serum biomarkers of oxidative and inflammatory stress in 25 post-COVID patients versus 25 healthy controls, finding elevated CRP, TNF-α, MDA, and uric acid alongside reduced vitamin D and antioxidant capacity in the patient group. The authors recommend vitamin D supplementation, antioxidant-rich diet, and aerobic exercise as interventions to reduce oxi-inflammatory stress in post-COVID populations.

This pilot study evaluated a brief inpatient rehabilitation program for 22 long COVID patients, measuring outcomes with the Barthel Index of ADL at admission, discharge, and pre-COVID baseline. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in motor, respiratory, and functional capacity from admission to discharge (Barthel Index 60.7→92.5, p<0.001), though patients did not fully return to baseline levels.

Doctoral thesis analyzing baseline data from the EXER-COVID cohort study, comparing physical condition, ventilatory efficiency, muscle strength, autonomic function, and oxidative metabolism in long COVID patients versus healthy controls. This is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Describes development of an adapted Autonomic Profile (aAP) home-based test for evaluating neuro-cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction in conditions including Long COVID. This is a methods/tool development paper with no treatment intervention or clinical trial results.

This paper describes a machine learning framework for identifying Long COVID articles in scientific literature using human-in-the-loop data programming and active learning. It does not study treatments or interventions but rather develops computational methods to classify and organize existing Long COVID research.

This study analyzes Twitter posts from long COVID patients to understand their emotional and mental well-being, classifying tweets by content and detecting six basic emotions. The analysis reveals that negative emotions dominated, with peaks during COVID variant outbreaks, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study uses machine learning algorithms to identify and predict persistent inflammatory biomarkers in 290 post-COVID-19 patients based on clinical data from Iraqi hospitals. While relevant to long COVID, the paper is a diagnostic/predictive modeling study without testing any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

This paper applies machine learning techniques to analyze and predict multi-organ dysfunction in 466 post-COVID patients from Iraq. It is a retrospective data analysis focused on model development for early detection, not a treatment study or clinical trial, and does not present original treatment outcomes or interventions.

A cross-sectional study of 913 post-COVID-19 patients in Iraq examining the prevalence and patterns of gastrointestinal symptoms during recovery. Machine learning analysis identified age, gender, disease severity, comorbidities, and illness duration as significant predictive factors for GI symptoms like diarrhea, abdominal pain, and nausea.

This paper presents a deep learning method for multimodal deformable image registration to align CT and MRI scans of long COVID patients' lungs. It is a technical methodology paper focused on imaging alignment rather than evaluating a treatment or clinical intervention for long COVID.

This paper develops an LLM framework for mining emerging health opinions from Reddit, using long COVID treatment discourse as a case study. It introduces the LC-Stance dataset for evaluating claim identification and stance detection tasks, but does not conduct an actual clinical trial or treatment study of long COVID patients.

This study performs statistical and predictive analysis on the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort to identify risk factors for long COVID intensity and develop predictive models. While the research is about long COVID, it is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data rather than a treatment trial or intervention study.

This paper develops and evaluates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for answering long COVID clinical questions, comparing different corpus configurations from expert guidelines to large literature databases. It is a methodological study of AI chatbot performance rather than a treatment trial or clinical study of patients.

This paper presents a computational framework for counterfactual inference to estimate individualized risk of PASC-related heart failure admissions and identify hypothetical intervention pathways. It is a methodological study applying predictive modeling and optimization algorithms to retrospective health system data, not a treatment trial testing interventions in patients.

This study develops S-MEDSeg, a deep learning method for automated segmentation of lung lesions in chest CT images, and applies it to long COVID inpatients. The research examines the effect of post-acute infection vaccination on the extent of lung findings in long COVID patients.

This paper presents UpTime, a wearable sensor metric calculated from ankle-mounted IMU devices, as an objective measure of disease severity in ME/CFS and Long COVID patients. The study compares UpTime measurements across 55 healthy controls, ME/CFS patients, and Long COVID patients over 7 days, finding that UpTime significantly distinguishes long COVID patients from controls, though it does not test any intervention or treatment.

This study examines challenges of returning to work for people with long COVID residual symptoms and explores occupational therapy's role in supporting clients. The research is descriptive/qualitative rather than an intervention trial testing a specific treatment.

This study evaluated the effect of Synaid, a combined nutraceutical with nootropic properties, on cognitive function and mood in 40 elderly patients with self-perceived cognitive decline following SARS-CoV-2 infection. After 3 months of treatment, Synaid significantly improved functional status, MMSE scores, and psychological parameters associated with mild cognitive impairment, with good tolerability.

This cross-sectional study used MR spectroscopy to examine brain metabolic changes in 11 long COVID patients with brain fog symptoms compared to 14 healthy controls. The study found changes in Glx and Lac concentrations suggesting an ischaemic background but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study develops and validates the LC risk score, a machine learning-based predictive tool to assess the risk of developing long COVID using data from 1,150 patients in the Polish STOP-COVID registry. The score identifies eight risk factors (female gender, age 40-49, BMI, hospitalization, arthralgia/myalgia, taste/smell loss, symptom duration ≥14 days, unvaccinated status) and achieves AUC=0.630 for predicting long COVID development.

Observational study of 142 post-COVID syndrome patients with musculoskeletal lesions, examining clinical presentation and treatment outcomes. Long-term administration of L-arginine, L-carnitine, and quercetin in rehabilitation improved treatment results for post-COVID arthropathy and related symptoms.

This is a case-control study comparing biochemical and cardiovascular markers between 33 children with PIMS-TS and 115 control children during the post-COVID recovery period. The study identifies predictive biomarkers but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a retrospective analysis of existing clinical data, not a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional study examining the frequency and role of anti-interferon α autoantibodies in 78 children with COVID-19 and long COVID. Found anti-IFN-α antibodies in 2.6% of all children and 3.4% of those with long COVID symptoms, suggesting potential biomarker relevance but requiring larger cohort studies for clinical significance.

This pre-test/post-test experimental study evaluated the effectiveness of osteopathic CV4 (fourth ventricle compression) technique on respiratory capacity in 20 post-COVID patients with mean age 23.3 years. The technique significantly improved FVC, FEV1, and PEF compared to baseline, though oxygen saturation changes were not statistically significant.

Cross-sectional study examining immune dysfunction and cancer risk in long COVID patients, finding elevated DAMP levels and altered NK/T cell populations in those with malignant lesions. The authors propose immunological screening tests to predict disease progression in patients with comorbid post-COVID syndrome and cancer.

This study evaluates detoxification nutritional support (specialized jelly) as a treatment for COVID-19 patients, including those with post-COVID symptoms. A survey of 283 people with prior coronavirus infection who received one month of detoxification nutritional support showed significant reduction in intoxication symptoms including weakness, fatigue, temperature fluctuations, and psychological symptoms.

Open-label case series of 25 post-COVID patients treated with a biologically active food supplement for 1 month to evaluate effectiveness for chronic fatigue syndrome. All patients showed improvement in fatigue scores (FAS scale), normalized inflammatory markers, and reported good tolerability with no adverse events.

This peer review report describes a mass spectrometry study detecting prolonged inflammatory responses in serum samples from asymptomatic and mildly affected COVID-19 patients 40-60 days post-infection. The paper is excluded because it is a peer review report (not a primary research article) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigated pulmonary and extrapulmonary causes of chronic cough in 58 post-COVID-19 patients in West Georgia, stratifying them into pulmonary (46.5%) and extrapulmonary (53.5%) groups. Spirometry and laboratory markers (CRP, H. pylori, IgE, Vitamin D3) revealed significant differences between groups, with pulmonary obstruction/restriction observed only in the pulmonary cough group.

This study investigates the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in post-COVID syndrome pathogenesis by comparing NET formation in hospitalized post-COVID patients, outpatient post-COVID patients, acute appendicitis patients, and healthy controls. The research aims to clarify the immunological mechanisms underlying post-COVID symptoms through molecular analysis of neutrophil activation.

This paper describes the development of an Electronic Register of post-COVID-19 patients in Moldova to monitor health status and quality of life outcomes. It presents a framework for assessing health indicators in COVID-19 survivors but does not report treatment intervention results or clinical trial data.

This is a peer review report (not a research article) evaluating a study on prolonged inflammatory responses detected via mass spectrometry in asymptomatic and mildly affected post-COVID patients. As a peer review document rather than primary research, it is excluded from the trial screening pipeline.

This study develops and evaluates machine learning models to predict mental health disorders and long COVID status among recovered COVID-19 patients using an existing dataset. The research does not involve testing or evaluating any treatment intervention, instead focusing on predictive modeling of long COVID prevalence and associated risk factors.

This cross-sectional study investigates immune dysregulation and endothelial dysfunction in post-COVID syndrome patients with cardiorespiratory symptoms, measuring cytokine profiles, lymphocyte subsets, and markers of microvascular dysfunction. The authors identify persistent pro-inflammatory activation and reduced regulatory immune activity associated with dyspnea, palpitations, and decreased exercise tolerance, suggesting immunological parameters as potential severity predictors.

This study characterizes cytokine imbalance and immune dysregulation in patients with cardiorespiratory post-COVID condition through clinical and immunological assessments. The findings demonstrate correlations between pro-inflammatory markers and symptoms like dyspnea and reduced exercise tolerance, but no intervention or treatment is evaluated.

A pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest study assessing the effectiveness of a self-instructional module on knowledge regarding management of post-COVID syndrome among 60 recovered patients. The intervention significantly increased knowledge scores from 13.50±1.80 to 19.58±2.22 (p<0.001), with associations found between knowledge improvement and education level, comorbidities, and comorbidity treatment.

Computational study integrating biomedical data to identify genes associated with SARS-CoV-2 host response and predict long-term systemic effects like vascular remodeling and fibrosis. Identifies candidate drugs targeting relevant pathways but does not evaluate any treatment in patients.

An uncontrolled case series of 33 long COVID patients treated with ivermectin at varying doses (0.2-0.4 mg/kg) for 2-4+ days. The study reports clinical improvement in 94% of patients and complete symptom resolution in 87.9% after initial dosing, with additional doses given to non-responders.

This study validates the SNP-PC19 scale, a new instrument for measuring neuropsychological and psychiatric symptoms in post-COVID-19 syndrome, in a sample of 53 participants 6-7 months post-infection. The scale demonstrated good psychometric properties, with fatigue/energy loss identified as the most prominent symptom and participants reporting an average of 9.4 symptoms of mild to moderate severity.

This paper examines hypertension and COPD comorbidities in acute COVID-19 patients during the active infection phase (2020-2021). It does not focus on long COVID or persistent post-infection sequelae, and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

A prospective uncontrolled study of 50 post-COVID patients who underwent 3 months of breathing exercises (diaphragmatic breathing, chest expansion, incentive spirometry, pranayama) and exercise testing. The intervention showed significant improvements in resting and post-exertion oxygen saturation and exercise capacity on 6-minute walk test.

This paper proposes a hypothesis that toxin-like peptides from gut bacteria may contribute to long COVID neurological symptoms, based on proteomic analysis of samples from COVID-19 patients. It presents mechanistic speculation and suggests antibiotics as a potential treatment but does not conduct any clinical trial or treatment evaluation.

This study characterizes cognitive abilities in patients with post-COVID cognitive symptoms, examining neurological disorders including cognitive, asthenic, vegetative and anxiety disorders. The research aims to understand long-term neurological effects of COVID-19 and their impact on quality of life and recovery.

This paper describes a cross-sectional clinical neurological examination of 358 post-COVID syndrome patients to characterize the distribution and presentation of neurological symptoms. The study identifies high prevalence of cognitive and psychoemotional dysfunction as complications of post-COVID syndrome but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

An uncontrolled case series of 33 long COVID patients treated with ivermectin at varying doses over 2-4+ days. The study reports 94% of patients showed clinical improvement and 87.9% achieved complete symptom resolution after initial treatment, with remaining patients reaching resolution after additional doses.

This cross-sectional study examines psychosomatic changes in patients following COVID-19 recovery, assessing how these changes impact daily quality of life. The research documents serious health consequences and calls for intervention programs and further research to prevent physical and mental health deterioration in post-COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study compared heart rate variability (HRV) measurements across three groups: participants with post-COVID syndrome (PCS), recovered COVID-19 patients, and never-infected controls (n=60, ages 18-45). The study found that PCS participants exhibited sympathetic nervous system dominance and autonomic dysfunction compared to controls, with significantly lower RMSSD and HF variables.

This paper evaluates neuroimaging results from MRI studies in post-COVID syndrome patients using statistical analysis. However, it appears to be a methods/protocol paper describing statistical approaches rather than reporting original trial data or treatment outcomes.

The paper proposes a predictive algorithm using clinical and laboratory indicators to identify patients at risk of developing long COVID after acute infection. It does not study any treatment or intervention, only risk stratification.

This cross-sectional study examines vestibular dysfunction and autonomic nervous system abnormalities in 82 post-COVID patients with chronic cerebral ischemia compared to healthy controls. The authors found that vestibular dysfunction in the post-COVID period develops with pathological autonomic characteristics and altered cerebrovascular reactivity, particularly in the subcompensated stage of chronic brain ischemia.

This study investigates autonomic nervous system function in 78 post-COVID syndrome patients (46 male, 32 female) compared to a control group over 4-12 weeks, measuring vegetative tone, vegetative reaction, and vegetative support of activity. The findings document local, generalized, permanent, and paroxysmal autonomic disorders in all post-COVID patients assessed.

A descriptive study of 53 post-COVID-19 patients enrolled in a Functional Recovery Program, evaluating functional capacity and self-care abilities. Found associations between hospitalization length, surgical history, and self-care capacity with impaired instrumental activities of daily living (IADL).

This cross-sectional study evaluated static balance and mobility deficits in 41 long COVID patients versus 32 controls using smartphone inertial sensors placed on the lower back. The study found greater postural instability in long COVID patients but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention—it is a diagnostic/assessment study without an intervention arm.

Cross-sectional study of 151 post-COVID patients examining how anxiety-depression symptoms impact cognitive performance using neuropsychological batteries. Findings show worse cognitive outcomes in patients with combined anxiety-depression symptoms compared to asymptomatic controls, particularly in language, memory, and executive function.

This study compared perivascular space (PVS) density on MRI between 392 long COVID patients and 212 healthy controls to investigate potential glymphatic dysfunction as a mechanistic pathway for neurological symptoms. Although PVS density was initially higher in COVID patients, the difference was not significant after controlling for age, suggesting PVS is not a reliable biomarker for long COVID.

This paper compares cognitive performance and plasma neuroinflammatory markers in long COVID patients versus healthy controls, supplemented with a mouse model study. It is a mechanistic/biomarker study without any treatment intervention, functioning as a secondary analysis of pre-existing cohorts.

This cross-sectional study assessed discourse impairments and inflammatory markers in 97 long COVID patients 3-8 months post-hospitalization, finding discourse deficits in 10-15% of participants. The study identified associations between poorer discourse performance and dysregulated immune responses, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive performance and peripheral inflammatory cytokine levels between 24 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment and 25 healthy controls. Results showed cognitive deficits in attention and memory domains in LC patients, accompanied by reduced peripheral cytokine levels, suggesting IL-4, IL-18, and TNF may predict long-term cognitive outcomes.

This paper describes the validation of the COVID Check-In (CCI), a patient-rated outcome measure co-designed for long COVID assessment within the DisCOVeRY integrated care model. The study presents preliminary psychometric analysis with a small sample (n=20) and indicates that further validation is ongoing (n=260), but no treatment outcomes or intervention results are reported.

A feasibility study of a 12-week outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program for long COVID patients in Brazil with 28 participants (82.1% adherence). The program resulted in significant improvements in exercise capacity, functional capacity, functional status, depressive symptoms, and dyspnea.

A one-group pre-test post-test study of 100 long COVID patients with pre-existing lifestyle diseases who completed an 8-week lifestyle modification program. The study found statistically significant improvements across multiple domains of health-related quality of life measured by SF-36, including general health, physical function, and social engagement.

This study examines psychological features (anxiety, temperament, empathy, personality type) in post-COVID syndrome patients across different age, gender, and social strata. The authors propose that psychological assessment and targeted interventions could help prevent neurotic manifestations and accelerate recovery from long COVID.

A cross-sectional study assessing CT scan findings in patients with post-acute COVID sequelae (PASC) at 3 months post-infection to evaluate lung injury and imaging patterns. The study characterizes radiological manifestations of long COVID-related pulmonary complications without testing a specific intervention or treatment.

Observational cross-sectional study comparing antibody profiles (IgG, IgM) and D-dimer levels in long COVID patients versus recovered controls to assess diagnostic and prognostic value. Study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely diagnostic/observational.

This paper uses causal inference models and graph neural networks to identify risk factors for post-COVID complications (kidney injury, arrhythmia, stroke) in COVID-19 survivors. It is a computational modeling study without testing any actual treatment interventions, and therefore does not constitute a treatment trial.

This paper uses a neuromachine learning model to analyze the effects of long-term COVID-19 on patients with pre-existing neurological disabilities. The study identifies fatigue and shortness of breath as persistent symptoms but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This paper analyzes the effects of long-term COVID-19 on patients with pre-existing neurological disabilities using a machine learning model. The study found that long COVID symptoms (physical fatigue, shortness of breath) persist regardless of demographic factors (race, age, gender, socioeconomic status).

This paper validates the Turkish version of the Modified COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRSm) as a measurement instrument for post-COVID syndrome symptoms and functional ability. It is a psychometric validation study of an assessment tool, not a treatment intervention trial.

This prospective study analyzed clinical manifestations of kidney injury in 62 patients with post-COVID sequelae, comparing acute versus chronic pathological patterns. Findings show that long-term kidney injury post-SARS-CoV-2 is characterized by diffuse endocapillary proliferation that can lead to chronic renal failure.

This study assesses the health status of ENT (ear, nose, throat) patients in the post-COVID period and identifies challenges faced by otolaryngologists and audiologists. It is a descriptive cross-sectional analysis of health outcomes in long COVID patients with ENT involvement, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This multicentre study evaluates the prevalence of pulmonary abnormalities on chest HRCT imaging 90 days after COVID-19 symptom onset in hospitalized patients. While it demonstrates high prevalence of radiographic abnormalities in post-COVID patients, it is a diagnostic/observational cross-sectional study with no intervention, treatment, or control group, and thus does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trial.

Describes development and validation of a respiratory pattern analysis software system for monitoring post-COVID patients. The paper is a technical/methodological report on a device prototype with no treatment intervention or patient outcomes data.

Retrospective analysis of autonomic function testing in long COVID patients with postural tachycardia syndrome and dysautonomia symptoms, comparing pre- and post-COVID autonomic test results. The study characterizes the presence of small fiber neuropathies in post-COVID autonomic dysfunction but does not test any treatment intervention.

This retrospective study analyzes brainstem auditory evoked potential (BAEP) test results in 18 post-COVID syndrome patients to investigate the pathophysiology of tinnitus, comparing latency values between those with and without tinnitus. The study found significantly increased wave V latency and III-V interval in tinnitus patients, suggesting prolonged conduction in the brainstem auditory pathway, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated neurological manifestations in 60 post-COVID syndrome patients using clinical assessments, neuroimaging, and neurophysiological studies. The most common symptoms were headaches (48.3%), cognitive impairment (41.6%), and sleep disorders (40%), with evidence of neuroinflammation and vascular dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study of 437 long COVID patients characterizes pain phenotypes (nociceptive, neuropathic, and central sensitization) and identifies associated risk factors. The study found that female sex, chronic diseases, lack of exercise, and pre-existing thyroid disease were significant risk factors for certain pain types.

This prospective case-control study compared histological changes in nasal olfactory epithelium biopsies from 20 post-COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction to 20 controls with non-COVID-related olfactory dysfunction. Both groups showed similar inflammatory and atrophic changes, with no significant histological differences, though post-COVID olfactory dysfunction persisted longer (6 vs 2 months).

This paper uses molecular docking and dynamics simulations to explore alpha-mangostin's potential as a Nrf2 inhibitor for long COVID treatment. It presents only computational predictions without any experimental validation or clinical trials.

A community service study providing psychological and social support to post-COVID-19 patients in Semarang, Indonesia to reduce anxiety and promote adaptive behavior. The intervention was effective in reducing anxiety levels among participants, with most being women and housewives.

This cross-sectional study measured D-dimer concentrations in 30 long COVID patients stratified by infection frequency (single, double, triple infection) and gender. The study found higher D-dimer levels in patients with multiple reinfections and in females, but this is a descriptive biomarker study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This paper reports retrospective and prospective studies examining the combined effects of COVID-19 and mTBI on chronic neurological symptoms, biomarkers, and disease mechanisms. The research demonstrates that combined infection and brain injury produces worse outcomes and provides mechanistic insights suggesting increased risk of neurodegeneration.

A cross-sectional immunophenotyping study comparing immune dysregulation in 26 post-COVID-19 vasculitis patients versus herpesvirus-associated vasculitis cases and healthy controls using flow cytometry. Post-COVID-19 vasculitis showed reduced regulatory T-cell frequencies and memory CD4+ T-cell expansion, with more severe dysregulation in patients aged 45-63 years.

This paper estimates the economic burden of long COVID in Australia using stock-and-flow modeling and labour market data analysis from 2021-2023. It does not study any treatment or intervention, instead focusing on prevalence estimates, economic costs, and societal impacts of long COVID.

This study evaluated post-COVID syndrome severity in 260 patients admitted for sanatorium-based rehabilitation, with 54 patients receiving additional aerophytotherapy (sage essential oil + audio-relaxation) and 181 receiving standard rehabilitation. Both groups showed improvements in clinical parameters and dyspnea measures, with the aerophytotherapy group demonstrating significant additional benefits for emotional well-being, vitality, and overall health status.

A modeling study estimating the prevalence of long COVID in Australia during 2022-2024 using SEIR and labor supply models. Projects that 310K-1.4M Australians had long COVID symptoms in September 2022, with an associated GDP loss of $9.6 billion, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This paper describes electrophysiological findings in 50 severe COVID-19 survivors discharged from ICU, identifying mononeuritis multiplex (multiple axonal mononeuropathies) in 16% of patients as a complication often initially misdiagnosed as critical illness neuromyopathy. The study characterizes the prevalence and clinical features of these focal neurological impairments in post-COVID recovery but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study evaluated the effectiveness of an 8-week home-based pulmonary rehabilitation program in 45 patients with pulmonary fibrosis, including post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis. The intervention significantly improved pulmonary function, exercise capacity, dyspnea, oxygen saturation, and quality of life.

This study compares brain activation patterns between long COVID patients (n=21) and healthy controls (n=20) using fMRI during cognitive tasks, finding greater activation in the precuneus and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex in COVID patients. The research investigates neurobiological mechanisms of long COVID symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study examines how search engine content ranking and individual COVID-19 fear influence online health research behavior (cyberchondria) when searching for long-term COVID-19 effects. It does not test any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study investigates cerebral venous oxygenation in post-COVID syndrome patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms, comparing them to convalescent COVID-19 controls. The researchers found that PCS patients had altered brain venous oxygenation that was associated with slower locomotion, suggesting cerebral microcirculation dysfunction as a potential mechanism underlying post-COVID neurological symptoms.

Pilot study using hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI to measure ventilation heterogeneity in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients. Found abnormal ventilation textures and patchy ventilation in PACS patients compared to healthy controls, but no significant longitudinal changes between 6- and 12-month timepoints.

This paper demonstrates a deep learning approach to accelerate 3D-PREFUL MRI ventilation imaging in post-COVID-19 patients by reconstructing images from undersampled data. It is a technical feasibility study on imaging methodology rather than an intervention trial, and appears to be a conference abstract without clinical outcomes.

This paper describes a cross-sectional imaging study using hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI to assess gas exchange impairment in 6 long COVID patients with dyspnea on exertion. The study is primarily a diagnostic/investigational imaging assessment rather than an intervention trial, and presents preliminary findings from a very small non-interventional cohort.

This study evaluates functional connectivity in elderly long COVID patients compared to controls using brain imaging focused on areas with reduced cerebrovascular reactivity. The results show significantly lower connectivity in long COVID patients, potentially linking vascular changes to cognitive dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study used dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI to assess pulmonary microvascular perfusion in COVID-19 survivors compared to healthy controls. The researchers found significantly reduced peak enhancement and slower contrast arrival in survivors, indicating persistent microvascular perfusion deficits months after initial infection, but this is a mechanistic imaging study without treatment intervention.

This study compared brainstem volumetric changes in long-COVID and ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls using neuroimaging. The abstract appears to be from a conference meeting and reports only preliminary findings without complete results or methodology details.

Retrospective analysis evaluating the feasibility of using hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI as a multi-site outcome measure in post-COVID-19 patients, comparing gas exchange imaging across three sites. Results show strong correlation with pulmonary function testing and support the use of this imaging technique in future multi-site trials.

This cross-sectional study used dynamic high temporal resolution free-breathing lung MRI to characterize respiratory patterns in post-acute COVID-19 patients with persistent cardiopulmonary symptoms. Post-acute COVID patients demonstrated larger tidal area, longer inspiration duration, and greater respiratory variability compared to baseline parameters.

This cross-sectional study used diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) to assess white matter microstructure in 20 participants with post-acute sequelae SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) at 6 months post-diagnosis. The findings showed lower white matter diffusivity in PASC participants that correlated with greater fatigue, suggesting possible glial proliferation and immune-related changes, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study compared lung water density (LWD) measurements via MRI in 187 COVID-recovered patients (5 months post-infection) versus 91 healthy controls. COVID-recovered patients showed significantly higher relative LWD values with abnormal local and global patterns, suggesting persistent pulmonary abnormalities post-COVID.

This preliminary study uses WEPCAST MRI to measure blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability in COVID-19 ICU survivors at 4 months post-infection. Results show significantly elevated BBB permeability-surface-area product (PS), providing evidence of BBB breakdown in severe long COVID survivors.

This study uses cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to analyze pulmonary perfusion in patients with previous COVID-19, investigating long-term cardiopulmonary sequelae. The findings show that older age and hospitalization are associated with worse pulmonary perfusion, suggesting impaired lung function as a long-term consequence of severe COVID-19.

This study compared brain structure and cognitive performance between long-COVID patients (>2 months symptoms) and normal recovery controls using MRI and neuropsychological testing. Despite detecting age-related effects, the study found no significant differences in white matter, brain volumes, or cognition between the two groups.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 65 COVID-19 patients with cardiac MRI to characterize suspected myocarditis as a post-acute sequela of COVID-19, using LGE and T1/ECV/T2 mappings to distinguish myocarditis cases. MRI strain analysis was found to be sensitive for detecting subclinical cardiac dysfunction in high-risk patients, but this is a diagnostic imaging study without any treatment intervention or therapeutic evaluation.

This cross-sectional study compared quantitative MRI findings in the lower limb muscles of 20 post-COVID-19 condition patients versus 20 matched controls. The study found no signs of inflammation or dystrophy but detected microstructural abnormalities suggesting possible deconditioning-related fiber changes, without testing any intervention.

This pilot study evaluates regional cerebral oxygen-extraction fraction (OEF) in COVID-19 ICU survivors compared to controls, finding elevated frontal OEF as a potential biomarker for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. The work investigates underlying mechanisms of PCS but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study uses 18F-FDG PET/CT brain imaging to investigate neural mechanisms underlying neuropsychiatric disorders in long COVID patients. The findings show significant reductions in metabolic levels in frontal, temporal, and parietal lobes and reduced metabolic connectivity between temporal and frontal networks, potentially explaining cognitive impairment in long COVID.

Longitudinal observational study using quantitative dynamic contrast enhanced MRI to assess pulmonary perfusion in 139 COVID-19 patients across acute (0-40d) and convalescent (91-365d) phases. Found associations between disease severity and perfusion abnormalities, particularly in patients with long-term complications, but the study is primarily methodological validation rather than treatment evaluation.

This study evaluates the repeatability of hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI measures of lung ventilation and gas exchange in long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea, fatigue, and neurocognitive symptoms. The findings suggest instability of pulmonary pathophysiology is characteristic of long COVID, but this is a methodology/validation study, not a treatment trial, and should be excluded from the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This study investigates cerebrovascular reactivity in long COVID patients using advanced CBV-based imaging (VASO at 3T) to compare vascular responses between patients and healthy volunteers. The research appears to be a preliminary or conference abstract examining potential biomarkers for long COVID diagnosis rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This study evaluates a transformer-based deep learning approach to improve image quality of radial undersampled lung MRI scans in post-COVID-19 patients. The method demonstrates significant image quality improvement but is a methodological/technical study without testing any therapeutic intervention for long COVID symptoms.

This study evaluates 129Xe MRI ventilation texture features as predictors of quality-of-life improvements in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients over 15 months. It is an observational study without intervention assignment that focuses on imaging biomarkers rather than treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the intervention trials dataset.

This study uses parahydrogen-polarized 13C MRI to detect brain metabolic alterations in an immune fatigue mouse model that mimics post-infection cognitive impairments. The work is preclinical research in animals without human subjects or treatment intervention, serving as a preliminary biomarker investigation rather than a clinical trial.

This MRI study compares brain structural anatomy and oxygen metabolism between long-COVID patients, ME/CFS patients, and healthy controls. While the study found reduced venous oxygenation in long-COVID patients compared to controls, it is a diagnostic/mechanistic cross-sectional study without any treatment intervention or comparison of therapeutic outcomes.

This study investigates white matter alterations in long COVID patients experiencing brain fog using advanced MRI metrics and voxel-wise analysis. It is an observational imaging study with no treatment intervention, appearing to be a conference abstract presenting preliminary findings rather than a completed study.

This cross-sectional study uses multimodal quantitative MRI (qMRI) to investigate the neurobiological mechanisms underlying long COVID symptoms (fatigue, anosmia, cognitive dysfunction). MRI metrics correlating with these symptoms suggest changes in neurite density, brain stem volume, mean diffusivity, and magnetic susceptibility are associated with persistent long COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study uses MR spectroscopy to investigate neurochemical alterations in the orbitofrontal cortex of 54 subjects with COVID-induced anosmia compared to healthy controls. The study found decreased NAA, Cho, and Cr levels in the brain OFC region correlated with anosmia duration and severity, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional fMRI study compares brain activity during cognitive tasks (Stroop test) in 19 long COVID patients versus 16 healthy controls using 7 Tesla imaging and independent component analysis. The study identifies widespread deficits in BOLD activity and sensorimotor changes in long COVID but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared brain MRI volumes in 29 long COVID patients with neurological symptoms (neuroPASC) to 29 matched controls using ultrahigh field 7T imaging. Results showed significantly decreased volumes in limbic structures (hippocampal subfields and amygdala subnuclei) in COVID patients, with sex-based differences observed.

This cross-sectional study uses proton MR spectroscopy to investigate neurobiological mechanisms of post-COVID fatigue, focusing on mitochondrial dysfunction in the posterior cingulate gyrus. The study finds reduced antioxidants and neuronal activity in post-COVID fatigue patients, suggesting persistent dysregulation of mitochondrial homeostasis.

This neuroimaging study uses graph theory analysis and fMRI to characterize brain network alterations in acute COVID-19 patients with fatigue and explore mechanisms linking to chronic symptoms. However, it appears to be a conference abstract presenting preliminary findings without complete clinical trial data or treatment intervention.

Multisite study using advanced MRI modalities (MRS, diffusion MRI, pCASL, T2 FLAIR) to investigate neurochemical, microstructural, and perfusion changes in long-COVID patients. Findings show long-lasting effects primarily in the brainstem, midbrain, and diencephalon, without overt white matter pathology.

This study investigates neuroinflammatory imaging markers in PASC patients using multi-shell diffusion MRI to identify potential biomarkers for long COVID. The research demonstrates altered diffusion parameters in PASC patients consistent with axonal injury and inflammation, but appears to be an imaging biomarker discovery study without clinical treatment intervention or outcomes.

This article presents a framework for explainable clinical decision support systems tailored to post-COVID care, integrating interpretable predictive modelling and uncertainty-aware inference. It is a methodological/architectural paper proposing an approach rather than reporting empirical trial results or treatment outcomes.

This study investigates functional brain network organization in adults 6-12 months post-COVID-19 pneumonia using graph theory analysis of the default mode network. The researchers found reduced functional integration within the DMN, particularly in brain areas involved in memory processing, providing insights into the neuropathology underlying long COVID neurological symptoms.

This cross-sectional study uses quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) to compare iron accumulation in the basal ganglia of long COVID patients with neurological symptoms versus recovered COVID-19 patients and uninfected controls. The study identifies elevated iron levels in the putamen and caudate nucleus of long COVID patients, proposing a potential biomarker for understanding neurological long COVID rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study used dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI to assess lung perfusion deficits in adults previously hospitalized with COVID-19. The research found significant correlations between MRI perfusion parameters and prior hospitalization severity, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study used advanced MR perfusion imaging (3D pCASL) to assess brain perfusion abnormalities in 30 elderly long COVID patients compared to 28 controls, all with mild initial infection. The study found prolonged arterial transit time and reduced cerebral blood flow in long COVID patients, correlating with cognitive deficits more than one year post-infection.

This paper develops an automated deep learning framework for analyzing respiratory motion patterns in lung MRI to classify post-COVID patients by symptom severity. The work presents a diagnostic/analytical tool rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluates 129Xe lung ventilation imaging in 60 long COVID patients (with and without dyspnea) and 20 controls to assess abnormal lung ventilation. The majority of long COVID patients showed normal ventilation imaging, though a subset with dyspnea had ventilation defects despite normal pulmonary function tests.

This cross-sectional study investigates pulmonary perfusion abnormalities in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome using phase-resolved functional lung MRI, comparing 44 PACS patients to 43 healthy controls. While it identifies significant perfusion defects in PACS patients, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This MRI study investigates neurobiological features of long-COVID using a multimodal protocol to measure iron accumulation, myelin content, inflammation, and microstructural alterations in the brain. Machine learning classification identified myelin alterations as a distinguishing feature of long-COVID compared to controls and recovered individuals, suggesting potential myelin involvement in long-COVID pathophysiology.

This study investigates blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction in post-acute COVID-19 patients using advanced MRI techniques (DP-pCASL) to measure water exchange rates. The researchers found reduced water exchange across the BBB in post-acute COVID-19 participants compared to controls, suggesting glymphatic system dysfunction may underlie persistent neurological symptoms.

This study uses 7T MRI to investigate hippocampal subfield volumes in long COVID and ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls. The researchers found that hippocampal subfield volumes were atypically larger in long COVID and ME/CFS patients, suggesting potential neurological differences that may inform understanding of both conditions.

This study investigates the neurobiological mechanisms underlying fatigue and cognitive dysfunction in long COVID using multimodal MRI in healthy controls, COVID-recovered individuals, and long COVID patients. Results show white matter and cerebellar microstructural alterations and iron-myelin dysregulation correlate with fatigue and cognitive impairment symptoms.

This study examines chronic cerebral blood flow deficits in COVID-19 ICU survivors using advanced imaging to compare vessel architecture and perfusion between COVID-19 survivors, non-COVID ICU survivors, and healthy controls. The findings suggest reduced capillary blood flow is associated with acute coagulation during ICU stay, but the study appears to be a conference abstract without complete results presentation.

This study examines brain network organization in long COVID patients during the acute phase using functional neuroimaging analysis. While it identifies differences in brain integration and segregation associated with fatigue, it is a neurobiological characterization study rather than a treatment trial and should be excluded as a protocol/preliminary analysis from a conference meeting.

This study uses a pseudo-infectious mouse model (polyI:C-induced) to investigate brain metabolic changes via hyperpolarized 13C MRI, not actual long COVID patients or human subjects. While the motivation references long-lasting symptoms after RNA virus infections, the research is purely preclinical animal work without any human intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study investigates the relationship between chronic inflammation, white matter microstructure, and cognitive deficits in long-COVID patients using DTI/NODDI imaging and blood markers. The authors found elevated inflammation markers and white matter alterations correlated with cognitive deficits, but this is a conference abstract presenting preliminary mechanistic findings without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This pilot study uses MRI (WEPCAST) to measure blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability in ME/CFS patients with and without PASC and healthy controls. The researchers found significantly higher BBB permeability in classic non-PASC ME/CFS compared to PASC ME/CFS and controls, providing imaging evidence of neuroinflammation in ME/CFS pathophysiology.

This is a conference abstract presenting preliminary QSM neuroimaging results comparing long-COVID patients to controls, measuring susceptibility changes in white matter and subcortical gray matter. The work appears to be an early-stage study or technical validation without complete results or peer-reviewed publication status.

This study compares resting-state fMRI brain activity (fALFF) in the default mode network between 29 PASC patients, 27 non-PASC controls, and 31 healthy controls. The findings show that alterations in different frequency bands of brain activity are associated with cognitive and depressive symptoms in PASC patients, but this is observational characterization without testing any intervention or treatment.

This study compares hippocampal volumetric data from MRI imaging between post-COVID-19 patients with cognitive impairment and healthy controls using Freesurfer segmentation. Patients with post-COVID condition showed reduced bilateral hippocampal volume in most regions of the hippocampal body compared to controls, suggesting structural brain alterations associated with neurocognitive impairment.

This cross-sectional study used quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) imaging to assess magnetic susceptibility in subcortical brain regions, comparing PASC patients with recovered individuals and COVID-naive controls. PASC patients showed elevated iron accumulation in the right hippocampus, caudate, and putamen, identifying potential biomarkers for PASC-related neurological impairment, but the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This prospective cohort study validates CoreFA, a data-driven MRI-derived imaging marker, for detecting white matter changes in long COVID patients and correlates it with [18F]FEPPA PET neuroinflammatory markers. The study demonstrates that CoreFA has high diagnostic accuracy (AUC=0.81-0.77) and shows strong correlation with neuroinflammation in brain regions with reduced white matter integrity.

A longitudinal neuroimaging study using proton MRS to investigate neurochemical changes in the posterior cingulate gyrus of 10 post-COVID CFS/ME patients at two time points. While neuronal activity showed recovery over time, clinical fatigue symptoms persisted and markers of mitochondrial dysfunction remained unchanged, suggesting dissociation between neurochemical and clinical recovery.

This study measures regional cerebral oxygen extraction fraction in ME/CFS patients with and without long COVID using QSM venography, comparing results to healthy controls. The researchers found significantly lower oxygenation in the straight sinus of PASC patients, suggesting altered oxygen metabolism in deep brain regions.

This study evaluates hybrid CMR/FDG-PET imaging as a diagnostic tool to detect and classify myocardial injury in long COVID patients. The abstract presents feasibility results showing injury classification in 32 patients but appears to be a conference abstract without full study results or longitudinal outcome data.

This cross-sectional study uses MRI χ-separation imaging to assess iron accumulation and myelin integrity in 132 subjects across three groups: no COVID (n=41), mild COVID (n=33), and long COVID (n=58). While the study identifies significant differences in susceptibility and R2* values in white matter regions that may serve as biomarkers for COVID-related brain involvement, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study uses MRI spectroscopy to measure GABA and GLX levels in the rostral anterior cingulate cortex of post-COVID-19 patients compared to controls. The findings show elevated GABA levels associated with depression severity and reduced excitation-inhibition balance, suggesting potential biomarkers for neuropsychiatric sequelae, but no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

This study measures xenon-129 MRI biomarkers (RBC chemical shift, RBC T2*, M T2*) in COVID-19 hospitalized patients with and without residual lung abnormalities at 6 months and 1 year post-infection. The results show that RBC chemical shift correlates with diffusion abnormalities and may be a sensitive marker for monitoring gas transfer deficits in post-COVID lung disease.

This study examines cardiac findings in post-COVID syndrome patients presenting with palpitations using Holter monitoring. It is a descriptive cross-sectional assessment of cardiac function rather than an intervention study.

This cross-sectional study investigates the relationship between acute inflammation/coagulation markers during COVID-19 ICU stay and post-COVID neurofluid dynamics (BOLD-CSF coupling) in ICU survivors. Results show weaker post-COVID BOLD-CSF coupling correlates with higher inflammation and hypercoagulation markers, suggesting these acute phase factors may impair cerebral waste clearance mechanisms in long COVID.

This cross-sectional study examined 29 post-COVID syndrome patients alongside comparison groups to assess the psychiatric and environmental factors underlying their symptoms. The study found that post-COVID syndrome has predominantly psychogenic etiology with leading anxiety spectrum disorders, suggesting that long-term anxiety exposure causes cognitive dysfunction and psychosomatic pathology.

Systematic pathological study of lung tissue from 43 COVID-19 patients at late stages (>28 days post-symptom onset), examining histopathologic features, imaging, and persistent SARS-CoV-2 RNA. Findings show acute lung injury and fibrotic changes persist for months, with RNA detectable up to 174 days after infection onset, supporting the concept of long COVID as a post-acute complication.

Retrospective observational study comparing transbronchial biopsy findings in 18 long COVID patients (9 immunocompetent, 9 immunocompromised) versus 28 control patients with organizing pneumonia. Found long COVID patients had lower inflammation but higher fibrotic remodeling, with SARS-CoV-2 RNA detectable in some tissue samples.

This cross-sectional study assessed pituitary hormone abnormalities in 25 long COVID patients one month after COVID-19 infection using hormone level testing and glucagon stimulation tests. Findings showed 12% had growth hormone deficiency, 8% had cortisol abnormalities, and pituitary dysfunction correlated with fatigue severity, providing evidence that SARS-CoV-2 affects the pituitary gland.
