The study finds declining renal function at follow-up with altered cytokine levels, particularly elevated TGF-β in patients with kidney involvement, suggesting a potential manifestation of long COVID.

Prospective cohort study following 233 hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia patients for 12 months post-discharge, stratified by ventilation severity, measuring clinical symptoms, radiological findings, and pulmonary function. Most symptoms resolved by month 12, though brain fog, memory loss, and anosmia/dysgeusia persisted in some patients, and CT abnormalities remained common despite normalized pulmonary function in most cases.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment on post-acute COVID-19 symptoms beyond 3 months using propensity score matching on 12,245 matched pairs. Early NMV-r treatment reduced hospitalization and ER visits but did not significantly reduce post-acute COVID-19 symptoms or mortality risk.

This retrospective cohort study of 2.4 million patients examines the long-term risk of herpes zoster (HZ) infection following COVID-19 recovery, finding a significantly elevated HZ risk in the COVID-19 cohort (HR 1.59) over 12 months. The study does not test a treatment intervention but rather observes the natural epidemiological association between COVID-19 and HZ risk.

Prospective longitudinal study tracking hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 24 months to examine post-COVID symptoms and inflammatory markers. Findings show 37-39% of patients had persistent symptoms associated with prolonged inflammation, which gradually resolved by 24 months post-infection and after vaccination.

Large-scale retrospective study examining prevalence and risk factors for long COVID 6-12 months after Omicron infection in 6,242 nonhospitalized patients in Hong Kong. Found 55% reported long COVID symptoms with fatigue most common; identified female gender, middle age, obesity, comorbidities, and specific acute-phase symptoms as significant risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study using propensity score matching to evaluate whether nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment reduces the long-term risk of neuropsychiatric sequelae in nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients. Treatment with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir was associated with significantly reduced risks of neuropsychiatric complications including dementia, depression, insomnia, and anxiety disorder during the 90-day to 1-year follow-up period.

Prospective cohort study evaluated Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) effects on long COVID risk in 647 high-risk COVID-19 patients followed 6 months post-discharge. Paxlovid treatment was associated with reduced long COVID incidence and lower COPD assessment test scores compared to untreated patients.

This study examines the prevalence of neutralizing autoantibodies against type I interferons in a Danish cohort of 279 long COVID patients compared to 94 controls with mild COVID-19. The findings show that anti-type I IFN autoantibodies are rare and no more prevalent in long COVID patients than controls, suggesting they are unlikely to drive long COVID symptoms.

This study compares semen parameters before and after COVID-19 diagnosis in 114 patients and a control group to assess the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on male reproductive function. The findings show significant decreases in semen volume and sperm quality post-infection, with fever during acute infection being a negative risk factor, but this focuses on acute COVID-19 effects rather than long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions.

Retrospective cohort study examining the effect of oral antiviral agents (nirmatrelvir-ritonavir and molnupiravir) on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) in nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients over 30 days to 1 year. While the study shows antivirals reduced MACE risk, it focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes and prevention of short-term cardiovascular complications, not long COVID treatment or sequelae.

This comparative study assessed retinal and vitreous alterations in 38 participants before and after COVID-19 infection using swept-source OCT and angiography, with follow-up imaging at 1 and 3 months post-infection. Findings showed significant retinal changes including ganglion cell thinning, vascular density alterations, and vitreous hyper-reflective dots in 71.1% of patients, suggesting direct or indirect virus-induced ocular injury.

Retrospective cohort study of 30,892 COVID-19 patients examining the association between nutritional deficiency anemia (NDA) and post-acute sequelae using propensity score matching. Patients with NDA had significantly higher risk of post-COVID-19 condition, all-cause hospitalization, and mortality during 90-180 day follow-up.

This Polish Long-Covid Cardiovascular study observational analysis examined clinical and electrocardiographic correlates of myocardial dysfunction in 448 nonhospitalised post-COVID patients. The study identified QRS fragmentation, arrhythmias, and male gender as independent predictors of myocardial dysfunction but did not test any treatment or intervention.

Observational cohort study of 1,611 vaccinated individuals examining whether nirmatrelvir treatment during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces subsequent Long COVID risk. Treatment was not associated with reduced Long COVID symptoms at 5.4 months (OR: 1.15, p = 0.45), and viral rebound after treatment was not associated with Long COVID symptoms.

Multicenter cross-sectional study measuring the prevalence of orthostatic intolerance and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (PoTS) in 277 long COVID clinic patients versus 50 healthy volunteers using standardized NASA Lean Test. Found 52% of long COVID patients developed OI symptoms during testing and 15% had abnormal test results, but the study is purely descriptive/diagnostic with no treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study investigated the prevalence and risk of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in COVID-19 survivors compared to uninfected controls using data from the US TriNetX network over 12 months. COVID-19 patients showed significantly increased OSA risk at 3 months (HR: 1.51) and 1 year (HR: 1.57) follow-up, with consistent elevations across age, sex, and racial subgroups.

A retrospective cohort study of 211 COVID-19 patients (vaccinated and unvaccinated) examining the impact of early antibiotic therapy on acute phase recovery and long COVID development. Early antibiotic initiation was associated with significantly shorter recovery time (HR=4.74) and a notable reduction in long COVID development among patients treated within 3 days.

Prospective cohort study following 762 COVID-19 survivors at 2-year and 613 at 3-year follow-up to assess persistent symptoms, respiratory impairment, and quality of life. Found persistent symptoms (39.8% at 3 years) including fatigue and shortness of breath, with stable pulmonary function impairment and radiographic abnormalities over time, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This retrospective cohort study examines cerebrovascular disease risk in COVID-19 survivors stratified by prior vaccination status using propensity score matching. The study does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention for long COVID patients, but rather compares outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated cohorts using existing data.

This retrospective study of 1,349 post-COVID syndrome patients investigates risk factors for inappropriate sinus tachycardia (IST), a manifestation of PCS occurring 12-16 weeks after acute infection. The authors identify insulin resistance (measured by triglyceride/HDL ratio) as a significant risk factor for IST development but do not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir (NMV-r) effectiveness in reducing short-term adverse outcomes and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in high-risk pediatric patients aged 12-18 years using propensity score matching. NMV-r treatment significantly reduced hospitalization, ED visits, and mortality in the initial 30 days but showed non-significant reductions in PASC symptoms during the 30-180 day follow-up period.

Multinational propensity-matched cohort study examining the risk of cutaneous immune-related adverse events in long COVID patients across South Korea, Japan, and the UK using national claims-based data. Found increased cirAE risk in long COVID (HR 1.10) that was attenuated by COVID-19 vaccination, particularly with multiple doses or heterologous regimens.

Binational population-based cohort study examining the risk of alopecia areata following SARS-CoV-2 infection using claims data from South Korea and Japan. Found that SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with increased AA risk (aHR 1.66), with effects persisting up to 6 months and modulated by COVID-19 severity and vaccination status.

This matched case-control study investigated risk factors for post-coronavirus disease (PCC) condition among Japanese adults across different COVID-19 variants, comparing 4,185 infected individuals with 3,382 noninfected controls. The study found PCC prevalence was 15.0% in infected cases, with female sex, comorbidities, and hospitalization as positive risk factors, while vaccination was inversely associated with PCC, especially in Alpha and Delta waves.

This longitudinal cohort study examines associations between monoclonal antibody therapy or COVID-19 vaccination and symptom resolution in COVID-19 patients over 9 months (April 2021–January 2022). The study does not focus on long COVID per se but rather on acute symptom recovery in the general COVID-19 population, and it is observational (non-interventional) rather than testing a specific treatment protocol.

This study follows 366 maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients for 12 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to characterize long COVID prevalence and risk factors in this high-risk population. The researchers found that 78% of MHD patients developed long COVID, identified risk factors for development and persistence, and showed that >80% of symptoms resolve within one year, with a critical turning point at 6 months.

This retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data evaluated whether COVID-19 vaccination reduces the development of long COVID (PASC) and mortality in patients aged ≥65 years. Vaccinated patients showed significantly lower incidence of PASC symptoms (HR=0.852) and all-cause mortality (HR=0.231) compared to unvaccinated matched controls during 30-180 days follow-up.

This study examined antibody responses to common viruses in 1,083 individuals from a population-based cohort, comparing responses across COVID-19 severity and PASC status. While it identifies associations between viral antibody levels and PASC (particularly neuropsychiatric PASC), it is an observational cross-sectional study without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

Prospective observational cohort study identifying metabolomic biomarkers in serum samples from COVID-19 patients that predict pulmonary fibrotic sequelae one year after hospitalization. Found glucose, valine, and fatty acids as potential biomarkers with 80.82% sensitivity and 72.22% specificity for distinguishing patients who develop radiological pulmonary fibrosis.

This retrospective cohort study using TriNetX EHR data examined whether Paxlovid use during acute COVID-19 reduces stroke and mortality risk in the long COVID period (>90 days post-diagnosis). Among 181,992 matched pairs, Paxlovid use was associated with significantly reduced risk of ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke (HR 0.85) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.68), with consistent benefits across age, sex, and comorbidity subgroups.

The VIPER study compared SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection in plasma, stool, urine, and nasopharyngeal samples between 57 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID symptoms and 55 matched controls without symptoms at 2 years post-infection. RNA was detected in only 5.2% of nasopharyngeal samples in the post-COVID group and no samples in controls, and was not found in plasma, stool, or urine, suggesting no association between viral persistence in these compartments and post-COVID symptomatology.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (NMV-r), an oral antiviral for acute COVID-19, reduces long COVID risk using propensity score-matched data from the TriNetX network. Overall, NMV-r use was not associated with reduced long COVID risk, though symptom-specific analyses showed mixed effects.

This population-based cohort study from South Korea examines the association between pre-existing mental illness and the risk of postacute sequelae of COVID-19 across 12 health domains and 141 specific diseases. While it identifies significantly elevated risks in individuals with mental illness, it is a secondary epidemiological analysis without testing any specific treatment or intervention.

A prospective cohort study following 649 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors in Brazil for 12 months to assess health-related quality of life using EQ-5D-3L. The study found impaired HRQoL (median score 0.69) and 13.4% mortality at one year, with older age, comorbidities, and need for oxygen therapy associated with worse outcomes.

A retro-prospective study evaluating the incidence and characteristics of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and other autonomic dysfunctions in 793 long COVID patients from an Asian primary care setting. Found POTS incidence of 0.1% and autonomic dysfunction in 1.5% of patients, with fatigue and dyspnea on exertion as common symptoms.

Prospective cohort study comparing persistent symptoms in SARS-CoV-2-infected versus non-infected household members at 6 and 12 months post-infection. Found infected adults had higher prevalence of respiratory symptoms and fatigue, with persistent symptoms associated with reduced quality of life and increased anxiety/depression, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

A prospective observational cohort study monitoring lung ultrasound changes in 24 patients recovering from acute COVID-19 over 20 weeks. While the paper tracks recovery trajectories of respiratory abnormalities, it focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not test any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study used the National COVID Cohort Collaborative to evaluate the association between malnutrition and post-acute COVID-19 sequelae in 4.3 million individuals. While it addresses long COVID outcomes, it is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data examining risk factors rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This binational population-based cohort study examined the association between post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 and alopecia areata (AA) among individuals with mental illness using Korean and Japanese national health databases. The study found an elevated risk of AA onset following COVID-19 infection, particularly in those with mild mental illness and within 6 months post-infection, but this is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data without testing or evaluating any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 100 COVID-19 patients tracking olfactory function over 1 year using smell identification tests and symptom surveys. Found that 75% had baseline smell loss, declining to 40% at 1 month and persisting in 29% at 1 year, with phantosmia as a predictor of worse olfactory outcomes.

This retrospective cohort study using propensity score matching from the TriNetX database examines whether COVID-19 infection increases the risk of subsequent chronic rhinosinusitis diagnosis. While the paper documents a post-COVID association with CRS development, it does not study a treatment intervention and falls outside the scope of long COVID clinical trials.

Retrospective analysis of 100 long COVID patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction, examining clinical factors affecting smell recovery using standardized testing and quality-of-life measures. Found that impaired nasal airflow and aeroallergen sensitivity negatively influence olfactory performance, but the study does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Longitudinal observational cohort study of 190 patients with post-COVID olfactory dysfunction followed over 24 months with quantitative testing (Sniffin' Sticks TDI) and parosmia assessment. Study describes prevalence of parosmia (73.7%), associated QoL impact, and modest improvements in olfactory scores over time, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This retrospective study examines anosmia (loss of smell) recovery rates in acute COVID-19 patients over 4-8 weeks post-infection. While it identifies factors associated with recovery (smoking, ageusia, headache, nasal discharge), it focuses on acute infection outcomes rather than long COVID sequelae.

A case-control study comparing smell and taste disorders in 99 post-COVID-19 patients with simple olfactory/gustatory complaints and 81 with complex multi-symptom post-COVID syndrome against 148 matched non-COVID post-infectious controls. The study found post-COVID cases had lower anosmia prevalence, higher overall smell scores, and more frequent parosmia/phantosmia, with greater quality-of-life impact in simple cases.

Multicenter real-life study comparing combined corticosteroid + olfactory training versus olfactory training alone versus no treatment for persistent COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction in 44 patients. Combined treatment improved both olfactory threshold-discrimination-identification score and patient-perceived smell, while olfactory training alone improved test scores but not perceived function.

This study examines semen quality and immune factors in 781 infertile men who recovered from COVID-19, tracking changes at different time points post-infection. Findings show temporary decreases in sperm parameters in the first month that reversed by month three, with no direct treatment intervention studied.

This paper examines blood gas composition in patients with pulmonary hypertension and chronic heart failure following COVID-19. While it mentions COVID-19 as a precipitant, the study focuses on acute cardiopulmonary complications rather than long COVID syndrome (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

Retrospective cohort study of 81 patients presenting with upper aerodigestive complaints (dysphonia, dysphagia, sore throat) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with characterization of symptoms and natural history. The study describes clinical presentations and outcomes but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

Retrospective cohort study examining thrombotic and surgical complications in microsurgical reconstruction patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus matched controls. Finds COVID-19 associated with increased postoperative complications and flap loss, but this is not a long COVID study—it focuses on acute/early post-infection surgical outcomes rather than persistent long COVID symptoms or treatments for long COVID patients.

This single-center observational cohort study examined the association between new sleep disturbance at 1-month post-COVID-19 hospitalization and cognitive impairment at 6-months in 120 survivors. The findings show that 74% of participants with new sleep disturbance developed significant worsening in cognitive function compared to 40% without sleep disturbance.

Prospective follow-up study tracking overactive bladder symptom progression in 26% COVID-positive participants over 12 months post-infection. Most participants showed symptom resolution to baseline levels, though a subset maintained persistent symptoms suggesting potential long COVID-related urological effects.

Retrospective cohort study comparing neurological and psychiatric sequelae in 388 COVID-19 patients versus 149 flu patients, with symptom onset tracked over time. Study characterizes neuro-PASC prevalence and risk factors (female sex, older age) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and anatomical location of musculoskeletal pain in individuals post-COVID-19 hospitalization, with analysis of associations between pain and fatigue, physical activity, and other clinical factors. Finds musculoskeletal pain significantly more prevalent in long COVID patients (56.3%) compared to general population (34%), highlighting need for targeted rehabilitation strategies.

Observational study tracking lingering COVID-19 symptoms in 284 adult survivors across two cohorts (2020-2021 and 2021-2022) from a mid-Michigan COVID registry. Found that 47-66% remained symptomatic ≥3 months post-diagnosis, with females reporting significantly higher symptom burden than males, but no significant effect of time since diagnosis on symptom experience.

This cross-sectional study compares resting-state fMRI brain networks and neuropsychological performance between 42 long-COVID patients with cognitive complaints and 43 matched healthy controls. The study found significant differences in network efficiency and cognitive test scores but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Population-based cross-sectional study examining the association between BMI and recovery outcomes in 11,296 long COVID patients from Germany. Higher BMI was associated with impaired general health and working capacity recovery, and increased prevalence of fatigue, cognitive impairment, and chest symptoms.

Prospective multicenter cohort study of 1,009 COVID-19 patients examining upper respiratory symptoms (taste and olfactory disorders) as manifestations of long COVID in Japan. The study identifies risk factors for persistent taste/olfactory symptoms at 3 months and their impact on quality of life, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This retrospective descriptive study characterizes long COVID prevalence and demographic patterns among 31.8 million US Medicare beneficiaries from April 2020 to May 2022. It found ~194,000 post-COVID diagnoses with higher rates in nursing home residents, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective cohort study examining lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in patients hospitalized with acute COVID-19, assessing prevalence, clinical course, and associations with vaccination status. While symptoms were tracked post-discharge, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization rather than long COVID sequelae, and makes no mention of post-acute or persistent long-term complications beyond 3 months.

Prospective cohort study comparing functional outcomes and follow-up care utilization in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls 90 days after discharge from inpatient rehabilitation. COVID-19 patients showed similar functional improvements to controls and fewer readmissions, but this is a secondary/comparative analysis of rehabilitation outcomes rather than a treatment intervention study.

Retrospective cohort study comparing COVID-19 and post-COVID outcomes between people with MS, SCI, or TBI and matched controls. Found no difference in mortality but increased risk of weakness, mobility difficulties, and cognitive dysfunction in the disabled group.

Prospective cohort study tracking functional recovery and fatigue in 92 COVID-19 survivors at 1 and 6 months post-hospitalization. Found that while 50-79% of patients with new impairments at 1 month partially or fully recovered by 6 months, 21-50% did not recover, with lower socioeconomic status and age ≥65 associated with worse outcomes.

Retrospective chart review of 23 children with long COVID examined using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to identify mechanisms of exertional symptoms and exercise intolerance. Found 47% had decreased exercise capacity from various causes including deconditioning, body habitus limitations, and bronchospasm, but this is a diagnostic/assessment study without treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 82 adolescents with persistent pulmonary symptoms ≥4 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed for ~6.5 months. Describes clinical phenotypes (inhaled corticosteroid responsiveness, paradoxical vocal fold motion, deconditioning, dysautonomia) and identifies risk factors (obesity, anxiety, female sex) associated with reduced exercise tolerance and dyspnea.

This observational study followed 41 children hospitalized with COVID-19 pneumonia, assessing pulmonary sequelae at 3 and 6 months post-discharge through clinical assessment, lung ultrasound, and pulmonary function tests. While 17% of children reported persistent symptoms including decreased exercise tolerance and dyspnea, this is a natural history/surveillance study without any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study comparing lung function and ultrasound patterns in 28 children with long COVID versus 30 asymptomatic controls at median 4.5 months post-infection. Found no differences in lung function or structural abnormalities, but long COVID patients showed lower FeNO values, suggesting a potential biomarker role.

Retrospective cohort study comparing lung function in asthmatic children with and without acute COVID-19 infection. Finds that obesity is a risk factor for small airway dysfunction (FEF25-75 decline) after acute infection, but no significant effects on overall lung function measures.

This study analyzes the prevalence of pulmonary hypertension in COVID-19 related lung disease patients listed for lung transplantation using UNOS registry data. While it examines acute respiratory complications from COVID-19, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent post-infection symptoms) and is not a treatment intervention study.

Prospective cohort study of children hospitalized with COVID-19 pneumonia followed for 3 months to determine long COVID incidence (39.7%) and identify risk factors. Found that older age, allergic diseases, and living in polluted areas were significantly associated with developing long COVID, with exercise intolerance, cough, and fatigue as the most common persistent symptoms.

This observational cohort study followed 56 Thai children aged 7-18 years who had COVID-19 infection to assess respiratory sequelae up to 6 months post-infection. Post-COVID-19 symptoms were identified in 25% of patients (primarily fatigue, cough, dyspnea), abnormal pulmonary function in 17.8%, and significant association was found between symptoms and prior pneumonia.

A prospective cohort study of 72 Dutch children (43 with MIS-C, 29 with COVID-19) evaluated long-term respiratory and systemic sequelae 5-12 months post-hospitalization using clinical assessment, HRQoL surveys, lung function tests, and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Long-term respiratory symptoms and fatigue occurred in both groups, with COVID-19 patients showing higher rates of respiratory symptoms, impaired HRQoL, and abnormal pulmonary/cardiopulmonary function compared to MIS-C patients.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms in 69 PAH/CTEPH patients at median 155 days post-infection. Over 60% reported persistent long COVID symptoms with fatigue, joint pain, and muscle pain being most common, while pulmonary hypertension prognosis remained stable post-COVID.

Prospective cohort study of 100 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months post-discharge to assess functional recovery and identify risk factors for persistent limitations. Patients showed significant functional improvement over the 3-month period, with female sex, older age, and longer hospital/ICU stays identified as risk factors for slower recovery.

This retrospective study examines pulmonary perfusion abnormalities in 37 long-term survivors of severe COVID-19 ARDS treated with ECMO, assessing V/Q imaging at least 3 months post-treatment. The study found no persistent pulmonary perfusion defects despite high rates of thromboembolic events during acute illness, but focuses on acute COVID-19 sequelae rather than long COVID syndrome and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiopulmonary endurance and symptoms in 32 long COVID athletes versus 13 asymptomatic controls at 3 months post-infection. Found that PASC patients had a median 27% decrease in cardiopulmonary endurance, worse dyspnea and quality-of-life scores, with 31% unable to engage in any cardiovascular exercise.

This study evaluates hemostasis and fibrinolysis parameters in COVID-19 ICU survivors at 6 months follow-up, comparing patients with and without venous thromboembolism during admission. While it addresses long COVID sequelae, it is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective analysis of COVID-19 patients with pulmonary embolism followed up to 6 months post-acute event, evaluating persistence of dyspnea and pulmonary vascular sequelae through imaging and exercise testing. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a secondary analysis from the FENIX study examining natural disease progression rather than evaluating a specific therapy.

Pilot study evaluating efficacy of chikujountanto (CUT), a traditional Kampo medicine, for persistent cough in mild COVID-19 patients. While results suggest CUT may reduce cough symptoms, the paper focuses on acute/mild COVID-19 rather than long COVID (post-acute sequelae persisting weeks to months after infection).

Post hoc analysis of a prospective multicenter cohort study examining gastrointestinal symptom progression and psychological comorbidities in post-COVID-19 patients with disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs). Finds that post-COVID-19 DGBI patients experience progressive gastrointestinal symptom deterioration and persistent psychological distress compared to non-DGBI and pre-existing IBS/FD controls.

A prospective observational cohort study following 345 COVID-19 patients at 6, 9, and 15 months post-discharge to assess long-term functional, nutritional, and symptom outcomes. While it documents long-COVID symptoms (fatigue, cognitive impairment, decreased mobility), it does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated Kampo (Japanese traditional) medicine for treating persistent symptoms in 70 non-hospitalized long COVID patients followed from October 2020 to September 2021. Results showed 53.5% of patients had complete symptom improvement, with Kampo formulae used in 53-76% of patients across different treatment phases, suggesting potential benefit for symptom management.

This prospective national cohort study tracked COVID-19-related smell and taste dysfunction in 363 participants through follow-up surveys over 1-6 months and again at 2+ years post-infection. Most participants recovered within weeks to months, with older age and female gender associated with slower recovery and significant quality-of-life impacts.

This prospective multicenter cohort study evaluated the effect of statin use on long-term respiratory symptoms and pulmonary fibrosis in COVID-19 patients with diabetes mellitus over a 90-day follow-up period. Statin users had significantly lower odds of chronic cough and dyspnea, and may have reduced pulmonary fibrosis progression in patients with long-standing diabetes.

Cross-sectional study of 714 post-COVID-19 patients examining the effect of various medications (corticosteroids, antivirals, vitamins, anticoagulants, etc.) on self-reported recovery of taste and smell function. Nitazoxanide showed a trend toward improved recovery, while oral zinc was associated with worse outcomes, though no medication demonstrated clear efficacy overall.

This paper analyzes psychiatric illness risk following COVID-19 using electronic health records, finding a 25% increased risk in the early post-acute phase compared to other respiratory infections. It is a secondary analysis of existing EHR data rather than a treatment trial, and does not study any intervention or therapy.

Longitudinal cohort study tracking recovery of olfactory dysfunction in 122 post-COVID-19 patients using psychophysical assessment (Sniffin' Sticks test) at baseline and 1-year follow-up. Found that 55.1% of patients still had confirmed olfactory dysfunction at 1-year, with improvements in smell threshold but not discrimination or identification.

Observational study examining whether pre-pandemic IL-6 plasma levels predict chronic fatigue development in long COVID. Found chronic fatigue prevalent in mild COVID-19 cases but not predicted by baseline IL-6; elevated BMI was associated with fatigue risk.

Population-based cross-sectional study examining olfactory and gustatory dysfunction 4 months after COVID-19 infection in a German community cohort. Found 60.5% had objective olfactory dysfunction (hyposmia/anosmia) and 9.3% had gustatory dysfunction, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

Longitudinal study examining the bidirectional relationship between fatigue and depression/anxiety in 860 healthcare and social workers with post-COVID syndrome using cross-lagged panel analysis. Findings show significant reciprocal effects between fatigue and mental health symptoms, particularly among PCS-affected individuals, suggesting psychotherapeutic intervention may benefit this population.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study following 3,127 Belgian adults with recent SARS-CoV-2 infection for three months to assess anxiety and depression in post-COVID condition (PCC). Found that 50% of participants developed PCC symptoms, with significantly higher rates of anxiety (11%) and depression (19%) in the PCC group compared to uninfected controls.

Prospective cohort study nested within 5 RCTs assessing the association between acute COVID-19 severity and 1-year quality of life outcomes in 1,508 post-hospitalized patients. Patients requiring mechanical ventilation had significantly lower quality of life and higher rates of mortality, cardiovascular events, and new disabilities at 1-year follow-up.

This cross-sectional study examined the incidence and psychosocial correlates of long COVID in 686 adults from a large U.S. city using different case definitions (PAC, PCS-1, PCS-2, PCS-3). The study found high prevalence of long COVID symptoms and identified female sex, certain ethnicities, and low social support as risk factors, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This study examined structural brain connectivity and cognitive performance in 12 former COVID-19 hospitalized patients (6 ICU, 6 non-ICU) over 2 months post-discharge using MRI and cognitive testing. While cognitive performance improved over time in both groups, the study is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This prospective observational study uses [68Ga]FAPI PET/CT imaging to investigate pulmonary fibroblast activation protein expression in 18 long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea compared to 15 matched controls. The study demonstrates elevated FAP expression in long COVID patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study used [18F]FDG-PET imaging to examine brain metabolic dysfunctions in 26 patients with neurological symptoms across acute, subacute, and chronic COVID-19 phases. The fronto-insular cortex emerged as the key hypometabolic hallmark, with progressive recovery over time, suggesting transient CNS involvement linked to inflammation and hypoxia.

A retrospective study comparing brain [18F]FDG-PET scans in 56 long COVID patients at two timepoints (7 and 16 months post-infection) versus 51 healthy controls. Results show persistent hypometabolism in limbic areas, brainstem, and cerebellum at both timepoints with minimal recovery, indicating durable brain metabolic deficits in patients with persistent long COVID symptoms.

A prospective imaging study comparing hepatic and renal changes in 37 COVID-19 survivors versus 24 controls using T1 mapping and IVIM-DWI MRI sequences. Results showed dynamic alterations in liver and kidney imaging parameters over time, suggesting mild, non-symptomatic organ impairment that may improve for liver but persist for kidney function.

This study describes paired inspiratory/expiratory CT imaging findings in 48 long COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms, performed 72 days after symptom onset and at least 30 days after hospital discharge. The study documents high prevalence of air trapping (77%) and other parenchymal abnormalities, but is a descriptive cross-sectional imaging study without any treatment intervention and therefore excluded from the trials pipeline.

This prospective longitudinal study used hyperpolarized 129Xe MRI to investigate pulmonary diffusion and microvascular perfusion in COVID-19 convalescents, comparing them to healthy controls at baseline (~12.6 weeks) and follow-up (~38 weeks post-symptom onset. While the study documents natural recovery of microvascular function over time, it is an observational cohort study with no treatment intervention—participants were simply followed longitudinally without receiving any treatment as part of the study protocol.

Prospective cohort study examining pulmonary diffusing capacity (DLCO) changes and imaging findings (HRCT, V/Q SPECT) in 153 COVID-19 patients at short-term (5.6 months) and intermediate follow-up (12.5 months). The study found severity-dependent DLCO reduction at short-term follow-up that recovered by intermediate follow-up, though restrictive ventilatory disturbances and morphological changes persisted.

This retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX research network investigates the association between vitamin D deficiency and post-acute outcomes of COVID-19 in 16,600 propensity-matched patients. The study found that vitamin D deficiency was associated with higher risk of ED visits, hospitalization, and death during 90-180 day follow-up, but not with post-COVID-19 condition diagnosis.

This pilot observational study examined 88 patients with post-COVID manifestations, comparing 68 with herpesvirus reactivation (CMV, EBV, HHV6) to 20 controls without detectable herpesvirus DNA. Patients with herpesvirus reactivation showed more frequent fever, headache, neuropsychological disorders, pulmonary abnormalities, myalgia, and elevated inflammatory markers, suggesting herpesvirus reactivation may contribute to post-COVID syndrome severity.

This cross-sectional study recruited 80 long COVID patients without prior rheumatic disease diagnosis to assess the prevalence and overlap of inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRD) symptoms and biomarkers. The study found IRD in 6.25% of patients and documented significant symptom and biomarker overlap between long COVID and rheumatic diseases, but did not test any treatment intervention.

This study investigates DNA damage in COVID-19 survivors using the comet assay method, comparing damage levels during the acute infection period versus the post-COVID period across ICU and non-ICU patients. While focused on long COVID sequelae, the paper is an observational biomarker study without treatment intervention or clinical outcomes, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective observational study of 85 severe/critical COVID-19 patients who received inpatient rehabilitation targeting neuromuscular and respiratory recovery in a Turkish hospital. While the study shows rehabilitation effectiveness (improved functional status, reduced O2 dependence), it focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery during hospitalization, not long COVID sequelae occurring weeks-to-months post-infection.

Prospective cohort study evaluating olfactory and chemosensory function recovery in 72 patients with sudden smell loss due to acute COVID-19 infection. At 5 weeks post-infection, 37% had persistent olfactory dysfunction, with odor threshold detection more affected than odor identification.

Prospective observational study following 34 post-COVID-19 patients for 6 months post-hospital discharge to assess changes in left ventricular function, arterial stiffness, and autonomic function compared to controls. Found impaired cardiac deformation and autonomic dysregulation in long COVID patients at 1-month follow-up that partially improved but did not normalize by 6 months.

This study measures retronasal olfactory function in early COVID-19 patients over 7 weeks using the Candy Smell Test. While subjective smell perception improved, objective olfactory measurements showed no significant recovery, indicating this is an assessment of acute COVID-19 symptoms rather than post-COVID sequelae.

Observational study assessing olfactory dysfunction in 102 COVID-19 patients 3-15 months post-infection using standardized chemosensory tests and quality-of-life questionnaires. Findings show persistent hyposmia in 72.5% of patients with varied recovery patterns, but no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

Prospective cohort study tracking recovery of taste and smell dysfunction in 132 COVID-19 patients over 18 months via telephone surveys. Found that 93% recovered gustatory function and 87% recovered olfactory function by 18 months, with severity at onset and early improvement predicting recovery trajectory.

Retrospective cohort study comparing SNOT-22 questionnaire scores across patients with olfactory dysfunction from post-COVID-19, non-COVID postinfectious causes, and chronic rhinosinusitis. The study found that SNOT-22 lacks disease-specificity for CRS and cannot reliably distinguish between different etiologies of olfactory dysfunction.

This prospective observational study followed 403 patients with mild COVID-19 to track the prevalence and recovery of smell/taste dysfunction over 3 years. Among patients with initial chemosensory dysfunction, 92% reported complete resolution by 3 years, with ongoing recovery observed even at the 2-3 year timepoint.

A prospective observational study following 48 COVID-19 patients with chemosensory dysfunction for up to 24 months to assess long-term recovery of smell and taste. Most patients did not fully recover after 2 years, with 53% experiencing persistent smell impairment and 42% persistent taste impairment at follow-up.

This cohort study of 701 post-COVID-19 patients evaluates the association between chemosensory impairment (taste and smell dysfunction) and neuropsychiatric symptoms using standardized assessment instruments. The findings show significant associations between chemosensory abnormalities and cognitive dysfunction, particularly memory impairment, suggesting a potential neurobiological link in post-COVID-19 syndrome.

Prospective follow-up study of 36 severe COVID-19 ICU survivors assessed at 6 and 12 months post-discharge using fiberendoscopic evaluation and patient-reported outcome measures. While most patients regained normal swallowing by 1 year, substantial proportions experienced persistent dysphagia (40%), laryngeal dysfunction (53%), and anxiety/depression (24-36%).

This cross-sectional study evaluated cognitive functioning in 92-122 COVID-19 survivors at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge compared to healthy controls and depression patients, using neuropsychological testing. Approximately 75-79% of survivors showed cognitive impairment, particularly in psychomotor coordination and processing speed, with depression being a key factor affecting outcomes and quality of life.

Observational study characterizing olfactory and taste dysfunction in post-acute COVID-19 across 906 survey participants and 108 cohort participants followed for up to 360 days. Identifies a distinct phenotype of persistent smell/taste disorder with slow recovery (90 days median) but good overall quality of life and mental health outcomes.

A cross-sectional neuropsychological cohort study of 18 post-COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between clinical parameters (including anosmia) and cognitive/memory impairment. The study found that anosmia was a significant predictor of memory disorders with temporo-mesial dysfunction, suggesting a possible olfactory route of SARS-CoV-2 brain infection.

This cross-sectional study screened 1,638 Egyptian COVID-19 survivors at 3 months post-infection to determine the prevalence and severity of neuropsychiatric post-acute sequelae, including fatigue (24.6%), insomnia (16.4%), depression (15.3%), and anxiety (14.4%). The study found that non-vaccination and severe acute COVID-19 increased odds of neuropsychiatric manifestations, while full vaccination before infection was associated with reduced severity of fatigue, insomnia, and other symptoms.

A prospective registry study of 1,022 long COVID patients at a German university clinic tracking neuropsychological symptoms and ME/CFS prevalence over time. While symptom severity decreased from first to second visit, 19.4% of patients still met ME/CFS criteria at follow-up, demonstrating persistent long-term burden.

An observational pilot study evaluating a 3-week multidisciplinary bio-psycho-social rehabilitation program with physiotherapy focus in 33 post-COVID-19 patients with fatigue and reduced physical capacity. The program showed feasibility with high completion rates and numerical improvements in 6-minute walk distance, though not statistically significant.

This cross-sectional study examines discrepancies in disease severity perception between post-COVID patients and their healthcare providers (internists, psychiatrists/psychologists), using validated assessment scales. The findings reveal patients consistently rate their health as worse than providers, with fatigue and mood disorders negatively correlating with patient health perception.

Prospective observational study of 79 post-COVID syndrome patients receiving a 14-day comprehensive multimodal inpatient integrative therapy program in Germany. Treatment significantly reduced fatigue symptoms and improved subjective work ability at discharge and 6-month follow-up.

This cross-sectional study compares brain structural and functional changes in 51 quarantined COVID-19 survivors 15 months post-discharge versus 74 healthy controls, finding subjective cognitive decline associated with gray matter enlargement in Heschl's gyrus and elevated inflammatory markers. The study is observational only—no intervention or treatment is tested or evaluated, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

A longitudinal observational study following 42 non-hospitalized individuals with post-COVID cognitive deficits over six months, using comprehensive neuropsychological testing and symptom questionnaires. While objectively measured cognitive disorder decreased from 61.9% to 42.9%, subjective complaints remained high and neuropsychiatric symptoms were unchanged.

Prospective cohort study following 127 COVID-19 survivors for mental health symptoms (PTSS, anxiety, depression) at 2 months and 2 years post-discharge. Identified acute COVID-19 severity and blood biomarkers as risk factors for long-term mental health outcomes, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.

Prospective observational study examining cognitive, EEG, and MRI abnormalities in COVID-19 survivors at 2 and 10 months post-discharge. Found cognitive impairment, EEG connectivity changes, and white matter hyperintensities that improved over time, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective cohort study comparing anxiety (GAD-7) and depression (PHQ-9) symptom scores between 455 long COVID patients and 94 general internal medicine controls at a single academic medical center. Long COVID patients, particularly those without prior psychiatric history, showed significantly higher anxiety and depression symptom burden than controls.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function in 319 post-COVID patients stratified by acute COVID-19 severity against 109 healthy controls. Severe-critical patients showed significant deficits in executive function and general cognition, with acute symptom patterns predicting long-term cognitive outcomes.

This prospective monocentric cohort study assessed neurocognitive function in 52 non-hospitalized post-COVID-19 patients at baseline (≥3 months post-infection). Extended neuropsychological testing revealed neurocognitive disorder in 59.6% of participants, with impairment predominantly in learning/memory and executive functions, though the paper does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed symptom burden in 86% of COVID-19 pneumonia patients at follow-up using standardized data collection during virtual clinic appointments. The study documents residual symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, myalgia) more common in females but does not test any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal study of 106 long COVID patients followed for 1 year, tracking neuropsychiatric symptoms (anxiety, depression, fatigue, cognitive impairment) and treatment outcomes. Most participants improved over time but 72.5% still reported symptoms at 1 year, with 29% starting new medications primarily for fatigue management.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long COVID patients with and without neurocognitive impairment, identifying risk factors (female sex, mild acute infection, pre-existing mental health diagnoses) and associated immune dysregulation (lower IgG levels). Patients with neurocognitive symptoms showed poorer quality of life initially but gradual improvement over 20 months post-infection.

A prospective longitudinal study comparing 88 post-COVID patients with cognitive complaints to 50 healthy controls using neuropsychological testing to assess processing speed and attentional deficits. The study found that PCS patients show significant cognitive slowing with longer reaction times that persists unchanged at 6-month follow-up, with reduced alertness correlating with higher fatigue severity.

This prospective observational study assessed autonomic nervous system dysfunction in 180 post-COVID patients using the COMPASS-31 questionnaire and active stand testing, finding autonomic symptoms in a substantial proportion with more severe orthostatic intolerance in those with neurological complaints. The study characterizes the prevalence and patterns of dysautonomic symptoms but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings in 84 patients with neurological manifestations of post-COVID-19 syndrome from two specialist clinics. The majority of samples were normal, with elevated total protein (24%) and blood-CSF barrier dysfunction (13%) being the most common pathological findings, suggesting CSF analysis has limited diagnostic value but helps exclude differential diagnoses.

This ISARIC-COVID-19 follow-up study examines long-term neurological symptoms in adult patients hospitalized with acute COVID-19. It is an observational prospective cohort that characterizes symptom prevalence and patterns but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

This study uses an international registry of COVID-19 patients with neurological manifestations to identify prognostic factors for 6-month outcomes, with 31.5% reporting persistent neurological symptoms. While it addresses long COVID, it is an observational registry analysis (not a treatment trial) and functions as a secondary analysis of registry data rather than a primary trial.

Nationwide cohort study comparing long COVID symptoms in 37,522 SARS-CoV-2 positive children (0-17 years) to 78,037 controls via electronic questionnaire. Found that long COVID symptoms lasting >4 weeks were common in both groups but more frequent in infected school-age children (0.8% difference), with most symptoms resolving within 1-5 months.

The NEUROCOG-COVID study evaluated long-term cognitive and psychiatric outcomes in 74 patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19, finding that 73% presented with cognitive disorders including executive dysfunction (66%), memory disorders (31%), and language disorders (19%). The study characterizes the neuropsychological profile of post-COVID cognitive impairment but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This prospective follow-up study assessed persistent respiratory symptoms and pulmonary function in 50 children 3 months post-COVID-19 infection. The study found respiratory symptoms persisted in 28% of patients with abnormalities in FEV1/FVC, lung clearance index, and DLCO, suggesting ongoing inflammatory effects despite mild acute disease.

This prospective study compared post-COVID-19 symptoms in 200 children infected with Delta vs Omicron variants, assessed via questionnaire >12 weeks after infection. Delta variant infections showed significantly higher rates of weakness, fatigue, anxiety disorder, and gastrointestinal changes compared to Omicron.

Prospective cohort study examining age-related prevalence and symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition in 785 children followed for 6 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found 8% incidence of PCC with fatigue as the most common symptom, and identified age-group-specific associated factors (gastrointestinal/neurological symptoms in ages 0-2, comorbidities in older children).

A prospective multicenter registry study of 458 children with preceding COVID-19 assessed the prevalence of thyroid autoimmunity and dysfunction, finding 6.6% newly diagnosed thyroid autoimmunity and 4.0% ultrasound-proven autoimmune thyroiditis with no association to vaccination. The study documents long-lasting thyroid alterations in 73.3% of affected children but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Longitudinal study reassessing cardiopulmonary function in 13 children with post-COVID-19 and 23 matched controls at baseline and 6-month follow-up using exercise testing. While this is a valid longitudinal observational study, it does not evaluate a specific intervention or treatment—it passively follows natural recovery without assigning any treatment to participants.

A retrospective clinical analysis of 44 long COVID patients presenting with neurologic symptoms at a Chicago neuro-infectious disease clinic between 2020-2022. The study documents presentation patterns, diagnostic findings (cognitive assessments, EEG, autoantibodies, CSF), and 12-month outcomes, finding that most patients continued experiencing neurologic symptoms though over half reported moderate or marked improvement.

This multicenter study (PoCoRe) examined dysfunctional coping patterns (avoidance-endurance model) in 481 post-COVID syndrome patients at the start and end of multimodal rehabilitation. The majority of patients (81.8%) exhibited dysfunctional illness behavior at baseline, with significant shifts toward adaptive/functional patterns during rehabilitation, though 10-15% deteriorated.

Extension cohort study documenting rheumatic and musculoskeletal symptoms in hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 6 months post-hospitalization via telephone surveys. Found that 59.6% had persistent symptoms at 6 months, with fatigue (31.6%), joint pain (18.6%), and myalgia (15.1%) being the most common rheumatologic manifestations, with female patients at higher risk.

Observational cohort study examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination and long COVID symptoms in 28,356 UK participants infected with SARS-CoV-2 prior to vaccination. First and second vaccination doses were associated with 12.8% and 8.8% reductions in long COVID odds respectively, with sustained improvement after the second dose.

This longitudinal descriptive study evaluated swallowing abnormalities in 127 post-COVID-19 patients with oropharyngeal dysphagia using fiberoptic endoscopic assessment at 1-4 weeks post-discharge. The study identified risk factors for aspiration (higher EAT-10 scores, dysphonia, respiratory rate, mechanical ventilation duration) and found associations with ageusia/anosmia, but is observational without testing any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study of 26 post-COVID patients examining bronchoalveolar lavage cellularity, lung function impairment, and HRCT findings. Found that persistent inflammatory responses with CD4+ T-cell lymphocytosis in the lungs were associated with reduced lung function, suggesting a role for alveolar inflammation in post-COVID pathogenesis.

This cross-sectional study compared olfactory function in acutely ill COVID-19 patients versus recovered patients using a psychophysical identification test. While it documents persistent olfactory dysfunction as a long-COVID sequela, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study followed 165 COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-hospitalization to assess the prevalence and predictors of long-term neurological manifestations. Fatigue (34%), memory/attention problems (31%), and sleep disorders (30%) were common, with 40% exhibiting neurological abnormalities; older age, comorbidities, and COVID-19 severity were independent predictors.

This observational study evaluated a neuropsychological assessment model in 12 post-acute COVID-19 patients receiving rehabilitation, using cognitive tests (MMSE, MoCA) and psychological scales (AD-R, NPI) at baseline, discharge, and 3-month follow-up. Patients showed cognitive impairment at baseline with improvement in depression and behavioral scores, suggesting rehabilitation may benefit psychological and behavioral outcomes in post-COVID patients.

A 9-month prospective follow-up study of 95 COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and predictors of long-COVID symptoms. Found that female sex, higher symptom burden, and acute neuropsychiatric manifestations were associated with chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive deficits at follow-up, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared long COVID prevalence and symptoms in 118 healthcare workers with prior COVID-19 infection versus 118 matched controls without infection in Morocco. The study found 47.4% long COVID prevalence with predominant symptoms of asthenia, myalgia, and brain fog, but does not test any treatment or intervention.

A retrospective cohort study of 137 COVID-19 patients evaluated 1 year post-discharge to identify predictors of persistent brain fog using cognitive and psychological assessments. Depression was identified as the strongest independent predictor of cognitive complaints after adjusting for demographic and clinical variables.

A matched cohort study using German health care data comparing incident autoimmune disease rates between 641,704 COVID-19 patients and matched controls followed 3-15 months post-infection. Patients with prior COVID-19 had 43% higher likelihood of developing new-onset autoimmune diseases, with strongest associations for vasculitis.

Prospective cohort study following 191 mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients for 1.5 years to assess prevalence and characteristics of persistent pain symptoms. Found 31.9% experienced persistent pain (headache 29.8%, myalgia 5.8%, neuropathic pain 4.2%) with female gender and neuropathic pain as predictors of long-term headaches.

This prospective observational cohort study examines perioperative outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus unexposed controls. While the paper documents increased pulmonary complications and longer operative times in COVID-exposed patients, it is not about long COVID treatment—it focuses on acute surgical risk in cancer patients, not long COVID symptoms or interventions.

This retrospective cohort study compares cerebrospinal fluid and serum cytokine profiles in post- versus para-infectious Guillain-Barré syndrome associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. While the paper studies a COVID-related neurological complication, it is not about long COVID (which focuses on persistent multi-system symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational cohort study of 275 patients 3 months post-COVID-19 evaluating serological markers, pulmonary function tests, and chest CT findings. Anti-S antibody levels were independently associated with reduced diffusing capacity and severe acute COVID-19, but the study did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective observational study evaluating coenzyme Q10 and alpha lipoic acid (Requpero) in 174 chronic COVID syndrome patients, comparing 116 treated patients with 58 untreated controls. The treatment group showed significantly higher FSS complete response rates (53.5% vs 3.5%) and lower non-response rates (9.5% vs 25.9%), meeting primary and secondary outcomes.

Retrospective cohort study examining whether corticosteroids, antibiotics, or anticoagulants administered during acute COVID-19 hospitalization reduce the risk of developing post-COVID-19 syndrome at 6-month follow-up in 123 hospitalized patients. Corticosteroid treatment was associated with significantly lower odds of post-COVID syndrome (OR 0.32), while antibiotics and anticoagulants showed no significant protective effect.

Retrospective study of 52 COVID-19 pneumonia patients with serial chest CT scans ~3 months apart to assess radiologic resolution. 57.7% showed complete resolution while 42.3% had residual lung abnormalities, with risk factors including severe initial CT involvement, ICU admission, and elevated WBC.

Follow-up cohort study of 526 long COVID patients assessing chronic autonomic dysfunction severity, POTS prevalence, and impact on quality of life. No interventions tested; purely observational characterization of autonomic symptoms and associated risk factors in an established LC cohort.

Retrospective chart review of 27 post-COVID patients evaluated for autonomic dysfunction at Mayo Clinic between March 2020 and January 2021. Found abnormal autonomic testing in majority of patients (36% sudomotor, 27% cardiovagal), with orthostatic intolerance being most common; no treatment intervention was tested.

This case-control study compares patients with pulmonary embolism (PE) who had prior COVID-19 infection (n=18) to PE patients without prior COVID-19 (n=54) and healthy controls, evaluating biochemical and clinical parameters. The study describes differences in thrombotic markers and clinical characteristics but is observational without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study assessed clinical outcomes and quality of life in 995 COVID-19 survivors at median 811-day follow-up using questionnaires and blood tests. While the paper documents long COVID symptoms and biomarkers (inflammation, liver injury, myocardial markers), it is an observational survey with no intervention or treatment tested.

The PoCoRe study evaluated neuropsychological deficits in post-COVID condition patients undergoing multidisciplinary indoor rehabilitation at six German centers, measuring fatigue, attention, and cognition at admission and discharge. Significant improvements were observed across multiple measures, with 63% of patients showing improvement in cognitive assessment scores from pathological to normative levels.

This prospective observational cohort study examined retinal microcirculation in 41 post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) patients compared to matched healthy controls using Retinal Vessel Analysis (RVA). The study found persistent endothelial dysfunction in PCS patients with reduced venular flicker-induced dilation and narrower arteries, correlating with symptom severity, but did not test any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared right ventricular functions in 105 mild COVID-19 patients 3 months post-infection versus 105 healthy controls using echocardiography. The COVID-19 group showed significantly impaired RV function parameters, suggesting subclinical RV dysfunction in long-term post-COVID recovery.

Prospective cohort study evaluating cardiac involvement in 100 COVID-19 recovered patients using speckle tracking echocardiography. Found impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain in almost all patients regardless of infection severity, with right ventricular impairment only in hospitalized patients.

This prospective observational study uses sublingual videomicroscopy to assess microvascular structure and function in 27 long COVID patients (>12 weeks symptoms) compared to healthy controls and critically ill COVID-19 patients. The study documents persistent capillary rarefaction and reduced microvascular health in long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examined myocardial ischemia in 340 COVID-19 survivors presenting with chest pain or shortness of breath using SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging. It found significantly higher rates of abnormal MPI in the COVID-19 group (23%) compared to controls (16%), suggesting prior COVID-19 predicts myocardial ischemia.

This observational study assessed functional outcomes and cardiac function in 60 post-COVID patients with persistent dyspnea compared to 30 healthy controls using clinical scoring, exercise ECG, and echocardiography. Post-COVID patients demonstrated reduced functional capacity, elevated inflammatory markers, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, and impaired left atrial strain function.

This paper compares cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) findings in patients with cardiac symptoms after COVID-19 versus after COVID-19 vaccination. It is a cross-sectional descriptive study of cardiac complications, not a treatment intervention trial.

This paper analyzes symptom patterns in long COVID using data from nine UK longitudinal studies with over 42,000 participants, comparing symptom prevalence across COVID-19 status groups. It identifies characteristic symptoms of acute COVID-19 and long COVID through latent class analysis but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study assessed cardiac function via echocardiography in 146 COVID-19 patients at 6 weeks post-discharge, comparing first and second wave patients. While mild cardiac abnormalities were found in 27-29% of patients, these were not associated with symptom burden (NYHA class) and did not differ between waves, suggesting long-term post-COVID symptoms are not explained by cardiac dysfunction.

Prospective follow-up study of 350 COVID-19 hospitalized patients assessed 6-12 months post-discharge for gastrointestinal, sleep, and neurological symptoms. Found 13.3% reported GI symptoms (nausea/vomiting most common) and associations between GI/liver abnormalities and sleep problems or cognitive impairment, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study of 332 long COVID patients in Ukraine characterizing symptom prevalence, demographics, and physiological risk factors. Found 23% long COVID prevalence with fatigue, muscular pain, and anosmia as most common symptoms, alongside elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, fibrinogen) associated with age >38 years, female sex, and unhealthy lifestyle.

This large Norwegian cohort study (n>70,000) characterized excess risk and symptom clusters associated with long COVID up to 12 months post-infection. Key findings identified 13 of 22 symptoms significantly associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, with fatigue showing 4.8-fold increased risk, and discovered two main symptom factors suggesting multiple underlying mechanisms rather than a single syndrome.

This prospective cohort study (with retrospective matching) examines nirmatrelvir-ritonavir's effects on myocardial injury and long-term cardiovascular outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during the Omicron wave. While it demonstrates that nirmatrelvir-ritonavir reduces troponin elevation and major adverse cardiovascular events, it focuses exclusively on acute COVID-19 hospitalization and post-acute cardiovascular complications, not persistent post-COVID syndrome (long COVID).

This retrospective cohort study examined electronic health records from 1.32 million COVID-19 patients to assess whether glucocorticoid treatment during acute infection affects long COVID development. Patients who received glucocorticoids had higher long COVID incidence (16.95% vs 11.23%), with an adjusted OR of 1.28, suggesting corticosteroid use during acute COVID may increase long COVID risk.

A 6-country collaborative cross-sectional study characterizing the incidence and clinical presentations of long COVID across Europe and North America, finding incidence rates ranging from 17-46% with variable symptom profiles by country. The study primarily describes the prevalence and symptomatology of long COVID but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Retrospective analysis comparing fatigue, sleepiness, and sleep quality in 287 long COVID patients infected with different SARS-CoV-2 variants (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) during three epidemic waves in Hungary. Found that long COVID symptomatic patients had significantly higher fatigue and poor sleep quality scores than asymptomatic patients, with symptom severity remaining consistent across variants.

Prospective longitudinal study following 146 COVID-19 patients for up to 6 months post-discharge to characterize clinical, virological, and serological outcomes and identify predictors of long-COVID. Found that weak anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody response, severity of illness, and female gender are associated with persistent symptoms, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

This longitudinal study examined relationships between changes in post-COVID fatigue dimensions and neuropsychiatric symptoms in 233 individuals at 1 and 3 months post-infection using canonical correlation analysis. Mental fatigue emerged as the dominant fatigue component in the chronic phase and showed the strongest associations with depression, anxiety, PTSD, and cognitive impairments, particularly in the persistent fatigue group.

Retrospective study of 114 patients with inborn errors of immunity (IEI) who had SARS-CoV-2 infection, examining outcomes and complications across 16 Italian reference centers. 16.85% reported long-lasting COVID symptoms, primarily in patients on immunoglobulin replacement therapy, with overall infection fatality rate of 3.5%.

A 2-year longitudinal survey comparing COVID-19 incidence and long COVID prevalence between Seventh-day Adventists and non-Adventists in the UK. The study found Adventists had significantly lower long COVID rates (OR 0.30, p=0.01), potentially associated with their lifestyle factors including plant-based diet and abstinence from alcohol and coffee.

Multicentric observational study assessing long COVID prevalence in Italian CVID patients using CDC survey methodology. Found 65.7% LC prevalence with fatigue, arthralgia/myalgia, and dyspnea as most common symptoms; complicated phenotype, obesity, and female sex were significant risk correlates.

This study analyzes immunological abnormalities in convalescent severe COVID-19 patients at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge, identifying persistent immune dysfunction and thrombotic markers. The research documents biomarker persistence but does not test any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cohort study comparing incident diagnoses in New York State Medicaid children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2021 versus uninfected controls. Found low incidence of post-acute sequelae with mostly weak or marginal increases in sequelae of infectious disease, general symptoms, pericarditis, and suicidal ideation.

A multicenter observational study of 979 postcovid syndrome patients across Russia and neighboring countries assessing the prevalence of PCS manifestations and the effectiveness of Cortexin (10-20 mg i.m. for 10 days) treatment. Cortexin showed efficacy in correcting cognitive and asthenic symptoms, with anti-anxiety and antidepressant effects, more pronounced at the 20-mg dose.

This study used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to assess retinal neurodegeneration in COVID-19 recovered patients at 1 month and 12 months post-infection compared to healthy controls. The findings demonstrate subclinical structural changes in the retina persisting at 12 months, but this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Prospective multicenter cohort study of 90 patients assessing factors associated with health-related quality of life and mental health outcomes 3 months after COVID-19 diagnosis. Found impaired QoL in 31% of patients, with younger age, longer hospitalization, sleep impairment, and anxiety as independent predictors.

A retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort study (BQC-19) tracking health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in 2,163 COVID-19 survivors over 18 months using the EQ-5D-5L scale. The study identified trajectories of HRQOL decline and found that age, sex, disease severity, and fatigue were key predictors of decline, with stronger effects in the hospitalized subgroup.

Prospective cohort study of 56 severe COVID-19 ICU survivors assessed at median 101 days post-discharge, examining prevalence and correlates of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Found 29% with depressive symptoms and 23% with anxiety symptoms, associated with younger age, cognitive complaints, ICU-related memories, and post-discharge health problems.

Prospective observational study of 106 severe COVID-19 patients admitted to ICU, evaluating quality of life one year after discharge using the EQ-5D index. The study identified female sex and duration of mechanical ventilation as independent predictors of worse quality of life, with 91% of patients experiencing sequelae including neuropsychiatric symptoms.

summary: Prospective cohort study of 96 cancer patients followed for 12 months to assess long COVID prevalence and impact on quality of life, symptom burden, and psychological wellbeing. Found 79.6% of SARS-CoV-2 infected cancer patients reported long COVID symptoms with higher prevalence than healthy controls, with fatigue, myalgia, and sleep disturbance being most common.

Longitudinal cohort study following 500 COVID-19 survivors for one year to identify trajectories of physical/mental HRQoL, fatigue, and dyspnoea. Found substantial heterogeneity in outcomes with associations between older age, comorbidities, and worse trajectories, but no specific intervention was tested.

A retrospective cohort study measuring health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in Italian patients up to 3 years after COVID-19 hospitalization using the SF-36 questionnaire. The study found significantly lower HRQoL compared to normative data, with mental health remaining impaired over time despite improvements in physical health.

Quasi-experimental longitudinal cohort study examining how long COVID impacts individuals and how response-shift effects (changes in cognitive appraisal and standards of comparison) influence symptom burden over 3 years. Study found notable response-shift effects across COVID-specific adversity outcomes, particularly in those with high symptom burden.

Longitudinal observational study following COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID condition (PCC) over 3 years to examine health-related quality of life (HRQoL) changes measured by EQ-5D-5L. Found wide individual variation in HRQoL over one year, with female sex and older age associated with certain patterns of change, but no intervention was tested.

Retrospective cohort study investigating whether oral anticoagulant (OAC) use at acute COVID-19 infection reduces subsequent long COVID/PASC development using propensity score matching on TriNetx data. Found that OAC users had increased risk of long COVID features compared to non-users, with no evidence supporting OAC as preventive therapy for long COVID.

This multicenter observational study compared post-COVID-19 outcomes in non-dialysis dependent CKD patients versus matched controls without COVID-19. While it documents acute COVID complications (AKI, respiratory symptoms, mortality) in CKD patients, it does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection) or any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional descriptive study of 277 long COVID patients presenting to a referral clinic, analyzing fatigue presentations according to ME/CFS criteria and exploring correlations with anxiety, depression, and brain fog. While it clearly characterizes the fatigue phenotype in long COVID, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention and is a non-interventional descriptive study rather than a treatment trial.

Longitudinal study profiling lipoproteins and inflammatory cytokines in long COVID patients at multiple timepoints (5-20 months post-infection) using NMR spectroscopy and flow cytometry. Found persistent hyperlipidemia and altered inflammatory markers in LC compared to acute COVID and healthy controls, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

Retrospective cohort study comparing circadian rhythm disorders and anxiety levels in 278 patients with and without COVID-19 history. Found that post-COVID patients had significantly higher rates of delayed sleep phase disorder and elevated anxiety levels, establishing an association between post-COVID anxiety and circadian rhythm disturbances.

This observational cohort study followed 76 elite athletes infected with SARS-CoV-2 and 51 uninfected controls, assessing cardiac function via echocardiography at 1, 5, and 9 months post-infection. The study found elevated global longitudinal strain shortly after infection but within normal ranges, with no cardiac injury detected and no adverse effects from return to training.

This pilot study evaluated mountain spa rehabilitation (high-altitude environment combined with targeted spa therapy) in 14 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 15 healthy controls. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in clinical symptoms, lung function, and platelet mitochondrial respiration markers.

Prospective cohort study examining renal function changes in young healthy adults following mild or asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection over 6 months. Finds mild COVID-19 associated with reduced creatinine clearance and albumin leakage without acute kidney injury.

Naturalistic observational study evaluating cytokine-blocking agents (anakinra, tocilizumab, sarilumab, reparixin, mavrilimumab) for preventing post-COVID depression in 588 COVID-19 survivors (131 treated with cytokine blockers). Cytokine-blocking treatment reduced depressive symptomatology severity and development of clinically relevant depression, with effects mediated by lowering systemic inflammation.

This study examines variation in primary care scheduling and follow-up after COVID-19 hospitalization in Michigan during 2020, focusing on patterns of outpatient care rather than testing a treatment intervention. It does not evaluate a specific treatment or intervention but rather describes existing follow-up practices and their variation across hospitals.

A 3-year longitudinal study examining epigenetic aging in 54 volunteers (27 with COVID-19 history) using eight different epigenetic clocks. COVID-19 exposure was associated with accelerated epigenetic aging in several clocks (DNAmGrimAge, DNAmGrimAge2, DNAmFitAge), suggesting mild long-term effects on aging trajectories.

A monocentric cohort study characterizing post-COVID-19 syndrome in outpatients 3-10 months after mild infection, comparing COVID-positive (n=418) and COVID-negative (n=89) patients.
