COVID-19 critical illness was associated with elevated risk of new mood and anxiety disorders but not overall mental health diagnoses or psychotic disorders.

Prospective cohort study following 173 COVID-19 patients (91 inpatients, 82 outpatients) from March-April 2020 for one year to assess persistent symptoms. Nearly half (47.9%) experienced at least one persistent symptom at 12 months, with shortness of breath, fatigue, anxiety, and brain fog being most common.

This observational cohort study followed 211 patients hospitalized for acute COVID-19 respiratory failure at 2, 6, and 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term respiratory impairment. While it documents persistent dyspnea and functional abnormalities in long COVID, it is an observational natural history study with no intervention or treatment evaluated, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

This retrospective cohort study examines the effect of corticosteroids administered during acute COVID-19 hospitalization on long-term immune responses (antibodies and T cells) measured 1 year post-infection. The paper focuses on acute hospitalization outcomes and immunological sequelae in COVID-19 survivors, not on long COVID as a syndrome or on treatment of long COVID patients.

Retrospective matched cohort study examining long-term healthcare utilization in COPD patients following COVID-19 infection in Ontario, Canada between 2020-2022. COVID-19 positive patients had 9% higher healthcare utilization rates than negative controls, with variation by variant and vaccination status.

Prospective observational study phenotyping 127 post-COVID patients with echocardiography and strain imaging at 4-12 weeks post-diagnosis. Found that while most had normal left ventricular ejection fraction, over half had abnormal global longitudinal strain, suggesting subclinical cardiac dysfunction in the recovery phase.

This study followed anti-IFN-α2 autoantibody levels over one year in 97 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to investigate their association with long COVID. The authors found that acute-phase high autoantibody levels were not associated with post-COVID sequelae, though a small subset developed detectable antibodies at 12 months.

This prospective observational study profiled plasma mediators and transcriptomic/epigenomic changes in 926 adults six months post-COVID, identifying five distinct PACS phenotypes driven by different immunological mechanisms. The study documents dysregulation of IL-1, IL-17, and anti-inflammatory pathways but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence of objective cardiovascular autonomic abnormalities in 61 long COVID patients using beat-to-beat hemodynamic testing. Overall, 72% of patients met criteria for at least one autonomic disorder (most commonly IOH at 66%, followed by POTS at 30%), with significantly higher POTS prevalence in females (37%) than males (0%).

Prospective study following 33 COVID-19 patients over 16 months to assess long-term liver function and structure changes. Found no significant functional or structural liver changes but documented metabolic deterioration (increased cholesterol, lipids) post-COVID.

A 12-month follow-up study of COVID-19 ICU and non-ICU survivors examining cognitive, psychological, and sleep outcomes using high-density EEG. The study found executive and psycho-affective deficits and altered sleep spindle patterns, particularly in non-ICU participants, but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective follow-up study of 822 COVID-19 hospitalized patients assessed 6-11 months post-discharge to identify risk factors for hospital readmission. Found 68% reported recurrent post-COVID symptoms, 10% required re-hospitalization, with persistent diarrhea, orotracheal intubation, and comorbidities as significant risk factors.

This controlled case-control study compared metabolic markers in 88 long COVID patients (stratified by initial severity) versus 29 healthy controls. The study identified reduced HDL-cholesterol and elevated ferritin as key metabolic abnormalities associated with long COVID severity, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study compared event-related potentials (ERPs) during a working memory task between 43 healthcare workers with mild COVID-19 (~1 year post-infection) and 34 uninfected controls. The COVID-19 group showed distinct neural patterns (lower N1, higher P2 amplitudes) without behavioral differences, suggesting compensatory neural mechanisms, but this is a cross-sectional observational study without any treatment intervention.

Observational cohort study comparing functional, cognitive, and neuropsychiatric outcomes in 115 COVID-19 patients (median 2.9 years post-infection) versus 30 COVID-negative controls. Found significantly higher neuropsychiatric symptoms in COVID-19 patients but no differences in cognitive or functional status; among patients with repeated measures, functional status improved over 3 years while cognition remained stable.

A prospective cohort study following 162 severe COVID-19 patients for one year to identify predictors of persistent fatigue. Found that 36% experienced fatigue at 12 months, with depressive symptoms and impaired lung function in the first month being key predictors of long-term fatigue.

An observational study evaluating the effect of a nutritional supplement (Apportal®) on chronic fatigue and quality of life in 201 subjects after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Results showed statistically significant improvements in fatigue, mental fatigue, and health status measures at both 14 and 28 days of supplementation.

Retrospective cohort study comparing treatments (low-dose naltrexone, amitriptyline, duloxetine, physical therapy) in 108 post-COVID-19 patients, evaluating improvements in fatigue, pain, dyspnea, and brain fog. Low-dose naltrexone showed significantly higher hazard of improvement (HR=5.04) compared to physical therapy alone.

Prospective cohort study measuring Myl9 serum concentrations in 195 COVID-19 patients during hospitalization and at 3- and 6-month follow-up to investigate the association between Myl9 levels and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Study identifies prolonged high Myl9 levels as associated with residual respiratory symptoms at 6 months, suggesting involvement of prolonged inflammation or endothelial damage in PACS pathogenesis.

This prospective cohort study examined fat oxidation capacity as a marker of mitochondrial function in 187 post-COVID syndrome patients undergoing inpatient rehabilitation. Exercise-based rehabilitation significantly improved fat oxidation capacity (+44.2% overall, p<0.0001) and exercise tolerance, suggesting that metabolic disturbance in PCS patients is partially reversible through rehabilitation.

This case-control study compared vitamin D levels in 75-73 post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients versus non-PCS controls measured from 2019-2022, finding significantly lower vitamin D in the PCS cohort (17.0-17.6 ng/ml vs 22.3-23.7 ng/ml). The study is observational without any treatment intervention and does not qualify as a treatment trial.

A prospective observational cohort study of 199 critically ill COVID-19 ICU survivors in Spain tracking nutritional, functional, and quality-of-life outcomes over 12 months post-discharge. While documenting significant improvements in malnutrition risk (83% to 2%), sarcopenia, functional independence, and EQ-5D scores, this is a passive observational study with no intervention administered—it measures natural recovery trajectories rather than testing a treatment.

This retrospective cohort study compared mesotherapy with oral medication (diclofenac, thiocolchicoside, cyanocobalamin) for treating post-COVID pain syndrome in 96 patients. Mesotherapy with lidocaine and cyanocobalamin showed significantly greater improvements in pain and neuropathic symptoms compared to oral treatment.

Prospective cohort study following 103 mild COVID-19 patients over 6 months via phone interviews to characterize symptom onset, duration, and resolution. Found that 46% of patients had at least one unresolved symptom at 6-month follow-up, with fatigue, smell/taste changes, and breathing difficulties being most common.

Retrospective cohort study following 125 COVID-19 patients with anosmia/ageusia to assess recovery rates at 6+ months post-onset. While it documents long COVID sequelae (persistent olfactory/gustatory disorders in 24% of patients), it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This observational cohort study follows 199 COVID-19 survivors discharged from ICU over 12 months, tracking nutritional status, sarcopenia, functional recovery, and quality of life. While it documents recovery trajectories in post-ICU COVID patients, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection) but rather on acute COVID-19 recovery from critical illness.

Prospective observational study of 407 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining nutritional status, complaints, and sarcopenia risk during and after hospital stay. Finds high prevalence of nutrition-related complaints (58% decreased appetite, 43% shortness of breath), acute weight loss (22%), and sarcopenia risk (73%), with limited dietetic follow-up post-discharge.

This study assessed lung function and inflammatory biomarkers in 100 COVID-19 survivors at median 104 days post-symptom onset, comparing mild/moderate and severe disease groups. A diffusion deficit (DLCO <80%) was present in 52% of patients and was significantly associated with prior severe COVID-19, suggesting persistent pulmonary impairment in long COVID recovery.

Prospective cohort study following 1,137 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to assess persistence of symptoms. Found 60% had at least one symptom at 6 months, with female gender, multiple admission symptoms, and ICU admission as independent risk factors for persistent multi-symptom disease.

This prospective observational study follows COVID-19 hospitalized survivors to describe long-term outcomes and persistence of symptoms post-discharge. Patients with lower oxygen levels during acute illness showed worse recovery trajectories and required longer follow-up, with resolution of chest imaging lesions associated with better oxygenation status during hospitalization.

This prospective observational study assessed the prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 syndrome in 599 hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients 6 months after acute infection. While it identifies important epidemiological findings (40.2% prevalence, female gender and ICU admission as risk factors), it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 377 COVID-19 patients assessing long COVID prevalence and associated risk factors. Found female gender, older age, and active smoking independently associated with long COVID syndrome (69% prevalence), but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective study examining the association between vaccination status, humoral immune responses, and post-COVID-19 syndrome persistence at 1 year in 479 patients. Finds no significant difference in symptom worsening between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups, but identifies natural infection-induced antibodies as associated with persistent symptoms.

This prospective cohort study followed 737 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 12 months post-discharge to assess persistence of post-acute symptoms. The study found that 27% had three or more persistent symptoms at 12 months, with women reporting symptoms more frequently than men, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Retrospective cohort study of 188,532 older Singaporeans examining whether early nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment reduces risk of postacute sequelae after COVID-19. Treatment did not significantly reduce risk of postacute cardiovascular, neurological, respiratory, autoimmune diagnoses, or symptoms up to 180 days post-infection.

This prospective study followed 60 COVID-19 patients and healthy controls for 12 months using PREFUL MRI to assess longitudinal changes in pulmonary perfusion and ventilation defects. While pulmonary perfusion impairment persists at 12 months and is associated with developing long COVID, this is an observational descriptive study with no treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examined the association between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination status and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in South Korea during the Omicron-predominant period (January-March 2022). Vaccination with at least two doses was associated with significantly reduced risk of multiple post-acute conditions including cardiac events, venous thromboembolism, renal failure, and pulmonary complications.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating whether intravenous remdesivir reduces long-term multisystemic sequelae (cardiovascular, neurological, respiratory, autoimmune diagnoses and symptom persistence) in 30,175 COVID-19 hospitalized adults in Singapore. Remdesivir treatment did not significantly reduce the risk of long-term diagnoses or symptom persistence compared to untreated individuals at 300 days post-hospitalization.

This cross-sectional study compared resting-state functional MRI patterns in 39 long-COVID patients with and without cognitive impairment, finding altered default mode network connectivity and stronger visual-ventral stream connectivity in cognitively impaired patients. The study is observational and non-interventional, examining neurobiological correlates of cognitive dysfunction rather than testing a treatment.

This cross-sectional study examined 52 adults (COVID-positive and COVID-negative controls) to investigate the relationship between inflammatory factors and neuropsychiatric symptoms in long COVID (neuro-PASC). The study found elevated neuropsychiatric symptoms and altered immune profiles (particularly elevated MIG/CXCL9) in COVID-positive participants with neuro-PASC, supporting the role of immune dysregulation in long COVID neuropsychiatric sequelae.

This cross-sectional study uses a custom olfactory-action meter to quantify olfactory detectabilities and neurocognitive impairments in COVID-19 patients during and post-infection (4-18 months), comparing symptomatic patients, asymptomatic carriers, and healthy controls. Results show persistent olfactory learning deficits in both symptomatic patients and recovered subjects during and after infection, suggesting long-term neurocognitive impairment from COVID-19.

Retrospective cohort study examining long-term multi-systemic complications in Singaporean children aged 1-17 years infected with SARS-CoV-2 Delta/Omicron variants compared to test-negative controls. Found modestly increased risk of respiratory sequelae (particularly bronchitis) post-infection, with reduced chronic sequelae in predominantly mild Omicron cases compared to historical influenza hospitalizations.

This retrospective cohort study uses real-world clinical data from the National COVID Cohort Collaborative to evaluate whether selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), particularly those with sigma-1 receptor agonist activity, reduce the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). The analysis of 17,908 patients found that SSRIs with S1R agonist activity reduced PASC risk by 29% and non-S1R agonist SSRIs by 21%, suggesting a potential preventive benefit of SSRIs in PASC.

Population-based study examining the association between COVID-19 booster vaccination and risk of post-COVID condition during the Omicron wave in 7,936 infected participants. Found that ≥3 vaccine doses before infection were associated with lower PCC risk (OR 0.69), particularly for neurological symptoms in women, suggesting booster vaccination may provide some protective effect.

Retrospective study of 1,426 long COVID patients treated with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) or Western medicine at a Chinese hospital between December 2022 and June 2023. TCM treatment was associated with significantly shorter symptom recovery times compared to Western medicine alone, with younger patients and those with lower BMI showing better outcomes.

This cross-sectional study compared immunological markers between 82 long COVID patients and recovered controls, finding elevated complement C3 and increased CD8 and Th1 T lymphocyte populations in post-COVID condition patients. The study characterizes biological markers of long COVID pathology but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This longitudinal prospective study evaluates circulating calprotectin as a biomarker for persistent olfactory dysfunction in post-COVID patients, comparing treated patients (n=36) receiving three months of olfactory training with two control groups. Higher calprotectin levels in hyposmic patients decreased significantly after olfactory training, suggesting calprotectin's potential as a biomarker for monitoring treatment response.

A prospective cohort study of 32 severe COVID-19 patients assessed sensory neuropathy development using quantitative sensory testing at baseline and 1-year follow-up. The study evaluated sensory thresholds (vibration, cold, warm, heat perception) as natural outcomes but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between long-COVID symptoms and IL-6 signalling factors, including the rs2228145 variant of the IL-6R gene, in 175 COVID-19 survivors. The findings reveal that rs2228145 AA genotype is associated with elevated long-COVID risk in the summer sub-cohort, suggesting IL-6 and genotype markers may be predictive biomarkers for long-COVID development.

This cross-sectional study analyzes circulating inflammatory markers (cytokines) in 87 COVID-19 survivors to identify immune profiles associated with post-COVID depression. While the research provides insights into the neurobiological mechanisms of post-COVID depression, it is an observational biomarker study without a treatment intervention and does not qualify as a treatment trial.

Prospective study measuring CNS injury biomarkers (NfL, GFAp, GDF-15) in acute COVID-19 patients and following them for 6 months. Found that biomarkers normalized by follow-up despite persistent neurological symptoms like fatigue and brain fog, indicating long COVID sequelae are not accompanied by ongoing CNS injury.

This nested longitudinal case-control study examined plasma proteome differences in 156 healthcare workers to identify biomarkers predicting persistent symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found that proteomic signatures at seroconversion associated with long COVID development but does not test any intervention or treatment.

IMPACC is a prospective observational study of 1,164 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 1 year post-discharge, identifying risk factors for acute disease severity and PASC development. While the study includes PASC follow-up data, it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is purely observational surveillance, making it ineligible for inclusion in a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This prospective observational cohort study examined long COVID symptoms in 1,267 infected and exposed household members approximately one year after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found higher prevalence of persistent symptoms in infected women, men, and adolescent girls compared to exposed counterparts, with symptoms tending to cluster within families.

This UK Biobank cohort study identifies 10 core post-COVID symptoms and classifies patients into four distinct subtypes (ENT, cardiopulmonary, neurological, general fatigue) based on symptom clustering. The study examines virus- and host-related risk factors for long COVID and assesses impacts on physical and mental health outcomes, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study of 276 children and adolescents followed for 8 months post-delta infection examining the relationship between antibody responses and persistent long COVID symptoms. Found that higher delta antibody titres were significantly associated with persisting symptoms, and adolescents had higher rates of long-term symptoms than children.

Retrospective cohort study examining long-term cardiovascular outcomes in patients with pre-existing coronary artery disease after SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing hospitalized COVID+ patients, non-hospitalized COVID+ patients, and COVID- controls. Study found that hospitalized COVID-19 patients had higher risk of MACE, mortality, CHF, MI, and stroke up to four years post-infection, but this is an observational outcome study without any treatment intervention being tested.

A prospective cohort study investigating blood DNA methylation patterns in PASC patients compared to post-COVID without PASC and healthy controls. Identifies differentially methylated regions specific to PASC and uses machine learning to stratify severity, suggesting circadian rhythm-regulating pathways are involved in PASC pathophysiology.

Prospective cohort study examining plasma biomarkers (pTau-181, GFAP, NfL, amyloid) in essential workers before and after COVID-19 onset, comparing those who developed neurological PASC (N-PASC) with controls. Found that increased pTau-181 levels after COVID-19 were associated with central neurological symptoms in N-PASC patients, suggesting potential Alzheimer's disease-like pathology.

Retrospective study comparing serial transthoracic echocardiogram measurements in COVID-19 patients before and after infection to assess post-COVID cardiac changes. Found minimal clinically significant changes in ventricular strain, though patients with new symptoms were more likely to show worsening strain values.

Prospective cohort study examining pathophysiological mechanisms of post-acute sequelae following COVID-19 (PASC) in non-hospitalized patients, comparing 311 PASC participants with 490 recovered controls across biomarkers and symptoms. Found dynamic associations between persistent symptoms and inflammatory/vascular biomarkers, particularly in earlier disease stages, suggesting polymorphic pathophysiology beyond persistent inflammation.

A two-year longitudinal proteomic study of 181 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors profiling plasma samples at 6-month, 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups to identify differentially expressed proteins and pathways associated with long COVID. The study identified protein biomarkers in complement/coagulation and cardiomyopathy pathways linked to lung function recovery and smell disorder, providing mechanistic insights into long COVID pathophysiology.

This study compares cardiac structure and function (via echocardiography) between 190 long COVID patients and 979 propensity-matched pre-COVID controls from the same community. It finds subclinical systolic dysfunction and impaired global longitudinal strain in long COVID patients, which is weakly associated with functional impairment.

Longitudinal observational study comparing cardiopulmonary abnormalities and symptoms in 58 post-COVID-19 patients versus 30 matched controls at 3 and 6 months post-infection. Findings show that while objective cardiopulmonary measures improve over time, persistent symptoms at 6 months do not correlate with detectable cardiac, lung, or exercise impairment.

A prospective, population-based cohort study of 1,442 German COVID-19 survivors that characterizes post-COVID syndrome severity, prevalence, and predictors at 6-12 months post-infection. The study develops and validates a symptom-based PCS severity score and identifies acute phase symptom intensity and personal resilience as key predictors of long COVID outcomes.

This study examined cognitive deficits in 46 COVID-19 survivors who received critical care, comparing their cognitive performance to matched controls at ~6 months follow-up. While it documents persistent cognitive impairment related to acute illness severity, it is a cross-sectional observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for a trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective cohort study comparing cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) findings in 18 PASC patients with dyspnea/exercise intolerance to age- and sex-matched controls with unexplained dyspnea from the pre-COVID era. Despite prominent dyspnea, PASC patients showed similar physiological findings on CPET to matched comparators, with 67% having normal CPET results.

Prospective multicentre study assessing frequency and severity of fatigue and cognitive impairment in 969 long COVID patients (≥6 months post-infection) compared to matched non-COVID controls. Found 19% had clinically relevant fatigue and 27% had mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment, with distinct risk factors for each condition, suggesting separate pathophysiological pathways.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data comparing cardiovascular outcomes in 4.1M COVID-19 survivors vs matched controls over 12 months post-infection. Documents elevated risks of stroke, arrhythmia, myocarditis, heart failure, and thromboembolic events, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective longitudinal cohort study followed 288 COVID-19 survivors for 2 years after infection to track changes in pulmonary function, dyspnea, and exercise capacity across disease severity groups. Corticosteroid therapy during hospitalization was associated with improved lung function recovery from 6 months to 1 year, though pulmonary parameters declined from year 1 to year 2.

Retrospective multi-centre observational cohort study of 12,891 COVID-19 patients examining kidney function recovery and mortality outcomes following acute kidney injury (AKI) during acute hospitalization. Study identifies factors associated with worse kidney recovery and mortality, but focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae.

Prospective observational study comparing structural brain imaging (MRI) in 50 post-COVID fatigue patients versus healthy controls and MS patients. Found characteristic thalamic and basal ganglia changes correlated with fatigue severity, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Prospective cohort study of 1,243 children with confirmed COVID-19 followed for up to 18 months to identify risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and characterize longitudinal recovery patterns. Found that acute-phase hospitalization, pre-existing comorbidities, pre-Omicron variants, and older age (>10 years) were associated with higher PCC risk, with most children recovering over time.

Prospective cohort study tracking physical frailty in 2,419 UK adults hospitalized with COVID-19 using Fried's Frailty Phenotype at 5 months and 1 year post-discharge. No intervention is given; the study passively observes frailty prevalence and risk factors in recovering COVID-19 patients without assigning or evaluating a treatment.

Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from Hong Kong and UK to assess post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 infection in 551,586 patients with COVID-19 and matched controls. Study documents increased risk of cardiovascular, pulmonary, neuropsychiatric, renal, and other complications during the post-acute phase, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This prospective cohort study assessed cognitive performance (working memory, attention, reasoning, motor control) in 3,335 UK COVID Symptom Study participants, comparing those with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. Cognitive deficits were detected in individuals with long COVID symptoms (~2 years post-infection), particularly those with ≥12 weeks of ongoing symptoms, but not in those who reported full recovery.

This prospective cohort study develops and validates the Post COVID-19 Condition Stigma Questionnaire (PCCSQ) to measure stigma experienced by long COVID patients, finding high reliability and validity. The study identifies associations between stigma scores and depression, anxiety, disability status, and functional impairment, but does not test any treatment intervention.

This retrospective multi-centre cohort study used electronic health records from 30,422 COVID-19 patients to characterize seven distinct long COVID (PASC) sub-phenotypes and their temporal attributes using distributed representation learning. The study identified sub-phenotypes and estimated prevalence rates (15.7% with ≥1 symptom, 5.98% with multiple symptoms), with joint pain and dyspnea being most prevalent, but did not test any specific treatment or intervention.

This is a prospective observational cohort study examining the incidence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition in 286 pregnant and postpartum women followed for a mean of 92 weeks after acute COVID-19 infection. The study does not evaluate any treatment intervention; instead, it documents natural disease progression and identifies demographic and clinical risk factors (34.2% developed post-COVID-19 symptoms), making it an epidemiological study rather than a treatment trial.

Prospective population-based study comparing long-term symptom profiles in 10,171 UK participants with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, non-COVID-19 acute respiratory infections, or no infection. Study identifies symptom clusters and severity groups but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective multinational cohort study following 1,796 SARS-CoV-2 patients for 12 months to identify clinical phenotypes of post-COVID syndrome and associated risk/protective factors using cluster analysis and machine learning. Identifies 4 distinct phenotypes (chronic fatigue, respiratory, chronic pain, neurosensorial syndromes) with different risk factors and QoL impacts, but does not test a specific intervention—instead analyzes existing risk factors and prior treatments retrospectively.

Prospective population-based cohort study following 3,038 German COVID-19 survivors for up to 26 months to assess long-term trajectories of fatigue and cognitive deficits and identify predictors of recovery. Found that 46% recovered from fatigue and 57% from cognitive deficits within two years, with depression, headache, male sex, older age, and lower education as risk factors for non-recovery.

Prospective observational cohort study tracking 106 post-COVID-19 patients with moderate-to-severe fatigue over 20 months, measuring symptom severity and biomarkers (hand grip strength, cardiovascular function, laboratory parameters). Patients meeting ME/CFS criteria showed persistent high symptom severity and fatigue/PEM, while general PCS patients improved; lower grip strength at onset correlated with symptom persistence.

Prospective observational cohort study following 111 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in South Africa for up to 40 days post-discharge to assess lung outcomes and functional impairment. Found substantial pulmonary and functional morbidity, with 78.9% elevated respiratory symptom scores and 49.5% with spirometry abnormalities, particularly in patients with pre-existing TB, HIV, or extreme BMI.

Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence of long COVID in people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes compared to matched controls in a UK population. The study found similar or lower long COVID prevalence in diabetic individuals, with some sex-specific differences and associations with age and BMI.

This national retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records for 4.7 million Scottish adults to estimate long COVID prevalence (0.02-1.7% depending on identification method) and identify associated risk factors. The study found long COVID more common in females, middle-aged adults, those with comorbidities, immunosuppression, or prior hospitalization, but is not a treatment study and should be excluded from the intervention trials dataset.

This OpenSAFELY study analyzed electronic health records from 19 million adults in England to describe the incidence and demographic characteristics of recorded long COVID diagnoses in primary care between 2020-2023. The findings show very low EHR recording of long COVID (55,465 cases) with declining incident records over 2022, highlighting limitations of diagnostic coding for case identification.

This retrospective cohort study from the RECOVER Initiative compares the incidence of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) in females who acquired SARS-CoV-2 during pregnancy versus outside of pregnancy using electronic health record data from 19 U.S. health systems. The study found that SARS-CoV-2 infection acquired during pregnancy was associated with lower overall PASC risk (25.5% vs 33.9%) but increased risk for specific complications including abnormal heartbeat and thromboembolism.

A 3-year prospective cohort study following 1,319 children post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to characterize long COVID prevalence, predictors, and outcomes. Found that age >12 years, infection with original/alpha variants, and lack of vaccination were significant risk factors for long COVID duration, with vaccination associated with lower risk at 3, 6, and 12 months.

This study evaluates BNT162b2 vaccine effectiveness in reducing long COVID risk in children and adolescents using real-world EHR data from the RECOVER PCORnet. The vaccine showed 95.4% effectiveness during Delta and 60-75% during Omicron, with mediation analysis indicating protection is primarily through preventing initial SARS-CoV-2 infection rather than direct mitigation of post-infection sequelae.

Prospective cohort study following UK COVID-19 hospitalized patients with and without diabetes at 5 and 12 months post-discharge. Finds people with diabetes have worse physical outcomes, higher fatigue, frailty, lower physical performance, and poorer cognitive function compared to those without diabetes.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 771,725 children across 24 U.S. health systems to examine racial and ethnic differences in long COVID (respiratory and neurological PASC). Among children with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection, the study found that Hispanic White children and those under 5 years had higher odds of respiratory PASC, while older children and those with pre-existing neurologic conditions were more likely to have neurologic PASC, with disparities potentially reflecting inequities in healthcare access.

International retrospective cohort study estimating the incidence of 25 WHO-proposed post-acute COVID-19 symptoms across healthcare settings in seven countries using routinely-collected data. Found that joint pain, abdominal pain, and gastrointestinal issues were most common, with higher incidence in the COVID-infected cohort compared to general population.

Longitudinal descriptive study examining the relationship between PCC-related stigma, disease manifestations, and health outcomes in 99 Canadian participants followed over ~1.6 years. Found that baseline stigma significantly correlates with subsequent symptoms, depression, and functional decline, but no intervention or treatment was administered.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study following 254 COVID-19 patients for 12 months after hospital discharge to assess persistence of long COVID symptoms. Found that 40.5% reported at least one symptom at 12 months, with fatigue, dyspnea, and cough being most common, and identified age, frailty, and baseline symptom burden as risk factors for symptom persistence.

A cross-sectional study of 101 COVID-19 patients 10 months post-hospitalization assessing symptoms, lung function, and psychological measures. Found high prevalence of fatigue (49%), shortness of breath (49%), and cognitive impairment (39%), with associations to depression and quality of life but not to objective measures of lung function or physical capacity.

This interrupted time series study evaluated subcutaneous lidocaine-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin injections in 103 post-COVID patients over 24-36 weeks of home-based treatment. The treatment was associated with significant improvements in quality of life and symptom burden, with 27 of 30 symptoms improving significantly by week 24, though mild adverse events occurred in 89% of participants.

Retrospective cohort study of 204 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessing the prevalence and recovery trajectory of chronic fatigue symptoms over 12+ weeks post-infection. Fatigue remained elevated (66.17%) at >12 weeks, predicted by female sex and younger age, but this is an observational follow-up study with no intervention or treatment tested.

Observational study analyzing the prevalence and persistence of long COVID sequelae in cancer patients from the OnCovid registry over 12 months post-infection. Found that 16.6% of patients reported sequelae (fatigue, respiratory, neuro-cognitive), with 8-9.8% experiencing persistence at 6-12 months, highlighting need for supportive strategies in this population.

A multicenter prospective cohort study of 2,000 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors from Madrid hospitals examining associations between acute-phase symptoms and long-term post-COVID symptoms one year after discharge using network analysis. The study identifies which acute symptoms predict the development and clustering of post-COVID symptoms in previously hospitalized patients.

Prospective study of 232 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors evaluated lung ultrasound (LUS) as a diagnostic tool compared to chest CT for assessing residual lung pathology at 3-month follow-up. LUS showed high sensitivity (91% at cut-off ≥3) for detecting pathological findings and good agreement with CT, suggesting LUS could replace CT in resource-limited settings for post-COVID pulmonary assessment.

A prospective cohort study of 112 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for one year to assess autonomic symptoms and quality of life using standardized questionnaires (COMPASS-31 and SF-36). The study found that 47% of patients experienced worsening autonomic symptoms at 6 and 12 months post-infection, suggesting a long-COVID autonomic syndrome, though the paper does not test a specific treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study using multi-parametric MRI to assess organ health in blood cancer patients who recovered from COVID-19, comparing multi-organ abnormalities to healthy controls. While the study documents persistent organ impairment in post-COVID blood cancer patients, it is observational without any treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.

This retrospective observational study examines long COVID symptoms in healthcare workers at a nephrology department in Malaysia, documenting prevalence and symptom patterns. It is excluded as a secondary analysis that does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective follow-up study examines kidney function and prognosis in COVID-19 survivors who required kidney replacement therapy during acute infection, tracking outcomes 90 days post-hospitalization. The paper assesses post-acute kidney sequelae in this severe COVID-19 subgroup but does not test an intervention or treatment.

Retrospective follow-up study comparing chest CT changes at 6 and 12 months post-COVID-19 in patients with diabetes, secondary hyperglycemia, and controls. Found that 54.6% of patients had residual lung abnormalities at 6-month follow-up, with diabetes/hyperglycemia patients showing significantly higher incidence.

This study investigates associations between ambient air pollution, temperature exposure, and recovery duration in COVID-19 patients from the initial 2020 outbreak in Changsha, China. It finds that short-term exposure to CO and PM2.5 are associated with prolonged recovery, while ozone exposure is protective, but does not study any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 655 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors followed for up to 11 months to investigate acute kidney injury phenotypes and late kidney dysfunction. Community-acquired AKI was independently associated with late kidney dysfunction affecting 28% of survivors, highlighting renal long COVID as a frequent complication.

This retrospective cohort study examines long-term kidney function outcomes in COVID-19 survivors who were hospitalized, comparing those who developed acute kidney injury (AKI) during hospitalization with those who did not. The study tracks the evolution of renal function over time in post-COVID survivors to assess whether AKI during acute infection leads to persistent kidney dysfunction.

This study examines the association between air pollution exposure and objective lung health measures (pulmonary function and radiological abnormalities) in 95 long COVID patients 3-6 months post-infection. The findings show that personal PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased risk of airway abnormalities on follow-up CT imaging, suggesting air pollution may play a role in long COVID pathophysiology.

Observational follow-up study of 204 COVID-19 survivors assessing prevalence of long COVID (20.1%) and associations with thyroid function and autoimmunity. Found female sex and high viral load predicted long COVID occurrence, but thyroid function tests were not associated with long COVID; incident anti-TPO positivity was observed and may be protective for symptom resolution.

This study assessed psychiatric and cognitive outcomes in 425 COVID-19 survivors 6-9 months after hospitalization using standardized clinical interviews and psychometric tests. The authors found elevated rates of depression (8%), anxiety (15.5%), and PTSD (13.6%), with 51.1% reporting memory decline, but no significant association between acute-phase disease severity and neuropsychiatric impairment.

This study screened gastrointestinal biopsies and fluids from endoscopy patients (100 without known COVID-19 and 12 with previous COVID-19 diagnosis) for SARS-CoV-2 RNA and viable virus. The findings showed persistent viral RNA detection in some patients post-COVID but no infectious virions recovered, suggesting the gut may serve as a long-term viral reservoir without posing significant infection risk.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive function 3-4 months after COVID-19 hospitalization in 29 patients, finding clinically significant cognitive impairment in 59-65% with verbal learning and executive functions most affected. Cognitive impairment correlated with subjective complaints, lower work function, poorer quality of life, elevated d-dimer levels, and residual pulmonary dysfunction.

A prospective cohort study following COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 12 months post-discharge, assessing postural balance, mobility, and handgrip strength at multiple timepoints. The study documents high prevalence of impairments in these physical functions persisting 12 months after discharge, highlighting the need for long-term physical therapy, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data comparing erectile dysfunction risk in men with COVID-19 versus non-infected controls, matched for age, race, BMI, and comorbidities. Found significantly increased risk of new-onset erectile dysfunction post-COVID-19 infection.

Observational study documenting the natural history of psychiatric and neuropsychological symptoms in 64 long COVID patients over 24 months post-infection. Tracks prevalence changes over time but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study following 95 patients with pseudo-chilblain lesions (acrosyndrome) during the COVID-19 pandemic to assess relapse frequency and persistent skin symptoms over 10 months. Found that 54% experienced recurrent episodes and 67% reported persistent cutaneous symptoms consistent with long COVID, though no specific treatment was tested.

Retrospective population-based cohort study of 84,034 COVID-19 survivors matched to controls, examining risk of incident thyroid dysfunction during the post-acute phase (median follow-up 303 days). Study found no significant increase in thyroid dysfunction risk post-COVID, with reassuring findings across multiple secondary outcomes and subgroup analyses.

A 24-month prospective cohort study of 1,565 COVID-19 survivors examining mental health outcomes including anxiety, depression, PTSD, and insomnia. The study identified associated factors but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention, making it an observational follow-up study rather than a treatment trial.

Retrospective cohort study examining the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) compared to matched non-IMID controls using Danish national registers. Found increased PASC risk in IMID patients, particularly those with spondylarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriasis.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study comparing long-term GI and mental health symptoms in COVID-positive vs COVID-negative patients at 6-12 months follow-up. Found that after accounting for sadness and anxiety, there was no association between COVID-19 status and GI symptoms, suggesting psychological factors mediate post-COVID GI symptoms.

A naturalistic case series evaluating telepsychotherapy outcomes in COVID-19 survivors with psychiatric symptoms, primarily anxiety and depression. The study found that patients recovering from moderate to severe COVID-19 illness could successfully engage with virtual psychotherapy platforms and showed reductions in psychiatric symptoms.

This observational cohort study measured salivary levels of cell cycle regulatory proteins (p53, cyclin D1, CDK4) and protein carbonylation in 40 post-COVID patients at baseline and 6-month follow-up. The study found significant increases in p53, cyclin D1, and protein carbonylation levels, suggesting long-term cellular effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A national matched cohort study comparing persisting symptoms in children and young people with and without prior COVID-19 infection. The study identifies fatigue, headache, shortness of breath, and loss of smell as common long COVID symptoms and examines risk factors (older age, female sex, minority ethnicity, pre-existing health issues) and the role of vaccination in mitigating existing long COVID.

Retrospective analysis of 118 heart transplant recipients who had COVID-19 to assess the incidence of long COVID. Found only 3% (4/118) met criteria for long COVID, suggesting lower incidence in this immunosuppressed population compared to general population estimates.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term organ transplant function (heart, liver, kidney) between COVID-19 infected and uninfected recipients at a single center. Heart transplant recipients showed significant decreases in ejection fraction post-infection, while kidney and liver function changes were not statistically significant.

A retrospective cohort study comparing COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome in symptomatic and asymptomatic patients in Bangladesh. The study identifies risk factors for developing post-COVID-19 (age, duration, respiratory distress, blood group, severity) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study tracked 22 severely hospitalized COVID-19 patients at acute, 1-month, and 6-month timepoints to investigate the relationship between prolonged inflammation markers and long-term cardiovascular complications. The authors identified IL-18 as a key driver of cardiovascular inflammation and established immune-related biomarkers for stratifying patients at high CVD risk, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study identifies 477 U.S. patients who underwent lung transplantation for COVID-19 respiratory failure between March 2020 and December 2022, tracking trends in transplant rates and post-transplant outcomes. The procedure increasingly addresses post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis rather than acute ARDS, with a 1-year post-transplant mortality of 13.7%.

Prospective cohort study comparing prevalence and severity of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) three months after Omicron infection versus Delta, test-negative controls, and population controls across 4,138 Omicron cases. Finds PCC prevalence 41% lower after Omicron (10.4%) than Delta (17.7%), with reinfection associated with more severe long-term symptoms.

Observational study comparing post-acute sequelae prevalence between vaccinated and unvaccinated hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at 2-month and 1-year follow-up using multidisciplinary assessment. Vaccination status is a risk stratification variable, not a treatment intervention assigned by the study.

Retrospective cohort study of 128 lung transplant recipients who contracted COVID-19, examining risk factors for persistent decline in lung graft function. While studying post-COVID complications in transplant patients, this is not a long COVID study as it focuses on organ allograft dysfunction rather than persistent symptoms in the general long COVID population.

This study analyzed 1,058 Chinese medicine (CM) clinical records from 150 post-COVID patients to identify persistent clinical conditions and their associations with CM syndromes. Researchers found three common CM syndrome patterns (Qi and Yin Deficiency, Lung and Spleen Deficiency, Spleen-Lung Qi Deficiency) associated with nine persistent symptoms including fatigue, poor sleep, and shortness of breath, with significant associations to female gender and pre-existing chronic conditions.

Retrospective study of 22 long-COVID patients comparing pulmonary function decline (>10% FEV1 decrease) vs stability using serial spirometry and chest CT imaging. Identifies neutrophil counts, lymphocyte ratios, and imaging markers (reticulation, ground-glass opacities) as potential predictors of post-COVID lung function decline.

This prospective cohort study analyzes regulatory T cell profiles in pediatric patients recovering from COVID-19, including those who developed multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C), at two timepoints between 2-15 months post-infection. The findings show that MIS-C patients had elevated Treg cell counts and a temporary immunosuppressive state during early convalescence that normalized around one year post-infection.

This cross-sectional study investigates exaggerated exertional tachycardia (EET) in 79 long COVID patients, comparing cardiac and pulmonary characteristics between those with EET versus normal exertional tachycardia using 6-minute walk tests and echocardiography. The study identifies oxygen desaturation during exercise as a predictor of abnormal heart rate response, showing EET is associated with impaired pulmonary function and reduced cardiac systolic/diastolic function.

Prospective cohort study of 46 former ICU patients treated for COVID-19, assessed at 4 and 12 months post-discharge using validated instruments. Study found persistent fatigue (82%), cognitive impairment improving from 52% to 31%, and low employment rates, indicating poor long-term recovery without clear improvement in physical or psychological outcomes.

Retrospective cohort study of 494 COVID-19 patients followed for ~1 year to identify risk factors for long COVID affecting the digestive system. Found that liver function abnormality on admission was associated with a 3.5-fold increased risk of developing digestive long COVID syndrome.

This retrospective observational study describes the 3-month sequelae in 51 young, comorbid patients who recovered from severe COVID-19, including persistent symptoms (fatigue 74.5%, dyspnea 66%), pulmonary imaging abnormalities (64.7%), diffusion impairment (46.3%), and anxiety (51%). The study is a descriptive cohort follow-up without any intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for intervention trial analysis.

A systematic assessment of 116 healthcare workers infected with COVID-19 in March-April 2020, evaluated at a mean of 67 days post-infection for physical and psychological outcomes. The study found persistent symptoms in 64 participants (55%) including fatigue and dyspnea, significant anxiety in one-third, and overall high satisfaction with the multidisciplinary assessment program, but it is a descriptive follow-up survey without treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 641 sailors (413 COVID-positive, 206 COVID-negative) followed for 12 months post-outbreak to characterize long COVID symptoms and their prevalence. Found that 53.7-55.2% of COVID-positive participants reported persistent symptoms at 6-9 months, with common symptoms including concentration/memory difficulties, fatigue, and sleep disorders.

Retrospective study comparing long COVID risk across SARS-CoV-2 variants (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) in 325 hospitalized patients with genomic sequencing. Found Omicron associated with lower odds of long-term sequelae compared to Alpha, while ICU admission and antiviral/immunomodulatory treatment predicted higher risk.

A prospective cohort study that followed 51 COVID-19 patients with impaired lung diffusion capacity (DLCO) from 3 months to 1 year post-infection. While some patients showed improvement, 71% still had abnormal DLCO at 1 year, with obesity associated with lack of improvement—a natural history study without an intervention.

This prospective cohort study followed 129 ambulatory COVID-19 patients using telemedicine software to monitor symptom evolution over time. At 3+ months follow-up, 43% of patients remained symptomatic with persistent fatigue, anosmia/ageusia, respiratory symptoms, and other long COVID manifestations, demonstrating high symptom persistence in non-hospitalized cases.

Longitudinal serological and immunological follow-up of 256 SARS-CoV-2 positive healthcare workers over 7 months, examining antibody dynamics and persistence of symptoms. 32.4% of followed participants reported persistent symptoms consistent with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome, with no active treatment intervention studied.

Prospective multicenter follow-up study of 179 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 12 months post-discharge, assessing pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and symptom burden. While pulmonary physiology improved (6MWT distance increased significantly), persistent symptoms including fatigue, depression, and anxiety did not improve over the follow-up period.

This study assessed functional capacity and exercise tolerance in 200 COVID-19 survivors at 3 months post-discharge using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and related measurements. About one-third showed functional limitations, primarily due to muscular impairment, with the study calling for future research on targeted rehabilitation rather than testing an intervention.

Observational study of 63 non-severe COVID-19 outpatients followed for 6 months to characterize persistent symptoms and document natural recovery rates. At 6 months, 30% had complete recovery, 57% partial recovery, and 13% no recovery, with dyspnea and asthenia/myalgia being the most persistent symptoms.

Retrospective study of 180 long COVID patients examining the prevalence and clinical characteristics of acute pericarditis as a manifestation of long COVID-19 syndrome. Found pericarditis in 22% of patients, with heart palpitations/arrhythmias and autoimmune/allergic disorders as independent risk factors.

Prospective case-control study comparing endothelial vascular function in acute COVID-19, post-COVID patients, and matched controls using reactive hyperemia peripheral arterial tonometry. Found significantly impaired endothelial function in post-COVID patients (101.5 days post-symptom onset) compared to acute and control groups, suggesting persistent systemic vascular dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study compared exercise capacity and cardiopulmonary function in UK military personnel with and without post-COVID syndrome using imaging and exercise testing. Results showed stepwise declines in exercise capacity and cardiac/pulmonary function in those with prolonged post-COVID symptoms, though findings may reflect deconditioning as well as direct COVID-19 pathology.

This retrospective study of 51 pediatric patients examines cardiovascular complications in PIMS-TS (pediatric multisystem inflammatory syndrome temporally associated with COVID-19), a serious acute inflammatory complication occurring weeks after COVID-19 infection. While PIMS-TS is technically temporally associated with prior COVID-19, this paper is fundamentally about acute post-infection inflammatory syndrome rather than long COVID, and contains no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This prospective study examined cardiac inflammation and remodeling in COVID-19 survivors with myocardial injury during acute infection using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Findings showed high prevalence of myocardial and pericardial involvement (43-50% of patients), with some partial reversal on follow-up imaging.

Observational study evaluating myocardial injury in 20 non-hospitalised patients with persistent symptoms >4 months after mild COVID-19 using cardiac MRI and pulmonary investigations. Found a higher-than-expected burden of myocardial fibrosis (scar on LGE imaging) in this long COVID cohort despite absence of abnormal T1/T2 values.

ARCA post-COVID is an observational study investigating the prevalence of new cardiac alterations (NCA) in 502 COVID-19 recovered patients between June 2020 and December 2022. The study found NCA in 27.49% of patients, with pericardial effusion in 11.95%, and identified risk factors including older age, smoking, prior CAD, and stroke/TIA history.

This cross-sectional study compared circulating angiogenic progenitor cells (CAC) and endothelial cells (CEC) in 14 post-hospitalized post-COVID syndrome (PH-PCS) patients versus 7 matched controls at ≥18 months post-infection. The study found suggestive but imprecise evidence of unbalanced CAC and CEC apoptosis in PH-PCS patients, with possible associations between reduced flow-mediated dilation and cellular markers.

Longitudinal study tracking anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels in 61 convalescent patients over 8 months and their association with post-COVID syndrome symptoms. Found stable antibody titers in 92% of participants and 46.8% prevalence of post-COVID syndrome, primarily affecting olfactory and gustatory function.

A 90-day prospective cohort study comparing symptom trajectories in 210 SARS-CoV-2 positive vs 630 negative healthcare workers. Found persistent loss of taste/smell in 30% of positive cases and prolonged dyspnea at low levels, while most other acute symptoms resolved by 30 days.

This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence of long-term sick leave (≥4 weeks) among 30,950 working-age COVID-19 patients in German general practices and identifies associated risk factors. The study is observational without treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective cohort study examining associations between post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) and cardiac outcomes in 997,785 U.S. military members. PASC was significantly associated with increased odds of multiple cardiac events including myocarditis, heart failure, and arrhythmias.

Prospective follow-up study of 94 COVID-19 survivors one year post-hospitalization, assessing symptoms, imaging, and pulmonary function. Found high prevalence of chest CT abnormalities (71%) and muscle fatigue/insomnia as most common symptoms, with urea nitrogen associated with impaired lung diffusion capacity.

This study measured serum biomarkers (laminin, vWF, SP-D, RAGE) in 52 COVID-19 survivors 6 months post-discharge compared to 30 healthy controls. No treatment was administered; it is a purely observational study examining persistent lung injury indicators rather than evaluating any intervention.

A 6-month prospective study of 75 patients with non-severe acute COVID-19, tracking long COVID symptoms occurring 1-12 weeks post-infection. Documents prevalence of fatigue (33%), anxiety (40%), brain fog (20%), respiratory symptoms, and other manifestations, with findings that symptom burden correlates with patient age.

Prospective observational cohort study following 199 patients hospitalized with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to characterize long-term sequelae. At 6 months, 47% had persistent exertional dyspnea and 32% had fatigue; imaging showed high prevalence of persistent abnormalities despite some functional improvement over time.

Multicenter observational study tracking the recovery trajectory of post-COVID-19 symptoms in 1,593 previously hospitalized patients at two timepoints (8.4 and 13.2 months post-hospitalization). Found that symptom burden decreased over time, with 61.8% of patients reporting fewer symptoms at the later follow-up.

Multicenter retrospective cohort study of 1,969 COVID-19 patients hospitalized in Madrid, assessing clinical risk factors associated with long-term post-COVID symptoms at 8.4 months follow-up. Found that higher symptom load during acute phase (female gender, comorbidities, specific symptoms like vomiting, dyspnea, headache) predicted greater number of long-term symptoms, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 316 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed 4 months post-discharge to identify risk factors for long COVID-19 persistence. Found that female sex, hypertension, and higher number of initial symptoms were significantly associated with persistent symptoms, but acute severity measures were not.

Longitudinal surveillance study tracking post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in Long Beach residents from April-December 2020, with follow-up at 1 and 2 months post-testing. Identified prevalence of PASC, associated risk factors (age, gender, race, comorbidities), and most common symptoms (fatigue, anosmia, dyspnea).

Multicenter prospective cohort study describing long-COVID symptoms in older adults (>65 years) versus younger individuals across Israel, Switzerland, Spain, and Italy. Found older adults more symptomatic with higher rates of fatigue (38%) and dyspnea (30%), plus pulmonary impairment, while female gender and obesity emerged as independent risk factors across age groups.

Longitudinal cohort study following 226 nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients from the Faroe Islands with up to 8 months follow-up to assess long COVID prevalence and symptom burden. Found 39% reported persistent symptoms and 8% reported severe persistent symptoms, with fatigue and smell/taste dysfunction being most common.

This study compares post-acute COVID-19 symptoms 3-15 months after infection between unvaccinated and vaccinated individuals with breakthrough infections using questionnaire data from the Norwegian COVID-19 cohort. Vaccination offered minor protection against PASC symptoms overall, with vaccinated participants reporting fewer memory problems than unvaccinated participants.

Prospective observational cohort study following 155 COVID-19 patients at 2-4 months and 7-14 months post-infection to assess health-related quality of life using the SF-12 questionnaire and identify predictors of post-COVID syndrome. Patients with persistent symptoms had significantly lower physical composite scores that did not improve over time, with lower baseline physical function and elevated resting heart rate identified as predictors of long COVID at 1 year.

Prospective study examining short- and long-term immune changes across COVID-19 severity groups at presentation, week 2, and week 24. Findings show differential immune responses by severity, with severe/critical patients showing initial dysfunction but partial normalization by 24 weeks.

This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence, risk factors, and healthcare costs of long COVID in 180,759 Israeli COVID-19 patients, identifying 14,088 cases (7.8%). Long COVID was associated with increased hospitalizations and significantly higher direct medical costs ($2,810 vs $1,021 for non-long COVID patients), highlighting the substantial economic burden of the condition.

Population-based cohort study characterizing 10,196 Swedish patients diagnosed with post-COVID-19 condition (U09.9) during the first 16 months of ICD-10 code implementation. Study describes sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, and disease patterns but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

An 18.5-month prospective cohort study of 208 COVID-19 convalescents documenting sequential improvements in physical and psychological sequelae, but with persistent symptoms in 45.2% and abnormal lung imaging in ~30% at the final timepoint. The study identifies ongoing pathophysiological alterations and risk factors for symptom persistence but does not test any intervention.

Prospective cohort study following hospitalized and nonhospitalized COVID-19 patients in South Africa across three variant waves to assess post-COVID-19 condition prevalence at 6 months. Found 46.7% of hospitalized and 18.5% of nonhospitalized participants had persistent symptoms; identified risk factors including age, sex, comorbidities, and severity but found no intervention or treatment being tested.

Population-based retrospective cohort study examining incident diabetes risk following COVID-19 infection using BC COVID-19 Cohort data. Finds increased diabetes incidence in COVID-19 infected individuals, particularly among males and those with severe disease (HR=1.16-3.32).

Observational study comparing persistent symptoms in 639 Argentine children with prior COVID-19 versus 577 uninfected controls. One-third of infected children experienced long COVID symptoms; older age, symptomatic infection, and comorbidities were independent risk factors.

Retrospective analysis of 83 cases of Clostridium difficile colitis occurring during or after COVID-19 infection in post-COVID patients, examining risk factors and therapeutic outcomes. The study found that prior broad-spectrum antibiotic use was a major risk factor (occurring in 55% of cases), and demonstrated efficacy of vancomycin, metronidazole, and fidaxonicin treatments with 14% recurrence rate and FMT used in severe cases.

This prospective cohort study tracks 2,197 long COVID patients over 2 years to identify symptom evolution patterns using trajectory modeling. The study identifies three trajectories: 91% with slowly decreasing symptoms, 5% with rapid improvement, and 4% with persistent symptoms, but does not test any intervention.

This is a secondary analysis of the DigiHero cohort study examining how SARS-CoV-2 variants, vaccination, and previous infections affect post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) risk. The study does not test or evaluate any intervention—it is purely observational, comparing PCC risk across variant exposures and vaccination histories.

Prospective observational cohort study evaluating the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on long COVID (post-COVID condition) symptoms, immune responses, and viral persistence in 86 patients. Vaccination was associated with significant decreases in symptom count and organ system involvement, increased well-being scores, and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, though SARS-CoV-2 viral antigens persisted in blood regardless of vaccination status.

A prospective cohort study of 806 long COVID patients followed for 1.5 years post-infection, comparing symptom severity and prognosis across SARS-CoV-2 variants (wild-type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron). The study found no clinically meaningful improvement over 1.5 years, with >57% of patients showing persistent severe symptoms regardless of infection variant.

Prospective multicenter cohort study of 502 patients hospitalized for COVID-19, examining whether in-hospital treatments (steroids, anti-inflammatory, antiviral) predict long-term health problems at 2-year follow-up. Found that in-hospital COVID-19 treatments were not significantly associated with long-term health problems including dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive failures, or quality of life.

A prospective cohort study of 231 French long COVID patients followed for 12 months to examine symptom course, impact on daily life, and factors associated with improvement. Found that only 8.7% achieved complete remission, 28.6% improved significantly, and most symptoms persisted; presence of pre-vaccination SARS-CoV-2 antibodies predicted improvement while ageusia predicted worse outcomes.

This study analyzed pre-pandemic predictors of long COVID in a representative Dutch population of 3,022 participants, identifying sociodemographic, medical, and psychosocial factors associated with long COVID development. The authors used K-means clustering to identify four distinct symptom clusters and their respective predictors, revealing heterogeneous presentations of long COVID.

Prospective cohort study tracking 14 somatic and cognitive symptoms in 120,605 Norwegian adults with pre-infection baseline measurements and follow-up for up to 22 months. Study confirms COVID-19 associated with persistent cognitive symptoms, anosmia, dysgeusia, dyspnea, and fatigue, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from South Korean COVID-19 patients aged >60 years to investigate whether oral antivirals (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir) reduce the risk of postacute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) within 30-120 days post-infection. Both antivirals showed significant protective effects against multiple PASC outcomes, including cardiovascular complications, respiratory diseases, and renal disorders, suggesting oral antivirals may mitigate long-term COVID-19 effects.

Prospective cohort study comparing post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) prevalence in Delta- vs Omicron-infected adults over 12 months with population controls. PASC prevalence was higher for Delta initially (34.3% at 3 months) than Omicron (18.7%), but both declined over time and converged by 12 months.

This is a secondary analysis of national electronic health records examining hospitalization and mortality outcomes in COVID-19 and Long COVID patients, stratified by vaccination status and cardiovascular disease. While about Long COVID, it analyzes existing data rather than testing a specific intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term sequelae 31-300 days post-hospitalization between Omicron COVID-19 (n=70,628) and influenza (n=10,454) patients in Singapore, stratified by vaccination status. Found higher risks of cognitive impairment and fatigue post-COVID-19 vs influenza, but lower cardiac sequelae risk, with vaccination modifying outcomes.

Retrospective survey-based cohort study of 26,474 Quebec healthcare workers examining long COVID risk, prevalence (5.6%), and severity in relation to reinfections, variants, and acute infection severity. Reinfections, Omicron variant, and nonsevere acute infection were associated with lower long COVID risk, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This binational cohort study in South Korea and Japan examined the long-term risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in 1.1M individuals with type 2 diabetes, using propensity score weighting and Cox proportional hazards models. The study found increased risks of sequelae across 8 organ systems in COVID-infected vs non-infected individuals, with risks peaking within 12 months, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study analyzing PASC prevalence and risk factors using Dutch primary care EHR data from 19,638 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients. Identifies comorbidities (lung disease, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, kidney disease) and demographics (age ≥45, female gender) as significant predictors of long COVID onset and duration.

This study compares nasal microbiota and clinical features in 291 individuals with acute flu-like illness, stratified by COVID-19 status and long COVID outcomes (persistent symptoms >3 months). While COVID-19-positive individuals showed lower nasal microbiota diversity and those who developed LC had more acute cardiorespiratory symptoms, no LC-specific microbial profile was identified.

This retrospective cohort study examines all-cause mortality risk in COVID-19 hospitalization survivors versus matched uninfected controls over 3.5 years of follow-up. The study found elevated mortality in hospitalized patients (HR 1.69) with differential risk by age group, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed lymphocyte subset counts in 40,537 patients across pre-COVID, mass infection, and post-COVID phases to assess persistence of immune alterations. The findings demonstrate sustained lymphopenia 20 months post-infection, particularly in older adults, males, and cardiovascular disease patients, characterizing long COVID as a condition of long-lasting immune compromise.

Develops and validates static and dynamic PASC scoring systems in a multicenter Korean cohort of 4,668 participants (4,388 infected, 280 controls) followed for up to 24 months. Identifies nine symptoms associated with long COVID and establishes quantitative diagnostic criteria, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating whether early neutralizing monoclonal antibody (mAb) treatment reduces post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in high-risk unvaccinated or immunocompromised individuals in Singapore. While mAb therapy did not significantly reduce overall PASC risk, it was associated with increased autoimmune complications and elevated thrombosis risk.

Prospective cohort study examining the incidence of post-COVID-19 syndrome and its association with acute COVID-19 severity in 280 discharged patients. Found 71.43% developed post-COVID-19 syndrome with higher rates in severe cases, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A prospective cohort study following 310 Greenlandic adults over 12 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess acute and long-term COVID-19 outcomes. Found that 53.7% recovered within 4 weeks, but long COVID symptoms (fatigue, mental exhaustion) persisted in a subset up to 12 months post-infection.

This prospective cohort study tracked 396 Japanese patients for up to 12 months post-COVID to examine labor productivity changes and economic impacts across three symptom progression groups (non-long COVID, recovered, persistent). The persistent long COVID group showed significantly reduced work productivity compared to other groups, highlighting the substantial socioeconomic burden of ongoing long COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study characterizes monocyte subpopulation patterns in 89 patients across acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, long COVID-19 syndrome, and viral controls (Zika/CHIKV) using flow cytometry. The study found elevated classical and intermediate monocyte counts in acute infection and long COVID patients compared to other viral infections, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines B cell dynamics and herpesvirus reactivation during acute COVID-19 and long-term follow-up (up to 460 days) in 120 patients. While the paper measures long COVID proxy (anosmia) and discusses PASC pathophysiology, it is a natural history observational study that does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

This study identifies neural injury biomarkers (GFAP and NF-L) associated with neurologic sequelae one year after SARS-CoV-2 hospitalization, comparing COVID-19 patients to historical pre-COVID controls. Elevated biomarker levels remained significantly associated with long-term neurological symptoms after adjusting for demographic and severity factors.

This prospective cohort study uses target trial emulation to compare the risk of new-onset long COVID symptoms between 1,055 SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals and 52,310 uninfected controls from the CHASING COVID Cohort. The study found infected participants had significantly higher risks of long COVID symptoms (22.6% vs 11.3% at 4-8 months) across neurological, autonomic, and exercise intolerance clusters, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 2,524 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 12 months to assess long COVID prevalence across different SARS-CoV-2 variants and lineages. Found 35.2% prevalence at one month with similar overall rates across variants, though specific lineages (Delta AY.126, AY.43, Omicron BA.1.17, BA.2.56, BA.5.1) showed stronger symptom severity correlations.

Prospective longitudinal study of adolescents (12-17 years) with anxiety disorders treated with duloxetine or escitalopram, examining the impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on anxiety and depressive symptoms over time. Found that COVID-19 infection was associated with worsening anxiety symptoms and a 33% worsening in syndromic severity in this anxious youth population.

Population-based cohort study (BAMSE) comparing lung function in young adults before and after COVID-19 infection using spirometry and serology. Found no significant differences in lung function decline between seropositive and seronegative participants, and asthma/ICS use did not modify outcomes.

This prospective observational study evaluated 24 long COVID patients with symptoms of orthostatic intolerance using head-up tilt table testing to characterize autonomic dysfunction. Nearly all patients demonstrated orthostatic intolerance on testing, with those having provoked orthostatic intolerance showing earlier symptom improvement compared to those with POTS.

Observational study of 408 long COVID patients with persistent chemosensory dysfunction (smell/taste loss) followed across 2021-2023, assessing predictors of recovery and symptom characteristics. Finds that cigarette smoke phantosmia predicts persistence while environmental allergies and hypertension predict recovery; no treatments resolved the dysfunction, though nasal steroids were reported helpful by recovered patients.

This retrospective cohort study examined whether nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) reduced the incidence of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in vaccinated patients with pre-existing cardiovascular disease. The treatment group showed a significantly lower rate of PASC (26% vs 30.6%) compared to untreated controls over 6 months of follow-up.

This longitudinal observational cohort study followed 89 patients from an original cohort of 144 at 1-year and 2-year visits to investigate pulmonary and renal long COVID manifestations. The study identified fibrous lung stripes in 17.8% and renal involvement in 23.9% of patients at 2-year follow-up, with machine learning models predicting these outcomes from early clinical and multi-omics data, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares autonomic function measures in patients with long COVID, healthy controls, and patients with pure autonomic failure using quantitative autonomic testing including heart rate, blood pressure, Valsalva, and tilt-table assessments. Patients with long COVID showed autonomic dysfunction patterns similar to pure autonomic failure patients when adjusted for age and sex, with abnormalities persisting up to 40 months post-infection.

This observational study characterizes postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) in long COVID patients using self-reported data from the Yale LISTEN cohort (n=578, surveyed May 2022–July 2023).
