This prospective observational study measured pulse wave velocity (PWV) in 143 COVID-19 patients at median 3.8 months post-infection and compared them to 143 age/sex-matched hypertension controls. COVID-19 patients showed significantly higher PWV values (10.5 vs 8.9 m/s), suggesting SARS-CoV-2 infection causes increased arterial stiffness, though no intervention or treatment was tested.

A retrospective cohort study following 43 patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia for over one year to assess cardiovascular event incidence. No major cardiovascular events occurred during the 384-day follow-up period, though the authors note longer studies are needed to fully investigate long-term cardiovascular consequences of COVID-19.

Prospective follow-up study of 110 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors examining the prognostic role of subclinical myocardial dysfunction detected via echocardiography at 6 months, with 21-month clinical follow-up. Subclinical myocardial dysfunction predicted major adverse cardiovascular events, but long-COVID condition itself had no independent prognostic significance.

Retrospective analysis of 244 hypertensive COVID-19 patients comparing outcomes between those treated with ACE-inhibitors vs ARBs, with 46 patients followed up after 260 days. Study found no difference in mortality, complications, or long-term sequelae between the two treatment groups, but does not evaluate treatment of long COVID itself.

This observational cohort study followed 56 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with severe pneumonia at approximately 6 months post-discharge to assess pulmonary impairments, neurologic disorders, and cardiac dysfunction. The study found that while pulmonary function and cardiac function largely recovered, patients frequently reported persistent fatigue and dyspnea, attributed to critical illness myopathy and neuropathy (CRIMYNE).

This study evaluated cardiac function using speckle-tracking echocardiography in 157 children recovered from asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection, compared to 107 healthy controls. While no treatment was tested, the findings showed subtle subclinical left ventricular systolic impairment in 60% of post-COVID children at 148±68 days follow-up, suggesting potential long-term cardiac effects despite mild acute illness.

This study investigates relative bradycardia (RB) prevalence in 269 COVID-19 inpatients and its association with long COVID symptoms at 16-month follow-up. While it does identify RB as a predictor of post-acute symptom burden, it is a secondary analysis examining a physiological marker rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This study develops a prognostic score (HOPE-2) to predict long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in 2,575 COVID-19 survivors followed from a multicenter registry. It identifies risk predictors through retrospective analysis but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed cardiac biomarkers (NT-proBNP) in 85 patients 48 days after COVID-19 pneumonia onset, stratified by disease severity. Patients with severe and critical COVID-19 showed significantly elevated NT-proBNP levels compared to moderate cases, suggesting elevated cardiac risk in the early post-COVID period.

Population-based prospective cohort study comparing echocardiographic and electrocardiographic parameters in 425 patients during the COVID-19 pandemic versus 713 pre-pandemic controls. Found significant enlargement of cardiac chambers and aortic root in the pandemic group, suggesting long-term cardiovascular impact of SARS-CoV-2, but this is a passive observational study without any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 224 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining the association between right ventricular dysfunction and 1-year mortality outcomes. This paper focuses on acute hospitalization outcomes during the pandemic, not long COVID sequelae.

This multicentre observational study evaluated 511 elite soccer players to assess the prevalence and diagnostic significance of new ECG patterns following COVID-19 infection. 3% of athletes showed de-novo ECG changes, 88% of whom had CMR evidence of inflammatory cardiac sequelae, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal cohort study of 85 elite athletes examining cardiac abnormalities (CMR, arrhythmias, symptoms) after SARS-CoV-2 infection with mean 7.8-month follow-up. Found 4.7% myocardial abnormalities with varying clinical courses, no important arrhythmias, and all athletes returned to sports without reported cardiac events.

A prospective observational study of 46 post-COVID patients examined at baseline and 2 months to assess cardiovascular disorders and kidney dysfunction. Found that 26% developed or maintained hypertension, 44% had diastolic dysfunction at 2 months, and renal function abnormalities persisted in about one-third of patients.

A prospective cohort study of 145 Post-COVID-19 Syndrome patients undergoing center-based exercise-based rehabilitation, examining sex-specific differences in pulmonary function, cardiopulmonary capacity, and health-related outcomes. Exercise-based rehabilitation improved pulmonary function, cardiopulmonary fitness, and disease burden in both women and men, with sex-specific benefits suggesting tailored rehabilitation approaches.

This observational study assessed dysfunctional breathing (DB) in 109 long COVID patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), with two independent raters identifying DB cases. The study found moderate inter-rater agreement (kappa=0.41) for DB identification, with 36% of patients showing confirmed DB, predominantly females with lower cardiorespiratory fitness.

Population-based cohort study comparing cardiovascular disease incidence in COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected individuals over 12 months of follow-up. Study observes increased CVD risk in the first 3 months post-infection, particularly thrombosis and arrhythmias, without testing any treatment intervention.

This longitudinal nested cohort study examined pro-inflammatory cytokine levels (IL-1β, TNF-α) in 69 long COVID patients with and without cardiovascular symptoms over 2 years post-hospitalization. The study found significantly elevated cytokine levels in patients with cardiovascular symptoms compared to those without, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzes the SHARE Corona survey data from 4,004 European respondents aged 50+ to examine how multimorbidity and socioeconomic factors affect long COVID symptom presence and burden. The paper is excluded because it is an observational study without treatment evaluation—it documents symptom prevalence patterns rather than testing any intervention.

This non-interventional multicenter study compared cardiopulmonary fitness in 679 post-COVID syndrome patients versus 474 recovered controls one year post-infection using exercise testing. While PASC patients showed significant impairments in maximal power and heart rate metrics, the study does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention—it is purely observational and descriptive.

This cohort study followed 759 Turkish children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection at 1, 3, and 6 months post-diagnosis to characterize long COVID symptom persistence beyond 12 weeks. The study found that 9.6% of children had ongoing symptoms (fatigue, muscle-joint pain, headache, loss of smell/taste), with female gender and symptomatic disease onset as risk factors, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A longitudinal observational study measuring pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and TNF-α) in 80 severe COVID-19 survivors at multiple timepoints from acute infection through 24 months post-infection. The study found elevated cytokine levels persisted in PASC patients at 2 years, particularly in those with ongoing symptoms like fatigue, palpitations, and dyspnea.

Longitudinal cohort study of 5,181 Belgian COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months to assess the prevalence, symptom patterns, and risk factors of post-COVID-19 condition. Found that 49.6% reported PCC with fatigue, headache, and memory problems most common; identified female sex, lower education, obesity, chronic disease, and hospitalization as significant risk factors.

Prospective cohort study of 1,029 COVID-19 patients followed at 1 and 3 months post-diagnosis to characterize persistent symptoms. Found that 27.6% reported at least one persistent symptom by 3 months, with muscle aches, shortness of breath, and fatigue being most common; persistent symptoms were more prevalent in women, older patients, and those with comorbidities.

Prospective cohort study following 5,083 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients for 6 months to characterize post-COVID conditions and identify risk factors. Found 21.8% prevalence of post-COVID with fatigue, myalgia, and dyspnea as most common symptoms; older age, female gender, poor economic status, comorbidities, and ICU admission were significant risk factors.

This Dutch longitudinal cohort study (N=76,503) identified four distinct symptom profiles of post-COVID-19 condition (muscle pain, fatigue, cardiorespiratory, ageusia/anosmia) and characterized their shared and unique risk factors including sex, weight status, chronic disease, and vaccination status. The study provides epidemiological characterization of long COVID subtypes but does not test any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal analysis of 47,964 Europeans aged 50+ examining how the COVID-19 pandemic impacted well-being across 2020-2021, with 73% of infected respondents reporting persistent Long COVID symptoms. The study found that individuals with COVID-19 and Long COVID experienced significantly larger declines in well-being than unaffected individuals, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 5,446 COVID-19 patients for 6 months to assess prevalence and predictors of self-reported anxiety and depression using the EQ-5D-3L scale. Found anxiety/depression decreased from 18.5% at 1 month to 15.4% at 6 months, with associations to female gender, economic status, disease severity, and ICU admission.

Population-based German cohort study comparing health outcomes in 350 SARS-CoV-2 infected and 4467 non-infected adults at >1 year follow-up. Found infected individuals had significantly higher rates of persistent health complaints (fatigue, dyspnea, smell/taste disorders) and incident diseases, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.

A longitudinal online survey following 1,153 long COVID patients from November 2020 to November 2021, characterizing symptom patterns and identifying common triggers for symptom exacerbation. Findings show 95% of participants had not fully recovered, with 45% reporting constant illness patterns and common triggers including physical activity (44%), stress (40%), cognitive effort (27%), and social effort (25%).

A matched cohort study using German healthcare data comparing incidence of post-COVID-19 condition diagnoses in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls over one year. The study found serious diagnoses like chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive impairment persisted longer in the COVID-19 group, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This matched cohort study used German healthcare insurance data to compare long COVID incidence and persistence in children/adolescents with COVID-19 versus matched controls through 2021. About 40% more COVID-infected individuals had post-COVID diagnoses at 3 months, with most resolving within 12 months, though a notable minority persisted longer in younger children.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,378 workers exposed to biohazards assessed post-COVID syndrome prevalence and symptoms in workers who developed COVID-19, with 70% (115/164) reporting persistent symptoms one month after infection. The study describes symptom patterns, comorbidity burden, sleep quality, fatigue, anxiety, and work ability impairment at follow-up but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study used Polish social insurance data (2020-2022) to quantify COVID-19-related work absence and associated economic costs, including post-COVID-19 condition. It found 52.9 million total work absence days with €4.3 billion in indirect costs, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Population-based retrospective cohort study comparing healthcare utilization in 307,994 Italian adults previously infected with SARS-CoV-2 versus matched uninfected controls over 6 months. Found that SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals, particularly those hospitalized or admitted to ICU, had significantly higher outpatient visits, diagnostic tests, and hospitalizations.

A multicenter retrospective cohort study characterizing long COVID in 533 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors in the UAE, documenting symptom prevalence, demographic associations, and impact on daily functioning. The study identifies risk factors (female gender, ICU admission, comorbidities) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study analyzes SHARE survey data from 1,909 European adults aged 50+ who reported a positive COVID-19 test to identify sociodemographic and health factors protective against post-COVID conditions. The findings show that male sex, higher education, healthy BMI, absence of comorbidities, COVID-19 vaccination, and non-Visegrad country residence are protective factors, with education level showing strong association with health outcomes.

This is an observational cohort study examining employment outcomes in 206,299 UK survey participants with long COVID compared to pre-infection baseline. The study documents associations between long COVID status and labour market inactivity/workplace absence, estimating ~27,000 UK working-age adults were inactive due to long COVID in July 2022, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This case-control study compared memory impairment rates between 140 COVID-19 survivors and 139 unexposed controls at one year post-infection in Tunisia. The study found a significantly higher incidence of memory impairment in the COVID-19 group (17.9% vs 9.4%), with age, female gender, diabetes, anxiety/depression, and obesity as risk factors.

A retrospective cohort study analyzing determinants of long COVID illness duration and healthcare service use in an Irish community sample (n=1,505). The study identifies factors associated with recovery (marital status, prior physical activity, COVID-19 infection count) and patterns of service utilization, finding that recent variants are associated with faster recovery.

Longitudinal cohort study identifying four distinct symptom profiles in post COVID-19 condition patients (muscle pain, fatigue, cardiorespiratory, ageusia/anosmia) using latent profile analysis on 642 cases from the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort. Examines demographic, lifestyle, and health-related risk factors associated with each symptom profile rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 1,648 COVID-19 patients hospitalized in Copenhagen examining ethnic disparities in disease severity as predictors of long COVID diagnosis. Found no excess long COVID risk among migrants (RR=1.20) but identified ethnic disparities in acute disease severity (oxygen requirements, inflammation markers) that may predict subsequent long COVID.

This study examines productivity loss in Dutch workers with acute COVID-19 and post-COVID condition using data from the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort across 31 waves (March 2020–October 2022). Workers with post-COVID condition experienced twice the average productivity loss (€7,118) compared to those with acute COVID-19 (€3,410), highlighting the chronic economic burden of long COVID.

Danish nationwide cohort study examining long COVID risk and symptoms among ethnic minorities compared to native Danes using register-based data from 2,334,271 COVID-19 diagnosed individuals. Found that ethnic minorities from North Africa, Middle East, Eastern Europe, and Asia had significantly higher risk of long COVID diagnosis, with hospitalization as a significant risk factor.

Population-based descriptive study of long COVID patients included in Belgium's post-COVID care trajectory program in primary care during 2023. Reports demographic characteristics, treatment types (mainly monodisciplinary with physiotherapy focus), and program uptake but does not evaluate treatment outcomes or compare intervention effects.

Swedish register-based retrospective cohort study examining long COVID risk in migrants compared to Swedish-born individuals. Found higher long COVID rates among migrants from multiple regions, primarily driven by greater disease severity rather than vaccinations or social inequalities.

Prospective observational study following working-age COVID-19 patients for 1 year post-discharge to assess autonomic syndrome occurrence and impact on work ability. Found autonomic syndrome in one in three patients at 1, 6, and 12 months, associated with reduced work ability, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.

This retrospective cohort study of 3.6 million Medicare beneficiaries examines the incidence of Long COVID and its association with prior COVID-19 vaccination. Findings show that those with 4+ vaccine doses had a 39% lower adjusted rate of Long COVID compared to unvaccinated beneficiaries.

Secondary analysis of the FADA retrospective cohort study characterizing long COVID symptoms, severity, and associated factors in an Irish sample of 2,338 long COVID patients. Study found fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and breathlessness as predominant symptoms, with baseline comorbidities and smoking as risk factors for persistence and severity.

This observational study examines the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms across age groups using a nationally representative US sample from 2020. It finds that approximately 48% of COVID-diagnosed individuals reported symptoms three months post-infection, with no significant age-related differences in symptom burden.

Retrospective cohort study of 86 older adults in Brazil examining the impact of physiotherapy rehabilitation on functional recovery after COVID-19. Found that while those recommended for physiotherapy had worse initial functional status, long-term functional capacity showed no significant difference between those who received treatment and those who did not.

Retrospective cohort study examining long COVID incidence and symptom patterns among 1,886 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in the Netherlands, stratified by migration background. Reports 26% long COVID prevalence at 12 weeks post-discharge with differences in symptom presentation and risk by migration status, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining the use of Long COVID Clinics (LCCs) in the Veterans Health Administration among 494,547 veterans with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found that only 2% of the cohort used LCCs and 17.4% of those with a long COVID diagnosis used them, with significant geographic disparities in access.

Prospective cohort study examining effects of acute COVID-19 infection on male reproductive and hormonal parameters in 50 recovered men followed for 3 months post-recovery. Findings show erectile dysfunction and spermatogenesis impairment gradually improve over time, with hormonal recovery within 3 months.

Cross-sectional study examining sperm count changes in 20 Indian men post-COVID-19 recovery, finding 70% had reduced sperm counts with a mean reduction of 48.83% at 74 days post-recovery. This is an observational study documenting a post-COVID symptom without testing any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome (PACS) symptoms and risk factors in 108 patients from the Rutgers Post-COVID Recovery Program, stratifying participants by cognitive complaint status and test performance. The analysis identifies age, depression, anxiety, and fatigue as risk factors associated with cognitive impairment in long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cross-sectional study evaluating semen parameters and inflammation in men 1 and 3 months after COVID-19 recovery. Found that 25% of recovered men had semen impairment with elevated inflammatory markers, though parameters improved by 3-month follow-up.

This retrospective cohort study examines cardiovascular event risk in COVID-19 patients with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease using NHS England data from 2020-2021. While it studies post-COVID outcomes, it focuses on general post-COVID cardiovascular complications rather than long COVID-specific persistent symptoms, and does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Longitudinal study of healthcare workers who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, tracking their antibody titers and symptoms over 7-8 months to investigate the relationship between immune response and post-COVID-19 syndrome development. Found no statistically significant difference in initial viral titers or antibody levels between those who developed PCS and those who did not.

Prospective study examining sperm parameter changes in 45 men with mild COVID-19 infection, measured before infection and 17-516 days post-infection. Study found significant decreases in sperm concentration, motility, and vitality persisting beyond 100 days post-infection, but this is observational follow-up of natural disease sequelae rather than an intervention trial for long COVID treatment.

This cross-sectional study of 508 Omicron-infected adults examines whether chronic post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms form distinct clusters with different risk factors, replicating earlier pre-Omicron findings. While confirming two separate symptom clusters (cognitive complaints and anxiety-depression), the study is observational without treatment intervention and therefore excluded from the intervention trials pipeline.

A prospective cohort study comparing prevalence and severity of symptoms 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection in cases versus test-negative and population controls in the Netherlands. Finds that 48.5% of cases report significantly elevated symptoms, with vaccination protective against loss of smell and taste but not other long COVID symptoms.

Retrospective cohort study of 94,595 COVID-19 patients examining associations between COVID-19 severity and long-term cardiovascular and mortality outcomes 31-120 days post-infection. Study identifies increased risk of stroke, MI, PE/DVT, heart failure, and death following severe COVID-19, with most events occurring 31-60 days post-infection.

Longitudinal analysis of 33 long COVID patients examining autoimmune activation and cytokine profiles over 7-11 months post-acute infection. Found persistent autoimmunity, elevated proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, G-CSF, IL-17A), and increased effector T cells; suggests immunomodulation as potential treatment target but does not test any intervention.

Population-based cohort study comparing the risk of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) diagnosis after Omicron infections versus Delta, Alpha, and wild-type variants in Stockholm, Sweden. Found significantly lower PCC risk following Omicron infection (0.2%) compared to earlier variants (0.5-1.3%), with adjusted hazard ratios ranging from 3.26 to 6.31.

This study measured soluble markers of inflammation in a SARS-CoV-2 recovery cohort at early and late timepoints to identify biological processes associated with PASC. The findings showed that individuals who developed PASC had higher levels of inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ-induced protein 10, IL-6) during recovery, suggesting persistent immune activation may underlie ongoing symptoms.

A prospective cohort study following 52 individuals with mild COVID-19 and uninfected controls from pre-infection through 2 years post-infection to characterize lung function trajectories. Results show mild COVID-19 causes excess decline in FEV1 and FVC in the first 6 months post-infection with limited recovery, while DLco showed improvement between 6-24 months.

This observational cohort study followed 102 participants with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection to characterize mucosal viral RNA clearance and symptom persistence over time. The study identified obesity as a risk factor for prolonged mucosal viral RNA (≥1 month) and symptom persistence (≥3 months), and found lower anti-spike IgG levels associated with reinfection risk.

This cross-sectional study examined the association between prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-COVID symptoms among fully vaccinated Canadian paramedics. It found no significant association between known or unknown prior infection and the presence of post-COVID symptoms.

Prospective cohort study of 2,960 non-hospitalized adults examining risk factors for postacute sequelae (long COVID) following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Identified older age, female sex, rural residence, high BMI, greater acute severity, chronic lung disease, and poor baseline health as risk factors; recent vaccination reduced risk while antiviral therapy did not.

Population-based cohort study of 331,042 individuals in Stockholm examining the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on the risk of developing persistent post-COVID condition (PCC) after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination significantly reduced PCC risk, with 2-3 doses showing 58-63% risk reduction compared to unvaccinated individuals.

This cross-sectional study of 4,108 mild COVID-19 patients investigates the association between post-COVID syndrome (PCS) symptoms and chronic low-grade inflammation in blood cells, comparing samples from 12-24 weeks before and 24 weeks after infection. The findings suggest that PCS symptoms including fatigue, cough, dizziness, and palpitations are associated with elevated inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, NLR, PLR) and immune cells, with women and healthcare workers showing higher symptom prevalence.

Uses temporal-informed PheWAS to identify new diagnoses occurring after COVID-19 in a large EHR cohort of 30,088 COVID-positive patients. Identifies increased risk for 43 diagnoses across respiratory, cardiovascular, neurological, and other systems, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines the risk of major osteoporotic fractures in older adults (≥50 years) following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to matched controls in Hong Kong. COVID-19 patients had significantly higher risks of major osteoporotic fractures, hip fractures, and falls in both acute and post-acute phases, with increased fracture risk partly attributed to elevated fall risk.

Analysis of the OnCovid registry examining association between inflammatory markers at COVID-19 diagnosis and development of post-COVID sequelae in cancer patients. Study found elevated CRP, lactate dehydrogenase, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio associated with sequelae risk, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study uses EHR data mining and propensity matching to identify conditions and symptoms associated with pediatric long COVID (PASC), comparing children with the PASC diagnosis code to matched controls without infection. It is an observational cohort analysis derived from existing medical records rather than a treatment intervention study.

A prospective cohort study examining the association between preinfection workplace stressors and long COVID development in 1,539 Japanese workers. The study found that high job demands, poor job control, and low social support were associated with increased odds of developing long COVID, though it does not test any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal metabolomic analysis of 1,132 COVID-19 patients from the IMPACC cohort identifying metabolic signatures and biomarkers associated with acute disease trajectory and post-acute sequelae (PASC). Study identifies dysregulated lipid metabolism, particularly phospholipids and sphingolipids, as potential biomarkers linked to PASC severity but does not test any treatment interventions.

Retrospective study of 139 pediatric long COVID patients evaluated in a rehabilitation clinic, assessing prevalence of anxious and depressive symptoms using validated scales. Found 40% had elevated anxiety/depression scores, with prior mental health diagnoses associated with higher symptom severity.

This retrospective claims database analysis compares erectile dysfunction risk following COVID-19 infection to other common viral infections (influenza, RSV, enterovirus, etc.) using propensity score matching. While the study examines post-infection outcomes, it is not a long COVID study as it does not focus on persistent COVID-19 symptoms but rather uses COVID-19 as a comparator for a specific post-viral complication observed across multiple viral infections.

Prospective cohort study describing persistent symptoms in 53 pediatric COVID-19 and 22 MIS-C patients at 2-month follow-up. Study is a descriptive follow-up of naturally occurring symptoms without testing any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term complications and mortality in older adults (≥60 years) with and without COVID-19 infection using UK Biobank and Hong Kong electronic health records. COVID-19 infection was significantly associated with higher risks of cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, neuropsychiatric outcomes, renal disease, and all-cause mortality over 18-28 months of follow-up.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed Military Health System records from October 2021–October 2022 to determine the incidence of diagnosed post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) among active duty service members and identify demographic risk factors and co-occurring diagnoses. Among 7,171 ADSM diagnosed with PCC, females had 3.7× higher incidence than males, older service members (55–64 years) had the greatest risk, and respiratory symptoms (particularly shortness of breath) were the most common co-occurring diagnosis.

This retrospective cohort study followed 1,000 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to evaluate long-term kidney outcomes in those who experienced acute kidney injury (AKI) versus those without AKI. Patients with COVID-19-associated AKI had significantly worse kidney function at 180-day follow-up, with higher rates of chronic kidney disease development and greater GFR decline.

This prospective observational study examined the fungal etiology and clinical profile of suspected mucormycosis in post-COVID patients, identifying Rhizopus arrhizus as the most common causative agent with rhino-orbital-cerebral mycormycosis as the most frequent clinical form. While the paper involves post-COVID patients, it is primarily a mycological epidemiology study of a secondary opportunistic fungal infection rather than a treatment trial for long COVID itself, and mucormycosis is an acute post-COVID complication rather than persistent long COVID syndrome.

Cross-sectional study examining erectile dysfunction prevalence in 33 men recovered from COVID-19 using questionnaires and penile duplex ultrasonography. Found 64.3% had erectile dysfunction with significant vascular abnormalities, suggesting tissue hypoxia during acute infection may contribute to persistent sexual dysfunction.

This retrospective cohort study of 1,000 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examines the association between acute kidney injury (AKI) during acute infection and long-term mortality outcomes over 180 days post-discharge. The study finds that AKI during acute COVID-19 is independently associated with higher 180-day mortality (11.8% vs 4.5%), but focuses entirely on acute-phase complications rather than long COVID syndrome.

A retrospective cohort study of 93 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed for 12 months to assess whether acute infection severity predicts chronic kidney disease progression. The study found no significant association between COVID-19 severity and CKD progression, with 21.5% of survivors developing CKD progression regardless of initial disease severity.

Retrospective observational study examining outcomes in 12 advanced chronic kidney disease patients hospitalized with COVID-19 from March-December 2020. 42% experienced post-infection pneumology symptoms (cough, dyspnea), 8% neurological symptoms, and 8% loss of smell, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This multicenter registry study examines how chronic kidney disease and glomerular filtration rate affect the course of acute COVID-19 infection and post-COVID outcomes in 8,496 patients across 7 countries. The study found that CKD significantly increased severity during acute infection and mortality risk within 12 months post-COVID, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective study of 77 CKD patients presenting with post-COVID-19 sequelae (hematuria, proteinuria, kidney dysfunction) at 56 days post-infection. Documents higher mortality and need for dialysis in CKD patients with post-COVID complications, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This is a multicenter observational cohort study analyzing acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence in COVID-19 patients and its impact on post-COVID outcomes using the ACTIV international register. The study found AKI in 11.6% of hospitalized COVID-19 patients and was associated with higher mortality risk both during acute infection and at 3-month follow-up, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study examining the impact of acute COVID-19 infection on renal function in patients with pre-existing glomerular disease, evaluating eGFR changes and the effect of Paxlovid treatment. Findings show accelerated renal function deterioration in proteinuric patients following acute infection, not long COVID sequelae.

This retrospective cohort study followed 2,212 long-COVID patients in post-COVID recovery clinics to assess kidney function changes over 12 months. Patients experienced a 2.96 mL/min/1.73 m² decline in eGFR (3.39% reduction), with higher declines in hospitalized and diabetic patients, indicating long-COVID's impact on renal function.

This retrospective cohort study from Stockholm examines whether COVID-19 infection is associated with accelerated kidney function decline compared to pneumonia survivors. The study found that COVID-19 survivors showed greater acceleration in eGFR decline, particularly among those with severe infection requiring hospitalization, suggesting a need for post-COVID kidney function monitoring.

The CARTESIAN study is a prospective multicenter cohort of 938 COVID-19 survivors followed at 6 and 12 months post-infection to assess arterial stiffness and its relationship with kidney function. The study found that individuals with lower kidney function and severe COVID-19 history exhibit higher arterial stiffness and accelerated vascular aging, but this is an observational follow-up study with no treatment intervention tested.

Retrospective cohort study examining acute kidney injury (AKI) in 409 hospitalized COVID-19 patients and its association with long-term renal and mortality outcomes over two years. While the paper follows patients post-discharge, it focuses on acute COVID-19 complications during hospitalization and their sequelae, not on long COVID as a distinct syndrome or any intervention/treatment.

Retrospective single-center study of 71 hemodialysis patients examining the prevalence of long COVID and identifying predictors of the syndrome. Found 25% of COVID-19 positive patients developed long COVID, with initial symptom severity being the only significant predictor; no analytic markers or baseline characteristics predicted long COVID development.

Prospective observational study comparing long COVID outcomes in 70 CKD patients versus 50 non-CKD patients over three years. CKD patients showed slower recovery from PASC symptoms (60% persistent fatigue at 12 months, 45% cognitive dysfunction at 18 months) with no permanent renal impairment, and ARB/ACEi therapy did not exacerbate symptoms.

This nationwide Swedish registry study examines the risk of kidney injury following acute COVID-19 infection up to 6 months post-onset using the Self-Controlled Case Series method. While it documents an association between COVID-19 severity and kidney injury risk, it focuses on acute post-infection complications rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months later).

This cross-sectional study of 214 long COVID patients assessed the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on occupational status and quality of life. While relevant to long COVID, it is observational only (no treatment intervention) and therefore excluded from the treatment trial pipeline.

Prospective cohort study examining associations between night shift work, sleep disruption, and COVID-19 outcomes in 3,319 Spanish adults. Found that night shift work and sleep problems were associated with increased risk of long COVID, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines sick leave patterns in 2,569 Belgian workers with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to workers absent for other infectious diseases. The study finds that long-term sick leave (>12 weeks) occurred in 14 per 1,000 COVID-positive workers, lower than in other infections, and identifies age, prior sick leave, and low education as risk factors for prolonged absence.

This retrospective cohort study examined the long-term effect of COVID-19 on kidney function (eGFR trajectory) in patients with chronic kidney disease, comparing 268 COVID-infected cases to 534 matched controls followed over ~3 years. While COVID-19 was not associated with increased kidney failure risk, it was associated with a greater annual decline in eGFR (0.71 ml/min/1.73 m² difference).

This retrospective cohort study evaluates factors associated with return-to-work outcomes in 222 military personnel with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae undergoing a structured recovery program, tracking occupational deployment status over 18 months. Fatigue, shortness of breath, cognitive impairment, and mental health symptoms were identified as predictors of persistent work disability.

This cross-sectional study examined 216 long COVID workers attending a multidisciplinary day-hospital program to identify factors associated with sick leave and sick leave duration. While the program provided comprehensive assessment and care, the paper is observational/descriptive rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention, and lacks a control group or comparison arm.

Prospective observational study comparing pulmonary fibrosis severity in 56 healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 syndrome versus 56 matched non-healthcare worker controls over 3 years. Healthcare workers, especially pediatricians, showed higher risk of severe pulmonary fibrosis (≥50% fibrosis), with CT score, respiratory support duration, viral load, and serum TGF-β1 identified as predictors.

A prospective follow-up program that screened 891 oil industry workers with high-risk COVID-19 infections using telephone/video interviews 4-6 weeks post-diagnosis to identify long-COVID presence and impact on quality of life. The study identified 42.3% prevalence of long-COVID symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, smell/taste disorders) and referred symptomatic patients to specialists, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This is a workplace health surveillance study examining post-COVID syndrome prevalence, symptom patterns, and associations with occupational factors and mental health in 1,378 workers. It does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment for long COVID patients.

Retrospective telephone follow-up of 266 COVID-19 patients discharged from Henry Ford Hospital, assessing 30-day outcomes including symptoms, oxygen requirements, and readmissions. No active intervention or treatment was administered; this is a passive observational assessment of natural recovery patterns.

A one-year follow-up cohort study of 303 COVID-19 survivors from a single Italian center documenting persistent long COVID symptoms. At 12 months post-infection, 81% of patients reported at least one symptom, with fatigue (52%), pain (48%), and sleep disorders (47%) being most prevalent, with no significant difference based on acute phase severity.

Prospective longitudinal multicenter cohort study following 288 COVID-19 patients for 6 months to investigate persistent symptoms and their association with immune cytokine profiles. Approximately 10% of recovered patients had persistent symptoms at 6 months, with elevated inflammatory markers (IL-17A, IL-1β, MCP-1, PDGF-BB) in symptomatic patients compared to asymptomatic and healthy controls, suggesting ongoing chronic inflammation in long COVID.

This is a retrospective cohort study analyzing electronic medical records and surveys from 1,015 Military Health System beneficiaries to characterize long-term clinical outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents persistent symptoms and elevated cardiovascular diagnoses through 3 months post-infection but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 26,339 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to estimate the incidence of post-COVID dyspnea and interstitial lung disease (ILD) at 3-6 months post-discharge. The study identified risk factors (length of stay, age, obesity, comorbidities) but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

RWJBarnabasHealth's Pediatric Post-COVID CARE program evaluated 64 children (ages 0-21) with persistent symptoms >4 weeks post-COVID-19, providing multidisciplinary care including infectious disease assessment, subspecialty consultation, physical therapy, and psychological support. 28% of patients had at least one symptom at 4+ weeks, with common findings including fatigue (55.6%), shortness of breath/cough (50%), brain fog (50%), and anxiety/depression (44.4%).

This prospective cohort study follows 60 COVID-19 patients for 6+ months to identify clinical and biomarker predictors of post-COVID syndrome (PCS). The study found that female gender, prior stroke/TIA, DVT, kidney dysfunction, elevated ReSARS N IgG antibodies, and elevated IL-10 were associated with PCS development.

Retrospective cohort study examining post-acute COVID-19 complications in ED patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to matched controls. Found increased rates of supplemental oxygen requirement and cardiovascular complications in previously infected patients during subsequent ED visits.

This prospective cohort study followed 87 participants from a peginterferon-lambda trial for uncomplicated COVID-19 to assess long COVID prevalence and associations at 4, 7, and 10 months post-infection. Female sex and gastrointestinal symptoms during acute illness were significant risk factors for developing long COVID, with persistent symptoms in ~23-34% of participants over 10 months.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 63 SARS-CoV-2-positive adults followed one year post-infection to assess persistence of long COVID symptoms. Over half (52%) reported long COVID symptoms at one year, with 17 individuals (52% of those with long COVID) experiencing unresolved symptoms, with fatigue, loss of smell, and loss of taste being most common.

A retrospective cohort study describing self-reported post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 symptoms at 6 months post-hospitalization in 57 patients using symptom questionnaires. The study documents symptom burden and identifies sex and age differences in symptom prevalence and functional impairment, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective follow-up study of 49 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessed at 6 and 12 weeks post-discharge to document persistent symptoms. Found 96% reported one or more persisting symptoms at 12 weeks, with fatigue, dyspnea, cough, chemosensory dysfunction, and headache as main symptoms, but this is a descriptive observational study with no intervention tested.

Prospective cohort study following 315 COVID-19 survivors from a Dutch hospital for 12 months, assessing health-related quality of life, anxiety, depression, and PTSD using standardized questionnaires. Participants showed significant recovery by 12 months to levels similar to healthy controls, except ICU-admitted patients who continued experiencing bodily pain and decreased physical function.

Retrospective observational study of 312 cancer patients at MD Anderson assessing the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms following acute COVID-19 infection. Found that 60% of cancer patients reported long COVID symptoms persisting up to 14 months, with fatigue, sleep disturbance, myalgia, and gastrointestinal symptoms being most common.

This study examined the prevalence and impact of post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (PASC) among people experiencing homelessness in Seattle shelters, following up with 22 participants at days 5, 10, 30, and 60+ after positive SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis. The majority reported persistent symptoms at 30+ days, with limited access to medical care, highlighting that PASC may worsen existing health challenges in this vulnerable population.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in 235 patients with postacute COVID syndrome, finding MAFLD present in 55.3% at follow-up. The study identifies insulin resistance, BMI, and metabolic syndrome as independent predictors of MAFLD but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective cohort study describes the spectrum, magnitude, and patterns of postacute symptoms in 179 adults with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection, assessed at 4-month intervals up to 8 months. Fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive impairment, and anosmia/dysgeusia were the most common persistent symptoms with variable patterns and substantial impact on quality of life and functional performance.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 1,296 COVID-19 survivors followed at 12 months post-infection to characterize rheumatic symptoms (joint pain/swelling) and identify risk factors. This is an observational study with no intervention tested, so excluded as it does not study treatment effectiveness.

This prospective cohort study of 233 long COVID patients identifies three distinct symptom clusters through cluster analysis: pain-dominant, cardiovascular-dominant, and minimal symptoms. The study characterizes clinical phenotypes and their associations with functional impairment but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

LUNG INJURY COVID-19 is a prospective observational cohort study following 305 COVID-19 survivors (162 moderate, 143 severe cases) for 12 months post-infection to assess long-term outcomes and recovery. At 12 months, most patients reported persistent symptoms including muscle weakness and dyspnea, with nearly one-third of severe cases showing impaired pulmonary diffusion and imaging abnormalities including fibrosis.

A 23-month prospective follow-up study of 170 COVID patients tracking persistence of long COVID symptoms, including fatigue, taste/smell dysfunction, and cognitive difficulties. This is an observational study without treatment intervention and appears to be a secondary analysis of an existing cohort.

This multicenter study examines whether COVID-19 vaccination protects against postacute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) using a large national health research network with propensity-score matching. The data show significant protective effects of vaccination against PASC symptoms and new-onset conditions (hypertension, diabetes, heart disease) at 28 and 90 days post-COVID diagnosis, with 65-79% risk reduction.

Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) in 51,630 German primary care patients during the 12 months following COVID-19 diagnosis. Found PCC in 8.3% of patients, with increased risk associated with older age, female sex, asthma, stress disorders, and somatoform disorders.

Observational cohort study examining how SARS-CoV-2 infecting genotype and vaccination status correlate with patient-reported symptoms using FLU-PRO Plus scores in 764 participants. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 infection outcomes and does not address long COVID or post-acute sequelae, and no treatment intervention is evaluated.

This prospective cohort study followed 289 COVID-19 patients for 12 months to describe long COVID symptom patterns and burden according to initial disease severity. The study found that 59.5% reported persistent symptoms at 12 months, with higher symptom frequency and count in those with initially moderate/severe acute illness, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This matched cohort study examines long COVID incidence in UK adults stratified by COVID-19 vaccination status during April 2020–November 2021. The study found that vaccination was associated with a significantly lower risk of persistent symptoms (9.5% vs 14.6% in unvaccinated), but does not study any treatment intervention for long COVID.

This prospective cohort study identified three distinct symptom clusters in long COVID patients across two recruitment periods, examining how SARS-CoV-2 variants and vaccination affected symptom presentation. The study is observational with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective cohort study of 659,286 children examining the clinical features and burden of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) using electronic health records from 9 US children's hospitals. Found that 42.0% of PCR-positive children had at least one systemic/syndromic/medication feature of PASC versus 38.2% in PCR-negative children, with higher risk in those with ICU care, younger age, and complex chronic conditions.

Retrospective cohort study of 180,759 COVID-19 patients in Israel identifying risk factors and complications associated with long COVID development, with analysis of healthcare utilization and costs. This is an observational study characterizing the burden of long COVID rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

Longitudinal observational study analyzing CD4+ and CD8+ T cell markers and inflammatory cytokines in COVID-19 survivors with post-acute sequelae (PASC). Found associations between specific T cell activation patterns and individual PASC symptoms like dyspnea, confusion, and chest pain, suggesting ongoing immune activation as a mechanism underlying long COVID.

Longitudinal cohort study of US military personnel examining post-COVID functional impairment, finding that 34.3% of SARS-CoV-2 positive subjects reported new or increased difficulty exercising compared to 14.8% of negative subjects, with impairment persisting at 12 months. This is an observational study with no intervention—subjects were passively followed to assess outcomes, not given a treatment.

Prospective cohort study tracking pulmonary function recovery (DLCO, spirometry, 6MWT) in 110 patients recovering from acute SARS-CoV-2 infection across severity groups at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months post-discharge. Study documents natural recovery patterns without intervention, showing abnormal DLCO tended to revert to normal by month 3.

Prospective cohort study following 112 mild COVID-19 cases and 44 uninfected controls for 2 years post-infection, with surveys at 6, 12, and 24 months assessing symptom persistence and quality of life. Found that 50% of cases reported persistent symptoms at 2 years (primarily fatigue and smell/taste alterations) with significantly higher fatigue scores and lower quality of life compared to controls, but no intervention or treatment was provided.

Prospective cohort study comparing post-acute COVID-19 symptoms in individuals infected before versus after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in the Seattle region (March 2020-March 2022). Found that PASC prevalence was significantly higher in those infected pre-vaccination (32%) compared to post-vaccination (6%), though vaccination status was not an intervention administered by the study.

This study describes the clinical spectrum of COVID-19 infection in 163 children presenting to a US health system, including acute COVID, MIS-C, and post-COVID complications. Long COVID was diagnosed in 42 children (6.3% of symptomatic cohort) with persistent symptoms affecting daily function beyond 3 months post-infection.

Retrospective cohort study tracking 94 solid organ transplant recipients hospitalized with COVID-19 during the first pandemic wave, with 2-year follow-up outcomes. Documents high rates of mortality, allograft rejection/failure, secondary infections, and long-COVID symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, and cardiac/renal complications.

This paper describes clinical features and long-term outcomes of 104 pediatric patients with persistent unwellness following acute COVID-19 seen at a Post-COVID Clinic, with follow-up data showing 79% of patients were improved or back to normal at median 6-month follow-up. The study characterizes symptom presentation and natural recovery patterns but does not test or evaluate a specific intervention or treatment.

Multicenter prospective cohort study using latent class analysis to identify distinct phenotypes of post-COVID symptoms at 3 and 6 months post-infection in 4504 COVID-positive and 1459 COVID-negative participants. Found four distinct phenotype classes with minimal symptoms in 70% of participants and substantial symptom class switching over time, but no specific treatment intervention was tested.

This prospective cohort study followed 71 non-hospitalized individuals with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, measuring viral shedding and inflammatory markers during the acute phase and assessing PASC symptoms 4-8 months later. The study found associations between prolonged RNA shedding, elevated inflammatory cytokines during acute illness, and subsequent PASC development, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Online cohort study examining risk factors associated with Long COVID symptoms in 1,480 respondents from the COVID-19 Citizen Science study. Found that acute symptom severity, lower socioeconomic status, pre-infection depression, and earlier COVID variants were associated with Long COVID symptom persistence at a median of 360 days post-infection.

Cross-sectional study assessing postacute COVID-19 sequelae (PASC) in 989 Lima, Peru participants at median 4.7 months post-diagnosis using questionnaires and clinical examinations. Found high burden of respiratory symptoms (68.3%), depression (20.7%), and cognitive impairment (8.0%), with female sex and older age as key risk factors.

Community-based cohort study comparing the risk of new-onset long COVID following SARS-CoV-2 reinfection versus first infection among UK COVID-19 Infection Survey participants. Found that reinfection carried lower risk of long COVID for those ≥16 years (aOR 0.72) but no significant difference for those <16 years.

This retrospective cohort study analyzes 17,487 COVID-19 patients and propensity-score matched controls to identify long COVID sequelae that are specifically associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to other viral respiratory infections. The study found that fatigue, chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, and other symptoms are more frequent post-COVID-19, though some commonly attributed long COVID symptoms do not differ significantly from post-infection effects of other viral illnesses.

Prospective cohort study following 230 COVID-19 survivors from the first wave to assess post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence and characteristics at 2 years post-infection. Finds 36.1% persistent post-COVID syndrome with fatigue, rheumatological and psychiatric symptoms as most common; vaccination and reinfection did not influence syndrome dynamics.

This study examined the gut microbiome in 394 COVID-19 patients during acute infection to identify predictors of long-term outcomes, with 84 (21%) developing long COVID. The researchers found distinct microbial composition in long COVID patients during the acute phase, suggesting potential predictive value, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 94 COVID-19 patients (Omicron variant) for 12 months to assess long COVID symptom persistence and quality of life. Found that 52.5% still experienced long COVID symptoms at 12 months, with fatigue, concentration difficulties, and memory problems being most common.

Retrospective claims-based cohort analysis examining long COVID incidence and symptomatology across sociodemographic groups in 8.4 million Medicare/Medicaid/Commercial members (Oct 2021–Dec 2022). Found overall PASC incidence of 0.61% with disparities by race/ethnicity and insurance type; pulmonary (36%), neurologic (17%), and cardiac (15%) symptoms most common.

Retrospective chart review of 173 long COVID patients at a Brooklyn clinic examining how age, gender, ethnicity, comorbidities, and vaccination status relate to symptom severity and duration. Findings show unvaccinated patients, those 50-69 years old, and certain ethnic minorities with comorbidities experienced higher symptom burden and longer symptom duration.

This multi-centric prospective cohort study followed 315 COVID-19 patients for up to 12 months post-discharge to assess long COVID prevalence and identify predictors of persistent symptoms. The study found 24% of patients reported continuing symptoms at 1 year, with disease severity and education level as significant predictors, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examined whether Paxlovid treatment during acute COVID-19 reduces the incidence of post-COVID conditions (PCC) across three age groups using claims data from 564,303 adults ≥50, 292,818 adults 18-49, and 17,178 adolescents. Results showed Paxlovid reduced PCC risk in older adults (RR=0.92) but showed mixed or increased risk in younger adults and adolescents.

Retrospective analysis of 107 pediatric long COVID patients at Children's Hospital of Los Angeles examining symptom presentation and the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on disease course. Vaccination led to symptom improvement in 42.9% of patients who received it after long COVID onset, with fatigue and headache identified as predominant symptoms.

This cross-sectional study assessed objective cognitive function in military personnel with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection using the BRACE app at 9 months post-infection. No significant difference in cognitive impairment was found between infected and uninfected participants, despite self-reported cognitive symptoms in long COVID patients.

A prospective cohort study following 235 COVID-19 patients over 24 months to assess long COVID symptom persistence, quality of life, and mental health outcomes. While demonstrating that 62% of completers still experienced long COVID symptoms at 24 months with associated anxiety and depression, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention and therefore is not eligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Prospective cohort study of 169 ambulatory adults with mild COVID-19 followed for 6 months to assess neurological symptoms of long COVID. Found 90% developed new neurological symptoms post-acute period, with fatigue, headache, and sleep disorders being most common, peaking in incidence during first 3 weeks.

This is a chart review of 150 long COVID patients at a clinical clinic examining the prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms and pre-COVID mental health disorders. The study is descriptive/epidemiological in nature and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence of long COVID (U09.9 codes) among 468,620 US hospitalized veterans, comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated groups from October 2021 to March 2023. The study found a 3.93% overall long COVID prevalence, with unvaccinated hospitalized veterans showing ~3-fold greater prevalence (8.78%) compared to vaccinated veterans (3.50%), but does not test any intervention or treatment.

A prospective observational study of 414 Indian patients with breakthrough COVID infections that characterizes long COVID prevalence and develops a predictive risk scoring model based on age, hypertension, and asthma. The study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective chart review comparing PASC patients with matched controls to assess whether acute COVID-19 treatments (nirmatrelvir-ritonavir, tocilizumab, remdesivir, dexamethasone) prevent PASC development. Found no significant differences in treatment exposure between PASC and non-PASC groups, suggesting acute-phase treatment alone is not protective.

This is a case-control study comparing radiographic and physiological findings in long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea versus those with resolved dyspnea, part of the larger EPICC cohort study. While it is about long COVID, it is a secondary analysis examining correlates of symptoms rather than testing a treatment intervention, and should be excluded.

Retrospective chart review of 57 VA patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome to identify epidemiological and clinical risk factors. Found common comorbidities (psychiatric diagnoses, obesity, hypertension) and predominant symptoms (fatigue, brain fog, dyspnea) but normal inflammatory markers in most patients.

Prospective cohort study assessing the prevalence of persistent symptoms consistent with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in rural Wisconsin during the Omicron variant period. Found that 27% of Omicron-infected individuals reported ≥2 persistent symptoms compared to 24% among never-infected individuals, with elevated but non-significant risks for cardiac, pulmonary, neurologic, and menstrual symptoms.

This is a retrospective cohort study using EHR data from the RECOVER Program to analyze temporal evolution of pediatric PASC subphenotypes (cardiac, respiratory, musculoskeletal) over 1-6 months post-infection, with propensity-score matched COVID-negative controls. The study characterizes prevalence patterns and seasonal trends but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapy for long COVID.

Retrospective survey of 615 high-risk COVID patients who received monoclonal antibody treatment, assessing long COVID incidence and symptom prevalence through follow-up questionnaire. Identifies female sex, vaccination status, and timing of immune modulators as predictors of long COVID development, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment for long COVID itself.

This retrospective cohort study compares healthcare encounters in Military Health System beneficiaries with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection over 12 months post-diagnosis. The analysis found elevated medical encounters in the first month post-infection, with only pulmonary diagnoses remaining elevated at 9 months, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Prospective cohort study comparing self-reported physical fitness outcomes between US military service members with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection history over 1 year. While the study documents long COVID-related fitness impairment and shows vaccination reduces risk, it is observational and does not test a specific intervention—vaccine status is an exposure variable, not an assigned treatment.

The CONTAIN-Extend study is an 18-month follow-up of the CONTAIN-RCT examining whether COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) therapy affects post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) symptoms in 281 hospitalized patients. CCP showed no lasting benefit over placebo for PASC symptoms or health outcomes, though demographic factors (female sex, age 45-64, race/ethnicity) significantly influenced symptom reporting.

Retrospective cohort study examining whether COVID-19 vaccination status affects the development of medically diagnosed PASC following breakthrough infection in a US health system. Found no significant association between vaccination status and PASC diagnosis, with PASC prevalence driven instead by age, sex, hospitalization, and comorbidities.

This retrospective cohort study uses National COVID Cohort Collaborative data to evaluate the association between preexisting chronic lung disease (CLD) and long COVID development within 6 months post-infection. It identifies CLD, obesity, and depression as significant risk factors for long COVID but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective review of 117 long COVID patients to assess the prevalence and clinical utility of routine ANA testing. Found 43% ANA positivity but low rates of rheumatological diagnosis and treatment, suggesting routine ANA testing may not be cost-effective in this population.

Prospective cohort study comparing long COVID prevalence and symptom severity between vaccinated and unvaccinated adults infected with SARS-CoV-2. Found that vaccination was protective against long COVID development and reduced symptom severity at 90 days postinfection (13% overall; 27% unvaccinated vs 8% vaccinated).

This emulated trial investigates whether metformin prescribed within 6 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces long COVID or death over 180 days, comparing metformin users to those receiving other off-label COVID drugs in the N3C EHR database. Metformin was associated with a 53% reduction in long COVID/death risk (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.25-0.89), though results varied by timing of prescription.

This prospective cohort study examined cardiac complications in youth with SARS-CoV-2 infection, including mild outpatient cases, using echocardiography and ECG screening. The study found minimal cardiac abnormalities (3.1%) that resolved within 3-6 months, and supports against routine cardiac screening in young people with mild infection—this is about acute COVID-19 sequelae in the immediate post-infection period, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months later).

This paper analyzes patient demographics and referral patterns to a newly established Long COVID Clinic at a VA medical center, using the Area Deprivation Index to assess socioeconomic factors. It is an observational study documenting clinic utilization rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study using claims data to characterize incidence of long COVID conditions during the first year post-hospitalization for COVID-19 among 92,913 patients. Observational study with no intervention—patients were not assigned treatments, only passively followed to document symptom incidence over time.

Prospective cohort study following 147 COVID-19 survivors stratified by disease severity (mild to critical) with quality of life assessments at baseline, 1, 3, and 6 months post-infection using the RAND-36 questionnaire. The study documents natural recovery patterns in physical and mental component scores over 6 months, with 83% achieving normal mental health scores and 63% achieving normal physical scores by month 6, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A multicenter prospective cohort study in Brazil following 989 participants with mild COVID-19 infection for 12 months to assess health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using EQ-5D-3L. The study identified factors associated with worsening HRQoL, including older age, female sex, obesity, comorbidities, and mental health disease, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study tracking fatigue prevalence in 643 symptomatic adults testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 over 6 months, stratified by age and BNT162b2 vaccination status. Found fatigue persisted in 18.5% at 6 months, with vaccinated participants showing significantly lower fatigue prevalence compared to unvaccinated.

This is a secondary analysis of the Test Us at Home study examining the association between SARS-CoV-2 viral rebound during acute infection and subsequent long COVID development. The study found that participants with viral rebound had significantly higher odds of developing long COVID with fatigue or taste/smell changes, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Longitudinal sub-analysis of 284 NIAID cohort patients examining effects of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection on post-acute sequelae (PASC) and pulmonary function. Reinfection was not associated with worsening PASC symptoms or decline in pulmonary function; notably, two-thirds of reinfected patients reported symptom improvement or resolution.

Cohort study of 3.6 million Medicare beneficiaries examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and long COVID risk over one year of follow-up. Found a dose-response relationship with prior vaccines reducing long COVID risk (aHR=0.60 with ≥4 vaccines vs none), but this is an observational analysis of vaccination exposure rather than a study of an active treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

This is a prospective observational cohort study from the German National Pandemic Cohort Network (NAPKON) that tracks health-related quality of life (HrQoL) using EQ-5D-5L in 1,494 COVID-19 patients at baseline, end of acute phase, 3-month, and 12-month follow-ups. The study reports that despite 61% of patients having persistent post-COVID symptoms at 3 months and 57% at 12 months, overall HrQoL scores were not significantly impaired compared to the general population, though symptom severity correlated with HrQoL decline.

Multicenter cross-sectional study comparing long-term COVID-19 symptoms in 2,954 pediatric cases and 1,500 controls across 16 Lima hospitals using screening surveys and clinical evaluation. Found 54.3% of cases had positive screening for long-term symptoms lasting ≥3 months, with cough, pain, and GI symptoms being most common; study is descriptive and does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study of 222 COVID-19 patients followed for 9 months to identify predictors and prevalence of long COVID. Found that detectable nucleocapsid antigen and need for supplemental oxygen during acute illness were associated with 3-4x higher odds of long COVID, with CNS and psychological symptoms most common among the 41% with persistent symptoms.

This retrospective cohort study compares post-acute complications following dengue infection versus SARS-CoV-2 infection in a Singapore population, using national healthcare databases. While it documents sequelae after dengue infection, the paper is primarily focused on dengue rather than long COVID, and does not study a treatment intervention.

This study evaluates the effectiveness of BNT162b2 bivalent COVID-19 vaccine in preventing long COVID symptoms among older adults ≥50 years old who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2. While the paper is about long COVID, it is an observational analysis of vaccine effectiveness as a preventive intervention rather than a treatment study for existing long COVID, and represents a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort (NCT05160636).

topics: health-related quality of life|longitudinal outcomes|symptom burden|functioning
summary: The ADAPT post-COVID study followed 172 participants (86% with mild/moderate infection) over 24 months, assessing health-related quality of life using the Wilson-Cleary model across multiple domains including symptoms, functioning, and wellbeing. 37% developed long COVID and showed sustained impairment across most health domains over 2 years, with little improvement despite some gains in return to work.

This retrospective cohort study examined whether treating acute COVID-19 with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir reduces the risk of post-COVID-19 conditions (PCC) using real-world claims data from 291,433 treated and 582,866 untreated patients. Treatment reduced PCC risk in adults 50-64 years (aHR 0.93) and ≥65 years (aHR 0.88), but had minimal to no effect in younger age groups.

This cross-sectional study measured plasma SARS-CoV-2 antigens and proteomics in 100 convalescent patients at 3 and 12 months post-infection to determine if antigenemia differentiates patient subgroups. No significant differences were found in plasma proteins or immune cell expression between those with and without detectable antigen.

Prospective cohort study comparing cognitive function before and after COVID-19 infection using the Cognivue Clarity device in a 45-year-old average population. Found no significant decrease in cognitive function 1 year post-infection, suggesting cognitive impairment may not be a primary long COVID sequela in this population.

Prospective longitudinal registry study comparing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) trajectories in SARS-CoV-2 positive vs negative participants over 12 months using latent transition analysis. While it documents HRQoL recovery patterns in long COVID, it is a secondary analysis of registry data without testing any specific intervention, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective observational study of 50 long COVID patients treated with low-dose aripiprazole, examining changes in functional status and symptom severity. Treatment was associated with significant improvements in functional status scale and composite symptom scores, with 22% of patients showing clinically meaningful ≥30% symptom reduction.

This prospective observational study of 508 U.S. Veterans measures peripheral blood cytokines during acute and late SARS-CoV-2 infection stages and associates them with COVID-19 severity and long COVID outcomes (fatigue, cognition, dyspnea) at 3 months post-infection. While about long COVID, the study does not evaluate or test any treatment—it is a purely observational biomarker study examining immune correlates of disease severity and long COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study compared long COVID symptoms and immune activation profiles between people with HIV (PWH) and without HIV (PWOH) in a prospective cohort, examining 273 participants at ~890 days post-COVID infection with flow cytometric analysis of immune cells. Findings showed that long COVID symptom presentation differed by both HIV and obesity status, with obesity associated with higher post-exertional malaise and cardiovascular symptoms in PWOH but not PWH, while peripheral immune response differences were primarily driven by HIV status alone.

This longitudinal cohort study followed 57-54 individuals with post-acute COVID-19 respiratory manifestations at 4 and 7 months post-infection, examining pulmonary function, imaging, and immunological/inflammatory markers. The study identified chronic immune dysregulation and inflammation associated with respiratory impairment but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compared long-term post-hospitalization outcomes between 736 children with MIS-C and 503 with acute COVID-19, tracked over 2 years using ICD-10 codes. Children with MIS-C more frequently developed cardiac dysfunction and cardiovascular conditions, while COVID-19 hospitalized children more frequently developed asthma, respiratory, gastrointestinal, and sleep disturbances—both groups experienced new symptoms in ~55% of cases.

This study analyzes wearable sensor data (heart rate, activity, sleep) from 190,000 participants in the German Corona Data Donation Project to compare long-term physiological recovery between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection. It demonstrates that vaccination is associated with faster recovery in vital signs and fewer extreme changes during acute infection, but does not test any specific long COVID intervention.

Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study examining racial disparities in SARS-CoV-2 testing and outcomes in Canadian children presenting to emergency departments. While it includes post-COVID condition (PCC) as an outcome at 90-day follow-up in 153 children, it does not study any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

This paper analyzes temporal trends in post-COVID condition incidence by body system from 2020-2024 using electronic health data from the Track PCC surveillance network. It is a descriptive epidemiological study of disease incidence patterns, not an intervention trial, and appears to be a secondary analysis of surveillance data rather than original trial results.

This cross-sectional study describes post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) in 68 South African healthcare workers, documenting symptom prevalence and severity using the MRC dyspnoea scale. The study identifies persistent symptoms including headaches, cough, fatigue, and breathing difficulties but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This observational study examined cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) outcomes in 21 patients with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (PASC) presenting with exertional dyspnea and exercise intolerance. The study identified breathing dysregulation as a key mechanism underlying these symptoms, present in 95% of patients despite normal oxygen uptake and cardiovascular function.

A longitudinal cohort study of 511 COVID-19 patients in Texas examining the incidence and predictors of Long COVID symptoms persisting beyond 3 months. The study found 19-59% experienced Long2 COVID, with Hispanic white background and baseline depression as significant risk factors, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study analyzing incidence and predictors of PASC and Long COVID in 13,940 adults and children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection from electronic health records. Identifies demographic and clinical risk factors associated with post-COVID conditions but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 449 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months examining long COVID prevalence and risk factors. Found that remdesivir treatment was associated with 35.9% reduction in long COVID incidence, while ICU admission and longer hospitalization increased risk.

A prospective cohort study of 574 COVID-19 patients with type 2 diabetes followed for 1 year post-discharge, examining associations between glycemic control and short- and long-term outcomes including fatigue, sweating, and respiratory symptoms. While the study does document long-term sequelae consistent with long COVID, it is observational without any intervention—patients are passively followed, not given a treatment to evaluate.

This prospective longitudinal cohort study compared physical capacity and health-related quality of life over 6 months in 360 adults across three groups: controls without COVID, those with short COVID, and those with long COVID. The long COVID group showed persistent impairments and significant improvements in fatigue but limited clinical meaningful changes in other outcomes.

Prospective cohort study of 68 COVID-19 ICU survivors monitored for 6 months post-discharge to assess functional independence and the impact of ICU-acquired weakness (ICUAW). Patients with ICUAW showed worse functional outcomes at 6 months compared to those without ICUAW (66.7% vs 22.8% with persistent limitations).

Observational study of 105 rheumatic and musculoskeletal disease patients hospitalized with COVID-19, followed from discharge through October 2020 to assess persistent symptoms and sequelae.
