Found 68.6% reported at least one persistent symptom (dyspnea, fatigue, chest pain) and 29.5% had sequelae, with no significant differences between autoimmune and non-autoimmune disease groups.

This cross-sectional study assessed cardiac function, functional capacity, and quality of life in 34 Egyptian long COVID patients using echocardiography, 6-minute walk tests, and quality-of-life questionnaires. The study found that 20.6% of patients had impaired left ventricular systolic function (abnormal GLS), with dyspnea being the most common symptom (94.1%), and identified correlations between cardiac dysfunction and reduced functional capacity.

This retrospective cohort study develops age-specific prediction models for all-cause mortality in COVID-19 survivors during the post-acute phase, using logistic regression and machine learning on clinical parameters from 891,246 patients. The study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, but rather builds prognostic models for mortality risk stratification in long COVID patients.

topics: health-related quality of life|rheumatic disease|pandemic impact
summary: UK prospective observational cohort study of rheumatic disease patients followed from April 2020 to December 2021, measuring health-related quality of life, COVID-19 infection rates, and long COVID incidence across four timepoints. Patients were passively followed without receiving any intervention; study assesses pandemic impact rather than testing a specific treatment.

Cross-sectional study comparing right ventricular function in mild COVID-19 recovered patients with and without post-COVID syndrome symptoms using speckle tracking echocardiography. Found significant impairment in RV function parameters in post-COVID syndrome patients correlated with symptoms like fatigue, palpitations, and chest pain.

This retrospective cohort study uses TriNetX data to investigate the association between post-COVID herpes zoster reactivation and subsequent uveitis and optic neuritis risk in COVID-19 survivors. While it documents significant associations with long-term complications, it is excluded as a secondary analysis of existing database records rather than a prospective treatment trial or intervention study.

This retrospective cohort study followed 28 pediatric patients with MIS-C (multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children) associated with COVID-19 for 6 months to evaluate cardiac outcomes. The study found significant improvement in vital signs and laboratory markers at 6-month follow-up, with good functional recovery and coronary outcomes.

This is an interim report from an ongoing longitudinal study (NCT04542031) examining long COVID prevalence and risk factors in rheumatic disease patients using web-based surveys across 14 months. The study found that post-COVID syndrome patients had significantly worse mental health outcomes than acute COVID patients, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective study examines baseline DMARD use and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) risk among 510 patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases. The analysis found that CD20 inhibitor users had significantly higher odds of developing PASC compared to conventional synthetic DMARD users, but this is an observational analysis of existing medication use rather than a treatment intervention study.

Retrospective EMR review of 210 long COVID patients examining whether pre-existing sleep disorders are associated with fatigue severity and brain fog. Found that sleep disorders contributed little to post-COVID fatigue or functional impairment.

This cross-sectional study analyzes sleep disturbance and fatigue prevalence in long COVID patients from the Cleveland Clinic ReCOVer Clinic cohort (n=682) using standardized PROMIS questionnaires. The study describes symptom severity and associations with demographics and mood symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Prospective observational study comparing fatigue levels between COVID-19 survivors and matched controls at two time points (~1 year apart) using the PROMIS Fatigue scale. Found significant between-group differences in fatigue at both timepoints, but modest effect sizes and no evidence of worsening long COVID symptoms over the follow-up period.

Prospective follow-up study of 285 COVID-19 survivors from Howard University Hospital assessed sleep and cognitive impairment 6-12 months post-infection in a minority population. Found significant associations between sleep disturbance and age, diabetes, ICU admission, and elevated troponin, but this is an observational study with no intervention administered.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between sleep quality, rest-activity rhythms, and cognitive performance in 40 Neuro-PASC patients. Found that patients had impaired attention and executive function with abnormal sleep characteristics, but no direct causal intervention was tested—this is an observational assessment study, not a treatment trial.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from multiple research networks to examine whether pre-existing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a risk factor for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC/long COVID). The study found that adults with pre-existing OSA had significantly elevated odds of developing probable PASC, with adjusted odds ratios remaining significant even after controlling for age, sex, race/ethnicity, hospitalization status, obesity, and comorbidities.

An observational study comparing nocturnal blood oxygen levels and sleep characteristics in 25 long COVID patients versus 25 healthy controls using in-laboratory polysomnography. Long COVID participants showed persistently lower nighttime blood oxygen saturation and higher respiratory rates during REM sleep, suggesting long COVID affects sleep physiology.

Retrospective chart review of 452 long COVID patients at Boston Medical Center identifying sleep disturbance phenotypes (insomnia, hypersomnia, mixed, other) and their associations with comorbidities, PASC symptoms, and medications. Study characterizes prevalence and predictors of sleep phenotypes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and sleep impairment in 1,228 Military Health System beneficiaries using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Those with prior infection were significantly more likely to have poor sleep health (32% vs 21%), with results consistent across sensitivity analyses.

Longitudinal observational study monitoring 646 COVID-19 positive patients for up to 14 months to establish the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and their correlations with age, comorbidities, and acute infection severity. Found 50.2% developed long COVID with fatigue, cough, and dyspnea being most common; older patients experienced more severe symptoms and longer post-COVID duration.

This cross-sectional study compares sleep quality, mental health, and fatigue outcomes between UK individuals with varying COVID-19 symptom duration (asymptomatic, short, long) and uninfected controls using validated questionnaires. Long symptom duration (post-COVID) was associated with significantly worse sleep quality (PSQI, SCI), increased sleepiness and fatigue (ESS, CFS), and prior mental illness history across both infected and uninfected groups.

This retrospective cohort study compared hospitalized COVID-19 patients with and without Chagas heart disease (CHD) over a 22-month follow-up to evaluate CHD's impact on clinical outcomes and long-COVID manifestations. The study found no significant differences in mortality, in-hospital outcomes, or long-COVID manifestations between CHD patients and controls, identifying age and lymphocyte count as independent mortality predictors.

This paper describes a cross-sectional assessment of sleep complaints and home sleep testing referrals from a long COVID clinic in Northeast Ohio, evaluating 277 patients presenting 10 months post-infection. The study found sleep disorders (particularly sleep apnea) in a subset of fatigued patients, but sleep testing results did not clearly differentiate fatigue presentations, and no specific sleep intervention or treatment was evaluated.

Prospective cohort study of 2,406 Michigan adults with COVID-19 examining the association between Long COVID and sleep outcomes at 1.5 and 3 years post-infection. Long COVID was associated with shorter sleep duration, poor sleep quality, and higher risk of moderate-to-severe sleep disturbance.

Longitudinal study tracking cardiac alterations in 7 young adults 3-4 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection using transthoracic echocardiography at baseline, 1-month, and 2-month follow-up. Found subclinical myocardial changes including elevated stroke volume at 2 months and decreased pulmonary vein systolic flow, suggesting myocardial recovery in the months following acute infection.

A longitudinal study tracking autonomic and cardiovascular function in 11 young adults at 3-4 weeks and 8-12 weeks post-COVID-19 diagnosis. The paper appears to be a conference abstract presenting preliminary findings on sympathetic nerve activity and cardiovascular responses to physiological stress, without a treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 209 patients hospitalized in intensive care for severe COVID-19, followed up to assess long-term functional and social outcomes at 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge. Study documents persistent functional impairments and social limitations in COVID-ICU survivors but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study examines the association between respiratory requirements during COVID-19 hospitalization and follow-up pulmonary function testing (PFT) results in 138 patients seen at a COVID-19 Recovery Clinic within 8 weeks of discharge. While it does assess long COVID sequelae, it is an observational descriptive study without any treatment intervention—patients are simply followed up and tested, making it ineligible for the treatment trials dataset.

Retrospective study comparing pulmonary fibrotic changes on chest CT imaging in survivors of COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 ARDS pneumonia at 6 weeks post-discharge. COVID-19 survivors showed higher prevalence of fibrotic changes (69% vs 43%) but similar functional outcomes, suggesting potential long-term sequelae requiring follow-up monitoring.

Follow-up study examining aortic stiffness (carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity) in 69 patients 2 months after COVID-19 pneumonia hospitalization. Found aortic stiffness was associated with disease severity markers and proADM levels, suggesting persistent vascular damage in post-COVID patients.

This observational study assessed the incidence of chronic pain 1 year after ICU discharge in COVID-19 patients with acute respiratory failure using the Brief Pain Inventory survey. 44% of 65 respondents reported chronic pain and 28% experienced moderate-to-severe pain interference with daily activities, indicating long-term pain as a sequela of severe COVID-19 hospitalization.

Single-center observational study comparing pulmonary CT imaging and function tests in 100 long COVID patients (stratified by acute illness severity) versus 106 healthy controls. Findings demonstrate that small airways disease with air trapping is a persistent sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection independent of initial infection severity, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study comparing arterial stiffness (PWV) in 143 COVID-19 recovery patients vs 143 hypertension controls at median 3.8 months post-infection. Found elevated PWV in COVID-19 group correlated with lower oxygen saturation at admission, suggesting SARS-CoV-2 causes vascular damage, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This multicenter observational cohort study followed 666 patients with chronic liver disease (CLD) who had COVID-19, comparing long-term outcomes to a control group without COVID-19. While 30% of CLD patients reported long-COVID symptoms, the study is descriptive/observational with no treatment intervention tested, focusing on characterizing disease burden and prognostic factors rather than evaluating any therapeutic approach.

Retrospective study of 217 patients hospitalized with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection examining new onset hypertension during acute illness. Paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications during hospitalization, not long COVID or treatment interventions for post-COVID sequelae.

This cross-sectional study examined 81 hypertensive patients 3-6 months post-COVID to identify risk factors for developing post-COVID syndrome, comparing those with pneumonia (n=48) to those with mild illness (n=33). Patients with pneumonia showed higher blood pressure, enlarged cardiac chambers, reduced ejection fraction, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ferritin, D-dimer), identifying several cardiac and inflammatory risk factors for post-COVID syndrome development.

Retrospective cohort study of 70 hypertensive COVID-19 pneumonia survivors examining whether ongoing anti-hypertensive treatment (ACE-inhibitors, ARBs, or other agents) impacts medium-long term sequelae at ~260 days post-infection. Found no significant differences in biochemical, radiological, or respiratory outcomes across treatment groups, suggesting ACE-inhibitors and ARBs do not influence COVID-19 pneumonia sequelae.

This prospective cohort study followed 220 long COVID patients over 12 months to characterize new-onset hypertension and left ventricular dysfunction after acute COVID-19 pneumonia. The study found that 73% of patients developed hypertension by 12 months, with echocardiography showing persistent global longitudinal strain abnormalities despite preserved ejection fraction.

Retrospective study of 78 COVID-19 patients examining the frequency of newly verified or worsened hypertension in the post-acute phase (>30 days post-infection). Found that 12.48% of patients developed or worsened hypertension with median onset at 90 days, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This prospective cohort study followed 212 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (50% hypertensive) for 12 months post-discharge, assessing physical, emotional, and cognitive symptoms using standardized questionnaires. The study found that hypertensive patients had higher residual respiratory symptoms while non-hypertensive patients exhibited worse cognitive dysfunction, but no intervention was administered.

This paper reviews medical records from a Bulgarian cardiological outpatient practice to assess the impact of COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome on cardiovascular health. The study found high rates of prior COVID-19 infection and vaccination but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares endothelial function and biomarkers in 64 hypertensive patients 1.5 years post-COVID-19 versus uninfected controls. It finds elevated ADMA, CRP, and albuminuria in post-COVID patients, suggesting prolonged endothelial dysfunction, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study comparing arterial stiffness measures in 53 COVID-19 convalescents versus age and sex-matched controls at 10-16 months and again 6 months later. Found elevated ankle-brachial index in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, with the effect becoming more pronounced over time, though no significant changes in vascular age or CAVI.

A prospective observational cohort study of 786 kidney transplant recipients who survived COVID-19, assessing the incidence and risk factors for long COVID symptoms at 3 months post-infection. Found 28% developed long COVID with dyspnea, myalgia, and weakness as common symptoms; elevated risk associated with severe acute COVID features and adverse cardiovascular events.

This NIH RECOVER-Pregnancy Cohort study assessed the prevalence of long COVID (PASC) in 1,502 individuals who were pregnant during their first SARS-CoV-2 infection, with follow-up at median 10.3 months post-infection. The study found a 9.3% PASC prevalence and identified obesity, depression/anxiety, economic hardship, and oxygen treatment during acute infection as significant risk factors.

This substudy of CARTESIAN examines biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction and coagulation dysregulation in adults 3-9 months post-COVID-19 compared to controls. The study finds no persistent long-term dysregulation but identifies a significant association between D-dimers and renal function independent of age.

Retrospective follow-up study of COVID-19 survivors who experienced venous thromboembolism during acute hospitalization, evaluating post-discharge coagulation and inflammatory parameters. The study tracks long-term consequences in a cohort receiving anticoagulant management but does not test a specific new treatment intervention.

This paper compares acute versus chronic urticaria triggered by COVID-19 infection in 92 patients, identifying that urticaria onset more than 2 weeks after infection may predict chronicity. While it describes a post-COVID manifestation, it is not about long COVID as a syndrome and does not study any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study of 45,842 patients with alcohol use disorder examines cardiovascular outcomes in those with and without prior COVID-19 infection during a 1-year follow-up period. Patients with AUD and COVID-19 history had significantly higher risk of major acute cardiovascular events including myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, and arrhythmia compared to those without COVID-19 history.

Multicenter observational cohort study comparing long COVID risk among 2,423 individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 during pregnancy versus outside pregnancy, using propensity score matching to account for confounding. Found no significant difference in long COVID prevalence at 6 months between pregnant (10.2%) and non-pregnant (10.6%) groups.

A single-centre observational study tracking post-COVID-19 syndrome outcomes in 94 haematology patients across different SARS-CoV-2 variants (March 2020 to March 2022). The study found declining mortality (42% to 2%) and post-COVID syndrome rates (46% to 14%) from Original/Alpha to Omicron variants, with severe initial infection as a risk factor for persistent symptoms.

Prospective observational study comparing microvascular function in 23 critical COVID-19 patients versus 15 controls during acute disease and ≥3 months post-infection using laser speckle contrast imaging. Critical COVID-19 patients showed elevated basal skin perfusion and reduced endothelial-dependent/independent vasodilation acutely, with persisting microvascular dysfunction post-infection.

Prospective cohort study of 60 COVID-19 survivors who required mechanical ventilation, assessed 6 months post-discharge for impairments in cognition, mental health, and physical function. Found 80% met criteria for post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) with cognitive and mental health impairments, but study focuses on acute respiratory failure sequelae rather than long COVID specifically.

topics: post-intensive care syndrome|cognitive impairment|physical disability|psychological outcomes
summary: This prospective cohort study followed 22 ICU-admitted COVID-19 patients at a 6-month PICS follow-up clinic to characterize cognitive, psychological, and physical consequences of critical illness. Patients showed high burden of impairment including low grip strength, mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 24), and psychological distress, but no specific intervention was tested or evaluated.

Prospective observational study examining persistent skeletal muscle weakness and fatigue in 120 survivors of critical COVID-19 at short-term follow-up (44 days post-discharge) and a nested cohort of 11 patients with muscle biopsies at long-term follow-up (267 days). Found 93% reported fatigue, reduced 6-minute walk test performance, and aberrant mitochondrial activity (reduced complex II/IV activity) in muscle tissue compared to non-COVID controls.

This prospective observational study compares post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) outcomes between COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 ICU survivors at 3 months post-discharge using standardized assessments. While it includes COVID-19 ICU survivors, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months after acute infection) and does not test any treatment intervention, making it outside scope for a long COVID treatment trial meta-analysis.

This study describes the Post COVID Kids Bavaria project, which conducted comprehensive medical and psychiatric evaluations of children and adolescents experiencing post-COVID symptoms lasting more than 4 weeks. The findings document a wide range of emotional and cognitive sequelae including fatigue, mood changes, sleep disturbances, and memory/concentration problems, emphasizing the need for multidisciplinary diagnostic and treatment approaches.

Prospective observational study of 172 critical COVID-19 survivors assessing sleep quality and circadian rest-activity patterns 3 months post-discharge using actigraphy and validated questionnaires. Found 60.5% had poor sleep quality, with mechanical ventilation and mental health compromise as significant predictors of sleep disruption.

Prospective cohort study of 428 COVID-19 ICU survivors assessing frailty and disability transitions at baseline (pre-COVID) and 90 days post-discharge. Found that 31% became frail by day 90 and disabilities increased significantly, but the study is purely observational with no intervention evaluated.

This study assessed balance and sensory deficits in 25 hospitalized patients immediately after acute COVID-19 infection using clinical balance tests. While it found motor and sensory balance impairments in acutely infected patients, it focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization rather than long COVID's persistent post-acute sequelae.

This matched cohort study compared 1-year mortality and long COVID prevalence between 359 cancer and non-cancer patients hospitalized for acute COVID-19 in 2020. Patients with cancer had significantly higher mortality (23% vs 5%) and both groups showed long COVID symptoms in about one-third of cases, with respiratory and neurological symptoms most prevalent at 12 months.

topics: post-intensive care syndrome|physical rehabilitation|persistent impairment|long-term outcomes
summary: A prospective longitudinal cohort study following 156 survivors of severe COVID-19 discharged to long-term acute care hospitals, assessing impairments at one-year follow-up. Approximately two-thirds experienced persistent physical, respiratory, psychiatric, or cognitive impairments resembling post-intensive care syndrome, with most describing protracted recovery through rehabilitation and time.

This national study examines financial hardship across COVID-19 infection history and long COVID status using US Census Household Pulse Survey data from 2022-2024. It finds that financial hardship is significantly higher for those with activity-limiting long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining the association between acute COVID-19 infection during pregnancy and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) risk in pregnant women. While the study found transient increased GDM risk in the first month post-infection, it does not address long COVID (persistent post-acute sequelae) and therefore falls outside the scope of long COVID clinical trials screening.

This study examines whether pre-pandemic leukocyte count and hsCRP predict post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) severity in 1,237 postmenopausal women from the Women's Health Initiative. It is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data with no treatment intervention—participants were not given a treatment but rather followed up retrospectively based on pre-pandemic biomarkers collected 25 years earlier.

Prospective study of neurologic outcomes in COVID-19 ARDS survivors requiring ICU intubation, followed 3-6 months post-discharge. While some neurologic sequelae were observed, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 complications (ICU survivors) rather than long COVID as a distinct post-acute syndrome, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort analysis from the Women's Health Initiative examining associations between preexisting depressive and anxiety symptoms and risk of developing long COVID. Women with both depressive and anxiety symptoms had 78% higher odds of long COVID, while mental health symptoms were associated with lower compliance with COVID prevention measures.

Observational study of 56 post-COVID-19 patients completing 8-12 weeks of pulmonary rehabilitation (3 sessions/week). Pulmonary rehabilitation significantly improved 6-minute walk test distance (+84.3 m), dyspnea perception, depressive symptoms, and disease management knowledge.

Retrospective analysis comparing pulmonary rehabilitation outcomes in 192 patients with COPD, ILD, and Long COVID at a single academic center (2020-2022). All three groups showed significant improvements in functional capacity, dyspnea, quality of life, depression, anxiety, and stress with comparable outcomes across diagnoses.

Prospective observational study assessing quality of life, disability, anxiety, and insomnia in 199 COVID-19 patients at 4 and 8 months post-discharge after noninvasive ventilation/CPAP treatment. Found deterioration in quality of life, mobility, and pain over the follow-up period, particularly those with comorbidities.

This study evaluated cardiac sequelae 6 months after ICU discharge in 42 COVID-19 survivors using comprehensive cardiovascular screening including ECG, biomarkers, echocardiography, and cardiac MRI. Results revealed that 19% had newly diagnosed coronary artery disease, 24% had abnormal left ventricular strain, and 42% had CMR abnormalities, demonstrating significant long-term cardiovascular complications after severe COVID-19.

LOCHINVAR is a prospective longitudinal study comparing blood pressure and endothelial function in COVID-19 survivors versus controls at 12 months post-infection. The study documents persistent vascular dysfunction and increased BP in recovered COVID-19 patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective study assessed optic nerve head vessel density in 90 COVID-19 patients at 4 and 12 weeks post-diagnosis using OCT angiography. No significant changes in peripapillary vascularization were observed, and no correlation was found between vessel density and disease severity or clinical parameters.

This study prospectively assessed 90 children presenting to a designated long COVID clinic to characterize symptoms and clinical findings. Nearly 60% of children showed functional impairment at 1-7 months post-infection, with mild abnormal findings observed in approximately half the patients, primarily involving the respiratory system.

A prospective cohort study of 4,212 adults followed for 7 years identifying causal factors (cough, insomnia) for post-COVID chronic fatigue syndrome and evaluating Qingjin Yiqi granules as a potential herbal treatment through Mendelian randomization and virtual screening. The study found that two bioactive compounds in QJYQ bind with high affinity to ESAM, a protein linked to CFS-associated symptoms.

Prospective follow-up study of 175 COVID-19 patients discharged from hospital, tracked at 6, 9, and 12 months post-discharge to assess quality of life and long-term sequelae. Found increasing prevalence of sequelae (29.8% at 6 months to 51.1% at 9 months), with worse outcomes in females and severe/critically ill patients for fatigue, sleep disturbance, and joint/muscle pain.

Population-based survey of 1,813 nonhospitalized children and adolescents (ages 5-90) examining persistent COVID-19 symptoms in relation to SARS-CoV-2 antibody status, vaccine status, and demographic factors. Found 4.5% reported persistent symptoms, with children at lower risk than adults, and identified risk factors including severe initial infection, lack of vaccination, and unhealthy weight.

Matched cohort study comparing long COVID symptoms in 643 Icelandic children with SARS-CoV-2 infection to 602 uninfected age- and sex-matched controls. Found that infected children reported more symptoms (fatigue and concentration loss prominent in teenagers), with about one-third resolving at follow-up.

This retrospective cohort study examines post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in hospitalized US children over 5 months follow-up, documenting health care visits and burden of complications. The study is observational without intervention and does not evaluate any treatment.

A prospective cohort study of 244 children with COVID-19 followed for 6 months to determine post-COVID-19 condition prevalence and risk factors. Found 4.9% had persistent symptoms at 12 weeks, with female sex and >3 acute symptoms associated with increased risk.

This single-center observational cohort study describes the clinical features, presenting symptom clusters, and outcomes of 81 children and young people referred to a Post-Acute COVID Clinic with persistent symptoms ≥12 weeks. Most patients showed improvement by 6 months, but the study does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study followed children hospitalized with MIS-C or acute COVID-19 for up to 2 years post-discharge to assess long-term health outcomes. Approximately 20% of children in both groups experienced persistent symptoms including fatigue and headache beyond 1 year, highlighting the importance of long-term clinical follow-up.

A prospective single-center study describing clinical manifestations and biopsychosocial impact of post-COVID syndrome in 50 pediatric patients, assessing fatigue, exertion intolerance, school absenteeism, and mental health outcomes. The study found that 80% had typical pPCS while 20% had functional disorder presentations, with significant educational and social burden identified across both groups.

A retrospective study describing persistent symptoms of long COVID in a pediatric cohort and identifying risk factors for disease development. The study found 17.6% prevalence of long COVID in children, with respiratory symptoms early and neuropsychiatric symptoms developing over time, with chronic conditions, obesity, and adolescent age as risk factors.

This combined retrospective and prospective cohort study enrolled 618 children (437 with COVID-19, 181 with other respiratory infections) and tracked persisting symptoms and long COVID at 1-12 months post-infection. Long COVID occurred in 20.4% of COVID-19 cases with respiratory systems most affected; anosmia, pneumonia history, and delta/omicron infection were significant risk factors.

A multicenter retrospective cohort study of 1,969 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors assessed musculoskeletal pain prevalence and risk factors at 8.4 months post-discharge. The study found 45% reported post-COVID musculoskeletal pain, with female sex, prior pain history, acute myalgia/headache, and longer hospitalization as risk factors, but conducted no intervention testing.

This retrospective cohort study examined whether serological biomarkers measured at hospital admission predicted development of long-term post-COVID pain in 412 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors followed at 6.8 and 13.2 months post-discharge. The study found that while some biomarkers showed statistical associations with post-COVID pain, they explained only 6.9% of variance, suggesting other factors like initial symptom load are more relevant for pain development.

This cross-sectional study assessed vascular health in 223 children ~6.8 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to healthy controls, measuring pulse wave velocity, carotid intima-media thickness, and inflammatory biomarkers. While structural arterial changes were absent, the study found evidence of endothelial activation (elevated soluble ICAM-1) and approximately 24% of infected children reported long COVID symptoms, suggesting distinct pathophysiology in pediatric post-acute COVID-19.

Multicenter prospective cohort study tracking musculoskeletal pain prevalence in 1,593 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at three timepoints over 13 months post-discharge. Found musculoskeletal pain peaked at 8 months (43.4%) and declined by 13 months (37.8%), with female sex, pre-existing pain, and hospitalization duration as risk factors.

This observational cohort study characterized the occurrence and severity of pain and peripheral neuropathy symptoms in 542 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients compared to 1014 controls, assessed 30-90 days post-infection. SARS-CoV-2 infection was independently associated with significantly higher risk of peripheral neuropathy symptoms (28.8% vs 12.9%) and persistent symptoms at 90 days (6.1% vs 1.9%), as well as increased pain in extremities.

This retrospective cohort study uses electronic health records to examine whether chronic overlapping pain conditions (COPCs) predict the onset of long COVID features across three cohorts. The findings show that COPCs significantly increase the risk of long COVID across COVID, influenza, and noninfected populations, suggesting nociplastic mechanisms play a prominent role in long COVID pathophysiology.

This retrospective analysis examines 13,153 COVID-19 workers' compensation claims to identify attributes associated with prolonged impairment and high costs. The study finds that age is the strongest predictor of prolonged disability and increased medical costs, with 5% of claims accounting for 65% of total paid costs.

Retrospective analysis of 234 Wisconsin workers with long COVID in the workers' compensation system from March 2020 to July 2022, examining associations with age, race, vaccination status, and variant period. Identifies risk factors and occupational disparities in long COVID prevalence but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This prospective cohort study followed healthcare workers for 6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess symptom persistence, post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence, and health-related quality of life. While it documents high rates of post-COVID-19 syndrome (36.2%) and persistent HRQOL deterioration, it is an observational study that passively follows patients without administering any intervention or treatment.

This study describes utilization patterns and characteristics of patients referred to a rural post-acute COVID syndrome clinic between April 2021 and April 2022, using electronic health records to analyze 747 referrals and specialty care patterns. While it documents clinic operations and demonstrates the role of telehealth in expanding rural access to care, it is a descriptive utilization study without testing or evaluating a specific intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated neurocognitive screening evaluations (NCSE) in 64 employees with post-COVID-19 neurocognitive complaints, examining symptom validity and return-to-work outcomes. While the screening assessment was associated with faster return to work (~3 weeks), this is an assessment/diagnostic study rather than a treatment intervention trial.

Retrospective cohort study comparing work performance loss and annual monetary costs among Malaysian healthcare workers with and without long COVID using the Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Findings show healthcare workers with long COVID experience significantly higher presenteeism-related annual monetary losses (MYR 10,866.61 vs MYR 9,243.85).

Survey of 734 ultramarathon runners assessing COVID-19 infection rates and symptoms. Found 6.8% reported long COVID (>12 weeks symptoms), but the study is observational only—no intervention or treatment is tested.

This study examines the correlation between physical activity and metabolic syndrome risk factors in firefighters following COVID-19 recovery, comparing pre- and post-infection measurements. While the paper measures changes post-COVID, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months after infection) and instead emphasizes general metabolic health recovery in occupational populations.

This cross-sectional study assessed overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms in 65 deconditioned COVID-19 patients recovering at an inpatient rehabilitation facility between June-December 2020. The authors found that 45 patients (69%) developed new or worsening OAB symptoms with median symptom and quality-of-life scores of 17-19, suggesting urological manifestations may be an important component of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome.

Prospective cohort study of 350 long COVID patients with COVID-associated cystitis (CAC) followed for 21-28 months post-discharge, assessing outcomes of conservative overactive bladder (OAB) management. Overall 87% improved with standard therapies (behavioral modification), with 95.4% improvement in patients with new-onset symptoms and only 13% experiencing persistent lower urinary tract symptoms at follow-up.

Retrospective cohort study examining auditory and vestibular symptoms in 74 individuals with confirmed COVID-19 from the March-May 2020 pandemic wave, comparing symptoms documented during acute infection to self-reported symptoms in 2021-2022 follow-up survey. Found that vestibular symptoms persisted (58% initially, 43% at follow-up) while auditory symptoms increased over time (9% initially, 55% at follow-up), suggesting differential long-term impact.

This case series follows 60 COVID-19 patients treated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for severe pulmonary failure, assessing survival and functional recovery at 6 months. Among survivors to discharge, long-term recovery showed substantial deficits including cognitive impairment and depression, though most maintained cardiopulmonary stability and independence in daily living.

This prospective observational study examined perioperative complications in 167 COVID-19 survivors undergoing elective surgery, comparing outcomes based on time elapsed since infection. The study found that perioperative complications did not significantly differ by time since infection, though oxygen support requirements decreased with longer intervals since COVID-19 positivity.

Prospective single-center follow-up study of 34 COVID-19 patients treated with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), with physical, cognitive, and psychological assessments at 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge. Patients showed significant long-term sequelae including muscle weakness (67%), cognitive impairment (29%), anxiety (29%), and depression (23%), with most outcomes improving over time but cognitive and psychological symptoms remaining persistent.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates in-hospital outcomes and post-discharge status in severe COVID-19 patients who received ECMO support across two Brazilian hospitals, with 47% in-hospital mortality. Post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) symptoms were reported by two-thirds of survivors at 30 days and half at 90 days post-discharge, with most patients returning to work by 90 days.

Retrospective cohort study describing long-term consequences of COVID-19 in 694 recovered patients from Jordan, examining post-discharge symptoms, newly diagnosed comorbidities, and radiological findings. Found that severe/critical patients were more prone to developing symptoms, with diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension being the most common new comorbidities, though most radiological abnormalities resolved by follow-up.

Retrospective study of 110 COVID-19 patients examining intercostal muscle mass changes over 3 months post-infection using CT imaging analysis. Found that intercostal muscle wasting is pronounced and aggravated after 3 months, with prolonged follow-up and steroid use as significant predictors, but this is an observational cohort study without any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study assessed the prevalence and severity of vertigo and hearing impairment in 250 COVID-19 recovered patients using standardized questionnaires and audiometric testing. The findings identified a significant association between COVID-19 severity and increased risk of vertigo and hearing impairment in the post-recovery phase.

This nationwide cohort study examines long-term mortality outcomes in heart failure patients following COVID-19 infection in Korea using propensity-score matching. The study found that COVID-19 infection was associated with significantly elevated all-cause mortality within 30 days and up to 1 year post-infection in this population, but does not test any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines the incidence of new or worsening overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms in 1,895 participants with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to uninfected controls. The study found COVID-19 positive patients had significantly higher rates of OAB symptom worsening (35.7% vs 15.7%, OR 2.99) but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatments for post-COVID syndrome in 79 patients treated by TCM physicians in Germany and Austria. Results showed significant improvements in fatigue, physical performance, and exertional dyspnea after an average of 7 TCM consultations, with physicians rating global symptom improvement at 62% on average.

This study compared urodynamic characteristics between BPH patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection, finding higher incidence of detrusor underactivity in the COVID-19 group. The paper investigates a long-COVID symptom/sequela (urodynamic dysfunction) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

topics: cardiovascular|autonomic nervous system|physical activity|heart rate variability
summary: This retrospective study compared heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system function between COVID-19-exposed and nonexposed individuals, stratified by self-reported physical activity levels in 142 Saudi Arabian participants. While physically active participants showed better HRV metrics overall, the study found no significant differences based on activity duration and suggests COVID-19 may blunt the cardiovascular benefits of physical activity.

Prospective multicenter observational cohort study examining associations between long COVID fatigue subtypes (physical vs mental), depression, anxiety, acute COVID-19 severity, and health-related quality of life in 208 Portuguese patients. Found fatigue strongly linked to depression and anxiety, with mild/moderate acute cases showing greater fatigue and lower quality of life than severe cases.

Retrospective observational study of 229 COVID-19 survivors assessing pulmonary function and clinical parameters 3 months post-infection. No intervention was tested; the study passively characterized residual pulmonary dysfunction and symptoms in recovering patients.

This retrospective observational study evaluated two Traditional Chinese Medicine formulas (FZYF and FZAS) in 114 COVID-19 convalescent patients, measuring effects on psychological state, dyspnea, and quality of life using validated instruments (GHQ-12, Modified Borg Scale, SF-36). Both formulas showed significant improvements in psychological well-being and dyspnea symptoms, with SF-36 scores improving by approximately 22-23% across physical and mental health domains.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates the safety of tranexamic acid (TXA) in post-COVID patients undergoing major arthroplasty, using propensity-matched data from the TriNetX database. While the paper includes post-COVID patients, it is not about long COVID as a disease; it focuses on perioperative safety in patients who happen to have had recent COVID-19 infection undergoing elective surgery.

This prospective follow-up study compares cognitive function and mood changes in 90 older COVID-19 survivors versus 90 healthy controls at 1, 6, and 12 months post-infection. COVID-19 survivors showed lower cognitive function at months 1 and 6, but cognitive and mood differences resolved by month 12, with the exception of persistent memory impairment.

Prospective cohort study of 303 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed after discharge to assess incidence of post-COVID-19 IBS using Rome-IV criteria. Found 10.6% developed IBS post-COVID, with female sex, oxygen requirement, GI symptoms during acute infection, and elevated procalcitonin as independent risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study using N3C database to compare incidence of vestibular disorders in COVID-19 positive patients versus controls across different viral variants. While the paper demonstrates elevated vestibular disorder risk post-COVID, it is not about long COVID specifically and does not study any treatment intervention.

A retrospective observational study of 50 long COVID patients undergoing a rehabilitation program targeting fatigue, breathlessness, and pain. The program showed feasibility with significant improvements in symptom intensity and health-related quality of life.

Retrospective cohort study comparing 43 COVID-19 patients admitted to inpatient rehabilitation with 247 controls without COVID-19, examining functional outcomes and characteristics during rehabilitation. Although COVID-19 patients had worse baseline function, inpatient rehabilitation significantly improved their outcomes to comparable levels as controls at discharge.

Prospective observational study comparing inflammatory markers and outcomes in sepsis patients with vs without a history of severe COVID-19. Finds that prior severe COVID-19 is associated with worse sepsis outcomes and immune dysregulation, but does not study treatment of long COVID itself.

This retrospective cohort study examines how the ICD-10-CM diagnosis code for Post-COVID Conditions (U09.9) is being used in clinical practice across 382,400 US patients from October 2021 to June 2023. The study documents prevalence, timing, co-occurring conditions, and healthcare utilization patterns but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated chronic pain and fatigue in 157 COVID-19 patients 12 months post-hospitalization. About 27% experienced chronic fatigue and 15% reported severe chronic pain, with minimal use of formal treatments like physiotherapy or psychotherapy.

This study assessed body composition and physical performance in 69 patients 12 months after COVID-19 of varying severity using bioelectrical impedance analysis, 6-min-walk tests, and quality-of-life scales. While overall physical recovery was good, patients with severe acute COVID-19 showed worse outcomes including higher body mass index increases, reduced muscle mass, and poorer physical performance compared to those with mild or moderate infection.

A retrospective single-center study of 97 pediatric long COVID patients examining quality of life using PedsQL scores and associations with preexisting conditions. The study found that long COVID significantly impairs quality of life in children, with preexisting mood disorders, depression, and allergies worsening symptoms and outcomes.

This retrospective study evaluated the effects of enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP) therapy in 80 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment, comparing cognitive function before and after treatment. Results showed significant improvement in composite cognitive scores post-EECP in patients with objectively defined baseline cognitive impairment, with no safety concerns documented.

This multi-centre observational study assessed the prevalence and impact of olfactory and gustatory dysfunction among 1,734 COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia within 2 months post-infection. While it documents high prevalence of chemosensory symptoms and their quality-of-life impact, it does not study an intervention or treatment and focuses on acute/early post-infection symptoms rather than long COVID (which typically persists weeks to months after recovery).

Retrospective observational study assessing symptom patterns and health-related quality of life in 85 long-COVID patients. Found motor deficits and fatigue were most common, but symptom count did not correlate with quality of life outcomes.

Prospective observational study comparing gastrointestinal symptoms in 590 patients 5-8 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection versus negative controls, finding 19% prevalence in moderate-severe cases and 7.3% in mild cases versus 3% controls. Machine learning identified acute diarrhea and antibiotic use during acute infection as strongest predictors of persistent gastrointestinal symptoms.

A prospective study examining how psychological factors (somatic symptom burden, fear of COVID, chronic stress, depression, positive affect) predict the odds and severity of long COVID symptoms across acute, subacute (3 months), and chronic (6 months) phases in 137 PCR-positive participants. Findings indicate that psychological factors significantly influence the experience and persistence of post-COVID syndrome, with potential implications for psychological interventions.

This prospective cohort study tracked post-COVID pain symptoms in 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at three timepoints over 18 months, visualizing the fluctuating nature and recovery trajectory of pain. Results showed pain prevalence decreased from 41% at 8.4 months to 28% at 18.3 months, with lower extremity and widespread pain being most common; female sex, pre-existing pain, and hospitalization duration were associated with persistent pain.

This retrospective cohort study uses aggregated EHR data from >90 million patients to investigate the association between preexisting psychiatric conditions and long COVID diagnosis. It finds that patients with preexisting psychiatric diagnoses have 1.52× greater prevalence of long COVID diagnosis, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared SARS-CoV-2-specific immune responses and long COVID prevalence between people with HIV and HIV-negative individuals recovering from COVID-19. People with HIV had significantly higher odds of developing PASC (long COVID) and showed distinct CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell response patterns compared to HIV-negative controls.

This retrospective cohort study compares long COVID manifestations between people with HIV (PWH) and people without HIV (PWoH) using statewide electronic health records from South Carolina. The analysis finds PWH have significantly higher rates of long COVID diagnoses overall (16.3% vs 10.6%), with elevated risks particularly for nervous system diseases, mental disorders, and respiratory conditions.

This prospective cohort study measures plasma biomarkers of neurogenesis, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and inflammation in 44 people with and without HIV at baseline (10 days post-COVID), 3 months, and 6 months. The study finds transient BBB disruption and altered neurogenesis biomarkers (particularly in people with HIV), but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational study examined the risk of developing autoimmune diseases following COVID-19 infection using Japanese electronic medical records. While it documents associations between COVID-19 and autoimmune disease development, it does not study or test any specific treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study quantified lung metabolic activity and inflammatory biomarkers in 53 COVID-19 survivors with persistent symptoms compared to 45 healthy controls. The study found increased metabolic activity and elevated thromboinflammatory markers in survivors months after infection, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compared chest CT findings and pulmonary function tests (PFTs) between 63 post-COVID-19 respiratory condition patients and 23 asymptomatic controls. The study found that post-COVID patients had significantly greater lung abnormalities on CT, impaired PFTs (lower diffusing capacity, vital capacity, and total lung capacity), and that CT extent correlated with ICU admission and hospital stay duration.

This prospective observational study compared cardiac MRI findings in 29 children with post-COVID syndrome versus matched healthy controls. The study found evidence of myocardial inflammation and altered right ventricular volumetrics in PCS children but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study examining brain metabolism in 87 PASC patients with neurocognitive symptoms using [18F]FDG PET/CT imaging compared to 55 healthy controls. The study identified regional hypometabolism correlated with concentration and memory impairments, providing mechanistic insights into the neuropathophysiology of long COVID cognitive dysfunction.

This study follows 912 kidney transplant recipients who survived COVID-19, assessing their clinical, functional, and mental health outcomes at 3 months post-diagnosis. While it documents recovery trajectories in this immunocompromised population, it focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes in transplant patients rather than long COVID syndrome or post-acute sequelae.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study examining long COVID prevalence among kidney transplant recipients who had COVID-19. Found 27% developed long COVID with body aches as most common symptom, and acute illness symptom burden was the only independent risk factor; no treatment intervention was tested.

Prospective cohort study investigating Long COVID prevalence and risk factors among kidney transplant recipients during Omicron predominance in Brazil (52% prevalence, n=602). No treatment intervention tested; epidemiological study of symptom burden and associated risk factors in immunocompromised population.

Prospective observational study of 201 low-risk individuals with persistent symptoms 4 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, assessing organ function across heart, lungs, kidneys, liver, pancreas, and spleen using questionnaires, blood tests, and MRI imaging. Found that 70% of individuals had impairment in one or more organs, with multi-organ involvement in 25% and strong association with prior hospitalization.

Retrospective cohort study examining 105 Alzheimer disease patients in Brazil, comparing 28 COVID-19 survivors to non-infected controls over 5-year follow-up. Finds COVID-19 infection associated with accelerated AD progression and reduced survival, particularly in hospitalized patients, but does not study long COVID or test any interventions for long COVID.

Prospective registry study of hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessing neurological, functional, cognitive, and psychiatric outcomes at 3 months post-infection. Found that 71% experienced persistent neurological symptoms at 3 months, with fatigue (42%), PTSD (29%), and pain (64%) being most common.

Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from Mayo Clinic to identify post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 by comparing symptom and disease frequencies before and after COVID-19 diagnosis in 6,413 patients. Found significant enrichment of thromboembolism in males, hair loss in females, and hypertensive chronic kidney disease in the 3-6 months post-diagnosis period.

A non-randomized comparison of COVID-19 survivors with neuropsychiatric sequelae who received micronized/ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) 600 mg twice daily for 3 months versus those who declined treatment. The PEA-treated group showed significantly greater improvements in depression and fatigue, with treatment effects independent of baseline characteristics.

Retrospective cohort study measuring serum antibody levels, neutralizing capability, and T cell responses (IFN-γ and IL-2) in long COVID patients up to 40 months post-infection. Found no significant differences in immune responses among patients with ongoing long COVID, those recovered from it, or acute COVID-19 controls, suggesting no evidence of reduced immune function in long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study compared COVID-19 patients hospitalized post-viral clearance versus those not re-admitted after clearance, identifying pre-existing conditions (acute kidney injury, anemia, cardiac arrhythmia) associated with amplified post-viral hospitalization risk. The study highlights specific comorbidities that predispose some patients to long COVID complications despite confirmed SARS-CoV-2 clearance.

Prospective cohort study of 4,182 COVID-19 cases using the COVID Symptom Study app to characterize long COVID prevalence (13.3% at ≥28 days) and identify risk factors and early predictors. Developed a predictive model using symptoms at day 7 with 76% ROC-AUC to distinguish short from long COVID, potentially useful for identifying trial participants and targeting rehabilitation services.

Prospective cohort study of 61 subjects with persistent symptoms after acute COVID-19, examining pulmonary function and plasma biomarker profiles at median 9 weeks post-infection. Study identifies immune-fibrotic biomarkers (LCN2, MMP-7, HGF) associated with lung impairment but does not test any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal observational study measuring SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses, antibody levels, and inflammatory markers in 70 individuals up to 9 months post-infection, stratified by initial disease severity and symptom persistence. Found stable adaptive immune responses across disease severity and no substantial differences in immune markers between those with and without persistent COVID-19 symptoms.

Prospective cohort study following 127 COVID-19 patients 6 months post-infection via online surveys to characterize the prevalence and pattern of long COVID symptoms. Found 67% reported at least one symptom, with exertional dyspnea (30%), fatigue (25%), and diminished taste/smell (19%) most common; no intervention or treatment was tested.

A prospective observational study of 42 long COVID patients presenting with persistent fatigue 6 months post-infection, characterizing clinical features and comparing those meeting ME/CFS criteria to those who don't. This is an observational study without intervention—patients are clinically characterized but no treatment is tested or evaluated.

Prospective longitudinal study following 146 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for up to 6 months post-discharge to characterize clinical, virological, and immunological outcomes and identify predictors of long COVID. Found that lower peak S-IgG antibody titers, higher WHO severity score, and female sex predicted long COVID symptoms, but prolonged viral shedding did not.

A prospective observational cohort study enrolling 179 adults with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection and followed at 4-month intervals through 8 months post-infection to characterize post-acute sequelae (PASC/long COVID). The study documents persistent physical symptoms (fatigue, shortness of breath, cognitive issues), mental health symptoms, and reduced quality of life in a substantial proportion of participants, with collection of biospecimens to facilitate mechanistic research.

A prospective observational study comparing 44 long COVID patients who received SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (Pfizer or Oxford-AstraZeneca) with 22 matched unvaccinated patients from the same cohort. Vaccination was not associated with worsening of symptoms or quality of life, and vaccinated participants showed small improvements in symptom resolution compared to unvaccinated matched controls.

A prospective cohort study following 99 COVID-19 patients for 8 months to assess the prevalence and natural course of long COVID symptoms. The study found that 19% met the criteria for long COVID at 8 months with no significant improvement between 4-8 month assessments, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective follow-up study assessing the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms 12 months after mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection in 304 patients. The study found that 53% of patients reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue and olfactory/gustatory dysfunction being most common, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study following 958 non-hospitalized patients with mild COVID-19 for up to 7 months to characterize long-term health consequences. Found that 27.8-34.8% of patients experienced persistent symptoms (anosmia, ageusia, fatigue, shortness of breath) meeting post-COVID syndrome criteria, with lower baseline IgG levels and acute phase symptoms as risk factors.

Prospective multimodal evaluation of 30 long COVID patients to characterize clinical, immunological, and psychological features 5 months post-symptom onset. Found fatigue and pain prevalent, psychiatric distress common, but no novel biomarkers or SARS-CoV-2 serological correlates identified.

Prospective longitudinal surveillance study of healthcare workers characterizing long COVID symptoms 7.5 months after infection, identifying three symptom clusters (sensory, neurological, cardiorespiratory) more prevalent in cases than controls. This is an observational descriptive study with no treatment intervention, designed to characterize the condition rather than test therapeutic outcomes.

Population-based longitudinal cohort study of 1,355 Swiss school children with 6-month follow-up comparing seropositive and seronegative children for long COVID symptoms. Found low prevalence of symptoms lasting >4 weeks (9% seropositive vs 10% seronegative) and >12 weeks (4% vs 2%), with no hospitalizations reported among seropositive children.

Retrospective cohort study comparing post-acute sequelae incidence between COVID-19 and influenza patients using claims and EHR databases across three health systems. Characterizes the long-term symptom burden and diagnoses in over 440,000 COVID-19 patients without testing any interventions.

This is a descriptive cohort study of 107 patients seen at Mayo Clinic's Post COVID Care Clinic, characterizing clinical phenotypes and immune biomarkers in long COVID patients. The study identifies female predominance in fatigue-predominant phenotypes and elevated IL-6 levels, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study comparing immunological profiles of long COVID patients to controls, finding persistent activation of innate immune cells and elevated inflammatory cytokines 8 months post-infection. Identifies four biomarkers (IL-6, IFN-γ, MCP-1, VCAM-1) with 75.9% accuracy for long COVID classification, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Analysis of 10 UK longitudinal studies and electronic health records to identify risk factors associated with long COVID, examining symptom duration and sociodemographic predictors. Finds that age, female sex, pre-existing mental/general health issues, asthma, and obesity increase long COVID risk, with no intervention tested.

Prospective cohort study of MS patients from the UK MS Register examining long COVID prevalence and predictors, finding that 31.1% had symptoms ≥4 weeks and 13.1% ≥12 weeks. Study identifies pre-existing anxiety, depression, and physical disability as associated with prolonged COVID-19 symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This pre-post study compared health care service use in 700,000 Norwegian children who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 versus those who tested negative, measuring utilization up to 6 months post-infection. The study found elevated primary care use for up to 3-6 months in younger children after COVID-19, indicating measurable long-term health sequelae but not evaluating any treatment intervention.

Observational follow-up study of 990 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in North India, assessing long COVID symptom persistence at 4-16 weeks and 9-12 months post-discharge. Found ~40% reported long COVID symptoms with fatigue, myalgia, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and breathlessness being most common, with symptom duration associated with disease severity at admission.

This study investigates the relationship between post-COVID syndrome and inflammatory markers in 121 mild COVID-19 patients, with sex-stratified analysis. While it confirms associations between inflammatory markers (particularly neutrophil counts) and post-COVID symptoms like fatigue and anosmia, it is an observational cross-sectional study with no treatment intervention tested.

This observational cohort study from the NOR-Solidarity trial examined gut microbiota alterations and markers of gut barrier dysfunction in COVID-19 patients with persistent respiratory dysfunction at three months post-hospitalization. The findings show reduced microbial diversity, altered microbiota composition, and persistently elevated lipopolysaccharide-binding protein (LBP) levels in patients with persistent respiratory dysfunction, suggesting a potential gut-lung axis in long COVID pathogenesis.

This is a prospective cohort study measuring soluble immune markers (TNF-alpha, IP-10, IL-6) in SARS-CoV-2 recovered individuals at 90 days post-infection to identify biological correlates of PASC. The study found elevated cytokine levels associated with PASC development but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence of new-onset neuropsychiatric symptoms in children and adolescents 90-150 days after SARS-CoV-2 positivity using electronic health records from two New England health systems. Found 7.2% exhibited incident neuropsychiatric symptoms, with headache, mood/anxiety, cognitive symptoms, and fatigue most common; results suggest symptom prevalence post-infection is similar to pre-infection rates.

Prospective multicenter cohort study examining long-COVID symptom prevalence in 3,334 healthcare workers with varying SARS-CoV-2 exposure status. Found that workers with positive nasopharyngeal swab reported significantly more long-COVID symptoms than controls, while baseline physical activity was protective against neurocognitive impairment and fatigue.

Prospective cohort study examining how biological sex and sociocultural gender factors influence the prevalence and severity of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 2,927 Swiss individuals. Found that women experienced PASC more frequently than men, with personality traits, living situation, stress levels, and education level all contributing to symptom burden.

Longitudinal survey characterizing smell and taste recovery in 1,468 COVID-19 patients over ~200 days post-infection. Found persistent olfactory dysfunction in ~48-60% of participants with increasing parosmia (47%) and phantosmia (25%) at follow-up, suggesting smell impairment as a marker of long-COVID.

The COVID and Cognition Study is a cross-sectional and longitudinal observational study documenting cognitive problems in 181 long COVID patients and 185 controls. The paper identifies severity of initial illness and specific symptom profiles (neurological, fatigue, gastro-intestinal, cardiopulmonary) as predictors of cognitive symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A 9-month prospective follow-up study of 95 COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and predictors of long COVID symptoms. The study found that acute phase neuropsychiatric symptoms were associated with chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive deficits in the follow-up period, but acute disease severity was not predictive of long COVID symptoms.

This large matched cohort study of 157,134 individuals compared post-COVID-19 morbidity outcomes between COVID-19 patients and matched controls using comprehensive German healthcare data. While it documents substantial new-onset symptoms across multiple domains in both children and adults, it is a retrospective observational study without intervention and represents secondary analysis of existing health records rather than a prospective treatment trial.

Digital epidemiology study recruiting 318 participants from the DigiHero cohort to investigate molecular mechanisms underlying post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found that elevated IL-1ß, IL-6, and TNF-α cytokine levels are associated with persistent PASC symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, and concentration deficits.

This retrospective cohort study of 240,648 COVID-19-infected persons examines whether COVID-19 vaccination reduces long-COVID incidence and symptom progression. The analysis shows that pre-infection vaccination and post-infection vaccination (up to 12 weeks after diagnosis) both substantially reduce the probability of developing multiple long-COVID symptoms, with unvaccinated individuals 3–10 times more likely to report persistent symptoms.

Longitudinal study of 33 post-COVID syndrome patients followed 7-11 months after acute COVID-19 to characterize autoimmune activation and immunological abnormalities. Found persistent latent/overt autoimmunity and proinflammatory state with elevated cytokines and altered immune cell populations, but no specific treatment intervention was tested.

Community-based observational cohort study examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination and long COVID symptoms in 28,356 UK participants who were infected before vaccination. Vaccination was associated with initial reductions in long COVID symptoms that were sustained over follow-up, but this is an observational study without an intervention being assigned to participants—it passively follows vaccination patterns.

The COFLOW study prospectively followed 492 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for up to 12 months to assess persistence of long COVID sequelae. Physical and respiratory symptoms declined over time, but fatigue and cognitive symptoms persisted, with female gender being the strongest predictor of ongoing symptoms.

PHOSP-COVID is a prospective longitudinal cohort study following 2,320 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to assess recovery trajectories and inflammatory profiles at 5 months and 1 year post-discharge. The study found minimal recovery between 5 and 12 months, identified four distinct clinical clusters, and detected elevated inflammatory mediators in severe phenotypes, suggesting inflammation and obesity as potential therapeutic targets.

Population-based UK cohort study comparing incidence of diabetes and cardiovascular disease in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls up to one year post-infection. Observational epidemiological study with no intervention—patients passively followed for disease outcomes without receiving any treatment.

Prospective survey of 174 COVID-19 survivors with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases examining DMARD disruption, disease flare, and prolonged symptom duration. Study documents associations between hospitalization and symptom count with prolonged symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Nested cohort study examining symptom persistence 6 weeks after COVID-19 in vaccinated vs. unvaccinated healthcare personnel. Vaccination was associated with lower symptom prevalence and faster return to work, but this is a secondary analysis of a vaccine effectiveness study rather than a treatment trial for long COVID patients.

This study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID among 487 diagnosed COVID-19 patients in India with a median 44-day follow-up. It identified that 29.2% reported long COVID symptoms, with fatigue and cough most common, and found predictors including pre-existing conditions, disease severity, and hospitalization, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This matched cohort study examines whether COVID-19 vaccination prior to infection reduces the risk of developing long COVID symptoms. The analysis finds that double-vaccinated individuals had significantly lower odds (aOR 0.59) of reporting long COVID symptoms ≥12 weeks post-infection compared to unvaccinated controls, but this is an observational study examining vaccination as a preventive factor, not testing an active treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

Longitudinal study examining the impact of COVID-19 on economic vulnerability and work absence using monthly questionnaires from 16,910 UK participants. Findings show COVID-19, particularly in long COVID cases, was associated with increased household income inadequacy and long-term work absence, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This study uses propensity score matching and growth curve modeling to compare psychological symptom trajectories in long COVID vs short COVID participants from the UCL Covid-19 Social Study. While it identifies greater increases in depressive and anxiety symptoms in long COVID patients, it is a secondary analysis of existing longitudinal data rather than a treatment intervention trial.

Population-based retrospective cohort study examining prevalence and determinants of post-acute COVID-19 sequelae 6-12 months after infection in 11,710 German adults. Study documents symptom burden and impact on health recovery and working capacity but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study investigates mechanisms of cardiopulmonary symptoms in long COVID patients using advanced cardiac testing (CPET, CMR, rhythm monitoring) at median 17.6 months post-infection. The study found reduced exercise capacity and chronotropic incompetence associated with elevated inflammatory markers, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal analysis of 1,966 UK adults examining whether pre-infection stress and adversity worries predict long COVID development. Found that each additional worry about adversity in the month before infection increased long COVID odds by 1.25, with stress particularly associated with cognitive difficulties.

Retrospective cohort study examining clinical features and burden of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in children <21 years using EHR data from 9 US children's hospitals. Identifies symptom/condition features associated with PASC and estimates disease burden, finding 3.7% higher incidence proportion in PCR-positive versus PCR-negative children.

Intensive longitudinal study of 82 long COVID patients using smartphone app and wearable accelerometer data over 14 days to characterize symptom variation and correlations with physical activity. Found substantial within-individual symptom variation with weak correlations between activity and symptoms, suggesting altered central symptom processing in long COVID.

A prospective observational study of 128 COVID-19 patients assessed cognitive function and biomarkers at 2, 4, 8, and 12 months post-diagnosis. The study identified cognitive impairment in 16-26% of patients and found that kynurenine pathway metabolites were significantly associated with cognitive decline, suggesting a potential therapeutic target.

Retrospective EHR cohort study of 1.6M COVID-19 patients examining whether non-psychiatric post-COVID manifestations are associated with new-onset psychiatric disease. Found significant associations between multiple organ system PASC features (especially cardiovascular) and anxiety, mood, and psychotic disorders.

Prospective cohort study of 312 long COVID patients assessed at 6-month follow-up for lung and cardiac function, finding strong associations between hypertension and cardiac dysfunction, lung fibrotic changes, and elevated biomarkers. This is an observational study with no intervention or treatment—participants were passively assessed, not given a treatment to evaluate.

The OutSMART cohort study followed mild-moderate COVID-19 patients to assess long COVID outcomes at 6, 12, and 18 months post-infection. Patients endorsing ≥3 symptoms showed significantly poorer quality of life across physical, social, fatigue, pain, and general health domains.

This study profiles metabolomic and gut microbiome characteristics across a spectrum of community-based COVID and non-COVID illness, examining associations with illness duration including post-COVID syndrome. The findings highlight cardiometabolic dysfunction as a potential driver of prolonged illness duration, but the study is purely observational without any intervention or treatment.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study analyzing symptom profiles of post-COVID syndrome across 336,652 subjects using the COVID Symptom Study app. Identified distinct phenotypic clusters (cardiorespiratory, neurological, multi-organ) that vary by SARS-CoV-2 variant and vaccination status, with no intervention tested.

This retrospective cohort study from the RECOVER Program examined healthcare utilization patterns in children with chronic conditions following SARS-CoV-2 infection using EHR data from 8 pediatric health systems. The study found increased utilization across all care settings (inpatient, outpatient, ED) post-infection, particularly for inpatient care, with higher utilization correlating to severe acute COVID-19.

Retrospective analysis of 140 PASC patients at a post-COVID clinic examining symptom prevalence, functional status, and ME/CFS phenotype characteristics. Found 43% of patients met ME/CFS criteria with fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and brain fog being most common symptoms.

Observational retrospective cohort study comparing long-COVID symptoms and duration between vaccinated and unvaccinated hospitalized COVID-19 patients across three waves in India (n=6056). Found no significant overall difference in incidence or duration of long COVID between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups, though some symptom-specific differences were noted.

Retrospective cohort study of 58 long COVID patients with dyspnea and fatigue showing sonographic diaphragm abnormalities (low muscle thickness) in 57% of cases. Subset of 33 patients completed outpatient cardiopulmonary physical therapy with respiratory muscle training, and 75.8% (25/33) showed documented improvement.

Population-based serological study examining the prevalence and risk factors of post-COVID syndrome in children and adolescents aged 6 months to 17 years from Geneva, Switzerland. Found 9.1% prevalence of persistent symptoms among seropositive children, with higher rates in adolescents, and identified older age, chronic conditions, and lower socioeconomic status as risk factors.

Prospective longitudinal study comparing long COVID prevalence and risk factors in 814 participants (412 COVID-19 positive, 402 negative) with mild disease over one month follow-up. Found 29.6% prevalence of persistent symptoms in COVID-positive group vs 6% in controls, with female sex, older age, and polysymptomatic acute disease as risk factors.

This observational study examines the association between pre-existing chronic viral infections (EBV, CMV, HIV) and long COVID symptom development in a post-acute COVID-19 cohort of 280 adults. The authors found that serological evidence of EBV reactivation and HIV infection were independently associated with specific long COVID symptoms (fatigue and neurocognitive dysfunction), but this is a secondary analysis of viral serology in an existing cohort rather than an intervention trial.

This study examines polygenic risk scores (PRS) for asthma, allergic disease, and COVID-19 hospitalization in 983 World Trade Center responders with COVID-19 infection, assessing associations with severe COVID-19 and post-acute COVID-19 symptoms at 4-week follow-up.
