A prospective cohort study of 108 Japanese children hospitalized for COVID-19 and their parents, followed for 6 months to assess long-COVID prevalence, symptoms, and risk factors. Sleep disturbance was the most significant symptom affecting quality of life, with 22.8% of children still experiencing long-COVID symptoms at 6 months.

Prospective follow-up study of 138 children with post-COVID respiratory complaints, monitoring pulmonary function over 12 months. Found that 62% had persistent respiratory symptoms but pulmonary function abnormalities were rare and generally improved; no treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective cohort study assessing the prevalence and characteristics of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 208 solid organ transplant recipients (SOTRs), finding that 35% developed PASC with common respiratory symptoms, headache, and cognitive difficulties. Pre-transplant COVID-19 vaccination was protective, and severe acute COVID-19 and respiratory symptoms were associated with higher odds of developing PASC.

topics: lung function|fatigue|quality of life|home monitoring|recovery trajectory
summary: Prospective multicentre study tracking 133 COVID-19 hospitalized patients' recovery over 6 months using home spirometry, pulse oximetry, and quality-of-life assessments. Lung function improved significantly (19.1% increase in FVC), health status improved, but fatigue persisted; home monitoring was well-tolerated.

A prospective follow-up study of 633 athletes examined cardiovascular involvement and persistent symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. While myocardial injury was rare, 31% of athletes experienced long COVID symptoms, with female athletes and those with higher acute severity at increased risk.

Large cohort study of 650,156 Danish blood donors examining associations between 15 blood group antigens and COVID-19 susceptibility, severity, and long COVID outcomes. Found Lewis Lea antigen associated with reduced SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility, but this is an observational cross-sectional study without any treatment intervention or control comparison groups.

This is a prospective observational follow-up study of 30 severe COVID-19 ICU survivors assessed at 6 and 12 months post-discharge using neuropsychological testing. The paper documents cognitive sequelae and their correlates but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study examines post-infection pulmonary outcomes in 44 lung transplant patients who survived COVID-19, following them for a median of 4.5 months. The study documents persistent parenchymal opacities, significant lung function decline (40.9% of patients), and functional deficits, identifying low lymphocyte counts and elevated ferritin as predictive markers.

Retrospective cohort study examining bronchiectasis exacerbation frequency in 234 patients before and after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 infection. While the paper documents increased exacerbations following COVID-19 recovery, it is an observational study of a pre-existing condition rather than a long COVID intervention trial, as it does not evaluate any treatment or therapy.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) in 116 Taiwanese children at 1 and 3 months post-infection, assessing symptoms and behavioral manifestations using standardized questionnaires. While 44.8% of children met PCC criteria with persistent symptoms like fatigue and concentration difficulties, the study did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—only characterized symptom burden and behavioral outcomes in untreated children.

This study investigates HLA-G gene polymorphisms as host genetic factors associated with acute COVID-19 severity and long COVID susceptibility in a German cohort. It identifies specific HLA-G 3'UTR haplotypes and SNP variants as prognostic risk factors for fatal COVID-19 and long COVID symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating cardiac functions in neonates hospitalized with acute symptomatic COVID-19 infection at ~14 months follow-up. This study focuses on acute COVID-19 in neonates and cardiac sequelae of the acute infection, not long COVID in adults or post-acute sequelae in the long COVID population.

This is a prospective follow-up study of 142 kidney transplant recipients who recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection, tracking persistent symptoms and quality of life over 9 months. The study documents significant improvement in fatigue and quality of life measures over time, but does not evaluate any active treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study measuring pulmonary diffusing capacity metrics (DL,CO and DL,NO) in 148 COVID-19 patients at 5.7 and 12.5 months follow-up. Found severity-dependent decline in diffusing capacity at 5.7 months that partially improved by 12.5 months, with concurrent improvements in physical performance but no direct relationship between lung metrics and functional outcomes.

This observational longitudinal study assessed lung function recovery in 82 Mexican Hispanics with severe COVID-19 at a specialized clinic, measuring pulmonary function and CT imaging at median 94 and 362 days post-diagnosis. The study found that while 68% of patients showed lung function improvement and abnormalities decreased from 61% to 22% by 1 year, it was a passive follow-up study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This study investigates microRNA-34a in extracellular vesicles as a biomarker for predicting new-onset diabetes in COVID-19 patients with long COVID sequelae. It is a retrospective biomarker analysis without any treatment intervention or control group comparison.

Retrospective comparison of patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) admitted to a Chinese hospital, stratifying by prior COVID-19 history (171 with, 121 without). The study found that IIM patients with prior COVID-19 exhibited significantly greater cardiac damage, including higher rates of myocarditis, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and structural cardiac changes on echocardiography.

This study evaluated changes in respiratory, physical, and mental conditions in 16 moderate-to-severe COVID-19 patients admitted to a convalescent rehabilitation ward between March and September 2021. Patients showed improvement in dyspnea and walking distance, but persistent anxiety, depression, and other long-COVID conditions remained at discharge.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 341 Danish individuals self-reporting long COVID symptoms and tested for SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid antibodies to assess serostatus. The study found no significant difference in symptom burden between seropositive and seronegative individuals, suggesting overlap between long COVID symptoms and other conditions.

A prospective observational study tracking gut mycobiota changes in 46 COVID-19 patients over 2 years post-discharge, comparing to 37 healthy controls. The study identifies correlations between mycobiota composition and pulmonary function but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study investigating hyaluronan (HA) levels in COVID-19 patients across acute and convalescent phases, finding elevated systemic HA associated with reduced lung diffusion capacity and long-term respiratory impairment. Uses in vitro 3D-lung models to demonstrate SARS-CoV-2-induced dysregulation of HA metabolism, suggesting HA as both a biomarker and potential therapeutic target for COVID-19 long-term sequelae.

Prospective observational study of 174 SARD patients with COVID-19, examining DMARD disruption and SARD activity in relation to prolonged COVID-19 symptoms (≥28 days). Finds that 51% experienced DMARD disruption, 41% reported SARD flare, and those with prolonged symptoms had higher disease activity, pain, and fatigue compared to those without prolonged symptoms.

This study compares clinical and demographic characteristics of rheumatoid arthritis patients with and without post-COVID syndrome (PCS) following COVID-19 infection. It is a descriptive cross-sectional comparison with no intervention or treatment administered, making it a passive observational study rather than a treatment trial.

Observational descriptive study documenting rheumatic and musculoskeletal disease patterns in 23 patients diagnosed with new-onset RMD within 12 weeks post-COVID-19. Found reactive arthritis (69.7%), lupus-like syndromes (13.0%), and avascular necrosis (8.7%) as common post-COVID complications, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

This is a cross-sectional observational study characterizing post-COVID manifestations in 154 patients with rheumatic diseases (RA, AS, PsA) in Tatarstan, assessed at 3 and 6 months post-infection. The study documents symptom prevalence (90.3% experienced persistent symptoms) and mental health outcomes but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective cohort study followed 87 COVID-19 patients for two years post-discharge, collecting fecal samples at acute phase, 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years to assess gut microbiota recovery using 16S rRNA sequencing. The study identified two distinct enterotypes and found that Streptococcus-dominated enterotypes were associated with acute severity and slower cardiopulmonary recovery, while microbiota generally recovered to normal levels within 6 months.

This observational study examines how COVID-19 infection affects disease activity in 55 patients with spondyloarthritis (ankylosing spondylitis and psoriatic arthritis) and documents post-COVID symptoms during 6-month follow-up. The study finds increased arthritis disease activity and persistence of post-COVID manifestations (pain, fatigue, dyspnea) but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

Retrospective cohort analysis of 1,915 rheumatic disease patients from Argentina examining the prevalence and risk factors for long COVID, defined as persistent symptoms >4 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2. Found 12% prevalence (230 patients) with fatigue as the most common symptom; non-caucasian ethnicity, education level, cyclophosphamide use, severe acute illness, and ICU hospitalization were independent risk factors.

Observational study of 105 RA patients who experienced COVID-19, followed for 3 months post-infection to assess changes in RA activity and persistence of post-COVID symptoms. No intervention was administered; this is a secondary analysis of RA disease course in COVID-infected patients, not a treatment trial.

This retrospective cohort study examines how COVID-19 infection affects gout disease course and medication use in 84 male patients with gout, comparing pre-pandemic, during-infection, and 6-month post-infection periods. While it documents increased gout flares and reduced quality of life following SARS-CoV-2 infection, the focus is on gout exacerbation as a post-COVID complication in a pre-existing disease population, not on long COVID syndrome itself or any long COVID treatment intervention.

Observational study of 140 post-COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months to identify inflammatory arthritis manifestations, finding 15% (21/140) developed various forms including reactive arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and gout. Study characterizes frequency and demographics of post-COVID inflammatory arthritis but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining the persistence of post-COVID symptoms in 95 patients with inflammatory arthritis (RA, PsA, AS) over a median follow-up period. Found that 79% reported persistent symptoms after COVID-19 recovery, with cough, fatigue, headache, and arthralgias being most common; however, this is a purely observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

This is a prospective observational cohort study comparing physical and mental health outcomes 6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 11-17 year olds, stratified by vaccination status. It does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it only describes symptom prevalence and compares vaccinated vs unvaccinated groups passively, making it observational without treatment assignment.

Retrospective cohort study comparing mental health outcomes in 153,848 COVID-19 survivors versus contemporary and historical control groups. Finds significantly increased risks of anxiety, depression, sleep disorders, neurocognitive decline, and substance use disorders in COVID-19 survivors, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Observational cohort study of 28,356 UK participants examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination and long COVID symptom trajectories. First vaccine dose associated with 12.8% decrease in long COVID odds, second dose with 8.8% decrease and sustained weekly improvement of 0.8%, suggesting vaccination may reduce long COVID burden.

This prospective cohort study compared long-COVID incidence between 1,974 inflammatory rheumatic disease (iRD) patients and 733 healthy controls following Omicron infection. While 21% of iRD patients vs. 13% of controls met WHO long-COVID criteria, the difference was not statistically significant after adjusting for BMI and acute infection severity, concluding iRD patients are not more susceptible to long-COVID than the general population.

Prospective cohort study of 280 SARD patients examining the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on postacute sequelae (PASC) risk. Vaccinated patients had significantly more symptom-free days and lower odds of PASC at 28 and 90 days compared to unvaccinated/partially vaccinated patients.

Population-based longitudinal cohort study following 1106 SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals for up to 24 months to characterize recovery patterns and symptom trajectories of post-COVID condition. Study found 18-23% of participants had persistent symptoms at various timepoints, with higher symptom prevalence in infected vs uninfected individuals, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study of 271 patients with rheumatic diseases followed for 3-6 months post-COVID to assess incidence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome manifestations. Found 90.4% experienced persistent or new symptoms, primarily joint pain (91.1%) and fatigue/asthenia (52.9%), with disease activity at time of infection influencing severity.

This retrospective cohort study examined whether molnupiravir treatment within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces the risk of post-acute sequelae (PASC/long COVID) in 229,286 US Veterans Affairs participants. Molnupiravir was associated with a 14% relative risk reduction in PASC and reduced risk of 8 of 13 post-acute sequelae including fatigue, neurocognitive impairment, and thromboembolic complications.

Nationwide retrospective cohort study examining clinical sequelae of long COVID at one year post-infection in 1.9M Israeli patients with mild disease. Identifies increased risks for anosmia, cognitive impairment, dyspnoea, and weakness, with most outcomes resolving within a year—but this is an observational follow-up study without treatment assignment, making it unsuitable for the intervention trials pipeline.

Retrospective cohort study using claims data to characterize the risk of persistent and new clinical sequelae in adults aged ≥65 years during the post-acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing them to matched controls. Found that 32% of COVID-19 patients sought medical attention for sequelae in the post-acute period, with respiratory failure, fatigue, and memory difficulties showing the greatest excess risk.

Retrospective cohort study of 47,780 COVID-19 hospital survivors matched to general population controls, examining rates of organ-specific dysfunction and hospital readmission over 140 days. Found that discharged COVID-19 patients had 4-8 times higher rates of readmission and mortality, with increased risk of respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, kidney, and liver diseases compared to matched controls.

Population-based cohort study in Sweden examining COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness in preventing post-COVID-19 condition. This is a secondary analysis of existing cohort data rather than a treatment trial.

This observational study analyzed data from the Covid Symptom Study to characterize symptom duration in 1,734 children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Most children recovered within a week, but 4.4% experienced symptoms for at least 28 days, representing early evidence of prolonged COVID-19 in the pediatric population.

This register-based cohort study examines healthcare service use in 700,000 Norwegian children and adolescents for six months after COVID-19 infection. The study found increased primary care use in the first 1-3 months post-infection (mostly for respiratory conditions) but no increased specialist care use, concluding COVID-19 has limited long-term impact on healthcare services in children.

A retrospective cohort study using electronic health records from the National COVID Cohort Collaborative examining the association between glycemic control (HbA1c levels) and Long COVID development in patients with type 2 diabetes. The study found that poor glycemic control (HbA1c≥8%) was associated with higher risk of Long COVID symptoms 30-180 days post-infection, but this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This retrospective matched cohort study of 157,936 COVID-19 patients examined the association between acute and post-acute COVID-19 infection and new-onset diabetes mellitus, stratified by disease severity and time phases. The study found that hospitalized COVID-19 patients, particularly those with severe disease, had significantly elevated risk of new diabetes during the acute phase (HR 2.47) that attenuated but remained significant through 4-month follow-up, while non-hospitalized patients showed no increased risk.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed healthcare costs for COVID-19 recoverees versus matched controls in Israel from 2019-2022, finding that long COVID patients incurred 7.6% excess monthly costs that gradually diminished to baseline levels after 16 months. The study documents the economic burden of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Registry-based observational study following 8,042 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for up to 1 year post-discharge to characterize post-COVID sequelae frequencies. Found dyspnea, fatigue, and mental health issues in 18.6%, 10.5%, and 9.3% respectively at 30-60 days, declining to 11.9%, 6.6%, and 9% at 1-year follow-up; vaccination was protective against post-discharge mortality.

Secondary analysis of the ACT trials examining long COVID prevalence and risk factors across 14 countries in low-middle, high-middle, and high-income nations. Finds 25.1% prevalence with higher rates in lower-income countries and Arab/North African populations, with male sex, older age, and hospitalization as independent predictors.

The M-COVID study is a prospective observational cohort comparing cardiopulmonary, functional, cognitive, and mental health outcomes across four groups: hospitalized COVID-19 patients, community-based symptomatic patients, recovered community patients, and matched controls. Hospitalized and community-symptomatic groups showed significantly worse exercise capacity, mental health, and quality of life compared to controls, while those who recovered from mild-moderate COVID-19 showed no significant differences from controls.

This target trial emulation study evaluated the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on symptom severity in 910 long COVID patients (455 vaccinated, 455 unvaccinated controls matched by propensity score) from the ComPaRe e-cohort. Vaccination reduced the number of long COVID symptoms and doubled the rate of complete remission at 120 days, while also reducing symptom impact on quality of life.

This prospective observational study of 11,860 COVID-19 survivors across 17 countries characterizes long COVID symptomatology and prevalence across high-income and low/middle-income countries. The study documents higher prevalence of long COVID in HICs (69%) versus LMICs (45%), with key symptoms including fatigue, persistent dyspnea, and functional impairment, but does not test any interventions or treatments.

Prospective multicentre observational study following 2,187 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in France to identify risk factors and subphenotypes associated with persistent symptoms at six months post-discharge. Found that 50.7% had at least one persistent symptom, with worse functional outcomes in patients with more severe acute illness, but this is a natural history/prognostic study without any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study examining nutritional sequelae and functional loss in 288 COVID-19 survivors at 30 days post-discharge. No intervention was tested; this is a passive observational follow-up of hospitalized patients.

Retrospective observational study examining positive signs of functional limb weakness in 502 long COVID patients, assessing their diagnostic utility and prevalence (33.9%). While the study followed patients over 2 months and reports symptomatic improvements, it is observational without any intervention—patients were passively assessed rather than receiving a treatment.

Prospective observational cohort study assessing organ impairment in 201 low-risk individuals with persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms at a median of 141 days post-infection. Found that 70% had impairment in one or more organs (cardiac, pulmonary, hepatic, pancreatic, renal, splenic), with 29% showing multiorgan involvement and severe symptoms associated with radiological evidence of myocarditis.

Retrospective cohort study of 1,190 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to characterize long-term clinical outcomes and healthcare usage. Found persistent cardiopulmonary symptoms (dyspnea, 22.1% at 3 months), generalized symptoms (26.4%), and neuropsychiatric symptoms (24.2%) at 6 months, with increased morbidity in patients with severe acute COVID-19.

This is a retrospective cohort study comparing prescription rates in German outpatients with COVID-19 versus other acute respiratory infections over one year post-infection. The study does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for long COVID patients; it only observes patterns of medication prescriptions in the general population, making it ineligible as a treatment trial despite being long COVID-related.

A single-centre cohort study of 150 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients examined the long-term prevalence of olfactory and/or gustatory dysfunction and its impact on quality of life at 1 year post-infection. The study found 12.8% persistent olfactory/gustatory dysfunction with significantly impaired quality of life, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Observational cohort study examining brain MRI findings and neurocognitive function in 35 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 4-month follow-up. Majority had abnormal MRI (71%) or neurocognitive impairment (46%), with multiple white matter lesions being the most common finding, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Prospective inception cohort study of 14,392 COVID-19 survivors in Bangladesh examining the prevalence and risk factors of long COVID symptoms at 12-31 weeks post-diagnosis. Found 16.1% prevalence of long COVID with fatigue, pain, and dyspnea as the most common symptoms, with younger age, female gender, and rural residence identified as risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study examining risk factors for adverse long-term outcomes (respiratory, cardiovascular, mental health) in COVID-19 patients using EHR data from 57,748 US patients. Finds that severe COVID-19 (ICU/ventilation) patients had increased risk of new clinical conditions up to 6 months post-discharge, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 749 COVID-19 survivors followed 6 months post-discharge, developing a machine learning model to predict lung lesions using clinical parameters (dyspnea scale, oximetry, spirometry, chest X-ray). The model achieved 85% sensitivity and 70% specificity for detecting pulmonary abnormalities, with 63% of patients showing signs of pulmonary involvement.

Prospective cohort study developing machine learning models to predict fatigue in COVID-19 patients using vocal biomarkers from 296 participants with 1772 voice recordings. The study demonstrates feasibility of remote fatigue monitoring via voice analysis but does not test any therapeutic intervention.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and monoclonal antibodies in preventing post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in 53,239 patients across a US hospital system. Vaccination significantly reduced the likelihood of developing PASC (aOR 0.58) compared to both unvaccinated controls and monoclonal antibody treatment (aOR 0.77).

Prospective cohort study following 67 COVID-19 ICU survivors for 1 year to assess recovery of participation in society and identify early determinants of recovery. While the study examines long-term post-COVID sequelae in ICU survivors, it is observational without an intervention component—patients received standard rehabilitation care rather than a tested treatment, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

Prospective observational study of 801 COVID-19 survivors assessed 3-11 months after hospital discharge to evaluate their long-term functional status. Found prevalent conditions including muscle weakness, pain, anxiety, depression, breathlessness, and reduced mobility, with no clear trends of improvement over the follow-up period.

Longitudinal observational study examining economic impacts of COVID-19 using monthly questionnaire data from 16,910 UK residents. Finds that incident COVID-19 and long COVID are associated with economic vulnerability (inadequate household income, sickness absence) in the short and long term, but this is an epidemiological/economic analysis, not a treatment intervention study.

A prospective, multicentre cohort study in French primary care examining initial symptoms and 3-month persistent symptoms in 521 patients with suspected COVID-19, comparing confirmed cases, no-COVID cases, and uncertain cases. While the study identifies persistent symptoms in ~one-third of confirmed cases at 3 months, it is purely observational with no treatment intervention—patients were simply followed up to assess symptom persistence without any therapeutic intervention being tested or evaluated.

Retrospective cohort study analyzing routinely collected claims data from Bavaria, Germany to estimate the incidence of post-COVID syndrome and associated symptoms in ambulatory care. Found 14.2% of COVID-19 patients received a post-COVID diagnosis, with higher rates of fatigue, dyspnea, and smell/taste disturbances compared to controls, but the study does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 3,809 patients who received monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) during acute COVID-19 compared to 3,809 matched controls, evaluating whether early MAb treatment prevents long COVID (postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection). MAb treatment reduced acute complications (hospitalization 28%, ICU admission 41% at 30 days) but did not reduce postacute clinical sequelae or long COVID risk.

A longitudinal cohort study of 3,039 Belgian adults with recent SARS-CoV-2 infection followed for 3 months post-infection to characterize the distribution and classification of post-COVID-19 condition symptoms. Using latent class analysis, the study identified three distinct symptom classes (anosmia/ageusia, neurological symptoms, and other symptoms) with different risk factors, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study comparing health-related quality of life and respiratory outcomes 6 months after ICU discharge in critically ill COVID-19 survivors across different pandemic waves. The study found minimal differences in long-term HRQL between first and second/third wave survivors, with second/third wave patients showing slightly better role function and physical outcomes.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 575 and 793 long COVID patients followed from May 2020 to October 2022 that identified three macro symptom clusters (neurological, sensorial, physical) and associated predictive factors. The study found associations between long COVID symptoms and comorbidities, acute-phase medications (ACE inhibitors, inhaled steroids), and demographic factors, but did not test a specific intervention.

This retrospective cohort study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 1,207 patients hospitalized with COVID-19-related SARI at 1 year post-discharge using SF-36 questionnaires, examining associations with age, frailty, and disease severity. The study found significant correlations between baseline disease factors and physical functioning outcomes at 1-year follow-up.

Retrospective cohort study using real-world data (TriNetX) examining the association between Long COVID diagnosis and increased risk of mental health disorders in US patients. Found Long COVID patients had 2.6-fold increased risk of mental health disorders, with particularly strong associations for major depression (3.36×) and generalized anxiety disorder (3.44×).

Longitudinal cohort study (n=19,545) examining the association between COVID-19 severity and somatic symptoms in the Japanese general population over 1-year follow-up using the SSS-8 scale. Found that COVID-19 cases requiring O2 therapy were significantly associated with very high somatic symptom burden (OR 7.60), identifying severity of acute infection and pre-existing conditions as risk factors for long COVID symptoms.

A 9-month prospective cohort study of 287 individuals in Scotland tracking COVID-19 recovery and long COVID symptom persistence using a mobile app. Only 3.1% met long COVID criteria at 9 months; fatigue was the most persistent symptom, and older age and female gender were associated with higher symptom burden.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed sick note rates in 24 million primary care patients with COVID-19 in 2020-2022 using NHS data. The study found elevated sick note rates in COVID-positive patients compared to matched controls, with highest risk in the first 30 days, providing evidence of long-term COVID-19 impact but did not test any intervention or treatment.

An 18-month prospective follow-up survey of 5,464 Swedish COVID-19 patients examining how changes in physical activity relate to daily life functioning. Found that physical activity levels decreased post-infection and decreased PA was strongly associated with difficulties in daily activities, but this is a passive observational study without any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study tracking 1,478 COVID RADAR app users from 40 days before to 100 days after positive SARS-CoV-2 test to describe incidence and symptom clusters of post-acute COVID. Found 8% with persistent symptoms at 100 days, identifying three symptom clusters (non-respiratory, olfactory, respiratory) and associations with vaccination and acute disease severity.

Population-based cohort study using administrative health data from Manitoba to identify post-COVID condition cases and their prevalence (23% of 66,365 COVID-positive individuals). Reports predictive factors for PCC including female sex, older age, hospitalization, and comorbidities, while vaccination was protective.

A population-based longitudinal cohort study of 4,087 long COVID patients enrolled in UK rehabilitation clinics, tracking functional limitations, fatigue, quality of life, and societal costs over 6 months. Participants showed small improvements in functional limitations and fatigue, with mean WSAS score declining by 0.86 points, though significant societal costs (£931/month) were driven primarily by productivity losses.

Prospective cohort study of 210 acute COVID-19 patients followed 3-6 months post-infection to characterize post-COVID-19 condition phenotypes using cluster analysis. Identified four distinct clinical clusters (paucisymptomatic, physical sequelae, pulmonary comorbidities, functional somatic/mental symptoms) with differing demographics, comorbidities, and disease severity associations.

A prospective observational study following 166 COVID-19 hospitalized patients to identify early predictors of long COVID persistence at 12 months. Develops machine learning models to predict symptom persistence using baseline clinical, imaging, and laboratory data.

Retrospective cohort study examining determinants of post-COVID-19 clinic attendance among SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals in Stockholm, Sweden from 2020-2023. Found that mental health disorders and asthma were strongest predictors of clinic attendance in non-hospitalized patients, while prior sick leave was strongest predictor in hospitalized patients.

Prospective cohort study of 1,276 children in a Rio de Janeiro favela tracking symptom duration following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Median recovery was 11 days, with 9.5% experiencing symptoms beyond 33 days, but the study focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery in children, not persistent long COVID symptoms or interventions.

The CORFU study is a prospective longitudinal cohort study tracking post-COVID symptoms and health-related quality of life in 901 former COVID-19 patients across four severity groups (non-hospitalized, ward, ICU, and controls) over 24 months. While about long COVID, this is excluded because it is purely observational without any treatment intervention—patients are followed passively to assess symptom prevalence and QOL changes, not to evaluate the effectiveness of any therapeutic intervention.

This cross-sectional and longitudinal observational study from the PERCEIVE cohort examines depression as a moderator and mediator of functional status in 1,794 long COVID patients. The study demonstrates that depression mediates 36-51% of the association between post-COVID symptom severity and reduced functional capacity, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This nationwide retrospective cohort study examines how recurrent COVID-19 infections affect clinical outcomes in 313,760 COPD patients, finding progressive increases in exacerbation risk and mortality with repeated infections. Long COVID was more common after initial infection but diminished with subsequent reinfections, highlighting the importance of preventing initial COVID-19 exposure in COPD populations.

Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of new-onset conjunctivitis 3.5 years post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in 67,702 COVID-positive patients compared to 1,391,135 COVID-negative controls. Found COVID-positive patients had significantly higher risk of developing new incident conjunctivitis (adjusted HR 1.10-1.11) compared to controls.

A prospective cohort study following 3,590 long COVID patients from a specialist post-COVID service over 4 years to characterize recovery trajectory, symptom burden, and healthcare utilization. Only one-third of patients achieved satisfactory recovery (>75% of baseline health), with fatigue severity and vaccination status as key predictors of outcome.

Prospective observational cohort study comparing ongoing symptoms and functional impairment at 12 weeks post-infection between COVID-19 and influenza patients in a vaccinated Australian population. Found no significant difference in symptom prevalence or moderate-to-severe functional impairment between the two groups, suggesting long COVID manifests as a postviral syndrome of similar severity to seasonal influenza.

Serial cross-sectional study comparing well-being measures in 217 Australian participants with long COVID (symptoms >1 month) versus short COVID (symptoms ≤1 month) from a longitudinal cohort. Found lower well-being in the long COVID group before, during, and after infection, with persistent functional impairment.

This Swedish national observational cohort study analyzed clinical features and demographic characteristics associated with post-COVID syndrome diagnosis in 6,389 patients identified through multiregistry data from 2020-2021. The study compares PCS patients with matched COVID-negative and severity-matched COVID-positive controls but does not test any treatment or intervention.

Prospective cohort study examining how social factors (education, deprivation, employment) affect recovery from ongoing COVID-19 symptoms in two UK community cohorts. Found that individuals with greater pre-pandemic social disadvantage had lower likelihood of recovery from long COVID.

Ambispective study of 712 Tanzanian patients hospitalized with COVID-19, followed up 2 years later to assess residual cardiopulmonary complications. Found 44.5% had cardiopulmonary sequelae, with BMI ≥25, smoking, and non-steroid use as independent predictors.

Prospective observational cohort study of 93 severe COVID-19 survivors followed 3-7 months post-discharge to assess long-term psychosocial and physical consequences. Found high rates of anxiety (46.2%) and depression (34.4%), with employment return dependent on socio-economic status, but no significant differences vs matched non-COVID controls.

This retrospective cohort study compares post-acute outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 re-infection patients versus first-time infection patients in Hong Kong using propensity-score-weighted analysis. It found that re-infection was associated with significantly higher risk of mortality, hospital readmission, and emergency department attendance during the post-acute period.

Retrospective cohort analysis of 1,946 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during the first UK wave, examining clinical characteristics, outcomes, and short-term sequelae. While 70% of survivors reported ongoing symptoms including fatigue and breathlessness, the study is primarily focused on acute hospitalization and early post-discharge outcomes rather than long COVID as a chronic condition, and does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This observational study evaluates the Your COVID Recovery® digital programme, a staged online intervention for long COVID patients, in 110 individuals from primary and secondary care in England. Participants showed statistically significant improvements in quality of life (EQ-5D-5L VAS) and breathing-related symptoms (CAT score) after an average of 8.6 weeks on the programme.

Prospective cohort study comparing breakthrough infection outcomes and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in immune-disordered persons (n=219) versus healthy volunteers (n=63) from April 2021 to July 2023. Study found that immune-disordered individuals experienced higher rates of PASC, persistent infections, and reinfections compared to healthy controls, though breakthrough infection rates were largely equivalent between groups.

Prospective cohort study examining the bidirectional relationship between sleep problems and long COVID using monthly data from 3,994 UK participants. Poor pre-infection sleep quality and high sleep efficiency variability were associated with increased long COVID risk, while post-infection sleep duration changes were modest and largely resolved within months.

Prospective observational cohort study of 159 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors examined at 28-60 days post-discharge using CT imaging to characterize persistent pulmonary abnormalities and their relationship to patient outcomes. Persistent radiological abnormalities were common (56% of patients) and correlated with impaired quality of life, but no intervention was tested.

Multicentre prospective cohort study that performed cluster analysis on 935 long COVID patients to identify five distinct symptom phenotypes and their association with quality of life over 1 year. The study identified diverse patient clusters but is registered as a protocol study and does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study comparing mortality rates in COPD patients who recovered from COVID-19 versus matched controls in South Korea. Finds elevated mortality risk in the post-recovery period, particularly after severe COVID-19, but does not address long COVID or any specific treatment interventions.

A multicentre prospective cohort study of 1066 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Japan assessed long COVID prevalence at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection across three pandemic waves. The study found that patients hospitalized during the first wave had significantly higher rates of long COVID, particularly dyspnoea, compared to later waves, but did not test any specific treatment or intervention.

Multicentre prospective cohort study of 777 COVID-19 hospitalised patients followed for up to 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term multidimensional patient-centred outcomes including quality of life, symptoms, and recovery. Found that disease severity during hospitalisation was not associated with long-term HRQoL but was associated with self-perceived recovery, with age, sex, and pulmonary history identified as stronger independent risk factors.

Prospective observational cohort study of 214 long COVID patients characterizing self-reported symptoms and outcomes using latent class analysis, identifying three distinct subphenotypes: high burden constitutional symptoms, persistent olfactory/gustatory dysfunction, and minimal residual symptoms. Study found no association between viral persistence and symptom burden or subphenotypes.

This UK study evaluates the clinical and cost-effectiveness of diverse post-hospitalization healthcare pathways for COVID-19 patients using prospective data from 1013 patients at 12 months post-discharge. Comprehensive services offering assessment, rehabilitation, and mental health support were more clinically and cost-effective than limited or no services, with strong cost-effectiveness ratios.

This is a retrospective cohort study of COVID-19 healthcare trajectories in patients with chronic respiratory diseases using French national health database data. It does not study long COVID (persistent post-infection symptoms) but rather acute COVID-19 hospitalization outcomes and recovery patterns in a vulnerable population.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 159 post-COVID-19 patients evaluated for myocarditis using serial biomarkers, imaging, and patient-reported outcomes at baseline and 28-60 days post-discharge. The study found adjudicated myocarditis in 54% of patients and documented significant impairments in health-related quality of life, physical activity, and psychological wellbeing associated with cardiac involvement.

This study examines de-novo ECG changes in elite soccer players following acute COVID-19 infection, assessing their diagnostic significance for myopericarditis. The findings show that 3% of athletes demonstrated post-infection ECG changes, with 88% revealing evidence of cardiac inflammation, but this is focused on acute cardiac sequelae during active infection recovery, not long COVID syndrome.

This prospective cohort study of 106 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months investigates whether gut microbiota composition is associated with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). The study found that patients with persistent PACS symptoms showed distinct dysbiotic microbiota profiles characterized by higher Ruminococcus gnavus and Bacteroides vulgatus and lower beneficial Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, with specific bacterial taxa correlated to symptom types (respiratory vs neuropsychiatric).

Prospective multicentre controlled study comparing gastrointestinal symptoms and post-COVID disorders in 883 hospitalised patients (614 COVID-19, 269 controls) at baseline and 1, 6, and 12-month follow-up. Patients with COVID-19 had significantly higher rates of IBS than controls at 12 months, with gastrointestinal symptoms most prevalent early post-infection.

Prospective observational study monitoring gut microbiota composition across three timepoints (acute phase, convalescence, 6-month post-discharge) in COVID-19 patients using 16S rDNA sequencing. Found persistent reduction in microbiota richness at 6 months post-infection, associated with higher CRP levels and worse pulmonary function, suggesting gut dysbiosis may contribute to long COVID pathogenesis.

Retrospective cohort study comparing psychiatric sequelae in COVID-19 hospitalized patients versus influenza and other respiratory infection controls at 1-3 and 4-6 months post-infection. Finds COVID-19 associated with higher odds of psychotic disorder and insomnia acutely, but lower risk of new psychiatric sequelae at 4-6 months.

A retrospective observational cohort study examining whether late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac MRI predicts mortality or cardiovascular events in 169 COVID-19 recovered patients. The study found no significant association between myocardial scarring and adverse outcomes over 2-3 years of follow-up.

Staggered cohort study using electronic health records from UK, Spain, and Estonia examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination and risk of post-COVID-19 cardiac and thromboembolic complications. Found vaccination associated with reduced risks of heart failure, venous thromboembolism, and arterial thromboembolism in both acute and post-acute COVID periods.

This cross-sectional study analyzes protective factors against post-COVID-19 conditions in adults aged 50+ across Europe using data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) collected in June-August 2021. It identifies male sex, COVID-19 vaccination, higher education, healthy BMI, and absence of comorbidities as protective factors, and highlights significant health inequalities between Western Europe and Visegrad countries.

Population-based longitudinal survey study examining associations between long COVID and financial disruption across four UK cohorts. Found that post-COVID syndrome was associated with worse financial well-being and increased benefit claims, but this is an observational epidemiological study without any treatment intervention.

This prospective cohort study follows elite athletes infected with SARS-CoV-2 to assess long-term cardiac consequences of infection combined with high-level sports participation. The study found no significant cardiac abnormalities or adverse events during 26.7 months of follow-up, demonstrating the safety of resuming elite-level sports after COVID-19 infection.

This longitudinal study analyzes pre-infection stress and adversity as risk factors for developing long COVID in 1,962 UK adults from the UCL COVID-19 Social Study. It finds that pre-infection adversity worries and experiences are associated with increased odds of long COVID and specific symptoms like self-care difficulties, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational case-control study comparing cardiac structure and function between 84 COVID-19 survivors (mean 60 years old, assessed 28+ days post-infection) and 40 non-COVID controls using echocardiography with speckle tracking. COVID survivors showed significantly increased left ventricular mass index, left atrial diameter, relative wall thickness, and reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain compared to controls, suggesting subclinical cardiac remodeling in long COVID.

Observational study of 65 individuals recovering from mild COVID-19 that examined T cell alterations in long COVID patients and response to histamine receptor antagonists (HRAs). Found persistent T cell perturbations in long COVID patients, with 72% of those receiving HRA reporting clinical improvement.

Prospective community cohort study examining how deprivation, migration status, and ethnic minority status influence post-COVID condition (PCC) risk in England using the Virus Watch study. Findings show higher PCC probability among deprived and migrant populations driven by increased infection risk rather than differential post-infection susceptibility.

Retrospective review of 62 long COVID patients who underwent autonomic testing at a tertiary referral centre between May 2020 and October 2021. Study characterized autonomic dysfunction presentations (PoTS in 12 patients, syncope in 11) but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal study of 5,248 NHS healthcare workers examining the prevalence and risk factors for post COVID-19 syndrome over 32 months. Found that 33.6% reported prolonged symptoms consistent with PCS, with fatigue, concentration difficulty, insomnia, and mental health symptoms being most common; identified risk factors including female sex, older age, direct COVID-19 patient contact, and pre-existing respiratory illness.

This observational study assessed the prevalence of somatic symptom disorder (SSD) and psychiatric comorbidities in 50 patients with unexplained neurological symptoms following mild COVID-19. The study found that 64% of patients met DSM-5 criteria for SSD and 90% met criteria for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 113 UK Armed Forces personnel exposed to COVID-19 at 5, 12, and 18 months post-infection, comparing fatigue, cognitive, and mood outcomes against matched controls. Found significant improvements in depression, PTSD, and fatigue symptoms by 18 months, with persistent exercise intolerance through 12 months.

This cross-sectional analysis of the COVID-19 Infection Survey examines occupational differences in long-COVID prevalence and severity among working-age participants (2021-2022). The study finds that public-facing industries (teaching, social care, healthcare) and caring/leisure occupations have higher long-COVID rates, but it is an observational survey without any treatment or intervention being tested.

This study examines multisystem illness trajectories in 168 hospitalized post-COVID patients, comparing healthcare workers (n=36) to non-healthcare workers over 450-day follow-up. It is a secondary analysis of trial NCT04403607 without any treatment intervention, observing outcomes in already-hospitalized patients rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.

Population-based prospective cohort study (COVICAT, 2020-2023, Catalonia) examining occupational determinants of Long COVID among 2,054 workers, finding that jobs with high COVID-19 exposure risk (healthcare, education, retail, transport) increased LC risk by up to 1.58-fold due to close contact and inadequate protective measures. This is an observational epidemiological study that does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention, so it does not meet criteria for the clinical trials pipeline.

Prospective cohort study examining cardiac abnormalities in 534 long COVID patients using cardiac MRI at baseline (6 months post-infection) and 12-month follow-up. Found that 19% had CMR abnormalities at baseline, with 58% showing persistent abnormalities at 12 months; however, this is a diagnostic/natural history study with no treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study examining recovery trajectories in 2,545 hospitalized COVID-19 patients stratified by pre-existing cardiovascular disease (CVD) or cardiovascular risk factors, assessed at 5 and 12 months post-discharge. Found that patients with CVD or cardiovascular risk factors had significantly lower rates of full recovery at 12 months, but the study does not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective study evaluating a digital care programme (DCP) combining personalised diet and integrative interventions in 202 adults with various autoimmune diseases and long COVID (14.9% of cohort). Programme participants showed statistically significant improvements across all 10 PROMIS health-related quality of life domains, with greater improvements in those with higher baseline symptom severity.

A multicentre retrospective study comparing nailfold videocapillaroscopy (NVC) findings in long COVID patients with and without systemic sclerosis, recovered COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls. Long COVID patients showed significantly more microvascular abnormalities including dilated capillaries, microhaemorrhages, and reduced capillary density, suggesting microvascular dysfunction contributes to persistent long COVID symptoms.

Survey study of 441 people with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases investigating prolonged COVID-19 symptom duration (≥28 days) from the COVID-19 Global Rheumatology Alliance Vaccine Survey. Found 24.2% experienced prolonged symptoms, with hospitalization, comorbidities, and osteoarthritis as significant risk factors.

Retrospective analysis of 1,946 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during the first UK wave, examining clinical characteristics, mortality, and short-term outcomes. While the paper documents persistent symptoms and sequalae in 67% of survivors at follow-up, it is a passive observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed respiratory symptoms in 131 patients following COVID-19 hospitalization using the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) at a mean of 32 days post-discharge. Over half of patients had CAT scores ≥10 indicating symptom burden, with breathlessness, activity limitations, and energy loss being the most commonly reported symptoms.

This study compares symptom burden and radiological severity at 8-10 weeks post-discharge between COVID-19 patients discharged from the emergency department versus admitted to hospital wards. It is a retrospective comparison of outcomes in two naturally occurring groups without any treatment intervention.

Retrospective follow-up study of 73 severe COVID-19 pneumonia patients (73% male, mean age 57.6) tracked clinically and radiologically at 6-12 weeks post-discharge via telephone review and chest X-ray. At median 9.6 weeks, 57 patients reported persistent symptoms including exertional dyspnea and fatigue, with 71.7% showing clear imaging and the remainder showing partial improvement.

This study followed non-ICU COVID-19 pneumonia patients for 3 months post-discharge to assess radiological changes, finding that 87% had normal chest X-rays by 3 months. The paper documents natural recovery patterns rather than evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Service evaluation of 70 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors assessed at 3-5+ weeks post-discharge via telephone consultations to evaluate short-term recovery outcomes. Most patients showed symptom improvement but 70% retained at least one symptom at 5 weeks, with persistent deficits in walking ability, stair-climbing, and dyspnoea scores.

Observational study of long COVID patients referred to a respiratory clinic describing clinical presentation, demographics, and lung function findings. No intervention or treatment evaluated; appears to be a clinical assessment/characterization study only.

Longitudinal study following COVID-19 patients over the first year post-discharge to assess radiological changes, particularly ground glass abnormalities and fibrotic changes on CT imaging. The paper suggests antifibrotic trials may benefit a small subset of patients with progressive fibrotic changes, but presents only follow-up imaging data without testing any actual intervention.

Longitudinal follow-up study of 21 PACS patients at 7 and 14 months post-infection examining lung function (DLCO), quality of life, and MRI pulmonary gas-exchange abnormalities. While DLCO and quality-of-life scores improved over time, abnormalities did not fully resolve by 14 months, but no intervention was administered to these patients.

Population-based longitudinal study examining economic impacts of COVID-19 in 16,910 UK adults, including those with long COVID (symptoms >4 weeks). Found increased risk of economic vulnerability measured by household income insufficiency and long-term sickness absence, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A 16-week observational cohort study of 66 long COVID patients from UK clinics measuring changes in functional status, respiratory muscle strength, and lung function. While some measures improved (6MWT increased from 322m to 430m), respiratory muscle strength and lung function remained reduced and unchanged, suggesting rehabilitation is needed.

This retrospective cohort study followed 350 hospitalized COVID-19 patients using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire to assess health-related quality of life at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks post-discharge. While the study documents persistent impairment in mobility, breathlessness, and psychological symptoms at 12 weeks compared to pre-COVID baseline, it is a passive observational study with no treatment intervention—patients were simply followed clinically without receiving any assigned therapy.

This observational cross-sectional study compares health status and activities of daily living (ADL) between SARS-CoV-2 positive individuals with and without post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and matched negative controls using the WHO case definition and five alternative PCC definitions. The study found that individuals with PCC have substantially worse health and more ADL impairment than negative controls across all case definitions tested.

This case series of 32 long COVID patients examined cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) abnormalities and the effects of CPET-guided treatment. A targeted treatment programme improved symptoms and physiological parameters in 14 of 20 patients, with improvements in peak oxygen uptake and oxygen pulse suggesting that structured rehabilitation addresses deconditioning or muscle-level oxygen utilization disorders.

Prospective observational cohort study following 110 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors at 8-12 weeks post-admission, finding 74% had persistent symptoms like breathlessness and fatigue with limitations in physical ability. While clinical abnormalities were less frequent (35%), the study concludes rehabilitation and general well-being are paramount but does not evaluate any specific intervention.

A prospective observational study following 12 weeks of post-COVID respiratory outcomes in previously hospitalized patients, documenting pulmonary function abnormalities and CT imaging findings. The study identifies associations between acute-phase oxygen supplementation and long-term respiratory outcomes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
