An observational descriptive study of 42 post-COVID-19 patients who required hospitalization, measuring cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, body composition, and perceived fatigue. Patients showed decreased strength, respiratory capacity, and moderate-to-severe fatigue, with inverse correlations between muscle strength and ICU duration.

Prospective observational study following 219 COVID-19 pneumonia patients with pulmonary function tests (PFTs) at 1 and 6 months post-discharge to assess long-term respiratory effects. Found pulmonary dysfunction in 36% at 1 month declining to 21% at 6 months, with imaging findings predictive of functional recovery.

Retrospective cohort study of 834 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized during the pandemic, examining the prevalence and risk factors for prolonged urinary retention post-discharge. Study found that 12.6% of catheterized patients could not have their catheter removed, with urinary retention associated with severe infection markers and pulmonary involvement.

topics: gender differences|quality of life|epidemiology|long COVID prevalence
summary: A prospective cohort study of 887 COVID-19 survivors in Brazil that tracked long post-COVID syndrome prevalence and quality of life outcomes at 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge. Women reported significantly higher rates of LPCS and greater deterioration in quality of life across all domains (mobility, personal care, activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression) compared to men.

This ambidirectional cohort study followed 190-160 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 6 and 12 months post-discharge to assess post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence and symptoms. The study found that 87.4% reported symptoms at 6 months declining to 67.5% at 12 months, with fatigue, memory problems, and hair loss being most common, and identified older age, lower income, and comorbidities as risk factors.

Prospective cohort study of 289 institutionalized older adults assessing the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on health and functional capacity over 6 months. COVID-19 infection was associated with increased functional dependence, weight loss, and blood pressure changes, but the study does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study of 887 COVID-19 survivors in Brazil examining long post-COVID syndrome (LPCS) prevalence and quality of life outcomes, stratified by gender at 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge. Women showed significantly higher LPCS prevalence and worse quality-of-life outcomes across all domains compared to men.

This ambidirectional cohort study evaluated renal function in 20 COVID-19 patients who experienced acute kidney injury, reassessing them after an average of 16.3 months. The study found a significant median reduction in eGFR and chronic kidney disease development in 45% of patients, with outcomes correlating with age, hospitalization length, and inflammatory markers.

Observational longitudinal study assessing respiratory and functional outcomes in 65 COVID-19 post-hospitalized patients at 15, 90, and 180 days after discharge. Findings show persistent dyspnea, reduced lung function, and low physical activity levels despite some improvement in exercise capacity over time.

Prospective cohort study examining the prevalence and risk factors for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-hospitalization. Found that 42.4% of 255 survivors experienced moderate to severe LUTS, with nocturia and frequency being most common, and identified diabetes, hypertension, and worse self-perceived health as risk factors.

This retrospective cohort study of 1.7M US Veterans examines kidney outcomes in 30-day COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected controls, finding significantly elevated risks of acute kidney injury, eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, and major adverse kidney events in the post-acute phase. The study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment and is therefore excluded from the clinical trials dataset.

Prospective follow-up study of acute kidney injury (AKI) survivors from acute COVID-19 hospitalization, comparing outcomes between COVID-19 positive and negative patients. The study focuses on renal outcomes and mortality post-discharge from acute infection, not on long COVID or any treatment interventions for persistent symptoms.

This prospective-retrospective study assessed functional status in 232 pediatric COVID-19 patients hospitalized during acute infection using the Functional Status Scale at three timepoints. The majority maintained adequate functional status during and after acute hospitalization, with no previous disease being a protective factor for long-term impairment.

A retrospective cohort study of 150 COVID-19 hospitalized patients (51 with pre-existing CKD) examining kidney function during hospitalization and at 6-month follow-up. The study documents persistent decline in glomerular filtration rate in patients who developed acute kidney injury during acute infection, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective follow-up of 123 COVID-19 patients discharged after Delta variant infection in Guangzhou, China, examining recurrent positive nucleic acid tests and symptom outcomes at 2 months. While the study documents some persistent symptoms (hair loss in 59.6% of patients), it focuses primarily on viral recurrence and vaccination status rather than evaluating a treatment intervention for long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study examined long-term kidney function changes in 457 COVID-19 patients followed in a post-COVID recovery clinic, finding a statistically significant decline in eGFR over 12 months post-infection, particularly in hospitalized and diabetic patients. The study documents a complication of long COVID rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed clinical, functional, and mental health outcomes in hemodialysis patients at 3 months post-COVID-19 diagnosis. The paper evaluates persistent symptoms and sequelae following SARS-CoV-2 infection in a vulnerable renal disease population but does not test a specific intervention or treatment.

This retrospective study describes kidney biopsy findings and outcomes in 23 COVID-19 patients with collapsing glomerulopathy, a severe acute kidney complication. While some patients received treatments (glucocorticoids, COVID-19 antivirals), the study focuses on characterizing an acute COVID-19 kidney pathology rather than long COVID sequelae or evaluating treatment efficacy.

Prospective study comparing long COVID symptoms in hospitalized versus non-hospitalized pediatric patients and healthy controls over 12 weeks post-acute infection. Hospitalized children experienced significantly more persistent symptoms including fatigue, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and headache, highlighting the need for targeted rehabilitation strategies.

This retrospective cohort study compares kidney disease outcomes between long-COVID and non-long-COVID adults who used ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers. It is an observational study examining associations between medication use and kidney outcomes, not a treatment trial testing an intervention.

This retrospective cohort study uses TrinetX data to compare kidney disease outcomes in 2.78M COVID-19 positive vs 6.76M negative patients over two years post-infection. It finds COVID-19 is a strong risk factor for incident CKD and glomerular disorders (RR 2.47) but contains no treatment intervention or evaluation.

This retrospective cohort study assessed clinical, instrumental, and laboratory outcomes in 213 COVID-19 patients 3-7 months after hospital discharge. While confirming post-COVID sequelae including cardiac abnormalities and elevated biomarkers, the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it observational rather than a treatment trial.

Retrospective observational study of taste dysfunction in long COVID patients presenting to a specialist smell clinic, describing prevalence and types of gustatory dysfunction. While the paper is about long COVID and uses a retrospective cohort design, it does not study or evaluate a treatment intervention—it only characterizes the natural history and symptom resolution of taste dysfunction over time.

This descriptive observational study compared functional capacity, pulmonary function, pain, depression, sleep, and quality of life between 26 post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients and 26 healthy controls. The study found no statistically significant differences in any measured outcomes between the infected and non-infected groups, suggesting no long-term effects of COVID-19 on this young adult cohort.

This study compares laboratory parameters (CBC, biochemical markers, cytokines) across three groups: symptomatic COVID-19 patients, long COVID patients, and controls without gastrointestinal symptoms. The findings show differential patterns in inflammatory markers and liver/kidney function between acute and long COVID phases, but the study is observational without any treatment intervention.

Open observational study evaluating aceclofenac and vinpocetine effectiveness in treating long COVID symptoms in 97 patients (42 with long COVID), with chronic cerebrovascular disease. Both medications showed significant improvements in functional status and pain within 10-20 days, with 59.5% reporting pronounced improvement after 30 days without significant adverse effects.

This open controlled prospective study assessed clinical and neurophysiological parameters in 16 epilepsy patients 4-6 months post-COVID-19, compared to 7 epilepsy patients without COVID history and 11 COVID-recovered controls. The study found increased epileptiform EEG activity, new seizures, and elevated sympathetic nervous system activity in post-COVID epilepsy patients, suggesting COVID-19 may exacerbate epileptogenesis and neuropsychiatric symptoms during long COVID recovery.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated sanatorium-resort therapy outcomes in 42 adolescents with post-COVID-19 syndrome of varying severity over 2 weeks of aftercare. Patients with moderate/severe COVID-19 showed lower initial life quality indices and slower respiratory recovery compared to those after mild COVID-19, with genetic polymorphisms in alpha-1-antitrypsin and serpin-1 associated with disease severity.

This study examined how CD-14 gene polymorphism affects rehabilitation outcomes in 97 post-COVID syndrome patients undergoing 21-day sanatorium-based treatment including climatotherapy, physical therapy, and respiratory therapy. Patients with the heterozygous CT genotype showed the most significant improvement in respiratory symptoms and quality of life during rehabilitation, while CC genotype patients had more severe baseline symptoms and less pronounced recovery.

This paper studies the impact of COVID-19 on the onset and course of mental disorders in 67 hospitalized elderly patients during acute infection (Feb 2020-Dec 2021), examining psychiatric diagnoses and cognitive outcomes during acute and long-term periods. While it mentions cognitive impairment in the 'long-term period of COVID-19', the focus is on acute psychiatric manifestations and mental illness exacerbation during active COVID-19, not on long COVID-specific persistent symptoms or treatment interventions for long COVID sequelae.

Retrospective study of 151 COVID-19 survivors identifying clinical and laboratory predictors of chronic heart failure development. Develops a risk prediction model based on age, inflammatory markers, and comorbidities but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This observational cohort study compared cardiometabolic and psychocognitive features in 223 elderly patients with atrial fibrillation, contrasting 110 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID syndrome against 113 patients without prior COVID-19. COVID-19 survivors showed significantly worse atherogenic lipid profiles, higher heart rate and pulse pressure, larger ascending aorta diameter, and higher prevalence of anxiety, depression, and moderate-to-severe cognitive impairment.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study following 65 severe COVID-19 survivors at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection to assess respiratory function, radiological changes, physical endurance, and quality of life. Results show persistent radiological abnormalities (63%) and reduced lung diffusion capacity (51%) at 12 months, though physical and psychological symptoms improved significantly over time.

This case-control study compares brachiocephalic artery stenosis in 105 post-COVID patients versus 58 controls without COVID history. The findings show that post-COVID patients have more severe vascular stenosis at a younger age, suggesting SARS-CoV-2 induces premature vascular aging.

This retrospective cohort study compares long-term outcomes (24 months post-hospitalization) in COVID-19 patients with and without cardiovascular multimorbidity, documenting higher mortality, hospitalization, and pulmonary decline in the multimorbidity group. While it does track persistent post-COVID outcomes, it is a secondary analysis of the TARGET-VIP registry rather than testing an intervention, and should be excluded as it does not study a treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cohort study assessing long-term outcomes in 341 patients with severe COVID-19 (CT grade 4 lung damage) at 6 and 12 months post-discharge. Study identifies mortality risk factors but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 215 COVID-19 survivors with severe lung damage (CT-4) followed at 6 and 12 months to assess symptom persistence and associated factors. Found dyspnea and other symptoms persisted in >50% at 6 months but improved by 12 months, with female gender and IL-6 inhibitor use associated with symptom persistence.

This retrospective cohort study followed 101 elderly asthma patients for 90 days after hospitalization for severe COVID-19, identifying risk factors associated with post-discharge mortality. While it addresses long-term COVID-19 complications, it is a passive observational follow-up study without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials pipeline.

A prospective observational cohort study comparing cardiorespiratory fitness and exercise response in 57 post-COVID-19 endurance athletes versus 34 unaffected athletes, with the COVID-19 group undergoing eight weeks of endurance training. The post-COVID group showed pulmonary and skeletal muscle limitations at baseline but responded positively to training with significant improvements in VO2peak, maximal inspiratory pressure, oxygen pulse, and workload.

topics: hyperbaric oxygen therapy|cognitive symptoms|mental health|physical functioning
summary: A prospective registry study evaluating hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) outcomes in long COVID patients, with 56-63% showing clinically relevant improvements in mental and physical component scores at 3-month follow-up. The study found cognitive symptoms showed the most improvement, though 13-19% of patients experienced deterioration, suggesting potential benefit with careful monitoring.

This retrospective cohort study examined oral manifestations, particularly tongue changes, in 426 individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection as part of post-COVID syndrome. The study tracked symptom duration and healing outcomes with and without treatment, finding that local therapy reduced symptom duration by 50% compared to no treatment, with most lesions resolving spontaneously over 4 weeks to 36 months.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates hearing loss in non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients by comparing pure tone audiometry measurements over 1 year before and after infection. The study found significant increases in pure tone thresholds post-COVID-19, with older adults (41-64 years) showing greater hearing loss in the left ear than younger adults.

This cross-sectional study of 1,310 Bulgarian citizens examines the relationship between ambient temperature conditions and Post-COVID-19 symptom severity. The findings show that high night minimum temperatures and small temperature amplitudes exacerbate cardiovascular symptoms, while neurological symptoms predominate at lower temperature amplitudes.

Cross-sectional study of 70 children in Sarajevo with post-COVID history, assessing cardiovascular parameters including ECG, echocardiography, and laboratory markers. Majority were asymptomatic; echocardiograms were normal in all patients, with some ECG abnormalities detected.

Prospective cohort study comparing longitudinal pulmonary function changes in people with and without HIV following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found no significant differences in FEV1, FVC, or DLCO decline between HIV-positive and HIV-negative participants, suggesting HIV alone does not increase pulmonary impairment risk after COVID-19.

A longitudinal observational study tracking olfactory dysfunction and parosmia in 45 mild COVID-19 patients at 1 week, 1 month, and 1 year post-diagnosis using questionnaires and smell identification testing. The study documents the prevalence and natural history of these symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines hemostatic (blood clotting) status in COVID-19 patients 4 months after hospital discharge to understand whether prothrombotic changes persist in post-COVID syndrome. It is a follow-up assessment of a previously studied cohort during hospitalization, measuring coagulation markers but not testing any intervention.

This cross-sectional study of 210 COVID-19 patients examines risk factors for developing post-COVID syndrome. It identifies moderate-to-severe acute COVID course, female gender, age >50, polymorbidity, and glucocorticoid treatment as key risk factors, with differential patterns by disease severity.

Retrospective chart review of 24 COVID-19 patients who received ECMO for severe ARDS, followed up at 8.8 months post-hospitalization with PROMIS Global-10 assessment. While functional outcomes were promising, this is a post-hoc follow-up study of acute critical care without a prospective treatment trial design or control group.

Prospective cohort study following 100 COVID-19 patients with HRCT imaging at acute infection and 6-month follow-up to assess prevalence of post-COVID respiratory complications. Found 64% had persistent chest symptoms (primarily cough and dyspnea) at 6 months, with significant correlation between symptoms and radiological findings of consolidation, crazy paving, and reticulation.

This retrospective cohort study examined long-COVID incidence proportions across three nationwide EHR networks (N3C, PCORnet, PEDSnet) using different computable phenotypes, finding 4% incidence in children and 10-26% in adults depending on definition used. The study characterizes temporal patterns and excess incidence but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This prospective observational study examines hemostatic imbalances in pregnant women who experienced COVID-19 during early pregnancy (14-16 weeks), comparing those with preterm delivery to those with term delivery. While the study tracks COVID-19 convalescence, it focuses on obstetric outcomes and pregnancy complications rather than treatment of long COVID symptoms in long COVID patients.

Descriptive hospital-based study of 150 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and persistence of olfactory dysfunction, with 2-year follow-up. Found that 76% experienced olfactory dysfunction with 77.2% recovering within 2 weeks, but persistence noted in 2 patients after 2 years; no intervention was tested.

A prospective cohort study of adolescents 12 months post-COVID-19 examining asthenia prevalence and its clinical correlates, finding asthenia in 16% with depression and autonomic dysfunction as independent predictors. The study does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials meta-analysis.

This retrospective cohort study examines cardiac biomarkers (sST2, VCAM-1, hs-TnI) and ECG J-waves in 254 COVID-19 hospitalized patients as predictors of long-term cardiovascular outcomes at 12-month follow-up. The study identifies elevated biomarkers as significant predictors of mortality and cardiovascular events but does not test any intervention or treatment.

A prospective cohort study examining how COVID-19 infection affects the development and progression of chronic adenotonsillar disease in children. The study found that prior COVID-19 increases risk of developing chronic adenotonsillar disease, particularly in preschool-aged children, but does not focus on long COVID syndrome or post-acute sequelae.

Retrospective comparison of cardiac MRI findings in 34 COVID-19 patients versus 13 pre-pandemic controls to assess myocardial injury patterns. Study demonstrates extended myocardial injury in post-COVID patients with gender differences in cardiac dysfunction, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines chronic heart failure outcomes in 102 post-COVID patients versus 61 controls without COVID history, assessed over 6 months. It is an observational comparison study that does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study tracking health-related quality of life in 134 patients hospitalized for moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia at two timepoints (2022 and 2024). The study found persistent decline in mental health component scores 4 years post-hospitalization, with no significant change in physical health, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Comparative analysis of COVID-19 course and post-COVID syndrome in 159 IBD patients infected with Omicron vs earlier strains, observed from April 2020 to May 2022. Study found Omicron caused milder disease with lower post-COVID syndrome prevalence at 3 months, though both groups experienced IBD exacerbations post-infection.

A retrospective observational study comparing target organ damage in 186 hypertensive patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection over 2 years. The study identifies risk factors for prolonged post-COVID syndrome in hypertensive patients but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This study examined facial nerve neuropathy (FNN) developing after COVID-19 in 16 patients and compared their clinical course to 21 non-COVID FNN patients, finding that post-COVID FNN showed more severe nerve damage and slower recovery. The authors evaluated acupuncture (reflexology) as part of complex therapy and concluded it was effective and safe for treating post-COVID FNN.

This study assessed the impact of post-COVID syndrome on quality of life in 62 patients with allergic rhinitis and/or polyposis rhinosinusitis compared to 65 unaffected controls, evaluating conservative therapy outcomes. Comparative analysis showed that quality of life indicators were directly dependent on post-COVID status, with treatment effectiveness assessable via standardized QoL measures (SF-36) at 1 and 3 months post-therapy.

Retrospective cohort study examining coagulation system changes in 130 children with COVID-19 compared to 113 healthy controls, assessing vascular-platelet and plasma-coagulation parameters in acute and post-COVID periods. Findings show persistent hemostasis disturbances lasting 4-4.5 months post-infection, with younger children (1-5 years) showing the most abnormalities and increased risk for thromboembolic complications.

Retrospective comparative study assessing quality of life in asthma and COPD patients before and after COVID-19 infection using visual analogue scale and EuroQol-5D questionnaire. Found significant post-COVID decline in quality of life, mobility, and mental health in both patient groups, but no intervention was tested.

Prospective cohort study evaluating whether COVID-19 infection triggers development of true rheumatoid arthritis in patients with post-COVID joint syndrome. Found that COVID-19 may act as a trigger for autoimmune diseases, with recommendations for monitoring rheumatoid arthritis markers and follow-up care.

Retrospective comparison of coronary artery stenting outcomes in 157 acute coronary syndrome patients with (n=69) and without (n=88) prior COVID-19 infection within 6 months. Study found higher prevalence of post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, dizziness) in the COVID-19 group and increased left anterior descending artery lesions, but no active treatment intervention was tested.

Observational study examining retinal microcirculation changes in 41 post-COVID patients vs 13 controls using optical coherence tomography-angiography at 6 weeks and 6 months post-infection. Found significant decreases in vessel density in moderate-to-severe COVID cases, with variable recovery patterns by severity, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This retrospective cohort study examines 64 military servicemen at 3 months post-hospitalization for COVID-19, comparing those with cytokine storm (n=44) to those without (n=20) across respiratory, cardiac, and hemostasis parameters. Patients with cytokine storm showed significantly elevated pulmonary damage, troponin T, D-dimer, and ferritin, indicating persistent organ dysfunction in the recovery period.

This retrospective cohort study examines the relationship between prior COVID-19 infection and development of aseptic necrosis of bone, identifying increased risk in patients with severe COVID-19 and high-dose glucocorticoid exposure. While it addresses a potential COVID-19 sequela, the focus is on bone necrosis as a complication rather than long COVID syndrome, and it does not study or evaluate a treatment intervention.

This study compares vascular remodeling of the upper extremities in 80 patients with vibration disease and hypertension who had COVID-19 versus 50 matched controls without COVID-19, using rheovasography measurements at baseline, 3, and 12 months. The main group showed progressive deterioration in vascular parameters at 3 and 12 months post-COVID compared to controls, indicating accelerated vascular remodeling in the post-COVID period.

Retrospective cohort study of 94 hospitalized patients over 75 years old with COVID-19, followed at 1 and 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term symptoms and functional impairment. Study documents high prevalence of persistent post-COVID symptoms including behavioral changes, cardiovascular symptoms, sensory problems, and functional limitations in elderly survivors.

This retrospective cohort study examines the effects of COVID-19 on male fertility and hormonal status in 62 men (aged 22-45) at 6 and 12 months post-infection. The study documents significant spermatogenesis disorders and decreased testosterone levels, particularly in those with severe COVID-19, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A descriptive cross-sectional study of 7,139 COVID-19 outpatients characterizing the prevalence and distribution of long COVID symptoms by demographic factors. Found long COVID symptoms in 23% of patients, with myalgia most common overall, and identified age, gender, and BMI as factors affecting symptom frequency.

This prospective observational study followed 200 long COVID patients and 105 controls over ~24 months to identify predictors of poor clinical outcomes. Long COVID patients had significantly higher hospitalization rates (44.5% with adverse events) and 2.1-2.2x increased risk of hospitalization and death compared to controls, with 20 identified prognostic indicators including symptom severity, psychological symptoms, and cardiac/vascular remodeling.

A prospective observational study evaluating psychiatric symptoms (anxiety, depression, acute stress, sleep disorders) in COVID-19 survivors during hospitalization and 6 months post-discharge. While the study documents long COVID psychiatric sequelae, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is a natural history/prognostic study without assigned treatment.

Retrospective analysis of 122 post-COVID patients examining relationships between fatigue and chronic illnesses, demographics, and obesity. Found that 77.9% reported fatigue, with obesity measures (BMI, weight) significantly associated with increased fatigue, but no correlation with most chronic conditions or demographic variables.

This descriptive cross-sectional study examines physical activity levels and sleep patterns in 34 adolescents two years after COVID-19 hospitalization. The study found that insufficiently active adolescents reported significantly greater sleepiness and longer sleep duration, with a strong negative correlation between activity level and sleep time.

This observational study evaluates functional status and quality of life in post-COVID patients with and without diabetes at two timepoints (73 and 376 days post-hospitalization). The study finds no significant differences between diabetic and non-diabetic groups, suggesting diabetes does not influence recovery outcomes in the first year after acute COVID-19 infection.

Cross-sectional study evaluating health-related quality of life in 67 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection using SF-36 scoring. Identifies gender, age >65, comorbidities, and hospitalization during acute infection as risk factors for post-COVID syndrome, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Prospective cross-sectional study of 106 post-COVID patients using contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI to assess the nature and prevalence of cardiac injuries. Found that 27.4% had signs of cardiac injury in various combinations, with 26.4% showing focal myocardial injury accompanied by left ventricular remodeling.

This prospective cohort study followed 45 patients with severe COVID-19-associated lung injury for 12 months to assess long-term respiratory and functional changes. While radiological and functional abnormalities showed gradual improvement, persistent CT changes and reduced lung diffusion capacity remained in a significant proportion of patients, indicating need for continued monitoring.

The THROW study assessed the prevalence and severity of residual symptoms in 98 COVID-19 patients at 8 months post-discharge through structured telephone interviews. Found that 60% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, weakness, dyspnea, arthralgia), with female gender and elevated CRP at admission being independent predictors of symptom persistence.

This study assessed pulmonary function in 31 COVID-19 patients at two time points (baseline and ~102 days post-hospitalization) using spirometry, plethysmography, and impulse oscillometry. Results showed significant improvement in lung function metrics over 4 months, though diffusing capacity remained reduced in most patients, suggesting gradual recovery of respiratory function in post-COVID syndrome.

Comparative study examining left atrial appendage thrombosis in 128 patients with persistent atrial fibrillation, comparing 36 post-COVID patients with 92 controls. Found higher incidence of LAA thrombosis (19.4% vs 6.5%) in COVID-19 patients but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective chart review of 831 long COVID patients examining neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) as a biomarker for monitoring neuroinflammation and disease progression from baseline through 24 months post-COVID. The study found elevated NLR at acute infection that normalized at 4-6 months then re-elevated at 16-24 months, suggesting systemic inflammation reactivation, but explicitly states the prospective phase is still being built.

Retrospective chart review of 543 long-COVID patients examining the relationship between peripheral neuropathy and demographic/comorbidity factors. Study reports incidence and risk factors for new-onset and progressing neuropathy but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective study examined cardiac function changes in 54 chronic heart failure patients 5-6 months after COVID-19 infection, finding decreased left ventricular ejection fraction and increased pulmonary artery systolic pressure. While it studies long-term COVID effects, it does not focus on long COVID as a distinct condition and does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.

This prospective cohort study of 15 post-COVID myocarditis patients describes clinical presentations, cardiac imaging findings, and evidence of SARS-CoV-2 persistence in myocardial biopsies up to 9 months post-infection. The study is primarily descriptive and mechanistic (documenting disease features and autoimmune/viral mechanisms) rather than evaluating a treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials dataset.

This retrospective cohort study used multislice CT scans to monitor lung macrostructure changes in 146 COVID-19 pneumonia patients over 2 years post-infection. The study found that residual lung changes (fibrosis, ground glass, bronchiectasis) persisted in older patients and those with severe initial pneumonia, with complete resolution in only 90% of the mildest cases by year 2.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates respiratory function dynamics in 60 patients with COVID-19-associated lung injury at two timepoints (1-6 months and 12-24 months post-discharge) using spirometry and diffusion capacity testing. The study documents improvement in restrictive ventilation disorders and lung diffusion capacity over one year, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This prospective cohort study followed 196 COVID-19 hospital survivors at 3, 6, and 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term sequelae and functional recovery. While most patients showed good overall recovery, 51% still had persistent symptoms at 12 months, with breathlessness and fatigue being the most common long COVID manifestations.

This prospective study investigated the incidence and factors associated with insomnia in COVID-19 survivors over a one-year period. The study found approximately 7% insomnia prevalence among recovered patients, with no significant correlation to infection severity, demographics, or comorbidities.

This retrospective observational study examines pathomorphological changes in the iliac artery of cyclists who recovered from COVID-19, comparing recreational and amateur cyclists over 3 years. The study investigates potential associations between post-COVID vascular changes and doping use, finding minimal progression in recreational cyclists but significant intima-media thickness changes in amateur cyclists potentially related to doping.

Prospective observational study of 40 post-COVID patients presenting with coronary artery disease symptoms, using coronary angiography to assess stenosis severity. Found high prevalence of coronary abnormalities including slow flow, stenosis with thrombosis, and total occlusion in this symptomatic cohort.

Retrospective study of 272 children (182 COVID-19, 90 MIS-C) examining D-dimer levels as a biomarker for disease severity and mortality prediction. D-dimer showed significant elevation in severe cases and non-survivors, with ROC-derived cutoff values of ≥4.58 µg/ml for COVID-19 and ≥4.73 µg/ml for MIS-C predicting mortality.

This cross-sectional study assessed residual pulmonary dysfunction in 50 post-COVID patients at 12 weeks post-discharge by correlating CT severity scores with pulmonary function tests and exercise capacity. Patients with significant lung involvement showed reduced FVC and breath holding time, suggesting impaired recovery despite clinical discharge.

A prospective cohort study of 230 COVID-19 patients in Kerala followed for 6 months to determine the incidence and risk factors for post-COVID syndrome. The study found a 42.2% incidence of post-COVID syndrome and identified age >60 years, female sex, comorbidities, unvaccinated status, and severe initial COVID-19 as significant risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study examining serum albumin levels as a prognostic marker in 52 post-COVID-19 patients admitted to an ICU. Patients with hypoalbuminemia had higher mortality (11.11%) compared to those with normal albumin (2.94%), but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective cohort study examining the relationship between COVID-19 infection and achalasia (esophageal motor disorder) in a patient cohort from 2015-2021. The study found increased achalasia frequency in 2020-2021 and a higher COVID-19 prevalence in type II achalasia patients, suggesting achalasia may be a COVID-19 sequela, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study comparing incidence of cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus in COVID-19 patients versus controls across different post-infection phases. Finds elevated CVD risk in acute and post-acute phases (up to 3 months) but no long-term elevation in CVD or DM prevalence.

This prospective observational study followed 25 COVID-19 patients for 2 months post-discharge to track symptom persistence and radiological changes. Two-thirds of patients still had symptoms at day 30, declining to half at day 60, with 18% showing chest X-ray abnormalities at 2 months, suggesting post-COVID sequelae warrant clinical attention and future intervention studies.

A prospective observational study of 119 post-COVID patients assessing the prevalence and characteristics of pulmonary fibrosis in the post-acute phase. Post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis was observed in 56.3% of cases, though only 3 patients showed residual lung fibrosis; elderly patients with comorbidities, longer hospital stay, and severity of initial infection were risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study documenting long COVID frequency (64.7%) and associated risk factors in 133 hospitalized COVID-19 patients from Turkey, with follow-up at 4 months post-diagnosis. Identifies female gender, severe COVID-19, comorbidities, diabetes, and depression as significant risk factors, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

A prospective cohort study of 300 young COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months to characterize auditory and vestibular symptoms. Auditory and vestibular complaints (vertigo, tinnitus, hearing problems, aural fullness) occurred in only 2-5% of patients during acute phase and resolved or nearly resolved by 3-month follow-up, suggesting these are not persistent long COVID sequelae.

Prospective cohort study tracking olfactory dysfunction recovery in 138 COVID-19 patients over 16 months using standardized smell testing (UPSIT). Found that 90.6% of patients achieved full recovery, with sudden-onset dysfunction showing better recovery rates than gradual-onset.

Prospective observational study following 199 COVID-19 patients with chemosensory deficits (anosmia and dysgeusia) over 8 weeks to assess persistence of these post-COVID symptoms. Found that residual chemosensory dysfunction persisted in most patients, with male predominance, raising concerns about long-term quality of life impact.

This prospective cohort study examines long-term cardiovascular outcomes in 858 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with 13-month follow-up, evaluating the association between early statin use and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). While it studies post-COVID cardiovascular complications, it does not focus on long COVID syndrome (persistent multi-system symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and is excluded because it is an observational cohort study without an assigned intervention—patients' statin use was not randomized or controlled.

This observational study compared demographic, clinical, and immunological characteristics between 90 long COVID patients and 116 controls, finding distinct immune profiles including elevated CD8+ T cells and altered B cell counts in long COVID patients. While the study evaluates QazVac vaccination effects, it is primarily descriptive and comparative rather than testing a treatment intervention in long COVID patients.

This retrospective matched cohort study compares health care resource use and direct costs between COVID-19 patients and matched controls over 6 months using administrative claims data. While it documents long-term COVID-related complications and economic burden, it is a secondary analysis of existing claims data rather than an intervention trial, making it ineligible for the meta-analysis.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated persistent symptoms in COVID-19 patients following hospital discharge from intensive care. The study found that fatigue was the most common long-term symptom, with symptom incidence increasing with patient age.

This retrospective cohort study compared post-COVID pulmonary complications between individuals vaccinated with BioNTech mRNA vaccine versus Sinovac inactivated vaccine. The study found higher rates of lung sequelae and elevated inflammatory markers in the Sinovac-vaccinated group, suggesting inferior protection from inactivated vaccines in severe COVID cases.

This study compared structural and functional vascular parameters and exercise tolerance in 31 patients at long-term follow-up (570±179 days) after COVID-19 hospitalization versus 31 non-hospitalized controls from the ESSE-RF epidemiological study. No significant differences were found between groups in vascular biomarkers (von Willebrand factor, IL-6, TMAO), arterial stiffness measures, or cardiopulmonary exercise test parameters.

This retrospective cohort study assessed pain, fatigue severity, and quality of life in 392 COVID-19 survivors at admission and 3 months post-discharge. While the paper documents natural recovery of symptoms over time, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Observational cross-sectional study examining ophthalmological abnormalities in 23 patients 44-85 days after acute COVID-19 infection. Found persistent dry eyes, abnormal color perception, and retinal layer abnormalities during late convalescence, with no active treatment intervention tested.

This study evaluates early stage I rehabilitation methods for COVID-19 patients with moderate-to-severe lung damage during acute hospitalization. While it does test a rehabilitation intervention, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery in the ICU rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection), making it outside scope for this long COVID trials database.

Prospective observational cohort study of 72 post-COVID-19 patients with intestinal symptoms, documenting clinical presentations, endoscopic findings, and histological changes including diarrhea, inflammatory changes, and in some cases pseudomembranous or ulcerative colitis. Treatment was symptom-oriented and 56.9% showed improvement during hospitalization with complete recovery in 27.8% within 4-8 weeks.

Retrospective analysis of 785 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and types of gastrointestinal symptoms during acute COVID and post-COVID syndrome, with follow-up assessments up to 2 years post-discharge. Found that GI symptoms persist in post-COVID patients (20% prevalence), with dyspeptic symptoms (heartburn, bloating) more common in long-term period compared to acute phase.

This study examines trends in sick sinus syndrome (SSS) incidence and pacemaker implantation rates before and after the COVID-19 pandemic using interrupted time series analysis. While it finds increased SSS incidence post-COVID-19, it does not study treatments for long COVID patients and focuses on a cardiac conduction disorder as a potential COVID-19 sequela rather than on long COVID itself.

A retrospective cohort study of 205 long COVID patients with dyspnea (3+ months post-infection) that identifies clinical and biomarker predictors of post-COVID syndrome, comparing those with prior severe vs mild acute COVID. Key predictors include anxiety/depression (OR 12.14), cognitive impairment (OR 6.12), reduced oxygen saturation on exertion, elevated NT-proBNP, and caspase-6 levels.

Observational cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID respiratory and neuromuscular sequelae in patients with and without type 2 diabetes at a primary care unit in Mexico. Found that respiratory sequelae (particularly cough) were more prevalent than neuromuscular sequelae, and patients with diabetes were more exposed to post-COVID effects.

Retrospective analysis of 152 long COVID patients examining the relationship between autonomic nervous system dysfunction (parasympathetic and sympathetic imbalance) and long COVID symptoms, with investigation of neuro-modulation as a potential therapeutic approach. The study proposes that oxidative stress and autonomic dysfunction explain the severity and prevalence of long COVID manifestations.

Cross-sectional study characterizing cardiac manifestations of post-COVID syndrome in 30 children and adolescents with a comparison group of 32 controls. Found 11.5% incidence of PCS with cardiac manifestations, including arrhythmic syndrome in 67%, asthenic syndrome in 70%, and persistent chest pain, palpitations, and fatigue at 3 and 6 months post-infection.

A prospective cohort study investigating the relationship between minute ventilation and metabolic contribution in long COVID patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Analysis is ongoing with no results reported yet; this is a study protocol without completed findings.

This prospective comparative study evaluated the long-term effects of favipiravir (Areplivir) treatment during acute COVID-19 infection in 190 patients with metabolic syndrome, following them for 1 year into the post-COVID period. Favipiravir-treated patients showed significantly lower inflammatory markers (IL-6/sIL6r and LIF/sLIFr) and reduced risk of cardiovascular complications including a 2.66-fold decrease in stroke and acute coronary syndrome incidence compared to untreated controls.

Prospective study of 74 long COVID patients referred to physical medicine and rehabilitation, evaluating persistent symptoms and impact on physical function and quality of life. Home exercise program resulted in significant improvements in physical function (1-MSTS), activity limitations, and quality of life measures.

Retrospective cohort study of 284 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining long COVID sequelae and associations between acute symptoms and long-term symptoms. Found that specific acute symptoms (anosmia, tiredness, fever, dyspnea) were significantly associated with long COVID outcomes, and symptom burden negatively impacted quality of life.

This study measured IgG antibody levels to toxoid vaccines and SARS-CoV-2 in COVID-19 patients over 17 months, including assessment for prolonged olfaction impairment as a proxy for long COVID symptoms. The researchers found no significant decline in vaccine-induced antibodies during or after COVID-19 infection, though temporary total IgG decline occurred in severe cases.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between endothelial dysfunction, arterial stiffness, and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in a prospectively enrolled cohort of 379 COVID-negative and COVID-positive participants. The study found that arterial stiffness (measured by augmentation index) and oxidized LDL were independently associated with PASC, particularly in patients with neurological and/or cardiopulmonary phenotypes, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 199 COVID-19 patients examining the frequency and characteristics of newly verified or worsened arterial hypertension following infection. Found that 16% of patients developed hypertension post-COVID, typically 3 months after infection, with younger patients affected and significantly elevated blood pressure readings compared to controls.

A 12-month prospective follow-up study of 643 Polish COVID-19 patients assessing the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome symptoms. The study identifies female sex and severe acute COVID-19 as risk factors for persistent symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal observational study following 152 COVID-19 patients at 3, 6, and 9 months post-discharge to assess long-COVID prevalence, risk factors, and impact on health-related quality of life. Found persistent long-COVID symptoms in 53-67% of patients with significant impairment in multiple QoL domains, particularly anxiety/depression, though this is a natural history study without any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study documenting post-discharge clinical, laboratory, and radiographic features in 126 COVID-19 patients (88 mild-moderate, 38 severe-critical) at two Japanese university hospitals. Found persistent symptoms (36.5%), abnormal imaging (83.3%), and lab abnormalities in substantial proportions at a median 46 days post-discharge.

This study analyzes 87 patients presenting with audiovestibular symptoms (hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo) persisting more than 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, confirming the existence of audiovestibular post-COVID syndrome. The paper describes symptom prevalence and characteristics but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A prospective cohort study comparing forced expiratory flow (FEF 25-75%) values between mild-moderate and severe-critical post-COVID-19 patients to assess small airway disease. Found no statistically significant differences in small airway function between severity groups, with only a small proportion of patients showing abnormal values.

Prospective cohort study examining the association between comorbidity status and emotional/behavioral disorder risk in 29 children following COVID-19 infection using the SDQ questionnaire. Findings show 48.3% prevalence of emotional and behavioral difficulties, with comorbidity status significantly associated with emotional problems (p=0.028).

Retrospective cohort follow-up study of 195 COVID-19 convalescents at ~4.7 months and 183 at ~11 months post-infection, assessing prevalence and severity of residual symptoms. Found that 63-75% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, joint pain, dyspnea most common) but severity remained low; no intervention tested.

Retrospective cohort study examining long COVID symptoms in 44 vaccinated women with PCOS, finding that 70% reported persistent symptoms (fatigue, hair loss). The study found no significant difference in PCOS symptoms before/after COVID-19 vaccination or infection, emphasizing vaccination importance for symptom mitigation.

This retrospective cohort study from the ACTIV registry analyzed 9,364 COVID-19 patients to examine how pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD) and acute kidney injury (AKI) impact disease course and long-term prognosis during acute infection and at 3, 6, and 12 months post-hospitalization. Findings show CKD and AKI significantly increased hospital mortality (3.94-fold and 4.88-fold higher at 3 months) and continued to elevate mortality risk in the post-COVID period.

This retrospective cohort study followed 1,438 COVID-19 survivors one year post-discharge to assess long-term neurological sequelae through self-reported symptoms. The study found that neurological symptoms were common (53.46% of severe cases, 27.84% of non-severe cases), with memory and attention deficits being most frequent, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This longitudinal observational cohort study tracked post-COVID syndrome symptom dynamics over 2 years in 225 patients (138 with prior positive PCR, 87 negative control), comparing symptom prevalence and associations with clinical/laboratory factors. Key findings: post-COVID severity is independent of PCR results; cardiac and respiratory syndromes decline 2-3 fold by year 2; asthenia persists as the longest-lasting symptom; risk factors shift from COVID severity and D-dimer in year 1 to age in year 2.

This cross-sectional study compared hemostasis and catecholamine metabolism markers in 60 long COVID patients versus 30 controls without post-COVID syndrome, examining associations with cognitive impairment. While the study confirms elevated catecholamines and cognitive dysfunction in long COVID patients, it is purely observational without any treatment intervention or control group comparison of therapeutic outcomes.

A prospective cohort study examining immunological and coagulation parameters in 34 children with COVID-19, measured during acute infection and 8 months post-disease. The study documents persistent immune and hemostasis abnormalities at 8 months follow-up but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study comparing immunological markers (IL-18, IL-6, rheumatoid factor) in 247 COVID-19 survivors stratified by gastrointestinal symptom duration: ongoing symptomatic (4-12 weeks), post-COVID syndrome (>12 weeks), and asymptomatic controls. Elevated IL-18 and IL-6 levels were significantly higher in both symptomatic groups, identifying IL-18 as a potential diagnostic marker for post-COVID gastroenterological manifestations.

This study examined clinical and microbiological features in 61 children with post-COVID-19 syndrome undergoing sanatorium-based rehabilitation. The findings showed that standard recreational and health-improving sanatorium activities promoted clinical and laboratory recovery, with improvements in fatigue, appetite, and microbiota composition.

This retrospective cohort study investigates the CONUT (Controlling Nutritional Status) score as a predictor of hospital stay length and long COVID risk in 151 COVID-19 patients followed for two years. The study finds that higher CONUT scores correlate with longer hospitalization and increased long COVID incidence, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

Retrospective observational study examining how COVID-19 infection affects the course of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in 28 children, comparing clinical and laboratory markers before and after infection. The study documents increased symptoms (fatigue, joint pain) and intestinal inflammation markers post-COVID, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study examines post-COVID conditions in 78 children (43 with post-COVID syndrome, 35 controls) and reports that 55% of children developed post-COVID symptoms, with herpesvirus reactivation occurring in 51.2% of affected children. Treatment with meglumine acridone acetate (Cycloferon®) achieved clinical improvement in 80% (20/25) of children with herpesvirus reactivation.

This study evaluated the effect of three hepatoprotectors (ursodeoxycholic acid, glycyrrhizic acid with phospholipids, and ademeteonin) versus no hepatoprotective treatment on liver function in 243 post-COVID-19 patients during early rehabilitation. Ursodeoxycholic acid showed the most pronounced effect on normalizing liver enzyme markers and bilirubin levels.

summary: This cross-sectional study assessed clinical and laboratory indicators of liver damage in 243 COVID-19 patients during early rehabilitation (10+ days post-infection, PCR-negative). The study found elevated liver enzymes, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and multiple clinical syndromes but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 5,446 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months post-diagnosis to assess prevalence and risk factors for anxiety and depression using EQ-5D-3L scale. Found anxiety/depression prevalence ranged from 18.5% at 1 month to 15.4% at 6 months, with female gender, poor economic status, higher symptom burden, and ICU admission as significant risk factors.

A prospective follow-up study of 90 COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between annexin A5 (ANXA5) levels and regression of pulmonary complications 6 months post-infection. The study is a secondary biomarker analysis without a specific treatment intervention being tested.

A prospective follow-up study of 700 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessed long-term sequelae at 3-7 months post-discharge through telephone contact and outpatient clinical evaluations. The study found that over half of patients experienced persistent symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, and chest pain, with CT imaging revealing persistent lung changes in patients with severe acute infection.

This cross-sectional study characterizes clinical recovery in 43 elderly post-COVID patients stratified by recovery duration (≤3 months vs >3 months) and lung parenchymal abnormality severity. Persistent fatigue (75%), dyspnea (59%), and joint pain were common, with respiratory functional impairment correlating with greater lung lesion volume (>25%).

This paper retrospectively analyzes 154 COVID-19 patients with prolonged anosmia, tracking their symptoms and neuropsychiatric manifestations over 9 months post-infection. It identifies anosmia as a predictor of anxiety, depression, and sleep disorders but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study followed 337 COVID-19 survivors with chest CT scans performed 102-361 days after disease onset to evaluate long-term pulmonary changes and their correlation with post-discharge dyspnea. While it documents natural disease progression and identifies imaging predictors of dyspnea, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective study evaluating whether chest CT findings influence pneumologist decision-making for diagnosis and management of pulmonary long COVID in 41 patients. CT did not influence diagnostic or management decisions, only modestly improved diagnostic confidence, and is not routinely necessary when pulmonary function tests and auscultation are normal.

Prospective hospital registry study examining clinical characteristics, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and long-term outcomes in post-COVID-19 patients with cardiovascular multimorbidity over 13 months of follow-up. Patients with CVMM were older, had higher all-cause mortality and hospitalization rates, and showed declining adherence to anticoagulant therapy, suggesting inadequate management of post-COVID cardiovascular complications.

A prospective cohort study following 306 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 2 years post-discharge to assess the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome. The study found 43.8% prevalence of PCS with fatigue, brain fog, and anxiety as most common symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective study of cardiac tissue from 9 patients undergoing heart surgery ~6 months post-COVID, examining SARS-CoV-2 persistence and inflammatory markers. Found viral RNA in 4/9 patients with elevated IL-6 and IL-1β in some cases, but this is observational tissue sampling with no intervention—a mechanistic investigation rather than a treatment trial.

A longitudinal observational study following 25 COVID-19 patients 8-16 weeks after discharge to assess radiological recovery, lymphocyte dynamics, and antibody levels. While it documents post-acute sequelae, it is a passive observational follow-up study without any intervention or treatment being administered to patients.

This retrospective cohort study examines the association between electrolyte supplementation and cardiac injury in 144 long COVID patients with cardiac complications, comparing supplementation (n=72) versus control (n=72) groups. Results show that electrolyte supplementation was associated with improved heart rate variability parameters, reduced premature contractions, and better quality of life scores.

Retrospective follow-up study of 129 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and risk factors for persistent postinfectious cough at median 8.1 months post-discharge. Found 20.9% developed postinfectious cough, with smoking and digestive symptoms during hospitalization as significant risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long COVID sequelae symptoms in Omicron-infected patients versus never-infected controls from a Japanese fever clinic. Found loss of taste/smell, hair loss, neurocognitive symptoms, and respiratory symptoms as specific long COVID sequelae, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 405 post-COVID patients comparing pulmonary function recovery in those who received corticosteroids during acute COVID-19 infection versus those who did not. Corticosteroid treatment was associated with faster recovery of FEV1 and FVC over long-term follow-up, even in higher-risk subgroups.

Prospective observational study tracking pulmonary function and exercise capacity in 38 post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients over 12 months compared to 25 healthy controls. Findings show significant impairments in FVC/FEV1 and 6-minute walk distance at baseline, with gradual improvement over time, but persistent deficits throughout follow-up.

This prospective observational study compared white matter integrity in patients with severe depression after multiple COVID-19 infections versus mild-to-moderate depression after single infection, using diffusion tensor imaging 3-6 months post-infection. The study found significant impairments in white matter integrity and negative correlations between psychological scores and fractional anisotropy, but involved no intervention or treatment—only assessment of existing neurobiological changes.

This study evaluates semen parameters in 36 male COVID-19 recovered patients versus 45 controls at median 177.5 days post-recovery. While the paper mentions long-term follow-up, it is not primarily about long COVID—it focuses on acute COVID-19's impact on male fertility and does not study an intervention or treatment for long COVID symptoms.

Retrospective study of 48 patients (88 hips) with post-COVID osteonecrosis of the femoral head treated with bisphosphonate therapy (zoledronic acid and alendronate) over a minimum 6-month follow-up. 95.5% of hips showed good clinical outcomes with improved pain scores and Harris hip scores, with only 4.5% requiring surgical intervention.

Retrospective cohort study assessing frailty syndrome in older patients who recovered from COVID-19 using the FRAIL screening tool. The study demonstrates that post-COVID patients show asthenic syndrome rather than age-related frailty and require individualized geriatric assessment and long-term rehabilitation.

This retrospective cohort study uses VA healthcare databases to characterize 6-month risks of death and post-acute sequelae in people with breakthrough COVID-19 compared to uninfected controls and COVID-19-infected non-vaccinated individuals. The study found elevated risks of multisystem post-acute sequalae (pulmonary, cardiovascular, neurologic, mental health, and others) following breakthrough infection, with risks varying by hospitalization status.

Multicentre retrospective study examining the prevalence and characteristics of prolonged symptoms (lasting >12 weeks) in Spanish children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found 14.6% of 451 children experienced long COVID symptoms, with age >5 years, PICU admission, and family history of prolonged symptoms as significant risk factors.

This study uses a representative sample of 308 U.S. COVID-19 infected individuals from the Understanding America Study to characterize long COVID prevalence and symptom trajectories over 12 weeks post-infection. The authors find that 23% experienced persistent new-onset symptoms (long COVID), with headache, fatigue, and GI symptoms most common, and obesity and certain acute symptoms significantly increasing risk.

Norwegian prospective cohort study of 312 COVID-19 patients (247 home-isolated, 65 hospitalized) tracking long-term symptoms at 6 months. Found 61% had persistent symptoms including fatigue (37%), impaired concentration (26%), and dyspnea (21%), with young home-isolated adults particularly affected by cognitive and respiratory symptoms.

Prospective observational cohort study of 42 long COVID patients examining clinical parameters and biomarkers associated with persistent fatigue and exertion intolerance 6 months post-infection. Found evidence of low-level inflammation and hypoperfusion as potential pathomechanisms, with hand grip strength diminished in most patients.

This retrospective cohort study uses EHR data from two large PCORnet networks (INSIGHT and OneFlorida+) to identify risk factors and develop machine learning prediction models for post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). The study characterizes which PASC conditions are predictable based on baseline factors but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed 229 Slovak young adults to investigate long-term psychological and physical symptoms following COVID-19 recovery. The study found significant effects on cognitive health (memory, concentration, task-handling) particularly in women, along with physiological changes including decreased fitness and headaches, but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This RECOVER Initiative study estimates long COVID (PASC) incidence across adult and pediatric populations using electronic health records from three nationwide research networks, finding 7% incidence in children and 8.5-26.4% in adults depending on classification algorithm. The paper is an observational epidemiological study examining incidence patterns and risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective observational study comparing clinical outcomes and long COVID occurrence in 100 acute pancreatitis patients with and without COVID-19 infection. Found no significant differences in mortality or severity between groups, though long COVID syndrome (specifically cough) was more common in the COVID-19 positive group.

Retrospective cohort study examining racial/ethnic differences in long COVID symptoms among 225,723 pediatric patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to 677,448 uninfected controls from the RECOVER Initiative. Findings show significant disparities in symptom prevalence by race/ethnicity and COVID-19 severity, including differential rates of fever, respiratory symptoms, hair loss, dysautonomia, and cognitive symptoms.

This study compared in-hospital rehabilitation outcomes between COVID-19 survivors who received rehabilitation (N=155) and those who did not (N=162), measuring functional status at discharge using Mental Status, ICU Mobility, and modified Barthel Index scores. Rehabilitation patients were older with more comorbidities and worse pre-admission dependency, and the study found that functional scores were impaired at discharge and associated with pre-admission dependency and various comorbidities, warranting follow-up of COVID-19 survivors for post-acute sequelae.

Prospective cohort study tracking symptom prevalence in 837 long COVID patients over 9 months using the ComPaRe e-cohort in France. Describes natural disease course rather than evaluating a treatment intervention, with 88.7% reporting persistent symptoms at 9 months and varying patterns of symptom resolution.

This retrospective cohort study uses VA healthcare databases to characterize cardiovascular complications in COVID-19 survivors at one year post-infection, comparing 151,195 COVID-19 patients to controls. The study identifies increased risks of various cardiovascular diseases in the post-acute phase but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This nationwide cohort study compares long COVID symptom prevalence in 37,522 SARS-CoV-2 infected children versus 78,037 uninfected controls using questionnaires. The study documents symptom prevalence and duration in children but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This large observational cohort study evaluated whether Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir) treatment within 5 days of SARS-CoV-2 infection reduces the risk of long COVID in 497,499 patients using electronic health records from PCORnet. Results showed Paxlovid was associated with a 12% reduction in long COVID risk (HR 0.88) in high-risk patients, but showed no significant benefit in low-risk patients.

Retrospective analysis evaluating the clinical utility of cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in 12 post-COVID patients with persistent breathlessness. The study found that while CPET identified various physiological limitations, it did not substantially improve clinical management and may not be a cost-effective diagnostic approach for post-COVID assessment.

Observational cohort study of 130 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (stratified by ventilation intensity) followed at one year with pulmonary function tests and health status questionnaires. Found lung function in lower normal limits without significant differences by initial disease severity, suggesting broader testing warranted in patients with lingering symptoms.

Prospective cohort study of 407 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed at 6 and 12 months post-discharge to assess long-term outcomes. Found persistent symptoms in ~24-27% at follow-up, with IMV patients at higher risk for dyspnea and neurological complications.

Prospective cohort study of 70 long COVID patients examining the role of respiratory muscle pump dysfunction in exercise intolerance, using cardiopulmonary exercise testing and respiratory muscle measurements over 12+ months. Found heterogeneous pathophysiology with respiratory muscle weakness associated with reduced oxygen uptake, suggesting respiratory muscle training as a potential therapeutic approach.

A national matched cohort study comparing post-COVID symptomatology in 11-17-year-old children with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection versus test-negative controls at 3 months post-infection. Test-positive children had higher prevalence of multiple symptoms (30.3% vs 16.2%), with symptom patterns analyzed by demographic and health factors.

Hospital-based observational study of 150 COVID-19 recovered children (3 months to 18 years) assessed 3 months post-discharge for long-term health impacts. Found 60% had persistent or new symptoms including cough, fatiguability, neurological changes, and MIS-C, indicating significant post-COVID sequelae in children.

Cross-sectional study examining long COVID symptom patterns across different age groups in 77 post-COVID patients and healthy controls. Finds that women aged 40-60 years report the most complaints, with weakness, anxiety, and mood disorders being most common, and higher prevalence in vaccinated individuals.

A prospective cohort study of 110 children (80 with post-COVID syndrome, 30 controls) examining clinical symptoms and laboratory characteristics including inflammatory markers, coagulation parameters, and IgG levels to SARS-CoV-2. The study found that post-COVID syndrome in children is characterized by multisystem symptoms (fatigue 91.3%, fever 96.3%, neurological and respiratory manifestations) associated with persistent inflammation, coagulation activation, and elevated IgG titers, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study of 100 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between new-onset hyperglycemia and disease severity/mortality during acute infection and 6-month follow-up. While the paper does track long-term outcomes post-discharge, it focuses on acute COVID-19 pathophysiology and diabetes development rather than long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions for persistent symptoms.

Retrospective comparison of coronary angiography profiles in diabetic patients before and after COVID-19, examining cardiovascular outcomes. Study found increased ACS presentations and coronary artery disease severity in diabetics post-COVID, but does not focus on long COVID sequelae or test any treatment intervention.

A prospective observational cohort study of 86 post-COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months to assess clinical and radiological changes. Found persistent fatigue (78%), dyspnea (52%), and progressive pulmonary imaging abnormalities (increased reticulations and fibrosis), with overall deterioration in quality of life.

This study measures Maximum Phonation Time (MPT) in COVID-19 recovered patients to assess post-infection changes in phonatory capacity. Results show significant and persistent reduction in phonation duration up to one year post-infection, attributed to reduced lung capacity.

A retrospective cohort study of 150 COVID-19 survivors followed for 3 months post-discharge at a tertiary hospital in India, characterizing long COVID manifestations and their relationships to disease severity and demographics. The study found that fever, dyspnea, and cough were the most commonly reported persistent symptoms, with symptom persistence significantly higher in those with severe acute disease.

Prospective cohort study of 57 COVID-19 ARDS survivors assessed at 3 months post-discharge, evaluating physical function, cognitive outcomes, quality of life, and disability. Most patients showed rapid recovery with normal physical and mental function scores, though 36% reported severe fatigue and 30 of 43 showed persistent chest imaging abnormalities.

Prospective observational cohort study following 135 COVID-19 patients at three months post-infection to assess neurological outcomes, smell disorders, cognitive function, and quality of life. Found 15% developed new neurological syndromes and 17% had persistent smell disorders, identifying long COVID neurological sequelae requiring further research.

Retrospective cohort study of 117 COVID-19 patients examining gastrointestinal sequelae at 3 months post-discharge, finding 45% experienced at least one GI symptom with identified risk and protective factors. This is a secondary analysis of hospitalization data rather than an intervention trial, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

Prospective cohort study of 355 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh followed for at least 1 month post-recovery to identify incidence and risk factors for post-COVID syndrome. Found 46% developed post-COVID symptoms (primarily fatigue), with female gender, respiratory distress, lethargy, and prolonged disease duration as significant risk factors.

This is a prospective cohort study of 462 COVID-19 patients followed for 90-150 days after disease onset, examining the development and reversal of pulmonary fibrosis on chest CT scans. The study focuses on acute post-infection pulmonary complications during the immediate recovery phase, not on long COVID persistent symptoms weeks to months later.

A 6-month prospective cohort study of 250 post-COVID patients in Kerala assessing dietary diversity, comorbidities, and post-COVID manifestations including fatigue, stress, and insomnia. Exercise showed an impact on fatigue, stress, diet pattern, and sleep, with 56.8% experiencing severe fatigue and 56% reporting subthreshold insomnia post-COVID.

This retrospective-prospective cohort study followed 464 COVID-19 patients discharged from a Wuhan hospital to assess long-term sequelae over 1-2 months. The study found high rates of psychosocial problems (57.7%), respiratory abnormalities (32.6%), and cardiac dysfunction (21.5%), with advanced age and ICU stay as key risk factors, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Prospective single-center study of COVID-19 survivors evaluating clinical sequelae and functional outcomes through cardiopulmonary exercise testing, imaging, and biomarker analysis. Over 50% of survivors exhibited symptomatic functional impairment with reduced peak oxygen consumption despite normal cardiac and pulmonary function tests.

A prospective cohort study of 93 COVID-19 ARDS survivors followed at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to characterize persistent disabilities. Most patients recovered physical functioning and independence by 6 months, but severe fatigue remained common (36%), and some had persistent respiratory and pulmonary function abnormalities.

A prospective cohort study of 717 COVID-19 survivors followed for one year after acute infection to characterize long-term complications across multiple symptom domains including fatigue, pain, neurological impairment, and sleep disorders. The study found that persistent symptoms remain common at 12 months, with no clear association between acute disease severity and long-term symptom burden.

This cohort study assessed psychiatric and cognitive morbidity 6-9 months after moderate/severe COVID-19 hospitalization in 425 survivors using structured psychiatric interviews and psychometric testing. It found high rates of depression (8%), anxiety (15.5%), PTSD (13.6%), and memory decline (51.1%), but does not test any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,560 German adolescents comparing long-COVID symptoms between seropositive and seronegative students. Found no statistical difference in symptom prevalence between groups, suggesting pandemic-associated rather than infection-specific mental health impacts.

Retrospective cohort study of 226,521 COVID-19 positive patients in UK primary care compared to matched controls, examining associations between COVID-19 infection and subsequent psychiatric morbidity, sleep problems, and fatigue. While the paper documents elevated risk of fatigue and sleep problems post-COVID, it is an observational epidemiological study without any treatment intervention evaluated.

Population-based retrospective cohort study comparing post-COVID-19 sequelae between 45,272 community-managed and 1,415 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in the UK, followed for up to 3 months. Study describes symptom and disease prevalence, healthcare utilization differences, and risk factors by severity and demographics, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study following 217 COVID-19 patients at 2 and 6 months post-infection to characterize long COVID symptoms, imaging findings, and associations with baseline characteristics. No intervention was administered; this is a natural history observational study documenting symptom prevalence and clinical associations rather than evaluating a treatment.

A prospective observational study of 59 COVID-19 survivors investigating ongoing symptoms and functional limitations at 4-5 months post-infection. Found that 72.9% reported ongoing symptoms at baseline (primarily fatigue), declining to 42.3% at follow-up, with 44.8% experiencing difficulty with daily activities.

A longitudinal surveillance study tracking post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in Long Beach residents from April-December 2020, documenting symptom prevalence at multiple time points post-infection. One-third of participants reported PASC two months post-testing, with fatigue, anosmia, and dyspnea most common, and older age, female gender, Black/African American ethnicity, and pre-existing asthma or obesity associated with higher odds of developing PASC.

Target trial emulation using propensity score matching from the ComPaRe long COVID cohort in France to evaluate COVID-19 vaccination effects on persistent long COVID symptoms. Vaccination reduced symptom severity, doubled complete remission rates, and decreased disease impact at 120 days follow-up.

Prospective cohort study examining serum biomarkers and clinical factors predicting symptom duration in 617 long COVID patients followed for up to one year. Found that lower anti-nucleocapsid IgG levels and prior lung disease were associated with longer symptom duration, but no intervention was tested.

Prospective cohort study comparing post-acute sequelae of COVID (PASC) outcomes in 453 vaccinated versus unvaccinated long COVID patients followed over 6 months.
