Found no significant differences in symptom improvement (anosmia, respiratory, depression, anxiety, PTSD, quality of life) between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups.

Population-based cohort study investigating prevalence, clinical characteristics, and risk factors for Post-COVID-19 symptoms in 1,732 German patients with confirmed COVID-19. Found that 66.7% of hospitalized and 39.4% of non-hospitalized patients experienced symptoms persisting ≥12 weeks, with fatigue, physical exhaustion, and difficulty concentrating being most common; female sex, comorbidity level, and acute COVID-19 severity were strongest risk factors.

A cross-sectional study of 318 participants from a German digital cohort investigating cytokine profiles and autoantibodies in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). The study identifies IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α as a cytokine triad associated with PASC symptoms and proposes macrophage activation as an underlying disease mechanism.

Longitudinal cohort study examining mental health and psychosocial outcomes in older adults with probable COVID-19 infection over 4-6 months. Finds increased depression, anxiety, loneliness, and financial hardship in infected participants, but focuses on acute/immediate COVID-19 effects rather than long COVID sequelae.

Retrospective epidemiological study of 1,164 long COVID patients in Brazil examining symptom prevalence, demographics, and comorbidities. Findings show pain and neuropsychological symptoms are common, with physical and pain symptoms increasing with age and varying by sex and race.

This prospective cohort study followed 749 COVID-19 survivors 6 months post-hospitalization to develop a screening protocol for detecting chronic lung lesions using clinical measurements and machine learning. The protocol combining chest X-ray, dyspnea scale, oxygen saturation, and spirometry accurately identified patients with CT-confirmed pulmonary changes (sensitivity 0.85), but did not evaluate or test any intervention—it is a diagnostic/screening study only.

Prospective cohort study following 534 COVID-19 patients for 15 months after hospitalization to assess persistent symptoms and psychological conditions. Found high rates of fatigue (17.2%), sleep disturbance (18.5%), and mental health issues, but no intervention was tested—this is a purely observational follow-up study with no treatment component.

Prospective cohort study of 1,873 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in South Africa during the second and third waves, followed up at 1 and 3 months post-discharge to assess post-COVID condition prevalence, symptoms, and associated risk factors. Found 66.7% reported persistent symptoms at 3 months, with fatigue, dyspnea, and cognitive dysfunction most common; risk factors included age, female sex, severe acute illness, and obesity.

This prospective cohort study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 vaccination improved symptoms in participants with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) and compared antibody dynamics between vaccinated and unvaccinated PACS patients. The study found no strong evidence that vaccination improves PACS symptoms, with comparable symptom burden and recovery rates between matched vaccinated and unvaccinated groups.

Prospective cohort study following 1,013 adults and 360 children hospitalized with COVID-19 in Moscow at 6 and 12 months post-discharge to assess prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition and identify risk factors. Found post-COVID prevalence of 50% in adults and 20% in children at 6 months, declining to 34% and 11% at 12 months; female sex and pre-existing hypertension were risk factors in adults, while neurological comorbidities were risk factors in children.

A retrospective epidemiological study of 1,164 long COVID patients in Brazil examining prevalence, demographics, clinical symptoms, and comorbidities. Found pain and neuropsychological symptoms were common, with prevalence increasing with age and varying by sex and race, and a correlation between physical symptoms and comorbidity burden.

This retrospective cohort study identifies plasma biomarkers (GFAP and neurofilament light chain) associated with neurologic sequelae in 61 COVID-19 patients followed for one year post-hospitalization, comparing them to 60 pre-pandemic historical controls. The study found that elevated GFAP and NF-L levels are associated with longer-term neurological symptoms and warrant exploration as biomarkers for long-term neurologic complications after COVID-19 infection.

A one-year prospective follow-up study of 73 COVID-19 recovered patients examining immune status and persistent lung CT abnormalities, comparing 40 patients with normal CT to 20 with abnormal CT findings. The study found that complement C3 levels were associated with persistent lung abnormalities, though overall immune recovery was observed.

Prospective multicenter study assessing frequency and characteristics of fatigue and cognitive impairment in 969 long COVID patients (~9 months post-infection) compared to matched non-COVID controls. Found 19% of long COVID patients had clinically relevant fatigue versus 8% of controls, and identified distinct pathophysiological pathways for the two sequelae.

This cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary function at 6 months post-hospitalization in 128 COVID-19 survivors, finding impairments in 22% of patients across spirometry, lung volumes, and diffusion capacity. Non-Hispanic Black patients showed significantly lower DLCO values compared to White and Hispanic patients after controlling for demographic and clinical factors.

Prospective longitudinal study following COVID-19 survivors over 24 months to characterize prolonged inflammation and its association with persistent symptoms. Found that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination administered at 12-16 months reduced inflammatory markers and dysregulated immune cells, even though symptoms persisted, suggesting vaccines may alleviate post-COVID syndrome.

Prospective cohort study examining long COVID symptoms in 1,267 infected and exposed household members (children, adolescents, adults) approximately 1 year after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found higher prevalence of moderate/severe persistent symptoms in infected vs exposed individuals, with symptom clustering within families, but no active intervention was tested.

A prospective cohort study of 313 post-COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and characteristics of peripheral neuropathy over 6-12 months using electromyography and electrophysiological assessment. The study found 74% of patients had PNP associated with age, education, and IgG antibody levels at discharge, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 732 COVID-19 patients followed for 12 months to characterize post-COVID neurological syndrome (PCNS), with clinical assessments and health surveys. Found 70.9% of patients at 12-month follow-up presented PCNS with distinct temporal profiles and subtypes, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Longitudinal observational study assessing frailty transitions in 450 patients hospitalized with severe COVID-19, using the Clinical Frailty Scale at hospital discharge and median 4.2-month follow-up. Findings show 42% worsened frailty scores and 12% became vulnerable or frail, but this is a passive follow-up cohort without any intervention administered.

This prospective cohort study compared pulmonary function and quality-of-life outcomes 6 months after ICU discharge in severe COVID-19 survivors from the first vs. second/third pandemic waves. The study found persistent respiratory impairment at 6 months in both groups with similar quality-of-life outcomes, indicating no improvement in long-term outcomes despite better ICU treatment strategies.

This study analyzes pre-pandemic IL-6 levels in TwinsUK participants to test whether pre-existing immune status predicts chronic fatigue post-COVID. The findings show pre-pandemic IL-6 was associated with chronic fatigue in COVID-negative but not COVID-positive individuals, suggesting pre-existing immune status does not specifically drive post-COVID fatigue.

A prospective national cohort study of 12,788 English adolescents examining the association between parental ongoing COVID-19 problems and adolescent long COVID reporting at 6 months post-SARS-CoV-2 exposure. Found that adolescents whose parents reported ongoing COVID-19 problems had 1.79-fold higher odds of reporting long COVID, independent of infection status and demographic factors.

This cross-sectional study examined blood coagulation markers in 191 patients recovered from COVID-19, comparing them to healthy controls. The study found elevated fibrinogen, soluble fibrin, and prethrombin-1 levels persisting over two months post-recovery, indicating a prolonged prethrombotic state correlated with initial COVID-19 severity.

This descriptive survey of a prospective inception cohort examined the prevalence and predictors of long COVID symptoms in vaccinated delta-variant survivors in Bangladesh, comparing pre-delta (N=14,392) and delta (N=13,475) cohorts. The study found higher prevalence of long COVID symptoms (25.2% vs 16.1%) and novel symptoms in musculoskeletal, functional, and cognitive domains among delta variant survivors, with various sociodemographic and clinical predictors identified.

Prospective cohort study of 194 Mexican patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19, followed longitudinally for up to 2 years to characterize long COVID symptoms and their persistence over time. No interventions were tested; this is a descriptive natural history study of symptom prevalence and duration.

A nationwide Swedish observational cohort study characterizing post-COVID syndrome incidence, clinical features, and risk factors in 1,057,174 SARS-CoV-2 positive individuals using diagnosis codes and matched controls. Found disease severity as the strongest risk factor for PCS, with dyspnea, malaise/fatigue, and abnormal pulmonary imaging as most common diagnoses.

This retrospective cohort study compares post-acute healthcare charges between patients hospitalized for COVID-19 and influenza using administrative billing data from 446 US hospitals. The analysis finds no significant differences in healthcare costs between the two groups in the 1-5 months following hospitalization, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment interventions.

This retrospective cohort study uses the TriNetX health database to compare PASC risk between people with HIV and the general population, finding that HIV confers higher risk but that COVID-19 vaccination is protective. The study is a secondary analysis of an existing health database rather than an original intervention trial.

A cross-sectional observational study using resting-state fMRI to assess functional brain network connectivity in 100 long COVID patients recovering from mild-to-moderate acute COVID-19. The study found characteristic patterns of altered brain network connectivity, with fatigue patients showing reduced default mode network activity and compensatory overactivity in lateral parietal regions.

Prospective cohort study following hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 participants across three variant waves in South Africa to assess post-COVID-19 condition prevalence at 6 months. Found 46.7% of hospitalized and 18.5% of non-hospitalized participants had persistent symptoms, with identified risk factors including age, sex, comorbidities, and infection severity.

This retrospective cohort study examines outcomes in COPD patients hospitalized for acute COVID-19, tracking re-admission and mortality at 12 months post-discharge. COPD patients had worse respiratory function at discharge and significantly higher risk of respiratory re-admission, but no difference in mortality.

This retrospective cohort study compared the risk of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) among type 2 diabetes patients taking metformin versus sulfonylureas or DPP4 inhibitors using electronic health records from the N3C Consortium. Results showed no statistically significant difference in PASC risk at 3 or 6 months between metformin users and comparators, though confidence intervals were wide.

Prospective cohort study following 70 unvaccinated participants for 24 months post-mild-to-moderate COVID-19 to characterize long COVID incidence, duration, and association with quality of life. Found 33% experienced long COVID with symptoms most common at 6 months, and 8% had not returned to pre-COVID health at 24 months.

Longitudinal observational study of 900 healthcare workers in Geneva followed from July to December 2021, assessing prevalence of post-COVID symptoms, functional impairment, and quality of life using validated scales. Study found increased symptom prevalence at follow-up (68.4% vs 54.3%), particularly fatigue, headache, and cognitive impairment, with associated functional impairment and absenteeism, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study comparing COPD patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection to assess long-term pulmonary and mortality outcomes. Finds that COVID-19 is an independent risk factor for acute exacerbations of COPD and increased mortality, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared 43 elderly COPD patients with newly onset persistent fatigue post-COVID (long COVID group) to 42 controls without long COVID symptoms, using pulmonary function tests, imaging, and blood proteomic analysis. The study identified key clinical features and proteomic disruptions in inflammation and energy metabolism that distinguish long COVID patients, suggesting these mechanisms underlie long COVID development in elderly COPD populations.

A prospective cohort study following 118 COVID-19 patients for 1 year post-discharge to assess long-term changes in liver function. While the paper documents persistent liver dysfunction in some patients and identifies risk factors, it is observational without any treatment intervention and does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trial.

Retrospective study of 122 COVID-19 patients with median 405-day follow-up evaluating CT imaging changes and laboratory parameters. Only 11% of patients showed residual CT lesions, with irregular opacities and reticular patterns being most common.

This cross-sectional study compared pulmonary function tests between 20 post-COVID-19 pneumonia survivors and 30 healthy controls at 3+ months post-recovery. While it documents significant restrictions in lung function and diffusion capacity in post-COVID patients, it is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention.

Online registry study comparing COVID-19 symptom persistence between participants with and without autoimmune disease medication use. People on autoimmune medications had significantly higher rates of persistent symptoms at 30 days, particularly shortness of breath and fatigue, suggesting autoimmune conditions as a vulnerability factor for post-acute sequelae.

Prospective observational cohort study examining the natural history and symptomology of long COVID in 323 participants from a US community health system, with baseline and 6-month follow-up assessments. Found that severe fatigue (23% at baseline) disproportionately affected younger women and was associated with anxiety, depression, higher resting heart rate, and worse health outcomes across multiple patient-reported measures.

Prospective cohort study of 306 discharged COVID-19 patients (including 112 ICU patients) assessed 4 months post-admission to determine whether corticosteroid use during acute infection reduced persistent symptoms. Corticosteroids showed no protective effect against persistent symptoms or symptom count, suggesting they are ineffective for preventing long COVID sequelae.

Prospective observational study comparing long COVID symptom trajectories in 323 patients who received monoclonal antibodies (mAb) during acute infection versus those who did not, followed for 6 months. mAb-treated patients reported fewer symptoms at baseline and 6-month follow-up, with both groups showing significant within-group symptom reduction over time.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 295 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia examining the relationship between long COVID symptoms and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using EQ-5D and self-report questionnaires. Fatigue, headache, and persistent cough were most common symptoms, and multiple regression showed these symptoms significantly predicted reduced HRQoL in pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression domains.

This observational study examines associations between inflammatory markers (IL-1β), catecholamine levels (epinephrine), and clinical outcomes in 79 PASC patients. The authors find that epinephrine and IL-1β correlate with fatigue, depression, anxiety, and cognitive function, suggesting these biomarkers may provide clinical utility for tracking PASC persistence or recovery.

This cross-sectional study evaluates overactive bladder symptoms in 66 long COVID patients undergoing inpatient rehabilitation using standardized assessment tools. The paper reports prevalence and severity of bladder dysfunction post-COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case-control study comparing ocular manifestations in 100 post-acute COVID-19 patients versus 100 controls, finding higher rates of retinal vascular occlusion, anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, uveitis, and central serous chorioretinopathy in the COVID group. This is an observational comparison of disease manifestations without any intervention or treatment being tested.

A single-center observational study assessing pulmonary function abnormalities in 64 convalescent COVID-19 patients (6-9 months post-infection), comparing severe vs non-severe cases. The study found that 56.5% of severe patients had diffusion dysfunction and identified imaging changes (nodules, ground-glass opacities) associated with disease severity, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study of 72 long COVID patients who completed a multidisciplinary clinic program incorporating personalized exercise, respiratory training, and monitored cardiovascular activity. Program was safe with no adverse events and showed significant improvements in functional outcomes including respiratory strength, walking tests, and overall health scores.

This prospective longitudinal study evaluated a 6-week Adapted Physical Activity (APA) protocol in 50 long COVID patients, measuring health-related quality of life and psychological outcomes at baseline, post-intervention, and 5-7 month follow-up. The intervention produced significant improvements in both physical and mental HRQOL, with anxiety and depression substantially reduced, suggesting structured physical activity is a feasible non-pharmacological strategy for long COVID recovery.

Retrospective observational study of 103 long COVID patients presenting to a neurological outpatient clinic, documenting the prevalence and characteristics of neurological manifestations including fatigue, cognitive disorders, olfactory dysfunction, and headache. Most patients showed mild improvement on follow-up but rarely achieved complete recovery; no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed depression frequency and quality of life in 75 post-COVID patients using PHQ-9 screening and cognitive testing. One-third of participants screened positive for clinically significant depression, with fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive symptoms as primary complaints, correlated with acute COVID-19 severity.

This is an observational cross-sectional study using the Platform C19 database examining risk predictors and symptom features of long COVID in a broad primary care population including both test-confirmed and untested COVID-19 patients. The study identifies demographic and clinical risk factors (age, female sex, frailty, A&E visits, hospitalization) and symptom features associated with long COVID persistence, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined anxiety levels in 1,756 post-COVID patients using the Beck Anxiety Inventory and investigated associations with demographic factors, acute COVID severity, and pulmonary function parameters. Younger age, female gender, and lower lung function (FEV1, DLCO, KCO) were associated with higher anxiety scores, while prior hospitalization and post-inflammatory chest changes were associated with lower anxiety.

A case series of 47 long COVID patients presenting with chronic venous insufficiency symptoms (edema, pain, varicose changes) in the post-infection period. Treatment with diosmin-based venotonic drug at 1000 mg/day for 1-2 months resulted in edema subsidence in 85% and pain reduction in most patients.

Retrospective analysis of COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between obesity, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and disease severity, with 71% showing elevated transaminases. A multicomponent drug therapy containing inosine, meglumine, methionine, nicotinamide and succinic acid was associated with improved transaminase levels and clinical course in severe COVID-19 patients.

This retrospective cohort study compared post-acute healthcare costs between SARS-CoV-2 test-positive and test-negative adults in Ontario over one year of follow-up. The study found significantly higher healthcare costs among test-positive individuals ($459-$514 mean difference), driven primarily by hospitalizations, long-term care, and specialist visits, demonstrating the substantial economic burden of post-acute COVID-19.

Retrospective analysis of 441 children with acute COVID-19 to characterize kidney involvement, finding renal dysfunction in 12.9% of cases ranging from proteinuria to acute kidney injury. This study focuses on acute COVID-19 manifestations in children rather than long COVID sequelae.

Prospective study of 52 patients with lung damage >50% assessed 12 weeks post-COVID-19, examining clinical features and severity by BMI status. Found that obesity was associated with worse respiratory outcomes, including higher rates of shortness of breath and cough, and greater lung function impairment.

A prospective observational study comparing retinal vessel and corneal endothelium alterations between acute and post-COVID-19 phases in 50 patients. The study found significant improvements in retinal hemorrhage, vessel tortuosity, and corneal cell density post-infection, highlighting ocular complications of COVID-19.

This study compares acute pyelonephritis outcomes in children with and without prior COVID-19 history, examining renal damage markers and long-term kidney function. While it documents post-COVID renal sequelae, it is not a treatment trial—it is a comparative observational study of infection complications rather than an intervention study.

This cross-sectional study compared clinical and demographic characteristics of 23 rheumatoid arthritis patients stratified by post-COVID syndrome (PCS) status, examining the intersection of RA and PCS. The study found that 47.8% of RA patients developed PCS, with higher RA activity and disease severity correlating with increased likelihood of PCS development, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

This cross-sectional study compared 21 long COVID patients with neurological symptoms to 13 controls with underlying neurological conditions, examining clinical manifestations and predictive factors for post-COVID syndrome. Results identified age >40, moderate-severe acute infection, cardiovascular risk, depression, anxiety, and central sensitization as significant predictors of long COVID development.

An observational case series evaluating the efficacy and safety of Alflutop (bioactive concentrate from sea fish) in 50 post-COVID patients with lower back pain and osteoarthritis. Treatment led to pronounced pain relief by day 14, with 80% of patients remaining pain-free at 2-month follow-up without notable laboratory changes.

Retrospective analysis of 100 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with lung injury, assessing prevalence of fatigue syndrome using the Fatigue Assessment Scale and identifying risk factors. Study documents that 66% of patients had objectively measured fatigue, with associations to obesity, infection severity, and comorbidities, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective-prospective study compared recovery patterns in 81 patients across three groups: ischemic stroke with COVID-19, COVID-19 alone, and stroke without COVID-19. While it examines post-acute complications of COVID-associated stroke, it does not study long COVID (persistent multisystem symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study examining clinical and laboratory features of post-COVID syndrome in 120 children aged 7-18, comparing 29 children with post-COVID syndrome to 91 without. The study found asthenic reactions (24%), cognitive deterioration (14%), and respiratory effects (17%) as common manifestations, but reports only medical supervision and expectant care rather than a specific treatment intervention.

This study examined surfactant protein-D (SP-D) as a biomarker in 70 patients with severe COVID-19-related lung damage, measuring respiratory function and SP-D levels at 3 and 12 months post-acute infection. The findings show that 57% of patients had persistent impaired lung diffusion capacity at 12 months, with elevated SP-D levels associated with worse lung function, proposing SP-D as a potential biomarker of post-COVID lung injury severity.

Prospective observational study of 63 patients at 6-month post-COVID follow-up examining cardiovascular complications during recovery. Found reduced left ventricular ejection fraction in moderate/severe COVID cases, recommending NT Pro BNP and echocardiography monitoring during follow-up.

This retrospective cohort study of 164 post-COVID patients identified persistent symptoms in 86%, with neuropsychiatric symptoms (42.7%) and respiratory symptoms (26.8%) being most common. The study characterized symptom patterns and severity associations but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This paper examines the effects of COVID-19 infection on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) over a three-year follow-up period. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 severity in CKD patients rather than long COVID sequelae.

A longitudinal quasi-experimental study assessing the prevalence of functional health limitations among 65 postgraduate students with post-COVID-19 syndrome before and after an instructional rehabilitation module. The study found that 52.3% of students severely suffered from post-COVID diagnosis with significant functional limitations, and showed improvement in rehabilitation outcomes following the instructional intervention.

Retrospective study of 72 post-COVID-19 patients comparing chest CT scans at baseline and 3-month follow-up to evaluate pulmonary sequelae and fibrosis development. While the study observes pulmonary changes, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is purely observational imaging assessment without therapeutic evaluation.

This paper compares cardiac arrhythmia parameters in STEMI patients with prior COVID-19 (1.5-6 months prior) versus those without COVID-19 history. While it examines post-COVID cardiac complications, it focuses on acute myocardial infarction management rather than long COVID as the primary condition being studied or treated.

This observational cross-sectional study assessed cardiopulmonary parameters (heart rate, O2 saturation, VO2 max) among 90 long COVID patients stratified by BMI using the 12-minute walk test. The study found that COVID-19 has similar effects on cardiopulmonary parameters across different BMI categories.

Retrospective study of 95 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining acute neurological presentations and long-term sequelae over 4-5 months of follow-up. Found that 63% had acute neurological manifestations and 83% of the most severe patients (those ventilated) developed neurological sequelae, but the study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study examines ferroptosis markers in 127 hospitalized COVID-19 patients stratified by oxygen therapy intensity, with 3-month telephone follow-up to assess long COVID development. The authors identify low baseline SLC7A11 (a ferroptosis marker) as a potential risk indicator for long COVID but do not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal study measuring biochemical and metabolic parameters in 470 COVID-19 patients across three time points (during hospitalization, 1 month, 3 months post-infection) stratified by disease severity. Findings show that multiple markers (glucose, urea, creatinine, liver enzymes) remain abnormal at 3 months in some individuals, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective cohort study comparing renal parenchymal stiffness between 92 post-long COVID-19 patients and healthy controls using strain wave elastography. The study found significantly elevated renal elastographic values in post-long COVID patients, suggesting that COVID-19 may cause renal stiffness as a systemic late effect.

A retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up examining malnutrition risk, sleep quality, and physical activity in 103 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in Saudi Arabia between 2021-2023. The study found worsening malnutrition risk and poor sleep quality in malnourished patients, with findings emphasizing the need for multidisciplinary rehabilitation programs integrating nutritional support and exercise.

Retrospective study of 138 mild COVID-19 patients examining salivary gland pathologies and the effects of various treatments including antivirals, moisturizing agents, antibiotics, saliva substitutes, photobiomodulation, and massage. Found statistically significant xerostomia, ectasia, and sialadenitis with treatments showing variable effectiveness in managing post-COVID oral complications.

Prospective cohort study following 50 severe COVID-19 ICU survivors for 6 months post-discharge to assess long-term complications and recovery. Found that clinical symptoms, laboratory markers, and radiological findings (ground glass opacities, consolidation) significantly improved by 6 months, with most parameters returning to normal range.

Prospective cohort study of 76 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 3 months post-discharge to characterize residual symptoms and their association with clinical factors. Found ~70% experienced post-COVID symptoms with decreased quality of life, but this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This prospective cohort study followed 76 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for up to 3 months post-discharge to identify biomarkers and factors associated with post-COVID-19 symptoms. The study found elevated IL-6 levels persisted in symptomatic patients and identified risk factors (age >50, critical illness) but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines acne exacerbation in 211 subjects following COVID-19 infection, identifying risk factors such as acne itch and daily physical exercise. While related to post-COVID sequelae, the paper focuses on acne outcomes rather than long COVID treatment or intervention, making it outside the scope of long COVID clinical trials.

This cross-sectional study evaluated chest CT findings in 52 COVID-19 pneumonia patients at an average of 43 days post-hospital discharge, stratifying them by lung abnormality severity. Elderly severe/critical patients with comorbidities showed higher rates of early fibrosis development, while younger patients with common COVID-19 demonstrated complete lung inflammation resolution.

Retrospective analysis of 127 COVID-19 patients examining long-term volumetric and radiological changes in lung anatomy using CT scans and 3D segmentation. Study found significant improvements in left lung volume and severity scores over time, but persistent pathological findings (interstitial thickening, fibrotic bands) particularly in elderly patients, with recommendations for antifibrotic therapies.

This cross-sectional observational study evaluated the manifestation of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and orthostatic hypotension (OH) in 60 patients recovered from severe/critical COVID-19, measuring blood pressure and heart rate at discharge and 2 months later. The study found that 65% of patients had OH or POTS at discharge, with most recovering within 2 months, characterizing this as an aspect of long COVID.

This study compared chest X-ray changes between post-COVID-19 patients with mild-moderate versus severe-critical severity at a long COVID clinic, assessing radiological findings at hospital admission, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks using the Brixia Score method. No interventions or treatments were administered; it is a purely observational imaging comparison study without treatment evaluation.

Prospective cohort study following 157 long COVID patients stratified by comorbidity risk for one year to examine neurological complications and disease associations. Found associations between oxygen saturation, inflammatory markers, comorbidities, and anticoagulant treatment outcomes, suggesting primary care monitoring approaches for long COVID sequelae.

Observational cohort study of 130 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for one year to assess lung function and health status outcomes. Found that lung function remained in lower normal limits at one-year follow-up regardless of initial disease severity, with no significant differences in health scales between ICU, high-flow oxygen, and standard oxygen groups.

This cross-sectional study examined oral cavity manifestations in 33 post-COVID patients, identifying candidal stomatitis, lichen planus, and periodontal damage as common findings. While it documents clinical observations of post-COVID oral pathology, it does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study of 157 COVID-19 patients (August 2021-August 2023) evaluates the efficacy and safety of anticoagulant therapies (VKA vs DOACs) in managing long-term post-COVID complications including thromboembolic disease. The study documents significant increases in cardiomyopathies (3.9%), joint diseases (14%), and psychoanxiety disorders (39.5%), with DOACs showing increased adoption in high-risk patients, suggesting personalized treatment strategies are needed.

A nationwide multicenter cohort study of 1,040 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized during the Alpha- and Delta-variant waves in Japan, examining post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) prevalence and associated mental health outcomes at 1-year follow-up. Found 45.4% had at least one PCC symptom, with dyspnea, fatigue, and muscle weakness most common; patients with PCC showed four times higher anxiety and depression rates than those without PCC.

Retrospective assessment of COVID-19 and post-COVID course in 89 children across different age groups in Samara, comparing severity, symptom patterns, and recovery duration by age. No intervention or treatment was tested; this is a passive observational study examining natural disease course without treatment assignment.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating long-term renal function outcomes (GFR, creatinine, BUN) in COVID-19 survivors at a minimum of 6 months post-recovery. Found significant changes in creatinine and GFR levels, particularly in patients with hypertension, diabetes, or female gender.

A web-based follow-up study examining fatigue severity in 239 long COVID patients from online support groups at two timepoints (10 and 23 weeks post-infection). The study documents persistent severe fatigue and distinguishes between physical and mental fatigue components, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective study of 112 COVID-19 patients monitored for ~1 year post-discharge to identify predictors of atrial fibrillation development in the long-term period. Found that age ≥60, male gender, smoking, reduced GFR, and poor psychological health were significant risk factors for AF development.

This study analyzed 2,213 longitudinal Reddit posts from 292 COVID-19 patients to identify and track physiological and psychological symptoms before and after recovery. The findings document the evolution of symptoms over time, showing that psychological symptoms like brain fog and fatigue persist longer as post-COVID sequelae, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A single-arm feasibility study evaluating self-administered virtual reality exercises at home for post-COVID-19 condition in 48 patients over 6 weeks. Virtual reality was found to be feasible and safe with significant improvements in physical performance and quality of life, though adverse events (mainly dizziness) occurred in 70% of participants.

This study develops a clinical phenotype for identifying long COVID patients in routine primary care data using a nationally representative UK cohort of 7.4 million patients. It is a retrospective database analysis comparing symptom patterns before and after COVID-19 infection, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal observational study assessing prevalence of PTSD, anxiety, and depression symptoms in long COVID patients at 3 and 6 months post-symptom onset. Found that 26.8-46.9% of patients reported significant psychological symptoms with minimal improvement over time and comparable rates between hospitalized and nonhospitalized groups.

This observational study compared sleep patterns between 122 long COVID patients and 588 controls using wearable devices, finding that long COVID patients had significantly decreased light sleep and deep sleep duration. The study characterizes sleep architecture changes in long COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study uses routine primary care data to compare clinical presentations of long COVID in people infected in hospital versus community settings, and examines all-cause mortality rates. It is a retrospective observational analysis of existing health records without any treatment intervention, focusing on symptom documentation patterns and mortality associations rather than evaluating a therapeutic intervention.

Prospective observational cohort study of 120 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors followed at 2 and 6 weeks post-discharge to characterize post-COVID-19 symptoms and identify risk factors. Found 60.8% had persistent symptoms at 6 weeks, with fatigue most common; female sex and steroid use were significant risk factors, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cohort study evaluated outcomes of 81 workers who participated in an occupational rehabilitation program for long COVID, measuring return-to-work status and changes in symptom severity scales. Only 53% returned to work (mostly to modified duties), with modest improvements in pain and psychological measures, but no significant improvement in functional capacity or PTSD symptoms.

Prospective observational study of 122 COVID-19 patients using wearable devices to monitor biometric data and assess compliance with continuous monitoring. Age was the primary determinant of compliance with wearables, with older patients showing better adherence to the monitoring protocol.

Observational study analyzing changes in medical imaging utilization and clinical findings during the COVID-19 pandemic in Israeli healthcare. Found increased abnormal findings in brain CT and musculoskeletal MR exams associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 hospitalization, suggesting post-acute COVID syndrome may contribute to these findings.

This study uses Veterans Affairs ICD-10-CM data from 367,148 patients to develop a data-driven case definition of long COVID, identifying 323 diagnosis codes grouped into 143 functional groups and 17 medical-specialty subtypes. The analysis characterizes risk factors (age, comorbidities, COVID-19 severity) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This bidirectional cohort study evaluates antibody durability after COVID-19 booster doses and protective effects against post-COVID symptoms in 327 Chinese participants. While it documents associations between antibody levels and some post-COVID symptoms like brain fog and sleep quality, it is not a treatment intervention trial—it evaluates vaccine effects on symptom outcomes without assigning any therapeutic intervention to long COVID patients.

A prospective observational cohort study evaluating the feasibility and acceptability of a remote monitoring system using wearables and home-based spirometry in 60 patients with chronic respiratory diseases and post-COVID-19 condition over 180 days. The study demonstrates that passive wearable data collection had superior adherence compared to active monitoring methods, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This multicenter registry study evaluates hyperbaric oxygen (HBO2) treatment for emerging indications including post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), with 149 of 378 emerging indication cases being PCC patients. Results show statistically significant improvements in PCC patients on the Neurobehavioral Symptom Inventory and quality of life measures.

This quality improvement study evaluated a specialist telephone consultation line (RACE line) for long COVID support in British Columbia primary care, analyzing 143 calls between August 2020 and June 2021. The study characterized patient demographics, common clinical queries, and symptom patterns (respiratory, fatigue, neurological) but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study analyzing healthcare resource use in 68,822 French patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19 during 2020, comparing pre- and post-discharge utilization patterns over 6 months. Found high mortality (23%) and increased outpatient care across multiple domains post-discharge, but without specificity to PACS and lacking confounding adjustment.

This retrospective cohort study examines the long-term risk of accidental injuries in SARS survivors and their relatives in Taiwan over 15 years, finding significantly elevated hazard ratios for various injury types. Although it studies post-infection sequelae, it focuses on SARS (2003), not long COVID (SARS-CoV-2), and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective study of 500 COVID-19 patients followed for at least six months post-recovery to evaluate treatment of severe headaches occurring after acute infection. Phenytoin added to standard analgesics (ibuprofen/acetaminophen) achieved 80% headache control in refractory cases compared to 60% with analgesics alone.

Prospective observational cohort study examining longitudinal patterns of physical activity, physiology, and patient-reported outcomes in 82 long COVID patients using Fitbit devices over 6 months. Found that physically inactive patients reported worse symptoms and declining social functioning, suggesting activity profiles should inform personalized treatment approaches.

Retrospective longitudinal study of 1,762 nursing staff in Iran documenting long-term COVID-19 complications over one year. Reports 64.3% incidence of complications including respiratory issues, pain, anosmia, and ageusia, with higher rates in women and younger staff—but is observational (passive follow-up) rather than a treatment intervention study.

Retrospective chart review of 84 pediatric patients with neurological symptoms following COVID-19 infection, meeting long COVID criteria, admitted to a tertiary center from December 2020 to end of 2021 with one-year follow-up. Most common manifestations were headache (55.95%), dizziness (22.6%), and visual disturbances (10.7%), with 22.6% requiring psychological support, but no specific treatment intervention was tested.

A prospective cohort study of 78 COVID-19 ICU survivors followed for 20 months post-discharge, assessing depression, anxiety, health anxiety, sleep quality, and cognitive abilities alongside inflammatory biomarkers (ESR, CRP, NLR, ferritin, D-dimer). The study found high prevalence of mental health problems and poor sleep quality, with D-dimer independently associated with cognitive impairment, though inflammatory markers from the acute phase did not fully explain long-term neuropsychological impairments.

This study evaluates the accuracy and utility of the ICD-10 U09.9 code for identifying long COVID patients across three health systems by validating it against WHO and CDC definitions through chart review. The analysis found that the U09.9 code has variable sensitivity (23.2-62.4%) across health systems and provides methodological recommendations for EHR-based long COVID case identification.

Retrospective analysis of joint pain and large joint pathologies as long-term complications of COVID-19, comparing two cohorts at 2 months and 2 years post-infection. Study identifies correlations between arthralgia and pulmonary insufficiency, immunoprophylactic agents, and antiviral medications, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional cohort study examined post-COVID-19 complications in 986 recovered patients 2-3 months after infection by collecting questionnaire responses and laboratory findings. The study identified chest pain (45.6%), headache (32.4%), and abnormalities in liver enzymes, renal function, and LDH levels as predominant long-term complications, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This retrospective cohort study using EHR data from 59 U.S. health systems examines the bidirectional association between chronic kidney disease (CKD) and long COVID among patients with acute COVID-19 from 2021-2023. It finds that baseline CKD increases risk of long COVID, and conversely, long COVID is associated with incident CKD and faster kidney function decline.

This longitudinal cohort study compared cognitive and functional decline in elderly Alzheimer's patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection over four years, using biomarker analysis and machine learning. While it examines long-term neurological effects of COVID-19, it does not focus on long COVID syndrome itself and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study comparing sleep quality in 137 post-COVID patients with a history of acute ischemic stroke versus 80 controls with stroke but no COVID-19 infection. Results show post-COVID patients report more 'extremely poor' sleep quality and similar overall Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, with findings suggesting COVID-19 may exacerbate sleep disorders and potentially trigger restless legs syndrome in stroke survivors.

This cross-sectional study compares cytokine and proteolytic enzyme levels in plasma between 56 patients with chronic cerebral ischemia (CCI) who had prior COVID-19 and 52 CCI patients without COVID-19 history. The study found gender-specific differences in IL-1, MMP levels, and proteolytic balance between groups, but does not represent a long COVID study as it focuses on CCI as the primary condition rather than post-COVID sequelae.

This study evaluates the effect of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy on cardiovascular risk markers (homocysteine and ST2) in type 2 diabetic patients during the post-COVID period over 9-12 months of follow-up. SGLT2i treatment showed significant reduction in both homocysteine and ST2 levels compared to standard metformin/sulfonylurea therapy, suggesting improved cardiovascular outcomes in post-COVID diabetic patients.

A prospective follow-up study examining D-dimer levels in post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) patients at admission, discharge, and 3 and 6 months post-discharge. Found persistently elevated D-dimer values correlating with PASC persistence, suggesting D-dimer may serve as a biomarker for long COVID.

A prospective cohort study following 116 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 6 months to assess prevalence of persistent symptoms and pulmonary impairments. Found that 46.6% reported persistent symptoms and 28.4% showed residual disease on chest CT, but no significant long-term pulmonary function deficits.

This study compared hemostatic parameters in 60 chronic cerebral ischemia (CCI) patients with prior COVID-19 versus 40 CCI patients without COVID-19 history, measuring seven coagulation markers via ELISA. While no treatment was tested, the study found persistent post-COVID hemostatic changes including elevated thrombomodulin (20.9%) and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (19.4%) in the COVID-exposed group, suggesting low-grade inflammation and fibrinolysis inhibition in late post-COVID period.

Retrospective observational study examining the incidence of newly-developed and uncontrolled diabetes mellitus in COVID-19 patients during follow-up at a tertiary care hospital. Found 0.195% incidence of newly-diagnosed DM and 13.33% incidence of uncontrolled DM, with older age and male sex as risk factors, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A prospective observational survey examining post-COVID-19 manifestations in 85% of subjects, with fatigue (56.36%), body ache (43.3%), and myalgia (36.81%) as the most common symptoms. The study identifies associations between post-COVID manifestations and disease severity and comorbidities.

This retrospective cohort study measures SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG antibody levels in 54 COVID-19 patients at 8 months post-symptom onset and identifies predictors of antibody persistence. While the paper studies long-term post-infection immunity, it does not focus on long COVID persistent symptoms and does not test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional clinical assessment of 130 post-COVID patients in Russia examining neuropsychiatric manifestations, cognitive function, and laboratory parameters. Study characterizes symptom prevalence and associations but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective cohort study following 252 COVID-19 patients in Kyrgyzstan over 12-96 weeks to characterize post-COVID syndrome manifestations and their relationship to viral strain and acute phase severity. The study documents symptom prevalence but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for long COVID.

This cohort study characterized symptoms and clinical manifestations in 892 long COVID patients referred to recovery clinics in British Columbia using standardized assessment tools. The most common symptoms were shortness of breath (85.9%), fatigue (75.7%), and weakness (56.1%), with phenotypes varying by infection wave and vaccination status.

A hospital-based retro-prospective study of 210 post-COVID patients assessing long-term complications and their impact on quality of life. 77% of patients used nutritional supplements to manage fatigue, and 52% reported depression during or after acute infection.

This retrospective cohort study compares the impact of Delta vs Omicron COVID-19 strains on lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). While all COVID-infected patients showed worsening LUTS, the paper does not study long COVID (persistent post-infection sequelae) but rather acute COVID-19 effects during active infection periods, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of COVID-19 ICU survivors followed at 6 months and 1 year post-discharge, measuring health-related quality of life via SF-36 questionnaire. While this tracks long-term outcomes in ICU survivors, it is not about long COVID specifically (does not study persistent long COVID symptoms) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined cardiac rhythm and conduction disorders in children 3-12 months post-COVID-19 using Holter ECG monitoring. High prevalence of various arrhythmias (sinus tachycardia 35%, ventricular extrasystoles 35%) and conduction disorders were documented, with QTc prolongation observed in 40.2% of pediatric patients.

Retrospective chart review of 806 long COVID patients at Post-COVID Recovery Clinics examining D-Dimer elevation and VTE incidence ≥90 days post-infection. Found 30.3% had elevated D-Dimer but only 1.1% were diagnosed with new VTE, suggesting D-Dimer is often elevated but new thromboembolism is rare in long COVID recovery.

Prospective observational study of 74 COVID-19 hospitalized patients evaluated two months post-discharge to characterize persistent symptoms and their associated factors. Found 54.8% had persistent symptoms (primarily fatigue and dyspnea), but study is descriptive only without any treatment intervention or control group.

Retrospective observational cohort study comparing clinical and immunological characteristics of COVID-19 in children aged 8-18 years during acute infection and 152 days post-illness. Study found persistent immunological abnormalities in the long-term period, particularly immune deficiency patterns requiring monitoring, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective analysis of 106 children's medical records examining lymphocyte dynamics during acute COVID-19 treatment. Identifies persistent lymphopenia despite clinical improvement as a potential risk marker for post-COVID reactions, but does not test any intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 329 Singapore Navy divers who recovered from COVID-19, assessing post-infection complications and diving-related injuries. Found no clinical or subclinical complications in this fully vaccinated, low-risk population with asymptomatic or mild COVID-19, with no diving-related injuries after recovery.

This cross-sectional study followed 116 COVID-19 survivors at least 4 weeks post-infection to characterize persistent symptoms and their correlations with CT imaging severity and laboratory findings. 52.5% of patients reported persistent symptoms (dyspnea, chest pain, cough, fatigue, etc.), with CT severity scores associated with symptom presence and certain laboratory abnormalities.

topics: insulin resistance|metabolic risk factors|long COVID predictors
summary: This retrospective cohort study from Stanford examined metabolic predictors of acute COVID-19 severity and long COVID development in 596 COVID-19 patients. The analysis found that insulin resistance (measured by triglyceride/HDL ratio) was independently associated with long COVID risk, but this is a retrospective analysis of existing EMR data, not a treatment trial.

This nationwide Korean cohort study investigates the incidence of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus in the post-acute phase of COVID-19 using health insurance data. The study finds that COVID-19 patients have significantly elevated risk of developing T2DM compared to matched controls, with risk increasing by acute severity.

This study compares metabolic health outcomes in type 2 diabetes patients with and without recent COVID-19 history, finding increased hepatic lipid content in COVID-positive participants. It is not a long COVID study as it focuses on acute/recent COVID infection in diabetic populations rather than long COVID syndrome, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study using the National COVID Cohort Collaborative examines the association between acute hyperglycemia during COVID-19 hospitalization and incident cardiovascular disease outcomes post-discharge in 5.2 million U.S. patients. While focused on COVID-19 hospitalization, the paper does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection) but rather acute hospitalization outcomes and immediate post-discharge cardiovascular complications.

topics: rehabilitation|functional outcomes|motor function|cognitive function|activities of daily living
summary: Observational cohort study of 61 post-acute COVID-19 patients receiving customized inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation treatment, examining whether acute disease severity predicts rehabilitation outcomes. Patients showed significant functional improvement with 88% weaning off oxygen, with acute severity affecting admission status but not discharge outcomes, indicating rehabilitation benefit regardless of initial disease severity.

This retrospective cohort study examines the association between prevalent metformin use and long COVID (PASC) incidence in adults with type 2 diabetes using EHR data from N3C and PCORnet databases. Results show metformin use is associated with a slightly lower incidence of death or PASC, with PASC incidence ranging from 1.6-2.1% in metformin users versus 2.0-2.5% in non-metformin diabetes medication users.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study examining the prevalence and trajectories of neuropsychological symptoms in 184 initially hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 9 and 15 months post-discharge. Found high prevalence of cognitive complaints (50%) and fatigue (52.5-55.6%), with most symptoms remaining stable and 31.5% developing delayed-onset symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Ambispective cohort study comparing post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) prevalence in COVID-19 ICU survivors from the first and second pandemic waves at 6-month follow-up. Found PICS in ~51-52% of patients regardless of wave or improved ICU management, with female sex and diabetes as risk factors; this is an observational follow-up study with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

Retrospective observational study of 779 post-COVID-19 patients evaluating a multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme, with some patients receiving additional respiratory muscle training. The programme showed significant improvements in 6-minute walk test distance, quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), and psychological distress (PHQ-4), with interaction effects suggesting differential benefit between groups.

This case-control study compared cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) outcomes in 13 elite cross-country skiers who recovered from mild-moderate COVID-19 versus 13 matched detrained controls. COVID-affected athletes showed earlier aerobic threshold onset but comparable peak exercise parameters, suggesting transient exercise deconditioning without persistent cardiac or pulmonary impairment.

Observational study examining the relationship between heart rate and physical activity levels in 16 people with post-COVID-19 condition using wearable devices over 4 days. Found that tachycardia paradoxically occurred more during sedentary periods than during moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, even after accounting for ME/CFS symptoms.

Prospective cohort study tracking physical activity recovery in 993 COVID-19 survivors over up to 23 months post-infection. While the study documents that habitual pre-infection physical activity reduced hospitalization risk but not long COVID incidence, it is observational with no intervention—participants were followed to assess their natural recovery patterns rather than receiving any treatment.

Prospective cohort study following 212 COVID-19 patients (122 hospitalized, 90 non-hospitalized) for 12 months to assess prevalence and changes in fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and activity limitations. Found persistent cognitive and fatigue deficits at 12-month follow-up with significant impact on daily-life activities, but no intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed psychological symptoms (PTSD, depression, anxiety, distress) in 163 Italian COVID-19 outpatients at 3-month follow-up, stratified by ventilatory support during acute infection. Patients reported significantly higher depression and anxiety than normative groups, particularly those who experienced COVID-19 as traumatic.

An observational cohort study of 23 patients who received multi-disciplinary inpatient rehabilitation after severe COVID-19. The study found significant improvements in lung function, diffusion capacity, and six-minute walking distance following rehabilitation, though many patients retained residual symptoms at discharge.

Prospective cohort study of 92 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors followed at discharge, 4 months, and 1 year to assess long-term functional status and rehabilitation needs in Greece. While documenting persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, pain, cognitive impairment) and poor rehabilitation service utilization, the study is observational without any intervention assignment and does not evaluate a treatment.

Retrospective study of 41 postacute COVID-19 patients who received inpatient motor and respiratory rehabilitation, evaluating functional outcomes via Barthel Index, 6-Minute Walking Test, and dyspnea scales. While the study shows rehabilitation improved functional outcomes in acute postacute COVID patients, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months after infection) but rather on acute postinfection recovery during the immediate rehabilitation phase.

topics: pulmonary rehabilitation|fatigue|quality of life|occupational outcomes|symptom improvement
summary: Longitudinal observational study examining pulmonary rehabilitation outcomes in 306 long COVID patients (inpatient vs follow-up rehabilitation groups) over 12 months. Most COVID-19 symptoms and fatigue improved significantly during rehabilitation with medium to large effect sizes, and improvements largely persisted one year later, with over 80% of employed participants returning to work.

This cross-sectional study compared cytokine profiles in osteoarthritis patients 6-9 months post-COVID-19 infection versus healthy controls. The study found imbalanced pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines in post-COVID OA patients but did not test any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 104 COVID-19 patients for one year to evaluate recovery of respiratory function and functional capacity. Patients showed progressive improvement in pulmonary function and 6-minute walk test distance by 6-12 months, with no correlation between improvement and physical activity levels.

Retrospective cohort study examining the relationship between post-COVID-19 syndrome and insulin resistance in 112 non-diabetic outpatients followed at baseline, 3 months, and 21 months post-infection. The study found that PCS was associated with increased insulin resistance, particularly in those with low baseline IR, with both conditions linked to elevated inflammatory markers.

This paper describes the establishment and methods of a multidisciplinary COVID-19 follow-up outpatient clinic to assess long-term consequences in survivors. It presents the clinic's assessment protocol and initial patient characteristics but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

A prospective cohort study comparing the prevalence of persistent post-COVID symptoms between older and younger adults at 6-8 weeks and 6-12 months post-infection. The study found that older adults experienced lower prevalence of dyspnoea, depression, anxiety, fatigue, and PTSD symptoms compared to younger adults at both timepoints.

Retrospective population-based cohort study examining consultation rates for long COVID, post-viral fatigue syndrome, and fatigue in English children using primary care data from 2006-2023. While about long COVID, this is a descriptive epidemiological study documenting consultation trends rather than evaluating any intervention or treatment.

This longitudinal prospective cohort study followed 192 COVID-19 patients over one year to identify risk factors and characteristics associated with Ongoing Symptomatic COVID-19 (persistent symptoms beyond 4 weeks). The study found a 17% incidence rate, with older age, severe respiratory symptoms, hospitalization, and chronic diseases as significant risk factors, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 3.5 million Welsh residents to assess the clinical coding and prevalence of long COVID in primary and secondary care. The study found only 0.2% had a LC diagnosis code recorded, highlighting significant underreporting and variation in clinical coding practices across primary care practices.

This retrospective cohort study assessed risk factors for residual pulmonary complications in 97 COVID-19 patients with severe ARDS at 6 weeks post-discharge, stratified by extent of lung involvement. The study identified associations between lack of dexamethasone use, prone positioning, and HFNC with worse radiological and functional outcomes, but represents a secondary analysis of hospitalized acute-phase treatment rather than a prospective trial of post-COVID interventions.

topics: long-term outcomes|quality of life|ICU survivors|respiratory function
summary: A retrospective cohort study evaluating 1-year survival, quality of life, and functional recovery in 268 COVID-19 patients discharged after invasive ventilation in Lombardy. The study found 99% one-year survival rate and good overall recovery, but does not test any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study using NHS Wales health records to describe sequelae in post-COVID patients across three SARS-CoV-2 variants (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) over 2-3 years of follow-up. Uses Cox proportional hazard regression to assess how time since acute infection and deprivation affect post-viral disease risk, finding Alpha wave had greatest disease burden and deprivation is a major risk factor.

An ambispective cohort study following 173 Spanish patients from October 2020 to May 2023 to determine the prevalence of long COVID two years post-infection and identify prognostic factors. Long COVID was observed in 32.36% of participants, with fatigue and anosmia/dysgeusia as the most frequent symptoms; higher initial infection severity, younger age, and reinfection were significant prognostic factors.

Retrospective cohort study examining associations between pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in Brazilian adults aged ≥60 years at three-month follow-up. Found that diabetes, smoking, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia were significantly associated with higher likelihood of PASC, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compares 431 patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD) diagnosed before versus after COVID-19 infection to identify predictors of disease progression during the post-COVID period. While it studies a post-COVID complication, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it only observes and compares disease outcomes in two patient groups based on CAD onset timing.

This paper describes long COVID symptoms and work ability outcomes in 53 hospitalized healthcare workers followed 18 months post-infection using questionnaire data from an occupational health surveillance program. It documents symptom persistence and fitness-to-work restrictions but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study followed 328 COVID-19 survivors with moderate-to-severe pneumonia for 12 months to identify biomarkers and predictors of long-term cardiovascular complications. The study found that elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and D-dimer levels were key predictors of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, with predictive models achieving 93% accuracy for risk stratification.

This paper analyzes long COVID symptom patterns across different SARS-CoV-2 variants (Wuhan, Delta, Omicron) using existing hospital data from Japan. It documents symptom prevalence, duration, and improvement over time by demographics and variant, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 328 post-COVID patients followed for 12 months to evaluate cardiovascular complications and identify prognostic risk factors. Found CV complications in 31.4% of patients, with elevated NLR, CRP, and D-dimer as significant biomarkers for predicting cardiovascular outcomes.

Prospective cohort study examining coagulation abnormalities in 50 pregnant women with post-COVID syndrome compared to 25 uninfected controls between 30-34 weeks of gestation. Found significant increases in fibrinogen and D-dimer levels and reduced platelet counts in post-COVID pregnant women, suggesting SARS-CoV-2 induces a hypercoagulable state in pregnancy.

This retrospective cohort study examines healthcare and rehabilitation service utilization among COVID-19 patients in Ontario, Canada, using administrative health data from 2020-2021. The paper focuses on acute-phase hospitalization and immediate post-acute rehabilitation services rather than long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months after infection.

A prospective population-based study in Delhi tracking post-COVID-19 symptoms in 11 districts with follow-ups at 3 and 6 months post-infection. Found that 79.7% of recovered COVID-19 patients reported persistent symptoms lasting up to 6 months, with joint pain (36.0%), dry cough (35.7%), and anxiety (28.4%) being most common.

This observational study measured angiotensin II (AT-II) and ACE2 activity in 122 adults one year after COVID-19, comparing those with and without cardiovascular complications. Patients with cardiac complications showed significantly elevated AT-II and reduced ACE2 activity, suggesting a persistent angiotensin system imbalance may contribute to post-COVID cardiovascular dysfunction.

This study evaluated pain, fatigue, anxiety, depression, and quality of life in 100 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during acute infection, with follow-ups at 1 and 3 months. It is an observational cohort study with no treatment intervention—patients were passively followed to assess natural symptom trajectories and associations with baseline severity.

A prospective observational cohort study of 184 COVID-19 survivors in South Kerala followed monthly for six months post-recovery to characterize the prevalence and clinical characteristics of long COVID complications. The study found that 69% experienced post-COVID complications at one month, declining to 22.8% by six months, with fatigue being the most common symptom.

A prospective observational study examining pulmonary function tests (spirometry and TL,CO) in 30 long-COVID patients at 1 and 3 months post-hospitalization to identify non-improvers and prognostic factors. FEV1 was found to accurately predict clinical improvement, but this is a descriptive/prognostic cohort study without a treatment intervention.

This study examined the effect of acute COVID-19 infection on static balance performance in professional handball players using a modified Romberg test. The authors found that players who contracted COVID-19 showed a significant decrease in balance ability post-infection compared to their pre-infection baseline, while uninfected players showed no change.

A cross-sectional study evaluating the effects of a 3-week pulmonary rehabilitation programme on 80 post-COVID patients at a Croatian hospital clinic. Results showed significant improvements in respiratory muscle strength, six-minute walk test parameters, and lung function metrics (FVC, FEV1, DLCO) with effect sizes ranging from small to large.

A prospective longitudinal study classifying symptoms of acute and chronic COVID-19 into clinical syndromes in a high-altitude population during the first and second pandemic waves. The study found that 64.55% of participants developed post-COVID-19 syndrome with high frequency of neurological symptoms, suggesting that hypobaric hypoxia may prolong inflammation and worsen post-COVID sequelae.

This retrospective observational study followed 34 severe COVID-19 ICU survivors for up to 26 months post-discharge to characterize long COVID sequelae, focusing on respiratory symptoms, pulmonary function, and imaging findings. While documenting the natural history and burden of post-COVID symptoms, the study does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Retrospective study assessing the incidence and associations of post-COVID syndrome among 202 patients discharged from a New Delhi hospital, finding 64.25% incidence with fatigue and body pain as most common symptoms. Study identifies significant associations between post-COVID syndrome and comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases) and demographic factors (smoking, alcohol use, vaccination status).

A prospective cohort study of 67 long COVID patients in Mexico that assessed pulmonary abnormalities using chest CT imaging at 6-30 months post-infection. Found high prevalence of persistent radiological findings (interstitial thickening 61%, ground-glass opacity 45%, bronchiectasis 19%) that showed decreasing trend over time, with hypertension as the most significant predictor.

This study assessed mental health outcomes (PTSD, anxiety, depression) in 186 COVID-19 survivors three months after hospital discharge, identifying female gender and psychiatric history as risk factors. While the paper documents increased psychological symptoms in COVID-19 survivors, it is an observational cross-sectional assessment with no treatment intervention tested.

This retrospective cohort study assessed sleep quality changes in Mexican adults over 60 years comparing pre-pandemic and post-pandemic periods (June 2021-August 2022). While it documents worsening sleep quality and increased alcohol/vitamin consumption post-COVID, it is a passive observational study with no intervention tested, making it ineligible for the treatment trials pipeline.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study of 200 COVID-19 survivors investigating immunopathological mechanisms of long COVID over 12 months, including immune markers, autoantibodies, lymphocyte function, and imaging findings. Key findings include persistent inflammation (elevated IL-6 and TNF-α), autoantibodies in 40% of participants, CD8+ T-cell reduction associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction, and multiorgan involvement in lungs, heart, and brain.

This study surveyed 855 post-COVID patients at 3 and 12 months using standardized phone interviews to assess rehabilitation needs and delayed disability using the Rehabilitation Routing Scale and Rivermead mobility scale. The findings show that post-COVID syndrome is associated with delayed disability development, supporting the use of structured rehabilitation assessment tools for post-COVID patient routing.

This cross-sectional study examined microcirculation characteristics in COVID-19 survivors with a family history of hypertension versus controls using laser Doppler flowmetry. The study found decreased perfusion and pathological vasoconstriction patterns in the hypertension-history group, indicating potential thrombotic risk in post-COVID patients.

This study evaluates surgical correction of chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) that developed post-COVID-19 in 59 patients, comparing 39 who underwent surgical treatment versus 20 receiving conservative management. Surgical intervention was significantly more effective than conservative treatment for reducing pain, edema, and healing trophic ulcers associated with post-COVID venous complications.

Retrospective cohort study of 777 children hospitalized for COVID-19, examining 98 cases (12.6%) who were rehospitalized after discharge. Found that 22.4% of rehospitalizations involved long COVID-like symptoms (fatigue, fever, abdominal pain, myalgia) with no other identified cause, suggesting long COVID may occur in children.

This retrospective cohort study examined 131 cardiological patients with pre-existing heart disease to assess changes in quality of life and cardiovascular function 2 months after COVID-19 infection. The study found significant declines in ejection fraction, increased hypertensive crises, and substantial reductions in reported quality of life, indicating post-COVID functional deterioration in this vulnerable population.

This study analyzed CT and SPECT imaging data from 74 post-COVID patients to characterize pulmonary fibrosis and microcirculation disorders one or more years after acute infection. It identifies imaging and functional predictors of post-viral interstitial lung disease but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Retrospective comparative analysis of echocardiographic findings in pediatric patients with congenital heart disease, comparing pre-pandemic and post-pandemic periods to assess the impact of long COVID on cardiac parameters. Found significant increases in left atrial size in the post-pandemic group, suggesting COVID-19 sequelae may influence cardiac chamber size in this vulnerable population.

topics: ICU-acquired weakness|muscle function|quality of life|physical rehabilitation
summary: Retrospective study examining long-term health-related quality of life and physical function in COVID-19 ICU survivors with acquired weakness, comparing outcomes between those with and without ICU-AW 18 months post-onset. Found that ICU-AW patients had significantly lower HRQOL scores and muscle strength, with MRC-SS at discharge correlating with long-term outcomes.

This study assessed microcirculatory disorders in post-COVID-19 patients with cardiovascular complications using high-frequency ultrasound Dopplerography, comparing 49 patients who received prophylactic anticoagulation (POACs) or sulodexide therapy versus controls. Results showed that sulodexide treatment improved microcirculatory blood flow and normalized coagulation parameters in post-COVID patients.

This prospective cohort study examined psychocognitive status in 134 hypertensive patients (73 with post-COVID syndrome and 61 without COVID history). Patients with PCS receiving agomelatine showed significantly lower rates of psychocognitive dysfunction (32% vs 94%, p=0.001) compared to those refusing the medication.

Comparative study of 87 multiple myeloma patients with and without post-COVID syndrome, examining clinical manifestations and laboratory parameters including hematological, biochemical, and pro-inflammatory markers. Found elevated D-dimer levels in COVID-19 infected MM patients and identified predictors of adverse outcomes, but did not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This observational study examines how COVID-19 affects patients with hereditary angioedema (HAE), measuring angioedema attack frequency and quality-of-life scores before, during, and after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 10 HAE patients. The study found no significant worsening of COVID-19 severity or quality-of-life scores in HAE patients, and no consistent pattern of increased angioedema attacks during infection.

A case series describing a telephone-based psychological consultation hotline service provided to 100+ long COVID survivors in Indonesia during September-October 2021. The intervention resulted in reduced psychological complaints in 90% of participants, with improvements in anxiety, insomnia, concentration, depression, and stress.

This study assessed anxiety, depression, and cognitive impairment in 82 individuals, comparing long COVID patients (n=61) to those who recovered from COVID-19 (n=21) and controls (n=20) at acute infection and 12 weeks later.
