Findings showed post-COVID syndrome patients had significantly higher anxiety and depression levels and lower cognitive scores than both comparison groups, though some impairment was also observed in non-post-COVID infected patients.

A prospective case analysis of 104 recovered COVID-19 patients presenting with ocular manifestations, documenting viral conjunctivitis, retinal vein occlusions, ophthalmoplegia, and mucormycosis-related orbital complications. The study reports treatment outcomes with antifungal therapy and emphasizes early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management to prevent visual disability.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term complications (36 months post-discharge) in 158 COVID-19 ARDS patients with varying lung damage severity, stratified by comorbidity status. Severe ARDS (>50% lung involvement) showed significantly higher rates of cardiovascular, neurological, endocrine, and thyroid complications compared to milder ARDS and controls.

This prospective cohort study followed 393 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 1 year to determine the incidence and predictors of long COVID. The study found 34.4% developed long COVID at follow-up, with disease severity, high BMI, and increased age as independent predictors, but did not test any treatment intervention.

A prospective observational study of 369 COVID-19 recovered individuals in Delhi assessed their quality of life (QoL) at baseline and 6 months post-recovery using the WHO-QoL BREF scale. The study found that participants with post-COVID syndrome had significantly worse QoL scores across physical, psychological, social, and environmental domains compared to non-PCoVS participants at 6-month follow-up.

Two-year follow-up study of 158 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessing quality of life and health status using the VR-12 questionnaire. Found persistent post-COVID consequences with differences by age and gender, but no active treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective analysis of 170 COVID-19 pneumonia patients in Grodno, evaluating long-term treatment outcomes via CT imaging at 3-5 and 6-12 months post-treatment. Study documents lung recovery patterns (35% complete recovery at 3-5 months, persisting interstitial changes in 65%) but does not test or compare specific interventions.

This study assessed cognitive impairment in 50 young people (age 19-35) with mild COVID-19 compared to 50 controls using neuropsychological testing. Patients showed mild cognitive impairment including slightly higher depression scores, decreased visual memory, and increased asthenia compared to controls, with complaints resolving after acute phase recovery.

Retrospective cohort study comparing cardiovascular endpoints in 447 patients with sick sinus syndrome (205 with prior COVID-19, 242 without) over 30 months. Study found increased myocardial infarction risk in the COVID-19 group but no differences in other endpoints (death, stroke, hospitalization).

This pilot observational study evaluated a food supplement containing hydroxytyrosol, acetyl L-carnitine, and vitamins B, C, and D in patients with post-COVID syndrome characterized by chronic fatigue. Results suggest the supplement showed promise and could warrant further clinical trial evaluation.

Retrospective analysis of 251 children with COVID-19 to identify clinical and laboratory predictors of long-COVID development. Found long-COVID symptoms in 12.4% of patients, with elevated leukocytes, neutrophils, monocytes, platelets, and D-dimer as significant predictive markers.

This study examined pain prevalence and its relationship to psychological and cognitive variables in 79 COVID-19 outpatients, measuring pain intensity, dyspnea, and quality of life at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Results showed that physical pain and inactivity symptoms improved by the third month, but no specific treatment intervention was administered or evaluated.

Retrospective study examining COVID-19 courses and long COVID symptom occurrence in B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma patients at an oncology center between 2020-2023. While the study documents higher long COVID symptom rates in this immunocompromised population, it is an observational cohort study that passively follows patient outcomes without testing or evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study of 254 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge to investigate the frequency and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome. Post-COVID syndrome was diagnosed in 57.5% of patients, with symptom frequency and severity improving over time, and severe acute infection and higher symptom burden at month 1 being significant predictors of long-term syndrome.

This study assessed the association between cardiovascular risk (CVR) and COVID-19 severity, and how CVR correlates with post-COVID-19 symptom development in 1,782 patients followed for 3 months. Patients with high/very-high CVR had significantly higher risk of post-COVID-19 development and greater disease burden compared to low-intermediate risk groups.

This observational cross-sectional study assessed persistent symptoms in 160 COVID-19 survivors 30-40 days post-recovery in India. The most common manifestations were dyspnea (74.3%), fatigue (56.25%), and disturbed sleep (64.3%), with stronger relationships found between pre-infection comorbidities and disease severity.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiac biomarkers and echocardiographic parameters between 126 COVID-19 recovered patients (mean 58 days post-infection) and 98 healthy controls. The COVID-19 group showed significantly elevated inflammatory markers (RDW, ESR, CRP, NT-ProBNP, D-dimer, troponin T) and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, indicating detectable cardiac injury during the post-acute phase.

This retrospective multicenter study evaluated the efficacy and safety of Polyoxidonium® (azoximere bromide) in 16,365 patients with inflammatory and infectious upper respiratory diseases, including post-COVID-19 syndrome. Treatment resulted in 40% complete symptom relief and 99.77% positive dynamics, with symptom resolution occurring primarily within 5 days and no treatment-related adverse events reported.

A two-center prospective cohort study of 10,545 post-COVID patients assessed respiratory dysfunction and compared two therapeutic approaches (budesonide vs beclomethasone/formoterol) for broncho-obstructive syndrome, which affected 72% of the cohort. The fixed combination therapy showed superiority over nebulized budesonide in MART mode, and the study identified risk factors for respiratory complications including severe acute COVID, ICU admission, and oxygen therapy need.

This is a prospective follow-up study of 71 post-COVID patients examining pulmonary function, imaging, hemostasis, and immune markers at two time points (30-60 and 61-180 days post-discharge). The study documents natural recovery patterns rather than testing any intervention, making it an observational natural history study without treatment.

This study evaluates pulmonary rehabilitation effectiveness in 34 patients with chronic bronchial pathology who experienced COVID-19 pneumonia, comparing 18 patients receiving rehabilitation (main group) to 16 untreated controls over 3 months. Patients receiving rehabilitation showed significant improvements in inflammatory markers, respiratory function (FEV1 and vital capacity increased 1.5x), lung tissue damage reduction (43.5% to 16%), and quality of life, with decreased risk of pulmonary fibrosis.

Retrospective cohort study of 69 children with pre-existing chronic nonspecific lung diseases (cystic fibrosis, bronchial/lung malformations, asthma) assessed ~1 year after COVID-19 infection using standardized ISARIC questionnaire. Found persistent post-COVID symptoms including fatigue, reduced physical activity, cognitive impairment, and appetite loss affecting daily functioning and learning, with calls for rehabilitation programs but no intervention tested.

This observational study compares carbohydrate and lipid metabolism markers in 50 children 6 months post-COVID-19 versus 58 healthy controls. The analysis found no significant differences in glucose levels, lipid profiles, or insulin resistance indices between the two groups.

Cross-sectional comparative study assessing incidence and severity of persistent symptoms in young healthy women with COVID-19 history versus controls. Found COVID survivors reported more memory impairment, headache, myalgia, and respiratory symptoms, though fatigue was similar between groups.

This is a retrospective analysis of 6,252 children and adolescents' medical records in Kemerovo to determine the frequency and clinical variants of post-COVID syndrome. The study found 49% prevalence with asthenic, respiratory, cardiac, and gastrointestinal variants, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This retrospective chart review evaluates LED photobiomodulation therapy for treating telogen effluvium (post-COVID hair loss) in 140 long COVID patients, comparing outcomes in those with and without androgenetic alopecia. After 12 weeks, LED therapy groups showed significantly greater cessation of hair loss and hair regrowth compared to untreated controls, with improvements in hair thickness and density.

This prospective observational cohort study assessed the incidence of myocardial injury in 75 young, physically fit male patients who recently recovered from mild/asymptomatic COVID-19 using cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging. The study found that 25% of patients had possible COVID-19-related myocardial injury, but it is an observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested, so it does not meet the criteria for treatment trial screening.

Cross-sectional study comparing asthenia severity and quality of life in post-COVID syndrome patients versus controls during acute infection and 12 weeks later using psychiatric scales. Found significantly higher asthenia and lower quality of life in post-COVID group, but no treatment intervention was tested—this is a descriptive assessment study only.

A prospective cohort study following 88 COVID-19 survivors for 12 months after hospital discharge to investigate persistent symptoms and risk factors. Over one-third of patients reported long-term symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, and activity limitations, with female sex, younger age, corticosteroid use, and imaging findings identified as risk factors for sequelae.

A retrospective cohort study of 140 healthcare workers in Jordan that evaluated the frequency and nature of persistent COVID-19 symptoms over 6-12 months post-infection. The study found that 59.3% reported post-COVID-19 syndrome with fatigue being the most common symptom, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This paper assesses the health impact of COVID-19 infection in children at multiple timepoints (during illness, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months post-infection) using analyses and ECGs. Post-COVID disorders were observed in the 3-6 month period, with the authors identifying common postcovid syndrome symptoms and recommending expanded monitoring and rehabilitation programs for affected children.

A prospective controlled study examining structural and functional changes in the left heart of COPD patients 12 months after COVID-19 infection compared to COPD patients without COVID history. The study found that COVID-19 survivors with COPD developed significant left ventricular dysfunction and diastolic impairment at 12-month follow-up.

Observational study comparing postcovid syndrome manifestations in 222 COPD patients with and without metabolic syndrome, followed for 12 months post-infection. Found postcovid syndrome more common in COPD+metabolic syndrome group (34.3%), with persistent weakness, anxiety, depression, and increased COPD exacerbations.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of persistent symptoms in 106 adults 3-4 months after COVID-19 in Suriname, finding that 39.6% experienced at least one persistent symptom with fatigue and alopecia most common. The study did not involve any treatment intervention, only symptom assessment and characterization of long COVID prevalence by demographic and health factors.

This retrospective cohort study from Czechia (Dec 2021–Aug 2023) analyzed national-level data to estimate the effectiveness of post-vaccination, post-infection, and hybrid immunity against severe COVID-19 and long COVID outcomes. While the study addresses long COVID, it does not test or evaluate a specific intervention or treatment given to long COVID patients—instead it analyzes existing population-level immunity patterns and their association with disease severity and long COVID incidence.

Prospective cohort study of 2,856 Swiss patients examining sex and gender differences in post-COVID syndrome (PASC) prevalence and risk factors. Found that sociocultural gender-related factors (stress, education, living situation, household income) are stronger predictors of PASC than biological sex alone.

This cross-sectional study evaluates fitness-to-dive assessments in occupational and recreational divers with post-COVID-19 changes, finding that 30% (13/43) were disqualified due to persistent lung CT abnormalities. The paper documents prevalence of CT findings over time but does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Longitudinal study tracking symptom duration in 102 non-hospitalised COVID-19 patients in Berlin during March-May 2020, with follow-up at days 30 and 60. While the paper documents that 20% of patients had persisting symptoms at day 60, it focuses on the acute/early post-infection period in 2020 and does not study long COVID as a distinct condition or test any interventions.

This epidemiological study documents cases of pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome (PIMS) temporally associated with COVID-19 in France during March-May 2020. The paper is about acute post-infection inflammation in children during the acute phase of the pandemic, not persistent long COVID symptoms weeks to months later.

A retrospective analysis of 67 deceased COVID-19 convalescents examining fatal outcomes and timing of complications in a multidisciplinary hospital. The study found that most deaths occurred within 1-2 months post-recovery, with cardiovascular disease (63%) and thrombotic complications as major causes, particularly in women.

Retrospective analysis of 116 post-COVID patients examining the relationship between carbohydrate metabolism disorders and chronic heart failure development. Study identifies HbA1c, LDL-C, and IL-8 as prognostic markers for CHF in post-COVID patients but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study (n=41) evaluating perfusion CT parameters to differentiate post-inflammatory from malignant pulmonary consolidations in long COVID patients with persistent lung changes 12 weeks post-discharge. Found vascular permeability (PS) and time to peak (TTP) contrast enhancement effectively distinguished benign from neoplastic lesions (AUC 87.5%), but this is a diagnostic imaging study, not a treatment trial.

This case-control study compares cognitive function (memory and concentration) in 30 long COVID patients at three recovery timepoints (2-3 weeks, 1-2 months, 6-7 months post-infection) versus 30 uninfected controls. The findings show that memory impairment and poor concentration persist for up to 6 months after COVID-19 recovery, but the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study examined 116 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors one year post-discharge to assess left ventricular function using echocardiography. The study found impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain in 57.5% of patients despite normal ejection fraction, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long COVID patients treated with a 'cocktail medication' protocol versus untreated controls, measuring changes in blood toxicity scores and symptom improvements. Treated patients showed significant symptom improvement and decreased toxicity scores, while untreated patients showed minimal improvement and increased toxicity scores.

Retrospective cohort study examining clinical, laboratory, and radiological parameters in COVID-19 patients after hospital discharge. Documents persistent post-COVID symptoms in low-risk patients during the first 30 days post-infection and identifies need for improved monitoring protocols.

This paper compares clinical and pathogenetic features of coronary heart disease combined with type 2 diabetes in patients with and without prior COVID-19 history. While it examines post-COVID complications (cardiac and metabolic disorders), it is primarily a comparative diagnostic study of coronary disease and diabetes rather than a treatment intervention trial for long COVID.

This cross-sectional study compared blood coagulation markers and endothelin-1 levels between 77 long COVID patients and 68 healthy controls. Long COVID patients showed prolonged prothrombin time, reduced prothrombin index, elevated INR, and significantly higher endothelin-1 levels, particularly 3-6 months post-infection, indicating persistent inflammatory processes and endothelial dysfunction with increased thrombosis risk.

A prospective cohort study comparing long-term effectiveness of four rehabilitation approaches (respiratory rehabilitation, oriental medicine, balneotherapy/physiotherapy, and no rehabilitation control) in 113 post-COVID syndrome patients followed over 6 months. Respiratory rehabilitation-based program showed highest effectiveness with 85.7% reduction in hospitalization risk compared to controls.

Cross-sectional study documenting long COVID symptoms in 120 Egyptian healthcare workers at least 3 months post-infection, with follow-up assessments at 1 month and 3+ months. Found persistent dyspnea and fatigue in ~27-33% at 3 months, with older age (≥35 years) associated with higher symptom burden and emerging complications including parosmia, hair loss, and memory problems.

Observational cohort study examining the prevalence and risk factors of post-COVID-19 condition in 175 children and adolescents. Found 14.8% prevalence with fatigue, muscle pain, and dysgeusia as key symptoms, and female sex and comorbidities as significant risk factors.

This retrospective cohort study examines the relationship between latent tuberculosis infection and post-COVID-19 sequelae in hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed up at 6 months. The study found no significant association between latent TB and long COVID symptoms, but identified age and chronic lung disease as risk factors for post-COVID sequelae.

Prospective cohort study measuring humoral and cellular immunity in 60 Russian children within one month after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found suppressed cell-mediated and humoral immunity with phagocytosis dysfunction, suggesting a predictor of chronic infection, but focuses on acute post-infection immune dynamics rather than long COVID management or treatment.

This is an observational cohort study monitoring immune status in 60 children at 1, 3, and 12 months post-COVID-19. It documents immunological changes over time but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case series of 44 men with post-COVID erectile dysfunction and reduced libido, stratified by testosterone levels and treated with PDE-5 inhibitors, antiasthenic drugs, and testosterone replacement where indicated. The study found that sexual dysfunction post-COVID may be reversible through rehabilitation and pharmacological interventions, with treatment outcomes depending on baseline testosterone levels.

A six-month prospective cohort study of COVID-19 survivor healthcare workers that assessed anxiety and depression symptoms using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. The study found no increased risk of anxiety or depression at six months post-infection compared to uninfected healthcare workers.

This cross-sectional study assesses general condition, laboratory parameters, and quality of life in post-reproductive women 12 months after asymptomatic or moderate COVID-19 compared to controls. While it documents persistent symptoms and impaired quality of life in the moderate COVID-19 group, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines serum interleukin levels (IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-18) in 146 patients with nervous system diseases, comparing those with and without prior COVID-19 infection. The study finds elevated proinflammatory interleukins in post-COVID patients, particularly IL-6, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective 6-month observational cohort study examining echocardiographic changes in 100 patients with lung damage after COVID-19 and their association with post-COVID syndrome manifestations. The study documents cardiac structural changes (chamber dilation, valvular regurgitation, diastolic dysfunction) that correlate with clinical symptoms but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational cohort study of 1,500 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months post-discharge examining blood sugar abnormalities and new-onset diabetes mellitus. Found significant associations between COVID-19 severity, inflammatory markers, and development of hyperglycemia and diabetes during post-COVID follow-up.

Retrospective observational study of 4,681 COVID-19 patients in Iran examining long-term symptoms and risk factors for long COVID syndrome. Identifies female sex, respiratory symptoms at disease onset, and illness severity as significant risk factors for persistent symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective analysis of 504 long COVID patients with pulmonary symptoms (persistent cough/dyspnea) to identify predictive factors. Study found that age >60, male gender, comorbidities, elevated inflammatory markers, parenchymal bands on CT, and prior oxygen therapy were associated with pulmonary manifestations.

This cross-sectional study uses [18F]DPA-714 PET imaging to assess neuroinflammation (via TSPO binding) in 47 long COVID patients with and without persistent fatigue and difficulty concentrating, ~2 years post-infection. While increased cerebral TSPO binding was found in some symptomatic individuals, indicating a neuroinflammatory subtype, the study is a biomarker characterization study without testing any intervention or treatment.

This study describes the prevalence of inflammatory cardiopulmonary findings in 98 long COVID patients using PET/MRI and DECT imaging, comparing them to 9 asymptomatic controls. While confirming high rates of cardiac and pulmonary abnormalities in long COVID, the study is a diagnostic/observational assessment rather than an intervention trial, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Descriptive study of hematological profiles in 87 hospitalized children with post-COVID-19 infection, primarily focusing on multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C). Reports prevalence of leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, elevated CRP, fibrinogen, ferritin, and D-dimer without testing any intervention or treatment.

This study examined 116 stage 2 hypertensive patients, comparing those with acute COVID-19 (symptomatic phase) versus post-COVID syndrome, to investigate the role of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system gene polymorphisms in post-COVID outcomes. The authors found higher systolic blood pressure during active COVID-19 infection compared to post-COVID syndrome and identified an association between AGT gene polymorphisms and blood pressure instability in the post-COVID phase.

This retrospective cohort study assessed myocardial dysfunction in 162 COVID-19 survivors at 3-4 months post-infection using longitudinal strain echocardiography. Patients with cardiovascular comorbidities, obesity, and lower SpO2/PaO2 at admission showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain, suggesting lasting cardiac involvement post-COVID.

This cross-sectional study examined autonomic dysfunction in 45 patients 3-6 months after COVID-19 recovery using ECG, orthostatic testing, and autonomic questionnaires. The authors found high prevalence of orthostatic hypotension (76%) and signs of autonomic dysfunction (82%), with severity correlating to acute COVID-19 severity.

This study examines lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress markers in 91 COVID-19 convalescents, comparing patients receiving rehabilitation treatment (including haloaerosol therapy) versus controls. The intervention reduced oxidative stress indicators and endotoxemia, though did not fully normalize biomarker levels, suggesting rehabilitation may help manage post-COVID pathophysiology.

This cross-sectional study compares clinical and microbiological features of IBS patients with vs without prior COVID-19 history, examining fecal microbiome composition in post-COVID IBS. The study found post-COVID IBS patients had more diarrhea and altered microbiota (decreased Bifidobacterium, increased E. coli) compared to non-COVID IBS and healthy controls, but no differences in pathogenic microflora.

This retrospective cohort study examined cardiac function changes in 130 CVD patients at 3, 12, and 26 months post-COVID-19 pneumonia using echocardiography. Over time, patients showed increased BMI and obesity prevalence, worsening diastolic function parameters, but improved left ventricular strain with decreased frequency of reduced strain values.

A cross-sectional study comparing 53 type 2 diabetes patients without post-COVID syndrome to 49 with post-COVID syndrome, assessing clinical symptoms, quality of life, cardiac function, and pulmonary function. Findings show post-COVID patients with diabetes have more severe dyspnea, fatigue, cardiac arrhythmias, structural myocardial changes, and reduced pulmonary function compared to diabetics without post-COVID.

This study compares morphological features, Toll-like receptor distribution, and immunosuppressive therapy responses between post-COVID myocarditis (n=42) and non-COVID myocarditis (n=35) patients with biopsy-proven disease. Post-COVID myocarditis showed higher morphological activity and improved response to immunosuppressive therapy compared to non-COVID cases.

This cross-sectional EEG study investigated cortical brain activity in 40 long COVID patients with cognitive fog, comparing those with and without anosmia to healthy controls. The study found persistent alterations in P300 and beta band rhythms associated with cognitive fog 1-8 months post-infection, but did not test any treatment intervention.

This paper studies CT imaging changes in 70 patients with acute COVID-19 pneumonia over 6-12 months of follow-up. It focuses on acute viral pneumonia and lung imaging dynamics during the acute/subacute phase, not persistent long COVID symptoms or treatment interventions.

Longitudinal study examining how psychosocial factors (loneliness, social relationships, family communication) during severe COVID-19 hospitalization predict mental health outcomes in 75 survivors over 2 years. Found that perceived loneliness and worse social relationships predicted higher depression and anxiety at follow-up, but no specific intervention was administered to patients.

This retrospective cohort study compares clinical and biochemical features of urolithiasis in 66 long COVID patients versus 52 controls without COVID-19 history. The study found that post-COVID syndrome negatively affects kidney stone formation and treatment outcomes, with slower recovery after stone removal and increased recurrence risk.

This case-control study compares cognitive function outcomes in 60 patients with chronic cerebral ischemia (CCI) who recovered from COVID-19 versus 40 CCI patients without COVID-19 history, assessed via MoCA at 4-12 weeks and 6-12 months post-infection. While it demonstrates cognitive recovery over time in the COVID-exposed group, it does not study or test any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

This cross-sectional study compared oxygen consumption (VO2max) and heart rate index values in 27 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients before infection and after symptom onset using treadmill testing. The study found significantly decreased aerobic capacity in PCS patients but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study compares drug therapy versus non-drug rehabilitation technologies (balneotherapy, magnetic therapy, inhalations) in post-COVID workers with intensive computer workload, evaluating clinical and laboratory markers. Non-drug interventions showed greater improvements in asthenization, fatigue, immune status, and antioxidant markers compared to drug therapy alone.

This study followed 70 male COVID-19 patients for 12 months to assess the development and persistence of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) post-infection. While it documents a significant increase in LUTS prevalence (80.9% of 42 included patients), it is an observational study with no intervention or treatment given to patients, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This study compares clinical and laboratory parameters in healthcare workers with hypertension during acute COVID-19 pneumonia and 3 months post-discharge versus a matched control group. It is a secondary analysis of a prospective registry examining post-COVID consequences rather than testing a specific intervention or treatment.

This observational study evaluated echocardiographic indicators and cardiovascular function in 20 locomotive crew workers who had recovered from COVID-19, stratified by infection severity and presence of risk factors. Workers with severe COVID-19 and comorbidities showed structural left ventricular remodeling and grade I hypertension, while those with mild infection showed only functional changes in heart rate and blood pressure.

This study evaluates ozone therapy as a rehabilitation treatment for long COVID patients with central nervous system dysfunction following COVID-associated pneumonia. The analysis compares symptom dynamics in a treated group receiving ozone therapy versus an untreated control group, finding improvements in cerebroasthenic and cerebral syndromes including fatigue, cognitive function, and olfactory symptoms.

Prospective observational study tracking persistent symptoms in 62 unvaccinated COVID-19 patients over 18 months, measuring fatigue, cognition, quality of life, anxiety, depression, and physical abilities. Found that 47% had severe fatigue at 7 months with minimal improvement at 13 months, and reduced grip strength at 18 months, but no specific intervention was tested.

A multicenter prospective observational study of 83 post-COVID patients with hyperammonemia, attention/memory impairment, and fatigue who received L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) 3g three times daily for 4 weeks. Treatment significantly reduced ammonia levels (97.6% of patients), improved cognitive function on number connection test, reduced fatigue scores, and normalized hepatic encephalopathy severity.

Post-hoc analysis of the LIRA-COVID observational program examining hyperammonemia and liver dysfunction in long COVID patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Treatment with L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) for 4 weeks showed significant effects on ammonia levels, particularly in NAFLD patients, supporting LOLA as a therapeutic intervention for post-COVID syndrome.

This study examined 45 post-COVID-19 patients to identify risk factors for thrombotic events, comparing outcomes in patients who received anticoagulant therapy (n=25) versus those who did not (n=20) during the post-acute period. Anticoagulant therapy for at least two months reduced thrombosis risk, while severe acute COVID-19 and absence of anticoagulant treatment were identified as significant risk factors for subsequent thrombotic events.

This retrospective cohort study using propensity score matching compares healthcare costs between hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients through 2020. While it quantifies the economic burden of long COVID sequelae, it is an observational cost analysis rather than a treatment intervention study, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the trials pipeline.

A prospective cohort study of 266 post-COVID patients identified 25 with post-COVID-19 interstitial lung disease, of whom 9 received off-label nintedanib therapy for 3 months. Nintedanib showed no significant effect on radiological patterns, disease progression, oxygen saturation, or dyspnea symptoms, suggesting antifibrotic therapy should be prescribed individually for longer than 3 months in select cases.

A descriptive observational study of healthcare workers at a Spanish hospital who developed persistent COVID symptoms, with assessment of clinical profiles and outcomes. Results showed that cognitive rehabilitation and physical exercise improved symptoms over time, allowing workers to continue their work activities.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records of 10,646 patients to assess the risk of future hospitalization for non-COVID-19 conditions in the 6 months post-COVID-19 infection. Patients with severe COVID-19 had significantly increased risk of future hospitalization for cardiovascular, respiratory, and clotting complications compared to mild/moderate or COVID-negative patients.

This study examines IL-6 as a biomarker for predicting severity and radiological outcomes in acute COVID-19 pneumonia across 1000 hospitalized patients. While it mentions post-COVID lung fibrosis as a secondary outcome, the primary focus is acute COVID-19 severity assessment during active infection, not long COVID intervention trials.

This paper describes a hotline consultation service established by the Department of Pulmonology and Respiratory Medicine to provide health advice and triage for COVID-19 survivors with long COVID symptoms in Indonesia. The service reached 60 survivors, most with mild symptoms requiring self-care observation, and identified 42% needing further specialist care, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Longitudinal study evaluating residual lung parenchymal CT changes in COVID-19 patients at median 137 days post-diagnosis. Found that 69.4% of patients had persistent CT changes, with significant reduction in CT severity scores between scans, but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular system impairment and its contribution to dyspnea in 87 post-acute COVID-19 patients stratified by acute illness severity. The authors find that dyspnea severity correlates with acute illness severity and is driven by residual lung changes and cardiovascular involvement, with recommendations for multidisciplinary management.

A 2-year prospective observational cohort study of 71 vaccinated college students infected with Omicron and 18 uninfected controls, measuring immune and metabolic parameters at multiple timepoints. The study documents persistent immune dysregulation and metabolic alterations for at least 1 year post-infection, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective observational study analyzed 53 COVID-19 related interstitial lung disease (ILD) cases at a tertiary hospital in Sri Lanka, examining demographic, clinical, and radiological characteristics. The majority of patients were male with multiple comorbidities, and HRCT findings demonstrated disease progression patterns, but the study does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study examining the prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions in Delta variant infections across vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. The study found similar prevalence of post-COVID conditions in both groups (61.4% vs 51.4%), with acute symptom burden as an independent risk factor, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A prospective observational study in Quebec examining the prevalence and risk factors of persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms at least 1 month after Omicron infection in PCR-confirmed cases. Found that 47.2% of 290 participants reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue, shortness of breath, and cough being most common; number of acute COVID symptoms was identified as a significant risk factor.

Retrospective study of 856 long COVID patients treated with ivermectin at a public hospital in Buenos Aires. Treatment with ivermectin reportedly led to faster reduction of long COVID manifestations and symptom duration.

This cross-sectional study assessed androgen status in 90 men (60 post-COVID, 30 controls) at 3 months post-infection using hormone measurement and questionnaires. Severe COVID-19 was associated with 61% reduction in total testosterone and elevated FSH, SHBG, and prolactin compared to healthy controls, with mild COVID showing less pronounced hormonal changes and erectile dysfunction.

This observational cohort study followed 385 COPD patients (55 without MS, 330 with MS) for 12 months to characterize the dynamics of metabolic syndrome features after acute COVID-19 infection. Post-COVID syndrome was diagnosed in 6.7-34.3% depending on MS status, with strong correlations found between post-COVID syndrome and carbohydrate metabolism disorders (VAI and HOMA-IR), though most metabolic parameters improved by 12 months while hypertension complications persisted.

Retrospective observational study examining associations between fatigue syndrome and inflammatory markers/medical interventions in 100 long COVID patients. Study identifies correlations between specific inflammatory markers and fatigue but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines coronary artery disease (CAD) patients at least 12 weeks after mild or moderate COVID-19 infection, comparing clinical, laboratory, and angiographic findings between the two groups. Patients with moderate acute COVID-19 showed worse cardiovascular outcomes including higher blood pressure, greater coronary artery lesions, and lower ejection fraction, indicating that moderate acute COVID increases long-term cardiovascular risk in CAD patients.

Retrospective analysis of 1,329 COVID-19 patients admitted to a rural hospital (March 2020–November 2021) examining baseline pulmonary conditions and changes in lung function. Found significant decrease in DLCO in surviving patients but no clear treatment intervention tested.

A 2-year prospective cohort study comparing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 413 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients versus 520 recovered controls using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire and Clinical Frailty Scale. The study found significant HRQoL decline in PCC patients up to 18 months, with notable impairment in pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression, and usual activities, highlighting the need for continued monitoring and mental health support.

A descriptive cross-sectional cohort study examining dermatological manifestations in 120 COVID-19 patients (≥12 weeks post-infection). The study documents acute-period skin lesions (urticaria, erythema) in 9.7% and post-COVID dermatological symptoms in 94.4% of patients (alopecia, xerosis, onychopathy, new-onset dermatoses), but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This multicenter retrospective cohort study examines the association between baseline parathyroid hormone (iPTH) levels and COVID-19 severity and post-acute outcomes in 142 hemodialysis patients followed for 20 months. While the study identifies iPTH as a prognostic biomarker for post-acute hospitalization and mortality in long COVID patients with kidney disease, it is observational without any treatment intervention, thus not eligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective observational study comparing lipid profiles and cardiac electrical axis measurements in 30 young patients during acute COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 recovery. Found increases in cholesterol and LDL after recovery, with leftward deviation of the electrical axis detected in 17% of patients post-COVID.

Retrospective cohort study of 1,969 COVID-19 patients examining the frequency and risk factors for carbohydrate metabolism disorders (type 2 diabetes, prediabetes) during the post-COVID period over 3.5 years. New-onset hyperglycemia during acute COVID-19 was a strong predictor of later carbohydrate metabolism disorders, with age, BMI, and glucose levels identified as independent risk factors.

Prospective cohort study examining kidney involvement during acute COVID-19 hospitalization as a predictor of cardiovascular complications within one year post-discharge. Finds that kidney dysfunction is independently associated with increased risk of CV events, with persistent inflammation and endothelial dysfunction as potential mechanisms.

This observational study characterizes the endocrine phenotype of post-COVID syndrome in 208 long COVID patients, identifying metabolic and cardiovascular risk factors associated with this phenotype. It is excluded because it is a passive observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluated—patients are merely assessed for existing conditions rather than given any treatment.

Prospective study assessing thyroid function and reproductive hormones in 171 women with menstrual disorders after COVID-19, comparing post-acute COVID (1-3 months) versus long COVID (3-6 months) phases. Findings show phase-dependent thyroid dysfunction patterns (transient thyrotoxicosis in post-acute phase, autoimmune hypothyroidism in long COVID) associated with specific menstrual disturbances, but no treatment intervention was administered or evaluated.

This observational study compares systemic inflammatory markers in 416 patients with stable coronary heart disease stratified by COVID-19 severity (mild vs. moderate) more than 12 weeks post-infection. Patients with moderate COVID-19 showed elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (MCP-1, TNF-α, IL-1β) and complement component C3, suggesting worse cardiovascular outcomes in the post-acute period.

This natural pre-post experiment compared olfactory function and brain imaging in 9 COVID-19 patients and 12 controls, using baseline assessments conducted before the pandemic. Despite subjective olfactory complaints, the study found reduced olfactory bulb volume in most COVID-19 patients but no significant morphologic differences in central olfactory regions compared to controls.

Retrospective observational study of 30 children with asthma who had COVID-19, assessing the course of acute infection and frequency of post-COVID syndrome development. Found that 13.3% of children developed post-COVID syndrome, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 122,045 COVID-19 patients in Japan to describe the incidence of post-COVID symptoms and nursing care requirements across three periods with different viral strains and vaccination coverage. It found lower post-COVID symptom incidence with increased vaccination and identified depression and disuse syndrome as more prevalent in older patients, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 53 post-COVID-19 patients using MRI and neuropsychological testing to assess cognitive outcomes and correlate them with structural brain changes at median 1.8 years post-infection. Found significant cognitive impairment in attention, executive function, and memory domains associated with reduced cortical thickness in specific brain regions, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A retrospective cohort study of 85 patients examining post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis development, identifying risk factors including age, smoking history, and mechanical ventilation. The paper documents prevalence of fibrotic changes but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational study of 101 COVID-19 survivors followed at 6 months and 1 year post-discharge to assess pulmonary sequelae using spirometry and imaging. Found that 26.7% had persistent symptoms at 6 months (primarily exertional dyspnea) with correlation between initial disease severity and pulmonary impairment.

Retrospective analysis of Rowan Medicine electronic patient data examining prevalence and characterization of memory dysfunction and 'brain fog' symptoms in long COVID patients. The study found no significant observations due to extremely small dataset size, limiting the ability to provide meaningful analysis.

A retrospective cohort study examining central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) as an ocular complication in post-COVID syndrome patients across three Egyptian hospitals. The study documents clinical characteristics and symptoms in CRVO patients post-COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective multicentric observational study examining D-Dimer as a biomarker in acute COVID-19 pneumonia to predict severity, mechanical ventilation need, and post-COVID lung fibrosis. While the paper mentions long-term post-COVID effects, it focuses on acute hospitalization outcomes during active infection rather than treating long COVID patients.

Multicenter prospective study examining the relationship between nutrition therapy in the acute phase of severe COVID-19 (requiring mechanical ventilation) and post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) outcomes at 10-month follow-up. Found that supplemental parenteral nutrition >400 kcal/day independently correlated with lower occurrence of physical PICS, but does not study long COVID specifically—focuses on acute ICU survivors and general post-ICU outcomes.

A prospective cohort study of 51 cancer survivors hospitalized for COVID-19, assessing post-acute symptoms including fatigue, nutritional status, anxiety, depression, and voice/swallowing impairments at discharge and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. By one year, 66% of patients retained at least one impairment, with fatigue and psychological symptoms persisting despite improvements in nutritional status and overall daily functioning.

This retrospective cohort study examines chest CT findings and pulmonary function test results in COVID-19 survivors during post-recovery phase (median 95 days post-symptom onset). The study correlates imaging abnormalities with lung function impairment but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study examining structural and functional cardiac changes in 221 COVID-19 patients at hospital discharge and 1-month follow-up using echocardiography, comparing hypertensive and normotensive subgroups. Found persistent left ventricular concentric geometry and diastolic dysfunction without improvement in the early post-discharge period, particularly in hypertensive patients.

This study examined 100 post-COVID patients admitted for stage 3 medical rehabilitation, assessing autonomic nervous system dysfunction using vegetative status assessment methods. After comprehensive rehabilitation, positive dynamics were observed in most patients, though residual symptoms persisted in those with autonomic dysfunction.

Prospective cohort study of 175 Brazilian COVID-19 survivors assessing long-term symptoms over >120 days post-infection. Study documents prevalence of persistent fatigue, dyspnea, cough, headache, and muscle weakness but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study of 36 IBD patients with prior COVID-19 assessing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and severity at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months via questionnaire and functional assessments (respiratory function, echocardiography, CT imaging). Found that post-COVID syndrome was more severe and prolonged in patients with respiratory distress during acute COVID-19, with minimal radiological changes in the non-RD group.

This study uses electronic health records to compare pre- and post-COVID-19 diagnostic codes to identify symptoms with higher incidence in the post-COVID period as potential long COVID sequelae. The work serves as a hypothesis-generation and monitoring method for long COVID symptoms in the population.

This retrospective cohort study compared the frequency and course of post-COVID syndrome in 140 patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) versus spondyloarthritis (SpA), assessing disease activity and exacerbation risk factors over 12 months post-infection. RA patients had significantly higher post-COVID syndrome incidence (73.7% vs 61.3%) with more frequent fatigue, pain, and cognitive symptoms; disease exacerbations peaked at 3 months, with cardiovascular disease and female gender identified as key risk factors.

Population-based cross-sectional study comparing prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition in 25,911 SARS-CoV-2 infected persons versus matched uninfected controls in Japan during the Omicron-dominant wave. Found 11.8% prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (≥2 months persistent symptoms), with female sex, comorbidities, and mild-to-moderate acute infection as risk factors.

This retrospective cohort study compared fatigue incidence rates between 4,589 COVID-19 patients and 9,022 propensity score-matched controls over a median 11.4-month follow-up period. The study found COVID-19 patients had significantly higher incidence rates of fatigue (10.2/100 person-years) and chronic fatigue (1.8/100 person-years) compared to controls, with hazard ratios of 1.68 and 4.32 respectively.

A 12-month observational follow-up study of 134 adults previously hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia, characterizing long-term sequelae including persistent cough, dyspnea, lung texture abnormalities, cognitive impairment, and fatigue. The study identifies risk factors (age, disease severity, comorbidities) associated with worse long-term outcomes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective comparison of electrodiagnostic findings in patients with post-COVID-19 Guillain-Barré syndrome versus non-COVID-19 GBS. The study analyzes electromyography results but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This population-based study compares the prevalence of post-acute COVID-19 symptom clusters between individuals infected with Omicron versus wild-type SARS-CoV-2 variants. The research examines whether long COVID manifestations and symptom patterns differ depending on which variant caused the initial infection.

This retrospective cohort study compared thrombotic event incidence in the year after COVID-19 versus other acute respiratory infections using PCORnet data from 2022-2023. It found a 63% increased risk for any thrombotic event and 73% increased risk in nonhospitalized patients with COVID-19, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study following 1,809 health and welfare workers with work-related COVID-19 infections over 26-32 months to identify predictors of persistent post-COVID symptoms. The study found that female gender, older age, pre-existing conditions, and severe acute symptoms were significant risk factors for prolonged recovery, with 60% still experiencing symptoms at 32 months.

A prospective cohort study tracking 1,810 German healthcare workers with post-COVID symptoms over 18 months to identify factors influencing symptom persistence and recovery. Found that 67% reported ongoing symptoms at 18 months, with female sex, age >50, pre-existing conditions, and severe acute symptoms as risk factors for prolonged recovery.

Cross-sectional study of 367 COVID-19 survivors examining the prevalence and intensity of musculoskeletal symptoms (fatigue, myalgia, arthralgia, muscle weakness) during the 6-month recovery period. Found high rates of musculoskeletal complications but no association with acute infection severity; does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective and prospective study examining factors associated with prolonged oxygen therapy need in COVID-19 patients discharged from hospital, with one-year mortality follow-up. While the study addresses post-discharge outcomes in COVID-19 survivors, it does not evaluate a specific treatment or intervention—it is a descriptive observational study of oxygen therapy use and outcomes, not a treatment trial.

This study compared neuropsychological and cognitive outcomes before and after COVID-19 infection in older adults from two ongoing longitudinal cohorts (Arizona APOE and ADRC). The authors found no significant differences in cognitive decline between pre- and post-COVID assessments, with members of both cohorts recovering well despite their age-related vulnerability.

Retrospective cohort study of 67,000 German primary care patients comparing incidence of mild cognitive disorder (MCD) in COVID-19 patients versus acute upper respiratory infection controls. Found significantly higher MCD incidence in COVID-19 patients (7.6 vs 5.1 per 1,000 person-years), particularly in women and younger patients, but no treatment intervention was studied.

Prospective descriptive study of 97 post-COVID-19 patients examining musculoskeletal symptoms and pain using VAS, DN-4, and SF-36 assessments. Found that arthralgia, myalgia, and neuropathic pain are common in post-COVID patients and negatively correlate with quality of life, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This retrospective cohort study followed 1,546 COVID-19 survivors from Wuhan for two years post-discharge to assess long-term neurological symptoms. The study found that 44.24% reported at least one neurological symptom, with fatigue (28.33%) and memory deficit (13.26%) most common, and severe cases experiencing higher incidence of neurological sequelae.

Retrospective cohort study comparing dementia incidence in 8,129 matched pairs of COVID-19 patients versus acute upper respiratory infection controls over 12 months. Found no significant association between COVID-19 and dementia risk (IRR 1.05, 95% CI 0.85-1.29).

Observational longitudinal study following 350 post-acute COVID-19 patients over 12 months, assessing muscle function, quality of life, fatigue, and lung function at multiple timepoints. Results show progressive improvement in quality of life, fatigue, and pulmonary function, with greater gains in the first 6 months.

This prospective cohort study assessed cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes in 208 long COVID patients 25 months post-infection and 17 months after initial evaluation, with some patients participating in neuropsychological rehabilitation. Results showed persistent cognitive deficits despite discrete improvement, with better outcomes in patients who completed rehabilitation, had higher education, and lower depression scores.

This paper conducted an exploratory factor analysis of self-reported symptoms in long COVID patients collected at two time points (mean 21.7 weeks apart) to identify which acute-phase factors predict long-term impairment. Early autonomic and gastrointestinal dysfunction emerged as significant predictors of later functional impairment and ME/CFS-like symptoms.

This study compares cognitive functioning and brain connectivity at 6-12 months post-discharge in COVID-19 patients with multiple organ failure versus non-COVID MOF patients and healthy controls. While it documents neurological deficits in long COVID, it is an observational cross-sectional assessment without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This paper analyzes thin-section CT imaging in 59 COVID-19 patients 24-39 days post-hospital discharge to assess pulmonary fibrosis development. While it follows patients after acute infection, it is primarily an acute COVID-19 imaging study conducted during early recovery without testing any treatment intervention, making it outside the scope of long COVID treatment trials.

This cross-sectional study compares post-COVID-19 symptoms in 120 children (stratified by acute COVID severity) and 35 healthy controls, finding post-COVID condition in 38.3% overall with higher prevalence (71%) in those with severe acute COVID. The study documents symptom frequency, duration, and Chalder fatigue scale scores but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined 221 hospitalized COVID-19 patients 1-2 days before discharge to assess associations between hypertension and clinical features during acute infection and residual functional disorders. While the paper mentions long COVID syndrome in the introduction, it does not study an intervention or treatment—it only characterizes acute-phase clinical features and discharge-status outcomes in hypertensive vs normotensive patients, making it a baseline/prognostic study rather than a treatment trial.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of clinical manifestations in 253 COVID-19 survivors at different time points (within 3 months and 3-12 months post-infection), stratified by acute illness severity. The study found that persistent symptoms were common (58-82% of patients), with fatigue, shortness of breath, and cough being most prevalent, though no treatment intervention was tested.

Comparative study of 37 post-COVID patients with joint hypermobility syndrome versus 21 controls without COVID-19, examining clinical manifestations and treatment response over 2 months. Treatment with NSAIDs, tofisopam (anxiolytic), and sulbutiamine significantly reduced pain, anxiety, and improved quality of life in the post-COVID group.

This retrospective cohort study followed 268 COVID-19 pneumonia patients discharged from hospital with longitudinal laboratory measurements over five follow-up visits to characterize residual effects and recovery patterns. The study identified persistent abnormalities in hematologic parameters, immune cell function, and lung imaging up to 75 days post-discharge, with sex and age-based differences in recovery trajectories.

Open observational study evaluating whether Maxilac® Baby synbiotic improves gastrointestinal symptoms, gut microbiota composition, and intestinal permeability in 16 children (ages 3-14) with mild-to-moderate post-COVID-19 syndrome, compared to 16 untreated controls. Synbiotic treatment was associated with reduced recurrence of GI symptoms 30 days post-recovery compared to control group.

This retrospective study assessed long-term pulmonary changes in 68 COVID-19 patients 1–2 years post-infection using CT, SPECT, spirometry, and DLCO measurements. The paper documents imaging and functional findings associated with persistent respiratory symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examines microvascular abnormalities in 78 children 3-12 months post-COVID-19 using slit lamp biomicroscopy to assess bulbar conjunctival microvasculature, comparing them to 30 healthy controls. While microcirculatory disorders were identified and the authors mention designing rehabilitation measures, the paper is a descriptive observational study without testing or evaluating any specific intervention or treatment.

This study compares clinical and laboratory characteristics in 62 hemodialysis patients with chronic kidney disease stage 5, stratified by prior COVID-19 infection history. The authors report significantly higher mortality (35%) in COVID-19-infected dialysis patients versus uninfected controls (4.7%), attributed to protein-energy deficiency.

Prospective cohort study following mild-moderate COVID-19 patients at 6 weeks, 12 weeks, and 12 months post-infection to identify persistent symptoms and health status impact. Found that asthenia, anosmia, dysgeusia, and cognitive problems were most common, with several patients not recovering to baseline health status one year later, particularly those over 40, female, or with comorbidities.

A cross-sectional study comparing olfactory and trigeminal event-related potentials in 77 long COVID patients (≥1 year post-infection) versus 21 healthy controls. The study identifies electrophysiological biomarkers of post-COVID olfactory dysfunction but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This RCT evaluated four rehabilitation regimens in 195 post-COVID patients, comparing standard care alone versus standard care with vitamin, mineral, or combined vitamin-mineral supplementation over 6 months. Combined vitamin-mineral supplementation showed the greatest improvement in quality of life (measured by SF-36), with all intervention groups showing 10-20% improvement over the study period.

Prospective study comparing lung CT scan findings in 60 COVID-19 patients at hospital admission and 3 months post-discharge. Found that 53.3% of patients had persistent abnormal lung findings at follow-up, with more severe initial involvement predicting worse outcomes, but this is a descriptive follow-up study without treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates the frequency and nature of cardiovascular and other complications during long-term follow-up after COVID-19 in patients with and without pre-existing cardiovascular disease. The study identifies cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes in long COVID patients to inform clinical management.

This prospective cohort study measured endothelial function markers (endothelin-1 and thrombomodulin) in 16 patients who experienced non-hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia, assessed at 60 days and one year post-onset, with 10 healthy controls. Most patients showed clinical improvement and recovered lung function by one year, but elevated thrombomodulin levels persisted in some patients, suggesting ongoing endothelial dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study comparing electrophysiological changes (EEG) in Chornobyl clean-up workers and Ukrainian military personnel who recovered from COVID-19 versus control groups. Study documents persistent cerebral dysfunction (delta and theta power abnormalities) in COVID-19 recuperates but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines surfactant protein A (SP-A) levels in 77 patients with dyspnea during the subacute post-COVID period (day 47 post-infection) to assess lung surfactant system dysfunction. The study finds that elevated SP-A levels (>59 ng/ml) are associated with severe/critical acute COVID-19 disease and predict dyspnea severity, but it is an observational biomarker study without any treatment intervention.

A retrospective study of 85 long COVID patients in eastern Canada who received weekly acupuncture for 8-12 weeks. Results showed 85% clinical effectiveness with reduction in shortness of breath, fatigue, body pain, and brain fog.

Retrospective analysis of 90 post-COVID syndrome patients hospitalized for respiratory and lung complications, documenting the frequency and types of secondary infectious complications including fungal and bacterial infections. Study identifies infectious complications in 53.3% of patients, with Epstein-Barr virus reactivation (30%), bacterial infections (15.6%), and opportunistic fungi as primary causes, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cohort study assessed cardiovascular function and imaging findings in 30 COVID-19 recovered healthcare workers 3-12 months post-infection. Despite preserved exercise tolerance, subclinical cardiac abnormalities including myocardial edema and reduced right ventricular function were detected in nearly half the participants.

This retrospective cohort study followed 332 COVID-19 survivors for two months post-discharge to assess persistence and risk factors for fatigue using the Chalder fatigue scale. The study found that 62.9% of participants still experienced fatigue two months after hospital discharge, with significant associations between fatigue and age, comorbidities, and baseline biomarkers.

A cross-sectional study of 261 long COVID patients in Croatia examining symptoms, functional status (PCFS scale), and risk factors for severe impairment. Found that female sex, oxygen therapy during acute disease, malignant disease, and hypertension were associated with greater functional impairment, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Descriptive observational study analyzing chest X-ray findings in 277 RT-PCR confirmed COVID-19 patients during acute infection, correlating radiological findings with clinical severity and short-term outcomes. While it documents post-COVID complications (fatigue, SOB on exertion) observed after discharge, it does not study or test any treatment intervention for long COVID.

This retrospective epidemiological study examines the incidence of ixodid tick-borne borreliosis and tick-borne encephalitis in Krasnoyarsk residents, hypothesizing that increased susceptibility among post-COVID-19 individuals may be due to immune dysregulation. The study found higher proportions of women with prior COVID-19 among borreliosis and encephalitis cases, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective observational study that assessed hormonal changes (thyroid, adrenal, and sex-steroid axes) in 15 long COVID patients at baseline and 3-6 months post-infection. The study found high prevalence of endocrine dysfunctions at follow-up but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational cohort study examining the frequency and pattern of chest pain in long COVID patients over 3 months of follow-up at a cardiology center. Found that 59% of patients developed cardiac symptoms at 3 months, with chest pain due to coronary artery disease being a common manifestation, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A prospective cohort study of 98 older adults with post-COVID syndrome in Kazakhstan investigating the effectiveness and safety of transitioning from multiple antihypertensive medications to a single-tablet strategy over 8 weeks. The intervention led to significant reduction in hypertensive crises and adverse events, with improved initial therapy adherence that declined by 10% by week 8.

This cross-sectional study assessed thyroid functional status in 58 COVID-19 survivors (>6 months post-infection) compared to 27 healthy controls, measuring thyroid hormones and autoantibodies. While most survivors showed normal thyroid function, female survivors had significantly lower FT3 and FT4 levels, and 17% showed abnormalities including thyroid toxicity or elevated autoantibodies.

Observational study of 56 RT-PCR confirmed COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh documenting long-term sequelae at follow-up. Found high rates of fatigue (44.6%), memory impairment (39.3%), joint pain (39.6%), and psychiatric symptoms (28.6%) among survivors.

Prospective observational study of 3,000 COVID-19 patients evaluating the role of CT severity phenotypes (mild/moderate/severe) in predicting disease outcomes and post-COVID lung fibrosis. While CT severity correlated with interventions needed and long-term sequelae, it showed inconsistency in predicting individual disease severity and early outcomes.

Retro-prospective observational study of 606 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh documenting post-COVID symptoms at 3-10 months follow-up. Describes symptom prevalence (33.8% with symptoms) and phenotypes (fatigue, palpitations, muscle pain, neurological) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of 670 archival patient records from a rheumatology department examining the relationship between COVID-19 infection and rheumatic disease exacerbation, identifying three patient groups including those with post-COVID syndrome. The study documents post-COVID symptomatology (asthenia, arthropathy, connective tissue features) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This nationwide cohort study examined the incidence of unspecified and idiopathic pain in COVID-19 patients versus matched controls during the 90 days following COVID-19 diagnosis. The findings show elevated risk of unspecified pain post-COVID, though results vary by control group selection, and it is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study examining the incidence and characteristics of chronic daily headache (CDH) after COVID-19 in 199 patients with persistent headaches followed for at least one year post-infection. The study found that 20.3% developed CDH, with prior headache history and acute-phase headache intensity identified as risk factors.

This observational cohort study followed 177 COVID-19 patients over 12 months to assess dynamics of respiratory function and exercise tolerance, comparing those who developed post-COVID syndrome with those who did not. While the paper demonstrates that post-COVID syndrome is associated with persistent respiratory impairment requiring long-term rehabilitation, it is observational in design with no intervention tested and therefore excluded from the treatment trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular manifestations in 175 children aged 8-17 years with post-COVID autonomic dysfunction syndrome, comparing them to 42 controls without SARS-CoV-2 exposure. The study identified cardiac arrhythmias, hypertension, ECG changes, and lipid profile alterations associated with IgG antibodies to SARS-CoV-2.

A prospective 3-month follow-up study of 76 COVID-19 survivors evaluating symptom persistence, antibody dynamics, and pulmonary function after hospital discharge. While documenting post-acute symptoms like fatigue, dyspnea, and chest tightness, the study is purely observational monitoring without any intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

This cross-sectional study compared clinical characteristics and persistent symptoms in 1,122 patients who visited a post-COVID clinic, categorizing symptoms into three groups based on prevalence patterns across acute and post-acute phases. While it documents the multi-organ nature of long COVID symptoms and identifies anxiety, depression, and fatigue as key factors, it is a descriptive epidemiological study without any treatment intervention or control group.

Prospective follow-up study of 147 mild COVID-19 patients from a South Korean community treatment center assessing persistent symptoms and health-related quality of life 3 months after discharge. Found that 55.8% remained symptomatic with neuropsychiatric, neurological, and constitutional symptoms, with female sex, metabolic disease, and anxiety associated with long COVID persistence and diminished HRQoL.

This study evaluates comprehensive rehabilitation management (exercise, nutrition, psychology) in severe-to-critical COVID-19 inpatients during acute hospitalization and early recovery. While it shows rehabilitation improves functional outcomes, it focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months after infection) and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria.

Prospective follow-up study of 187 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing long COVID symptoms and gut microbiota composition at one year post-discharge. Found that 44.9% reported long COVID symptoms with significantly altered gut microbiota profiles compared to healthy controls, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between dysbiosis and persistent symptoms.

Retrospective analysis of 440 post-COVID patients at a clinic examining prevalence and associations of neurological symptoms (brain fog, memory impairment, headache, dizziness). Found brain fog most common (38.6%), with associations to sleep problems, fatigue, depression, and olfactory/gustatory dysfunction.

This prospective longitudinal study followed 82 COVID-19 patients for 12 weeks post-discharge to characterize persistent symptoms and their impact on quality of life, frailty, and employment. The study found that 75.6% of patients reported at least one symptom at 12 weeks (fatigue being most common), with significant declines in functional status and 6 patients losing employment.

This prospective study compared viral, immunologic, and laboratory parameters in 57 COVID-19 patients (29 with PASC, 28 without) at three timepoints over 3 months. PASC patients showed significantly elevated nucleocapsid antigen and multiple cytokines (IL-2, IL-17A, VEGF, RANTES, etc.), suggesting prolonged immune dysregulation rather than autoimmune or hormonal abnormalities.

This cross-sectional study of 257 outpatients with mild COVID-19 identifies prognostic factors associated with longer symptom duration and development of post-COVID-19 conditions (>12 weeks), including vitamin D deficiency, leukocytosis, reduced lung function, and anxiety/depression symptoms. While the paper suggests antiviral agents and vitamin D supplements might help reduce symptom duration, it is a prognostic/observational study that does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance claims data examined stroke risk in COVID-19 survivors with asthma compared to those without asthma and the general population. The study found that severe COVID-19 was associated with significantly elevated stroke risk in asthma patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 583 lymphoma patients examining long-term COVID-19 outcomes and risk factors for prolonged infection. While the paper studies prolonged COVID-19 symptoms in immunocompromised patients, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely observational/epidemiological research on disease outcomes and prognostic factors.

A prospective cohort study comparing two long COVID diagnostic criteria (PASC index vs NASEM criteria) in 183 Korean adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed for 12 months. The study evaluates the prevalence and agreement between criteria but does not test any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective descriptive study examining long COVID patients with anosmia and agnosia symptoms at a single hospital in 2021, identifying 3 cases of persistent anosmia but no agnosia cases. Study describes demographic patterns (predominantly female, ages 20-30) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Analysis of insurance claims data for 42,859 young adults (18-29) with COVID-19 diagnosis, tracking healthcare utilization patterns over 180 days post-diagnosis. While documenting long-term symptoms in some patients, this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This dissertation analyzes data from the VASCO observational study to evaluate COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness against infection and long-term symptoms including fatigue and post-COVID condition. The study examines vaccine protection across variants and booster doses but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

Multinational population-based cohort study examining long-term gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary complications in COVID-19 patients across South Korea, Japan, and the UK. Found increased incidence of gastrointestinal diseases, hepatobiliary diseases, and digestive abnormalities persisting >6 months post-infection, with risk pronounced in severe COVID cases.

This prospective matched cohort study compares menstrual health, ovarian reserve biomarkers, and pregnancy outcomes in 316 women from North-East India stratified into long COVID (n=158) and matched post-COVID control groups (n=158). The study found that long COVID is associated with increased menstrual irregularities, reduced AMH levels, lower fecundability, and elevated risk of preterm birth and gestational hypertension.

Prospective cohort study following 324 symptomatic laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases for ≥12 months to describe persistent long-term health effects and their predictors by initial illness severity. At 1 year, 60% reported persistent symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, muscle weakness), and those with moderate/severe illness had significantly lower health-related quality of life scores despite adjusted analysis nullifying most symptom associations.

This study examines how post-COVID hemodynamic disorders affect postoperative wound healing in maxillofacial surgical patients using laser doppler flowmetry measurements. The study found that patients with a history of COVID-19 showed impaired endothelial function and less stable microvascular regulation compared to controls, with recovery taking longer.

An observational study examining high-resolution CT patterns in 56 post-COVID patients with pulmonary sequelae. Found ground glass opacities (89%), reticulations (86%), and unique dome-shaped subpleural fibrosis (54%) as common radiological findings.

A retrospective observational study of 71 long COVID patients examining the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on respiratory outcomes (oxygen saturation, MMRC dyspnea scale, cough, 6-minute walk distance) and inflammatory biomarkers over 3 weeks. Results showed significant improvements in respiratory function and normalization of biomarkers (CRP, D-dimer) in 61 of 71 patients.

Retrospective study examining thrombotic event risk in 145 patients with prior COVID-19 (≥12 weeks post-infection). Finds that prior COVID-19 alone is not a significant predictor of thrombotic events; main risk factors are comorbidities (hypertension, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation) and smoking.

A retrospective cohort study following COVID-19 patients from the Osh region of Kyrgyz Republic from 2020-2022, with follow-up assessment in 2024 to identify long-term manifestations of coronavirus infection. The study uses statistical analysis to estimate associations between post-COVID indicators and severity, age, year, and instrumental measures, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 170 adult COVID-19 patients at 6 and 12 months post-infection to assess persistent symptoms and quality of life. Found that 48.8% of patients had ongoing COVID-19-related symptoms at 12 months, predominantly neuropsychiatric symptoms (amnesia, insomnia, fatigue, anxiety), with significant impacts on quality of life and depression scores.

This retrospective cohort study compared psychocognitive function in 110 post-COVID patients with comorbidities to 123 non-COVID controls, finding significantly higher rates of depression and cognitive dysfunction in the post-COVID group. The study evaluated sulodexide as a potential therapeutic intervention, showing that patients receiving sulodexide had milder cognitive dysfunction compared to untreated post-COVID patients.

Comparative analysis of COVID-19 course and post-COVID syndrome in patients with rheumatic diseases, comparing early strains versus Omicron across a 12-month follow-up period. The study found higher severity and longer symptom duration with early strains, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective observational study of 239 post-COVID patients examining thrombotic complications (venous and arterial) occurring weeks to months after acute infection, with analysis of surgical intervention outcomes. Venous thrombosis was significantly more common than arterial thrombosis, predominantly affecting the lower extremities, particularly in women and those with comorbid cardiovascular disease.

This study analyzed data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) to examine four-year health and economic outcomes in long COVID patients compared to COVID-recovered and no-COVID groups.
