Found that pre-infection psychotropic use was associated with higher risk of slow or persisting symptoms, suggesting psychological conditions increase risk of poorer COVID-19 evolution and potential long COVID development.

This longitudinal observational study tracked 127 patients with work-related COVID-19 through inpatient post-COVID rehabilitation, assessing mental health, fatigue, and cognitive function at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months post-discharge. While cognitive function remained stable, mental health and fatigue improvements observed immediately after rehabilitation did not persist at follow-up, highlighting the need for ongoing aftercare and individualized interventions.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long COVID prevalence and predictors in hospitalized vs non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Brazil. Identifies female sex, hypertension, and depression screening as key predictors of long COVID development, but does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Prospective observational cohort study following 54 COVID-19 ICU survivors and 42 family members one year after discharge. The study documents long-term physical (fatigue 63%, dyspnea 68.5%), functional, and mental health consequences (anxiety, depression, PTSD) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal observational study assessing health-related quality of life and disability in primary caregivers of pediatric post-COVID-19 survivors compared to caregivers of unaffected children. Found significantly higher pain/discomfort in caregivers of COVID-19 patients (74% vs 52.5%), but this study does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it only measures caregiver outcomes.

Cross-sectional study of 318 post-COVID patients in Italy examining the prevalence and functional characterization of exertional dyspnea at 3 months post-infection. Identified five independent predictors of post-COVID exertional dyspnea (fatigue, respiratory comorbidities, allergy history, age, acute-phase dyspnea) with sex-specific risk patterns.

This nationwide retrospective cohort study examines one-year outcomes and mortality in COVID-19 patients compared to matched controls using South Korean claims data. It documents post-acute syndrome symptoms (coagulopathies, respiratory issues, mood disorders, cardiac disease) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study measured cardiorespiratory fitness (via peak VO2) in firefighters before and after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 infection, finding a 7.3% decline ~110 days post-infection that recovered by ~300 days. The study does not test any intervention or treatment; it is purely observational and therefore excluded.

Prospective cohort study following 706 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients in China over 6 months to characterize long COVID symptom prevalence, natural history, and associated risk factors. Found 68.4% experienced symptoms at 3 months declining to 49.7% at 6 months, with fatigue, dyspnea, and sleep disturbances as primary residual symptoms; older age and comorbidities were risk factors for persistent symptoms.

This observational study compared physical activity, perceived exertion, and quality of life between 10 long COVID patients and 10 healthy controls using wearable devices and standardized assessment tools. Long COVID participants showed significantly longer task completion times, higher perceived exertion, and worse physical quality of life, suggesting occupational therapy interventions could improve outcomes.

Prospective multicenter US cohort study examining ethnic and racial differences in self-reported symptoms, health status, activity level, and missed work at 3 and 6 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Findings show Hispanic and racial minority participants experienced greater health impacts at 3 months, with some disparities persisting at 6 months, highlighting inequities in long COVID outcomes.

This matched cohort study describes the prevalence and time course of long COVID symptoms up to 24 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 576 non-hospitalized German COVID-19 patients and 302 uninfected controls. Long COVID-compatible symptoms occurred in 42.9% of former patients versus 21.2% of uninfected controls, with most symptoms resolving within a median of 6.5 months, though taste/smell and neurological symptoms persisted longer.

Retrospective cohort study of 630 long COVID patients from a telehealth service examining the incidence and risk factors for post-acute cognitive symptoms at 12 weeks post-infection. Identifies female sex, fatigue, depression, and need for acute in-person care as independent risk factors for cognitive symptoms, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This prospective cohort study followed 1,374 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Norway for 4 months to compare symptom trajectories and risk factors between Delta and Omicron infections. The study found that Omicron patients had comparable overall symptom burden but less dyspnea and smell/taste problems than Delta patients, though some symptoms like depression and neurocognitive issues increased during follow-up; however, this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment component, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective observational study using Bahrain's national administrative database to characterize the burden of acute COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 conditions (PCC) from May 2021 to April 2023. Reports incidence and mortality rates across variant surges and identifies demographic risk factors for PCC, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective case-control study comparing clinical and serological predictors between 102 long COVID patients and 122 unaffected COVID-19 survivors. Found that long COVID cases had higher rates of anti-Spike and anti-RBD IgG positivity and greater neutralization efficiency, with clinical risk factors including obesity, time post-infection, and need for medical support.

Prospective cohort study tracking persistent symptoms in 1,536 children aged 6-18 years during 1-2 months post-Omicron infection using serial surveys (4 timepoints). Found that breathing and mental health problems persisted in >50% and ~95% of children respectively at 1-2 months, with symptom burden varying by age group.

This retrospective cohort study with propensity-score matched controls examines whether pre-COVID health-related quality of life predicts PASC symptoms and outcomes in 1,114 patients. While the study confirms associations between baseline HRQL and symptom severity, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

This prospective cohort study followed 355 first-time infected outpatients over 9 months post-omicron infection in China, tracking symptom prevalence and burden through repeated patient-reported surveys. The study identified symptom clusters, severity patterns, and demographic risk factors (younger age, female sex, BMI≥24) for prolonged symptoms, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Registry-based observational study examining long-term mortality and morbidity in COVID-19 hospitalized patients (n=22,571) compared to matched controls, with focus on baseline medication load as a predictor. No intervention or treatment is tested; this is a passive observational follow-up study of acute COVID-19 hospitalization outcomes.

Cross-sectional observational study examining musculoskeletal pain and disability in 195 long COVID patients, comparing hospitalized vs non-hospitalized individuals. Hospitalized patients showed greater disability and pain intensity, with ICU stay and mechanical ventilation duration as predictors of pain.

This observational study with control groups evaluates multimodal inpatient rehabilitation (somatomedical and psychotherapeutic) in post-COVID patients compared to psychosomatic and psychocardiological controls. Post-COVID patients showed significant symptom reduction across all domains during rehabilitation (effect sizes d=0.34–1.22), with improvements in walking distance (76.43m), self-efficacy, and activity participation, with no signs of post-exercise malaise.

This study longitudinally monitored recovery in breathlessness, symptom burden, and mental health in 58 individuals hospitalized for SARS-CoV-2 respiratory failure over 90 days post-discharge using smartphone-based assessments. While it documents symptom recovery after acute COVID hospitalization, it does not study long COVID (which requires persistent symptoms weeks-to-months after infection) nor does it test any treatment intervention.

This study followed 39 COVID-19 patients for two months post-discharge to assess functional and psychological recovery without structured rehabilitation intervention. Findings showed minimal improvements in functional parameters over the two-month period, highlighting the importance of supervised rehabilitation programs.

A retrospective analysis of 99 long COVID patients who participated in a resonant breathing program. Most participants showed improvements in symptoms and wellbeing, with 92% reporting improvement on the Patient Global Impression of Change Scale.

Retrospective observational study of 58 severe COVID-19 patients assessed 2-3 months post-discharge for clinical and functional status, including lung imaging, spirometry, and exercise capacity. No intervention was tested; this is a passive observational follow-up study characterizing natural recovery patterns.

This observational study evaluates functional recovery in subacute COVID-19 patients (71-180 days post-infection) who received multidisciplinary rehabilitation, comparing outcomes between those previously in ICU vs. medical care units. While it does study a treatment intervention (rehabilitation), it focuses on acute/subacute hospitalization recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection).

This cross-sectional observational study examined the relationship between post-COVID-19 symptoms and daily physical activity in 18 PCS patients using smartwatch tracking and daily symptom surveys. The study found that dizziness was negatively associated with physical activity, while lower fatigue and chest pain were linked to higher daily step counts, but no intervention was administered to participants.

A prospective multicenter study of 272 severe COVID-19 survivors examining the prevalence and factors associated with xerostomia (dry mouth). Found xerostomia in 20.6% of patients, with asthma/COPD, palpitations, and chest pain as independent risk factors.

This prospective observational study tracked 166 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors over 12 months to evaluate symptom dynamics and predict long COVID persistence using survey-based assessments and machine learning. While it demonstrates that symptom scales at 3 months can predict 12-month long COVID persistence with 91% accuracy, it is a purely observational natural history study with no treatment or intervention provided to participants.

A 4-month prospective cohort study of 2,471 Chinese participants examining changes in frailty after COVID-19 infection using interrupted time series and Cox regression analysis. The study found increased frailty post-pandemic and identified lifestyle factors (mood, physical activity, diet) associated with frailty reduction, but does not test a specific intervention—it is an observational study of natural health trajectories and associations with behavioral factors rather than a treatment trial.

This prospective cohort study assessed physical activity levels and their association with persistent COVID-19 symptoms in 64 non-hospitalized survivors at 8.5 months and 43 participants at 4.25 years post-infection. COVID-19 survivors with persistent symptoms showed significantly lower physical activity levels and daily steps compared to those without symptoms, though activity rebounded to pre-pandemic levels by 4 years.

This cross-sectional study compared physical capacities and health outcomes in 120 individuals with Long COVID, 120 with short COVID, and 120 controls without COVID history. While the study provides valuable descriptive data on physical impairments, pain, fatigue, and quality of life in Long COVID patients, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention and therefore does not meet criteria as a treatment trial.

This prospective cohort study examines COVID-19's short- and long-term effects on male reproductive hormones and semen parameters in 48 patients (30 asymptomatic, 18 symptomatic) followed for 6 months post-infection. While the paper documents temporary testosterone changes during acute infection recovery, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and is primarily about acute reproductive effects rather than treating long COVID complications.

Cross-sectional study examining cardiac abnormalities in 150 previously healthy outpatients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome 4-12 weeks after mild/moderate infection using echocardiography. Found cardiac abnormalities in 25.33% of patients, with significant correlations between symptom severity and cardiac dysfunction metrics.

This study examines the relationship between Mediterranean diet adherence and inflammatory/oxidative stress markers in long-COVID patients, comparing low and high adherence groups (n=188 total). High MD adherence was associated with reduced LDH, LDL-cholesterol, and glucose levels, with gut microbiota composition (specifically Oscillibacter abundance) mediating these effects.

This paper uses National COVID Cohort Collaborative (N3C) EHR data to create a balanced cohort of long COVID and non-long COVID patients and analyzes whether documented long COVID is associated with decreased survival length using Bayesian survival analysis. It is a secondary analysis of existing EHR data rather than an original treatment intervention study.

Retrospective cohort study examining long COVID risk factors and outcomes among solid organ transplant recipients, comparing graft failure and mortality rates between those with and without long COVID diagnosis. Found that long COVID was not significantly associated with death or graft failure in this transplant population, though relationships varied by transplant type.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated the effects of a multicomponent exercise program (Vivifrail) on frailty and physical function in older adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome who had been admitted to intensive care units. The intervention produced statistically significant improvements across multiple measures of frailty, muscle strength, balance, gait, and functional independence.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiac function via echocardiography in 112 long COVID patients with diabetes/metabolic syndrome versus 91 controls without metabolic dysfunction. Patients with metabolic disorders showed significantly higher rates of left/right ventricular dysfunction and diastolic dysfunction, with predictive associations between inflammatory markers and cardiac abnormalities at 6-month follow-up.

This cohort study describes COVID-19 patients hospitalized during acute infection in France, examining referral patterns to rehabilitation units post-hospitalization. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization and post-acute rehabilitation needs, not on long COVID as a distinct chronic condition months after infection.

This cross-sectional study compared left and right ventricular strain using echocardiography in 184 post-COVID patients versus 106 matched controls without COVID-19 history. The study found significantly reduced ventricular strain in recovered COVID-19 patients correlating with reduced exercise capacity, but did not test any specific treatment or intervention.

This CT imaging study compared thymic appearance in 102 COVID-19 patients with and without pulmonary sequelae at 3-month follow-up. Thymic involution was associated with a 9.3-fold increased odds of pulmonary sequelae, suggesting thymic reactivation may protect against long-term COVID outcomes.

This study evaluates plasma levels of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2, MMP-9) and TIMP-1 in acute COVID-19 patients at hospital admission and 3 months post-discharge, stratified by ARDS severity. It does not study long COVID patients or any treatment interventions, focusing instead on biomarkers of acute-phase disease and recovery.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates hs-TnI and sST-2 biomarkers as predictors of major cardiovascular events (MACE) in 251 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors during ~415-day follow-up. While relevant to long COVID sequelae, it is a secondary analysis of existing biomarker data rather than an intervention trial.

This retrospective observational study compared neuropsychological performance in 226 younger and older COVID-19 survivors at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months post-infection using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. The findings suggest COVID-19 survivors experience cognitive deficits characterized by attention/concentration difficulties affecting memory retrieval processes, consistent with post-COVID 'brain fog' symptoms.

This cross-sectional study examines factors contributing to persistent exercise intolerance in 120 long COVID patients 3-6 months post-infection with normal left ventricular function. The authors identify that male gender and specific cardiac/hydration parameters (late diastolic filling velocity, TAPSE, global peak systolic strain) are independently associated with reduced oxygen uptake at peak exercise.

This observational study examined the prevalence and evolution of diastolic dysfunction in 203 post-COVID-19 patients with and without obesity/metabolic syndrome, using transthoracic echocardiography at baseline and 6-month follow-up. While it demonstrates cardiovascular complications in long COVID, it is observational and descriptive with no intervention tested or evaluated.

Retrospective cohort and cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of long COVID-19 symptoms (34% at 2 years post-infection) and their association with anxiety and depression among 1,038 healthcare workers. The study found significant associations between acute-phase and long COVID symptoms and mental health outcomes, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Multicenter prospective cohort study following 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors at four timepoints (8-18 months post-discharge) to track the trajectory of self-reported fatigue and dyspnoea symptoms. Found that fatigue prevalence decreased from 56.94% to 42.66% and dyspnoea from 28.71% to 12.04% over follow-up, with female sex identified as a risk factor for persistent symptoms.

A prospective longitudinal study of 106 older patients (≥65 years) who recovered from COVID-19, assessing body composition, muscle strength, and sarcopenia prevalence at 3 and 12 months post-infection. The study found high sarcopenia at 3 months that improved by 12 months alongside functional and symptomatic recovery, without significant changes in lean mass.

This cross-sectional study examined arterial and aortic stiffness and diastolic dysfunction in 121 women with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (with and without metabolic syndrome) compared to 40 healthy controls using echocardiography and pulse-wave velocity measurements. Patients with concurrent metabolic syndrome showed worse cardiovascular parameters, with aortic stiffness, C-reactive protein, and triglyceride-glucose index identified as independent predictors of diastolic dysfunction.

This prospective study examined radiological pulmonary changes in 54 critically ill COVID-19 patients treated with mechanical ventilation, comparing intubation methods at 6-month follow-up. The paper focuses on acute respiratory failure during active infection rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Prospective case series of 278 PASC-CVS patients receiving guideline-oriented medical therapy (NSAIDs for pericardial effusion, heart failure medications for cardiac dysfunction). Three-month follow-up imaging in 82 patients showed significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction and reduction in pericardial effusion, with clinical symptom improvement.

This retrospective cohort study compares hospitalized COVID-19 patients with and without type 2 diabetes, analyzing in-hospital mortality and cardiovascular endpoints at 10-month follow-up. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes and comorbidity effects rather than long COVID symptoms or treatments.

This cross-sectional study compares clinical features and pulmonary involvement in 282 post-COVID patients assessed up to 12 weeks after acute COVID-19 recovery. Patients with pulmonary involvement showed distinct characteristics including older age, higher hospitalization rates, and significantly impaired pulmonary function, suggesting pulmonary involvement represents a distinct phenotype requiring individualized clinical approaches.

This observational cohort study evaluated muscle loss and functional status in 16 COVID-19 pneumonia patients during hospitalization and at follow-up points up to 6 months post-discharge. The study found significant reductions in muscle mass, handgrip strength, and quality of life that persisted 6 months after discharge, but did not test any specific intervention or treatment.

This prospective cross-sectional study compared immune cell profiles and pituitary-adrenal axis function in 29 long COVID patients versus 13 recovered controls at 6+ months post-infection. The study found dysregulation in certain immune cells and immune activation but no significant adrenal dysfunction or association between cortisol levels and clinical symptoms.

This cross-sectional study compared kidney function tests six months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection between patients with Post-COVID Syndrome (n=92) and controls (n=114). Post-COVID patients showed significantly elevated serum creatinine, reduced eGFR, and higher albuminuria, indicating persistent renal impairment that the authors argue requires ongoing monitoring and intervention strategies.

Prospective single-center study following 46 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors at 3 and 9 months post-discharge to assess persistent symptoms and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Identified fatigue as the most common persistent symptom, with 80-82% of patients reporting impaired HRQoL in at least one domain, particularly pain/discomfort.

A 12-month longitudinal study of 47 COVID-19 patients examining body composition changes and cytokine production in relation to insulin resistance (HOMA-IR). Patients with elevated HOMA-IR showed increased body fat, decreased lean mass, and altered cytokine profiles suggesting immune dysfunction and chronic inflammation.

A prospective cohort study examining hemoglobin levels and their relationship with fatigue in 95 long-COVID patients 3-6 months post-infection. While the study finds hemoglobin increase associated with lower fatigue odds, it is observational without any intervention or treatment—patients are followed passively without receiving a specific therapy.

Prospective cohort study following CKD and non-CKD patients for three years post-COVID-19 infection to examine long-term PASC outcomes and the impact of RAAS-blocker therapy. Results showed no permanent renal function changes and most patients recovered from PASC symptoms within a short period, though some required prolonged management.

Longitudinal descriptive study analyzing pharmacotherapy patterns in 95 long COVID patients across pre-COVID, acute, and post-COVID phases. Pre-COVID medication history is explored as a potential health status indicator for characterizing patients, but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.

Prospective observational cohort study of 88 long COVID patients (aged 40-65) followed monthly over 12-18 months to identify symptom progression trajectories for fatigue and dyspnea. Identified three distinct trajectories (decreasing, high persistent, low persistent) and found that lifestyle intervention participation, smoking status, sex, age, and COVID-19 severity were associated with symptom progression patterns.

This study implements a novel remote patient monitoring system to track symptom intensity changes over 15 days in 133 COVID-19 survivors and post-COVID syndrome patients across four recovery groups. The analysis reveals distinct symptom profiles among groups, with shortness of breath, fatigue, cough, headache, and body pain being most prevalent, providing insights for personalized care strategies.

This multinational retrospective cohort study investigates mortality risk in 651 acute COVID-19 survivors followed until December 2023, with comparison to age- and sex-matched COVID-negative controls. The authors identify 201 urinary peptides associated with post-acute mortality and develop a peptide-based classifier (DP201) that predicts death risk in post-acute COVID-19 patients, demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 infection significantly increases mortality risk for approximately one year post-infection.

Retrospective cohort study of 244 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed at a post-COVID clinic, comparing 110 patients who developed PASC with 134 who did not. Identifies female gender, type 2 diabetes, and acute COVID symptoms as risk factors for PASC development and prognostic markers for symptom evolution.

This retrospective observational study compared vitamin D and electrolyte levels in 406 hospitalized children with post-COVID-19 status versus SARS-CoV-2/EBV coinfection. While it examines post-COVID children, it is primarily an observational descriptive study of biochemical markers in acute/recent infection rather than a long COVID intervention trial.

This three-year follow-up study assessed 192 post-COVID patients using fatigue questionnaires and cardiopulmonary exercise testing to evaluate physical capacity and aerobic fitness. The study found that 24% of the population still exhibited persistent long-COVID syndrome with reduced cardiorespiratory fitness and increased symptom burden, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study investigated the occurrence of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) in 100 severe COVID-19 patients with pneumonia and thrombosis, testing for aPLs at multiple time points during hospitalization and 3-month follow-up. While the paper connects APS findings to post-COVID syndrome pathophysiology, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely a diagnostic/observational study examining aPLs prevalence and patterns.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data examining herpes zoster reactivation following COVID-19 and its association with renal, infectious, and autoimmune complications. Propensity-matched analysis found HZ after COVID-19 significantly increased risks of MAKE, sepsis, SLE, and RA over three-year follow-up.

This repeated cross-sectional study examined long-term health and cognitive effects of COVID-19 in 584 university students up to four years post-infection, assessing how variants, vaccination status, and illness severity impact outcomes. Results showed persistent fatigue and memory impairments, particularly in women and men respectively, with the ancestral variant having the greatest long-term impact and Omicron the least.

This retrospective cohort study assessed spirometric changes in 103 healthcare workers over three years post-COVID-19 infection, comparing pulmonary function at baseline, one year, and two years post-pandemic. While it documents significant declines in FVC and FEV1 associated with smoking and reinfection, it is an observational study without any intervention or treatment component.

This study evaluated sociodemographic factors and health status in 113 COVID-19 survivors at a Brazilian multidisciplinary clinic, classifying participants as having post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) or subacute infection. Key findings showed 63.7% had PACS, with ICU admission, hair loss, paresthesia, and slowed cognition significantly more prevalent in the PACS group, though acute infection severity did not predict PACS diagnosis in multivariate analysis.

Retrospective cohort study of 54 post-COVID patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) identifying clinical and echocardiographic predictors of thrombolysis treatment. Reduced TAPSE, lower SpO2, and decreased LVEDD were significant predictors of receiving systemic thrombolysis, providing a risk-stratification approach for managing post-COVID VTE.

This is a secondary analysis of the ORCHESTRA prospective cohort study examining associations between biochemical markers and post-COVID condition phenotypes at 18-month follow-up in 4,587 patients. The study found elevated CRP levels in respiratory phenotype patients but does not test any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials extraction pipeline.

This propensity-matched analysis from the HOPE-2 multi-center registry examines the effect of corticosteroid therapy on mortality and long-term COVID-19 symptoms in 1,188 patients with pre-existing cardiovascular disease (453 treated with corticosteroids). While corticosteroids showed no significant difference in 18-month mortality or long-term COVID symptoms, they were associated with shorter hospitalization duration, suggesting a potential balance between beneficial and adverse effects in this high-risk subgroup.

This study evaluated retinal microvascular changes in COVID-19 patients with bilateral pneumonia at 6 months post-discharge using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). The findings show persistent microvascular alterations and decreased vascular density at 6 months, indicating long-term structural changes from COVID-19.

Retrospective observational study of 60 long COVID patients examining pulmonary impairments using spirometry, chest X-rays, and CT scans. Despite normal spirometry in 88% of patients, 75% showed reduced diffusion capacity and 65% exhibited ground-glass opacities, indicating persistent lung damage without intervention testing.

This study followed 80 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients over time, measuring longitudinal changes in retinal microcirculation using optical coherence tomography angiography. The results showed vessel density remained stable with no significant changes during follow-up, suggesting stable microvascular characteristics in patients with physically stable PCS symptoms.

Cross-sectional study of 38 COVID-19 patients who underwent neuropsychological testing ~5 months post-hospitalization. Found high prevalence of processing speed deficits (42.1%) and verbal recall deficits (26.3%), with worse memory performance associated with ARDS severity and lower oxygen levels during acute illness.

This prospective cohort study assessed depressive symptoms and suicidality in 115 individuals at 3 months following hospitalization for COVID-19 using the PHQ-9 questionnaire. The study found that 14.8% met criteria for depression, with female sex, pulmonary comorbidities, and prior psychiatric history identified as significant risk factors.

This observational cohort study followed 130 COVID-19 survivors for 6 months to characterize post-acute symptoms and assess overlap with ME/CFS criteria. Only 13% of patients met ME/CFS diagnostic criteria, with fatigue being the most common symptom (47%), associated with older age and longer initial hospitalization.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between sleep quality and mental health symptoms in 79 long COVID patients presenting to a recovery clinic. While it documents the prevalence of insomnia and psychological comorbidities (depression, anxiety, PTSD), it is an observational assessment without any treatment intervention or control group.

A cross-sectional study of 64 inpatients and 79 outpatients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome examining cardiovascular abnormalities, mental health difficulties, and quality of life using echocardiography, mental health assessment, and standardized scales. The study found elevated rates of cardiac dysfunction, depression, and anxiety in post-COVID patients, particularly among inpatients, with these cardiovascular and mental health issues correlating with reduced quality of life.

This study evaluates neuromuscular involvement in 21 patients admitted for post-acute rehabilitation after COVID-19 using clinical and neurophysiological assessments. While it documents muscle and nerve injuries in rehabilitation patients, it is primarily focused on acute COVID-19 sequelae during critical illness rather than long COVID (chronic post-acute sequelae occurring weeks-to-months after infection) and does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 627 hospitalised COVID-19 survivors examining the association between vaccination timing and long COVID symptoms using Bayesian logistic regression. Finds that pre-infection vaccination shows a protective trend while post-infection vaccination reflects indication bias, with comorbidities and prolonged acute hospitalisation being the strongest independent predictors.

This retrospective cohort study compares neuropsychological, pneumological, and motor function outcomes in 37 long COVID patients admitted to rehabilitation who differed by respiratory support during acute infection (non-invasive vs invasive mechanical ventilation). At discharge, cognitive impairment persisted in 52% of reassessed patients, with Group-1 (non-invasive support) showing worse cognitive deficits across multiple measures; the study recommends long-term neuropsychological follow-up and treatment.

A prospective observational study of 64 post-acute COVID-19 patients (56 with brain fog) treated with multidisciplinary rehabilitation enhanced by individualized neuropsychological cognitive stimulation for 30 days. Treatment significantly improved Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores (20.4 to 24.7; p<0.0001), with 43% of cognitively impaired patients normalizing function by discharge.

Longitudinal cohort study following 144 recovered COVID-19 subjects in China for up to 2 years post-infection to assess quality of life and mental health status. Found low incidence of psychological problems (4.4% at 1 year, no new cases at 2 years) and improved quality of life over time, though some mental health issues persisted long-term.

Prospective cohort study following 230 COVID-19 survivors over 24 months to assess neuropsychiatric symptoms. Found 36.1% still had symptoms at 24 months, with depression and concentration problems as significant predictors, highlighting ongoing mental health support needs.

This observational study compares autonomic cardiovascular function between 39 post-COVID-19 patients and healthy controls using cardiac frequency variability and autonomic reflex tests. The study found no significant dysautonomia in post-COVID patients overall, but identified associations between paresthesia and altered cardiac vagal activity, suggesting peripheral nerve involvement.

This cross-sectional study investigated the frequency, characteristics, and correlates of cognitive complaints in 74 long COVID patients approximately 7 months post-infection using psychiatric, medical, and neuropsychological testing. The study found that cognitive complaints correlate with objective neuropsychological performance deficits, but is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it only characterizes cognitive symptoms and their clinical correlates through assessments.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study examining depression, anxiety, and neuropsychiatric symptoms in patients with persistent post-COVID olfactory dysfunction over one year. Finds that 38-41% report depression and 27-29% report anxiety, with word-finding and focus difficulties being most common persistent symptoms.

Observational study comparing 246 post-COVID-19 patients who received anti-IL-6 receptor agents (tocilizumab or sarilumab, N=88) versus controls (N=158), assessing effects on psychiatric and physical symptoms. Patients receiving IL-6 inhibitors showed lower post-COVID illness burden and improved emotion regulation, with tocilizumab showing the strongest effects.

Prospective telephone survey of 97 cancer patients to assess long COVID incidence 12+ weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with stratification by prior early anti-SARS-CoV-2 therapy exposure. Found 12.4% long COVID prevalence; no significant difference by early therapy use, but female sex and diabetes were associated with long COVID.

Population-based registry study comparing COVID-19 severity and survival in unvaccinated patients with hematologic malignancies versus non-cancer patients across two time periods (early vs. later waves). While 27.3% of evaluable patients had post COVID-19 condition, the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data examining long-term health risks (cardiovascular events, respiratory failure, sepsis, colorectal cancer) in COVID-19 survivors who developed herpes zoster reactivation versus those who did not. Findings show post-COVID herpes zoster is associated with increased risk of adverse outcomes including colorectal cancer, but this is an observational risk assessment study, not an intervention trial.

Retrospective case series evaluating co-ultraPEALut (anti-inflammatory) treatment in 26 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment over 10 months. Treated patients showed significant improvement in memory questionnaire (PRMQ) and subjective cognitive improvement compared to 15 untreated controls, suggesting neuroinflammation modulation may benefit neuro-long-COVID symptoms.

This study examined psychological distress in 40 patients admitted to rehabilitation after discharge from intensive care for COVID-19, comparing those who received invasive versus non-invasive ventilation. The research found that many subjects experienced emotional distress (anxiety, depression, PTSD), but found no significant differences between ventilation groups.

Prospective observational study of 162 COVID-19 patients assessing long-term smell and taste recovery using subjective VAS scales and objective testing (B-SIT, BTS) at multiple timepoints up to 180 days. Most patients showed full chemosensory recovery within 4 weeks, with no intervention or treatment provided.

This study compared heart rate variability data from 28 adolescents with dysautonomia (IST or POTS) following COVID-19 infection/vaccination to 64 historical controls with pre-pandemic dysautonomia, then evaluated treatment effects of low-dose propranolol, ivabradine, and omega-3 fatty acid supplementation. Low-dose propranolol was most effective at reducing heart rate elevation in both IST and POTS patients, followed by ivabradine and omega-3 supplementation.

This study measures brain injury biomarkers (NfL, GFAP, sCD163) in COVID-19 patients at hospital admission and 3 months post-discharge to assess neurological damage in acute and post-acute stages. It is a cross-sectional biomarker comparison study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trial meta-analysis.

Retrospective study of 1,250 children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection evaluated at a post-COVID clinic to characterize olfactory and gustatory dysfunction prevalence and evolution over 18 months. Found that anosmia and dysgeusia symptoms gradually decreased over time, with pre-Omicron variant infection and acute-phase dysfunction as significant risk factors for persistence.

A national matched cohort study of 20,202 children and young people describing symptom profiles 12 months after SARS-CoV-2 testing. The study found that those with positive tests reported more symptoms than those who never tested positive, with fatigue and mental health impacts noted, though no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Retrospective survey of 194 children 12 months post-COVID-19 assessing prevalence and characteristics of residual cough and asthma-like symptoms. Found 92.2% reported persistent symptoms with cough in 69.8%, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Retrospective chart review of youth with PASC examining symptom presentation, severity, and referral patterns to treatment programs. Findings suggest youth present with less severe PASC symptoms than adults, and most are not referred to treatment programs despite clinical presentation.

Retrospective study of 1,224 children tracking gastrointestinal symptoms from acute SARS-CoV-2 infection through 18-month follow-up, evaluating lactoferrin treatment effectiveness. Found GI symptoms persisted in a small proportion of children over 12-18 months, with a non-significant trend toward improvement with lactoferrin treatment.

This cross-sectional study assessed sleep disorders in 45 children and adolescents with long COVID using the CSHQ-DE questionnaire at multiple timepoints (pre-COVID, initial presentation, and re-presentation). Sleep disturbances were common initially but normalized over time without medical intervention beyond basic sleep consultation.

Descriptive study comparing characteristics of children aged 11-17 seeking treatment at a Post-COVID service in England (n=95) with participants in the CLoCk longitudinal observational study. Post-COVID service patients reported more severe symptoms and greater functional impact than the CLoCk cohort, though both groups met the research Delphi definition of Long COVID.

This cross-sectional study evaluated respiratory long COVID manifestations and comorbidities in 104 Italian children at least one month post-SARS-CoV-2 infection using spirometry, walking tests, and lung ultrasound. Results showed 27% had positive lung ultrasound findings, with significant associations between BMI and COVID-19 symptoms/ultrasound scores.

Prospective cohort study examining the association between pre-infection nutritional status, oxidative stress, and one-year long COVID persistence in 115 hemodialysis patients. Moderate pre-infection undernutrition predicted higher post-COVID oxidative damage and increased risk of long COVID persistence.

Longitudinal observational study assessing general health status in 40 COVID-19 patients at two time points (32 and 89 days post-discharge) using validated instruments including SF-20, fatigue, anxiety, depression, and cognitive assessments. Found persistent abnormalities across multiple health domains, with dyspnea being a key predictor of impairment in physical and social functioning.

Observational longitudinal study describing clinical characteristics and impacts of long COVID in 50 children and young people aged 14.1 years median, followed from December 2020-May 2021. Found high prevalence of fatigue (100%), neurocognitive disorders (74%), and muscular weakness (74%), with significant academic and social disruptions including school absences, reduced schedules, and decreased extracurricular participation.

Retrospective study examining prevalence of chronic olfactory dysfunction in 784 children evaluated at a post-COVID clinic, with 1.7% presenting olfactory impairment >3 months post-infection. Paper assesses impact on children's daily activities and family quality of life but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational comparison study examining the prevalence and characteristics of persistent symptoms one year after hospitalization in children with acute COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 conditions. Found no significant difference in persistent symptom rates between groups (34% vs 37%), classifying this as a descriptive epidemiological study rather than a treatment trial.

This retrospective cohort study compares echocardiographic findings in 22 children with MIS-C and 22 healthy controls at baseline and 1-year follow-up. While the paper studies post-COVID cardiac sequelae, it focuses on MIS-C (multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children) rather than long COVID as defined in the screening criteria, and contains no intervention/treatment evaluation.

Prospective cohort study of 97 adolescents with long-COVID, evaluating symptom prevalence, clustering, and persistence over a mean 340-day follow-up. Found that fatigue (62.9%) and dyspnea (43.3%) were most common, with 45.3% still symptomatic at final follow-up, and polisymptomaticity predicting longer persistence.

This longitudinal study followed 168 COVID-19 hospitalized patients for 6 months post-discharge to assess the onset of mental disorders using standardized questionnaires. While it documents a high incidence (57.34%) of common mental disorders in post-COVID patients, it is an observational study without any treatment or intervention being tested.

This cross-sectional study compared peripheral and central auditory function in 23 children/adolescents who had recovered from COVID-19 versus 23 pre-pandemic controls with normal hearing. The COVID-19 group showed significant auditory impairments including worse hearing thresholds at standard and high frequencies, absent otoacoustic emissions, longer brainstem auditory evoked potential latencies, and poorer central auditory processing performance.

Prospective observational study evaluating pulmonary function in children aged 6-18 years at ~10 months after asymptomatic or mild COVID-19 infection. Found no respiratory symptoms, abnormal lung function, or need for therapy in any of the 61 participants, indicating that mild infection in children does not lead to chronic respiratory impairment.

This retrospective cohort study of 17 ICU survivors evaluated psychosomatic, respiratory, and neurocognitive outcomes 12 months after discharge, identifying clinical and laboratory predictors of PASC symptoms. The study is primarily observational and prognostic, not an intervention trial, and focuses on identifying risk factors rather than testing a treatment.

This epidemiological study analyzes mortality attributed to post-COVID-19 condition using US National Center for Health Statistics data from 2018–2024. The paper reports 2,653 deaths classified under ICD-10 code U09.9, with higher mortality rates in males, older adults, and individuals who died at home.

This epidemiological analysis examines trends in suicide mortality across India from 2019-2022 and explores whether long COVID may have contributed to increases in suicide rates. The study found increased suicide rates post-COVID but found no association with COVID deaths and suggests long COVID may play a potential role.

Retrospective cohort study examining whether antipsychotic and SSRI use in veterans reduces the risk of developing long COVID. Antipsychotics showed 11-43% reduction in long COVID risk depending on age and COVID wave, while SSRIs showed no benefit.

Retrospective chart review of 155 long COVID patients from UConn Health's Long COVID Clinic examining the incidence and impact of neuropsychological symptoms. Study found high prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms that did not correlate with brain imaging findings, highlighting symptom burden but not evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 117 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 18 months post-discharge to assess evolution of mental health, sleep quality, and quality of life. Participants showed gradual recovery over time with substantial improvement by month 6, though complete return to pre-disease baseline was not achieved.

This prospective follow-up study evaluated the type, frequency, onset, and recovery duration of neurological symptoms in 110 COVID-19 patients at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge. Fatigue was the most common symptom (75.5%, lasting 10.43 weeks), followed by myalgia and headache, with forgetfulness persisting longest (22.03 weeks), highlighting the need for systematic neurological monitoring in long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study compares frailty characteristics between 106 long COVID patients and 97 geriatric patients at a VA Medical Center using the Fried phenotype. Long COVID patients were significantly younger but experienced higher rates of exhaustion and low activity, suggesting long COVID may predispose patients to develop frailty with distinct phenotypic features.

This study evaluates temporal changes in sperm parameters and inflammasome markers in men during the first three months following acute COVID-19 infection. Results show gradual recovery in sperm function and decreased TNF-α levels over time, but this is a post-acute observation study focused on male fertility recovery, not long COVID sequelae or treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines myocardial abnormalities using cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging in 94 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cardiac symptoms (≥3 months post-infection) compared to 100 controls. The study found subclinical myocardial dysfunction (reduced strain parameters) and higher major adverse cardiac event rates in post-COVID patients, but this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.

Comparative study of immunometabolic profiles in 78 patients: 35 with newly diagnosed carbohydrate disorders after COVID-19 (Post-COVID group) and 33 COVID-negative controls with metabolic syndrome. Post-COVID patients showed significantly elevated inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10) and worse metabolic control (higher fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids, uric acid) independent of traditional risk factors, indicating inflammation-driven metabolic dysfunction distinct from classical metabolic syndrome.

An observational case-control study identifying risk factors associated with post-COVID syndrome in older adults with hypertension. Found that female sex, younger age, lower systolic blood pressure, and rhythm disturbances were independently associated with PCS presence.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive function in 297 adults three years post-COVID-19 infection, stratified by disease severity. Findings showed persistent cognitive deficits (attention, memory, executive function) correlated with initial COVID-19 severity and age, but the study does not test any treatment intervention.

A disease-wide association study using the FinnGen registry to map risk factors and long-term sequelae following influenza and COVID-19, comparing 9,204 influenza and 4,258 COVID-19 patients against 420,005 unexposed controls. The study identifies broad multi-system morbidity signatures extending beyond respiratory tract including cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic, and mental health complications, reframing influenza as a systemic post-viral event analogous to long COVID.

This observational cohort study examined inflammatory and cardiac biomarkers in 978 COVID-19 patients to predict post-acute COVID-19 and 30-day mortality. The study identified NT-pro BNP and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as predictive biomarkers but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This prospective study assessed subclinical cardiac dysfunction in 66 COVID-19 patients at one-year follow-up, comparing those with and without persistent dyspnea using echocardiography. While it identified reduced myocardial performance (GCW and GWI) in dyspneic patients, it is an observational study without any treatment intervention or control group comparison.

This prospective/retrospective cohort study followed 160 COVID-19 patients at 5-month post-discharge to characterize cardiac sequelae, finding RV dilation, pulmonary hypertension, and bi-ventricular dysfunction. RV changes were associated with pneumonia severity and hemodynamic instability, while LV dysfunction correlated with inflammatory markers.

A case series of 98 COVID-19 patients admitted to inpatient cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, with functional assessments at admission, discharge, and 6-month follow-up. Inpatient rehabilitation resulted in significant improvements in mobility and quality of life, with 86% of patients exhibiting post-COVID-19 symptoms at follow-up, and vaccinated individuals showing fewer symptoms than unvaccinated counterparts.

This retrospective longitudinal study evaluated endocrine disturbances in 96 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 4-year follow-up, assessing dysglycemia and thyroid autoimmunity prevalence. While it is a long COVID observational study, it lacks a control/comparison group and does not evaluate any intervention or treatment, making it a secondary analysis of existing cohort data rather than a treatment trial.

A retrospective study of 16 post-COVID patients who underwent lung ultrasound (LUS) examinations at baseline and follow-up to assess lung residuals. LUS scores showed significant improvement over time, demonstrating reverberation artifacts decreased during rehabilitation, but this is an observational follow-up study with no treatment intervention being tested.

Retrospective analysis of 764 COVID-19 hospitalized patients from October-December 2020, examining disease severity, hospitalization duration, and post-discharge residual symptoms including fatigue (36%). Study characterizes long COVID symptomatology but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This observational study compares long COVID patients who are physically active versus sedentary to examine effects on fatigue, muscle power output, sleep quality, and cognitive function. Active subjects showed 50% greater fatigue reduction at 1 year and less muscle force decline compared to sedentary subjects, suggesting physical activity may mitigate certain long COVID functional impairments.

This observational cross-sectional study assessed 146 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain to identify variables associated with kinesiophobia. The study found that kinesiophobia levels were significantly associated with anxiety, catastrophism, and sensitization-associated symptoms, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective chart review examining the association between prior SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination and acute appendicitis presentation in pediatric patients from January–June 2022. Found a potential positive relationship between COVID-19 infection and subsequent appendicitis, but does not study long COVID or any long COVID treatment.

This study describes clinical findings from COVID-19 Recovery and Engagement (CORE) Clinics in the Bronx, where COVID-19 survivors underwent comprehensive assessment of physical, emotional, cognitive, and pulmonary function at 5 months post-infection. The authors found dyspnea, fatigue, and brain fog were common, with abnormal lung imaging and moderately restrictive pulmonary function in hospitalized patients, but rare neurological imaging abnormalities.

A prospective cohort study of 635 post-COVID patients that assessed complete radiological remission of COVID-19 pneumonia using HRCT imaging at 90 days post-infection. Found that 25.8% achieved complete radiological remission, with older age and persistent imaging features (ground glass, reticulations, pleural thickening) associated with worse outcomes.

A longitudinal case series of 17 long COVID patients examining the Adaptive Force (AF) parameter of elbow and hip flexors across three timepoints: pre-treatment, immediately post-treatment, and recovery. The study found that AFisomax increased significantly from ~50% of maximum at baseline to ~99-100% at recovery, correlating with substantial symptom improvement and improved maximal holding capacity.

Prospective observational study of 100 COVID-19 pneumonia patients and 61 controls examining persistent interstitial lung fibrosis after hospital discharge. Identifies risk factors (ESR, CRP, LDH, hospitalization duration) associated with post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared dry eye parameters in 44 patients (22 post-COVID, 22 controls) to investigate whether COVID-19 infection worsens dry eye disease. Results show post-COVID patients had significantly reduced lipid layer thickness, worse meibomian gland dysfunction, and shorter tear break-up time, suggesting COVID-19 may exacerbate dry eye as a long-term sequela.

Retrospective single-center analysis of 64 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors from the first wave to determine incidence of secondary sclerosing cholangitis (SSC-COVID) and its risk factors. Found 7.8% incidence of SSC-COVID in follow-up patients, all with prolonged ICU stays requiring mechanical ventilation, but no specific treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective analysis of flow cytometric data comparing lymphocyte populations in 106 post-COVID-19 patients (56 with PCC) versus healthy controls. Found significant reductions in B cell subsets and T helper cells in PCC patients compared to controls, but no specific immune cellular changes unique to PCC versus non-PCC COVID-19 patients.

This retrospective cohort study examined cardiac MRI findings in 129 patients referred for evaluation of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). The majority (57%) had normal cardiac results, but 30% showed non-ischemic myocardial fibrosis, suggesting a possible history of myocarditis as an explanation for persistent cardiovascular symptoms in PASC patients.

This study examines the relationship between quantitative CT imaging parameters and pulmonary function tests in COVID-19 patients at 6+ months follow-up. It is an observational study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline despite being long COVID-related research.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term health outcomes in 1,074 essential tremor patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection. COVID-19 was associated with increased risk of cardiovascular events, sleep disturbances, fatigue, dyspnea, falls, anxiety, and depression, but not mortality.

This prospective population-based study measured serum brain injury biomarkers (sNfL and sGFAP) in 146 individuals before, during, and after SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess association with neurological symptoms and long COVID status. While sGFAP significantly increased in long COVID patients, neither biomarker was associated with specific neurological symptoms, suggesting astroglial activation may occur in long COVID without symptom correlation.

Retrospective cohort study of 420 patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia tracking pulmonary fibrosis development at 3 months and 2 years post-hospitalization using CT scans and biomarkers. Found fibrosis in 68% at 3 months declining to 42% at 2 years, identifying risk factors including age, inflammatory markers, and pulmonary involvement patterns.

This cross-sectional study compared optic disc and retinal microvasculature changes in 40 post-COVID-19 patients versus 40 healthy controls using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) at baseline, 4 months, and 12 months. The COVID-19 group showed reduced vessel density in multiple retinal regions and increased foveal avascular zone measurements, suggesting ischemic changes, but the study is observational without any intervention or treatment.

This prospective cohort study examines the association between prior COVID-19 infection and long-term mortality in chronic kidney disease patients over 24 months, using echocardiographic parameters and survival analysis. While the study involves COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute complications and mortality in CKD patients rather than long COVID syndrome (persistent post-COVID symptoms), and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study comparing incidence of new-onset diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetic patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection over 3 years. While the paper studies a post-COVID complication, it does not study a treatment intervention and focuses on acute/short-term disease sequelae in diabetic patients rather than long COVID syndrome itself.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long-term kidney outcomes in transplant recipients with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection over four years post-infection. Found accelerated eGFR decline in infected patients (males primarily) but this is an observational study documenting sequelae, not evaluating any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compares pregnancy and childbirth outcomes in 133 women with a history of COVID-19 versus 96 unexposed women, finding significant associations between past COVID-19 infection and adverse outcomes including oligohydramnios and low birth weight. While the study examines long-term consequences of COVID-19 infection, it does not focus on long COVID syndrome (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) but rather on specific perinatal complications in pregnant women with prior infection.

This cross-sectional study examines cardiovascular manifestations in 176 long COVID patients using echocardiography and cardiac MRI, finding significant structural and functional cardiac changes. The study is observational and descriptive in nature, assessing disease characteristics rather than evaluating any treatment or intervention.

Observational cohort study examining long-term risks of ischemic stroke and transient cerebral ischemia (TCI) in COVID-19 survivors versus uninfected controls over 4 years. Finds elevated stroke and TCI risk in COVID+ patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This longitudinal cohort study examined brain volume changes 12 months after baseline MRI in 112 COVID-19 recovered patients (mild and severe) compared to controls. The study found severity-dependent right hippocampal atrophy in COVID-19 patients but no widespread progressive atrophy in other regions, highlighting long-term neurological vulnerability.

This longitudinal cohort study compares psychosocial outcomes, quality of life, coping strategies, and mental health between long COVID patients (n=86) and asymptomatic COVID-19 survivors (n=432) at 6 months post-infection. Long COVID patients showed significantly worse outcomes across depression, anxiety, quality of life domains, and greater use of disengagement and emotion-focused coping strategies.

Retrospective cohort study examining long-term cardiovascular and mortality outcomes in patients with pre-existing arrhythmia stratified by COVID-19 hospitalization status. While the paper studies post-COVID complications, it focuses on acute-infection sequelae in a pre-existing arrhythmia population rather than long COVID syndrome as defined by persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compared heart rate turbulence (HRT) measurements in 253 recovered COVID-19 patients versus 315 healthy controls, stratified by COVID-19 severity. The study found that severe COVID-19 recovery is associated with permanently blunted HRT and impaired autonomic nervous system function, suggesting increased risk of cardiac arrhythmias.

Retrospective cohort study of 762 COVID-19 hospitalized patients examining predictors of mortality at 10 months post-discharge, with overall mortality of 25.6%. Identifies NT-proBNP, urea, age, cognitive impairment, cancer, and leukocyte count as independent prognostic markers, but does not study any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

Single-center retrospective cohort study of COVID-19 patients hospitalized between November 2021-March 2022, documenting persistent health problems lasting ≥6 months post-acute infection. Study characterizes epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory features of long COVID with focus on systemic involvement and inflammatory/immune dysregulation mechanisms, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This retrospective study of 457 long COVID patients evaluates the characteristics and clinical presentation of persistent COVID-19 symptoms, with emphasis on demographic differences. The findings show that older age, non-vaccination status, and previous COVID-19 severity are associated with specific symptom patterns and comorbidities.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX database to evaluate the prevalence and incidence of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) following COVID-19 infection across age groups. Findings show COVID-19 significantly increased SIBO risk within 12 months post-infection, particularly in older age groups and patients on chronic opioid, proton pump inhibitor, or antidiarrheal medications.

This retrospective cohort study follows 100 COVID-19 survivors older than 80 years for 12 months to identify predictors of re-hospitalization. The study is excluded because it is a passive observational follow-up without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This retrospective cohort study examined the risk of new chronic respiratory conditions within 60 days of COVID-19 hospitalization in 18,686 positive and 37,372 negative matched Veterans. COVID-19 hospitalized patients showed significantly elevated risk of developing asthma, bronchitis, chronic lung disease, COPD, emphysema, and venous thromboembolism compared to negative controls.

Population-based prospective cohort study of 484 COVID-19 patients followed for six months to identify post-COVID complications and associated risk factors. Found 33.1% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, hair loss, loss of smell/taste, headache) with female sex, age ≥35, and higher COVID exposure as risk factors, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A prospective longitudinal study tracking anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbances in COVID-19 hospitalized patients at discharge, 3-6 months, 12 months, and 4-year follow-up. Most neuropsychiatric symptoms improved within the first year, though new-onset depression and psychiatric disorders emerged during long-term follow-up, with psychiatric disorder prevalence reaching 6-11% by year 4.

This single-hospital cohort study assessed quality of life in 76 post-COVID-19 patients 5 months after hospitalization using EQ-5D questionnaires and sociodemographic data. The study identified demographic and socioeconomic factors associated with reduced QoL (anxiety, mobility impairment, pain), but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This study assessed cognitive function and psychological distress in 63 convalescent COVID-19 patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation at a post-acute care facility. About 44% of patients showed reduced cognitive efficiency, which was associated with autonomic dysfunction markers, higher D-Dimer levels, severe prior illness, longer disease duration, and greater psychological symptoms.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function and psycho-emotional outcomes in 40 young adults recovering from mild COVID-19 versus 25 healthy controls. The COVID-19 group showed significantly increased depression and decreased inhibition, indicating persistent cognitive and mental health deficits following mild infection.

This cross-sectional study measured orthostatic intolerance and cerebral blood flow abnormalities in 29 long-haul COVID patients using tilt testing, stratifying by time since infection onset (3-28 months). While POTS prevalence decreased over time and most patients normalized hemodynamic response by 24 months, cerebral blood flow abnormalities persisted despite improvement.

An observational cross-sectional study comparing clinical and epidemiological profiles of primary healthcare professionals with acute COVID-19 versus long COVID, analyzing symptoms, comorbidities, and risk factors. The study identifies that women in healthcare are disproportionately affected by long COVID, and identifies specific symptoms and pre-existing conditions (obesity, overweight) associated with both acute COVID-19 and long COVID development.

A prospective study examining the effects of two arginine-based supplements (Astenor Energy® and Astenor Forte®) on fatigue in 505 post-COVID patients in Romania, measured via Fatigue Assessment Scale over 3 months. Both supplements significantly reduced total, mental, and physical fatigue scores, with Astenor Forte® showing greater improvements, suggesting L-arginine supplements may help restore performance in post-COVID fatigue.

This pre-post study with non-equivalent control group evaluated a telerehabilitation intervention combining education and respiratory/motor rehabilitation for 49 people with post-COVID sequelae during hospital-community transitions. Results showed improvements in oxygen saturation, heart rate, fatigue, functional capacity, and anxiety/depression symptoms in the intervention group compared to controls.

A prospective cohort study of 157 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 12 months post-infection to identify risk factors associated with lung function impairment. The study found 31.2% had persistent lung function impairment at 12 months, associated with factors including abnormal alpha-1 antitrypsin levels, higher disease severity markers, and specific genotypes.

Observational multicenter study analyzing the sociodemographic and clinical profile of 689 Spanish long COVID patients and their correlation with work-related disability. Found fatigue, brain fog, time since diagnosis, renal insufficiency, and tremors were associated with work disability, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal study following 56 COVID-19 patients discharged from a Taiwan hospital, assessing changes in quality of life and mental health at 1 week and 1 month post-discharge. Found that patients with abnormal respiratory function and those requiring intubation had lower quality of life and higher emotional problems (anxiety ~30%), though no specific intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive and psychological sequelae in 23 ICU patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome at 6 and 12 months post-discharge, compared to healthy controls. Results showed persistent visual-spatial dysfunction, psychological symptoms (anxiety/depression), and reduced quality of life, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Population-based prospective cohort study examining Long COVID prevalence and associated factors in 1,822 Brazilian adults and elders 12 months after COVID-19 hospitalization. Found 64.2% prevalence with neurological, musculoskeletal, and respiratory symptoms most common; severity of acute infection was the strongest predictor of Long COVID development.

Retrospective study of 116 long COVID patients who received health resort treatment (balneology, exercises, physical medicine, climate therapy) at a Polish sanatorium in 2021. Treatment significantly improved functional capacity, physical performance, and reduced fatigue levels compared to baseline.

Prospective cohort study examining the association between physical activity levels and mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, stress) in 190 women during recovery from COVID-19, with measurements at 2-4 weeks and 14-16 weeks post-infection. Higher physical activity at 3 months was significantly associated with improved anxiety and depression symptoms.

This retrospective cohort study identifies clinical characteristics and risk factors during acute COVID-19 that predict development of long COVID, including tachycardia, myalgias, severity, and antibiotic use. The study does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Prospective cohort study assessing quality of life outcomes in 38 patients recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia compared to 25 healthy controls over 12 months using validated QoL instruments (SF-36, EQ-5D-5L). Findings show persistently lower QoL in COVID-19 patients with gradual improvement over the follow-up period, particularly in physical functioning and social engagement.

Observational study comparing symptoms, physical activity, and functionality across 5 groups stratified by COVID-19 severity (healthy, mild, moderate, severe, critical). Results show that patients with higher COVID-19 severity experience greater frailty, fatigue, dyspnea, pain, and reduced functionality compared to those with lower severity.

A nationwide multicenter cohort study following 220 ICU patients with severe COVID-19 at 416 days post-discharge to assess prevalence of functional impairments and long COVID effects. The study found 77.7% had long COVID with dyspnea as the most common symptom, and identified multiple risk factors for functional impairment including fatigue, myalgia, and cognitive dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study examines psychological and cognitive pathways (posttraumatic stress, rumination, cognitive impairment, loneliness, posttraumatic growth) affecting quality of life in 258 patients 6-24 months post-discharge from COVID-19 hospitalization. The study identifies sex and time since discharge as moderators but does not test an intervention—it is purely observational/correlational.

This retrospective study evaluated health resort treatment (including balneological therapies, physical medicine, exercise, and psychological support) in 120 long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms. The treatment significantly improved sleep disorders, anxiety, depression, and dizziness, with greater improvements in patients receiving balneological factors.

A 4-month prospective follow-up study measuring hematological and hemorheological parameters in COVID-19 patients to assess long-term changes after acute infection. The study found persistent impairments in hemoglobin-related parameters and RBC aggregation at 4 months, with more pronounced changes in males.

Prospective observational study measuring biomarkers of endothelial activation and hypercoagulability in 208 COVID-19 survivors versus 30 controls at median 62 days post-symptom onset. Found persistent elevation of D-dimer, fibrin monomers, TFPI, and heparanase in survivors, with one in four showing at least one elevated biomarker, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Prospective longitudinal study of 151 unvaccinated healthcare workers with mild-moderate COVID-19, examining electrocardiographic changes at 6-12 months and >12 months post-infection. Found transient sinus tachycardia and subtle PR shortening consistent with post-viral autonomic effects, with no significant long-term arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities.

A prospective cohort study following 60 COVID-19 ICU survivors and 78 family members at 3 and 6 months post-discharge, assessing physical, social, and psychological functioning. Ninety percent of ICU survivors reported persistent symptoms at 6 months with impaired physical and social functioning, though no standardized intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional cohort study investigates the relationship between ambient air pollution exposure (PM2.5 and PM10) and long COVID symptoms in residents of Makkah, Saudi Arabia. While it confirms associations between air pollution and long COVID symptom severity, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This study assessed self-reported physical activity levels in 239 long COVID patients from online peer support groups at three and six months post-symptom onset. Patients demonstrated significantly reduced weekly walking time at follow-up compared to pre-COVID baseline, suggesting long-term functional impairment persists in this population.

A longitudinal study following 834 healthcare workers infected with SARS-CoV-2 in 2020 over three years to assess changes in health-related quality of life and mental health outcomes. The study found significant impairments in physical and mental HRQoL among those with persistent symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study comparing post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) outcomes in 466 hospitalized COVID-19 patients stratified by diabetes status and weight. Found that type 2 diabetes and overweight status are risk factors for PCS onset, but unexpectedly, diabetes patients had shorter PCS duration; study provides no active intervention or treatment evaluation.

This longitudinal cohort study evaluated quality of life (QoL) in 110 COVID-19 survivors over 6 months using the RAND SF-36 survey, with 42% having been hospitalized. The results show that hospitalization, post-acute sequelae (PASC), and disease severity were significantly associated with lower QoL scores in physical functioning, role limitation, energy/fatigue, social functioning, and general health.

A longitudinal study of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 1,506 healthcare workers at a German hospital from April 2020 to April 2021, tracking cumulative incidence and risk factors. While the paper identifies a high risk of long COVID development post-infection (31.5% of unvaccinated vs 5.3% of vaccinated workers reporting persistent quality-of-life impairment), it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study examines outpatient health care utilization changes in the 12 months following COVID-19 diagnosis across 11,326 patients, stratified by race/ethnicity and community social vulnerability. While the study documents increased primary and specialty care visits post-diagnosis, it does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention and focuses on healthcare access disparities rather than long COVID-specific outcomes or recovery.

Secondary analysis of a cohort study examining neurological and mental health symptoms in COVID-19 survivors at 3.5 months post-discharge. Found that cognitive dysfunction, anxiety, fatigue, and hyposmia/hypogeusia explained 28.8% of disability variation, suggesting need for early rehabilitation.

Retrospective longitudinal observational study of 182 hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia patients in Spain followed at 6 months and 5 years post-discharge to assess persistent symptoms, radiological evolution, and healthcare costs. Found 26.5% with residual symptoms at 6 months declining to 4.5% at 5 years, with minimal risk factors for persistence.

Population-based study of 20,601 COVID-19-positive Israeli children (5-18 years) examining demographic, clinical, and socioeconomic factors associated with long COVID syndrome diagnosis. Identifies severe acute infection, hospitalization, recurrent infections, and pre-existing ADHD, chronic urticaria, and allergic rhinitis as significant risk factors for LCS in children.

This retrospective cohort study examines whether World Trade Center–related medical conditions are risk factors for increased COVID-19 severity and post-acute sequelae in 1,280 WTC responders. The study finds that post-acute COVID-19 sequelae are associated with initial COVID-19 severity, upper respiratory disease, GERD, obstructive airway disease, heart disease, and depressive symptoms.

A cross-sectional observational study comparing respiratory function, functional capacity, and quality of life in 26 severe COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-ICU discharge versus 26 healthy controls. While the paper documents long-term sequelae of severe COVID-19, it does not study any treatment or intervention—only natural recovery outcomes without therapeutic evaluation.
