Retrospective cohort study of 155 Italian workers examining long COVID sequelae and impact on employment at one-year follow-up. Identifies smoking as a risk factor for occupational status change and persistent anxiety as more common in women, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective observational study assessed the prevalence of insomnia in 200 COVID-19 patients during early recovery using the Athens Insomnia Scale. The study found 32% had sleep disturbances and 21.5% met criteria for insomnia, with prevalence correlating with symptom duration.

A cross-sectional study of 214 COVID-19 survivors examining the relationship between fear of death during acute infection and post-infection mental health outcomes. The study found increased depressive and anxiety symptoms in survivors, with fear of death not independently predicting depression beyond overall symptom burden.

This prospective cohort study followed COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in Brazil at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to determine the prevalence and risk factors of post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS). The study found high prevalence (81% at 3 months, 61% at 6 months) with female gender, hypercholesterolemia, obesity, and pronation during hospitalization identified as significant associated factors.

A 34-country retrospective survey of 1,001 COVID-19 survivors assessing neurobehavioral symptoms (cognitive, affective, somatic) before, during, and after infection. The study found modest improvements in somatic and affective symptoms but minimal improvement in cognitive symptoms, identifying risk factors associated with persistent neurobehavioral dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study measured heart rate variability (HRV) in 44 healthcare workers 30 days post-COVID-19 infection compared to 44 age- and sex-matched controls. The study found significantly elevated sympathetic activity and reduced HRV metrics in post-acute COVID-19 cases, suggesting autonomic imbalance and increased cardiovascular risk in the early post-infection period.

Prospective observational study of 130 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors evaluated at 3 and 12 months post-infection to assess health-related quality of life using the SF-36 questionnaire. Found persistent dyspnea and asthenia in ~37% of patients with significant deterioration across all HRQoL domains, though most showed improvement over the 12-month period.

Observational follow-up study examining how COVID-19 survivors express their pandemic experiences through metaphors at 6 and 12 months post-infection. Findings show increasing negative psychological experiences over time, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

Retrospective EHR study comparing long-term COVID symptoms in 286 non-MIS-C and 26 MIS-C children from a diverse pediatric healthcare system. Found higher rates of chronic long COVID in MIS-C children (26.9%) versus non-MIS-C (15.3%), with significant disparities by sex, ethnicity, and insurance status.

A longitudinal comparative study of 588 pregnant women examining the prevalence, duration, and risk factors of post-viral fatigue following SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy in Brazil. Fatigue prevalence in symptomatic women was 40.6% at 6 weeks, declining to 27.8% at 6 months, with severity of initial infection and symptoms like cough and myalgia identified as independent risk factors.

This 12-month prospective cohort study of 147 Brazilian healthcare and support workers documents the prevalence and duration of persistent COVID-19 symptoms following mild acute infection. While it confirms that 20.3% of participants experienced symptoms lasting at least 12 months, it is an observational study without any treatment or intervention component and thus does not meet criteria for inclusion in a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This study identifies three distinct Long COVID phenotypes (Mild, Moderate, Severe) using hierarchical clustering analysis of 62 self-reported symptoms and quality of life measures in 9,504 SARS-CoV-2 infected individuals from Luxembourg. While the classification framework may inform personalized care, the paper is a descriptive cross-sectional analysis that does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.

Observational cohort study of 312 long COVID patients assessed at 6-month follow-up for lung and cardiac dysfunction using imaging and functional tests. Found associations between cardiac dysfunction and lung fibrotic changes in patients with comorbid hypertension or diabetes, but no intervention or treatment was administered.

This cross-sectional study examined post-COVID syndrome prevalence and symptoms in 1,378 workers, identifying 115 cases with persistent symptoms characterized primarily by sensory disturbances and fatigue. The paper found that workers with post-COVID had poorer sleep quality, increased fatigue, anxiety, and depression, along with decreased work ability compared to workers whose symptoms resolved, but describes no treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 100 long COVID patients undergoing NASA Lean Test (NLT) to detect orthostatic intolerance syndromes (PoTS and orthostatic hypotension) in a clinic setting, with comparison to symptom severity on the C19-YRS outcome measure. Found evidence of orthostatic intolerance in 38% of patients, but poor correlation between NLT findings and symptom severity scores.

This prospective observational study evaluated pulmonary rehabilitation outcomes in 483 post-acute COVID-19 patients across four pandemic waves, comparing patient characteristics and functional improvements. All cohorts achieved clinically significant improvements in exercise capacity and functional independence, with Wave 3+4 patients showing greater gains in the six-minute walk test.

Longitudinal cohort study in Hawaii examining employment outcomes in long COVID patients versus those without lingering symptoms, with analysis of vaccination's protective effects. While about long COVID, this is an epidemiological study documenting employment disparities rather than testing or evaluating a treatment intervention.

A prospective multicentric French cohort study that followed 189 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 6-8 months and one year post-infection to assess the prevalence of persistent symptoms and identify risk factors associated with long COVID. The study found associations between elevated liver enzymes, obesity, ICU stay, and anosmia with long-term symptom persistence, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A single-group feasibility study evaluating ReCOV, an allied-health-led multidisciplinary outpatient rehabilitation service for long COVID patients (n=143). The service was safe and mostly acceptable, with participants showing statistically significant improvements in illness perception and quality of life measures.

Prospective cohort study assessing mental health outcomes in 265 post-COVID patients at 17 and 22 months post-infection, using validated questionnaires for depression, anxiety, somatic symptoms, and fatigue. Found persistent severe PASC symptoms (80% of patients) with depression, anxiety, and somatic symptoms improving over time while fatigue and post-exertional malaise remained unchanged, identifying age and prior psychiatric illness as risk factors.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between vitamin D levels and long COVID symptoms in 442 patients referred to a specialized Post-COVID Clinic. The study found no significant association between vitamin D deficiency and long COVID symptom prevalence or severity, despite vitamin D insufficiency being observed in 26% of the population.

This retrospective cohort study examines the impact of COVID-19 infection on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in a Japanese population of 13,365 employees using insurance-based data over 18 months. While it demonstrates differential associations between COVID-19 and HRQoL decline by age group (notably a 1.7-fold increase in odds for those in their 30s), it is an observational study without any treatment intervention.

Post-hoc analysis of a prospective cohort study examining functional outcomes at 120 days post-COVID-19 according to respiratory support levels during acute hospitalization. Found no significant association between oxygen supplementation level and functional outcomes, though the IMV group showed greater muscle mass loss.

A single-center prospective observational study documenting the prevalence and clinical manifestations of long COVID in 697 children, finding 26.4% with symptoms at 30 days and 11.6% at 90 days post-infection. The study identifies associations between persistent symptoms and prior acute-phase presentations (anosmia, atopy, asthenia, cough) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examined surgical outcomes in long COVID patients compared to asymptomatic controls using a database of COVID-19 positive survey respondents. The analysis found no statistically significant differences in surgical outcomes between long COVID and asymptomatic patients, suggesting minimal surgical burden from long COVID despite increased healthcare utilization.

Longitudinal population-based study examining the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and new diagnoses of chronic conditions in 8,086 Swiss participants (2021-2023). Found that infected participants were more likely to develop new chronic conditions (aOR=2.15) but does not study any specific treatment intervention.

This prospective observational study examines lipid profiles and oxidative stress in COVID-19 patients compared to healthy controls, with long-term follow-up at a median of 514 days post-infection. While the paper documents long-term sequelae (lipid abnormalities and persistent inflammation), it is an observational cohort that passively follows patients without assigning or testing any treatment intervention.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study comparing retinal microvascular findings in 30 acute COVID-19 patients assessed at hospital discharge and 1-year follow-up using multimodal imaging. Found significant decreases in mean vein diameter and changes in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, suggesting retinal vasculature may be a biomarker of angiopathy in severe COVID-19.

This prospective cohort study of 102 post-COVID patients investigates the persistence of hemostatic abnormalities and their association with ongoing physical and neuropsychological symptoms. The findings suggest a procoagulant state may contribute to long-COVID symptoms through microthrombosis, but this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines whether baseline IL-6 levels during acute COVID-19 hospitalization can predict development of long COVID symptoms. The analysis of 184 hospitalized patients found elevated IL-6 associated with doubled risk of long COVID and specific symptom clusters, but the study does not test any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study examined skeletal muscle and adipose tissue changes in COVID-19 survivors 3-9 months post-discharge, stratified by inflammatory levels (NLR) during acute infection. The study found reduced skeletal muscle radiodensity and increased intramuscular fat infiltration in both groups, independent of acute-phase NLR levels, highlighting the need for targeted rehabilitation.

This retrospective cross-sectional study compared submaximal and maximal exercise capacities between post-COVID-19 patients with restrictive lung disease patterns and patients with chronic respiratory disease using spirometry and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. The study found similar patterns of impairment in both groups, with lung restriction degree influencing exercise distance and maximum ventilation.

This study investigates circulating exosomal microRNAs in COVID-19 ARDS survivors at 4 months post-recovery, stratified by chest imaging patterns (normal, pulmonary opacities, fibrosis-like lesions). It is a cross-sectional biomarker correlational study without any treatment intervention, focusing on characterizing existing radiological sequelae through microRNA profiling.

Longitudinal NMR-based metabolomics study characterizing metabolite profiles in severe COVID-19 patients at recovery timepoints compared to controls. The study identifies dysregulated amino acid metabolism, dyslipidemia, and energy metabolism disturbances but is a pathophysiology/biomarker study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study analyzes fecal microbiome composition in 79 long COVID patients at 3-6 months post-infection, identifying two distinct microbiome clusters. Cluster 2 patients showed significantly reduced lung function and higher rates of ICU admission during acute COVID, with altered bacterial composition including reduced butyrate-producing bacteria.

This study analyzes T regulatory cell (Treg) subpopulations and their function across acute COVID-19, early convalescence, and one-year recovery using flow cytometry on peripheral blood samples. The authors found decreased Treg populations during acute infection that did not fully recover to healthy donor levels one year later, suggesting persistent immune dysregulation in long COVID.

This cross-sectional study compares pericoronary inflammation levels in 158 chest pain patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection using CT angiography, finding elevated inflammation markers in post-COVID patients. The study does not examine long COVID—it focuses on acute post-infection cardiovascular inflammation in patients with angina and does not test any treatment intervention.

This observational study measured three serum proteins (neutrophil elastase, neuron-specific enolase, S100B) in diabetic and non-diabetic patients before and two years after COVID-19 to develop a predictive model for post-COVID syndrome. No treatment intervention was tested; the study is purely diagnostic/prognostic in nature.

Prospective observational study of 263 COVID-19 survivors one year post-hospitalization examining associations between Gas6/sAxl plasma levels and residual symptoms, particularly hair loss. Found decreased Gas6 and sAxl levels independently associated with hair loss development, with 26.2% experiencing hair loss and 23.7% reporting persistent hair loss at one-year follow-up.

This study examines gut microbiome composition in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and those with post-COVID-19 syndrome using shotgun metagenomics with cross-sectional and longitudinal follow-ups at 1 and 3 months. The findings identify distinctive microbiome signatures associated with acute infection recovery and post-COVID progression, highlighting potential diagnostic and prognostic markers.

A 4-year diffusion-weighted MRI study examining microstructural white matter changes in olfactory and taste-related brain regions following SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing 2020 and 2024 COVID variants. Findings show elevated ADC values at infection onset that decline over 3 years, with 2024 variants showing reduced neurological alterations compared to the original strain.

This prospective observational study characterizes inflammatory profiles in 68 severe COVID-19 patients at hospital admission and one month post-discharge, measuring macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) and multiple cytokines. Patients with severe disease showed persistently elevated MIF, IFN-γ, and TNF-α one month post-discharge, suggesting prolonged inflammatory responses indicative of post-acute immune dysregulation.

This cross-sectional study examined inflammatory and coagulation factors along with SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell responses in 196 unvaccinated individuals at 3 and 12 months post-infection. The study found elevated inflammatory markers and persistent T-cell immunity in long COVID patients but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 15 long COVID patients with suspected endocrine dysfunction who underwent anterior pituitary stimulation tests, revealing delayed hormonal responses particularly in gonadotropin secretion suggestive of functional hypothalamic involvement. Three patients were initiated on low-dose hydrocortisone and testosterone treatment based on findings of low cortisol and delayed hormone responses.

Prospective observational cohort study following COVID-19 pneumonia patients during acute hospitalization and 6 weeks post-discharge, measuring lung function and radiological changes. Study found that functional abnormalities persisted at follow-up and were associated with disease severity, but does not test any specific treatment intervention.

This study measured flow-mediated dilatation (FMD), a marker of endothelial function, in 27 COVID-19 patients three months post-hospitalization compared to nine controls. The authors found reduced FMD in COVID-19 survivors but found no association between FMD impairment and acute infection severity, and did not test any intervention.

Prospective observational study of post-COVID patients comparing those with persistent dyspnea to asymptomatic controls using cardiopulmonary exercise testing and biomarker analysis. Found significant ventilatory inefficiency and reduced exercise capacity in symptomatic patients, suggesting ventilation/perfusion mismatch as a potential mechanism.

This prospective cohort study followed 225 patients hospitalized for moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia to assess cardiac sequelae, measuring left ventricular and right ventricular strain at 5-month and 12-month follow-ups. Left ventricular subclinical myocardial injury was found in 36% of patients and was associated with male gender and cardiovascular risk factors, with no significant improvement by 12 months.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between post-COVID fatigue severity and serum anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels in 101 patients. Found that severe fatigue is associated with significantly lower anti-S-Ig and anti-NC-Ig antibody levels, suggesting immune response correlates with symptom severity.

This retrospective cohort study investigated long COVID characteristics and risk factors in 5,750 healthcare workers at a university hospital, comparing BMI and comorbidities between those who developed 35-day long COVID and those who did not. The study found that overweight status and previous pulmonary disease were significant risk factors for developing prolonged COVID symptoms, but does not describe an intervention or treatment study.

Retrospective cohort study following 587 COVID-19 hospital survivors for one year post-discharge, assessing clinical outcomes, mortality, and post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence. 90% of hospitalized patients reported ongoing symptoms at one year, including breathlessness, tiredness, anosmia, and ageusia, with 7.5% mortality rate.

A longitudinal cohort study of 67 kidney transplant recipients assessed the presence of post-COVID-19 syndrome 6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using standardized questionnaires. The study found that 70.1% of recipients had post-COVID-19 syndrome with persistent symptoms including fatigue, hair loss, and dyspnea, and demonstrated significant reductions in health-related quality of life compared to baseline.

A longitudinal cohort study of 79 hemodialyzed patients followed at 3 and 6 months post-COVID-19 to assess persistent symptoms and health-related quality of life. The study found that 93.7% and 81% of patients reported at least one persistent symptom at 3 and 6 months respectively, with fatigue, muscle weakness, and palpitations being most common, and significant declines across all EQ-5D-5L domains.

Retrospective cohort study of 111 COVID-19 patients evaluated at a post-acute COVID clinic ~12 weeks after pneumonia diagnosis, tracking radiological and pulmonary function changes. Study reports natural evolution of respiratory symptoms and imaging abnormalities without testing any intervention, recommending watchful monitoring rather than active treatment.

Observational study examining residual symptoms after SARS-CoV-2 infection in Polish MS patients treated with various disease-modifying therapies. Reports symptom prevalence and duration but does not test or evaluate any intervention—patients were not given a treatment as part of the study design.

This observational cohort study tracked 116 patients with pulmonary hypertension or borderline pulmonary hypertension following acute COVID-19 infection over 3 and 6 months using transthoracic echocardiography. The study documented gradual, statistically significant improvements in systolic pulmonary artery pressure and right ventricular dysfunction parameters, though some patients experienced persistent symptoms.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of long COVID in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients at a tertiary referral center. Found 40% of 53 COVID-infected IBD patients developed long COVID (primarily asthenia), with no significant impact on IBD disease course.

A prospective cohort study following 45 COVID-19 survivors from a Danish hospital for 48 weeks after discharge to characterize persistence of long-term symptoms. The study found that 87% of patients reported at least one persistent symptom, with fatigue, dyspnea, and concentration difficulties being most common.

This retrospective cohort study evaluates myocardial injury as a prognostic factor in 172 COVID-19 survivors, comparing outcomes between those with and without elevated cardiac troponin levels on admission. Patients with myocardial injury showed higher one-year mortality/readmission rates and cardiac remodeling but no functional echocardiographic abnormalities at six months.

This study evaluated the impact of sarcopenia on rehabilitation outcomes in 34 post-acute COVID-19 patients undergoing a 28-day multidisciplinary rehabilitation program including psychiatric support, cognitive behavioral therapy, nutritional therapy, and physiotherapy. All patients showed improvements in respiratory, body composition, muscle strength, and functional parameters, with early sarcopenia diagnosis identified as important for predicting rehabilitation outcomes.

This multicenter cohort study examined sex differences in post-COVID symptoms among 1,969 COVID-19 survivors assessed 8.4 months after hospitalization in Spain. Female sex was associated with significantly higher rates of multiple post-COVID symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, pain, hair loss, and mood disorders.

This prospective observational study examines COVID-19 incidence, transmission routes, and severe outcomes in IBD patients from the ENEIDA registry (482 patients, 12-month follow-up). The study focuses on acute COVID-19 severity and mortality in immunosuppressed IBD patients, not long COVID sequelae or treatments.

Prospective observational study of 658 COVID-19 convalescent patients assessing endothelial function via flow-mediated dilation (FMD) at 3 months post-acute infection. Found significant endothelial dysfunction in hospitalized patients correlated with COVID-19 severity and pulmonary impairment, but no active treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective analysis of 65 long COVID patients seen at an outpatient clinic over 3 months, examining symptom progression and relationship to serum antibody titers. Most patients showed improvement in symptoms at 3 months, and higher antibody titers were associated with severe acute phase but not long-term symptom persistence.

A prospective cohort study of COVID-19 patients hospitalized in France, assessed remotely at 12 months post-discharge to evaluate persistent symptoms and functional capacity. The study found persistent impairments in physical and mental health domains at one year, with older age and frailty associated with worse outcomes, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study of 991 ICU-admitted COVID-19 patients followed 3 months post-discharge to assess factors associated with persistent post-COVID symptoms. Found that female sex, ICU duration, ICU-acquired pneumonia, and ARDS independently predicted persistent poor health post-COVID, with no intervention tested.

This study followed 83 mild COVID-19 patients over 12 months to assess persistence of specific immunity and long-term symptoms. While 61% reported persistent symptoms initially (declining to 28% by 12 months), the primary focus is immunological characterization rather than treatment evaluation, making it an observational cohort study that does not meet criteria for inclusion in the intervention trials pipeline.

An observational cross-sectional study of 100 post-COVID-19 patients examining pain burden, symptom prevalence, and quality of life outcomes following mild initial infection. Finds that 75% reported generalized pain and 40% met fibromyalgia criteria, highlighting the need for pain management in post-COVID syndrome.

Prospective observational study following 18 ICU survivors of severe COVID-19 at multiple timepoints (36–222 days post-discharge) to assess long-term health consequences and quality of life. Found persistent impairments in physical functioning, diffusion capacity, and imaging abnormalities despite some improvement over time.

Retrospective cohort study of 159 COVID-19 survivors from the first wave, examining 1-year outcomes and predictors of mortality. Identified age, diabetes, and R-R interval as significant predictors of 1-year mortality; no interventions were tested.

A prospective follow-up study of 218 patients hospitalized with COVID-19, assessing symptoms and pulmonary function 3 months after discharge. Fatigue was highly prevalent (65% with any fatigue, 18% severe), and ICU treatment was associated with significantly reduced diffusion capacity (DLCO < 80%).

Prospective cohort study of 248 COVID-19 patients followed for ~1 year post-discharge examining long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors. Found common persistent symptoms (shortness of breath, fatigue, palpitations) and identified critical illness as a risk factor for post-discharge diabetes incidence.

Retrospective cohort study examining the incidence of myocarditis and pericarditis in 196,992 adults after COVID-19 infection in Israel, compared to 590,976 matched controls. Found no significant increase in either condition in post-COVID patients (myocarditis aHR 1.08, pericarditis aHR 0.53).

This observational study identified 701 patients without comorbidities and compared 218 with long COVID to 270 without symptoms at 3-month follow-up. The research identified BMI, severe acute COVID course, and joint pain during acute infection as independent predictors of long COVID development, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This prospective cohort study investigates pulmonary diffusing capacity decline in 67 COVID-19 patients across three severity groups at 5-month follow-up, using lung function tests, HRCT, and VQ SPECT/CT imaging. The study finds that reduced diffusion capacity is severity-dependent and associated with restrictive lung disease and pulmonary fibrosis, but not pulmonary vascular disease.

Prospective multicenter follow-up study of 193 older patients hospitalized for acute COVID-19, reassessed 6+ months post-discharge to identify determinants of mortality and loss of independence in ADLs. Over 40% experienced death or functional decline, with cardiovascular disease and respiratory failure as leading causes of death; no intervention was tested.

Multicenter prospective observational study examining prevalence and risk factors of post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) in COVID-19 patients requiring mechanical ventilation. Found ~60% prevalence of PICS with cognitive impairment as primary domain, but does not study long COVID-specific sequelae or any intervention.

This prospective observational study followed 701 COVID-19 survivors discharged from hospital to assess whether myocardial injury during acute infection predicts cardiovascular sequelae and mortality. Patients with myocardial injury had significantly higher rates of death (21.3% vs 6.1%), major adverse cardiovascular events (25.3% vs 4.5%), and inflammatory heart disease at 270-day median follow-up.

A retrospective cohort study of 96 long COVID patients with suspected cardiovascular symptoms followed at a dedicated clinic for 1 year. Most patients had normal initial cardiac workup, 9% received new CV diagnoses (mainly self-resolving myocarditis), and 54% experienced symptom improvement with fair prognosis.

This cross-sectional study examined sociodemographic and clinical characteristics of 1,891 long COVID patients presenting to an outpatient clinic in Tokyo between January 2020 and October 2021. The study found associations between female sex, employment changes, and specific symptoms (fatigue, depression, brain fog, dyspnea) with lower performance status, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective multicentre study comparing health-related quality of life in COVID-19 outpatients versus controls one year post-infection using EQ-5D-5L scale. Found significantly reduced quality of life in COVID cases, particularly in pain/discomfort and daily activities, but does not test any specific intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational cohort study of 368 COVID-19 survivors aged ≥80 years assessing the long-term effects of hospitalization on frailty and quality of life at 1-year follow-up. While it addresses long-term sequelae of COVID-19 in older adults, the study does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—it is purely observational without assigned treatment.

Prospective cohort study following 679 children with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection for up to 12 months to assess prevalence and risk factors of persistent symptoms. Found fatigue (19%), headache (12%), and insomnia (7.5%) as most common persistent symptoms, with high recovery rates (99.3% by 12 months), but no treatment intervention was tested.

Prospective cohort study following 29 patients with post-COVID olfactory and gustatory disorders for 3-6 and 12 months post-hospitalization, using standardized smell and taste tests. Study documents persistent sensory dysfunction and its negative impact on health-related quality of life, but is observational with no treatment intervention.

Retrospective observational study comparing clinical and endocrinological features of 60 long COVID patients with sleep disturbance versus 303 without sleep symptoms at a Japanese COVID-19 aftercare clinic. Found increased sleep disturbance prevalence in Omicron-infected patients with elevated ACTH and reduced growth hormone, suggesting hypothalamic-pituitary stress.

Prospective cohort study following 166 COVID-19 survivors for 18 months post-discharge to characterize symptom prevalence and persistence. Findings show variable symptom trajectories: while overall symptom burden decreased over time, dyspnea, weakness, and brain fog remained elevated at 18 months, suggesting heterogeneous long-term recovery patterns.

This study characterizes a Danish post-COVID clinic cohort of 447 patients referred for persistent symptoms 6+ months after mild COVID-19, evaluating symptom prevalence and validating a post-COVID symptom questionnaire (PCQ). The work is descriptive and does not test any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible as a treatment trial despite being about long COVID.

This study evaluates cardiac mechanics in 157 children who recovered from COVID-19 infection using speckle-tracking echocardiography at an average of 148 days post-infection, comparing them to 107 healthy controls. The study found persistent left ventricular myocardial deformation abnormalities in post-COVID children, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective registry study examining outcomes and prognostic factors in COVID-19 survivors with underlying heart disease, following patients post-hospitalization. Vaccination was found to reduce all-cause mortality risk, while cardiovascular disease predicted worse outcomes including increased mortality during follow-up.

Two-year follow-up study of 45 complex post-COVID patients receiving coordinated multidisciplinary care including exercise, respiratory, olfactory, cognitive/speech therapy and psychological support. Results show significant reductions in dyspnea, anxiety and chest pain, with 2/3 of patients reporting improvement and partial/full return to work, though persistent fatigue and neurocognitive symptoms remained in many.

Retrospective study comparing autonomic nerve function testing results in PASC patients versus POTS patients and healthy controls. Findings suggest significant PASC patients have abnormal autonomic function tests with clinical features similar to POTS.

This observational cohort study followed 167 COVID-19 patients at 3 and 18 months post-infection to assess vascular function, inflammation, and coagulation markers. The study found persistent endothelial activation, systemic inflammation, and coagulation abnormalities 18 months after infection, but no increased macrovascular dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study compares erectile function in 95 male healthcare workers with prior COVID-19 infection (at different time points post-infection) versus 30 controls without COVID history using the IIEF-5 questionnaire. The study found erectile dysfunction was elevated early after COVID-19 but improved over time, particularly by 12 months post-infection, suggesting the condition may be temporary.

This retrospective observational study compared serum zinc levels in 194 long COVID patients, finding hypozincemia (low zinc) in 22.2% of cases, with higher prevalence in older patients and males. The study identified associations between zinc deficiency and symptoms like fatigue, dysosmia, and dysgeusia, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study of 121 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed for a mean of 17 months to assess persistence of long COVID symptoms and their associations with acute-phase factors. Finds that 60% of patients have persistent symptoms at follow-up, primarily fatigue and dyspnea, with vaccination and baseline neuropsychological symptoms being independent predictors of symptom persistence.

This pre-post observational study measured arterial stiffness and hemodynamic parameters in 32 patients with mild COVID-19 at baseline (up to 2 years pre-infection) and follow-up (2-3 months post-infection). The study found significant increases in arterial stiffness and alterations in central hemodynamics parameters, suggesting long-lasting vascular impairment following mild COVID-19.

A prospective observational study of 474 COVID-19 patients (252 ambulatory, 222 hospitalized) followed for 1 year post-infection to characterize long COVID symptoms and identify risk factors. The study found high prevalence of fatigue (87.5%), neurological symptoms, and psychiatric comorbidity, and identified two distinct patient phenotypes prone to long COVID.

Prospective registry study following 150 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge to identify cardiopulmonary long-term effects and predictors of long COVID. Found 75% met long COVID criteria; exertional dyspnea correlated with impaired pulmonary function and cardiac abnormalities, while hospitalization duration and ICU admission predicted long COVID development.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between physical activity levels and physical function in 1,846 COVID-19 survivors with post-acute symptoms. While it documents that reduced physical activity is associated with worse physical outcomes (lower handgrip strength, shorter 6MWT distance, higher fatigue), it is an observational study without any intervention assignment and therefore does not qualify as a treatment trial.

Prospective cohort study analyzing sex and age interactions as risk factors for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 in 452 adults and 925 children followed for median 7.8 months. Found statistically significant interaction between sex and age, with higher risk in males aged 0-5 and females aged 12-50, particularly for cardiovascular, neurological, gastrointestinal, and sleep symptoms.

Prospective case-control study comparing lung ultrasound (LUS) findings in children with persistent symptoms post-SARS-CoV-2 infection versus fully recovered children. LUS showed minimal differences between groups, with mostly normal findings in all children at median 2-month follow-up.

A prospective observational study examining ICU memories and their association with six-month psychological outcomes in COVID-19 critical illness survivors. The study found that lack of pre-ICU memories independently predicted worse psychological outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD), but focuses on acute COVID-19 ICU recovery rather than long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study examined 204 COVID-19 hospitalized patients to investigate associations between acute-phase electrolyte imbalances and persistent mental fatigue after recovery. Females with mild COVID-19 showed higher odds of post-COVID mental fatigue, particularly when dysnatremia occurred during hospitalization.

A retrospective observational study comparing long COVID patients with and without headaches, examining symptom prevalence, demographics, and quality of life impacts. Headache was found to significantly affect depression, QOL scores, and general fatigue in long COVID patients.

This study evaluates pulmonary functional outcomes, quality of life, and chest CT patterns in ICU survivors of acute COVID-19 ARDS at 3 months post-discharge across three pandemic waves. It is a retrospective comparison of acute COVID-19 survivors without a specific treatment intervention, focusing on acute-phase disease severity rather than long COVID sequelae.

This study assessed neuropsychiatric outcomes in 50 children 1-18 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using standardized clinical rating scales. Results showed elevated rates of internalizing symptoms (40%), anxiety (48%), sleep disturbance (28%), and cognitive/executive function impairment (52%), suggesting long-term mental health sequelae of COVID-19 in children.

A prospective cohort study of 184 post-COVID patients followed at 3 and 6 months in a rehabilitation clinic, documenting symptom burden, fatigue, cognition, and physiological abnormalities. While the comprehensive assessment shows significant clinical findings, this is an observational follow-up study without a specific treatment intervention or control group.

Prospective observational study of 1,966 patients following acute COVID-19 examining risk factors for PASC and outcomes based on acute-phase treatments. Patients treated with dexamethasone and/or remdesivir during acute illness showed lower median symptom duration, with female gender, obesity, asthma, and disease severity identified as PASC risk factors.

Prospective observational study comparing immunological profiles in hospitalized COVID-19 patients (n=64) at baseline and 6 months post-recovery versus healthy controls. Found persistent T-cell exhaustion markers (TIM3/PD1) despite normalization of some immune parameters, suggesting dysregulation that may increase reinfection risk.

This prospective study evaluated cardiopulmonary rehabilitation in 84 severe COVID-19 patients stratified into low- and high-intensity exercise groups over 3 months. Both groups showed significant improvements in lung function, ejection fraction, and exercise capacity, demonstrating that personalized rehabilitation strategies improve long-term cardiopulmonary outcomes in post-COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 225 patients hospitalized for COVID-19 pneumonia at five months post-discharge to identify predictors of persistent dyspnea using clinical assessments, echocardiography, and pulmonary function tests. Higher BMI, elevated C-reactive protein at admission, longer hospitalization duration, and right ventricular dysfunction were independently associated with persistent dyspnea.

A prospective cohort study of 952 long COVID patients at a German outpatient clinic examining symptom severity and PCS score variations over multiple visits. The study documents symptom prevalence and identifies female sex and coronary artery disease as predictors of higher severity, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiopulmonary exercise testing and echocardiography parameters between 44 long COVID patients and 102 controls without long COVID symptoms, all with normal left ventricular ejection fraction. The study identified diagnostic utility of spiroergometry parameters (FEV1/FVC%) and risk factors for long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective-prospective cohort study describes the epidemiological profile and clinical outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 809 hospital employees, tracking symptoms from acute infection through long COVID. It identifies 42 employees (41.6% of 101 respondents) with long-term symptoms including myalgia, dyspnea, and headache, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective observational study comparing serum ferritin levels and clinical characteristics across 234 long COVID patients with ME/CFS, non-ME/CFS fatigue, and no-fatigue groups. Study identifies serum ferritin as a potential predictor of ME/CFS development in long COVID patients, particularly in females, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

A prospective cohort study of 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors followed for up to 18.3 months post-discharge to assess prevalence of self-reported anosmia and ageusia. The study found that both anosmia and ageusia prevalence decreased over time, with female sex and asthma history associated with anosmia development.

A retrospective imaging study assessing lung CT abnormalities in 39 long COVID patients 4-7 months after moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia. Found persistent radiological changes (ground-glass opacities, fibrotic changes) in 94.9% of patients with no significant differences by initial severity or sex.

Prospective cohort study examining the prevalence and incidence of fatigue in 1,417 participants at baseline and 9-month follow-up during the initial COVID-19 pandemic wave. Found that COVID-19 positivity, symptom severity, and symptom duration were significantly associated with higher fatigue at follow-up, suggesting acute illness characteristics predict longer-term fatigue outcomes.

Prospective population-based cohort study in Canada tracking COVID-19 symptom evolution for up to 9 months in 1,349 participants, predominantly unvaccinated. Found 48% exhibited persistent symptoms ≥3 months post-infection, with female sex, symptom severity, and prior mental health conditions as key risk factors; no treatment intervention studied.

Observational study evaluating immunoadsorption (IA) therapy in post-COVID ME/CFS patients with elevated ß2-adrenergic receptor autoantibodies. Interim results from 10 patients show 7 responders with improved functional ability (10-35 point increase in SF36-PF at week 4), providing basis for future RCT with sham control.

This retrospective cohort study compares KL-6 biomarker levels in post-COVID patients stratified by acute COVID-19 severity across three groups (critical, non-critical, and home-hospitalized). KL-6 levels were found to be less elevated in mild COVID-19 patients compared to those with moderate or severe disease, with KL-6 associated with inflammatory, hepatic, and thrombosis markers.

Retrospective longitudinal study of 436 COVID-19 patients in Southeastern Italy assessing predictive factors for long COVID development at 12 weeks post-infection. Identified female sex and corticosteroid therapy during acute infection as independent predictive factors, with 71.8% of patients developing long COVID.

Prospective cohort study evaluating sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances in COVID-19 survivors with and without acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) at 4 and 12 months post-discharge. Found persistent sleep dysfunction (91.3% poor sleep quality, 58.7% insomnia) with no significant improvement between timepoints.

This retrospective cohort study assessed cardiovascular risk factors in 70 post-COVID patients at a rehabilitation clinic in Romania between September-December 2022. The study found increased hypertension risk (69.57% to 90%) and dyslipidemia after COVID-19, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Longitudinal cohort study comparing incidence, severity, and duration of smell and taste loss between COVID-19 positive and negative participants from the Dutch Lifelines biobank. Finds higher incidence and severity in COVID-19 cases but longer duration in non-COVID cases, with no intervention or treatment being evaluated.

Prospective cohort study of 184 children with post-COVID-19 condition and respiratory symptoms, characterizing pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and changes over time from November 2020 to December 2022. Most common finding was mild obstructive pattern (11%); diffusion limitation was rare unlike in adults; most children showed improvement on repeat testing, with older age and specific imaging findings predicting obstructive patterns.

An uncontrolled prospective observational pilot study examining sleep disturbances in 61 long COVID patients using self-reported scales and actigraphy. The study documents high prevalence of moderate daytime sleepiness and insomnia persisting beyond one month post-infection, with female gender and younger age associated with greater severity.

This retrospective cohort study followed 46 COVID-19 survivors who experienced respiratory failure, assessing pulmonary function and functional capacity at 3 and 9 months post-discharge. The findings show that severe respiratory impairment gradually improves spontaneously over time, though recovery is slower in patients who required intensive oxygenation support.

This observational study follows 122 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients (4-84 weeks post-symptom onset) to investigate the association between plasma osteopontin levels and post-acute COVID-19 symptoms. Elevated osteopontin was independently associated with severe dyspnea and impaired quality of life, but was not related to imaging or functional lung abnormalities.

Prospective observational study following 82 long COVID patients for 15 months post-recovery to identify predictors of persistent symptoms and exercise intolerance. Found that higher left ventricular volumes and increased fat content were independently associated with reduced peak VO2max (exercise capacity).

This prospective study evaluated a personalized 6-week rehabilitation program in 90 post-COVID-19 patients, measuring changes in muscle mass, body composition, and functional capacity. Rehabilitation improved fatigue, physical capacity, dyspnea, and functioning regardless of gender, with gender-specific benefits observed in body composition and grip strength.

A prospective longitudinal study of 74 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors assessed at 3 and 6 months post-discharge, examining health-related quality of life (HRQOL) using SF-36 questionnaire and pulmonary function testing. The study found impairment in social-related quality of life associated with respiratory sequelae and initial severity of pneumonia on CT imaging, but did not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This study evaluates the effects of acute COVID-19 infection on male sexual function and spermatogenesis in 31 patients followed for ~90 days post-infection. While it documents some cases of erectile dysfunction, the paper focuses on acute infection sequelae rather than long COVID, and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective longitudinal study of 238 COVID-19 patients in Romania examining liver injury markers and post-acute sequelae (PASC) in elderly versus younger populations over six months post-discharge. The study found more severe liver injury and PASC in elderly patients, with some improvement post-discharge, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Observational cohort study following 390 COVID-19 patients in Thailand for one year post-infection to assess long COVID prevalence and associated health outcomes during the vaccine and antiviral era. Found 77.7% long COVID prevalence with fatigue and cough as most common symptoms; mental health issues and poor sleep quality were also prevalent, particularly in younger patients and females.

This longitudinal study tracked 759 long COVID patients using the C19-YRSm outcome measure to identify and characterize clinical severity types through cluster analysis. The study found three consistent severity clusters (mild, moderate, severe) that remained stable over time, though 51% of patients shifted between severity categories, demonstrating the fluctuating nature of long COVID.

Retrospective analysis of 238 post-COVID-19 patients examining co-existing organ dysfunctions and symptom clusters, with 80 patients receiving comprehensive organ mapping. The study identifies four distinct post-COVID syndrome subgroups characterized primarily by respiratory and neurological involvement with multiorgan dysfunction present in 87.5% of patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study compares long COVID symptom prevalence and cardiovascular complications between males and females without comorbidities, using propensity score matching to control for age and BMI. It is an observational cross-sectional study that documents differences in symptom frequency and cardiac findings but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This prospective cohort study examined the relationship between delayed antibody response during acute COVID-19 infection and quality of life outcomes at 12-month follow-up in 274 severe/critical survivors. Patients with delayed antibody response (negative anti-spike antibodies at admission) had significantly lower mental component scores but similar physical component scores compared to those with prompt antibody response.

Prospective registry analysis examining long-term outcomes in COVID-19 survivors with elevated discharge troponin. No intervention was tested; this is a secondary analysis of existing registry data observing associations between cardiac biomarkers and long COVID symptoms.

Prospective multicenter cohort study following 696 young and middle-aged adults to assess persistence of fatigue, sleep disturbance, and depression at 6 months post-COVID-19. Found 30% experienced persistent fatigue, 21.4% sleep disturbance, and ~25% depression, with significant interrelationships among these symptoms.

Retrospective study examining changes in employment status among 545 employed long COVID patients in a Japanese outpatient clinic from 2021-2023. Found that 54.1% experienced work changes (leave, retirement, or reduced hours), with fatigue and poor QOL being significant factors, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Retrospective observational study using Korean national database comparing SARS-CoV-2 and influenza patients for post-acute symptoms up to 90 days post-infection. Found no elevated symptom risk at 90 days in either adults or children, and concludes post-acute COVID sequelae risk is not significantly different from postviral symptoms from other infections.

This cross-sectional study compared clinical and physiological variables between long COVID patients with and without persistent fatigue, one year post-infection. Patients with fatigue showed greater dyspnea, anxiety, reduced muscle strength, and worse quality of life, with fatigue severity influenced by these factors.

Retrospective cohort study comparing long COVID outcomes between hyperglycemic and normoglycemic patients in a Japanese hospital setting. Found that hyperglycemic patients had significantly longer recovery periods (421 vs 294 days) and worse metabolic/liver/renal function, but no difference in symptom severity.

This observational study followed 127 post-COVID patients over 12 months after inpatient rehabilitation to assess changes in physical health outcomes including functional capacity, strength, balance, and endurance. Despite persistent post-COVID symptoms (28.6-94.7%), patients showed significant improvements across physical health measures 6 and 12 months post-rehabilitation, with differential responses based on age, COVID severity, and comorbidities.

A prospective cohort study of 176 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed at 3, 6, and 9 months to assess pulmonary function and structural lung abnormalities post-infection. Severe/critical patients showed persistent reduced lung volumes and gas transfer deficits without significant improvement over time, with correlations observed between imaging findings and respiratory dysfunction.

Prospective cohort study examining sexual function and hormonal changes in 104 women (64 COVID-infected, 40 controls) measured at 1, 3, and 6 months post-infection. Findings indicate temporary disturbances in prolactin and oxytocin levels in the acute post-infection period, with no lasting effects on sexual function or hormone levels after six months.

Retrospective study evaluating the effects of PIRV-F20® (a combination of lactoferrin, lysozyme, lactobacillus, resveratrol, vitamins, and oligoelements) on exercise capacity in 44 post-COVID-19 patients. Patients receiving the supplement showed significant improvement in 6-minute walking distance (+40 m median vs +10 m in controls, p=0.01), though no differences were found in muscular strength, echocardiographic parameters, or symptom perception.

Observational study of 1,053 long COVID patients in a primary care clinic in Japan examining clinical characteristics, symptom distribution, and disease course between Delta and Omicron infection strains. Found that while symptom patterns differed between strains (possibly due to viral virulence and vaccination rates), the clinical course and prognosis were minimally influenced by infection strain.

Prospective observational study evaluating spa therapy as a supplementary treatment for post-COVID-19 symptoms in 78 participants with chronic conditions. Spa therapy significantly reduced fatigue, pain, brain fog, and cough while improving quality of life.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed 634 hospitalized COVID-19 patients, following 295 for 12-15 months post-discharge, to characterize headache prevalence, phenotypes, and risk factors in long COVID. While dexamethasone showed potential in reducing persistent headaches, the study did not test a specific treatment intervention but rather examined natural outcomes and associations with biomarkers.

A retrospective analysis of 122 long COVID patients who received health resort treatment (balneological factors, physical medicine, climate therapy, exercises) to assess cardiopulmonary symptom severity and treatment efficacy. Health resort treatment effectively reduced dyspnea, chest tightness, and sputum production in both men and women regardless of age, suggesting benefit as a continuation therapy for COVID-19 survivors.

Prospective observational study developing a risk prediction model for erectile dysfunction at 12 months post-COVID-19 recovery in 361 patients. The model identifies features associated with ED prevalence (55.9% in post-COVID group vs 44.1% controls) but does not test any intervention or treatment.

A service evaluation study of 112 long COVID patients discharged from a UK specialist community service, measuring long-term health status and outcomes using standardized patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). The majority of patients (90.2%) continued to experience long COVID symptoms and disability, with significant overlap with ME/CFS criteria.

This Danish population-based cohort study examines how comorbidity and age influence hospitalization and mortality risk up to 2 years after COVID-19 infection in 1,034,103 patients. While it follows patients longitudinally, it does not test any treatment intervention and focuses on acute/post-acute outcomes rather than long COVID-specific persistent symptoms.

This prospective cohort study examined sex differences in cardiovascular outcomes and mortality at 18-month follow-up after acute COVID-19 hospitalization during three pandemic waves. While the paper studies long-term outcomes post-infection, it focuses on acute hospitalization for pneumonia and cardiovascular sequelae rather than long COVID syndrome specifically, and does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

This prospective cohort study examines ophthalmological and microvascular findings in 44 post-acute COVID-19 patients using advanced imaging techniques including ICGA, OCT-angiography, and GlycoCheck. The study documents vascular anomalies including hyperreflective dots, capillary non-perfusion, and reduced capillary density, but does not test or evaluate any therapeutic intervention.

Retrospective multicenter study using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) to assess cardiac inflammation and fibrosis in 174 symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients. Found that 86% had non-ischemic late gadolinium enhancement and abnormal T1/T2 indices, with more severe findings in patients with severe acute COVID-19, but this is an observational imaging study with no intervention tested.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed healthcare resource utilization patterns for pain management among French COVID-19 survivors using claims data from 68,822 hospitalized patients. The study found non-specific increases in pain-related healthcare utilization post-COVID but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is a secondary analysis of administrative claims data rather than a treatment trial.

Register-based case-control study comparing cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks in the year following severe COVID-19 hospitalization requiring mechanical ventilation versus matched population controls. While the study examines post-acute sequelae, it focuses on acute severe COVID-19 (ICU/mechanical ventilation) rather than long COVID as a persistent condition weeks-to-months post-infection, and is purely observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.

A single-center cohort study evaluating long-term disability outcomes 3 years after post-acute rehabilitation in 27 severe COVID-19 survivors using WHODAS 2.0 assessment. Found that central neurological deficits and type 2 diabetes mellitus were significantly associated with higher disability scores, suggesting need for tailored rehabilitation programs.

This observational study in 1,946 Polish women assessed cardiovascular manifestations and identified predictors of long COVID occurrence at 12 months post-COVID. It found that severe acute COVID-19 infection and elevated TG/HDL ratio (>1.89) were independent predictors of long COVID, with additional age-dependent markers, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

A prospective cohort study evaluating an 8-week structured pacing rehabilitation programme based on WHO Borg CR-10 protocol for long COVID patients with post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE). The programme significantly reduced PESE episode frequency (15% fewer per week), duration, and severity, though symptom severity and functional disability improvements were not clinically significant.

A prospective controlled cohort study comparing hospitalization rates and quality of life outcomes in COVID-19 patients versus uninfected controls over three years in Germany. The study found no significant difference in hospitalization rates between groups, but COVID-19 patients reported significantly reduced health-related quality of life and functional status.

This cross-sectional study identified predictors of cardiovascular symptoms in long COVID patients from the Polish PoLoCOV-CVD cohort of 704 participants. Female gender and sleep disturbances were independently associated with cardiovascular complications in long COVID, highlighting demographic and psychological risk factors.

Prospective study following 198 severe/critical COVID-19 survivors over 3-12 months to assess long-term lung sequelae using imaging, pulmonary function tests, and clinical assessments. Found significant improvement in imaging, functional, and clinical parameters over time with no intervention provided, concluding against widespread post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis.

This prospective cohort study assessed whether inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, leukocyte count, suPAR) measured during acute COVID-19 hospitalization can predict long-term pulmonary function impairment in 110 survivors at 4-5 months post-infection. The biomarkers individually showed limited predictive value but combined demonstrated high negative predictive value (NPV 0.93) for identifying DLCO impairment.

An open-label cohort study of 199 long COVID patients receiving personalized, algorithm-based intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia conditioning (IHHC) treatment. The intervention significantly improved quality of life (SF-36 scores increased ~102 points) and reduced pain by 28-32% at 6-week and 6-month follow-ups.
