summary: Prospective follow-up study of 95 COVID-19 ARDS survivors assessed at 8, 12, and 24 months post-diagnosis for health status, exercise capacity, and quality of life. Over 60% had persistent symptoms including fatigue and cognitive issues, with significant improvements in quality of life but impaired pulmonary function and stable depression rates around 30%.

Prospective observational study comparing echocardiographic parameters and cardiac biomarkers in 88 long COVID patients with CKD versus 75 controls over 12 months. COVID-19 infection influenced ventricular function trajectories, with COVID survivors showing better preservation of some parameters despite no significant overall differences between groups.

Prospective observational study of 54 severe COVID-19 survivors assessing arrhythmia incidence and cardiac symptoms 3-6 months post-discharge using Holter monitoring and ECG recording. Palpitations were common initially but declined over 12 months; symptoms were associated with sinus tachycardia rather than actual arrhythmias.

This cross-sectional study examined 252 post-COVID patients at a Hungarian tertiary hospital over a 19-month period, characterizing cardiopulmonary outcomes and identifying a 10× higher prevalence of lupus anticoagulant positivity compared to the general population. The findings suggest autoimmunity may play a role in post-COVID syndrome pathomechanism, with worse cardiopulmonary outcomes associated with severe acute infections.

This retrospective case-control study compared long-COVID prevalence in 247 women with and without endometriosis/adenomyosis, finding significantly higher rates of persistent COVID-19 symptoms in those with gynecological conditions. The study identifies a risk factor association but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study evaluates quality of life and mental health outcomes in survivors of acute COVID-19-related ARDS who received venovenous ECMO support, with follow-up at 1.7 years post-discharge. While it reports persistent mental health issues in ECMO survivors, it focuses on acute respiratory failure outcomes rather than long COVID-specific symptoms or post-COVID syndrome.

This retrospective cohort study compared 216 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors who received intravenous remdesivir during acute infection with 216 matched controls who received no antivirals, following them for ~18 months to assess post-COVID-19 pain development. Remdesivir treatment was protective against overall post-COVID pain (OR 0.444) and lumbar spine pain (OR 0.347), suggesting early antiviral administration may prevent long-term pain sequelae.

Retrospective observational study examining brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels in 428 long COVID patients to assess its usefulness as a biomarker for severity evaluation. Finds that elevated BNP is more common in female patients and associated with respiratory symptoms and memory impairment, suggesting BNP measurement may help evaluate long COVID severity.

Retrospective study of 382 severely ill COVID-19 patients followed at 3 months using unsupervised machine learning to identify symptom phenotypes and patient clusters. The analysis found extreme heterogeneity with no identifiable distinct symptom clusters, preventing the generation of common diagnostic-therapeutic pathways.

Retrospective cohort study of 893 older adults (≥60 years) in Brazil examining the spatial distribution and incidence of post-COVID-19 health complications 12 months after acute infection. Found cardiovascular (39.5%) and metabolic diseases (27.3%) most frequent, with medication use and age associated with increased risk of complications.

Prospective cohort study assessing health-related quality of life in COVID-19 survivors >18 months after ICU discharge following ARDS and ECMO therapy. Found significant impairments in physical, mental, and cognitive health compared to non-COVID ARDS survivors, with longer ECMO duration associated with improved vitality and emotional well-being.

This study compared cognitive and emotional outcomes in 92 healthcare workers one year after mild COVID-19 infection (50 infected, 42 uninfected controls). While no significant cognitive differences were found between groups, the COVID-19 group showed higher trait anxiety and emotional distress, with burnout correlating with slower neuropsychological performance.

Retrospective cohort study comparing 774 long COVID patients with early recovery (<180 days) versus persistent symptoms (>180 days) during the Omicron period. Found female gender, higher symptom burden, and psychological symptoms associated with longer symptom persistence, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study examining the prevalence, severity, and trajectory of insomnia in 172 long COVID patients over 9 months using the Insomnia Severity Index and neuropsychological assessments. Found that 78% of patients experienced insomnia symptoms at baseline, with strong correlations between insomnia and cognitive dysfunction, mood symptoms, and fatigue; symptoms did not improve significantly over the follow-up period.

Prospective cohort study comparing objectively measured physical activity and physical function 12 months after hospital discharge in COVID-19 patients versus healthy controls. Patients had significantly lower daily step counts and movement intensity than controls, but outcomes were comparable between ICU and non-ICU admission groups.

This retrospective cohort study followed 93 COVID-19 pneumonia patients with CT imaging over 10 months to characterize persistent pulmonary imaging abnormalities and their clinical correlates. The study found that fibrotic-like changes persisted in 75% of patients and were associated with fatigue and chest pain, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A retrospective pre-post study of 14 post-COVID-19 patients with isolated dysphonia who received multimodal treatment including corticosteroids, inhalations, and voice therapy. High-speed videoendoscopy and patient-reported outcomes showed improvements in vocal fold oscillation, amplitude, regularity, and voice-related quality of life at 1-month follow-up.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating non-invasive ventilatory strategies (CPAP and HFNC) in long COVID patients with severe ARDS, comparing outcomes and sequelae before endotracheal intubation. CPAP showed a trend toward improved survival, though the data are hypothesis-generating and highlight the need for larger multicenter studies in this underrepresented population.

Retrospective cohort study comparing acute ischemic stroke presentation and outcomes in 26 long COVID patients versus 106 controls presenting to the emergency department. Long COVID patients showed higher rates of headache and facial drooping but similar stroke severity, ED time targets, and short-term outcomes.

A prospective observational study of 146 post-COVID-19 patients examining how metabolic syndrome affects rehabilitation outcomes, using functional tests (6MWT, spirometry) to measure recovery. The study found that comprehensive rehabilitation benefits all patients regardless of metabolic syndrome status, though age and comorbidities significantly predict rehabilitation effectiveness.

A prospective cohort study following 148 COVID-19 survivors (101 with Long COVID) from 12-18 months post-infection to assess changes in physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and associated functional outcomes. People with Long COVID showed increased light PA but decreased MVPA and sedentarism, with higher proportions experiencing functional impairment, dyspnoea, fatigue, and poor quality of life compared to controls, suggesting physical limitations drive activity behaviour changes.

This prospective longitudinal cohort study (12 months) compared health-related quality of life and biomarkers (inflammation, bone turnover, vitamin D) in 45 long COVID patients vs 40 well-recovered controls. Long COVID patients showed significantly lower HRQoL and more hand pain, but no differences in inflammatory markers or bone turnover markers were observed between groups.

This observational study examined late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) patterns on cardiac MRI in 50 COVID-19 ICU patients with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome to assess associations with cardiac dysfunction. LGE was present in 33.3% of patients and correlated with prolonged hospitalization duration but not with left ventricular dysfunction or remodeling.

Retrospective cohort study of 150 pregnant individuals with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy, examining long COVID symptomatology and adverse outcomes in a predominantly Black and Latina population. Study characterizes symptom prevalence (26.7% with long COVID symptoms) and outcome patterns but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining acute pulmonary edema in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and its long-term pulmonary sequelae at three-month follow-up. The study identifies predictors of APE and documents fibrotic changes and restrictive ventilatory defects in survivors, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Retrospective study of asthmatic children who contracted SARS-CoV-2, examining changes in lung function and persistent respiratory symptoms months after infection. The study documents symptom persistence and treatment modifications but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment for long COVID.

Population-based retrospective cohort study of 1,034,093 Danish adults over 40 examining prevalence and risk factors for COVID-19 sequelae diagnoses and their long-term health outcomes over two years. Study found 0.55% prevalence of sequelae, with higher comorbidity burden increasing risk of severe sequelae and complications including thromboembolic events, chronic lung disease, and infections.

A 12-month longitudinal feasibility cohort study comparing bone mineral density, body composition, and joint integrity in 45 long COVID patients versus 40 well-recovered controls. The study found no evidence of rapid bone loss but identified increased adiposity and joint symptoms, suggesting a need for ongoing monitoring of musculoskeletal health in long COVID.

This cross-sectional study examined 61 long COVID patients 16.5 months post-infection to explore associations between type I interferon gene expression, hematologic markers during acute infection, and long COVID symptom severity. The study found that elevated WBC/neutrophil counts, reduced monocyte counts, elevated LDH/SGOT, intubation history, and reduced MX-1 transcript levels during acute infection were associated with high long COVID symptom burden, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Secondary analysis of COVID-19 ICU survivors examining associations between mechanical ventilation duration and cognitive outcomes one year post-discharge. Findings suggest tracheostomy-based ventilation may be associated with better cognitive outcomes compared to endotracheal intubation, but this is a secondary analysis of published data rather than a primary treatment trial.

This observational study followed 233 oldest-old adults (≥80 years) for 18 months after COVID-19 hospitalization to assess transitions in physical function and frailty. While it documents post-hospitalization recovery patterns in elderly survivors, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and involves no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This prospective observational study examines MMP-2 and MMP-9 dysregulation in post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis patients at 6 and 12 months post-infection, comparing those with and without fibrotic changes. The study identifies biomarker patterns and inflammatory pathways but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A 32-month prospective cohort study of 94 ICU survivors with COVID-19 that documents the prevalence and persistence of post-COVID condition manifestations across five organ system domains. The study shows high initial prevalence (96.8% at discharge) declining over time, with respiratory symptoms resolving by 32 months while musculoskeletal/neuromuscular involvement persisted, and 36.5% of survivors developing new chronic conditions by 32 months.

Retrospective observational study of 97 post-COVID syndrome patients assessing longitudinal changes in pulmonary function over 22 months post-infection. Found progressive improvements in airflow measures up to 9-18 months but persistent diffusion abnormalities beyond 12 months, with greater impairment in patients with moderate acute COVID-19.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between obesity (measured by BMI and waist-to-height ratio) and post-COVID-19 condition in 376 male military conscripts with prior COVID-19 infection. Both BMI-defined and central obesity were significantly associated with increased odds of experiencing persistent post-COVID symptoms.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing retinal vascular perfusion (RPCP) between 80 post-COVID-19 patients and 30 healthy controls using OCT angiography. Found significantly lower retinal capillary perfusion density in post-COVID patients, particularly those with hypertension or prior antiviral/antiplatelet treatment, suggesting potential microvascular impairment.

This observational cohort study assessed left ventricular function in 125 COVID-19 patients without prior cardiovascular disease at 6-10 weeks post-discharge. The study found persistent systolic and diastolic dysfunction in a subset of patients, correlated with myocardial injury markers, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective observational study examining MRI imaging patterns in a cardiovascular center before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, analyzing 8,137 MRI studies from 2019-2022. Found that patients with COVID-19 history showed persistent cardiac symptoms and myocardial damage consistent with long COVID, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective observational cohort study assessed echocardiographic abnormalities in 102 previously healthy individuals recovering from COVID-19, monitoring cardiac patterns (LV dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, pericardial effusion) at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Most cardiac abnormalities improved over time, though diastolic dysfunction showed persistent changes, suggesting potential chronic cardiac sequelae in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome.

This study prospectively measured pulmonary function tests and exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO and CaNO) in 169 post-COVID patients 6 weeks to 1 year after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, stratified by initial severity. Elevated distal lung inflammation (CaNO) was found in severe/critical COVID-19 patients and inversely correlated with lung gas transfer, suggesting persistent alveolar inflammation may contribute to long-term pulmonary complications.

This prospective cohort study used optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) to compare retinal capillary perfusion parameters between non-hospitalized neuro-PASC patients and healthy controls. The study found statistically significant reduction in deep capillary plexus vessel length density in neuro-PASC patients, suggesting preferential involvement of the smallest blood vessels as a potential mechanism.

Observational cohort study of 114 long COVID patients investigating associations between serum biomarkers (cystatin-c, orosomucoid, arginine derivatives) and long COVID symptoms. Found that cystatin-c may indicate subclinical renal impairment and orosomucoid is associated with fatigue, but this is a cross-sectional biomarker analysis without treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 142 long COVID patients examining immune activation and amino acid metabolism changes associated with persistent symptoms. The study found that women report persistent symptoms more frequently and that alterations in tryptophan and phenylalanine metabolism correlate with symptom severity and recovery, but no treatment or intervention was evaluated.

The P4O2 COVID-19 extension is a prospective multicenter cohort study of 95 long COVID patients that includes a nested personalized counseling intervention trial to identify treatable traits and develop tailored therapeutic strategies. Results show persistence of respiratory (78.9%), neurological (68.4%), and fatigue symptoms (67.4%) at 3-6 months post-infection, with female sex and Delta variant infection associated with more persisting symptom categories.

This cross-sectional study evaluated psychological outcomes (depression, anxiety, PTSD, insomnia) and quality of life in 143 COVID-19 survivors 1-2 months after hospital discharge using standardized screening tools. Mental health symptoms were common (depression 19%, anxiety 27%, PTSD 39%, insomnia 33%) and more frequent in females; worse outcomes were associated with ICU admission and longer hospital stays.

Retrospective analysis of 2,007 long COVID patients comparing medication use before and after SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding significant increases in chronic medications across multiple drug categories. COVID-19 severity and age >65 were predictors of increased polypharmacy, while vaccination showed protective effects against medication burden.

This observational cross-sectional study measured 13 endothelial biomarkers in 68 long COVID patients and matched controls, finding elevated markers of endothelial activation/dysfunction in patients. The study correlates these biomarkers with fatigue, dyspnea, lung diffusion capacity, and functional capacity but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective observational study examining echocardiographic abnormalities in 203 long COVID patients, comparing those with and without dysautonomia. Found that most long COVID patients did not demonstrate cardiac dysfunction on echocardiography, and dysautonomia was not accompanied by structural or functional cardiac alterations.

This single-center observational study longitudinally evaluated pulmonary function in 140 COVID-19 survivors one year post-infection using spirometry and DLCO testing, stratified by disease severity. While significant improvements in DLCO and TLC were observed over one year, particularly in severe disease patients, this is a passive follow-up study without any treatment intervention and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria for treatment trials.

Prospective observational study measuring serum neural biomarkers (GFAP, s100b, total Tau) in 65 long-COVID patients versus 20 controls. Found elevated GFAP in long-COVID patients but no treatment intervention—this is a biomarker assessment study without therapeutic evaluation.

This cross-sectional study of 450 COVID-19 outpatients examines associations between acute symptom clusters and subsequent Long COVID fatigue, with analysis of sex-specific differences. The study finds that cognitive and mental symptoms during acute infection are strongly associated with fatigue severity months later, but it is an observational/descriptive study with no treatment intervention evaluated.

This cross-sectional study examined cerebral hemodynamic alterations in dialysis patients with prior COVID-19 infection (n=16) compared to matched controls without COVID-19 (n=21) using transcranial Doppler ultrasound measurements during hemodialysis. COVID-19 survivors showed significantly increased pulsatility index and lower heart rates, suggesting altered cerebral perfusion pressure regulation and potential long-term vascular effects from SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Retrospective study of 229 COVID-19 patients with olfactory dysfunction, comparing those with persistent symptoms (9.5 months post-infection) to those with resolved symptoms. Identifies asthma and cacosmia as predictive factors for olfactory dysfunction persistence, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Observational study of 17 adults with allergic disease and long COVID examining biomarkers of allergic inflammation and barrier integrity. Found associations between elevated ECP and FLCs with respiratory and systemic symptoms, but this is a descriptive biomarker study without treatment intervention or control comparison.

This paper examines the prevalence and predictive factors of persistent smell and taste dysfunction in COVID-19 patients one year after infection through questionnaires and psychophysical testing. While it documents that chemosensory dysfunction is a clinically relevant long COVID symptom, it is an observational study that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study follows 44 healthcare workers for up to 721 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess persistent chemosensory dysfunction and its relationship with adaptive immune responses. While it provides valuable epidemiological data on long COVID symptoms, it does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it observational only.

This study compares TSH levels in hospitalized COVID-19 patients (critical vs non-critical) and follows survivors at three months post-discharge to assess thyroid function recovery. While it includes post-discharge follow-up, it is purely observational with no intervention given and focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization rather than long COVID symptom management or treatment.

Prospective observational study of 143 non-diabetic hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed at 0, 4, and 12 months to examine the relationship between long COVID-19 syndrome and insulin resistance development. Found that 30.7% developed long COVID-19, and 75% of those with long COVID-19 developed diabetes within one year, with significant increases in glucose levels and insulin resistance in patients with BMI > 30 kg/m2.

This study compared treatment outcomes for post-COVID olfactory dysfunction in 45 long COVID patients treated with anti-neuroinflammatory therapy (um-PEA-LUT plus olfactory training) versus 40 MS patients treated with disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Results showed that 13 COVID-19 patients had residual olfactory impairment after treatment, while MS patients on certain DMTs (IFN-beta, glatiramer acetate) preserved olfactory function better, suggesting DMTs warrant investigation for refractory post-COVID smell disorders.

A prospective cohort study evaluating cardiopulmonary fitness in 2,732 post-COVID patients from a specialized clinic over 26 months, with 97 undergoing exercise testing compared to pre-pandemic controls. Found no significant relationship between VO2 max and post-COVID disability or COVID-19 severity, with cardiac symptoms occurring in only a small percentage of patients.

This multicenter observational study describes laryngotracheal complications in COVID-19 patients who required prolonged endotracheal intubation during acute illness in 2021. The study focuses on acute post-intubation sequelae (dysphonia, dyspnea, dysphagia, laryngeal mobility alterations) rather than long COVID syndrome, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational multicenter study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence and persistence across different SARS-CoV-2 strains in 308 Italian patients. Found substantial improvements in dyspnea and fatigue at 6-month follow-up, but minimal improvement in mental health and daily functioning domains.

This study follows 17 COVID-19 survivors who required ECMO support during acute infection for over one year post-discharge. While it documents long-term pulmonary and psychological outcomes after critical COVID-19, it does not focus on long COVID and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study followed 247 long COVID patients over 15 months to characterize symptom persistence, risk factors, and work ability. At 15-month follow-up, 75% of patients had returned to baseline health status; females had lower work ability and higher psychiatric symptoms, while pre-existing depression was associated with persistent symptoms.

This retrospective cohort study investigates the relationship between malnutrition and adverse clinical outcomes, including post-COVID-19 condition, within 90-180 days after acute COVID-19 infection using propensity score matching. The study finds that patients with malnutrition have significantly higher incidence of hospitalization, mortality, and post-COVID-19 condition compared to those without malnutrition.

This retrospective study evaluates the efficacy of two post-COVID rehabilitation programs in 33 ambulatory patients, comparing kinesiotherapy combined with High-Intensity Laser Therapy (HILT) versus kinesiotherapy alone, using the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) as a functional assessment tool before and after 10 daily sessions. The HILT plus kinesiotherapy group showed greater functional improvements than kinesiotherapy alone, with 96.96% of patients completing the 6MWT and performance improvements ranging from 3% to 60%.

Follow-up study of 51 SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia survivors evaluated 2 months post-discharge for pulmonary function, exercise capacity, radiological changes, and quality of life. Found residual lung function impairment and reduced physical capacity in a significant proportion, but is a passive observational assessment without any treatment intervention.

Single-centre observational study assessing respiratory muscle function (MIP/MEP) in 223 COVID-19 survivors at 3-6 months post-discharge. Found 54.3% exhibited respiratory muscle dysfunction associated with prior non-invasive ventilation use and female gender, but this is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention.

Retrospective descriptive study characterizing ME/CFS diagnosed in 279 long COVID patients at a COVID-19 aftercare clinic from February 2021 to April 2022. Found 16.8% prevalence of ME/CFS with fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and headache as most common symptoms, with no treatment intervention tested.

Retrospective descriptive study analyzing prescription patterns of Kampo (Japanese herbal) medicines in 102 long COVID patients with general fatigue at a COVID-19 aftercare clinic from Feb-Dec 2021. Hochuekkito was the most frequently prescribed Kampo medicine (71.6% of Kampo prescriptions), with other herbal medicines targeting qi deficiency used for symptom management including fatigue, dysosmia, dysgeusia, and insomnia.

Retrospective observational study comparing clinical characteristics of long COVID in 54 teenage patients versus adults at a single Japanese hospital from 2021-2022. Found that fatigue was the most common symptom in both groups, with teenagers having significantly higher rates of headache than adults.

This cross-sectional study of 3,636 post-COVID patients assessed the relationship between comorbidity burden (via Charlson Comorbidity Index) and post-COVID-19 syndrome development. The study found that patients with comorbidities had significantly higher risk of post-COVID syndrome, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

A retrospective cohort study of 117 long COVID patients (≥2 years post-infection) assessed at a rehabilitation clinic to evaluate prothrombotic and proinflammatory markers, stratified by presence/absence of pulmonary fibrosis. Patients with post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis showed significantly elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, neutrophils) and prothrombotic markers (D-dimer) despite functional recovery, with elevated D-dimer emerging as a predictor of impaired lung diffusion capacity.

This study examines the long-term effect of acute COVID-19 severity on kidney graft function in transplant recipients over one year of follow-up. While the paper studies post-infection outcomes, it focuses on acute COVID-19 complications in a transplant population rather than long COVID syndrome, and does not test any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study tracking 103 COVID-19 patients from diagnosis through 2-year follow-up to characterize long COVID symptoms and their impact on quality of life. At 2 years, the most common symptoms were asthenia, headache, memory disorders, and cardiovascular changes including palpitations and fluctuating blood pressure.

Retrospective observational study comparing long COVID characteristics across three periods: pre-Delta, Delta-dominant, and Omicron-dominant, with 353 total patients. Finds that Omicron-infected patients had lower rates of dysosmia, dysgeusia, and hair loss but higher rates of fatigue, insomnia, and cough compared to Delta-infected patients.

Prospective observational study following 68 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 3 and 12 months post-discharge to describe symptom persistence and quality of life changes using the SF-36. Found high symptom persistence (76.4% at 12 months) with evolving symptom profiles: myalgia/alopecia/cough decreased while sleep disorders and memory problems increased.

This prospective study examined optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) changes in the optic nerve head of 63 patients hospitalized with acute COVID-19 bilateral pneumonia, comparing them to 43 healthy controls two months after discharge. No significant changes in radial peripapillary capillary networks were observed, and the study does not address long COVID or any treatment intervention.

This study examines maternal and fetal outcomes of COVID-19 infection during pregnancy across all three trimesters in 105 pregnant women. While the paper does mention post-COVID symptoms (loss of smell, dry eyes, myalgia), it focuses primarily on acute COVID-19 complications during pregnancy and immediate postpartum outcomes, not on long COVID as a persistent condition or treatment of long COVID patients.

This prospective observational cohort study followed 85 survivors of severe/critical COVID-19 pneumonia for 12 months post-discharge, assessing lung function, radiological changes, and immune parameters. While it demonstrates significant long-term pulmonary and immunological impairments, it is a passive follow-up study without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX data examining the long-term impact of COVID-19 on osteoporosis risk in patients aged ≥50 years with overweight, obesity, or type 2 diabetes. COVID-19 was independently associated with increased osteoporosis risk, fragility fractures, and low T-scores, with risk peaking at 4 years post-infection and persisting through 6 years.

This study assessed chest CT and pulmonary function test abnormalities in 232 post-COVID-19 patients six months after infection, comparing them with 543 population controls. Most radiological abnormalities resolved within six months regardless of initial severity, with pulmonary function tests showing no significant differences from the general population.

This cross-sectional study compared respiratory function and physical performance in young adults (aged 18-25) at 3-6 months and 6-12 months post-COVID-19 against healthy controls. Young adults with prior asymptomatic or mild COVID-19 showed declines in forced vital capacity, peak expiratory flow, lower extremity muscle performance, and walking distance compared to controls, with some measures deteriorating further by 6-12 months post-infection.

This is a prospective longitudinal study following 210 patients hospitalized for COVID-19 at 3, 6, and 12 months to identify predictors of long COVID and assess post-COVID lung involvement. The study found minimal interstitial lung disease (0.5%) and no significant risk factors for 12-month outcomes, though longer initial hospitalization was associated with lower pulmonary function and more symptoms at early timepoints.

This retrospective cohort study followed 426 vaccinated COVID-19 survivors for 30 months, examining longitudinal changes in metabolic, endocrine, renal, cardiovascular, and inflammatory biomarkers with sex-stratified analysis. Males showed earlier metabolic and cardiac alterations while females exhibited more persistent endocrine and inflammatory shifts, highlighting sex-specific recovery patterns in long COVID.

Prospective cohort study tracking health-related quality of life (HRQoL) over 12 months in 93 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors in Lithuania using SF-36 assessments. Most HRQoL domains showed clinically meaningful improvement, though scores remained below population norms and emotional/social deficits persisted, with low rehabilitation uptake identified as a care gap.

This cross-sectional study investigates the association between vitamin D levels and long COVID signs and symptoms in 170 COVID-19 patients. While confirming a significant association between vitamin D deficiency and long COVID prevalence, the study does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is a purely observational assessment of vitamin D status and symptom prevalence.

Prospective study of pulmonary function in 250 mild COVID-19 patients during acute infection and home isolation in Thailand. Found abnormal lung function in 28.4% of patients, mainly restrictive patterns and small airway disease, but this is acute COVID-19 assessment, not long COVID follow-up.

Retrospective study of 119 long COVID patients comparing outcomes between shorter and prolonged health resort treatment stays. Prolonged treatment (~4 weeks) showed significantly greater improvements in functional status (PCFS), dyspnea (mMRC), and neuropsychiatric symptoms compared to shorter stays.

Retrospective cohort study examining pulmonary function in 100 pediatric COVID-19 survivors aged 5-18 years using spirometry. Found 47% prevalence of impaired lung function and 18% prevalence of long COVID, with persistent symptoms, undernourished status, and moderate-to-critical COVID severity significantly associated with abnormal spirometry.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) 600 mg treatment in 33 long COVID patients over 3 months, with outcomes measured by PCFS scale. Found significant differences in PCFS scores between hospitalized and home-care groups, with smoking identified as a risk factor (OR 8.13), suggesting PEA may be effective for long COVID symptom management.

This cross-sectional study characterized gut microbiome composition in 178 post-COVID-19 patients at three months post-infection using 16S rRNA sequencing. While no significant microbiome differences were found between severity groups, multiple associations were identified between specific bacterial taxa and immune/cardiovascular clinical parameters.

This longitudinal study investigates metabolic and immunological recovery patterns in 886 hospitalized severe COVID-19 patients and 513 non-hospitalized recovered patients using NMR-based metabolomics. While it characterizes recovery phenotypes and metabolic normalization timelines, it does not study or test any treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

Propensity score-matched cohort study examining metabolic disorder risk following COVID-19 infection in U.S. active-duty military personnel. Found increased hazards for hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and liver disease within one year post-infection, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study examined whether DNA methylation levels of the ACE2 promoter are associated with post-COVID-19 symptoms in 279 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors. The analysis found no association between ACE2 methylation and the presence of fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive problems, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

A retrospective cohort study analyzing 79 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to identify biomarkers and risk factors associated with long COVID development at 1.5-year follow-up. Found that 41.8% developed long COVID symptoms (predominantly fatigue), with elevated lymphocyte levels, NK cell subpopulation changes, and ICU admission during acute infection as significant predictors.

Longitudinal study comparing plasma cytokine levels (IL-1β, TNF-α, MIP-1α, etc.) in hospitalized COVID-19 patients who did or did not develop post-COVID symptoms at 6 months. Findings suggest elevated IL-1β, MIP-1α, and TNF-α at month 1 post-infection may predict long COVID development.

A prospective observational cohort study examining iron dyshomeostasis and anaemia in 108 COVID-19 patients followed at multiple timepoints (60-360 days post-infection). The study found anaemia and iron dyshomeostasis were frequent but did not relate to structural lung impairment, though they were associated with impaired stress resilience at long-term follow-up.

Retrospective observational study describing the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 354 hospitalized patients from the first wave in France, with 35.9% reporting persistent symptoms 9 months post-infection. The study compares symptom profiles and clinical characteristics between patients with and without persistent symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
