summary: A prospective observational study of 184 post-COVID-19 patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, examining clinical and functional predictors of response to the intervention. The study identified baseline 6-minute walking distance, forced vital capacity, and functional independence scores as key predictors of whether patients would achieve their target walking distance goals after rehabilitation.

This longitudinal cohort study assessed cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes in 108 COVID-19 participants at 6-month follow-up, comparing baseline and follow-up neuropsychological test results. Results showed significant improvement in cognitive domains (memory, processing speed, executive function) and higher anxiety/depression in those with subjective cognitive complaints, with no cognitive impairment linked to disease severity.

Prospective observational study of 109 COVID-19 patients examining associations between vitamin D status and long-term sequelae at 8 weeks post-infection. Low vitamin D levels were frequent but not associated with persistent symptoms, lung function impairment, or disease severity outcomes.

Retrospective analysis of 152 long COVID patients with pre- and post-COVID autonomic nervous system testing, comparing sympathetic/parasympathetic function before and after infection, with autonomic therapy intervention. Post-COVID patients showed reversed autonomic dysfunction patterns (parasympathetic excess and sympathetic withdrawal) with ~50% more autonomic symptoms, which improved with autonomic therapy.

This case-control study compared brain MRI findings in 30 post-COVID-19 headache patients versus 30 controls, finding significantly higher rates of white matter lesions (50% vs 20%, p=0.015) in the post-COVID group. The results suggest persistent post-COVID headaches may be associated with structural white matter changes, though the study does not test a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigates the relationship between vitamin D levels and persistent symptoms (fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance) in 149 long COVID patients assessed at median 79 days post-infection. The study found no significant association between vitamin D levels and measures of ongoing ill-health, suggesting these symptoms are independent of vitamin D status.

Prospective cohort study of 288 COVID-19 survivors followed at 30 days and 6 months post-discharge, evaluating persistent malnutrition, muscle strength loss, and functional decline. Patients with persistent impairment received dietary counseling, nutritional supplementation, physical activity guidance, physiotherapy, or post-care facility admission; 36% retained malnutrition at 6 months, with obesity and ICU admission as risk factors.

A population-based retrospective cohort study of 110,726 COVID-19 patients in Spain examining associations between metabolic status and mortality/post-acute COVID-19 outcomes. The study identifies risk factors for developing post-acute COVID-19 (female sex, older age, sleep apnea, asthma, elevated glucose/cholesterol) but does not test any interventions or treatments.

This study evaluated the effects of personalized rehabilitation on autonomy, malnutrition, and symptoms in 37 long COVID patients who were severely dependent and malnourished upon admission to a rehabilitation center. Results showed significant recovery of autonomy and improvement in most symptoms by 6 months post-discharge, although fatigue persisted in 70% of patients.

Longitudinal observational study examining quadriceps muscle strength in 98 post-hospitalized COVID-19 patients and 50 with mild COVID-19 PASC over 1.5 years. Found that muscle weakness was prevalent (~60-65%) at 14 weeks with modest improvement but no change in prevalence, with no large structural abnormalities on ultrasound.

This retrospective cohort study measures changes in chest CT-derived body composition (muscle, fat, liver) in 208 severe COVID-19 survivors over 6-7 months post-infection. The study documents continued muscle and visceral fat loss over time, with inflammatory burden (CRP) associated with greater skeletal muscle loss, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study tracking sarcopenia and malnutrition in 139 COVID-19 patients at 3 and 6 months post-discharge using EWGSOP2 criteria and DXA imaging. Found sarcopenia in 22 patients (16%) at 3 months associated with ICU stay, but 73% recovered by 6 months with weight returning to baseline.

This retrospective cohort study examines serum magnesium levels as a prognostic biomarker in COVID-19 patients hospitalized during acute infection. While the paper finds that low magnesium predicts long COVID symptomatology as a secondary outcome, it is fundamentally a prognostic study of acute COVID-19 mortality and complications, not a study of treatments for long COVID.

A retrospective analysis by nine Italian general practitioners evaluating palmitoylethanolamide co-ultramicronized with luteolin (PEALUT) supplementation in long COVID patients. Supplementation improved multiple symptoms including pain, anxiety, depression, fatigue, brain fog, anosmia, and dysgeusia, suggesting a role for neuroinflammation control in long COVID recovery.

Prospective cohort study comparing body composition changes in COVID-19 survivors versus uninfected controls using DXA scans acquired before and after the pandemic. Both groups gained weight and fat during the pandemic, but only COVID-19 survivors showed significant decline in lean body mass regardless of PASC status.

This cross-sectional study compared dietary intake, physical activity, and sleep patterns in post-COVID-19 patients with fatigue (n=confirmed) versus healthy controls over a 7-day period. The study found no significant differences in nutrition or physical activity between groups, but post-COVID patients had significantly longer sleep duration (49 minutes longer, p=0.003), suggesting sleep alterations rather than malnutrition as a factor in COVID-related fatigue.

Longitudinal observational study following COVID-19 survivors for 6 months post-discharge to assess handgrip strength changes and their associations with quality of life, dyspnea, and exercise capacity. While the paper studies long COVID sequelae, it is not a treatment trial—it passively follows patients' natural recovery without testing any intervention.

Post hoc analysis of the COVID-19 Recovery Study II examining risk factors for malnutrition one year after COVID-19 hospitalization. Identifies baseline BMI, hospitalization duration, dialysis status, and cognitive symptoms as independent predictors of long-term nutritional disorders.

This cross-sectional study compared masticatory function, strength, and effectiveness in 23 PACS patients stratified by sarcopenia status. PACS patients with sarcopenia showed significantly reduced masticatory effectiveness and strength compared to non-sarcopenic PACS patients.

A retrospective observational study comparing vitamin D deficiency (VDD) in 97 long COVID patients (68% with VDD) infected during the Omicron phase. VDD was associated with higher rates of dizziness, memory impairment, palpitation, appetite loss, fatigue, and depressive symptoms, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study of 94 postcritical COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between vitamin D levels and recovery outcomes during a 6-month multimodal rehabilitation program combining nutritional support and physical rehabilitation. Vitamin D deficiency was associated with longer hospital/ICU stays and worse muscle recovery, while normal vitamin D levels at follow-up correlated with better morphofunctional recovery, particularly in sarcopenic obesity patients.

Single-center case series of 227 patients with neurological post-COVID-19 syndrome examining symptom characteristics and therapeutic approaches. Most patients received symptomatic treatment with 44.95% showing positive outcomes on follow-up, and symptoms were more common in women with headache and cognitive impairment being predominant.

Retrospective chart review of 397 COVID-19 patients at a Canadian tertiary care center identifying 62 (27%) with long COVID based on consensus criteria. No intervention was tested; the study characterizes clinical and laboratory features of long COVID patients versus non-long COVID patients.

This retrospective cohort study compared the course of COVID-19 and long COVID prevalence between pre-Omicron and Omicron-dominant periods in 1,967 patients, with follow-up assessments at 3 months. The study identified risk factors for long COVID (female sex, asthma) but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—it is an observational epidemiological study tracking disease outcomes across pandemic periods.

Longitudinal observational cohort study examining fecal microbiota profiles in 145 SARS-CoV-2-positive and 32 negative adolescents/young adults at baseline and 6-month follow-up. Found specific bacterial taxa (Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Sutterella wadsworthensis, Streptococcus thermophilus, Clostridium spiroforme) associated with persistent fatigue and post-COVID condition, suggesting a role for dysbiosis in long COVID pathophysiology.

This retrospective comparative study examines pathomorphological changes in femoral head tissue from 41 post-COVID-19 osteonecrosis patients versus 47 non-COVID controls following hip arthroplasty. The study identifies mast cell clusters, fibrosis, and vascular thrombosis as key pathological features but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This prospective study evaluated a community pharmacy-based intervention program for 871 post-COVID patients in Serbia, where pharmacists provided counselling and guidance on self-medication. Patients showed significant symptom improvement with median severity scores dropping from 3 to 1 between first and follow-up visits.

This study examined the association between heart rate variability (HRV) measured at hospital admission and pulmonary function impairment or persistent symptoms in 171 COVID-19 patients followed 3-5 months post-discharge. HRV was not found to be associated with pulmonary function impairment or persistent symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition.

Retrospective study analyzing CT imaging findings in 76 long COVID patients at 3-12 months post-diagnosis to document persistent lung parenchymal alterations. While it contributes to understanding long COVID sequelae, it does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—it is purely observational/descriptive imaging research without a treatment component.

This is a sub-group analysis of nasopharyngeal samples from COVID-19 patients, comparing gene expression between those who developed long COVID and those who did not at day 14 post-infection. The study identifies dysregulated genes and pathways (complement, fibrinolysis, IL-7, neurotransmission) associated with eventual long COVID diagnosis but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study of pulmonary structural and functional outcomes in 71 severe COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 12 months post-discharge. While pulmonary function tests normalized in most patients, CT abnormalities persisted in 49/63 patients (82% improved, 14% stable, 2% worsened) with correlations to elevated D-dimer levels.

Observational study assessing detection of depressive symptoms in older adults with post-COVID syndrome using three screening methods (spontaneous complaint, direct question, GDS-15 scale). Found that spontaneous complaints substantially under-detect depression compared to standardized screening tools, with post-COVID patients showing higher rates of depressive symptoms than controls.

This cross-sectional study describes persistent symptoms in 118 post-COVID-19 patients attending follow-up clinic in Nepal, with mean follow-up of 28 days post-diagnosis. The study documents symptom prevalence (dyspnea 40.7%, fatigue 33.1%, chest heaviness 28%) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A two-year longitudinal study of 377 COVID-19 patients from the first wave in Madrid that tracked symptom evolution, recovery, and reinfection rates through August 2022. Identified risk factors associated with long COVID development (COPD, dyspnea, elevated LDH, lower D-dimer) and found 27% of patients experienced long COVID symptoms.

Retrospective study of 18 lung transplant recipients infected with SARS-CoV-2 during the pre-vaccination era, examining acute COVID-19 severity and lung function outcomes. While some patients showed persistent lung function decline, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications in a specialized transplant population rather than long COVID syndrome in the general population.

Prospective cohort study of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 123 people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy, assessing prevalence and risk factors for severe COVID-19 and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). Found that 26.7% of symptomatic survivors developed PACS at 6-month follow-up, with COVID-19 severity being the main predictor of PACS independent of other factors.

This study evaluates clinical and immune responses in children (0-14 years) during the 6-8 months following mild or asymptomatic COVID-19 infection. While some lung lesions persisted in younger children, most participants developed detectable neutralizing antibodies and specific cellular immune responses, indicating immune memory formation rather than long COVID sequelae.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and risk factors for persistent smell and taste disorders in 2,218 COVID-19 convalescents up to three months post-infection from the Polish PoLoCOV-CVD study. The analysis identifies that younger patients with fewer comorbidities and higher acute symptom burden, particularly those treated at home, were at greater risk of persistent chemosensory dysfunction.

COVEVOL is a retrospective observational study of 74 COVID-19 patients describing the natural course of symptoms at 6 months post-infection, identifying predictors of symptom persistence. The study found 71.6% experienced persistent symptoms, with older age, higher BMI, and prior hospitalization as risk factors, but no intervention was tested.

Retrospective analysis of 428 long COVID patients from a post-COVID outpatient service examining symptom patterns and risk factors. Found that SARS-CoV-2 variants (wild-type vs Alpha B.1.1.7) were associated with different long COVID symptom phenotypes, with female sex and severe COVID-19 course as main risk factors.

Prospective cohort study of 55 long COVID patients followed in family practice (May 2021–July 2022), with SPECT-CT brain imaging in 32 patients showing vascular encephalopathy. No treatment was tested; the study documents clinical phenotypes and natural recovery patterns over 18 months, with no intervention arm.

Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence of alternative diagnoses in 110 pediatric patients with suspected long COVID. Found that 47% had alternative somatic/mental diseases, 29% had LC, and 23% remained unclarified; neurological and respiratory symptom clusters were effective at identifying LC cases.

Retrospective analysis of 2,218 patients from the STOP-COVID registry examining long-COVID clinical features and risk factors at three-month follow-up. Identifies chronic fatigue, cough, and brain fog as most common symptoms, with female gender, severe acute COVID-19, dyspnea, and chest pain as significant risk factors.

This retrospective cohort study assessed outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infections in 98 fully vaccinated liver transplant recipients during the Omicron wave. While most had mild disease, 37.5% reported long-lasting symptoms for ≥4 weeks, with older age and female sex identified as risk factors.

This cross-sectional study measured SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels in COVID-19 convalescents at 5-6 weeks and 5-6 months post-infection, comparing those with and without post-COVID symptoms. The findings show that patients reporting multiple post-infectious symptoms had significantly higher anti-spike and anti-nucleocapsid antibody levels, suggesting dysregulated immune response as a potential mechanism underlying post-COVID syndrome.

This multicenter cohort study tracked gastrointestinal symptoms in 1,266 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors over 18 months post-infection using Sankey plots and exponential regression modeling. The study documents the natural recovery trajectory of gastrointestinal symptoms and diarrhea without any intervention, showing declining prevalence over time.

This study examined anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody dynamics and cell-free DNA as potential biomarkers for post-COVID syndrome over 12 months in 49 recovered individuals. The paper is primarily an observational immunological characterization study with no treatment intervention evaluated, and functions as a secondary analysis examining biomarkers in an existing cohort rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.

The GENCOV study characterizes risk factors associated with severe COVID-19 and persistent symptoms in 966 Canadian participants. Age, BMI, ethnicity, hypertension, and viral variants were identified as significant risk factors for hospitalization, with multiple symptoms including shortness of breath persisting beyond acute illness.

Retrospective analysis of 801 patients from the STOP-COVID registry examining post-COVID symptoms at 12-month follow-up stratified by vaccination status. The study found that unvaccinated patients reported significantly more frequent headache, arthralgia, and hypertension dysregulation, but does not test a specific intervention or treatment protocol.

This study performed a 2.5-year follow-up analysis of 110 COVID-19 convalescents to examine the relationship between early immune response (antibodies and T-cells), vaccination status, reinfection rate, and long-term post-COVID symptoms. While the paper is about long COVID, it is an observational cohort study without any intervention—it passively follows patients and measures immune markers associated with symptoms, rather than testing a treatment.

This prospective study evaluates lung ultrasonography (LUS) as a diagnostic tool for assessing lung involvement in 72 patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome, comparing LUS findings with chest CT scans. The study finds strong correlation between LUS and CT findings but does not test any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining PASC development rates in patients with hereditary connective tissue diseases using JH-CROWN consortium data. Found that connective tissue disease patients had elevated rates of PASC (9.52%) compared to the overall cohort (2.54%), suggesting a potential risk association.

A prospective cohort study of 199 long COVID patients followed 26 months post-infection that identified three distinct symptom clusters using cluster analysis. The study demonstrates that symptom clusters persist beyond two years but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examined whether four inflammatory polymorphisms (IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α, IFITM3) were associated with post-COVID symptoms in 408 previously hospitalized COVID-19 survivors. The study found no significant associations between these genetic variants and the development of post-COVID symptoms, despite the variants being linked to COVID-19 severity.

This is a retrospective analysis of an existing cohort study examining how different SARS-CoV-2 variants (wild-type, Alpha, Delta, Gamma, Omicron) influence the risk of developing post COVID-19 condition. It does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This prospective cohort study compared vascular function (arterial elasticity via EndoPAT) between COVID-19 survivors with and without persistent symptoms (PASC) and uninfected controls, stratified by sex. Female PASC patients showed the worst arterial elasticity, suggesting sex modifies COVID-19's effects on vascular function.

This observational study examined whether elevated herpesvirus antibody responses (EBV, CMV, HSV) are associated with symptom occurrence in acute COVID-19 and during 20-month post-COVID follow-up in 96 acute and 62 follow-up participants. High EBV antibodies were significantly associated with fourfold increased odds of fatigue, and high CMV antibodies with threefold increased odds of concentration problems and taste loss during follow-up.

Longitudinal metabolomics study comparing saliva metabolite profiles in COVID-19 patients at acute and post-acute phases to identify biochemical signatures associated with the transition to long COVID-like symptoms. Found distinct metabolite clusters and associations with overweight/obesity, vaccination status, and viral load, but this is observational research without treatment intervention.

This prospective longitudinal cohort study assessed the prevalence and phenotype of persistent long COVID symptoms two years after mild SARS-CoV-2 Delta infection in 1,258 vaccinated adults. The study found that 21.5% of respondents reported persistent symptoms, with female gender, smoking, and acute infection severity as significant risk factors, but did not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Prospective cohort study of 99 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining cardiovascular complications during acute infection (March-April 2021). Study focuses on acute-phase cardiovascular events and mortality during hospitalization, not long COVID sequelae or post-acute interventions.

A single-center observational study of 103 COVID-19 patients (53 severe, 50 mild) that assessed baseline immune dysregulation (T, B, NK cells) and followed up at 54 months to examine associations with late mortality and long-COVID symptoms. The study found that baseline lymphocyte dysregulation predicted increased late mortality but was not associated with long-COVID symptom persistence.

Prospective observational study of 62 hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia patients examining whether rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) predicts long COVID outcomes. Found that hypercoagulable ROTEM at discharge and 1 month post-discharge was associated with persistent symptoms and lung function impairment at 3 months, suggesting coagulation status may predict long COVID sequelae.

A 12-month prospective cohort study of 93 severe COVID-19 survivors examining clinical recovery trajectories and immune reconstitution through structured interviews and peripheral blood analysis. While most patients achieved substantial clinical improvement by 12 months, immune reconstitution lagged behind, with persistent immune dysregulation potentially associated with long COVID manifestations.

This prospective observational study assessed 41 long COVID patients at a dedicated clinic to examine relationships between fatigue severity, cognitive function, and depression using validated scales (FAS, MoCA, PHQ-9). The study found a strong association between severe fatigue and depression but no significant differences in cognitive performance by fatigue level, suggesting all PASC patients warrant routine cognitive screening.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed anonymized data from 192,651 patients in the Barcelona metropolitan area to determine whether chronic antihistamine use is associated with reduced long COVID incidence and thrombotic events. Results showed no long COVID cases among antihistamine users with three infections and significantly fewer thrombotic events in antihistamine users, though the authors note that randomized trials are needed for confirmation.

This cohort study compared post-COVID symptoms six months after hospitalization between BNT162b2-vaccinated and non-vaccinated COVID-19 survivors infected with the Delta variant (n=201). The study found no significant differences in post-COVID symptoms between vaccinated and non-vaccinated groups.

This retrospective cohort study examines factors contributing to chronic kidney disease (CKD) development in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection (March 2020–September 2021). The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications and antibiotic/antiviral treatments during hospitalization, not long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months post-infection.

Observational study examining associations between post-vaccination anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody titers (spike and nucleocapsid) and long COVID symptom severity in 107 patients followed over 17-24 weeks. Found that nucleocapsid antibody levels predicted complete remission but did not evaluate a specific treatment intervention beyond vaccination status.

This study evaluated dysautonomia in 38 children with long COVID, breakthrough infection post-vaccination, or post-vaccination symptoms using active standing tests and cardiac assessments. Eight patients were diagnosed with POTS and nine with inappropriate sinus tachycardia, with both groups successfully treated with omega-3 supplementation and pharmacotherapy.

This cross-sectional study compares lymphocyte subsets in 466 pediatric patients 2-12 months post-COVID-19 infection to pre-pandemic controls, finding dysregulation in CD19+ and CD4+/CD8+ lymphocytes. The paper investigates immune mechanisms underlying post-COVID complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective imaging study comparing COVID-19 sequelae rates and severity in vaccinated vs unvaccinated patients with follow-up CTs at 1, 3, and 6 months. Found that vaccination correlated with reduced sequelae rates and severity, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

A retrospective analysis of 60 long COVID and post-vaccine patients treated with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) at a Tokyo clinic, examining how TMS affects depression, anxiety, and other symptoms. The study found that TMS significantly improved psychiatric and physical symptoms, but the antidepressant effect was reduced in patients with severe fatigue.

This prospective cohort study examines the relationship between anti-spike protein antibody levels and multi-organ long COVID symptom severity in 198 long COVID patients stratified by vaccination status. The study finds that vaccinated patients with higher antibody levels experience fewer multi-organ symptoms, but is a secondary analysis of vaccination outcomes rather than a primary intervention trial.

This multi-center cross-sectional survey investigated long COVID prevalence and risk factors in 5,432 healthcare workers from north-eastern Italy during June-August 2022. The study found 24% prevalence at 30-60 days post-infection and identified hospitalization, early pandemic waves, viral shedding time, female sex, and age >40 years as significant risk factors, with vaccination providing protective effects.

Prospective cohort study of children and adolescents who had Delta-variant SARS-CoV-2 infection, assessing long COVID symptoms at 3 months post-infection and immunogenicity following BNT162b2 vaccination. The study documents long COVID prevalence (31% in children, 60% in adolescents) but focuses on vaccine immunogenicity rather than testing a treatment intervention for long COVID.

This cross-sectional study compared immune responses (antibodies, T cell subsets, viral neutralization) between long COVID patients and fully recovered individuals during the Omicron pandemic. The study found reduced T cell function in long COVID patients in early infection phases and sustained antibody responses with booster vaccinations, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective study analyzed CD8+ T cell responses in 26 severe COVID-19 patients at 1 and 10 months post-infection and compared them to vaccinated controls. The study found that total SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cells were significantly associated with protection against long COVID, suggesting CD8+ T cell response could serve as a biomarker for understanding post-acute sequelae evolution.

This study examines clinical features of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 500 Taiwanese children and investigates associations between vaccination status and symptom persistence. Vaccinated children showed higher odds of certain acute-phase symptoms but lower odds of gastrointestinal symptoms in the post-COVID phase.

A retrospective cohort study examining the relationship between BMI and SARS-CoV-2 infection risk among Italian healthcare workers in pre- and post-vaccination periods. While the paper mentions post-acute COVID-19 symptoms, it focuses on acute infection risk and vaccination response rather than studying long COVID as a persistent condition or testing treatments for long COVID patients.

This study evaluated the effectiveness of BNT162b2 BA.4/5 bivalent COVID-19 vaccine in reducing long COVID symptoms in US adults who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2. While the paper shows vaccination was associated with ~40% lower risk of long COVID at 6 months, it is an observational study comparing vaccinated vs unvaccinated groups, not a treatment intervention trial—vaccination status was not assigned by the study but rather a pre-existing characteristic.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of long COVID in a Barcelona healthcare consortium population (192,651 individuals) in relation to infection count and vaccination status, analyzing data from March 2020 and survey responses from 3,227 respondents. The study reports a 2.4‰ prevalence and identifies associations between reinfection and long COVID, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This study examines asthenic syndrome (fatigue/weakness) in acute ischemic stroke patients with concurrent mild COVID-19 infection versus stroke alone. While COVID-infected stroke patients showed worse asthenia outcomes, the paper is primarily about acute stroke pathophysiology and post-stroke recovery, not long COVID as a persistent condition independent of acute illness.

This observational study examines whether COVID-19 vaccinations received after long COVID onset affect symptom trajectories in two cohorts (128 clinic patients and 484 survey respondents). Most participants reported no symptom change after vaccination; about 20% reported worsening and 19-20% reported improvement.

A multicenter observational study evaluating the efficacy and safety of Aviandr, a new anxiolytic drug, in 170 post-COVID patients with anxiety disorders over 6 weeks of treatment. The drug achieved 72.35% remission rates with a 77.13% reduction in anxiety scores and demonstrated a good safety profile with minimal adverse events.

This study identifies the most pronounced and long-lasting neurological symptoms in the first 6 months after COVID-19 infection and proposes neurocytoprotection as a rehabilitation strategy to prevent neuronal damage and promote neuroregeneration. The focus is on determining a rehabilitation approach for post-COVID neurological symptoms through targeted neuroprotective mechanisms.

Retrospective analysis of coronary artery bypass grafting outcomes in COVID-19 convalescents with coronary heart disease. Study examines immediate surgical results and safety in post-COVID patients with documented long-term cardiovascular complications.

This longitudinal study evaluated the incidence of clinical and neurological alterations in post-COVID-19 patients in primary health care in Brazil, using questionnaires at multiple timepoints. Results showed that individuals experienced concerning sequelae such as fatigue, memory loss, and psychological alterations even 7-30 days after infection.

This cross-sectional study examines the phenotype of arterial hypertension and vibration disease in 289 post-COVID patients, comparing those with occupational vibration exposure to unexposed controls. The study documents cardiovascular changes including uncontrolled hypertension, refractory disease, and echocardiographic abnormalities 12 months post-infection, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is an observational cohort study using electronic health records to identify patient characteristics associated with clinically coded long COVID in England. It does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a secondary analysis of EHR data characterizing who gets diagnosed with long COVID and does not meet the treatment trial inclusion criteria.

A population-based cohort study analyzing the use of long COVID clinical codes across 58 million patient records in English primary care from February 2020 to May 2021. Findings show that long COVID coding was unevenly distributed among practices (23,273 recorded cases) with significant regional and demographic variation, but no treatment intervention was studied.

Prospective follow-up study of 80 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-discharge assessing clinical, radiological, and pulmonary function outcomes. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a descriptive observational study documenting natural recovery patterns and residual abnormalities.

Longitudinal retrospective cohort study following 2,383 adults from a 2021 cohort to assess the longevity of long COVID symptoms over time. Found that 27.3% reported persistent symptoms (fatigue and exercise intolerance most common) after 1+ year, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

Prospective matched cohort study examining the prevalence and prognostic factors for persistent fatigue after COVID-19 in primary care patients during the first pandemic wave. Found that COVID-19 patients had 3.65-fold higher odds of persistent fatigue at 15 months compared to matched controls, with psychosocial vulnerability factors being significant predictors.

This study follows GN patients with acute COVID-19 infection for 6+ months, comparing kidney outcomes between those with and without glomerular disease. The paper focuses on acute-phase and immediate post-infection kidney function recovery, not on long COVID syndrome or treatment interventions.

This retrospective cohort study examines in-hospital cardiovascular outcomes in acute myocardial infarction patients with prior severe COVID-19 hospitalization (≥3 months prior) versus those without prior COVID-19. While it studies post-COVID patients, it focuses on acute cardiac events rather than long COVID syndrome and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

Longitudinal study of 180 COVID-19 survivors followed for two months to identify predictors of pulmonary sequelae using CT imaging. Found that lung involvement >30% and prolonged hospitalization were independent predictors of adverse respiratory outcomes.

Retrospective cohort study following 128 COVID-19 patients discharged from hospital between April 2020 and March 2022 via telephone survey to determine frequency and characteristics of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Found that 38.7% experienced clinical manifestations lasting more than three weeks, with fatigue (50.9%), dyspnea (46.2%), and arthralgia/myalgia (17%) being most common.

Retrospective study of 486 children examining endothelial dysfunction markers (circulating endothelial cells, endothelin-1, nitric oxide metabolites) in children who developed broncho-obstructive syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Findings show significantly elevated endothelial dysfunction markers in post-COVID children with BOS, suggesting endothelial damage plays a critical role in post-COVID respiratory complications.

This retrospective cohort study compares cardiac imaging and biomarkers in 45 patients with chronic ischemic heart disease, stratified by prior COVID-19 infection, assessed 1–3 months post-infection. The study documents post-COVID cardiac progression (left ventricular enlargement, systolic-diastolic dysfunction, increased heart failure signs) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a passive observational comparison of pre- and post-COVID cardiac status.

This case-control study compares plasma hemostasis markers in 85 post-infarction cardiosclerosis patients who had COVID-19 versus 50 controls without COVID-19 infection, assessing blood clotting abnormalities months after infection. The study found persistent hypercoagulation and elevated D-dimer levels up to 12+ months post-COVID-19, with systemic inflammation markers remaining elevated, suggesting long-term thrombogenic changes in post-COVID patients with cardiac disease.

This retrospective cohort study examines neurological and psychiatric diagnoses of COVID-19 in healthcare workers at a Mexican hospital from February 2020 to July 2022, identifying 102 workers with persistent long COVID symptoms. The study is descriptive-epidemiological and does not test any intervention or treatment, making it ineligible for a treatment trial database.

This study examined structural and functional cardiac changes in young adults (18-44 years) following COVID-19 infection using echocardiography over a 12-month follow-up period. Key findings include persistent left ventricular systolic dysfunction in patients with obesity and metabolic disorders, myocardial remodeling 14-18 months post-infection, and increased cardiovascular complications including acute coronary syndrome and atrial fibrillation in ~10-16% of patients.

This retrospective cohort study compares long-term cardiac outcomes in 85 post-infarction cardiosclerosis patients who had COVID-19 versus 50 who did not, followed over 12 months post-infection. The COVID-19 group showed accelerated coronary atherosclerosis (36.4% vs 15.7%), worsened cardiac function markers, and increased rates of acute MI and heart failure progression compared to the non-infected control group.

A retrospective cohort analysis of 22,628 acute COVID-19 patients (including 772 with long COVID) hospitalized 2020-2022, examining age-associated comorbidities and their relationship to disease severity and outcomes. The study characterizes clinical and epidemiological patterns in elderly patients but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examined EEG parameters and central nervous system function in 37 university teachers 8-14 weeks after COVID-19 infection, finding psychoneurological symptoms in 75.6% and significantly reduced work capacity in 45.9% of participants. The study measured objective biomarkers (EEG, visual-motor reaction time) but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study examines CT imaging findings and dyspnea outcomes in 51 patients with extremely severe COVID-19 lung damage (CT-4) assessed 6-12 months post-discharge across different pandemic waves. It is an observational follow-up study describing residual lung changes and respiratory symptoms without testing any intervention or treatment.

A prospective observational study of 172 post-COVID patients tracking asthenic symptoms (fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, autonomic symptoms, sensory disturbances) at 6 and 12 months post-infection. Most symptoms showed significant improvement by month 12, with gait disturbance declining from 54.7% to 24.4%, memory impairment from 66.3% to 33.7%, and attention problems from 27.9% to 17.4%.

Retrospective observational study examining the relationship between SARS-CoV-2 anti-spike antibody titers and post-COVID conditions in recovered individuals. Found that higher antibody titers were associated with increased frequency of depressed mood but no significant difference in other post-COVID symptoms, suggesting distinct pathogenic mechanisms.

This study analyzes COVID-19 disease duration in 2,831 industrial and healthcare workers across 2021-2023, examining relationships between age, occupational physiological load, and infection length. While it identifies post-COVID fatigue as a symptom of post-COVID syndrome, it is a retrospective epidemiological study without any treatment or intervention being tested.

A retrospective observational study of 24 patients with post-COVID pathology syndrome and chronic respiratory insufficiency who underwent personalized exercise reconditioning in an Italian rehabilitation unit. The intervention led to significant improvements in 6-minute walking distance, functional independence, oxygen requirements, and dyspnea scores.

Retrospective cohort comparing long COVID symptom prevalence and presentation between patients infected with the original SARS-CoV-2 strain versus Omicron variant during their respective periods. Patients infected with the original strain had significantly higher long COVID prevalence (28.4%) with respiratory symptoms (cough, chest tightness), while Omicron-infected patients had lower prevalence (5.63%) with fatigue and dyspnea as primary symptoms.

This study evaluates a personalized preconception preparation algorithm for couples planning pregnancy after COVID-19, comparing 21 couples who received the protocol with 21 couples who conceived spontaneously. The intervention includes assessment of inflammatory markers, vitamin/micronutrient supplementation, and timing recommendations, with monitoring of blood coagulation during pregnancy.

Retrospective study evaluating CT findings in 69 post-COVID patients with sinonasal mucormycosis, correlating imaging features with clinical and epidemiological data. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a descriptive imaging and epidemiological analysis of a post-COVID fungal complication.

Retrospective cohort study examining new-onset metabolic disorders (diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia) in 380 COVID-19 patients post-recovery. Identifies age, COVID-19 severity, and inflammatory markers as risk factors but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational study following 55.32% of RT-PCR confirmed COVID-19 cases at a tertiary care hospital in India, characterizing long COVID symptom prevalence and biochemical parameters at 14, 30, 90, and 180 days post-discharge. Study documents fatigue as the most common symptom (48.9%), identifies risk factors (age >50, male sex, comorbidities), and reports abnormal hematologic and hepatic markers in long COVID cases, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational study following 273 children with RT-PCR/RAT confirmed COVID-19 over 3 years (2021-2023) via telephonic questionnaires to identify long-term sequelae. Most children returned to good health; common sequelae included repeated URTI episodes, hair loss, weight changes, and anosmia, with vaccination rates increasing to >90% by 2023.

Retrospective cohort study examining liver blood test abnormalities in 373 COVID-19 patients during acute infection and up to one year post-discharge. Findings show persistent abnormalities in 24% of patients at long-term follow-up, but the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective observational study of 80 COVID-19 survivors assessing pulmonary sequelae at follow-up, with lung function testing and chest imaging. Findings show restrictive abnormalities in 66% of patients and radiological improvement, but this is a passive observational follow-up study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated ophthalmic and ENT manifestations in 106 patients after recovery from COVID-19. The study documents the prevalence of these post-COVID symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 54 COVID-19 patients comparing chest CT scans at baseline and 12-month follow-up to identify risk factors for post-COVID fibrosis development. Found that 63% developed fibrosis, associated with older age, male sex, comorbidities, ICU admission, and elevated inflammatory markers, but this is acute COVID follow-up pulmonary imaging, not long COVID symptom management or treatment.

A prospective observational study following 244 COVID-19 survivors from a tertiary hospital in India to characterize post-COVID complications. Among survivors, 64.8% developed post-COVID complications including fatigue (35.8%), headache (10.5%), body aches (8.9%), and other persistent symptoms.

Retrospective cohort study of 60 post-COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between COVID-19 severity and coronary artery calcium (CAC) scores using CT angiography. Found a strong positive correlation between severe COVID-19 and elevated CAC scores, indicating increased cardiovascular risk in post-COVID patients.

This observational study assessed spirometry findings in 153 post-COVID patients at least 6 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing pulmonary function between those who required oxygen support during acute infection and those who did not. Results showed that patients requiring oxygen support during acute infection had persistent restrictive changes and abnormal pulmonary function tests, while those without oxygen support had better preservation of lung function.

Prospective cohort study following 150 COVID-19 survivors for 6 months to identify post-COVID syndrome (long COVID) characteristics and risk factors. Found significant correlations between hospitalization duration, comorbidities, smoking, and fatigue scores, with vaccination associated with lower symptom severity.

This retrospective cohort study examined radiological changes 6-12 months after COVID-19-associated pneumonia in 227 patients using high-resolution MSCT imaging. The authors found that post-inflammatory lung fibrosis was more frequently detected in patients with initial lung tissue damage affecting 50-75% of the lung compared to those with 0-25% or 25-50% initial damage.

Prospective follow-up study of 100 COVID-19 patients examining CT imaging findings at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to assess persistence of lung parenchymal abnormalities. Found that 49% achieved complete radiological resolution by 6 months, while 29% showed fibrotic changes and 22% showed residual ground glass opacity or interstitial thickening.

This retrospective observational study evaluated immunosuppressive therapy (methylprednisolone and/or mycophenolate mofetil) in 33 post-COVID-19 patients with interstitial lung disease over 6 months. Treatment showed significant improvements in respiratory function (FVC, FEV, DLCO), oxygen saturation, functional capacity (mMRC), and radiologic findings with no serious adverse effects reported.

This study compares CT imaging findings in post-COVID patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms across acute and chronic phases (80-242 days post-infection) to determine whether abnormalities represent residual damage from acute pneumonia or true interstitial lung disease. The findings show that 97% of chronic phase lesions are residua of acute infection with continuous improvement over time, not evidence of post-COVID ILD.

Prospective observational study assessing lung function using spirometry in 50 post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients 12 weeks after hospital discharge. Found restrictive pattern in 43.6%, normal function in 21.8%, and significant associations between age, comorbidities, and abnormal lung function.

This prospective cohort study followed 66 unvaccinated children hospitalized with acute COVID-19 for one year to assess long-term clinical outcomes. The study found high rates of emergency department revisits, readmissions, and mortality, with younger age and longer initial hospital stays as risk factors, but focuses on acute COVID-19 sequelae and comorbidities rather than long COVID syndrome.

A prospective cross-sectional study characterizing post-COVID syndrome complications, symptom prevalence, comorbidities, and impacts on quality of life in a cohort of affected patients. The study found cardiovascular and pulmonary complications were most prevalent, with cough and dyspnea as the most reported symptoms, and identified diabetes and hypertension as the most common comorbidities.

An observational case series of 30 post-COVID patients undergoing medical rehabilitation in the early recovery period (median 15 days post-discharge), with assessment of pulmonary function tests, dyspnea, and quality of life. Medical rehabilitation produced statistically significant improvements in lung function parameters (SVC, FVC, FEV1, DLCO) and reductions in dyspnea and quality-of-life scores.

This retrospective cohort study compares pulmonary function parameters in 64 COVID-19 survivors with chronic lung diseases before and after infection, measuring changes 77 weeks before and 35 weeks after COVID-19. While it documents significant declines in FVC, FEV1, and especially diffusing capacity post-COVID, it is purely observational without any treatment or intervention being tested or evaluated.

A prospective observational cohort study of 121 children with confirmed COVID-19 and 105 controls followed for 12 months to determine post-COVID condition (PCC) prevalence and associations with baseline functional disorders. The study found that PCC symptoms were mild, short-lived, and primarily occurred in children with pre-existing autonomic dysfunction or recurrent respiratory infections, suggesting PCC may be a functional rather than organic disorder in this population.

Retrospective comparative study of 180 post-COVID patients receiving either in-person day-hospital rehabilitation or telerehabilitation between May 2020 and February 2021. Day-hospital treatment showed significantly greater improvements in physical activity (Borg scale: 3.65 vs 1.43, p=0.001), while quality of life improvements were similar between groups (EQ-5, p=0.341), with telerehabilitation offering comparable efficacy without in-person contact.

This prospective cohort study examined the one-minute sit-to-stand test as a diagnostic tool for post COVID-19 condition in 53 patients, finding that lower heart rate response and oxygen saturation during the test were associated with post COVID-19 diagnosis. The study focuses on diagnostic assessment rather than treatment evaluation and does not involve a therapeutic intervention.

This paper examines vascular endothelium function in COPD patients with prior COVID-19 history compared to COPD patients without COVID-19. While it measures post-COVID changes, it is not specifically studying long COVID interventions or treatments, and focuses on COPD as the primary condition rather than long COVID sequelae.

This retrospective study tracked respiratory function changes in 29 patients at 1-4 months and 8-13 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection with lung damage. While it documents persistent dyspnea and small airway dysfunction in some patients, it is a passive observational study with no intervention tested.

This prospective observational study examines vascular endothelial function and arterial stiffness in COPD patients with prior COVID-19 (n=90) versus controls (n=43), comparing measurements at 3 weeks-3 months and 12 months post-infection. The study develops a mathematical model to predict preclinical atherosclerosis risk based on biochemical markers (endothelin-1, homocysteine, inflammatory cytokines) but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study examining whether initial chest imaging findings (Brixia Score and CT Severity Score) predict long COVID development at 6-8 weeks post-treatment in 54 COVID-19 patients. Found strong correlations between both imaging scores and long COVID symptom development (74.1% developed symptoms), but this is a diagnostic/prognostic study, not a treatment intervention trial.

This cross-sectional study compared allergic reactions in 100 patients with long-standing allergic histories, split between those who had COVID-19 (n=50) and those who had not (n=50). The study found increased frequency and severity of allergic reactions in patients post-COVID and assessed patient perceptions of antihistamine and corticosteroid effectiveness.

Retrospective comparative study of 400 patients examining acute and chronic pancreatitis in those with and without prior COVID-19 infection history. Findings show more severe inflammatory markers and aggressive clinical course of pancreatitis in COVID-19 survivors, but this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study evaluated cardiopulmonary symptoms and their predictors in 480 COVID-19 patients 90 days after hospital discharge. Female sex, in-hospital thrombosis, elevated troponin/CRP, and depression were independently associated with post-acute COVID-19 cardiopulmonary symptoms.

This paper describes clinical scenarios and follow-up monitoring protocols for COVID-19 convalescents with long COVID syndrome during the recovery period. It appears to be a protocol or guidance document outlining monitoring frequency and medical assessments rather than reporting results from a completed trial.

This cohort study uses cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to characterize the source of exercise intolerance in post-COVID-19 patients across different illness severities. The study found that peripheral muscle fatigue accounts for 92% of exercise limitations and suggests rehabilitation programs should include aerobic and strengthening components, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining coagulation and inflammatory markers in 20 patients three months after COVID-19 hospitalization and recovery. Found persistent micro- and macro-vascular thrombotic changes and serological abnormalities, suggesting long-term thrombotic risk and need for further investigation of prolonged anticoagulation strategies in post-COVID patients.

This study evaluated blood formula parameters using a non-invasive analyzer in 48 post-COVID patients compared to controls 8-12 weeks after acute infection. It found abnormal biomarker values in COVID patients but no statistically significant differences from controls, and proposes using the analyzer to guide rehabilitation direction without testing an actual intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines vestibular dysfunctions in 82 post-COVID patients with chronic brain ischemia, investigating the role of autonomic dysfunction and cervical spine degeneration. It characterizes clinical features and hemodynamic changes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational cross-sectional study evaluated SARS-CoV-2 spike antibody levels in 100 long COVID patients (81 vaccinated, 19 unvaccinated) at an outpatient clinic. The study found significantly higher antibody levels in the vaccinated cohort (11,356.86 U/mL vs 1,631.94 U/mL), suggesting potential immune differences between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals with long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed pre- and post-COVID cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) data from 43 highly active individuals to assess the impact of COVID-19 on cardiopulmonary function. Results showed minimal post-infection alterations in peak oxygen uptake and ventilatory efficiency, suggesting that high baseline physical activity provides protective benefits against long-term cardiopulmonary sequelae.

This cross-sectional study compared heart rate variability and autonomic nervous system parameters between 50 post-COVID-19 patients (≥6 months post-infection) and controls attending a cardiology clinic. Post-COVID patients showed increased parasympathetic activity but lower overall heart rate variability, suggesting autonomic dysregulation during post-COVID recovery.

An observational cross-sectional study examining the incidence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms in COVID-19 survivors in Padang, Indonesia from January to March 2021. The study found weakness and muscle aches to be the most common long COVID symptoms, with no correlation between clinical complaints and severity or lung function.

This study examines chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) outcomes in patients with a history of COVID-19 who have concomitant hypothyroidism and/or diabetes, comparing surgical treatment results between those with and without endocrine pathology. While it includes post-COVID patients and evaluates treatment, the primary focus is on CRS management in the context of endocrine disorders, not on long COVID as a primary condition.

Retrospective study evaluating a pulmonary rehabilitation program conducted in salt chambers for 591 post-COVID patients over 19 consecutive 3-week treatment stays. The intervention significantly improved chest mobility (4.07 to 5.95 cm, p<0.001) and endurance (79% showed improvement on 2-Minute Step Test), with fatigue being the most common symptom reported.

This prospective observational cohort study examines gastrointestinal manifestations of long COVID in 577 dialysis-dependent patients and kidney transplant recipients followed 3 months post-COVID-19 infection. The study found high prevalence of GI symptoms (anorexia 90.9%, loss of taste 64.4%, abdominal pain 62.5%) in this vulnerable population, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examined post-COVID syndrome symptoms in 97 children in the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic, finding cognitive dysfunction, neuroticism, depression, and emotional instability as the most prevalent symptoms. The study identified gastrointestinal, respiratory, and cardiovascular comorbidities but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cross-sectional study assessing post-COVID sequelae and functional limitations in 1,044 COVID-recovered individuals from a single medical college. Found that 53.4% had functional limitations with fatigue as the major symptom, and recommends early rehabilitation measures.

A retrospective follow-up study of 112 COVID-19 patients assessed persistence of neurological and otolaryngological symptoms two years post-infection, finding neuropsychiatric symptoms more prevalent in women (18.3% vs 5.7% in men) and otolaryngological symptoms largely resolved. While the study is about long COVID sequelae, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention, making it an observational descriptive study rather than a treatment trial.

Mixed retrospective and prospective cohort study assessing post-COVID-19 manifestations in 300 recovered patients over 18 months at a dedicated COVID hospital. Found 92.3% experienced post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, muscle pain, respiratory issues), with increased comorbidity prevalence, but no specific intervention or treatment was tested.

This retrospective cohort study examined 82 hypertension patients before and 6-12 weeks after COVID-19 to characterize how the infection affects hypertension course. The study found that COVID-19 significantly worsened hypertension severity, increased cardiac arrhythmias and heart failure, and decreased kidney function, but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective study examined cardiac ultrasound alterations in COVID-19 pneumonia patients, tracking left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) changes from 3 months to 1 year post-discharge. While it documents long-term cardiac injury following COVID-19, it is observational without testing any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study assessing cardiovascular pathology in 281 post-COVID syndrome patients during early rehabilitation using ECG and echocardiography. Found cardiovascular abnormalities in 90.75% of patients, with significant correlations between functional status decline and cardiac chamber enlargement and reduced ejection fraction.

This prospective observational study characterized the evolution of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 62 patients from Cochabamba, Bolivia, examining symptom persistence, severity, and impact on work performance and quality of life. Symptom persistence was found in 50% of patients and was significantly associated with hospitalization history, moderate baseline symptoms, and decreased quality of life.

Retrospective cohort study using insurance claims data to estimate excess healthcare costs in the 12 months following COVID-19 diagnosis. The study found that COVID-19 cases incurred $41.61-$97.30 more per member per month in healthcare spending compared to matched controls, with the largest increases in outpatient and prescription services.

This retrospective database analysis examines US commercial insurance payments for COVID-19 patients stratified by disease severity and duration, identifying patients with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) as those with symptoms lasting >12 weeks. The study documents that severe/critical cases with PCC incur substantially higher costs (~$95,000 more) than those with shorter disease duration, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective study of 84 women with menstrual cycle disorders following COVID-19, comparing post-acute phase (1-3 months) and long COVID phase (3-6 months). Documents hormone dysregulation and shift from functional to endocrine dysfunction but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational cohort study following 195 COVID-19 survivors for one year to characterize the spectrum of post-COVID syndromes and their frequency. Found post-COVID syndromes in 48.2% of survivors, with most common manifestations being fatigue, fever, myalgia, dyspnea, and persistent cough, alongside multi-system complications including cardiovascular, respiratory, neuropsychiatric, and gastrointestinal involvement.

This study evaluated post-infectious encephalopathy in 92 COVID-19 patients, comparing 54 who underwent second-stage rehabilitation with 38 who refused treatment. Rehabilitation significantly reduced cerebro-asthenic and vestibular ataxia syndromes after 2 weeks, demonstrating effectiveness for managing neurological complications of COVID-19.

This study evaluates rehabilitation therapy outcomes in psoriatic arthritis patients who previously had SARS-CoV-2 infection, measuring inflammatory markers and quality of life scores. While patients experienced improvements post-rehabilitation, the paper focuses on psoriatic arthritis management rather than long COVID symptoms or sequelae.

This case-control study compares oral microbiota composition in 26 post-COVID patients with mouth mucosa diseases (lichen planus, recurrent aphthae) versus 22 controls without COVID history. The post-COVID group showed significantly elevated pathogenic bacteria (S. mutans, S. aureus) and Candida spp., indicating immune dysregulation and oral microbiota imbalance in the post-COVID period.

Retrospective comparative study evaluating the effectiveness of rehabilitation programs for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome across three Russian rehabilitation centers. Developed a logistic regression model predicting rehabilitation effectiveness based on center type and patient characteristics, finding the National Medical Research Center in Moscow had the best outcomes for reducing dyspnea severity.

This study evaluates outpatient rehabilitation outcomes in 72 patients recovering from COVID-19 pneumonia, comparing a comprehensive rehabilitation program (n=37) with standard care (n=35). While the study shows that the enhanced rehabilitation program improved dyspnea, asthenia, and quality of life measures, it focuses on acute post-pneumonia recovery rather than long COVID syndrome.

This nationwide matched cohort study examined the incidence of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus in the post-acute phase of COVID-19 among 348,180 Korean adults. The study found that COVID-19 patients had a 30% increased risk of developing T2DM compared to matched controls, with risk stratified by acute illness severity.

This study evaluates the effectiveness of a medical rehabilitation course delivered in a day hospital setting for 54 post-COVID patients stratified by disease severity (mild, moderate, severe). The rehabilitation program improved functional impairments and disabilities across all severity groups, with most pronounced benefits for exercise tolerance, sleep, cognition, and respiratory function.

This retrospective cohort study followed 54 severe COVID-19 pneumonia patients 24 months post-discharge, assessing pulmonary function (spirometry) and quality of life (SF-36). The study found persistent functional and radiological abnormalities in a significant proportion of patients, demonstrating long-term sequelae but involving no specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective observational study comparing neurological manifestations between acute COVID-19 and long COVID-19 patients versus non-COVID neurologic patients. Primarily a descriptive comparison of symptoms and inflammatory markers without testing any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective case-control study compared heart rate variability (HRV) measurements in 117 post-COVID patients versus 108 matched controls using 24-hour Holter monitoring. Post-COVID patients showed significantly reduced HRV indices (lower SDNN, RMSSD, and frequency-domain measures), indicating autonomic dysfunction with increased cardiovascular risk and partial recovery during sleep.

This retrospective cohort study investigates the incidence of subacute thyroiditis (SAT) in long COVID patients (defined as 3+ months post-COVID) compared to a control group using Korean national health data. The study finds that COVID-19 patients have significantly elevated risk of SAT beyond 6 months (HR 2.30), particularly among hospitalized, female, and younger patients.

This study evaluates the role of TLR4 Asp299Gly genetic polymorphism in post-COVID syndrome severity and rehabilitation outcomes in 92 PCS patients receiving comprehensive rehabilitation (climatotherapy, exercise, massage, respiratory therapy). Results show that TLR4 genotype correlates with clinical symptom severity and rehabilitation effectiveness, with AG heterozygotes showing more pronounced initial symptoms but better rehabilitation response.

This prospective cohort study followed 122 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Iran to identify prognostic factors for imaging resolution at day 60. The study found that age, gender, baseline oxygen saturation, lung involvement percentage, and shortness of breath were predictive of recovery, but it focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization rather than long COVID syndrome.

This retrospective cohort study examined the incidence and risk factors for sarcopenia in 156 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors in Turkey. Female gender, psychiatric illness, and significant weight loss during hospitalization were identified as independent predictors of sarcopenia risk in the post-acute COVID period.

This retrospective cohort study examined 157 acute COVID-19 patients to identify predictors of long-COVID development. Chest CT severity score and age were found to be independently associated with long-COVID risk, suggesting they may help predict future long-COVID occurrence.

Prospective longitudinal observational cohort study following 34 pediatric COVID-19 patients (moderate and severe cases) for ~2 years to evaluate long-term pulmonary function changes using spirometry. Found 24% had abnormal pulmonary functions (predominantly obstructive pattern) but no significant differences between severity groups; 41% had persistent respiratory symptoms but no PFT differences based on symptom presence.

This prospective observational cohort study followed 110 COVID-19 patients for 3 months to identify factors associated with persistent symptoms and long COVID. The study found that 74% of patients had at least one symptom persisting at 3 months, with females showing higher symptom burden and health anxiety scores than males, particularly in those under 50 years old.

This study evaluates pulmonary function in 116 patients three months after hospitalization for COVID-19 pneumonia, comparing outcomes across alpha, delta, and omicron variant periods. The study found abnormal lung diffusion capacity and total lung capacity in a significant percentage of patients, with smoking, age, and female sex as independent predictors of abnormality, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective study of 99 COVID-19 patients examining the correlation between acute illness severity and respiratory function measured 6 months post-discharge. Found that patients requiring oxygen support or mechanical ventilation during acute infection had significantly impaired FVC, FEV1, and DLCO values in the post-infection period.

A Bulgarian cohort study evaluated clinical presentation, autoimmunity profiles, and vitamin D status in 14 post-COVID patients, with 8 receiving supplementation (melatonin, NAC, 5-HTP, vitamin D). Among the 5 patients available for follow-up, 80% reported clinical improvement, though statistical significance was not reached due to small sample size.

This retrospective comparison study examines acute primary angle closure (APAC) in patients who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 within 15 days before APAC onset versus pre-pandemic controls. While the paper identifies potential pathophysiological mechanisms linking acute COVID-19 infection to APAC, it focuses on an acute ocular complication rather than long COVID (persistent post-infection sequelae) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examined changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in COVID-19 survivors at multiple time points (4, 8, and 12 months post-infection) to identify risk factors for eGFR decline. The analysis found that normal pre-COVID eGFR, absence of diabetes, and hospitalization were principal risk factors for post-COVID eGFR reduction, though several factors including Ivermectin treatment and vitamin C were associated with protection.

This prospective study examined cytokine profiles in 79 long COVID patients to understand the immunological basis of diverse PASC symptoms. The authors found that symptom clusters (fatigue, brain fog, chest pain, etc.) were associated with elevated levels of specific cytokines like IL-10, VEGF, and inflammatory markers, suggesting common pathophysiological mechanisms including T-cell recruitment and vascular dysfunction.

Prospective observational cohort study examining postacute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) prevalence and risk factors in 1,615 adults with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, recruited between December 2020 and April 2021. Found 29.8% of respondents reported PASC with neurological/psychological symptoms predominant, and identified lower preceding vaccination and multiple infections as risk factors.

This retrospective cohort study followed 84 hospitalized COVID-19 patients from 7 Korean hospitals with outpatient assessments between January-March 2021 to track residual symptoms and pulmonary recovery. At 6 months post-infection, patients showed persistent chest discomfort (26.7%) and dyspnea (33.3%), with CT imaging demonstrating gradual improvement over time but slower recovery in severe cases.

This retrospective cohort study examines risk factors for postacute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 2,459 patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases using electronic health records. It identifies demographic and clinical factors associated with PASC but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A telephone survey of 680 COVID-19 patients in Korea identified prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), finding that 27.2% developed PCC, with higher risk among those with initial symptoms and prolonged hospitalization. This is an observational epidemiological study that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This paper analyzes longitudinal survey data to examine associations between pre-existing chronic conditions (hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, lung disease) and musculoskeletal post-COVID symptoms in long COVID patients. The study finds that hypertension and multimorbidity are associated with increased odds of developing musculoskeletal post-COVID symptoms.

Prospective multicenter follow-up study of 32 COVID-19 survivors with pulmonary tuberculosis at 3, 12, and 24 months post-discharge. Tracks persistence of sequelae symptoms (cough, fatigue, anxiety, sleep disturbance) and TB recurrence, finding that symptom prevalence decreased over time but anxiety and fatigue persisted.

An observational cross-sectional study of 88 COVID-19 patients assessed 3 months after discharge to characterize respiratory symptoms and pulmonary function abnormalities in long COVID syndrome. The study found high prevalence of respiratory symptoms (73%) and abnormal spirometry (67%), with restrictive patterns being most common, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study examining the prevalence and predictors of fatigue in 299 COVID-19 patients at 1 month and 12 months post-infection. Identified sedentary lifestyle, functional limitation, and dyspnea as significant risk factors for persistent fatigue at 12 months.

Prospective cohort study of 290 COVID-19 patients followed for up to 24 months post-infection to characterize long COVID prevalence and symptoms. Found 54.5% experienced long COVID within 6 months and 34.6% after 18+ months, with persistent radiological abnormalities and psychiatric complications, but did not test any specific treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study examining long-term pulmonary function, functional capacity, and muscle strength in 22 severe-to-critical COVID-19 survivors compared to healthy controls at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge. Findings show impaired pulmonary function and respiratory muscle strength in COVID-19 survivors with some recovery at 3-6 months, but no specific intervention or treatment is tested.

Descriptive longitudinal study assessing prevalence of persistent musculoskeletal symptoms (myalgia and arthralgia) six weeks post-COVID-19 in 333 Sri Lankan patients. Found 28.8% had persistent symptoms and 4.8% were confirmed with rheumatoid arthritis.

This study analyzes frailty development in severe COVID-19 survivors during acute hospitalization using data from a retrospective cohort of 669 ICU patients. While it describes clinical outcomes in acute-phase survivors, it does not focus on long COVID (persistent post-acute sequelae weeks/months after infection) or evaluate any treatment interventions.

summary: This paper presents trends in long COVID patients treated at a Kampo (traditional Japanese herbal) medicine outpatient clinic. It documents early cases and the characteristics of patients seeking Kampo-based treatment for long COVID sequelae.

Retrospective cohort study of 91 post-COVID-19 organizing pneumonia patients comparing early vs late steroid initiation timing. Early treatment (within 18.4 days) was associated with shorter steroid duration (43.1 vs 59.1 days) and lower dosage (0.5 vs 0.8 mg/kg/day).

A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between brain fog and symptom severity in 83 COVID-19 survivors with a minimum 7-month follow-up. The study found that symptom severity was significantly associated with concentration impairment and brain fog, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study comparing outcomes of a tailored multidisciplinary rehabilitation program (aquatic exercises, respiratory/motor exercises, neuropsychology, LASER, magnetotherapy) versus three alternative treatments (eastern medicine, balneotherapy, home exercise) in 113 long COVID patients followed for 6 months post-treatment. The experimental group showed significantly lower rates of hospitalization and need for additional care, with 85.7% relative risk reduction in hospital admissions compared to the standard rehabilitation group.

This observational study followed 60 COVID-19 patients at 4 and 12 months post-infection to identify immunological mediators associated with long-term pulmonary dysfunction. The researchers found that CXCL-9 was significantly elevated in 14 patients with persistent pulmonary dysfunction, and identified signaling pathways linked to cardiac dysfunction and impaired immune response.

A retrospective cohort study examining mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, insomnia, cognitive impairment) and quality of life among 1,596 COVID-19 survivors in northern Vietnam. The study identifies post-COVID syndrome and stigmatization as primary factors associated with worse mental health and quality of life outcomes, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study evaluated the reconfiguration of an Italian respiratory rehabilitation network during the COVID-19 pandemic, comparing admissions and outcomes from 2020-2021 to the pre-pandemic period (2019-2020). Among 2,089 admitted patients, 265 (12.62%) had post-COVID respiratory sequelae and received inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation, showing similar improvements in dyspnea and effort tolerance despite higher baseline disability and changes in discharge destinations.

This retrospective cohort study followed COVID-19 patients who required high-flow oxygen during acute hospitalization, evaluating long-term pulmonary sequelae over one year post-discharge through imaging, spirometry, and quality-of-life assessment. The study documents the burden of post-COVID pulmonary complications (dyspnea, DLCO alterations, radiological changes) but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

A retrospective case series evaluating systemic corticosteroid (deflazacort) treatment in 24 long-COVID patients with abnormal CT and hypoxia over 3 months. Treatment led to significant improvements in breathlessness, cough, MMRC grade, and chest imaging findings.

This observational study assessed sit-to-stand test performance and handgrip strength in 622 Brazilian patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome at the start of rehabilitation. The study found sex and age differences in physical function but identified no significant correlation with time since COVID-19 diagnosis and did not involve testing a specific intervention.

Retrospective study of 83 patients with post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications, describing the prevalence and types of respiratory sequelae including organizing pneumonia, fibrosis, and infections. The study documents complications and outcomes but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

A retrospective observational cohort study examining lung function, imaging findings, and clinical characteristics in patients with persistent dyspnea following COVID-19. The study found significant associations between abnormal CT imaging, reduced lung function parameters, and clinical variables including BMI, hospitalization history, and diabetes.

Prospective cohort study of 42 COVID-19 patients with interstitial pneumonia followed for up to 36 months post-discharge to evaluate evolution into fibrotic lung disease. Found 83.3% had residual parenchymal lung disease at 36 months, with severity correlating to initial pneumonia severity and persistent functional impairment in respiratory capacity.

A retrospective observational study of 90 post-COVID patients examined radiological lung abnormalities and evaluated the effect of off-label antifibrotic therapy (pirfenidone) over 6 months. Antifibrotic treatment showed only modest effects on post-COVID lung pathology, with one-third of patients developing persistent reticulations.

Retrospective study comparing outcomes of pulmonary rehabilitation in 96 severe COVID-19 survivors stratified by vaccination status (46 vaccinated, 50 unvaccinated).
