Both groups showed significant improvements in disability and physical performance measures, with vaccination status not influencing rehabilitation outcomes.

Prospective observational study comparing health outcomes across multiple domains in 158 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID syndrome, stratified by hospitalization status. Found significant impairments in dyspnea, fatigue, strength, and quality of life at 1-month follow-up, with greater radiological disease progression and functional limitations in previously hospitalized patients.

This study assessed psychological outcomes in 261 patients recovered from hospitalization for acute COVID-19 within two months of discharge, measuring anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress symptoms. High prevalence of psychological symptoms was found (28% anxiety, 17% depression, 36.4% PTSD), with few patients receiving psychological support despite identified mental health needs.

A prospective follow-up study of 13 COVID-19 hospitalized patients examined the persistence of autoantibodies at 3 and 6 months post-infection. The study found that autoantibodies persisted in 9 patients at 6 months, with 2 patients developing new autoimmune markers, suggesting potential long-term autoimmune sequelae of COVID-19.

Prospective observational study following 94 Malaysian COVID-19 survivors with severe or critical infection for 1 year to assess respiratory and functional recovery. Patients showed gradual improvement in dyspnea, cough, fatigue, and functional status over time, with normal spirometry findings increasing from 0% at baseline to 43.8% at 41-48 weeks.

Retrospective observational study evaluating bamlanivimab monotherapy for early COVID-19 treatment in a high-risk population in Umbria, Italy. Results showed a 20% hospitalization rate at 30 days, higher than the phase 2 trial, with worsening of baseline symptoms including asthenia, dyspnea, and new-onset non-restorative sleep, suggesting poor efficacy in preventing acute and post-acute sequelae.

This cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary manifestations in 36 long COVID patients in South Africa using spirometry, 6-minute walk tests, and chest imaging, conducted a median of 2.1 years post-infection. Respiratory abnormalities were documented in 33/36 patients on exercise testing and 7/36 on imaging, with higher prevalence in those with prior severe infection.

A 1-year follow-up observational cohort study of 22 COVID-19 survivors compared with 29 healthy controls using resting-state fMRI to examine brain function changes. The study found altered amplitudes of low-frequency fluctuation in multiple brain regions related to mood and sleep regulation, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study from the Turkish Thoracic Society registry follows 504 COVID-19 patients to identify predictors of long-COVID symptoms at 1 year. It documents symptom prevalence (27.1% with symptoms) and identifies risk factors (COPD, pneumonia, dyspnea severity) but does NOT test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study examining glycaemic control changes in type 2 diabetic patients over 6 months following COVID-19 infection. Found persistent impairment of glycaemic control post-infection despite drug titration, with severity correlating to infection severity.

This cross-sectional study assessed endocrine dysfunction in 83 COVID-19 recovered individuals 8-20 weeks post-infection, stratified by disease severity. The study found that 44.6% had endocrine dysfunction, most commonly thyroid abnormalities (21.6%) and secondary adrenal insufficiency (18.1%), with no association between COVID severity and dysfunction type.

This retrospective and prospective observational study examines new-onset hyperglycemia in 302 COVID-19 patients during acute hospitalization and at 1-year follow-up. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications and metabolic outcomes during active infection, not on long COVID syndrome or post-acute interventions.

A prospective observational study following 150 COVID-19 patients for 1 year post-discharge to estimate the prevalence of post-COVID symptoms at 1, 3, and 12 months and correlate symptoms with infection severity and inflammatory markers. The study found that 67% had symptoms at 1 month declining to 31% at 1 year, with fatigue, breathlessness, and insomnia being most common, with no significant correlation to initial infection severity.

Prospective observational study of 238 post-COVID patients with rhino-orbital cerebral mucormycosis undergoing surgical treatment (functional endoscopic sinus surgery, craniotomies, maxillofacial surgeries, orbital exenteration). Study describes perioperative challenges, clinical characteristics, and outcomes including 3% 15-day mortality rate, with most patients presenting with difficult airways and poor preoperative general condition.

Prospective observational cohort study of 800 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months post-discharge examining blood sugar abnormalities and diabetes outcomes. Study documents prevalence of transient hyperglycemia (43.75%), new-onset diabetes (8.59%), and aggravation of preexisting diabetes (12.75%), finding associations with inflammatory markers and disease severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study of 60 COVID-19-positive individuals followed for 6 months, stratified by presence or absence of loss of smell/taste, to assess incidence of new-onset psychiatric illness. Found psychiatric illness in 26.7% of those with smell/taste loss versus 6.7% without, with a relative risk of 4, suggesting olfactory/gustatory symptoms may be an early marker for neuropsychiatric sequelae.

Prospective observational study following 1,000 COVID-19 patients with lung involvement to assess radiological outcomes at 1-year post-discharge. Of 209 cases with residual lung abnormalities (RLAs), 72.24% showed resolving findings, 19.61% persistent, and 8.13% progressive, with significant associations between RLA severity and baseline clinical parameters.

Descriptive cross-sectional study of 72 long COVID patients at a rural tertiary care center documenting clinical manifestations and symptom burden. No active treatment or intervention was tested; the study passively records existing symptoms and outcomes in a patient cohort without assigning any intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 131 COVID-19 survivors assessed at 6+ months post-infection to determine incidence of glucose intolerance and new-onset diabetes and identify risk factors. Found 39% had dysglycemia, with age, BMI, and comorbidities as significant predictors, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

Longitudinal follow-up study assessing persistent symptoms in healthcare workers who recovered from COVID-19, evaluating symptom prevalence and quality of life impact. Found respiratory and cardiovascular systems most affected, with fatigue and weakness being common manifestations.

Prospective cohort study of 152 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months to characterize long COVID symptoms and identify risk factors. Found neurological, respiratory, and musculoskeletal symptoms most common, with female sex, sedentary lifestyle, high BMI, and comorbidities as significant risk factors.

A retrospective case series evaluating the impact of 6-8 week outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation on 30 moderate-to-severe COVID-19 survivors with long COVID symptoms. The program showed significant improvements in subjective quality of life scores and objective measures including 6-minute walk distance, dyspnea scales, oxygenation, and muscle strength (p<0.001), though spirometry improvements were not statistically significant.

A prospective observational cohort study evaluating pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and health-related quality of life in 85 COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 6 months post-infection. The study found significant reductions in diffusing capacity and exercise capacity at 6 months compared to healthy controls, with substantial impairment in health-related quality of life.

Cross-sectional study evaluating neuropsychiatric manifestations in 106 post-COVID patients presenting to psychiatric and medicine outpatient clinics. Found anxiety disorders, depression, adjustment disorders, fatigue, and myalgia as prevalent late sequelae of COVID infection, with neurological symptoms more common in older patients with comorbidities.

This prospective study assessed the prevalence of major depressive disorder (MDD) among COVID-19 survivors at hospital discharge and 1 month post-discharge using the PHQ-9 questionnaire. While the paper does study mental health outcomes in COVID survivors, it focuses on acute COVID hospitalization effects rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection), and it is an observational study without any treatment intervention.

A prospective observational study following 106 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors for up to 2 years to assess long-term radiological and pulmonary function outcomes. The study found that 22.6% of patients had residual radiological abnormalities including fibrosis, with significant improvements in lung function parameters by 2 years except for exercise tolerance.

This prospective study compared gastrointestinal manifestations in 100 children with confirmed COVID-19 versus 98 with suspected but negative COVID-19 infections, collected from June 2020 to April 2021 with follow-up in August 2024. At 3.9-year median follow-up, the study found no higher incidence of chronic GI symptoms in the post-COVID extended phase, though diarrhea was more common during acute infection in COVID-positive children.

A prospective cohort study evaluating post-COVID sequelae on male reproductive function in 57 male COVID-19 patients, measuring semen parameters and hormone levels at 1 and 3 months post-discharge. The study found significant changes in sperm concentration, motility, and hormone levels correlated with disease severity, but this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed clinical patterns and quality of life impacts in 115 post-COVID patients at 3 months post-infection. The study found dyspnea, fatigue, and muscle/joint pain as most prevalent post-COVID manifestations, with significant quality of life impairment particularly in severe cases.

This case-control study of 669 COVID-19 survivors compared 169 patients with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) to 500 without PACS to identify risk factors and predictive biomarkers. Older age, male sex, smoking, diabetes, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, LDH) were associated with higher PACS risk, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This observational cohort study followed 100 COVID-19 patients for 3 months post-discharge, assessing pulmonary function via spirometry and DLCO testing, along with chest HRCT imaging. The study found significant long-term pulmonary sequelae including restrictive patterns (14.9%), obstructive patterns (17.8%), and combined defects (5.9%), with DLCO abnormalities being the strongest predictor of severe respiratory impairment during recovery.

Prospective cohort study following 137 COVID-19 survivors for 6 months to assess immune responses, laboratory markers, and CT imaging changes. Found gradual improvement in inflammatory markers and CT abnormalities over follow-up but no intervention was tested.

This prospective cohort study followed 35 ESRD patients on maintenance hemodialysis for 12 months after COVID-19 infection to assess long-term thrombotic and neuropsychiatric complications. The study found elevated D-dimer levels, high vascular access thrombosis incidence (25.7%), and very high prevalence of depression (94.3%) and anxiety (85.7%) symptoms in post-COVID ESRD patients.

Prospective observational cohort study examining associations between baseline mental health status and illness trajectory in 152 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors. Found that moderate-severe anxiety/depression symptoms were associated with myocarditis, worse quality of life, and lower physical function at ~14-month follow-up.

This retrospective cohort study examined 76 male COVID-19 patients to assess the relationship between acute COVID-19 severity and erectile dysfunction at 1 and 3 months post-discharge. The study found a statistically significant correlation between COVID-19 severity and both erectile dysfunction scores and testosterone levels, suggesting COVID-19 infection has a measurable effect on male sexual function.

This prospective cross-sectional study examined 146 post-COVID patients 30 days after acute infection to investigate associations between inflammatory markers (D-dimer, CRP) and pericardial effusion. The study found that D-dimer and CRP levels correlated with pericardial effusion presence, suggesting inflammatory mechanisms may explain cardiovascular complications in post-COVID syndrome.

Retrospective analysis of foetomaternal outcomes in pregnant women with acute COVID-19 who underwent caesarean section between April-June 2021. While some patients experienced post-discharge fatigue and myalgia, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 complications during pregnancy and does not address long COVID or test any treatments.

Single-center prospective observational study of 1,954 COVID-19 survivors followed up at 1 year post-recovery to assess musculoskeletal symptoms and functional status. Found 55.6% had MSK symptoms (most commonly fatigue, myalgia, backache, joint pain), with symptomatic COVID-19 patients showing higher incidence and greater functional limitations than non-MSK group.

This retrospective cohort study identifies risk factors for persistent diffuse parenchymal lung abnormalities in patients recovering from severe COVID-19 pneumonia. The study found that longer hospital stay was the only independent predictor of lung abnormalities at 6 months, and elevated baseline TGF-β levels were associated with persistent disease.

Retrospective cross-sectional study following 132 hospitalized mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients to characterize post-COVID symptoms and recovery times. Found that 80.35% experienced post-acute symptoms (cough, breathlessness, fatigue predominant), with delayed recovery associated with older age, female gender, and moderate disease severity.

Prospective observational study of 1,000 acute COVID-19 pneumonia patients examining ferritin as a biomarker for disease severity and lung fibrosis prediction during hospitalization. While the abstract mentions "long-term effects on lung functions" and post-COVID lung fibrosis, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 pneumonia management and severity assessment, not on long COVID patients or interventions.

A retrospective cohort study analyzing risk factors for development of pulmonary fibrosis in post-COVID-19 patients using baseline and follow-up CT imaging over 3-6 months. The study identified old age, smoking, comorbidities, low oxygen saturation, prolonged hospitalization, lymphopenia, and disease severity as independent risk factors for fibrosis development, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational study assessing pulmonary function tests (spirometry and DLco) in 96 COVID-19 survivors at 6-month follow-up. Most survivors had normal lung function, but 33.3% showed reduced DLco and restrictive patterns correlated with initial disease severity.

This prospective observational study of 1000 acute COVID-19 patients monitors serial IL-6 levels during hospitalization to predict disease severity and lung fibrosis outcomes. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 pneumonia and IL-6 monitoring during active infection, not on long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

This prospective observational study compared chronic airway obstruction profiles in 164 patients with and without prior COVID-19 history. While radiological findings differed significantly between groups, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention and primarily characterizes airway disease rather than long COVID-specific sequelae.

Prospective observational study of 493 post-COVID-19 patients followed between August 2022 and February 2024 to investigate cardiopulmonary complications. Found respiratory complications in 58.42% of patients (mainly ground-glass appearance and interstitial thickening), pulmonary fibrosis in 52.56%, and cardiovascular complications in 32%, with prolonged hospitalization and elevated inflammatory markers as key risk factors.

Prospective observational cohort study following 322 COVID-19 patients for 6 months to characterize long COVID pulmonary complications. Found that severe/critical cases developed restrictive lung impairment, lung fibrosis (22%), and secondary infections, while mild/moderate cases showed recovery.

This cross-sectional study evaluates pulmonary pulse transit time (pPTT) as a diagnostic tool for detecting long-term pulmonary dysfunction in COVID-19 survivors by comparing 102 post-COVID patients (≥1 year post-hospitalization) with 100 healthy controls. The study finds correlations between pPTT and various pulmonary and cardiac measures, suggesting pPTT may be useful for early prediction of pulmonary dysfunction in COVID-19 survivors, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This prospective cohort study followed 349 COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in 2022-2023, assessing musculoskeletal symptoms (myalgia, arthralgia, back pain, fatigue) at 1 and 3 months post-discharge. While 20.1% experienced musculoskeletal pain or fatigue during follow-up with symptoms gradually decreasing over time, no specific treatment intervention was tested; the paper recommends physiotherapy and patient education as potential improvements.

A follow-up comparative study evaluating the effect of an 8-week selective yoga regime on pulmonary function recovery in 82 COVID-19 survivors with deranged lung function. The intervention showed significant improvements in most spirometry parameters after the yoga rehabilitation program.

This cross-sectional study evaluated endocrine function abnormalities in 83 COVID-19-recovered individuals (8-20 weeks post-recovery) across hypothalamic-pituitary axes. Fifty-three percent had endocrine dysfunction, with pituitary axis dysfunction (33.7%), thyroid abnormalities (30.1%), and gonadal dysfunction being most common.

Prospective multicentric study of 600 post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients assessing pulmonary function at 12 weeks post-discharge via spirometry. Found 77.5% had abnormal lung function with restrictive pattern predominant; CT severity, age, gender, and timing of ventilatory support were significant factors.

Observational study assessing clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, and radiological changes in 75 post-COVID-19 patients with respiratory symptoms 4 weeks to 2 years after acute infection. Study documents high prevalence of restrictive lung patterns, abnormal DLCO, and CT findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study followed 86 patients with diabetic-range hyperglycemia first detected during acute COVID-19 hospitalization to determine if they developed persistent diabetes. Most patients (73.3%) returned to normoglycemic state post-discharge, but 11.6% developed new-onset diabetes and 15.1% developed pre-diabetes.

This prospective study compared breakthrough COVID-19 infections in vaccinated healthcare workers (n=401) with unvaccinated cases (n=390) over 78 weeks, finding 5.62% breakthrough incidence with 43.3% asymptomatic cases. The study demonstrates that vaccination reduced post-COVID-19 syndrome incidence from 57.2% in unvaccinated to 17.45% in vaccinated individuals, but does not evaluate any active treatment intervention.

This prospective observational study assessed sleep patterns and quality of life in 212 non-hospitalized adults 24 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found that 17% experienced sleep impairment and all dimensions of quality of life were adversely affected, with demographic and clinical factors influencing outcomes.

Retrospective study analyzing clinical, biochemical, and radiological profiles of 514 COVID-19 patients admitted across three pandemic waves at a dedicated COVID hospital in India, examining mortality predictors and outcomes in relation to COVAXIN vaccination status. While long COVID is mentioned as a clinical entity observed during the study period, this is primarily an analysis of acute COVID-19 hospitalization data and vaccination outcomes rather than a treatment intervention study for long COVID patients.

A prospective cohort study of 154 COVID-19 patients with minimal symptoms followed for 3 months after discharge from CFLTCs in Kerala, India. Found that 11.7% reported post-COVID symptoms at 3 months, with fatigue, headache, and myalgia predominating; fatigue, cough, breathlessness at admission, and household COVID exposure were significant risk factors.

Prospective observational study evaluating pulmonary function in 52 COVID-19 survivors at 3-6 months post-discharge, stratified by initial disease severity. Found restrictive patterns in 20.8% of patients with worse outcomes in those requiring oxygen support, particularly elderly patients.

Retrospective observational study of 71 long COVID patients receiving supervised pulmonary rehabilitation therapy over 3 weeks. Intervention resulted in significant improvements in oxygen saturation, dyspnea scale, cough score, six-minute walk distance, and normalization of inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, D-dimer) in 86% of patients.

This observational study explores correlations between psychological distress and the development of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and depression in COVID-19 patients during the follow-up period post-infection. The research investigates gut-brain interactions, COVID-19-related intestinal damage, and psychological factors as potential contributors to long-term gastrointestinal complications.

Retrospective observational study examining clinical presentations and outcomes of COVID-19 across three waves in India, with brief mention of long COVID symptoms (fatigue, cough, dyspnea, fibrosis) in recovered cases. Does not evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID—only describes symptom presentation and imaging findings.

This prospective study examines the impact of COVID-19 treatment protocols (particularly dexamethasone) on periodontal status in 103 hospitalized COVID-19 patients. While it follows patients post-infection and shows worsening periodontal disease at 6-month follow-up, the paper is about COVID-19's effects on oral health in recovered patients, not long COVID syndrome itself, and does not evaluate a specific treatment for long COVID.

A prospective cohort study following 248 post-COVID patients in Central India for 12 weeks to document persistent symptoms and their duration after discharge. The study found that 54.7% of participants had persistent symptoms at 12 weeks, with weakness (25.4%), body aches (16.1%), and taste loss (10.5%) being the most common, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Retrospective cohort study examining the frequency of musculoskeletal complaints in 100 long COVID patients. Found 27% had orthopedic impairments, with higher prevalence in younger, obese, and diabetic patients.

Prospective observational cohort study of 152 COVID-19 patients followed for 6 months to identify new-onset diabetes mellitus and associated risk factors. Found 25% developed new-onset diabetes with significant associations to comorbidities, sedentary lifestyle, tobacco use, and symptomatic COVID presentation.

The Isfahan COVID Cohort is a 5-year prospective multicentric study following 5,800 COVID-19 patients to investigate long-term consequences and persistent symptoms. At 1-year follow-up, 60% of 819 hospitalized patients reported persistent symptoms (primarily joint pain/myalgia and cough/dyspnea), with incident hypertension, diabetes, and coronary heart disease as the most common new conditions.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiopulmonary fitness (VO2 max) and heart rate variability in 35 young adults before and after COVID-19 infection. While the paper measures post-COVID changes in fitness markers, it does not study a treatment intervention and focuses on fitness impacts during confinement rather than long COVID syndrome specifically.

Prospective observational study evaluating cognitive impairment in 120 post-COVID-19 patients using standardized neuropsychological tests (MoCA, TMT, Digit Span) compared to 60 matched controls. Found significant cognitive deficits in post-COVID patients affecting attention, processing speed, and working memory, with no intervention or treatment tested.

This retrospective cohort study examined the frequency of musculoskeletal complications in 100 COVID-19 patients, finding that 27% experienced orthopedic impairments. The analysis identified obesity and diabetes as significant risk factors for musculoskeletal symptoms in patients with chronic COVID-19 syndrome.

This cross-sectional study of 85 post-COVID patients examined persistent respiratory symptoms and lung function abnormalities using spirometry and clinical assessment. The study found fatigue, breathlessness, and cough were common, with abnormal spirometry in 46% of subjects, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational study followed 231 COVID-19 survivors for up to 2+ years to assess persistent pulmonary symptoms and function impairment. Persistent dyspnea and impaired lung function were common at 2 years, particularly in females and those infected during the delta wave, but no intervention was tested.

Prospective follow-up study of 200 COVID-19 patients in India assessing long-term health effects at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post-recovery. Study documents symptom persistence, recovery trajectories, and complications, with >95% achieving clinico-radiological recovery by one year, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between CT scan severity, pulmonary function, and functional capacity in 53 COVID-19 patients assessed 6 months post-infection. Found significant negative correlations between CT severity and cardiorespiratory endurance, leg strength, and quality of life, suggesting potential benefit of pulmonary rehabilitation programs.

Prospective descriptive study of 72 COVID-19 patients treated with topical intranasal corticosteroids and olfactory training for post-COVID olfactory dysfunction. Most patients (47.22%) recovered within 3 weeks, with intranasal mometasone spray and olfactory training identified as useful treatment options.

A cross-sectional study that followed 1,902-1,464 COVID-19 patients at 3, 6, and 9 months post-infection to assess the prevalence and types of long COVID sequelae. Found post-COVID sequelae in 5.59%-8.81% of patients, with diabetes being the most common persistent condition.

Retrospective cohort study comparing quality of life measures (SF-36) in 125 long COVID patients at two time intervals (3 months and 3-6 months post-infection) from a single COVID-19 follow-up center. The study documents changes in symptoms and QoL but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Longitudinal neuroimaging study comparing brain structural changes in COVID-19 patients with and without sleep disturbances versus healthy controls at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Found persistent alterations in cortical thickness, grey matter volume, and hippocampal structures in COVID-19 patients with sleep disturbances, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining whether chronic kidney disease develops within 6 months post-COVID-19 in 1,008 patients. Found no significant decline in kidney function markers at 6-month follow-up, suggesting kidneys are not at risk for long-term CKD after acute COVID-19.

This prospective observational study compares perioperative outcomes in neurosurgery patients with prior symptomatic versus asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, conducted 7 months post-infection. While it uses long-COVID terminology, it is fundamentally a surgery outcomes study examining acute perioperative complications rather than long COVID treatments or long-term sequelae management.

Descriptive observational study of 165 post-COVID patients at 3 months post-acute infection, characterizing pulmonary and clinical features including dyspnea, fatigue, and radiological abnormalities. Identifies predictors of severe symptoms and exercise desaturation (smoking, obesity, ICU admission, comorbidities) to guide early intervention strategies.

Prospective cohort study assessing pulmonary function in 20 children 7-14 months after COVID-19 infection. Found normal pulmonary function tests across all severity groups, suggesting mild/moderate pediatric COVID-19 does not cause long-term respiratory sequelae.

A prospective observational study following 95 post-COVID-19 patients for 16 weeks to characterize persistent symptoms and new-onset diseases after acute COVID-19 infection. The study found that 51.6% developed post-COVID-19 syndrome, with fatigue, breathlessness, and cough being the most common persistent symptoms, and 25 patients developing new-onset conditions including diabetes, hypertension, and tachycardia.

Retrospective and prospective follow-up study examining prevalence and recovery of olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in COVID-19 patients at 36 weeks post-infection in Singapore. The study assessed symptom recovery through subjective questionnaires and objective smell identification testing, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

An observational cohort study of 24 post-COVID-19 patients with platypnoea-orthodeoxia syndrome who received inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation. All participants achieved resolution of symptoms and good functional independence by hospital discharge.

Prospective observational study of 3,000 COVID-19 patients with lung involvement, following 622 cases with residual lung abnormalities at 1-year post-discharge. Classified radiological phenotypes as resolving (77%), persistent (15%), or progressive (7%), and identified associations with laboratory parameters, comorbidities, and respiratory function.

This nationwide cohort study evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes among COVID-19 survivors who received exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation compared to propensity score-matched controls using real-world data from the TriNetX Research Database. The rehabilitation group showed significantly lower risks of mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction, heart failure, and cardiomyopathy compared to controls.

Retrospective analysis of 87 post-COVID patients presenting to an emergency department, characterizing their comorbidities and clinical features. Study identifies associations between inflammatory markers and acute complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared baseline nailfold capillaroscopy findings between 53 COVID-19 patients who did and did not develop long-COVID syndrome one year after infection. No significant differences in abnormal capillaroscopic findings were detected between groups, suggesting baseline microvasculopathy does not predict long-COVID development.

This study characterizes post-COVID persistent cough in the Omicron era by comparing prospective and retrospective cohorts of post-COVID cough patients with non-COVID chronic cough controls using patient-reported outcomes and clinical assessments. While the longitudinal follow-up shows symptom improvement over time, this is an observational descriptive study without any intervention or treatment assignment, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trial.

This retrospective cohort study examines the long-term risk of ischemic heart disease in adults with asthma following COVID-19 using Korean health insurance claims data. While severe COVID-19 was associated with increased IHD risk, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 sequelae in an asthma population and does not study long COVID or any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining home oxygen prescriptions after acute COVID-19 hospitalization between October 2020-September 2021. While the paper discusses post-hospitalization outcomes, it focuses on acute COVID-19 sequelae (oxygen requirements during recovery from acute illness) rather than long COVID syndrome (symptoms persisting weeks to months after acute infection).

This non-randomized case-control study evaluated the effects of an 8-week supervised rehabilitation program on post-COVID-19 sequelae in 119 patients. Rehabilitation participation was associated with clinically important improvements across multiple outcomes including physical function, fatigue, cognitive impairment, dyspnea, and quality of life, regardless of patient age, sex, or disease severity.

A 6-month follow-up study of UK patients who self-reported loss of smell during the COVID-19 pandemic, documenting recovery trajectories and the development of parosmia. While this confirms long COVID symptoms persist, it is an observational survey without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a clinical trials analysis.

Retrospective cohort study comparing semen analysis and reproductive parameters in 134 infertile men before and 2 years after COVID-19 infection. Found no significant changes in sperm parameters, hormonal levels, or testicular size regardless of infection severity.

This longitudinal cohort study followed 1,468 COVID-19 patients with smell loss over ~200 days to characterize olfactory and gustatory recovery patterns. The study found persistent smell impairment in ~48-60% of participants and emerging parosmia/phantosmia in ~25-47%, but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A prospective observational study evaluating olfactory training as a treatment for persistent post-COVID-19 olfactory loss in 114 participants over 4 months. Among adherent participants, 57% achieved clinically significant improvement in orthonasal olfaction and 56% in retronasal olfaction, with improvement rates substantially higher than in non-adherents.

Prospective cohort study assessing disability in ICU survivors of COVID-19 at 3 and 6 months post-discharge using WHODAS 2.0, comparing invasively ventilated versus non-ventilated patients. Found that 86% of subjects retained some disability at 6 months regardless of ventilation status, with participation domain showing higher disability in ventilated patients.

This prospective cohort study (COVORTS) followed 76 COVID-19 patients with olfactory dysfunction for up to 15 months, measuring quantitative and qualitative olfactory dysfunction using Sniffin' Sticks tests and questionnaires. The study found that olfactory dysfunction remained prevalent (69.1% at 15 months) with low recovery rates, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cohort study examined long-term functional status in older adults (>60 years) hospitalized for acute COVID-19 at two Argentine hospitals, finding that 55% had functional limitations at 2-year follow-up. The study identifies risk factors for poor functional outcomes but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention for long COVID.

This retrospective cohort study analyzed US national claims data to quantify patterns of healthcare utilization up to 360 days after COVID-19 diagnosis in a large insured population. The results show that COVID-related medical visits decline substantially after the first month and continue declining to very low levels throughout the study period.

Prospective observational study tracking 600 COVID-19 survivors at discharge, 1 month, and 6 months to document short-term and long-term symptom outcomes. Found that fatigue, depression, and sleep disturbance are common post-COVID complications that generally improve over time, though some patients experience persistent effects.

This observational cohort study compares two work ability assessment instruments (Work Ability Index vs Work Ability Score) in 384 Spanish workers with persistent COVID-19 across four hospitals. The paper evaluates measurement tools rather than testing an intervention, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

This prospective controlled follow-up study assessed smell and taste dysfunction at six months post-COVID-19 across three severity groups (ICU, ward, home-isolated) and healthy controls using psychophysical testing and self-reported measures. The study found no significant differences in smell/taste recovery, dysfunction prevalence, or olfactory bulb abnormalities between severity groups, suggesting sensory recovery is independent of acute disease severity.

This paper reports a cross-sectional assessment of disability, anxiety, and life impacts in 16 COVID-19 survivors interviewed 6-12 months post-discharge, including aeromedical evacuees. The study found that perception of isolation care experience was associated with long-term consequences, but anxiety and disability scores showed no relationship with each other.

Prospective observational study following 174 older adults (≥65 years) hospitalized for COVID-19 at ~15 months post-discharge to assess cognitive performance and associated risk factors. Found that 44.3% showed reduced cognitive performance, with female sex, lower education, and higher comorbidity burden as independent risk factors, but this is a passive observational follow-up study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Prospective cohort study following 1,371 COVID-19 patients for 12 months to identify predictors of long COVID symptoms. Female sex, non-White race, acute-phase symptom burden, BMI, and reinfection were independent predictors of higher symptom burden in post-COVID syndrome.

Retrospective study describing the frequency and types of post-discharge symptoms in 30 COVID-19 survivors from a Nigerian treatment center, with 56.7% developing features suggestive of post-COVID syndrome. The study characterizes symptom burden (cough, fatigue, dyspnea most common) over a 3-week to 9-month follow-up period but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This observational cohort study compared cardiopulmonary responses to submaximal exercise tests (6MWT and 1-min-STST) in older adults with and without prior COVID-19 at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection. While post-COVID participants showed recovery over time, they did not return to baseline fitness levels of unaffected controls at 12 months.

This prospective cohort study compared maternal and neonatal outcomes in 84 pregnant women with mild COVID-19 and 88 uninfected controls. Women with COVID-19 showed significantly higher rates of fetal growth restriction, premature birth, postpartum depression, and long COVID symptoms (median 60 days duration).

A retrospective cohort study following patients without prior diabetes who developed hyperglycemia during moderate-to-severe COVID-19, evaluating persistent hyperglycemia at 6 months. The study found that 77% of participants continued antidiabetic therapy or had persistent hyperglycemia, associated with higher glucose at presentation, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study examining the relationship between acute-phase inflammatory biomarkers (D-dimer, procalcitonin, CRP, etc.) measured during COVID-19 pneumonia hospitalization and long-term respiratory function outcomes assessed 6 months to 1 year post-discharge. Found that elevated D-dimer and procalcitonin levels during acute infection independently predicted reduced DLCO, TLC, and RV at follow-up, suggesting biomarkers can predict long-term respiratory impairment in post-COVID patients.

Prospective cohort study of 132 COVID-19 survivors assessed 12 weeks post-infection to evaluate persistent symptoms and associated risk factors. Found fatigue in 36% of patients with strong associations to anxiety, depression, and reduced functional capacity, but not to disease severity.

This study assessed geriatric function in 90 long-term care residents before and after acute COVID-19 infection during an outbreak. It documents acute COVID-19 impact on functional decline and mortality risk factors, but does not address long COVID or treatment interventions.

A prospective cohort study comparing lung function and respiratory outcomes in 55 children with prolonged post-COVID respiratory symptoms versus 55 healthy controls, assessed 4+ weeks after infection. Found restrictive breathing patterns and reduced DLCO/6MWT distances in the long COVID group, but most values remained within normal ranges; FeNO was not useful for monitoring.

Retrospective cohort study of 338 Swiss healthcare workers with SARS-CoV-2 infection assessing persistence of symptoms at 3 and 12 months post-infection. Found 26.5% and 13.5% reporting persistent symptoms at 3 and 12 months respectively, with fatigue, anosmia, and weakness most common; older age, depression history, and pre-existing lung disease were associated with symptom persistence.

Prospective bicentric cohort study of 90 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for 1 year post-discharge to assess long COVID prevalence and predictors. Found 70% experienced long COVID symptoms (fatigue, concentration issues, shortness of breath), with severity of initial illness and hospitalization duration as key risk factors.

This cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary function tests (PFT) and thorax CT findings in 86 COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-infection, stratified by normal vs restrictive PFT patterns. The study is descriptive/observational without testing any intervention or treatment, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study followed 1,069 community members and 3,309 healthcare workers in Beijing for five months post-COVID-19 to assess long-term physical and psychological symptoms. The study found that 39.2% of community members and 28.7% of healthcare workers reported persistent symptoms including fatigue, insomnia, cognitive dysfunction, and depression/anxiety, with community members experiencing more severe physical consequences but healthcare workers showing higher rates of psychological symptoms.

Retrospective observational study of 373 patients examining blood biochemistry patterns in long COVID patients stratified by acute COVID-19 severity and post-COVID functional status. Study identifies biochemical markers (transaminases, creatinine, CRP) associated with chronic inflammation in long COVID but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined T cell immunity profiles in 100 post-COVID patients, comparing those with newly diagnosed hyperglycemia (impaired glucose tolerance or type 2 diabetes) to those without metabolic complications. The findings revealed dysregulated T cell subpopulations in post-COVID patients with hyperglycemia, particularly elevated cytotoxic and regulatory T cells, with the most pronounced immune activation in those with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes.

This study measured cytokine and metabolic biomarker levels (IL-6, adiponectin, leptin) in post-COVID patients with metabolic syndrome up to 360 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated groups. The findings show persistent pro-inflammatory changes and elevated leptin in MetS patients post-COVID, with vaccination reducing some inflammatory markers but not eliminating persistent elevation.

Retrospective cohort study of 242 COVID-19 patients examining whether cellular immune dysfunction (reduced lymphocyte proliferation) is associated with post-COVID syndrome development. Found decreased PHA-induced lymphocyte proliferation in post-COVID patients and elevated cyclooxygenase-producing cells potentially contributing to chronic inflammation, but this is an observational biomarker study without any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 41 kidney transplant patients examining changes in renal function during one-year follow-up after COVID-19 hospitalization. Identifies elevated inflammation markers and baseline proteinuria as predictors of post-COVID renal dysfunction, but does not address long COVID syndrome or test any interventions.

This retrospective cohort study examines how the severity of acute COVID-19 infection correlates with the development and severity of post-COVID syndrome manifestations, particularly cardiovascular and endocrine complications. The authors found that patients with more severe acute lung damage (CT3-4) had significantly higher rates of cardiovascular disease exacerbations and glucose metabolism disorders in the post-COVID period, suggesting direct viral and immunological effects on multiorgan pathology.

This study compares cytokine levels in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients with and without post-COVID syndrome history, measuring 17 cytokines at baseline and 28 days post-treatment. The findings show elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1) in post-COVID ACS patients compared to non-COVID ACS controls, with some improvement after standard cardiac intervention.

This case-control study compares cognitive function between 49 long COVID patients and 26 controls using standardized neuropsychological assessments. While it documents that cognitive impairment (particularly attention and verbal fluency deficits) is present in 27% of post-COVID patients, it is a diagnostic/observational study with no treatment or intervention administered to participants.

Observational study examining ocular and vascular pathologies in 49 post-COVID-19 patients to assess viral effects on the central nervous system. No treatment intervention was evaluated; the study was purely diagnostic/observational in nature.

A prospective cohort study examining radiological and functional changes in the cardiovascular and respiratory systems of cancer patients who recovered from COVID-19, comparing 67 post-COVID patients with 63 controls. The study found that 49.2% of post-COVID patients exhibited persistent post-COVID syndrome manifestations, with increased cancer therapy complications, interstitial lung changes, restrictive ventilatory disorders, elevated D-dimer levels, and altered immune markers.

This cross-sectional study compares cardiovascular function in 76 children who experienced mild COVID-19 to 55 children with acute respiratory viral infections, using ECG, echocardiography, and 24-hour monitoring. Children post-COVID showed higher rates of arrhythmias, blood pressure abnormalities, and parasympathetic dysfunction, but this is an observational assessment study with no intervention or treatment being evaluated.

This study compares transient and shear wave elastography techniques for assessing liver stiffness in post-COVID patients versus controls and cardiohepatic syndrome patients. It is a diagnostic imaging validation study with no treatment intervention, only assessment of a diagnostic tool across patient groups.

Descriptive observational study of 115 post-COVID-19 patients assessing prevalence and demographic/clinical factors associated with persistent symptoms. Found 10.4% reported at least one persistent symptom with fatigue being most common (49%), and vaccination status was not significantly associated with symptom prevalence.

This retrospective cohort study followed 104 COVID-19 ICU survivors to identify predictors of post-COVID-19 Syndrome incidence and mortality. ICU length of stay was a significant predictor of PCS (cut-off 8 days, RR 2.5) and mortality, but ventilator duration was not correlated with either outcome.

This retrospective cohort study examined prognostic factors for pulmonary fibrosis persistence in 77 COVID-19 survivors, comparing CT findings and clinical markers 6-8 months post-discharge. The paper characterizes disease outcomes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective observational study followed 73 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over age 65 to assess frailty development as a long-term effect of acute COVID-19 infection. Patients showed a statistically significant 60.3% increase in FRAIL score from hospitalization to 3-month follow-up, indicating increased frailty due to systemic inflammation from COVID-19.

Prospective observational study of 853 COVID-19 survivors in Myanmar examining the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and risk factors for long COVID syndrome. Found 40% prevalence of long COVID with fatigue, insomnia, and palpitation as most common symptoms, but no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

Prospective observational study of 2,707 patients with rheumatic diseases and confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed from August 2020 to June 2023. Found that 18.9% developed long-COVID syndrome, with fibromialgia, acute COVID-19 treatment, and severe acute illness associated with increased risk, while Mestizo ethnicity showed protective effect.

A quasi-experimental longitudinal cohort study evaluating the effects of a 3-month supervised physical exercise program (3 sessions/week) on physical fitness in 20 post-COVID-19 patients. The intervention produced significant improvements in VO2max, maximum strength, endurance strength, and flexibility (p≤0.005), with positive impacts on cardiorespiratory fitness and quality of life.

A prospective cohort study of 260 Iranian COVID-19 pneumonia patients tracked respiratory function via chest CT and spirometry at 3 and 6 months post-discharge. The study documents natural recovery of lung abnormalities over time but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiovascular autonomic regulation in 42 individuals 6+ months post-mild COVID-19 versus 43 pre-pandemic controls, measuring heart rate variability, blood pressure variability, and baroreflex sensitivity at rest and during standing. The COVID-19 group showed subtle persistent alterations in heart rate dynamics during postural challenge, suggesting incomplete autonomic adjustment to physiological stress.

Retrospective observational study of 60 post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis patients followed for 10 weeks at a hospital in Tirana, examining clinical management and outcomes. Found that 25.6% showed significant improvement, 64% slight improvement, and 10.4% no improvement, with elderly patients and those with severe acute phase symptoms at higher risk of moderate-severe sequelae.

Prospective comparative study examining tinnitus development in COVID-19 infected vs uninfected patients and assessing treatment response over 10 weeks using Tinnitus Handicap Inventory scoring. COVID-19 patients showed significantly lower improvement rates (30%) compared to non-COVID patients (51.56%), with vaccination status appearing protective.

This retrospective cohort study examines how COVID-19 infection affects the course of rheumatoid arthritis in 134 patients, comparing outcomes in vaccinated vs. unvaccinated groups. Long COVID symptoms (weakness, memory impairment, reduced work capacity) persisted for ~42 days post-infection, though no RA disease exacerbations were observed in vaccinated patients.

Observational study of 500 post-COVID-19 patients followed for 15 months after hospital discharge to assess prevalence and types of complications. Found 34.6% had complications (weakness, lung problems, psychological difficulties), with higher rates in older patients and males, but no treatment intervention was studied.

A 3-year prospective cohort study of COVID-19 survivors examining the progression and persistence of pulmonary sequelae and radiological lesions over time. The study provides longitudinal data on the natural history of post-COVID-19 syndrome without testing any specific intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining health-related quality of life in 169 non-hospitalized COVID-19 SARI patients one year after discharge using SF-36 questionnaires across age groups. Found significant reductions in all HRQoL domains compared to normative data, with physical and emotional components most affected, but age had minimal impact on severity.

Cross-sectional study examining psychosocial impacts and quality-of-life changes among COVID-19 survivors in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. Study identifies risk factors for poor mental health outcomes including lack of social support and psychiatric care, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective study of 203 COVID-19 patients admitted to ICU during early pandemic, analyzing mortality risk factors and long-term functional outcomes in 22 survivors. Found elevated mortality (81.8%), mechanical ventilation as independent mortality risk factor, and significant deterioration in ADL, nutrition, and frailty scores at 169-day median follow-up.

Prospective study comparing psychological and physical symptoms (hopelessness, fatigue, dyspnea, exercise capacity) in 120 university students before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Found significantly increased hopelessness, fatigue, and dyspnea, and decreased exercise desire in students with SARS-CoV-2 history, attributed to post-COVID syndrome and lockdown-related immobility.

This cross-sectional study examined post-COVID-19 cardiovascular and pulmonary complications in 100 recovered patients in Pakistan using spirometry, echocardiography, biomarkers, and imaging. The study characterized long-term organ dysfunction following COVID-19 but did not test any interventions or treatments.

An observational prospective open-label study evaluating the effect of nutraceutical therapy on 113 patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and post-COVID syndrome. The study assessed outcomes in patients receiving the treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of post-infectious complications in ischemic stroke patients with concurrent COVID-19, examining comorbidity patterns and organizational care improvements. Study focuses on epidemiological relationships rather than testing a specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

A prospective cohort study of 63 patients who recovered from moderate to critical COVID-19, assessing functional outcomes using the Barthel Index at discharge and 1-6 months post-discharge. The study found significant functional decline from pre-morbid status at discharge, with limited follow-up data due to high dropout rates.

Observational study of 157 migraine patients infected with SARS-CoV-2, examining how infection affected headache characteristics and migraine patterns. Found that individuals with worsening post-COVID migraine had more severe baseline migraine, prominent headache during acute phase, and greater disability.

This cross-sectional survey study followed 366 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients 12 months post-diagnosis to assess persistent symptoms and their impact on work ability. The study identified that 47% reported persistent symptoms (primarily olfactory/taste impairment and fatigue) and determined predictors of long-term symptoms, but did not test any treatment or intervention.

Bidirectional observational cohort study of 468 hospitalized COVID-19 patients and healthcare workers followed at 6 and 12 weeks post-discharge to assess prevalence of persistent symptoms. Found 39.7% of patients had residual symptoms (cough, breathlessness, joint pain), with post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis in 21 patients; no treatment intervention was evaluated.

This observational study followed 89 COVID-19 patients discharged from a UK hospital to assess the incidence and risk factors of long COVID at 3, 6, and 9 months post-discharge. The study found that 62% had long COVID at 3 months and 49% at 9 months, with COVID-19 pneumonia identified as the strongest predictor.

This observational study evaluated subclinical left ventricular dysfunction in post-COVID patients with significant pulmonary involvement using echocardiography and spirometry. The study found that nonhospitalized patients had evidence of myocardial dysfunction (lower LVGLS) and higher pulse rate responses compared to hospitalized patients, suggesting cardiac involvement in long COVID despite absence of documented cardiac disease.

Prospective observational study comparing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and complications across COVID-19 variants (alpha, delta, omicron) in 3,840 hospitalized patients followed for 6 months. Found delta variant patients had highest prevalence of post-COVID syndrome (82.38%) with mucormycosis, new-onset diabetes, and pulmonary fibrosis as most common complications.

Retrospective observational study analyzing neurological manifestations in COVID-19 patients during acute infection (Feb-Dec 2020), examining CNS and PNS presentations including stroke, seizure, and encephalopathy. Does not test any intervention or treatment, only characterizes neurological complications during acute infection rather than long COVID management.

This retrospective study examines the effect of acute COVID-19 infection on menstrual cycles in 350 women, finding that 59.1% reported menstrual changes including irregular cycles and altered flow, with most recovering within 1 year. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 infection rather than long COVID sequelae and does not study any treatment intervention.

This prospective observational study followed 50 COVID-19 survivors with serial HRCT chest imaging at baseline and 3-month intervals to track lung changes post-infection. It found that 56% developed post-COVID lung fibrosis, with initial consolidation and older age as risk factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cohort study analyzed occupational therapy utilization in long COVID patients using data from the All of Us research program. The study found that OT is currently used but may be underutilized in long COVID care.

Prospective observational study of 90 COVID-19 patients with persistent respiratory symptoms lasting weeks to months post-infection, characterizing clinical and radiological profiles. Describes symptom prevalence (dyspnea, hypoxia) and CT findings (ground-glass opacities, organizing pneumonia, fibrosis) without testing any intervention.

This historical-cohort study examined the prevalence and medical costs of long-COVID among patients in a large Israeli health provider, comparing healthcare resource utilization and direct healthcare costs before and after COVID-19 infection. The study defined long-COVID cases using physician diagnosis and symptom-based criteria at ≥4 weeks post-infection to assess the economic burden of the condition.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated 59 COVID-19 myocarditis patients with elevated troponin, examining correlations between myocardial injury biomarkers and cardiac function parameters (LVGLS, RVGLS) over 6-month follow-up using cMRI and echocardiography. While confirming associations between troponin elevation and left ventricular strain impairment, the study is observational without any treatment intervention being tested.

Prospective study evaluating the prevalence of dyspeptic symptoms and functional dyspepsia in 320 COVID-19 patients at discharge and 3, 6, and 9 months post-hospitalization using Rome IV criteria. Found that while formal FD criteria were rarely met, persistent GI dyspeptic symptoms occurred in ~20% of patients at 6 and 9 months, suggesting the Rome IV timeframe may underestimate post-COVID dyspepsia.

A retrospective cohort study following 101 hospitalized acute COVID-19 patients for 6 months post-discharge to assess long COVID prevalence and symptom burden. Found 16% developed long COVID symptoms (primarily fatigue and exercise intolerance), but no treatment or intervention was tested—this is purely observational surveillance.

Prospective longitudinal study of 200 COVID-19 patients assessed at 30 and 90 days post-symptom onset to characterize persistent clinical symptoms. Found median 3 persisting symptoms at day 90 (down from 7 at day 30 and 12 at presentation), with persistence hindering routine activities and work capacity.

This study evaluated cardiac function in COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-infection using echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers, comparing them to matched healthy controls. The findings showed no significant differences in ventricular or atrial function between survivors and controls, suggesting uncomplicated recovery.

This study followed 34 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent dyspnea, measuring 6-minute walk distance, spirometry, and lung involvement via CT imaging at 1 and 3 months. Walking distance improved significantly by month 3, particularly in patients with less lung involvement, but spirometry values showed no significant changes across radiological groups.

Prospective observational cohort study of 406 hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to describe mid- to long-term clinical consequences. Found persistent symptoms in 39% with chest pain as the most common complaint, with symptom frequency decreasing over 3-6 months; age, comorbidities, and inflammatory markers predicted ongoing cardiovascular symptoms.

Prospective observational study describing the spectrum of clinical symptoms and their persistence in 174 long COVID patients followed from 2020-2024 in Kyrgyzstan. Reports symptom prevalence at 2-year follow-up, including asthenic syndrome, neurological disorders, and respiratory problems, but contains no treatment intervention or control group comparison.

This study used dual-energy CT imaging to examine long-term lung perfusion changes in COVID-19 patients, comparing findings on initial and follow-up scans performed 80-94 days post-infection. While it documents persistent lung perfusion deficits associated with long COVID symptoms, it is an observational imaging study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Observational analysis comparing clinical and radiological manifestations of long COVID across 150 patients stratified by initial COVID-19 severity (mild, moderate, severe). Findings show that patients with severe acute COVID-19 develop more serious long-COVID manifestations including fatigue, respiratory symptoms, and imaging abnormalities.

This retrospective cohort study examines COVID-19 outcomes in 96 patients with amyloid A protein amyloidosis secondary to rheumatic diseases, focusing on hospitalization rates, ICU admission, and mortality. While the paper mentions post-COVID-19 proteinuria progression in some patients, it primarily studies acute COVID-19 outcomes in a specific disease population rather than long COVID syndrome and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey study examined long-term sleep disturbances in 246 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients using the Massachusetts General Brigham Research Patient Data Registry, comparing sleep patterns before and after infection. Results showed significant increases in sleep initiation difficulty (31% to 39%), sleep maintenance problems (43% to 57%), and daytime sleepiness (36% to 58%), with 28% of participants experiencing persistent sleep symptoms beyond 12 months post-infection.

A monocentric observational study of 10 long COVID patients treated with oral L-arginine supplementation for one month, assessing changes in exercise capacity and cardiac function. Treatment with L-arginine 1.66g twice daily was associated with improvements in fatigue and exercise tolerance metrics.

This retrospective cohort study assessed cognitive impairment in 200 patients at 6 and 12 months after moderate COVID-19 with respiratory insufficiency using standardized cognitive tests. The study found persistent cognitive deficits across all participants, with particular vulnerability in memory and speech domains, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study examines immune parameters (leukocyte counts, phagocytic activity, ATP levels) in 70 acute COVID-19 patients and 54 post-acute patients at multiple timepoints up to 90-95 days post-discharge. Findings show persistent proinflammatory changes and reduced phagocytic parameters in the post-acute period, particularly in those with severe initial infection, suggesting prolonged immune dysfunction during post-COVID recovery.

A prospective multicenter observational study aimed at identifying predictors of persistent shortness of breath in post-COVID patients and analyzing their survival outcomes. The abstract is incomplete (cut off mid-sentence), suggesting this may be a protocol or draft rather than a completed study with results.

A single-center cohort study of 83 post-COVID-19 patients examining systemic inflammatory and humoral immune responses across three time windows (1-3, 3-6, and 6-12 months post-infection). The study found persistent IgM positivity in ~25% of patients at all timepoints combined with elevated procalcitonin and IL-10 levels, suggesting ongoing compensated inflammation.

Prospective cohort study examining the correlation between inflammatory biomarkers (Hs-CRP and NLR) and functional capacity (VO2max) in 30 post-COVID-19 patients receiving 6 weeks of supervised cardiopulmonary exercise. NLR was negatively correlated with functional capacity in the moderate-intensity exercise group, suggesting moderate-intensity cardiopulmonary exercise may help accelerate recovery in post-COVID syndrome.

A prospective cohort study examining the prevalence and predictors of post-COVID syndrome in 358 Kyrgyz patients following acute COVID-19 infection. The study characterized the multisystem symptoms and clinical outcomes in this population.

Observational study assessing functional capacity and quality of life in post-COVID-19 patients (1-6 months post-infection) using 6-minute walk test and SF-36 questionnaire across mild, moderate, and severe cases. Found that severe COVID-19 cases had the most reduced functional capacity and quality of life, with progressive decline from mild to severe severity.

This retrospective cohort study compared 58 CKD patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection to 54 uninfected CKD patients over 36 months, finding that COVID-positive patients experienced significantly greater kidney function decline (median eGFR slope −4.0 vs −1.5 ml/min/1.73 m²/year). The study demonstrates that SARS-CoV-2 infection independently increases the risk of rapid CKD progression in patients with pre-existing kidney disease, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Longitudinal observational study evaluating fatigue severity, quality of life, and functional status in post-COVID-19 patients at 2 weeks and 1 year post-discharge. Findings show significant improvement in all metrics over the 1-year follow-up period, with most patients achieving excellent health and no functional limitations.

Retrospective cohort study evaluating physiotherapy-based rehabilitation effects in post-COVID-19 patients, measuring dyspnea, oxygen requirements, and functional independence. Results showed substantial improvements across all outcome measures, with 92.3% of patients reaching room air and 86.7% achieving full activity by program completion.

Descriptive retrospective study of 567 post-COVID-19 patients hospitalized for medical rehabilitation in Romania (April 2020–September 2021), analyzing rehabilitation interventions and outcomes. Most patients received respiratory and physical therapy with ~90% discharged in improved condition, highlighting the multidisciplinary rehabilitation needs of post-COVID patients.

Study of 152 patients with slowly resolving COVID-19 pneumonia (4-12 weeks duration) examining digestive system manifestations and their relationship to pneumonia duration. Diarrhea, flatulence, and altered taste were the most common digestive symptoms, with no significant correlation found between these manifestations and prolonged pneumonia duration.

Prospective longitudinal cohort study of 27 pediatric multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) cases in rural India, with most patients treated with methylprednisolone. Study found favorable treatment response with methylprednisolone monotherapy, and identified serum ferritin as a predictor of prolonged hospitalization and organ impairment as a predictor of inotrope use.

This prospective observational study examines Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in children 1-3 years old following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing 42 post-COVID patients to 32 controls without COVID history. While it documents higher EBV infection rates and clinical symptoms in post-COVID children, it is not a long COVID treatment trial—it is purely an epidemiological/mechanistic study of viral reactivation with no intervention evaluated.

Retrospective analysis of outpatient charts examining the prevalence of chronic noninfectious diseases (digestive, circulatory, neurological) in patients following COVID-19 infection, comparing pre- and post-infection disease frequency. The study documents increased disease prevalence in the post-COVID period, with digestive organ diseases increasing nearly twofold in mild cases and cardiovascular/digestive diseases increasing to ~22% in moderate cases.

A prospective cohort study of 58 COVID-19 patients followed up at 6 and 8 months to assess long-term consequences and functional status. Most patients recovered with residual symptoms (fatigue, memory problems, dyspnea, insomnia), and severe disease and female gender/smoking were significant predictors of post-COVID functional limitation.

This is a peer review report, not a research article. It documents reviewer comments on a study about multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) following COVID-19, not the actual study itself.

This study evaluated the effects of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection on lower urinary tract symptoms in 33 patients with benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH), comparing pre- and post-infection measurements at 1 month. The study found significant increases in urinary symptom scores, PSA levels, and post-void residual urine volume following COVID-19 infection, with post-COVID IPSS being an independent predictor of acute urinary retention.

A cross-sectional study of 200 COVID-19 survivors assessing persistent post-infection symptoms and their relationship with age. The study reports that 99% of patients experienced residual complaints, with cardiac symptoms increasing significantly with age, and recommends complex rehabilitation as part of treatment.

This is a report from the N3C team analyzing medications and treatments commonly used in long-COVID/PASC patients based on claims data, describing cohort definitions and medication usage patterns at the time of PASC diagnosis. It is a secondary analysis/review of existing treatment data rather than a prospective study testing a specific intervention.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study following 53 COVID-19 survivors at 3 and 6 months post-discharge to assess pulmonary function, functional capacity, and health-related quality of life. Nearly half the patients showed persistent pulmonary impairment, primarily restrictive patterns and reduced diffusion capacity, with minimal improvement over the 6-month follow-up period.

This study evaluated the applicability of occupational reinstatement protocols for workers with post-COVID-19 syndrome, assessing 21 workers with persistent symptoms using stress testing and the SEVECO-19 tool. Results showed 56.52% of proposed rehabilitation plans had high applicability, with 100% of workers with mild-to-moderate sequelae successfully returning to work.

A prospective cohort study of 23 Senegalese patients hospitalized with severe COVID-19, followed for 7 months to characterize cardiorespiratory and biological sequelae. At 6 months, patients showed improvement in pulmonary and inflammatory markers but persistent cardiac ischemic changes, anemia, and hypocalcemia, highlighting the need for integrated cardiological follow-up in long COVID management.

A retrospective cohort study of 163 COVID-19 patients hospitalized in northwestern Syria, investigating post-discharge persistent symptoms using a questionnaire-based assessment. Findings showed increased fatigue, joint pain, and cognitive symptoms in the post-COVID period, with re-hospitalized patients experiencing more severe and prolonged symptomatology.

Retrospective cohort study following 400 COVID-19 patients admitted to a Brooklyn VA hospital from March–May 2020 at 30, 60, 90, and 180 days post-discharge via telehealth to track persistent symptoms and outcomes. Most patients had respiratory dysfunction at 30 days post-infection, and at 6 months the majority reported new or ongoing mental/behavioral problems including anxiety, depression, and anxiety disorders, followed by residual respiratory symptoms.

This study analyzes late pulmonary changes and pulmonary embolism (PE) occurrence in patients with post-COVID syndrome through V/Q scans and D-dimer levels from 281 examinations conducted in 2020-2021. The research focuses on diagnostic assessment and complication patterns rather than testing an intervention, making it an observational analysis of post-COVID sequelae.

This case-control study compares lipid profiles and clinical outcomes in 74 chronic heart failure (CHF) patients with prior COVID-19 versus 35 CHF patients without COVID-19 history. The study found significant differences in total cholesterol and modified LDL levels between groups, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study examining persistent clinical laboratory abnormalities (leukocyte counts and formulas) in 30 seafarers 6+ months after COVID-19 infection. Found typical changes including persistent lymphopenia, neutrophilia, and disrupted neutrophil-lymphocyte ratios as biomarkers of post-COVID syndrome.

This cross-sectional study compared exercise capacity, muscle function, balance, and cognitive status in 20 post-COVID-19 patients versus 20 healthy controls. The study found that long COVID patients had significantly reduced exercise capacity, increased fatigue, dyspnea, pain, and movement fear, but preserved muscle strength and cognitive function.

A prospective observational cohort study of 520 COVID-19 patients followed in a pulmonology clinic at three time intervals (0-4 weeks, 4-12 weeks, >12 weeks post-infection) to document long-term respiratory findings and complications. The study found that 96.3-89.8% of patients had persistent symptoms (exertional dyspnea, fatigue, cough) and complications including pulmonary fibrosis increased from 4.7% to 24.4% over the follow-up period.

Retrospective cohort study assessing long COVID-19 symptoms in 300 recovered COVID-19 patients from Nepal, finding 77% prevalence with fatigue, hair loss, and dyspnea as most common symptoms. This is an observational study without any treatment intervention—it passively documents symptom prevalence and associations with demographic variables.

A prospective observational cohort study of 72 COVID-19 patients assessed the frequency of functional gastrointestinal diseases (IBS, functional dyspepsia) at 6 months post-infection, stratified by presence/absence of GI symptoms during acute illness. Patients with acute GI symptoms showed significantly higher rates of post-COVID IBS (29% vs 7%) and concurrent digestive disorders, with diarrhea, abdominal pain, and anosmia as significant risk factors.

Retrospective comparison of liver function in cirrhosis patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection history. Findings show patients with COVID-19 history experienced more severe liver damage and post-COVID syndrome manifestations.

Longitudinal cohort study following 42 low-income adults hospitalized for moderate-severe COVID-19, assessing cognitive and behavioral outcomes at 12-18 and 24-30 months post-discharge. Found significant cognitive improvement over two years but persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms including increased anxiety and depression.

Prospective cohort study following 123 COVID-19 patients for ~2 years to evaluate the incidence and characteristics of chronic daily headache (CDH) as a long COVID symptom. Found 52% experienced persistent headache post-COVID, with 20.3% developing CDH; previous headache and acute-phase severity were risk factors.

A retrospective cohort study of 174 COVID-19 patients from a Taipei hospital integrated clinic followed for 6 months post-isolation, characterizing symptoms and risk factors of post-COVID condition (PCC). The study documents symptom prevalence (39.7% with PCC) and associations with gender, comorbidities, and acute-phase hospitalization, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Longitudinal follow-up study of 173 long COVID patients assessed at ~6 months and 20 months post-infection using validated questionnaires for fatigue, sleepiness, anxiety, depression, and work capacity. Found worsening of neuropsychiatric symptoms and significant reduction in work ability over time, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention tested.

This longitudinal observational study follows 602 long COVID survivors at three timepoints (7, 20, and 25 months post-infection) to assess neuropsychiatric symptoms and work capacity using standardized questionnaires. The study found persistent fatigue, sleepiness, anxiety, and depression symptoms, with reduced work capacity remaining consistent across all timepoints, but represents a secondary analysis from an existing database rather than a primary treatment intervention trial.

A prospective cohort study of 2,535 COVID-19 hospitalized patients followed for one year post-discharge across 16 countries, tracking long COVID symptoms, quality of life, and clinical outcomes. While comprehensive in documenting long COVID burden (56% reported major symptoms at 1 month, 25% at 9-12 months), the study is purely observational with no intervention or treatment evaluation, and therefore does not meet the criteria for inclusion in a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This retrospective cohort study examined biochemical anomalies (electrolytes, enzymes, kidney/liver markers) in 150 acute COVID-19 patients over 44 weeks. While the paper describes long-term biochemical changes, it focuses on acute infection and post-acute sequelae monitoring rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

A longitudinal prospective study evaluating cognitive and neuropsychiatric changes in 58 long COVID patients at baseline and 6-month follow-up using cognitive testing and psychiatric inventories. Cognitive complaints were associated with depression and anxiety but were not predictive of actual cognitive decline, with improvement observed at 6 months.

Retrospective cohort study of 243 patients admitted to Qatar Rehabilitation Institute for inpatient rehabilitation post-COVID-19, assessing functional outcomes using validated instruments (FIM, BBS, DGI, mMRC) at baseline and discharge. IPR resulted in statistically significant improvements across all functional outcome scales, with 98% reduction in respiratory support need and 95% reduction in tracheostomy dependence.

Descriptive cohort study following 500 discharged COVID-19 patients in Sri Lanka to document persistent symptoms at one month post-discharge. Found high prevalence of fatigue (63.6%), breathlessness (32.6%), and musculoskeletal pain, highlighting the need for systematic follow-up care but making no treatment interventions.
