Retrospective cross-sectional study examining the incidence of avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head in 86 patients with COVID-19 history, identifying significant associations with steroid use and specific comorbidities. The study documents a post-COVID complication but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

This pilot study compared functional rehabilitation outcomes in 20 post-COVID-19 stroke patients versus 20 non-COVID stroke patients using a mixed prospective/retrospective design with measures including FIM, ARAT, NIHSS, and PCFS. Both groups showed significant functional improvements with rehabilitation, though non-COVID stroke patients demonstrated larger gains, suggesting that additional COVID-19 complications may impair recovery potential in post-COVID stroke.

A retrospective cohort study of 30 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent dyspnea investigating the relationship between cardiac dysfunction and respiratory symptoms. The study found left ventricular dysfunction in 63.3% of patients and myocardial perfusion defects in 33.3%, suggesting cardiac involvement as a cause of persistent dyspnea in the absence of pulmonary sequelae.

This study compared neurological symptoms and immune parameters in 95 long COVID patients divided by Gam-COVID-Vac vaccination status. Vaccination was associated with statistically significant reductions in headaches, sleep disturbances, and dizziness (p=0.035) and increased B-lymphocyte counts, suggesting immunization may help mitigate CNS symptoms in post-COVID-19 syndrome.

This retrospective cohort study examined the incidence of neurological and psychiatric disorders following COVID-19 diagnosis using electronic health records data from June 2021 to December 2021. The study found that 82% of 200 COVID-19 patients received a neurological or psychiatric diagnosis within six months post-infection.

Retrospective cohort study examining lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in 78 mild COVID-19 patients 1-6 months post-recovery. Found that increased urinary urgency and frequency were common post-COVID sequelae, particularly among diabetic patients, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This follow-up study compares semen parameters in 14 COVID-19 survivors between baseline (6+ months post-infection) and follow-up timepoints to assess long-term effects on male fertility. Results show a significant decrease in semen pH at follow-up (7.9 vs 7.4), but the study is observational without intervention and does not test any treatment.

This prospective cohort study followed 321 kidney transplant recipients for 6 months after COVID-19 infection to assess late renal effects. The study found stable glomerular filtration rates but increased proteinuria prevalence post-infection, with no specific treatment intervention tested.

This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated long-term quality of life and respiratory function in patients with severe COVID-19 at ICU discharge and 12 months post-discharge using the Nottingham Health Profile and Modified Medical Research Council Scale. Although statistically significant improvements were detected at 12 months, patients remained substantially impaired across multiple domains including pain, emotional well-being, sleep, social isolation, and physical activity.

Retrospective observational study comparing healthcare utilization in 132 COVID-19 patients from Brunei's first wave before and after infection, with 12 months of follow-up. Found significantly increased healthcare visits post-COVID (mean 5.0 visits) compared to pre-COVID, but attributed primarily to scheduled post-COVID follow-up visits rather than disease-related complications.

Prospective observational study following 995 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 6, 12, and 18 months post-discharge to estimate long COVID prevalence and identify risk factors. Found >40% had at least one symptom at 18 months, with remdesivir treatment and complete vaccination associated with lower long COVID rates.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated cognitive functions and dementia in 64 COVID-19 survivors two years after hospitalization, finding cognitive impairment in 25% of patients and new-onset dementia in 12.5%. The study identified age, pre-existing neurological comorbidity, and anxiety as independent risk factors for cognitive impairment but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study evaluates the effects of a 3-month supervised physical rehabilitation program (PRP) on muscle strength and exercise capacity in 28 post-COVID-19 patients. Results show significant improvements in peripheral and respiratory muscle strength, cardiorespiratory fitness, and exercise tolerance following the intervention.

Post hoc analysis of 1,500 medical records from a Russian hospital examining neurological manifestations of post-COVID syndrome from July 2020 to February 2022. Identified 455 patients with post-COVID neurological disorders, primarily affecting the central nervous system (91.6%), but this is a passive retrospective chart review with no intervention or treatment being tested.

This prospective observational study assessed the prevalence and types of chronic neuropathic pain in 150 post-COVID patients, comparing mild/moderate versus severe disease groups. The study found that 53.3% of patients experienced neuropathic pain, with significantly higher prevalence (65%) and severity in those who had severe initial COVID-19 infection.

This multi-center retrospective study analyzes cardiovascular sequelae in COVID-19 survivors using electronic health records, echocardiography, electrocardiography, and biomarker analysis across diverse demographics. Findings reveal significant long-term cardiovascular complications including myocardial injury, arrhythmias, and thrombotic events, with greater risk in older adults and those with pre-existing cardiovascular conditions.

This study examines the relationship between lymphocytopenia (low lymphocyte count) and the persistence of long COVID symptoms in recovered COVID-19 patients over a 3-8 month period. It investigates whether lymphocytopenia is associated with increased likelihood of experiencing long COVID symptoms at the 8-month follow-up.

A 1-year retrospective cohort study of 66 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cough who received systematic investigation and treatment at a specialist cough clinic. One-third of patients had persistent cough at 12 months, with airway eosinophilia and abnormal laryngeal sensation identified as key factors associated with cough persistence.

Prospective observational study comparing high-resolution CT chest findings in severe COVID-19 patients from admission to 5-week follow-up, stratified by steroid exposure. While it documents radiological changes in the recovery phase (including persistent bronchiectasis and fibrosis), it is an observational imaging assessment without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Prospective observational study evaluating lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in 85 COVID-19 patients across infection severity groups at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months post-infection. Findings show highest LUTS during acute infection with persistent symptoms in mild cases, though the study is observational without intervention and does not test a treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared reaction time, psychomotor speed, and concentration in 56 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection versus 56 healthy controls. The COVID-19 group showed significantly longer reaction times and reduced psychomotor speed, but this is an observational assessment study without any intervention or treatment provided.

This retrospective cohort study examines acute kidney injury (AKI) in COVID-19 patients during acute infection, identifying hypoalbuminemia as a risk factor for non-recovery. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae.

A retrospective cohort study of 1,534 long COVID patients examining whether antivirals, IL-6 inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, and corticosteroids given during acute COVID-19 reduce subsequent long COVID symptoms. The study found no protective effect of these drug classes in multivariable analyses, though corticosteroids and IL-6 inhibitors showed unexpected negative associations with some symptoms.

This cross-sectional study examines the correlation between spirometry measurements and CT imaging findings in post-COVID-19 patients hospitalized during 2020-2021, assessed one year after infection. The research characterizes pulmonary dysfunction and persistent respiratory symptoms in long COVID survivors, with dyspnea being the most commonly reported symptom.

This retrospective cohort study compared dermatological conditions between COVID-19 patients and non-COVID controls from 2020-2022, finding mostly reduced risk for common skin conditions but increased pallor in COVID-19 patients. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 manifestations within three months of infection, not persistent long COVID sequelae.

Prospective cohort study comparing COVID-19 outcomes, vaccine response, and long COVID incidence between IMID patients and healthy controls during the pandemic. While the paper includes long COVID analysis, it is primarily a secondary analysis of a larger vaccination/immunosuppression study rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This study followed 100 acute COVID-19 patients for 12 months to assess ECG changes during acute infection and arrhythmia incidence in the post-COVID period. While it documents post-COVID arrhythmia outcomes, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is purely observational in nature.

Prospective cohort study following 489 patients for 8 months after mild-to-severe COVID-19 infection to characterize persistent post-COVID syndrome symptoms. Age, BMI, body aches, and fatigue were significant predictors of post-COVID syndrome at 4.3-month median follow-up.

Longitudinal observational study of 2,887 COVID-19 hospitalized patients with follow-up assessments up to 12 months post-discharge, evaluating laboratory and instrumental findings. Study documents persistence of abnormal lab values (C-reactive protein, fibrin degradation fragments, liver enzymes) at long-term follow-up and their association with pulmonary dysfunction, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational study comparing pulmonary function tests (PFT) and lung diffusion capacity in 25 young healthcare workers who recovered from mild COVID-19 within 3 months versus 25 uninfected controls. Found statistically significant decreases in FEV1, FEV1/FVC ratio, and FEF 25-75% in post-COVID group, but most other PFT parameters were normal.

This retrospective cohort study uses electronic health records from 4,437 COVID-19 patients matched with 4,437 controls to examine the incidence of neurological and psychiatric diagnoses over 4 years post-infection. The study is excluded because it is an observational epidemiological study documenting disease prevalence in COVID-19 survivors, not a treatment intervention trial.

Retrospective analysis of 262 emergency department presentations >14 days post-COVID-19 infection, documenting symptom patterns and hospitalization outcomes. Study describes disease burden and clinical evolution rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

Retrospective study characterizing clinical and electrophysiological features of critical illness neuromyopathy in 22 COVID-19 patients admitted to an ICU. Found that electrophysiological severity correlated with functional outcomes (muscle strength and daily living scores) at baseline, 1 month, and 6 months, suggesting early electrophysiological assessment can predict short- to medium-term recovery.

Prospective observational study of 785 post-acute COVID-19 patients examined 4-12 weeks after infection, assessing pulmonary function tests and symptom persistence across disease severity groups. Found dyspnoea, anosmia, and PFT decline correlated with acute disease severity, with females experiencing more persistent symptoms.

This retrospective-prospective study examined thyroid function in 160 post-COVID-19 patients at two, four, and eight weeks post-infection. While the paper documents thyroid dysfunction as a post-COVID complication, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This study analyzed the frequency and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 132 patients with primary Sjögren's syndrome who had acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a mean 137.8-day follow-up. The authors identified risk factors for developing post-COVID-19 syndrome (raised CRP, hydroxychloroquine use, hospitalization) but did not test any intervention or treatment, making it an observational epidemiologic study rather than a treatment trial.

A cross-sectional study of 116 children hospitalized for SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed up to 12 months post-discharge to assess long COVID symptom prevalence and characteristics. Found that 11.2% met chronic/post-COVID definitions, with fatigue and concentration difficulties as the most common ongoing symptoms, more prevalent in older children.

This prospective observational study examines post-COVID-19 psychological symptoms in 619 systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients, comparing 493 COVID-19-infected patients with 126 uninfected controls using standardized assessment tools (VAS, MFI, PHQ-9, PSQI). The study identifies general fatigue and feeling down/hopeless as core symptoms in infected SLE patients, with COVID-19 symptoms like shortness of breath and weakness linked to worse post-COVID mental health outcomes.

This prospective observational study examines early rehabilitation interventions by physical therapists in severe COVID-19 patients requiring mechanical ventilation and their association with post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) physical impairment at one year. Early rehabilitation was significantly associated with reduced PICS physical impairment, but the study focuses on acute COVID-19 ICU outcomes rather than long COVID as a distinct condition.

An observational cross-sectional study assessing the status of ojus (Ayurvedic concept of vital essence) and prakriti (constitutional type) in 71 post-COVID subjects. Results showed significant changes in ojus across different prakriti types, but the study does not evaluate a treatment intervention—it is a descriptive assessment of Ayurvedic constitutional markers.

This retrospective cohort study examines pulmonary fibrotic-like changes on follow-up chest CT scans in 84 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors at 3-6 months post-infection. The study documents radiological sequelae (35% developed fibrotic-like changes) but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study describes neurological sequelae in 50 mild COVID-19 patients at a mean of 99 days post-infection, finding headache and cognitive dysfunction as the most frequent complaints. The study is observational/descriptive with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective observational study examining electromyography and nerve conduction findings in 60 COVID-19 patients with neurological symptoms, mean 76 days post-diagnosis. Found abnormal EMG findings in 75% of patients, including sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy, acute polyneuropathy, myopathy, and entrapment neuropathy; critical illness neuropathy and myopathy were most common in mechanically ventilated patients.

This observational study surveyed 256 COVID-19 hospitalized patients with persistent symptoms to identify risk factors for long COVID development. The study found dyspnea, fatigue, and arthralgia-myalgia as the most common sequelae, with pre-existing lung disease and ICU history identified as independent risk factors, but does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

This cross-sectional study assessed quality of life and its determinants in 173 long COVID patients referred to a pulmonary rehabilitation center, using SF-36 questionnaire and physical/psychological evaluations. The study identified predictors of impaired QoL (low exercise capacity, poor psychosocial status, fatigue, young age, male sex) but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed clinical, functional, and radiological outcomes in 126 COVID-19 survivors at three months post-discharge, examining persisting symptoms and imaging changes. It found that 64.6% of patients had persistent pulmonary pathologies, primarily fibrotic-like changes (44.2%) and ground-glass opacities, with dyspnea being the most common symptom, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This prospective study evaluated 30 long COVID patients undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, measuring changes in dyspnea (MRC scale) and functional independence (FIM). Patients showed positive functional outcomes post-rehabilitation, though some symptoms persisted, suggesting need for continuous monitoring.

Prospective observational study following 1,234 COVID-19 patients in Northern India for a median of 91 days to describe clinical features and risk factors of post-COVID sequelae. Found that 40.1% had persistent symptoms, with myalgia, fatigue, and dyspnea most common; hospitalization, hypothyroidism, and hypoxia during acute illness were identified as risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study of 53 mild COVID-19 patients followed up at 30 days post-discharge to identify clinical predictors of persistent symptoms and symptom phenotypes. Found diarrhea at presentation and longer gap between symptom onset and admission were associated with persistence of symptoms (mainly fatigue, cough, myalgias), but this is a passive observational follow-up without any intervention given.

Observational study comparing respiratory and physical function outcomes 14 days post-discharge between patients with delta VOC versus ancestral SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found residual imaging abnormalities in 56.5% of patients but no significant differences between variant groups.

A retrospective study of 30 sailors with persistent haematological changes after COVID-19, examining WBC count and differential patterns at long-term follow-up. The study documents typical laboratory changes (neutrophilia, lymphopenia, leukopenia patterns) in post-COVID syndrome but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examined 162 COVID-19 patients 6 months post-infection to assess associations between continued angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI) or angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) use and long-term clinical outcomes. ARB users showed significantly lower fatality rates and lower prevalence of in-hospital adverse outcomes, though no intervention was administered—the study passively observed outcomes by medication use status.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 172 patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 at a neurology clinic to assess post-COVID neurological symptoms during the post-infectious phase. Results showed 51.7% reported at least one persistent neurological symptom, with hyposmia/anosmia, chronic fatigue, and dysgeusia being most frequent.

A single-center cross-sectional study of 914 outpatients evaluated cardiovascular symptoms and abnormalities at median 126 days post-COVID-19, comparing patients with different severity of acute infection. The study found associations between initial COVID-19 severity and persistent cardiovascular symptoms (dyspnea, chest pain, fatigue) plus subtle cardiac alterations on follow-up testing.

Prospective follow-up study of 40 COVID-19 patients discharged from rehabilitation to identify predictors of functional recovery at 30 days post-discharge. Functional tests at discharge were the strongest predictors of 6-minute walk distance, while lung ultrasound revealed subclinical damage without clear functional correlation.

This study evaluates the long-term effectiveness of 12-month olfactory training (OT) in 83 patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction following COVID-19 infection. Results show significant improvement in olfactory VAS scores over time, with 50% achieving full recovery and only 1 patient showing no recovery.

This retrospective cohort study tracked the course of fatigue symptoms in 204 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients at multiple timepoints (0-4 weeks, 4-12 weeks, >12 weeks post-infection). The study found that fatigue prevalence peaked at 76.96% within 4 weeks and remained elevated at 66.17% beyond 12 weeks, with female sex and initial symptom severity as significant predictors.

Retrospective observational study examining temporal patterns of neurological manifestations in 905 COVID-19 patients with 6-month follow-up across Pakistani centers. Study describes symptom evolution over time but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examined circulating microRNAs (miR-17-5p, miR-223-3p, miR-146a-5p) targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway in 31 COVID-19-associated ARDS survivors 4 months post-recovery, stratified by radiological outcomes (fully recovered, pulmonary opacities, fibrosis-like lesions). The study found significant differences in miRNA expression patterns across groups, suggesting NLRP3-related miRNAs as potential therapeutic targets for preventing fibrotic progression in long-term pulmonary sequelae.

A prospective longitudinal study characterizing ophthalmological manifestations in 90 COVID-19 recovered patients followed at a national convalescent care clinic from February 2021 to June 2023. The study found that 25.5% of patients presented ocular diseases, with conjunctivitis and dry eye being most common, and noted that some conditions improved over time while others persisted.

Two-center cohort study of 67 COVID-19 ICU survivors assessing long-term cognitive function at 6 months post-admission using standardized neuropsychological tests (RBANS, TMT, IQCODE). Results show significant cognitive impairment in 33% of survivors, with particular deficits in memory and attention compared to age-adjusted population norms.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence and associations of insomnia in 280 long COVID patients at a specialized clinic, finding 50% with significant insomnia at initial visit. The study identified demographic and psychiatric correlates of insomnia severity but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective observational study of 126 long COVID patients in Bangladesh examining outcomes of pulmonary rehabilitation, including center-based and home-based interventions. Results showed significant improvements in respiratory function (FEV1, FVC), pain, fatigue, and activities of daily living, with 92.85% of participants showing substantial improvement.

This retrospective cohort study compares cardiac function and outcomes in 135 chronic ischemic heart disease patients with (n=85) and without (n=50) prior COVID-19 infection, measured 6-12 months post-infection. It documents progression of atherosclerosis, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events in COVID-infected patients, but does not test any treatment or intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compares outcomes in alcoholic liver disease (ALD) patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection using telemedicine follow-up over 12 months. While it examines post-COVID complications in ALD patients, it does not study a specific treatment intervention and focuses on liver disease outcomes rather than long COVID as the primary condition.

Prospective cohort study of 68 chronic pulmonary disease (CPD) patients after acute COVID-19 infection, analyzing disease course and exacerbation patterns over 12 months. Found that 63.2% of patients experienced CPD exacerbations in the first 6 months post-COVID, with most occurring in the first 3 months; most frequent complaints were weakness, cough, and dyspnea during the post-COVID period.

This observational cohort study describes the characteristics, symptoms, and service utilization patterns of 726 people with persistent COVID-19 symptoms presenting to the Alfred Health post-COVID clinic between 2020-2022. The study found that 60% of respondents reported at least one persistent symptom (most commonly cognitive, respiratory, and fatigue symptoms), but does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares gastrointestinal pathology and microbiota composition in 60 relatively healthy post-COVID patients versus 40 controls without COVID-19, all presenting with GI symptoms. The post-COVID group showed significantly higher rates of esophagitis and reduced beneficial bifidobacteria, confirming that SARS-CoV-2 infection causes persistent inflammatory changes in the GI tract weeks to months after acute infection.

A prospective observational cohort study of 89 patients with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 followed over 18 months to characterize respiratory dysfunction and phenotypes of lung diffusing capacity (DLCO) disorders. The study found persistent DLCO reduction in severe COVID-19 patients and identified three distinct phenotypes (perfusion-predominant, ventilation-predominant, and ventilation-perfusion disorder) associated with disease severity and CT imaging patterns, but provided no treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compares postoperative complications in 30 CABG patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus 30 without COVID history. Patients with prior COVID-19 experienced higher rates of bleeding, prolonged extracorporeal circulation, and late complications including cardiac arrhythmias and CHF, suggesting elevated perioperative risk.

Observational study of 27 elite athletes with prior COVID-19 infection who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging a mean of 182 days post-infection, compared to 9 healthy controls. CMR found no acute myocarditis or myocardial damage despite 54% reporting symptoms lasting >4 weeks, though athletes showed enlarged ventricle volumes and increased left ventricular mass compared to controls.

Observational analytical cohort study comparing psychocognitive status in 223 elderly patients with atrial fibrillation and comorbidities, stratified by presence/absence of post-COVID syndrome. Found higher rates of cognitive dysfunction and anxiety-depressive syndrome in patients with post-COVID syndrome compared to controls without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.

This retrospective cohort study examined neuropsychiatric symptoms and psychotropic medication use among nursing home residents with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection (73.9% of 111 participants) compared to uninfected residents at 3-month follow-up. No significant changes in neuropsychiatric symptoms were observed during follow-up, though infected residents had higher psychotropic medication prescriptions, particularly antidepressants and antipsychotics.

Retrospective study examining echocardiographic parameters in COVID-19 patients over a two-year follow-up period, assessing cardiac function recovery. While documenting natural recovery of cardiac measures post-infection, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 194 Iranian COVID-19 patients at six months post-infection using the EQ-5D-3L questionnaire. While it documents significant impairment in HRQoL after acute COVID-19 recovery, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This retrospective and prospective cohort study examines cardiovascular changes in 400 children 24-36 months after COVID-19 infection, identifying persistent ECG abnormalities, rhythm disorders, and BP dysregulation in school-age children. While it demonstrates long-term post-COVID cardiovascular effects, it is an observational study with no treatment intervention tested.

Prospective observational study measuring sexual function in 96 COVID-19 patients using the IIEF questionnaire at 0, 1, 3, and 6 months post-infection. Found temporary sexual dysfunction in the first month that gradually resolved by 6 months, with age and education as confounding factors.

A longitudinal follow-up study of 260 COVID-19 patients assessing cognitive function at 3 months and 1 year post-hospitalization using the blind Montreal Cognitive Assessment. The study found cognitive scores significantly declined over time and identified risk factors including older age, elevated inflammatory markers (CRP), hypertension, and severe pulmonary involvement.

A retrospective study of 400 Iranian COVID-19 recovered patients examining chronic dyspnea prevalence and associated factors. Found 61.8% experienced dyspnea with higher likelihood associated with increased BMI and age, while exercise was protective.

This cross-sectional survey study examined short-term menstrual cycle changes in 268 women following acute COVID-19 infection, comparing outcomes by vaccine type received prior to infection. The study found temporary menstrual disturbances were common but resolved within two cycles, with some differences between vaccine types.

This retrospective cohort study examined long-term pulmonary outcomes in 98 severe COVID-19 survivors at three-month follow-up, stratifying patients by initial CT severity scores. Patients with higher initial lung involvement showed greater reductions in lung function and more severe dyspnea, demonstrating a correlation between acute lung severity and post-COVID respiratory sequelae.

Retrospective cohort study of 1,738 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients followed for a median of 352 days to assess incidence and determinants of long COVID syndrome. Found 87.8% experienced at least one long COVID symptom, with depression (69.1%) and hair loss (23.9%) most common, and identified risk factors including anemia, diabetes, and prior acute infection severity.

Prospective study examining proximal nailfold capillaries via dermoscopy in COVID-19 patients and healthy controls, finding significant microvascular abnormalities in COVID patients. This is an observational study without treatment intervention; it characterizes microvascular changes but does not test any therapeutic intervention.

This observational case-control study compares ovarian reserve (AMH levels) and menstrual cycle characteristics in 50 women with severe COVID-19 versus 53 controls during the post-COVID recovery period in 2022. The study found decreased AMH levels and increased dysmenorrhea severity in severe COVID-19 cases but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational study compared wound healing outcomes in dental extraction wounds between 35 COVID-19 recovered patients and 35 unaffected controls using clinical healing indices and pain scales. Recovered COVID patients showed delayed early-phase healing with bleeding on day 3, suggesting prolonged wound healing as a potential long COVID manifestation in the oral cavity.

This retrospective cross-sectional study examines short- and long-term manifestations of COVID-19 in 295 hospitalized pediatric patients, following them for up to 12 weeks post-infection. Disease severity correlated with pulmonary manifestations and fatigue persisting at long-term follow-up, highlighting the need for targeted monitoring of post-COVID sequelae in high-risk children.

This cross-sectional study evaluated pulmonary gas exchange abnormalities in 33 long COVID patients one year post-severe COVID-19, using combined DLNO and DLCO measurements. The findings demonstrate that gas exchange impairment is primarily driven by vascular component dysfunction rather than alveolar membrane diffusion defects.

This study compares lung microvascular injury (capillary blood volume loss) between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals following paucisymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection using lung function measurements. While it addresses long COVID pathophysiology and vaccine protection, it is observational without treatment assignment and should be excluded as it does not test an intervention given to long COVID patients.

This study compares brain imaging parameters (BOLD and DTI) in long COVID patients with mild vs severe emotional symptoms after multiple infections, assessed 3-6 months post-infection. Results show decreased FA and increased ALFF in specific brain areas associated with transformation from mild to severe emotional problems.

Retrospective cohort study examining factors associated with depression in 510 post-COVID-19 patients using PHQ-9 assessment. Found that female gender, increased symptom count, and specific symptoms like ageusia/anosmia were significantly associated with higher depression risk, but this is an observational study analyzing associations rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

Retrospective descriptive study of persistent COVID-19 symptoms in older adults attending Peruvian senior centers, with telephone follow-up up to four months. Found that only 4.4% of COVID-19 cases in this population had symptoms persisting over three weeks.

This longitudinal study uses pre- and post-pandemic MRI and NIH Toolbox cognitive data from the ABCD Study to compare brain morphometry and cognitive performance in adolescents with and without COVID-19 history. The study observes morphometric abnormalities in COVID-infected youth but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study examined dyssomnia (sleep disorders) in 126 patients across three groups: post-COVID syndrome patients (28), anxious patients with coronaphobia (48), and pre-pandemic neuropsychiatric disorder controls (50). The authors identified high prevalence of dyssomnia in post-COVID patients (88%) and evaluated psychopharmacotherapy approaches to treat sleep disturbances and associated anxiety in the post-COVID population.

Retrospective chart review comparing pneumonia presentations in 141 patients with and without prior COVID-19 history between December 2021 and January 2023. Found no significant differences in clinical, radiologic, or prognostic parameters except elevated LDH in post-COVID group; does not focus on long COVID sequelae or test any intervention.

This paper analyzes hospital discharge data from Chile in 2021 to characterize long COVID patients requiring hospitalization, examining demographics, duration of stay, and regional variation. It is a descriptive epidemiological analysis of secondary administrative data (ICD-10 coded hospital records) with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This study uses 129Xe MRI imaging to monitor longitudinal pulmonary recovery in 13 long-COVID patients over >1 year following infection, measuring ventilation, gas-exchange, exercise tolerance, and quality of life. The paper reports imaging findings and physiological improvements but presents no intervention or treatment—it is a natural history/observational study without a therapeutic component.

Prospective observational study of 300 COVID-19 patients followed for 4 months to identify risk factors for symptom persistence, examining the impact of age, sex, comorbidities, and infection severity. Findings show that severity of acute illness was the most important predictor of symptom persistence, but the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective cohort study of 72 pregnant women with mild COVID-19 infection during pregnancy, followed through delivery and 3 months postpartum. Study focuses on acute COVID-19 outcomes during pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, with long COVID mentioned only as an incidental finding (47.2% frequency) but not as the primary research focus.

Observational cross-sectional survey of 70 hospital workers diagnosed with COVID-19 between March 2020 and March 2023 to determine long COVID incidence and characterize persistent symptoms. Found 9.8% incidence of long COVID with predominantly musculoskeletal (51%), mental health (50%), and otorhinolaryngological (42%) symptoms, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study of 81 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with post-acute syndrome examining cardiac dysfunction via echocardiography at 2 months post-discharge and following cardiovascular adverse events at 3 and 6 months. Found longitudinal strain abnormalities in 22% of patients (LV-GLS 9.87%, RV-FWLS 14.8%) with no major adverse events during follow-up.

A prospective hospital-based cohort study following 264 COVID-19 patients hospitalized during the delta wave for 12-18 months post-discharge to determine long COVID incidence and symptom burden. Found 17% incidence of long COVID, with higher prevalence in women and older individuals, but no interventions were tested.

This prospective case series of 183 COVID-19 patients evaluated a dietary supplement and nutrition protocol designed to boost immune function and prevent long-term post-COVID complications. The protocol resulted in significant reductions in COVID severity scores and reportedly achieved complete recovery within 10-13 days, preventing long-term symptoms.

This retrospective cohort study followed 398 adults in Iraq two years post-COVID-19 to assess long COVID prevalence and risk factors. The study found 85.9% had persistent symptoms, with hospitalization and reinfection increasing risk and vaccination showing no protective effect.

Retrospective study analyzing EMR data from 2017-2023 to compare cough prevalence and types before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic across age groups. Findings show a significant increase in acute cough incidence post-COVID-19, particularly unspecified cough, highlighting long-term respiratory consequences.

This retrospective cohort study examines the relationship between lung damage severity during acute COVID-19 and metabolic biomarkers (tryptophan and TMAO levels) in 30 long COVID patients. The authors find significant associations between severe acute COVID-19 and reduced tryptophan/elevated TMAO in long COVID patients, contributing to understanding of pathogenic mechanisms.

This study compares lung function parameters, specifically diffusion capacity (DLCO), between 99 athletes with post-COVID-19 sequelae and 36 uninfected control athletes. The authors found that 30% of post-COVID athletes had reduced DLCO and significantly lower forced vital capacity and FEV1 compared to controls, with dyspnea during infection associated with lower DLCO values.

A prospective observational study following 60 children after acute COVID-19 to investigate the prevalence, symptoms, duration, and risk factors of long COVID. Found that 31% developed long COVID symptoms (mostly respiratory and neuropsychiatric), which typically resolved within 3 months.

A prospective observational study comparing health-related quality of life and persistent symptoms in 53 pediatric COVID-19 survivors versus 52 controls at median 4.4 months post-infection. While it documents long COVID prevalence (23%) and symptom burden, it does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Study examines clinical and immunological features of herpesvirus nervous system lesions in 96 patients with and without post-COVID syndrome history. Patients with post-COVID showed higher rates of CNS lesions, autonomic dysfunction, and elevated autoantibodies to neuronal proteins, but this is a retrospective comparison study without any treatment intervention.

A longitudinal cohort study of 240 hospitalized COVID-19 pneumonia patients followed for 4 months to assess prevalence of persistent symptoms and CT scan abnormalities (PCA). The study found 75.8% had persistent symptoms at 1 month and 65% had PCA at 4 months, with older age, longer hospital stay, and dyspnea as independent predictive factors for PCA.

Descriptive prospective study assessing physical and psychological symptoms of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 79 Indonesian patients using the C19-YRS screening scale. Found 20.3% had at least one PCS symptom, with shortness of breath and psychological effects like nightmares and PTSD being most common.

Retrospective observational study comparing long COVID patterns between vaccinated (n=913) and unvaccinated (n=4616) hospitalized COVID patients in India across three pandemic waves. Found no significant difference in long COVID incidence or duration between groups, though some symptom type differences existed and comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension) increased symptom risk.

A retrospective and prospective cohort study of 233 Thai children followed for 9 months post-COVID-19 infection to determine long COVID incidence and risk factors. The study found that 35.6% had persistent symptoms at 3 months, decreasing to 10.3% at 6 months, with moderate-severity acute infection identified as an independent risk factor for persistent symptoms.

This cross-sectional study compares symptom profiles across long COVID patients (n=436), functional somatic disorder patients (n=264), and general population controls (n=9,656) using questionnaires. While 11% of long COVID patients exhibited FSD-like symptom profiles and fatigue/muscle pain were common, the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A 9-month prospective follow-up study of 48 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Iran documenting the prevalence of persistent symptoms post-discharge. Findings show 10.4% experienced dyspnea, 6.2% olfactory complications and fatigue, and 10.4% reported new-onset symptoms, predominantly neurological.

A prospective cohort study of 173 kidney transplant recipients who survived acute COVID-19, followed for 24 months to assess long-term effects on graft function and survival. Severe COVID-19 cases showed significant declines in glomerular filtration rate and increased graft loss and mortality compared to mild/moderate cases.

This retrospective study examines pulmonary fibrosis development in 49 hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection (March-September 2020) and explores how environmental factors in Lahore affect post-infection recovery. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization outcomes rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study monitored cardiac haemodynamics in COVID-19 patients with coronary heart disease over 12 months post-hospitalization, measuring ejection fraction, ventricular volume, and inflammatory markers. While demonstrating partial cardiac recovery, the study was observational with no intervention applied, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 2,252 post-COVID-19 patients in Argentina to characterize persistent symptoms and their impact on cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurocognitive function. Fatigue (28.2%), dyspnea (21.8%), and cognitive symptoms (10.2%) were common; however, no significant differences in cardiovascular or respiratory function were found between those with and without post-COVID syndrome, though older patients (>50 years) showed worse neurocognitive performance.

Population-based cohort study of 24 million English adults examining the relationship between COVID-19 and gastrointestinal diseases up to two years post-infection, stratified by vaccination status and severity. Found elevated incidence of gastrointestinal diseases after COVID-19, particularly after hospitalization, with lower rates among vaccinated individuals.

Multicenter Canadian cohort study examining factors associated with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) symptom deterioration following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in 476 patients. Found that 28.8% experienced symptom deterioration after vaccination, with Moderna vaccine and persistent cough as significant risk factors.

An observational cohort study of 33 participants tracked from 2019 to 2023 to investigate the relationship between post-COVID syndrome and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO), examining melatonin dysregulation, inflammatory cytokines, and dysbiosis. The study found that SIBO-positive participants had significantly reduced melatonin levels, elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-12, IL-17), severe dysbiosis, and elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA19.9), suggesting SIBO may represent a pre-cancerous condition in post-COVID patients.

Prospective observational study evaluating 210 post-COVID patients to assess correlations between acute COVID-19 pneumonia and long-term lung injuries using clinical, radiological, and biomarker analyses. Found persistent lung injuries in 32% of cases with elevated biomarkers (KL-6, D-dimer) and decreased lung function, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a prospective cohort study examining neurophysiologic changes in 145 people with post-COVID fatigue over 12-45 months post-infection, measuring cortical excitability, muscle fatigue, and autonomic function. While it identifies accumulating dysfunction in those with persistent symptoms (>200 days), it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—only characterizes the natural progression of the condition.

Observational registry study of 120 children and young adults (ages 7–25) with post-COVID condition that identifies acute-phase risk factors for severe PCC, including ≥12 acute symptoms, female sex, orthostatic intolerance, and trouble concentrating. No intervention or treatment is tested; the study is descriptive/prognostic only, examining predictors of disease severity rather than evaluating a treatment.

Prospective cohort study following 545 PCS patients over 15 months to identify patterns of fatigue change using trajectory analysis. Found six distinct fatigue trajectories, with severe fatigue persisting and moderate fatigue showing improvement over time.

This case-control study compares cellular and humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 and EBV between 27 neuropsychiatric long COVID patients and 27 matched recovered controls at 3-6 months post-symptom onset. The study found no differences in virus-specific T-cell responses but identified diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity as a potential prognostic marker for neuropsychiatric long COVID development, particularly associated with fatigue persistence at 12 months.

All Eyes on PCS is a prospective observational study comparing retinal microvascular structure and function between post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) patients, ME/CFS patients, and healthy controls using retinal vessel analysis. The study found persistent endothelial dysfunction and retinal microvascular alterations in PCS patients that correlate with symptom severity and inflammatory markers, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational cohort study examines associations between oropharyngeal and gut microbiota composition with lung function recovery in 83 ICU patients with severe COVID-19 at 3, 6, and 12 months post-hospitalization. The study identifies distinct microbiota patterns in patients who recovered lung function versus those with persistent impairment, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Retrospective cohort study using TriNetX EHR data comparing cardiovascular, renal, and pulmonary outcomes in 315,612 adults with vs without long COVID, stratified by age and sex. Found long COVID associated with increased risk of adverse CRP outcomes, with higher relative risks in younger adults, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Population-based cohort study examining healthcare resource use and costs attributable to COVID-19 in Ontario, Canada, stratified by social determinants of health. Study documents post-acute phase costs and identifies disparities in burden across marginalized communities, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cohort study using EHR data from 910,393 patients to evaluate whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases risk of new-onset obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) up to 4.5 years post-infection. Found that both hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID+ patients had significantly higher adjusted risk of OSA compared to COVID− controls, with downstream cardiovascular complications in hospitalized patients.

This observational cohort study followed 360 critically ill COVID-19 patients with acute kidney injury in ICU, analyzing AKI stages, kidney replacement therapy, and outcomes at 90 and 365 days. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 in hospitalized/ICU patients during active infection, not on long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

This cross-sectional study assessed sleep quality in 82 post-COVID-19 patients using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index questionnaire, with data collected three years after hospitalization. The study found persistent poor sleep quality in post-COVID patients but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional survey study comparing healthcare utilization and demographics between long COVID patients (n=63) and non-long COVID patients (n=21) from two hospital systems. Long COVID patients reported persistent symptoms and experienced significantly greater difficulty paying bills and accessing healthcare, with no significant differences in primary care visits.

Retrospective study examining whether nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment during acute COVID-19 infection reduces the risk of developing long COVID in immunodeficient patients. Findings suggest the antiviral significantly lowers long COVID risk in this high-risk population.

A prospective cohort study examining post-viral pulmonary complications in 104 COVID-19 survivors, with clinical assessments, imaging, and pulmonary function testing followed over 18 months. Rehabilitation programs improved functional outcomes in 68% of participants, with significant reductions in dyspnea and improvements in exercise capacity.

This longitudinal study compares psychological symptoms (depression, anxiety, memory problems) in 112 COVID-19 infected participants versus 86 uninfected controls, stratified by time since infection (3 months, 3-9 months, 9+ months). The study found that anxiety and depression showed cyclical patterns with worst outcomes at 3-9 months post-infection, and memory/remembering ability declined over time in the infected group.

This study investigates KL-6 as a biomarker for predicting secondary pulmonary fibrosis in acute COVID-19 patients during hospitalization. It is focused on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months after infection.

This cross-sectional study followed 49-51 patients with olfactory dysfunction that developed during COVID-19 infection over a 24-month period, using the Connecticut Chemosensory Clinical Research Center test to measure recovery. The study found that younger age and pulmonary involvement were associated with longer duration of olfactory impairment.

This prospective cohort study followed 50 moderate-to-severe COVID-19 survivors for 6 months, assessing clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, and radiological changes via PFT and HRCT at multiple timepoints. The study found spontaneous resolution of post-COVID symptoms, inflammatory markers, and pulmonary impairment over time, with no progressive fibrosis observed.

Prospective cohort study following 165 COVID-19 survivors with acute kidney injury for two years post-ICU discharge, tracking metabolic and renal parameters. Patients showed progressive central obesity, increased cardiometabolic medication use, and worsening albuminuria despite stable renal function—but no specific intervention was tested or evaluated.

This prospective cohort study follows 3,012 hospitalized omicron-infected patients in Shanghai to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes over 12 months based on acute cardiac biomarker levels (cTnT and NT-proBNP). The study found that elevated biomarkers during acute infection predict increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, death, and cardiovascular rehospitalization, but focuses exclusively on acute COVID-19 outcomes and does not address long COVID or any treatment intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 80 patients (40 with CKD, 40 with AKI) for one year post-COVID-19 to assess renal prognosis and kidney function recovery. Found that COVID-19 exacerbates CKD with greater GFR decline and higher proteinuria, while only 35% of AKI patients showed improvement.

This study followed 253 discharged COVID-19 patients in China for 2 months to assess liver function recovery during the acute post-discharge period. While it documents liver injury patterns in acute COVID-19, it does not address long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months later) and makes no mention of long-term sequelae or chronic conditions beyond the immediate recovery phase.

Prospective cohort study of 104 severe COVID-19 patients one month post-ICU discharge, with 81 patients receiving group or home-based rehabilitation interventions. Main findings include high prevalence of fatigue (75.96%), dyspnea (64.42%), cognitive decline, and musculoskeletal impairment, with 50% reporting moderate quality-of-life limitations.

Retrospective analysis of 191 COVID-19 convalescents who received TCM treatment compared to those who did not, examining clinical and biochemical outcomes. TCM treatment was associated with improvements in immune markers (IL-6, procalcitonin), hematologic parameters, and hepatic/cardiac function biomarkers.

This two-year longitudinal neuroimaging study followed 17 recovered COVID-19 patients using diffusion tensor imaging and cognitive assessments to examine white matter changes and recovery trends. While the study found persistent white matter abnormalities at two years post-infection and correlations between inflammation levels and cognitive deficits, it does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Prospective cohort study following 814 participants (412 COVID-19 positive, 402 negative controls) to determine prevalence and risk factors for long COVID, with 29.6% of COVID-19 positive individuals reporting residual symptoms at one month. Study identified older age and polysymptomatic acute disease as risk factors for long COVID, with fatigue, olfactory disorder, and myalgia as most frequent persistent symptoms.

A prospective cohort study of 749 COVID-19 survivors followed for ~200 days that characterized persistent symptoms (pain, fatigue, PTSD most common) and identified clinical, sociodemographic, and environmental factors associated with post-COVID-19 syndrome. Found that COVID severity, comorbidities, female sex, younger age, low socioeconomic position, and air pollution exposure were associated with different persistent symptoms.

This retrospective cohort study examined bone mineral density (BMD) trajectories in 1,767 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over a mean follow-up of 181.5 days post-discharge. The researchers identified three distinct BMD trajectory patterns and found significant associations between these trajectories and clinical outcomes including mortality and length of hospital stay.

This is a secondary analysis from the HVTN 405/HPTN 1901 observational cohort study that characterizes post-COVID symptom profiles and duration across 759 participants in multiple countries. The study correlates demographics, comorbidities, and acute COVID severity with symptom persistence, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A 16-week prospective cohort study profiling the persistent and episodic nature of long COVID symptoms and their impact on quality of life and functional status through repeated physiological and patient-reported outcome measures. The study documents symptom fluctuations and functional impairment over time but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective cohort study followed 410 symptomatic COVID-19 patients from 7-9 months post-diagnosis to characterize long-term symptom persistence. It found that 39% reported residual symptoms, with fatigue (20.7%), anosmia/ageusia (16.8%), dyspnea (11.7%), and headache (10.0%) being most common.

Prospective observational cohort study examining associations between social determinants of health at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID risk in 3,787 RECOVER-Adult participants. Found that financial hardship, food insecurity, medical discrimination, and lack of social support significantly increased long COVID risk, but the study does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study analyzes clinical laboratory markers in the RECOVER-Adult cohort to identify potential biomarkers differentiating SARS-CoV-2 infection and PASC from uninfected controls. The analysis found no routine laboratory values that serve as clinically useful biomarkers for PASC.

A prospective longitudinal cohort study following 326 COVID-19 survivors (hospitalised and non-hospitalised) over two years in Bangladesh to assess the burden and evolution of long COVID symptoms and complications. Findings show hospitalised survivors experienced higher rates of persistent symptoms at two years, while vaccination significantly reduced respiratory and psychiatric sequelae in both groups.

This binational cohort study investigates the long-term risk of autoimmune inflammatory rheumatic diseases (AIRDs) following COVID-19 infection in Korean and Japanese populations. The study found that COVID-19 patients had increased risk for incident AIRD compared to uninfected controls, with risk increasing alongside acute COVID-19 severity.

A prospective cohort study characterizing persistent symptoms and medical sequelae in 189 COVID-19 survivors versus 120 controls at the NIH Clinical Center. Extensive diagnostic evaluation revealed no specific pathophysiologic cause of reported PASC symptoms in most participants, with findings limited to symptom burden and quality-of-life measures.

Prospective observational study comparing psychological outcomes and quality of life between COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 ICU survivors at 6 and 12 months post-discharge. While the study includes COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute critical illness sequelae rather than long COVID specifically, with COVID-19 patients showing better outcomes than non-COVID ICU survivors.

Prospective observational cohort study of 187 long COVID patients with persistent dyspnoea who received low-intensity spa-based rehabilitation treatment. 88.2% reported improvement in dyspnoea and 80.6% in both dyspnoea and fatigue, with older age, obesity, and comorbidities predicting poorer treatment response.

Prospective cohort study of 250 COVID-19 patients examining post-COVID cardiovascular manifestations, with detailed follow-up at 60 and 90 days post-infection. Observational study with no treatment intervention; documents persistence of symptoms including palpitations, dyspnea, and other sequelae rather than evaluating a specific therapy.

This cross-sectional study examined the occurrence of long COVID in 3,127 healthcare workers at a university hospital, finding that 10 workers developed moderate long COVID with symptoms including asthenia, anosmia, and neuromuscular disorders. The paper focuses on epidemiological characterization and insurance/compensation challenges rather than testing any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining risk factors for long COVID among 256 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. Identified fatigue during admission, chronic kidney disease, thrombocytosis, and positive RT-PCR at discharge as risk factors, while vaccination was protective—but this is observational epidemiology, not a treatment trial.

This observational cohort study followed 312 cancer patients after acute COVID-19 to assess the prevalence and persistence of post-acute sequelae (PASC). 60% of patients reported long COVID symptoms persisting up to 14 months, with fatigue, sleep disturbance, and myalgia being the most common, with higher prevalence in females.

Prospective cohort study of 388 long COVID patients in Malaysia followed for 6 months to identify symptom patterns and risk factors. The study is observational without intervention assignment—it documents natural disease progression and medications patients happened to take, not a treatment evaluation.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 452 COVID-19 patients in Malaysia assessing long COVID prevalence (27.4%) and associated risk factors at 4-5 weeks post-infection. Identifies fatigue, cough, and myalgia as common symptoms and female sex, cardiovascular disease, and asthma as risk factors, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This study tracked 230 professional athletes over ~1 month after returning to training following Omicron infection, measuring changes in fatigue, sleep quality, and mood using standardized scales. While it documents psychological recovery in acute post-infection period, it does not study persistent long COVID symptoms or test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between CRP/albumin ratio and pulmonary function parameters in 157 patients at 12 weeks post-acute COVID-19, stratified by pneumonia severity during acute infection. The study found that CRP/albumin ratio was negatively correlated with respiratory function measures, suggesting potential prognostic value, but it does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational study of 93 hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring prolonged oxygen therapy after testing negative for SARS-CoV-2, examining factors associated with failure to wean and mortality. Identifies age ≥50 years with multiple comorbidities as a risk factor for prolonged hospitalization and poor outcomes, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study comparing post-COVID syndrome incidence and outcomes over 12 months between 298 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection and 298 unexposed controls in rural Kerala. The study found higher PCS incidence in the exposure group (91.9%) versus controls (83.2%), with persistent functional impairments and overlapping symptom burden between groups.

This case-control study compared pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life between post-COVID-19 subjects (1 year post-recovery) and healthy controls. While lung function was relatively preserved, the post-COVID group showed reduced diffusion capacity (DLCO), reduced exercise capacity, and impaired quality of life scores in energy/fatigue and physical function domains.

Longitudinal observational study of 145 COVID-19 patients followed over 6 months to characterize pulmonary recovery trajectories using CT imaging, lung function tests, and clinical parameters. Study identified phenotypes of recovery and developed machine learning classifiers to predict incomplete pulmonary recovery from non-imaging biomarkers.

This real-world study characterized 141 outpatients with subacute or chronic post-COVID cough, collecting clinical data, prescriptions, and cough severity over follow-up visits. The authors evaluated treatment effectiveness and found ICS/LABA to be the most effective option for post-COVID cough, with a higher prevalence in females.

A cross-sectional study of 186 COVID-19 recovered medical doctors in Bangladesh examining post-COVID symptom prevalence, duration, and associated risk factors through telephone interviews. Female sex and comorbid conditions were identified as significant risk factors for long-lasting post-COVID symptoms.

This observational study tracked chest X-ray findings in 429 COVID-19 patients at hospital discharge and 30-day follow-up. While it documents long-term radiological sequelae (consolidation, reticular thickening) and symptoms like fatigue post-COVID, it is an observational monitoring study without any treatment intervention.

A prospective cohort study of 279 older adults hospitalized with COVID-19, followed for 90 days post-discharge to assess post-COVID syndrome prevalence, symptom patterns, and functional outcomes. The study found 23.6% of patients reported at least one clinical feature at 90 days, with fatigue being the most common symptom (8.9%), while functional status (ADL/IADL) largely returned to baseline.

A prospective cohort study following 1,000 COVID-19 patients at 30 and 90 days post-discharge to assess long-term neurological sequelae. Found that headache and insomnia were the most common neurological symptoms, with prevalence declining over time but highlighting the persistent neurological complications of COVID-19.

Longitudinal study measuring sleep quality changes in 500 COVID-19 patients from ICU/isolation discharge to 30-day follow-up using PSQI scores. Found significant increase in insomnia prevalence post-COVID (45.1% vs 12.1% pre-COVID), but no intervention was tested or evaluated.

Multicentric retrospective cohort study in Iraq comparing inflammatory polyneuropathy rates in 1,344 COVID-19 patients versus 896 controls over six months. Found 1.14% of COVID-19 patients developed inflammatory polyneuropathy (vs 0.29% in controls, RR=6), with 44.4% of cases occurring 4-12 weeks post-infection and GBS as the most common type (72.2%).

Retrospective observational study of 84 long COVID patients with pneumonia admitted to a tertiary care hospital, analyzing microbial isolates and antibiotic resistance patterns. Treatment with targeted antimicrobial therapy based on culture and sensitivity results achieved 91% survival and discharge rate, with resistance patterns (MDR/XDR strains) correlating with mortality outcomes.

Longitudinal study measuring sexual function in 300 female COVID-19 survivors using the FSFI scale at discharge and 60 days post-discharge. Found significant decline in sexual function scores post-infection (28.16 vs 24.43, p<0.0001), but this is a natural history/observational study without any treatment intervention.

Prospective follow-up study comparing pulmonary function, mental health, and quality of life outcomes 3+ months post-ICU discharge in COVID-19 ARDS survivors who received non-invasive versus invasive mechanical ventilation. Patients requiring mechanical ventilation showed greater impairment in pulmonary function and reduced physical quality of life, suggesting need for enhanced rehabilitation.

A prospective observational study of 48 COVID-19 patients with dyspnea assessed factors associated with persistence of dyspnea and health-related quality of life at discharge and 60 days post-discharge. Early pulmonary rehabilitation resulted in significant improvements in dyspnea and quality of life scores, with age and BMI identified as significant predictive factors.

Observational cross-sectional study identifying risk factors for severe long COVID-19 using questionnaire data from 220 respondents. Found that age >45 years, ≥15 COVID-19 symptoms, and obesity were significant predictors of severe long COVID-19.

This retrospective cohort study followed 2,000 COVID-19 patients discharged from a Pakistani hospital, documenting persistent symptoms at discharge and 12-month follow-up. The study found fatigue as the most common long-term symptom (6.78% at follow-up) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective case series of 36 post-ICU COVID-19 survivors evaluated at admission, discharge, and 3-month follow-up after an inpatient multimodal rehabilitation program. Study found significant improvements in respiratory muscle strength, cough effectiveness, and functional capacity between discharge and 3-month follow-up, though fatigue levels worsened despite overall functional recovery.

A follow-up observational study examining body composition and metabolic changes (fat distribution, insulin, HOMA-IR) in 441 individuals before and after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 infection. The study documents acute post-infection metabolic dysregulation but does not address long COVID or test any intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares health-related quality of life (HRQL) in hospitalized COVID-19 patients six months post-discharge versus non-hospitalized patients and healthy controls using multiple validated questionnaires (EQ5D5L, SF36v2, FACIT-F, PCFSS). While the paper documents significant HRQL impairment in hospitalized patients and suggests potential for rehabilitation programs, it is excluded because it does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment—it is purely observational and descriptive in nature.

Prospective observational study of 476 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in South India followed at 1, 2, and 4 weeks post-discharge to assess persistence of symptoms and quality of life using the 15D questionnaire. Most symptoms resolved by 4 weeks with improved health-related quality of life and physical performance, contrasting with findings from other global regions.

This retrospective pathology study analyzes tissue specimens from COVID-associated mucormycosis cases to characterize histomorphological patterns and fungal characteristics. While the cases occur post-COVID, the paper is a descriptive pathology analysis of acute fungal complications during active infection sequelae, not a treatment trial for long COVID.

A retrospective cohort study of 42 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with organizing pneumonia comparing glucocorticoid treatment (dexamethasone vs prednisone vs none) and their impact on oxygen requirements and outcomes over 12 months post-discharge. Steroids were associated with improved oxygen weaning, though incidence of post-COVID organizing pneumonia was lower than expected at 0.05% with 14% mortality.

This cross-sectional study evaluates autonomic dysfunction and silent ischemia in 128 post-COVID-19 outpatients (55 asymptomatic, 73 symptomatic) using 24-hour ambulatory ECG and heart rate variability analysis. The study found that symptomatic patients had significantly higher ST depression burden and were at greater risk of silent ischemic attacks, but no treatment or intervention was tested.

Descriptive cross-sectional study assessing post-acute COVID-19 complications in 100+ patients at a teaching hospital in North India through clinical examination, echocardiography, and pulmonary function testing. Found fatigue as the most common persistent symptom and cardiac/pulmonary changes on imaging even in asymptomatic patients.

This longitudinal observational cohort study followed 146 COVID-19 recovered patients for up to 12 months with monthly assessments to identify persistent sequelae and associated risk predictors. Key findings include pulmonary (40%), psychiatric (25%), and neurological (21.7%) sequelae, with comorbidities, older age, higher BMI, and severe disease identified as significant risk factors.

Retrospective analysis of post-COVID-19 patients with pulmonary embolism who received anticoagulant therapy, assessing predisposing factors and vascular reperfusion outcomes over six months. Study found high rates of complete reperfusion with anticoagulation alone and identified hypertension, diabetes, and obesity as prevalent risk factors, but did not evaluate or compare treatment interventions.

Retrospective cohort study of 504 COVID-19 patients from a Saudi Arabian hospital examining the incidence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 syndrome. Found 45% incidence with fatigue, joint pain, and decreased exercise tolerance as most common persistent symptoms; female gender, multiple comorbidities, steroid use, and acute infection complications were significant risk factors.

Retrospective cohort study comparing chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) severity before and after COVID-19 infection in 33 patients, with 17 having COVID-19 history and 16 as controls. Found no significant differences in SNOT-22 scores between groups, and no significant association between intranasal corticosteroid use and COVID-19 infection status (except in asthma patients).

A retrospective cohort study of 41 long COVID patients treated with stellate ganglion block (SGB) to manage persistent symptoms. Results showed 86% of patients experienced symptom reduction following SGB treatment.

Retrospective observational study of 617 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases in India comparing post-COVID-19 condition prevalence and characteristics between Delta and Omicron variants. Found 6.48% reported persistent symptoms, with Delta cases showing higher prevalence (12.38%) than Omicron (5.27%), but no treatment intervention was tested.

This retrospective cohort study examines post-discharge healthcare usage and costs for 200 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 across four pandemic surges. The study compares utilization patterns and identifies high-cost patient groups, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

A retrospective analysis of 289 COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between demographic factors (age, gender, smoking), clinical variables (vaccination, disease severity), and post-COVID symptoms. Female gender, higher BMI, and smoking were identified as risk factors for symptom prevalence, while booster vaccination showed promise in reducing symptoms.

A 12-month observational pilot study evaluating a combination treatment (systemic corticosteroids, mesoglycan, diuretic, and vitamin complex) in 87 patients with persistent post-COVID hyposmia and dysgeusia. Both olfactory and gustatory functions improved significantly from baseline to 12 months, with earlier treatment initiation associated with better recovery.

Retrospective study comparing patients with chronic epipharyngitis who have or lack previous COVID-19 infection, evaluating differences in symptoms and endoscopic findings. Long COVID patients showed higher severity scores and different symptom profiles (fatigue, brain fog), with epipharyngeal abrasive therapy recommended as treatment.

This observational cohort study followed 100 hospitalized COVID-19 patients over 24 weeks to evaluate pulmonary function, dyspnea scores, and antibody levels in long COVID. Results showed slower improvement in lung function parameters in patients with severe acute COVID-19 compared to moderate cases, with no difference in neutralizing antibody levels between groups.

This retrospective cohort study examines the prevalence and outcomes of persistent sinus tachycardia 12-16 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in 1.36 million patients from the TriNetX network. Patients with post-COVID tachycardia showed significantly higher mortality, critical care utilization, and ventilator use compared to matched controls, with worse outcomes in unvaccinated individuals.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive performance and sleep quality in 138 long COVID patients at 11 months post-infection using standardized cognitive tests (MMSE, MOCA) and sleep assessment. The study found cognitive deficits in 15-79% of participants but did not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

A prospective cohort study evaluating the use of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) to assess cardiac and pulmonary abnormalities in 24 PASC patients presenting with cardiopulmonary symptoms to a COVID-19 recovery clinic. Most patients (62.5%) had normal lung ultrasounds and 87.5% had normal cardiac findings, suggesting cardiopulmonary symptoms may arise from etiologies not detected by POCUS.

Retrospective cohort study investigating serum mitokines (GDF-15 and FGF-21) as predictive biomarkers for long COVID in non-hospitalized patients. Elevated GDF-15 levels in the acute phase showed potential as a biomarker for predicting long COVID development, but the study does not test any intervention or treatment.

Prospective observational study examining cardiac damage in 97 COVID-19 patients at 3 and 6 months post-infection, stratified by severity. Found no significant long-term cardiac damage on ECG or echocardiography, with most measurements remaining within normal ranges.

A prospective observational study of 553 COVID-19 recovered patients in Delhi that assessed the prevalence and burden of long COVID syndrome and its associations with demographics and health parameters. Found 45.6% had long COVID with fatigue and dry cough as most common symptoms, associated with comorbidities, hypertension history, and COVID vaccination.

This cross-sectional study assessed residual symptoms and functional status in 50 COVID-19 patients at three months post-discharge using spirometry and six-minute walk tests. The paper documents high rates of persistent dyspnea and reduced exercise capacity but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining association between zinc deficiency and post-acute COVID-19 outcomes in 3,726 patients from the TriNetX database. Found that zinc deficiency was associated with increased hospitalization, mortality, and cardiac/renal complications during 6-month follow-up.

This retrospective study assessed the prevalence of long COVID in a Portuguese primary care cohort of 334 patients with mild acute COVID-19, finding 43.4% symptomatic at ≥3 months and 17.1% at 2 years. The study identified symptom patterns (fatigue, myalgia, post-exertional malaise, cognitive dysfunction) and functional impact but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This retrospective study examines CT imaging findings in COVID-19 patients during acute infection and identifies risk factors for pulmonary fibrosis development. While it follows patients with comorbidities, it focuses on acute-phase imaging and fibrosis risk during active COVID-19 rather than long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions.

This prospective observational cohort study followed 96 COVID-19 survivors for six months to assess glycemic changes and diabetes risk. The study found that severe COVID-19 was significantly associated with higher diabetes risk at six months (OR=5.5), but it is an observational follow-up study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This observational study assessed post-COVID-19 functional status and complications in 244 COVID-19 survivors using the PCFS scale at a tertiary healthcare center in Bangladesh. The most prevalent complications were fatigue (77.9%), sleep disturbances (51.6%), anxiety (41.8%), and breathing difficulties (40.2%), with sleep and breathing issues significantly associated with functional impairment grades.

Retrospective study of 38 pediatric patients with post-COVID-19 multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) examining the prevalence and characteristics of cardiac manifestations including valvulopathies, cardiomegaly, and coronary abnormalities. The study describes disease prevalence and symptomatology but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated the prevalence and predictors of chronic fatigue syndrome among 500 COVID-19 survivors in rural India from 2023-2024. The study found a 21.4% prevalence of CFS, with older age, female gender, and comorbidities identified as significant risk factors, but did not test any specific treatment intervention.

summary: This retrospective cohort study followed 454 severe COVID-19 ICU survivors for one year after discharge to assess long-term clinical sequelae and outcomes. The study found significant declines in quality of life, increased readmission rates, and persistent respiratory symptoms, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed PASC symptoms and pulmonary function in 65 COVID-19 survivors >90 days post-infection in a South Indian secondary care setting.
