The study found 55.4% PASC prevalence with dyspnea as the most common symptom and reduced forced vital capacity in 23.1% of subjects, but it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This retrospective chart review examined autonomic dysfunction (orthostatic intolerance and POTS) in 16 pediatric patients following COVID-19 infection or vaccination, using tilt table testing and other autonomic assessments. The study found that 62.5% met POTS criteria with elevated norepinephrine levels and some evidence of small fiber neuropathy, highlighting the association between COVID-19 and autonomic dysfunction in children.

Retrospective observational study examining pulmonary function test and 6-minute walk test results in 19 patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms following mild COVID-19. Found weak correlations between dyspnea severity and objective lung function impairment, but strong correlation between dyspnea and fatigue.

This retrospective cohort study evaluated neurologic music therapy (diaphragmatic breathing, vocal intonation, therapeutic singing) in 69 adults recovering from COVID-19/PASC during inpatient rehabilitation, with 33 receiving NMT and 36 receiving standard care only. NMT participants showed significantly greater reductions in activity-based oxygen use and improved sustained phonation with higher rates of home discharge.

This retrospective study examines hip avascular necrosis (AVN) outcomes in 118 patients following COVID-19 infection, with 2-year follow-up and comparison of conservative vs surgical treatments. While the paper documents a post-COVID complication and evaluates treatment modalities, it is not about long COVID as a syndrome—it focuses on a specific orthopedic sequela (AVN) rather than the constellation of persistent symptoms defining long COVID.

A retrospective single-center study of 74 long COVID patients in Switzerland examining clinical symptoms and laboratory biomarkers over a mean follow-up of 14.4 weeks. While the study documents symptom trajectories and immune dysregulation (elevated ferritin and ANA), it is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Prospective cohort study following 51 ICU survivors of severe COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation for one year post-discharge, tracking HRQoL, functional capacity, nutritional status, and return to work. While showing significant improvements in these domains over one year, this is an observational follow-up study without any intervention assigned to patients.

This paper compares neurophysiological markers (EEG, event-related potentials) in long COVID patients with prolonged cognitive fatigue to healthy controls and patients with persistent post-concussion symptoms. The study identifies altered brain activity patterns (reduced P300 amplitude, impaired processing speed) as objective biomarkers of cognitive dysfunction in long COVID, but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study of 52 long COVID patients who underwent stellate ganglion block (SGB) injections at a Boston institution between 2022-2024. Most patients reported improvement in brain fog, fatigue, dizziness, and headache, though with high variability in symptom improvement duration and some adverse effects reported.

This cohort study followed 109 COVID-19 survivors over three years to assess the longitudinal persistence of anxiety symptoms using the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale. Results showed significant improvement in anxiety scores over time, with mean HAM-A scores declining from 17.06 at discharge to 1.13 at three years, suggesting positive mental health recovery trajectory in long COVID survivors.

Multicenter retrospective cohort study examining persistent post-COVID symptoms among 163 hemodialysis patients. Identifies diabetes as a key risk factor for long COVID development and describes prevalence of fatigue, anxiety, dyspnea, and other symptoms in this vulnerable population.

A prospective cohort study of 50 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Hungary assessing long-term pulmonary changes via chest CT imaging at admission and 3 months post-infection. While patients showed remarkable recovery, over 40% exhibited persistent lung abnormalities including ground-glass opacities, fibrotic changes, and distorted lung architecture.

This retrospective study examined feeding and swallowing dysfunction in 95 non-intubated older adults hospitalized with acute COVID-19 between 2020-2022, finding that 21% experienced impaired swallowing at the end of isolation. The study associates post-isolation swallowing dysfunction with prolonged hospital stay but does not address long COVID or test any interventions for long-term sequelae.

Retrospective study of 58 long COVID patients examining temporal changes in chest CT features of pulmonary fibrosis at 3 and 12 months follow-up. Found that CT features of irreversible pulmonary fibrosis remain static over time, with subpleural curvilinear lines and parenchymal bands not correlating with breathlessness or impaired lung function.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 668 outpatients recovered from COVID-19 using physical examination, ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac MRI to assess subclinical cardiovascular involvement and its association with symptoms and risk factors. Only 5 cases of myocarditis were diagnosed, and abnormal cardiac findings were uncommon, suggesting cardiovascular complications in recovered COVID-19 patients are rare.

Prospective cohort study examining haematological variables in 59 COVID-19 patients to determine their association with post-infection cardiovascular complications. Found that neutrophil counts, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and prothrombin time were highly significant predictors of cardiovascular complications post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, but the study does not test any intervention.

Retrospective study comparing physical performance metrics in 120 adolescent soccer players with and without prior COVID-19 infection, measured at baseline and follow-up timepoints. While the study documents acute post-infection performance deficits and recovery trajectories, it does not assess long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection) or test any treatment intervention.

This study describes post-COVID symptoms in 675 patients using a virtual review pathway stratified by acute COVID severity. Fatigue was the most common ongoing symptom (50.3% in high-risk patients), and mental health symptoms (depression, anxiety, PTSD) were prevalent, with virtual triage effectively identifying patients needing face-to-face review.

Retrospective matched cohort study comparing health care use and new diagnoses in 3,397 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 versus 6,658 matched controls over 6 months post-discharge. Hospitalized COVID-19 patients had significantly greater physician visits, ED visits, and hospital admissions, with new diagnoses across multiple organ systems.

This retrospective cohort study examined emergency department visit rates in US veterans diagnosed with long COVID versus those with COVID-19 infection only, using VA electronic health records from March 2021 to December 2021. Veterans with long COVID had a 34% higher risk of ED visits in the six months post-infection compared to those without long COVID diagnosis.

Post-discharge observational study following 62 COVID-19 hypoxia patients 1-3 months after hospitalization to assess persistence or reappearance of respiratory symptoms. Found that males were more prone to ongoing respiratory problems compared to females, with most patients showing symptom improvement by follow-up.

This prospective longitudinal cohort study followed 144 patients hospitalized for severe COVID-19 in Gabon for 12 months to assess the prevalence and evolution of long COVID symptoms. The study found a 52.1% prevalence of long COVID, with fatigue, cough, sleep disorders, and anxiety predominating early post-hospitalization, and most patients experiencing symptom resolution by 12 months.

US population survey estimating the prevalence of long COVID among adults (7%) and children (1%) using national survey data. This is an epidemiological study documenting disease burden, not an intervention trial.

This cross-sectional study examined associations between self-reported COVID-19 infection, SARS-CoV-2 serology results, and persistent physical symptoms in 26,823 French adults. The findings suggest persistent symptoms may be more associated with belief of infection than laboratory-confirmed COVID-19, raising questions about psychological vs. biological mechanisms.

Cross-sectional study describing sociodemographic and clinical features of 219 long COVID patients, of whom 139 had persistent olfactory dysfunction confirmed by testing. Found olfactory dysfunction associated with longer symptom duration and significant impact on daily activities, with ageusia as a risk factor.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity and ME/CFS-like symptoms in German children and adolescents using the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire. Found minimal increased risk of ME/CFS symptoms after adjustment, suggesting small risk of post-COVID ME/CFS in children, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey study estimates the prevalence of long COVID among 16,091 US adults with confirmed COVID-19 and identifies sociodemographic risk factors. The study found 14.7% of respondents reported persistent symptoms beyond 2 months, with higher risk among older adults and women, and lower risk among those vaccinated prior to infection.

Cross-sectional study of cardiac screening in professional athletes with prior COVID-19 infection to assess prevalence of inflammatory heart disease. While the study examines post-COVID cardiac complications, it focuses on acute infection sequelae in a specific athletic population during return-to-play screening, not long COVID syndrome, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID-19 symptoms between 360 hospitalized and 308 nonhospitalized patients at 2 years follow-up. Found 59.7% of hospitalized and 67.5% of nonhospitalized patients had at least one symptom, with fatigue, pain, and memory loss most common; no treatment intervention tested.

This cross-sectional study examines understanding of and access to care for long COVID symptoms among undocumented Latino immigrants presenting to US emergency departments. It is an observational study without any treatment intervention, focused on prevalence, healthcare barriers, and health disparities rather than evaluating a therapeutic intervention.

Population-based survey study examining the prevalence and functional impact of cognitive symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition in US adults. Finds that 56.7% of individuals with post-COVID-19 condition report daily cognitive symptoms, which are associated with greater functional impairment, reduced full-time employment, and depressive symptom severity.

Cross-sectional study evaluating self-reported taste dysfunction in long COVID patients using psychophysical testing methods. This is a descriptive/diagnostic study documenting symptom prevalence without testing any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional survey study examines health care access and affordability challenges among US adults with post-COVID-19 condition, comparing outcomes across three groups: those with PCC, COVID-19 survivors without PCC, and those never diagnosed. Adults with PCC reported significantly higher rates of unmet health care needs due to costs, difficulty finding clinicians, appointment delays, and insurance authorization problems.

Cross-sectional study comparing taste and smell function between 340 individuals with prior COVID-19 and 434 without COVID-19 history using validated psychophysical tests (WETT and UPSIT). Found persistent smell loss in ~30% of COVID-19 patients at ~395 days post-infection, while taste function was unaffected; earlier SARS-CoV-2 variants associated with greater smell loss.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition and activity-limiting symptoms among US adults. It is an epidemiological survey with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional survey study examined the association between food insecurity and long COVID prevalence among US adults using 2022-2023 National Health Interview Survey data. While the study found that food insecurity was associated with greater odds of current long COVID and lower odds of recovery, it is an observational epidemiological study that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

This cross-sectional study uses nationally representative NHIS data to assess the prevalence of psychiatric symptoms, treatment uptake, and cost-related barriers to mental health care among US adults with post-COVID-19 condition. The study documents higher rates of depression, anxiety, sleep difficulties, cognitive problems, and fatigue in people with PCC compared to those without, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study estimating the prevalence of lasting COVID-19 symptoms among US children and adolescents stratified by sociodemographic characteristics. This is an observational survey without treatment intervention, so does not meet criteria for the intervention trials pipeline.

Cross-sectional survey of 238,828 American Red Cross blood donors examining the prevalence of long-term symptoms (>4 weeks) associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection using self-report and serologic testing. Finds 43.3% of SARS-CoV-2 infected donors reported new long-term symptoms compared to 22.1% of uninfected controls, with highest associations for taste/smell changes and respiratory/cardiac symptoms.

Cross-sectional study comparing neurological and cognitive symptoms in 50 long COVID patients with varying initial hospitalization severity, using standardized clinical measures, neuropsychological testing, and brain MRI. Found mild cognitive deficits and fatigue-related impairment, with microbleeds only in initially hospitalized patients, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional study examined the association between social determinants of health (SDOH) and long COVID prevalence in 4,584 US children and adolescents. Economic instability with food insecurity and poor social/community context were associated with significantly higher odds of long COVID, but the study did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed frontal lobe cognitive function 12 months post-COVID-19 using eye tracking assessments in recovered patients versus healthy controls. While it demonstrates impaired inhibitory cortical control in long COVID patients, particularly those with severe disease, it is a descriptive cross-sectional study without any treatment intervention and therefore not eligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

Multicenter cross-sectional study comparing long COVID prevalence and functional impacts in people with MS/related disorders versus controls. Finds pwMSRD have higher odds of long COVID (aOR=1.6-2.3) and experience greater physical function decline and disability progression when affected.

Cross-sectional survey study describing long COVID symptoms and associated factors in persons with self-reported arthritis history (n=171). Finds 53.5% report long COVID with fatigue, myalgia, weakness, and breathlessness most common; substantial functional declines reported compared to pre-COVID status.

Cross-sectional survey of 320 long-COVID patients assessing prevalence and patterns of dysautonomia symptoms using the COMPASS-31 questionnaire. Study found high prevalence of autonomic dysfunction symptoms, particularly in gastrointestinal, secretomotor, and orthostatic intolerance domains, with correlation between symptom severity and disease duration.

Cross-sectional survey of 27,907 American Red Cross blood donors comparing prevalence of new long-term symptoms lasting ≥4 weeks between those with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, stratified by occupation and industry. Finds 45% of previously infected vs 24% of never-infected reported new long-term symptoms, with prevalence varying by occupation (26-41%) and industry (26-55%).

Cross-sectional study measuring health utility values in COVID-19 patients with olfactory dysfunction using multiple instruments (EQ-5D, VAS, TTO, SG). Patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction reported significantly lower health utility scores compared to those with resolved or no olfactory dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study assesses the prevalence, characteristics, and quality of life impact of parosmia (distorted smell perception) in COVID-19 patients with olfactory dysfunction. While it addresses a long COVID symptom, it does not evaluate or test any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey using 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data to estimate prevalence of COVID-19 and long COVID across U.S. industries and occupations. Identifies healthcare, protective services, and specific occupations (bartenders, farmworkers, personal care workers) with elevated long COVID prevalence, but does not test or evaluate any interventions or treatments.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive dysfunction in Chinese older adults post-COVID-19 using the SCD-18 questionnaire. Found that COVID-infected participants, particularly females and rural residents, showed significantly higher cognitive impairment scores within 1-6 months of infection, with gradual recovery after 6 months.

Cross-sectional cognitive assessment of 187 COVID-19 survivors one year after hospitalization in Brazil, with detailed neuropsychiatric testing on a subset of 26 participants. Found impairments in global cognition, attention, orientation, and episodic memory in those with abnormal TICS-M screening scores.

This retrospective cross-sectional study examines malnutrition risk and nutritional indicators in 174 COVID-19 patients during the rehabilitation phase in Hong Kong. While the paper studies patients in rehabilitation post-COVID, it focuses on acute/post-acute hospitalization outcomes rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study nested within a prospective cohort examining caregiver burden in 52 older adults with post-COVID syndrome and their caregivers. Found 54.2% prevalence of caregiver burden, significantly associated with caregiver depressive symptoms, highlighting the need for long-term psychosocial support.

This cross-sectional study uses 2022 BRFSS data to assess the prevalence of functional disabilities and adverse well-being among workers by employment status and COVID-19/Long COVID history. It finds that long COVID is associated with substantially elevated prevalence of cognitive disability and depression compared to 2019 pre-pandemic levels, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID patients (n=26) and healthy controls (n=57) to examine neuropsychiatric symptoms, inflammatory markers, and gut microbiome alterations. Found elevated depression, increased CCL23 levels, and dysbiosis in post-COVID patients but no differences in Alzheimer's disease markers.

Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining employment status, work limitations, and sickness absenteeism among US adults with and without long COVID (n=26,270). Long COVID was associated with higher odds of work limitations, cognitive dysfunction, and sickness absenteeism, but the study does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive assessment tools (MoCA vs PROMIS) in long COVID patients. Finds that self-rated PROMIS cognitive function scores are better predictors of functional impairment than traditional neuropsychological testing in long COVID patients.

A cross-sectional study nested in a prospective cohort examining cognitive, clinical, and functional outcomes in 80 elderly Brazilian patients with post-COVID syndrome (mean 10 months post-infection). The study found high prevalence of cognitive impairment (77.5%), functional disability (73.33%), frailty (37.50%), and dyspnea (88.75%), with implications for early identification and management in aging populations.

Cross-sectional study comparing neuropsychiatric testing outcomes in 279 patients with and without long COVID, finding that long-COVID patients had significantly worse cognitive test results and higher rates of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) diagnoses. The study includes COVID-negative controls and COVID-positive patients both with and without long-COVID symptoms, using standardized UDS3 cognitive testing and NACC diagnostic criteria.

This cross-sectional study examines the occurrence and risk factors of PTSD among 144 discharged COVID-19 patients in China, finding a 16% PTSD occurrence rate. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery and psychological outcomes, not long COVID or treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between cognitive impairment and functional disability in 80 elderly people 2-24 months after COVID-19 infection. Found significant correlations between cognitive impairment and functional disability across multiple domains, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 844 COVID-19 recovered patients examining associations between self-stigma, PTSD, mental health, quality of life, and insomnia using structural equation modeling. Found that mental health mediates relationships between COVID-related self-stigma and PTSD with quality of life and insomnia outcomes, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study comparing neurologic manifestations of long COVID across age groups in 200 hospitalized and 1,100 non-hospitalized patients. Found that younger and middle-aged adults experience higher symptom burden and cognitive dysfunction despite lower rates of abnormal neurologic findings compared to older patients.

Prospective cross-sectional study of 226 post-COVID-19 patients examining new-onset chronic pain, neuropathic pain, and their clinical associations. The study characterizes pain trajectories and phenotypes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or outcome.

Cross-sectional survey of 29,079 Norwegian type 2 diabetes patients examining gender differences in COVID-19 experiences and long COVID symptom reporting. Finds that 27.3% of infected patients reported long COVID symptoms, with women significantly more likely to experience prolonged illness compared to men.

Cross-sectional survey of 410 post-COVID patients assessing depression prevalence using PHQ-9 and identifying associated factors. Found 23.7% prevalence of depression with multiple demographic and clinical correlates, but is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence in 99 pregnant women who had COVID-19 during pregnancy versus 99 uninfected controls. Finds 74.7% of infected women had at least one long COVID symptom (fatigue, myalgia, anosmia most common), with prevalence correlating to acute disease severity.

Cross-sectional observational study examining resting-state fMRI brain dynamics in post-COVID patients with and without persistent headache, using Hurst exponent as a measure of functional brain scaling. Finds that patients with ongoing post-COVID headache show suppressed brain dynamics compared to those without headache, suggesting a potential neurophysiological biomarker for this symptom.

A cross-sectional study of 370 long COVID patients from a community rehabilitation service that characterizes symptom severity and functional disability using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale. The study identifies three distinct severity phenotypes (mild, moderate, severe) and explores correlations between symptom severity, functional disability, and overall health, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,062 healthcare workers assessing the prevalence (10%), determinants, and consequences of post-COVID including workplace contamination and return-to-work outcomes. Study documents symptoms and risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for post-COVID.

Retrospective cohort study comparing lung water density (LWD) measured by MRI in 185 COVID-19 survivors versus 109 healthy controls. Findings show elevated LWD in survivors, associated with hospitalization, comorbidities, elevated inflammatory biomarkers, and higher BMI.

A cross-sectional study of 48 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 in the first wave, interviewed ~553 days post-discharge to assess persistent symptoms and quality of life. Found 77.1% had ≥5 persistent symptoms (fatigue 79.2%, dyspnea 68.8%, weakness 60.4%), with 81.3% reporting poor quality of life and persistent fatigue significantly associated with symptom burden and reduced QoL.

Cross-sectional study comparing ventilation and perfusion scintigraphy findings in 33 post-COVID-19 individuals (23 symptomatic, 10 asymptomatic). Symptomatic patients showed significantly reduced radiopharmaceutical activity and pulmonary function compared to asymptomatic individuals, with up to 50% reduction in severe cases.

Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence and risk factors of memory impairment among 1,157 recovered COVID-19 patients in Iraq using the MAC-Q test. Found 34.49% with memory impairment and identified female gender, older age, repeated infections, severe disease, and multiple variant exposure as independent risk factors.

Cross-sectional study of 128 Brazilian adults examining associations between COVID-19 sequelae and periodontal disease/obesity. Found that individuals with both obesity and generalized periodontitis had 86% higher probability of reporting COVID-19 sequelae, but no significant associations in the overall sample.

This prospective cross-sectional study compares health utility values and olfactory-specific quality of life between patients with COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction and those with chronic rhinosinusitis/rhinitis-related olfactory dysfunction. While it includes COVID-19 patients, the study is primarily about comparing two etiologies of olfactory dysfunction rather than investigating long COVID or testing any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study profiled 332 long COVID patients in the Brazilian Amazon region, examining hematological, coagulation, immunological, metabolic, hepatic, renal, and muscular biomarkers. The study identified associations between acute phase hospitalization and persistent laboratory abnormalities, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing patient-reported functional outcomes and fatigue 30 days after COVID-19 hospitalization in 55 survivors. Found high rates of new ADL difficulty/dependence and clinically significant fatigue worsening, but this is observational follow-up without intervention—not a treatment trial.

This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and risk factors for persistent symptoms (Long COVID) in 226 adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection presenting to primary care in Brazil. Key risk factors identified include ≥5 symptoms, female sex, and ages 40-49 and 70+ years, with cognitive symptoms (memory loss, attention loss) and anxiety showing the strongest associations.

This case-control study compares health-related quality of life (HRQOL) outcomes in COVID-19-recovered patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) versus matched controls without SARD. While it confirms post-COVID syndrome prevalence and documents HRQOL impairment, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined electromyography (EMG) findings in 29 non-hospitalized long COVID patients and compared symptom severity, quality of life, and physical function between those with and without myopathic EMG changes. Myopathic EMG findings were present in 62% of patients, but no significant differences in clinical outcomes were observed between groups, suggesting myopathic EMG changes in long COVID should be interpreted cautiously within clinical context.

Cross-sectional observational study of 200 post-COVID-19 patients assessing fatigue and anhedonia using self-assessment scales. Found high prevalence of both symptoms with positive correlation between them, and negative correlation with time since recovery, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 48 COVID-19 patients >1 year post-inpatient rehabilitation to examine how social determinants of health factors relate to long-term functional status and quality of life outcomes. Found that male gender, higher income, and urban residence were associated with better functional recovery and quality of life measures after rehabilitation.

Cross-sectional survey measuring compassion fatigue, work engagement, and psychological distress in 116 healthcare workers caring for long COVID patients. Finds that HCWs with personal history of long COVID and those in early career stages report significantly worse outcomes across all measures.

This retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 1,237 long COVID patients at a post-COVID recovery clinic in British Columbia characterizes rehabilitation needs using objective tests and patient-reported outcomes. The study identifies high prevalence of rehabilitation needs across pulmonary, mental health, and neurological domains but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared postural balance, fatigue, muscle strength, and quality of life between 40 post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) patients and 40 controls. PCS patients showed significantly worse postural balance and fatigue, with balance deficits correlating with reduced quality of life, but no intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional survey study compared mental and physical health outcomes between adults with diagnosed long COVID, self-reported long COVID, and no long COVID in California. While it documents significant differences in anxiety, depression, fatigue, and physical function across groups, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study comparing personality traits and psychological characteristics between 26 healthcare workers with long COVID and 141 without long COVID. Found that long COVID group had higher neuroticism scores and poorer mental health, suggesting neurotic tendency and high symptom burden may be risk factors for long COVID.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing functional capacity in 159 adults and older people 1 month after COVID-19 hospitalization using the Barthel Index. Found that hospitalization impairs functional status, with older people showing greater functional decline; age, sarcopenia, and frailty were associated factors.

Cross-sectional study examining ECG abnormalities in 244 Ugandan long COVID patients at least 2 months post-infection. Found 18.9% had abnormal ECG findings, with non-specific T-wave inversion being most common; no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 765 young Australians (aged 15-29) assessing the prevalence and impact of long COVID. Found 11.2% reported long COVID with significant impacts on work and daily functioning, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 4,315 healthcare workers in Germany examined the prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID fatigue symptoms in spring 2021, using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory. Severe fatigue occurred in 10.7% of respondents and was associated with preexisting mental/respiratory conditions, acute infection severity, psychological distress, lower quality of life, and work incapacity.

Cross-sectional comparison of health-related quality of life (SF-12) in 192 severe vs 192 non-severe COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge. Severe COVID-19 patients had significantly lower HRQOL scores (34.45 vs 39.64), suggesting long-term quality of life impairment correlates with acute infection severity.

Cross-sectional study examining brain metabolic connectivity using FDG-PET in 44 long COVID patients across acute, subacute, and chronic phases compared to healthy controls. Found hyperconnectivity in executive and attention networks in acute/subacute phase that becomes hypoconnectivity in chronic phase, suggesting connectivity dysfunction may underlie persistent neurological symptoms.

Population-based survey of 1,087 Michigan adults diagnosed with COVID-19 examining predictors of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Study found that long COVID (symptom duration >60 days), pandemic-related economic disruption, and worse acute symptom severity were associated with poor mental health outcomes, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed olfactory recovery patterns in 200 recovered COVID-19 patients using subjective and objective measures (Sniffin' Sticks test) over three months. While 55% of patients reported subjective smell recovery at 3 months, objective testing revealed only 1% had normal olfactory function, indicating persistent objective deficits despite perceived recovery.

This online survey of 3,472 COVID-19 patients across France and Mexico explores associations between self-reported olfactory loss and cognitive/affective complaints. While it documents symptom associations relevant to long COVID, it is an observational cross-sectional survey that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, and therefore does not meet criteria for inclusion in a clinical trials meta-analysis.

This case-control study compared neuropsychological performance between 20 long COVID patients with fatigue and 20 SARS-CoV-2 negative controls via telephone-based testing. Results show that post-COVID fatigue is significantly associated with decreased cognitive performance on standardized neuropsychological measures.

A cross-sectional survey of 535 COVID-19 survivors 1 year post-discharge assessed mental health outcomes including anxiety, depression, PTSD, fatigue, and sleep quality using standardized scales. Chronic disease history, smoking, and low education were identified as risk factors for poor psychological and physical outcomes in survivors.

Cross-sectional clinical phenotyping study of 157 post-COVID patients evaluating applicability of proposed subtypes (postintensive care syndrome, secondary diseases, fatigue, exacerbation, minimal complaints) using standardized neurological and psychological assessments. While the paper discusses treatment recommendations (SSRIs, psychotherapy, monitoring), it is a descriptive phenotyping study without an active intervention trial or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between persistent olfactory dysfunction and cognitive impairment in 241 long COVID patients in Brazil using standardized assessments (CCCRC and MoCA). Found a weak but significant association between olfactory severity and cognitive impairment (OR=2.87), suggesting olfactory dysfunction as a potential marker for cognitive monitoring.

This cross-sectional study assessed episodic memory function in 157 post-COVID condition patients versus 74 healthy controls using comprehensive neuropsychological testing. Patients with PCC showed significant impairment in memory encoding, learning, and retrieval processes, with findings relevant for characterizing cognitive deficits but no intervention or treatment evaluated.

A large-scale cross-sectional study of 793 patients (723 PASC, 70 PVS) assessing cognitive function, depression, and fatigue using standardized neuropsychological tests and inflammatory markers. Cognitive impairment was highly prevalent (61.7% working speed deficits, 54.7% attention deficits), associated with older age, lower education, depression, and elevated CRP, with similar patterns observed in post-vaccination syndrome.

Multicenter retrospective cohort study assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 respiratory symptoms at 11.2 months after hospital discharge in 1,950 COVID-19 survivors. Found 2.5% prevalence of long-term cough with no clear associated risk factors.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive and neuropsychological outcomes in 62 COVID-19 patients stratified by disease severity (outpatients vs. inpatients with hypoxemic pneumonia). Found that inpatients with hypoxia had greater impairments in attention and memory, while fatigue, depression, and anxiety were similarly high in both groups.

A cross-sectional study comparing cardiopulmonary function in 20 children with post-COVID-19 and 28 matched controls using exercise testing. Found significantly lower peak oxygen uptake in the post-COVID group, attributed to deconditioning rather than cardiac or pulmonary dysfunction.

A cross-sectional study examining brainstem raphe alterations in 70 long-COVID patients using transcranial sonography and their association with depressive and anxiety symptoms. Hypoechogenic brainstem raphe was found in 28.6% of patients and independently associated with higher depressive symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A multicentre cross-sectional cohort study comparing long COVID symptoms in children and adolescents infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant versus uninfected controls. Most PCS-associated symptoms were comparable between groups, though concentration disorders and impaired physical performance were more frequent in the COVID-19 group.

A cross-sectional study comparing long-COVID prevalence and clinical characteristics in 147 children with and without immunodeficiency using a parent-completed questionnaire. Immunocompetent children showed higher long-COVID prevalence (60% at 12 weeks vs 35.7% in immunocompromised) and greater impact on daily functioning, with immunocompromised children experiencing milder symptoms overall.

This cross-sectional study evaluates lung ultrasound and diaphragm excursion in 45 COVID-19 ARDS survivors to assess their relationship with dyspnea and exercise tolerance. While the study assesses long COVID sequelae (persistent dyspnea in post-ICU survivors), it is a diagnostic/observational study without any intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials analysis.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 366 UK long COVID patients to quantify productivity losses and informal care burden since infection. While directly relevant to long COVID, the paper is an observational survey without any treatment intervention—it measures economic impact rather than testing a therapy or intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 520 Arabic COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome, finding 25% developed persistent symptoms lasting ≥28 days. The study identified female sex, hospitalization during acute infection, and chronic diseases as significant risk factors, but did not evaluate any interventions or treatments.

Cross-sectional study of 2023 that classifies long COVID patients into five symptom clusters based on subjective symptoms at first outpatient visit and evaluates their background characteristics including autonomic dysfunction and work status. Study provides descriptive classification but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study comparing physical activity levels, respiratory and peripheral muscle strength, and pulmonary function in 54 young post-COVID-19 patients versus 46 controls at least 6 months after mild COVID-19 infection. Found that respiratory and peripheral muscle strength and physical activity levels were significantly reduced in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, with persistent dyspnea and fatigue.

This cross-sectional study examines the financial burden of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome in German patients, including employment status changes, income loss, and out-of-pocket payments for diagnostics and therapies. While it is about long COVID, it does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention—it only documents patients' financial experiences and their use of various paid services.

Cross-sectional study of 25,389 US adults examining family history of cancer as a risk factor for Long COVID using National Health Interview Survey data. Found that adults with family history of cancer were 1.26 times more likely to have Long COVID, with 30% of the association mediated through underlying health conditions.

This cross-sectional study compared left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) in 70 asymptomatic outpatients who recently recovered from COVID-19 versus 70 matched healthy controls using echocardiography. The COVID-19 group showed significantly impaired LV-GLS, suggesting subclinical myocardial dysfunction during early recovery, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study measuring flow-mediated dilation (FMD) to assess endothelial dysfunction in 59 COVID-19 patients and 33 controls two months post-infection. Found COVID-19 independently predicted endothelial dysfunction, but the study is observational without treatment intervention and therefore excluded from the treatment trial pipeline.

Secondary analysis of National Health Interview Survey data (2022-2023) examining cognitive difficulties in individuals with ME/CFS and long COVID. Found ME/CFS and long COVID significantly associated with reported cognitive impairments, with comorbid cases showing greatest risk.

A cross-sectional study of 318 long COVID patients assessing health-related quality of life using SF-36 and RehabNeQ instruments, stratified by symptom duration and symptom count. Finds that both mental and physical quality of life are significantly reduced compared to general population, with symptom burden and work ability as key drivers of these deficits.

This study analyzes the 100 most-viewed YouTube videos about long COVID, examining their sources, engagement metrics, and content. The paper is a descriptive analysis of media content rather than a clinical study or intervention trial, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

A cross-sectional study comparing symptom presentation and quality of life between people with ME/CFS, post-COVID condition, and healthy controls in Australia. The study found both patient cohorts experienced similar debilitating symptoms and significantly lower quality-of-life scores compared to controls, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A retrospective cross-sectional study assessing myocardial function and exercise capacity in 56 symptomatic long COVID patients, stratified by prior COVID-19 severity. Found subclinical left ventricular dysfunction (increased global wasted work, decreased work efficiency) and substantially reduced peak oxygen uptake, with severity being an independent predictor of myocardial dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study comparing pupillary light responses in 35 post-COVID subjects (71% with long COVID) versus 30 healthy controls using infrared pupillometry. Found significant alterations in pupillary contractile responses indicative of parasympathetic dysfunction, with correlations between symptom severity and pupil metrics, but no treatment intervention tested.

This epidemiological study analyzes long COVID prevalence and disability across demographic groups in the US using national survey data, finding higher rates among women, Hispanic people, sexual/gender minorities, and those without college degrees. The paper does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, focusing instead on prevalence patterns and workplace accommodation disparities.

Cross-sectional analysis of 414 long COVID patients identifying mental health symptoms through patient-generated text data, using BERTopic analysis to categorize anxiety (35%), depression (29%), cognitive impairment (22%), and mood disturbances. Study develops understanding of mental health impact but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional investigation comparing symptom clusters and patient-reported outcomes between people with ME/CFS and post-COVID condition (PCC). The study identifies associations between autonomic symptoms and functional impairment but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examined multidimensional correlates of long COVID symptom burden in 656 participants, using latent profile analysis to categorize participants into low, medium, and high symptom-burden groups. While the study identifies important social, behavioral, and healthcare factors associated with symptom severity, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional structural equation model analysis of 535 adults from the Quebec Action for Post-COVID cohort examining interrelationships among fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, activity/role functioning, and mental health in post-COVID-19 syndrome. Study identifies fatigue and self-reported cognitive concerns as key factors associated with mental health symptoms but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome and its impact on health-related quality of life among 249 healthcare workers at a Tunisian university hospital. Found that 65% experienced post-COVID syndrome with 28.6% reporting low overall quality of life, with gender, post-COVID status, and time off work significantly associated with QoL scores.

Cross-sectional survey of 350 COVID-19 recovered patients identifying new or worsening overactive bladder symptoms 10-14 weeks post-hospitalization, with median OAB symptom and quality-of-life scores reported by sex. The study documents the prevalence and burden of post-COVID genitourinary symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective follow-up study of individuals tested for SARS-CoV-2 at Geneva University Hospitals assessed the prevalence, severity, and impact of post-COVID fatigue and post-exertional malaise at 6+ months post-infection using standardized scales (ECOG, Chalder, DePaul). The study characterizes symptom burden and functional impairment in long COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining health service utilization patterns and barriers to care among US adults with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC). Finds that individuals with PCC history were significantly more likely to use various health services and report both financial and nonfinancial barriers to care compared to other US adults.

This national survey study examines self-reported long COVID symptoms among 409,087 working-age U.S. adults and their associations with demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. The paper documents that long COVID is disproportionately reported among Hispanic individuals and economically disadvantaged populations, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study validates the RECOVER PASC diagnostic scoring tool in 130 long COVID patients and 60 recovered controls to assess its sensitivity and specificity for LC diagnosis. The PASC score showed 100% specificity but limited 80% sensitivity, and the authors identified symptom combinations (loss of smell/taste, post-exertional malaise, sexual dysfunction) with superior diagnostic accuracy.

An observational cross-sectional study evaluating the Alcohol Sniff Test (AST) as a screening tool for post-viral olfactory dysfunction (PVOD) in patients with flu-like syndrome. While the paper mentions COVID-19 as one cause of PVOD, it is primarily focused on diagnostic tool validation rather than studying a treatment for long COVID patients.

A cross-sectional survey of 114 Irish senior physicians assessing burnout and long COVID prevalence during the pandemic. While the paper includes long COVID prevalence data (25% reported personal or colleague experience), it does not study or evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing caspase 3, caspase 8, and BDNF levels in individuals with and without COVID-19 to assess associations with psychiatric symptoms. Found elevated biomarkers in COVID-19 patients but no significant associations with symptom severity or psychiatric conditions.

This cross-sectional study compares gut microbiome composition and inflammatory markers between post-COVID-19 individuals and healthy controls. While it identifies significant alterations in microbiome diversity and inflammatory profiles in long COVID patients, it is observational without any intervention or treatment being tested.

This prospective cross-sectional study evaluates olfactory and gustatory symptoms in 76 patients with mild acute COVID-19 during a 2-week follow-up period. The study documents prevalence and time course of smell/taste loss during acute infection, not post-acute sequelae or long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing neurologic manifestations and cognitive profiles between post-hospitalization and non-hospitalized long COVID patients in Nigeria. Findings show high prevalence of brain fog, fatigue, and sleep problems, with some evidence of mild cognitive impairment on standardized assessments.

Cross-sectional study examining longer-term mental health consequences of COVID-19 infection (≥6 months post-infection) in 277 Black and White adults, with analysis of moderation by race and socioeconomic status. COVID-19 history was associated with significantly greater depressive, anxiety, PTSD, and insomnia symptoms, with education level moderating these relationships.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of chronic fatigue syndrome and post-traumatic stress disorder among 120 COVID-19 survivors 6 months post-infection using validated questionnaires. The study found low prevalence rates (CFS 2.5%, PTSD 5.8%) with no significant association between the two conditions, but did not test or evaluate any interventions.

A cross-sectional study assessing long-term persistent symptoms in 112 COVID-19 patients with and without diabetes mellitus at 9 months post-infection. Patients with diabetes reported significantly higher rates of fatigue, shortness of breath, and chest pain compared to non-diabetic patients.

Cross-sectional analysis of 50,402 COVID-19 patients in Germany identifying risk factors for long COVID syndrome development. Lipid metabolism disorders and obesity are identified as strong independent risk factors, along with age, female sex, and pre-existing conditions like asthma and depression.

A cross-sectional survey of 744 Saudi Arabian COVID-19 recovered patients assessing the prevalence and severity of persistent post-COVID symptoms. Found that 47.5% experienced ongoing symptoms, most commonly fatigue (25.4%), headache (15.9%), and myalgia (8.5%), with notable anxiety and depression rates.

Cross-sectional pilot study (n=67) measuring respiratory muscle function in long COVID patients ~5 months post-infection, comparing hospitalized vs non-hospitalized groups. Found respiratory muscle dysfunction in 88% of symptomatic patients, with pathological P0.1/PImax ratio associated with exercise intolerance and reduced functional status.

Cross-sectional survey of 909 post-COVID patients in Jena, Germany using cluster analysis of quality-of-life measures to identify post-COVID subgroups. Study found two distinct clusters: 29.4% with markedly diminished QoL (post-COVID disease) and 70.6% with near-normal QoL (post-COVID condition), suggesting heterogeneous disease impact.

Cross-sectional analysis of 2023 National Health Interview Survey data examining the association between asthma and long COVID prevalence in U.S. adults. Found that adults with asthma had significantly higher odds of long COVID (OR 1.58) and poor asthma control was associated with increased long COVID risk, but this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study from the German Ageing Survey examines associations between physician-diagnosed long COVID and psychosocial outcomes (depression, loneliness, social isolation, life satisfaction) in 4,017 middle-aged and older adults. While long COVID was associated with perceived social isolation (particularly in women), the study is observational without any treatment intervention and does not evaluate treatment outcomes.

Community-based cross-sectional survey of 562 adults in a Tribal community examining associations between nicotine use and COVID-19 health outcomes, including recovery time and disease severity. The study is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it observationally examines nicotine exposure as a risk factor, not a therapeutic intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life in 200 Indonesian individuals with long COVID at four recovery timepoints (< 6 months to > 24 months) using the SF-36 survey. The study found that mental health challenges were prevalent (56.1%) and persisted even after 24+ months of recovery, with fatigue, concentration difficulties, sleep disorders, and anxiety being common symptoms.

A mixed-methods cross-sectional survey examining long COVID symptoms and health outcomes in Black Americans, comparing qualitative and quantitative descriptions. The study found that Black adults with long COVID reported significantly worse mental health outcomes including anxiety, depression, and suicidal ideation, despite similar qualitative reporting of physical symptoms.

This case-control study compared cognitive function, sleep quality, depression, and fatigue between 45 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients and 60 healthy controls from April-December 2021. The PCS group showed significantly higher rates of cognitive impairment (13.3% vs 1.6%), depression (53.9% vs 25.9%), and sleep disturbances (53.9% vs 18.6%), though working memory performance did not differ between groups.

A cross-sectional survey of 843 members from three American Indian Reservation communities exploring attitudes and experiences of long COVID. The study found that 40% of COVID-19 survivors reported ongoing symptoms, with distinct symptom clusters associated with different sociodemographic factors, highlighting health and workforce sequelae in these communities.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 fatigue and depression among 361 confirmed COVID-19 cases in Saudi Arabia. Found 22.7% reported fatigue and identified COVID-19 severity and depression as significant predictors of post-COVID fatigue.

This cross-sectional study analyzes 2022-2023 BRFSS data to examine racial/ethnic, metropolitan, and healthcare access disparities in long COVID prevalence among U.S. adults. The study finds higher odds of long COVID among American Indian/Alaskan Native and Other/Multiracial respondents, and among non-metropolitan and uninsured populations, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 369 vaccinated individuals in Saudi Arabia examining the persistence of post-COVID-19 symptoms. Found that 54.8% experienced persistent symptoms 3-6 months after recovery and 29.1% reported symptoms lasting >6 months, with symptom duration varying by age group and vaccination timing.

Cross-sectional study of 105 long COVID patients examining how self-compassion and psychological flexibility moderate the relationship between physical symptoms and psychosocial impact. Found that both constructs significantly buffer the effect of symptom burden on daily life, suggesting they are important therapeutic targets for multidisciplinary rehabilitation.

This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 143 patients after mild COVID-19 infection using standardized instruments (SF-36, FSS, HADS, MMSE-2, SDMT). The study found that fatigue, depression, anxiety, and cognitive complaints were negatively correlated with all HRQoL domains, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study describing chronic pain characteristics in 143 COVID-19 ICU survivors nine months post-discharge, finding that 54% developed new-onset chronic pain predominantly from secondary causes (musculoskeletal, post-traumatic, neuropathic). The study characterizes pain patterns and their associations with psychological symptoms but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study develops a machine learning model to identify post-COVID condition cases from administrative health data in Alberta, Canada, achieving 96% accuracy in detecting PCC from healthcare utilization patterns. The study estimates PCC period prevalence at 9.3% in the general population but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper analyzes data from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey to quantify the relationship between COVID-19 (including symptoms lasting 3+ months) and health care-related financial toxicity in the US adult population. It finds that individuals with severe or prolonged COVID-19 symptoms are significantly more likely to experience financial hardship, delayed/forgone care, and medication nonadherence, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 254 healthcare workers at a Tunisian university hospital investigating the persistence of COVID-19 symptoms at 1-6 months post-infection. Found that >70% retained symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, anosmia, headache, memory problems), with persistence significantly associated with female gender, older age, non-smoking status, and asymptomatic initial presentation.

Cross-sectional analysis of 27,651 survey respondents comparing symptom profiles between long COVID, ME/CFS, and combined presentations. Found subjects with both conditions report higher rates of memory issues, anxiety, depression, fatigue, and reduced physical activity, suggesting potential overlap in pathophysiological mechanisms.

Cross-sectional survey of 253 long COVID patients in Scotland examining symptom prevalence, frequency, and severity. Found post-exertional malaise (95%), fatigue (85%), and cognitive impairment (68%) as most prevalent, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

A nationwide cross-sectional survey of 19,784 Japanese respondents assessing prolonged symptoms after COVID-19 and their impact on quality of life. The study identifies headache, chest discomfort, dysgeusia, and dysosmia as independently associated with long COVID and documents reduced health-related QOL, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study characterizing fatigue severity and laboratory markers (cortisol, cytokines) in 100 long COVID patients with fatigue-dominant symptoms. Findings show severe fatigue correlated with lower plasma cortisol levels, particularly for mental fatigue components, providing reference data for understanding postviral fatigue.

Cross-sectional survey of 2022 examining symptom prevalence, frequency, severity, and functional impact of long COVID in Scottish patients (n unclear from abstract). Study documents significant work disability, study impairment, and caregiving burden associated with fatigue, pain, and cognitive impairment, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of 2022 BRFSS data examining prevalence and determinants of long-term post-COVID conditions in US COVID survivors. Found 21.7% prevalence with associations to female sex, BMI, comorbidities, and lifestyle factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 24,803 US adults examining the association between obstructive sleep apnea and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). The study found obstructive sleep apnea was associated with increased odds of PASC-related symptoms, with this risk mitigated in patients receiving sleep apnea treatment.

This cross-sectional study analyzes health insurance coverage and healthcare access among U.S. working-age adults with long COVID using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data (n=18,117). While it documents that long COVID patients use healthcare services more frequently but face greater cost-related barriers to care, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of two nationwide surveys (BRFSS and NHIS) identifying demographic and clinical factors associated with long COVID prevalence. Finds that middle age, female sex, lack of college degree, and severe acute COVID-19 infection are associated with increased long COVID risk.

Cross-sectional survey study of 423 long COVID patients examining internal tremors and vibrations as a symptom phenotype. Participants with internal tremors/vibrations had worse quality of life and higher rates of new-onset mast cell and neurologic conditions compared to those without these symptoms.

Descriptive study of 441 long COVID patients from the Yale LISTEN cohort characterizing symptoms, treatments tried, and psychological/social/financial impacts. Does not evaluate efficacy of any specific treatment—participants self-reported prior treatment attempts without outcome assessment.

This study uses 2022 National Health Interview Survey data to identify factors associated with recovery from long COVID in US adults. It finds that 48.5% of those with long COVID reported recovery, with significant variations by age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, and initial COVID-19 severity, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 1,135 working-age COVID-19 survivors in British Columbia assessing health-related quality of life >2 years post-infection using the EQ-5D-5L instrument. Found that 19.2% with current post-COVID condition had significantly lower health utility and functional deficits compared to those without symptoms or who had recovered.

A cross-sectional survey of 253 long COVID patients in Scotland documenting symptom prevalence, frequency, severity, and duration. The study found post-exertional malaise (95%), fatigue (85%), and cognitive impairment (68%) as the most prevalent symptoms, with socioeconomic deprivation associated with symptom burden.

Secondary analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining prevalence and types of complementary medicine use among US adults with post-COVID-19 symptoms. Finds 46.2% of post-COVID respondents used complementary medicine in the past 12 months, with higher use of mind-body medicine and massage.

Prospective survey of 437 COVID-19 patients assessing prevalence and predictors of post-acute sequelae (PASC). Found 34.9% had persistent symptoms, with fatigue, sleep issues, and anosmia most common; female sex and psychological impact were key predictive factors.

Cross-sectional study examining echocardiographic changes in 100 COVID-19 patients within 3 months of infection, stratified by disease severity and symptom persistence. Found high prevalence of right and left ventricular dysfunction, with worse cardiac function associated with moderate-to-severe disease and persistent symptoms.

This cross-sectional study examined peripheral microvascular endothelial dysfunction in 92 symptomatic long COVID patients using peripheral arterial tonometry and measured NT-proBNP levels over time. While 41% of patients showed microvascular endothelial dysfunction with associations to NT-proBNP increases, this is an observational study without treatment intervention—it only characterizes disease pathophysiology without testing any therapeutic intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 30,130 Japanese individuals assessing health-related quality of life and somatic symptoms in post-COVID patients versus controls using EQ-5D-5L and SSS-8 scales. Found that COVID-19 survivors, especially those with severe disease, had significantly lower quality of life and higher somatic symptom burden, with vaccination associated with better outcomes.

This cross-sectional study examined metabolic profiles in 39 diabetic patients post-COVID-19 at a Tunisian nutrition institute. The study found that COVID-19 infection disrupted metabolic control in diabetic patients, including worsening glycemic control, lipid abnormalities, and increased cardiovascular risk, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional descriptive study examined residual symptoms of post-COVID syndrome in 39 diabetic patients at a Tunisian nutrition institute. The study found that 92.3% of diabetic patients experienced post-COVID symptoms, predominantly fatigue and psychomotor slowing (79.5%), with dyspnea, dry cough, anosmia, chronic headaches, and memory disorders also commonly reported.

A prospective cross-sectional study comparing smell and taste function in 35 COVID-19 recovered patients versus 35 COVID-naïve controls using standardized testing (UPSIT and Burghart tests). Results showed no significant difference in chemosensory recovery between groups, suggesting patients who experience COVID-related smell/taste disturbance regain sensory ability similar to pre-COVID baseline.

Secondary analysis of 2022 BRFSS data comparing long COVID prevalence between 17,362 cancer survivors and non-cancer individuals in the US. Found cancer survivors have 24.0% long COVID prevalence vs 21.6% in non-cancer individuals (adjusted OR=1.17), with higher relative risk in those under 45.

This cross-sectional survey of 1,455 ED patients from 11 US sites assessed awareness, understanding, and receipt of care for long COVID symptoms in underserved populations. The study found high prevalence of long COVID symptoms (33.2% with >1 month, 20.3% with >3 months) but limited awareness and understanding, particularly among African American and Latino/a patients, with significant gaps in care access.

Cross-sectional study of 264 long COVID patients examining associations between physical activity levels and cardiorespiratory fitness, sleep quality, and quality of life. Found that greater physical activity was associated with better fitness, sleep quality, and quality of life, with gender differences in cardiorespiratory outcomes.

Cross-sectional study measuring prevalence of depression (27.9%) and anxiety (43.6%) among COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia using DASS-21 and Brief-COPE scales. Found that hospitalized patients had higher anxiety levels and that approach coping strategies reduced while avoidant coping increased odds of depression and anxiety.

Population-based telephone survey of 121 adults hospitalized for COVID-19 in Quebec assessing long-term functional deficits at ≥2 months post-infection using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Screen. Found 94% reported increased fatigue, 90% deteriorated global health, with significant reductions in mobility, employment, and daily activities; time since diagnosis was associated with functional outcomes.

A cross-sectional survey of 491 long COVID patients examining symptom profiles and their association with self-efficacy for symptom management using latent profile analysis. The study identified four distinct symptom burden profiles and found that higher self-efficacy was associated with lower symptom burden, but does not test an intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between PTSD symptoms and health-related quality of life in 636 post-COVID-19 patients in primary care settings. Found that 21.4% had PTSD symptoms and over half had affected quality of life, with PTSD significantly associated with worse HRQoL outcomes.

Cross-sectional analysis of 1,913 European adults ≥50 years examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and long COVID prevalence, stratified by chronic multimorbidity. Finds that vaccination is associated with lower long COVID rates only among those with chronic multimorbidity, not in those without.

Cross-sectional study examining autoantibodies targeting vasoregulatory and autonomic receptors in 72 long-COVID patients versus controls. Found significantly elevated autoantibody levels in long-COVID patients that correlate with neurological symptom severity including fatigue and cognitive impairment.

This cross-sectional study evaluated long COVID prevalence (64%) and associated hematological and biochemical parameters in 150 mild COVID-19 survivors at 6-15 months post-infection compared to 75 healthy controls. The study found differential biochemical markers (hemoglobin, RBC, WBC, IL-6, ALT, ALP, vitamin D3) between groups and across recovery timepoints, suggesting distinct metabolic and biochemical status at different intervals following infection.

Cross-sectional survey of 96 convalescent COVID-19 patients examining correlation between immune markers and self-reported depression during early recovery phase. Study found associations between depression and elevated white blood cells/neutrophils but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional physician chart audit describes clinical features, diagnostic pathways, and treatment approaches for POTS in 599 patients, comparing 361 pre-COVID cases with 238 post-COVID cases across 153 physicians in multiple countries. The study documents real-world management patterns, diagnostic delays, and treatment escalation from non-pharmacological to pharmacological interventions, highlighting similarities in diagnostic and treatment approaches between post-COVID and non-COVID POTS cohorts.

This cross-sectional MRI study examines blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability in 97 long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms compared to 31 recovered controls. The study finds significantly elevated BBB permeability in LC individuals associated with motor dysfunction, but this is an observational biomarker study without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive and neurophysiological characteristics of long COVID patients versus recovered COVID-19 controls using qEEG analysis, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, and Self-Rating Questionnaire. Found lower memory scores and altered temporal-occipital connectivity in long COVID group, indicating persistent cognitive deficits and brain fog, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study examines executive function deficits in 8,102 Norwegian participants comparing 4,183 SARS-CoV-2 positive individuals to uninfected controls using the BRIEF-A questionnaire. The study found significantly higher rates of executive deficits, particularly in metacognition and working memory, in the SARS-CoV-2 positive group 6-12 months post-infection, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional study investigating whether fatigue and depressive symptoms are associated with altered reward and effort processing in decision-making at different timepoints after COVID-19 infection. The study found that greater fatigue in the long-term phase (beyond 12 weeks) is more strongly associated with reduced reward sensitivity compared to the early phase, suggesting potential neural dysregulation in post-COVID-19 fatigue.

Cross-sectional study of 500 participants in Jordan assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms and treatment approaches. Found high burden of sensory, psychiatric, and other complications, with distinct symptom patterns associated with different vaccine types; primarily a descriptive epidemiological survey rather than a treatment intervention study.

Cross-sectional study examining the Glittre-ADL test as a functional assessment tool in 37 post-COVID-19 patients, correlating performance with pulmonary function and muscle strength measures. The study finds that lung function and quadriceps strength are strong predictors of functional performance but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between childhood trauma and mental health outcomes in 641 participants (487 with post-COVID syndrome, 154 controls) recruited through the DEFEAT platform. The study finds that childhood trauma, particularly emotional abuse, is significantly associated with higher rates of depression and anxiety in PCS patients, with lower health-related quality of life, suggesting the need for trauma-informed care approaches.

Population-based cross-sectional survey comparing prevalence of disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) before and after the COVID-19 pandemic across UK and US populations. Study found increased DGBI prevalence post-pandemic and identified long COVID as a significant associated factor, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional observational study examining chronic pain prevalence in 242 patients at least 3 months after hospitalization for COVID-19. Found 31.8% reported chronic pain, with female sex and obesity identified as risk factors, but this is a prevalence survey with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study examined associations between fatigue, dysautonomia, depression, and cognitive impairment in 141 long-COVID patients referred to a neuro-long-COVID service. The study used self-reporting questionnaires to compare fatigued and non-fatigued patients and identified significant associations between fatigue and autonomic dysfunction, cognitive impairment, and depression.

Retrospective cross-sectional study evaluating the clinical significance of low-field MRI lung opacity in 62 post-acute COVID-19 patients. Found that lung opacity severity correlated with decreased DLCO on pulmonary function tests but was not associated with patient-reported outcomes.

Cross-sectional study comparing skeletal muscle energy metabolism and oxidative capacity during exercise in 71 long COVID patients versus 63 healthy controls. Found reduced peak fat oxidation and impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics in long COVID patients, with muscle power output mediating this relationship.

Cross-sectional analysis of 2023 BRFSS survey data examining prevalence and sociodemographic/health factors associated with long COVID among cancer survivors. Found 15.2% of COVID-positive cancer survivors reported long COVID, with associations to age, sex, vaccination status, and comorbid conditions.

A nationwide random sampling cross-sectional survey in France (August-November 2022) estimated long COVID prevalence in the adult population using multiple definitions, finding 4.0% prevalence using WHO-PCC criteria. The study examined variations by sociodemographic and infection characteristics but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional pilot study examining vagus and phrenic nerve dysfunction in 30 post-COVID-19 patients compared to 14 COVID-recovered and 16 uninfected controls using ultrasound and respiratory testing. The study found structural and functional nerve abnormalities in PCC patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive performance between college students who had COVID-19 and uninfected controls using data from 24 cognitive psychology experiments. The findings indicate that COVID-19 infection has minimal impact on cognition in university students, contradicting concerns about long-term cognitive impairment from long COVID.

Cross-sectional survey of 3,251 U.S. adults examining the frequency and duration of long-term symptoms (>4 weeks) and healthcare utilization among adults with and without disabilities following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found that those who tested positive had significantly higher odds of reporting long-term symptoms, with healthcare utilization approximately twofold higher among adults with disabilities.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between Long COVID and housing stability/accessibility among 1533 people with disabilities (514 with Long COVID, 1019 without). Finds Long COVID associated with higher rates of housing instability, financial concerns, and home maintenance issues, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzed how vaccination status and SARS-CoV-2 re-infections influenced changes in sports-related physical activity one month after infection in 5,829 adults. The study documents a decline in physical activity post-infection but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance in 81,337 participants using the Great British Intelligence Test, examining associations between COVID-19 infection history and cognitive deficits. Found significant cognitive deficits in COVID-19 survivors including non-hospitalized cases, suggesting multi-domain cognitive impact from SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Cross-sectional survey study (N=212) investigating life satisfaction among long COVID patients and predictors using mixture model analysis. Found heterogeneous patterns: social support significantly predicted life satisfaction in one cluster but not the other, suggesting tailored psychosocial interventions may improve quality of life.

A multicenter cross-sectional study assessing long-term quality of life, sleep patterns, psychological health, and work ability in 491 severe COVID-19 survivors 18+ months post-discharge. The study found persistent psychological disorders, sleep disturbances, and poor work ability despite overall physiological improvement.

This cross-sectional pilot study assessed long COVID prevalence and characteristics 7-12 months post-hospitalization among 145 patients from a safety-net hospital serving predominantly Black and Hispanic populations in Chicago. The study found 34% reported persistent symptoms, with acute COVID-19 severity being a significant risk factor for long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing neurocognitive function and brain structure in 75 participants: healthy controls, COVID-19 survivors without brain fog, and COVID-19 survivors with brain fog. Found persistent cognitive deficits and structural brain alterations (reduced gray matter, altered network connectivity) even after mild infection, particularly in those with brain fog.

Cross-sectional descriptive study of 1,047 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients in Colombia documenting symptom prevalence and demographics. Reports high rates of fatigue (53.3%), dyspnea (40.3%), arthralgia (43%), and sleep disorders (35.7%), with 72% experiencing four or more symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 288 elderly adults with post-COVID condition in the Brazilian Amazon examining disability and self-care capacity using the WHODAS 2.0 assessment. Found that older age (≥70 years) and shortness of breath are associated with increased disability scores.

This multicentre cross-sectional study compared cognitive function in 270 long COVID patients versus two control groups using web-based reaction time and vigilance tasks. The study identified pronounced cognitive slowing in long COVID patients that was not explained by comorbidities, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study assessed the frequency and characteristics of long COVID-19 in 30 heart transplant recipients through telephone surveys and chart reviews.
