While it confirms long COVID occurs in this population with significant morbidity, it is an observational descriptive study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study comparing prevalence of fibromyalgia syndrome and anxiety in rheumatic disease patients versus controls who recovered from COVID-19. Finds significantly higher rates of fibromyalgia (22.5% vs 12%) and anxiety (27% vs 16%) in RD patients post-COVID, with severity, diabetes, and anxiety as predictors.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 239 Iranian COVID-19 survivors to assess the prevalence of musculoskeletal symptoms in the post-acute phase. The study found that 98.74% of patients experienced persistent musculoskeletal symptoms, with fatigue being the most common (91.2%), but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional cohort study comparing COVID-19 and long COVID outcomes in 732 Chinese psoriasis patients treated with IL-23 inhibitor versus other therapies. IL-23 inhibitor treatment was associated with decreased risk of COVID-19 and long COVID, with treated patients more likely to be asymptomatic after recovery.

Cross-sectional online survey comparing health-related quality of life and social participation across 3,188 German participants with long COVID, recovered from COVID-19, and never infected. Long COVID participants showed significantly lower quality of life and social participation scores compared to both comparison groups.

A cross-sectional study of 100 adults (ages 18-70) examining the effects of long COVID on memory and cognitive function. The study documents memory impairment and cognitive issues as part of the broader long-term health sequelae following COVID-19 infection.

Cross-sectional study comparing myocardial work and exercise capacity in 52 severe COVID-19 survivors versus 31 controls using echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Findings show significantly reduced aerobic capacity, lower myocardial efficiency, and abnormal heart rate response in COVID-19 survivors, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study evaluating sexual dysfunction prevalence and risk factors among 391 long COVID patients at a multidisciplinary COVID clinic. Sexual dysfunction was reported by 36% of men and 28% of women, significantly associated with age, long COVID symptoms (cough, chest pain, paresthesia), and emotional distress.

Observational cross-sectional study evaluating associations between lung function and endothelial dysfunction in 32 long COVID patients (mean 32 months post-infection). Found impaired endothelial function and significant correlation between KCO (lung diffusion) and vascular response, suggesting persistent cardiovascular complications in long COVID recovery.

Cross-sectional study of 439 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors in Brazil assessing long COVID symptoms, risk factors, and quality of life 2-12 months post-infection. Found 84% reported persistent symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, arthralgia, depression/anxiety), with ICU admission and dysgeusia as independent risk factors.

Cross-sectional survey of 460 long COVID patients examining the relationship between social support and psychological resilience, mediated by personal mastery and self-esteem. Study found that instrumental social support protects long haulers by promoting resilience through self-esteem and personal mastery.

Cross-sectional study investigating the relationship between TFPI gene polymorphisms, D-dimer levels, and post-COVID-19 condition in 144 patients. Found no significant associations between TFPI polymorphisms and PCC development, though TFPI -33T>C homozygosity may predict lower hospitalization risk during acute COVID-19.

A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between HLA alleles, KIR receptors, and long COVID development in 153 COVID-19 patients from Spain. Findings show HLA-A*03 is less frequent in long COVID patients and is associated with enhanced CD8+ T cell and NK cell responses.

Cross-sectional survey of 136 long-COVID patients recruited from online support groups to assess prevalence and severity of mast cell activation (MCA) symptoms compared to general population controls and MCAS patients. Found that post-COVID long-COVID subjects had MCA symptom profiles identical to untreated MCAS patients, suggesting mast cell dysfunction may underlie part of long-COVID pathophysiology.

Cross-sectional study estimating PCC prevalence among 1,546 COVID-19 patients in Alexandria, Egypt (June 2022–February 2023) and investigating associated risk factors. Found 49.2% reported PCC symptoms; primary manifestations were shortness of breath (94.2%), mood changes (13.9%), and fatigue (8.8%), with older age, hospitalization, and comorbidities (asthma, hypertension, diabetes) as significant risk factors.

Population-based cross-sectional study of 9,752 German employees assessing work ability 6-12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Identifies post-COVID symptom clusters (neurocognitive impairment, fatigue, mental disorders) associated with reduced work ability but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID among 486 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia, finding that 61% reported persistent symptoms including fatigue, breathlessness, and loss of smell. The study identifies demographic patterns and symptom burden but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 164 healthcare workers who recovered from COVID-19, assessing post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms months after infection. Found 48% of participants reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue being the most common (71%), but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Cross-sectional analysis of menopause symptom prevalence in 122 women attending post-COVID syndrome clinics in England. Study found high prevalence of menopause symptoms in women aged 40-54, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A multicenter cross-sectional study of 1,011 Greek patients with long COVID documenting clinical presentation and symptom burden across multiple organ systems. The study is descriptive/observational with no intervention tested, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study investigating circulating and urinary inflammatory mediators and extracellular vesicles in post-COVID condition patients stratified by hospitalization status during acute infection. Found higher urinary extracellular vesicles and specific immune mediators in hospitalized post-COVID patients, suggesting remnant renal inflammatory processes.

Cross-sectional study examining psychological distress and its predictive factors (cognitive failures, avoidance, rumination, injustice perception) in long COVID patients recruited from a hospital clinic and online. Found that these factors significantly predicted psychological distress but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 44,652 young adults examining the association between post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) and serious psychological distress, with prior mental health diagnosis as a moderator. Finds PASC associated with 53% increased odds of psychological distress, with stronger association in those without prior mental health diagnosis.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairments in 194 long-COVID patients at a clinic, comparing their performance to age/sex/education-matched controls. Finds 44-53% of patients have clinically relevant cognitive impairments, particularly in global cognition, working memory, and executive function, with associations to poorer work function and quality of life.

Secondary analysis of Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data examining associations between anxiety/depression symptoms and social vulnerabilities (expenses, employment, food, housing, insurance) among long COVID patients across racial/ethnic groups. Found that social vulnerabilities partially mediated racial disparities in anxiety and depression outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between social network characteristics and depressive/anxiety symptoms in 410 long COVID patients from Germany. Found that larger social networks and living with others were associated with fewer depressive and anxiety symptoms, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of probable post-COVID cardiac sequelae (PCCS) among 336 healthcare workers in India, finding 11.9% prevalence with higher risk in females, hypertensive individuals, and those with moderate-severe acute COVID. The study also examined health-seeking behavior, finding that 55% of those with PCCS did not seek further evaluation.

A nationally representative cross-sectional telephone survey of 3,143 Rwandan COVID-19 survivors characterizing the prevalence and factors associated with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). The study found 34% PASC prevalence with leading symptoms including back pain, headache, dizziness, and fatigue, identifying women, older adults, and those with multiple infections as at higher risk.

Cross-sectional study of 165 older adults hospitalized for COVID-19, assessing prevalence and patterns of persistent symptoms 76.8 days post-discharge. Found 83% reported at least one persistent symptom, with fatigue (53.1%) and dyspnea (51.5%) most common, but no specific treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study analyzing the association between long COVID and food insecurity among low-income US adults using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data. Found that individuals with long COVID had significantly higher risk of marginal and low/very low food insecurity, particularly among non-participants in food assistance programs.

Cross-sectional study comparing neuropsychiatric symptoms of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients. Found no significant differences in neuropsychiatric manifestations between the two groups.

This cross-sectional study analyzes medication utilization patterns and polypharmacy prevalence in 414 post-COVID syndrome patients from a Quebec cohort, finding that 11.7% used 5+ medications with notable anticholinergic/sedative burden and drug-drug interaction risks. The study observes medication use patterns in PCS patients rather than testing or evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptoms in 18-20 year-olds with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection versus test-negative controls in England at median 7 months post-testing. Study found high symptom prevalence in both groups (61.5% test-positive, 47.5% test-negative) with no significant difference in quality of life, though test-positives reported significantly more tiredness.

This cross-sectional study examined predictive variables (physical exertion, heart rate, oxygen saturation) for assessing physical activity levels in 34 adults with long COVID-19 syndrome using the 6-Minute Walk Test and IPAQ assessment. The study identified Borg Dyspnoea Scale, maximum oxygen uptake, and resting oxygen saturation as key predictors of physical activity in long COVID patients, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing health-related quality of life in COVID-19 survivors 10 months after acute infection using the EQ-5D instrument. Found that anxiety/depression and mobility were most affected, with worse outcomes in females, older patients, and those with comorbidities or prior hospitalization.

This cross-sectional survey describes acute and long COVID-19 symptoms among 80- and 90-year-old Swedish adults, identifying predictive factors for symptom development. The study finds that 37% reported long COVID general symptoms and 35% reported orofacial symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing gait patterns in 12 individuals with prior COVID-19 history versus 20 controls using inertial sensor analysis. Found that post-COVID individuals exhibited significantly more asymmetrical gait patterns despite full clinical recovery, suggesting persistent neuromotor effects.

Cross-sectional online survey of 1,046 Australian adults with type 2 diabetes assessing long COVID prevalence and its impact on diabetes management and physical activity. Found 30% reported long COVID symptoms, with significant impacts on blood glucose control, weight, and exercise capacity, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

This study evaluates the frequency and clinical relevance of post-COVID-19 condition in childcare facility employees using both prospective and retrospective questionnaire data. It documents symptom prevalence (fatigue, impairment of focus, reduced stamina, headache, dyspnea) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study evaluating functional capacity (Glittre-ADL test) in 42 men with long COVID 3 years post-infection, alongside measures of lung function, muscle strength, and quality of life. Found functional capacity mostly normal but not reflected in muscle strength or QoL improvements, requiring continued monitoring.

A cross-sectional study comparing the prevalence of post COVID-19 condition (symptoms lasting ≥2 months within 3 months of onset) between patients infected with Omicron versus other SARS-CoV-2 strains using propensity score matching. The study found significantly lower prevalence of post-COVID conditions in the Omicron group (5.6%) compared to the control group (55.6%).

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and predictive factors of post-COVID-19 neuropsychiatric symptoms in 180 children and adolescents. Findings show higher neuropsychiatric symptom prevalence in adolescents, with distinct risk factors identified for each age group, and vaccination associated with reduced cognitive symptoms in adolescents.

This cross-sectional surveillance study assessed long COVID symptoms in 4,047 residents of Toyonaka City, Japan, using a mobile app and paper survey, finding a 5.2% prevalence of persistent symptoms 30 days post-infection. The study identifies risk factors (BMI, severe acute illness, variant strain) and notes declining prevalence with the Omicron variant's dominance.

This cross-sectional survey of 21,108 Japanese individuals examined the prevalence and temporal patterns of persistent COVID-19 symptoms, finding that various symptoms including pain, sensory loss, and cognitive impairment were associated with COVID-19 history 2-6 months or >12 months post-infection. While the study characterizes long COVID symptom burden and duration, it is observational without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional survey of 457 post-COVID patients examining factors associated with symptom development and persistence. Study identified female sex, younger age, and low BMI as key risk factors for various post-COVID symptoms, but conducted no intervention testing.

A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 360 COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and natural history of post-COVID conditions (PCCs) at 1, 2, and 3 years post-infection. The study identifies demographic and clinical factors associated with PCC persistence beyond 2 years, finding that lower BMI, underlying medical conditions, and multiple early symptoms predict longer symptom duration.

A national representative cross-sectional study in Saudi Arabia characterizing symptoms and conditions occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 314,821 confirmed COVID-19 cases. The study found that 22.5% of patients experienced late/persistent symptoms, with anosmia, ageusia, fatigue, dyspnea, and cough being the most common post-acute manifestations.

Cross-sectional survey of 5,053 UK healthcare workers assessing prevalence and impact of persistent symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection across vaccination and variant periods. Found persistent symptoms in 21.6-32.7% of participants with significant work-related impacts, but this is an observational epidemiological study without treatment intervention.

National cross-sectional survey of 5,946 COVID-19 patients assessing persistent symptoms at least 4 weeks post-infection in Saudi Arabia. Found 79.4% experienced unresolved symptoms including fatigue (53.5%), muscle ache (38.2%), and loss of smell (35.0%), with female sex and comorbidities as predictors of delayed recovery.

This cross-sectional study assessed nutritional risk in 159 elderly COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia using NRS-2002 and MNA-sf screening tools. The study found associations between age, BMI, vaccination status, and cardiovascular disease with malnutrition risk, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey comparing long-COVID symptoms in pregnant versus non-pregnant women in Ecuador, based on 457 self-reported online responses. Found that 54.1% reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue, hair loss, and concentration difficulties most common in pregnant women.

A cross-sectional survey of 73 twice-vaccinated hospital employees examining the incidence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms 8 weeks after post-vaccination SARS-CoV-2 infection. Study found that 31.5% reported post-acute sequelae, with fatigue, dysgeusia, dysosmia, headache, and concentration difficulties being strongly associated with symptom persistence, particularly in those with initial high symptom burden.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 83 individuals in Chile to estimate the frequency and characteristics of post-COVID-19 symptoms, finding that 80.7% reported persistent symptoms with sleep disturbances, anxiety, and memory problems being most common. The study identified symptom severity risk factors but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 243 vaccinated healthcare workers in Saudi Arabia assessing long COVID symptoms after acute infection. Found low prevalence of symptoms persisting >3 months (mainly hair loss, cough, diarrhea) with no significant associations between symptom persistence and demographic or clinical characteristics.

This cross-sectional study analyzes Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data from June-October 2022 to examine racial, ethnic, and sex disparities in long COVID incidence and cognitive symptomology among U.S. adults. Findings show Black, Hispanic, and female COVID survivors have higher long COVID prevalence (3+ months), with varying symptom patterns across demographic groups.

A nationwide cross-sectional survey of 130,443 Danish COVID-19 survivors assessed the prevalence and risk factors for de novo widespread musculoskeletal post-COVID pain. The study found 5.3% of nonhospitalized survivors reported new widespread pain at ~14 months post-infection, with older age, female sex, higher BMI, and history of migraine and other conditions identified as significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional survey investigated the prevalence and risk factors of de novo post-COVID pain in 4,712 previously hospitalized Danish COVID-19 survivors at 21 months post-infection. The study found that 18.0% reported multitype post-COVID pain, with female sex, higher BMI, ICU admission, anxiety, and younger age as significant risk factors.

Cross-sectional survey of 240 participants examining long COVID symptom patterns and associated distress using Latent Class Analysis. Study identifies three distinct symptom classes and demonstrates that multiple COVID-19 infections increase symptom severity and distress, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey study examining relationships between pain, fatigue, disease impact, and psychological factors with physical function in post-COVID-19 syndrome, fibromyalgia, and chronic fatigue syndrome patients (n=707). Results show disease impact and fatigue consistently predict physical function, while pain interference, dyspnea, sleep disturbance, and psychological factors have variable relationships across conditions.

Cross-sectional study evaluating cognitive dysfunction in 50 long COVID patients using comprehensive neuropsychological testing and symptom scales. Found significant impairments in attention, executive function, processing speed, and episodic memory, with correlations to olfactory dysfunction and sleep quality.

This cross-sectional study of 693 participants examines risk and protective factors for long COVID symptom severity using network analysis, assessing gender, prior mental health, COVID-19 severity, and social connectedness. The study identifies prior mental health conditions and lower social connectedness as risk factors for severe post-COVID symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional population study examining associations between somatic symptom disorder, depression, anxiety, and persistent symptoms with daily life impairment in post-COVID patients. Finds that fatigue and dyspnea are strongest predictors of daily life impairment, and somatic symptom disorder may play an important role in post-COVID syndrome.

Cross-sectional descriptive study comparing clinical, demographic, and lifestyle characteristics between 104 long COVID patients and 83 recovered individuals in Western India, with observations extending up to four years post-infection. Fatigue (79.8%), cough, and anxiety were the most persistent symptoms; severe acute COVID-19, Remdesivir use, and mechanical ventilation were associated with increased odds of developing long COVID.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, CRP, TNF-α) and neuropsychiatric symptoms in 80 PASC patients approximately 6 months post-infection. Found elevated IL-6 and CRP in over one-third of participants, associated with fatigue, anxiety, depression, cognitive impairment, and reduced quality of life.

Cross-sectional analysis of the prospective CovILD cohort examining how persistent somatic symptoms shape illness perception in long COVID patients one year post-infection. Found that fatigue, physical performance, and symptom count—not cardiac or pulmonary imaging findings—drive illness perception, suggesting psychological interventions targeting illness beliefs could improve outcomes.

This pre-registered cross-sectional study compared stress, anxiety, and depression severity among 2,872 US adults with no history, previous history, or current long COVID symptoms. Individuals with current and previous long COVID reported significantly greater psychological symptom burden compared to those with no history of long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing prevalence of depressive symptoms in 1,247 French adults with and without long COVID using PHQ-9 screening. Found long COVID patients 4-fold more likely to have depressive symptoms, with three depressive symptoms independently associated with long COVID diagnosis.

Cross-sectional survey of 4,316 US adults examining associations between trait forgiveness and physical/mental health in individuals with and without long COVID. Found that long COVID patients reported significantly less self-forgiveness and that forgiveness dimensions were associated with health outcomes, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 110 post-COVID patients assessing cognitive function via standardized neuropsychological tests and mental health screening. Found high prevalence of cognitive deficits (verbal fluency, working speed, delayed recall, attention) but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Cross-sectional analysis of 452 post-COVID participants examining the prevalence and biopsychosocial correlates of acute versus chronic fatigue. Found that depression and somatic distress are strongly associated with both forms of fatigue, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional study compares social contact behavior between 49 post-COVID patients and 49 healthy controls, finding reduced touch frequency, lower satisfaction with socializing, and increased preferred interpersonal distance in post-COVID patients. The study is observational with no intervention tested, making it ineligible for the treatment trials pipeline.

This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed the prevalence and determinants of long COVID conditions (PCCs) among stroke survivors using the 2022 BRFSS dataset, finding PCCs in 30.6% of stroke survivors compared to 22.4% of non-stroke survivors. Key risk factors for PCCs in stroke survivors included female sex, stroke-belt residence, pulmonary disease, and depression, while age above 64 years was protective.

This study analyzes Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 2022 to assess health-related quality of life among stroke survivors with post-COVID conditions in the US. It found that post-COVID conditions were associated with worse self-reported general health and more days with compromised mental/physical health, though the association was not statistically significant in multivariate analysis.

This cross-sectional study measures serum concentrations of 14 metals in 25 recovered COVID-19 patients versus 38 healthy controls at 6+ months post-discharge. The findings show persistent abnormal metal homeostasis and disrupted metabolic processes in recovered patients, suggesting long-term biochemical sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

This cross-sectional survey study examines how vicarious experience with long COVID (knowing someone who suffered from it) influences vaccination intentions through protection motivation theory dimensions. The study finds that knowing long COVID patients increases perceived risk and vaccine efficacy but decreases self-efficacy, ultimately associating with higher vaccination intentions—but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study evaluating whether maximum phonation time tests can predict forced vital capacity impairment in post-COVID-19 patients. Findings show MPT has only moderate discriminatory power and is not a reliable indicator of pulmonary function in this population.

Cross-sectional analysis of employed US respondents from the 2022 National Health and Wellness Survey examining work productivity losses (absenteeism and presenteeism) among adults with physician-identified long COVID. The study found substantial heterogeneity in activity limitations, with presenteeism ranging from 24.2% to 92.8% across tertiles and strong associations between activity limitations and depression/anxiety, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining prevalence of dysphonia and voice disorders in 160 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection in Lombardy. While dysphonia was common (43.7%), this study focuses on acute COVID-19 symptoms during active infection, not long COVID sequelae, and includes no treatment intervention.

An observational cross-sectional study of 1,366 Ecuadorian outpatients examining post-COVID-19 symptoms and their severity across different initial infection levels. The study found that 64.3% had symptoms 4-6 weeks post-infection, with fatigue (67.3%) and headache (45.2%) being most common, and identified risk factors including sedentary lifestyle and pre-existing comorbidities.

This study analyzes nationally representative data from Mexico's 2022 Health and Nutrition Survey to characterize the epidemiology of long COVID and identify determinants of PASC prevalence. It is a secondary analysis of survey data without any intervention or treatment component, making it ineligible for the treatment trials pipeline.

Observational multi-center cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID sequelae among 679 healthcare workers 12-52 weeks post-infection. Found 30.34% prevalence of COVID sequelae (fatigue, insomnia, dyspnea, arthralgia), with severity of acute illness, female gender, advanced age, and comorbidities as significant risk factors.

Population-based cross-sectional survey assessing the burden of long COVID symptoms in three districts of Haryana, India by linking to a prior seroprevalence study. Found cough as the only statistically significant persistent symptom after adjustment, with higher physical morbidity in women, but did not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) results in 200 patients with and without post-COVID-19 syndrome, conducted 45-120 days post-infection. Patients with post-COVID syndrome showed significantly lower peak VO2 and higher symptom occurrence during exercise, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study of 384 recovered COVID-19 patients in Dhaka examining prevalence of long-term physical and psychological complications at 6 months post-discharge. Found high rates of general weakness (58.5%), insomnia (82.0%), and age-related differences in dementia prevalence and hospital stay duration, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Community-based cross-sectional study of 12,789 adults infected with Omicron in December 2022–January 2023, assessed one year later for long COVID prevalence and health outcomes. Found 7.8% experienced long COVID (5.1% persistent), with fatigue and post-exertional malaise most common; no intervention was tested or evaluated.

This cross-sectional survey assessed the prevalence of functional, psychological, and social complaints in 200-300 patients 2-3 months after hospitalization for severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study describes persistent symptoms, identifies risk factors, and characterizes healthcare and psychosocial support needs in this emerging long COVID population.

Cross-sectional survey of 107 people with multiple sclerosis assessing post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence and risk factors, stratified by vaccination, infection frequency, and disease-modifying therapy categories. Found 6.5% PCS prevalence associated with category I DMTs and repeated infections, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study using nailfold capillaroscopy to evaluate microvascular changes in 97 participants (52 acute COVID-19, 45 convalescent including long COVID). Found increased capillary hemorrhages in convalescent group (40%) vs acute (17%), but no clinically significant structural differences in capillary width or density.

Survey of 1,000 dialysis patients at 6 months post-COVID-19 infection to characterize long COVID sequelae prevalence and associated risk factors. Found 17.9% (179/1000) experienced at least one sequela, with muscle loss/weight loss (53%), fatigue (29%), and depression/anxiety (16%) most common; severe acute COVID, older age, overweight, and comorbidities associated with sequelae presence.

Cross-sectional survey of 201 workers in tertiary sector (banking, telecommunications) examining prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms including sleep disorders. Found 17.9% of workers reported one or more post-COVID symptoms at time of study, with fatigue, exhaustion on effort, anxiety, and memory problems being most common; sleep disturbances were rare.

Cross-sectional study of 694 COVID-19 patients in Spain assessing long-term symptoms and quality of life 4.7-24 months post-infection. Found 16.57% reported not fully recovering, with fatigue, anosmia, and cognitive dysfunction most prevalent; female gender and older age were independent risk factors.

This cross-sectional study compares the prevalence of post-acute COVID-19 symptoms and functional impairment in healthcare workers versus the general population in Switzerland (April-July 2021). Healthcare workers showed significantly higher rates of fatigue, headache, concentration difficulty, and functional impairment both overall and specifically associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

This cross-sectional study compared retinal and choroidal parameters between post-COVID-19 patients with neurologic symptoms and healthy controls using spectral-domain OCT imaging. The study found thinning of the ganglion cell layer and inner plexiform layer in post-COVID patients, suggesting direct or indirect effects of SARS-CoV-2 on retinal structure, but concludes these are not indicative of long-term neurodegeneration.

This cross-sectional study compared the clinical and psychosocial profiles of 55 post-COVID syndrome patients with healthy controls and recovered COVID-19 patients. Post-COVID patients showed significantly worse outcomes across pain intensity/interference, central sensitization, insomnia, kinesiophobia, catastrophizing, depression, anxiety, and stress.

A cross-sectional telephone survey study of 2,070 patients assessing the prevalence, clinical characteristics, and predictive factors of long COVID. The study found a 41.6% prevalence of long COVID with ageusia, cognitive problems, and fatigue as the most common symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This population-based longitudinal survey study compares different survey-based definitions of long COVID to understand variation in prevalence estimates across a Michigan cohort. The paper documents that prevalence rates range from 10.8% to 24.5% depending on the survey question used, with disparities by race/ethnicity and income, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 182 participants 6 months post-COVID-19 assessing sleep quality and mental health outcomes using standardized instruments (PSQI, PTSD Checklist, SCL-90). Found that 91.2% had psychiatric symptoms including poor sleep (64.8%), PTSD (28.6%), and anxiety (28%), with risk factors including female sex, diabetes, oxygen support, and elevated neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between underlying health conditions and long COVID among 4,507 Vietnamese COVID-19 survivors, stratified by hospitalization status. Found that health literacy moderates the negative impact of underlying conditions on long COVID in non-hospitalized individuals but not in hospitalized survivors.

Cross-sectional survey of CUNY students examining associations between long-COVID, COVID-related stress, and comorbid depression/anxiety outcomes in Winter 2021-2022. Found that women, lower-SES participants, those with high stress, and those with long-COVID had significantly higher odds of probable comorbid depression and anxiety.

Cross-sectional cohort study of 7,601 German participants examining associations between SARS-CoV-2 infection, pandemic burden, and mental health outcomes measured via online surveys. Found that past infection, particularly with persistent symptoms 12 weeks post-infection, was associated with mental health deterioration (exhaustion, fatigue, concentration deficits, memory problems), independent of pandemic burden.

Cross-sectional study developing prediction models to identify individuals at risk of long COVID based on pre- and post-infection factors in a Chinese community population of 420 COVID-19 patients. The study identifies age, psychological factors, and acute-phase symptoms as key predictors but does not test any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of PTSD symptoms and associated risk factors among COVID-19 survivors from the first pandemic wave, including 1,108 participants after propensity score matching. Identified four key risk factors: higher COVID-19 severity, fatigue, COVID-related stigma, and poor sleep quality.

Cross-sectional study of 1,354 adults aged ≥50 in Europe investigating risk factors for post-COVID-19 conditions using logistic regression. Found that older age, lower education, and COVID-19 hospitalization significantly increase risk of persistent post-COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between multimorbidity and anxiety symptomatology in 389 post-COVID patients using the HAD anxiety scale and linear regression analysis. The findings show that each additional chronic condition is associated with a mean increase of 0.11 in anxiety scores, suggesting that comorbidity management is important for mental health outcomes in post-COVID care.

Cross-sectional study examining post-traumatic stress disorder risk in COVID-19 survivors in Colombia, finding 13.3% PTSD-R prevalence. Study identifies depression, insomnia, low income, and marital status as associated factors but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 502 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing the prevalence and persistence of post-COVID symptoms beyond 12 months. Found that ~25-33% of patients reported at least one symptom at 6-24 months post-infection, with fatigue, dyspnea, and olfactory dysfunction being most common, particularly in those with moderate/severe acute infection.

Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 749 respondents examining the association between marital status and post-COVID-19 symptom development. Found that single patients, particularly those aged 40+ with mild COVID-19, experienced higher rates of depression and memory impairment, suggesting a need for targeted psychological support.

This study validates the concordance between evaluator-administered and self-assessed versions of the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status Scale (PCFS) in 97 post-COVID patients. While the study is about long COVID, it does not test a treatment intervention—it only evaluates agreement between two assessment methods.

A nationally representative survey study examining Americans' knowledge about Long COVID and the relationship between meta-ignorance (overconfidence in knowledge) and public health outcomes. The study found that over one-fifth of Americans express high confidence in their Long COVID knowledge despite having lower objective knowledge, and this meta-ignorance is associated with vaccine hesitancy and increased Long COVID risk.

A prospective descriptive cross-sectional survey of 206 post-COVID-19 patients documenting symptom prevalence and impact on quality of life. The study characterizes long COVID symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, joint pain, dyspnea, cognitive impairment) and notes greater quality-of-life impairment in women and older adults, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This national cross-sectional survey assessed long COVID symptom prevalence and risk factors among 2,665 COVID-19 patients in Malta 3-6 months post-infection. Female sex, hospitalization, and initial acute symptoms were associated with higher odds of persistent fatigue, shortness of breath, anxiety, and other long COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study evaluates fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) as a potential biomarker in 68 post-COVID patients compared to 29 healthy controls. The findings suggest FeNO is not useful as a biomarker for post-COVID-19, though sex-based differences were observed.

A cross-sectional study of 142 patients hospitalized with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 pneumonia examining the prevalence and predictive factors of post-COVID syndrome at 12 weeks. The study found a 26.1% prevalence of post-COVID syndrome with dyslipidemia as an independent risk factor, but it is an observational cohort study with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing diabetogenic risk markers (insulin resistance, beta-cell function, glucose tolerance) between recovered COVID-19 patients and unexposed controls in Ghana. Recovered COVID-19 respondents showed higher insulin resistance and beta-cell dysfunction, indicating elevated type 2 diabetes risk, but no intervention was tested.

A cross-sectional descriptive study of 372 long COVID patients (>12 weeks post-infection) hospitalized or followed in ambulatory care at a military hospital in Morocco, assessing symptom prevalence and quality of life using the EQ-5D instrument. The study found that 20-25% of patients reported difficulties with mobility, activities of daily living, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression, with neuropsychiatric manifestations being prominent in this population.

International cross-sectional study examining the bidirectional relationship between insomnia and long COVID across 16 countries using web-based surveys. Finds that pre-pandemic insomnia increases long COVID risk (RR 1.33) and that long COVID is associated with higher incident insomnia rates (RR 2.00), highlighting sleep as an important management factor.

This international cross-sectional survey examines changes in excessive daytime sleepiness, excessive sleep quantity, and fatigue during the COVID-19 pandemic across 18,785 participants in 15 countries. While COVID-19 is mentioned and associated with increased sleepiness and fatigue, the study focuses on pandemic-related sleep changes in the general population rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 170 healthcare workers at a Tunisian hospital with prior COVID-19 infection, assessing the frequency and evolution of respiratory symptoms in long COVID. Among 90 patients (52.9%) reporting persistent symptoms, 32 had respiratory manifestations (dyspnea, chest tightness, cough) with mean duration of 13±7 weeks; 26 were followed up 14 months later, with 10 still reporting exertional dyspnea despite inhaled corticosteroid treatment.

International cross-sectional survey of 1,001 COVID-19 survivors examining self-reported sleep health across 6 dimensions (regularity, satisfaction, alertness, timing, efficiency, duration) compared to pre-infection baseline. Finds worse current sleep health associated with greater COVID-19 symptom severity and poorer quality of life, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence of sleep disorders 3 months after hospitalization for SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in 50 patients using the Insomnia Severity Index and HADS scales. Found sleep disturbances in 68% of patients (predominantly insomnia at 80%), associated with obesity, ICU admission history, longer hospitalization duration, and depression scores.

Cross-sectional study using electronic nose technology and chemometric analysis to discriminate volatile organic compounds in exhaled breath samples between COVID-19 patients, post-COVID syndrome patients, and healthy controls. The study demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (97.6-100%) for identifying post-COVID patients but is a diagnostic proof-of-concept study without treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study examined how socioeconomic position (SEP) influences the relationship between post-COVID-19 condition and health-related quality of life in a representative sample of 1,448 French adults surveyed in autumn 2022. The study found that PCC, low education, and low household income negatively impact HRQoL, with greater PCC-induced impairment among people without tertiary education, unemployed individuals, and business owners.

A national online survey of 1,507 Czech adults assessing the frequency and types of sleep disorders occurring after COVID-19 infection. The study found that 81.3% reported at least one sleep difficulty post-infection, with insomnia (59.4%), night sweats (38.4%), and hypersomnolence (33.3%) being most common; sleep symptoms persisted in over 62% even 9+ months after infection.

Cross-sectional analysis of 206,969 US household survey responses (Sept 2022-Apr 2023) examining the association between long COVID and housing insecurity. Found that people with long COVID were 1.5-2x more likely to experience housing difficulties, with highest risk among low-income adults and those with functional limitations.

This cross-sectional study compared respiratory and metabolic profiles between 20 post-COVID-19 soccer players and 20 healthy controls during cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Post-COVID athletes showed increased respiratory work and hyperventilation during exercise with elevated resting and maximal lactate levels, but no difference in maximal oxygen uptake.

This multicenter cross-sectional study evaluates the impact of pulmonary embolism (PE) on health outcomes in COVID-19 patients at 3 months after hospitalization. Patients with PE showed reduced quality of life and greater pulmonary impairment, suggesting PE is a marker of COVID-19 severity with potential long-term health implications.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,883 California residents to assess long COVID prevalence using five different definitions. Found prevalence ranged from 4.9% (severe long COVID) to 20.9% (incomplete recovery), with vaccination status inversely associated with long COVID risk.

Cross-sectional analysis of 8,757 U.S. adults examining associations between COVID-19 booster vaccination status and long-COVID prevalence using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data. Booster-vaccinated individuals had significantly lower adjusted odds of long-COVID (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.93) compared to unvaccinated individuals.

Cross-sectional survey of 3,042 U.S. adults during June-July 2022 estimating SARS-CoV-2 prevalence (17.3%) and long COVID prevalence among those infected >4 weeks prior (21.5%). Study documents inequitable distribution of infection and long COVID burden across demographic groups and socioeconomic strata.
