summary: A cross-sectional study describing mortality, rehospitalization, quality of life, and post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) symptoms in 124 COVID-19 patients discharged from ICUs in Argentina, assessed 6-18 months post-discharge via telephone interview. The study documents outcomes including 7.3% mortality, cognitive impairment in 54.4%, PICS in 66.7%, and reduced quality of life, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 179 long COVID patients in Mexico assessing physical and psychosomatic manifestations and their association with decreased quality of life. Found that pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression, and persistence of ≥3 symptoms were independently associated with decreased QOL, with authors suggesting neuropsychological rehabilitation might benefit patients but noting that such interventions require evaluation.

Population-based cross-sectional study of 121,379 US adults examining associations between Long COVID prevalence and risk factors including COPD, smoking status, and COVID-19 vaccination. Finds 21.8% Long COVID prevalence, with protective effect of 3-4 vaccine doses and increased risk with COPD and current smoking.

Cross-sectional study of 478 COVID-19 survivors (mean 30 days post-infection) assessing cognitive performance and symptom clusters. Finds domain-specific cognitive deficits in processing speed and reasoning, with cognitive impairment correlating to physical symptoms rather than mental health symptoms.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of 2,533 Michigan residents with confirmed prior SARS-CoV-2 infection examining prevalence and predictors of eight Long COVID symptom clusters. Found neuropsychiatric symptoms (23.7%) most prevalent, with female sex, pre-existing psychological conditions, and ICU admission as strong predictors; notably, age and pre-existing conditions showed differential associations across symptom clusters.

This is a cross-sectional analysis from the EPICOVID 2.0 Brazilian survey examining associations between self-reported changes in physical activity during the pandemic and post-COVID symptoms in 33,250 participants. The study found that participants who maintained physical activity had lower odds of tiredness and joint pain, but it is an observational study of associations without testing an intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 214 children in Indonesia assessing prevalence of long COVID symptoms more than four weeks after positive COVID-19 test. Found 28.5% with respiratory disorders, 26.2% with sleep disorders, 23.4% with fatigue, and other symptoms, demonstrating long COVID occurs in children though less frequently than adults.

This cross-sectional study examines whether EEG-based frontal aperiodic exponent values can serve as an objective biomarker for cognitive fatigue in Long COVID and multiple sclerosis patients. While it identifies a promising diagnostic biomarker, it does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This international cross-sectional survey examined the prevalence and predictors of post-COVID-19 condition in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases versus healthy controls, analyzing data from 1,677 respondents surveyed >90 days post-infection. Post-COVID-19 condition was reported in 10.7% of autoimmune rheumatic disease patients versus 5.3% of controls, with female sex, disease duration, comorbidities, and severe acute COVID-19 identified as significant risk factors.

A national cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence in Danish children aged 0-14 years with matched uninfected controls. Children with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection reported significantly higher rates of long-lasting symptoms, though quality-of-life differences were minimal and not clinically meaningful.

Cross-sectional cohort study investigating the persistence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in diverse tissues at 1, 2, and 4 months post-infection and its association with long COVID symptoms. Found viral RNA in 30% of tissues at 1 month declining to 11% at 4 months, with significant association between viral persistence and long COVID development (OR 5.17), but this is an observational study examining correlation with disease mechanisms rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study identified three distinct long COVID phenotypes based on symptom burden using cluster analysis of 8,630 survey respondents. The analysis found that symptom count (rather than type) predicts healthcare use and quality of life, with higher-burden patients consulting significantly more providers.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,331 post-COVID patients examining the prevalence and severity of tinnitus and its association with other long COVID symptoms. The study found that 27.9% of patients reported post-COVID tinnitus, with severity strongly associated with poor recovery outcomes, hearing loss, and anxiety.

Cross-sectional study assessing psychiatric symptoms and diagnoses in 101 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints using standardized psychometric scales and psychiatric interviews. Found that 47.4% of referred patients had psychiatric diagnoses (adjustment disorder, anxiety, depression, PTSD), but the study is observational without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study compared depressive symptoms and subjective cognitive decline between 50 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection and 54 healthy controls using validated questionnaires. While the paper demonstrates that COVID-19 patients report greater depression and cognitive decline, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention and is observational in nature.

This study is a secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey investigating associations between COVID-19 vaccination (≥3 doses) and self-reported long COVID symptoms in Hong Kong residents with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. While about long COVID, it does not study an intervention/treatment given to patients—it only observes existing vaccination status as a passive exposure variable without administering or testing any treatment for long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance fatigability, perceived fatigability, and trait fatigue between 34 post-COVID-19 patients and 36 recovered controls. Found performance fatigability in processing speed tasks in the PCC group but no correlations between fatigue domains.

Cross-sectional study examining long-term psychological effects (anxiety, depression, PTSD, sleep disorders) in children and adolescents 6+ months after COVID-19 infection. While the paper documents post-COVID psychological sequelae, it is observational without any treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance between COVID-19 survivors and controls using smartphone-based cognitive tests. Found no significant differences in cognitive performance between groups at baseline, highlighting the need for longitudinal follow-up.

Cross-sectional study examining how anxiety and depression symptoms moderate the association between COVID-19 infection and memory performance in 84 Canadian adults. Found that anxiety symptom severity had a significant moderating effect on delayed verbal and visual memory retrieval in COVID-19 positive participants, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing cognitive and psychiatric disturbances in 101 post-COVID patients using neurological screening (MoCA) and psychiatric questionnaires. Found cognitive deficits in 34% and psychiatric symptoms in ~60%, but no intervention was tested or evaluated—this is a descriptive assessment study, not a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from a prospective cohort study comparing cognitive fatigue (brain fog) patterns between long COVID patients, resolved COVID patients, and uninfected controls using the Wood Mental Fatigue Inventory. Long COVID participants had significantly higher fatigue scores than control groups, but this paper reports only baseline/cross-sectional data without intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional survey of 134 healthcare workers who tested positive for COVID-19 at a tertiary hospital in Beirut, finding that 47.7% reported post-COVID syndrome symptoms lasting over three months, with fatigue, shortness of breath, and cognitive issues being most common. The study identifies risk factors (direct COVID-19 patient care and higher acute infection severity) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

International multicenter cross-sectional study describing how 10 pediatric post-COVID care programs organize and manage 584 children with persistent symptoms. Study documents current clinical practices and identifies gaps in evidence-based treatment rather than testing a specific intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,731 Australian children 12 weeks after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection to assess post-COVID symptoms and functional impairment. Found that 11.7% reported continued symptoms, with only 37.3% of clinically reviewed cases meeting post-COVID condition criteria and 12.4% meeting long COVID definition.

PECOS is a prospective longitudinal cohort study comparing long-term outcomes in 654 pediatric participants (541 SARS-CoV-2 infected, 113 uninfected) with baseline assessments at enrollment. Infected children reported significantly more constitutional, respiratory, and gastrointestinal symptoms and had worse parent-reported outcomes in fatigue, pain, physical and cognitive functioning compared to uninfected controls.

Cross-sectional survey of 5,919 vaccinated adults examining associations between obesity, probable long COVID (via PASC score), and sleep disturbances. Found obesity associated with higher odds of probable long COVID and both obesity and probable long COVID linked to increased sleep problems, but no treatment intervention tested.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between nighttime sleep duration and post-COVID risk in 5,918 fully mRNA-vaccinated respondents. While mRNA vaccination reduced post-COVID risk by 21%, short sleepers (<6 hours) showed greater post-COVID risk regardless of vaccination status.

REACT-2 is a large representative community survey of 606,434 adults in England examining the prevalence and predictors of persistent COVID-19 symptoms lasting 12+ weeks. The study finds 37.7% experienced persistent symptoms at 12 weeks, with higher risk in females, older age, obese individuals, smokers, hospitalized patients, and healthcare workers.

A cross-sectional study characterizing immune mediators in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma of patients with varying severity of Neuro-COVID, identifying blood-brain barrier impairment, microglia activation, and polyclonal B cell responses as key pathological features. The study identifies potential therapeutic targets but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining whether BNT162b2 mRNA vaccination is associated with reduced reporting of post-COVID-19 symptoms in Israeli individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 between 2020-2021. Found that double-vaccinated individuals reported 50-66% lower prevalence of common long COVID symptoms (fatigue, headache, weakness, muscle pain) compared to unvaccinated infected individuals.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) among 96 COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia using Rome IV criteria. Found IBS prevalence of 19.79% in self-quarantined COVID-19 survivors.

Cross-sectional study of 152 severe COVID-19 survivors (90-120 days post-discharge) examining cognitive impairment, psychiatric symptoms, and plasma biomarkers. Found selective cognitive deficits (episodic/working memory, executive function, attention) with elevated inflammatory markers and neuropsychiatric manifestations (anxiety, depression).

A cross-sectional survey comparing mental health and neurocognitive symptoms between seropositive and seronegative adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic, conducted as part of the SchoolCovid19 study in 1,560 students. The study found no significant differences in long COVID symptoms between seropositive and seronegative adolescents, suggesting long COVID may be less common in youth than previously thought.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 127 COVID-19 survivors in Japan to investigate post-acute sequelae, psychological distress, and work impairment at a median of 29 days post-infection. The study found 52% had persistent symptoms, with olfactory/taste disorders and cough most common, and identified age and female sex as risk factors for sequelae and psychological distress.

A nationwide cross-sectional study of 5,652 long COVID patients identifying distinct symptom patterns through factor analysis, revealing five symptom clusters (cold/flu-like, smell/taste changes, dyspnea/chest pain, cognitive/visual, cardiac). The study characterizes the symptom landscape but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 275 individuals examining immune phenotyping and biological features associated with long COVID compared to matched controls. Identified distinctive myeloid/lymphocyte populations, exaggerated humoral responses, and altered immune mediator levels in long COVID patients, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 285 COVID-19 patients across 5 Japanese facilities assessing the prevalence and risk factors of long COVID symptoms at 1 year post-infection. Found that over half reported long COVID symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive issues, alopecia) with significant QOL impact, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This crowdsourced survey study from the Global Consortium for Chemosensory Research assessed chemosensory recovery patterns (smell, taste, chemesthesis) in Italian COVID-19 patients after resolution of respiratory symptoms during the first pandemic wave. The study identified two recovery patterns (partial and substantial) associated with age and degree of initial loss, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional web survey of 501 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection mapping long-term impairments using the WHO ICF framework and investigating contextual factors. Found that 96% reported moderate-to-severe impairments, with fatigue (79.6%) and tiredness (86.9%) being most frequent, and severity of acute infection as the strongest risk factor.

This cross-sectional study compared retinal vessel integrity and retinal tissue volume across normal controls, mild COVID-19 cases, and severe COVID-19 cases using optical coherence tomography imaging. The severe COVID-19 group showed significantly reduced retinal vessel density and retinal volume, suggesting retinal microvascular loss may be a biomarker of COVID-19 severity.

Retrospective questionnaire study of 812 elite aquatic athletes assessing COVID-19 infection rates, symptoms, and vaccination experiences during a World Championship. While 10% of infected athletes reported long COVID symptoms (fatigue and shortness of breath), this is a descriptive cross-sectional survey with no treatment intervention or control group.

Cross-sectional observational study of 232 post-COVID patients at a PACS clinic characterizing frailty and resilience phenotypes in relation to quality of life and intrinsic capacity. Study found that frail/non-resilient and fit/non-resilient phenotypes predicted worse QoL and impaired intrinsic capacity, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study examining mucosal immune responses (sIgA and IgG levels) in 180 healthcare workers with and without prior COVID-19 history. Found elevated salivary and mucosal IgG levels in those with severe COVID-19 correlating with post-COVID symptoms including fatigue and reduced physical/social functioning.

This cross-sectional study compared functional status, physical activity levels, fatigue, and quality of life between 170 long COVID patients and COVID-19 patients without persistent illness. The study found significant relationships between reduced functionality, lower physical activity, increased fatigue, and poorer quality of life in long COVID patients, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined long COVID prevalence and risk factors among 3,329 healthcare workers at an Indian tertiary hospital, finding 6.19% had long COVID symptoms. The study identified female sex, alcohol consumption, and blood group B as significant risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cross-sectional study examining correlations between subjective autonomic symptom questionnaires and objective autonomic testing in 2,627 patients, including 61 with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19. Found no significant correlations between subjective and objective measures of dysautonomia, highlighting limitations of questionnaire-based screening.

Cross-sectional observational study of 807 patients in Northeastern Mexico examining prevalence of Long COVID and its association with vaccination status, reinfections, comorbidities, and demographic factors. Found Long COVID in 20.9% of participants, with protective factors including male gender, complete vaccination, and specific blood types, while higher BMI was a risk factor.

A cross-sectional study examining IL-6 and IL-17 levels in 80 hemodialysis patients to understand the relationship between pre-existing hypertension and long COVID sequelae. The study found higher inflammatory markers and greater long COVID prevalence in patients with uncontrolled blood pressure, but is a mechanistic biomarker study without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the prevalence of long COVID in 804 Mexican patients and its association with vaccination status, demographics, and comorbidities. Found 20.9% met long COVID criteria, with vaccination and male gender as protective factors and higher BMI as a risk factor for symptom duration.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing chemosensory, trigeminal, and salivary functions in 100 post-COVID-19 patients versus 76 healthy controls. Patients showed significantly higher prevalence of parosmia, hyposmia, anosmia, dysgeusia, and dry mouth, with multiple dysfunction combinations identified.

Cross-sectional observational study examining functional brain connectivity in 66 post-COVID-19 patients using resting-state fMRI and graph theoretical analysis. Found significant alterations in brainstem, olfactory cortex, cingulate cortex, thalamus and cerebellum correlating with fatigue, cognitive complaints, and sleep disturbances.

A cross-sectional study of 802 young women examining whether regular physical activity reduces symptoms during and after COVID-19 infection. While physical activity did not prevent COVID-19 or post-COVID condition, it significantly reduced the number of mental and neurological symptoms, with higher activity levels showing greater benefit.

Cross-sectional comparative study of cognitive profiles in 218 post-COVID condition patients vs 218 multiple sclerosis patients matched by age, sex, and education. Found similar cognitive impairments in both groups with greater fatigue severity in PCC, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study assessing pulmonary diffusing capacity (DLCO) among 458 adults with long COVID recovering from mild to moderate acute infection. Found impaired DLCO in 17% of participants, with higher prevalence in women and those with moderate-severe dyspnea.

Cross-sectional study examining systemic antibody and cytokine responses in 195 participants across four groups (no COVID, acute recovery, recovered, and PASC). Findings show PASC patients have decreased neutralizing antibody titers and elevated inflammatory cytokines (GM-CSF, ANG-2) particularly in females, with no intervention tested.

This paper applies machine learning algorithms to survey data from COVID-recovered patients in Bangladesh to identify post-COVID-19 health factors and their correlations with demographic, physiological, and neurological variables. It is a descriptive epidemiological study using predictive modeling rather than a treatment intervention trial, and thus excluded from the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study examining healthcare service use among long COVID patients in Brazil 6 months post-infection. Finds that long COVID patients use more health services than non-affected individuals, with utilization patterns varying by symptom type.

This cross-sectional study compared objective and subjective cognitive function across 162 participants: 50 with Post-COVID Syndrome, 59 COVID-recovered, and 53 COVID-naïve controls. Objective cognitive deficits were associated with COVID-19 exposure and neurological symptoms, with improvement over time in recovered patients but not in those with persistent Post-COVID Syndrome.

Cross-sectional study investigating associations between physical symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, post-exertional malaise, myalgia) and movement behaviors/functional capacity in 102 long COVID patients using accelerometry and functional tests. Found that fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and symptom co-occurrence negatively associated with physical activity, while dyspnea negatively associated with functional capacity.

Cross-sectional study of 1,642 long COVID patients characterizing phenotypes of dyspnea and associated factors. Identifies two dyspnea phenotypes (fatigue-dominant vs. pulmonary-abnormality-dominant) and their clinical associations, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional analysis of 86,833 participants from the German National Cohort examining self-perceived health and symptoms in post-COVID condition (PCC) patients versus uninfected and infected-but-asymptomatic controls. Found that PCC patients reported significantly worse health outcomes (OR 1.84), with symptom burden explaining the health impairment difference between groups.

A multinational cross-sectional survey of 11,801 participants from 33 countries assessing the prevalence and predictors of long COVID. Identified key risk factors including ICU admission, female sex, acute fatigue, and Hispanic ethnicity, with 19.8% of COVID-19 survivors experiencing long COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study examines leukocyte counts and cytokine profiles in long COVID patients in the Amazon region to characterize immune dysregulation. The study finds altered inflammatory markers (elevated lymphocytes, eosinophils, monocytes) and cytokine levels (IL-2, IL-10, IFN-γ, IL-6) that vary by disease duration and COVID-19 severity, suggesting a persistently pro-inflammatory state that diminishes after 12 months.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,134 transgender and nonbinary people in the US examining the prevalence of long COVID (≥3 months symptom duration) and its association with gender identity and hormone therapy. Found 10% of participants with COVID-19 history reported long COVID symptoms, with higher prevalence in transmasculine and nonbinary individuals assigned female sex at birth, with no evidence of association with hormone therapy use.

This multicentric, community-based cross-sectional study assessed long-term health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among COVID-19 recovered patients in two Indian cities using the EQ-5D-5L instrument. The study found regional variation in HRQoL scores (Delhi mean 0.89 vs Bhubaneswar mean 0.66) and identified age as a significant correlate, but did not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing COVID-19 symptoms at 12 months post-hospitalization in 486 Spanish patients, identifying neurological (46.3%) and respiratory (41.4%) symptoms as most frequent. Female sex, obesity, anxiety history, and fibromyalgia/chronic fatigue were independent risk factors for symptom presentation.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between smoking status (combustible cigarettes, heated tobacco products, and dual use) and persistent symptoms in 5,068 participants with a history of COVID-19. Finds that smoking, particularly dual use of combustible and heated tobacco products, is associated with significantly elevated odds of arthralgia, chest pain, dyspnea, dysgeusia, and dysosmia.

Cross-sectional study comparing the relationship between somatic symptom disorder, anxiety, depression, and daily life impairment across 371 patients with post-COVID syndrome, asthma, and COPD. Finds that SSD has greater impact on impairment in post-COVID patients than in asthma or COPD patients, with implications for rehabilitation approaches.

A nationwide cross-sectional study analyzing risk factors for long COVID and its economic and mental health consequences using data from over 375,000 U.S. adults from the Household Pulse Survey. The study identifies sociodemographic predictors of long COVID and quantifies associations with unemployment, financial hardship, anxiety, and depression, estimating $211-218 billion in lost earnings.

A nationwide French cross-sectional survey of 1,813 adults assessing factors associated with long COVID using multiple case definitions. The study identifies demographic, medical, psychological, and social risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared the prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions in 1,410 non-hospitalized COVID-19 positive patients versus 1,129 negative controls from primary care. PCC symptoms (fatigue, sleep difficulty, concentration problems) were significantly more prevalent in COVID-positive patients, though substantial symptom overlap exists with common primary care complaints.

Cross-sectional observational study of 931 individuals (hospitalized and non-hospitalized) assessing symptoms, physical function, and mental health outcomes after COVID-19. Identifies clusters of physical and mental impairments but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of 107,249 US adults from the 2022 BRFSS examining associations between e-cigarette use and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PCS). E-cigarette use was not significantly associated with PCS, though female gender, obesity, current smoking, and history of depression, asthma, and COPD were significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional study assessed anxiety and depression levels among healthcare workers two years post-COVID-19 infection using PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scales. While the paper includes long COVID patients (50.8% prevalence), it is a descriptive/validation study of mental health outcomes rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This cross-sectional survey study evaluates psychiatric symptoms and coping mechanisms in long COVID patients compared to recovered COVID-19 controls from a large international cohort. While the paper identifies associations between psychiatric outcomes and various factors, it is an observational study without any treatment or intervention tested, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This retrospective cohort study analyzes 9,666 medical rehabilitation cases for post-COVID syndrome covered by German Pension Insurance in 2021. The analysis finds that 80.7% of patients showed improvement in symptoms through rehabilitation, with 88% maintaining employment and over 90% deemed capable of working 6+ hours on the general labor market.

This cross-sectional study investigates the prevalence of chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) in patients with long COVID, examining the relationship between persistent smell disorders and CRS in post-COVID populations. The paper addresses controversial findings in the literature regarding CRS prevalence among COVID-19 patients experiencing long-term sequelae.

Retrospective cross-sectional analysis examining olfactory dysfunction prevalence, severity, and duration in long COVID patients across different SARS-CoV-2 variants. The study compares symptom manifestation between variants and investigates associations between risk factors and symptom presentation.

This paper analyzes work disability claims data from German AOK insurance records to assess the prevalence and duration of Long COVID-related absences from work between 2021-2022. It is a secondary analysis of administrative claims data rather than a primary treatment trial or intervention study.

This retrospective cross-sectional survey assessed the experience and satisfaction of 211 healthcare workers with post-COVID syndrome who underwent rehabilitation measures (inpatient, outpatient, or both). 65.9% of participants reported subjective symptom improvement following rehabilitation, with similar outcomes between outpatient and inpatient settings.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of 619 former SARS-CoV-2 infected persons in Lübeck assessing Post-COVID syndrome prevalence, symptoms, quality of life, and healthcare utilization. Found 54% self-reported PCS with significantly higher symptom burden and unmet care needs, but no intervention was tested or evaluated.

Population-based cross-sectional study of 667 participants with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection examined between November 2020 and June 2021, assessing smell dysfunction using questionnaires, visual analog scales, and objective testing with extended Sniffin' Sticks Test. The study characterizes chemosensory impairment as a persistent symptom of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

School health examination survey in Jena, Germany (2014/15–2022/23) assessing obesity, behavioral problems, and health behaviors in children and adolescents, including prevalence of long COVID in this population. This is an epidemiological survey with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between body composition (fat, muscle, bone) and vertigo in 105 post-COVID-19 patients using bioimpedance analysis. Found significant associations between body composition metrics and self-reported vertigo, but did not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study assessed health literacy and care experiences among 407 long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms using the HLS-EU-Q16 and RehaQ-N1 questionnaires. The findings show that 53.7% of patients had problematic or inadequate health literacy, with the majority having unmet care needs and 47.7% expressing dissatisfaction with their treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 121 Australian adults with long COVID assessing disability, function, and quality of life using standardized instruments (WHODAS 2.0 and SF-36). Study found significant functional impairment and reduced quality of life compared to population norms, with 86% reporting clinically significant disability.

This case-control study compared olfactory bulb volume and olfactory sulcus depth between 41 long COVID patients (10-12 months post-infection) and 42 healthy controls, finding significantly reduced measurements in the COVID-19 group. The study is an observational comparison study without any intervention or treatment component.

This cross-sectional study investigates correlations between post-COVID symptoms and RT-PCR cycle threshold (Ct) values, age, and hospitalization status using questionnaire data. The analysis found no significant correlations between viral load and post-COVID symptom occurrence, though there was a positive trend with advancing age.

This cross-sectional study estimates the prevalence of post-COVID syndrome and its clinical spectrum among 2,070 non-severe COVID-19 patients in southern Tunisia, finding a 41.6% prevalence with ageusia, cognitive difficulties, and fatigue as most common symptoms. The paper identifies demographic and clinical factors associated with post-COVID syndrome but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 958 Chinese college students examining the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and their association with anxiety and depression ~2-3 months post-infection. Study identifies long COVID somatic symptoms, insomnia, and fatigue as mediators between COVID-19 infection and mental health outcomes, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study of 53 long-COVID patients at a neurology clinic identifies symptom patterns using cluster analysis and examines associations with psychological health, sleep quality, and well-being. Patients with higher symptom burden (>17 symptoms) showed significantly worse depression, anxiety, sleep quality, and overall well-being outcomes.

Cross-sectional study comparing functioning and disability in 442 post-COVID-19 patients versus 198 controls using WHODAS 2.0, 6-minute walk test, and hand grip strength assessments. Found significantly reduced functioning in PCC patients, with comorbidities, anxiety, depression, and smoking predicting worse outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining inflammatory markers (CRP, neutrophil count, fibrinogen) in 121 patients with post-COVID syndrome versus recovered controls. Found elevated biomarkers associated with PCS symptoms, particularly fatigue and sensory loss, with notable sex differences in risk profiles.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) in 437 post-COVID-19 patients using IOM diagnostic criteria. The study found 8.1% of participants met ME/CFS criteria, with 2.8% having COVID-19-related ME/CFS and 3.7% having long COVID, demonstrating a connection between ME/CFS and post-COVID symptoms.

This cross-sectional study analyzed 2022 National Health Interview Survey data to assess long COVID prevalence and characteristics among U.S. adults with asthma. The study found that long COVID prevalence was 13.9% among adults with asthma versus 6.2% without asthma, with older age, female sex, obesity, and asthma attack history as risk factors.

Cross-sectional community survey of 1,564 individuals examining symptoms and predictors of deteriorated quality of life associated with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found that fatigue, anxiety, depression, activity intolerance, and work/school difficulties significantly predict reduced QOL in long COVID patients.

Cross-sectional survey of 424 college students examining sensory and cognitive processing after COVID-19 infection. Study found associations between lingering symptoms, perceived severity, and difficulties with sleep quality, sensory processing, and cognitive function, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and patterns of abnormal menstruation in women with a history of COVID-19 infection, comparing pre- and post-infection rates. While the study identifies menstrual dysfunction as a long COVID symptom, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This study validates a Spanish translation of the PAC-19QoL, a disease-specific quality of life questionnaire for long COVID patients, using a cross-sectional design with 206 participants. The translated instrument demonstrates high internal consistency and validity but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing cognitive and autonomic function in young adults 28 months post-COVID-19 (n=34) versus matched controls (n=34). Found subtle cognitive inefficiencies in working memory and executive function tasks but minimal overall long-term impact on cognition or autonomic regulation.

This cross-sectional study characterizes the epidemiology and organ-specific sequelae in 200 adult long COVID patients referred to a COVID recovery clinic in Texas. The study documents symptom burden (dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive dysfunction) and functional impairment (13% using home oxygen, 10% unable to return to work), with median time to clinic presentation of 37 days and follow-up extending to 10 months post-infection.

Retrospective cross-sectional study identifying risk factors for post-COVID-19 cardiovascular symptoms in 204 patients. Found anxiety, depression, elevated C-reactive protein, D-dimer, and LDL-C as independent risk factors.

Cross-sectional questionnaire study (N=220) comparing fatigue levels and quality-of-life between COVID-19 patients and controls using FSS and WHOQoL instruments. Found that severe subjective fatigue is associated with lower quality-of-life and occurs even in mild disease courses, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Questionnaire survey of 3,000+ Bremen residents with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, assessing post-COVID-19 condition presence at least 3 months post-infection. Found that mild COVID-19 poses risk for developing post-COVID condition, with females and those reporting fatigue, breathing difficulties, and cognitive symptoms at infection showing higher odds of later post-COVID symptoms.

A cross-sectional study of 439 UAE women examining menstrual symptom changes after COVID-19, using online questionnaires and standardized psychological scales. Findings show increased menstrual symptoms, pad usage, bleeding days, and pain medication use in the post-COVID period, along with higher stress levels.

This cross-sectional study proposes a standardized method for using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) to describe health status in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients. The study validates interrater agreement for linking ICF codes to clinical instruments and exams measuring quality of life, anxiety, depression, fatigue, and exercise capacity.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive performance and psychological symptoms in 120 long COVID patients versus recovered and never-infected controls using neuropsychological tests and self-report questionnaires. Long COVID patients showed poorer attention/working memory and higher cognitive, anxiety, and depression symptoms, but the study did not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional survey of 1,031 adults with long COVID in Laval, Canada examined rehabilitation service utilization (PT, OT, SLP, Psychology) and identified barriers to care. Only 3-8% of participants accessed rehabilitation services, with unmet needs attributed to lack of referrals, financial barriers, and not knowing who to contact.

Cross-sectional study of 300 participants in Pakistan examining health and psychosocial outcomes in long COVID patients (n=54). Found fatigue and muscle problems most common (14.7%), with moderate-to-severe perceived stress in most participants.

Cross-sectional survey study investigating demographic, chronic illness, and psychiatric correlates of long-COVID-19 in an urban sample of CUNY students. Found that Latinx participants, those with prior chronic illness, and those meeting criteria for probable psychiatric diagnoses had higher odds of long-COVID-19.

This cross-sectional study examined how long COVID affects performance of activities of daily living (ADL) in 30 participants in a municipality-based rehabilitation program. Participants reported decreased quality of performance in both personal and instrumental ADL tasks, with fatigue showing a moderate correlation with ADL ability.

Cross-sectional survey of U.S. adults examining self-management practices for persistent COVID-19 symptoms using alcohol, marijuana, and prescription medications. Found that adults with symptoms persisting 13+ weeks had significantly higher rates of substance use for symptom management compared to those with shorter symptom duration.

Cross-sectional study measuring depression prevalence in COVID-19 survivors in Colombia using PHQ-9 screening. Nearly 50% of survivors scored above depression cut-off, with associations to female gender, younger age, and severity of acute infection.

A cross-national survey of 34 European countries examining Long COVID definitions and diagnostic criteria used in clinical practice. The study documents significant variation in definitions across countries and calls for standardized, unified approaches to support clinical management and data collection.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between anxiety, depression, stress, and psychological distress with sociodemographic factors in 119 COVID-19 survivors at three months post-acute infection. Finds that female patients, those who lost loved ones, and those with physical symptoms show higher rates of severe psychological distress, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of Hong Kong adults examining resilience as a mediator between COVID-19 infection and post-COVID depressive symptoms, with family functioning as a moderator. Study finds resilience protects against depressive symptoms and family functioning enhances this protective effect, particularly in women, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional survey compared fatigue and somatic symptom burden among 2,872 U.S. adults with current, previous, or no history of long COVID. Both current and previous long COVID were significantly associated with elevated fatigue and somatic symptom burden compared to those never experiencing long COVID.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the clinical utility of teleneuropsychology services for cognitive screening in 76 pediatric long COVID patients, comparing in-person (n=33) versus teleNP (n=43) testing modalities. Findings showed similar neuropsychological performance across both modalities, supporting the feasibility of remote cognitive assessment in pediatric long COVID populations.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,872 US adults examining bidirectional associations between pre-existing somatic syndromes and long COVID development. Found that pre-COVID somatic syndromes increased odds of long COVID by 2.8-fold, and long COVID was strongly associated with post-infection somatic syndromes (aOR=10.90).

Cross-sectional study examining correlations between self-reported long COVID and mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, PTSD, suicide ideation) in a community sample of 655 people aged 20-50. Uses structural equation modeling to show functional challenges mediate associations between long COVID and mental health, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 1,910 middle-aged and older Europeans examining the association between combined COVID-19 and influenza vaccination and long COVID prevalence using SHARE survey data. Found that participants vaccinated with both vaccines had lower risk of long COVID compared to unvaccinated individuals, but this is an observational study examining vaccination status as a natural factor, not an intervention trial.

This cross-sectional study uses the SSTICS tool to assess subjective cognitive complaints in 68 COVID-19 patients with brain fog, characterizing the intensity and nature of cognitive deficits. The study found that >10% of patients reported cognitive complaints mostly in memory, attention, language, executive functioning, or praxis domains, with scores correlating to quarantine duration and loss of smell.

This cross-sectional study of 442 participants from four countries assessed executive function impairments in long COVID patients using the BRIEF-A questionnaire and regression analysis. The study found persistent domain-specific cognitive impairments (working memory, planning, task monitoring, cognitive flexibility) even 6 months post-infection, with severity predicted by experienced disease severity.

Cross-sectional study of 79 PASC patients that characterizes the prevalence and correlates of coronavirus anxiety, depression, general anxiety, and objective/subjective cognitive dysfunction using standardized scales and neuropsychological testing. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a descriptive study of symptoms and their associations.

Cross-sectional study describing respiratory function and physical capacity in 60 non-hospitalized long COVID patients 10.8 months post-infection. Found abnormal breathing patterns (95%), reduced lung volumes (10%), low respiratory muscle strength (54%), and decreased physical capacity (69%), with poor correlations between clinical measures.

Cross-sectional survey of 332 long COVID patients examining the association between self-compassion and psychological distress (depression, anxiety, stress). Found that self-compassion dimensions were significantly associated with reduced distress levels, suggesting potential for intervention development.

Cross-sectional survey of 27,651 US adults from the 2022 NHIS examining prevalence and predictors of complementary and integrative health (CIH) use among individuals with long COVID. Found 44.4% of long COVID patients used CIH approaches (meditation, yoga, massage) in the past 12 months, with use associated with younger age, female sex, higher education, and insurance coverage.

Cross-sectional survey of 246 long-COVID patients examining how cognitive and emotional illness perceptions relate to fatigue, depression, anxiety, and quality of life using Leventhal's common-sense model. Illness perception dimensions explained 28-37% of variance in health outcomes, with poor understanding and low perceived control of long-COVID associated with worse outcomes.

Cross-sectional study assessing post-COVID symptoms in 443 patients from the first pandemic wave in Spain using the C19-YRS screening tool, administered 10 months post-infection. Found 62.3% reported ongoing symptoms (fatigue 37.2%, exertional dyspnea 33.4%), with greater symptom burden in women, older patients, and those requiring hospitalization.

Cross-sectional survey of 840 premenopausal women with menstrual pain/endometriosis examining long COVID prevalence and risk factors. Finds that surgically confirmed endometriosis doubles the risk of long COVID, with comorbid anxiety/depression further increasing risk.

This cross-sectional study validates the inter-instrument reliability between Camry electronic and Jamar hydraulic dynamometers for measuring hand grip strength in older post-COVID-19 patients aged ≥65 years. The study found excellent correlation (r=0.88, ICC=0.92) between devices, supporting their interchangeable use in outpatient settings.

A cross-sectional survey of 556 post-COVID-19 patients investigating their preferences and needs for e-Health symptom management interventions. The study identifies design preferences (smartphone-accessible, app-based, 10-20 min sessions) and desired intervention topics but does not test or evaluate any actual treatment intervention.

A nationwide Danish questionnaire study examining postacute symptoms 4 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron period in 36,109 individuals. The study found that Omicron cases experienced substantial postacute symptoms compared to controls, with lower risks than Delta variant cases, and booster vaccination was associated with fewer postacute symptoms.

Cross-sectional study comparing functionality (ADL/IADL) in older adults with post-COVID-19 infection versus those never infected. Found no significant differences in ADL or IADL scores between groups, with higher BMI and education associated with COVID-19 infection.

Cross-sectional study comparing neuropsychological test performance in 67 mild-to-moderate COVID-19 patients with and without persistent cognitive complaints. Found no significant differences in global cognitive composite scores between groups when controlling for demographics, cardiovascular risk, and mood symptoms.

This study describes 97 patients with persistent neuropsychiatric symptoms (particularly brain fog) who sought treatment at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Post-COVID Treatment Program. The paper characterizes patient demographics, symptom profiles, and functional impairment, finding that most participants had not returned to baseline health and reported impaired job performance following COVID-19 infection.

Cross-sectional study describing psychiatric symptoms (anxiety, depression, stress) and cognitive impairment in 92 PASC patients referred to a treatment program at UAB. Authors suggest need for behavioral and psychological interventions but do not evaluate any treatment outcomes.

Cross-sectional survey of 173 US residents with active COVID-19 symptoms examining the relationship between symptom duration and reported cognitive problems. Found that longer COVID-19 symptom duration significantly predicted self-reported cognitive issues including forgetfulness, difficulty concentrating, and brain fog.

This cross-sectional study compared neuropsychological outcomes in 22 non-hospitalized adults with mild COVID-19 history and 20 healthy controls, assessing cognitive deficits and psychological symptoms. While the study documents significant cognitive and anxiety alterations in long COVID patients, it is excluded because it is observational without treatment intervention—it describes symptoms rather than evaluating a treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive and emotional impairment in 114 long COVID patients in Rio de Janeiro using standardized screening tools (TRIACOG, DASS-21). Found high prevalence of depression (66.7%), anxiety (55.9%), and stress (65.7%), with executive function and memory most affected, suggesting persistent long-term cognitive comorbidity.

An Internet-based cross-sectional study of 4,445 subjects examining the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection, COVID-19 severity, and vaccination on cognitive performance and health outcomes. Found that COVID-19 severity was negatively associated with cognitive performance, while vaccination was positively associated with intelligence and information processing precision.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairment and neuropsychiatric symptoms in 127 patients with mild COVID-19 using standardized neuropsychological tests. Found that the Symbol Digit Modalities Test was more sensitive than MMSE-2 for detecting cognitive changes, with fatigue, depression, and anxiety present but only weakly correlated with cognitive performance.

Secondary analysis of U.S. Household Pulse Survey data examining associations between cognitive deficits and sociodemographic characteristics among 385,370 adults with long COVID. Study identifies varying cognitive deficit risks across demographic groups but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study assessing persistent symptoms in 214 university students, 148 of whom had mild COVID-19 without hospitalization (1-39 months post-infection). Found COVID-19 associated with increased fatigue and cognitive/mental health effects that persisted or deteriorated over time, even in younger individuals with mild cases.

This cross-sectional study compared neuropsychiatric and somatic symptoms in vaccinated hospital workers with and without Omicron breakthrough infections, finding no significant differences in symptom burden between groups. The study demonstrates an absence of long COVID symptoms after Omicron breakthrough infections in fully vaccinated individuals, rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing white matter microstructure in COVID-recovered patients versus healthy controls using diffusion MRI tractography. Found statistically significant microstructural alterations in limbic system tracts (uncinate fasciculus, cingulum, arcuate fasciculus) in COVID survivors that correlate with infection severity, providing neuroimaging evidence for long COVID pathology.

This large-scale observational study tracked 3,111 French respondents over 9 months to characterize COVID-19-related olfactory disorders and their impact on quality of life. Most patients recovered within 1 month, but persistent olfactory dysfunction lasting 1-10 months was associated with increased age, female sex, and significant quality-of-life impairment.

Population-based survey of 593 Michigan COVID-19 survivors estimating PASC prevalence at 30 and 60 days post-infection. Found PASC prevalence of 52.5% and 35.0% at 30 and 60 days respectively, with higher rates in hospitalized and severely symptomatic patients.

Cross-sectional study assessing psychological sequelae (anxiety, depression, PTSD) in 100 COVID-19 survivors 6 months post-discharge. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a descriptive prevalence study of psychological outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Population-representative survey of 3,042 US adults estimating long COVID prevalence at 7.3% (~18.8 million adults) and its impact on daily living. Identifies risk factors including female sex, comorbidities, and vaccination/booster status.

A dual-cohort cross-sectional online survey (n=2,050) exploring phenotypes of acute and persistent COVID-19 symptoms in nonhospitalized outpatients in Austria and Italy. The study identified distinct acute COVID-19 phenotypes and found that multiorgan syndrome was associated with protracted recovery, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between SARS-CoV-2 variants, vaccination status, and post-acute sequelae (PASC) symptoms among 2,912 Swiss healthcare workers. It finds that pre-Omicron variants (wild-type and Alpha/Delta) were significantly associated with higher symptom burden, while Omicron BA.1 showed reduced symptom frequency; vaccination was not clearly protective against PASC symptoms.

Cross-sectional study comparing clinical features and immunologic biomarkers in 181 patients with PASC (with and without MECFS) and PACVS. Found shared symptom overlap but distinct biomarker patterns, particularly elevated autoantibodies in PACVS, suggesting autoimmune involvement without testing any specific treatment.

Prospective cross-sectional survey of 156 patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMID) assessing post-COVID-19 symptoms and quality of life. Found 25% met WHO criteria for post-COVID-19 condition, with significantly lower quality of life scores (61.9 vs 71.5) in affected patients.

Cross-sectional study comparing myocardial work parameters and cardiopulmonary exercise capacity in 52 patients recovered from severe COVID-19 versus 24 healthy controls. Found impaired myocardial efficiency and reduced aerobic capacity in post-COVID patients but no intervention/treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study comparing anxiety and depression levels in 388 ambulatory and hospitalized long COVID patients with cardiovascular symptoms referred to cardiology consultation. Found significantly higher anxiety and depression in hospitalized versus ambulatory patients, with stronger correlations in females.

Cross-sectional study (n=1,794) examining depression as a moderator and mediator of functional status in post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), with longitudinal follow-up (n=461). Depression mediated 36-51% of the association between PASC severity and reduced functional capacity, suggesting mental health interventions are needed alongside physical rehabilitation.

Cross-sectional study measuring physical activity and sedentary behavior patterns in 37 COVID-19 survivors at 3-6 months post-hospitalization using objective 24-hour activity monitoring. Findings show survivors are physically inactive for most of their time regardless of disease severity or cardiac dysfunction, with no significant differences across patient subgroups.

Cross-sectional assessment comparing functional impairment in daily life and work activities between long COVID patients with and without cardiopulmonary symptoms (n=534, Brazil). Individuals with cardiopulmonary symptoms reported significantly greater difficulty with work/study activities (49.4% vs 27.2%) and concentration.

Cross-sectional survey of 3,768 long COVID patients in the Netherlands assessing symptom prevalence, duration, and health-related quality of life using EQ-5D-5L. Found that fatigue, reduced physical condition, and cognitive problems are common, with increasing symptom burden associated with decreased quality of life.

Cross-sectional survey of 10,194 long COVID patients examining symptoms, health-related quality of life, fatigue, and mental well-being stratified by time since acute infection. Found fatigue and concentration problems were most debilitating regardless of duration, with worst outcomes in the 3-6 month post-infection group and improvement by 13-18 months.

A French cross-sectional survey estimating long COVID prevalence in the general adult population using an online questionnaire with 27,537 respondents. The study found 4% prevalence of long COVID (1,086 participants), higher in females (4.6% vs 3.3%) and younger age groups, and assessed impacts on quality of life and mental health.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between plasma cytokine profiles and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) abnormalities in 71 long COVID patients 3-12 months post-infection. Found that pro/anti-inflammatory cytokine ratios (TNF-α/IL-10+IL-13) were independently associated with CMR tissue characterization abnormalities, suggesting persistent immune dysregulation affects myocardial remodeling.

Population-based cross-sectional study assessing COVID-related symptoms ~1.5 years after SARS-CoV-2 infection in 255 Essen citizens, examining participation bias in long COVID research. Found 55% still reported persistent symptoms, with higher rates in previously hospitalized individuals (69% vs 53%), but this is an observational follow-up survey with no intervention tested.

Cross-sectional study of 134 long COVID patients in Spain measuring their level of health activation and self-management skills using the Patient Activation Measure (PAM). Found over half had adequate activation levels, though the study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey combining health survey data (n=315,586) with primary care electronic health records to compare symptom prevalence and severity across non-infected, infected, and post-COVID groups in the Dutch population. Individuals with post-COVID reported significantly more frequent, longer-lasting, and more severe symptoms (fatigue, respiratory problems, loss of smell/taste) compared to non-infected individuals, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

Cross-sectional survey of 150 GPs in Belgium and Malta examining their knowledge, perception, and experience managing long COVID patients. Most GPs reported insufficient scientific knowledge and lack of educational resources, highlighting the need for evidence-based guidelines and training across Europe.

Cross-sectional study of 11,513 UK healthcare workers examining long COVID prevalence (20.2% reported COVID-19, 22.5% with LC symptoms) and associated risk factors. Found nursing/midwifery roles and mental health conditions associated with higher LC odds, with no significant ethnicity differences.

Online survey of 1,699 patients with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) examining utilization and subjective effectiveness of physical, psychological, and alternative therapies, with particular focus on 310 patients with concurrent chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). Results show that CFS patients use rehabilitation services more frequently but derive less symptomatic benefit from active therapies compared to PCC patients without CFS, with 20-30% experiencing symptom worsening.

Secondary analysis of GP Patient Survey 2023 data examining long COVID prevalence and patient characteristics in English primary care. No treatment or intervention studied; purely observational assessment of disease burden and demographic patterns.

This cross-sectional epidemiological study examines long COVID prevalence across multiple definitions and identifies risk factors in a French population sample. The paper does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study compares psychological outcomes (anxiety, depression, sleep quality) 2 years post-infection between COVID-19 survivors hospitalized with COVID, hospitalized without COVID, infected non-hospitalized, and uninfected controls from Portugal. COVID-19 survivors showed significantly higher anxiety symptoms (19.3% vs 13.6%) but no significant differences in depression or sleep quality compared to uninfected groups.

This cross-sectional study analyzes gender-specific disparities in COVID-19 impacts across the UAE population using data from four independent surveys. While it documents that females report higher rates of long COVID symptoms post-discharge, it is an epidemiological survey without any treatment or intervention component, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study assessing long COVID prevalence among 8,802 healthcare workers across five Spanish hospitals between 2020-2024, finding a combined prevalence of 4.2% with higher rates in women and workers over 50 years old. The study identifies occupational risk factors and inequalities but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey examining subjective memory impairment (SMI) prevalence among 9,296 German adults with and without self-reported long COVID. Current long COVID was associated with 2.2-fold higher risk of SMI compared to non-infected individuals, but the study is observational without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study surveys 4,687 primary care patients in Belgium to explore health outcomes and care experiences among adults with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), comparing those with and without PCC symptoms. While it identifies PCC prevalence (12.9%) and documents poorer health outcomes in PCC patients, it is an observational epidemiological survey that does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This serial cross-sectional study examined ICD-10 coding rates for long COVID (U09.9) among US nursing home residents from October 2021 to April 2023 using Medicare claims data. The research found low and geographically variable long COVID coding rates, with the highest rates among residents with recent COVID-19 diagnoses, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional analysis examines Long COVID prevalence differences across 27 European countries using data from 4,004 middle-aged and older adults surveyed in summer 2021. The study identifies significant cross-country variation in Long COVID rates (32-89%) and shows that both individual-level and country-level factors (healthcare systems, pandemic response, health status, governance) influence Long COVID occurrence, with recommendations for tailored national recovery plans.

Cross-sectional survey of 6,060 German adults with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection estimating prevalence of self-reported medically diagnosed long COVID (6.2%) and identifying sociodemographic and health-related correlates. Finds higher prevalence in females, older age, low education, chronic conditions, and reinfections.

This paper estimates the prevalence of activity-limiting long COVID (post-COVID conditions) among US adults using modeling of reported infections and household survey data from November 2021. It is a secondary analysis of surveillance data rather than a primary research study testing an intervention.

Population-based survey of 33,250 Brazilians in 2024 assessing the prevalence and symptoms of post-COVID-19 condition 4 years after pandemic onset. Found that 65.1% of COVID-19 survivors met WHO criteria for PCC, with highest prevalence (85.3%) among those requiring hospitalization and oxygen support.

This cross-sectional study examines semen quality and SARS-CoV-2 detection in 43 men who recovered from COVID-19. While it documents reproductive impairment post-infection, it is not a long COVID study (focuses on acute sequelae in recovery phase) and does not test any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional study surveying 505 people in Liberia who had laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection 3-6 months prior to assess the prevalence and characteristics of persistent symptoms (PASC). Found that 50.2% of initially symptomatic individuals reported at least one persistent symptom, with fatigue, headache, and cough being most common; hospitalization and female sex were associated with increased prevalence of PASC.

Cross-sectional study comparing sexual function in 1,313 cisgender women across three groups: never COVID-19, COVID-19 without long COVID, and long COVID. Found that women with long COVID had significantly lower sexual function scores than both other groups, though no causal mechanism was identified.

Cross-sectional study examining serum IL-17 levels in hemodialysis patients with and without post-COVID syndrome at 5 and 10 months post-infection. Found elevated IL-17 associated with persistent post-COVID symptoms, particularly in mRNA-vaccinated patients, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study comparing kidney outcomes (eGFR, albuminuria, haematuria) in 443 subjects 9 months after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 versus 1,328 non-COVID controls from a population-based cohort. Found slightly lower mean eGFR in post-COVID subjects but no evidence of progressive kidney sequela or clinically significant kidney injury.

This cross-sectional study compares oxidant/antioxidant markers in hemodialysis patients with post-COVID conditions stratified by vaccination status (vaccinated with breakthrough infection, vaccinated without infection, unvaccinated with post-COVID). The findings suggest vaccinated HD patients with post-COVID have greater oxidative imbalance and may benefit from antioxidant supplementation, but this is an observational characterization study without testing any intervention.

This study analyzes the prevalence and disease burden of post-COVID-19 condition in patients with chronic kidney disease, on dialysis, and kidney transplant recipients using data from the RECOVAC vaccination study. It is a cross-sectional analysis of existing study participants rather than an intervention trial, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional analysis of 743 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors examining the relationship between skeletal muscle parameters and kidney function 7 months post-discharge. Found that survivors with sarcopenia had significantly lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), suggesting muscle-kidney crosstalk in post-COVID recovery, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

Survey study comparing prevalence of persistent symptoms (≥4 weeks) among 784 adolescents stratified by SARS-CoV-2 test status (positive, negative, never tested). Adolescents who tested positive reported symptoms lasting ≥4 weeks more frequently than negative/untested groups, with most symptoms resolving within 3 months.

This retrospective cohort study examines long-term kidney function in 359 patients from Moscow, comparing those with and without pre-existing CKD who experienced COVID-19 in 2020-2022. While the paper addresses post-COVID sequelae, it is observational and contains no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials database.

Cross-sectional survey assessing long COVID prevalence (47.5%) among Singapore healthcare workers and its impact on work-role functioning using standardized questionnaires. Study found that HCWs with long COVID had significantly lower work functioning scores, particularly those with prolonged symptoms (≥12 weeks).

Cross-sectional survey of 603 UK doctors with long COVID examining symptoms, perceived determinants, and occupational impact. No treatment intervention tested; paper documents disease burden and occupational exposure risks in healthcare workers.

Cross-sectional study assessing long-term work productivity and activity impairment among healthcare workers who had COVID-19 infection during the first wave, using the WPAI-GH questionnaire. Study found high rates of presenteeism and absenteeism linked to post-acute COVID-19 symptoms, particularly shortness of breath, cough, and itching from acute infection.

Cross-sectional study of 474 healthcare workers in Tunisia examining the prevalence and persistence of respiratory symptoms following COVID-19 infection. Found that 23.8% experienced shortness of breath on effort at 3-month follow-up, with symptoms more prolonged in those not hospitalized during acute infection.

This cross-sectional survey of 5,432 healthcare workers from northeastern Italy investigated the prevalence of long COVID symptoms at 30-60 days and 60+ days post-infection, identifying key risk factors including infection timing, hospitalization, female sex, and age >40. The study found prevalence rates of 24% at 30-60 days and 16.3% at 60+ days post-first infection, with neurological, general, and psychological symptoms being most persistent.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID syndrome (PCS) in 170 healthcare workers at a Tunisian hospital who contracted COVID-19 between October 2020 and May 2021. The study found that 52.9% developed PCS with common symptoms including exertional dyspnea, fatigue, and memory impairment, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed long-term health outcomes in COVID-19 patients at 17 months post-infection in Wuhan, China, examining persistent symptoms, radiographic abnormalities, and pulmonary function. The study identified female sex, severe disease, and higher initial symptom burden as risk factors for persistent sequelae but did not test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,176 healthcare workers assessing post-COVID syndrome (PCS) prevalence and symptom persistence at least 12 weeks after infection. Found that 71% of PCR-confirmed infected workers reported persistent symptoms, with only 19% reporting full recovery, highlighting workforce and occupational health implications.

A cross-sectional survey of 290 COVID-19 patients 1-6 months post-discharge examining the prevalence and predictors of persistent symptoms (PASC). Found that 39.7% reported persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, and mental fog, with risk factors including moderate-severe acute illness, female sex, and middle age.

This cross-sectional descriptive study assessed the prevalence and impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 246 patients previously hospitalized for COVID-19, measuring symptoms and quality of life at multiple timepoints (3-12 months post-discharge). The study found 76% met post-COVID criteria with significant impairment in quality of life dimensions, but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional observational study evaluated 232 patients at a post-acute COVID-19 clinic to characterize frailty and resilience phenotypes and their relationship to quality of life and intrinsic capacity. The study found that resilience is complementary to frailty in identifying clinical phenotypes with different impacts on wellness, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey assessed the burden of long COVID in 742 nonhospitalized Danish adults with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection matched to seronegative controls. The study found that 25% of cases reported at least one persistent symptom, with significantly worse physical and mental health scores compared to controls, but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Descriptive cross-sectional survey of 336 long COVID patients in Mexico characterizing symptom prevalence across multiple organ systems. No treatment intervention tested; purely descriptive epidemiological study of disease presentation.

The PRIME study assessed the prevalence of long-term post-COVID-19 symptoms using 6 different case definitions in a population-based sample of 7,405 COVID-positive and 2,392 COVID-negative adults. Prevalence estimates varied substantially (26.9-64.1% in positive individuals, 11.4-32.5% in negative controls), with attributable prevalence ranging from 17.9-26.3%, highlighting inconsistency in post-COVID-19 case definitions and the importance of including negative controls.

summary: Cross-sectional survey assessing the burden of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) among healthcare workers in an NYC public hospital, examining symptom prevalence, severity, and impact on quality of life and mental health. Findings show 61% of surveyed HCW had PASC with multiple symptoms, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 318 post-COVID patients using RehabNeQ and SF-36 instruments. Found that both mental and physical HRQoL scores were significantly reduced compared to non-infected controls, with symptom burden and perceived work ability as key predictors of impairment.

This cross-sectional study uses Mississippi hospital discharge data (Oct 2021-Sep 2022) to characterize hospitalizations associated with long COVID diagnoses. It is a retrospective analysis of existing administrative data without any treatment intervention, focusing on patient demographics, comorbidities, and in-hospital outcomes.

Cross-sectional study comparing SARS-CoV-2-specific immune responses in 1041 discharged COVID-19 patients at 12 months post-infection, stratified by presence or absence of long COVID symptoms. Long COVID patients showed significantly higher RBD-IgG antibody levels but no difference in T-cell responses compared to convalescent controls; this is an observational immunological characterization study, not a treatment intervention trial.

This paper analyzes US Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data to compare demographic characteristics of long COVID patients versus those with resolved COVID-19 and uninfected controls. The study found that long COVID patients are younger, poorer, more female, and more likely to be Hispanic, highlighting disparities in the affected population.

A US Census Bureau online survey (N=68,544) compared self-reported health metrics (mobility, vision, hearing, concentration) across groups with unresolved long COVID, resolved long COVID, short COVID, and no COVID. Unresolved long COVID patients reported significantly greater impairment across all four health domains, while short COVID patients reported the least challenges.

This cross-sectional analysis of the US Census Bureau's Household Pulse Survey (N=68,544) examines the relationship between long COVID and mental health outcomes as measured by the PHQ-4. The study found that long COVID patients report significantly higher rates of anxiety, depression, anhedonia, and hopelessness compared to those with short COVID or no COVID history.

Cross-sectional study of 203 Mexican patients with persistent COVID assessing cardiovascular manifestations using PASC score ≥12 as diagnostic criterion. Found high prevalence of cardiovascular symptoms (82.8%), with palpitations, tachycardia, and chest pain most common; symptoms more frequent in women and associated with multiple COVID-19 infections and severe initial disease.

Cross-sectional pilot study comparing cognitive performance and quality-of-life outcomes in 132 long COVID patients (mean 2.4 years post-infection) versus 42 controls. While long COVID participants reported significantly worse self-perceived cognitive function and quality of life, objective neurocognitive testing showed no significant differences between groups.

This cross-sectional study compared immunologic biomarker patterns across 78 participants with PASC (with and without MECFS) and post-COVID-19 vaccination syndrome, analyzing abnormalities in cytokines, T cells, and autoantibodies. The study found high anti-HSP-70 antibody positivity in all groups and elevated autoimmunity markers in the PVS group, but is limited by small sample size and lack of control group.

Cross-sectional analysis of 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data examining long COVID prevalence and associated factors among US adults. Finds 7.2% overall prevalence with higher rates in women, middle-aged individuals, those with lower socioeconomic status, and various comorbidities; vaccination associated with lower rates.

A cross-sectional study comparing mast cell activation patterns in blood and terminal ileum tissue of 21 long COVID patients versus 11 controls at 2 years post-infection. Findings show elevated mast cell activation, tryptase, zonulin, and tissue-resident spike protein in long COVID patients, suggesting ongoing immune activation and intestinal damage.

This cross-sectional analysis of US Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data (N=68,544) compares social connectedness metrics between long COVID, resolved COVID, and non-COVID populations. While confirming that long COVID patients report significantly lower social connectedness and emotional support than comparison groups, the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

An observational cross-sectional study measuring fatigue severity and postexertional malaise in 213 long COVID patients using validated questionnaires. The study found that 71.4% experienced chronic fatigue and 58.7% met PEM thresholds, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 1,031 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients examining prevalence and associations of mobility and balance decline. Found 44.9% had reduced mobility and 37.1% had balance deterioration, associated with older age, hospitalization, comorbidities, and obesity, which correlated with functional impairment in daily activities.

This is a retrospective cross-sectional analysis from the RECOVER cohort characterizing physical function impairment (30-second sit-to-stand test) in adults with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found minimal clinically meaningful differences in physical function between groups, suggesting individual responses to interventions may be more relevant than group-level comparisons.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and risk factors of suicidal ideation among 1,297 COVID-19 survivors in Wuhan, China. Found 6.7% reported suicidal ideation, with fatigue, stigma, and sleep disorder as positive risk factors, while marriage and peace of mind were protective.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between food insecurity and long COVID prevalence in 956 Brazilian adults from the PAMPA cohort. Found that food insecurity was associated with increased probability of long COVID and specific symptom domains (neurological, pulmonary, gastrointestinal).

This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence of cardiac arrhythmias in 100 patients 1-6 months post-COVID-19 recovery. Findings showed 17% developed arrhythmias, with inappropriate sinus tachycardia most common (7%), and associations between absolute lymphopenia during acute infection and arrhythmia prevalence.

This case-control study assessed conjunctival surface changes in post-COVID patients using impression cytology, comparing 32 post-COVID cases with 32 controls. The study found no statistically significant inflammatory or neoplastic changes in the conjunctiva between groups, except for lymphocyte infiltration.

Retrospective survey of 139 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection assessing prevalence of pulmonary and extrapulmonary long COVID symptoms.
