Study documents symptom frequencies across multiple organ systems (respiratory, cardiac, neurological, psychological, gastrointestinal) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 400+ New Giza University staff assessing long COVID prevalence and identifying predictors of post-COVID symptoms. Found higher BMI, middle age, and male gender (for sleep disturbance) associated with increased long COVID symptom occurrence, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study examining sleep disturbances and associated PASC symptoms in 494 patients from the ReCOVER cohort using sleep studies and PROMIS-Sleep Disturbance assessments. Found that lower REM sleep percentage and specific PASC symptoms (dyspnea, joint pain, headaches) are associated with greater sleep disruption, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

This cross-sectional study compared physical function outcomes in 10 idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM) patients versus 40 healthy controls at 30 days post-COVID-19 infection. While IIM patients showed greater deterioration in physical function and higher fatigue compared to controls, this is an observational study without treatment intervention and should be excluded as it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

Cross-sectional survey of 90 COVID-19 patients (assessed 308+ days post-infection) examining sleep characteristics and their association with acute COVID-19 severity. Found that COVID-19 severity (hospitalization, oxygen therapy, ventilation) significantly predicted poor sleep quality and daytime sleepiness, though effect sizes were small.

Cross-sectional analysis of 26,260 US adults from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining the relationship between COVID-19 status and sleep outcomes. Long COVID was associated with significantly shorter sleep duration (0.3 hours less per night) and poorer sleep quality compared to those without COVID-19.

Cross-sectional study examining B-cell subpopulations in 30 pediatric patients 6 months after COVID-19 recovery, including 6 MIS-C cases. Found normal CD19 and B-cell counts post-recovery with no significant variations between different COVID-19 presentations.

Cross-sectional study comparing nitric oxide-dependent cutaneous vasodilation in adults recovered from COVID-19 versus healthy controls, with assessment of physical activity status. Found no significant differences in NO-mediated vasodilation or microvascular function between groups, and no correlation with symptom severity or physical activity levels.

The COVAD study surveyed 1,677 respondents (45% with autoimmune rheumatic diseases, 12.5% with non-rheumatic autoimmune diseases, 42.5% healthy controls) >90 days post-COVID to assess long COVID prevalence and risk factors. Individuals with autoimmune rheumatic diseases had higher long COVID prevalence (10.8% vs 5.3% in controls), with comorbidities, advanced treatment, and ICU admission emerging as significant risk factors.

Retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of sleep disorders in 250 pediatric long COVID patients and their association with comorbid conditions and symptoms. Finds that 26% of youth with long COVID have sleep disturbances, which correlate with worse well-being, fatigue, anxiety, and depression.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between low HDL levels and inflammatory markers in long COVID patients undergoing hemodialysis one year post-infection. Found that long COVID patients had significantly lower HDL and elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-17, CRP), with pronounced inflammation in those with concurrent low HDL.

Cross-sectional study of 80 long COVID patients examining GPCR autoantibodies and their relationship to vascular dysfunction, endothelial function, and inflammation. Found that GPCR antibodies are present in 65% of long COVID patients and correlate with vascular parameters like blood pressure and FMD, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between pre-infection blood pressure control, serum IL-17 levels, and long-COVID sequelae in hemodialysis patients. While the paper studies long COVID outcomes, it is an observational analysis of existing patient cohorts without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional survey describes the structure, operations, and assessment practices of 39 post-ICU and post-COVID recovery clinics across 29 U.S. health systems. It documents clinic demographics, funding models, staffing, and outcome measures rather than evaluating treatment efficacy or patient outcomes.

Cross-sectional study comparing arterial stiffness (PWV) and haemodynamic parameters in 30 young adults with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection versus 30 matched controls. COVID-19 group showed significantly elevated PWV and systolic blood pressure, suggesting accelerated arterial stiffening even in mild cases, but this is an observational study with no intervention tested.

This retrospective cross-sectional study examined cognitive dysfunction in 427 long COVID patients using self-reported online survey data, analyzing associations between cognitive impairment and other health domains. Findings showed 72.4% presented with cognitive dysfunction, which was significantly associated with fatigue, disability, reduced employment, and difficulty with usual activities.

This large-scale Japanese internet survey (n=32,000) examined the overlap between chronic pain and long COVID-like symptoms, finding that chronic pain is independently associated with symptom burden regardless of COVID-19 history. The study is observational with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study comparing resilience, fear, sleep disorders, and menopausal symptoms in 304 COVID-19 positive climacteric women versus 934 noninfected controls from 9 Latin American countries. COVID-19 patients showed significantly lower resilience, higher fear of COVID-19, greater sleep disturbances, and higher rates of severe menopausal symptoms and hypnotic use at median 8 months post-infection.

This cross-sectional study uses 2022 National Health Interview Survey data to examine the prevalence of long COVID in the US workforce and its associations with chronic conditions and work outcomes. The study found that long COVID affects work attendance and disability risk, particularly in patients with comorbid mental health, cardiovascular, malignancy, metabolic, and musculoskeletal conditions, but does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Secondary analysis comparing self-reported functional disability in people with long COVID and myalgic encephalomyelitis, both characterized by post-exertional neuroimmune exhaustion (PENE). Found few significant differences between groups in functional burden, suggesting similar impacts across conditions regardless of precipitating event.

Self-reported survey of 420 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and severity of hair loss after infection, finding that 77.6% reported hair loss with onset typically within 3 weeks and resolution within 1 year. This is an observational cross-sectional study documenting a symptom feature of post-COVID condition, not evaluating any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing health status and functional capacity in 54 adults with post-COVID-19 condition using clinical assessments, spirometry, and functional tests. Found reduced functional capacity and high prevalence of fatigue, dyspnea, and other persistent symptoms compared to predicted values.

Cross-sectional study of 500+ workers assessing cognitive complaints, inflammatory biomarkers, and psychological well-being 4 months after mild/asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found elevated inflammatory markers and reduced well-being in those with long COVID symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A cross-sectional study comparing clinical characteristics in 150 pediatric post-COVID-19 patients versus 55 noninfected controls. The study identified respiratory symptoms and laboratory abnormalities persisting up to 16 weeks post-infection but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of employed COVID-19 survivors in British Columbia assessing work productivity loss using the Valuation of Lost Productivity questionnaire. Long COVID patients reported 99.2 more hours of productivity loss per 3 months than non-long COVID survivors, highlighting economic burden of the condition.

Cross-sectional study of 280 healthcare workers examining long-term symptomatic recovery from COVID-19 up to 3 years post-infection using validated questionnaires. Found that 73.4% experienced long COVID with significantly worse quality of life, depression, anxiety, and stress compared to non-long-COVID group, but no difference in fear of COVID-19.

Cross-sectional study analyzing 4,496 Doctor's First Reports to examine prevalence and risk factors for long COVID among California workers. Finds 11% prevalence with higher rates in males, ages 45-54, and essential industry workers, and identifies age, symptoms, and mixed essential industries as risk factors.

A multicenter cross-sectional study characterizing long COVID symptoms among Chinese healthcare workers, finding that 17% reported long COVID with neurological and psychological symptoms being most prevalent. This is a descriptive epidemiological survey without any treatment or intervention being tested.

Cross-sectional study of 333 semiconductor plant workers examining associations between work environment, lifestyle factors, and PASC risk. Found night shift work and prolonged medical treatment positively associated with PASC, while exercise was protective.

Secondary data analysis examining correlates of mental health and employment in individuals with long COVID using cross-sectional data from 1901 participants. Study found minimal employment differences between those with and without long COVID (60.9% vs 61.7%) but identified associations between mental health and employment status.

This cross-sectional study characterized cognitive and psychosocial symptoms in 52 COVID-19 survivors 4 months post-illness using cognitive testing batteries and surveys. The study is excluded because it is purely observational without any treatment intervention—it only describes symptom prevalence and correlations, not treatment outcomes.

International cross-sectional study using questionnaires to assess long-term symptoms of COVID-19 and prevalence of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome in recovered patients. Examines persistent symptoms occurring weeks to months post-infection across a large global cohort.

Cross-sectional survey study examining whether preexisting otologic conditions increase risk of exacerbated symptoms after COVID-19 infection in 1,499 PCR-positive patients. Found that individuals with preexisting dizziness, vestibular neuritis, or vestibular migraine were significantly more likely to report worsening otologic symptoms post-infection.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 468 female college students to investigate long COVID's effects on menstrual cycles and evaluated acupuncture as an intervention. Acupuncture treatment was associated with reduced menstrual disruptions compared to no treatment (41.18% vs 64.71% impact on cycle), suggesting potential therapeutic value for long COVID symptoms.

A cross-sectional survey of 564 COVID-19 survivors conducted December 2022–February 2023 that measured insomnia prevalence (63.12%) and severity using the ISI scale, and cataloged treatment approaches used by patients. The study found insomnia symptoms remain common and mostly untreated, with education level and occupation as influencing factors.

This cross-sectional survey assessed post-COVID general health symptoms in 1,518 patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) in the Netherlands, comparing those with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. Patients with previous infection reported significantly higher prevalence of general health symptoms (56.2% vs 43.9%) and fatigue (42% vs 32%), with associations remaining significant after adjustment for potential risk factors.

This cross-sectional study examined factors associated with quality of life in 53 long-COVID patients, measuring QoL, fatigue, psychological health, and cognitive function at 8.7 months post-infection. While the study identifies fatigue and psychological distress as significant contributors to reduced QoL, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing auditory function in recovered asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 patients versus healthy controls using OAE and ABR measurements. Found no significant differences in cochlear or retrocochlear function between groups, concluding SARS-CoV-2 infection does not cause detectable hearing loss in asymptomatic recovered patients.

Cross-sectional study of 457 long COVID patients examining prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbances, and sexual dysfunction in a psychiatry unit. Found females 4.8× more likely to experience neuropsychiatric symptoms than males, with age inversely associated with symptom likelihood.

Cross-sectional study of 285 COVID-19 survivors examining long-term cognitive impairment ('brain fog') and associated psychosocial factors. Found 6.3% prevalence of moderate/severe cognitive impairment, with associations to sex, sleep quality, perceived severity, mental distress, and social discrimination.

Cross-sectional observational study documenting persistent symptoms in 156 long COVID patients at a median of 351 days post-infection, measuring impacts on physical function, cognition, and quality of life. Study characterizes symptom prevalence and triggers but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study describes a clinical evaluation protocol (combining clinical assessment, ultrasound, and robotic testing) in 74 post-COVID patients with fatigue and neurological deficits. The paper reports the protocol and diagnostic findings (41% sarcopenia prevalence, multisensory integration deficits) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing COVID-19 symptoms and post-COVID conditions between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals in Pakistan (n=250). Finds that vaccination reduces symptom duration, symptom variety, and post-COVID condition prevalence, but does not test any specific treatment intervention.

This study examines fibrinolytic system parameters in donor groups stratified by anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG titers to investigate potential mechanisms of post-COVID-19 coagulopathy. The authors found significant changes in fibrinolytic parameters (plasminogen, tPA, PAI-1, inhibitory factors) across different IgG titer groups, suggesting anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG may influence coagulation dysfunction in long COVID.

Cross-sectional study of 69 hospitalized post-COVID-19 patients examining predictors of functional status using muscle strength, functional capacity, and quality-of-life assessments. Found that functional mobility, muscle quality, length of stay, and female sex are independent predictors of post-COVID functional status, but no intervention or treatment was provided.

Observational cross-sectional study comparing sleep quality, fatigue, and pain between post-COVID-19 patients (n=201) and controls (n=206) using validated questionnaires. Found significantly worse sleep quality and higher fatigue in long COVID patients, with strong positive correlations between sleep quality and fatigue severity.

This cross-sectional study evaluated post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) symptoms among 93 solid organ transplant recipients who had COVID-19 during the Omicron period. Female sex, longer time since transplantation, and receipt of tixagevimab-cilgavimab prophylaxis were associated with lower odds of developing PASC symptoms.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 2,764 adults ≥12 weeks post-COVID to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with functional changes in long COVID. The analysis found that prior hospitalization, longer time since infection, comorbidities, and obesity were significantly associated with functional decline including fatigue, reduced mobility, and decreased participation in daily activities.

This cross-sectional study of 1,218 long COVID patients identified four distinct psychological symptom clusters using cluster analysis, finding that anxiety, depression, and somatoform symptoms significantly impact mental health outcomes. The authors conclude that tailored psychological interventions targeting specific symptom clusters may improve both mental and physical outcomes in long COVID.

This study analyzed self-reported long COVID symptoms from Twitter users, identifying 89 individuals who shared data about their experiences. The most common symptoms reported were fatigue, shortness of breath, pain, and brain fog, typically occurring in an episodic pattern.

This cross-sectional study uses quantitative chest CT and machine learning to identify imaging phenotypes in 257 long COVID survivors 6-12 months post-hospitalization. The analysis identified four distinct clusters including a small airways disease phenotype with characteristic pulmonary function abnormalities, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This retrospective cross-sectional study characterizes post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) in 84 patients from Mount Sinai's recovery program, documenting persistent symptoms at mean 151 days post-infection including fatigue (92%), cognitive impairment (74%), and weakness (68%). The study is descriptive and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, focusing instead on symptom prevalence and impact on quality of life.

This cross-sectional study rapidly enrolled 246 racially and ethnically diverse individuals at least 3 months post-COVID to characterize the prevalence and patterns of persistent symptoms (PASC). The study found that 26% had not recovered to baseline health, with fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and sensory disturbances being most common; older age and hospitalization were protective factors for recovery.

Cross-sectional study using PROMIS surveys to characterize persistent symptoms in post-COVID syndrome patients, measuring fatigue, sleep, pain, physical functioning, and social roles. Findings show significant deficits in social roles and elevated fatigue and pain scores in a predominantly female cohort.

Retrospective questionnaire study of COVID-19 infection and post-COVID complications among 271 healthcare workers at a cancer centre. Documents that 51.8% experienced post-COVID syndrome with effects on QOL and productivity, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional study analyzing cell-mediated immune responses in 74 long COVID patients, measuring T cell and NK cell responses to SARS-CoV-2 via flow cytometry. The study found that 96% of patients showed specific cellular immunity despite negative serology, with abnormal immune cell populations suggesting immune dysregulation as a potential mechanism in long COVID pathogenesis.

Observational cross-sectional online survey measuring chronic fatigue and post-exertional malaise severity in 213 long COVID patients using validated questionnaires (FACIT-F, DePaul). Found 71.4% experienced clinically relevant chronic fatigue and 58.7% met myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome thresholds for PEM, with significant impacts on physical activity and social functioning.

Community-based cross-sectional survey of 508,707 people in England examining the prevalence and characteristics of persistent symptoms 12+ weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Study identifies risk factors (age, sex, obesity, hospitalization, deprivation) and symptom clusters but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 457 COVID-19 patients identifying risk factors for long COVID development and persistence. Finds that women, younger age, and low BMI are risk factors for symptom development, with 26.3% reporting symptoms at 6 months and 8.8% at 12 months.

Secondary analysis of the Covid Infection Survey estimating the prevalence of disabling long COVID (symptoms >12 weeks with activity limitation) in UK population aged <35 years. Reports approximately 39,000 cases of disabling long COVID seeded by confirmed infections through July 2021, highlighting the burden in younger populations.

Cross-sectional study describing persistent symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, chest pain) in 602 long COVID patients from a Brazilian post-COVID health center, stratified by acute disease severity. Documents symptom burden, quality-of-life impacts, and laboratory abnormalities (elevated HbA1c, CRP, anemia) with higher symptom prevalence in women.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between cardiopulmonary symptoms in post-acute phase SARS-CoV-2 infection and echocardiographic findings, cardiac biomarkers, and inflammatory markers in 102 participants. Found female sex, prior hospitalization, SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, and C-reactive protein associated with cardiopulmonary symptoms, with pericardial effusions noted in symptomatic cases.

This cross-sectional observational study investigates orthostatic intolerance in 85 adults with long COVID using active stand and tilt testing. The study characterizes the relationship between orthostatic symptoms and hemodynamic responses, finding that POTS is infrequent despite initial orthostatic heart rate differences.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance on standardized tests between 282 post-COVID patients and 52 healthy controls, finding significant deficits in delayed memory, attention, and executive function. No treatment or intervention is tested; this is a descriptive/observational assessment of cognitive dysfunction and its relationships with clinical variables.

Cross-sectional study examining cardiac-related post-acute sequelae symptoms in 442 community-dwelling adults after COVID-19 infection. Found 43% reported persistent cardiac symptoms and identified cardiovascular risk factors, pre-existing conditions, and hospitalization as key risk factors for cardiac PASC.

Secondary analysis of the SAPRIS-SERO cohort examining persistent symptoms in relation to SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity and self-reported COVID-19 infection in 26,823 French individuals. Identifies three potential long COVID sub-syndromes (anosmia, respiratory symptoms, and fatigue-related symptoms) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Population-representative survey of 3,042 US adults estimating long COVID prevalence at 7.3% (~18.5 million adults) and characterizing impact by demographics, comorbidities, and vaccination status. Findings show higher prevalence among females, those with comorbidities, and unvaccinated individuals, with 25% reporting substantial impact on daily activities.

Cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom reporting between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 between March 2020 and November 2021. Finds that vaccination with two doses was associated with substantially reduced reporting of common post-acute symptoms.

Cross-sectional analysis of 15,307 survey respondents examining associations between long COVID symptoms and employment status. Long COVID was associated with higher unemployment rates and lower likelihood of full-time work, with cognitive symptoms showing stronger associations with reduced employment.

Cross-sectional baseline analysis of a US cohort study examining physical and mental disability in long-COVID patients (n=7,926) compared to recovered and never-infected controls. Finds 65% of long-COVID participants have at least one disability, with dizziness, heavy limbs, and dyspnea strongly associated with disability burden.

Population-based cross-sectional analysis of 201,799 UK participants examining socioeconomic inequalities in Long COVID prevalence. Found that participants in the most deprived areas had higher Long COVID risk (11.4% vs 8.2%), with larger disparities in females and healthcare/education workers.

A cross-sectional survey of 231 long COVID patients at 12-month follow-up describing symptom course, daily life impact, and factors associated with symptom relief. Found that most symptoms persisted (83% asthenia, 92% neurocognitive/neurological), only 8.7% achieved complete remission, and pre-vaccination SARS-CoV-2 antibodies were associated with better improvement while persistent ageusia predicted worse outcomes.

Cross-sectional survey of 732 COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia examining depression prevalence and associated factors using the PHQ-9 instrument. Found 47.3% had mild to severe depression, with female sex, younger age, overweight/obesity, having long COVID, and poor self-perceived health as significant associated factors.

This is a large US population-based cross-sectional analysis of 153,543 adults examining sociodemographic predictors and socioeconomic/mental health consequences of long COVID. While the paper provides important epidemiological data on long COVID burden and risk factors, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely observational and descriptive.

Cross-sectional survey of 108 Greek workers with post-COVID-19 syndrome examining impacts on daily life and work productivity, with analysis of resilience and social support as protective factors. Finds that 68.5% report great impact on daily life and 56.5% report great impact on work productivity, with dysautonomia and symptom duration as key predictive factors.

A cross-sectional study assessing the psychosocial and health impacts of long COVID in 300 Pakistani participants, of whom 54 had persistent symptoms beyond 12 weeks. The study found high rates of fatigue, breathing problems, and cognitive issues, with moderate to severe stress levels in a majority of participants.

A cross-sectional pilot study examining serum biomarkers in long COVID patients with neuro-cognitive symptoms to identify clinically meaningful subgroups for precision medicine. The study identified three major PASC subgroups based on biomarker profiles (HERV-W ENV, neurofilaments, IL-6) but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This nationally representative survey of 24,434 Mexican adults characterizes the prevalence and determinants of long COVID (PASC) in 2022, finding 21.21% prevalence among previously diagnosed COVID-19 cases with musculoskeletal pain, headache, and brain fog as most common symptoms. The study identifies reinfections, depressive symptoms, and social lag as risk factors, while vaccination and Omicron variant infections were associated with lower prevalence.

Cross-sectional survey of 24,803 U.S. adults examining the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). OSA was associated with increased odds of PASC-related symptoms, with the association mitigated in those with treated OSA.

The PRIME post-COVID study assessed the prevalence of long-term symptoms in COVID-19 tested adults using six different case definitions, comparing positively and negatively tested individuals. Prevalence ranged from 26.9-64.1% in positive cases and 11.4-32.5% in negative controls, highlighting significant variation depending on which definition is applied.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of 385,617 US adults using the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System to estimate COVID-19 and long COVID prevalence by state and demographic characteristics. Found 7.4% of all adults reported long COVID (21.9% of those with prior COVID), with fatigue, shortness of breath, and taste/smell loss being most common reported symptoms.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of long COVID symptoms among 330 children aged 5-12 in Duhok, Iraq, using IgG serology and symptom interviews. Found 4.6% (14 children) reported long COVID symptoms lasting >4 weeks, with fatigue, cough, and post-exertional malaise most common.

This case-control study compares serum levels of galanin, its receptor (GalR1), electrolytes, and inflammatory markers in 90 long-COVID patients versus 60 recovered controls. The study identifies galanin and GalR1 as potential biomarkers for long-COVID disease but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This study estimates the disability burden of Long COVID in US adults using cross-sectional survey data from 2022-2023, calculating Years of Life with Disability (YLDs) and comparing NIH funding allocation relative to disease burden. It finds that Long COVID affects ~1.5% of respondents with substantial disability impact, particularly in women, but receives disproportionately low NIH research funding relative to its burden.

This study analyzes data from two nationally representative U.S. surveys (BRFSS and NHIS) to identify demographic and clinical risk factors associated with long COVID. The analysis finds that middle age, female gender, Hispanic ethnicity, lower education, and initial infection severity are associated with higher long COVID risk.

Cross-sectional immune-endocrine profiling study of 165 individuals with and without long COVID comparing sex differences in symptom manifestations and immune characteristics. Found distinct immunological patterns and symptom burdens between males and females with long COVID, with testosterone levels inversely associated with symptom severity.

This paper uses 2022 BRFSS survey data to compare the prevalence and correlates of cognitive impairment and long COVID across 50 US states. It is a secondary analysis of existing survey data without testing any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study of 24,803 U.S. adults examines associations between pre-existing sleep issues (insomnia, poor sleep quality, short sleep duration) and the prevalence of post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) using three different case definitions. The study finds that insomnia, poor sleep quality, and short sleep duration are associated with increased PASC prevalence, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment—only identifies sleep problems as potential risk factors for PASC development.

This cross-sectional analysis compares health outcomes and risk factors among 385,617 adults from the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System, stratifying by long COVID status, positive COVID test only, and no prior infection. The study found long COVID patients had worse chronic disease burden than those with just COVID, and higher vaccination rates were associated with reduced long COVID prevalence, but the paper does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing blood samples from PASC patients with cardiovascular symptoms, recovered COVID-19 patients, and SARS-CoV-2 negative controls to identify inflammatory biomarkers. Found elevated trace-level pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-12, IL-1β, MCP-1, IL-6) in PASC-CVS patients at ~18 months post-infection that directly affected stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte function in vitro.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in TB-exposed populations in Peru and Kenya, assessing clinical phenotypes and quality-of-life impacts. The study found high LC prevalence in Peru with neurological and musculoskeletal predominance, but no evidence of TB-associated differences; it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence of autonomic dysfunction markers in 100 long COVID patients using heart rate variability, NASA lean test, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, and COMPASS-31 scale. Found dysautonomia present in 82% of patients and identified it as a significant contributor to symptom burden, particularly orthostatic intolerance and gastrointestinal domains.

Large-scale internet-based epidemiological survey (n=32,000) in Japan examining the relationship between chronic pain and long COVID-like symptoms. Finds that chronic pain is an independent risk factor for 15 of 17 long COVID-like symptoms, suggesting these symptoms are not specific to COVID-19 but associated with chronic pain status.

This cross-sectional study evaluated working memory impairment in 1,064 participants using an online survey, comparing clinically diagnosed, self-reported, and non-long COVID groups. Results show that long COVID significantly impairs working memory, with the greatest deficits in clinically diagnosed cases and correlations between memory deficits and brain fog severity.

Cross-sectional study comparing plasma cortisol concentrations in 200 individuals 3-6 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, stratified by long COVID status and ME/CFS-like symptoms. Found no overall difference in morning cortisol between long COVID and recovered groups, though time-specific differences emerged in subgroups with ME/CFS-like symptoms or severe long COVID.

This cross-sectional study compares the clinical symptomatology of long COVID (n=441) and post-vaccination syndrome (n=241) using questionnaire data and machine learning to identify distinguishing symptoms between the two conditions. The analysis identifies distinct symptom profiles—long COVID characterized by brain fog, smell/taste changes, and dyspnea; PVS by burning sensations and neuropathy—suggesting different underlying biological mechanisms.

A multicentre cross-sectional study characterizing cardiopulmonary dysfunction in 86 post-COVID patients with exertional dyspnoea, identifying preload insufficiency and ventilatory limitations as key contributors. The study identifies three distinct phenotypes but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of post-COVID cognitive symptoms (memory loss and concentration issues) at 9 and 12 months post-infection in Lisbon and Tagus Valley. Found significantly higher rates of cognitive symptoms in COVID-19 positive cases compared to negatives, with female sex associated with higher prevalence.

Population-based survey study tracking longitudinal trends in Long COVID prevalence among NYC adults from 2021-2023, with stratification by socio-demographic characteristics. Demonstrates increasing population prevalence (5.9%-14.3%) and significant health equity disparities, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing self-reported long COVID cases to COVID-19-infected controls without long COVID among healthcare workers in Quebec to assess functional impact and work performance. Long COVID was associated with lower work ability, reduced work functioning, and greater dyspnea-associated impairment, particularly among workers with pre-existing chronic conditions.

This paper analyzes GP Patient Survey data from 759,149 English patients to explore prevalence and patient uncertainty about Long COVID, finding 4.8% reported having LC and 9.1% were unsure, with higher prevalence in older age groups, females, and marginalized populations. The study identifies significant disparities and knowledge gaps but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey examining anxiety symptoms related to long COVID across different age groups in Kerala, India using big data analytics and communication methods. The study found that COVID-19 and vaccination concerns generate psychological anxiety in the population, with beliefs that the virus persists in the body and manifests as new diseases.

This cross-sectional analysis examines the association between long COVID and financial hardship (food insecurity, inability to pay bills, lost services) across income and education levels using nationally representative BRFSS data from 271,076 adults. The study finds significant positive associations between long COVID and financial hardships, with mediation analysis showing that employment loss or reduced work hours accounts for 6-20% of the economic impact.

This cross-sectional survey examines the association between COVID-19 infection and erectile dysfunction in Italian males during April-May 2020. The study found a higher prevalence of ED in COVID-positive subjects (28% vs 9.33%), but focuses on acute COVID-19 infection rather than long COVID sequelae.

This study compared physical performance, balance, gait, and activities of daily living between 124 older individuals with long COVID syndrome and age-matched controls without COVID-19 history. The study found that long COVID patients had significantly lower upper extremity mobility and transfer ability, but similar balance and ADL independence compared to controls.

Cross-sectional study comparing corneal confocal microscopy findings in 33 long COVID patients versus 22 matched controls, assessing sub-basal nerve plexus morphology and dendritic cell density. Long COVID patients showed reduced corneal nerve density, shorter nerves, increased dendritic cell density, and microneuromas in 24.2%, consistent with neuroinflammatory changes.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between baseline inflammatory markers, internalizing symptoms, and loneliness in 74 adolescent COVID-19 survivors. Found that loneliness, anxiety, and parental anxiety were associated with depressive symptoms, but no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

This cross-sectional survey of 214 UK adults examines associations between persistent post-COVID physical symptoms and mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, insomnia). The study finds that more persistent physical symptoms are associated with poorer mental health, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 217 long COVID patients assessing the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction via echocardiography. Older patients with cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, elevated ASCVD score) had 24% prevalence of LV dysfunction, suggesting these factors should guide screening decisions.

Cross-sectional study comparing clinical characteristics and SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity in 113 children attending a specialist long COVID clinic. Found no significant clinical differences between seropositive and seronegative children, but both groups reported multiple symptoms, fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and substantial functional impairment.

Cross-sectional cohort study examining headache prevalence as both an acute COVID-19 onset symptom and a post-COVID-19 symptom 6 months after hospitalization in patients infected with Wuhan, Alpha, or Delta variants. Found that Delta variant had significantly higher rates of both acute and post-COVID headache compared to other variants.

Population-based cross-sectional analysis of 759,149 UK GP patients examining long COVID prevalence (4.8%) and uncertainty (9.1%) across sociodemographic groups. Identifies significant disparities with higher prevalence in females, older adults (35-54 years), minoritised groups, and those with long-term conditions.

This cross-sectional survey study (N=433) assesses socio-economic inequalities in healthcare access among long COVID patients in Austria, examining self-perceived barriers, facilitators, and unmet needs. The study finds that rural residence and poor economic situation are associated with higher unmet healthcare needs, particularly in GP and specialist care, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of long COVID 12 months after acute infection in 1,033 Brazilian adults and identifying risk factors. Found 60.3% prevalence with female sex, ICU treatment, and multimorbidity as significant predictors, but the study is observational without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,205 Australian residents assessing long COVID prevalence, symptom clusters, and predictors during the Omicron period. Identifies two symptom clusters (pauci-symptomatic and polysymptomatic) associated with worse functioning, with female sex, comorbidities, and acute infection severity as key risk factors.

A cross-sectional questionnaire study of 4,188 people with HIV in the UK assessing COVID-19 infection history, long COVID prevalence (10.8%), and vaccine uptake. No treatment intervention is tested; this is an observational epidemiological study of long COVID prevalence and associated factors.

A retrospective cross-sectional survey of 115 elderly female COVID-19 survivors investigating post-COVID symptoms and their association with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). Fatigue, cognitive impairment, stress, sleep disturbances, and recurrent falls were significantly associated with CFS-like symptoms in the post-recovery period.

Cross-sectional survey of 287 COVID-19 survivors characterizing post-COVID-19 manifestations and their relationship to disease severity. Finds that 89.2% of survivors report symptoms, most commonly fatigue (72.8%), with severity linked to initial COVID-19 disease severity.

Cross-sectional study of 276 COVID-19 survivors assessing psychological symptoms and quality of life across three patient groups (outpatient, hospitalized, ICU). Found high prevalence of depression (20.3%), anxiety (16.7%), PTSD (28.6%), and reduced quality of life, particularly in outpatient group.

Cross-sectional study comparing symptoms and functional capacity in 562 post-COVID-19 patients versus community controls, finding that 69% had long COVID symptoms but only 27% had subjective and 14% had objective functional impairment. Results suggest exercise training may benefit appropriately selected patients, with a pilot showing 20% increase in peak workload after training.

A national Danish survey of 17,627 children with prior COVID-19 and 54,656 matched references investigated associations between COVID-19 status, weight changes, psychological symptoms, and long COVID symptoms. COVID-19 was associated with weight loss in 2-3-year-olds and lower weight gain in older children; any reported long COVID symptom correlated with weight changes regardless of COVID-19 status.

A cross-sectional study describing the prevalence and characteristics of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, depression) in 114 previously hospitalized patients, comparing symptom frequency and severity by participant demographics. The study found anxiety (66.7%), fatigue (64.0%), and cognitive difficulties (57.9%) were most prevalent, with female participants and unvaccinated patients reporting higher symptom distress.

Descriptive cross-sectional study examining nocturia in 70 long COVID patients, identifying urinary tract dysfunction as the dominant aetiological factor. Study characterizes relationships between patient age, nocturia frequency, and underlying aetiological factors (urinary, cardio-metabolic, sleep) but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 403 older Brazilians with long COVID examining perceived quality of life and associated factors. Identifies race, home ownership, screen time, musculoskeletal/anxiety symptoms, and work situation as significant predictors of QoL, but does not test any intervention.

This descriptive cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of long-term COVID-19 symptoms in 509 surgical nurses from Turkey, assessed 12+ weeks post-infection. The study documents high rates of persistent symptoms including palpitation, headache, dyspnea, and burnout but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This multicentre cross-sectional study assessed functional impairments and symptoms in 102 COVID-19 survivors 6-9 months post-infection using validated questionnaires. The study found 13-30% reported significant cognitive, emotional and physical impairments, with associations to acute severity and chronic disease, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This descriptive cross-sectional survey of 5,163 long COVID survivors from online support groups characterizes the frequency, duration, and health impact of post-acute sequelae symptoms. The study found participants experienced a mean of 21 symptoms with fatigue, headache, and shortness of breath most common, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study of 2,816 German healthcare workers comparing mental health outcomes and psychological/social factors between those with and without post-COVID condition (332 with PCC). Found that HCW with PCC exhibit higher depression, anxiety, PTSD symptoms, and work-family conflict, with lower social support and sense of coherence associated with higher post-COVID symptom severity.

This cross-sectional survey of 200,000 German stem cell donors examines the prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions in the working-age population and identifies risk factors. The study found significantly higher rates of physical, cognitive, and psychological symptoms in those with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, with severity of acute infection and age as major risk factors, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 4,264 New Zealand children and young adults assessing post-COVID-19 symptoms following the country's first widespread SARS-CoV-2 transmission in February 2022. Over one-fifth reported persisting symptoms including coughs/colds (24.5%), fatigue (20.6%), headaches (21.7%), and anxiety (13.1%), with those reporting prior infection having significantly poorer self-rated health status than uninfected peers.

Cross-sectional analysis of hospitalized COVID-19 survivors 2 months post-discharge assessing neurocognitive function, psychiatric symptoms, and quality of life using standardized instruments. Found high prevalence of neurocognitive impairment (58.7%), psychiatric morbidity (39.1%), and poor QoL, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and clinical manifestations of long COVID among 297 California farmworkers, finding 61.8% prevalence with persistent fatigue, dyspnea, taste/smell problems, and functional limitations. The study is excluded because it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely observational/descriptive research characterizing long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors in a vulnerable population.

This cross-sectional survey study investigates sleep and dream alterations in 270 long-COVID patients and 113 short-COVID controls from May-November 2021. The findings show that long-COVID patients experience greater sleep disturbances and psychological factors are key determinants, but no intervention or treatment is evaluated.

Population-based cross-sectional study examining rural-urban disparities in long COVID prevalence among Michigan adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 (2020-2022). Found 15-27% higher prevalence of 30/90-day long COVID in nonmetropolitan vs metropolitan areas, with disparity patterns changing between pre- and post-vaccine eras.

International cross-sectional survey of 26,539 adults examining dream-enactment behaviours during the COVID-19 pandemic. Found that dream-enactment behaviours (a hallmark of REM sleep behaviour disorder) were 1.8–2.9 times more prevalent in COVID-19-positive cases, suggesting potential neurodegenerate effects of COVID-19.

Cross-sectional survey of 11,710 COVID-19 positive participants investigating whether pre-existing sleep disturbances predict development of post-COVID-19 syndrome at 8.5 months post-infection. Found pre-existing sleep disturbances independently associated with post-COVID syndrome (adjusted OR 2.7, 95% CI 2.27-3.24), with sleep disturbances also being a common symptom within the syndrome itself.

This cross-sectional population survey of 2,919 adults in Brazil examined the association between long COVID symptoms and sleep problems. The study found that 48.3% had long COVID, sleep problems were reported by 41.2%, and individuals with sleep problems had significantly higher prevalence of altered sensitivity, nasal congestion, musculoskeletal symptoms, respiratory issues, and overall long COVID symptoms.

Observational cross-sectional study examining relationships between fatigue, perceived social support, and symptomatology in 374 Spanish long COVID patients. Study identifies fatigue and pain as negatively correlated with perceived social support, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 305 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Brazil assessing long-term prevalence of taste and olfactory dysfunction at mean 179 days post-infection. Found high persistent rates (45% olfactory, 50% taste dysfunction) with older age associated with higher olfactory dysfunction prevalence.

This cross-sectional study compared antibody reactivity patterns against EBV EBNA1 antigen in 48 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients versus 48 fully recovered COVID-19 convalescents. PCS patients showed enhanced IgG reactivity to specific linear epitopes within EBNA1, particularly in the glycine-alanine repeat region and central region, though no differences in autoantibodies against other nuclear/cytoplasmic antigens were detected.

This cross-sectional study of 33,610 blood donors investigates the association between SARS-CoV-2 antibody profiles and long COVID occurrence, finding that higher anti-nucleocapsid levels associate with increased long COVID risk while higher anti-spike levels associate with lower risk. The study identifies four clinical subphenotypes with distinct symptom patterns (neurological, respiratory, psychiatric, multi-systemic) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing depression levels in 325 COVID-19-recovered patients in Bangladesh 14 days to 3 months post-infection using the PHQ-9 questionnaire. Found 31% had signs of depression, with associations to hospitalization duration, employment loss, and fear of reinfection, but no intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study compares balance confidence and fall risk in older adults with long COVID (n=30) versus non-long-haulers (n=60) and healthy controls (n=52) using the Activities-Specific Balance Confidence Scale and Falls Efficacy Scale-International. Long-haulers showed significantly lower balance confidence and greater concern of falling, suggesting increased fall risk in this population.

This cross-sectional study evaluated multi-organ and metabolic dysfunction in 21 long COVID patients (5-7 months post-hospitalization) versus 10 matched controls using comprehensive imaging, exercise testing, and metabolic assessments. Patients exhibited greater insulin resistance and perceived fatigue despite comparable muscle strength, cardiac function, and cerebral architecture, suggesting a need for metabolic and physical intervention strategies.

This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between acute GI symptoms and COVID-19 severity, and examined post-COVID disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) in both hospitalized and ambulatory patients using a two-phase internet survey. Among 164 post-COVID participants, 66% met criteria for at least one DGBI, with 75% being new-onset post-infection, and depression was significantly more common in those with post-COVID DGBI.

This case-control study compared executive functions in recovered COVID-19 patients (n=25) versus healthy controls (n=25) using cognitive testing batteries (WCST, Stroop, N-back). The study found statistically significant impairments in executive function in post-COVID patients, with correlations to sleep quality but not disease severity.

Cross-sectional study of 2,000 Danish COVID-19 survivors examining whether pre-existing rheumatological conditions are risk factors for developing widespread post-COVID pain. Found that rheumatological conditions were not associated with post-COVID pain development, though hospitalization status and female sex were risk factors.

Cross-sectional study estimating the prevalence of persistent symptoms post-COVID-19 in English children aged 5-17 years and associated risk factors across 10 rounds of population surveys (March 2021 to March 2022). Found 4.4% of younger children and 13.3% of older children reported symptoms lasting ≥3 months, with higher age and pre-existing conditions as risk factors.

Cross-sectional questionnaire study comparing joint pain prevalence and rheumatological symptom changes in 2,000 COVID-19 survivors (hospitalized vs non-hospitalized) at 6 months post-infection. Found hospitalized patients experienced significantly higher rates of new-onset joint pain (18.9% vs 5.5%) and worsening of pre-existing rheumatological conditions in both groups.

Cross-sectional survey of 216 master athletes assessing prevalence of post-COVID condition and its associations with quality of life and C-reactive protein levels. Found 21% with moderate-to-severe symptoms associated with reduced quality of life and low-grade inflammation, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional survey from the COVAD study assessed the prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID syndrome (PCS) in 1,677 patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases, non-rheumatic autoimmune diseases, and healthy controls surveyed >90 days post-COVID. Patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases had significantly higher PCS prevalence (10.8%) compared to healthy controls (5.3%), with comorbidities, female sex, and severe acute COVID-19 requiring intensive care identified as independent risk factors.

This cross-sectional study compares symptom networks across long-COVID, chronic fatigue syndrome, and other medically unexplained syndromes using network analysis of questionnaire responses. It finds that long-COVID has a more connected symptom network than CFS and other conditions, supporting a connectionist rather than modular biological basis for these syndromes.

Cross-sectional study comparing corneal nerve morphology and dendritic cell density in 40 long COVID patients versus 30 controls using corneal confocal microscopy. Found reduced corneal nerve fiber density and increased dendritic cells in patients with neurological symptoms, suggesting CCM as a potential objective biomarker for long COVID identification.

Cross-sectional study describing development and validation of a remote COVID-19 rehabilitation assessment tool for triage and management of 155 post-COVID patients. Study documents symptoms and rehabilitation needs but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Population-based cross-sectional study of 11,710 adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection assessing post-COVID symptom clusters 6-12 months after acute infection. Found 28.5% prevalence of post-COVID syndrome with fatigue and neurocognitive impairment as major contributors to reduced health and working capacity.

Population-based cross-sectional study of 373 COVID-19 patients in Iceland examining the association between illness severity and risk of depression, anxiety, and PTSD. Found that severe illness course (hospitalization, prolonged bed confinement, high symptom burden) was associated with significantly increased risk of depression and PTSD but not anxiety.

A cross-sectional serological survey in Geneva, Switzerland examining the prevalence of persistent symptoms in children and adolescents after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Among seropositive adolescents (12-17 years), 4.4% reported symptoms lasting over 4 weeks, with fatigue, headache, and loss of smell being most common; younger children showed no meaningful difference in persistent symptoms compared to seronegatives.

A cross-sectional study of 4,804 older Chinese adults examining the interaction between economic status and healthy lifestyle in long COVID prevalence. The study found 57.3% had long COVID symptoms, with low economic status associated with 48% increased risk, and a significant interaction between economic status and lifestyle factors.

Cross-sectional survey examining social support, well-being, and distress in 256 long COVID patients and 50 relatives from Austria, Germany, and Switzerland. Emotional support was associated with higher well-being and lower anxiety/depression, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Observational cross-sectional survey of 654 Canadians assessing long COVID symptoms and healthcare utilization patterns. Identifies symptom profiles (fatigue, cognitive issues, dyspnea, headaches) and healthcare-seeking behavior but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional evaluation of 3,754 long COVID patients using the Living With COVID Recovery digital health intervention, assessing baseline functional limitations and symptom burden. Fatigue was identified as the primary determinant of functional limitations, with 53% of patients reporting moderately severe or worse functional impairment and substantial impacts on work ability.

Cross-sectional survey of 8,804 UK participants with ME/CFS or long COVID examining symptom clustering, diagnosis delays, and healthcare experiences. Found overlapping symptom patterns (fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, postexertional malaise) but significant delays in diagnosis and low satisfaction with NHS services, with minimal reported benefit from NICE guidelines.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence of long COVID among 11,513 UK healthcare workers and identifies demographic and occupational risk factors associated with the condition. The study found that 20.25% reported COVID-19, of whom 22.52% experienced long COVID, with higher prevalence in nursing/midwifery roles and those with psychological/respiratory conditions.

Cross-sectional study of 3,240 Israeli children examining prevalence of long COVID symptoms in children with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection history. Found most long COVID symptoms (headaches, weakness, fatigue, abdominal pain) more prevalent in infected children, particularly adolescents, though some somatic symptoms were more common in uninfected children.

Population-based cross-sectional telephone survey in Tuscany assessing prevalence of long COVID symptoms in the general population. Found fatigue, concentration impairment, and skin rashes significantly more prevalent in individuals with previous COVID-19, particularly in recent cases and females.

This cross-sectional study of 315 post-COVID patients examined correlations between fatigue and pulmonary abnormalities 6-12 months after hospitalization. The study found fatigue was weakly correlated with pulmonary disorders but strongly associated with reduced musculoskeletal strength, anxiety, depression, and poor quality of life.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of depression and anxiety among 269 COVID-19 recovered patients in Nepal using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Depression and anxiety affected 30.5% and 38.7% of recovered patients respectively, with social support and longer recovery duration serving as protective factors.

Cross-sectional study of 1,086 school workers in Vancouver assessing prevalence and functional impact of pandemic-related chronic health symptoms. Found 31.1% reported new-onset chronic symptoms lasting ≥3 months after COVID-19 infection, associated with poorer mental health, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, but no treatment intervention was studied.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,131 French working adults investigating occupational and non-occupational factors associated with post-COVID-19 condition. The study identified work-related factors (care provision, colleague contact, workload) and demographic/health factors as risk factors for PCC, but did not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining health-related adverse work outcomes in British Columbia adults with post-COVID-19 condition compared to those without. Finds that PCC is associated with significantly higher rates of occupational changes, reduced workload, increased sick days, and early retirement, particularly in patients with fatigue, fever, weakness, palpitations, and brain fog.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,113 long COVID service users in Wales measuring health-related quality of life using EQ-5D-5L, finding significantly lower scores (0.502 vs 0.856 in general population). Study documents disease burden and estimated QALY losses but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 GP Patient Survey (759,149 patients in England) compares the impact of long COVID on daily activities and healthcare support received versus diabetes and mental health conditions. The study found that long COVID patients experience greater functional impairment than those with diabetes but comparable to mental health conditions, while reporting significantly less engagement with primary care management planning.

A longitudinal follow-up survey of long COVID patients from November 2020 to 2021 characterizing recovery patterns and functional impact. The study found that 68.8% still experienced symptoms at 18+ months, with significant impacts on work (61.1%), relationships (51.4%), and self-care (33.2%), highlighting the prolonged and heterogeneous nature of long COVID recovery.

Population-based survey of 7,500 US respondents examining whether chemical intolerance predisposes individuals to worse COVID-19 outcomes and long COVID prevalence. Found that those with high chemical intolerance reported significantly greater COVID-19 severity and long COVID prevalence compared to medium/low CI groups, with differential effects by race/ethnicity.

This cross-sectional study examined novel ECG patterns in elite soccer players following COVID-19 infection, finding that 3% demonstrated novel ECG changes with ~90% subsequently diagnosed with cardiac inflammation. The study documents cardiac sequelae post-COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared Long COVID outcomes in 673 UK hospital survivors across SARS-CoV-2 waves (wildtype vs Alpha variant) at 6 weeks post-discharge. It found that pre-existing lung disease and admission symptom severity predicted higher Long COVID symptom burden, but variant type did not significantly impact Long COVID presence or symptom count.

Cross-sectional study of 458 UK military personnel assessing post-COVID-19 symptoms across two COVID-19 waves using remote rehabilitation assessments at DMRC Stanford Hall. Found post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence decreased from 43% to 2% between waves, with symptom patterns differing by wave and alert level, but did not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 177 COVID-19 ICU patients assessing the association between long COVID complaints and psychiatric disorders 4 months post-hospitalization. Found that long COVID complaint burden was significantly higher in patients with psychiatric disorders and new-onset psychiatric disorders, but this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 718 Belgian Defence personnel with confirmed prior COVID-19 infection assessed the prevalence of long COVID symptoms, associated risk factors, and impact on quality of life. Nearly half reported persistent symptoms lasting ≥3 months, with fatigue, low energy, and breathing difficulties most common; physical activity >3 hours/week reduced risk by half.

Web-based cross-sectional survey investigating the prevalence of fibromyalgia in 616 post-COVID-19 patients 6 months after diagnosis. Found that 30.7% met ACR criteria for fibromyalgia, with male gender and obesity as strongest predictors, but this is an observational study with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining risk factors for cardiac-related postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) in 442 community-dwelling adults after acute COVID-19 infection. Found 43% prevalence of cardiac PASC symptoms, with pre-existing conditions and hospitalization status as significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional study assessed work productivity impairment in 89 healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 syndrome using the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment Questionnaire. Patients with post-COVID syndrome showed significantly higher drops in productivity and daily activities compared to those without persistent symptoms, highlighting occupational health impacts of the condition.

Cross-sectional survey assessing knowledge and prevalence of long COVID complications among 118 electronics industry employees in South India. Approximately 75% reported post-COVID complications (mainly fatigue and respiratory symptoms), but the study is observational only—it does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,038 MSM in the UK examining COVID-19 history and long-COVID prevalence via self-report questionnaire. Found 32.8% reported COVID-19 history with 25.2% of those reporting long-COVID symptoms, but this is an observational prevalence study with no treatment or intervention evaluated.

This conference abstract examines the relationship between health deprivation and post-COVID fibrosis development in COVID-19 survivors. It is excluded because it presents only a conference abstract with summary data rather than a full study protocol or results, and does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 384 COVID-19 hospitalized patients assessed a median of 54 days post-discharge to document persistent symptoms, biomarker abnormalities, and imaging changes. Found high prevalence of breathlessness (53%), fatigue (69%), and abnormal chest radiographs (38%), but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study uses phase-resolved functional lung MRI to characterize lung perfusion abnormalities in children and adolescents with post-COVID-19 condition compared to healthy controls. While it identifies distinct lung perfusion phenotypes correlated with fatigue and heart rate, it is a diagnostic imaging study without any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials dataset.

Cross-sectional study comparing oxygen uptake kinetics and cardiopulmonary function in 35 severe COVID-19 survivors (3-6 months post-ICU) versus 18 matched controls. Found significant impairments in VO2 kinetics, peak oxygen uptake, and chronotropic responses in survivors, suggesting metabolic dysfunction underlying post-COVID exertional intolerance.

Cross-sectional study comparing lung morphology and function via low-field MRI in children and adolescents with post-COVID-19 condition versus healthy controls. Found reduced ventilation-perfusion matching in both recovered and long COVID groups compared to controls, but no treatment or intervention was tested.

Secondary analysis of the French SAPRIS-SERO cohort examining persistent symptoms in relation to IgG seropositivity and self-reported long COVID. Identifies three potential long COVID subsyndromes (anosmia, respiratory, fatigue-related) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study comparing grip and leg strength between 99 long-COVID patients and 97 controls, finding significantly lower muscle strength in COVID survivors. The reduced strength was largely mediated by lower appendicular lean mass index, suggesting muscle wasting is a key contributor to functional limitations in long COVID.

This cross-sectional study examines heart rate variability (HRV) as a potential cardiac health indicator in individuals with varying COVID-19 infection and vaccination histories. The study finds correlations between increased COVID-19 exposure and decreased HRV but does not test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey measuring anxiety prevalence in 250 post-COVID-19 patients using the Hamilton Anxiety Scale in Mexico. Found 92% of participants had some level of anxiety, with 44% moderate and 18% severe anxiety.

A cross-sectional study comparing cardiorespiratory abnormalities in 52 ICU survivors with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) stratified by mechanical ventilation use, versus 19 uninfected controls. The study found that PASC patients had significant cardiorespiratory dysfunction independent of whether they received invasive mechanical ventilation, with abnormalities related to ventilatory inefficiency and impaired aerobic metabolism rather than ventilation type.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of persistent COVID-19 symptoms among Palestinian adults in the West Bank and their associations with hospitalization and recovery duration. Provides epidemiological insights into long-term consequences of SARS-CoV-2 infection in a Middle Eastern population.

Cross-sectional study of 100 post-COVID patients assessing olfactory and gustatory dysfunction using standardized chemosensory tests and oral health-related quality of life measures. Found high prevalence of persistent smell and taste alterations (62% and 68% respectively) correlated with poor oral health outcomes, with blood group as a predisposing factor for smell loss.

Cross-sectional survey of 50+ year-olds in Europe examining the association between pre-existing diabetes and long COVID-19 risk. Finds that diabetes increases odds of long COVID (OR=1.37) and this relationship is moderated by age, with strongest effect at age 50.

This cross-sectional study examined menstrual cycle changes in 141 women of reproductive age following COVID-19 infection and vaccination. While it documents post-COVID menstrual abnormalities as a sequela, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed olfactory function and quality of life in 65 COVID-19 patients using standardized olfactory tests and questionnaires, comparing results to healthy controls and patients with olfactory loss from other viral infections. While QoL was significantly impaired in COVID-19 patients with olfactory dysfunction, the study did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing cognitive performance and mental health outcomes in 1,218 long COVID patients versus 314 controls using behavioral tests and questionnaires. Found significant impairments in verbal memory, attention, and inhibitory control in LC patients alongside elevated depression, anxiety, fatigue, and stress.

This cross-sectional study assessed the impact of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) on quality of life and activity participation in 134 patients discharged from ICU in Kuwait. While it documents PASC symptoms and their association with functional outcomes, it is observational without a treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.

Cross-sectional survey of 214 children in West Sumatra assessing prevalence of long COVID symptoms 4+ weeks post-infection. Found 28.5% with respiratory disorders, 26.2% with sleep disorders, 23.4% with fatigue, and other neurological/gastrointestinal symptoms, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and impact of long COVID among mining employees in South Africa, finding ~7% prevalence with no significant productivity differences. The study explicitly acknowledges limited generalizability and calls for future research on treatment interventions rather than evaluating any specific treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared sleep disturbances in 21 post-COVID patients versus 10 healthy controls using polysomnography and questionnaires. Post-COVID patients showed significantly higher sleep apnea prevalence (60% vs 10%), elevated apnea-hypopnea index, and worse self-reported sleep quality, indicating sleep disorders are common in long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing circulating endothelial cells (CECs), microthrombosis, and NETosis markers in 23 long COVID patients versus 7 controls at a VA clinic. Found significantly elevated CECs, microclots, and dysregulated platelet aggregation in long COVID cases, suggesting these may serve as biomarkers or mechanisms of vascular dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) symptoms and depressive symptoms/perceived stress in 197 COVID-19 survivors. Found that PASC and cardiac PASC were significantly associated with higher odds of moderate-severe depression and high perceived stress, with authors recommending integrated mental health interventions in PASC care.

Cross-sectional study evaluating spirometry patterns in 72 post-COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms. Found 55.5% had normal spirometry, with obstructive respiratory disorder being the most common abnormality (29.2%), suggesting dyspnea may warrant further investigation beyond spirometry.

Cross-sectional observational study examining clinical differences between POTS and IST in 200 post-COVID-19 patients at a Swedish hospital (2020-2023). Found POTS more common than IST with 31% overlap, significant differences in age and hypertension prevalence, and Ivabradine/Pyridostigmine as most frequently prescribed pharmacological treatments.

Cross-sectional study of 75 post-COVID patients in Tunisia assessing prevalence of fatigue, cognitive complaints, dyspnea, anxiety, and depression using validated scales. Study found high prevalences of these symptoms (fatigue 88%, cognitive complaints 80%, anxiety 44%, depression 28.6%) with significant associations between symptom clusters.

Cross-sectional survey of 97 PASC (long COVID) patients examining the association between socioeconomic status, race/ethnicity, and negative health behaviors during and after the pandemic using the COVID-19 Behavior Questionnaire. Finds that lower-income and non-white patients report significantly higher negative health behaviors, particularly in chronic health maintenance and public health awareness domains.

This cross-sectional study compares cardiorespiratory recovery outcomes between post-COVID-19 patients who exercise regularly versus those with sedentary lifestyles using 6-minute walk tests and Harvard step tests. Regular physical exercise was associated with significantly higher cardiopulmonary efficiency and better baseline oxygen saturation, supporting the integration of structured physical activity into post-COVID rehabilitation.

Cross-sectional study examining exercise capacity and chronotropic incompetence in people with HIV (PWH) with and without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and PASC. Found that PWH had reduced peak oxygen consumption and adjusted heart rate reserve compared to controls, but PASC was not strongly associated with reduced exercise capacity in PWH.

Cross-sectional survey of 100 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID symptoms 6-12 weeks after recovery. Found 87% developed one or more symptoms (weakness, body ache, neuropsychiatric symptoms), with 47% requiring some treatment, but the study is observational and does not evaluate any specific intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines whether acute COVID-19 infection affects menstrual cycle patterns in 200 female medical students in Iraq. While it reports that 28% of infected participants experienced cycle irregularities, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 infection effects rather than long COVID (persistent post-infection symptoms weeks to months later).

Cross-sectional survey of 307 Chinese patients assessing the impact of long COVID on health-related quality of life using EQ-5D-5L and propensity score matching. Found that 40% had persistent symptoms with lower health utility scores compared to non-long-COVID group, identifying fatigue, coughing, and cognitive decline as common symptoms.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between lifetime interpersonal violence experience and post-COVID-19 condition symptoms among women in Kentucky. Found that women with lifetime interpersonal violence history had significantly higher rates of post-COVID symptoms (aRR=2.09), but this is an observational study assessing risk factors rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing symptom duration in 372 children with SARS-CoV-2 vs other viral illnesses. Finds no significant difference in symptom persistence between COVID-positive and COVID-negative children.

This cross-sectional survey assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among 325 patients recovered from COVID-19 in Vietnam using the EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS scales. While the study identifies significant HRQoL impairment associated with long COVID symptoms, it is observational only and does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining long COVID symptom patterns among 4,033 UK healthcare workers, stratified by ethnicity, sex, and occupational role. Identifies distinct symptom profiles (neurocognitive, cardiopulmonary, systemic) varying by demographic and occupational factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional online survey compared subjective cognitive decline between 98 adults with COVID-19 diagnosis and 317 never diagnosed, using the Everyday Cognition Scale. COVID-19 diagnosis was significantly associated with greater subjective cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory, language, attention, organizational ability), but the study does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compared healthcare expenditures between U.S. adults with and without long COVID using 2022 MEPS data (16,762 adults). Individuals with long COVID had significantly higher total healthcare spending ($11,567 vs $7,448), primarily driven by increased office-based visits (35% higher) and outpatient services (118% higher).

Cross-sectional analysis of 51,288 U.S. adults from the 2022 Census Household Pulse Survey examining the association between long COVID and vision difficulties. Adults with long COVID had significantly higher odds of reporting vision difficulties compared to those without COVID (47.6% vs. 31.9%), though the study is observational without treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining prevalence of COVID-19 infection, mortality, and post-infection lung fibrosis in 1,039 patients with type 2 diabetes. While the paper mentions post-COVID lung fibrosis, it focuses on acute COVID outcomes and vaccination effects in diabetic populations rather than long COVID syndrome treatment or interventions.

Cross-sectional study of 178 long COVID patients examining the relationship between elevated serum IL-1ra levels and symptom prevalence. Found that patients with elevated IL-1ra were 2.9–3× more likely to report fatigue, muscle aches, and dyspnea on exertion, suggesting a mechanistic link between systemic inflammation and symptom type.

This cross-sectional study from the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examines COVID-19 outcomes, including long COVID, among U.S. adolescents aged 12-17 years, stratified by vaccination status. The study reports prevalence estimates and associations between vaccination and COVID-19 outcomes, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

Cross-sectional study characterizing post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) symptoms and functional impact among 3,037 COVID-19 survivors in a Malaysian rehabilitation center.
