Found PCC in 71.1% of patients with fatigue and dyspnea as most common symptoms, and significant reductions in respiratory, ambulatory, and musculoskeletal function compared to non-PCC patients.

Cross-sectional study of 183 Black people with HIV in the UK assessing post-acute sequelae of COVID-19, including functional impairment, frailty, respiratory symptoms, and mental health outcomes. Found that COVID-19 history was associated with reduced ability to carry out daily activities and various health issues, though 85% of those with COVID-19 history reported full recovery.

This cross-sectional study evaluated neuropsychiatric symptoms in 50 Long COVID patients referred for neuropsychological evaluation using the Neurobehavioral Symptom Inventory. The study found clinically elevated symptoms in 76% of patients, with cognitive and affective domains most affected, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 193 Hong Kong residents with long COVID symptoms exploring the impact on daily activities and treatment preferences. Study identifies respiratory, systemic, sleep, and cognitive symptoms as most prevalent and notes strong preference for traditional Chinese medicine, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional survey examined physical activity and sedentary behavior in 154 individuals with post-exertional malaise from long COVID, comparing activity levels before and after COVID-19 infection. The study found that patients became significantly more sedentary and inactive post-COVID, with greater declines in women and those more severely affected, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey assessed Long COVID prevalence among healthcare workers in two Singapore tertiary hospitals and its impact on work-role functioning using the WRFQv2.0 instrument. While the study found 47.5% Long COVID prevalence with significant work functioning impairment, it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention—it is purely observational/epidemiological.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,764 COVID-19 positive residents in Quebec comparing employment status changes between those with long COVID and those who recovered, identifying clinical and demographic factors associated with decreased employment. Finds that long COVID patients are significantly more likely to experience employment decrease (15.6% vs 5.4%), particularly those with moderate-to-severe health decline, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between resilience and health-related quality of life in 97 post-COVID-19 patients, with and without lingering symptoms. The study found that approximately 35% of post-COVID patients had low resilience levels, and that age and depression significantly impacted resilience, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A cross-sectional survey study of 3,094 adults from a virtual COVID-19 clinic identifying risk factors for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). The study found that severe acute COVID-19 symptoms, female gender, hospitalization, psychological repercussions, and prolonged recovery time were associated with PASC development, but conducted no intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional survey (N=605) uses the Health Belief Model to examine how awareness and understanding of long COVID shape COVID-19 preventive behavior intentions among U.S. adults. The study finds that perceived susceptibility to long COVID and self-efficacy predict intent to adopt preventive behaviors like masking and booster vaccination, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

Cross-sectional survey of 308 COVID-19 infected individuals in Iran examining associations between clinical/sociodemographic factors and long COVID symptoms. Identifies females, educated persons, reinfection history, underlying diseases, and COVID severity as risk factors for long COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 490 long COVID patients examining the relationship between long COVID symptoms and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, suicidal ideation). Finds that 30% screened positive for depression, 46% for anxiety, and that female sex and symptom burden are associated with increased psychiatric risk.

A cross-sectional survey of 491 adults with post-COVID-19 symptoms that uses exploratory factor analysis to identify symptom clusters across different timeframes (5-8 weeks vs 9+ weeks). The study identifies six coherent symptom clusters including respiratory, cognitive, cardiac, and mental health domains, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated perception of verticality in 60 post-COVID-19 patients (24 hospitalized, 36 non-hospitalized) using subjective visual vertical and subjective haptic vertical tests. The study found that hospitalized patients with post-COVID-19 showed significantly less accurate visual and haptic verticality perception compared to non-hospitalized patients, correlating with infection severity.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,644 Swedish young adults examining the prevalence and characteristics of long-term COVID-19 symptoms (≥4 weeks) from August-November 2020. Long-term symptoms occurred in 10.8% of those with suspected COVID-19 and were associated with pre-existing conditions like rhinitis, migraine, and lower self-rated health.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,912 Chinese college students assessing physical and mental health symptoms 3 months after COVID-19 recovery. Identifies three clusters of symptom severity through latent class analysis but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 201 German adults with long COVID examined how self-compassion and self-coldness mediate the effects of stigma on well-being and flourishing. While the study identifies psychological mechanisms and suggests interventions, it is observational without any treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between lifestyle factors (physical activity, substance use, diet) and psychiatric symptoms (depression, anxiety, PTSD) in 730 COVID-19 survivors at 6-11 months post-hospitalization. While the paper addresses long COVID sequelae, it is observational and does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study compares psychological distress (anxiety and depression) in 220 long COVID patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction (>6 months duration) versus 102 asymptomatic controls. The study found significantly higher rates of depression and anxiety in the OD group, with severity correlating with olfactory and nasal symptom severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 342 post-COVID-19 patients to evaluate acceptance of eHealth interventions for symptom management using the UTAUT model. Findings showed moderate-to-high acceptance, with higher acceptance in patients with lower education, moderate-to-severe initial infection, ongoing impairment, and comorbid mental illness.

Cross-sectional survey of 213 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia conducted ≥3 months post-infection to characterize persistent symptoms and risk factors for delayed return to baseline health. Found 51.2% had residual symptoms (fatigue, anosmia, muscle aches most common) and 71.4% reported return to baseline, with chronic comorbidities as a significant predictor of delayed recovery.

A cross-sectional survey assessing sleep disturbance prevalence among 312 PASC clinic patients using the PROMIS-Sleep Disturbance framework. Found 41% with no sleep disturbance, 51.3% with mild-to-moderate disturbance, and 7.7% with severe disturbance, with modest negative correlation to time since initial COVID infection.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,108 primary care patients assessing prevalence and predictors of post-acute COVID-19 symptoms in an Italian population. Found 29% prevalence with fatigue, memory, and concentration impairment as most common symptoms; identified female sex, age >50, BMI >25, and autoimmune disease as significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional study examined functional cognition and health in 118 community-dwelling adults, comparing 25 with prior COVID-19 infection to uninfected controls. No significant differences were found between infected and uninfected groups, though men showed better functional cognition and health measures than women overall.

Cross-sectional survey of 536 long COVID clinic patients assessing symptom improvement and perceived helpfulness of various interventions including medications, supplements, and neuromodulation. Patients reported significant symptom improvement from baseline, with low-dose naltrexone (58%), vagal nerve stimulation (53%), and fisetin (64%) rated as most helpful, though complete recovery remained low at 23 months post-infection.

A cross-sectional study assessing health-related quality of life among 271 COVID-19 survivors in Nepal using the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire. The study identifies employment, exercise, and family structure as positive factors for QoL, while chronic disease is a significant barrier to well-being.

This cross-sectional analysis uses Household Pulse Survey data to examine associations between race, socioeconomic status, and long COVID prevalence in the U.S. The study finds that socioeconomic status buffers racial disparities in long COVID risk, with larger protective effects among White individuals than racial/ethnic minorities.

Cross-sectional survey of 167 airline crew members examining factors affecting quality of life, including post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence (4.2%) and its impact across physical, psychological, social, and environmental domains. Found significant differences in QoL scores based on age, job role, years of service, and post-COVID-19 syndrome status, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 845 COVID-19 survivors examining predictors of persistent long COVID symptoms at 1 year post-infection. Identifies female sex, higher income, and greater acute symptom burden as risk factors for symptom persistence.

This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed symptom experiences and perceived health status in 86 individuals with long COVID in Thailand using telephone interviews and standardized screening. The study found that 75.6% of participants experienced long COVID with multiple symptoms lasting a median of 5.6 months, with significant correlations between symptom severity and negative health perception, but it does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 251 mild COVID-19 patients assessing the prevalence and symptom spectrum of long COVID-19 (defined as symptoms persisting >28 days) and its impact on quality of life. Found 28.2% prevalence of long COVID-19 with musculoskeletal and respiratory symptoms most common, and significantly worse fatigue and quality of life scores compared to patients without long COVID-19.

A cross-sectional study assessing the correlation between vitamin D levels and anosmia (loss of smell) in 143 patients attending a post-acute COVID syndrome clinic. The study found an association between anosmia and vitamin D deficiency in patients under 65 years, but this pattern did not hold in older age groups.

This cross-sectional study compared carotid intima-media thickness between 47 recovered severe COVID-19 patients (3-6 months post-hospitalization) and 42 healthy controls using Doppler sonography. The study found significantly lower cIMT in recovered COVID-19 patients compared to controls, suggesting endothelial dysfunction may not be the primary driver of post-COVID vascular complications.

An exploratory cross-sectional study evaluating long-term home oxygen therapy (LTOT) as a strategy to reduce hospitalization time in COVID-19 patients with persistent hypoxemia. Most patients did not need to maintain LTOT beyond 15 days post-discharge, suggesting it is effective as a temporary intervention for both ICU and ward patients.

A cross-sectional study of 1,124 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients describing the clinical profile and prevalence of persistent symptoms >4 weeks post-infection. Found that 76.6% reported persistent symptoms, with cognitive disorders and asthenia being the most common complaints, showing gradual improvement over 12+ months.

Cross-sectional survey of 90 patients in Agadir describing taste and smell disorders during and after acute COVID-19, documenting prevalence and recovery patterns. While the study addresses post-acute COVID symptoms, it is descriptive/observational without testing any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional observational study examines the relationship between prior traumatic stress history and autonomic symptom burden in 404 US adults with and without COVID-19 infection. The study finds that prior traumatic stress positively moderates the association between COVID-19 history and autonomic dysregulation, but is a passive observational survey without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study of 121 long COVID patients examining headache characteristics pre- and post-infection, comparing changes in frequency, severity, and analgesic use. Found that pre-existing headaches worsened significantly post-COVID while new-onset headaches were common and typically resolved within one month.

This paper maps rehabilitation provision for UK patients after COVID-19 hospitalization as part of the PHOSP-COVID study. It is a survey/mapping study of existing rehabilitation services rather than a treatment trial, and does not evaluate outcomes of a specific intervention.

Observational cross-sectional study characterizing clinical profile and symptoms in 89 long-COVID patients via internet survey using the C19-YRS screening tool. Found significant impairments in dyspnea, fatigue, pain, psychological distress, and quality of life, plus additional sequelae including throat sensitivity, swallowing problems, and cognitive issues.

Cross-sectional study of 276 long COVID patients in Indonesia treated with inhaled long-acting bronchodilators and corticosteroids (LABACS) over 3 months, assessing symptoms, respiratory function, and imaging. Treatment with all three LABACS regimens showed significant improvements in lung obstruction, spirometry measurements, mMRC scores, and chest X-ray findings.

This cross-sectional study examined dyspnoea quality, mental health symptoms, and exercise responses in 49 COVID-19 survivors 4 months post-illness, comparing those with and without persistent dyspnoea. The dyspnoea group showed greater anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress symptoms, ventilatory inefficiency, and deconditioning, suggesting persistent dyspnoea post-COVID-19 is linked to abnormal pulmonary gas exchange and psychological burden.

A cross-sectional study examining associations between long COVID, physical activity level, functional decline, and health-related quality of life in 121 older adults (age 60-90) at 6 months post-infection. Found that fatigue, pain, low physical activity, and cognitive-communication problems were significant predictors of reduced physical and mental health-related quality of life.

Cross-sectional study of 421 Latin American participants characterizing new daily persistent headache (NDPH) after SARS-CoV-2 infection and identifying associated risk factors. Finds 25% of persistent headache cases meet NDPH criteria, with occipital location, burning character, and palpebral edema during acute infection as significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional study followed 1,806 COVID-19 patients infected with omicron variant three months post-discharge to identify factors associated with long COVID development. The analysis found female sex, allergy history, and higher vaccination doses as risk factors, with persistent fatigue, amnesia, and insomnia being the most common long COVID symptoms.

This study uses repeated surveys from the COVID-19 Schools Infection Survey to describe the weighted prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition and persisting symptoms among English schoolchildren aged 4-18 years during 2021/22. It found that 1.8-6.9% of children met the definition of post-COVID-19 condition depending on age group, with specific symptoms like loss of smell and taste more prevalent in those with previous positive COVID-19 tests.

A cross-sectional household survey of 12,925 SARS-CoV-2 cases in Bangladesh examining the prevalence and clinical presentation of pain symptoms in long COVID patients. The study found pain affects 1-3.1% of the population and significantly reduces quality of life, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 150 general practitioners (GPs) in Belgium and Malta examining their knowledge, perceptions, and experience caring for long COVID patients. The study found that GPs frequently encounter long COVID patients but report insufficient knowledge and lack of multidisciplinary coordination, with most providing care independently rather than through coordinated multidisciplinary teams.

Cross-sectional survey of 12.61% long COVID prevalence among primary healthcare workers in Jiangsu, China, identifying age, sex, work stress, and vaccination as risk/protective factors. Study is observational without intervention and does not evaluate any treatment or therapeutic outcome.

This cross-sectional study investigated associations between clinical symptoms, vaccination status, antibody responses, and post-COVID-19 sequelae in 110 Thai COVID-19 patients infected with Delta or Omicron variants during a 1-year follow-up period. Key findings showed Delta infections were associated with pneumonia and post-infection symptoms like forgetfulness and hair loss, while Omicron was linked to upper respiratory symptoms, with vaccination and antibody responses showing differential patterns between variants.

This cross-sectional study identifies symptom clusters in long COVID patients 9 and 12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using hierarchical cluster analysis on 552 individuals from a Portuguese surveillance database. Four clusters were identified (no/minor symptoms, multi-symptoms, joint pain, and neurocognitive-related), with clusters remaining stable over time except for increased memory loss and concentration issues in the neurocognitive cluster at 12 months.

This cross-sectional survey assessed quality of life, functional impairment, and cognitive decline in 435 long COVID patients compared to those who recovered or never had long COVID symptoms, measured at a median of 23.3 months post-infection. The study found that long COVID patients experienced significantly greater impairment across all health domains, with persistent cognitive complaints and fatigue even among those who reported recovery.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 114 long COVID patients to assess neuropsychiatric symptoms and explore how personality traits and social support relate to psychological distress and cognitive decline through mediation analysis. While the paper is about long COVID, it is an observational survey without any treatment intervention—participants were not given or evaluated for any specific therapy.

Cross-sectional observational study examining renal function in 246 long COVID patients from a clinical care program in the Amazon region. Found renal function decline in 33.7% of patients, with older age and glycaemic alterations as risk factors, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional study assessing post-COVID functional status and associated sociodemographic factors among 3,067 residents of vulnerable neighborhoods in two Brazilian cities. Found 34.6% prevalence of post-COVID functional limitations, with increased risk in those with comorbidities, reinfection, and healthcare access barriers.

Cross-sectional study measuring heart rate variability (HRV) as a marker of autonomic nervous system function in 173 COVID-19 patients with and without long COVID symptoms. Found that young to middle-aged patients with LC showed lower HRV in the very-low-frequency domain and higher rates of autonomic dysfunction compared to those without LC.

This cross-sectional study assessed the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on quality of life, mental health, and functional capacity in 25 ethnically diverse and socioeconomically vulnerable individuals from the Brazilian Amazon. The study found high rates of fatigue (88%) and psychological symptoms, with worse outcomes associated with older age, lower education, and lower income, but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines coagulation abnormalities in 1,473 COVID-19 patients compared to 2,310 controls, tracking multiple time points from acute phase to 12 months post-infection. The findings document persistent coagulation dysfunction in long COVID patients, including abnormal D-dimer (66.96% at 12 months) and prolonged PT/INR, but no intervention or treatment is tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 535 long COVID patients in Quebec assessing symptom profiles, functional impact, and quality of life priorities. Study identifies fatigue and post-exercise malaise as primary concerns but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 6,572 Chinese participants examining the relationship between vaccination status and COVID-19 infection outcomes and long COVID symptoms. Study found that booster shots reduced risk of specific symptoms, but vaccination timing was associated with persistence of symptoms like fatigue and headache beyond one month.

Cross-sectional observational study examining mental health symptoms (depression, anxiety, insomnia) in 228 long COVID patients and their association with autoimmune markers. Found high prevalence of mental health symptoms in long COVID with association to autoantibody positivity, particularly ANA and anti-TPO antibodies.

This cross-sectional study evaluates neurocognitive screening tools and cognitive impairment rates in 102 COVID-19 patients (ambulatory vs hospitalized) 24 days post-infection. While highly relevant to long COVID, it is excluded because it is a descriptive assessment study without any treatment intervention—patients are only evaluated, not treated.

Cross-sectional survey of 783 healthcare workers in Qatar examining prevalence and profile of long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors. Three-quarters reported long-term symptoms post-infection, with fatigue most common and significant gender disparities observed; no interventions or treatments were tested.

Cross-sectional study of 699 patients from a COVID-19 telehealth service examining the prevalence and associated factors of long COVID symptoms. Found 26.8% prevalence of long COVID with cognitive symptoms, chronic diarrhea, and cough being most common; female sex, lower education, lower income, and anosmia during acute COVID were significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional study used comet assay to measure DNA damage in 29 post-COVID-19 patients stratified by initial COVID-19 severity, compared to 10 healthy controls. The study found significantly elevated DNA damage in long COVID patients correlated with COVID-19 severity, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 93 COVID-19 survivors evaluated ~20 weeks post-discharge to identify risk factors and radiological/functional sequelae of long COVID. Found obesity, ICU admission, and NIV requirement associated with long COVID; 45% of patients had long COVID with fatigue and dyspnea as most common symptoms.

This multicentre cross-sectional study investigates the prevalence of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and thrombus resolution in COVID-19 survivors who experienced acute pulmonary embolism. The findings indicate that CTEPH is not more common after COVID-19-associated PE than after non-COVID PE, and thrombus resolution patterns are similar between groups.

A psychological needs analysis of 47 long COVID clinic patients assessing anxiety, depression, and PTSD using validated instruments (GAD-7, PHQ-9, PCL-5, b-IPQ). The analysis identifies depression as a key intervention target but presents only baseline assessment data without testing or evaluating any actual treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining cognitive symptoms and brain structural changes in 109 long COVID patients versus 28 healthy controls approximately two years post-infection in Argentina. Found persistent cognitive complaints, brain atrophy in cerebellum and parietal regions, and reduced cortical thickness despite no significant objective cognitive impairment on testing.

This study assessed long-term self-reported disability in public employees after COVID-19 compared to controls with negative PCR tests using the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule. It found higher disability rates in the post-COVID phase (64%) versus controls (52%), with more severe disability among women, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining Alice in Wonderland syndrome (AIWS) symptoms in 421 adults with persistent headache after COVID-19 across Latin America. Found that 25.2% reported AIWS symptoms, with younger age and pre-existing migraine as risk factors, but this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 936 school-aged children in China examining COVID-19 symptoms and long COVID (LC 28) prevalence following infection in early 2023. Found LC 28 in 3.4% of children, with alopecia, cognitive dysfunction, and emotional problems being the most common persistent symptoms.

Cross-sectional study developing a prediction model for depressive symptoms among middle-aged/elderly CVD patients who recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection in Wuhan, China. While it identifies long COVID-related predictors (fatigue, insomnia, PTSD, anxiety), it is a secondary analysis of baseline depression prevalence rather than a treatment evaluation study.

This study validates a Thai translation of the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) for assessing long COVID symptom severity in community members. While focused on long COVID, it is a validation study of a measurement tool, not a treatment intervention study, and therefore does not meet criteria for the clinical trials pipeline.

A nationwide cross-sectional survey in China examining acute and long COVID-19 symptoms and associated risk factors during the omicron-dominant period in 32,528 COVID-19 patients. The study reports a 19.68% long COVID rate at 3+ months post-infection, with muscle weakness, headache, and smell/taste disorders as primary symptoms, identifying age, smoking, gender, and vaccination as risk factors.

Population-based cross-sectional survey in Iran examining the prevalence and patterns of long COVID symptoms among 1,561 individuals with prior COVID-19 infection and a control group. Found 36.4% experienced persistent symptoms post-recovery, with older age, prior hospitalization, cardiovascular disease, and steroid/chemotherapy use associated with long COVID development.

This international survey study (ICOSS-II) examined associations between changes in sleep duration and self-rated health among 1,509 COVID-19 survivors across 16 countries. It found that both decreased and increased habitual sleep duration after infection were associated with lower self-rated health and post-COVID symptoms like fatigue and shortness of breath, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional survey assessed post-COVID-19 manifestations in 428 Saudi Arabian college students, categorizing them by symptom duration (recovered, prolonged, or persistent). Young adults showed mild overall symptom severity with persistent symptoms including loss of smell/taste and shortness of breath, and a significant association with depression.

This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence of long COVID and characterized symptom clusters among 337 previously infected individuals in Bangkok, Thailand. The analysis identified three symptom clusters (common symptoms/communication, fatigue/functioning/nutrition, psychosocial impacts) and found a significant relationship between symptom severity and functional disability, with no intervention or treatment tested.

This cross-sectional study analyzes the association between long COVID symptoms and functional disability (BADL/IADL) in Brazilian adults and seniors using data from the SulCovid-19 study. The findings show that specific symptoms like dyspnea, joint pain, and muscle pain are associated with limitations in daily functioning, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A nationally representative cross-sectional survey of Mexican COVID-19 survivors estimating the prevalence of post-COVID conditions (37.0%) and characterizing common persistent symptoms including fatigue, myalgia, and respiratory distress. This is an observational prevalence study with no treatment intervention, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the intervention trial pipeline.

A prospective cross-sectional study examining potential long-term ocular complications in 21 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-recovery using ophthalmological exams and imaging. Found no evidence of retinal damage or vascular complications, concluding ocular complications are unlikely at 3 months without prior eye involvement.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition among young adults (n=2,098) and its associations with general health, stress, and lifestyle factors three years post-pandemic onset. Found 10.5% with previous and 3.9% with ongoing PCC symptoms, with reduced physical activity and worsened dietary habits in the ongoing PCC group, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional study assesses the prevalence and distribution of persistent symptoms in young adults (aged 18-25) with long COVID using the Symptom Burden Questionnaire, evaluating 123 symptoms across 17 health domains. The research finds high rates of mental health issues, sleep disturbances, and cognitive dysfunction, with female participants reporting greater symptom severity.

This is a cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System survey examining the prevalence of long COVID among US adults and factors associated with it. The study reports 7.2% prevalence of long COVID and identifies higher risk among women, middle-aged individuals, and those with chronic conditions or socioeconomic disadvantage, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined the association between adverse childhood events (ACEs) and long-term COVID-19 symptoms using 2022 BRFSS data from 14,560 participants. The study found that exposure to ACEs, particularly sexual abuse, household substance abuse, and household mental illness, was positively associated with increased risk of long-term COVID symptoms, with no intervention tested.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between physical activity levels and various outcomes (symptoms, cardiovascular fitness, sleep quality, QoL) in 219 long COVID patients. The results show that moderate-to-high PA is associated with better cardiorespiratory fitness, heart rate recovery, sleep quality, and QoL domains, but this is an observational study without intervention assignment—patients self-selected into PA groups rather than being assigned a treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 780 long COVID patients examining gender differences in disability, employment, sick leave, and activities of daily living. Finds women report significantly higher mental fatigue than men, but ADL challenges are largely similar between genders.

This cross-sectional study compared accelerometer-measured physical activity and sleep quality between 65 COVID-19 recovered individuals (including 3 with post-COVID syndrome) and 65 healthy controls in the UAE. The study found no significant differences in physical activity or most sleep parameters, except longer sleep latency in recovered individuals, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined associations between long COVID symptoms and loneliness among 5,692 World Trade Center Health Registry enrollees who reported acute COVID-19 infection in 2022-23. The study found that enrollees with long COVID symptoms had significantly higher prevalence of loneliness (PR=1.19) compared to those without symptoms, with stronger associations for emotional loneliness.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of 3,048 Slovenian adults examining relationships between pre-pandemic lifestyle patterns and mental health outcomes in people with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Found 29.5% of infected individuals met PASC criteria with elevated stress, anxiety, and depression alongside reduced well-being, though this is an observational study without treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 530 post-COVID patients assessing body composition and risk factors for sarcopenia 3 months after moderate-to-severe COVID-19. Found that age >60, obesity, and prolonged hospitalization with mechanical ventilation were associated with higher sarcopenia risk, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between obesity and long COVID prevalence, as well as obesity's impact on physical and mental health outcomes in 3,663 SARS-CoV-2 infected participants. While about long COVID, this is an observational epidemiologic study that does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

A multi-centre cross-sectional study of 3,693 Chinese individuals examining long COVID prevalence, symptom patterns, and risk factors using a WHO-based definition. Older age, female sex, and reinfection increased long COVID risk, while vaccination and traditional Chinese medicine use were protective factors.

Cross-sectional study of 997 Thai university students assessing the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and identifying risk factors. Found 21.9% prevalence with respiratory, neurological, and psychological symptoms as common manifestations, and identified severe initial infection, illness duration, and poor sleep quality as significant predictors.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between muscle quality index (MQI) and pulmonary function in 748 post-COVID-19 patients with severe-to-critical disease history. Found that low MQI is independently associated with reduced respiratory function, suggesting musculoskeletal weakness as a marker of post-COVID pulmonary impairment.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications in 405 recovered COVID-19 patients from Ethiopia. Found 14.1% prevalence of pulmonary complications associated with older age and lung consolidation on imaging.

Cross-sectional study of 52 patients with respiratory symptoms 4 months after COVID-19 hospitalization, measuring lung function, muscle strength, and physical capacity. Finds 90% had objective respiratory abnormalities, but this is a descriptive assessment study without treatment intervention—it measures existing dysfunction rather than testing a treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,170 nurses in Slovakia examining the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on their health, wellbeing, and working conditions from January to November 2021. About two-thirds reported long COVID symptoms, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely observational and descriptive of prevalence and burden.

Cross-sectional survey of 350 healthcare workers in Iran assessing prevalence and characteristics of long COVID-19 symptoms. Found 75.7% experienced long COVID symptoms, with fatigue, cough, and muscle weakness being most common, and identified several clinical risk factors.

Cross-sectional study of 1,911 Tunisian COVID-19 survivors examining long COVID prevalence (46.5%) and risk factors. Identifies female gender and age ≥60 as risk factors, with complete vaccination as protective, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 362 French nurses about their roles in Long COVID care, finding that nurses informally delegate tasks including psychological support, screening, and therapeutic education. The study identifies implications for formalizing nursing responsibilities in emerging chronic disease management but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared thyroid function (TT3, TT4, TSH) in COVID-19-positive unvaccinated patients, COVID-19-negative vaccinated individuals, and healthy controls. While it documents thyroid hormone abnormalities in post-COVID patients that gradually recover over time, it is a passive observational study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigated insomnia prevalence and risk factors among 437 nurses with long COVID in China using questionnaire surveys and LASSO regression. While the study identifies eleven risk factors associated with insomnia in long COVID patients, it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study examining stigmatization and psychologization experiences in 2,053 adults reporting long COVID or post-COVID-19 vaccination syndrome. Finds high prevalences of stigma (83-90%) and psychologization (82-91%), which correlate with negative mental health outcomes including depression, anxiety, and loneliness.

This cross-sectional survey study of 10,462 Dutch patients with post-COVID-19 condition examined self-perceived barriers to healthcare access. The majority (83.2%) reported at least one barrier, most commonly not knowing who to turn to for help and lack of provider knowledge about PCC.

Cross-sectional population survey of 1,813 French adults examining associations between multimorbidity and post-COVID condition (PCC). Found that multimorbidity, particularly with anxiety or low back pain, significantly increases risk of PCC, but the study is observational without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This paper is a cross-sectional analysis of long COVID treatment programs and centers at top US hospitals, describing their characteristics, services offered, and clinical trial participation. While about long COVID, it does not study treatment outcomes or test an intervention—it is a descriptive survey of existing clinical infrastructure rather than a treatment trial.

This U.S. national survey study (n=16,446) examines the association between cumulative social disadvantage and long COVID prevalence using 2022-2023 NHIS data. The study finds that adults in the highest quartile of social disadvantage have 2.52 times higher odds of long COVID, with pronounced effects among women and non-Hispanic Blacks, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This is a prospective cohort study evaluating patient satisfaction with COVID-19 aftercare one year after hospitalization, using a questionnaire to assess satisfaction with information provision, rehabilitation, and follow-up care. While it addresses post-COVID recovery, it is a satisfaction survey rather than a treatment intervention study, and does not assign or test a specific intervention.

An intersectional analysis of long COVID prevalence and activity limitations using US Household Pulse Survey data from 2022-2023. Findings show that women, people of color, sexual and gender minorities, and those without college education have higher odds of long COVID and activity limitations, with pronounced disparities at the intersection of multiple marginalized identities.

This patient-engaged cohort survey assessed healthcare needs, utilization, and access barriers for long COVID patients in Brazil's universal healthcare system up to 24 months post-hospitalization. The study found high prevalence of long COVID symptoms and significant gaps between healthcare needs and actual access, particularly for specialized services and rehabilitation, with disparities associated with socioeconomic status.

Cross-sectional survey of 202 Ecuadorians examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and long COVID symptom occurrence/intensity. Finds vaccination is protective against long COVID while age and initial infection severity are risk factors, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of 572 post-COVID-19 patients assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using SF-36 and EQ-VAS scales at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection. Study found significantly reduced HRQoL scores compared to normative values, with worse outcomes associated with female gender, comorbidities, and anxiety/depression/sleep disorders, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional survey study measured health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in 406 UK participants with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 at multiple timepoints: pre-COVID, acute COVID, long COVID, and post-COVID. The study found that HRQoL decreased during both acute and long COVID phases but returned to pre-COVID levels by post-COVID assessment, suggesting recovery even among those who experienced long COVID.

Cross-sectional survey of 457 Japanese COVID-19 patients assessing health-related quality of life differences between those with and without persistent symptoms lasting >4 weeks. Finds that ongoing long-COVID symptoms are associated with significantly lower EQ-VAS and EQ-5D-3L scores, representing substantial disease burden.

Cross-sectional survey of 214 long COVID patients examining how reinfection frequency, vaccination status, and risk factors influence long COVID symptomatology. Study finds that more reinfections correlate with more LC symptoms, while vaccination and absence of risk factors are associated with fewer symptoms.

Cross-sectional study of 2,054 COVID-19 survivors examining the association between activities of daily living (ADL) limitations and quality of life in post-COVID-19 patients. Found that 44.35% exhibited post-COVID symptoms with significantly lower quality of life scores across all domains compared to asymptomatic cases, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 384 Malaysian long COVID patients assessing mental health status and quality of life using standardized questionnaires. Found 80% reported mental health decline, with significant associations between long COVID symptoms and negative mental health outcomes and reduced QoL across all domains.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of long COVID symptoms in 300 rural Indian participants who had recovered from COVID-19, measuring both physical symptoms (cough, fatigue, dyspnea) and psychological symptoms (fear, anxiety, sleep problems). The study found that physical and psychological symptoms were positively correlated, with hospitalized patients reporting more symptoms than non-hospitalized patients.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,036 Iraqi COVID-19 survivors examining the prevalence and symptoms of long COVID syndrome and their impact on daily life and mental health. The study reports a 60% prevalence of long COVID with fatigue, joint pain, and hair loss as common symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing mental health status (depression, anxiety, PTSD) in 70 COVID-19 survivors using standardized instruments. Found high rates of post-traumatic stress (41.4%), mild depression, and anxiety, particularly among those with symptomatic acute infection.

Cross-sectional study examining inequalities in work disruption and income loss among COVID-19 infected adults in Brazil, with long COVID as one of several analyzed variables. Finds that individuals with long COVID had 46% greater prevalence of work worsening and 24% greater prevalence of income loss compared to those without long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive status in 1,539 elderly COVID-19 survivors (assessed 6 months post-discharge) versus 466 uninfected controls using standardized cognitive instruments. Severe COVID-19 patients showed significantly higher rates of cognitive impairment and decline compared to non-severe patients and controls, but the study is observational without any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional community survey of 1,027 German patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 examining the prevalence and impact of post-COVID symptoms on functioning and quality of life. The study found 61.9% reported persistent symptoms >3 months, primarily fatigue and sleep disturbances, but concluded that impacts on quality of life and work ability were generally low.

A cross-sectional household survey of 12,925 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh measuring the prevalence and spectrum of long COVID symptoms requiring rehabilitation using the C19-YRS scale. Found that 22% of SARS-CoV-2 cases experienced long COVID symptoms, with 17 new symptoms identified, but the study does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 1,317 COVID-19 patients at University Hospital Verona assessing psychological and psycho-social outcomes at 3, 6, 12, and 18 months post-infection using HADS, SF-36, and IES-R scales. Found 16% reported clinically significant mental distress, with females and younger patients showing worse anxiety/depression outcomes and persistent impairment in quality of life over time.

This cross-sectional survey of 433 long COVID patients in Austria identifies healthcare access barriers and facilitators, with central coordination units reducing reported barriers from 21.0 to 17.4. The study provides health systems research and policy recommendations but does not test any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared dexterity and bimanual coordination between people with long COVID (~16 months duration) and ME/CFS (~16 years duration) using the Purdue pegboard test. Both patient groups showed similarly impaired motor coordination compared to healthy controls, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 302 COVID-19 survivors (mild, moderate, severe) assessing cognitive performance and mental health symptoms at 18+ months post-infection. Found cognitive difficulties in 11.7%-48.9% across groups, with working memory and visual memory inversely associated with symptom severity.

Cross-sectional study assessing resilience and quality of life in 225 patients one year after mechanical ventilation for severe COVID-19. Found that 61.3% resumed daily activities without limitations, while 38% experienced significant decline in quality of life, with high resilience strongly associated with better outcomes.

A cross-sectional survey examining health-related quality of life, disability, and health status in 82 individuals with self-reported long COVID using standardized instruments (EQ-5D-5L, WHODAS 2.0, PROMIS). Found significant chronic health burden with mean EQ-5D-5L utility of 0.51 and WHODAS score of 49.0, with no significant differences across recovery time or acute infection severity.

Cross-sectional survey of 230 COVID-19 survivors (83% Latino) assessing health-related quality of life and social determinants of health 8.1 months post-infection. Financial concerns and interpersonal conflict were associated with significantly worse HRQoL outcomes across multiple domains.

Cross-sectional comparative study assessing cognitive functions in 32 healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 versus 60 healthy controls, using ACE-III test and depression/anxiety scales. Found significant negative effects of post-COVID-19 on attention and memory, with elevated anxiety and depression scores in the post-COVID group.

Cross-sectional study examining sexual dysfunction and psychiatric symptoms in 62 women 6 months post-COVID-19. Found 58% prevalence of sexual dysfunction associated with fatigue, oxygen therapy during acute infection, and vaccination side effects, but no significant differences in psychiatric measures between groups.

This case-control study examines the prevalence of major depressive disorder in post-COVID-19 patients and explores the relationship between TNF-α levels and depression severity. While it includes a control group, it is observational research measuring biomarkers and psychiatric outcomes without testing any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of psychiatric complications (depression and anxiety) in early post-COVID patients (1-3 months post-infection) and their association with inflammatory/coagulation markers and COVID-19 severity. Found depression in 45.6% and GAD in 42.1% of patients, with COVID severity and elevated D-dimer as key predictors.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 100 COVID-19 patients who developed post-COVID ENT complications including anosmia, mucormycosis, and voice changes. Study documents incidence, risk factors, and outcomes but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is purely observational/descriptive of complications.

This cross-sectional study examined 235 post-COVID-19 patients to assess the relationship between dietary patterns (pro- and anti-inflammatory diets) and post-COVID fatigue severity using the Fatigue Assessment Scale and Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Index. Higher intake of anti-inflammatory foods was associated with lower fatigue levels, while pro-inflammatory diet patterns and probiotic use were linked to fatigue reduction, suggesting diet and microbiome support may play a role in post-COVID fatigue recovery.

A cross-sectional study surveying 123 Egyptian patients with persistent COVID-19 symptoms beyond 12 weeks to determine symptom prevalence and use of complementary therapies. The study found high rates of persistent symptoms affecting health, finances, and lifestyle, with many patients using complementary medicine such as probiotics and herbal remedies.

Cross-sectional study examining the frequency, patterns, and determinants of persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms in hospitalized COVID-19 patients using a novel symptom score. Found that myalgia, arthralgia, and activity restriction were most common persistent symptoms, with oxygen therapy need, hypertension, and comorbidities as main determinants of persistent symptoms.

A prospective cross-sectional study of 30 COVID-19 survivors assessing bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cellular patterns and microbial isolates to characterize post-COVID pulmonary complications. Found neutrophilic inflammation in 93.3% and bacterial secondary infections in 63.3% of patients, highlighting persistent pulmonary involvement in post-COVID syndrome.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between COVID-19 stigma and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD) in 1,541 survivors, with resilience as a mediating factor. No treatment intervention was tested; this is an observational study of psychological associations.

Cross-sectional study of 2,281 COVID-19 survivors assessing the persistence of neuropsychiatric symptoms ~2 years post-infection. Found that 34.7% of those with early PCNS had persistent symptoms, with chronic fatigue being the most common, and identified older age as a risk factor for persistence.

This prospective cross-sectional study evaluated pulmonary hemodynamics using right heart catheterization in 20 COVID-19 survivors with suspected post-COVID pulmonary hypertension between April 2022 and March 2024. The study characterized the prevalence, severity, and etiologies of post-COVID PH, finding that interstitial lung disease-related PH was the most common mechanism (55%), followed by CTEPH/CTED (25%) and COVID-19-associated PAH (20%).

A cross-sectional study of 150 COVID-19 survivors examining functional status and persistent symptoms 6 months post-discharge. Found that reduced functional status was associated with severe disease course, prolonged hospitalization/ICU stay, elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ferritin, D-dimer), and persistent neurological/respiratory symptoms.

Cross-sectional study examining affective state and associated factors in 100 long COVID patients using standardized scales (HADS, MoCA, Sit to Stand Test, ISI). Finds that better physical functioning and worse sleep quality are predictors of worse affective state, but this is an observational assessment study with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing anxiety, depression, and PTSD symptoms in 50 COVID-19 survivors in Tunisia 1-3 months post-infection. Found 28% with clinically significant PTSD, 20% with depression, and 30% with anxiety, but no treatment intervention was tested or evaluated.

Cross-sectional study assessing mental health outcomes (depression, anxiety, stress) in 466 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors using the DASS-21 scale. Found elevated rates of depression (14%), anxiety (18%), and stress (17%), with associations between prolonged ICU stays, reduced oxygen saturation, and mental health symptoms.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder in 154 post-COVID-19 patients using psychometric scales. Found high prevalence of psychological distress (24.7% anxiety, 11% depression, 13.6% PTSD) and subjective memory impairment (18.8%), with correlations between psychological symptoms and memory deficits.

Cross-sectional study of 154 COVID-19 hospitalized patients assessing post-traumatic stress disorder using the Impact of Event Scale-Revised, finding 13.6% met PTSD criteria with associations to marital status. Study is observational/screening only without testing or evaluating any intervention or treatment for long COVID.

A cross-sectional study of 154 post-COVID patients assessing sleep disorders using the Insomnia Severity Index, finding 23.4% had insomnia with significant associations to anxiety, depression, and PTSD. The study identifies sleep dysfunction as a key quality-of-life concern in post-COVID management.

This nationwide French survey examines the association between anxiety/depression symptoms and post-COVID-19 condition in 1,095 PCC patients and 1,021 infected controls without PCC. The study finds that anxiety and depression are highly prevalent in PCC but challenges their inclusion in the PCC definition, suggesting pre-COVID chronic anxiety/depression may share vulnerability factors with PCC rather than defining it.

Cross-sectional study of 137 long COVID patients in Tunisia examining associations between post-COVID symptoms and anxio-depressive disorders using the HAD scale. Found that arthralgia (but not other post-COVID symptoms) was independently associated with anxiety/depression in this observational cohort.

This cross-sectional study assessed the frequency of psychiatric disorders (anxiety, depression, PTSD, sleep disorders) in 104 patients 3 months after COVID-19 hospitalization. The study identified risk factors for psychological distress but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing mental health and quality of life in 276 COVID-19 survivors one year post-hospitalization at Tehran hospitals. Found impaired mental health in 83.7% of survivors with inverse relationship between mental health status and all quality-of-life dimensions.

Cross-sectional study of 137 long COVID patients in Tunisia assessing physical symptoms and anxio-depressive disorders using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression scale. Found high prevalence of anxiety (28% severe) and depression (24% severe), with dyspnea, mood disorders, and myalgia being the most common symptoms.

Cross-sectional study comparing corticotroph and somatotroph functions between recovered COVID-19 patients and those with long COVID. Found that long COVID patients were more likely to have anterior pituitary deficiencies, supporting an endocrine hypothesis for long COVID pathogenesis.

This cross-sectional survey examined medical diagnoses and treatment outcomes in 57 ultra-endurance athletes with and without prior COVID-19 infection during a 2022 triathlon championship. The study found no significant associations between recent COVID-19 infection and medical care outcomes, though COVID-19 symptom severity was associated with muscle cramping during competition.

This cross-sectional study examined physical activity levels and symptoms in 22 adults during acute COVID-19 infection, finding reduced weekly physical activity post-diagnosis and an association between inactivity and difficulty breathing. The paper focuses on acute infection phase rather than long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months after infection.

This cross-sectional study compares cardiovascular parameters (pulse rate, central aortic systolic pressure, systolic and diastolic blood pressure) in 79 university teachers who had COVID-19 versus 116 teachers without COVID-19 history. The findings show that post-COVID cardiovascular changes depend on age and pre-existing hypertension status, with non-hypertensive individuals showing decreased heart rate and blood pressure while those with prior hypertension showed increases.

Cross-sectional study using BOLD-fMRI to assess brain activation patterns during working memory tasks in 29 people with post-COVID condition versus 21 healthy controls. Participants with PCC showed greater brain activation and compensatory neural processes but similar cognitive performance, with greater activation predicting worse neuropsychiatric symptoms.

This cross-sectional study using the 2022 National Survey on Health and Disability examines unmet healthcare needs among people with pre-existing disabilities who have long COVID, finding that 73% reported unmet needs compared to 62.6% without long COVID. The paper identifies themes including healthcare system navigation challenges, provider gaslighting, and financial burdens, but does not study or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed life quality and health perception among 337 recovered COVID-19 patients using a 26-item questionnaire. Results show that 46% of respondents reported COVID-19 negatively affected their quality of life and health, with risk increasing with symptom count, duration, and severity.

Cross-sectional study of 953 healthcare workers with COVID-19 assessing prevalence and risk factors for neuropsychological manifestations including both acute and long COVID symptoms. Found 72.6% had neuropsychological manifestations acutely, with memory impairment, anosmia, and headache being common long COVID symptoms; associations identified with age, gender, smoking, and comorbidities.

Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examining associations between medical history, COVID vaccination, and long COVID development in US adults. Found that chronic conditions (obesity, hypertension, asthma, anxiety, depression) and older age were associated with higher long COVID risk, while prior COVID vaccination was associated with lower risk.

This cross-sectional study compared insulin resistance prevalence and determinants in 510 Ghanaian adults with and without prior COVID-19 infection. It found higher insulin resistance prevalence in those with past COVID-19, but made no treatment assessments.

This cross-sectional study compares the prevalence of long-COVID symptoms in non-hospitalized COVID-19 positive patients (n=1,410) versus negative patients (n=1,129) in primary care using electronic health records and questionnaires. The study found long-COVID symptoms significantly more prevalent in COVID-positive patients, with fatigue (59.5% vs 41.3%), difficulty sleeping (52.1% vs 41.9%), and concentration problems (50.6% vs 28.5%) being most common.

This cross-sectional study assessed pulmonary function, exercise tolerance, and quality of life in 207 Indian subjects who recovered from COVID-19, comparing those with prior pneumonia to those with mild disease. The study found significant impairment in lung function (restrictive defects, reduced DLCO) and exercise capacity in the COVID-19 pneumonia group, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 483 women from Jordan and Iraq examining menstrual cycle changes following COVID-19 infection. Found that 47.2% reported changes in cycle length or blood loss, with perceptions of COVID-19 impact varying by education level, location, marital status, and smoking status.

Cross-sectional survey of 396 Egyptian patients examining prevalence and predictors of post-COVID symptoms. Found 87.63% prevalence with fatigue as most common symptom; identified severe disease, antibiotics, and corticosteroids as predictors but did not evaluate any intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 979 Saudi Arabian COVID-19 patients describes the prevalence and severity of long-term post-recovery symptoms across multiple body systems, including fatigue, neurological symptoms, sensory loss, and gastrointestinal effects. The study proposes a classification system for post-COVID symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Online cross-sectional survey of 732 COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia examining prevalence and associations of long COVID symptoms. Found 20% reported long COVID with fatigue, brain fog, depression, anxiety and insomnia as common symptoms; females and those with moderate/severe acute COVID had higher odds of long COVID.

Cross-sectional study of 1,164 long COVID patients in Brazil evaluating symptomatology, complications, and quality of life 2-3 months post-acute infection. Found high prevalence of dyspnea, fatigue, and chest pain, with newly diagnosed metabolic disorders and post-acute hospitalization in a majority black/mixed-race population.

Cross-sectional study examining menstrual cycle changes in 956 Saudi females following SARS-CoV-2 infection, stratified by vaccination status and COVID-19 severity. Found 26.1% of unvaccinated and 15.3-26.4% of vaccinated individuals reported menstrual changes, with 6.4% experiencing persistence beyond six months, correlating with infection severity.

Cross-sectional study of 198 COVID-19 convalescent patients examining the incidence and predictors of fibromyalgia syndrome post-infection. Found 15% incidence of post-COVID fibromyalgia, associated with female gender, high traumatic stress, and low resilience, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study uses National Health Interview Survey data to examine whether COVID-19 severity is a risk factor for chronic pain, comparing pain prevalence across infection severity groups. It finds that moderate/severe COVID-19 infection is associated with higher odds of chronic pain, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

Secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial examining loss of socioemotional and occupational roles in 100 long COVID patients in primary care. Study found median loss of 3 roles, with cognitive impairment and lack of active work role as predictors, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 990 Jordanian respondents assessing long COVID prevalence, symptoms, and associated risk factors. Found significant associations between long COVID and age, obesity, chronic illness, vitamin D intake, and infection history, with tinnitus, concentration problems, and musculoskeletal pain as most common symptoms.

Cross-sectional study comparing pro-inflammatory SARS-CoV-2-specific cytokine levels in recovered COVID-19 and long-COVID patients versus unexposed controls. Found elevated IL-1β and IL-6 in long-COVID group but no interventions or treatments were tested.

A cross-sectional study documenting the incidence, characteristics, and risk factors of post-COVID chronic pain in Thailand from 1,019 participants assessed 3-6 months post-infection. Female sex and greater COVID-19 severity were identified as significant risk factors, with overall chronic pain incidence of 3.2%.

Cross-sectional study of 939 recovered COVID-19 patients in Thailand examining prevalence of long COVID symptoms (79.3%) and mental health status (depression 11.1%, anxiety 19.1%, stress 4.8%). Found significant associations between long COVID symptoms (especially fatigue, shortness of breath, chest tightness) and mental health disorders, with female sex, medical history, and low income as risk factors.

Population-based cross-sectional study using US Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data (June-December 2022) to characterize long COVID prevalence, demographic patterns, and associations with mental health and functional impairment. While descriptive of long COVID burden, this observational epidemiological study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 460 long COVID patients examining associations between substance use, psychiatric symptoms, and psychosocial factors. Found high rates of substance use (tobacco 82%, opioids 67%, cocaine 53%) positively associated with depression, anxiety, and PTSD, while personal mastery and social support were protective factors.

This cross-sectional observational study compared 33 long COVID patients who underwent pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) with 32 who did not, evaluating respiratory function and exercise capacity using the 6-minute walk test. Patients receiving PR showed significantly better walking distance, less dynamic hyperinflation, and improved impulse oscillometry findings compared to controls, suggesting PR provides measurable pulmonary benefits in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome.

Cross-sectional survey of 416 long COVID patients examining symptom prevalence, disease burden, and impact on work/quality of life across demographics and vaccination status. Study characterizes long COVID as a heterogeneous condition affecting multiple life domains but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 609 healthcare workers assessing prevalence and predictors of post-acute COVID syndrome (PACS). Found 50.7% prevalence with fatigue, cough, and musculoskeletal pain as most common symptoms; female sex, asthma, and COVID severity were risk factors while booster vaccination was protective.

This cross-sectional survey of 468 COVID-19 survivors examines the prevalence and risk factors for otological symptoms (tinnitus, hearing loss, aural fullness, dizziness) weeks to months after infection. Sex, age, initial symptom duration, and vaccination status were identified as risk factors for various otological manifestations of long COVID.

Cross-sectional characterization of 267 long COVID patients enrolled in the MedStar COVID Recovery Program, assessing clinical symptoms, quality-of-life, fatigue, and work productivity. Participants showed significant impairment across all domains, with 63% reporting activity impairment and 61% experiencing work productivity loss.

Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in 150 COVID-19 recovered patients in Ghana using EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS instruments. Found relatively good QoL overall, with symptom persistence and rehabilitation access as significant predictors, but this is an observational assessment study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and determinants of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome among 340 severe COVID-19 survivors at 2-year follow-up in Ethiopia. It identified risk factors including older age, female sex, comorbidities, and alcohol use as predictors of PACS, with fatigue and cough being the most common persistent symptoms (38.1% prevalence overall).

Cross-sectional web survey of 138 Medicaid enrollees assessing PASC symptom prevalence and associations with sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities, stratified by HIV status. Found no significant difference in PASC symptoms between individuals with and without HIV, but identified inadequate income and comorbidities (cardiac, cancer, fibromyalgia) as independent predictors of higher symptom burden.

Cross-sectional study of 41 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessed ~2 years post-discharge using comprehensive neuropsychological testing. Found that greater COVID-19 severity was associated with more brain fog symptoms, worse global cognitive functioning, and reduced attention/working memory performance.

This study analyzes Reddit communication patterns of 6,107 users before and after COVID-19 to identify psychological and linguistic traits associated with Long COVID development. The research is observational and does not involve any treatment intervention, focusing instead on identifying pre-existing risk factors through social media text analysis.

Cross-sectional analysis using 2022 National Health Interview Survey data examining financial toxicity in Long COVID patients compared to other comorbidities. Finds that adults with Long COVID experience significantly higher financial hardship than those with epilepsy, dementia, cancer, or cardiovascular/respiratory conditions, with vulnerable populations at greatest risk.

Cross-sectional study using 2022 BRFSS data examining health-related quality of life (HRQL) among 108,237 US COVID survivors, comparing those with post-COVID conditions (PCCs) to those without. Finds that PCC-positive survivors report significantly worse HRQL across general health, mental health, physical health, and daily functioning, with dizziness on standing, mood changes, and musculoskeletal pain most strongly associated with poor HRQL.

Cross-sectional study of 249 long COVID patients at a dedicated clinic identifying factors associated with symptom presence and intensity. Found anxiety symptoms, longer COVID-19 duration, and hypercholesterolemia correlated with greater symptom burden, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of 9,825 adults assessing ME/CFS-like illness prevalence in a large integrated health system. Found 1.67% prevalence overall, with 14.12% of ME/CFS cases developing after COVID-19, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 209 Indiana residents examining the association between self-reported periodontal disease and long COVID symptoms, with attention to socioeconomic disparities. Found significant associations between periodontal disease markers (bleeding gums, tooth loss, gum disease) and reduced sense of taste/smell in long COVID patients, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing health symptoms across post-COVID-19, ex-COVID, and non-infected individuals using merged survey and primary care data from 315,586 respondents. Post-COVID-19 individuals reported significantly more frequent, longer-lasting, and more severe symptoms compared to both ex-COVID and non-infected groups.

A cross-sectional survey of 374 Spanish long-COVID patients examining relationships between fatigue severity, mood disturbances, and other clinical manifestations using validated scales (FSS and EVEA). The study found significant correlations between fatigue, anxiety/depression, and neurological, psychological, locomotive, and pain symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional survey of 4,231 Brazilians examining the prevalence of long COVID (56.4%) and identifying associated factors including sex, vaccination status, comorbidities, hospitalization, and health-related behaviors. This is an observational study of disease prevalence and risk factors, not a treatment trial, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional analysis of 734 COVID-19 survivors examining associations between skeletal muscle parameters and kidney function 7 months post-discharge. Found skeletal muscle mass associated with eGFR but sarcopenia not independently associated with poor kidney function outcomes.

Cross-sectional study of 1,587 long COVID patients from British Columbia clinics examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination status, SARS-CoV-2 variants, and symptom severity using patient-reported outcome measures. Found that full vaccination was associated with reduced PTSD likelihood in non-hospitalized patients, and infection with alpha/delta variants was associated with increased dyspnea reporting.

A cross-sectional population-based study of 2,919 individuals from southern Brazil who had COVID-19 and symptoms persisting 6-9 months later, examining prevalence and associated factors of long COVID. The study found 48.3% prevalence and identified female gender, anxiety, chronic morbidities, and hospitalization as risk factors, with physical activity as a protective factor.

This cross-sectional study compares hematological inflammatory markers (NLR, MLR, PLR, SII, SIRI, AISI) in 147 patients with unstable angina, stratified by post-COVID-19 syndrome status and smoking history. Patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome demonstrated significantly elevated inflammatory markers compared to those without post-COVID, with the highest elevations observed in smokers with post-COVID syndrome.

This cross-sectional study compared 70 long COVID patients with 45 controls to characterize persistent symptoms and their associations with demographics, anxiety-depression, kinesiophobia, and quality of life. The study found fatigue, weakness, myalgia, and back pain as most common complaints, with higher prevalence in females and those with severe acute infection, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 133 long COVID patients in Italy via telephone interview to characterize persistent symptoms at 6-12 months post-infection. The study found that 58% of recovered COVID-19 patients (77/133) experienced long-haul symptoms including asthenia, breathlessness, myalgia, brain fog, and psychological disorders, but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study evaluates abnormal breathing patterns during cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in 20 post-COVID patients and assesses the inter-rater reliability of a classification method. The study finds that one-third of patients exhibit abnormal breathing patterns associated with lower exercise capacity, which may contribute to exercise-related symptoms in post-COVID syndrome.

This cross-sectional survey examined associations between self-reported SARS-CoV-2 infection status, antibody testing, and common longer-term COVID-19 symptoms in Canadian adults using data from April-August 2022. The study found discordance between self-reported infection and serological findings, and concluded that common longer-term symptoms reported by some may have been caused by other infections or diseases, without testing any interventions or treatments.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing arterial stiffness measured by pulse wave velocity in 53 long COVID patients versus 21 controls. Long COVID group showed significantly elevated carotid-radial PWV and arterial stiffness index compared to controls, suggesting persistent vascular dysfunction.

This cross-sectional study evaluated pulmonary function tests in 74 post-COVID-19 patients in Erbil, Iraq, analyzing demographics, clinical characteristics, and respiratory symptoms. Spirometry patterns were found to significantly correlate with severity of post-COVID-19 symptoms, suggesting their value as prognostic markers.

Cross-sectional study of 320 COVID-19 patients evaluated for long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) needs two months post-discharge. While descriptive of LTOT requirements and associated risk factors, this is a retrospective observational study without an intervention being tested or evaluated—it passively follows up patients rather than studying treatment outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between COVID-19 vaccination (dose and type) and the incidence of post-acute sequelae COVID-19 (PASC) in 133 respondents from Ternate City. Found no significant association between vaccine administration and PASC incidence, though post-booster vaccination showed higher PASC rates.

Cross-sectional study examining menstrual symptom changes in 180 women recovered from COVID-19, comparing pre- and post-infection menstrual patterns. Found significant increases in menstrual symptoms, fatigue severity, and menstrual pain in post-COVID individuals, with prolonged fatigue, muscle-joint pain, dyspnea, and GI symptoms associated with worse menstrual outcomes.

Cross-sectional study evaluating factors associated with disability in 32 patients discharged from COVID-19 ICUs ≥12 months post-discharge, using WHODAS 2.0 scale and clinical parameters. Found 25% were disabled, with neurological symptoms, impaired cognition, and mobility limitations significantly associated with length of hospitalization and clinical severity.

A cross-sectional survey of 122 Greek patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome examining quality of life, anxiety, and depression using standardized instruments. The study found significant reductions in QoL and increases in anxiety/depression symptoms, particularly in patients with dysautonomia and females, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study measured the prevalence of post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) in 126 COVID-19 survivors discharged from the ICU, assessing cognitive, psychological, and physical impairment using the Barthel scale. The study found a PICS prevalence of 14.3%, with higher rates of dependence in activities like urination, mobility, and stair climbing among those with comorbidities such as elevated BMI, diabetes, and hypertension.

This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence and duration of COVID-19 sequelae in 202 patients discharged from three tertiary hospitals in Ceará, Brazil, conducted via telesurvey between August-October 2021. Fatigue was the most common symptom (45-47%), followed by appetite loss and dyspnea, with some symptoms persisting up to 6 months post-discharge.

Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life and functional status in Colombian COVID-19 survivors using SF-36 and post-COVID functional status scales. Finds persistent impairments in vitality, general health, and physical role, with common symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, and pain beyond six months post-discharge.

This cross-sectional study compared inflammatory markers and autoantibodies to neuroproteins in blood serum of COVID-19 previously infected persons, vaccinated persons, and uninfected controls. Results show persistent elevated inflammatory markers and neuroautoimmune activation in both post-COVID and vaccinated groups, suggesting long-term humoral neuroautoimmune reactions that may contribute to neurological complications.

Cross-sectional study of 505 children hospitalized with post-COVID-19 syndrome examining clinical manifestations and system involvement. Found sensory and nervous systems most commonly affected (80.20% and 78.61% respectively), with higher prevalence in older children and males.

A cross-sectional survey of 303 COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia assessed the prevalence and types of long COVID symptoms at least 14 days after negative RT-PCR results.
