The study found that 31% experienced long COVID symptoms, with fatigue, headache, and joint/muscle pain being most common, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 366 adults in Long Beach, California who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, assessing the prevalence and demographic characteristics of post-acute sequelae 2 months after infection. The study found that one-third reported at least one symptom, with higher odds among those aged 40-54, females, and those with preexisting conditions, and identified racial/ethnic disparities in symptom reporting.

Cross-sectional study investigating the correlation between muscle-specific creatinine kinase (CK-MM) levels and persistent myalgia in COVID-19 survivors. Found no significant association between CK-MM levels and myalgia incidence, with all myalgia patients having normal CK-MM levels.

This National Center for Health Statistics report provides health data on long COVID prevalence among children in the United States in 2022. It is an epidemiological surveillance report rather than a treatment intervention study.

CDC analysis of Household Pulse Survey data examining prevalence of long COVID and significant activity limitation among U.S. adults by age group from June 2022 to June 2023. Study found long COVID prevalence decreased from 7.5% to 6.0% overall and from 18.9% to 11.0% among those with prior COVID-19, with 26.4% of long COVID patients reporting significant activity limitation.

CDC survey comparing prevalence of long-term symptoms in 22,000+ U.S. adults with positive vs negative SARS-CoV-2 test results. Found that 65.9% of those testing positive reported long-term symptoms (vs 42.9% in negative group), with fatigue, anosmia/dysgeusia, and dyspnea being most common; also noted respondents believed vaccination improved symptoms.

Cross-sectional survey of 100 patients at a Level 1 trauma center examining the prevalence and severity of long COVID symptoms and their association with overall health status. Found that nearly one-fourth of the population experienced long COVID symptoms (shortness of breath, fatigue) with significant decline in health rankings post-infection, but no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of psychological distress and PTSD in 672 COVID-19 survivors in Kashmir using the IES-R scale. While the paper studies recovered COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute post-infection psychological outcomes during early recovery (2020) rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months later), and is purely observational without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study measuring TREC/KREC biomarkers of T and B cell function in 4,433 apparently healthy adults in Russia, comparing pre-pandemic (2020) and post-pandemic (2023) populations. Finds 3.6-fold increase in abnormal TREC levels and immunological disturbances post-COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,120 employees using a post-COVID-19 syndrome questionnaire to assess symptom prevalence and associated risk factors. The study found 47% reported at least one symptom reducing quality of life, with anxiety, depression, age, and symptom severity as key correlates, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between inflammatory markers, abdominal obesity, and post-COVID syndrome in 166 COVID-19 convalescents. Finds that elevated IL-6 and insulin levels are associated with increased odds of abdominal obesity in post-COVID patients, with sex-specific differences in inflammatory marker associations.

This cross-sectional study of 127 COVID-19 survivors examined the prevalence and correlates of neurological long COVID symptoms including poor sleep quality (59.8%), chronic fatigue syndrome (51.2%), and cognitive impairment (33.9%). The study found that survivors with more than five acute-phase COVID-19 symptoms had significantly higher odds of developing chronic fatigue and cognitive impairment compared to those with fewer acute symptoms.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and long-term persistence of olfactory and taste disorders among 53 health professionals with confirmed or suspected COVID-19 exposure. The study found a high prevalence of smell and taste alterations in COVID-19-positive individuals, with 31 of 53 participants meeting long COVID criteria, but no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

This descriptive epidemiological study analyzes 2,948 deaths attributed to post-COVID conditions in Brazil using 2021 mortality data, examining sociodemographic patterns across regions. The study documents that post-COVID deaths disproportionately affected males (58%), elderly patients (66.9% aged 60+), and white populations (51.8%), with regional variation in mortality rates.

Cross-sectional study evaluating nutritional status, swallowing disorders, and musculoskeletal manifestations in 38 post-COVID patients stratified by muscle mass loss. Found both groups at risk of malnutrition and obesity with persistent fatigue, weakness, and joint pain at 6 months post-discharge.

This cross-sectional survey of 1,295 Brazilian participants investigated public perceptions and awareness of long COVID symptoms. The study found that 33.4% of those who had COVID-19 experienced persistent symptoms lasting at least three months, with fatigue, headache, and hair loss being most common, but highlights a lack of public awareness linking these symptoms to COVID-19.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the functional capacity and health-related quality of life in 286 post-COVID-19 patients referred for rehabilitation, comparing cohorts infected in 2020 vs 2021. Results showed worsening symptom severity, greater functional impairments, and declined quality of life in the 2021 cohort, demonstrating the need for structured post-COVID rehabilitation interventions.

Cross-sectional survey of 73 physiotherapists assessing their knowledge and experience treating post-COVID-19 patients. While most physiotherapists recognize the importance of post-COVID rehabilitation, the study documents their practices and knowledge gaps rather than testing an intervention or treatment outcome.

Cross-sectional observational study of 109 nursing professionals examining associations between sociodemographic factors, lifestyle, mental health habits, and long COVID prevalence. Identifies male sex, high resilience, and positive affect as protective factors, while nursing technician category increases long COVID risk.

Cross-sectional study assessing exercise capacity, lung function, and physical function in 135 COVID-19 survivors 1-3 months post-infection in Brazil. Found common muscle disability and lung dysfunction (reduced diffusing capacity, lower 6-minute walk distance) associated with hospitalization severity and computed tomography findings, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 226 nursing professionals in Brazil comparing their identification and management of post-COVID conditions symptoms in primary versus specialized care settings. Study highlights gaps in PCC recognition, lack of standardized protocols, and inadequate training among healthcare providers rather than evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined autoantibody expression in 55 severe COVID-19 patients two years post-discharge compared to 21 uninfected controls. Results show significantly elevated autoimmune markers (ANA, VDRL, RF, PCT, CRP) in long COVID patients, suggesting hyperinflammation and autoimmunity may underlie persistent symptoms.

This cross-sectional survey study from Brazil (2023) analyzed COVID-19 morbidity patterns across sociodemographic and health characteristics, identifying long COVID in 32% of COVID-19 positive individuals with higher rates among women, those with financial difficulties, and those with preexisting chronic diseases. The study documents epidemiological associations and disease burden but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 204 adults post-COVID-19 to investigate persistent speech-language-hearing symptoms and their functional impact. The research identified memory loss, tiredness, and anosmia/ageusia as common long-term symptoms with significant emotional, physical, and occupational consequences.

Cross-sectional study of 270 people with post-COVID-19 syndrome examining social determinants of health and prevalent symptoms in Brazil. Identifies associations between demographic factors, social determinants, and symptom prevalence, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of urinary incontinence in 59 post-COVID-19 patients using structured interviews and validated questionnaires. The analysis found urinary incontinence in 28% of women but not men, with insomnia identified as an associated factor, though the authors note incipient evidence for a direct SARS-CoV-2 association.

Cross-sectional study of 160 COVID-19 survivors one year after hospitalization, assessing functional capacity and muscle strength using standardized instruments. Found that 67.5% had functional limitations and 50.9% had muscle strength changes, with female gender, sarcopenia, smoking, and intubation associated with greater impairment.

This cross-sectional study examined 54 post-COVID-19 patients referred for pulmonary rehabilitation, comparing clinical and functional outcomes between obese and non-obese individuals. Despite obesity being prevalent (75.9%), there were no significant differences in dyspnea, fatigue, respiratory muscle strength, or other clinical measures between groups.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of chronotropic incompetence (inadequate heart rate increase during exercise) in 93 long COVID patients and its association with sedentary behavior and reduced aerobic capacity. Found CI in 20.4% of participants, with strong associations between CI, sedentary behavior, and lower exercise tolerance.

A cross-sectional study of 125 long COVID patients examining the association between hypomagnesemia and 25-hydroxyvitamin D deficiency and clinical manifestations. The study found that patients with these nutrient deficiencies had significantly more symptoms including fatigue, memory loss, joint pain, and anxiety.

Cross-sectional study of 80 post-COVID-19 patients in Brazil that assessed cardiorespiratory function using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), comparing metrics across disease severity groups. Found that patients with severe COVID-19 history showed altered cardiorespiratory optimal point (COP) values but the study does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing the prevalence of neurological complications in 385 post-COVID-19 patients using the Edinburgh Questionnaire. Found high prevalence of fatigue (73.5%), muscle weakness (66.2%), and chronic pain (64.1%), but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional study evaluates the effect of oxygen concentrators on oxygen saturation in 108 patients (42 using concentrators, 66 not) presenting to a pulmonology clinic after COVID-19 infection. Patients using oxygen concentrators were older, had longer hospital stays, higher rates of pulmonary involvement, and lower oxygen saturation levels, suggesting that dyspnea during acute infection predicts later need for supplemental oxygen.

Cross-sectional study examining burnout among nursing home care providers and its association with work stress, fatigue, and coping during the COVID-19 pandemic. While 85.7% of care providers reported long COVID symptoms, the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients—it studies occupational health outcomes in healthcare workers.

This cross-sectional study examined the association between post-COVID sleep disturbance (PCSD) and neurocognitive function in 8,692 COVID-19 survivors using propensity score matching. The study found that nearly half of survivors reported sleep disturbance, which was significantly associated with impaired cognitive performance on standardized tests.

Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life outcomes in 60 patients with neurological post-COVID syndrome manifestations (headaches, pain, fatigue, cognitive/mood symptoms) versus 20 controls with only the underlying neurological disease. Found that age >40, high anxiety, depressive and asthenic syndromes negatively affect QOL in post-COVID patients.

Cross-sectional online survey of 101 long COVID patients assessing fatigue and functional status one year post-infection using the Chalder Fatigue Scale and post-COVID functional status scale. Found that 38.61% reported fatigue and most participants had minimal to no functional limitations.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 265 military sailors in the Arctic examining risk factors for COVID-19 severity during the first and second waves. Found that 88.7% of those who recovered showed post-COVID syndrome symptoms (asthenia, dyspnea, dyssomnia, arthralgia), with age >35 and lower education as risk factors for more severe disease.

Cross-sectional study of 665 long COVID patients identifying 7 main clinical phenotypes and their associations with demographic factors, acute COVID severity, and comorbidities. Observational study with no treatment intervention—patients were surveyed about symptoms and disease course rather than receiving or being evaluated for any treatment.

Cross-sectional study comparing hemodynamics, autonomic regulation, and psychological stress resistance in 69 university students with and without prior COVID-19 infection (1.5-2.5 years post-infection). Students with prior COVID-19 showed persistent differences in cardiovascular function, sympathetic nervous system predominance, and elevated stress markers compared to unaffected peers.

Population-based telephone survey of 398 adults discharged from hospital post-COVID-19 assessing prevalence and types of long COVID symptoms. Found 31.5% reported persistent symptoms, with female sex, higher education, and obesity as associated factors, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of Canadian adults conducted April-August 2022 investigating factors associated with post COVID-19 condition occurrence, severity, and resolution. Found 17.2% of confirmed infection cases experienced PCC, with female sex, comorbidities, and severe initial infection as major risk factors; no treatment intervention was studied.

This cross-sectional study examines factors influencing long COVID patients' willingness to pay for digital medical platforms using structural equation modeling and stress-coping theory on 371 patients. The research shows that role stress and coping strategies significantly predict patients' behavioral intentions toward digital health platform adoption, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional observational study examines autonomic nervous system function in young adults with a history of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 compared to healthy controls. The research investigates whether body mass index and physical activity levels modulate autonomic function differences between COVID-19-infected and uninfected participants.

This cross-sectional study examined electrocardiographic abnormalities in 225 COVID-19 convalescents and their association with cardiometabolic parameters and inflammatory markers. ECG abnormalities were found in 29.3% of convalescents and were associated with male sex and elevated IL-6 levels.

This cross-sectional study examined lipid profile parameters (cholesterol, HDL, LDL, VLDL, triglycerides) in COVID-19 donors with varying anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG titers to investigate biochemical changes in the post-COVID period. The study found significant variations in lipid concentrations across different antibody titer groups, suggesting potential cardiovascular disease risk in long COVID patients, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional observational study evaluating clinical manifestations and functional impacts in 137 long COVID patients 3-12 months post-infection, stratified by presence/absence of prior comorbidities. Patients with comorbidities showed significantly greater impairments in mobility, work productivity, physical functionality, and cognitive function compared to those without comorbidities.

A cross-sectional observational study examining caspase-6 levels and inflammatory markers in 186 long COVID patients with dyspnea compared to controls. The study identifies associations between severe acute COVID-19 pneumonia and reduced caspase-6 levels, arterial stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers in the post-COVID period.

Cross-sectional observational study of 103 post-COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between pain and functional capacity using VAS, dynamometry, and functional status assessments. Found significant correlations between pain severity and reduced muscle strength/functionality, with age associated with worse performance in mobility tasks.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairment in COVID-19 patients and developing a prognostic scale for psychopharmacotherapy selection. Identified risk factors (lower education, older age, endocrine disorders, elevated respiratory rate) but did not test or evaluate a specific intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluates detailed screening procedures for detecting post-COVID-19 consequences in 970 patients, assessing physical function, pulmonary status, and comorbidities. While the paper identifies high prevalence of respiratory impairment and multimorbidity in post-COVID patients, it does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention, only screening protocols.

A cross-sectional study describing the most frequent symptoms in post-COVID-19 patients in Paraguay during 2021. The study documents persistent symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, anosmia, and neurological manifestations following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection.

This cross-sectional study assessed working capacity and mental state in 62 young COVID-19 convalescents at 90 days post-discharge using psychological questionnaires. The majority showed reduced working capacity and asthenic syndrome, attributed to post-illness fatigue and post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms.

This cross-sectional screening study identified predictors of newly diagnosed chronic heart failure in 878 long COVID patients with shortness of breath. While about long COVID and using a valid study design, it does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment—it is purely observational/epidemiological in nature.

This OECD PaRIS survey assessed Long COVID prevalence and impact in 107,011 primary care patients aged 45+ across 19 countries (2023-2024), finding ~7% reported ever having Long COVID and ~5% reported current symptoms. The study documents worse self-rated health and healthcare experiences in Long COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated long-term persistent symptoms and quality of life in 231 mild COVID-19 outpatients using adapted questionnaires. The findings show that non-hospitalized patients experience persistent symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive impairment, headache), with higher symptom frequency in younger patients and women, but no treatment or intervention is tested.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 105 people living with HIV to examine associations between long COVID (PASC) symptoms and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D instrument. The study found that PASC symptoms were significantly associated with poorer quality of life outcomes, but it is observational only with no treatment intervention tested.

Cross-sectional study surveying 5,770 family caregivers of COVID-19 survivors in Punjab, Pakistan to quantify economic burden using structural equation modeling. Identified that female caregivers over 45, unemployed, with low income, and those performing household/medical/personal care tasks faced higher financial strain.

A cross-sectional comparative study assessing blood sugar levels (HbA1c) among post-COVID patients stratified by diabetes status versus non-diabetic controls. The study found significantly elevated HbA1c levels in post-COVID diabetic patients (9.82±3.22) compared to non-diabetic post-COVID patients (5.83±3.32), indicating differential glycemic effects post-infection.

This case-control study compared mental fatigue and cognitive flexibility in 102 young adults with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae versus 111 controls using the Mental Fatigue Scale and Cognitive Flexibility Inventory. The study found significantly higher mental fatigue and lower cognitive flexibility in the long COVID group, identifying COVID-19 infection as a risk factor (OR: 2.74), but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 31 long COVID patients examining the association between neurological symptoms (myalgia, anosmia, headache) and D-dimer levels as a potential biomarker of hypercoagulability. Found significant correlation between D-dimer levels and number of neurological symptoms (OR=1.05, p=0.020), suggesting hypercoagulable conditions may contribute to long COVID neurological manifestations.

Cross-sectional study assessing post-COVID health effects and psychological impact in 153 patients discharged from a tertiary COVID care hospital in southern India. Found high prevalence of physical symptoms (fever, breathing difficulty) and psychiatric sequelae, with significant associations between psychological impact and demographic/lifestyle factors.

A cross-sectional survey of 150 COVID-19 survivors assessing the prevalence and symptom patterns of post-COVID-19 syndrome in the Indian population. The study found 39.33% prevalence with fatigue, myalgia, and cognitive symptoms being most common, but did not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional survey assessing psychological distress in 167 COVID-19 survivors, finding high prevalence of depression, anxiety, sleep disturbances, and cognitive impairment. No treatment or intervention was tested; this is a descriptive epidemiological study of post-COVID psychological symptoms without an experimental or therapeutic component.

A cross-sectional study of 128 healthcare workers in India assessed long COVID symptomatology at 4 weeks post-infection, documenting the prevalence of constitutional, respiratory, neurological, and musculoskeletal symptoms. The paper describes symptom patterns and functional impact but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed quality of life in 1,162 COVID-19 recovered patients in South India using the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire, comparing those with moderate/severe versus mild disease. While it documents long-term effects on QOL, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely observational/descriptive and therefore not eligible for the trials database.

This multicenter cross-sectional study describes the sociodemographic and clinical profile of 611 long COVID patients attending Brazilian rehabilitation hospitals, documenting prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms (65%), memory/attention impairment (55.6%), pain (53.7%), and fatigue (51.6%). The study reports functional status and mobility outcomes but does not evaluate or test a specific treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 100 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing quality of life using the SF-36 questionnaire. Found mild-to-moderate impairment in quality of life domains, with general health and emotional well-being most affected, and persistent breathlessness and fatigue post-recovery.

Cross-sectional survey of general practitioners in Belgium and Malta examining their knowledge, perception, experience, and definitions of Long COVID care in primary health care settings. This observational study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

Comparative cross-sectional study comparing symptom presentation and quality of life between post COVID-19 condition patients (n=31), ME/CFS patients (n=61), and healthy controls (n=54) using validated instruments. Found that both patient groups had comparable symptom profiles and significantly impaired QoL compared to controls, with ME/CFS showing higher rates of specific symptoms like muscle weakness and memory loss.

Cross-sectional study assessing the incidence of breakthrough COVID-19 infections and prevalence of post-COVID syndrome symptoms (fatigue, dyspnea, mood changes, concentration difficulty) among medical staff and students at a tertiary care hospital in Telangana. Found 9.40% breakthrough infection incidence and 21.16% post-COVID syndrome prevalence, with fatigue as the most common symptom.

This cross-sectional study examines how social networking sites (YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok, LINE) influence self-protective behaviors and attitudes to prevent long COVID among 400 working-aged Thai participants. While the paper addresses long COVID prevention, it does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention—it only measures correlations between SNS exposure and self-reported behavioral intentions.

A cross-sectional study of 1,500 Iranian women examining menstrual cycle changes during the COVID-19 pandemic, comparing women with and without COVID-19 infection and vaccination status. The study found higher rates of menstrual changes in infected and vaccinated women but does not address long COVID or any treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional survey of 956 long COVID patients from a Twitter community assessing symptom prevalence and incidence at 60+ days post-infection. Identifies smoking and female gender as risk factors for cutaneous signs and smoking as a correlate of tachycardia/hypertension incidence, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 400 COVID-19 recoverees in Iran measuring prevalence of depressive symptoms, anxiety, and stress using validated screening instruments (PHQ-9, DASS-21), and examining self-medication behaviors. Finds 35.1% with moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms and 32.8% reporting self-medication, with depression significantly associated with self-medication behavior.

This cross-sectional study assessed long-term complications in 105 children hospitalized with COVID-19, evaluating outcomes 3 months after discharge through family questionnaires and medical records. The most common complications were mood disorders (35.2%), loss of appetite (22.9%), and fatigue (20%), with higher incidence in older children; however, this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.

A cross-sectional study describing cardiac and autonomic findings (24-hour Holter monitoring and tilt table testing) in 83 post-COVID-19 patients. The study documents prevalence of abnormal findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between persistent COVID-19 symptoms, vaccination status, and somatization disorders in Lebanese adults. Found that persistent COVID symptoms were associated with increased somatization, while vaccination was associated with decreased somatization.

This cross-sectional study assessed sleep quality in 56 COVID-19 patients with severe pulmonary involvement six months after ICU discharge using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. The findings show that 80.4% of participants exhibited sleep disorders post-discharge, with gender differences noted, but this is an observational prevalence study without any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 1,005 long COVID patients presenting to an internal medicine clinic ≥120 days post-infection, documenting the prevalence and frequency of persistent symptoms. The most common symptoms were fatigue (11.2%), shortness of breath (6.1%), and back/low back pain (4.6%), with mean 1.38 persistent symptoms per patient.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 385 recovered COVID-19 patients in Indonesia to determine the prevalence of persistent COVID-19 syndrome and associated risk factors. Among respondents, 66.5% experienced persistent symptoms with fatigue, cough, and muscle pain being most common, and pneumonia was identified as the strongest predictor of developing persistent COVID-19 syndrome.

This case-control study compares lipid metabolism and hemostasis parameters in 104 hypertensive patients >2 months post-COVID-19 against 117 hypertensive controls without COVID history. Results show elevated cholesterol, LDL, triglycerides, D-dimers, and platelets, plus altered coagulation in the post-COVID group, indicating atherogenic and prothrombotic changes in the long-term period after COVID-19.

This cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 National Health Interview Survey examined multilevel determinants of long COVID prevalence, including social factors and internet access as a proxy for telehealth viability. The study found long COVID more prevalent among older adults, Black individuals, and low-income households, but identified no disparities in internet access that would prevent telehealth implementation.

Cross-sectional survey of 133 medical professionals and students assessing health-promoting behaviors and anxiety about long-term COVID-19 complications during the pandemic. While nearly half of participants expressed concerns about long-term effects, the study does not investigate long COVID itself or test any treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between long COVID symptoms and quality of life in 50 rural COVID-19 survivors using WHO questionnaires. Found that symptom count was weakly associated with lower physical quality of life (p=0.009) but not with overall QoL.

This cross-sectional study evaluated anxiety and depression in 51 healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 condition using Hamilton scales and assessed associations with inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, MLR, SII). The study found high frequencies of anxiety (72.5%) and depression (51%) but found no significant association between inflammatory markers and these psychiatric symptoms.

This prospective cross-sectional study evaluated lung ultrasonography findings in 54 patients with prior COVID-19 pneumonia to explore relationships between lung changes and prolonged COVID-19 symptoms. The study found that B lines detected by lung ultrasound are significantly associated with dyspnea in long COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between biomass consumption and Post-Acute COVID-19 Syndrome (PACS) in 110 recovered patients from Peru. Found no significant link between prior biomass use and PACS development, though tracheostomy and ICU stay were associated with PACS.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of persistent symptoms ('COVID fog') and quality of life impacts in 125 patients admitted to a COVID-19 ward between March 2020-2021. Found high prevalence of fatigue (57%), memory loss (52%), and insomnia (50%), with decreased quality of life correlating with age, chronic comorbidities, and symptom severity.

Cross-sectional study of 110 COVID-19 patients treated at Udayana University Hospital describing occupational characteristics and return-to-work outcomes during recovery. While 27.27% experienced symptom reoccurrence 4-5 months post-infection, the study is observational without any intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in COVID-19 survivors in Bogor City using the SF-36 instrument. Identifies educational status, income, comorbidities, obesity, symptom duration, and COVID-19 recovery duration as significant factors associated with poorer quality of life outcomes.

Cross-sectional survey of 122 long COVID patients using the SF-36 questionnaire to assess quality of life impacts. Found that general health and vitality were significantly impaired in patients with symptoms lasting >3 months, with fatigue, brain fog, and olfactory disturbances being most common.

This cross-sectional study compared the collagenolysis system in 178 patients with and without long-term post-COVID syndrome (≥12 weeks post-infection). Results show that long COVID patients have elevated TIMP1 levels and a collagenolytic pattern compared to asymptomatic controls, suggesting fibrosis-related pathogenic mechanisms in long COVID development.

This cross-sectional observational study examines the association between chronic disease risk factors and post-COVID syndrome severity in 270 COVID-19 convalescents. It identifies glucose levels, diastolic left ventricular dysfunction, and visceral adiposity as key factors associated with moderate post-COVID syndrome severity, but does not test any intervention.

This case-control study compares periodontal disease severity in 20 long COVID patients versus 20 non-COVID controls using secondary clinic data. The study found increased generalized periodontitis distribution in long COVID survivors but no significant difference in periodontitis severity by staging/grading methods.

Cross-sectional study examining risk and protective factors associated with stress levels in 66 COVID-19 survivors, measuring stress using the Hopkins Symptom Checklist-25. Found that sex was the most influential sociodemographic factor on stress levels, with no significant relationship between measured risk/protective factors and stress outcomes.

Cross-sectional observational study of 270 COVID-19 convalescents examining associations between metabolic and inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, hs-CRP, C-peptide, etc.) and post-COVID syndrome severity. Found IL-6 and hs-CRP levels elevated in patients with post-COVID syndrome compared to those without, with stronger associations in men and those with moderate severity.

A cross-sectional survey of 201 sub-urban Sri Lankan residents assessing knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding long-term complications of COVID-19. The study found that while most participants had heard of long COVID, knowledge about risk factors was inadequate and adherence to preventive measures was low.

This cross-sectional study analyzes persistent symptoms after COVID-19 infection in patients from a health unit in northern Palmas, Brazil, using questionnaire-based data collection. The results show that pre-existing comorbidities are directly correlated with post-COVID syndrome development, with symptoms persisting from the acute phase up to four weeks or longer across mild, moderate, and severe acute infections.

Cross-sectional survey of 300 post-COVID-19 patients in Iraq documenting persistent symptoms after recovery. Found fatigue (70%), headache (69%), dizziness (64%), cough (61%), and breathing difficulty (56%) as most common, with higher prevalence in males.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between long COVID and anxiety symptoms in 60 individuals in Banyumas, Indonesia. Found that 66.7% of long COVID patients experienced anxiety (ranging from mild to severe), with a statistically significant association between long COVID status and anxiety onset.

This is a cross-sectional analysis of in-depth medical examinations conducted in the Kursk region of Russia in 2022, identifying risk factors and health status distributions in the general population with a focus on long COVID sequelae. The study identifies cardiovascular disease as the leading health condition and describes sociodemographic differences in risk factors, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzes disparities in COVID-19, long COVID prevalence, and mental health outcomes among US adults by employment sector using Census Bureau survey data from September-November 2022. Results show workers in healthcare, social assistance, and accommodation/food services had significantly higher odds of long COVID diagnosis and associated mental health impacts compared to other sectors.

This observational cross-sectional study characterized persistent symptoms, depressive symptoms, and functional status in post-COVID-19 patients at a Mexican hospital (4-25 weeks post-discharge). 100% of patients showed functional status alterations, with pain (66.6%) and fatigue (66%) most common, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study analyzes geographic and sociodemographic disparities in Long COVID prevalence across US states and metropolitan areas using Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey data from June-October 2022. It documents significant variation in Long COVID prevalence (24-43.6% by state) but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluates personality traits in 93 post-COVID syndrome patients compared to matched controls using the Big Five Structure Inventory and neuropsychiatric assessments. Patients with post-COVID showed lower emotional stability and conscientiousness, with personality traits predictive of anxiety and depression but not cognitive function or fatigue.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,027 German patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 assessing long-term symptoms and functional impact using the SF-36 and RehabNeS questionnaires. Found that 61.9% reported persistent symptoms >3 months post-infection with activity limitations, but overall impact on quality of life and work ability was low.

Cross-sectional study identifying high prevalence of respiratory muscle dysfunction in persistently symptomatic COVID-19 patients. Respiratory muscle impairment was associated with exercise-induced deoxygenation, reduced exercise tolerance, and impaired functional outcomes.

This cross-sectional analysis of 3,901 COVID-19 patients with neurologic symptoms from the COVID-19 Neuro Databank describes the epidemiological profiles and geographic/income-based variations in neurologic manifestations, including a subset identified as Long COVID. The study documents the prevalence and distribution of conditions like neurocognitive disorders, fatigue, headache, and anosmia but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 172 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors in Jakarta assessing the prevalence and impact of long COVID symptoms on health-related quality of life domains using WHOQOL-BREF. Found that 30.2% experienced long-haul COVID symptoms with significant effects on most quality-of-life domains, but this is observational assessment without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 172 recovered COVID-19 inpatients in Jakarta assessing long-haul COVID prevalence and its effects on health-related quality of life domains using WHOQOL-BREF. Found that 30.2% experienced long-haul symptoms, which significantly impacted quality of life in physical, psychological, and social domains.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between HDL cholesterol levels and long COVID persistence in hemodialysis patients one year post-infection. Finds that low HDL (<1.22 mmol/L) is associated with enhanced inflammatory markers and long COVID persistence, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing hearing loss patterns in chronic otitis media patients with and without prior COVID-19 infection. Finds higher prevalence of mixed and sensorineural hearing loss in COVID-positive patients, but does not study long COVID or test any intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and severity of fatigue in 155 SARS-CoV-2 patients using the Fatigue Severity Scale. Found 3.96% fatigue prevalence with weak negative correlation between fatigue severity and RTPCR values, concluding that fatigue severity does not depend on viral load.

Community-based cross-sectional survey assessing post-COVID fatigue, dyspnea, and functional state among 299 recovered COVID-19 patients in urban India. Study found significant associations between fatigue and dyspnea with functional impairment, but conducted no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 457 COVID-19 patients assessing risk factors for long COVID development and persistence. Identified female sex, younger age, and low BMI as key risk factors for specific symptoms and overall symptom persistence at 6-12 months post-infection.

A cross-sectional survey assessing the prevalence and determinants of post-COVID-19 symptoms among 773 recovered COVID-19 patients in North India. The study found 33.2% had symptoms at 4+ weeks (declining to 12.8% at 12 weeks), with fatigue, joint pain, and hair loss most common; vaccination with 2 doses reduced symptom odds by 45%.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive status in 1,013 elderly COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-infection compared to 262 uninfected controls using standardized cognitive assessments (TICS-40 and IQCODE). COVID-19 patients showed significantly lower cognitive scores and greater cognitive decline, particularly among those with severe disease, older age, mechanical ventilation, or hypertension.

Cross-sectional study of 574 COVID-19 survivors 5-8 months post-discharge describing prevalence of long-term clinical sequelae (55.9% general symptoms, 46.2% respiratory) and immunological abnormalities compared to healthy controls. No intervention or treatment was administered; this is a purely observational characterization study.

This cross-sectional survey study assessed persistent symptoms and work ability 12 months after non-hospitalized COVID-19 in 366 Swedish patients, finding 48% reported remaining symptoms with impaired smell, taste, and fatigue being most common. The study identified predictors of persistent symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared gait patterns in 12 individuals with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 history versus 20 controls, finding significantly more asymmetrical gait patterns in the COVID group. The study does not evaluate a treatment intervention, only characterizes gait abnormalities in post-COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study comparing morphological and functional lung imaging (LF-MRI) in 54 pediatric post-COVID-19 patients (29 recovered, 25 with long COVID) and 9 healthy controls. Found persistent ventilation-perfusion abnormalities in both recovered and long COVID patients compared to controls, with no morphologic changes but significant functional deficits.

A descriptive cross-sectional study of 300 long COVID patients in the Brazilian Amazon examining symptom patterns and persistence over 15 months, with analysis of environmental and socioeconomic factors on clinical presentation. Finds that 84% experienced symptoms lasting over three months, with symptom burden increasing over time, particularly among those with initially mild acute COVID-19.

Cross-sectional survey of 728 non-hospitalized Danish adults with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection matched to 7,280 seronegative controls to assess long-COVID burden. Found 25.1% attributable risk of persistent symptoms, significantly worse physical and mental health in cases, with female sex and initial infection severity as major risk factors.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiac biomarkers (cTnI and NT-proBNP) in 275 Peruvian adults with and without post-COVID-19 status, stratified by metabolic syndrome presence. Found no significant differences in elevated cardiac marker proportions across groups, suggesting mild post-COVID-19 does not substantially elevate these markers regardless of metabolic syndrome status.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiac biomarkers (NT-proBNP, troponin I, nitric oxide) and imaging findings (echocardiography, CMR, cardiac PET) in 105 post-acute COVID-19 patients with and without symptoms (palpitations, exercise-associated fatigue). Symptomatic patients showed elevated NT-proBNP, reduced nitric oxide levels, and increased 18F-FDG uptake on cardiac PET suggesting myocardial fatigue, while echocardiography and CMR were normal.

This cross-sectional study evaluates electronic nose technology and chemometric analysis to discriminate volatile organic compounds in breath of post-COVID patients with lung damage versus recovered controls without lung damage. The diagnostic test achieves 83.8% classification accuracy with high sensitivity (88.9%) and specificity (96.9%), suggesting potential as a screening tool for post-COVID pulmonary sequelae.

Cross-sectional survey of COVID-19 survivors assessing functional status, symptom prevalence, and rehabilitation participation using questionnaires. Found that 65.5% reported no functional limitations, with fatigue (26-33.3%) and shortness of breath (15%) being common symptoms; 49.2% underwent rehabilitation measures in the first three months post-infection.

Cross-sectional survey of 773 hospital employees in India assessing self-reported post-COVID-19 symptoms and associated risk factors. Found 33.2% prevalence of PCS with fatigue, arthralgia, and myalgia most common; vaccination reduced odds of developing PCS by 39%.

A cross-sectional study of 51 Mexican healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 condition examining associations between epigenetic age, inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, MLR, SII), and cognitive/neuropsychiatric manifestations. The study found that elevated inflammatory markers were associated with cognitive impairment and increased epigenetic age, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compares cardiovascular autonomic function between 28 post-COVID patients (3-8 months post-infection) and 31 controls using heart rate variability, cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests, and baroreceptor sensitivity. The study found significantly altered cardiovascular reactivity in post-COVID patients, including higher orthostatic hypotension and abnormal reflex responses, but did not test any specific intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional descriptive study comparing long COVID prevalence among people with preexisting disabilities versus the general population using 2022 National Survey on Health and Disability data. Found 40.6% prevalence in people with disabilities versus 18.9% in the general population, highlighting health disparities and barriers to care.

Cross-sectional study of 94 outpatient clinic visitors in Japan assessing SARS-CoV-2 antibody and PCR positivity rates. Finds 6.4% antibody prevalence but focuses on diagnostic methods for acute/recent COVID-19, not post-acute sequelae or long COVID treatment.

This retrospective case-control study compared health-related quality of life between COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 pneumonia patients at 9-month follow-up using the RAND-36 questionnaire. While it documents post-COVID symptoms and reduced health perception, it is a passive observational study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed depression, anxiety, and quality of life in 324 post-COVID-19 patients across three time points (2020-2022) using standardized instruments (SF-36, GAD-7, PHQ-9). The study found improvements in mental health and quality of life over time, with depression scores declining significantly and vaccination rates increasing, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward long COVID among 591 community members in China using a self-designed questionnaire. The paper reports KAP scores and correlations but does not test, evaluate, or report outcomes of any specific intervention or treatment for long COVID patients.

Cross-sectional comparative study assessing short- and long-term effects of COVID-19 on health-related quality of life and psychological outcomes (anxiety, depression) in a Saudi Arabian population. Found significant reduction in social functioning one year post-infection, with mild anxiety and depression levels across all groups.

Community-based cross-sectional study examining the association between COVID-19 infection and new-onset hypertension among 333 residents in Saudi Arabia. Found that 8.1% of infected individuals without prior hypertension developed new-onset hypertension, with age and dyslipidemia as significant risk factors.

Cross-sectional national survey examining the prevalence and predictors of viral arthropathy and myalgia following COVID-19 in 1,065 participants. Found that 26.5% reported arthralgia and 53.2% reported myalgia, with 9.9% and 6.0% respectively reporting new-onset symptoms after acute COVID-19 resolution.

Cross-sectional study characterizing new-onset chronic musculoskeletal pain in 30 long COVID patients, examining clinical features, sensory abnormalities, and functional/psychological impacts. Findings reveal widespread pain with central sensitization markers, pro-inflammatory profiles, reduced mobility and strength, and moderate depression/anxiety with severely compromised quality of life.

A cross-sectional survey of 757 Indonesian post-COVID-19 patients examining sleep disturbances and their impact on quality of life using standardized questionnaires (PSQI, ISI, ESS, STOP-BANG, SF-36). The study found that sleep quality and insomnia significantly affected patients' physical, emotional, and social functioning, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study assessing insomnia prevalence and associated factors among 325 COVID-19 recovered patients in Vietnam, finding 34.5% had insomnia. Identifies age, social support, anxiety, depression, and stress as significant factors associated with insomnia in post-COVID patients, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining ocular manifestations in 200 COVID-19 and post-COVID patients at a teaching hospital in India. Found ocular abnormalities in 18% of patients including conjunctivitis, dry eyes, and glaucoma, with most cases resolving within 1-4 weeks.

Cross-sectional survey of 3,165 COVID-19 patients in China assessing long COVID prevalence (9.73%) and health status differences using propensity score matching. Study found long COVID cases had significantly lower health scores and identified healthy lifestyles and mental decompression as protective factors, but did not test any intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 180 post-COVID patients in India assessing the prevalence, profile, and determinants of post-COVID syndrome ≥12 weeks after recovery from acute COVID-19. Found 72.8% prevalence with fatigue (62%), hair fall (45%), and sleep disturbance (24%) as common symptoms, with significant associations to age, gender, comorbidity, hospitalization duration, and anticoagulant use.

This study assessed quality of life in 62 children aged 5-17 years with post-COVID syndrome compared to 30 children with other respiratory infections using the PedsQL 4.0 questionnaire. Children with COVID-19 history showed significantly reduced quality of life across all age groups at 6-month follow-up, with differences noted between child and parental assessments.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between self-efficacy and adherence to therapeutic regimen among 133 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients at a chest outpatient clinic. The study found a positive correlation between self-efficacy levels and therapeutic regimen adherence, but does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed sleep disorders, cardiovascular symptoms, and body weight dynamics in 253 women with post-COVID-19 syndrome using questionnaires and vital sign measurements. The paper documents symptom prevalence and correlations but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study assessing women's knowledge, practices, and attitudes toward post-COVID-19 syndrome in Fayoum governorate, Egypt. The study found 80% had unsatisfactory knowledge about post-COVID syndrome, though 90.4% reported satisfactory practices and attitudes were mixed (43.5% positive, 56.5% negative).

Cross-sectional study examining the effect of COVID-19 infection on ovarian reserve in 120 infertile women using assisted reproductive technology. Found no statistically significant differences in AMH, AFC, FSH, and LH levels before and after COVID-19 infection across disease severity groups.

Cross-sectional screening study of 88 nurses with COVID-19 history using the MINIDEP tool to assess post-COVID depression prevalence. Found 13.6% had post-COVID depression, with female sex, illness duration, and sleep disturbance as significant correlates, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study describes delayed effects of COVID-19 in 137 hospitalized children in Iran from 2021-2023, using medical records and parental interviews. Fatigue was the most common complication (21.1%), with other effects including cough, rhinorrhea, and nausea; the study calls for personalized follow-up care but does not test any intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared pain, fall frequency, fear of falling, and physical activity levels in 48 older people who had recovered from COVID-19 versus 66 healthy controls. The COVID-19 group showed significantly higher pain, fatigue, cognitive impairment, fall frequency, and fear of falling, but this is an observational comparison study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines clinical characteristics and risk factors for prolonged hospital stays in 52 post-COVID-19 patients readmitted 30-90 days after acute infection. The study identifies severe COVID-19 history and lung consolidation as independent risk factors for extended hospitalization, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared sexual activity in 110 women before and after acute COVID-19 infection, measured at baseline and one month post-infection. The study found significant decreases in sexual activity scores following infection, with greater severity correlating to larger declines.

Cross-sectional study of 382 Iraqi medical students assessing the frequency of persistent respiratory symptoms 60+ days after COVID-19 infection. Found that intermittent cough (47.4%), dry cough (46.6%), and chronic cough (40.6%) were the most common persistent symptoms.

This cross-sectional study assessed vitamin D levels in 82 long COVID patients with fatigue or neuropsychiatric symptoms and examined correlations with symptom severity using standardized scales. While 73.2% of participants had vitamin D deficiency, the analysis found no association between vitamin D levels and any clinical outcomes including fatigue, depression, anxiety, sleep quality, or cognitive function.

Cross-sectional survey of 160 Egyptian children assessed 12 weeks post-COVID-19 infection to determine prevalence and nature of persistent symptoms. Found 36.25% exhibited post-COVID symptoms including fatigue, sleep disturbances, and neuropsychiatric issues, but this is an observational prevalence study with no treatment intervention tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed cardiovascular disease risk and fitness levels (via VO2 max) in 150 post-COVID middle-aged industrial workers, finding that 34% had moderate-to-high cardiovascular risk and reduced cardiorespiratory fitness particularly in the 45–55 age group. The study is observational without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.

Cross-sectional questionnaire study examining correlations between medications used during acute COVID-19 infection and post-recovery symptoms in recovered patients. The study found differential symptom persistence associated with various medications (vitamin D, ACE inhibitors, azithromycin, H2 antagonists) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment given to long COVID patients—it only retrospectively associates prior acute-phase medications with symptom outcomes.

Cross-sectional survey of 657 COVID-19 recovered patients in Jordan assessing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and risk factors. Study identifies 71.9% PCS prevalence and six significant risk factors (female sex, age ≥30, diabetes, hypertension, respiratory disease, neuropsychological disturbance) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A hospital-based cross-sectional questionnaire study of 385 COVID-19 patients in Hiroshima investigating persistent symptoms at median 23.5 days post-infection across different viral variants (Wild-type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron). The study identifies symptom clusters and examines risk factors but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts/behaviors in COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected controls using standardized mental health questionnaires. Found significantly higher depression and anxiety scores in those with COVID-19 history, with symptoms overlapping post-COVID syndrome presentation.

This cross-sectional study compared biochemical and immunological markers (ferritin, CRP, D-dimer, LDH, antibodies, liver enzymes) in four groups: infected, recovered, vaccinated recovered, and vaccinated non-infected subjects in Baghdad. While the paper includes recovered COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute phase reactants and vaccine response rather than persistent post-COVID symptoms or long COVID interventions.

Population-based cross-sectional survey of 2,712 COVID-19 patients across 4 Chinese cities examining the prevalence of long COVID symptoms, symptom patterns, and associated risk factors using WHO definitions. Found 90.4% prevalence of long COVID with female gender, certain occupations, poor health status, and critical COVID-19 severity as risk factors; vaccination protective.

This study analyzes self-reported smell disorder descriptions from 1,560 COVID-19 patients across two timepoints using natural language processing to characterize olfactory dysfunctions in long-haulers versus non-long-haulers. While it provides insights into smell disorder phenotypes in long COVID patients, it is a secondary analysis of survey data without testing any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study assessing demographic, clinical, and quality of life profiles of 54 older adults with diabetes during COVID-19 in Brazil, with 48.1% infected by COVID-19 and 61.5% of those progressing to long COVID. The study found that long COVID patients experienced fatigue/muscle weakness and had significantly impacted quality of life, particularly in anxiety and worry dimensions, but this is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Online cross-sectional survey of 1,262 Chinese participants investigating the prevalence of tinnitus and ear-related symptoms following COVID-19 infection. Found that 42.8% reported ear symptoms post-COVID, with tinnitus being the most common and impactful symptom, particularly in females and younger individuals.

This study validates the German Revised eHealth Literacy Scale (GR-eHEALS) instrument in 330 individuals with post-COVID-19 condition, assessing their ability to find and understand health information online. The instrument demonstrated good reliability and validity, though it does not test any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and clustering of unhealthy lifestyle behaviors (smoking, drinking, diet, physical inactivity, sedentary behavior) among 5,890 Vietnamese COVID-19 survivors, with emphasis on sex differences. The study identifies notable sex differences in lifestyle patterns post-COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is purely observational and behavioral assessment.

Population-based cross-sectional study examining associations between acute COVID-19 symptom profiles and long COVID prevalence in 4,169 adults. Found that multi-symptomatic and shortness of breath profiles had highest long COVID risk (39.7% and 22.4% prevalence respectively), with significant demographic variations by sex and ethnicity.

Cross-sectional study of 1,062 Chinese participants investigating associations between COVID-19, long COVID, and sleep disturbances using standardized questionnaires (PSQI, PHQ-9, GAD-7). Found that long COVID is strongly associated with significant sleep disturbances, particularly among older adults and those with lower socioeconomic status, though the study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional questionnaire study of 245 hospitalized COVID-19 patients at 4 months post-discharge, assessing prevalence of persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms and their associations with fatigue, anxiety, and trauma. Found 71.8% of patients experienced persistent symptoms, with significant differences by sex and hospital length of stay, but no intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 3,962 French civil servants assessing long COVID prevalence (1.54% diagnosed, 6.08% suspected), associated risk factors, disease knowledge, and vaccination attitudes. Study found long COVID underdiagnosed among workforce, with associations between vaccination status and long COVID likelihood, but no treatment intervention evaluated.

This cross-sectional study examined correlations between metabolic, inflammatory, and hemostatic parameters in 105 patients with MASLD stratified by SARS-CoV-2 antibody status. While the paper addresses post-COVID metabolic dysfunction, it is an observational correlation study without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study examining depression, anxiety, and suicidal thinking/behavior in COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected controls using questionnaire responses from 506 U.S. adults. Found significantly elevated PHQ-9 and STAI scores in those with COVID-19 history, with symptom overlap to Post-COVID Syndrome, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This retrospective cohort study assessed cardiovascular manifestations in 650 post-COVID patients attending a dedicated outpatient department, using echocardiography and standardized cardiac classifications. Among the cohort, 22.5% of patients had cardiac manifestations including angina, arrhythmia, and NSTEMI, with higher prevalence in those with multiple comorbidities.

Observational cross-sectional study of 101 COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia examining factors associated with long-term COVID-19 occurrence. Found that comorbid status and longer treatment duration were significantly associated with long COVID development, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 65 nursing students in Malang assessing physical, psychological, and spiritual health status after COVID-19 recovery. Study documents persistent symptoms including fatigue (58.3% moderate), shortness of breath (42.9% moderate), and high rates of psychological distress (anxiety 75.4% very severe), alongside spiritual wellbeing status.

Cross-sectional observational study of 102 COVID-19 survivor students assessing knowledge and attitudes toward healthy eating patterns for preventing long COVID syndrome. Study found good knowledge (72.94%) and positive attitudes (88.82%) toward nutrition, but no correlation between dietary knowledge/attitudes and nutritional status.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 1,000 post-COVID patients (4 weeks to 12 months post-infection) to characterize the prevalence and nature of neurological, somatic, and mental health complaints. The study found high rates of fatigue (77.5%), cognitive impairment (69.5%), hair loss (49.5%), and gender-specific differences in symptom severity, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 732 COVID-19 survivors in Malaysia assessing depression prevalence and associated factors using the PHQ-9 questionnaire. Found that 47.3% had mild to severe depression, with female gender, younger age, overweight/obesity, presence of long COVID, and perceived poor health as significant risk factors.

A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between social determinants of health and chronic diseases in two parishes in Ecuador during 2022-2023. The study found significant associations between social determinants and risk for hypertension, osteoporosis, and BMI, but does not focus on long COVID or study any treatment interventions.

This cross-sectional survey of 194 COVID-19 recovered individuals identified predictors of taste and smell loss (profession, smoking status, allergies, respiratory infection frequency) and examined associations with post-COVID symptoms. The study found that sensory loss was associated with higher rates of post-COVID gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and skin symptoms, but does not constitute a treatment trial.

Retrospective quality-improvement analysis characterizing baseline symptoms and functional impairments in 422 long COVID patients attending outpatient rehabilitation in the UK. Found high prevalence of fatigue (76%), breathlessness (69%), depression (55%), and work/social dysfunction (57%), but this is a descriptive baseline assessment, not a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,044 COVID-19 patients conducted 4+ weeks post-infection to assess long COVID symptom prevalence and impact on quality of life. Found 65.6% reported persistent symptoms, with myalgia, fatigue, joint pain, and anosmia most common; no intervention tested.

Cross-sectional study of 100 long COVID patients in Sweden assessing functioning, activity, and disability using ICF-based questionnaires. Found widespread impairments in body functions (fatigue, cognition, sleep, respiratory) and activity limitations (work, leisure, social), suggesting need for multidisciplinary rehabilitation.

Cross-sectional survey assessing how persistent olfactory dysfunction after COVID-19 impacts quality of life in 1,072 participants using the QOD-NS questionnaire. Study documents that olfactory impairment significantly affects QOL but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional survey of 614 post-COVID-19 patients examining the impact of self-reported fatigue on daily functioning and its associations with sociodemographics, physical capacity, and work ability. The study found fatigue is common and negatively impacts functioning, suggesting rehabilitation interventions may be beneficial, but does not test any specific treatment.

This cross-sectional study assessed cardiovascular autonomic function in 47 long COVID patients (with and without type 2 diabetes) compared to 45 diabetic controls without COVID-19, using autonomic reflex tests and heart rate variability measures. The study found that COVID-19 exacerbates autonomic dysfunction in diabetic patients and impairs autonomic function in non-diabetic long COVID patients to a similar degree as diabetes alone.

Cross-sectional observational study measuring physical activity and sedentary time in 159 adults with post-COVID-19 condition using activity monitors. Study identifies associations between symptoms (POTS, palpitations, paraesthesia) and activity levels, but does not test or evaluate any intervention—it is purely descriptive/observational.

This cross-sectional study characterizes pulmonary function and disability in 32 post-acute COVID-19 patients admitted to an Italian rehabilitation unit and proposes an early rehabilitation protocol. However, the paper focuses on acute post-hospitalization recovery during active disease sequelae in the immediate post-ICU period, not long COVID as persistent symptoms weeks-to-months after infection.

Cross-sectional study comparing chronic pain prevalence in 52 COVID-19 patients (evaluated 4.2 months post-infection) versus 52 matched healthy controls using painDETECT and DN4 questionnaires. Found 70% chronic pain prevalence in COVID-19 group (similar to controls), with 10% of COVID patients reporting new-onset or worsened pain post-infection, particularly neuropathic pain.

This descriptive cross-sectional study compares referral patterns for COVID-19 recovered participants versus a general population control group using Qatar Biobank data. It identifies that diabetes is the most common reason for healthcare referral in COVID-recovered patients, in contrast to osteopenia in the general population, suggesting increased post-COVID metabolic complications.

Cross-sectional study assessing nutrition status and quality of life in 40 post-COVID-19 patients using dietary frequency analysis and SF-36 questionnaire. Found nutritional deficiencies (vitamin D, B vitamins, iron, selenium), excess fat and calories, and impaired quality of life scores, particularly in emotional and mental health domains.

Online survey of medical workers assessing residual clinical manifestations of COVID-19 during early (0-6 months) and late recovery periods (6-15 months), including fatigue, cognitive impairment, alopecia, and affective disorders. Study is descriptive/observational with no treatment intervention tested.

A cross-sectional study examining the relationship between D-dimer levels and post-COVID neurological syndrome (PCNS) in 100 COVID-19 patients 3-6 months after hospitalization. Found a statistically significant positive correlation between elevated D-dimer and PCNS symptoms (p=0.003), suggesting hypercoagulability in post-COVID neurological manifestations.

Retrospective analysis of 2020 CDC National Health Interview Survey data comparing functional and behavioral limitations associated with frailty risk in older adults (65+) stratified by COVID-19 infection status and symptom severity. Older adults with moderate-to-severe COVID-19 demonstrated significantly greater frailty-related limitations including tiredness, self-care deficits, and anxiety/depression compared to COVID-negative controls.

This observational cross-sectional study examines the association between long COVID-19 symptoms and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in 4,463 Vietnamese COVID-19 survivors, investigating health literacy as a protective modifier. The findings show that long COVID-19 symptoms are associated with higher PTSD likelihood, and higher health literacy is protective against PTSD.

A cross-sectional study assessing subjective quality of life and health outcomes in 64 COVID-19 survivors (mean ~1 year post-infection) in Kazakhstan using the SF-36 instrument. Most participants reported stable or slightly worse health compared to pre-COVID baseline, with women reporting lower quality of life than men.

Cross-sectional survey of 94 COVID-19 survivors presenting with unresolved respiratory symptoms at a pulmonology clinic in Lagos, Nigeria. Study documents prevalence of respiratory morbidity (fatigue 85.1%, dyspnea 56.4%, cough 62.8%) and functional impairment but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study assessing objective and subjective olfactory dysfunction in 147 post-COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia. Findings showed persistent anosmia/hyposmia was significantly associated with delayed onset, longer duration of symptoms, and longer overall COVID-19 symptom duration.

Cross-sectional survey of 381 adults assessing persistent COVID-19 symptoms and socioeconomic correlates one year post-infection. Identifies fatigue, memory deficit, headache, hair loss, and cough as most common symptoms, with higher prevalence in females, unvaccinated individuals, and lower-income groups.

This cross-sectional survey of 168 Pakistani participants assessed the prevalence and symptom profile of long COVID syndrome, finding that 78.6% experienced persistent symptoms beyond 4 weeks post-infection, with fatigue, fever, and loss of taste being most common. The study identified risk factors including male gender, existing chronic illnesses, and hospital isolation, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and patterns of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in 108 post-COVID patients with articular and musculoskeletal symptoms between August-October 2021. The study found that 29% tested positive for ANA, with higher prevalence in patients >6 months post-infection, suggesting COVID-19 may trigger autoantibody development but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared metacognitive beliefs and mental health in 122 post-COVID-19 patients and quarantined individuals using questionnaires (MCQ and GHQ-12). While the paper identifies psychological sequelae in long COVID patients, it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is a descriptive/observational assessment only.

A cross-sectional survey of 220 pediatric patients in Latvia that characterized the prevalence and types of long COVID symptoms across age groups (< 1.5 years to 11-18 years). The study identified fatigue, persistent cough, mood swings, and impaired physical activity as the most common symptoms but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional survey assessed knowledge and anxiety levels regarding long COVID-19 among 50 respondents in Semarang Regency, Indonesia. The study found that 74% had low knowledge and 54% experienced mild anxiety, but it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—only measures baseline knowledge and psychological status.

This cross-sectional study examines how sociodemographic and clinical characteristics correlate with BMI and recovery time in individuals with long COVID-19 from Bangladesh. The research focuses on understanding how persistent COVID-19 symptoms affect age, gender, education, and occupational functioning.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between PTSD and psychosomatic symptoms in long COVID patients at a regional hospital in Indonesia (n=73). Found significant correlation between PTSD factors and long-lasting psychosomatic symptoms (P=0.001), but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional comparative study examining attention and memory deficits in adults with central auditory processing disorder (CAPD), comparing those with and without prior COVID-19 infection. Found no significant differences on the Neuropsi test between groups overall, though differences emerged in specific attention and memory domains when stratified by age, education, and time since COVID infection.

This descriptive cross-sectional study examined post-acute COVID-19 syndrome symptoms in 30 recovered patients, finding that fatigue, persistent cough, and loss of taste/smell were the most commonly reported symptoms 1-2 weeks after infection. The study describes symptom prevalence and severity but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between social support, socioeconomic status, age, and psychological well-being in 255 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. Found significant positive relationships between these factors and psychological well-being, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional descriptive study estimated the prevalence of persistent symptoms in 114 individuals who had recovered from COVID-19 infection in Kerala, India. The findings showed that 57.9% of participants reported persistent symptoms, with fatigue (39.5%) and joint pain (20.2%) being the most common, but no specific treatment or intervention was tested.

A cross-sectional study of 52 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors in Brazzaville assessed long-term radiographic and spirometric outcomes at least 6 months post-infection. The study found abnormal chest imaging in 42.3% of patients and ventilatory disorders in 71.1%, with advanced age, comorbidities, and mechanical ventilation associated with worse outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in 219 post-COVID-19 patients and its association with symptom severity. Found 84% had deficient vitamin D levels but detected no significant link between vitamin D status and post-COVID symptoms.

This paper assesses the population's need for post-COVID rehabilitation services in Primorsky Krai, Russia, and evaluates the capacity of sanatorium-resort facilities to meet that demand. It is a descriptive needs assessment study without any intervention, treatment evaluation, or patient outcomes data.

This cross-sectional study tested whether SARS-CoV-2 induces persistent genome instability in endothelial cells of long COVID patients by examining micronuclei and chromosomal bridges in 51 COVID-recovered and 43 COVID-naive individuals. The hypothesis was not confirmed; no cases of genome instability were detected in either group, suggesting that any systemic endothelial effects from COVID-19 may be reversible.

This study analyzes the relationship between COVID-19 severity and cognitive impairment in students during the post-acute phase, and examines associations with chronic diseases. It is a cross-sectional assessment of post-COVID symptoms but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 4,450 SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals in Missouri that developed machine learning models to predict clinical outcomes including hospitalization, ICU admission, and long COVID using viral sequences, host genetics, and environmental factors. The study identified risk factors for long COVID including prior hospitalization, ventilation, and female sex, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life, cognitive, and psycho-emotional status in post-COVID patients with and without metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Patients with MAFLD showed significantly impaired quality of life, increased anxiety/depression, and worse cognitive function compared to controls.

Cross-sectional study of 90 COVID-19 patients discharged from a medical college in Bangalore, India, assessing symptom persistence post-discharge and associated risk factors. Found 41.1% had persistent symptoms (mostly fatigue), with age, hospitalization, obesity, and smoking as risk factors.

Retrospective multicenter cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID syndrome in 435 Russian children at 7.6 months post-infection. Found that asthenia, neurocognitive disorders, and respiratory disorders persisted in approximately half of children, with comorbidities increasing risk of PCS manifestations.

A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID syndrome in an urban community in Bangalore, India, recruiting 82 participants aged 18+ years. The study found that 85% experienced fatigue, 84% malaise/discomfort, and 82% mood disturbance, with multiple organ systems affected, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 294 long COVID patients in Bangladesh examining symptom characteristics and associations with demographics and comorbidities. The study describes prevalence (15.6%), symptom severity using pain and fatigue scales, and demographic patterns but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 60 residents of Kharkiv assessing prevalence of post-COVID symptoms and their impact on daily functioning.
