Primary findings: fatigue (61.7%), brain fog (58.3%), exercise intolerance (56.7%), muscle pain (45%), sleep disorders and joint pain (43.3%). Paper recommends comprehensive rehabilitation but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

A cross-sectional study evaluating inflammatory biomarkers (LDH, RF, CRP, ferritin, uric acid) in 139 long COVID patients with arthritis symptoms in India. The study found that inflammatory markers decreased over six months of follow-up, but this is an observational characterization study without testing any active intervention or treatment.

Observational cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of ongoing symptoms and laboratory abnormalities in 42 COVID-19 cases at least 12 months post-infection in Wellington, New Zealand. Found that 90% reported at least two ongoing symptoms including anxiety, depression, dyspnoea, pain, and sleep difficulties, with minimal laboratory abnormalities.

This is a secondary analysis of 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data examining the relationship between long COVID, cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's Disease risk factors across 29 states. The study is observational/descriptive (no intervention tested) and uses existing survey data rather than conducting a primary research study.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between metabolic risk factors (BMI, blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, stroke) and long COVID risk in 990 New Zealand survey respondents. Found high BMI strongly associated with long COVID (aOR 2.35) but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A cross-sectional study of 27 post-COVID patients with hypertension examining transforming growth factor β1 as a potential biomarker for cardiovascular complications. The study found elevated TGF-β1 levels associated with worse glucose control and uncontrolled hypertension in post-COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study of 83 long COVID patients in Aragon examining employment status and associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. Finds 44.6% on temporary work disability, with greater symptom burden and male gender predicting work incapacity.

Retrospective analysis comparing physical development and fitness indicators between freshmen who had COVID-19 and those who did not in 2022. No treatment intervention was administered; this is an observational study examining differences in physical fitness outcomes stratified by BMI.

Cross-sectional web-survey analyzing factors associated with long COVID in 228 Brazilian adults who tested positive for COVID-19. Found associations between long COVID persistence and age, lower family income, lack of physical activity, hypertension, and specific acute symptoms (chills, headache, cough, anosmia, ageusia, dyspnea, diarrhea), with fatigue being the most prevalent long COVID symptom.

Descriptive cross-sectional study comparing physical development and functional indicators (endurance, strength, fitness) in first-year university students who recovered from COVID-19 versus those who never had the infection. The study documents persistent post-COVID effects on motor function and exercise tolerance but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional study of 115 post-COVID patients examining the frequency and characteristics of sleep disorders after COVID-19 infection. The study found restless leg syndrome was the most common sleep disorder, and moderate-to-severe COVID-19 infection was associated with 11.6-fold higher risk of reduced sleep quality in younger patients (26-59 years).

Cross-sectional study examining factors affecting quality of life, physical activity, cognitive function, and dyspnea in 176 long COVID patients (12+ weeks post-infection). Found that female gender, older age, and disease severity negatively impact these outcomes, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study of long COVID patients in New Zealand examining the impact of long COVID on people's ability to work. Characterizes work disability prevalence and burden in the long COVID population.

Observational cross-sectional study examining quality of life in 122 COVID-19 ICU survivors one year after discharge using the SF-36 questionnaire. Found that persistent sequelae, depression, and anxiety significantly negatively affected all dimensions of quality of life, with emotional well-being and general health most affected.

This cross-sectional study examined oral health complaints and dental pathology in post-COVID patients using the OHIP-14 questionnaire and clinical examination. While it documents elevated rates of dry mouth (30.04%), taste loss (24.90%), and oral mucosal lesions in COVID-19 survivors, it is a descriptive epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment component.

This cross-sectional study compares ocular blood flow parameters in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) who recently had COVID-19 versus those without prior COVID-19 infection using laser speckle flowgraphy. The study identifies significant changes in microvascular hemodynamics in the optic nerve head and peripapillary retina in POAG patients with moderate post-COVID-19 syndrome, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective cross-sectional study assessed sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) in 100 post-COVID-19 patients using pure tone audiometry. The study documents that SNHL is a common extrapulmonary complication of COVID-19, with 45% of patients experiencing bilateral moderate hearing loss, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 197 individuals assessing persistent symptoms in those partially or fully recovered from COVID-19. Found post-COVID syndrome present in 52.3% of respondents, with women showing higher risk for depression, anosmia, dysgeusia, and alopecia, while obese participants reported more arthralgia, dyspnea, cough, and odynophagia.

This cross-sectional study assessed the frequency of depression and anxiety in 450 COVID-19-positive patients using PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scales during April-May 2021. The study found depression more prevalent in older age groups and anxiety in younger age groups, but it is a descriptive epidemiological study that does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Descriptive cross-sectional study of 88 COVID-19 patients with cardiovascular disease history, examining patient demographics and long COVID prevalence. Findings show majority were aged 60-75 years, female, with hospitalization <14 days, but no treatment intervention was studied.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing respiratory muscle strength, lung function, and exercise capacity in 49 post-COVID-19 patients two years after recovery. Found diffusion impairment (32%), reduced exercise capacity (44%), and respiratory muscle weakness (41%), but provides no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,055 COVID-19 recovered individuals in Jordan assessing mental health outcomes using the MHI-38 inventory. Found high prevalence of depression (46.3%), anxiety (45.8%), and loss of control (47.2%), with employment status, tobacco use, and COVID-19 severity as risk factors.

Observational cross-sectional study of 457 elderly Turkish patients (≥65 years) with persistent musculoskeletal complaints after COVID-19 infection. Found widespread pain (81%), myalgia (63.7%), and arthralgia (44.4%) significantly associated with comorbidities, hospitalization, and pulmonary involvement.

This cross-sectional study assessed the clinical and psychological consequences of COVID-19 in 96 Russian adolescents (48 with prior COVID-19, 48 controls) at various time points post-infection. The study found post-COVID syndrome characterized by asthenia, impaired attention/taste/smell, high anxiety, and depressive symptoms, with the most severe emotional symptoms occurring around the second month post-infection.

Cross-sectional study examining insomnia, dysfunctional beliefs about sleep, and depression in COVID-19-infected individuals. While the paper addresses post-infection sleep disorders, it focuses on acute COVID-19 infection outcomes rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

Cross-sectional study of 447 COVID-19 patients in Tehran examining the prevalence and types of persistent/late-onset complications at least 4 weeks after symptom onset. Found 77.2% experienced complications (cardiopulmonary and skin-related most common), with associations to older age, female sex, psychological stress, and inadequate rest.

This study analyzes serological testing for SARS-CoV-2-specific antibodies (IgM and IgG) in 12,860 urological hospital patients from 2021-2025, monitoring immune response patterns over time. It is an observational study characterizing immune markers in post-COVID syndrome rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 188 COVID-19 survivors 1-6 months post-infection examining sleep disturbances (poor sleep quality and insomnia) and associated factors including anxiety and depression. Found 43.6% reported poor sleep quality and 41% reported insomnia, with higher anxiety and depression scores associated with worse sleep outcomes.

Cross-sectional study of 85 COVID-19 patients evaluated >3 weeks after acute infection to assess symptom persistence and associated factors. Found 52% had persistent symptoms (fatigue 49%, cough 33%), associated with female sex, obesity, age 35-55, and initial hospitalization, with symptoms generally resolving over time.

This comparative cross-sectional study compared physical manifestations in COVID-19 recovered individuals versus uninfected controls, finding significantly elevated risks of fatigue, anosmia, ageusia, irregular heartbeat, and dyspnea in the recovered group. The study is descriptive/observational and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, so it does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

A cross-sectional survey of 635 mild COVID-19 patients in Turkey assessed the presence and frequency of persisting symptoms at 6+ months post-infection. The study identified fatigue, muscle pain, memory problems, joint pain, and smell disorders as the most common long COVID symptoms, with significant associations between symptom persistence and factors like initial lung involvement and anticoagulant use.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive function and ammonia levels in 41 post-COVID patients versus 19 controls, finding cognitive impairment in 45% of COVID survivors (more pronounced in those with post-COVID syndrome) and hyperammonemia in 54% of survivors. No significant correlation was found between hyperammonemia and cognitive impairment.

Cross-sectional survey of 556 workers with intensive computer workload examining the timing and frequency of post-COVID syndrome manifestations occurring 1-4 weeks after hospital discharge. Study ranked occupational risk factors and symptom patterns but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and persistence of post-COVID symptoms among medical workers employed in COVID clinics and laboratories in Russia. While it documents long-term sequelae including chest pain, joint pain, shortness of breath, and cognitive impairment, it is a passive epidemiological survey with no intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the treatment trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional survey of French general practitioners documenting the prevalence of long COVID patients in primary care and their most common symptoms. This is an epidemiological survey of GP experience, not a treatment intervention study.

This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and patterns of long COVID symptoms in 3, 6, 9, and 18 months post-hospitalization among COVID-19 survivors in Aruba. The study identified female sex and respiratory comorbidity as risk factors for persistent symptoms, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This observational cross-sectional study assessed long COVID symptoms in 45 children aged 5-17 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection at a tertiary hospital in 2021. Two-thirds of children developed long COVID symptoms, most commonly fatigue (45.2%), decreased appetite (38.7%), and muscle aches (32.3%), with symptoms occurring across all initial COVID severity levels.

Cross-sectional study examining new symptoms reported at primary care visits among 3,154 NYC patients during three post-acute COVID-19 follow-up intervals (0.5-9 months post-infection). Found that 16% of patients had new diagnoses, with respiratory complaints and fatigue being most common, but this is an observational epidemiological study with no treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of the 2022 MEPS dataset examining work absenteeism in US adults with long COVID, comparing missed workdays across three groups: never had COVID, COVID-19 without long COVID, and long COVID. Finds that long COVID patients miss 171% more workdays annually than those without COVID infection.

Cross-sectional survey of 488 university students measuring prior SARS-CoV-2 infection prevalence (41%) via antibody testing and assessing persistent symptoms post-infection. Found 11.4% of symptomatic students reported persistent symptoms consistent with post-acute COVID-19 a median of 132 days after infection, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without treatment intervention.

This paper analyzes the economic burden of long COVID by estimating lost labor costs among US adults using the 2022 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey. It found that individuals with long COVID had more than twice the lost labor costs compared to those without COVID, totaling approximately $12.8 billion in population-level lost labor costs.

This cross-sectional study compared choroidal thickness measurements using OCT imaging between 40 post-COVID-19 patients and 40 age-matched controls. Post-COVID patients showed significantly increased choroidal thickness across all measured regions, suggesting vascular involvement in post-COVID syndrome pathogenesis.

Cross-sectional survey of 183 long COVID patients investigating associations between fatigue, autonomic symptoms, interoceptive sensibility, illness perceptions, and distress. Findings show fatigue is severe and multifaceted, with autonomic symptoms and illness perceptions explaining 21-54% of variance, but no intervention or treatment is evaluated.

Cross-sectional survey of 250 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing sleep disturbances and sleep quality using standardized questionnaires. Found high prevalence of sleep problems (77.6% poor sleep quality, 53.6% subthreshold insomnia) and identified associations with reinfection and daytime tiredness, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of healthcare workers at a Nepalese medical academy assessing the prevalence and symptom profile of long COVID-19 using the COVID Yorkshire Rehabilitation Screening Tool. Study found 68.1% prevalence with fatigue, anxiety, and dyspnea as the most common symptoms, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A descriptive cross-sectional study of 108 healthcare professionals who recovered from COVID-19, assessing the prevalence and types of post-COVID health problems they experienced. Found that 42.6% experienced various symptoms including fatigue, persistent cough, headache, and malaise, with no significant association with age, sex, or vaccination status.

Community-based observational study documenting the prevalence and clinical presentation of post-COVID syndrome in 265 patients recovered from acute COVID-19 in North Kerala, India. Found 9.81% had post-COVID symptoms beyond 3 months, with female gender, comorbidities, and treatment severity as significant risk factors.

This cross-sectional study examines the association between COVID-19 infection and new-onset diabetes in 38 patients at a tertiary care hospital in Nepal. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications (hyperglycemia and diabetes onset during active infection) rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not test any treatment intervention.

This study develops and validates the PCS Fatigue Severity Measure V1, a 10-item instrument for quantifying fatigue in post-COVID-19 syndrome, using Rasch analysis on 414 participants from the Quebec Action for Post-COVID cohort. The measure showed strong correlations with criterion measures and distinguished between working individuals and those on sick leave, providing initial evidence for measuring PCS fatigue at a single time point.

This cross-sectional study compared oxidative stress markers in hemodialysis patients with and without long-COVID sequelae 3.5 months post-infection. Long-COVID patients showed significantly elevated malondialdehyde and reduced antioxidant levels, suggesting oxidative stress may contribute to persistent symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional cohort study examines oxidative stress markers in hemodialysis patients with and without post-COVID syndrome, measuring blood levels of malondialdehyde, paraoxonase-1, myeloperoxidase, and other biomarkers. The study identifies an elevated MPO/PON-1 ratio as a potential predictive biomarker for post-COVID syndrome in HD patients, with 88.5% sensitivity and 68.4% specificity.

This cross-sectional survey of 215 Malaysian COVID-19 survivors documents the prevalence and types of prolonged symptoms (lethargy, concentration difficulty, cough) at 1-3 months post-infection, and identifies female sex, chronic lung disease, and hypertension as risk factors. The study is descriptive and observational with no intervention tested, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

Three-centre cross-sectional study examining COPD course in 46 patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection stratified by extent of viral pulmonary involvement. Found high rates of COPD exacerbation (69.6%) and new-onset COPD (26.1%) in post-COVID period, with worse outcomes in those with severe pulmonary involvement, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines kidney pathology (glomerulonephritis) occurring 8-12 months after moderate COVID-19 by measuring TGF-β1 and VEGF levels in blood and urine across three groups: GN patients with prior COVID-19, COVID-19 patients without GN, and healthy controls. While the paper confirms an association between moderate COVID-19 and delayed GN manifestation, it is excluded because it does not test or evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely a biomarker study of disease pathology.

This cross-sectional study examines the psycho-emotional state of 80 women with infertility after COVID-19 infection, comparing them to a control group. The authors found significantly higher rates of anxiety (91.2% vs 30%) and depression (13.8% vs 2.5%) in the long COVID group, with strong correlations between psycho-emotional severity and personality traits.

This cross-sectional study examined the association between vitamin D levels and inflammatory markers (CRP and D-dimer) in 70 post-COVID recovery patients. The study found that vitamin D deficiency was associated with significantly higher CRP and D-dimer levels, but it is an observational assessment without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study examining risk factors for post-COVID-19 syndrome in 65 children with recurrent/chronic lung diseases. Found no statistically significant associations with demographic or acute-phase clinical variables, but identified increased airway hyperreactivity in children with asthma as a potential long-term risk factor.

Cross-sectional study examining quality of life in 132 post-COVID syndrome patients, comparing those with newly diagnosed carbohydrate metabolism disorders (impaired glucose tolerance or type 2 diabetes) to those without. Finds that post-COVID patients with carbohydrate metabolism disorders have significantly reduced quality of life on physical and role functioning scales.

This Ukrainian study examines post-COVID syndrome (PCS) prevalence and its association with cognitive dysfunction and quality of life in 200 hemodialysis patients (118 with PCS, 82 without). While the paper documents worse cognitive function and quality of life in hemodialysis patients with long COVID, it is a passive observational cross-sectional study with no intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study assessing functional status and long COVID-related limitations in 142 nurses at a Ecuadorian hospital during 2022. 45.1% experienced minimal to severe functional limitations, with significant associations found between functional status and age/infection count.

Cross-sectional survey comparing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and symptoms among senior students at two Ukrainian universities, finding high rates of neurological and psychological symptoms affecting academic performance. The paper identifies symptoms and their impact but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 201 post-COVID-19 discharged patients assessing health problems and persistent symptoms during recovery. Found high prevalence of weakness (71.64%), fatigue (60.69%), and cough (39.80%) in the post-recovery period, with recommendations for follow-up care and lifestyle modifications.

This descriptive-quantitative study investigates factors influencing cycling as physical activity in elderly post-COVID-19 patients using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Results show 88.6% of elderly participants cycle due to awareness of exercise benefits, with higher participation among females aged 55-60.

This cross-sectional study examined determinants of support systems and quality of life in 110 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. The study found significant relationships between quality of life and factors like family attitudes/behavior, age, and comorbid conditions, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing white matter macro- and microstructure in 31 neurologic long COVID (NeuroPASC) patients versus 41 asymptomatic controls using brain MRI and cognitive testing. Found larger cerebral white matter volume, higher white matter mean kurtosis, and lower cognitive performance (attention, processing speed, verbal learning) in NeuroPASC patients, along with elevated interferon levels suggesting immune dysregulation.

A cross-sectional study comparing 120 COVID-19 survivors with 120 healthy controls on cognitive, somatic, and psychiatric measures using standardized questionnaires. Findings show survivors have significantly higher cognitive difficulties, body sensations, and anxiety, but not depression.

This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and predictors of long COVID among 1,338 COVID-19 cases at a university in Washington, DC, finding 36% prevalence and identifying risk factors including underlying conditions, female sex, smoking, and acute symptom severity. The study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis despite being relevant long COVID research.

Cross-sectional study of 11,057 US school-aged children examining functional limitations and illness-related absenteeism in children with and without long COVID. Found that children with long COVID had higher rates of functional limitations (18.3% vs 8.6% memory difficulty) and chronic absenteeism, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between antibody levels (IgM and IgG) and ongoing symptoms in 105 COVID-19 survivors who donated plasma. The findings show that IgM and IgG levels vary with time elapsed, prior medications (favipiravir, hydroxychloroquine), and demographic factors, contributing to understanding of post-COVID symptom persistence.

Cross-sectional study of 524 post-COVID patients with dizziness, measuring dizziness-related disability using the Dizziness Handicap Inventory. Finds that 51.8% have moderate/severe dizziness disability, particularly during head movements and strenuous activities, suggesting vestibular impairment.

This cross-sectional study compares post-exertional malaise (PEM) experiences between 80 long COVID patients and 151 ME/CFS patients using questionnaires about PEM triggers, symptoms, recovery, and prevention. While it finds that long COVID patients experience PEM similarly to ME/CFS patients in some ways, it is a purely observational comparison study with no treatment intervention or control group assignment.

Cross-sectional comparative study examining cardiometabolic characteristics in elderly patients (aged 60-89) with comorbidities who experienced mild-to-moderate COVID-19 versus controls. Found that post-COVID patients had significantly worse lipid profiles, elevated fasting glucose, reduced renal function, elevated heart rate, and higher NT-proBNP levels, suggesting persistent cardiometabolic sequelae of COVID-19.

Cross-sectional study of 30 long COVID patients (>3 months post-infection) undergoing outpatient neurorehabilitation, characterizing physical and neuropsychological sequelae. Fatigue (86.6%), dyspnea (66.7%), cognitive impairment (63.3%), and neurological sequelae were prevalent, with rehabilitation addressing these persistent symptoms regardless of acute COVID severity.

Population-based cross-sectional study of 1,459 COVID-19 patients in Germany examining long-term symptoms ≥12 weeks post-infection. Found 72.6% prevalence in hospitalized patients and 46.2% in non-hospitalized patients, with fatigue, exhaustion, and cognitive difficulties as most common symptoms; identified female sex and comorbidity severity as key risk factors.

Cross-sectional study of 135 type 2 diabetes patients 3-24 months post-COVID-19 examining endothelial dysfunction and thrombotic markers. Found elevated D-dimer, von Willebrand factor, and cell adhesion molecules in many patients despite normal coagulation parameters, but this is a descriptive observational study without treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 497 Portuguese COVID-19 patients assessed 12-16 weeks after disease onset to estimate prevalence of post-COVID conditions and describe baseline characteristics. Found 47.5% cumulative incidence with fatigue (30.4%) and dyspnea (26.4%) as most frequent symptoms; male gender and certain BMI ranges were associated with lower odds of post-COVID conditions.

A cross-sectional study of 150 patients with prior COVID-19 infection presenting to an otolaryngology department, identifying otorhinolaryngologic symptoms in 84.67% and finding a 16% prevalence of long COVID syndrome (>12 weeks). The study describes symptom patterns including rhinorrhea, hyposmia, dysgeusia, and anosmia, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in acute COVID-19 patients with anosmia using a translated questionnaire. Focuses on acute infection symptom burden rather than long COVID or any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey study (n=1,482) examines the prevalence of persistent post-COVID symptoms and their associations with depression, anxiety, and insomnia in Sweden at 18 months post-pandemic. The paper reports high prevalence of persistent symptoms (84.5%) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it an epidemiological/observational study rather than a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional survey of 98 patients recovering from moderate-severe COVID-19 in Vietnam examining prevalence of post-COVID health issues. Found 73.5% experienced persistent symptoms at ≥12 weeks, most commonly hair loss, fatigue, dyspnea, and sleep difficulties, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A cross-sectional survey of 384 post-COVID-19 recovering patients examining the relationship between cold-heat patterns in Traditional Chinese Medicine and post-COVID-19 symptoms. The study found significant associations between gender, cold-heat patterns, and post-COVID-19 status, providing TCM characterization of post-COVID syndrome.

Compares static balance, dynamic balance, and knee joint position sense between 15 women with acute/recent COVID-19 and 15 healthy controls. Finds significant differences in balance metrics and proprioception, but does not study long COVID (persistent post-acute sequelae) or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional descriptive study assessing psychosocial distress in 101 post-COVID-19 survivors using the Self-Reporting Questionnaire 29 (SRQ-29). Found that 82.17% of survivors experienced psychosocial problems including PTSD (43%), anxiety/depression (20%), and psychosis disorders (20%), but no treatment intervention was tested or evaluated.

Cross-sectional study of 220 diabetic and non-diabetic COVID-19 patients assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) after hospitalization using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Found that diabetic patients had significantly lower HRQoL scores than non-diabetic patients, with education and diabetes being independent predictors of quality of life outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between academic stress and quality of life among 106 nursing students who are COVID-19 survivors using standardized instruments (ASS and WHOQoL-BREF). Found no significant association between academic stress and quality of life domains, though authors recommend further research on factors affecting quality of life in COVID-19 survivors.

This retrospective observational study examines the relationship between COVID-19 reinfection and menstrual pattern changes in 155 women at a health polytechnic in Indonesia. While it documents menstrual changes associated with COVID-19 infection, it does not study long COVID specifically (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and contains no treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional descriptive study of 181 COVID-19 recovered patients in Bangladesh examining long-term health problems and their associations with demographic and clinical factors. The study found post-viral fatigue (85%), shortness of breath (74%), and cognitive symptoms as the most common long-term sequelae, with significant associations between symptom severity and comorbidities.

Cross-sectional study measuring thyroid hormone levels (TSH, FT4) in 100 post-COVID patients with fatigue, comparing home-treated (n=50) vs hospital-treated (n=50) patients. Found significantly higher TSH and FT4 levels in home-treated patients, but this is a descriptive observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study of 236 post-COVID patients examining metabolic parameters including glucose, lipids, ferritin, and renal function. Found significant metabolic abnormalities including elevated blood glucose, HbA1c, serum ferritin, and dyslipidemia, suggesting increased risk of diabetes and systemic complications.

Cross-sectional descriptive study measuring fatigue levels in 40 elderly long COVID survivors in Pekanbaru, Indonesia at least 14 days post-infection. Found that 55% experienced mild fatigue, 25% moderate fatigue, 5% severe fatigue, and 15% no fatigue, with recommendations for post-isolation nursing assessment and intervention.

Cross-sectional study investigating histopathological changes in lung tissue of long COVID patients through transbronchial biopsies. Findings show patterns of diffuse alveolar damage, vascular abnormalities, inflammation, and fibrosis over weeks to months post-infection, providing mechanistic insight but not evaluating any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between body composition, muscle mass, strength, and physical function with Long COVID symptom severity in 17 adults. Found that higher muscle mass and strength are associated with lower Long COVID symptom scores, while greater body fat and BMI correlate with higher symptom severity.

This cross-sectional diagnostic validation study evaluated the KINDL questionnaire and CSSI-24 inventory for measuring quality of life and symptom burden in 84 children and adolescents with pediatric long COVID. The study established screening thresholds and found that these tools can help clinicians identify high-risk pediatric PASC cases, but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study investigates olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in 228 mild COVID-19 patients during acute infection (March-April 2020), finding high prevalence of these symptoms with mostly spontaneous improvement within months. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 symptoms during active infection, not long COVID or post-acute sequelae, and does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study surveyed COVID-19 survivors about persistent symptoms four weeks post-infection using online questionnaires. While documenting the prevalence and impact of long COVID symptoms on daily activities, it does not evaluate or test any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study investigated cellular stress responses, immune dysregulation, and biochemical signatures in 120 post-acute COVID-19 patients ≥30 days post-infection. The authors found persistent elevations in ER stress markers, inflammatory cytokines, and oxidative biomarkers that correlated with fatigue and dyspnea symptoms, suggesting quantifiable molecular disturbances underlying long COVID pathophysiology.

Cross-sectional study assessing lung function abnormalities using spirometry in 100 symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients 6-8 weeks post-discharge at a tertiary hospital in Bangladesh. Found 66% had restrictive changes in spirometry, significantly associated with disease severity and comorbidities like hypertension and diabetes.

A retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 281 women comparing post-COVID syndrome manifestations between those with laboratory-confirmed vs non-confirmed COVID-19, stratified by age groups. Women with confirmed COVID-19 experienced 1.5–2.0 times higher rates of symptom burden including decreased quality of life, cardiac symptoms, hair loss, and arthralgia, with age-dependent patterns in laboratory abnormalities (ESR, D-dimer, platelet counts).

A cross-sectional study of 145 long COVID patients at a Turkish hospital assessing 77 symptoms and quality of life using standardized instruments. The study found fatigue (53.1%), forgetfulness (40%), and dyspnea (26.9%) as most common symptoms, with sleep disorders and muscle pain most affecting quality of life.

Cross-sectional survey of 100 COVID-19 survivors in Padang, Indonesia examining factors associated with long COVID occurrence. Found 53% experienced long COVID, with comorbidities and smoking habits as significant risk factors, but the study is observational without intervention or treatment evaluation.

Cross-sectional observational study of 200 COVID-19 survivors assessing prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress using the DASS-21 scale and correlating mental health outcomes with severity of acute COVID-19 infection. Found high prevalence of psychological morbidity (38.5% depression, 38.5% anxiety, 11% stress) with significant correlations between acute infection severity and psychological distress.

This cross-sectional observational study of 798 patients examined the association between endothelial dysfunction (measured by endothelial quality index via thermal monitoring) and long COVID-19 symptoms. The study found that fatigue, chest pain, and neuro-cognitive difficulties were significantly associated with impaired endothelium function, but no treatment intervention was tested or evaluated.

This cross-sectional study compares plasma cytokine and monocyte levels in COVID-19 convalescents with pulmonary long COVID (PASC) versus recovered controls. The findings demonstrate elevated CD169+ monocyte counts and increased monocyte activation in long COVID patients, with correlations to reduced pulmonary function and inflammatory cytokines.

Cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence of hypocortisolism in 41 patients with a history of COVID-19 pneumonia using corticotropin stimulation testing. Found 27% had hypocortisolism (predominantly secondary), with over half reporting persistent fatigue and some requiring glucocorticoid replacement.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 10,194 adults with post-COVID-19 condition to compare symptoms, health-related quality of life, fatigue, and mental well-being across different time periods since acute infection (3-6 months to >24 months). The study found that fatigue and concentration problems were the most debilitating symptoms throughout, with worst outcomes at 3-6 months post-infection and slight improvement by 13-18 months, though health-related quality of life remained low even beyond 24 months.

This cross-sectional study analyzes the correlation between heart rate variability (HRV) and palpitation symptoms in 272 female healthcare workers with long COVID, comparing HRV parameters across three groups (with palpitations, other symptoms, asymptomatic). The study finds that reduced HRV parameters (SDNN, HRVIndex, LF, TP) are significantly associated with palpitations, suggesting autonomic dysfunction underlies palpitation symptoms in female long COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study examining gut integrity and oxidized lipid markers in 415 participants (85 with PASC, 72 without PASC, COVID-negative controls). Found significantly elevated zonulin and oxidized LDL in PASC patients, with strong associations between these biomarkers and PASC diagnosis.

Cross-sectional study comparing SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses, antibody levels, and autoantibodies in 51 healthcare workers with and without long COVID symptoms at 18-23 months post-infection. Found significant associations between elevated anti-TPO antibodies and long COVID incidence, but this is an observational characterization study with no intervention tested.

A prospective multicenter cross-sectional study evaluating clinical characteristics and post-COVID-19 persisting symptoms in 20-week follow-up after acute infection, including hematological and radiological findings. Found that 21.4% of symptomatic patients had persisting symptoms lasting ≥20 weeks, with significant associations to COVID-19 illness duration and comorbidities.

Cross-sectional ultrasound study of 312 long COVID patients assessing rectus femoris and vastus intermedius muscle thickness and echo intensity 3-11 months post-hospitalization. Muscle characteristics were significantly associated with demographic, clinical, and functional parameters including age, handgrip strength, sleepiness, and inflammatory markers.

A cross-sectional survey of 2,466 long COVID patients across 16 Latin American countries assessing symptom burden, activity limitations, and healthcare utilization patterns. While highly relevant to long COVID epidemiology, this is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation, and therefore does not meet criteria for the trials pipeline.

This cross-sectional study examines the prevalence and patterns of benzodiazepine and Z-hypnotic consumption among Spanish adults with long COVID, stratified by gender. While the paper is about long COVID, it does not study a treatment intervention but rather observes existing medication use patterns in the population, making it observational epidemiology rather than a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional study investigating hyposmia (reduced smell) incidence and recovery in 349 hospitalized non-severe COVID-19 patients infected with Omicron variant in Shanghai. Finds 6.3% had hyposmia with higher rates of respiratory and gastrointestinal symptoms, with 72.7% recovering within 1 month.

Cross-sectional study measuring cognitive function, balance, and retinal changes in 166 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints in Barcelona. Found cognitive impairment in 68.67%, balance dysfunction in 51.52%, and retinal alterations in 9.2%, with no significant association between symptom duration and cognitive impairment.

The PRIME post-COVID study assessed the prevalence of post-exertional malaise (PEM) and orthostatic intolerance (OI) in 3,783 people living with post-COVID-19 condition compared to uninfected controls. The study found that PEM and OI are highly prevalent in post-COVID patients (48.1% and 29.3% in women, respectively) and significantly more common than in controls, with age ≤60 years, comorbidities, and living alone as associated factors.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,355 COVID-19 recovered patients in Saudi Arabia examining long COVID prevalence and associated sociodemographic and clinical risk factors. Women reported 17.4% more LC symptoms than men, and acute-phase symptom severity correlated with long COVID symptom count.

This cross-sectional study assessed patient satisfaction among COVID-19 survivors in Northeast India using the Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire-18 (PSQ-18) administered via telephone interviews. While the study addresses long COVID survivors' healthcare experiences, it is not a treatment trial—it merely surveys satisfaction with existing healthcare services without testing or evaluating any specific intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared 90 vaccinated and 217 non-vaccinated long COVID patients in Kazakhstan to assess the impact of QazVac vaccination on clinical manifestations and immune responses. Vaccinated individuals showed significantly reduced frequencies of neurological, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and rheumatological symptoms, suggesting a protective role of vaccination against long COVID sequelae.

A cross-sectional survey of 490 university students in Saudi Arabia assessing awareness and clinical manifestations of long COVID symptoms. The study reports that 43.6% of females and 33.3% of males experienced long COVID symptoms, with tiredness, taste/smell loss, and brain fog being most common, and identifies gender differences in symptom presentation.

This cross-sectional study compares exercise capacity and pulmonary function in long COVID patients stratified by HIV status and acute COVID-19 severity, assessing 63 individuals 2 years post-infection. The study found that long COVID patients with HIV had similar functional capacity to those with prior mild/moderate COVID-19 but better outcomes than those with severe acute infection, despite lower spirometry values.

Cross-sectional study comparing leukocyte telomere length and HbA1c levels between 44 type 2 diabetes patients who developed post-COVID-19 syndrome and 22 who did not. Found significantly shorter telomeres and higher HbA1c in PCS patients, suggesting these as potential biomarkers for post-COVID syndrome.

This retrospective cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of post-COVID symptoms and conditions in 10 Croatian primary care practices and identified associated risk factors including pre-existing chronic diseases, vaccination status, and infection severity. Key findings include associations between older age, diabetes, obesity, and neurological comorbidities with various post-COVID sequelae including thromboembolism and brain fog.

Cross-sectional study of 220 long COVID patients examining associations between symptom burden and functional limitations using the PCFS scale. Identifies fatigue, dizziness, and memory loss as independent predictors of functional impairment, with symptom count explaining 51.3% of variance in disability.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,314 long COVID patients assessing autonomic dysfunction severity using the COMPASS-31 scale. Found 66% of PASC patients had moderate to severe autonomic dysfunction, with severity independent of acute COVID-19 hospitalization status.

Cross-sectional study of 657 older adults examining the association between serologically confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and objective cognitive function. Found that those with antibodies from prior infection had poorer global cognitive functioning compared to uninfected controls, particularly in language comprehension and temporal orientation.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive impairments in 134 long COVID patients 1-16 months post-infection, finding executive dysfunction in 56% and inhibition deficits in 38.8%. The paper does not test or evaluate any intervention, but rather characterizes the prevalence and associations of cognitive symptoms over time.

Cross-sectional study of 322 pediatric COVID-19 patients assessing neurological and psychological symptoms 3-5 months post-infection. Found persistent long COVID symptoms (22% at 3-5 months) including headache, fatigue, and anosmia, with associated anxiety and PTSD in older children, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

This cross-sectional observational study compared resting brain functional connectivity via fMRI in 51 non-hospitalized individuals with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome to 15 controls with non-COVID infection symptoms, assessed 4-5 months post-infection. The study found that COVID-19 patients had lower temporal and subcortical functional connectivity correlated with symptom severity, but it does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study comparing tactile sensation thresholds in 30 long COVID patients versus 46 healthy controls using Semmes-Weinstein monofilament testing. COVID patients showed subclinical increases in tactile sensation thresholds despite normal overall perception, suggesting possible peripheral sensory nerve involvement.

This cross-sectional study examined cognitive impairment in 53 long COVID patients 1.8 years post-infection using multimodal neuroimaging (MRI, DTI, fMRI) and neuropsychological testing. The study found that over half of participants had executive and attentional deficits, with abnormal white matter diffusivity and functional connectivity patterns correlating with memory impairment.

This cross-sectional study examined headache characteristics in 102 long COVID patients, comparing those with and without pre-COVID headache history. The study found that long COVID headaches are often disabling, tend to worsen compared to pre-COVID status, and are associated with other symptoms like insomnia and paraesthesia, but it is an observational descriptive study with no treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional observational study compared white matter microstructure and emotional health in 54 non-hospitalized individuals with post-acute COVID syndrome (PACS) versus 14 symptom-matched COVID-negative controls, assessed 4-5 months after infection. PACS patients showed distinct white matter alterations (reduced mean/axial diffusivity, increased mean kurtosis) that correlated with emotional sequelae severity, providing mechanistic insights into post-COVID neurological effects.

This cross-sectional survey study of 732 long COVID patients and 40 controls assessed the prevalence of new or worsening comorbidities following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found significantly higher rates of pain, cognitive dysfunction, and ME/CFS in long COVID patients compared to controls, with substantial overlap between long COVID and ME/CFS (58% vs 0%).

This cross-sectional study compares cognitive function in 70 older adults (aged 60-78) who had COVID-19 6 months prior versus 153 healthy controls, using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Basic and screening for depression and anxiety. The study found significantly higher rates of cognitive impairment in the COVID-19 group and identified risk factors (age, lower income, overweight, ageusia, anxiety) associated with greater cognitive decline.

A large cross-sectional study of 25,796 participants characterizing subjective brain fog and its associations with demographic, symptom, and cognitive variables. The study identifies brain fog as an impairment of concentration associated with long COVID, migraines, and reduced cognitive performance, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional analysis of 101 long COVID patients at a university clinic assessing clinical presentation, fatigue, cognitive symptoms, depression, anxiety, and olfactory impairment. Findings show 93% had fatigue (especially females), 82% impaired concentration, and thyroid disease as common comorbidity, but no interventions were tested.

Cross-sectional study of 131 long COVID patients examining the relationship between poor sleep quality, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and olfactory dysfunction using standardized assessment tools (PSQI, BAI, CCRC, MoCA). Found that anxiety and olfactory disorder are significantly associated with poor sleep quality in long COVID patients, suggesting neurological symptoms are interconnected aspects of the condition.

This cross-sectional study of 1,085 long COVID patients in India at 2.5 years post-infection compared neuropsychiatric manifestations between those with prior severe (hospitalized) vs. mild disease. The study found that post-hospitalization patients were older with more cardiac symptoms, while non-hospitalized patients had more fatigue, and overall cognitive dysfunction (4.9%), stress (10.4%), anxiety (12.7%), and depression (9.2%) were prevalent without significant differences between groups.

Cross-sectional study examining serum cytokine profiles and inflammatory markers in 227 post-COVID-19 patients 6-12 months post-hospitalization, comparing symptomatic groups with controls. Findings show distinct inflammatory signatures associated with different long COVID phenotypes and reduced muscle function, particularly in males.

A cross-sectional study assessing nutritional status and body composition in 144 post-acute COVID-19 patients referred to rehabilitation after hospital discharge. Found high prevalence of malnutrition (18-21%), low muscle mass, and dynapenia, particularly in bedridden patients, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 178 hospitalized COVID-19 patients examining neuropsychiatric symptoms at 3 months post-infection using structural equation modeling. Found associations between pre-health conditions, cognition, and addiction with post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms including pain, fatigue, and autonomic dysfunction.

A cross-sectional study of 834 cancer inpatients examining the association between baseline nutritional status and post-COVID-19 syndrome risk. The study found that poor nutritional status (high NRS score) was associated with significantly higher prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome (32.7% vs 19.5%), but this is an observational analysis without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines exercise capacity, quality of life, and clinical parameters in 29 pediatric post-COVID patients (mean 210 days post-infection). Patients show reduced exercise capacity (76.6% VO2peak predicted) and increased symptoms like shortness of breath and concentration difficulties, but quality of life remains relatively preserved and is not significantly affected by exercise capacity status.

This cross-sectional study investigates predictors of orthostatic intolerance in 85 long COVID patients using active stand and tilt tests. The study finds orthostatic intolerance associated with higher initial heart rate response but does not identify or test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between extracellular-to-total body water ratio, cardiorespiratory fitness, and muscular fitness in 71 older adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome. Found higher ECW/TBW ratio was associated with lower cardiorespiratory fitness and greater comorbidity burden, but not with muscular fitness.

Cross-sectional study of 72 mild-to-moderate COVID-19 survivors assessing cognitive outcomes via remote testing. Found 40% had objective cognitive impairment, particularly in executive functioning, with younger age and increased symptom burden associated with worse cognition.

This cross-sectional study characterized neurocognitive deficits in 282 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients compared to 52 healthy controls using cognitive testing. Patients showed significant impairments in delayed verbal memory, attention, and executive functioning, with hospitalization, fatigue, and age identified as clinical predictors.

Cross-sectional study of 147 long COVID patients assessing associations between anxiety, headache, insomnia, and quality of life using SF-36 and standardized symptom scales. Found that sleep disorders, headache, and anxiety were independently associated with poorer QoL across multiple domains, particularly Vitality and Mental Health.

Cross-sectional study of 861 individuals recovering from COVID-19 examining the relationships between sleep quality, anxiety, depression, and fear of progression. Anxiety and depression mediated the association between poor sleep quality and fear of progression, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 379 individuals with self-reported long COVID examining associations between physical activity levels and perceived physical/mental health. Higher PA levels were associated with better perceived physical health and lower symptom burden, but the study is observational without intervention assignment and therefore does not evaluate a specific treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 265 non-hospitalized long COVID patients at an outpatient clinic assessing prevalence of cognitive and psychological symptoms (anxiety, depression, PTSS) and identifying risk factors. Found 40% high anxiety, 43% high depression, 31% high PTSS, and 79% reporting cognitive symptoms, with physical symptoms and catastrophizing as risk factors.

Cross-sectional study examining psychosocial, inflammatory, and dopaminergic pathways in COVID-19 survivors experiencing persistent sequelae. No treatment intervention tested; observational assessment of associations between PTSS, rumination, and quality of life outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining sleep quality, insomnia, and self-esteem in parents and children affected by pediatric long COVID using questionnaires. Finds parents with persistent symptoms report poorer sleep and higher insomnia, while children experience sleep difficulties and psychosocial burden.

Cross-sectional study of 61 long COVID patients over 60 years old examining psychological distress and its associations with temperament and emotional dysregulation using validated questionnaires (K10, TEMPS-A, DERS). Found that patients with high psychological distress had higher cyclothymic temperament and impaired emotional regulation, suggesting psychological sequelae are associated with specific affective and regulatory phenotypes in older long COVID survivors.

This cross-sectional study compared cardiopulmonary function in long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea versus non-dyspneic COVID-19 recovered individuals and healthy controls. The findings show that persistent dyspnea in long COVID is not associated with measurable cardiopulmonary impairment or exercise intolerance, suggesting dyspnea management interventions may be more appropriate than cardiopulmonary-focused treatments.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive deficits in 141 long COVID patients with persistent neurological symptoms (>3 months post-infection) and correlating findings with APOE genotypes. Cognitive impairment was more frequent in hospitalized patients and those with lower education, but was not associated with APOE polymorphisms; depression was a recurrent comorbidity.

Cross-sectional observational study of 574 COVID-19 survivors at 6-month follow-up assessing prevalence of PTSD symptoms and their relationship with quality of life. Found 77.9% reported at least one persistent symptom (fatigue most common) and 11.15% met PTSD criteria; no intervention or treatment was tested.

Population-based cross-sectional survey in China examining associations between long COVID symptomology, perceived symptom burden, and mental health outcomes in 25% of COVID-19 patients experiencing prolonged symptoms. Found significant positive associations between long COVID symptomology and depression/anxiety, and between perceived symptom burden and depression/anxiety/stress.

This cross-sectional study compared sleep quality in 70 older adults with post-COVID syndrome (6+ months post-infection) versus 153 controls using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. While no significant difference in poor sleep quality was found between groups (52.9% vs 43.8%), psychosocial factors and pre-existing conditions (anxiety, polypharmacy, joint disease, glucose intolerance) were stronger predictors of poor sleep than SARS-CoV-2 infection itself.

Cross-sectional study of 75 post-COVID-19 patients assessing the prevalence and characteristics of anxiety and PTSD symptoms using validated questionnaires (GAD-7 and PCL-5). Found clinically significant anxiety in 31% and PTSD in 29% of participants, with high comorbidity between these conditions and depression/fatigue.

Cross-sectional study investigating taste and smell loss in 104 COVID-19 healthcare workers and associated psychological distress. While the paper acknowledges that these dysfunctions can persist post-recovery, it is an observational study without any treatment or intervention—it merely surveys symptoms and psychological impact without testing any therapeutic approach.

Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life (SF-36) in long COVID patients versus healthy controls using an online survey. Found significantly lower QOL scores in long COVID patients across multiple domains, but this is an observational assessment study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study of 246 hospitalized COVID-19 patients assessing prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) and its impact on quality of life. Found 76% prevalence of PCS with common symptoms including cognitive impairment, dyspnea, and fatigue, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective cohort study examining the prevalence and impact of long COVID among 3,250 participants in Bangladesh, with focus on co-prevalence with cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Study documents symptom patterns and mortality outcomes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms among 481 previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh, six months after discharge. Found 45% reported mental health symptoms, with higher rates among women and those experiencing socioeconomic changes.

Cross-sectional population survey of 2,063 Saudi Arabians assessing prevalence of post-COVID fatigue and health-related quality of life. Found 52% prevalence of fatigue and identified female gender, higher education, pre-existing chronic disease, and acute respiratory symptoms as independent predictors, but did not test or evaluate any intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed mental health and cognitive functioning in 376 COVID-19 survivors from three hospitals in India, comparing 99 patients with 31 matched controls using standardized cognitive and mental health assessments. Results showed COVID-19 survivors had significantly elevated rates of depression (91% increased risk), anxiety (68%), and insomnia (140%), with depression and anxiety strongly associated with cognitive decline and mild cognitive impairment.

This cross-sectional study measured health-related quality of life in 547 post-COVID-19 patients using the EQ5D-3L questionnaire at a mean of 287 days post-infection, comparing results to normative population data and chronic pain patients. The study found that post-COVID patients reported significantly impaired quality of life (mean EQ5D-3L index: 0.57), with 89.6% experiencing pain/discomfort and 82.5% reporting activity limitations, though quality of life appeared better than in chronic pain surgery patients.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,056 non-hospitalized COVID-19 survivors assessing insomnia prevalence and associations with depression and anxiety. Found 76.1% prevalence of insomnia with significant associations to depressive and anxiety symptoms, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional survey examining prevalence of depression symptoms among individuals with self-reported SARS-CoV-2 infection in China (n=2,726). While the study mentions COVID-19 symptoms lasting >13 days, it does not focus on long COVID specifically and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 172 recovered COVID-19 inpatients from Jakarta examining the prevalence and impact of long COVID symptoms on health-related quality of life domains using WHOQOL-BREF. Found 30.2% had long COVID symptoms with significant negative effects on most quality-of-life domains, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional survey of 184 post-COVID patients examines personal resources, organizational support, and care pathways that facilitate return to work. The study finds that coping ability and workplace structural modifications are the strongest predictors of successful work reintegration, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines gender differences in symptomatology and quality of life among 206 Spanish long COVID patients using an online questionnaire. While the study confirms long COVID affects both genders with similar symptom profiles, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated long-term gastrointestinal symptoms and sleep quality in Chinese adolescents following COVID-19 infection using standardized questionnaires (GSRS and PSQI). The study found that GI symptoms increased by 11.86% and sleep quality decreased by 10.9% post-infection, with female sex, older age, and higher education identified as risk factors, though symptoms gradually improved over time.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,828 US adults examining awareness of long COVID and receipt of medical care across racial and ethnic groups. Found that 62.5% had heard of long COVID, with significantly lower awareness among Black and Hispanic respondents, and only 26.8% of those with long COVID symptoms received medical care.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,510 participants examining the prevalence of musculoskeletal pain after COVID-19 infection and associated factors. Found 42.6% exhibited musculoskeletal pain post-COVID, with education level and concomitant symptoms as risk factors, while exercise duration and stress scores were protective.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between spiritual health and quality of life in 475 COVID-19 patients with long-term complications in Iran. Found that patients with complications had significantly lower spiritual well-being and quality of life scores, with positive correlation between spiritual health and quality of life outcomes.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 368 COVID-19 confirmed cases in Qatar during 2022 to determine the prevalence and predictors of post-COVID-19 syndrome. Female gender, lack of social support, and obesity were significant predictors of PCS, with fatigue, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms being most commonly reported; however, this is an observational epidemiological study with no treatment intervention.

Community-based cross-sectional survey of 1,485 Chinese residents examining the prevalence of post-COVID persistent symptoms and associations with reinfection. Found that 89.1% of previously infected participants reported ongoing symptoms, with reinfection associated with higher odds of headaches, smell/taste changes, sleep impairment, and brain fog.

This cross-sectional study examined cognitive performance and psychological factors (anxiety, social support) in 227 Peruvian adults with varying COVID-19 symptom histories. The paper identifies associations between anxiety, social cognition, and cognitive outcomes but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 364 long COVID patients in the Brazilian Amazon examines factors associated with access to healthcare services, finding that only 45.88% received treatment. The study identifies symptom severity and pre-existing chronic disease as key factors determining healthcare access, rather than demographic or socioeconomic variables.

This paper describes a national virtual clinic project in Saudi Arabia that assessed the frequency and types of post-COVID conditions in 5,913 recovered COVID-19 patients at least 4 weeks after infection. While it provides epidemiological data on post-COVID symptom prevalence and identifies risk factors, it is an observational cross-sectional survey without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study of 5,735 adults in rural Indonesia examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status, vaccine type, and long COVID prevalence. While the paper addresses long COVID, it is observational without testing or evaluating any treatment intervention—vaccination status is assessed as a risk factor rather than an assigned treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,511 individuals with tinnitus examining associations between tinnitus onset and COVID-19 infection, long COVID, or vaccination. Findings show tinnitus severity is higher in COVID-associated groups compared to pre-existing tinnitus, with depression/anxiety as key predictors, but no intervention or treatment is tested.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between long COVID and burnout, anxiety, and depression among US healthcare workers using survey data from 1,678 respondents. Found that long COVID was significantly associated with higher burnout, anxiety, and depression scores compared to those without long COVID.

Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional community survey examining prevalence and risk factors for long COVID in 168 households (14,769 weighted total) in Houston, Texas. Identifies symptom severity, comorbidities (heart disease, asthma), and acute symptoms (anxiety, chest pain, palpitations) as significant risk factors for long COVID development, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System examined associations between post-COVID-19 condition and risk factors (physical inactivity, vaccination status, non-communicable diseases) among 27,074 U.S. adults reporting long COVID symptoms. The study found that adults with low physical activity, incomplete vaccination, and chronic conditions had significantly higher odds of reporting post-COVID-19 condition, but did not test or evaluate any treatment interventions.

A cross-sectional survey examining post-COVID-19 complications and management patterns among 659 participants treated in hospitals versus home settings in Bangladesh. The study documents differences in recovery time and complication rates (fatigue, chest pain, digestive disorders) between treatment settings but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between sociodemographic, medical, psychiatric, and neuropsychological factors and employment status in 59 post-COVID-19 individuals months after acute illness. The findings show that those who took time off work experienced significant physical, psychiatric, and neurocognitive burden, though occupational impairment appeared to reflect subjective rather than objective cognitive deficits.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the construct validity of three different administration methods of the Danish Post-COVID-19 Functional Status (PCFS) scale in 437 long COVID patients. The study found that none of the three methods effectively captured work-related functional limitations, with only 50-54% of patients on sick leave meeting the expected PCFS severity threshold.

A cross-sectional study of 409 people in Bangladesh assessing rehabilitation needs for post-COVID syndrome (PCS) using the C-YRS scale. Found fatigue (34.3%), muscle pain (20%), and dyspnea (12.2%) as most common symptoms, with strong correlation between symptom severity and functional impairment, suggesting potential for severity-based stratification in rehabilitation planning.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence and severity of PTSD, anxiety, depression, and fear in 227 COVID-19 survivors 3 months post-hospitalization. Finds high prevalence of psychological symptoms (40% PTSD, 38.4% anxiety, 36.6% depression) with significant gender differences, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study characterizes pain profiles in 153 long COVID patients, distinguishing neuropathic from non-neuropathic pain and examining associations with cognitive dysfunction and quality of life. The study is observational without any intervention or treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for the treatment trial extraction pipeline.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing physical and cognitive function between 23 post-COVID-19 participants and 23 healthy matched controls using standardized assessment tools. Found significant impairments in physical and cognitive function in post-COVID participants at 4 months post-infection, with moderate-to-high correlations between these impairments and quality of life.

Cross-sectional study comparing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) changes following SARS-CoV-2 infection between Jewish and Arab/Druze populations in Israel up to 12+ months post-infection. Found that HRQoL declined significantly more in the Arab/Druze population after 12 months despite socioeconomic adjustments, suggesting COVID-19 may widen pre-existing health inequalities.

Cross-sectional study examining cerebral vasoreactivity in 49 patients 300 days post-COVID-19 using transcranial Doppler ultrasound and breath-holding tests. Found that long COVID patients had impaired cerebral vasoreactivity and chronic endothelial dysfunction compared to baseline expectations.

Cross-sectional study examining cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging findings in 121 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cardiac symptoms, comparing hospitalized vs non-hospitalized groups. Over half of patients showed non-ischemic cardiac injury on CMR, but this is a diagnostic/observational study with no treatment intervention evaluated.

Cross-sectional study comparing heart rate variability at rest and during active standing in 31 long COVID patients with orthostatic intolerance, 15 infected asymptomatic individuals, and 14 healthy controls. Found reduced resting HRV measures in long COVID patients but preserved physiological response to active standing, suggesting autonomic function recovery over time.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,246 Israeli respondents examining socioeconomic and demographic factors associated with self-reported long-COVID symptom prevalence. Findings show greater long-COVID prevalence among low-income and marginalized groups, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluates oxidative stress markers (d-ROM, BAP, OSI) in 77 long COVID patients and identifies associations with symptoms, inflammatory markers, and thyroid function. Findings suggest oxidative stress markers, particularly OSI, may serve as indicators for long COVID diagnosis and prediction of neurological symptoms like brain fog, with gender-dependent differences.

Cross-sectional study comparing neurovascular coupling and endothelial function between older adults with mild cognitive impairment who had COVID-19 (COV+, N=31) versus those without prior infection (COV-, N=11). Found significantly decreased neurovascular coupling in the prefrontal cortex and reduced endothelial function in the COV+ group, suggesting COVID-19 exacerbates cognitive decline mechanisms.

Cross-sectional study comparing autonomic nervous system function across 758 patients with post-COVID syndrome, chronic fatigue syndrome, and Lyme disease using multiple diagnostic modalities. While it identifies distinct autonomic patterns differentiating these conditions, it does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a diagnostic/characterization study only.

Cross-sectional study of 152 long COVID patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction, examining associations between smell alterations, headache, and cognitive impairment (brain fog). Found that patients with headache or mental clouding had significantly increased risk of severe olfactory loss, supporting neuroinflammatory mechanisms.

A cross-sectional descriptive study of 304 long COVID patients examining symptom clusters and their associations with drug use, stratified by sex. While descriptive of treatment patterns, this is an observational study that does not evaluate the efficacy or outcomes of any specific intervention—it passively documents current medication use in an existing patient population.

A cross-sectional pilot study assessing cognitive functioning, psychological symptoms, and long-COVID complaints in 31 adolescents 3-6 months post-COVID-19 infection using telehealth. Found high prevalence of cognitive difficulties (45% category fluency issues), depression (80.6%), anxiety (61.3%), and long-COVID symptoms (58%), with significant associations between physical symptoms and mental health outcomes.

Cross-sectional study of 1,460 post-COVID-19 patients comparing symptom burden between those with and without depression, finding that depressed patients had higher frequencies of post-COVID symptoms and greater illness burden. The study suggests antipsychotics and mood stabilizers may help reduce burden in post-COVID patients with mixed depression, but this is a clinical observation rather than a treatment evaluation study.

Cross-sectional online survey assessing long COVID prevalence, symptoms, and associated factors among Chinese residents in Canada (n=491). Study found 12.83% reported long COVID and identified associations with multiple reinfections, over-the-counter medicine, and traditional Chinese medicine use.

This retrospective cross-sectional study examines morning serum cortisol levels in 86 long COVID patients from Stanford's Long COVID Clinic, accounting for circadian timing and sleep patterns. Contrary to prior reports, the study found that low cortisol was rare (1.2%), with most patients having normal or elevated levels, suggesting the need for prospective studies to clarify cortisol's utility as a biomarker.

This cross-sectional study characterizes the cognitive profile of 108 long COVID patients 6 months post-infection, stratified by hospitalization severity. Persistent fatigue, anxiety, and depression were associated with worse cognitive function, though no overall cognitive impairment was found relative to illness severity.

Cross-sectional study of 219 long COVID patients examining the association between APOE ε4 polymorphism and cognitive decline symptoms. Found higher prevalence of APOE ε4 allele in patients with cognitive decline (30.8% vs 16.4%) and identified anxiety and sleep disorders as co-occurring factors, but this is an observational/genetic association study without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey investigating associations between pre-pandemic sleep quality, sleep deterioration during the pandemic, and circadian preferences with long COVID symptoms in 384 recovered COVID-19 patients. Found that poor sleep quality, pandemic-related sleep worsening, and extreme chronotypes were significantly associated with long COVID symptoms including fatigue and memory problems, but no intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study of 212 long COVID patients examining associations between demographic factors, clinical characteristics, and neurocognitive complaints six months post-infection. Found that cognitive difficulties are primarily associated with physical symptom burden and education level rather than infection frequency.

This cross-sectional study examined language proficiency across 1,244 children in Hong Kong comparing those with long COVID, recovered from COVID-19, and those with no COVID history. Children with long COVID showed significantly lower language proficiency, particularly in speaking and listening, especially among primary and secondary school students.

Cross-sectional study examining relationships between dysautonomia symptoms and dry-eye disease (DED) in 162 long-COVID veterans using standardized questionnaires and autonomic testing. Finds strong associations between pupillomotor/secretomotor symptoms and DED, and between blood pressure variability and ocular pain, suggesting autonomic dysfunction relates to ocular manifestations in long-COVID.

Cross-sectional survey of 396 Italian children investigating prevalence, symptoms, and risk factors for long COVID syndrome. Found 25% prevalence and identified specific comorbidities (allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, respiratory/gastrointestinal/rheumatologic disease) and acute-phase symptoms as risk factors, but this is an observational study with no treatment evaluation.

This cross-sectional study investigates social stigma experienced by children with Long COVID using an online survey administered at a pediatric post-COVID clinic. Children diagnosed with Long COVID reported significantly higher stigma across multiple dimensions (embarrassment, social judgment, perceived dishonesty) compared to children who recovered from COVID-19.

Cross-sectional survey comparing neuropsychological symptoms and quality of life in 396 COVID-19 patients (99 with long COVID) versus 111 healthy controls in Italian children. Long COVID patients showed higher rates of fatigue, emotional instability, pain, and mood disturbance compared to non-long-COVID patients, but this is a survey study without treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study comparing cognitive performance in 109 post-COVID patients versus 38 controls using psychophysical tests (2AFC and SRT) and EEG metrics. Severe-COVID patients showed significant deficits in decision-making, visual sensitivity, and information processing speed compared to mild-moderate cases and healthy controls.

Cross-sectional survey of 377 Saudi Arabian adults examining prevalence and predictors of parosmia and phantosmia following COVID-19. Found over 60% experienced negative quality of life impact from smell/taste distortions, but no significant demographic or clinical predictors identified.

This cross-sectional study compared physical function, exercise capacity, and muscle strength between 115 paediatric post-COVID-19 condition (PPCC) patients and 227 healthy controls. While PPCC patients showed significant impairments in physical function and daily activities, this is a descriptive study without treatment intervention or control group assignment, so it does not meet the criteria for a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional survey of 204 UK adults examining relationships between persistent COVID-19 symptoms, psychological flexibility, and mental health outcomes in people with and without chronic pain. Found that people with persistent pain experience more symptoms and poorer mental health, with psychological inflexibility associated with worse mental health outcomes, but no evidence of psychological flexibility buffering this relationship.
