Cross-sectional assessment of fatigue in Italian COVID-19 survivors using the Fatigue Assessment Scale at two timepoints post-discharge. Finds females experience more persistent fatigue than males, with initial prevalence of physical over mental fatigue.

Cross-sectional survey of 706 healthcare workers in four African countries assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition using WHO case definition. Found 58.8% prevalence of PCC with common symptoms including headache, fatigue, and muscle pain, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional survey of 755 adults in Jordan and Kuwait examines the association between endorsement of COVID-19 conspiracy theories and self-reported long COVID symptoms. The study finds that participants with high conspiracy theory scores are significantly more likely to report long COVID symptoms, along with sociodemographic predictors like female sex and lower household income.

Cross-sectional retrospective study characterizing neuropsychological outcomes and cognitive performance in 84 PASC patients referred for evaluation across four sites (USA and Germany). Finds mild cognitive deficits primarily in processing speed and executive function, with mood symptoms and fatigue being more frequent than objective cognitive impairment.

Cross-sectional survey of 285 Mauritian COVID-19 survivors examining prevalence of long COVID using WHO and NICE/SIGN/RCGP definitions, with assessment of associated symptoms and quality-of-life impacts. Study found 64.2% prevalence of long COVID, with fatigue being the most common symptom and strongest predictor of physical quality-of-life decline.

Cross-sectional study of 305 university students examining associations between time since COVID-19 infection, disease severity, sex, and mental health outcomes using the SCL-90-R questionnaire. Found that female sex, longer time since infection, and greater disease severity were significantly associated with mental health issues.

This study analyzes 2022 MEPS survey data to examine associations between long COVID and decreased quality of life and increased mental disability among US adults. The findings show that long COVID patients report 3-4% lower QoL and 26% higher mental disability scores, but the study is a secondary analysis of existing survey data without an intervention component.

This cross-sectional study analyzes data from the 2023 Census Household Pulse Survey to examine the association between long COVID and severe cognitive limitations among U.S. adults. Adults with long COVID were significantly more likely to report severe cognitive limitations (13.1% vs. 4.1%, aOR = 1.64) compared to those without COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing cardiorespiratory and musculoskeletal function between post-COVID-19 patients (stratified by time since infection) and healthy controls using standardized performance tests. Found that patients 6-12 months post-infection showed significantly reduced handgrip strength, shorter 6-minute walk distance, and higher physiological stress responses compared to those within 6 months and healthy controls.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the feasibility of the 30-second sit-to-stand test administered via telehealth in 79 non-hospitalized long COVID patients and its relationship to persistent symptoms. The test was feasible and safe, with lower performance correlating significantly with greater fatigue, dyspnea, pain, and functional impairment.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and risk factors for functional dependence in 987 Brazilian adults one year after COVID-19 infection. Found 5.0% prevalence of functional dependence associated with factors including long COVID, ICU admission, invasive ventilation, and multimorbidity.

This cross-sectional study of 146 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID pain used network analysis to examine associations between demographic, sensory, psychological, and other variables. The findings support a model of post-COVID pain as a nociplastic condition with connections between sensitization, neuropathic symptoms, and psychological factors, with gender as a key factor.

This cross-sectional study measured arterial stiffness using photoplethysmography in 225 Polish patients recovering from COVID-19 hospitalization, comparing stiffness indices across acute phase severity and time elapsed since infection. The study found no significant differences in arterial stiffness by acute COVID-19 severity or time since disease onset, with age, sex, time from disease onset, and diabetes identified as key determinants of arterial stiffness.

This prospective cross-sectional study compared retinal structural and vascular parameters using OCT and OCTA imaging between young adults with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection (≥180 days post-infection) and healthy controls. The study found no clinically significant ophthalmological differences between groups, concluding that young, otherwise healthy individuals recover from mild COVID-19 with no lasting eye-related sequelae.

This cross-sectional study compares clinical and pathophysiological characteristics of ME/CFS and post-COVID syndrome in Russian populations, examining immune dysfunction, autonomic nervous system dysfunction, and microcirculation patterns. The study finds that 75% of post-COVID patients meet ME/CFS criteria and show more pronounced postural orthostatic tachycardia and similar microcirculation abnormalities compared to healthy controls.

This cross-sectional study measured circulating autoantibodies against neuronal and CNS autoantigens in 169 COVID-19 patients versus 77 controls to investigate autoimmune mechanisms in long COVID. The paper documents dysregulated autoantibody levels correlating with disease severity but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Observational cross-sectional study examining cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) findings in 85 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cardiovascular symptoms. Found non-ischemic myocardial injury in 78.8% of patients and identified pericardial effusion, irregular heartbeat, and prolonged cardiovascular symptoms as independent predictors of lower quality of life.

A descriptive cross-sectional study comparing corneal confocal microscopy findings in 60 long COVID patients versus 28 controls, measuring corneal nerve parameters and dendritic cell density. The study demonstrates neuroinflammatory findings (reduced nerve density, increased dendritic cells, microneuromas) in long COVID patients but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study evaluating pulmonary function, exercise tolerance, and muscle strength in 153 healthy military personnel infected with SARS-CoV-2 at different time periods. Found that those infected during earlier waves (March 2020–August 2021) had greater impairments in FVC, FEV1, DLco, 6-minute walk distance, and sit-to-stand performance compared to those infected later (September 2021–October 2022).

This cross-sectional study compared electrocardiographic abnormalities (abnormal P-wave axis) between 252 recovered COVID-19 patients stratified by disease severity and 251 healthy controls. The study found that recovery from severe COVID-19 was an independent predictor of abnormal P-wave axis, but it is observational without intervention and thus ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

Retrospective cross-sectional study comparing autonomic nervous system profiles in POTS patients with syncope, chronic fatigue syndrome, and post-COVID-19 syndrome using tilt testing and heart rate variability analysis. Identifies distinct autonomic dysfunction patterns across disease contexts but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing structural and hormonal characteristics in 75 post-COVID-19 women versus 75 uninfected controls. Found higher rates of structural pelvic abnormalities (53.5% vs 12.0%), elevated ferritin/estradiol/fibrinogen, and altered TSH/AMH levels in the post-COVID group, suggesting endocrine disruption and persistent inflammation.

A cross-sectional survey of 7,520 SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals in Saudi Arabia examining the prevalence and risk factors of post-COVID-19 conditions. The study found 36% prevalence of long-term complications and identified female sex, older age, chronic comorbidities, and hospitalization as significant risk factors, but did not test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study evaluating health-related quality of life in patients with CHF and/or COPD three months after COVID-19 hospitalization using EQ-5D and KCCQ questionnaires. While the study measures post-COVID recovery, it focuses on pre-existing chronic conditions (CHF, COPD) rather than long COVID-specific persistent symptoms, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between resilience, social support, and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, quality of life) in post-COVID-19 patients. Finds that resilience and social support are protective factors reducing anxiety and depression and improving quality of life, but does not test an intervention.

Survey of 340 New Zealand university students examining dietary changes following COVID-19 infection, with focus on chemosensory alterations (taste/smell) and their impact on eating behavior. Study found ~25% reported sensory changes and higher protein/sodium consumption post-COVID, but is an observational cross-sectional survey without treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing psychological, social, and quality-of-life outcomes in 1,097 Italian long COVID patients using SF-12 and Hikikomori scales. No intervention or treatment was tested; the study documents symptom prevalence and psychosocial consequences without evaluating any therapeutic intervention.

summary: Cross-sectional study of 727 long COVID patients with parosmia (distorted smell) examining food triggers and the relationship between smell distortion and disgust. Study found strong correlation between distortion strength and disgust, with 84% of distorted items described as unpleasant, demonstrating significant impacts on eating behaviors and quality of life.

Cross-sectional study of 2,846 patients examining the relationship between hyperventilation syndrome (HVS) and history of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found increased occurrence of HVS in COVID-19 survivors who were not hospitalized (aOR=1.93), suggesting HVS may be associated with post-COVID symptoms.

Cross-sectional study assessing psychological distress (depression, anxiety, stress, PTSD) in 250 patients recovering from acute COVID-19 in Pakistan within one month of treatment. While it documents mental health outcomes post-infection, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID as a distinct condition (post-infection beyond weeks/months).

This is a cross-sectional observational study describing sociodemographic and clinical characteristics of long COVID patients in Spanish primary care, examining symptomatology by gender, age, and vaccination status. While it provides valuable epidemiologic data on long COVID presentation and symptom prevalence (particularly fatigue in females), it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

Cross-sectional study comparing frailty risk factors in perimenopausal women with long COVID-19, recovered COVID-19 women, and healthy controls. Long COVID group showed significantly higher prevalence of frailty-related factors and greater symptom impact, with strong correlations between COVID-19 disability and frailty variables.

This community-based cross-sectional survey assessed the prevalence, risk factors, and impact of long COVID among 975 South Korean adults aged 19-64 years at 1 and 3 months post-diagnosis. Long COVID prevalence was 19.7-24.9% in females and 12.7% in males, with significant associations with female sex, older age, and underlying diseases; 54.2% of those with long COVID experienced activity limitations.

Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life, fatigue, and physical symptoms in 400 post-COVID-19 patients versus 565 uninfected controls. COVID-19 participants reported significantly higher fatigue scores and lower quality of life on multiple SF-36 domains, with persistent symptoms including weakness, muscle pain, respiratory symptoms, and sensory loss.

Cross-sectional survey comparing long COVID symptom prevalence between 165 previously hospitalized and 165 non-hospitalized individuals in Alberta. Hospitalized individuals reported significantly higher rates of long COVID symptoms (49.1% vs 25.5%) with greater functional limitations.

This descriptive cross-sectional study compares disabling symptoms in currently working long COVID survivors one year post-infection, stratifying by prior hospitalization status (n=465). Previously hospitalized long COVID patients report significantly worse symptom severity, functional disability, and perceived global health compared to non-hospitalized survivors.

An analytical cross-sectional study examining how sociodemographic factors, physical well-being, and functionality influence quality of life and mental health symptoms in long COVID patients. The study identifies age, sex, physical functioning, and disease duration as significant predictors of asthenia, anxiety, and low mood, concluding that better physical independence is protective against mental health complications.

Cross-sectional study of 109 healthcare workers evaluated ~1 year post-COVID-19 to assess health-related quality of life and its association with self-reported dyspnea. Found that 20.2% reported dyspnea, which was significantly associated with reduced quality of life scores and functional impairment.

Cross-sectional survey of 401 Portuguese adolescents examining menstrual cycle changes following COVID-19 infection and/or vaccination. Found significant correlation between menstrual changes and vaccination but not infection, with most common changes being blood clots, darker blood, and irregular cycles.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms 18 months after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection in 370 adults from southern Brazil. Found 66.2% prevalence of long COVID with persistent symptoms including memory loss (42.7%), fatigue (32.2%), and anxiety (23.5%), with higher rates among females, those with lower income, and those with poor sleep quality.

This cross-sectional study examined persistent symptoms in 189 COVID-19 survivors six months post-infection in Egypt and identified associated risk factors. It found that hospitalization during acute infection and female gender were significant risk factors for long COVID, but the study is observational without testing any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among 1,024 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia, finding that 63.8% experienced long COVID symptoms with significantly lower HRQoL scores compared to those without long COVID. The study identified older age, pre-existing conditions, and higher symptom burden as predictors of poor outcomes but did not test any interventions.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 1,530 Chinese adults with prior COVID-19 infection to estimate long COVID prevalence (18.0%) and assess its association with COVID-19-related worries and preventive behaviors. While it identifies long COVID as prevalent and associated with increased anxiety, it does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional analysis using 2022 MEPS data quantifies excess healthcare expenditures associated with long COVID among US adults, finding that those with long COVID have 1.5 times higher total healthcare costs ($4,098 excess) compared to those without COVID. The study is primarily an economic burden assessment without testing any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,002 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh examining treatment patterns, persistent symptoms, and depression. Found 20% experienced persistent symptoms (diarrhea, fatigue most common) and 48% had moderate-to-severe depression, with depression associated with persistent COVID symptoms and other comorbidities.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between food consumption patterns and post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 1,322 Brazilian elderly people. The study found that unhealthy food consumption (sugar-sweetened beverages, sweets) was associated with higher PASC occurrence, while fruit consumption was protective, but this is an observational association study rather than an intervention trial.

Cross-sectional analysis of 2,334 COVID-19 patients in Ghana examining determinants of hospitalization length and long COVID risk. Found that hypertension and diabetes mellitus were associated with longer stays and increased odds of long COVID, while higher education was protective.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,118 medicine students examining prevalence and risk factors for long COVID symptoms, finding 47.5% of previously infected students reported symptoms with anxiety and prior COVID diagnosis as significant risk factors. This is an observational study documenting symptom prevalence and associations, not evaluating any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 250 Italian adults with prior COVID-19 describing sociodemographic, clinical, and symptom profiles of long COVID patients. Found that even young adults without comorbidities experience persistent fatigue, weakness, and muscle/joint pain, with women reporting higher persistent fatigue than men.

Cross-sectional study of 200 long COVID patients at Stanford clinic using comprehensive sleep questionnaires (ASQ, ISI, ESS) to characterize sleep disturbance prevalence and phenotypes. Identified two phenotypic clusters with varying severity of sleep complaints, insomnia, and systemic symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This study examines COVID-19 case trends and health disparities across North Carolina counties, correlating infection rates with demographic factors, income, and social vulnerability to identify populations at risk for long-COVID. It does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, serving instead as an epidemiological analysis of disparities in acute COVID-19 infection patterns.

This population-based study assessed the prevalence of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in COVID-19 patients 1.5-6 months post-infection using survey data from hospitalized and non-hospitalized subjects in Norway. Female sex, being born outside Norway, and dyspnea during COVID-19 were associated with persistent PTSD symptoms, with no significant difference in PTSD prevalence between hospitalized and non-hospitalized groups.

Cross-sectional survey of 316 dental students and faculty in Saudi Arabia assessing COVID-19 prevalence (19.6%), clinical manifestations, and long-term complications. Reports 37.1% of infected personnel developed long COVID, but is a passive epidemiological survey without any treatment intervention or control group.

This cross-sectional study compares physical fitness indicators (handgrip strength, cardiovascular responses, oxygen saturation) between post-COVID-19 survivors and obstructive sleep apnea patients during a 6-minute walking test. The findings show post-COVID-19 patients have reduced muscle strength and lower oxygen saturation compared to OSAS patients, suggesting targeted rehabilitation may be needed.

This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated factors associated with persistent anosmia and ageusia in 808 Saudi COVID-19 patients recruited 14+ days after acute infection. While the paper documents long COVID symptoms, it is an observational study with no treatment intervention—it only characterizes symptom persistence and risk factors, not treatment outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining the occurrence of long-COVID symptoms in 136 male university students aged 18-25, stratified by physical activity levels during distance vs. contact learning. Found that 16-17% had prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, with pandemic impacts on physical activity, weight, and screen time associated with symptom occurrence.

Cross-sectional study estimating the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition in a community setting through a standardized questionnaire of 579 individuals from three primary health care centers. Found an overall prevalence of 14.34%, higher in women than men, with fatigue, smell impairment, and dyspnea as the most frequent persistent symptoms.

This cross-sectional observational study examines autonomic nervous system (ANS) function in young adults after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 infection, comparing those with and without prior infection. The study finds that post-COVID participants show increased sympathetic activity and decreased parasympathetic activity, with these changes modulated by BMI and physical activity levels, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 477 long COVID patients examining the relationship between physical activity levels and LC symptoms. Most participants (74.84%) reported that physical activity worsened their symptoms, and received contradictory PA recommendations from healthcare providers.

Cross-sectional survey of 203 Mexican residents examining the relationship between COVID-19, long COVID syndrome, and mental health disorders using the DASS-21 scale. Found high prevalence of mental health effects in long COVID patients, with significantly elevated rates of severe depression, anxiety, and stress compared to non-COVID controls.

A cross-sectional survey of 2,053 German health workers examining long-term symptoms following COVID-19 infection, with 73% reporting persistent symptoms beyond three months. The study identifies risk factors (age, gender, disease severity) and demonstrates impaired quality of life in affected workers, highlighting rehabilitation needs.

This study analyzed how US state health departments communicated about long COVID on Facebook from 2020-2022, finding that while COVID-19 posts were extensive, long COVID posts were rare (137 out of 49,310). The authors concluded this represents a missed opportunity for health departments to inform the public about long COVID risks and support those affected.

This cross-sectional study assessed self-reported health outcomes in 168 Swedish patients 3 months after COVID-19 hospitalization, examining differences by age, sex, and ICU status. The study found that 72% reported fatigue, 64% respiratory difficulties, and 37% anxiety symptoms, but did not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 62 frontline healthcare workers in South Africa assessing persistent symptoms 2 months post-COVID-19 infection. Study documents prevalence of long COVID symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, sleep difficulties, chest pain, muscle pain, brain fog) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional retrospective survey of 300 non-hospitalized COVID-19 survivors examining the association between brain fog symptoms and quality of life at work across multiple time intervals post-infection. The study identifies brain fog symptoms (memory impairment, multitasking difficulties) as predictors of poor work-related quality of life persisting beyond 12 weeks post-COVID-19.

Cross-sectional study comparing fatigue and cognitive symptoms in 26 long COVID patients recruited from social media support groups to pre-pandemic data from non-fatigued controls and chronic fatigue syndrome patients. While it characterizes long COVID symptom profiles, it is excluded as a secondary analysis comparing to historical control data rather than a primary treatment trial.

Cross-sectional survey of 932 individuals with COVID-19 history examining factors influencing long COVID symptom severity and type. Found that older age and higher BMI significantly correlate with worse symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, and mobility problems, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 6,016 COVID-19 survivors comparing depression and anxiety severity (via PHQ-9 and GAD-7) between those with and without prior psychiatric history. Finds that depression and anxiety are more severe in survivors with psychiatric history, with significant interaction effects between psychiatric history and time since infection.

This cross-sectional study of 77 post-COVID syndrome patients assessed the relationship between occupational status and clinical symptoms including fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, depression, and anxiety. The study found that non-working patients had higher fatigue levels and lower cognitive performance, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and characteristics of long-lasting olfactory dysfunction in 164 hospital workers in Madrid, Spain, during the first COVID-19 wave. While it documents a high prevalence of olfactory loss persisting ~10 weeks post-infection and identifies specific odorants most affected, it is an observational descriptive study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,103 Ecuadorian participants examining long COVID symptom prevalence across different altitudes from April-July 2022. Found 52.3% reported long COVID symptoms, with higher rates in high-altitude residents (71.7% vs 29.3%), predominantly affecting women aged 21-40.

Cross-sectional study of 448 long COVID patients referred to occupational therapy in Denmark, measuring mental fatigue, ADL problems/ability, sick leave, and functional status. Finds 75% experienced moderate-severe mental fatigue, 56% on sick leave, and 94% referred to rehabilitation, but does not test any intervention.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 70 COVID-19 recovered outpatients at three months post-infection to characterize long COVID symptoms and examine correlations with viral load. The analysis identified common persistent symptoms (fatigue, nervousness, anosmia, diet changes) and found a negative correlation between initial viral load and symptom burden, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This prospective real-world data study analyzed factors associated with post/long-COVID using online survey data from 99 individuals, identifying COVID-associated anxiety, hyposmia, heart palpitations, and fatigue as significant predictors of PLC development. The study is observational and does not test any intervention or treatment, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study examines differences in consumer purchasing behavior between individuals with long COVID, recovered COVID-19 patients, and those without COVID-19 exposure. While the paper confirms that long COVID affects consumer behavior (increasing pleasure in purchases but requiring higher trust levels), it is not a treatment/intervention trial and therefore falls outside the scope of the intervention trial screening pipeline.

This exploratory cross-sectional study investigates gender differences in mental health and quality of life outcomes following COVID-19 in 147 participants (83 women, 64 men). Women reported higher rates of anxiety, depression, and neurological complications, with prolonged symptom duration associated with increased anxiety.

Cross-sectional study evaluating hepatic laboratory profiles in 243 long COVID patients up to 20 months post-infection. Found elevated ALT, AST, LDH, GGT, and ferritin levels, with higher ferritin associated with more liver function abnormalities.

This cross-sectional study assessed long COVID prevalence and symptom patterns among 135 Chinese COVID-19 patients using traditional Chinese medicine telemedicine services in Hong Kong, 12 weeks post-infection. The study documents symptom burden and correlations but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing pain characteristics and clinical presentation in 69 long-COVID patients versus recovered COVID-19 patients and healthy controls. Finds that long-COVID patients have significantly greater pain intensity, widespread pain, and reduced quality of life, with frequent pain in neck, legs, and head regions.

Cross-sectional survey of 253 long COVID patients examining associations between social stigma experiences and mental health outcomes including stress, depression, anxiety, and quality of life. Finds that social stigma is significantly related to worse mental health but not physical health-related quality of life after controlling for confounders.

Cross-sectional observational study of 318 Italian healthcare workers examining post-COVID-19 symptoms approximately 2 months after acute infection. Study identifies fatigue, dyspnea, and musculoskeletal pain as most common residual symptoms and associates them with acute illness severity, pre-existing pneumological disease, and high BMI, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey of 330 long COVID patients in Alberta examining their experience accessing rehabilitation and recovery services. Study documents service utilization patterns between hospitalized and non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients, highlighting gaps in multidisciplinary care pathways rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 766 post-COVID-19 patients assessing perceived consequences and factors associated with low life satisfaction. Majority reported physical fatigue, mental fatigue, dizziness, and reduced aerobic capacity, with reduced aerobic capacity and fatigue identified as key factors associated with low life satisfaction.

Cross-sectional study examining depression and generalized anxiety symptoms in COVID-19 survivors versus non-infected controls in Iraqi Kurdistan, with 727 participants assessed using PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scales. Found higher anxiety in infected group and identified risk factors (older age, female gender, unemployment, prior psychiatric history) associated with post-COVID mental health symptoms, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Observational cross-sectional study describing audiometric findings in 47 post-COVID-19 patients with audiological symptoms. Study reports prevalence of ear fullness (74.4%), tinnitus (59.6%), and hearing loss sensation (51.1%) but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey study of 999 COVID-19 patients from UC San Diego Health examining symptom clustering and risk factors for long COVID. Identifies five symptom clusters (GI, MSK, neurocognitive, airway, cardiopulmonary) and their associations with demographics and comorbidities like depression/anxiety, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing long-term quality of life in 923 hospital staff members post-COVID-19 infection using the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire. Found that 63.4% reported persistent symptoms, with obesity, lack of partnership, and low education as independent risk factors for reduced quality of life.

Cross-sectional study of 17,909 patients at an Australian digital mental health service measuring the prevalence of long COVID (10%) and identifying predictors such as older age, female sex, depression, and reduced functional ability. No treatment or intervention was tested; this is a descriptive epidemiological survey only.

This cross-sectional study assessed prevalence of physical impairment and its association with cognitive dysfunction in 292 long COVID patients attending a post-COVID clinic. Physical impairments were common (23-59% prevalence) and weakly to moderately associated with cognitive dysfunction, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

This cross-sectional survey of French hospital staff who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 examines factors associated with delayed return to work, including persistent symptoms lasting >7 days and asthenia. While it identifies long COVID-related symptoms as barriers to work return, it is observational without any treatment intervention—staff naturally recovered or did not.

Cross-sectional study comparing health status and symptoms in 52 non-hospitalized and 75 hospitalized individuals 7-8 months post-COVID-19 infection. Non-hospitalized individuals reported higher fatigue (87%) and anxiety (69%) with lower quality of life, suggesting that post-COVID burden is independent of acute infection severity.

This cross-sectional descriptive study examines the lived experiences and economic impacts of long COVID among 258 North Carolina residents, comparing outcomes between Black and White populations. The study found that while both groups were affected by long COVID, the experiences differed by race, with lower employment continuation rates and perceived family support varying between groups.

Cross-sectional survey of 4,239 Brazilian adults examining anxiety and stress in long COVID using the DASS-21 scale and GAMLSS regression modeling. Identifies sociodemographic and clinical predictors (female gender, chronic diseases, hospitalization) of anxiety and stress symptoms, highlighting the mental health burden of post-COVID syndrome in the Brazilian population.

Cross-sectional retrospective survey of 309 college students examining the relationship between physical activity levels and long COVID symptom severity. Found no association between self-reported physical activity and symptom burden, though physical education students reported fewer symptoms than peers in other programs.

This cross-sectional study of 2,486 marathon runners examines sociodemographic differences in COVID-19 recovery experiences and perceived impact. It documents that older participants, retirees, and those with lower education reported greater COVID-19 impact and longer recovery periods, while younger and college-educated runners showed more complete recovery.

Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary function, respiratory muscle strength, and cardiopulmonary fitness between men and women 30 months post-COVID-19 across five Brazilian sites (n=86). Women exhibited significantly worse respiratory and cardiovascular outcomes, including lower FEV1, MIP, and VO2 peak, with hospitalization duration correlating with impairment severity.

A cross-sectional survey of 416 COVID-19 survivors in Tunisia estimating long COVID prevalence (64%) and its determinants. The study identifies fatigue, myalgia/arthralgia, and cognitive symptoms as most common, with risk associations for acute COVID-19, young women, and central region residence.

Cross-sectional study examining oxidative stress markers (MDA and total hydroperoxide) in 80 Italian workers with previous COVID-19 infection versus 47 healthy controls. Found elevated oxidative damage in post-COVID subjects, with MDA levels showing high specificity (78.7%) for distinguishing long COVID from asymptomatic post-COVID cases, suggesting oxidative stress involvement in long COVID pathogenesis.

Cross-sectional study measuring hemostatic and endothelial proteins in 63 COVID-19 ICU survivors one year post-discharge to assess associations with cardiovascular events. Found that lower levels of coagulation factors and higher von Willebrand factor were associated with cardiovascular complications and elevated NT-proBNP.

Cross-sectional survey of 150 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence, duration, and recovery predictors of smell and taste loss. Most patients recovered within two months, but the study focuses on acute COVID-19 symptom recovery rather than long COVID intervention trials.

Cross-sectional study analyzing type I interferon (IFN-α, IFN-β) and ISG transcripts in working-age adults one year post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to identify biomarkers for long COVID diagnosis and monitoring. Found higher IFN-β levels in hospitalized long COVID patients and elevated IFN-α/IFN-β in non-hospitalized long COVID patients compared to matched non-long COVID controls.

Multi-center cross-sectional study of 1,027 long COVID patients identifying six symptom patterns (cognitive, pain-syndrome, pulmonary, cardiac, anosmia-dysgeusia, headache) and their associations with patient characteristics and disease severity. This is an observational descriptive study that characterizes symptom patterns but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study evaluating the prevalence of post-SARS-CoV-2 telogen effluvium (hair loss) in 31.3% of COVID-19 patients discharged with pneumonia, with higher rates in females (73%) than males (26.7%). The study found no significant associations between alopecia and COVID-19 severity markers but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 113 post-COVID patients examining neuropsychological predictors of fatigue using machine learning models. Found no reliable neuropsychological predictors of cognitive fatigue and concluded that cognitive and fatigue dysfunction have different pathophysiological mechanisms in post-COVID syndrome.

This cross-sectional study assessed exercise tolerance in 80 adults with long COVID using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), finding that 50% did not reach target heart rate thresholds. The study identified predictors of exercise capacity (younger age, longer time since illness) but did not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study evaluating pulmonary function tests and 6-minute walk test performance in 75 post-COVID patients stratified by initial COVID-19 severity. Found mild restrictive spirometric patterns and desaturation during exercise in very severe patients, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study of 147 post-COVID patients undergoing rehabilitation examining the association between headache during acute COVID-19 and anxiety/depression symptoms. Found that 65% experienced headache during COVID-19, and those with headache had significantly higher anxiety and depression scores, with psychological variables mediating 39-68% of headache's effect on quality of life.

Cross-sectional study of 90 COVID-19 survivors assessing the prevalence and characteristics of chronic pain syndromes post-infection. Found 63.3% prevalence of chronic pain, with low back pain being most common, and identified neuropathic pain in 24.4% of patients.

Cross-sectional study comparing aerobic capacity in vaccinated vs unvaccinated individuals 3 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. While it measures long COVID-related outcomes (reduced aerobic capacity), it is a passive observational comparison, not a treatment/intervention trial, and should be excluded as it does not test a therapeutic intervention for long COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study evaluates 296 children post-COVID-19 infection to assess whether allergies correlate with COVID-19 symptoms, particularly anosmia. The study finds a significant relationship between allergies and symptomatic COVID-19 and anosmia, but focuses on acute infection outcomes rather than long COVID sequelae.

This is a descriptive cross-sectional study of Spanish long COVID patients examining the relationship between symptom persistence and functional dependency. The study found that neurological symptoms (headaches, dizziness) and older age were associated with higher dependency status, but it is an observational survey with no intervention—it does not test or evaluate any treatment.

This cross-sectional survey of 1,050 participants >28 days post-SARS-CoV-2 infection investigated associations between pre-infection health status (comorbidities, daily medication) and post-infection symptoms. The study found that pre-infection medication use predicted increased frequency of both acute and persistent symptoms, but comorbidities alone did not predict persistence.

Cross-sectional study comparing breathing patterns at rest and during exercise in 42 long-COVID patients with unexplained dyspnoea versus 40 healthy controls using cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Found that LC patients had abnormal breathing patterns indicative of diaphragmatic fatigue, though this is a diagnostic/mechanistic study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system function between 47 long COVID-19 patients and 42 healthy controls. Patients showed reduced parasympathetic activity (lower HF indices) and elevated inflammatory markers, suggesting autonomic dysfunction is associated with long COVID-19 symptoms.

This cross-sectional study investigates the association between soluble integrin subunits (sITGaM and sITGb2) and long-term pulmonary complications in post-COVID-19 patients by comparing 40 patients with persistent interstitial lung lesions to 40 controls. The study finds that elevated sITGaM and sITGb2 concentrations are significantly associated with pulmonary complications and proposes these as potential biomarkers for predicting post-COVID complications.

Cross-sectional study of 296 COVID-19 survivors in Northern Cyprus examining risk factors for long COVID symptoms at 4-12 weeks and 3+ months post-infection. Identifies female gender, chronic illness, and symptomatic acute infection as risk factors but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This study surveyed 225 patients from the Indiana University Health COVID registry to characterize taste and smell dysfunction in long COVID and COVID reinfection cohorts. It found persistent chemosensory dysfunction in 29-46% of respondents but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional pilot study evaluates indicators of central sensitization in 42 long COVID patients using experimental pain measurements (pressure pain thresholds, temporal summation, conditioned pain modulation) and the Central Sensitization Inventory. The study found central-sensitization-associated symptoms in 64.3% of patients but limited objective evidence of nociceptive processing abnormalities, highlighting discrepancy between patient-reported and experimental pain measurements.

Cross-sectional study of 113 women examining the prevalence and characteristics of menstrual cycle changes after COVID-19 infection. Found that women with more severe COVID-19 symptoms were more likely to report menstrual changes, with symptoms persisting into long COVID; no treatment or intervention was tested.

A cross-sectional study examining health-related quality of life in Spanish adult long COVID patients and the effects of clinical and sociodemographic variables. The study found reduced quality of life overall, with sex, time since infection, and occupational imbalance as significant predictors of worse outcomes.

Cross-sectional study evaluating the association between lung function and coexistence of obesity with dynapenia and sarcopenia in 711 post-COVID-19 hospitalized patients. Found that dynapenia and sarcopenia are associated with significant reductions in pulmonary function, respiratory muscle strength, and peak expiratory flow.

This cross-sectional study describes the prevalence and predictors of opioid and non-opioid analgesic use in 390 post-COVID-19 patients. It is observational/descriptive in nature and does not evaluate the efficacy or outcomes of any specific treatment intervention, so it does not qualify as a treatment trial.

This cross-sectional cluster analysis of 506 long COVID patients identifies three distinct phenotypes (none/mild, moderate, severe) based on symptom profiles and evaluates their associations with general health status and work ability. The study does not test any intervention or treatment, making it ineligible for the clinical trials analysis despite being about long COVID.

Cross-sectional survey of 402 Polish students examining the relationship between long COVID symptoms, physical activity levels, and back pain using IPAQ, ODI, and NDI instruments. Found that students with long COVID reported significantly more cervical and lumbar spine pain, and men without long COVID symptoms were more physically active, but no strong correlations between PA level and back pain severity.

This cross-sectional study compared sensorimotor processing, integration, and motor fitness between 60 collegiate athletes with long COVID and 60 matched controls. The study found that athletes with long COVID exhibit abnormal neurophysiological variables and diminished motor fitness (balance, agility, vertical jump) compared to uninfected peers, but did not test or evaluate any specific intervention.

A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the association between personality profiles (particularly type D personality) and long COVID symptoms in 116 patients from a Post-COVID clinic. The study identifies two personality clusters with different symptom burdens and psychological profiles, but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 402 Polish students examining the relationship between fatigue, Internet addiction, and long COVID symptoms. Found higher fatigue and Internet dependence levels in students with long COVID symptoms, with a positive correlation between dependence and fatigue in this subgroup.

A cross-sectional study documenting the prevalence and characteristics of persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms in 90 Indigenous Zapotec participants from Oaxaca, Mexico, with mean symptom duration of 13.87 months. The study identifies sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with symptom persistence, including age, vaccination status, and blood group, but does not test any intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared heart rate variability and arterial stiffness in 60 elite male athletes with prior COVID-19 infection versus 60 uninfected controls. The study found elite athletes demonstrated cardiovascular resilience post-COVID-19 with only minor vascular differences and maintained cardiac autonomic function.

Cross-sectional study comparing autonomic nervous system function in 440 patients across three groups: chronic fatigue syndrome of unknown etiology, chronic fatigue syndrome secondary to post-COVID-19, and healthy controls. Both chronic fatigue groups showed significant autonomic dysfunction compared to controls, with post-COVID syndrome demonstrating distinct hemodynamic patterns.

Cross-sectional survey of 101 Italian healthcare workers (nurses and social workers) examining compassion fatigue and its relationship to long-term COVID-19 symptoms. Found high rates of mood alteration, headaches, and fatigue, with significantly higher prevalence in workers with long-term COVID compared to those without.

Cross-sectional study comparing fatigue intensity and characteristics across 429 participants with post-COVID condition, fibromyalgia, and multiple sclerosis. Found fatigue was significantly higher in PCC and fibromyalgia vs MS, with distinct profiles in heat sensitivity, mood impact, and recovery from rest.

Cross-sectional study of long COVID prevalence and symptoms among 903 healthcare workers at a Romanian pediatric hospital in 2024. Describes long COVID epidemiology and symptom burden in this occupational population, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 895 Lithuanian participants investigating new comorbidities and medications after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection. While focused on long COVID sequelae, this is an observational study that does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it only documents symptom patterns and medication use in uncontrolled fashion.

This cross-sectional study compared postural balance assessments between 30 post-COVID-19 patients and 30 controls, evaluating five different balance tests (Tinetti, FRT, BBS, TUG, MBESTest). The Tinetti Balance Test was identified as the most effective predictor of functional decline in post-COVID-19 individuals, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational cross-sectional study examined retinal microvascular changes in 104 post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) patients using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and their relationship to cognitive performance. The findings showed that severe PCC cases had reduced retinal vascular density and larger foveal avascular zones, which were associated with cognitive impairment, particularly in executive function and speed processing.

This cross-sectional study examines CT imaging metrics and their association with reduced lung diffusion capacity in 45 post-COVID patients with minimal residual lung lesions. The findings suggest that diffuse vascular and parenchymal changes, beyond alveolar volume reduction, may contribute to persistent diffusion impairment after COVID-19.

This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between anthropometric measurements and retinal vascular caliber in 284 persistent COVID-19 patients. The study found that obesity is associated with increased venous caliber and decreased arterio-venous index, but this is observational research without an intervention—it passively characterizes patients rather than testing a treatment.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome among 265 COVID-19 patients in Oman, finding a 48.5% prevalence with fatigue and joint pain as the most common symptoms. Female gender was identified as a significant independent predictor of post-COVID-19 syndrome development.

Cross-sectional study of 145 COVID-19 survivors assessing quality of life and psychological distress using SF-36 and SCL-90-R questionnaires alongside clinical data. Found that 67.6% reported fatigue and 44.8% reported pain, with physical pain, loss of smell, and female gender associated with poor quality of life.

Cross-sectional study comparing retinal microvasculature imaging (OCT-A) and retinal layer thickness in 40 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients versus 40 healthy controls at ~15 months post-infection. Found no significant differences in vascular or retinal parameters between groups, suggesting absence of long-term retinal damage.

This cross-sectional study compared homocysteine levels, depression, and cognitive function in 62 long COVID patients (≥3 months post-infection) versus 64 controls. Long COVID patients had significantly higher homocysteine levels and lower cognitive scores (MoCA), with a strong negative correlation between homocysteine and cognitive performance.

This cross-sectional survey study examined the prevalence and impact of persistent olfactory and gustatory dysfunctions on quality of life in 431 long COVID patients. While the paper confirms that POD and PGD are frequent long COVID symptoms that significantly reduce mental health-related quality of life, it is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention or control group.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,649 adults in Norway, UK, USA, and Australia examining sociodemographic predictors and health correlates of self-reported long COVID. Found long COVID associated with higher psychological distress, fatigue, and perceived stress, with greater effects in men than women.

Cross-sectional study comparing chemosensory dysfunction (smell, taste, chemesthesis) in 133 long COVID patients vs 75 controls using self-reported and direct psychophysical testing methods. Found significant impairment of all three chemical senses in long COVID patients with moderate to large agreement between assessment methods.

Cross-sectional study of 471 long COVID patients in a rehabilitation program assessing symptom frequency and correlations with sex, disease severity, time since onset, and exercise capacity. Found fatigue and dyspnea are highly prevalent (99.57% and 99.36%), more common in women, do not resolve by 6 months post-onset, and correlate with impaired lung function and reduced exercise tolerance.

This cross-sectional study evaluated 53 long COVID patients previously hospitalized with severe COVID-19 to assess the prevalence and types of cardiac arrhythmias, finding arrhythmias in 41.5% with atrial fibrillation most common. Metformin therapy was inversely associated with arrhythmia occurrence, suggesting a potential protective effect.

A cross-sectional study surveying 549 previously COVID-19 infected individuals in Romania to assess post-COVID-19 syndrome outcomes, risk factors, and symptom prevalence at 3, 6, and 12 months post-infection. While the study documents the epidemiology and burden of long COVID, it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trial extraction pipeline.

This cross-sectional study compared hemodynamic, vascular, and autonomic responses to maximal exercise in 38 young adults with and without long COVID, stratified by sex. The authors found that young physically active adults with long COVID showed preserved cardiovascular and autonomic responses during and after exercise, with no clinically relevant impairments compared to controls.

Cross-sectional study of 215 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia characterizing headache phenotypes using ICHD-3 criteria and assessing impact on quality of life via SF-36. Found 21.4% had poor QoL related to headache, with unemployed status, early headache onset, and high severity predicting worse outcomes—but this is a descriptive epidemiological study, not a treatment trial.

Cross-sectional study examining relationships between brain fog symptoms and diet, sleep quality, mood, and gastrointestinal health in long COVID patients. Found mood and gastrointestinal symptoms were significant predictors of brain fog, while MIND diet adherence showed no significant relationship.

Observational cross-sectional study of 206 outpatients assessing persistence of COVID-19 symptoms and quality of life using SF-36. Finds 73.3% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, headache), with female gender and comorbidities associated with reduced QoL, but no intervention/treatment is evaluated.

Cross-sectional survey of 235 participants examining factors associated with prolonged COVID-19-induced smell loss (>28 days). Found older age and increased illness severity were associated with prolonged recovery, while flossing was associated with rapid recovery.

Cross-sectional survey of 406 long COVID patients comparing quality of life and functional status between those who reported completing rehabilitation (44.8%) and those who did not (55.2%). Rehabilitation status was associated with significantly better outcomes on most SF-36 domains and PCFS scales, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of ME/CFS and post-exertional malaise among 465 long COVID patients using validated questionnaires. Found 58% of participants met ME/CFS case definition, with evidence of both over- and under-diagnosis on self-report.

This cross-sectional study evaluates sarcopenia prevalence and risk factors in 30 post-critical COVID-19 outpatients using ultrasound, bioimpedance analysis, and functional tests. The study identifies ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, and age as predictors of sarcopenia but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining metabolic and laboratory markers in 215 long COVID patients from an Amazon region clinical program. Finds that abnormal metabolic profiles (elevated BMI, triglycerides, HbA1c, ferritin) are more prevalent in patients with worse long COVID presentations and prior hospitalization.

Cross-sectional study comparing muscle strength and fatigue characteristics in 45 post-COVID survivors versus 49 healthy controls using dynamometry. Post-COVID participants showed significantly higher fatigue in extensors/flexors and reduced power output, highlighting the need for rehabilitation considerations.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between Mediterranean Diet adherence and vascular structure/function in 304 long COVID patients. Found that Mediterranean Diet components (olive oil, pulses, fewer pastries) were associated with better vascular outcomes and lower vascular aging measures.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between Mediterranean diet adherence and cardiovascular risk factors/metabolic syndrome in 305 long COVID patients. Higher Mediterranean diet scores were associated with lower uric acid, fewer metabolic syndrome components, smaller waist circumference, and higher HDL cholesterol.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between body composition phenotypes and insulin resistance in 483 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients without diabetes. Found that obesity and dynapenic obesity are significantly associated with insulin resistance, but the study is observational without treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed subjective and objective cognitive impairments in 372 non-hospitalized persons 9 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection using standardized neuropsychological tests. The study found high prevalence of cognitive complaints and test abnormalities but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional case-control study examining associations between serum calprotectin, arterial stiffness, and long COVID symptoms in kidney transplant recipients. The study characterizes long COVID manifestations and identifies calprotectin as a potential biomarker but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined symptom burden, healthcare utilization, and healthcare experiences in 304 non-hospitalized Germans 2 years after SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding that 69.1% had post-COVID-19 syndrome with significant functional limitations. The study identifies gaps in patient information and access to specialized care, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 307 healthy volunteers examining cardiac function and biomarkers in those with prior COVID-19 infection (IgG-SARS positive, n=70) versus negative controls. Found decreased left ventricular filling, increased inflammation markers, and decreased hemoglobin in previously infected participants, but does not study long COVID patients or any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between alcohol consumption and vascular structure/arterial stiffness in 305 adults with persistent COVID. The results show that heavy alcohol use is associated with higher carotid intima-media thickness and carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, suggesting increased cardiovascular risk in this population.

This cross-sectional study evaluated hematological laboratory markers in long COVID patients from a clinical care program in the Amazon region, examining associations with clinical findings and long-term outcomes. The study found persistent changes in blood cell parameters and coagulation markers up to 985 days post-infection, with differences based on symptom severity and disease duration.

Cross-sectional study of 322 COVID-19 hospitalized patients at 2-year follow-up examining prevalence and predictors of long-term working ability impairment (41.6% reported impaired ability). Female sex, diabetes, oxygen during hospitalization, and age were independent predictors of impaired working ability, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 2,226 Vietnamese schoolchildren estimating long COVID prevalence (5.6%) and symptom profile, including cognitive symptoms (memory loss, poor concentration) and fatigue. Study documents impacts on schooling, daily activities, and health service utilization but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing eating behavior, sleep quality, and anxiety levels between 756 adults who had COVID-19 infection versus those who did not during the final phase of social isolation. The COVID-infected group showed higher weight, BMI, anxiety, sleep disorders, and worse sleep quality, with associations between ultra-processed food consumption and worse mental health outcomes.

This case-control study investigates genetic susceptibility to long COVID by comparing 199 long COVID patients with 79 COVID-19 patients without long COVID symptoms to detect associations between ten functional polymorphisms in thrombophilia and immune response genes. The study found that IFNG genotype AA and MTHFR genotype CC were more frequently present in long COVID patients, suggesting a genetic component to long COVID development.

The VAXILONG study surveyed 567 long COVID patients to assess the effect of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination on persistent symptoms. Among 380 vaccinated patients with ongoing symptoms, 52.8% reported a global effect (21.8% improvement, 31% worsening), with no differences by vaccine type and good immunogenicity in seronegative patients.

This cross-sectional online survey of 235 long COVID patients in Bavaria examined the relationship between vaccination status, timing, and symptom severity/functional outcomes assessed at three timepoints. The study found that vaccination prior to infection was associated with lower symptom severity, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

This cross-sectional study of 1,036 patients examines the relationship between autonomic nervous system dysfunction (measured via head-up tilt testing) and serological markers of past/persistent infections in post-COVID syndrome, chronic fatigue syndrome, and Lyme disease. Findings show that antibody status—particularly to HSV-1, HHV-6, Coxiella burnetii, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia—significantly predicts tilt test outcomes and orthostatic intolerance in these post-infectious conditions.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive impairment, anxiety, and depression in university students with and without prior COVID-19 infection using standardized assessment scales (MoCA, PHQ-9, GAD-7). Found that 32.4% of students with COVID-19 history had cognitive impairment compared to 16.8% without COVID-19, with affective symptoms negatively affecting cognitive function.

This cross-sectional study assessed long-term sequelae of COVID-19 in 141 Brazilian patients, identifying symptom patterns across cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological systems. No intervention or treatment was tested; it is an observational epidemiological study examining symptom prevalence and risk factors.

Cross-sectional analysis of 2022 US National Health Interview Survey data examining the association between COVID-19 booster vaccination status and long COVID prevalence among previously infected individuals. Found that booster vaccination was associated with lower odds of moderate/severe symptoms and long COVID, though primary series alone was not protective.

This cross-sectional study examined changes in physical activity levels in 5,829 respondents at one month post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, analyzing determinants including vaccination status, re-infection, and disease severity. While it documents significant PA declines post-infection, it is an observational survey without any treatment intervention and thus excluded from the treatment trial analysis.

Cross-sectional study of 155 long COVID patients in Barcelona assessing prevalence of anxiety, depression, and stress using the DASS-21 scale. Found high rates of severe stress and extremely severe anxiety, with significant differences by age and job role.

This cross-sectional study uses 2022 National Health Interview Survey data (n=27,651) to assess the prevalence of COVID-19 outcomes and associated risk factors among U.S. adults. It identifies high-risk groups for long COVID and evaluates associations between vaccination status and COVID-19 severity, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional analysis of 2022 BRFSS data examines the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and associated factors among U.S. adults, finding that over 21% of those with prior COVID-19 report long COVID symptoms. The study identifies demographic, health, and vaccination-related factors associated with long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional follow-up study of 473 adults from a 2020 COVID-19 outbreak examining long COVID prevalence (28.1%) and the impact of vaccination, particularly booster doses. Booster vaccination reduced long COVID risk by 74% and symptom count by 55%, but the study is a secondary analysis of an existing cohort examining association rather than testing a specific intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 947 Brazilian COVID-19 survivors assessing the prevalence and duration of persistent neurological symptoms after acute infection. Memory impairment was the most persistent symptom, with 39.7% of patients reporting it for over a year, indicating a significant functional impact requiring therapeutic interventions.

Cross-sectional study assessing long-term complications in 91 COVID-19 patients at 2 weeks and 1 month post-discharge, measuring symptom prevalence and pulmonary function. Found persistent fatigue (62.6% at 2 weeks, 35.7% at 1 month) and dyspnea (46.4% at 1 month) as primary symptoms, with significant improvements in spirometry measures but no significant change in 6-minute walk distance.

Cross-sectional descriptive study examining health complications in 67 COVID-19 patients six weeks after hospitalization discharge. Reports prevalence of long-term symptoms including weakness/fatigue (34.4%), cough (13.4%), and dyspnea (8.9%), with correlations between gender, comorbidities, and symptom severity.

This cross-sectional kinanthropometric study examined 536 post-COVID adults in India to assess the relationship between body composition (BMI) and pulmonary function parameters (FVC, FEV₁, SpO₂). Results showed a consistent inverse association between BMI and pulmonary function, particularly in women, suggesting elevated BMI adversely affects post-COVID respiratory recovery.

A retrospective case series of 93 long COVID patients with psychiatric and behavioral disorders hospitalized in Kazakhstan between April 2020 and January 2023. The study characterized clinical presentations and psychopharmacological treatment (antidepressants, neuroleptics, tranquilizers), finding gender differences in symptom prevalence including depression and cognitive impairment in males and anxiety-phobic syndromes in females.

This cross-sectional survey examined menstrual cycle changes in 271 Indonesian adolescents following COVID-19 infection and vaccination. The study found that both post-infection and post-vaccination groups experienced changes in menstrual cycle duration and bleeding patterns, but does not constitute long COVID research as it focuses on acute post-infection/vaccination effects rather than persistent long COVID syndrome.

A cross-sectional survey of 239 women aged 21–35 assessing long-term health effects of COVID-19, including reproductive outcomes and persistent post-COVID symptoms. The study found that 80% reported good pre-COVID health, but most experienced prolonged symptoms (fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, sleep disturbances, hair loss) lasting over 3 months, with 32% experiencing preterm births or miscarriages.

Cross-sectional study comparing medical and social characteristics of 80 women with infertility and long COVID symptoms versus 40 controls without COVID history. Women with infertility and long COVID showed higher stress, lower socioeconomic status, greater fear of COVID-19, and high prevalence of autonomic dysfunction (82.5%) and fatigue.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the role of systemic inflammation and immune markers in neuropsychological disorders among 145 post-COVID-19 patients. Found no significant relationship between standard inflammatory markers and cognitive status, but identified correlations between specific chemokines and fatigue severity.

Cross-sectional survey comparing prevalence and symptoms of post-COVID-19 syndrome among senior university students at two Ukrainian institutions. Study documents high rates of neurological symptoms (headache, memory impairment, insomnia, anxiety, fatigue) and their impact on academic performance, with recommendations for cognitive and physical rehabilitation, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention.

Descriptive cross-sectional study of 90 nurses with long COVID examining psychological impacts including anxiety (32.2%), stress (13.3%), and depression (4.4%). This is an observational study describing symptoms and mental health burden in affected healthcare workers, not evaluating any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study analyzes the frequency and nature of dermatological symptoms in 107 post-COVID-19 patients from Gomel, Russia, using survey data. The study documents various skin manifestations including angiitis, rashes, and urticaria, with severity correlating to initial COVID-19 infection severity, but does not test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey examined oral cavity manifestations in young adults (18-30 years) who had recovered from COVID-19, identifying pathological changes in oral mucosa associated with post-COVID syndrome. The study is excluded because it is purely observational with no treatment intervention—it documents post-COVID dental symptoms without testing or evaluating any therapeutic approach.

Cross-sectional study of 261 Jordanian healthcare students examining musculoskeletal symptoms 3 months after mild-to-moderate COVID-19 infection. Found 21.4% reported musculoskeletal symptoms with fatigue (71.6%), headache (60.9%), and muscle pain (52.5%) most common; females showed significantly higher risk.

Retrospective cross-sectional study examining demographic factors, vaccination status, and PCR test results in 300 hospitalized COVID-19 patients in Semey, Kazakhstan between 2019-2022, including those with post-COVID symptoms lasting >12 weeks. The study characterizes risk factors and vaccination effectiveness but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

Cross-sectional descriptive study examining neuropsychological and cognitive disorders in 46 long COVID patients using standardized cognitive and neuropsychological assessments. Found high prevalence of memory impairment (66%), sleep disorders (63%), fatigue (53%), anxiety (47%), and mild cognitive deficits in calculation and visual-spatial processing.

This cross-sectional study compares spirography indicators in 90 unvaccinated schoolchildren with IgG antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 versus 79 matched controls without antibodies. The study found mild post-COVID obstructive respiratory dysfunction in the exposed group, but it is observational with no intervention tested and thus excluded as it does not study a treatment.

Retrospective descriptive study assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 conditions (PCCs) among 346 health workers in a Thai hospital and their occupational impacts. Found 30.9% prevalence with fatigue, cough, and sleep disturbance as common symptoms; over half reported work impacts including shift modifications and absenteeism.

Cross-sectional study measuring cardiorespiratory fitness levels in 385 COVID-19 survivors in Makassar City using the Six Minute Walk Test. Found that 61.3% of survivors had low cardiorespiratory fitness, with older age, obesity, comorbidities, and acute infection phase associated with worse fitness levels.

A descriptive cross-sectional study of 24 long COVID patients in Indonesia examining clinical signs and symptoms based on immunopathology. Found that headache (36%) and fatigue (24%) were the most common symptoms, with manifestations potentially mediated by immune dysfunction and cytokine storms.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 84 medical faculty and family members in Pakistan who had suffered COVID-19, finding that 60.7% developed post-COVID symptoms including fatigue (48%), muscle pain (19%), and brain fog (13%). The study documents prevalence patterns but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional study assessing knowledge about post-term effects of COVID-19 in vaccinated versus unvaccinated populations. The paper appears to be a research protocol or proposal with objectives and hypotheses but no actual results reported.

This cross-sectional study assessed the incidence and burden of long COVID symptoms among 100+ post-COVID patients in India over 3 months. The majority reported persistent dermatological (hairfall), neurological (memory loss), and musculoskeletal (muscle weakness) symptoms weeks after COVID-19 negativity.

Cross-sectional survey of 100 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID symptoms 6-12 weeks after recovery. Found 87% developed post-COVID symptoms (weakness, body ache, neuropsychiatric), with 47% requiring some treatment, but no intervention trial or controlled comparison.

A cross-sectional observational study examining pulmonary function test abnormalities in post-COVID-19 discharged patients at a single Indian hospital. The study found varying degrees of pulmonary restriction correlated with disease severity, with DLCO/Va ratios significantly reduced in severe cases.

Cross-sectional descriptive study of 101 COVID-19 recovered patients assessing post-COVID symptoms at a tertiary hospital in India. Documents symptom prevalence including fatigue (13.86%), breathlessness (8.91%), and cough (14.85%), but is purely observational with no treatment intervention or control group.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 250 COVID-19 patients in a tertiary hospital in India to characterize post-COVID symptoms and manifestations during recovery. Results showed that 88% of recovered COVID-19 patients experienced various post-COVID symptoms, with fatigue (75%) being most common, along with serious complications including stroke, renal failure, myocarditis, and pulmonary fibrosis.

Cross-sectional study of post-COVID pain prevalence and characteristics in 668 nonhospitalized older adults in China, examining pain subtypes and associations with quality of life, sleep, and mental health. Found 9.4% prevalence of post-COVID pain, with neuropathic pain associated with lower quality of life and higher depression levels.

Cross-sectional study of 100 COVID-19 survivors followed for 2 years to assess short- and long-term post-recovery manifestations using WHO criteria. Found 14% had lingering symptoms beyond 4 weeks, with fatigue, cardiac complications, and neurological issues being most common persistent manifestations.

A cross-sectional study of 250 post-COVID-19 patients examining ENT manifestations and their prevalence following COVID-19 recovery. The study identifies high rates of olfactory dysfunction (47%), nasal blockage (44%), taste loss (38%), and facial pain/swelling (59%) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 52 post-COVID patients examining ophthalmological manifestations and complaints during recovery. Describes prevalence of conditions like cataract, dry eye, and diabetic retinopathy but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional observational study of 200 post-COVID-19 patients examining the prevalence and types of persistent symptoms weeks to months after acute infection recovery. Found fever (48.5%), cough (38%), dyspnea (25.5%), and loss of taste/smell as common persistent manifestations, with recommendations for long-term follow-up and rehabilitation programs.

Cross-sectional study of 390 COVID-19 positive healthcare workers assessing post-viral fatigue syndrome using the Profile of Fatigue Related Symptoms (PFRS) score and its association with inflammatory markers (LDH and CRP). Found 51.54% had post-viral fatigue syndrome, with significant associations between fatigue and elevated inflammatory markers (p < 0.001).

Cross-sectional study comparing plasma galanin and galanin receptor-1 (GalR-1) levels between 90 long-COVID patients and 60 recovered controls using ELISA. Found significantly elevated galanin and GalR-1 levels in long-COVID patients, suggesting these biomarkers may be involved in disease pathology, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment.

Cross-sectional study examining demographic and clinical characteristics of ischemic heart disease patients with COVID-19 in Bangladesh. Compares post-COVID-19 patients with and without IHD but does not study treatment interventions for long COVID.

Cross-sectional study comparing serum Anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibody levels in post-COVID-19 patients with and without ischemic heart disease (IHD). Found significantly higher IgG levels in post-COVID patients with IHD, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional retrospective study of 1,301 COVID-19 patients surveyed in 2022 about persistent symptoms ≥3 months post-infection. Identifies female gender and diabetes mellitus as independent risk factors for long COVID, with myalgia, arthralgia, and back pain as most prevalent symptoms.

Retrospective study of 394 moderate COVID-19 patients in Dubai followed up 3 months post-diagnosis to assess residual symptoms. Found 22.1% reported persistent symptoms including body pain, sleep disturbances, dyspnea, and fatigue, with higher prevalence in ages 31-49 and patients with chronic conditions.

This cross-sectional descriptive study examined the clinical characteristics and factors associated with post-COVID syndrome among 120 healthcare workers at Adam Malik Hospital in Indonesia. The study identified risk factors such as gender, age, vaccination status, and comorbidities, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) and sit-to-stand test performance in 40 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia. Found a significant moderate positive correlation (r=0.515, p=0.001) between MIP and functional performance, suggesting respiratory muscle strength assessment may inform rehabilitation strategies.

This cross-sectional survey evaluated long COVID prevalence, symptoms, and quality of life impact in 521 COVID-19 survivors 3-12 months post-infection. The study found that 81% experienced post-COVID symptoms (primarily fatigue and shortness of breath), with significant reductions in quality of life, and reported that SARS-CoV-2 vaccination improved both quality of life and symptom burden.

This cross-sectional survey examined dental health impacts in 201 participants (134 with COVID-19 history, 65 controls) assessed 9-12 months post-infection using AI/ML analytics. The study found that 90 COVID-19 infected participants (67.3% of infected group) reported oral pain, including conditions like hyperesthesia, grinding teeth, and gum bleeding, with older age and female sex associated with greater severity.

Retrospective analysis of 70 outpatient charts assessing mental health outcomes in COVID-19 patients at primary care level. Found high prevalence of depressive syndrome, PTSD risk, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbances, particularly in those with severe disease and low quality of life.

This cross-sectional study assessed functional limitations and quality of life in 87 COVID-19 survivors at 6 months post-infection using telephone questionnaires. The study found significant negative correlations between functional status and multiple quality-of-life domains, but it does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
