This cross-sectional study analyzed symptom manifestations in 100 mild COVID-19 patients during acute phase and 6-month follow-up, comparing somatic, neurological, and psychoemotional presentations. The study found that patients with mild acute COVID-19 developed pronounced neurological and psychoemotional manifestations during the postcovid period, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 26 long COVID patients from Paraguay assessing fatigue using the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS). The study found that over 2/3 of respondents experienced increased need for rest due to COVID-19, with physical impact being the primary concern while cognitive functions appeared largely unaffected.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 75 COVID-19 recovered patients in Pakistan to characterize persistent post-recovery symptoms and quality of life impact 2-10 months after infection. Fatigue (66.7%), cough (46.7%), and headache (44%) were the most common symptoms, with significant deterioration across physical, psychological, environmental, and social quality-of-life domains.

Cross-sectional study evaluating lung function and quality of life outcomes in 189 severe COVID-19 survivors at 12 months post-hospitalization in Brazil. Finds persistent dyspnea (43%), restrictive ventilatory changes, and impaired quality of life, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 826 Egyptian COVID-19 survivors assessing the prevalence and persistence of xerostomia, taste, and smell disturbances over 3 years. Found high prevalence of oral symptoms (73.6% xerostomia, 67.8% smell disturbances, 54.6% taste alterations) with most symptoms resolving within 1 year, though some persisted up to 3 years and impaired quality of life.

Cross-sectional study examining associations between BMI, depression, and post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (PASC) symptoms in 226 infected nurses in Indonesia. Found depression was associated with increased fatigue risk, but BMI and gender showed no significant associations with PASC symptoms.

This cross-sectional study uses a specialized questionnaire to assess the frequency and severity of sensory system damage (olfactory, auditory, vestibular, voice) in COVID-19 patients across two observation periods (2020-2021 vs 2022-2024). The study documents persistent sensory disorders in a subset of patients, with hearing impairment increasing from 56% to 61% over time and delayed-onset symptoms becoming more common.

This cross-sectional study assessed psychological symptoms (anxiety, depression, insomnia) in 187 Indonesian nurses exposed to COVID-19, using standardized questionnaires (PHQ-9, GAD-7, SCI). About one-third of nurses reported mild to severe anxiety or depression, and 9.1% experienced insomnia, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 165 recovered COVID-19 patients in Baghdad. Found 66.7% prevalence of post-COVID syndrome with fatigue, hair loss, and anosmia being the most common symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This study uses the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status (PCFS) scale to assess functional impairment in 281 long COVID patients compared to 20 recovered controls. Results show long COVID patients have significantly higher PCFS scores (mean 13.34), with 63.35% reporting substantial activity limitations, and functional impairment correlates with initial COVID-19 severity and comorbidities.

This cross-sectional study examined the relationship between self-efficacy and resilience in 107 COVID-19 survivors in Jakarta, finding a significant positive correlation (p=0.023) between the two constructs. The paper is a descriptive observational study measuring psychological outcomes rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining kidney, liver, and lipid dysfunction in Type 2 Diabetes patients at various stages post-COVID-19 recovery compared to controls. While focused on post-COVID organ dysfunction, it is a passive observational study with no treatment intervention and thus excluded from the treatment trials pipeline.

Cross-sectional survey of 385 healthcare workers and 111 controls in Russia comparing clinical features of acute COVID-19 and post-COVID outcomes. Found healthcare workers had significantly higher prevalence of long COVID (77.3% vs 66.7%) and more frequent ARVI-like presentation, with vaccination status significantly influencing acute infection severity.

This cross-sectional study evaluated voluntary breath-holding time in 367 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID respiratory complications, stratified by demographics and lung tissue damage. Results showed significantly reduced breath-holding capacity correlating with severity of lung involvement, independent of age, sex, or comorbidities.

A cross-sectional survey comparing long COVID symptom persistence between 756 vaccinated and unvaccinated patients in Iraq, stratified by infection duration. The study found vaccinated participants reported more long-term symptoms (cough, hair loss, taste loss, dyspnea) compared to unvaccinated participants with similar infection duration.

Cross-sectional analysis of 5,000 COVID-19 survivors across income regions assessing long COVID prevalence, symptom profiles, and healthcare system preparedness. Found 30% reported persistent symptoms with fatigue, cognitive impairment, and dyspnea most common; specialized clinics and rehabilitation were effective interventions with 60% of patients reporting improvement.

Cross-sectional study of 308 Pakistani patients examining associations between COVID-19 vaccination status, medications used, and post-COVID complications through haematological and pathological blood tests. No direct treatment intervention was evaluated; the study passively compared outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients based on retrospective medication use.

Cross-sectional study comparing kidney and thyroid function markers between SARS-CoV-2 exposed and unexposed individuals in Nigeria. Found no significant differences in renal or thyroid function between groups, suggesting full recovery during the acute infection period rather than long-term sequelae.

A cross-sectional survey of 1,039 participants in Duhok, Iraq examining the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID-19 symptoms. The study found 26.7% of infected participants had long COVID-19, with fatigue, hair loss, and olfactory/gustatory dysfunction as the most common manifestations, showing significant correlations with age, gender, comorbidities, and infection duration.

Cross-sectional survey of 90 COVID-19 survivors assessing emotional, cognitive, and behavioral effects and perceptions about the disease from April 2020 to June 2021. Found that most survivors experienced weakness and depression, with some reporting prolonged loss of taste and smell.

A descriptive cross-sectional survey assessing post-COVID symptoms in 249 COVID-19 survivors in Central Vietnam at multiple timepoints (initial survey, 6 months, and 9 months). The study found that 21.2% had persistent symptoms including fatigue, weakness, and cough, but symptoms largely resolved within 6-9 months post-infection.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies and long COVID-19 symptoms in 330 children aged 5-12 years in northern Iraq between October 2022 and April 2023. While 4.6% of seropositive children reported long COVID-19 symptoms, the study is purely observational with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

Cross-sectional observational study of 277 long COVID patients at a tertiary hospital in Thailand examining the prevalence and factors associated with persistent symptoms lasting >4 weeks post-infection. Found 80.9% reported persistent symptoms (dyspnea, insomnia, myalgia most common), with female gender and oxygen therapy as independent risk factors.

Descriptive cross-sectional study of 166 healthcare professionals assessing post-COVID-19 symptoms ≥4 weeks after infection. Reports symptom prevalence (fatigue, cognitive impairment, weakness, functional disability) and associations with risk factors, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Online survey of 900 COVID-19 patients in Korea assessing long-term sequelae ≥6 months post-infection. Found 65.7% experienced long-term sequelae with fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and mood disorders most common; female gender identified as risk factor.

A prospective cross-sectional study examining motor and non-motor progression in 38 Parkinson's disease patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome compared to 20 matched controls without PCS, assessed at baseline and 6 months. The study found significant differences in levodopa equivalent daily dose and UPDRS III scores between groups, with new-onset non-motor symptoms including anosmia, dysgeusia, and skin rashes, but identified no specific prognostic factors for PCS in Parkinson's patients.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and associations of post-COVID-19 symptoms in 212 patients at one month after acute infection. Found 98.11% of patients had at least one persistent symptom, with fatigue, dyspnea, and feverishness most common, and identified demographic/clinical risk factors for symptom development.

Cross-sectional study of 52 post-COVID patients examining correlations between personality traits, emotional intelligence, and COVID-19 severity. Found no significant relationships between psychological variables and infection severity, with only employment status associated with disease severity.

This cross-sectional study compared psychological symptoms, gut microbiome composition, and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels between 114 post-COVID patients and 236 matched controls. Post-COVID individuals showed significantly greater depressive and anxiety symptoms, higher stress levels, and elevated CRP, with CRP emerging as a potential biomarker for post-COVID depression.

Cross-sectional study of 394 COVID-19 survivors in Vietnam examining post-infection symptoms, mental health, and quality of life using standardized scales (DASS-21, EQ-5D-5L). Found 76.4% reported symptoms (fatigue 42.1%, cognitive dysfunction 42.9%), with depression/anxiety/stress in 28.7%, 26.4%, and 20.6% respectively; female sex and QoL issues were significant risk factors.

Cross-sectional survey comparing long COVID prevalence and risk factors between omicron and pre-omicron COVID-19 infection groups across 1,113 respondents. Found significantly lower long COVID rates in omicron group (9% at 6 months vs 28% pre-omicron), with hospitalization and underlying conditions as key risk factors.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (long COVID) in Jordan and identifying associated risk factors among 291 COVID-19 patients. Found 70.4% reported persistent symptoms, with headache, muscle pain, fatigue, and cough most common; female gender and obesity were significant risk factors.

Cross-sectional study of 1,337 COVID-19 survivors assessing clinical features and hemostatic biomarker alterations in long COVID syndrome. Found associations between VTE during acute phase and long COVID development, with elevated thrombomodulin and PAI-1 levels in ongoing symptomatic patients.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and clinical spectrum of post-COVID syndrome in 53 patients with inflammatory rheumatic disease. PCS was observed in 67.9% of patients, with fatigue and weakness being the most common symptoms; no independent risk factors were identified except smoking which showed a protective effect.

This cross-sectional study examined how COVID-19 and post-COVID symptoms affected the mental health and wellbeing of 41 children and adolescents with intellectual disabilities in North Kosovo over a two-year period. The researchers found that severity of COVID-19 symptoms independently predicted mental status deterioration, and that children with ID experienced higher prevalence of both COVID-19 infection and post-COVID sequelae.

A cross-sectional survey of 101 participants assessing the impact of post-COVID syndrome on disability levels using the WHODAS 2.0 instrument. The study found that long COVID causes moderate disability, with brain fog, tiredness, and neuropsychiatric symptoms most prevalent.

Cross-sectional study examining endothelial biomarkers (VCAM-1, ICAM-1, P-selectin, fractalkine) in 345 COVID-19 survivors one year after hospital discharge compared to 119 healthy controls. Found no significant differences in endothelial biomarkers between survivors and controls, suggesting SARS-CoV-2 infection may not impose higher long-term cardiovascular risk despite 39% having post-COVID syndromes.

Retrospective cross-sectional survey of 60% of mild COVID-19 patients in Cape Town reporting ≥1 long COVID symptom two months post-diagnosis, documenting symptom prevalence, work impact, and healthcare-seeking behavior. Study is descriptive/observational with no treatment intervention or control group; excluded as it does not test or evaluate any treatment.

Cross-sectional study assessing mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD, obsessive-compulsive symptoms) in 200 COVID-19 survivors 3-6 months post-infection using validated psychiatric scales. Older survivors (≥50 years) showed significantly higher rates of depression, anxiety, PTSD, and OC symptoms compared to younger survivors.

A cross-sectional study of 361 young adults assessing cognitive state, depression, anxiety, and musculoskeletal pain in those with post-COVID-19 syndrome compared to uninfected controls. While the study confirms higher depression and cognitive impairment in long COVID patients, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 98 COVID-19 survivors 2 years post-discharge assessing psychological, cognitive, and functional outcomes at a tertiary care hospital. The study documents prevalence of anxiety (22.1%), depression (25.3%), and functional disability (60%) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study assessing HPA axis dysfunction in 69 COVID-19 survivors 3 months post-infection using cortisol testing. Found secondary adrenal insufficiency in 13% of patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 123 post-COVID patients in Turkey examining long-term symptoms, respiratory function, and radiological changes after acute COVID-19. The study identifies risk factors for post-COVID syndrome but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 1,370 participants assessing quality of life differences between acute COVID-19, long COVID-19, and non-infected groups using SF-12 questionnaire. Long COVID-19 significantly reduced both physical and mental quality of life compared to acute COVID-19 or uninfected controls.

Cross-sectional study assessing functional status and mental health outcomes in 114 post-COVID-19 patients in Maharashtra, India. The study found significant functional limitations and mental health challenges, with depression being the strongest predictor of delayed recovery, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey assessing quality of life in 213 post-COVID-19 undergraduate students using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire. Found 61.5% reported poor QOL with fatigue (99.6%) and hair loss (92.4%) as most common symptoms; comorbidities associated with worse outcomes.

Cross-sectional study investigating prevalence of long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors among 422 children and adolescents in Vietnam. Found 39.3% reported long COVID symptoms, with higher prevalence in girls, younger children, overweight individuals, and those unvaccinated or with prolonged acute illness.

Cross-sectional survey of 498 college students examining the association between healthy lifestyle factors and post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms including fatigue, anxiety, dyspnea, and depression. Results show significant negative correlation between healthy lifestyle behaviors and symptom severity, suggesting lifestyle modification as a rehabilitation option for long COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study examining vitamin D (25OHD) levels in 84 patients 3-6 months post-COVID-19 infection and their relationship to persistent long COVID symptoms. Found high rates of vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency (80%) but no significant association between vitamin D status and post-COVID symptoms.

Cross-sectional survey of 114 COVID-19 recovered patients examining the prevalence and timing of telogen effluvium (hair loss) as a post-COVID sequela. Found that 72% of patients experienced hair loss, typically appearing 2-3 weeks post-infection, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing corneal endothelial parameters in 129 COVID-recovered patients versus 123 healthy controls using specular microscopy. Found decreased hexagonality and increased cell size in recovered patients, but this is a descriptive comparison of post-infection anatomical changes, not a treatment intervention study.

Cross-sectional study of 647 recovered COVID-19 patients in Northern India to assess prevalence of persistent post-COVID symptoms 3+ months after infection. Found 27.5% had post-COVID symptoms with gender and comorbidity-related differences, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional study compared 31 young adults one month post-mild COVID-19 with 31 healthy controls, measuring heart rate variability, body composition, and persistent symptoms. Findings showed impaired autonomic function (lower rMSSD), increased body fat, and persistent fatigue and dysgeusia in COVID-19 participants, but no intervention or treatment was administered.

Cross-sectional study estimating the prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) in 450 patients from Anand district, India, and identifying associated factors. Found 25.11% PCS prevalence with weakness and breathlessness as common symptoms, associated with hospitalization status and certain medications, but no treatment intervention was tested.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and predictors of fatigue among 142 Thai women after COVID-19 recovery. Found that 39.4% experienced fatigue, with fear, anxiety, and insomnia collectively explaining 47% of variance in fatigue symptoms.

This community-based cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and burden of long COVID among 420 adults in rural Bengaluru, India, finding a 6.4% prevalence with fatigue as the most common symptom. The study identified older age, female gender, and ICU admission during acute infection as risk factors for long COVID but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional study of 938 post-COVID patients in Kerala assessing persisting and new-onset symptoms and functional limitation using the PCFS scale. Found common persistent symptoms (myalgia, fatigue, dyspnea) and new-onset symptoms (shortness of breath, fatigue) with 63.8% showing negligible functional limitation; identified sociodemographic and clinical determinants of functional impairment.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing post-COVID functional status (PCFS) in 80 recovered patients using the PCFS scale. Found 88.75% experienced persistent symptoms (fatigue, anxiety, cough) and comorbidities/vaccination significantly influenced functional outcomes, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study assessed functional limitations and long COVID symptoms in 54 post-COVID individuals using standardized instruments (PCFS scale, Barthel Index). The study found functional decline in 68.52% of participants and long COVID symptoms in 72.22%, with no intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional hospital-based study assessing mental health burden (anxiety, depression, stress, fatigue) among 101 COVID-19 survivors using standardized scales. Finds high prevalence of psychological symptoms but does not study long COVID specifically or test any intervention.

A cross-sectional study assessing disability in 50 COVID-19 survivors (3+ months post-infection) using the WHODAS 2.0 scale. While it documents significant functional impairment in post-COVID patients, it is a descriptive observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

A cross-sectional community survey in rural northern India investigating the prevalence and determinants of long COVID symptoms among 2,954 adults. The study found 23% of COVID-19 infected individuals reported long COVID symptoms, with higher prevalence in females and those with pre-existing morbidities.

This cross-sectional observational study assessed the prevalence of depression and continued symptoms in 273 COVID-19 patients using telephone surveys at immediate and short-term follow-up (3 months post-infection). Findings showed 12.8% developed depression immediately and 5% at 3 months, with depression associated with higher symptom burden and comorbid diabetes.

Cross-sectional survey of 600 home-treated COVID-19 patients in Baghdad assessing prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms. Found 38.5% had persistent symptoms >4 weeks, with fatigue, cough, and anosmia most common; identified age, female sex, and smoking as risk factors.

Cross-sectional study examining latent hyperopia in 271 young adults with mild manifest hyperopia and normal visual acuity, assessing its association with post-COVID asthenopia. Found latent hyperopia present in all participants with significantly higher asthenopia prevalence in those with latent hyperopia ≥ +0.50 D (84.9% vs 49.2%), correlating with screen exposure and near work.

Retrospective cross-sectional study examining long COVID prevalence and symptom patterns in 64 patients with rheumatologic diseases (RA, SLE, and others) compared to the general population. Found long COVID is common in rheumatologic patients with symptom prevalence similar to non-rheumatic populations, though SLE patients showed lower fatigue rates.

Cross-sectional study comparing dental caries prevalence and salivary antioxidant capacity between COVID-19-recovered and non-COVID subjects in an Indian population. Found higher dental caries prevalence and lower salivary TAC in COVID-recovered individuals, suggesting a potential long-term oral health sequela of COVID-19.

Cross-sectional survey of 383 Saudi Arabian COVID-19 survivors assessing prevalence of persistent loss of taste and smell. Found 43.3% reported persistent anosmia/dysgeusia, with 34.3% experiencing permanent changes in taste or smell.

Cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of anxiety, depression, PTSD, and obsessive-compulsive symptoms among 119 COVID-19 survivors in North India using standardized psychiatric scales. Found high prevalence rates (anxiety 44.54%, depression 61.34%, PTSD 25.21%) with older survivors showing more symptoms, but this is an observational assessment study with no treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 508 girls aged 16-24 examining menstrual irregularity during the second wave of COVID-19 in India, finding 29.1% prevalence and associations with depression, stress, and insomnia. The study does not focus on long COVID sequelae and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and determinants of post-COVID-19 syndrome among 300 patients 6+ months post-discharge from a teaching hospital in South India. The study found 21% had at least one persistent symptom (fatigue 11%, dyspnea 7.7%), with ICU admission, age, COPD, and CKD as risk factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 667 post-COVID patients at a district clinic in Kerala documenting the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID manifestations including dyspnea, fatigue, and cough, and identifying risk factors such as age, gender, and severity of acute infection. The study calls for integrated rehabilitation but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 87 long COVID patients one year post-infection assessing neurasthenia, fatigue, and cognitive symptoms using standardized clinical scales. Found that 49.4% met ICD-10 criteria for neurasthenia with fatigue and cognitive difficulties as key persistent symptoms, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of the COMPASS-31 questionnaire for detecting autonomic nervous system dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients (3-6 months post-infection) by comparing 28 long COVID patients with 31 controls using autonomic reflex tests and heart rate variability. The COMPASS-31 score showed fair diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.68) with optimal sensitivity and specificity at a cutoff of 12.5, but this is a diagnostic validation study with no treatment intervention tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 424 medical students assessing prevalence of post-COVID-19 symptoms and associated risk factors. Found 80.7% reported at least one symptom, with headache and cough most common; diabetes, asthma, and vitamin D deficiency were associated with post-COVID syndrome, though associations were not statistically significant.

A cross-sectional study of 133 patients discharged from a COVID hospital assessing the proportion and types of persistent symptoms and functional limitations. Found that 69% of patients reported persistent symptoms (primarily fatigue, weakness, dyspnea), with 56% experiencing functional limitations.

Retrospective cross-sectional study of 35 COVID-19 survivors discharged from a hospital in Karnataka, assessing post-COVID symptoms and patient satisfaction with care. Fatigue and dyspnea were the most common sequelae, with 34.3% of patients reporting symptoms after discharge, but no intervention or treatment was provided or evaluated.

This cross-sectional study examined fatigue and quality of life among 99 elderly COVID-19 survivors (age >50) in India using standardized questionnaires. Findings show positive correlations between age and fatigue, with significant negative impacts of fatigue on overall quality of life.

Cross-sectional study examining ocular manifestations in 105 hospitalized post-COVID-19 patients in India. Found 11.4% developed ocular signs and symptoms including dry eye, subconjunctival hemorrhage, and retinal hemorrhage.

This retrospective cohort study assessed health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using EQ-5D-5L in 107 COVID-19 ICU survivors 6-12 months post-discharge. The study found that ICU survivors had impaired HRQoL (mean utility 0.51), with significantly worse outcomes in patients with comorbidities and longer ICU stays.

Cross-sectional study of 210 recovered COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and patterns of long COVID symptoms over 12 months post-infection. Found common symptoms including fatigue (67.6%), breathlessness (42.8%), and cognitive issues, with elevated inflammatory markers correlating with symptom persistence.

Cross-sectional study examining polypharmacy prevalence in 90 COVID-19 recovered elderly patients (>60 years) with multimorbidities and its association with quality of life and medication adherence. Found high polypharmacy prevalence (94.4%) associated with significantly poorer quality of life and medication adherence, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey evaluated ocular problems in 210 healthcare workers ≥6 months after COVID-19 infection, finding that 60% experienced post-COVID ocular issues, with ocular surface manifestations being most common. The study describes the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID-related eye problems but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey assessing gastrointestinal symptoms in 307 long COVID patients using the GSRS scale, comparing symptom prevalence before, during, and after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found that 86.97% of patients developed new GI symptoms during acute illness, with 12% experiencing persistent GI symptoms at mean follow-up of 20.1 months, primarily abdominal pain, constipation, and reflux.

Cross-sectional survey of 915 Iraqi COVID-19 survivors assessing post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence and its relationships with age, sex, comorbidities, and vaccination status. Found 67.7% reported post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, hair loss, cognitive dysfunction most common), with higher incidence in females, severe acute infection, and comorbid disease; vaccination reduced symptom incidence.

A cross-sectional study of 15 long COVID patients examining the physiological mechanisms underlying exercise intolerance through cardiopulmonary exercise testing, muscle strength assessment, and imaging. The study identifies peripheral skeletal/neural contributions to exercise intolerance but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 206 patients examining prevalence of long COVID symptoms and their association with demographic and clinical risk factors (age, sex, blood group, oxygen levels). Found fatigue and muscle pain most prevalent, with higher rates in females, younger ages (19-29), and specific blood groups, suggesting potential risk stratification factors.

Cross-sectional study measuring tissue creatine levels in long COVID patients using MR spectroscopy, finding significantly reduced creatine concentration in skeletal muscle and brain regions compared to reference populations. This biomarker study characterizes biochemical abnormalities in long COVID without testing any intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of aggression and associated personality factors in 134 COVID-recovered patients in India. Found 17.9% had positive aggression scores, with longer recovery duration and lower agreeableness in the aggression group.

Cross-sectional observational study describing ocular manifestations in 85 COVID-19 survivors attending an eye clinic, finding that 63.5% had at least one ocular sign including conjunctival hyperemia, follicular conjunctivitis, and more serious complications like central serous chorioretinopathy and mucormycosis. Study documents the pattern and prevalence of eye-related long COVID symptoms but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

A multicentric cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of psychological distress (anxiety, depression, PTSD) among 103 moderate-to-critical COVID-19 survivors at 30 and 60 days post-discharge. Found clinically significant anxiety in 21.4% at day 30 declining to 9.5% at day 60, with depression and PTSD showing similar declining patterns.

A cross-sectional study of 86 long COVID patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction, assessing the relationship between smell loss and mental health outcomes using standardized psychological scales. Found significant associations between olfactory dysfunction and increased post-traumatic stress, anxiety, hopelessness, and reduced quality of life.

This cross-sectional study compared balance ability and quality of life between 40 older adults with a history of mild COVID-19 and 40 without COVID-19. Older adults who recovered from mild COVID-19 showed significantly longer timed up and go test duration and reduced quality of life compared to controls.

This cross-sectional study of 694 Thai participants examined the association between short-term PM2.5 exposure and long COVID respiratory symptoms. It found that PM2.5 exposure ≥1 hour/day, urban living, and not wearing masks were associated with increased risk of long COVID respiratory involvement, but the study is observational with no treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 325 post-COVID syndrome patients in Benghazi examining persistent symptoms at least 2 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Fatigue was the most common symptom, followed by loss of taste/smell and cough; age and gender were predictors of PCS severity.

Cross-sectional study of 413 recovered COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia using the Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) to assess persistent post-COVID symptoms. Found that 50% reported persistent symptoms at 4 weeks post-infection, including laryngeal complications, fatigue, and swallowing changes.

This cross-sectional population-based survey assessed persisting chemosensory dysfunction (smell, taste, trigeminal function) in 667 German residents 9.1 months after PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. It found high prevalence of subjective olfactory (45.6%) and gustatory (36.2%) dysfunction, with significant differences in objective olfactory testing compared to healthy controls, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional telephone survey of 133 COVID-19 recovered patients in Italy documents the prevalence of long COVID symptoms 6-12 months post-infection, finding that 58% (77/133) were long-haulers. The study characterizes common symptoms including asthenia, breathlessness, myalgia, psychological disorders, and brain fog but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study examining D-dimer elevation in 322 post-COVID-19 patients, measuring how long elevated levels persist after acute infection. No intervention or treatment was administered; this is a descriptive epidemiological study of biomarker kinetics in the post-COVID period.

This case-control study compared serum tryptase levels between 50 post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS) patients, 37 asymptomatic COVID-19 convalescents, and 46 COVID-negative controls to investigate mast cell activation as a proposed mechanism. The study found no significant differences in tryptase levels among groups, providing evidence against mast cell activation as a key pathogenic factor in PACS.

Cross-sectional analysis of post-COVID interstitial lung disease (ILD) characteristics in 262 long COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms 3+ months post-infection. Identifies risk factors (smoking, severe acute COVID, elevated LDH) and documents spontaneous improvement in 13-20% at 6-month follow-up without specific treatment.

This cross-sectional study compares sleep quality between 243 COVID-19 recovered patients and 132 non-infected controls in the same sociocultural environment. While the paper documents significantly worse sleep disturbances in post-COVID patients (sweating, morning headaches, restlessness, anxiety), it is not a treatment trial—it is purely descriptive/observational with no intervention tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 121 healthcare workers assessing persistent post-COVID symptoms at least 12 weeks after infection. Found that 63% had symptoms lasting >3 weeks, with fatigue (33%), loss of smell (22%), and concentration problems (21%) most common, significantly impacting quality of life.

Cross-sectional survey of 444 patients with subacute/chronic respiratory complaints examining herbal product and dietary supplement use, finding 49.3% used these products with post-COVID syndrome patients significantly more likely to use them. Study did not test or evaluate any treatment interventions, only surveyed existing supplement use patterns.

A cross-sectional survey of vaccinated Maltese adults investigating Long COVID prevalence, clinical characteristics, and associated mental health impacts using standardized anxiety and depression assessment tools. Found 41% reported Long COVID with significantly higher depression and anxiety scores compared to those without persistent symptoms.

Cross-sectional survey of 266 long COVID patients assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) using the EuroQoL 5D-3L scale and its association with symptom type. Female gender, lower education, visual problems, and myalgia were identified as risk factors for reduced HRQoL, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A cross-sectional survey study assessing the prevalence and severity of post-COVID symptoms in individuals who recovered from COVID-19. The study documents common long COVID manifestations including fatigue, respiratory distress, cognitive impairment, anxiety, and depression, and examines their impact on daily life and correlation between physical and mental health consequences.

Cross-sectional study examining mucosal humoral immune responses in 180 healthcare workers during the post-COVID-19 period, comparing those with varying COVID-19 severity history to uninfected controls. Found significant alterations in salivary and respiratory sIgA and IgG levels, with most pronounced changes in workers with severe disease history, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study examined the neuropathic component of chronic musculoskeletal pain in 163 post-COVID-19 patients, finding that 19% had neuropathic pain as assessed by LANSS scoring. The study identified correlations between neuropathic pain and pulmonary involvement, hospitalization history, and pain characteristics, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

An online survey of 381 participants examining whether pre-COVID-19 physical activity status protects against long COVID symptom development. The study found no significant difference in post-COVID health status between those meeting physical activity guidelines and those who did not, suggesting cardiorespiratory fitness does not fully prevent long COVID development.

This cross-sectional study established peak expiratory flow (PEF) reference values in a Peruvian population of 316 healthy adults aged 20-60 years without cardiac or pulmonary pathologies. While the study notes that individuals who recovered from COVID-19 had lower PEF values than those without COVID-19 history, it is primarily a respiratory health assessment study establishing population norms, not a long COVID-focused investigation or treatment trial.

Cross-sectional study of 445 healthcare workers assessing the prevalence and characteristics of long COVID symptoms at a 6-month follow-up in Iran. The study identified a 9.44% prevalence of long COVID, with anxiety and mood disturbances as the most common persistent mental symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study surveying 1,000+ Jordanian COVID-19 survivors about persistent and new symptoms at ≥90 days post-infection. Found high prevalence of smell loss (34.7%), fatigue (34.6%), and taste loss (29.5%), with greater symptom persistence in females and those requiring oxygen therapy, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and determinants of long COVID among COVID-19 survivors in a rural area of Maharashtra, India. Found a 17.5% prevalence of long COVID, with risk factors including elderly age, male sex, severe acute COVID presentation, and history of intubation.

Cross-sectional study of 400 home-treated COVID-19 patients in Baghdad examining prevalence and risk factors for persistent symptoms beyond 4 weeks. Found 30.25% had long-lasting symptoms, with fatigue (23.5%), smell/taste loss (14.75%), and cough (2%) most common; age, smoking, comorbidities, and initial symptom burden significantly associated with symptom duration.

Cross-sectional study evaluating symptom persistence and health-related quality of life in 225 COVID-19 patients at 6 months post-discharge using the EuroQol scale. Most patients (76.9%) showed no symptoms or significant deterioration in quality of life at follow-up.

This cross-sectional survey assessed insomnia and sleep disturbances in medical students who recovered from acute COVID-19, using standardized insomnia severity (ISI) and sleep quality (PSQI) indices. The study found 65% of 117 students had some degree of insomnia and 78.6% reported sleep difficulty, with significant correlations between sleep measures and emotional health.

Cross-sectional study of 160 COVID-19 patients investigating the frequency and severity of telogen effluvium (hair loss) as a post-COVID consequence. Found telogen effluvium in 28.8% of patients with higher frequency in females, but this is a descriptive epidemiological study without any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing endocrine disease prevalence in 724 athletes with prior COVID-19 versus 390 uninfected controls examined in 2021-2022. Found significantly higher rates of hypothyroidism, autoimmune thyroiditis, thyrotoxicosis, and type 1 diabetes in the COVID-19 group, suggesting post-COVID autoimmune endocrine sequelae.

This cross-sectional survey of 121 COVID-19 survivors examined the relationship between taste/smell alterations and post-COVID syndrome, finding 12.4% with persistent olfactory symptoms and 9.1% with persistent gustatory symptoms at 12 months. The study is descriptive epidemiology documenting symptom prevalence and recovery patterns, not a treatment intervention study.

A cross-sectional study assessing quality of life and functional status in 100 post-COVID-19 patients within 6 months of infection using EQ-5D-5L and PCFS scales. The study found high prevalence of mobility limitations (43%), pain/discomfort (65%), and functional impairment (65%), but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study assessed clinical manifestations of post-COVID-19 syndrome in 80 patients using questionnaires and standardized scales for fatigue, dyspnea, and cognitive dysfunction. The study found gender differences in symptom presentation, with men reporting more severe fatigue and women more frequently experiencing headaches, but it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Retrospective cross-sectional study characterizing COVID-19 prevalence and clinical profile among 107 Brazilian farmworkers, with 52% reporting long COVID symptoms (predominantly fatigue and breathlessness). This is an observational epidemiological survey with no treatment intervention tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 539 long COVID patients examining the physical and psychosocial symptom profile to determine if symptoms constitute a defined syndrome. Found high prevalence of persistent symptoms (fatigue 52%, cognitive dysfunction 42%, dyspnea 39%) at 3 and 6 months post-infection, but analyses did not identify a distinct post-COVID syndrome.

Cross-sectional study assessing knowledge, awareness, and attitudes toward post-COVID-19 syndrome among 355 medical students across four Malaysian universities. Study found significant associations between age and knowledge, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.

A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and clinical outcomes of long COVID in 1,600 patients from a large municipality in northeast Brazil. The paper highlights the burden of long COVID on an already overwhelmed healthcare system and provides real-world data on disease prevalence in a low-to-middle-income country context.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 510 residents of Mosul, Iraq to document the prevalence and types of long-term health effects following COVID-19 infection. The study found that COVID-19 caused persistent complications across multiple organ systems, with the highest rates in cardiovascular (67.1% tachycardia), neurological (60.6% chronic headache), and ophthalmological (69.9% blurred vision) domains.

A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence of post-COVID-19 syndrome among 300 recovered COVID-19 patients in Erbil, Iraq, finding 54.67% experienced persistent symptoms. The study examines associations between symptom persistence and factors like disease severity, chronic disease comorbidities, and disease duration, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional survey of 306 people (98 with COVID-19 history) assessed whether post-COVID-19 syndrome (PPCS) symptoms correlate with signs of aging using a 17-item questionnaire. The study found significantly higher frequency of aging signs in post-COVID individuals and developed diagnostic procedures using Bayesian and neural network methods, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing serum IL-6, IL-10, and vitamin D levels in 252 asthmatic and non-asthmatic subjects with and without post-COVID condition. Findings show elevated IL-6 and vitamin D in asthmatics with PCC, with complex correlations between inflammatory markers and vitamin D status.

A cross-sectional study comparing cardiovascular risk factors and metabolic markers in 10 post-COVID patients (1-3 months post-infection) versus 21 controls, all with obesity or metabolic syndrome. The study finds higher cardiovascular risk indicators in the post-COVID group and suggests obesity may accelerate aging post-COVID, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This paper analyzes self-reported long COVID symptoms from 165 Twitter posts to characterize symptom prevalence and patterns in patient-reported experiences. It is a descriptive analysis of social media content rather than a treatment trial or clinical study.

Cross-sectional study assessing quality of life in 44 children with long COVID versus 49 recovered controls using the PedsQL 4.0 questionnaire. Children with long COVID showed significantly lower quality of life scores across physical, emotional, and educational domains compared to fully recovered peers.

Cross-sectional follow-up study of healthcare workers at least 12 weeks post-COVID-19 recovery describing clinical profiles and health outcomes. Found persistent physical symptoms (fatigue 25%, breathlessness 23%, muscle weakness 16%) and mental health issues (depressive symptoms 45%, anxiety 18%) in recovered workers.

A cross-sectional study of 228 COVID-19 recovered individuals identifying post-COVID syndrome symptoms using structured questionnaires. Found that 60.5% experienced moderate symptoms and 28.5% severe symptoms, with fatigue, shortness of breath, cough, and joint pain being most common, persisting for an average of 12 months.

Cross-sectional web-based survey of 1,172 Indian adults comparing neuropsychiatric symptoms (depression, anxiety, PTSD-like symptoms) in COVID-19 survivors versus controls. Found significantly higher rates of depression, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms in post-COVID patients, highlighting the need for mental health interventions in long COVID care.

Cross-sectional study of 125 COVID-19 survivors in Lahore assessing the prevalence and characteristics of chronic fatigue and related symptoms post-COVID. Found 55% experienced chronic fatigue, with strong associations between fatigue and body aches, low energy, and other post-COVID symptoms.

Cross-sectional study assessing right ventricular function via echocardiography in COVID-19 survivors with lung involvement. Found statistically significant differences in RV functional parameters between severe and mild lung involvement groups, but this is a passive observational assessment without any treatment intervention or long COVID focus.

A cross-sectional survey of 341 recovered COVID-19 patients in Baghdad assessed the prevalence and duration of post-COVID-19 symptoms at various timepoints after acute infection. The study found that fatigue (12.3%), cognitive impairment (11.7%), and taste/smell loss (11.4%) were the most common persistent symptoms, with some lasting beyond 12 weeks.

Descriptive cross-sectional analysis of post-COVID-19 syndrome incidence in South Korean Army personnel using a self-completed survey. Study reports 32.9% overall incidence rate with symptom variation by dominant variant, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 218 Italian adolescents examining the relationship between post-pandemic psychological distress (anxiety, depression, stress) and perceived decline in physical activity. Stress, anxiety, and depression were significant predictors of reduced physical activity, with depression showing the strongest effect and notable gender differences favoring greater psychological distress in females.

Cross-sectional study comparing symptom intensity between 59 post-COVID patients entering rehabilitation and 57 non-COVID controls using a 31-item questionnaire. Found post-COVID patients reported significantly higher intensity for fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, cognitive dysfunction, and musculoskeletal pain, though some symptoms overlapped with the non-COVID cohort.

Cross-sectional study comparing quality of life and functional capacity between 33 symptomatic long COVID patients and 37 asymptomatic individuals 6-18 months post-infection using standardized outcome measures. Symptomatic patients showed significantly lower functional capacity (6MWT, 30s-STS) and worse quality of life scores across multiple SF-36 domains.

Cross-sectional study examining the frequency and characteristics of long COVID in 131 healthcare workers, finding that 48.1% had long COVID symptoms with fatigue, myalgia, and arthralgia being most common. The study identifies associations between hospitalization/oxygen need during acute infection and long COVID development, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional descriptive study surveyed 390 post-COVID-19 patients with insomnia at two traditional Chinese medicine hospitals in Vietnam (Dec 2022–Jun 2023) to characterize traditional medicine clinical patterns and their associations with comorbidities. The study identified common traditional medicine syndromes (Heart-Spleen deficiency 31.28%, Heart-Kidney discord 17.44%, Heart-blood deficiency 11.79%, Heart-yin deficiency 11.28%) and found significant associations between these patterns and comorbidities like hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia.

Retrospective cross-sectional study describing the clinical and sociodemographic profile of 193 adults with long COVID in Costa Rica, comparing them to 198 controls without persistent symptoms. Identifies female sex, age ≥40 years, severe acute symptoms, and mental health disorders as significant risk factors for long COVID development.

Observational cross-sectional study of 396 post-COVID patients documenting persistent symptoms and their demographic/clinical correlates. Found that 87.9% experienced at least one persistent symptom, with fatigue, cough, and dyspnea being most common; no intervention or treatment was evaluated.

Cross-sectional observational study examining clinical features and symptom severity stratification in 101 post-COVID patients using standardized cognitive and psychological assessments. Identified three patient subgroups based on symptom severity scores, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between sleep quality and learning concentration in 49 post-COVID-19 patients in Malang Raya using PSQI and concentration questionnaires. Found a statistically significant but weak association (p=0.029, r=0.312) between sleep quality and concentration.

Characterization study of clinical symptoms in young adults (18-44 years) with post-COVID syndrome using a validated self-assessment questionnaire. Findings show high multisystem manifestation (86.3% neurological, 61.2% cardiovascular) with women reporting significantly higher symptom burden than men.

This cross-sectional survey of 264 youth in Bengaluru assessed the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and quality of life using demographic questionnaires and the SF-36 instrument. The study found 43.2% had long COVID symptoms with significant gender differences in symptom patterns and mental health as the most affected quality-of-life domain.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between fatigue and dyspnea in 56 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia using the Fatigue Severity Scale and Borg Scale. Found a moderate positive correlation (r=0.498) between fatigue level and dyspnea, but this is an observational study with no intervention tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 275 nursing students assessing sleep pattern disturbances post-COVID-19 using insomnia severity index and Epworth sleepiness scale. Found 83.64% had mild sleep disturbances, 76.4% reported insomnia, and 57.1% experienced daytime sleepiness, with women showing higher sleepiness tendencies.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between anxiety levels and dyspnea in 56 post-COVID-19 patients in Malang, Indonesia using standardized anxiety and dyspnea scales. Found a statistically significant moderate correlation (r=0.503, p<0.001) between anxiety and dyspnea severity.

This cross-sectional study compared functional features (lung capacity, exercise tolerance, cardiac rhythm) in 101 adolescent students who had COVID-19 versus 25 controls without prior infection. While it documents post-COVID sequelae including asthenia and reduced exercise capacity, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is purely descriptive and observational.

Cross-sectional study assessing factors associated with quality of life and persistent dyspnea in 100 COVID-19 survivor healthcare workers using EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, and mMRC scales. Found that post-COVID syndrome symptoms including activity limitation, cough, and fatigue were significantly associated with lower quality of life and persistent dyspnea.

This cross-sectional follow-up survey assessed long-COVID outcomes in 219 participants from two prior RCTs comparing individualized homoeopathy as adjunct therapy versus placebo alongside conventional treatment for moderate-to-severe COVID-19. The homoeopathy group showed significantly better functional status scores (0.83 vs 1.33, p=0.04) and lower rates of post-COVID complications including diabetes, hypertension, and exertional breathlessness.

Cross-sectional study assessing small airway obstruction and associated factors in 89 COVID-19 survivors under 50 years old at a hospital in Indonesia (2020-2022). Found a 19.1% incidence of small airway obstruction but no significant associations with age, gender, comorbidities, disease severity, or post-COVID symptoms.

Hospital-based descriptive cross-sectional study documenting the sociodemographic and clinical profile of 261 post-COVID patients with neurological manifestations. Study identifies tremor (50.6%), sleep disturbance (39.5%), neurocognitive decline (30.3%), and anosmia (29.9%) as the most common neurological presenting complaints but does not evaluate any treatment interventions.

Cross-sectional survey of 203 people assessing attitudes toward physiotherapy and psychotherapy for post-COVID recovery. Finds that 80.3% of respondents had COVID-19 infection, but only 25-30% sought physiotherapy or psychotherapy despite reported physical and mental sequelae.

This cross-sectional study examined fatigue and associated risk factors among 100 mild COVID-19 survivors working in an Indonesian hospital from September to December 2022. The study found significant associations between post-COVID syndrome symptoms (particularly confusion, insomnia, myalgia, arthralgia, throat pain, headache, and chest pain) and fatigue incidence, but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 720 post-COVID individuals examining immediate and long-term neurological complications and their association with comorbidities. Found neurological complications in 6.38% (immediate) and 3.34% (long-term) of participants, with significant associations between diabetes/hypertension and neurological symptoms.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the relationship between baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and spirometry results in 80 severe COVID-19 survivors. Found no significant correlation between elevated NLR and lung function parameters (FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, FEF 25-75%).

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of psychiatric disorders (insomnia, anxiety, depression, PTSD) among 100 post-COVID patients in an outpatient psychiatry clinic. Finds high rates of psychiatric complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional prevalence study of 750 individuals (aged 44-64) infected with COVID-19 during India's second wave, assessing chronic fatigue syndrome using the Fatigue Assessment Scale 1 year post-infection. The study found mild to moderate CFS prevalence in both hospitalized and home-quarantined individuals, with females more affected and significant correlations with age and smoking status.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing functional capacity and quality of life between COVID-19 survivors (second wave) and healthy controls in Ahmedabad, using 6-minute walk test and WHO-BREF questionnaire. Found no significant difference in functional capacity but significantly lower quality of life scores in COVID survivors.

Cross-sectional survey of 160 recovered COVID-19 patients investigating the prevalence and types of persistent post-COVID symptoms 4-5 months after infection. Found that a considerable proportion of patients had ongoing symptoms even after mild-to-moderate disease, though gender was not associated with quality-of-life differences.

A cross-sectional survey of COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia assessing the prevalence of olfactory and gustatory dysfunction and their impact on quality of life. While the paper mentions long-standing symptoms, it focuses on acute COVID-19 symptom prevalence rather than long COVID as a distinct post-acute condition, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary function, functional capacity, and physical activity in 80 patients with non-severe COVID-19 (≥3 months post-recovery) versus 80 matched controls. Found significant impairments in all three domains in the COVID-19 group, suggesting long-term respiratory and physical consequences warranting rehabilitation.

A cross-sectional descriptive study assessing anxiety and depression in 34 obstetrics and gynecology healthcare workers 3 months post-COVID using the Hospital Anxiety Depression Scale. Found that 32.5% had borderline anxiety, 23.4% had abnormal anxiety, 26.5% had borderline depression, and 32.4% had abnormal depression scores, suggesting persistent psychological effects of COVID-19.

A cross-sectional study assessing cognitive alterations in 44 COVID-19 recovered patients treated in cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, using the Neuropsi test to measure attention, concentration, and memory. The study found mild cognitive impairment in attention/concentration (47.7%) and short-term memory (77.3%), suggesting potential impacts on functionality and quality of life.

This cross-sectional study compared pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and physical activity levels in 80 non-severe COVID-19 patients (≥3 months post-infection) versus 80 matched uninfected controls. Results show significant long-term impairment in FVC, FEV1, exercise tolerance, and work-related physical activities in the COVID-19 group, suggesting a need for rehabilitative interventions.

Survey study examining post-COVID anxiety and stress disorders in 2021 among COVID-19 recovered patients in Pakistan, analyzing associations with demographics and severity of acute illness. Finds elevated psychological symptoms particularly in women and those with severe acute COVID, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared dental caries, periodontal disease, and salivary biomarkers (TAC and alpha amylase) between 90 COVID-19 recovered individuals and 90 never-infected controls in North Karnataka, India. COVID-19 recovered subjects showed higher prevalence of dental caries and periodontal disease with decreased salivary TAC and increased SAA levels, suggesting increased oxidative stress and stress markers.

A cross-sectional survey assessing knowledge of breathing exercises among 60 post-COVID patients in Kerala using a self-administered questionnaire. The study found that 58% had adequate knowledge, 30% had poor knowledge, and only 12% had good or excellent knowledge regarding breathing exercises.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 112 Saudi COVID-19 patients one year post-recovery to document post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) symptoms and identify predictors. The study found PCS in 73.2% of patients, with fatigue, cognitive problems, and muscle pain as most common, and identified female sex, comorbidities, and obesity as risk factors.

This cross-sectional study assessed functional capacity and quality of life in 50 female nurses who worked during the COVID-19 pandemic using 6-minute walk test and SF-36 questionnaire. The study found reduced functional ability and low quality of life scores, particularly in role limitations due to physical health.

Cross-sectional study following 200 COVID-19 patients one year post-discharge to assess long-term symptoms and sequelae. Found that 58% reported breathlessness and 50% reported fatigue, while 25% were symptom-free, with long COVID affecting multiple organ systems.

Cross-sectional study examining gene expression patterns (serotonin, IL-4, IL-1β, SOCS3, ILF13, IFNL4) in 56 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients and their association with clinical characteristics. Found female sex and drug use as risk factors, while serotonin, SOCS3, and IFNL4 expression had protective effects against specific symptoms like fatigue and cognitive impairment.

Cross-sectional survey of 147 long COVID patients examining associations between anxiety, headache, insomnia and quality of life using SF-36, Beck Anxiety Inventory, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Found that sleep disorders, anxiety, and headache significantly worsen QoL domains, with sleep disorders quadrupling risk of diminished vitality.

Cross-sectional study examining sleep quality and associated neurological symptoms in 288 long COVID patients using standardized assessments (PSQI, BAI, CCRC, MoCA). Found high prevalence of poor sleep quality (27%) linked to anxiety and olfactory dysfunction, with recommendations for symptom monitoring in clinical management.

A cross-sectional study assessing cognitive complaints and neurological status in 136 long COVID patients using clinical scales, cognitive assessments, and biomarker analysis. Findings show 94% reported cognitive complaints with subjective cognitive decline being most common; cognitive decline was associated with hospitalization, ICU admission, and anxiety.

This ecological study compares the incidence of inflammatory polyneuropathy (Guillain-Barré syndrome) hospitalizations in São Paulo before and after the COVID-19 pandemic using national health system data from 2018-2024. The authors found a 28.2% increase in cases during the post-pandemic period and hypothesize a potential link to COVID-19 immunological effects, though they acknowledge the need for further confirmation.

Cross-sectional study of 50 COVID-19 patients assessed 6 months post-infection to evaluate long-term impacts on sleep quality and mental health using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Found high prevalence of poor sleep (66% in severe/critical groups) and psychological disturbances including phobic anxiety and paranoid ideation across disease severity groups.

Cross-sectional study assessing cognitive function and psychiatric disorders in 46 long COVID patients previously admitted to ICU with severe acute COVID-19. Finds high prevalence of cognitive impairment (69.6% with MCI or dementia) including deficits in executive function, memory, language, and visuospatial abilities years post-infection.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of post-COVID-19 symptoms among 30 healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses, paramedical staff) at a tertiary hospital in Lahore, Pakistan, comparing symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. The majority of symptomatic participants (22/30) reported multiple long COVID symptoms including dyspnea (67.7%), breathlessness (70%), tiredness (93%), and headache (66.7%), though the study did not evaluate any specific treatments or interventions.

Cross-sectional retrospective observational study examining serum ferritin and other hematological parameters as predictive markers for pulmonary fibrosis in post-COVID-19 patients. Found significant positive correlation between serum ferritin levels and CT severity scores, suggesting ferritin may be a cost-effective biomarker for predicting lung fibrosis development in long COVID.

Cross-sectional study examining cognitive performance in 33 long COVID patients using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and its associations with sociodemographic factors, self-perceived health, and vaccination status. Found significant correlations between cognitive performance and education level and self-perceived health, but no significant associations with vaccination or reinfection history.

Cross-sectional study examining gender-specific differences in risk of dementia, anxiety, and depression in 1,000 post-COVID-19 patients using the Clinical Dementia Rating scale and questionnaire-based assessment. Found associations between demographic factors and neuropsychiatric outcomes in the post-COVID population, highlighting the need for preventive health measures in vulnerable groups.

Cross-sectional study comparing 51 elderly long COVID patients with 94 controls to identify prevalence and frequency of post-COVID symptoms. Found sweating, fatigue, dyspnea, and memory loss were most common, with higher rates of diabetes and cardiac disease in the long COVID group.

Ecological retrospective study analyzing mortality trends from inflammatory polyneuropathy in Brazil (2018-2023), with focus on possible neuroimmunological effects of COVID-19. Found increased mortality from inflammatory polyneuropathy post-pandemic, suggesting delayed post-COVID neuroimmunological impact.

Cross-sectional study of 87 COVID-19 patients examining the relationship between pre-COVID physical activity history, COVID-19 severity, and post-COVID syndrome incidence. Found that low physical activity and moderate-severe COVID-19 were significantly associated with post-COVID syndrome development, but the study is observational without intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared COPD disease control outcomes in patients with prior moderate COVID-19 infection versus those without COVID-19, measuring symptom severity, spirometric parameters, and exacerbation risk at baseline (2020) and follow-up (2025). While the paper documents long-term impacts of COVID-19 on COPD progression, it does not study long COVID as a distinct condition or test any specific intervention for long COVID patients.

Descriptive cross-sectional study measuring self-stigma incidence in 86 post-COVID-19 patients in Indonesia using the Self Stigma Scale questionnaire. Found that 84% of respondents experienced self-stigma to varying degrees, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 30 individuals (23+ months post-COVID) compared pulmonary function, exercise tolerance, sleep parameters, and quality of life across control, mild, and moderate/severe COVID-19 groups. Moderate/severe cases showed significantly impaired FEV1/FVC, respiratory muscle strength, exercise tolerance, sleep efficiency, and quality of life domains.

Cross-sectional descriptive study of 120 post-COVID-19 patients in Da Lat, Vietnam assessing symptom prevalence and quality of life impact. Found persistent cough (85.8%), sleep disturbances (50.8%), and dyspnea (50%) as most common symptoms, with disease severity in acute phase correlating with post-COVID syndrome severity and affecting 95% of patients' quality of life.

Cross-sectional observational study examining the association between baseline inflammatory markers (CRP and D-dimer) and functional exercise capacity (6-minute walk test) in 80 severe COVID-19 survivors. Found that elevated baseline CRP was significantly associated with poor 6MWT performance, suggesting inflammatory markers may predict functional recovery.

A cross-sectional descriptive study of 50 COVID-19 recovered patients in Pakistan assessing post-infection manifestations and their impact on quality of life. The study documents prevalence of long COVID symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.
Cross-sectional survey of 762 adults in Turkey examining post-COVID syndrome prevalence (20%) and COVID-19 vaccine confidence. Does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID patients.

Retrospective descriptive study of 135 post-COVID patients attending a convalescent clinic in Cuba, documenting demographic characteristics and symptom prevalence. Male predominance (51.8%), arterial hypertension as most common comorbidity (44.4%), and fatigue as the primary symptom (88.9%) were identified.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of lung fibrosis in 150 post-COVID patients using high-resolution CT scans. Found that 41.3% of patients had pulmonary fibrosis, with higher prevalence in males and those aged ≥50 years.

A cross-sectional survey study of 400 patients assessing post-COVID-19 neurological symptoms and risk factors at least 4 weeks after infection. Found 73.3% had neurological involvement with headache, myalgia, and sleep disturbance most common; depression, female gender, hospitalization, and favipiravir use were independent predictors.

This study compared cognitive status in 36 COVID-19 survivors with and without metabolic syndrome using MMSE and BCRS assessments. Results showed significant differences between groups in concentration, memory, functioning, and self-care domains.

Retrospective cross-sectional study analyzing the profile of neurological sequelae in COVID-19 patients in Palmas, Brazil from 2021-2023, with 4.2% prevalence and memory problems as the most persistent symptom. This is an observational study of existing sequelae without any treatment intervention or evaluation.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and characteristics of mood disorders in 91 post-COVID-19 patients using standardized psychiatric and neuropsychological assessments. Found that 50.8% of post-COVID patients had mood disorders with apathy (78.7%), anxiety (66.7%), and fatigue (60.6%) being most common, with strong correlations between depressive symptoms, fatigue, and sleep disturbance.

A cross-sectional survey of 699 COVID-19 recovered patients in Pakistan documenting the prevalence of persistent post-recovery symptoms including shortness of breath (27%), fatigue (23.5%), insomnia (11%), and tooth sensitivity (12%). The study describes symptom prevalence in the recovered population but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining correlations between chronic fatigue, post-traumatic stress disorder, and symptom severity in 155 COVID-19 survivors. Found that 73.5% reported post-recovery fatigue and 56% experienced high-impact PTSD, with greater prevalence in females.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 596 kidney transplant recipients to characterize long COVID prevalence, risk factors, and clinical phenotypes using a novel diagnostic method based on symptom clustering. The study identified long COVID in 33.7% of respondents and described eight distinct symptom phenotypes, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Descriptive cross-sectional study characterizing post-COVID syndrome in 66 healthcare workers at a triage center in Honduras, documenting symptom persistence at 4 and 12 weeks post-infection. Found that 75.8% of participants reported persistent symptoms at 12 weeks, with headache, fatigue, and hair loss being the most common manifestations.

A cross-sectional survey of 382 post-COVID patients in Rawalpindi and Islamabad assessing chronic fatigue prevalence using the fatigue severity scale. Found 65.4% of participants reported chronic fatigue, with higher prevalence in females (71.5%) than males (58.3%).

Cross-sectional study comparing health-related quality of life between 29 students with confirmed COVID-19 and 21 with unconfirmed COVID-19 using the SF-36 questionnaire. Students with confirmed COVID-19 showed significantly lower quality of life scores, particularly in mental health domains (p<0.001).

Cross-sectional study of 111 long COVID patients (mean 5.8 months post-infection) documenting prevalence of neuromuscular symptoms including fatigue (63.1%), myalgia (41.4%), headache (39.6%), and back pain (36%). Study identifies fatigue, myalgia, headache, and back pain as most common long COVID manifestations, with some sex differences in symptom presentation.

Cross-sectional survey examining menstrual cycle changes in 182 Libyan women following COVID-19 infection and vaccination. While menstrual disturbances were reported (33% post-infection, 18.1% post-vaccination), this is a symptom prevalence study of acute/vaccination side effects, not a long COVID study, as it does not investigate persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection in a long COVID population.

This cross-sectional study compared motor performance and attention levels in children aged 6-14 years with post-acute COVID-19 (≥4 weeks post-infection) versus uninfected controls. Children with post-acute COVID-19 showed significantly impaired attention (CPRS-R:S scores), but no significant differences in motor performance (TUG and stair climbing tests).

This cross-sectional study surveyed 124 Pakistani COVID-19 patients over 5 months to assess the prevalence of persistent olfactory symptoms (anosmia, parosmia) and associated mental health issues. The study found high rates of parosmia (81%) and odynophagia (79%), with significantly elevated depression and anxiety in patients experiencing long-term parosmia.

A cross-sectional survey of 174 Saudi Arabian individuals with prior COVID-19 infection assessing long-term olfactory dysfunction and its impact on quality of life. Olfactory training showed significant association with parosmia and phantosmia, and olfactory dysfunction negatively affected eating habits and social activities in substantial proportions of participants.

A retrospective descriptive study of 157 recovered COVID-19 patients examining post-infection complications and their association with demographic characteristics. Found high prevalence of persistent symptoms including respiratory failure (46.5%), hypercoagulability (35.7%), diarrhea (33.1%), and musculoskeletal pain.

A cross-sectional study assessing the prevalence and types of post-COVID symptoms among students at a Vietnamese university. The study found that students experienced common long COVID symptoms including fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, dyspnea, and cardiovascular symptoms, with additional findings of menstrual cycle changes in female students.

Cross-sectional study of Complex Stress Reaction Syndrome (CSRS) in 977 individuals across four continents, examining psychiatric symptoms (anxiety, depression, PTSD) and neuropsychiatric symptoms (cognitive deficits, fatigue) in both general population and long-COVID patients. Study identifies vulnerable populations showing elevated stress-related symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined depression, anxiety, and stress levels among 512 COVID-19 survivors 3-12 months post-discharge in Thailand, finding high prevalence of severe mental health symptoms. Risk factors included pulmonary disease history, education level, BMI, and income, but the paper does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated chronic pulmonary sequelae on CT scans in 94 COVID-19 patients followed for at least three months post-discharge. 83% of patients showed evidence of chronic pulmonary involvement, with ground-glass opacity and parenchymal bands being the most common findings.

A cross-sectional survey of 169 COVID-19 survivors in Saudi Arabia examining the prevalence of long-term post-COVID symptoms and their correlation with blood group and chronic disease status. The study found that blood group and chronic disease history were significantly correlated with symptom severity, with O+ being most common and A- showing the mildest symptoms.

This cross-sectional study compared cognitive functions between 75 long COVID employees (≥3 months post-infection) and 75 uninfected controls using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. While cognitive functions did not significantly differ between groups, post-COVID cases had significantly higher depression scores.

Cross-sectional study of 100 Iraqi participants examining changes in food preferences and taste-related characteristics following COVID-19 infection or vaccination. Finds that vaccination status is significantly associated with taste-related changes in eating behaviors, with vaccinated participants more likely to attribute dietary changes to taste variations.

This cross-sectional study compared sleep quality between medical students with and without a history of COVID-19 infection in Northern Vietnam using the Sleep Quality Scale. Students with COVID-19 infection demonstrated significantly poorer sleep quality, with poorer outcomes associated with younger age, female gender, living with others, and longer duration of infection.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between quality of life and echocardiographic findings in 31 healthcare workers with long COVID. Found that most participants (28/31) had both good quality of life and normal echocardiographic results, with only 3 showing abnormal cardiac imaging.

Cross-sectional study examining the correlation between sleep quality and cognitive function in healthcare workers with post-COVID-19 symptoms at a hospital in Banda Aceh. Found no statistically significant correlation between sleep quality (PSQI) and cognitive function (MoCA-Ina) in the 54 healthcare worker participants.

Cross-sectional study comparing long COVID symptom prevalence between vaccinated and non-vaccinated individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2. Found no significant statistical differences in post-COVID conditions risk between vaccination groups.

Cross-sectional study of 266 COVID-19 patients assessing frequency, severity, and impact of fatigue on quality of life during the prolonged post-COVID period. Found that 33.6% experienced persistent fatigue beyond acute illness, which significantly impaired quality of life, particularly in energy and physical activity domains.

Cross-sectional study assessing psychiatric illness and quality of life in 200 COVID-19 patients three months post-hospitalization. Found 39.5% had psychiatric disorders (depression, anxiety, adjustment disorder), but this is an observational survey without intervention, so it does not study a treatment.

This is a cross-sectional survey of 248 post-COVID patients in Panama examining long-term symptom prevalence and associated risk factors. The study documents symptoms persisting after acute infection (headaches, dyspnea, fatigue) and identifies risk factors like female gender and multiple acute-phase symptoms, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study of 254 COVID-19 patients identified post-COVID symptoms and risk factors for chronic post-COVID syndrome at 5 and 12 weeks post-infection. Female sex and specific radiological findings were significant risk factors for chronic symptoms, while long-term ARB use was associated with lower symptom burden.
