Cross-sectional study examining correlations between complete blood count (CBC) inflammatory markers measured at hospital admission and long COVID symptoms reported at 6-month follow-up in 167 patients. Found that neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and lymphopenia correlated with specific symptoms like decreased libido and poor concentration, suggesting CBC markers may predict long COVID symptom development.

A cross-sectional study of 329 COVID-19 patients in Turkey assessed symptom persistence nine months after infection, finding that 79.3% still had at least one symptom with fatigue, cognitive impairment, and effort loss being most common. This observational study describes the natural course of long COVID symptoms without evaluating any intervention or treatment.

Cross-sectional survey comparing long COVID symptom prevalence between 167 non-hospitalised and 95 hospitalised COVID-19 patients. Found long COVID in 59.9% overall, more frequent in non-hospitalised patients (68.3% vs 45.3%), with neuropsychiatric manifestations being most common.

Cross-sectional study of 183 COVID-19 patients examining relationships between smoking status, physical activity, and COVID-19 outcomes including sequelae. Active and former smokers reported higher rates of sequelae (memory issues, fatigue) compared to non-smokers, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the interrelationship between functional capacity tests (6-minute walk test, timed stair climbing, timed up and go) in 50 post-COVID-19 survivors, comparing hospitalized vs non-hospitalized patients. The study found moderate correlations between the tests, suggesting they measure related but distinct aspects of functional capacity in long COVID patients.

This study assessed functioning in 79 post-COVID syndrome patients using the Functioning in Chronic Illness Scale (FCIS) at a mean of 5.8 months post-hospitalization. Results showed medium functioning levels overall, with better functioning observed in men and younger patients, but without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID symptoms and treatment patterns between elderly and young patients. Found age was a key factor with elderly patients experiencing significantly more cardiac complaints and shortness of breath, while fatigue and hair loss showed gender differences.

This cross-sectional study assessed brain fog symptoms in 303 non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients retrospectively across four time periods post-infection, comparing symptom prevalence between women and men. Women reported significantly higher rates of cognitive problems (writing, reading, counting, thought communication) compared to men at various timepoints post-infection, but the study is descriptive/observational without evaluating any intervention or treatment.

A cross-sectional study of 100 long COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction that identifies predictive risk factors (age, duration, smoking, comorbidities, socioeconomic status) associated with persistent smell loss. The study is descriptive and observational with no intervention or treatment component, making it ineligible for the trials pipeline.

This is a descriptive cross-sectional study characterizing long COVID symptoms in 85 Indonesian patients using survey data. The study found fatigue as the most prevalent symptom (83.5%) among long COVID patients but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study applies the WHO ICF framework to characterize functional limitations, disabilities, and health-related conditions in 213 long COVID patients with persistent respiratory symptoms in Turkey. The study identifies impairments across body functions, activities, participation, and environmental factors but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 74 post-COVID-19 patients in Brazil to characterize their socio-epidemiological profile and long COVID effects using self-report questionnaires. The study found that 69% reported persistent symptoms (memory loss, hair loss, fatigue) and 13% reported cognitive impairment, but no intervention or treatment was tested or evaluated.

A cross-sectional study of 186 recovered healthcare professionals investigating the duration and risk factors for long-term post-COVID symptoms through phone interviews and logistic regression analysis. Female sex and pre-existing medical conditions were identified as significant risk factors for prolonged post-COVID effects, with fatigue being the most commonly reported symptom.

Cross-sectional observational study comparing clinical, physical, and psychological outcomes in 75 long COVID patients stratified by functional limitation level. Individuals with high functional limitation showed worse quality of life, reduced functional capacity, increased pain, and higher rates of ICU admission and prolonged hospitalization compared to those with low functional limitation.

This cross-sectional survey study of 13,461 respondents from 16 countries examined associations between habitual sleep duration, pre-existing medical conditions, and Long COVID risk using data from the 2021 International COVID Sleep Study II. The study found that short sleepers with pre-existing conditions had 3-fold higher odds of Long COVID, but this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional survey of 24,803 US adults examining associations between preexisting sleep issues (insomnia, poor sleep quality, short sleep duration) and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) using three different PASC definitions. Found significant associations between insomnia, poor sleep quality, and short sleep duration with PASC across all three models, suggesting these may be risk factors for PASC.

Cross-sectional study comparing restless legs syndrome (RLS) prevalence in 136 long-COVID patients versus 136 controls, with retrospective assessment of pre-COVID-19 baseline symptoms. Found RLS prevalence increased from 5.7% pre-COVID to 14.8% post-COVID in female LC patients, suggesting RLS as a potential long-COVID sequela.

Cross-sectional survey of 11,697 Western Australian adults assessing long COVID prevalence 90 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection during the 2022 Omicron wave. Found 18.2% prevalence with fatigue and concentration difficulties as most common symptoms; no treatment or intervention was tested.

This cross-sectional survey of 1,430 Korean respondents identified clinical features and medical access patterns among 745 patients with long COVID, finding ear/nose/throat complications and fatigue as most common symptoms. The study documents unmet medical needs and quality-of-life impacts but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examined the prevalence and clinical predictors of post COVID-19 condition in 186 pediatric patients (aged 0-18) compared to matched controls. The study found a 15% prevalence of post COVID-19 symptoms, with hospitalization and age 5-11 years identified as significant predictors of persistent symptoms including cough, rhinorrhea, and taste loss.

A stratified random health survey of 11,174 COVID-19-positive Australians and 1,514 controls assessed persistent symptoms at mean 12.6 months post-infection. 39.1% of COVID-19-positive respondents reported persistent symptoms, with 14.2% meeting clinical long COVID criteria; risk factors included female sex, age 40-49, infection severity, and chronic illness.

Cross-sectional survey of 500 young adults in Pakistan assessing long-term post-COVID-19 health impacts including physical, mental, and social consequences. Study documents high symptom prevalence (90% of vaccinated individuals) and widespread burden including mental health issues (46%), sleep disruption (42%), stress/depression (66%), and social/economic impacts, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 200 COVID-19 survivors examining the relationship between physical activity, body composition, and cardiovascular health outcomes post-COVID-19. The study identifies associations between activity levels and cardiovascular recovery but does not test or implement any intervention—it is purely observational.

Cross-sectional study of 300 COVID-19 recuperated individuals in Iran examining the prevalence and predictive factors of post-COVID cognitive disorders using standardized assessments and Bayesian analysis. Found cognitive disorders in 27% of participants, with PTSD, older age, lower oxygen saturation, and longer hospitalization identified as robust predictive factors.

Cross-sectional study comparing objective and subjective cognitive functioning between 57 adults with COVID-19 history and 57 without, in a community-dwelling sample. Found no significant differences in objective cognitive tasks, but long-haul COVID patients reported greater subjective cognitive impairment than those with short-term symptoms.

This cross-sectional study investigates the correlation between serum biomarkers (GFAP, creatine kinase, lactate dehydrogenase) and depression severity in 150 long COVID patients. The authors find elevated levels of these neurobiological markers in patients with severe depression, particularly in males, suggesting potential CNS mechanisms underlying neuropsychiatric manifestations of long COVID.

This school-based prospective cohort study examined Long COVID prevalence in 1,120 Swiss children and adolescents using standardized interviews and expert adjudication of symptom reports. Only 3.5% reported persisting symptoms, and adjudication concluded Long COVID was likely in 0/20 interviewed cases, suggesting questionnaire-based prevalence estimates substantially overestimate disease burden in children.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of persistent COVID-19 symptoms in 194 hospitalized patients at 4 weeks post-discharge in 2021-2022. The majority experienced at least one prolonged symptom (32%), with fever, dyspnea, weakness, and cough being most common, highlighting the need for long-term care in post-COVID patients.

Cross-sectional study measuring the prevalence of psychological distress (depression, anxiety, stress) among 300 Iranian COVID survivors from July 2021-February 2022. Found prevalence rates of depression (49%), anxiety (53%), and stress (61%), with determinants including ICU admission, intubation, and time since infection.

Cross-sectional study of 152 post-COVID patients examining associations between physical symptoms (fatigue, breathlessness, pain), physical activity levels, and health-related quality of life at >6 months post-infection. Found fatigue was the only symptom significantly associated with lower physical and mental health outcomes.

Cross-sectional study examining bone mineral density (BMD) in 164 post-COVID-19 patients and its associations with demographic and clinical characteristics. Found that older age and lower BMI were associated with higher osteoporosis risk, but the study is observational without testing any intervention.

A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of post-COVID hair loss (alopecia) in Indian patients and its association with COVID-19 severity and stress levels. The study found a 37.8% prevalence of COVID-induced hair loss, with female sex, COVID severity, and high stress as significant independent predictors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey assessing knowledge, attitudes, and experiences of physiotherapists in the UAE regarding long COVID management and rehabilitation. Study identifies gaps in screening and exercise prescription for long COVID patients, with majority of participants expressing need for additional training and education.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the frequency and risk factors for functional gastrointestinal disorders (FGIDs) one year after COVID-19 recovery in 357 patients. Results showed IBS (15.4%), GI symptoms (44.9%), and functional dyspepsia (9.5%) were common sequelae, with anxiety and depression as key risk factors, particularly in women.

Cross-sectional descriptive study of 667 COVID-19 patients in Long Ho district, Vietnam (2022-2023) assessing post-COVID prevalence and associated factors. Found 60.9% post-COVID prevalence, with psychiatric symptoms most common (50.8%) and gastrointestinal symptoms least common (7.9%); hospitalization and comorbidities were associated factors.

This cross-sectional study assessed cognitive and neuropsychiatric disorders in 20 Tunisian patients one month after COVID-19 hospitalization, using standardized cognitive tests (MMS, FAB, TMT, maze task). Found that 70% of patients had at least one cognitive dysfunction, with memory and executive functions most affected.

Cross-sectional study of 500 Egyptian women examining the prevalence of telogen effluvium (hair loss) as a post-COVID-19 dermatological manifestation. Found statistically significant association between COVID-19 hospitalization and telogen effluvium, but is an observational prevalence study without any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study followed 200 Egyptian COVID-19 survivors for six months to evaluate long-term post-COVID syndrome manifestations including insomnia, fatigue, dizziness, palpitations, dyspnea, chest pain, and depression. The study found statistically significant associations between symptoms and decreased oxygen saturation, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study comparing cerebral blood flow (ASL imaging) in 125 long COVID patients with cognitive symptoms versus 34 controls across 146 brain regions. Found significant reductions in cerebral blood flow in frontal, temporal, and parietal regions, suggesting vascular dysfunction as a potential biomarker for cognitive long COVID.

Cross-sectional study of 120 post-COVID-19 patients examining hair loss characteristics, timing, severity, and biochemical correlates (vitamin D, ferritin). Study documents clinical presentation and trichoscopic findings but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study measured body composition and phase angle values in 63 COVID-19 survivors (1-3 months and 3-6 months post-infection) using bioelectrical impedance analysis. The results showed significant improvements in basal metabolic rate, lean body mass, and cell integrity markers over the 3-6 month recovery period, with no active intervention tested.

This paper analyzes serum samples from 99 post-COVID patients to test for antibodies to three tick-borne bacteria (Borrelia burgdorferi, Coxiella burnetii, Bartonella henselae), finding that 74% had antibodies to one or more bacteria. The study is a diagnostic survey only with no treatment intervention, control group, or clinical trial design.

This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge regarding post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications among 40 recovered COVID-19 patients in Bangalore using a 25-item questionnaire. The study found that 55% of participants had poor knowledge, 35% had average knowledge, and only 10% had good knowledge, highlighting gaps in patient awareness about persistent respiratory symptoms and home monitoring.

A cross-sectional study of 312 Iraqi long COVID patients characterizing hematological abnormalities and coagulopathy patterns, finding high prevalence of elevated D-dimer (62.5%), lymphopenia (43.6%), fibrinogen elevation (38.1%), and thrombocytopenia (28.2%). The study documents disease pathophysiology and identifies hematological markers associated with symptom severity but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining secondary chronic musculoskeletal pain development in COVID-19 patients with and without lung involvement over a 3-month period. Findings indicate that patients with lung involvement had lower pain intensity, potentially due to stress-induced analgesia rather than long-term COVID-19 sequelae.

This cross-sectional study examined the frequency and correlates of subjective fatigue in 110 COVID-19 patients at 3 months post-infection. Key risk factors for fatigue included older age, chronic disease, severe acute infection (fever, pneumonia), and longer hospitalization duration.

Cross-sectional study of 62 patients with chronic neuropathic pain after COVID-19 examining lifestyle factors using questionnaires and pain scales. Found that activity levels and alcohol use were negatively associated with lifestyle quality in this population.

Cross-sectional survey of 90 post-COVID patients examining symptom prevalence and associations with demographic factors and comorbidities. Found 24.4% experienced symptoms >6 months, with fatigue and concentration difficulty most common, but no treatment intervention was evaluated.

This cross-sectional study examined anxiety-depressive disorders in 90 post-COVID patients using standardized scales (HADS, Beck depression scale). The study found no clear association between viral presence and anxiety-depressive manifestations, suggesting psychosocial factors may be the primary driver rather than direct pathophysiology.

Cross-sectional survey of 1,300+ COVID survivors in Karachi (Oct 2021–Apr 2022) examining the prevalence and factors associated with long COVID symptoms and impact on work performance. Over 35% reported symptoms lasting ≥6 weeks, with frequent coughing and appetite loss; the study emphasizes the need for awareness and prevention strategies but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study examines associations between physical activity, mental health, and quality of life in 193 women with prior COVID-19 using questionnaires (IPAQ, DASS, WHOQOL). The study found partial associations between physical activity and mental health parameters, but no correlation with quality of life, and calls for longitudinal research with objective activity measurement.

A cross-sectional survey of 189 Korean nurses assessing long COVID symptoms and associated risk factors using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale. The study found 94.7% of nurses experienced long COVID symptoms, with fatigue, weakness, and breathlessness most prevalent, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A cross-sectional survey of 134 elderly Vietnamese patients with hypertension and diabetes examining their knowledge and behavior regarding post-COVID health care. While 89% understood post-COVID self-care recommendations (nutrition, exercise, continuous treatment), only 48% actually followed them, and 36% required hospitalization due to unstable blood pressure and glucose levels.

This cross-sectional study of 150 Thai patients with post-COVID respiratory symptoms investigates Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome patterns and their correlation with spirometry and fatigue severity. While it identifies TCM syndromes in post-COVID patients, it is a descriptive/diagnostic study without treatment evaluation and therefore excluded from the intervention trials pipeline.

Cross-sectional survey study of 263 Brazilian residents examining the prevalence and correlates of self-reported post-COVID-19 fatigue between March 2023 and March 2024. Found 90.5% fatigue prevalence, associated with symptom persistence >4 weeks and alcohol consumption, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 308 COVID-19 survivors in Indonesia examining factors associated with long COVID occurrence. Found 80.2% prevalence of long COVID with fatigue, brain fog, and cough as most common symptoms; gender and comorbidities were significantly associated with long COVID, but age and healthcare worker status were not.

This cross-sectional case-control study examines oxidative stress markers in post-COVID-19 survivors compared to controls in Central India. The findings show that superoxide dismutase levels were lower and serum malondialdehyde levels were altered in post-COVID cases relative to controls, suggesting a role for oxidative stress in long COVID pathophysiology.

Cross-sectional study of 30 long COVID patients examining the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and fatigue in those with olfactory dysfunction. Finds high prevalence of neuropsychiatric symptoms (66.7% depression, 53.3% anxiety and fatigue) with significant negative impact on quality of life dimensions.

This cross-sectional survey assessed the prevalence of insomnia among 300 post-COVID-19 elderly patients using the Insomnia Severity Index scale. The study found significant insomnia prevalence, with different gender distributions across the first and second COVID-19 waves.

Observational cross-sectional study assessing pulmonary function tests (PFT) in 50 Indian adults recovered from COVID-19, finding restrictive lung patterns in 56% of subjects. Study documents post-COVID respiratory sequelae but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

A prospective cross-sectional study examining chest CT findings six months after COVID-19 pneumonia in 43 patients. The study documents residual radiological manifestations (ground glass opacities, subpleural lines) in approximately half of patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 150 participants investigating the prevalence and factors associated with telogen effluvium (temporary hair loss) in individuals recovering from COVID-19 in Pakistan. Found that 73.3% of participants reported post-COVID hair loss, with significantly higher rates in females (68.2%), but this is a passive observational survey with no intervention or treatment tested.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of Hyperventilation Syndrome among 377 COVID-19 recovered patients using the Nijmegen Questionnaire, finding that 63.66% exhibited HVS with common symptoms including anxiety, palpitations, and blurred vision. The study is a descriptive prevalence survey with no intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

A cross-sectional study of 225 COVID-19 survivors in Pakistan assessing the prevalence and severity of long-term respiratory symptoms including dyspnea, chronic cough, and pleuritic pain. Demographic factors such as older age, lower education, and female gender were associated with higher symptom severity, highlighting the need for targeted screening and rehabilitation.

A cross-sectional descriptive study examining post-COVID-19 sequelae and biochemical parameters in vulnerable populations aged 50-65 years. The study found high prevalence of hypertension (42%), normal glucose and creatinine levels in most participants, and significant comorbidity burden, but describes monitoring and characterization rather than testing a specific intervention.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on health-related quality of life in 53 individuals from Santa Cruz, Brazil using the SF-36 questionnaire. Found no significant relationship between quality of life and long COVID, with time since acute infection not affecting health-related quality of life outcomes.

Cross-sectional survey of 307 COVID-19 survivors assessing long COVID prevalence, symptom types, and associated factors. Found 40.1% prevalence with cardiopulmonary and general symptoms most common, but no significant associations with demographic or clinical characteristics.

Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary function (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC ratio) in 43 COVID-19 survivors and 53 non-COVID-19 controls among medical students and laboratory volunteers at Andalas University. All participants had normal average pulmonary function, with no intervention or treatment evaluated.

Cross-sectional observational study assessing pain prevalence and characteristics in 76 patients recovered from COVID-19 using the Brief Pain Inventory questionnaire. Found 33.78% prevalence of post-COVID pain, with chest pain, neck pain, headache, and low back pain being most common, and pain severity higher in older patients, females, and those with comorbidities.

Cross-sectional study measuring functional limitation in 76 patients recovered from COVID-19 using the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status scale. Found that 39.5% had negligible functional limitation, 34.2% slight, 14.5% moderate, and 9.2% severe limitation, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study examining demographics, risk factors, and post-COVID-19 syndrome manifestations among 410 patients in Iraq. Describes prevalence of symptoms (fatigue, cognitive impairment, joint pain, respiratory issues) across age groups but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study of 247 long COVID patients examining chronic musculoskeletal pain prevalence and associated factors after hospital discharge. Found 87% pain occurrence rate, with female sex, low income, recent discharge, and mechanical ventilation as significant risk factors for pain presence and intensity.

A retrospective cross-sectional study of 536 COVID-19 patients in Nigeria that describes the clinical spectrum and predictors of post-COVID syndrome, finding 18.3% prevalence with fatigue and headache as common symptoms. Pre-COVID vaccination was associated with reduced PCS risk, and affected patients had lower quality of life scores across multiple domains.

Cross-sectional analysis of 653 COVID-19 hospitalization survivors examining the association between physical activity levels and lung/kidney abnormalities 8 months post-discharge. Physically active survivors showed significantly lower prevalence of lung (28% vs 40%), kidney (14% vs 23%), and combined lung-kidney abnormalities (4% vs 9%) compared to inactive survivors.

Cross-sectional observational study of 515 COVID-19 survivors in western Libya examining prevalence and duration of post-COVID-19 symptoms. Study found 72% reported persistent symptoms with recovery occurring within 3 months in 75.5% of cases, identifying fatigue, cough, anosmia, and anxiety as most common sequelae.

A cross-sectional study examining the prevalence and factors associated with acute telogen effluvium (hair loss) in 100 COVID-19 PCR-positive patients in Pakistan. While the paper documents a long COVID sequela (64% of female participants experienced hair loss post-COVID), it is purely observational without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional survey compares COVID-19 recovery outcomes between 53 physically active and 47 inactive subjects (ages 30-44), finding that regular exercise was associated with fewer symptoms and faster recovery. The study does not focus on long COVID specifically, but rather on general COVID-19 recovery in younger adults without chronic diseases.

Cross-sectional study assessing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in 60 individuals who were hospitalized for COVID-19 and investigating relationships with sociodemographic variables, quality of life, muscle strength, and functional capacity. Found 48.3% had PTSD with significant associations to sedentary behavior, reduced functional capacity (TUG, 6MWT), and impaired quality of life domains.

Cross-sectional study evaluating kidney injury prevalence in 75 long COVID patients at 6, 12, and 24 months post-infection. Found progressive glomerular injury over time (50.7% with reduced eGFR) and tubular injury in 50.6% of patients, suggesting decoupling between glomerular and tubular mechanisms.

This cross-sectional study characterized post-COVID-19 condition in Kenya by measuring clinical symptoms, anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, and inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP) in 189 participants. The study found post-COVID-19 in 30% of previously infected individuals but found no significant differences in antibody or inflammatory marker levels between symptomatic and asymptomatic groups.

Cross-sectional survey of 348 Portuguese healthcare workers examining the prevalence of long COVID and its impact on quality of life and work performance. Found 64.1% reported long COVID history with significant associations between extreme fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and reduced work performance and life satisfaction.

This cross-sectional study assessed clinical long-term complications in 100 COVID-19 patients within 3 months of hospital discharge in Pakistan. The most frequent symptoms were fatigue (59%), dyspnea (47%), and loss of taste/smell (41%), reflecting respiratory, musculoskeletal, and neurological complications of post-COVID syndrome.

This study evaluates the readability, reliability, and quality of 100 websites providing patient education materials about post-COVID-19 pain. It finds that most materials are too difficult to read, lack credibility, and are of poor quality, with only a small percentage meeting recommended standards.

A retrospective cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of long COVID in Thailand during Delta and Omicron epidemic periods, analyzing associated biological factors through logistic regression and comparing spike protein mutations. The study found higher long COVID prevalence during Omicron (74.5% vs 66.0%) and identified epidemic variant, age, symptomatic medication use, and vaccination status as associated factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional survey of 52 COVID-19 patients in Bahrain assessing persistent symptoms 3 months post-infection using a symptom intensity scale. Found emotional stress, anosmia, and neurological symptoms were most common persistent symptoms, with associations between symptom intensities (e.g., dyspnea linked to pulmonary dysfunction).

This cross-sectional online survey examined symptom clusters and their relationship to quality of life in 220 people with long COVID, identifying five distinct symptom clusters (digestive-cognitive, respiratory-fatigue, pain-dermatological, sensory, and emotional). While it provides valuable epidemiological data on symptom patterns, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional survey assessed post-COVID-19 symptoms and quality of life in 158 recovered COVID-19 patients in Pakistan, finding that 94.9% experienced at least one post-discharge symptom with fatigue being most prevalent (82.9%). The study did not test any intervention or treatment, only evaluated symptom prevalence and associations with QoL and disease severity.

Cross-sectional study assessing disability in COVID-19 survivors at three months post-infection using WHODAS 2.0. Found fatigue and dyspnea most common, with females and symptomatic patients showing significantly greater disability.

Cross-sectional survey of 85.3% of post-COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia identifying manifestations including fatigue, musculoskeletal complaints, neuropsychiatric symptoms, and gastrointestinal issues. Study identifies risk factors (gender, age, smoking, BMI, comorbidities, severity) associated with post-COVID-19 syndrome but does not evaluate any interventions or treatments.

Cross-sectional study characterizing the clinical and laboratory profile of 259 patients visiting a post-COVID clinic in India, with 168 (64.9%) meeting PASC criteria. Identifies fatigue, breathlessness, and cough as common symptoms and hypertension, obesity, and persistent chest X-ray abnormalities as potential risk factors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective chart review and survey study of 72 COVID-19 patients from a primary care clinic in Alabama, assessing prevalence of lingering symptoms at 3+ months post-infection. Found that 50.9% reported long COVID symptoms (fatigue, brain fog, shortness of breath), with women more affected than men, but no association with comorbidities.

Cross-sectional survey study evaluating the prevalence of post-COVID symptoms in a tertiary care center in northern India at 3, 6, and 12 weeks post-infection. Found that disease severity, BMI, and comorbidities significantly affected persistence of post-COVID symptoms, but this is an observational epidemiological study with no treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional observational study examined the prevalence of hair loss among COVID-19 recovered patients in Saudi Arabia and its impact on quality of life using questionnaires. The study found that 52.7% of 806 participants experienced post-COVID hair loss associated with high temperature during infection, female gender, and prior hair loss history, with 8.6% reporting severe quality of life impact.

This retrospective cross-sectional study examined the prevalence of hair loss among 343 patients visiting dermatology clinics in Saudi Arabia during 2020-2022, finding that 48% of post-COVID patients reported hair loss, predominantly telogen effluvium. The study describes the manifestation and types of hair loss but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

A descriptive cross-sectional study of 227 post-COVID patients attending a tertiary care clinic in India, characterizing the prevalence and types of persistent symptoms including dyspnea (72%), cough (48%), and fatigue (42%). The study documents symptom patterns but is purely observational without any intervention or treatment component.

Cross-sectional survey of 13,530 COVID-19 patients in Saudi Arabia documenting long-term otolaryngology manifestations, with vertigo being the most common long-term symptom (43.3%), followed by persistent fever and ear blockage. This is an observational prevalence study with no intervention or treatment component.

Cross-sectional study comparing depression and anxiety symptoms in COVID-19 survivors at six months post-recovery versus matched controls using standardized rating scales. Found significantly elevated anxiety and depression scores in survivors, with severity correlating to initial disease severity.

Cross-sectional survey of 54 adolescents examining the impact of post-COVID-19 syndrome on school and physical performance. Study found that prolonged symptoms (fatigue, cough) were associated with decline in sports participation but not academic performance, with multiple infections and incomplete vaccination increasing symptom persistence.

Cross-sectional study of 286 COVID-19 patients in Bangladesh assessing post-COVID-19 symptom prevalence and characteristics. Found 18.5% reported post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, myalgia, anorexia, palpitations), with higher rates in older patients and those with severe initial disease.

Cross-sectional study of 194 COVID-19 patients examining prevalence and patterns of olfactory and gustative dysfunctions, with assessment of psychosocial impact. While the study documents that sensory symptoms persisted beyond acute infection (meeting long COVID criteria), it does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional study assessing the incidence of long-term fatigue in 343 Saudi COVID-19 survivors using the Chalder fatigue scale. Found 55.7% prevalence of long-term fatigue, with higher rates in females and those with longer post-infection duration.

Cross-sectional web survey of 404 fibromyalgia patients examining the relationship between fibromyalgia and post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Found that 19.8% met ACR fibromyalgia criteria, with female gender and dyspnea as significant predictors.

Cross-sectional survey of 346 women in Saudi Arabia examining the effect of COVID-19 on menstrual cycle regularity, duration, frequency, and pain severity. Found significant increases in menstrual irregularities during and after COVID-19 infection compared to pre-infection baseline.

This hospital-based cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence and determinants of long COVID among 212 outpatients with confirmed COVID-19 history in India, using symptom checklists, PHQ-9 depression screening, and diagnostic tests. The study found a 37.3% prevalence of long COVID, with depression and COVID-19 severity identified as significant determinants, but did not test any treatment or intervention.

A cross-sectional study comparing auditory and visual working memory capacity in 17 medical students recovering from mild COVID-19 versus 18 healthy controls. The study found selective impairment of auditory working memory in long COVID cases but no overall differences in visual working memory or attention span.

Prospective longitudinal study of COVID-19 survivors in India assessing long COVID symptoms and pulmonary function abnormalities. Found that breathlessness and restrictive lung patterns were prevalent in long COVID patients, particularly those with severe initial infection and female participants.

A cross-sectional study of 196 COVID-19 patients in Islamabad examining the prevalence of long COVID symptoms and their association with blood group and demographic factors. The study found no association between long COVID and ABO blood groups, but identified females as more likely to experience long COVID symptoms, particularly in those with perceived severe acute infection.

Cross-sectional survey of 482 Saudi adults examining the association between COVID-19 infection and back pain prevalence in the Eastern Province. The study found that 10.1% of participants reported back pain with varied durations, and among those with back pain, 24.7% attributed it to COVID-19, highlighting back pain as a potential post-COVID symptom.

Cross-sectional study comparing asthma-like symptoms and clinical parameters between 39 post-COVID patients and 37 asthmatic controls in Dubai. Post-COVID patients showed improvement with bronchodilator therapy (inhaled corticosteroids and long-acting beta-agonists), suggesting potential efficacy of anti-asthma treatment for managing post-COVID respiratory symptoms.

Cross-sectional study comparing pulmonary function tests (PFTs) in post-convalescent COVID-19 patients versus controls and smokers. Found minimal differences in most PFT parameters between groups, with only FEV1/FVC% and PEFR showing statistically significant increases in smoking patients.

Cross-sectional study examining the association between acute COVID-19 severity and persistent dyspnea in 385 recovered adults, stratified by infection severity (mild to critical). Found a strong correlation between initial COVID-19 severity and both persistence and severity of dyspnea symptoms, with oxygen therapy recipients showing higher clinical scores.

Cross-sectional study of 100 Pakistani patients examining neurocognitive and emotional outcomes of long COVID, using standardized assessments including MMSE and ADHD screening. Found significant correlations between COVID-19 symptoms and depression, anxiety, and ADHD, with females reporting higher psychological burden.

A cross-sectional survey of 2,153 Saudi Arabian residents assessing public awareness of post-COVID-19 syndrome symptoms and risk factors between June-August 2023. The study found low overall awareness (64.09% had low awareness) with significant knowledge gaps regarding PC19S symptoms and risk factors.

Cross-sectional study of 335 COVID-19 patients discharged from a tertiary care hospital in India, assessing persistent symptoms at 28 days post-symptom onset via telephonic interview. Found 66% had persistent symptoms, with fatigue (32.5%), dyspnea (23%), and cough (13.4%) being most common; higher persistence in severe cases and those with comorbidities.

Cross-sectional survey of 735 nurses assessing anxiety and depression levels two years after COVID-19 infection, comparing long COVID (n=263) vs non-long COVID (n=472) groups. Found that nurses with long COVID had significantly higher depression and anxiety scores, with older age and depression severity as independent risk factors.

Cross-sectional study of 287 post-COVID-19 patients with rhino-orbital fungal infections in India, identifying Fusarium, Aspergillus, and Mucor as causative organisms. Study evaluates epidemiology and risk factors (diabetes, steroids, immunosuppression) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A descriptive cross-sectional study assessing pulmonary function tests in 155 COVID-19 recovered health science students six weeks post-infection at a medical college in India. The study found altered respiratory function patterns (primarily restrictive disease) in recovered subjects compared to predicted values, with female participants showing significantly reduced FEV and FEF values.

Cross-sectional study comparing cognitive function between 29 young adults with mild COVID-19 infection (≥2 years post-infection) and 29 matched controls using NIH Toolbox cognitive assessments. Found no statistically significant differences in cognitive domains (executive function, flexibility, attention, memory, processing speed) between cases and controls.

Cross-sectional study comparing mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, sleep quality) in 240 healthcare workers with and without post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Found significantly higher anxiety and poorer sleep quality in the post-acute COVID-19 group, but no significant difference in depression.

Cross-sectional study assessing autonomic nervous system dysfunction and inflammatory markers in 150 COVID-recovered patients three months post-infection. Found that 36 patients had autonomic dysfunction with significantly elevated inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, CRP) and correlations between inflammation and autonomic function parameters.

Cross-sectional study examining the prevalence of post-COVID pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) among 854 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors and its association with CT severity scores. Found 12.1% prevalence of PAH with significant association between chest CT severity during acute infection and PAH development.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of cognitive impairments including memory loss, attention deficits, and executive function disorders in 539 post-COVID-19 recovered individuals in Saudi Arabia. While it documents significant cognitive symptoms (39.15% with memory changes), it is observational without any intervention or treatment arm, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

This cross-sectional study assessed the prevalence of cognitive impairment in 204 long COVID patients with psychiatric sequelae at a specialized mental health clinic in India. The study found that 86.8% of patients had cognitive impairment, which was significantly correlated with depression but not associated with socio-demographic factors; however, this is an observational study with no intervention or treatment being tested.

Cross-sectional study comparing post-COVID-19 menstrual abnormalities in 204 medical students treated at home vs. hospital during acute infection. Menstrual cycle abnormalities were more prevalent in the hospital group (61.9%) than home treatment group (46.9%), with premenstrual syndrome being the most common abnormality; most irregularities resolved within six months.

Cross-sectional study comparing heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system function between young adults with bronchial asthma who have and have not had prior COVID-19 infection. Asthma patients with prior COVID-19 showed significantly lower parasympathetic markers and elevated sympathetic activity, indicating post-COVID autonomic dysfunction.

Cross-sectional study examining the relationship between long COVID syndrome severity and quality of life in 67 COVID-19 survivors aged 15-64 years. Found significant negative correlations between severity and quality of life across physical, mental, and social domains.

Cross-sectional study assessing taste and smell impairment in university students with and without COVID-19 history using standardized flavor recognition tests. Found that COVID-19 infection moderately impaired ability to identify salty and bitter tastes, with 63.3% reporting taste loss and 69.4% reporting smell loss.

This cross-sectional study describes the clinico-epidemiological profile of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) as a post-COVID complication in a North Indian tertiary care hospital. While MIS-C is temporally related to COVID infection, the paper focuses on acute inflammatory complications rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection) and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Comparative cross-sectional study assessing cognitive impairment in severe post-COVID-19 patients admitted for rehabilitation versus ICU controls. Found no significant difference in cognitive impairment between post-COVID and control groups across multiple cognitive domains.

Cross-sectional study of 312 adolescents examining the association between physical activity time and chronic post-COVID syndrome. Finds that female sex, post-pubertal status, and insufficient physical activity are significant predictors of developing post-COVID syndrome.

This nested case-control study examines the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and dementia risk in 1.1 million Israeli adults aged ≥50, matching 27,280 dementia cases to 272,800 controls. The study finds that hospitalized COVID-19 patients had 75-93% increased dementia risk, but this is an epidemiological association study with no treatment intervention, and long COVID is not the primary focus.

This cross-sectional study assessed quality of life and fatigue symptoms in 38 post-COVID-19 patients in Brazil using the EQ-5D-5L and CFQ-11 scales. Results show 60.53% exhibited fatigue symptoms and 26-29% reported moderate problems with pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression, with median health quality-of-life scores of 70-80.

Cross-sectional observational study examining post-COVID symptom prevalence across vaccination types and booster dose effects in 110 Bangladeshi participants. Study reports symptom patterns by vaccine type but lacks a treatment intervention—booster status is an observational variable, not an assigned treatment, making this an epidemiological assessment rather than a treatment trial.

A retrospective cross-sectional study characterizing long COVID sequelae in 138 patients attending primary care in Mexico from 2023-2025. The study identified respiratory symptoms (cough, odynophagia) as most common sequelae and found vaccination offered protection against dyspnea but was associated with increased cough.

Case-control study examining racial and ethnic disparities in outpatient rehabilitation utilization among post-COVID-19 patients using the TriNetX database. Finds that African American/Black individuals received rehabilitation services at lower rates despite similar symptom incidence, highlighting healthcare access inequities.

A case-control study developing a urinary peptidomic diagnostic model (PASC195) to distinguish long COVID patients from controls using 195 differentially abundant peptides. While the study suggests potential therapeutic interventions (exercise, GLP-1RAs, MRAs) based on in silico analysis, it does not test or evaluate any actual treatment interventions in patients.

Case-control study comparing cognitive performance and brain network organization in 42 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints versus 43 healthy controls using MRI and neuropsychological testing. Found long COVID patients had significantly impaired memory, attention, and executive function with reduced efficiency in salience/ventral attention and global networks.

A case-control study comparing whole-body [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging between 13 long COVID patients and 26 matched melanoma-free controls to investigate systemic inflammation and brain metabolism patterns in long COVID. The study found characteristic brain hypometabolism in long COVID patients and multi-organ inflammatory changes on PET imaging, suggesting distinct temporal inflammatory sequences between brain and systemic involvement.

This cross-sectional study compares semen quality (sperm concentration, motility, morphology) between 100 men who recovered from acute COVID-19 and 100 men who never had COVID-19. The study found decreased sperm concentration in the COVID-19 recovered group but no significant differences in motility or morphology, focusing on acute post-infection effects rather than long COVID sequelae.

A 6-month prospective case-control study of 320 health workers examining the incidence, evolution, and recovery of COVID-related olfactory and gustatory dysfunction. The study found that 64% of COVID cases experienced olfactory dysfunction and 61% experienced gustatory dysfunction, with 89% showing total or partial recovery by 6 months, though 11% showed no recovery.

Case-control study examining the association between previous SARS-CoV-2 infection and new antidepressant prescription in an Italian region from 2020-2022. Finds that COVID-19, especially severe infection, is associated with increased antidepressant treatment, with vaccination appearing protective.

A case-control study evaluating serum ferritin as a biomarker in post-COVID telogen effluvium (hair loss), comparing 100 COVID-19 convalescents with controls. The study reports that dietary supplements (vitamin C, D, lactoferrin, zinc) used during acute infection showed preventive value against post-COVID hair loss, while certain medications (azithromycin, ivermectin) were associated with increased telogen effluvium.

This case-control study compared cognitive function and serum BDNF levels between 54 COVID-19 patients and 36 healthy controls, finding significant cognitive decline and lower BDNF levels in the COVID-19 group. The study is observational/pathophysiological in nature and does not evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

Case-control study investigating autonomic nervous system dysfunction in long COVID patients compared to healthy controls using sympathetic skin response and vagus nerve ultrasound measurements. Found differences in ANS function between long COVID patients and controls, suggesting ANS maladaptation as a potential pathogenic mechanism.

This case-control study compared autonomic cardiac function in 56 pediatric long COVID patients versus 27 healthy controls using ECG, Holter monitoring, and echocardiography. The study found significant abnormalities in heart rate variability parameters in long COVID patients, suggesting an imbalance toward parasympathetic predominance, but no significant structural cardiac differences.

Case-control study comparing nasal cytological alterations in 36 patients with persistent post-viral olfactory dysfunction versus two control groups (recovered from COVID-19 without olfactory loss, and non-COVID controls). Found increased lymphocytes, neutrophils, and ciliocytophthoria in olfactory dysfunction patients, indicating chronic local inflammation in the olfactory cleft.

Case-control study comparing headache prevalence and severity in 188 post-COVID patients versus 27 controls with prior COVID or other infectious disease history. Found significantly higher headache prevalence, worse quality of life, and higher depression/fatigue in PCC patients, emphasizing the need for multi-professional symptom assessment.

Prospective cross-sectional study comparing qualitative and quantitative smell/taste dysfunction in 17 COVID-19 patients versus 21 healthy controls using standardized testing and questionnaires. Finds persistent qualitative disorders (phantosmia, parosmia, phantogeusia, parageusia) in ~35% of recovering patients, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Case-control study comparing mental health outcomes in 103 children with long COVID versus 113 uninfected controls. Found that long COVID was associated with memory difficulties but not with higher rates of emotional-behavioral problems; parental economic stress and worries were stronger predictors of children's distress than LC diagnosis itself.

This case-control study assessed olfactory and gustatory function in 93 post-COVID-19 patients compared to matched controls at 1-year and 2-year follow-up using standardized psychophysical testing. While chemosensory dysfunction improved over time, COVID-19 cases still showed significantly higher rates of olfactory dysfunction at 2 years compared to controls.

A case-control study comparing echocardiographic findings in 270 children with PASC and 400 age-matched controls using deep learning to detect cardiac abnormalities. Standard echocardiographic parameters showed no differences, but a ResNet-50 model achieved 96.6% accuracy in distinguishing subtle image-based differences between groups, though clinical significance remains unclear.

Case-control study comparing 88 long COVID patients with 96 controls to identify demographic, laboratory, and genetic factors associated with long COVID syndrome. Found that severe acute COVID-19, elevated BMI, CRP, IL-6, and specific HLA alleles (A*11, C*07) were significantly associated with long COVID development.

Prospective case-control study comparing gene expression levels (ALOX12, ITGA2B, F13A1, PF4) in pregnant women who recovered from COVID-19 versus uninfected controls. Finds significantly elevated expression of three candidate genes in post-COVID-19 survivors, suggesting potential association with placenta-mediated pregnancy complications.

This case-control study compared pulmonary function, respiratory endurance, and cardiovascular responses between 45 COVID-19 convalescent patients and 45 healthy controls. COVID-19 convalescent patients showed significant declines in multiple pulmonary function measures (FVC, FEV1, FEF metrics) and increased lung age, indicating long-term respiratory impacts of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

This case-control study examines hearing loss patterns in acute COVID-19 infected adults and children born to COVID-19 infected mothers. The paper focuses on acute infection effects (transient hearing loss detected at day 7), not long COVID or any treatment intervention.

A pilot case-control study investigating blood-brain barrier permeability in 14 long COVID patients with cognitive complaints compared to 10 controls using SPECT imaging and cognitive testing. Found no significant differences in blood-brain barrier permeability or cognitive function between groups, suggesting disruption of the blood-brain barrier is unlikely the primary mechanism of COVID-related brain fog.

A retrospective case-control study comparing serum serotonin levels between 34 PASC patients and 14 healthy controls. The study found no significant differences in serotonin levels and concluded that peripheral serotonin is not a reliable biomarker for PASC.

Case-control study comparing 174 COVID-19 patients at 6-month follow-up with 75 matched controls to assess persistent symptoms, quality of life, and markers of inflammation and cardiac injury. Found persistent shortness of breath, fatigue, and elevated inflammatory markers in post-COVID patients, but this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This case-control study compares postural sway and physical capacity between people with long COVID (~16 months duration), ME/CFS (~16 years duration), and age-matched healthy controls. Both long COVID and ME/CFS groups showed similarly impaired balance and physical capacity compared to controls, with no significant differences between the two patient groups.

This prospective multicenter case-control study evaluated sulodexide treatment in 79 long COVID patients with endothelial dysfunction compared to 131 untreated controls, followed for 21 days. Sulodexide treatment was associated with significant improvements in endothelial function and reduction in long COVID symptoms including chest pain, palpitations, fatigue, and neuro-cognitive difficulties.

This case-control study compared the prevalence of PTSD and complex PTSD (CPTSD) among 21 individuals with long COVID, 20 with ME/CFS, and 20 healthy controls using the International Trauma Questionnaire. Long COVID participants had significantly higher PTSD and CPTSD prevalence (5% and 33% respectively) compared to ME/CFS and controls, with greater symptom scores across all PTSD and DSO domains.

This case-control study compared flow-mediated dilation (endothelial function) in 17 long COVID patients, 17 ME/CFS patients, and 17 healthy controls. Both long COVID and ME/CFS groups showed significantly impaired endothelial function compared to controls, with no difference between the two patient groups.

This case-control study compares well-being and cognitive function between people with long COVID (~16 months duration), ME/CFS (~16 years duration), and age-matched healthy controls. While both patient groups show similar impairment on well-being measures compared to controls, this is an observational comparison study that does not test any intervention or treatment.

Nested case-control study comparing oral microbiota differences between long COVID patients and controls using 16S rRNA sequencing. Identifies distinct microbial dysbiosis and marker bacteria associated with long COVID, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared dexterity and bimanual coordination between people with long COVID (~16 months), ME/CFS (~16 years), and healthy controls using the Purdue pegboard test. The study found that both long COVID and ME/CFS patients showed similarly impaired dexterity and bimanual coordination compared to controls, but did not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Case-control study comparing 37 post-COVID patients with 30 healthy controls using objective balance assessments (CDP, VEMP, v-HIT). Found significant impairments in balance-related systems in COVID-19 survivors, including decreased visual scores, altered vestibular responses, and persistent dizziness persisting after clinical recovery.

This case-control study compared 140 long COVID patients with persistent fatigue and post-exertional malaise to 80 recovered controls, finding that EBV reactivation occurred in 28.6% of patients versus 11.3% of controls (p=0.003). The study identifies EBV reactivation as a potential mechanism in long COVID syndrome, though it does not test an intervention.

Case-control study comparing cognitive functioning between older adults with serologically confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and seronegative controls. Found that infected individuals had significantly lower scores in memory, attention, and executive functions, supporting the 'Cognitive COVID' construct.

This case-control study compares post-COVID-19 fatigue prevalence in 52 type 2 diabetes patients who had COVID-19 versus 56 matched controls without COVID-19. Findings show T2D patients post-COVID had significantly higher fatigue scores, increased inflammation markers, and reduced physical activity, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A case-control study examining the role of galanin system and insulin resistance parameters as diagnostic biomarkers in long COVID patients compared to healthy controls. The study identifies altered biomarkers and develops a neural network model for LC prediction, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing oral microbiota composition, salivary cytokines, and short-chain fatty acids between long COVID patients and healthy controls. Found no significant differences in microbiota diversity or cytokines, with only weak uncorrected signal for valeric acid; study is mechanistic rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This case-control study examines the association between pre-infection BMI and long COVID development in 315 Spanish COVID-19 patients. It finds that overweight/obesity significantly increases the risk of developing long COVID and moderate-to-severe functional limitations, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Case-control study examining central and peripheral autonomic nervous system dysfunction in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients (n=7) versus matched healthy controls (n=7) using sympathetic skin response and fNIRS imaging. Found prolonged SSR latencies and altered fronto-parietal network connectivity in PCS patients, but this is a mechanistic/biomarker study without any treatment intervention or evaluation.

summary: A case-control study of 126 healthcare workers examining cardiovascular autonomic function in 58 long COVID patients versus 53 never-infected and 14 recovered controls, testing the effect of slow-paced breathing on heart rate variability. Long COVID patients showed reduced resting vascular modulation but improved baroreflex sensitivity during slow-paced breathing, suggesting breathing exercises may help restore vascular reactivity.

This retrospective case-crossover study analyzes associations between ambient temperature, air pollution, and SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in individuals who later developed post-COVID condition (PCC) versus those who did not. The study identifies cold exposure and air pollution as risk factors for infection severity and PCC development, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This case-control study examined the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and low back pain (LBP) in 878 Bangladeshi participants, finding significantly higher LBP prevalence among post-acute COVID-19 patients (24.4% vs 15.7%). The study identified SARS-CoV-2 infection as an independent risk factor for LBP, with moderate COVID-19 symptom severity as a significant predictor among long COVID patients.

This nested case-control study examines the burden of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), dialysis patients, and kidney transplant recipients. It documents the prevalence and symptom burden of PCC in these high-risk populations but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional case-control study compared exercise capacity in 20 ACS patients with concurrent COVID-19 infection to 20 controls without COVID-19, assessed 6-12 months post-revascularization via cardiopulmonary exercise testing. The COVID-19 group showed significantly reduced oxygen consumption (74% vs 86.7% predicted) and ventilatory inefficiency, with 50% meeting long COVID symptom criteria and demonstrating the most compromised exercise capacity.

This prospective case-control study compared cardiac function and long-COVID symptoms in children 1 year post-COVID-19 (n=Group 1) versus healthy controls without SARS-CoV-2 exposure. While conventional echocardiography was normal, Group 1 showed persistent reduction in left ventricular GLS (subclinical myocardial dysfunction) and 23.6% reported long-COVID symptoms (fatigue 16.6%, palpitations 2.0%).

A matched case-control study examining prevalence and risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition in Japanese children aged 5-17 years. The study found that SARS-CoV-2 infected children had significantly higher odds of persistent symptoms than uninfected controls, with older age, low household income, and pre-existing conditions increasing risk, while vaccination reduced risk.

Case-control study investigating complement system activation in post-COVID-19 condition by comparing protein levels (C3, C4, C5, C7) and hemolytic activity between 57 long COVID survivors and 27 matched controls. Found no overall complement pathway differences between groups, though specific complement proteins were lower in patients with post-COVID fatigue or dyspnea.

Retrospective case-control study analyzing 1,086 long COVID patients and matched controls from a US health system to identify risk factors for developing long COVID. Findings show chronic pulmonary disease, migraine, and fibromyalgia as significant risk factors, with severe acute infection markers associated with long COVID development.

This retrospective cohort and case-control study using Japanese health insurance data examined risk factors for COVID-19 infection and post-infection sequelae in patients aged ≥60 years hospitalized by December 2020. The study identified mental/behavioral disorders and pulmonary conditions as major risk factors for developing sequelae, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared 31 long COVID patients with 27 healthy controls using oxygenation-sensitive cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) to assess vascular function during breathing exercises. The study found that long COVID patients had blunted hemodynamic and myocardial oxygenation responses compared to controls, suggesting endothelial dysfunction contributes to long COVID pathophysiology.

This case-control study compared 167 biomarkers between long COVID patients and COVID-recovered controls 12-24 months post-infection, identifying a panel of 4 markers (αGAD, IL-10, potassium, CD16brightCD56- cells) that distinguished the two groups with >88% accuracy. The study characterizes the immunological and biochemical profile of post-COVID condition but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared static and dynamic balance and fall risk between 30 individuals with mild to moderate COVID-19 and 30 healthy controls 3-6 months post-infection. Significant differences were found in most balance measures including mCTSIB, Fall Risk Test, and Unipedal Stance Test, demonstrating persistent balance disorders even in mild to moderate COVID-19 cases.

A nested case-control study of 55 long COVID patients with fatigue who were taking Macaranga sinensis, comparing treatment responders (n=27) to non-responders (n=28) using OLink proteomic analysis. The study identified CX3CL1 as a candidate biomarker for predicting treatment efficacy of the herbal intervention.

This case-control study recruited 163 long-COVID patients with new-onset chronic pain and 151 controls to identify factors associated with quality of life. Key findings show that anxiety and symptom complexity negatively impact QoL, while aerobic capacity and employment status positively influence it, though this is an observational characterization study without any treatment intervention.

This German case-control study compared cognitive performance in 410 adults with post-COVID syndrome, 87 recovered controls, and 64 healthy controls. Adults with PCS showed worse episodic memory and visuospatial abilities but no impairments in executive function or global cognition.

This case-control study compared psychosocial dimensions between Italian children with long COVID, children who had COVID-19 without long COVID, and children without prior COVID-19 infection. While it confirms a link between maternal health anxiety and child long COVID, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case-control study evaluating the impact of early post-COVID clinic attendance on downstream healthcare utilization, costs, and mortality in 2,814 matched long COVID patients over 6 months. Early clinic usage was associated with reduced inpatient stays, ED visits, costs, and mortality, with increased outpatient utilization suggesting successful care shift to outpatient settings.

This case-control pilot study compares growth hormone secretion and metabolic markers between long COVID patients (n=10) with neurologic symptoms and recovered controls (n=13). The study finds reduced GH secretion associated with fatigue and brain fog in PASC patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional case-control study compared psychosocial characteristics of 29 Italian children with long COVID (15% of 198 children exposed to SARS-CoV-2) against two control groups (never infected and COVID-recovered without LCS). The study found that maternal health anxiety and child deprivation were elevated in long COVID cases, predominantly presenting with neurological/neuropsychiatric symptoms, highlighting the need for integrated psychosocial care.

A case-control study comparing tissue oxygenation responses in 30 long COVID patients versus 16 cardiovascular disease patients and 11 healthy controls using near-infrared spectroscopy during an arterial occlusion protocol. Findings show that long COVID patients have altered tissue oxygen consumption rates, with slower desaturation during ischemia and slower reoxygenation after cuff release compared to controls, potentially explaining fatigue and physical impairment symptoms.

Retrospective case-control study examining the association between COVID vaccinations and antiviral treatments (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, remdesivir) with long COVID outcomes beyond 6 months in a large US healthcare system. Study found inverse associations between vaccination doses and antiviral treatments with long COVID diagnosis, suggesting protective effects of vaccination and early antiviral therapy.

Case-control study comparing cardiopulmonary function, muscle strength, and quality of life in 50 COVID-19 recovered patients (3-6 months post-recovery) versus 50 matched healthy controls. Found significant reductions in the COVID-19 group across all measured domains, but did not test any intervention or treatment.

This case-control study compared 152 COVID-19 survivors with 152 matched controls to investigate obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) phenotypes and their association with long COVID. REM-predominant OSA was significantly more common in COVID-19 survivors (47.4% vs 17.8%) and was independently associated with fatigue, a surrogate marker of long COVID.

This nested case-control study across three Italian regions examined the risk of new antidepressant prescriptions following SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding that previously infected individuals had significantly higher risk, with stronger associations in hospitalized patients. SARS-CoV-2 vaccination appeared to reduce this risk, suggesting an effect-modifying role of vaccination on post-infection neuropsychiatric outcomes.

Case-control study of 7,051 Brazilian healthcare personnel comparing 1,933 who developed long COVID to 5,118 who did not, identifying risk factors including female sex, age, and multiple SARS-CoV-2 infections. Study found vaccination and infection with delta/omicron variants were protective against long COVID development.

Case-control study examining the association between preexisting hypertension and post-COVID symptoms in hospitalized patients. Found that hypertension is independently associated with greater number of long-term post-COVID symptoms and poor sleep quality, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study compared emotional and personality functioning in 44 long COVID patients with 50 post-concussion syndrome patients using the Personality Assessment Inventory (PAI). While both groups showed similar elevated somatic preoccupation and depression scores, the PCS group had significantly higher paranoia, antisocial features, stress, and suicidal ideation, with the authors suggesting psychological treatment strategies from PCS may benefit long COVID patients.

A case-control study comparing nursing home residents with and without prior COVID-19 infection to characterize postacute sequelae (PASC) and long-term functional outcomes. The study found that COVID-19-infected residents had significantly higher rates of functional decline, hospice entry, and mortality in the year following infection, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A case-control study comparing neuropsychological test performance in 50 COVID-19 recovered patients versus 53 healthy controls across cognitive domains. While subtle executive function differences were observed, the study found no objective cognitive impairment and attributed subjective complaints to potential symptom exaggeration rather than demonstrating treatment efficacy.

Case-control study comparing neuropsychiatric symptoms in electronic health records between COVID-19 hospitalized patients (n=6,619) and non-COVID-19 hospitalized controls up to 150 days post-discharge. Found that fatigue, mood/anxiety, and cognitive impairment were common but occurred at similar rates in both groups, suggesting these symptoms are not specific to post-COVID sequelae.

This case-control study compares chronic neuropsychiatric symptoms in adults with long COVID (>1 year post-infection) versus never-infected controls using app-based questionnaires, mental health measures, and neurocognitive tests. Key findings show significantly higher fatigue in the post-COVID group, with lack of pre-infection vaccination and material deprivation predicting higher symptom burden, and symptoms clustering into cognitive-fatigue and anxiety-depression phenotypes.

This nested case-control study examines circulating mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) and cellular damage markers in 128 long COVID patients versus 100 recovered controls, analyzing associations with cognitive function, psychological distress, and inflammation. The findings show PASC patients have lower relative ccf-mtDNA and elevated CRP, with mitochondrial dysfunction potentially mediating inflammation differences between groups.

Case-control study examining sociodemographic factors, biomarkers, and comorbidities associated with Long COVID and post-acute complications in UK Biobank. This is an observational analysis of existing biobank data without any intervention, treatment, or therapeutic evaluation.

This case-control study measured plasma biomarkers linked to Alzheimer's disease pathology in UK Biobank participants before and after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding associations between infection and β-amyloid pathology changes. While it studies post-infection sequelae, the focus is on dementia risk and neurodegenerative pathology rather than long COVID syndrome per se, and it is not a treatment study.

Case-control study comparing extended coagulation profiles in children with long COVID versus those who recovered post-infection. Found elevated D-dimer levels in long COVID patients, particularly those with three or more persistent symptoms, suggesting endothelial involvement in pediatric post-COVID condition.

Case-control study comparing heart rate variability (HRV) at rest and during deep breathing in 21 long COVID patients versus 20 controls. Found significant reductions in HRV measures in long COVID patients, suggesting impaired cardiac autonomic control.

Case-control study comparing 39 long COVID patients with erectile dysfunction to 20 healthy controls, measuring hormone levels (testosterone, LH, FSH, SHBG) and sexual function. Found significantly lower testosterone and free testosterone in long COVID patients with ED, suggesting hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis dysfunction, but the study is observational with no intervention tested.

Case-control study analyzing host genetic variants associated with COVID-19 severity and long-COVID in a Colombian population using NGS. Identified genetic associations and developed a predictive model combining genetic and clinical variables, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared visual reaction time and correct responses in a stereoscopic virtual reality environment between 130 post-COVID syndrome patients and 49 healthy controls. The study found that PCS patients had significantly slower reaction times and fewer correct responses, suggesting that VR-based testing of stereoscopic vision could serve as a novel objective diagnostic marker for cognitive impairment in long COVID.

A case-control study examining the prevalence and factors associated with erectile dysfunction (ED) in 609 Japanese men hospitalized with COVID-19 one to two years after acute infection. ED was present in 19% of participants and was associated with depression, anxiety, pain/discomfort, and sleep disturbance, but not with COVID-19 severity or vaccination status.

A UK multicentre case-control study comparing functional outcomes in COVID-19 patients with versus without neurological or psychiatric complications. The study is observational (comparing existing cases and controls without assigning treatment) and appears to be a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data rather than a primary intervention trial.

This case-control study compared 44 type 2 diabetes patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome to 21 without PCS, measuring mitochondrial DNA levels, HbA1c, and inflammatory markers. The study identifies low mtDNA content and elevated HbA1c as independent predictive factors for PCS development but does not test any treatment or intervention.

Genome-wide association study (GWAS) of post-COVID syndrome severity in 2,247 German participants, examining genetic variants associated with PCS symptom complexes. Identifies suggestive genetic associations with olfactory dysfunction and cellular immune processes, but finds no genome-wide significant variants, indicating complex polygenic etiology.

Case-control study comparing retinal and choroidal microvasculature between COVID-19 patients and healthy controls at acute phase and 3 months post-infection using OCTA and OCT imaging. Found reduced vascular density and choroidal vascularity index in COVID-19 patients acutely, with further reductions in deep capillary plexus density at 3 months, indicating long-term microvascular changes.

A nested case-control study examining risk factors for cardiac-related post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 using Hong Kong Hospital Authority electronic health records. Identifies hospitalization and peripheral vascular disease as risk factors, and shows COVID-19 vaccination is protective against cardiac PASC.

Population-based case-control study comparing 1,706 Icelanders with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection to 14,398 controls, assessing 88 symptoms and objective physical measures 5-18 months post-infection. Found 41 symptoms associated with infection but few objective physical differences (poorer smell/taste, grip strength, memory recall), estimating long COVID prevalence at 7%.

A case-control study evaluating cognitive remediation therapy (CRT) in 15 COVID-19 survivors with post-acute cognitive deficits compared to 30 matched untreated controls. CRT showed significant improvement in global cognitive functioning and verbal fluency, with benefits persisting at follow-up.

Case-control study examining the association between ABO blood group and post-COVID-19 syndrome (long COVID) in outpatients with mild acute COVID-19. Finds blood group O is associated with 6-fold increased risk of PCS and more intense inflammatory burden compared to other blood groups.

Danish-Swedish case-control study comparing cognitive performance, psychological distress, and hand grip strength in 181 post-COVID syndrome patients versus 155 recovered controls. Found reduced cognitive processing speed in PCS patients, particularly those infected early in the pandemic, though differences were not clinically significant.

This case-control study compares plasma cytokine profiles in 20 neuro-PASC patients versus 20 matched controls to identify immune dysregulation markers. It finds reduced TNFα and downstream chemokines in neuro-PASC cases, suggesting immune attenuation rather than hyperinflammation.

Case-control study comparing polysomnographic parameters in 17 long-COVID patients with insomnia versus 34 matched chronic insomnia controls without long-COVID history. Findings show that insomnia in long-COVID patients resembles typical chronic insomnia on PSG, with no significant differences between groups, suggesting similar pathophysiology and therapeutic approaches.

This case-control cohort study examines neurological outcomes in SARS-CoV-2 infected versus uninfected adults, comparing acute (<3 months) and post-acute (3-9 months) phases.
