The study found significantly increased risk of death and new neurological disorders (encephalopathy, dementia, seizure, brain fog, inflammatory myopathy, coma) in infected individuals, particularly those with premorbid neurological conditions.

A nested case-control study comparing long COVID patients with and without significant fatigue to identify risk factors and explore pathophysiology. Found that peak exercise heart rate and memory impairment were independent risk factors for fatigue, suggesting a limbic-vagal mechanism.

A prospective case-control study comparing symptom trajectories and immune responses in mild COVID-19 cases (n=233) followed for 12-18 months versus seronegative controls. The study documents high prevalence of persistent symptoms (46% at 12 months) including fatigue, cognitive problems, and dyspnea, with associations between spike-specific immune responses and symptom burden, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case-control study examining endothelial dysfunction one month post-discharge in COVID-19 hospitalized patients versus controls using flow-mediated dilation. This is a cross-sectional assessment of post-COVID sequelae (long COVID) without any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing cardiovascular and thrombotic event risk in 3,023 severe COVID-19 patients treated with mechanical ventilation versus 28,463 matched controls over 6 months post-discharge. Found significantly increased risk for ASCVD (HR 4.0) and pulmonary embolism (HR 89.8) in discharged ICU patients, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Prospective case-control study comparing cardiac structure, function, perfusion, and myocardial energetics in 20 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients versus 10 matched controls using CMR and 31P-MRS imaging. Found no significant differences in cardiac parameters between groups, suggesting myocardial abnormalities are not a major feature of post-COVID-19 syndrome in this cohort.

This case-control study compared COVID-19 survivors (n=127) with uninfected controls (n=48) at 3-year follow-up to assess long-term cardiovascular outcomes. Cases showed significantly higher arterial stiffness (diastolic reflection area) and lower hemoglobin levels, suggesting potential chronic cardiovascular and hematologic effects of COVID-19 infection.

A case-control study comparing cardiopulmonary limitations in young long COVID patients versus healthy controls. The study characterizes functional impairments but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Case-control study examining genetic variants associated with cardiorespiratory symptoms in long COVID patients (n=2,147). Found no significant associations between genetic variants and cardiorespiratory symptoms of long COVID, though cases had a more favorable cardiovascular risk profile than controls.

A case-control study comparing 174 COVID-19 recovered patients with 75 controls at 5-month follow-up to assess residual myocardial and autonomic injury. The study found reduced heart rate variability (RMSSD) in COVID-recovered subjects, indicating poor autonomic nervous system function, but no differences in cardiac biomarkers or blood pressure.

A case-control study nested within the HEROES-RECOVER cohort examining whether COVID-19 mRNA vaccination reduces the risk of post-COVID conditions in persons with mild infections during Delta and Omicron variant periods. The study found that 3 vaccine doses were associated with lower odds of gastrointestinal, neurological, and other PCC-related symptoms compared to unvaccinated participants.

This case-control study examines the long-term risk of arrhythmic events in patients who survived critical COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation, compared to matched population controls with 12-month follow-up. While it documents increased arrhythmia risk post-ICU, it does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months after infection) but rather acute COVID-19 complications in ICU survivors, and is observational without testing an intervention.

Case-control study comparing cardiovascular health and physical functioning between non-hospitalised ex-COVID-19 patients and age/sex-matched healthy controls at 5 months post-infection. Found no significant differences in cardiovascular parameters or physical functioning between groups, suggesting no increased long-term cardiovascular risk in home-recovered COVID-19 patients.

Propensity score-matched case-control analysis comparing preinfection neutralizing antibody titers between tertiary hospital staff who had Omicron BA.5 breakthrough infections (cases) and those who did not (controls). The study found that lower preinfection antibody titers predicted breakthrough infection risk, but antibody levels were not associated with long COVID incidence among infected individuals.

This paper investigates complement system activation and immunological characteristics in IgA nephropathy (IgAN) patients who experienced COVID-19, comparing them to IgAN patients without COVID-19 history. While it examines post-COVID renal complications, it is not about long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection) and does not study a treatment intervention.

A matched case-control study comparing long-COVID symptoms in hemodialysis patients versus matched controls without COVID-19, using the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale at baseline, 1 month, and 6 months. The study found hemodialysis patients with COVID-19 experienced significantly worsened fatigue, dyspnea, and decreased perceived health compared to pre-COVID period and matched controls.

This case-control study compared 6,061 COVID-19-positive Quebec healthcare workers with 4,390 test-negative controls to assess the prevalence and characteristics of post-COVID conditions (PCC), including physical, psychological, and cognitive symptoms. The study found PCC4w in 46% of nonhospitalized cases and 76% of hospitalized cases, with hospitalization, female sex, and age as risk factors; cognitive dysfunction (concentration difficulties, forgetfulness, disorganization) was reported by a substantial proportion and was associated with PCC symptoms, psychological distress, and fatigue.

Case-control study examining COVID-19-like symptoms at 6 weeks post-infection in healthcare personnel, stratified by vaccination status. While the study measures post-infection symptoms, it focuses on acute/subacute COVID-19 outcomes and vaccine effectiveness rather than long COVID as a persistent condition, and does not test a treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

Case-control study examining the association between COVID-19 vaccination status and post-COVID-19 venous thrombosis risk among Military Health System beneficiaries. This is a secondary observational analysis of existing medical records rather than a treatment intervention trial.

A case-control study comparing health outcomes and mortality in adults with post-COVID-19 condition versus controls over a one-year follow-up period. Results showed elevated rates of adverse health outcomes and mortality in the PCC population, highlighting the need for continued clinical monitoring.

This case-control study compares speech and swallowing outcomes in COVID-19 vs non-COVID ARDS patients post-extubation from mechanical ventilation. The authors explicitly state data extraction is incomplete and results are not ready, making this a protocol/incomplete study without confirmatory conclusions.

This case-control study examined the frequency of newly verified or worsened hypertension in 108 post-COVID patients compared to acute COVID patients, stratified by time since infection. Hypertension occurred in 12% of patients, with higher prevalence in chronic phase (90-180 days post-infection) and significantly elevated blood pressure compared to the rest of the cohort.

This case-control study examines monocyte subset distribution and activation markers in hemodialysis patients with acute COVID-19 infection at three timepoints (before, during, and ~10 months after). While it includes follow-up data, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 pathophysiology and immune responses during active infection rather than persistent post-COVID symptoms or interventions.

This case-control study examines the prevalence of non-neuropsychiatric long COVID symptoms in 274 children and adolescents visiting a pediatric infectious disease clinic. The study found prolonged symptoms were significantly more frequent in the long COVID case group (17.0% vs 4.8%), with abdominal pain being the most common symptom.

This case-controlled study compared circulating platelet activation markers in 14 children with Long COVID versus 14 healthy controls using flow cytometry. Children with Long COVID showed significantly increased expression of the P-selectin activation marker compared to controls.

Multicenter case-control study comparing long-term pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in COVID-19 ARDS survivors versus matched controls at 22 months post-discharge. Found persistent impairments in lung function (reduced DLCO), exercise capacity, and quality of life in survivors, with imaging abnormalities including ground-glass opacities and emphysema.

This case-control study compares pulse wave velocity and arterial stiffness in post-COVID patients with and without de novo arterial hypertension (90 patients: 30 cases, 60 controls). The study found that arterial stiffness was significantly associated with post-COVID syndrome, with 4.9-7.9 times higher risk of hypertension in those with stiffness compared to controls, particularly in the 35-49 age group.

Case-control study of 64 patients with post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis, comparing clinical characteristics, imaging findings, and outcomes between those who survived and those who died. Identifies risk factors (smoking, asthma) associated with ICU admission and mortality in severe pulmonary complications following COVID-19.

A case-control study comparing 369 COVID-19 patients with myalgia at hospital admission to 369 without myalgia, assessing long-term musculoskeletal pain 7 months post-discharge. Patients with acute myalgia had higher odds of developing persistent musculoskeletal post-COVID pain and multiple post-COVID symptoms.

Prospective case-controlled study comparing cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) results in 61 children with long COVID versus 29 healthy controls. Children with long COVID showed significantly impaired functional capacity (lower peak VO2) and signs of deconditioning compared to controls, suggesting CPET as a diagnostic tool for phenotyping functional limitations.

This case-control study examines the association between small fibre neuropathy and painful long-COVID syndrome by comparing 26 patients with painful long-COVID, 33 with painless long-COVID, and 30 asymptomatic post-COVID controls using clinical assessments, quantitative sensory testing, and skin biopsies. The study finds that approximately 50% of patients with painful long-COVID symptoms meet diagnostic criteria for small fibre neuropathy, though this complication is unrelated to demographic and COVID-19 clinical variables.

This case-control study compares the prevalence of neck pain between 439 post-acute COVID-19 survivors and 439 age/sex-matched unaffected controls in Bangladesh (n=878 total). Neck pain was significantly more common in post-acute COVID patients (21.4% vs 8.9%), with adjusted OR=2.63, but this is an observational prevalence study with no treatment intervention.

A multicenter case-control study comparing headache prevalence and risk factors between postacute COVID-19 survivors (≤90 days post-infection) and non-COVID controls. The study found higher headache prevalence in COVID survivors (26.2% vs 10.7%) but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Case-control study comparing neuropsychiatric symptoms (fatigue, mood/anxiety, cognition) in 6,619 COVID-19 hospitalized patients versus non-COVID hospitalized controls up to 150 days post-hospitalization. Symptoms occurred at similar rates in both groups, suggesting they may reflect post-hospitalization sequelae rather than COVID-19-specific effects.

This retrospective case-control study analyzes 8,325 long COVID patients matched to 41,625 controls from 31 U.S. health systems to identify demographic, clinical, and comorbidity risk factors associated with PASC. The analysis identifies middle age, female sex, severe acute COVID-19, and specific comorbidities as significant risk factors, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective EHR analysis comparing 1,086 long COVID patients with matched controls to identify risk factors for long COVID development. Found that chronic pulmonary disease, migraine, and fibromyalgia history, along with severe acute infection markers, were associated with long COVID diagnosis.

Case-control study among Brazilian healthcare workers examining risk factors for long COVID development. Identifies female sex, age, and multiple infections as risk factors, while vaccination and newer variants were protective—but this is an observational study of risk factors, not a treatment intervention trial.

This paper develops and validates a precision phenotyping algorithm using EHR data from 295k patients to identify PASC (long COVID) cohorts more accurately than ICD-10 codes, identifying 24k PASC patients with 79.9% precision and estimating 22.8% prevalence. The study is a methodological/algorithmic contribution for cohort identification rather than an intervention trial, focusing on improving case definition for future research.

This retrospective case-control study investigates etiological factors associated with chronic pain syndrome in 120 young adults with post-COVID-19 conditions. The study identifies prolonged isolation, fear, stress overload, and impaired rehabilitation as significant risk factors for chronic pain development.

Case-control cohort study of 39,746 incarcerated individuals examining whether COVID-19 infection increases risk of incident hypertension in the post-acute period. Finds COVID-19 significantly increases hypertension incidence (HR 1.44-2.05) with largest effects in those with higher BMI and pre-pandemic blood pressure, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
Pilot case-control study examining MRI findings in recovered COVID-19 patients with persistent anosmia or hyposmia. Descriptive imaging study with no treatment intervention or outcomes evaluation.

This population-based case-control study investigates pre-existing respiratory conditions as risk factors for long COVID in non-hospitalized patients with mild-to-moderate acute COVID-19. The study finds that patients with long COVID have significantly higher prevalence of pre-pandemic respiratory illnesses (asthma, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infections) compared to matched controls.

A retrospective case-control survey of 1,816 U.S. and U.K. respondents investigating whether joint hypermobility is a risk factor for developing Long COVID. Both generalized joint hypermobility and extreme hypermobility were found to significantly predict Long COVID risk, with extreme hypermobility showing particularly strong association (OR 2.12).

This study compares brain imaging and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in COVID-19 ICU patients with delirium versus non-COVID encephalopathy controls, examining acute brain injury during active hospitalization. The paper focuses on acute-phase COVID-19 complications in hospitalized patients, not post-COVID sequelae or long COVID, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case-control study examining the association between pre-infection COVID-19 vaccination and long COVID incidence and symptom severity. Findings show vaccination is associated with reduced long COVID risk and fewer symptoms, but this is an observational study of vaccination as a risk factor, not a treatment intervention trial.

Case-control cohort study of 29,470 incarcerated individuals examining the association between COVID-19 infection and incident diabetes mellitus in the post-acute period. Found that COVID-19 significantly increased diabetes risk (HRR: 1.17), with estimated 2-year cumulative risk increase from 2.7% to 3.2%, though testing frequency changes may partially explain the effect.

This case-control study used quantitative muscle MRI to assess muscular alterations in 20 post-COVID-19 patients versus 20 healthy controls, examining possible mechanisms for musculoskeletal complaints and fatigue. While no signs of inflammation or dystrophy were found, diffusion tensor imaging revealed microstructural abnormalities potentially reflecting reversible fiber hypotrophy from deconditioning.

This multicentre case-control study compares long COVID symptom prevalence and severity between obese and non-obese hospitalised COVID-19 survivors at 7.2 months post-discharge. Obesity was associated with a greater number of post-COVID symptoms and poor sleep quality, but no significant differences in individual symptom prevalence were found.

A case-control study evaluating intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIg) as an immunomodulatory treatment for severe post-COVID syndrome in patients unresponsive to supportive care. The study compares outcomes between post-COVID patients treated with IVIg and appropriate controls, testing whether autoimmune mechanisms can be therapeutically targeted.

This case-control study prospectively compared 280 COVID-19 patients with 264 healthy controls to assess the development of post-infection functional gastrointestinal disorders at 1, 3, and 6 months follow-up. The study found significantly higher rates of IBS, uninvestigated dyspepsia, and chronic bowel dysfunction in COVID-19 patients compared to controls, but it is an observational study documenting disease outcomes rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares coronary microvascular function between patients with chest pain 30-60 days post-COVID-19 and controls without COVID history, measuring angio-derived microcirculatory resistance via angiography. Patients with prior COVID-19 showed significantly elevated microcirculatory resistance, suggesting coronary microvascular dysfunction may contribute to post-COVID chest pain.

This case-control study compared objective and subjective olfactory and gustatory function in 42 post-COVID-19 patients versus 41 matched controls with no COVID history. While it documents significant dysfunction in taste and smell (hyposmia in 73.8% of post-COVID patients), it is a descriptive cross-sectional assessment study, not a treatment/intervention trial, and therefore does not meet criteria for inclusion.

A case-control study comparing serum mast cell activation markers (TPSB2 and CPA3) between 24 long-COVID patients and 24 matched healthy controls with prior COVID-19 infection. The study found no significant differences in mast cell markers between groups and no correlation with exercise intolerance, concluding mast cell activation is not a key pathogenic mechanism in long-COVID.

This case-control study examines asthma control, mental health, and exhaled nitric oxide levels in asthmatic children 1 month after COVID-19 infection. While it measures outcomes post-infection, it does not study long COVID (persistent sequelae weeks-to-months later) or any treatment intervention—it is a cross-sectional assessment of correlations between asthma control and anxiety/depression in the acute post-infection period.

This case-control study compares long COVID incidence and clinical features in rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis patients versus healthy controls at 12 weeks post-infection. It documents higher symptom burden and disease activity worsening in rheumatic disease patients, particularly females, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case-control study comparing 352 long COVID patients with 1,464 non-long-COVID controls from a retrospective online survey to identify whether joint hypermobility is a risk factor for long COVID. Found that both generalized joint hypermobility and extreme hypermobility significantly predict long COVID risk, operating through increased severity of initial COVID-19 symptoms and direct pathophysiological pathways.

This case-control study from the British COVID Symptom Study Biobank examines whether joint hypermobility is a risk factor for non-recovery from COVID-19 in 3,064 participants surveyed in August 2022. While it finds a significant association between hypermobility and self-reported non-recovery (OR 1.33), this is an observational analysis of biobank data without any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.

Retrospective case-control study comparing post-COVID symptoms in IBD patients versus infected household members without IBD and IBD patients without infection. Study is observational/descriptive with no treatment intervention—it characterizes disease prevalence and associations rather than testing a therapeutic intervention.

Retrospective case-control study comparing luminal areas of large conducting airways between PASC patients, acute COVID-19 patients, and healthy controls using 3D CT reconstruction. Found PASC and COVID-19 patients have significantly enlarged airways compared to controls, but no differences between PASC and acute COVID groups.

This case-control study compares cardiac autonomic function in 14 long-COVID POTS patients versus 15 healthy controls, measuring heart rate variability and hemodynamic responses to head-up tilt. Findings show long-COVID POTS patients have impaired parasympathetic (vagal) modulation with reduced high-frequency heart rate variability, suggesting parasympathetic dysfunction contributes to disease pathophysiology.

This pilot case-control study compared 15 athletes with cardiovascular post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (CV-PASC) to 7 control athletes without prior COVID-19 using stress cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. CV-PASC athletes showed reduced coronary flow reserve and impaired myocardial strain, suggesting coronary microvascular dysfunction related to endothelial injury as a mechanism underlying cardiovascular symptoms in long COVID.

Case-control study comparing 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure profiles in 100 post-COVID POTS patients versus 100 population-based controls. Finds that post-COVID POTS patients show higher mean systolic BP and disrupted circadian BP rhythm, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This case-control study compares blood pressure regulation in 100 COVID-19 patients with new-onset POTS to 100 healthy controls using 24-hour ambulatory monitoring. Post-COVID POTS patients showed significantly higher nighttime systolic BP, more daytime hypotensive episodes, and disrupted BP regulation patterns (non-dipper and reverse-dipper), suggesting altered hemodynamic mechanisms beyond sinus tachycardia.

Case-control study nested within a cohort examining the association between pro-inflammatory cytokines during acute COVID-19 infection and subsequent major depressive disorder, treatment-resistant depression, and suicidal ideation in long COVID patients. The study identifies elevated cytokine levels as a risk factor for psychiatric outcomes in long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares functional autoantibody levels in 4 PASC patients with POTS versus 4 age/gender-matched healthy controls. The study demonstrates elevated autoantibodies to G-protein coupled receptors in POTS patients but is a secondary analysis of previously identified subjects and is too small for statistical testing.

A prospective case-control study comparing long COVID patients with fatigue to COVID-19 recovered controls without fatigue, measuring fatigue severity, sleep, cognition, mood, and inflammatory markers at baseline and 6 months. Physical fatigue improved over time but psychological fatigue persisted, with significant differences in sleep quality, cognitive impairment, anxiety, and TNF-α levels between groups.

A case-control study comparing oculomotor behavior in 75 long COVID patients versus 42 healthy controls using eye-tracking and reading tests. Long COVID patients showed significantly impaired eye movement performance, suggesting cognitive rather than muscular dysfunction, but this is a diagnostic/observational study with no treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared the prevalence of PTSD and Complex PTSD (CPTSD) in individuals with long COVID (n=21) and ME/CFS (n=20) versus healthy controls (n=20) using the International Trauma Questionnaire. Long COVID patients showed significantly higher rates of PTSD (5%) and CPTSD (33%) compared to ME/CFS and controls, with greater symptom scores across all PTSD and DSO (Disturbances in Self-Organization) domains.

Case-control study of 205 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with acute headache versus 410 without acute headache, followed 7.3 months post-discharge. Found that acute-phase headache was associated with higher prevalence of long-term post-COVID headache and fatigue, but the study is observational without any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing long COVID incidence in SLE patients versus healthy matched controls after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Found higher long COVID prevalence in SLE patients (54.5% vs 34.6%) with certain symptoms more common, but this is an epidemiological comparison study, not a treatment intervention trial.

This case-control study compares blood biomarkers of vascular transformation between long COVID patients and controls to identify diagnostic signatures. While it identifies elevated angiogenesis markers, it is a diagnostic/mechanistic study without testing any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case-control study examining uveitis relapse rates in patients with versus without COVID-19 infection in China during late 2022-early 2023. Finds COVID-19 increases relapse risk, but focuses on pre-existing uveitis complications rather than long COVID syndrome or post-acute sequelae.

Case-control study comparing post-COVID-19 neuropsychiatric symptoms in 204 migraine patients versus 204 non-migraine controls 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Migraine patients showed significantly higher rates of fatigue, anosmia, depression, anxiety, insomnia, and chronic headache transformation, but no treatment intervention was tested.

This case-control study compared the prevalence of musculoskeletal health complaints (MHC) between post-acute COVID-19 patients and matched controls who never tested positive, conducted in Bangladesh in 2022. While it found a robust association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and MHC, it is a purely observational epidemiological study with no intervention or treatment evaluation and thus does not qualify as a treatment trial.

This case-control study compares macular thickness between post-COVID-19 patients and healthy controls using optical coherence tomography. While it found subtle retinal thinning in older post-COVID patients, it is not a treatment/intervention trial and does not qualify as a long COVID study (no documentation of persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection, measuring structural changes in acute/early post-infection phase).

This retrospective case-control study from N3C identifies risk factors associated with PASC/long-COVID diagnosis by comparing 8,325 cases to 41,625 matched controls across US health systems. While relevant to long COVID, it is a secondary analysis of observational data focused on epidemiological associations rather than testing a specific treatment intervention.

Case-population study comparing SARS-CoV-2 infection timing (first vs second wave) between long COVID patients and general population in France. Finds long COVID patients more likely to have been infected during the first wave, suggesting contextual factors influence symptom persistence.

This case-control study uses machine learning on Swedish primary care data to identify diagnostic predictors of PASC, including prior COVID-19 hospitalization, fatigue, and post-viral syndromes. It is a retrospective analysis using existing health records without testing any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case-control study examining healthcare utilization patterns in 12,698 Long COVID patients diagnosed in Colorado between 2021-2023 compared to 25,376 matched controls. Found that Long COVID patients significantly increased outpatient healthcare utilization after diagnosis while decreasing acute care usage, suggesting diagnosis improves patient management.

Prospective case-control study comparing cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy findings in 20 long COVID patients versus 10 healthy controls. Study found no significant abnormalities in myocardial structure, function, perfusion, or energy metabolism between groups, suggesting these pathways are not primary drivers of long COVID pathophysiology.

This prospective case-control study examined diaphragm function in 10 patients 1 year after severe COVID-19 ARDS compared to matched controls. Six patients with persistent dyspnea on exertion showed impaired diaphragm function and voluntary activation, suggesting diaphragm dysfunction may contribute to post-COVID exertional dyspnea.

Case-control study comparing prevalence of depression, anxiety, fatigue, and headache in 5,589 long COVID patients versus 47,561 matched controls from Stockholm regional health records. Findings show long COVID patients had higher pre-pandemic and post-diagnosis frequencies of these conditions, suggesting an association between mental health vulnerabilities and long COVID.

This case-control study compared cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging findings in 50 soldiers with cardiopulmonary symptoms following COVID-19 recovery to 50 matched healthy controls, evaluating the prevalence and characteristics of cardiovascular post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (CV PASC). The study found cardiovascular pathology in 12% of symptomatic soldiers and CV PASC in 37% at follow-up, but does not test any treatment intervention.

Multicenter case-control study of 153 COVID-19 patients with post-COVID organizing pneumonia (OP) compared to 140 without OP, examining risk factors, radiological outcomes, and response to corticosteroid treatment. Follow-up over 12 months found progressive radiological improvement but persistent fibrotic-like changes in 57% of OP patients, with higher corticosteroid doses not associated with better long-term prognosis.

This case-control study compared auditory cognitive abilities (attention and memory) between 40 post-COVID-19 patients and 40 matched controls using psychophysical tests and electrophysiological measures. Post-COVID patients showed significantly impaired auditory cognitive function and prolonged P300 latency, but the study does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This nested case-control study of 899 female COVID-19 survivors (47 cases with fatigue vs 852 controls) conducted 2 years post-hospitalization in Wuhan, China, identified age and cerebrovascular disease as significant risk factors for post-COVID fatigue. Fatigue was moderately correlated with depression but not airway obstruction, suggesting distinct mechanistic pathways.

Case-control study examining factors associated with need for physical rehabilitation in post-COVID patients, comparing those from a post-COVID clinic undergoing rehabilitation with COVID-19 patients from the general population who did not need rehabilitation. Post-COVID sarcopenia, age >60, acute hospitalization, and comorbidities increased rehabilitation need, while vaccination with ≥3 doses reduced it.

This case-control study compared autonomic cardiovascular regulation between 13 long-COVID POTS patients and 16 healthy female controls using orthostatic stress tests, respiratory sinus arrhythmia, and Valsalva maneuvers. The study found that long-COVID POTS patients had impaired parasympathetic function (reduced RMSSD and high-frequency heart rate variability) but normal sympathetic function, suggesting parasympathetic dysfunction may contribute to long-COVID POTS pathogenesis.

Longitudinal case-control study comparing cognitive performance and mental health in 50 post-COVID-19 patients and 48 matched healthy controls over 10 months, starting 2 years post-infection. Patients showed initial cognitive deficits but improved over time, though fatigue and mental health issues persisted.

Retrospective case-control study comparing vitamin D levels between 50 long COVID patients and 50 matched controls at 6 months post-hospitalization. Found significantly lower vitamin D levels in long COVID patients (20.1 vs 23.2 ng/mL), particularly in those with neurocognitive symptoms, with vitamin D deficiency independently associated with long COVID diagnosis.

Case-control study comparing vestibular function in 30 post-COVID patients (2 weeks to 1 year post-infection) versus 30 matched controls using videonystagmography. Found increased saccade velocity and smooth pursuit phase shift in post-COVID group, with BPPV diagnosed in 20% of cases, suggesting COVID-19 affects the vestibular system.

A prospective case-control study comparing procedural motor skill learning in 105 long COVID patients versus 210 matched controls over 2 days of sequential typing training. Patients showed comparable early learning but significantly reduced overnight consolidation and slower initial performance, suggesting deficits in procedural memory formation and executive function.

Retrospective case series of 16 long COVID patients with new-onset small fiber neuropathy (SFN), comparing 9 patients treated with IVIG to 7 untreated controls. IVIG treatment showed significant clinical response in neuropathic symptoms (9/9 treated vs 3/7 untreated, p=0.02) and was associated with evidence of neurovascular dysregulation and dysautonomia on cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

This case-control study examines long COVID symptom presentation and disease burden in patients with spinal cord injury (SCI) at a rehabilitation center in Bangladesh. The study is observational and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, focusing instead on symptom characterization and risk factors.

Nested case-control study examining the association between NSAID use during acute COVID-19 and long COVID development in 225,458 Korean patients. Found suggestive but not statistically significant increased odds of long COVID with NSAID exposure; antiviral drugs showed stronger association with long COVID risk.

A pilot case-control study comparing 10 long COVID patients with cognitive symptoms to 7 fully recovered COVID-19 patients on neuropsychological tests, quality of life, and biomarkers. Found lower letter fluency, quality of life, and NGF levels in the long COVID group, with evidence of prolonged inflammatory processes.

This case-control study examines associations between inflammatory biomarkers (ACE2, IL-8, PGE2, CRP), periodontal clinical parameters, and COVID-19 history in 47 participants. While the study finds elevated biomarkers in individuals with COVID-19 history, it is a cross-sectional biomarker study of periodontal disease, not a study of long COVID interventions or outcomes.

A case-control study comparing olfactory function in healthcare workers who recovered from COVID-19 versus unexposed controls at 15 months and 2.6 years post-infection. Found significantly higher prevalence of olfactory dysfunction (37% vs 20%) and parosmia (51% vs 5%) in COVID-recovered individuals, with symptoms persisting in 24% at 2.6 years.

This case-control study compares pulmonary function and IgG antibody responses between COVID-19 recovered individuals (n=29) and controls (n=64), assessing respiratory outcomes and immune response to vaccination. While the study documents long COVID pulmonary abnormalities, it is observational without any treatment intervention—vaccination was administered to all participants for comparison purposes, not as an experimental intervention being tested.

Case-control study comparing testosterone levels in 55 COVID-19 recovered post-hospitalized male patients (~60 days post-discharge) versus 40 age/BMI-matched controls. Found significantly lower testosterone and higher prevalence of testosterone deficiency (50.9%) in recovered patients, with visceral obesity as a predictor.

This cross-sectional study compares levels of soluble fms-like thyroxine kinase-1 and endothelial antibodies in 118 acute coronary syndrome patients with prior COVID-19 versus 121 without COVID-19 history. The study found elevated biomarkers and more severe ACS outcomes in the post-COVID group but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing neuropsychological and mood profiles of 45 COVID-19 patients versus 16 matched controls from 2021-2022. Found no significant differences in cognitive function or mood between groups, suggesting COVID-19 survivors have similar cognitive and psychological outcomes as controls.

Case-control study comparing autonomic responses to head-up tilt table testing between 16 long COVID patients and 10 recovered controls. Long COVID patients showed higher COMPASS 31 scores, elevated heart rate during tilt, and more frequent symptoms during testing, but most did not meet diagnostic criteria for abnormal hemodynamic response.

A case-control study comparing sleep disorder incidence in patients with primary headaches who had COVID-19 (n=135) versus those without (n=77). The study found that 28.8% of COVID-19 patients developed new-onset sleep disorders persisting ≥6 months, but this is an observational comparison without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

This case-control study compared diaphragm function and central activation in 10 severe COVID-19 ARDS survivors one year post-discharge against 10 healthy controls using ultrasound and invasive pressure measurements. Survivors showed reduced diaphragm thickening, impaired central voluntary activation, and persistent dyspnea on exertion despite normal pulmonary and cardiac function tests.

This case-control study examines the effects of acute and chronic SARS-CoV-2 infection (Omicron variant) on male reproductive function, semen parameters, and sex hormones in vaccinated men. While the paper does compare COVID-infected and uninfected groups, it focuses on acute COVID infection effects rather than long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing persistent symptoms in 206 children with post-COVID-19 condition to 176 controls with other acute respiratory infections at one year post-infection. Found low prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (1.5%) but significantly higher rates of taste/smell disturbances and fatigue in COVID-19 cases compared to controls.

This case-control study compares left atrial strain and structural remodeling between 30 post-COVID patients with exertional dyspnea and 30 healthy controls. The study identifies reduced left atrial reservoir strain as a predictor of post-COVID dyspnea and fatigue but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study compared 80 long COVID patients seeking infertility treatment, stratified by ART success/failure, to identify risk factors associated with unsuccessful assisted reproductive technology outcomes. The study identified psychological symptoms (depression, anxiety), stress, endocrine dysfunction, metabolic disorders, and menstrual irregularities as significant risk factors but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing physical and mental fatigue in 46 COVID-19 long-haulers with PIFS versus 46 recovered controls without residuals, using clinical fatigue questionnaires and electromyography. Found that prolonged COVID-19 illness duration and higher ferritin levels predicted PIFS, with electrophysiological abnormalities in peripheral motor units.

Case-control study comparing persistent symptoms in 103 COVID-19 survivors (13-16 weeks post-infection) versus 40 matched controls. Found 41.75% prevalence of post-COVID symptoms, with fatigue most common (38.83%), and identified hospitalization, ICU stay, and comorbidities as significant risk factors.

This case-control study examines the association between post-COVID-19 myocardial infarction and antiphospholipid syndrome in patients at Qena University Hospital. The study found that APS was significantly associated with post-COVID-19 MI, with elevated antiphospholipid antibodies and inflammatory markers in MI cases, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This case-control study compared 30 COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID syndrome symptoms to 30 asymptomatic survivors to identify predictive biomarkers for post-COVID syndrome. The authors found that elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, LDH, IL-6) and severe lung involvement on initial CT imaging were associated with later development of post-COVID syndrome.

A multicenter case-control study comparing cognitive function and neurological symptoms in 176 post-COVID survivors (at 4 weeks post-diagnosis) versus 92 healthy controls across Algeria, Egypt, and Libya. The study found cognitive impairment in 32.3% of survivors, with higher prevalence in females, smokers, and highly educated individuals, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared periodontal disease markers and proinflammatory cytokine levels (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) between long COVID patients and non-COVID controls with gingivitis or periodontitis. The study found higher IL-6 and TNF-α in periodontitis patients with long COVID, but no significant differences in gingivitis patients, suggesting a potential but inconsistent association between long COVID and periodontal inflammation.

Case-control study examining the relationship between comorbid diabetes mellitus and long COVID-19 symptoms in 91 COVID-19 patients from Indonesian hospitals. Found no significant association between diabetes and long COVID risk (p=0.240), concluding diabetes is not a risk factor for post-acute symptoms.

This case-control study compares oxidative stress markers and biochemical indicators between post-COVID-19 patients with neurological symptoms and uninfected controls. The findings reveal significant alterations in oxidative and inflammatory biomarkers in post-COVID patients, particularly those with neurological complaints, suggesting potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

This matched retrospective case-control study compares the incidence of new diagnoses and health care resource use among 41,577 patients with prior COVID-19 infection versus matched controls over a 6-month period, stratified by Omicron versus pre-Omicron waves. It analyzes the influence of vaccination status on long COVID symptoms and health system burden but is an observational epidemiological study without testing any active intervention or treatment.

This case-control study examined whether diabetes is a risk factor for long-term post-COVID symptoms in 145 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with diabetes matched with 144 controls. The study found no significant differences in post-COVID symptom burden, anxiety, depression, or sleep quality between diabetic and non-diabetic patients, concluding diabetes was not a protective or risk factor for long-term post-COVID outcomes.

Case-control study examining one-carbon metabolism markers and genetic polymorphisms in post-COVID patients who developed acute myocardial infarction versus controls without AMI. This is a prognostic/biomarker study, not a treatment intervention trial, and focuses on risk factor identification rather than testing any therapeutic intervention.

This retrospective cohort study compared the frequency of pericardial effusion detected by transthoracic echocardiography in 110 patients who recovered from COVID-19 (1-2 months post-infection) versus a matched control group from pre-pandemic records. Pericardial effusion was found in 43% of COVID-recovered patients versus 3% of controls, suggesting it is a specific post-COVID manifestation requiring echocardiography monitoring.

This case-control study compares one-carbon metabolism markers (homocysteine and folic acid) in 49 cardiac patients at various timepoints after COVID-19 (6, 12, and 24 months) versus 33 controls without COVID-19 history. The findings show that post-COVID cardiac patients have significantly elevated homocysteine and reduced folic acid levels, with an exacerbated imbalance at 24 months, suggesting disrupted one-carbon metabolism may underlie long COVID-related cardiovascular complications.

This case-control study compared auditory thresholds in COVID-19 patients (measured ~170 days post-infection) with 589 matched controls, finding no significant differences in hearing across frequencies or timepoints. The study does not examine treatment interventions and should be excluded as it is observational research without intervention.

This case-control study examined the relationship between comorbid hypertension and long COVID-19 symptoms in 120 COVID-19 patients (65 cases, 55 controls) from two Indonesian hospitals. The study found a statistically significant correlation between hypertension and long COVID-19 symptoms, with hypertensive patients showing higher risk of experiencing symptoms like fatigue, cough, and dyspnea.

Case-control study comparing fatigue and depression symptoms in 185 SARS-CoV-2 positive subjects vs 168 negative controls at 12 and 19 months post-infection. Found initial 3.8-fold higher odds of fatigue in positive group, declining to 2.6-fold at follow-up, with motor fatigue more persistent than cognitive fatigue or depression.

This retrospective matched case-control study examined longer-term mortality in dementia patients with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to those without infection. The paper identifies risk factors for excess mortality in the post-acute phase but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional case-control study compared symptom prevalence between 3,694 long COVID patients and 3,672 negative controls in Japan at 4-18 months post-infection. The study identified key long COVID symptoms (brain fog, dyspnea, anosmia, ageusia) with elevated odds ratios but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A case-control study examining microvascular hemodynamics and thrombosis in COVID-19 survivors compared to healthy controls using conjunctival video capillaroscopy. Found significantly reduced blood velocity and increased microvascular occlusion in COVID-19 patients despite thromboprophylaxis, suggesting a possible mechanism for long COVID symptoms.

This case-control study compares the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) between 52 long COVID patients and 80 healthy controls with prior COVID-19 to identify predictive biomarkers for long COVID. The study found AIP to be an independent predictor of long COVID but does not test any treatment or intervention.

A case-control study comparing anxiety disorder clinical features and predictors in 145 individuals with recent COVID-19 infection versus controls. The study identified that anxiety disorders develop more frequently in the post-COVID period, with circadian rhythm disorders and prior anxiety levels as key predictors.

This case-control study compared physical deconditioning patterns between 150 COVID-19 survivors and 150 non-infected controls during the post-pandemic period (2021-2022). The study found that COVID-19 patients exhibited significantly more severe deconditioning, fatigue, and dyspnea, with greater impairment in daily activities, but did not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This case-control study examines myocardial perfusion imaging in patients recovered from severe COVID-19 hospitalization compared to matched controls and healthy volunteers. The study focuses on acute myocardial damage and microvascular sequelae in the immediate post-COVID period (~2 months post-discharge), not on long COVID syndrome or any long-term treatment interventions.

A case-control study comparing endocrine parameters in COVID-19 survivors versus pre-pandemic controls at 6 months post-infection. Found suppressed thyroid function, elevated prolactin, and lower testosterone in COVID-19 survivors, indicating long-term endocrine consequences without intervention testing.

Secondary analysis of a matched case-control dataset examining demographic and medical risk factors associated with PASC dysautonomia in US active duty service members. Identifies dysautonomia as a rare but significant post-COVID condition with distinct risk profiles, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A prospective case-control study comparing brainstem neurochemical profiles using 7T MR spectroscopy in 34 hospitalized COVID-19 patients versus 15 healthy controls. Found correlations between inflammation severity and myo-inositol concentration but no significant metabolite differences between groups, highlighting the need for further investigation into neuroinflammation in post-acute COVID-19.

This case-control cross-sectional study compared hemoglobin and hematocrit levels between COVID-19 non-naive (n=28) and naive (n=196) adults to investigate long-term effects of COVID-19 on oxygen-carrying capacity. Results showed a trend toward lower hematocrit in females with COVID-19 history and vitamin B12 intake was significantly associated with hemoglobin levels in COVID-19 non-naive males.

Case-control study investigating whether pre-existing migraine is associated with post-COVID symptoms in 57 hospitalized COVID-19 survivors with migraine history versus 144 matched controls. Found that migraine patients had significantly more post-COVID fatigue but no difference in headache prevalence.

This prospective case-control study (n=252) compares platelet dense granule storage pool deficiency (δ-SPD) in POTS patients with and without COVID-19 history against healthy controls. The work identifies δ-SPD as a comorbidity in long COVID patients with POTS but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared long COVID symptoms and biomarkers between people living with HIV (PLWH) and people not living with HIV (PNLWH) at 6 months post-infection. PLWH exhibited higher cardiovascular risk biomarkers but lower symptom burden and similar inflammatory markers compared to PNLWH, suggesting HIV status modifies long COVID presentation.

This case-control study compares the prevalence of hypothyroidism and bipolar spectrum disorders in long COVID patients with CFS/ME symptoms versus pre-pandemic control populations. The study identifies these conditions as potential predisposing factors but does not test any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing 20 PASC patients with persistent respiratory symptoms to 20 healthy controls, measuring lung perfusion, clotting, and autoimmune responses. Found correlations between IgA antibodies and clinical symptoms/clotting parameters, but is primarily an observational mechanistic study without treatment intervention.

Cross-sectional case-control study comparing sleep quality and sleep-disordered breathing in post-hospitalized COVID-19 patients (n=47) versus non-infected controls (n=46). Found significantly higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (97.4% vs 72.5%), worse sleep quality, and greater daytime sleepiness in COVID-19 cases, though AHI differences were not significant after adjusting for age and BMI.

Case-control study evaluating the effectiveness of physical rehabilitation combined with L-acetyl-carnitine therapy versus rehabilitation alone in post-COVID syndrome patients. Treatment group showed statistically significant improvements in pain scores, quality of life, and depression, with combined exercise and acetyl-carnitine identified as a promising treatment approach.

Case-control study comparing 17 women with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome to 15 matched controls on functional status, mood state, and physical activity. Found that PASC patients had elevated mood disturbance, poorer functional status, and reduced leisure-time physical activity compared to controls, but this is an observational comparison study without treatment intervention.

This case-control study compared autoantibody levels against vasoactive receptors in 100 long COVID patients versus three control groups to investigate a proposed pathomechanism for orthostatic intolerance. The study found elevated ETAR autoantibodies in long COVID patients and correlation with quality-of-life impairment but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective propensity score-matched case-control study examining whether early treatment with monoclonal antibodies or antivirals reduces long COVID risk in 737 COVID-19 patients. Treated patients showed significantly lower long COVID incidence (11% vs 34% in controls), with mAbs/antivirals independently associated with reduced risk (OR 0.44).

Case-control study comparing endothelial function (flow-mediated dilation) in 133 convalescent COVID-19 patients versus 133 matched controls. Found significantly impaired endothelial dysfunction in post-acute COVID-19 patients, correlated with pulmonary severity, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

A case-control study comparing symptom prevalence between COVID-19-infected and non-infected individuals in Brazil, analyzing 2,886 participants from October 2023 to May 2024. The study found that long COVID significantly impacts cognitive health with memory problems, fatigue, and shortness of breath being most prevalent, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study compares Enhanced External Counterpulsation (EECP) treatment outcomes in 33 long COVID patients to 33 matched controls, finding significant improvements in fatigue, dyspnea, and functional capacity in the EECP group. Results suggest EECP is a potential low-risk treatment for long COVID symptoms, though the study is limited by small sample size and lack of information about concurrent treatments in the control group.

Case-control study nested in a prospective cohort comparing cardio-pulmonary function and biomarkers between long COVID patients with and without persistent headache (3+ months post-infection). Found no significant differences in cardio-pulmonary dysfunction between groups, suggesting headache persistence is not causally linked to cardio-pulmonary dysfunction.

This case-control study assessed functional capacity and cardiopulmonary function in 34 individuals with persistent symptoms 17 months after severe COVID-19 infection using 6-minute walk testing, spirometry, and quality of life measures. Individuals with long COVID demonstrated significantly reduced exercise tolerance, lower oxygen uptake, and decreased quality of life compared to controls.

This retrospective case-control study of 1.3 million patients examined anxiety diagnosis incidence up to four years post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing COVID-19 patients to non-COVID-19 controls. COVID-19 patients had significantly higher likelihood of anxiety diagnosis (aOR=1.26 matched), with greater risk among Black and Hispanic patients.

Case-control study comparing 14 long-haul COVID patients with 14 ME/CFS patients (post-EBV and insidious-onset) using tilt testing and Doppler measurements to assess orthostatic intolerance and cerebral blood flow. Found higher POTS prevalence in long-COVID (100%) versus post-EBV (43%) and insidious-onset (50%) groups, but comparable OI symptomatology and objective abnormalities between groups.

A case-control study comparing serum Pentraxin 3 (PTX3) levels and inflammatory markers in 40 previously COVID-19-infected healthcare workers versus 40 never-infected controls. The study found elevated PTX3 and other pro-inflammatory proteins in previously infected subjects, suggesting PTX3 as a biomarker for prolonged inflammatory responses in post-COVID conditions.

Case-control study comparing behavioral and sleep disorders in 107 children/adolescents 1 month to 1 year post-COVID-19 versus pre-pandemic controls. Found significant differences in sleep-related issues and internalizing problems (anxiety/depression) in the post-COVID group, with adolescents most affected.

This nested case-control study investigates circulating noncoding RNA expression in 98 long COVID patients 18 months post-hospitalization, comparing symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. The study identifies LEF1-AS1 downregulation as a potential biomarker for persistent symptoms but does not test any treatment or intervention.

This case-control study investigates circulating autoantibodies against G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) in 11 severe long COVID patients versus 4 asymptomatic post-COVID controls. The findings suggest GPCR autoantibodies may serve as diagnostic biomarkers and identify potential therapeutic targets for a subset of long COVID patients, though the study is observational and does not test any intervention.

This case-control study examined autonomic nervous system recovery in young adults with prior COVID-19 infection, comparing heart rate variability and physical activity levels at baseline and 6 weeks post-immunization. While it documents ANS recovery following infection, it is an observational follow-up study without an active intervention—immunization status is not a treatment being tested, but rather a temporal marker for follow-up assessment.

This case-control study compared new diagnoses, prescriptions, and healthcare resource utilization in 38,167 COVID-19 survivors versus matched controls over 6 months. It found increased neuropsychiatric diagnoses, psychoactive drug prescriptions, and healthcare visits in post-COVID patients, but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This case-control study compares optical coherence tomography findings in acute coronary syndrome patients with versus without prior COVID-19 infection within the past 12 months. While it documents higher prevalence of plaque erosion and vulnerable plaque morphology in post-COVID ACS patients, it is not a long COVID study as it focuses on acute coronary syndrome rather than long COVID symptoms or sequelae.

This retrospective case-control study examined retinal changes in post-COVID healthcare workers using OCT imaging, comparing 25 COVID-19 infected individuals with 30 non-infected controls six months post-infection. While the study identified increased central macular thickness in the post-COVID group, it is observational in nature and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing fibromyalgia prevalence in post-COVID-19 patients versus COVID-negative controls using standardized ACR 2016 diagnostic criteria. Findings indicate significantly higher odds of fibromyalgia diagnosis in the post-COVID group, but this is an observational association study with no intervention tested.

Case-control study examining arterial stiffness (aortic and cerebral) in 851 patients with borderline mental disorders comparing those with and without prior COVID-19 infection. Found no significant differences in arterial stiffness between post-COVID and non-COVID groups, except in patients over 80 years old.

This paper characterizes post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) using electronic health record data from 63,675 COVID-19 survivors and develops risk prediction models to identify patients at high risk for PASC. It is a secondary analysis of existing health records rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This case-control study examines the association between eight genetic variants in hemostasis system genes and venous thrombosis risk in post-COVID patients. The researchers identified four genetic variants (F2 20210G>A, F5 1691G>A, ITGA2 807C>T, ITGB3 1565 T>C) significantly associated with increased thrombosis risk in 172 post-COVID patients compared to 141 controls.

This retrospective case-control study compares tracheal stenosis outcomes in COVID-19 patients requiring prolonged intubation versus non-COVID patients at two European referral centers. While it analyzes a complication from severe acute COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation, it does not study long COVID (persistent post-infection sequelae weeks to months after recovery) and focuses on acute-phase complications rather than post-COVID syndrome.

Case-control study of 10,426 Chinese adults examining factors associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection incidence, symptom persistence, and severity during the Omicron wave. Female sex, older age, comorbidities, and vaccination interval were key risk factors for persistent and moderate-to-severe symptoms.

This retrospective case-control study examined herpesvirus reactivation (CMV, EBV, HSV) in 40 long COVID patients compared to 40 controls without COVID-19 history. Cytomegalovirus was the most frequently reactivated virus (30%), significantly more common in moderate-to-severe COVID-19, with elevated inflammatory markers and distinct clinical features including lymphadenopathy and fever.

A case-control study comparing 216 COVID-19 survivors treated with remdesivir during acute infection against 216 matched untreated survivors, assessing post-COVID symptom development at 18.4 months follow-up. Remdesivir treatment was associated with significantly lower odds of developing long COVID overall and specifically for fatigue, pain, dyspnea, cognitive symptoms, and dermatological manifestations.

This case-control study compared hematological parameters between 58 long COVID patients and 58 matched controls in Iraq, finding significant alterations in RBC, MCHC, and MCV levels. The study documents post-COVID hematological changes but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case–control study investigates medium-term cardiovascular effects of COVID-19 by comparing 161 COVID-positive patients with 72 uninfected controls over a median follow-up of 173.5 days. The study found significantly reduced heart rate variability (RMSSD) in some COVID cases but no differences in cardiac biomarkers, arrhythmias, or blood pressure between groups.

This case-control study compares lipid profile abnormalities between 108 post-COVID patients (>6 months post-infection) and 108 age- and sex-matched controls. The study finds statistically significant alterations in lipid profiles in post-COVID patients, though LDL cholesterol was not significantly different.

A retrospective cohort study analyzing determinants of post-discharge mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients from the National Clinical Registry, with follow-up data collected over 2.5 years from 31 hospitals. The study found that age, male gender, disease severity, and comorbidities were associated with higher post-discharge mortality, while post-COVID condition (PCC) was reported in 17% of participants and associated with delayed mortality.

This case-control study assessed retinal and choroidal changes in COVID-19 recovered patients using optical coherence tomography angiography, comparing 180 recovered patients to healthy controls three months post-infection. While it documents microvascular alterations in long COVID patients, it is an observational assessment without any treatment intervention or control group receiving a treatment.

This case–control study compared hematological and biochemical parameters in 300 middle-aged individuals 10 months after mild COVID-19, stratifying them into long COVID and control groups. While findings show elevated liver enzymes and blood count alterations in long COVID patients, the study is observational without testing any specific treatment or intervention.

This case-control study investigates the association between fear, loneliness, and mental health outcomes (anxiety, depression, PTSD) in long COVID patients compared to a control group. The paper examines psychological and emotional factors in long COVID rather than testing a specific intervention.

Case-control study comparing Janus kinase inhibitors (baricitinib, tofacitinib) versus corticosteroids for treating pulmonary involvement in ongoing symptomatic COVID-19 (long COVID). JAKi group showed faster oxygen liberation (median 9 days vs 19 days, P=0.003) with similar inflammatory marker reduction.

Case-control study examining insulin resistance in long COVID patients versus controls, with assessment of depression and inflammatory markers. Finds long COVID associated with increased insulin resistance predicted by acute infection severity, which may contribute to depressive symptoms.

A matched case-control study comparing chemosensory function (smell, taste, nasal trigeminal sensitivity) in 100 COVID-19 patients versus 100 matched controls at a median of 401 days post-infection. The study found significantly higher rates of olfactory (46% vs 10%), gustatory (27% vs 10%), and chemesthesis impairment in COVID-19 cases, associated with emotional distress and depression, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case-control study comparing oxidative stress biomarkers and antioxidant defenses between 80 long-COVID patients and 40 healthy controls. Findings show elevated oxidative damage markers and reduced antioxidant enzyme activity in long-COVID patients, with associations to chronic fatigue and mood symptoms, but no intervention or treatment is tested.

This case-control study compared cardiovascular autonomic function and body fat distribution between COVID-19-recovered patients (n=31) and age/gender-matched controls (n=29) in India. Results showed significantly elevated diastolic blood pressure, galvanic skin response, and visceral fat percentage in post-COVID patients, suggesting dysautonomia and metabolic changes in recovered individuals.

This case-control study compared nutritional status and psychological health outcomes in hemodialysis patients 6 months after COVID-19 infection versus matched controls without prior COVID-19 infection. The infected group showed significantly worse scores on malnutrition inflammation, depression, anxiety, somatic symptoms, and insomnia scales.

This retrospective cohort study compared the incidence of myocarditis and pericarditis in 500 COVID-19 patients after acute infection recovery versus 1000 matched controls, investigating whether these cardiac conditions are part of long COVID syndrome. The study establishes baseline prevalence rates of cardiac inflammation during the post-acute recovery phase in COVID-19 survivors.

Case-control study comparing semen parameters between 53 recovered COVID-19 patients and 457 healthy controls at an average of 157 days post-infection. Found no statistically significant differences in sperm motility, morphology, or concentration between groups.

A case-control study examining epigenetic regulation of the TLR7 gene in post-COVID syndrome patients versus controls, using bisulfite pyrosequencing and flow cytometry to assess DNA methylation patterns, gene expression, and immune cell profiles. The study identifies TLR7 methylation changes and anomalies in immune cell populations associated with persistent innate immune activation, proposing TLR7 methylation as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target, but does not test any treatment intervention.

A prospective case-control study comparing psychiatric disorder rates between post-COVID patients with and without persistent olfactory complaints (anosmia). Found significantly higher psychiatric disorder prevalence (41.7%) in patients with olfactory complaints versus controls (18.8%), suggesting psychiatric history may be a risk factor for persistent anosmia in long COVID.

This cross-sectional case-control study compared arterial stiffness markers and vascular aging in COVID-19 recovered young patients (120 total: 90 cases, 30 controls) at 6-18+ months post-infection. Patients showed significantly increased heart rate, pulse wave velocity, and arterial stiffness indices compared to healthy controls, indicating elevated risk of vascular aging post-COVID.

This retrospective case-control study examined sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with general practitioner-led long COVID diagnosis using electronic health records from Australian primary care clinics (1,588 diagnosed long COVID patients vs. controls). It found that female sex, age 40-59, high socioeconomic status, and pre-existing mental health, respiratory, cancer, and musculoskeletal conditions were significantly associated with GP-led long COVID diagnosis.

This case-control MRI study investigates functional brain changes in young adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome compared to matched controls, examining blood-brain barrier integrity, oxygen metabolism, and cerebral blood flow. The findings show transient blood-brain barrier dysfunction and prolonged impairments in cerebral blood supply and oxygen metabolism, providing pathological evidence for long-COVID neurological manifestations.

A case-control study comparing multi-system structural and functional deficits between 141 long COVID patients and 280 controls using MRI, blood pressure, autonomic function, and exercise testing. Found minimal overall deficit differences except for elevated blood pressure in long COVID cases, suggesting most community-based long COVID patients do not have marked residual multi-system deficits.

Retrospective case-control study comparing 19 long COVID patients with persistent parenchymal lung changes at 10 weeks post-infection to 19 controls with improved outcomes. Identifies neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio >3.13 and invasive mechanical ventilation as risk factors for chronic lung changes, but does not test any intervention or treatment.

This case-control study compared 62 long COVID patients with sleep and memory complaints to 52 controls without these symptoms, examining clinical features and symptom prevalence 5-8 months after COVID-19 infection. Cases showed significantly higher rates of cognitive and mental health complaints (sadness, anxiety, disability), highlighting interconnected psychological phenotypes in long COVID.

Case-control study comparing cognitive dysfunction in 776 college students who survived COVID-19 versus 1,374 uninfected controls in Saudi Arabia. Found significantly higher neurological fatigue and cognitive impairment in infected students, with negative correlations between fatigue/cognitive failure and academic performance (GPA).

This case-control study compared neurological symptoms in 174 healthcare workers who acquired SARS-CoV-2 with 152 matched controls, assessing long-term cognitive complaints and headaches over a 6-month period. Healthcare workers with prior SARS-CoV-2 infection showed significantly higher rates of headache (RR=1.51) and cognitive complaints (RR=2.02) compared to controls.

Case-control study comparing pulmonary function tests (spirometry) in 66 post-COVID-19 patients versus 67 controls matched for demographic criteria. Found significantly lower FVC and FEV parameters in post-COVID patients, particularly in younger age groups (18-29 years), indicating long-term respiratory impairment following COVID-19.

A randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial evaluating whether stellate ganglion block (SGB) is effective for treating COVID-19-induced parosmia in 48 participants. The study found no significant difference between SGB and placebo in response rates (43% vs 38%, p>0.05), leading to the conclusion that SGB should not be recommended for this indication.

A quasi-experimental study evaluating the effects of 12 sessions of combined aerobic and resistance training on 26 post-COVID-19 patients. The intervention improved maximal and submaximal exercise tolerance, lung function, fatigue, and quality of life.

A single-arm pre-post pilot study examining online peer support (8 weekly sessions) for mental health in 18 individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19. Depression severity significantly decreased post-intervention, with participants reporting emotional support, bonding, and perspective changes.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating a 6-week cardiopulmonary rehabilitation protocol (respiratory, aerobic, and resistance training) versus educational control in 33 post-COVID-19 patients. The intervention group showed significant improvements in submaximal exercise tolerance (100.46 m increase in 6-minute walk test), reduced dyspnea, and increased upper limb muscle mass compared to controls.

Pilot study evaluating intranasal and intraoral photobiomodulation (PBM) for treating anosmia and ageusia in 20 subjects with COVID-19-induced smell and taste loss. Results showed significant improvement in both olfactory and gustatory function following 12 sessions of laser-based PBM treatment.

A double-blind randomized controlled trial testing colchicine versus placebo in 346 adults with long COVID across 8 hospitals in India. Colchicine did not improve 6-minute walk test distance, inflammatory markers, or other patient-reported outcomes at 52 weeks, suggesting the need for alternative therapeutic approaches.

A prospective cohort study evaluating a 6-week structured pacing protocol (WHO Borg CR-10 5-phase) in 31 post-COVID syndrome patients with long symptom duration (average 17 months). The intervention significantly reduced post-exertional symptom exacerbation episodes from 3.4 to 1.1 per week and improved health-related quality of life scores.

Randomized crossover trial comparing postexertional symptoms in 31 long COVID patients versus 31 healthy controls across three exercise modalities (HIIT, MICT, strength training). Long COVID patients tolerated exercise similarly to controls but showed lower aerobic capacity, reduced muscle strength, signs of myopathy and POTS, and greater exacerbation of muscle pain after HIIT and concentration difficulties after MICT.

A prospective interventional cohort study evaluating intranasal insulin therapy for persistent post-COVID-19 olfactory dysfunction in 16 patients with treatment-resistant anosmia or hyposmia. The intervention yielded significant improvements in qualitative, quantitative, and global olfactory scores over 1 month of twice-weekly treatment with minimal adverse effects.

An open-label pilot study evaluated transcranial and whole-body photobiomodulation (PBM) therapy in long COVID patients with brain fog and cognitive dysfunction over 4 weeks. Both PBM delivery methods showed significant improvements in neuropsychological testing and quantitative EEG measures.

Randomized controlled trial testing a brief outpatient cognitive-behavioral rehabilitation program for patients with mild to moderate post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) versus care as usual. The intervention group showed statistically and clinically significant improvements in physical function (SF-36-PFS) and most secondary outcomes including fatigue, postexertional malaise, and symptom burden at treatment completion and 12-month follow-up.

Randomized controlled trial testing bimodal visual-olfactory training with patient-preferred scents versus unimodal training with physician-assigned scents for COVID-19 related olfactory loss. Active interventions, particularly bimodal training with patient-preferred scents, showed larger improvement than controls on self-reported measures, though differences between treatment arms were not statistically significant on objective testing.

A single-arm feasibility study of an 8-session personalized respiratory physiotherapy program in 13 PASC patients with persistent respiratory symptoms. The program achieved 100% retention with significant improvements in quality of life, functional status, and self-efficacy, with qualitative data highlighting patient satisfaction with the personalized approach.

This is a secondary analysis of the STOP-PASC randomized trial examining digital biometric measures (physical activity, heart rate, oxygen saturation) from smartwatches in long COVID patients treated with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir versus placebo. The analysis identified distinct longitudinal biometric trajectories that correlate with symptom severity, though no significant differences were found between treatment arms.

This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cell (UC-MSC) transplantation in 10 long COVID patients who received intravenous infusions on days 0, 7, and 14. UC-MSC treatment was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events and showed potential in alleviating long COVID symptoms (sleep difficulty, depression/anxiety, memory issues) and improving lung lesions, with immunological changes observed including shifts in T cell and B cell populations.

A 3-year intervention study evaluating individualized stress-controlled training therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy for 78 post-COVID-19 patients with fatigue and sensorimotor instability. Key symptoms including fatigue, sensorimotor instability, and neuropsychiatric symptoms showed significant improvement across the cohort, with quantified therapeutic effects measured by Cohen's d.

The PAX LC trial is a Phase 2, double-blind, randomized controlled trial testing nirmatrelvir/ritonavir versus placebo in 100 long COVID patients using a decentralized design with home-based blood draws and digital diaries. Primary outcome is change in PROMIS-29 Physical Health Summary Score at Day 28, with secondary endpoints including mental health, quality of life measures, and immunophenotyping to identify biomarkers.

This study evaluated high-frequency transcutaneous auricular vagal nerve stimulation (TA-VNS) as a treatment for olfactory dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients (n=10) compared to healthy controls (n=30). TA-VNS improved olfactory discrimination and intensity/pleasantness ratings in post-COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction, with no improvement seen in healthy individuals.

This case series evaluates the safety and feasibility of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection into the olfactory clefts in 87 COVID-19 patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction lasting a mean of 15.7 months. PRP injection was well-tolerated with minor adverse events, and patients showed significant improvements in olfactory function scores at 2-month follow-up, though the authors note randomized controlled trials are needed to establish superiority over placebo.

A 10-week randomized controlled multicentre trial of individualized, symptom-titrated resistance and aerobic training in 118 post-COVID patients (INT: n=58, control: n=60). Training significantly reduced fatigue (FSS: -1.14) and improved mental (SF-12: +5.94) and physical quality of life (SF-12: +4.33), functional aerobic capacity (+22.72 steps), and handgrip strength in the intervention group, with no increased risk of symptom exacerbation.

A nonrandomized controlled trial evaluating fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) for sleep disturbance in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients with insomnia. FMT showed significantly higher remission rates (37.9% vs 10.0%) and improvements in sleep quality, anxiety, and fatigue compared to controls at 12 weeks.

This case series evaluated a 10-session virtual reality and augmented reality rehabilitation program in 60 long COVID patients aged >60 years, stratified by baseline functional performance.
