Both low and medium performance groups showed statistically significant improvements in 6-minute walking test distance post-intervention, with medium performance patients approaching normative values.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating Lianhua Qingke tablets for treating persistent cough in long COVID patients across 19 hospitals and 23 community health centers in China (n=482). The treatment group showed significantly faster cough disappearance, higher 14-day cough remission rates, and greater improvements in symptom scores compared to placebo, with no serious adverse events.

Secondary analysis of the ACTIV-4c RCT evaluating whether extended thromboprophylaxis with apixaban improves quality of life in patients discharged after COVID-19 hospitalization. Extended anticoagulation was not associated with significant improvements in EQ-5D-5L domains at 30 or 90 days post-discharge.

This study evaluated the effect of a 28-day nutritional supplement (Apportal®) containing amino acids, minerals, vitamins, and plant extracts on muscle function and fatigue in 30 COVID-19 survivors. The supplement showed significant improvements in hand grip strength, strength endurance time, chair stand repetitions, and self-rated health status.

A prospective randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effectiveness of coordination complex with succinate acid anion (CCSA) for treating post-COVID chronic fatigue syndrome and cognitive impairment using functional brain MRI in 30 patients. CCSA treatment showed statistically significant improvements in fatigue severity (MFI-20 score reduction of 20 points vs 12 in placebo, p=0.043) and cognitive function (MoCA improvement of 2 points vs 1 in placebo, p<0.05).

Single-center interventional pre-post study evaluating the safety and efficacy of low-dose naltrexone (LDN) in 52 long COVID patients over 2 months. LDN was well-tolerated with improvements in 6 of 7 quality-of-life parameters (recovery, activity limitation, energy, pain, concentration, sleep; p≤0.001), though the authors note randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings.

This quasi-experimental trial evaluates acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients, comparing treatment (n=15) to a wait-list control group (n=15) with outcomes measured at post-test and 3-month follow-up. ACT significantly improved resilience and health-related quality of life compared to controls, with effects sustained at 3-month follow-up.

A single-arm pre-post study evaluating a 6-week virtual mindfulness intervention in 20 women with long COVID dysautonomia symptoms. The intervention produced significant reduction in insomnia severity and pro-inflammatory gene expression (CTRA), but no improvements in objective dysautonomia measures or most psychological symptoms.

A pilot study evaluating low-dose naltrexone (4.5 mg/day) combined with NAD+ iontophoresis patches in 36 long COVID patients with persistent fatigue. Treatment showed significant improvements in SF-36 quality of life scores and Chalder fatigue scale at 12 weeks, with 52% of patients classified as responders and generally mild adverse events.

This paper presents results from clinical trials investigating high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with cognitive training for treating neurocognitive symptoms in long COVID patients. The study examines treatment efficacy during both acute and chronic recovery phases, identifies prognostic factors predicting better treatment response, and discusses directions for future research.

A double-blind RCT testing 14 days of beetroot juice supplementation versus placebo in 25 adults with long COVID. Beetroot juice failed to improve functional outcomes (fatigue resistance, 6-min walk test) but showed beneficial changes in gut microbiota composition and inflammatory markers compared to placebo.

A 10-week randomized controlled trial examining individualized, symptom-titrated resistance and aerobic training in 118 post-COVID patients. Training significantly reduced fatigue and improved mental/physical health-related quality of life and functional aerobic capacity compared to waitlist control, with no increase in post-exertional malaise.

Phase 3 RCT evaluating ensitrelvir (a protease inhibitor) given in the acute phase of COVID-19 to prevent post-COVID condition (long COVID) in 991 patients with mild-to-moderate disease. Treatment showed variable symptom reductions at 85, 169, and 337 days post-symptom onset, with more pronounced effects in neurological symptoms and among patients with high baseline symptom burden.

A randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial evaluating a combined plant extract (CPE) formulation in 66 long COVID patients over 7 days. The CPE group showed significant reductions in total symptom score, moderate-to-severe fatigue, and post-exertional malaise compared to placebo, with an acceptable safety profile.

A pilot study evaluating Biosound Therapy (multimodal treatment combining biofeedback, vibroacoustic therapy, and binaural beats) in 13 long COVID patients (9 intervention, 4 control) over 4 weeks. Intervention group showed significant improvements in anxiety (GAD-7), depression (PHQ-9), cognitive function, fatigue, and concentration/memory with no reported side effects.

Open diagnostic study of 30 long COVID patients assessing airflow limitation via methacholine bronchial provocation test and diurnal FEV1 variability, with 3-week asthma treatment intervention. Treatment normalized mean diurnal FEV1 variability from 18.0% to 7.3% and reduced LC symptom burden.

This RCT evaluated major ozone autohemotherapy (O3-MAH) combined with conventional therapy versus conventional therapy alone in 73 PASC patients. O3-MAH showed greater efficacy with 71% symptom response versus 45% in controls, along with significant improvements in pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and inflammatory markers.

A prospective pilot study evaluating three traditional East Asian herbal medicines (Bojungikgi-tang, Kyungok-go, and Cheonwangbosim-dan) for treating fatigue and cognitive dysfunction in 45 long COVID patients over 12 weeks. Herbal treatment showed significant fatigue improvement (46-80% success) but more modest cognitive benefits, with high medication adherence and no serious adverse events.

A randomized controlled trial investigating donepezil hydrochloride as a treatment for post-COVID memory impairment in 25 patients, with assessments at baseline, 4 weeks, and 12 weeks using the Wechsler Memory Scale-Revised. While no significant overall improvement was observed in memory scales compared to controls, the drug group showed improvements in specific memory subtests (visual reproduction and verbal paired associates).

Baseline analysis of a randomized controlled trial testing acupressure and qigong interventions in 235 post-COVID syndrome patients, characterizing their medication use patterns, symptom burden, and demographic profile. The study documents high prevalence of off-label drug use and complementary medicine adoption among PCS patients seeking relief from persistent fatigue and multi-systemic symptoms.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing celecoxib monotherapy (100 mg twice daily for 6 weeks) versus placebo in 62 patients with moderate depressive symptoms following COVID-19 infection. Celecoxib showed superior improvement in depression scores with 70% response rate and 67% remission rate compared to 9% and 0% in placebo, with no significant difference in adverse events.

This pilot study evaluated intranasal immunotherapy using M2 macrophage conditioned medium for treating post-COVID hyposmia in 7 patients with persistent olfactory dysfunction (7-24 months post-infection). Treatment was well-tolerated and resulted in significant improvements in olfactory perception, odor recognition, and subjective smell at 6-12 month follow-up, with 5/7 patients reporting high satisfaction.

Randomized controlled trial comparing nintedanib vs pirfenidone for treating post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis in 30 patients followed for 12 weeks. Both treatments improved pulmonary function and exercise capacity, with nintedanib showing greater benefits for exercise and oxygen saturation but more adverse effects than pirfenidone.

Open-label pilot study of oral minocycline (100 mg daily for 42 days) in 55 ME patients including 19 with long COVID, showing 80% favorable response (≥2 point improvement in functional status) among 51 completers, with 89% response in long COVID subgroup. Early treatment (<6 months disease duration) predicted better outcomes, with significant symptom improvements in fatigue, post-exertional malaise, brain fog, and orthostatic intolerance.

This interventional cohort study evaluates Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy (PSRT), a 13-week virtual therapy program, in 23 adults with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). PSRT significantly reduced somatic symptom burden and secondary outcomes including dyspnea, fatigue, and pain.

Open trial evaluating a six-week biofeedback intervention (heart rate variability and temperature biofeedback) in 20 long COVID patients for alleviating mood, somatic, and sleep symptoms. Participants showed significant improvements in somatic, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and quality of life with moderate-to-large effect sizes, though the lack of control group is a major limitation.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating eight weeks of Pilates Method against supervised physical exercise and control in 59 post-COVID-19 patients. Pilates group showed significant improvements in 6-minute walk distance, post-exercise fatigue, and sleep quality compared to controls.

Prospective cohort study of COVID-19 mRNA revaccination safety in 103 individuals with prior adverse vaccine reactions and/or long COVID. Revaccination was safe and well tolerated, with mild immediate reactions in 4.9% and common post-vaccination symptoms (fatigue, headache, muscle pain) reported at 7-day follow-up.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating early physiotherapy and health education in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during acute infection. While the study shows benefits for reducing hospitalization duration and improving physical conditioning during acute illness, it does not study long COVID patients or long-term post-COVID sequelae—it focuses on acute COVID-19 hospital care.

A pilot study evaluating the feasibility and effectiveness of a two-week audio-guided and mindfulness-based forest bathing intervention in 36 moderately affected long COVID patients using a repeated-measures pre-post design. Results showed significant improvements in overall long COVID symptoms, fatigue, and well-being, with a 22% dropout rate, suggesting forest bathing may be a feasible complementary treatment approach.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated a lifestyle adjustment intervention focused on symptom monitoring and functional improvement in 54 long COVID patients (27 intervention, 27 control). The intervention group showed significant improvements in quality of life, disability (self-care subscale), and functional impairment compared to controls receiving standard care plus informational leaflet.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week telerehabilitation training program in 182 long COVID participants compared to physical activity counseling alone. The intervention significantly improved walking behavior, total physical activity, exercise self-efficacy, and sleep quality, but did not improve cardiorespiratory fitness or health-related quality of life.

This study evaluates a cognitive rehabilitation program (RehaCom) in acute COVID-19 survivors using a quasi-experimental design with pre-test/post-test and control group. However, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 patients during active infection, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months after infection), and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria.

A 10-week randomized controlled multicenter trial evaluated individualized, symptom-titrated resistance and aerobic training in 118 long COVID patients with chronic fatigue. The intervention group showed significant improvements in fatigue (FSS: -1.14), health-related quality of life (SF-12 mental: 5.94, physical: 4.33), functional aerobic capacity (CST: 22.72 steps), and handgrip strength compared to waitlist controls, with no increased risk of symptom exacerbation.

Secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial examining vortioxetine treatment effects on depressive symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition, with anxiety as a moderator. Found that vortioxetine significantly reduced depressive symptoms in 147 participants, with anxiety symptoms moderating treatment efficacy.

The PAIN-COVID randomized controlled trial evaluated a follow-up program combining patient education and psychological intervention (based on Rehm's self-control model) for critical COVID-19 survivors at risk of post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) and chronic pain. The intervention was not superior to standard care in improving quality of life at 6 months, though the data may inform future strategies for managing PICS and pain in this population.

A randomized controlled trial (n=42) comparing thoracic spinal manipulation plus pulmonary rehabilitation versus pulmonary rehabilitation alone in long COVID patients. The intervention group showed significant improvements in pulmonary function and thoracic spine mobility, supporting the therapeutic benefit of spinal manipulation for long COVID respiratory symptoms.

A bicentric randomized controlled trial evaluating the feasibility and effects of singing-based respiratory training (SBRT) in 45 post-COVID syndrome patients with breathing disorders. SBRT showed high compliance (96%), with medium effect sizes on health-related quality of life, anxiety, and depression, though SBRT aimed at reducing respiratory rate did not outperform regular SBRT.

This observational study evaluates immunoadsorption therapy in 12 post-COVID patients with ME/CFS symptoms, finding that the treatment effectively removes autoantibodies and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokines while improving neuropsychological function and grip strength. However, self-reported symptoms and ME/CFS questionnaire scores did not show significant improvement, and removed proteins rebounded within one month.

A randomized controlled trial testing intermittent hypoxia exposure (IHE) versus normoxia exposure as a treatment for dyspnea and fatigue in 95 PASC patients. IHE significantly improved 6-minute walk distance, spirometry parameters, and dyspnea/fatigue scales with no severe adverse events.

Open-label study evaluating safety and efficacy of prolonged-release pirfenidone in 70 patients with post-acute COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis over 3 months. Treatment was well-tolerated with significant improvements in pulmonary function tests, 6-minute walk test, dyspnea, and symptoms.

A phase 2 double-blind randomized controlled trial testing nirmatrelvir-ritonavir versus placebo for treating long COVID in 100 US participants, with treatment given for 15 days. Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir showed no significant improvement in PROMIS-29 physical health scores compared to placebo at day 28, though the trial demonstrated feasibility of decentralized long COVID trials.

A feasibility trial evaluating a specialized 8-session cognitive-behavioral group intervention for inpatients with post-COVID-19 condition in a neurological rehabilitation setting. The program was well-received and showed significant improvements in subjective fatigue and disease coping, though findings are limited by lack of control group, small sample size, and high drop-out rate.

An uncontrolled case series of 95 post-COVID patients treated with SSRIs, finding that two-thirds showed good to strong response with substantial improvements in brain fog, sensory overload, fatigue, and dysautonomia. The authors propose neurobiological mechanisms underlying SSRI efficacy in post-COVID syndrome, particularly involving the kynurenine pathway and immune dysregulation.

This pilot study evaluated 8 weeks of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) in healthy controls (n=12), people with PASC (n=9), and people with mild-to-moderate ME/CFS (n=12). All groups improved in inspiratory pressure, 6-minute walk distance, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, and sleep symptoms; ME/CFS participants additionally showed improvements in vascular function, autonomic questionnaire scores, and pain.

A feasibility study evaluating individually tailored exercise (endurance and strength training) in 26 post-COVID-19 patients with POTS over 12 weeks. The intervention showed good adherence (76%), high completion rates (96%), and preliminary improvements in symptom burden, psychological function, and physical outcomes.

A pilot clinical trial of 14 long COVID patients undergoing 10-week aerobic exercise training, analyzing serum extracellular vesicle RNA profiles before and after intervention. Exercise training modulated EV-associated gene expression, suppressing inflammation and metabolism-related genes at peak exertion post-training, suggesting potential molecular mechanisms of symptom improvement.

The PsyLoCo project developed a psychotherapeutic treatment manual addressing psychosocial burdens in long COVID patients across four modules: coping/distress management, physical complaints/pain, chronic fatigue/affective symptoms, and social/working life. The manual was tested for feasibility and effectiveness in a multicentre randomized controlled pilot study.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial evaluated the effects of a multispecies probiotic on post-acute COVID-19 symptoms in 21 patients over 6 months. The probiotic group showed significant improvements in respiratory function, immune markers, microbial richness, and serum metabolome compared to placebo.

A pilot study evaluating high-tone therapy (HTT), a form of electrotherapy, on functional capacity and quality of life in 22 post-COVID-condition patients with fatigue. Patients receiving ten 60-minute HTT sessions showed significant improvements in the one-minute sit-to-stand test (23.5 to 35.5 repetitions, p<0.001), SF-12 quality of life scores (both physical and mental components), post-COVID severity score, and subjective work ability.

This non-randomized controlled study compared neuropsychological rehabilitation (8 participants, 6-month intervention) versus no treatment (7 controls) in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients with similar baseline cognitive profiles. The treatment group showed significant improvements in verbal memory and action naming, while the control group improved only in action fluency, suggesting that cognitive rehabilitation may benefit some post-COVID cognitive impairments.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating the acute effects of osteopathic treatment on autonomic nervous system function (measured via heart rate variability) in long COVID patients with fatigue syndrome compared to sham treatment. The study aims to assess whether osteopathy can positively influence post-COVID fatigue by measuring HRV changes.

This study evaluates diaphragm muscle weakness and exertional dyspnea at 2 years post-COVID-19 hospitalization, and investigates the impact of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) on these outcomes in long COVID patients. The research determines the persistence of diaphragm dysfunction and demonstrates whether targeted respiratory muscle training can improve symptoms in this population.

A pilot double-blind randomized controlled trial evaluating classical homeopathy as a treatment for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (long COVID). The study tests whether homeopathy, which has shown benefits for chronic diseases with similar symptom profiles, may be effective for the diverse symptoms associated with long COVID.

Pilot randomized controlled trial evaluating a 12-week cognitive rehabilitation intervention adapted for long COVID patients with objective cognitive impairment. Intervention group showed non-futile trends in processing speed, learning, memory, language, and executive function, with significant self-reported improvements compared to time-matched controls, supporting further evaluation in a larger trial.

This non-randomized trial evaluated an 8-week supervised exercise intervention (resistance training plus aerobic exercise) in 32 healthcare workers with post-COVID symptoms, stratified by severity. Physical exercise significantly improved aerobic fitness (VO2peak), functional capacity (6MWT, 30-second sit-to-stand), mental health outcomes, and work ability, with greater benefits observed in those with severe fatigue.

A feasibility study of occupational therapy-based energy management education (EME) in 17 post-COVID patients with fatigue using a pre-post design. The intervention showed large effect sizes on fatigue impact, self-efficacy, daily activity competency, and quality of life, with promising results supporting further research.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating photobiomodulation therapy for treating dysgeusia (taste disturbance) in long COVID patients. The study found variable treatment responses and calls for further research to elucidate optimal outcomes.

An 8-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of vortioxetine (5-20 mg) versus placebo in 149 adults with post-COVID-19 condition. Vortioxetine did not significantly improve primary cognitive outcome (Digit Symbol Substitution Test) in unadjusted analysis but showed cognitive benefit when adjusted for baseline CRP; significant improvements in depressive symptoms and quality of life were observed.

Randomized controlled trial of 44 long COVID patients comparing 4 weeks of supervised strength-endurance training versus usual care. Exercise intervention significantly improved VO2peak and oxygen-pulse compared to control, though fatigue and quality of life improvements were not statistically different between groups.

A randomized, sham-controlled, double-blind trial of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) in 60 post-COVID syndrome patients with symptoms lasting ≥3 months. HBOT significantly improved global longitudinal strain (GLS) compared to sham, suggesting recovery of subclinical left ventricular dysfunction in post-COVID patients.

The PERCEIVE randomised controlled trial evaluated a 6-month multidisciplinary exercise intervention (aerobic and resistance training plus medical management) versus usual care in 133 long COVID patients with exercise intolerance. The intervention significantly improved peak oxygen uptake and cardiorespiratory fitness but had no significant effect on mood or quality of life.

A feasibility study evaluating individualized tailored physical training in 23 patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) following COVID-19 over 12 weeks. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in physical function (6MWT), psychological outcomes (PHQ-9), POTS-specific symptoms (MaPS, VOSS, FSS), quality of life (EQ-5D), and increased time spent in upright position by 49%.

This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of a 2-month out-of-hospital exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation program in 30 long COVID patients. The program resulted in significant improvements in symptoms, muscular strength, cardiopulmonary parameters, and psychological measures without adverse effects or dropouts.
Phase 2 randomized controlled trial evaluating efgartigimod (FcRn antagonist) for treating post-COVID POTS by reducing autoantibody levels. This is a study protocol with no results yet reported.

The InsCOVID trial is a randomized controlled trial evaluating home-based inspiratory muscle training (IMT) in 26 long COVID patients with prior COVID-19 pneumonia, comparing IMT to usual care over 12 weeks. IMT significantly improved peak oxygen consumption (+4.46 mL/kg/min), chronotropic index, and quality of life dimensions.

A prospective observational study of 506 COVID-19 outpatients treated with bamlanivimab monoclonal antibody, examining the frequency and predictors of long COVID at 24 weeks post-treatment. Long COVID occurred in 18% despite early effective monoclonal antibody therapy, with smoking, female sex, and non-Hispanic ethnicity as independent risk factors.

Two single-arm pilot studies evaluated MY-Skills Mobile, an 8-week remote intervention combining therapeutic yoga with digital self-management education for older adults with multiple chronic conditions (Study 1: N=24) and long COVID patients (Study 2: N=9). Both studies met feasibility benchmarks and showed improvements in depressive symptoms, fatigue, pain interference, and self-efficacy with no adverse events reported.

A feasibility study evaluating individually tailored physical training in 15 patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) associated with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. After 12 weeks of supervised exercise, patients showed significant improvements in 6-minute walking test, upright time tolerance, POTS symptoms, and depression scores, with no severe adverse events reported.

Randomized controlled trial comparing functional exercise versus aerobic exercise combined with breathing techniques via telerehabilitation for long COVID patients over 8 weeks. Both interventions improved stress and quality of life; functional exercise showed more promising results for fatigue and functional capacity.

SPRINTER was a randomized controlled trial testing inhaled interferon beta-1a (SNG001) in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with a secondary analysis examining effects on long COVID symptoms at 60 and 90 days post-treatment. SNG001 showed relative risk reductions for common long COVID symptoms including fatigue (35.4%), dyspnea (28.3%), and loss of smell/taste (61.4%) compared to placebo.

This case series evaluates high-dose intravenous N-acetylcysteine as a treatment for post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis in hospitalized patients. Repeat CT scans showed significant regression of ground glass opacities and pulmonary consolidation following the treatment.

A pilot study evaluating intravenous laser irradiation of blood (ILIB) therapy in 6 long COVID patients with brain fog, measuring cognitive function via MoCA/MMSE and sleep quality via AIS. Results showed significant improvements in cognitive function and sleep quality post-treatment, with molecular analysis revealing upregulation of mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation pathways and downregulation of inflammatory pathways.

This study evaluates whether CPAP treatment for obstructive sleep apnea improves cognitive fog in 14 post-COVID patients using neuropsychological testing. Results show significant improvements in processing speed, executive function, and cognitive function after 4 weeks of CPAP therapy, with improvements correlated to nightly CPAP use duration.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating an 8-week supervised cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program (3 sessions/week with aerobic, resistance, and inspiratory muscle training) versus usual care in 40 long COVID patients. The intervention significantly improved VO₂ peak, ventilatory efficiency, and symptom burden compared to controls.

A prospective non-randomized controlled trial evaluating intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG) as a treatment for long COVID in 21 patients versus 29 controls receiving supportive care only. IVIG treatment resulted in significant improvements in vascular endothelial function (+27% FMD), neurocognitive function, fatigue, and disability compared to supportive care alone.

This study examined impaired endothelial function in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) and tested whether combined exercise training (aerobic, resistance, and inspiratory muscle training for 8 weeks) could restore vascular function. The exercise intervention significantly improved endothelial function, VO2peak, and reduced dyspnea and fatigue compared to controls, reaching levels similar to healthy individuals.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of 6-week exercise training on cardiovascular autonomic function in 42 amateur runners recovering from COVID-19, comparing a Performance Improvement Group with a Safety First Group. The study found significant reductions in minimum heart rate and improvements in autonomic function measures post-training, with stratified analyses by baseline characteristics.

This is a randomized online experiment testing how different types of messaging and information about long COVID affect public expectations and understanding of the illness. The study is excluded because it does not evaluate a treatment or intervention for long COVID patients—it is a behavioral/communication study about perceptions in the general public, not a clinical trial testing therapeutic outcomes.

A before-and-after feasibility study evaluating personalized computerized cognitive training (CCT) in 89 long COVID patients with cognitive dysfunction over an 8-week period. Participants showed significant improvements across cognitive domains (26-52% score increases), with most improving in attention, memory, coordination, perception, and reasoning.

A non-randomized interventional study evaluating psychophysiologic symptom relief therapy (PSRT) in 23 adults with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). The intervention significantly reduced somatic symptom burden, dyspnea, fatigue, and pain over a 13-week treatment course.

A feasibility study of heart rate variability biofeedback breathing (HRV-B) as a home-based intervention for long COVID dysautonomia symptoms in 13 participants. The intervention showed statistically significant improvements in multiple outcomes including C19YRS-m, quality of life, COMPASS-31 (autonomic symptom score), and RMSSD, with high participant satisfaction and adherence.

A randomized controlled trial of imatinib versus standard of care in 156 COVID-19 hospitalized patients, with follow-up at 30 days and 1 year including assessment of long COVID symptoms. The trial found no convincing benefit of imatinib in reducing mortality, improving recovery, or preventing long COVID symptoms like fatigue, sleep problems, and memory difficulties.

RE2SCUE is a non-randomized controlled study comparing an 8-week face-to-face rehabilitation program to remote monitoring in 37 long COVID patients. The rehabilitation group showed significant improvements in dyspnea, anxiety, and cognitive function, while both groups improved in fatigue, suggesting exercise-based rehabilitation benefits certain long COVID sequelae.

A pilot randomized controlled trial (n=16) evaluating Constraint-Induced Cognitive Therapy (CICT) combined with Speed of Processing Training for long COVID brain fog and cognitive dysfunction. CICT produced very large improvements in instrumental activities of daily living (d=2.6) and brain fog (d=-2.9) compared to treatment-as-usual, with four of five non-retired participants returning to work, warranting a larger-scale RCT.

The PAX LC trial is a Phase II decentralized, double-blind randomized controlled trial testing Paxlovid for long COVID treatment. This paper compares the demographic characteristics of trial participants (100) with the 2023 National Health Interview Survey to assess representativeness, finding good geographic and age/gender diversity but underrepresentation of Hispanic and Non-Hispanic Black participants compared to the broader US long COVID population.

The REGAIN study is a multicentre randomised controlled trial evaluating an online supervised group physical and mental health rehabilitation programme for adults with post-COVID-19 condition. The trial tests clinical effectiveness of combined physical and psychological rehabilitation delivered remotely.

A single-arm open-label feasibility trial testing the safety and tolerability of a CBD-dominant cannabis-based medicinal product in 12 long COVID patients over 21 weeks. The treatment was safe and well-tolerated with high adherence, though the study lacked a control group and had recruitment limitations.

The reCOVer trial is a phase IIa randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind crossover study of BC007 (rovunaptabin), a monoclonal antibody targeting GPCR-autoantibodies, in 30 post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients with persistent fatigue. BC007 was well-tolerated with no significant adverse event differences versus placebo, and showed significant improvements in fatigue severity and quality of life in this autoimmune subgroup of PCS patients.

Pilot study of 13 long COVID patients with reduced growth hormone secretion who received 9 months of daily GH injections. GH treatment significantly improved fatigue and mood symptoms but did not improve cognition, sleep quality, or physical performance.

A single-arm feasibility study evaluating a 6-week theatre-based wellness programme using movement, voice, drama, and creative exercises for people with long COVID. The programme showed acceptable uptake and completion rates, with significant improvements in self-rated health and chronic fatigue symptoms, plus qualitative benefits in community, illness acceptance, and quality of life.

A randomized, double-blind, controlled pilot trial evaluating cranial electrotherapy stimulation (CES) as an adjunctive therapy to rehabilitation for anxiety in 40 patients with post-COVID-19 condition. Both CES and sham stimulation groups showed significant improvements in anxiety symptoms with no significant difference between groups, suggesting CES provided no additional benefit beyond rehabilitation alone.

A randomized controlled trial testing photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) on muscle performance and functional capacity in 15 post-COVID patients. PBMT showed no significant improvement over placebo in peak isometric strength or sit-to-stand performance, suggesting no effect of the intervention.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating high-intensity interval training (HIIT) versus standard care in 28 individuals previously hospitalized for COVID-19, with cardiac MRI as the primary outcome. HIIT significantly increased left ventricular mass (6.8 g difference, p=0.029) and showed descriptive improvements in functional status, demonstrating exercise as an efficacious intervention for cardiac recovery post-COVID-19.

This is a secondary analysis of the ACTIV-4a randomized trial examining P2Y12 inhibitor effects on quality of life in critically ill COVID-19 patients at 90 days. The study found that P2Y12 inhibitor treatment was associated with improved EQ-5D-5L utility scores and may reduce post-acute COVID symptoms, though this is a pre-specified secondary analysis of an existing trial rather than a primary trial publication.

Randomized controlled trial testing nintedanib versus placebo for post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis in 135 patients over 12 months. Nintedanib did not significantly influence FVC decline compared to placebo, with both groups showing improvement at 12 months.

The BATTLE trial is a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT testing BCG vaccine in adults with mild COVID-19 during convalescence to prevent long COVID development. At 6 and 12-month follow-ups, BCG reduced hearing problems, sleeping, concentration, memory, and vision problems compared to placebo, with mechanistic analyses suggesting immunomodulation through Fas ligand inhibition and increased IL6/IL10 expression.

A multicenter clinical study evaluated L-Arginine and Vitamin C supplementation versus multivitamin control in 1,390 long COVID patients over 30 days. Treatment group showed significantly lower symptom scores and improved exercise tolerance compared to control.

An interventional pilot study testing enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP) in 10 long COVID patients with microvascular dysfunction and angina. The treatment improved six-minute walk distance, reduced angina and fatigue symptoms, and improved quality of life measures, warranting larger controlled studies.

The ReLoAd trial is a randomized controlled trial comparing a 3-week symptom-based inpatient rehabilitation program versus usual care for post-COVID condition (PCC), stratified by symptom clusters (fatigue, cognition, somatization). The rehabilitation intervention significantly improved quality of life and exercise capacity in the fatigue-dominant cluster but not in cognition or somatization clusters at 3-month follow-up.

Randomized controlled trial testing creatine supplementation (6g or 18g daily) combined with physical activity versus placebo in 67 long COVID patients with fatigue over 4 weeks. Creatine 6g/day significantly reduced fatigue scores (PFS-R -2.05, p=0.005) and improved grip strength compared to placebo, with minimal adverse effects.

The ReLoAd RCT evaluated symptom-based multimodal rehabilitation versus usual care in 104 post-COVID patients stratified by predominant symptom clusters (fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, somatic). Rehabilitation significantly improved quality of life and mental health in fatigue and somatic clusters, but showed limited benefit for cognitive dysfunction beyond anxiety reduction.

This is a secondary analysis of the ACTIV-4a randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of P2Y12 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and crizanlizumab on one-year quality-of-life outcomes in critically ill COVID-19 patients with long-term sequelae (PASC). The study found no significant differences in PROMIS quality-of-life scores between treatment groups, though physical and mental health scores were reduced across all groups.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating nintedanib versus placebo in 103 patients with interstitial lung disease following COVID-19 pneumonia. Nintedanib did not significantly improve forced vital capacity, diffusing capacity, or six-minute walk distance at 180 days compared to placebo, with similar adverse event rates between groups.

This quasi-experimental study evaluated Pain Apprehension Re-Activation of Movement (PARAM) using virtual reality compared to conventional exercises for treating kinesiophobia in 84 long COVID patients (silk weavers). Both interventions reduced kinesiophobia and pain, but the VR-based PARAM protocol showed significantly faster and more consistent improvements across all measured outcomes.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation with functional exercises in 67 individuals after COVID-19 hospital discharge. The intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in functional capacity (6MST), walking performance (2MSWT), chair stand test, and quality of life compared to controls.

This study evaluates erectile dysfunction (ED), anxiety, and depression in 114 men with long-term COVID-19 infection, with 40 ED patients receiving daily tadalafil 5 mg supplementation for 2 months. The results show ED is primarily psychological in COVID-19 patients and responds completely to tadalafil treatment.

This RCT compared synchronous vs asynchronous telerehabilitation programs in 36 COVID-19 survivors with severe respiratory impairment over 8 weeks. Both approaches significantly improved exercise capacity and lower extremity function, with synchronous telerehabilitation showing marginal additional benefits for physical function and anxiety reduction.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of supervised telerehabilitation via video-calls compared to home exercise and control groups in 36 post-COVID patients with persistent dyspnea. Telerehabilitation showed significant improvements in dyspnea, fatigue, respiratory muscle strength, and exercise capacity at 6 and 12 weeks, while home-based exercises produced more limited benefits.

This prospective randomized double-blind controlled trial tested sodium phytate nasal spray versus saline in 52 post-COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction lasting >90 days. Sodium phytate significantly improved olfactory function and reduced nasal calcium levels compared to placebo.

Randomized controlled trial (n=392) evaluating bovhyaluronidase azoximer (Longidaza®) versus placebo in patients with long-term pulmonary sequelae of COVID-19 over 180 days. Treatment was associated with significant reductions in exertional desaturation (60%), exertional dyspnea (33-39%), and sustained benefits in older patients, females, and those with cardiovascular disease.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of 8 weeks of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) on aerosol deposition and pulmonary perfusion in 19 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients using gamma scintigraphy imaging. The IMT group showed significant improvements in both aerosol deposition and pulmonary perfusion in both lungs compared to controls, supporting IMT as a rehabilitation strategy for enhancing lung function in post-COVID patients.

Randomized crossover trial testing the impact of surgical masks on exercise performance and cardiorespiratory responses in hospitalized COVID-19 patients near discharge. Mask increased dyspnea at rest and during exercise but did not affect cardiorespiratory parameters or performance in 28 acute post-hospitalization patients.

A double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT evaluating topical glutamate diacetate (GLD) treatment for post-COVID olfactory dysfunction in 66 participants over 6 months. GLD treatment produced statistically significant improvements in olfactory function (threshold, discrimination, and identification scores) and reduced nasal calcium levels compared to placebo, though changes did not reach clinical significance thresholds.

Open-label pilot study (N=45) evaluating the feasibility of a wearable brain-activity sensing device (Muse-S) for stress reduction in long COVID patients over 180 days. Treatment resulted in significant improvements in cognition, sleep, quality of life, stress, and anxiety, with 97% of participants satisfied and planning to continue use.

A pre-post clinical trial evaluating a 4-week individualized digital physiotherapy intervention in 32 long COVID patients. The intervention produced statistically significant improvements in quality of life (SF-12 physical +4.04, mental +6.55; EuroQoL-5D +0.87) with small-to-medium effect sizes, and patients reported high satisfaction rates.

This interim analysis evaluates a hybrid pulmonary rehabilitation program (combining outpatient and home-based sessions) in 15 long COVID patients allocated to rehabilitation (n=10) or usual care (n=5). Results show the rehabilitation program improved exercise tolerance compared to usual care.

This interim analysis evaluates a hybrid pulmonary rehabilitation program (outpatient + home-based sessions) versus usual care in 15 long COVID patients with excessive fatigue, measuring effects on quality of life, emotional status, and functional capacity. Results show that pulmonary rehabilitation improves quality of life and functional capacity in long COVID patients.

A parallel-group RCT testing an online breathing and wellbeing programme (ENO Breathe) using singing techniques in 150 long COVID patients with persistent breathlessness. The intervention improved mental health component of quality-of-life and breathlessness during running compared to usual care.

A randomized controlled trial testing whether 10 minutes of vocal chanting improves psychological wellbeing, social wellbeing, and breathing function in 41 Australian adults with dysfunctional breathing (including long COVID) compared to guided relaxation. Chanting increased positive mood more than relaxation and provided greater benefits for those with dysfunctional breathing on flourishing and social connection measures.

RCT evaluating a remotely-delivered weight management programme for long COVID patients with overweight/obesity (n=234, UK). The intervention was cost-effective compared to usual care with an ICER of £14,754/QALY and showed potential for cost savings from a societal perspective.

A feasibility study of a 4-week Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback (HRV-B) intervention using diaphragmatic breathing in 13 long COVID patients with dysautonomia symptoms. The intervention showed statistically significant improvements in multiple outcome measures (C19-YRS-m, COMPASS-31, RMSSD, WHODAS, EQ5D) with high participant adherence and satisfaction, supporting further investigation in a larger RCT.

ACTIV 4c is a randomized controlled trial testing whether extended thromboprophylaxis with apixaban for 30 days after hospital discharge improves quality of life in COVID-19 patients, measuring outcomes via EQ-5D-5L at 30 and 90 days post-discharge. The trial found that apixaban did not improve quality of life or individual EQ-5D-5L domains compared to placebo, with about one-third of patients experiencing persistent impairment in usual activities up to 90 days after discharge.

This study evaluates the effect of a hybrid pulmonary rehabilitation program (combining outpatient and home-based sessions) on exercise tolerance and quadriceps strength in 38 long COVID patients compared to usual care. The rehabilitation group showed significant improvements in exercise capacity, oxygen consumption, and leg strength, while the usual care group showed no significant changes.

COVCOG is a multicentric randomized trial comparing cognitive psychoeducation versus emotion management counselling for long COVID patients with cognitive difficulties. This is a protocol paper with no results yet reported.

Randomized controlled trial investigating effects of three supervised exercise programs (endurance, strength, concurrent) versus control on physical fitness, pain, fatigue, and biomarkers in older patients with post-COVID-19 sequelae. This is a protocol registration with no results reported.

A randomized pilot study comparing virtual pulmonary rehabilitation delivered via video conference versus self-directed video in 14 post-COVID patients with respiratory symptoms over 8 weeks. The intervention was feasible and safe, with significant improvements in sit-to-stand capacity and symptoms related to fatigue, neurocognitive, and autonomic domains.

This pilot study evaluates a novel micro-choice based concentrated group rehabilitation program delivered over 3-4 days to patients with long COVID (along with low back pain and type 2 diabetes), with 3-month follow-up assessment. Results show high treatment satisfaction (CSQ-8 mean 28.9) and significant improvements in work/social adjustment (WSAS), illness perception (BIPQ), and health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L) across diagnoses (all p<0.001).

This RCT evaluates a multidisciplinary rehabilitation program for COVID-19 patients hospitalized in ICU, comparing standard care with functional and respiratory rehabilitation interventions. While it is a treatment trial in COVID-19 patients, it focuses on acute ICU recovery (hospitalization and 12-week follow-up) rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection), making it outside the scope of long COVID research.

This is a randomized placebo-controlled trial protocol evaluating whether nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) treatment during acute COVID-19 can prevent the development of long COVID, with a target enrollment of 2,000 participants. The protocol describes the study design and primary endpoints but contains no results data.

This is a registered study protocol (NCT05710770) for a double-blinded, randomized, sham-controlled trial of immunoadsorption in ME/CFS patients, including those with post-acute COVID-19 CFS. The abstract describes the planned methods and objectives but does not report any results, as the trial is still recruiting participants.

This RCT evaluated a 6-week semi-supervised exercise intervention in 54 post-COVID healthcare workers, randomized to exercise or control groups. Exercise training significantly improved muscle strength, endurance, and rowing intensity, with within-group reductions in depression and anxiety, and no adverse events reported.

This is a phase 2b randomized controlled trial of umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells for acute respiratory distress syndrome in COVID-19 patients during active infection (April-October 2020). The paper studies acute SARS-CoV-2-induced ARDS, not long COVID, and does not meet inclusion criteria.

topics: mesenchymal stem cells|fatigue|quality of life|post-COVID syndrome
summary: An expanded access program evaluating autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell (HB-adMSC) therapy in 10 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients who received 5 intravenous infusions over 14 weeks with 40-week follow-up. Treatment resulted in significant improvements in fatigue, visual analog symptom scores, and quality-of-life measures (SF-36) with a favorable safety profile.

A randomized crossover trial testing supervised exercise training versus usual care in 89 non-hospitalized post-COVID-19 patients. Exercise training significantly improved peak VO2 (7.43 ml/kg/min difference), muscle strength across multiple measures, and reduced weakness symptoms compared to usual care.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) as a treatment for neurocognitive symptoms in long COVID patients. The study demonstrates that HBOT improves neurocognitive functions and other symptoms associated with post-COVID condition.

This study evaluated the effects of an individualized progressive exercise program on 12 long COVID patients over ~8 weeks. Participants showed significant improvements in 6-minute walk distance, strength, gait speed, fatigue, and quality of life scores, with no post-exercise malaise reported.

A pilot study of 6 long-COVID patients treated with paraprobiotics for 4 weeks, measuring clinical and immunologic outcomes via standardized questionnaires, smartphone app, and wearable sensors. Treatment resulted in improvements in dysautonomia, fatigue, and depression, with reduced activation markers on B cells and nonclassical monocytes and decreased TLR2 expression on T cells.

Randomized controlled trial testing a 12-week home-based exercise training program versus standard care in 32 pediatric COVID-19 patients (4 months post-discharge). Exercise intervention did not improve health-related quality of life but showed trends/improvements in cardiopulmonary parameters including oxygen uptake at anaerobic threshold and heart rate recovery.

This prospective pilot study evaluated virtual pet-assisted therapy (VAT) as a non-contact intervention for long COVID patients at a specialized clinic, with 42 participants engaging with a virtual dog for 10 minutes before clinical consultation. The intervention resulted in statistically significant reductions in total symptom score (7.2%), fatigue (9.5%), dyspnea (17%), memory impairment (13%), and tinnitus (22%), though the study lacked a control group.

This study evaluates an 8-week home-based inspiratory muscle training (IMT) intervention in 147 adults with postacute COVID-19, comparing 111 intervention participants to 36 usual care controls. While IMT produced heterogeneous improvements in inspiratory muscle strength with a dose-response relationship, it showed minimal effects on perceived dyspnea and quality of life, with older age, longer time post-infection, and baseline dyspnea severity associated with smaller strength gains.

RCT comparing 8 weeks of exercise training (aerobic, resistance, combined) versus control on biochemical and hematological markers in COVID-19 survivors. All exercise interventions improved multiple markers; combined training was superior.

A pilot study evaluating a 4-week pulmonary rehabilitation program (3 sessions/week) in 14 Tunisian post-COVID-19 patients with moderate to severe symptoms. The program significantly improved health-related quality of life, anxiety/depression scores, and physical activity levels compared to baseline.

This study evaluates a two-month low-dose methylprednisolone treatment protocol in long COVID patients to assess improvements in symptomatic, radiologic, and laboratory findings. It represents a case series approach to testing corticosteroid therapy for managing post-COVID residual symptoms.

This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of two drugs (MexiB 6 and Cholytilin) in 100 post-COVID patients with fatigue, anxiety/depression, and cognitive impairment over 60 days. Both treatments showed significant improvements: MexiB 6 reduced fatigue and anxiety/depression severity, while Cholytilin improved cognitive function with 74% showing complete regression of cognitive impairment.

An open-label RCT of 60 long COVID patients with hypomagnesemia and vitamin D deficiency compared magnesium chloride plus vitamin D supplementation versus vitamin D alone over 4 months. Combined supplementation was significantly more effective at reducing depressive symptoms (73.2% reached BDI <11 vs 34.5% in control group, p=0.006).

A randomized controlled trial evaluating ethylmethylhydroxypyridine succinate (Neurox), an antioxidant/nootropic agent, for treating post-COVID asthenic syndrome in 129 patients with 4 weeks of follow-up. The treatment group showed statistically significant improvements in fatigue and general symptoms (VAS, MFI-20) compared to controls, suggesting efficacy for post-COVID asthenia.

A non-randomized controlled trial comparing standard post-COVID rehabilitation (n=24) versus standard rehabilitation plus intravenous cytoflavin (n=21) in 45 patients with post-COVID fatigue syndrome. Cytoflavin treatment significantly improved functional status, reduced depression and fatigue, and increased physical exercise tolerance compared to standard rehabilitation alone.

This study evaluated combination therapy (Traumeel S, Ubichinon compositum, Coenzyme compositum) versus eleutherococcus extract plus B vitamins for post-COVID asthenic syndrome in 104 patients. The combination therapy group showed greater improvements in headache and musculoskeletal pain, with better correlation between symptom severity and quality of life compared to the comparison group.

Uncontrolled case series evaluating Anvifen (a GABAergic nootropic with anxiolytic effect) in 92 post-COVID patients with brain fog, stratified by hospitalization status. Treatment with Anvifen 500 mg three times daily for 21 days significantly improved anxiety, depression, cognitive function (MoCA), processing speed (TMT-B), fatigue, sleep quality, and quality of life measures.

This study evaluated the efficacy of Cortexin (a neuroprotective drug) in treating post-COVID cognitive impairment in 109 patients, comparing a treatment group (n=52) receiving 10 mg intramuscularly for 20 days with a comparison group (n=57). The treatment group showed statistically significant improvements in concentration and no adverse events, with the authors concluding Cortexin is effective and safe for post-COVID cognitive dysfunction.

This multicenter prospective open-label study evaluated the efficacy and safety of Aviandr (20 mg twice daily for 4 weeks) for treating anxiety in 109 patients with adjustment disorders following COVID-19 infection. Treatment resulted in 83.5% response rate with significant improvements in anxiety, mood, asthenia, and cognitive function, with sustained benefits after discontinuation and minimal adverse events (3.6% definitely drug-related).

A randomized controlled trial investigating the use of electroacupuncture according to Voll's diagnostic system to determine individualized ribavirin dosing in long COVID patients. The study evaluated the feasibility of using electrodermal activity of acupuncture points to guide treatment dosing.

Randomized controlled trial comparing transcranial electrical stimulation (TES) combined with pharmacotherapy versus pharmacotherapy alone in 150 post-COVID syndrome patients with neurological symptoms. Results show TES as an effective adjunctive component for improving cognitive function, fatigue, and inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6).

This study evaluates the effect of Cytoflavin on autonomic dysfunction in 70 post-COVID syndrome patients divided into treatment (Cytoflavin + standard therapy) and control (standard therapy only) groups over 35 days. The results show that Cytoflavin therapy normalized heart rate variability indicators and reduced asthenia severity, suggesting potential benefit in correcting dysautonomia in post-COVID patients.

This study evaluates hypoxic-hyperoxic therapy as a rehabilitation intervention in 44 patients recovering from acute SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia during the early recovery phase. While it compares treatment outcomes between groups, the paper focuses on acute post-infection recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months later), making it outside the scope of long COVID clinical trials.

This RCT evaluated Tonsilgon N herbal drops added to standard treatment for SARS-CoV-2 associated pharyngitis in 164 patients (81 intervention, 83 control), with 12-week follow-up assessment for post-COVID syndrome development. The intervention group showed significantly reduced throat pain and discomfort, fewer secondary infections, and most notably 3.3 times lower occurrence of post-COVID syndrome compared to control (7.2% vs 25.9%, p=0.001).

This study evaluates a six-week mindfulness-based group therapy intervention (Post-COVID Resilience Program) on depression and anxiety symptoms in long-COVID patients from a hospital COVID Recovery Clinic. Pre- and post-intervention questionnaires showed no significant improvement in depressive or anxiety symptoms, though results were limited by small sample size.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating systemic ozone therapy added to pharmacological treatment for post-COVID cognitive impairment in 140 patients aged 18-45. The intervention group showed statistically significant improvements in BDNF levels and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores compared to pharmacological treatment alone, with 95% of subjects achieving complete resolution of cognitive symptoms.

A non-randomized controlled trial evaluating BESTFertil antioxidant complex in 60 men with post-COVID history, comparing treated (12 weeks) vs control groups on semen parameters and asthenic syndrome. Treatment group showed statistically significant improvements in total motile sperm count and sperm DNA fragmentation, with reduced asthenic symptoms compared to controls.

RCT of 150 post-COVID patients comparing transcranial electrical stimulation plus monopharmacotherapy versus monopharmacotherapy alone for depression and sleep disturbances. Treatment group showed significant improvements in depression, clinical global impression, and insomnia severity, with 95% achieving complete remission of post-COVID manifestations.

This randomized controlled trial (n=51) evaluated the effectiveness of ozone therapy added to comprehensive rehabilitation programs for post-COVID patients. Daily ozone therapy showed greater effectiveness than control and every-other-day approaches on laboratory parameters and quality of life measures, with no adverse reactions reported.

This study evaluated the effects of a nutraceutical combining green tea extract, vitamin C, D, and zinc on biochemical markers and symptom questionnaires in post-COVID patients. Results showed improvements in inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6) and patient-reported outcomes including post-exertional malaise and sleep quality.

A quasi-experimental study evaluating a 14-day complex cardiopulmonary rehabilitation programme in 68 post-COVID syndrome patients, measuring respiratory function, exercise capacity, and quality of life. The intervention significantly improved 6-minute walk test distance, dyspnea scores, quality of life (EQ-5D, PCFS), and respiratory function metrics.

A single-centre interventional study evaluating progesterone therapy (oral and vaginal forms) for menstrual cycle disorders in women with long COVID, with or without gastrointestinal symptoms. Vaginal micronized progesterone showed better efficacy and tolerability than oral forms, with 87-89% of participants experiencing improvement after 6 months.

This is a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial comparing a six-week supervised multimodal rehabilitation program (including isometrics, breathing exercises, aerobic conditioning, and cognitive remediation) to self-guided education in PASC patients. No results are presented as recruitment is ongoing.

This appears to be a study protocol for investigating pulmonary rehabilitation in post-acute COVID-19 patients. The abstract is incomplete and does not present results, indicating this is a protocol-only publication.

This study reports on 24 long COVID patients treated with dual antiplatelet therapy (clopidogrel + aspirin), a direct oral anticoagulant (apixaban), and a proton pump inhibitor for one month. All 24 treated patients reported resolution of main symptoms including fatigue, with corresponding decreases in fibrin amyloid microclots and platelet pathology scores.

This is a 1-year follow-up study of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of mesenchymal stem cell treatment in severe COVID-19 patients. While it studies a treatment intervention in a rigorous RCT design, it focuses on acute/severe COVID-19 recovery (lung lesions, imaging, basic symptoms) during the acute phase, not on long COVID sequelae occurring weeks-to-months post-infection.

A double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized crossover trial testing whether high-dose coenzyme Q10 (500 mg/day) reduces the number or severity of post-COVID-19 condition symptoms over 20 weeks in 119 participants. CoQ10 treatment did not significantly improve EQ-5D health index or PCC symptom scores compared to placebo.

A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled pilot study evaluating transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) on the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for post-COVID fatigue in 47 patients. Active tDCS showed statistically significant improvement in physical fatigue at end of treatment and one-month follow-up compared to sham, with secondary benefits for depressive symptoms.

This double-blinded multicenter randomized trial evaluated olfactory training, um-PEA-LUT (palmitoylethanolamide with luteolin), and combination therapy in 202 long COVID patients with persistent smell dysfunction lasting >6 months. Combined therapy (olfactory training plus daily um-PEA-LUT) achieved 89.2% improvement in odor identification at 90 days, significantly outperforming either monotherapy alone.

Randomized controlled trial (n=50) evaluating a dietary supplement for post-infectious fatigue and astheno-neurotic symptoms in 38 ARVI and 12 COVID-19 patients over 14 days. The supplement showed modest benefits in reducing C-reactive protein levels and fatigue scores (FAS scale) compared to control, with no significant differences in dyspnea or depression.

This quasi-experimental study evaluated the effect of olfactory training on restoring smell and taste in 200 COVID-19 patients divided into study and control groups. Olfactory training significantly accelerated smell restoration (3.0 vs 5.5 weeks) and taste recovery compared to control, with p<0.0001.

This RCT evaluates oral vitamin A combined with nasal steroid spray for recovery of olfactory dysfunction in COVID-19 patients. However, the study focuses on acute post-infection anosmia/hyposmia rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months after acute infection), and does not meet the inclusion criteria for long COVID research.

Randomized controlled trial comparing pedometer-based walking alone versus combined with laser acupuncture in 60 post-COVID patients over 4 weeks. Both treatments significantly improved outcomes including fatigue, exercise capacity, and quality of life, with combined therapy showing greater improvements.

Open-label case series evaluating tofisopam (Grandaxin®) 150 mg/day for anxiety, vegetative symptoms, and insomnia in post-COVID patients over 6 weeks. Treatment significantly reduced anxiety (HAM-A 31.4 to 12.08), vegetative disorders, and insomnia severity in all patients, with maximum improvements at 6 weeks.

A randomized controlled trial comparing diaphragmatic stimulation combined with breathing exercises versus breathing exercises alone in 204 patients with respiratory dysfunction including post-COVID patients. The combined intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in pain, FEV1 (6.6%), and oxygen saturation (3.9%) compared to control.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated pirfenidone plus prednisolone versus prednisolone alone in 50 patients with post-COVID-19 fibrosis, measuring lung function and quality of life outcomes over 3 months. The pirfenidone group showed significantly greater improvements in all parameters including 6-minute walk distance, lung function, and CT severity scores by 3 months.

This study evaluated the effect of 8 weeks of combined exercise training (aerobic, resistance, and breathing exercises) versus breathing exercises alone on functional capacity in 40 post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis patients. Combined exercise training significantly improved dyspnea scores and 6-minute walk test distance compared to breathing exercises alone, with no significant change in pulmonary function.

A quasi-experimental pre-post study evaluating the effect of a telehealth-delivered physiotherapy intervention program on dyspnea, fatigue, and functional status in 60 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients. Results showed statistically significant improvements across all three outcomes at 8 weeks post-intervention and 12-week follow-up.

A randomized controlled trial testing vitamin D and omega-3 supplementation in 110 post-COVID patients with persistent anosmia versus 110 healthy controls. Treatment group showed significant improvements in smell recovery (24.1 vs 28.9 days) and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, TNFα, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, CRP) compared to control.

This interventional parallel study evaluated the effect of mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) on mental health, mindfulness, and sleep quality in post-COVID university students (n=students from nursing/midwifery faculties, 67% with COVID history). MBSR significantly improved general health scores but showed no significant effects on mindfulness or sleep quality compared to controls.

A randomized clinical trial evaluating Bharangi Guda, an Ayurvedic rejuvenation therapy, in 30 post-COVID patients with persistent fatigue, weakness, and respiratory symptoms. The treatment showed significant improvements in subjective parameters and some objective parameters.

This study evaluated the efficacy of recombinant interferon α-2b with antioxidant vitamins for treating chronic recurrent prostatitis in 52 post-COVID-19 patients across three treatment groups. Combined interferon therapy and monotherapy with interferon showed sustained clinical and laboratory improvements at 3 and 6 months, compared to antibiotic-only treatment.

This interventional study evaluated Ayurvedic Virechana Karma (purgation therapy) treatment in 15 post-COVID patients to assess effects on Dosha imbalances. Results showed significant improvements in Vata, Pitta, and Kapha Dosha markers post-treatment, with particularly strong effects on Pitta-related symptoms.

A randomized controlled trial of a 3-week web-based yogic breathing and meditation program in 68 long COVID patients, comparing intervention to waitlist control. The intervention showed significant improvements in mood disturbance, dyspnea dimensions, and somatic symptom burden, with participants reporting enhanced resilience and symptom management through the digital platform.

This study evaluates a structured exercise protocol for COVID-19 patients during and after ICU hospitalization to improve physical functional performance. While it addresses post-ICU recovery, it focuses on acute COVID-19 patients recovering from active infection rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months after acute infection).

This pilot study evaluates the effects of short-term hyperbaric oxygen treatment on long COVID symptoms in a series of patients. The research investigates whether hyperbaric therapy can improve the physical, neurocognitive, and psychiatric symptoms characteristic of long COVID.

Prospective pilot study (n=22, 15 followed up) evaluating a 2-day multidisciplinary team assessment for post-COVID-19 condition patients in specialist care, with 6-month follow-up. No statistically significant improvements in pain, anxiety, depression, fatigue, or cognition were observed, though 76.9% of participants perceived the intervention as helpful.

Randomized controlled trial comparing videoconferencing-guided synchronous telerehabilitation versus mobile application-guided asynchronous telerehabilitation in 27 COVID-19 survivors over 8 weeks. Both interventions improved respiratory, exercise, and activity parameters, with videoconferencing showing superior effects on resting oxygen saturation and post-exertion saturation.

This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness of a nutritional supplement combination (VITAMIC BIOSEN®) containing curcumin, vitamin C, and Boswellia serrata in individuals with long COVID symptoms. The research assesses outcomes in vaccinated patients with persistent symptoms lasting more than 4 weeks post-infection.

This study evaluates the effectiveness of inosine pranobex treatment in 20 long COVID patients with human herpes virus type 6 (HHV6) reactivation, compared to 20 healthy controls. Treatment demonstrated 60.1% clinical efficacy and 79.4% virological efficacy over 12 weeks with good tolerability and safety.

Open-label pilot study evaluating transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (auricular branch) in 15 long COVID/chronic fatigue syndrome patients. Eight of 15 patients (53%) showed positive response to treatment, meeting the pre-specified success criterion of ≥33% response rate.

This interventional study evaluated the effect of 8 weeks of yoga on pulmonary function tests and arterial stiffness in 30 post-COVID-19 patients with mild to moderate disease. Yoga practice resulted in significant improvements in FEV1, FVC, and respiratory parameters, as well as significant reductions in arterial stiffness markers (baPWV and cfPWV).

Open-label study comparing 30 post-COVID-19 subjects receiving 150 mg daily Pycnogenol® supplement plus standard management to 30 controls receiving standard management alone over 3 months. Pycnogenol® group showed significantly greater improvement in endothelial function, microcirculation, and post-COVID symptoms with no reported adverse effects.

A controlled trial comparing Selank (an immunotropic peptide) plus neuroprotective complex versus neuroprotective complex alone in 64 post-COVID patients with asthenia and cognitive dysfunction. Selank showed efficacy in improving fatigue, mental performance, and associated anxiety/depressive symptoms over 30 days.

This study evaluated the feasibility and acute effects of combined aerobic, strength, and breathing exercises on pulmonary function in 36 women with post-COVID-19 syndrome. The exercise intervention was safe and feasible, producing significant improvements in most pulmonary function measures and oxygen saturation with medium to large effect sizes.

A pilot study evaluating a 10-week singing and breathing retraining intervention (SingStrong) for long COVID patients. Participants (n=21) showed significant improvements in breathlessness, usual activities, pain, voice quality, and cognitive symptoms, with positive qualitative feedback supporting the intervention's promise.

This study evaluated a lactobacillus and inulin blend on 126 COVID-19 patients (40 early phase, 86 chronic phase with average 120 days of symptoms) over 30 days. Cough, fatigue, and well-being scores significantly improved in both groups, with 82% of those with baseline GI symptoms showing improvement, suggesting the probiotic intervention may benefit long COVID patients with gut dysbiosis.

A randomized controlled trial comparing traditional resistance training (TRAD) versus elastic resistance training (ELAS) in 8 long COVID patients over 12 weeks. Both interventions safely increased handgrip strength by ~12% and reduced fatigue, bone/joint pain, and memory loss scores by 48-53%, with the elastic resistance group showing significant overall symptom score reduction (~45%).

Randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of a 6-week physical therapy program on quality of life and cardiorespiratory endurance in 60 COVID-19 patients during long-term rehabilitation. The intervention group showed significant improvements in physical functioning, vitality, mental health, and 6-minute walk test distance at 6 weeks and 12 months compared to controls.

A 12-week blended digital and community-based rehabilitation programme combining remote and in-person exercise sessions was delivered to 601 long COVID patients in the UK. The programme significantly improved dyspnea, activity status, wellbeing, and quality of life scores, and reduced healthcare utilization.

A quasi-experimental study evaluating the effectiveness of Active Cycle of Breathing Technique (ACBT) on VO2 max improvement in 15 COVID-19 survivors using a pre-post test design. The intervention significantly increased VO2 max (mean pretest 9.04 ± 0.479 vs posttest 9.68 ± 0.307, p = 0.000), demonstrating that ACBT breathing exercises are effective for improving cardiorespiratory function in post-COVID individuals.

This prospective study evaluated the efficacy of a biologically active supplement (syrup containing choline, glycine, lysine, B vitamins, zinc, magnesium, and herbal extracts) plus routine care versus routine care alone in 65 children aged 7-11 years with post-COVID anxiety disorders over 42 days. The treatment group showed significant improvements in asthenic syndrome symptoms and behavioral/sleep outcomes compared to controls, with good tolerability.

A feasibility study of individually tailored internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (ICBT) for psychological symptoms in adults during the final phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, with 66.7% of participants meeting post-COVID syndrome criteria. The study found statistically significant improvements in depression, anxiety, PTSD, loneliness, and exhaustion, though completion rates were low (62.5% post-treatment assessment).

This study evaluates the long-term safety and post-COVID-19 complications in 34 patients who received plitidepsin during acute COVID-19 hospitalization, with follow-up median 16.8 months post-treatment. Results show favorable long-term safety profile with low rates of post-COVID complications (14.7% with recurrent infection, 5.9% with new chest X-ray findings), normal spirometry/lung function in most patients, and no disease-related rehospitalizations.

This non-randomized trial evaluated a developed physical therapy program for elderly post-COVID patients with sarcopenia compared to standard protocol-based rehabilitation. The intervention group showed statistically significantly better outcomes in hand grip strength, balance, and activities of daily living compared to both controls and standard rehabilitation.

A non-randomized experimental study comparing three dosages of pulmonary rehabilitation programs (12, 24, or 36 sessions) in 60 post-severe COVID-19 patients who had received mechanical ventilation. All groups showed significant improvements in respiratory function, exercise capacity, and quality of life that persisted at 1-year follow-up, with no significant differences between dosages.

The COVIVA study is a prospective comparative cohort study with a nested randomized controlled trial of ivabradine for long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) or inappropriate sinus tachycardia (IST). This is a protocol paper describing the planned study design and methodology, with no results reported yet.

A non-randomized study of 58 COVID-19 patients comparing those who received oral bacteriotherapy (probiotics) during hospitalization (n=24) versus standard treatment only (n=34), with fatigue assessment at 6-month follow-up. Probiotic-treated patients showed significantly lower fatigue rates (41% vs 76%) and distinct serum metabolite profiles suggesting mechanisms involving glucose utilization and energy pathways.

One-arm open-label study of 51 long COVID patients evaluating a dietary supplement formulation containing β-caryophyllene, pregnenolone, and seven other compounds. All 12 measured symptoms (fatigue, weakness, cardiac, neurological, dyspnea, GI, anosmia/ageusia, anxiety, joint pain, rash, cough, insomnia) showed significant improvement at 2 and 4 weeks, with 72-84% of participants experiencing symptom attenuation and no significant adverse effects.

Open-label case series evaluating pyridostigmine's effect on hand grip strength in 20 post-infectious ME/CFS patients. Pyridostigmine produced immediate improvement in hand grip strength post-exertion (median 2.6 kg increase) and reduced orthostatic heart rate response.

A pilot study evaluated transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (t-VNS) as a treatment for 24 female long COVID patients, with assessments at baseline, post-intervention (10 days), and 1-month follow-up. Significant improvements were observed in cognition, anxiety, depression, and sleep at post-intervention, with fatigue improvements delayed until 1-month follow-up, supporting further rigorous investigation through larger RCTs.

A prospective, multicenter, open-label single-arm study of a 16-week tele-yoga intervention in 86 long COVID patients with elevated psychological stress, showing significant reductions in perceived stress, anxiety, and insomnia at week 4 and 16. Both 25 and 50-minute yoga programs proved safe and effective, with symptom improvements correlating with session adherence.

A feasibility study of a four-week multidisciplinary rehabilitation program including whole-body cryostimulation for 16 post-COVID patients with obesity. The program showed significant improvements in anthropometric measures, inflammatory profiles, physical performance, pain reduction, and psychological well-being, with cryostimulation identified as a safe complementary intervention.

topics: autonomic nervous system|heart rate variability|virtual reality|rehabilitation
summary: A study of 18 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients assigned to either 16 or 24 sessions of multimodal immersive virtual reality intervention combining cognitive training, physical exercise, and mindfulness practices. HRV parameters temporarily decreased mid-intervention then recovered by end, with no significant differences between groups, suggesting session intensity may matter more than duration for modulating HRV in PCC patients.

This non-randomized controlled trial evaluated the efficacy of yogic breathing techniques (short and long duration protocols) in COVID-positive patients, COVID-recovered patients, and healthcare workers. The intervention reduced D-dimer levels and improved exercise capacity (6-minute walk test distance) in COVID-recovered and post-COVID populations, suggesting potential benefit for managing persistent post-COVID symptoms.

A case series of 9 long COVID patients with persistent symptoms received a 4-day prednisone course, with immune profiling before and after treatment plus 4-month follow-up. Corticosteroid treatment reversed pro-inflammatory immune alterations and correlated with clinical symptom improvement.
