A non-randomized controlled trial evaluating slow-paced breathing (SPB) with HRV biofeedback as an intervention for long COVID symptoms in healthcare workers. After one month of at-home SPB training, participants showed significant improvements in cognitive impairment, chest pain, fatigue, headache, and dizziness, with modest gains in manual dexterity.

This feasibility study evaluated an 8-week online music therapy protocol (singing, wind instruments, music visualizations) in 24 long COVID patients with respiratory symptoms. Participants showed significant improvements in dyspnea (MRC Dyspnea, p=0.008) and breathing perception, with gains maintained at 12 weeks.

A randomized controlled trial testing whether PEA-LUT (palmitoylethanolamide and luteolin) with or without olfactory training improves olfactory dysfunction and memory in 69 long COVID patients. PEA-LUT therapy showed significant improvement in odor identification scores at 3 months, with benefits sustained at 6 months.

A prospective case series evaluating individualized and controlled exercise training in 41 long COVID patients over 12 weeks in an ambulatory setting. The intervention significantly improved fatigue scores and exercise capacity (sit-to-stand test), with greater improvements in patients with moderate versus severe post-COVID syndrome severity.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of balneotherapy (thermal baths, mineral wraps, halotherapy) on musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and quality of life in post-COVID-19 patients across three treatment modalities versus control. The study found significant within-group improvements in pain, muscle tension, fatigue, and sleep, with modest between-group differences favoring ambulatory and inpatient balneotherapy at 3–6 month follow-up.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) versus sham training in 19 individuals with post-COVID-19 syndrome over 8 weeks. IMT significantly improved respiratory muscle strength (MIP), sleep quality (PSQI), quality of life (SF-36), and functional capacity (6MWT distance).

A feasibility study of a physiotherapy-led outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program (twice-weekly aerobic and resistance training) for patients recovering from COVID-19. Enrollment was low (12 of 65 eligible patients) with 25% dropout, but tolerability was high among participants (83-100% for most measures), suggesting the program may be feasible for a subset of recovering patients.

A quasi-experimental pre-post study evaluating a 4-week digital physiotherapy intervention in 32 long COVID patients, measuring functional capacity (1-min STS and SPPB) and treatment adherence. The intervention showed statistically significant improvements (p < 0.05) with small to medium effect sizes and high adherence rates, demonstrating feasibility and safety.

A pilot clinical trial evaluating the effects of a 16-session pulmonary and functional rehabilitation program (including inspiratory muscle training, aerobic exercise, and peripheral muscle strength training) on 29 post-COVID-19 patients. The program resulted in significant improvements in functional capacity (6-minute walk distance increased from 326.3 to 445.4 meters), pulmonary function, and respiratory muscle strength.

A before-and-after feasibility pilot study evaluating a personalized computerized cognitive training (CCT) intervention for 73 long COVID patients with self-reported cognitive dysfunction. Most participants showed significant improvements across cognitive domains (attention, memory, coordination, perception, reasoning) after 8 weeks of home-based gamified training.

A pilot clinical trial evaluating hand exoskeleton-based robotic rehabilitation in 13 post-COVID-19 patients with upper extremity impairment over a 6-week intervention. Results showed significant improvements in motor function (60.4% passive flexion, 28.7% active flexion) and quality of life measures.

A prospective pilot study evaluating hyperbaric oxygenation (HBO) as a treatment for long COVID syndrome in 59 patients who received 10 sessions of HBO over 75 minutes. The study found statistically significant improvements in physical functioning, role limitations, energy, and reduced activity limitations at post-treatment and 3-month follow-up.

A pilot study evaluating aerobic exercise training (20 sessions over 10 weeks) in 14 long COVID patients, measuring cardiorespiratory fitness, quality of life, and immune function. Exercise training improved peak work rate, V.O2peak, fatigue severity, depression, anxiety, and dyspnea without detrimental immunologic effects.

A single-center exploratory pilot study of hochuekkito (traditional Japanese medicine) in 20 long COVID patients with general fatigue, conducted at a specialized outpatient clinic. Results showed a trend for improvement in fatigue scores after 8 weeks of treatment (mean decrease of 4.7 points, 95% CI: 0.5-8.9).

A prospective non-randomized trial of a two-week pulmonary rehabilitation program (respiratory exercises, aerobic training, muscle strengthening) in 77 post-COVID patients in Poland. The intervention significantly improved pulmonary function parameters (FVC, FEV1, DLCO), reduced inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer), and enhanced quality of life across physical, psychological, and environmental domains.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating an epicatechin-enriched supplement (ECES) in 46 long COVID patients with chronic fatigue over 90 days. The study found significant improvements in inflammatory markers, endothelial dysfunction markers, handgrip strength, fatigue scales, and quality of life in the ECES group compared to placebo.

This interventional study evaluated the effectiveness of a 3-week home-based motor and respiratory tele-rehabilitation program in 23 long COVID patients following in-hospital rehabilitation. The program produced significant improvements in motor and respiratory function, including an 18.3% increase in walking distance, suggesting feasibility and potential benefit despite the lack of control group.

This study evaluated vitamin D supplementation (bolus vs daily dosing) in 54 post-COVID-19 condition patients over 2 months, measuring biomarkers (IL-6, GPx) and psychiatric outcomes (HADS). Both supplementation strategies improved antioxidant activity and reduced IL-6 levels, with daily dosing additionally reducing anxiety and depression scores, though neither improved respiratory or fatigue symptoms.

This before-after controlled trial evaluated spinal cord transcutaneous stimulation (scTS) combined with respiratory training in 5 patients with post-COVID-19 respiratory deficits. Results showed scTS + RT produced twice the effect size of RT alone, with significant improvements in forced vital capacity and peak expiratory flow.

This study evaluated hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) as a treatment for post-COVID-19 syndrome in 31 patients who underwent 15 compression sessions. Results showed significant improvements in quality of life, endurance, strength, spirometric parameters, and cognitive function (working memory and attention), with sustained benefits at follow-up.

A pilot study of 7 long COVID patients with ME/CFS and elevated autoantibodies (β2-adrenergic and M3-muscarinic) treated with plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulins. The study found negative associations between autoantibody concentration and quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), suggesting potential therapeutic value of antibody-lowering methods.

Pilot interventional study of 16 post-COVID-19 patients with adhesive capsulitis treated with ultrasound-guided hydrodistension infiltration and early rehabilitation. Treatment resulted in significant improvements in shoulder range of motion and pain reduction (VAS 6.9 to 1.0) over 10 weeks.

This study evaluates recombinant human IL-2 (rhIL-2) as a treatment for post-COVID syndrome by measuring NK cell phenotype and functional activity in patients 3 months after acute COVID-19. Treatment with rhIL-2 was shown to restore peripheral blood NK cell count and functional potential in patients with low NK cell levels.

Single-arm case study evaluating a 12-week personalized supine strengthening exercise program in 17 women with long COVID. The program showed significant improvements in fatigue scores and reductions in body fat percentage, particularly in participants with overweight or obesity.

Pilot study evaluating the feasibility, usability, and safety of an AI-powered telerehabilitation system (ARC Intellicare) for home-based motor and respiratory rehabilitation in 11 post-COVID-19 patients and 10 Parkinson's disease patients. Clinical outcomes including dyspnea, walking distance, fatigue, anxiety, depression, and quality of life improved significantly with no adverse effects reported.

This double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT (n=52) evaluated a multistrain synbiotic formula (Kebirah®) in acute and post-acute COVID-19 patients, administered for 35 days starting at diagnosis. The synbiotic group showed preserved gut microbiota diversity, maintained lymphocyte counts and hemoglobin levels, and enrichment of beneficial bacteria compared to placebo.

This study evaluated the effect of grape polyphenol concentrate supplementation added to standard spa treatment in elderly patients with bronchial asthma and post-COVID syndrome, comparing 40 intervention patients to 30 controls. The intervention group showed statistically significant reductions in C-reactive protein and circulating lipopolysaccharide levels, suggesting the polyphenol concentrate may reduce low-grade inflammation and endotoxemia associated with long COVID.

This study evaluated a multi-component rehabilitation program combining transcutaneous interferential current therapy and therapeutic exercises in 62 post-COVID-19 patients with musculoskeletal symptoms. The treatment significantly reduced back pain, myalgia, arthralgia, and fatigue while improving functional mobility and range of motion.

A prospective interventional trial evaluating an 8-week pulmonary rehabilitation program (3 sessions/week) in 60 post-COVID-19 patients, comparing outcomes between those with severe/critical vs mild/moderate initial infection. Both groups showed significant improvements in handgrip strength, timed up-and-go, 6-minute walk distance, and functional capacity measures, with similar improvement patterns regardless of initial severity.

This study compared two combinative treatment approaches for SARS-CoV-2-induced arthritis: NSAIDs plus corticosteroids versus NSAIDs plus chondroprotective agents. The research hypothesized that the corticosteroid-NSAID combination would produce better clinical outcomes than the chondroprotective-NSAID combination in managing post-COVID arthritis.

A non-randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy of Alvenorm forte and Roncoleukin® in 26 post-COVID patients undergoing outpatient rehabilitation, compared against 30 healthy donors. Treatment resulted in resolution of dyspnea and tachycardia in most patients and restoration of immune and blood parameters.

This study evaluated stochastic resonance therapy (SRT) as a complement to pulmonary rehabilitation in 120 post-COVID patients, comparing a treatment group receiving 15 SRT sessions over 3 weeks with a control group. Both groups improved significantly, but the SRT group showed statistically better improvements in functional efficiency and dyspnea reduction.

This study evaluates the effects of 12 weeks of yogic practice on physical parameters (BMI, muscular endurance, flexibility) in young to middle-aged housewives from rural and urban areas post-pandemic. While it addresses post-COVID health, it does not focus on long COVID specifically (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months after acute infection) and instead studies general post-pandemic wellness in the general population.

Open-label pilot trial of HRG80 Red Ginseng in 188 patients with chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, and post-viral fatigue. Treatment resulted in 60.1% self-rated improvement with significant gains in energy (67%), mental clarity (48%), and stamina (72%).

A randomized placebo-controlled trial evaluating intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxic therapy combined with standard rehabilitation in 50 osteoarthritis patients with post-COVID syndrome. The treatment group showed significant improvements in joint pain (51.4%), depression (52.9%), breathlessness (71.2%), and general health compared to placebo and standard care alone.

A randomized controlled trial of 28 long COVID patients comparing aquatic training in bromine-sodium chloride brine versus fresh water pools. The brine group showed significant improvements in sympathetic nervous system activity, oxidative metabolism, exercise tolerance, and microcirculation compared to fresh water controls.

Open-label comparative effectiveness study testing vortioxetine, escitalopram, and sertraline for treating major depressive disorder in post-COVID syndrome patients over 8 weeks. Vortioxetine showed significant improvements in cognitive function (DSST) and depression/fatigue outcomes compared to the other two antidepressants.

This pilot study evaluated a 16-week hydrogymnastics intervention in 40 adults with obesity and post-COVID cardiopulmonary conditions, comparing an intervention group (n=26) to a comparison group (n=14). The intervention showed improvements in diastolic blood pressure and heart rate in the intervention group, while the comparison group showed broader improvements in weight, BMI, and blood pressure, suggesting potential cardiovascular benefits of aquatic exercise for post-COVID populations.

Open randomized controlled trial evaluating pantohematogen (an iron-rich dietary supplement derived from deer antlers) as an adjunct to sanatorium rehabilitation in 30 post-COVID patients. Results showed pantohematogen improved physical asthenia, dyspnea, autonomic dysfunction, and anxiety compared to rehabilitation alone.

This study evaluated the effects of different frequencies of early physical rehabilitation (1 vs 2 sessions per day) in 102 ICU patients with severe COVID-19 on functional status, cognitive function, and post-COVID syndrome manifestations. Increased rehabilitation frequency led to better psychosocial outcomes and reduced post-COVID symptoms, though short-term improvements in cognitive and physical function were not statistically significant.

Clinical observations of delayed skin manifestations in COVID-19 survivors in the Russian Far East, documenting cutaneous complications during the recovery period. The paper discusses long-term effects and rehabilitation needs but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating Chatushashti Prahari Pippali (CPP), an Ayurvedic herbal intervention, combined with rehabilitation guidelines versus rehabilitation alone for post-COVID syndrome in 112 patients. The combined therapy group showed statistically significant improvements in symptom relief, 6-minute walk test performance, and quality of life measures compared to rehabilitation only.

This study evaluated comprehensive treatment of elderly patients with COPD who experienced COVID-19 in the preceding 3-6 months, comparing nebulizer therapy with N-acetylcysteine and hypertonic saline plus glycine (main group, n=30) against standard acetylcysteine alone (control group, n=30) over 6 months. The main group showed no disease recurrence while the control group had 20% recurrence, suggesting the combined nebulizer and glycine regimen improved outcomes in post-COVID COPD patients.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating web-application guided bimodal olfactory training (MaMadeleine) in 83 long COVID patients with persistent dysosmia. Training improved subjective olfactory function, Sniffin' Sticks test scores, and quality of life in both simple and semantic training groups, with no significant between-group differences but exploratory evidence suggesting potential benefit for patients with semantic memory impairment.

This study evaluated a synthetic peptide derived from GM-CSF (Acegram-spray) applied topically to mucous membranes in 21 post-COVID patients with immune system disturbances. The treatment significantly improved neutrophil bactericidal activity and T helper cell percentages, but showed limited effects on other immune parameters, suggesting the need for additional immunomodulatory approaches.

A randomized controlled trial comparing pharmacotherapy alone versus pharmacotherapy plus cognitive behavior therapy (CBT) for post-COVID-19 depression in 156 Indian patients. CBT combined with medication showed significantly better improvement in depression scores than medication alone.

Prospective intervention study evaluating a 6-week telemedicine-based pulmonary rehabilitation program in 50 recovered COVID-19 pneumonitis patients. Post-intervention assessments showed significant improvements in respiratory function (6MWT, mMRC, 30s-STS), quality of life (SF-36), and anxiety levels.

This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with aerobic exercise in systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome. The intervention targets pain and fatigue symptoms associated with long COVID.

A randomized controlled trial evaluating an 8-week supervised multicomponent exercise program versus WHO physical activity recommendations in 48 Honduran adults with persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms. The exercise intervention group showed significant improvements in anxiety, sleep quality, cognitive function, and functional capacity (Sit to Stand test and 6-minute walk distance) compared to the control group.

A case series evaluating the efficacy and safety of iWALL tablet, a polyherbal Ayurvedic formulation, in 25 patients with mild post-COVID syndrome over 3 months. The study reports statistically significant improvements in symptoms including fatigue, myalgia, cough, sore throat, and shortness of breath.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the impact of home-based exercise on menstrual pain severity in 30 post-acute COVID-19 women, comparing an exercise group (n=15) to a control group avoiding exercise. The exercise group showed significant reduction in pain intensity (p=0.000) while the control group showed no significant change, suggesting exercise is beneficial for menstrual pain relief in post-COVID women.

An open-label, two-armed randomized controlled Phase II pilot trial evaluating an Ayurvedic herbal immunity booster formulation in post-COVID survivors experiencing prolonged symptoms including fatigue, recurrent infections, and cognitive disturbances. The study aims to assess efficacy and safety of the herbal formulation in improving immune function and quality of life.

This study evaluated blue light therapy in 43 long COVID patients with persistent fatigue, with participants receiving 10 sessions of full-body blue light irradiation over 5 consecutive days. Results showed significant improvements in fatigue severity, quality of life, and serum biomarkers (tryptophan, kynurenine, serotonin) following treatment.

This study evaluates the impact of non-surgical scaling and root planing (SRP) on HbA1c levels in post-COVID patients with chronic periodontitis, comparing treated (n=10) versus untreated (n=10) groups over 3 months. Results show that SRP treatment significantly improved HbA1c levels and clinical parameters in post-COVID patients compared to controls, suggesting a link between periodontal treatment and metabolic markers in the post-COVID population.

This study evaluated the effect of a 4-week telerehabilitation pulmonary program on functional status in COVID-19 survivors using the 30-Second Sit-To-Stand Test. Results showed significant improvement in functional status post-intervention (7.75±2.19 to 13.70±4.23 repetitions), with a strong positive correlation between pre- and post-program assessments.

This study evaluates hyperbaric oxygen therapy as a pulmonary rehabilitation method for long COVID patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, comparing 23 treated patients to 20 controls over three months. The treatment group showed significant improvements in exercise tolerance, inflammatory markers (CRP, ferritin), FEV1 values, and CT-measured lung involvement, while the control group showed minimal changes.

A pre-experimental study evaluating the effectiveness of diaphragmatic breathing exercises on respiratory problems in 60 post-COVID patients attending outpatient clinics in Pune, India. The study found significant reduction in respiratory symptoms (chest pain, cough, cold) following the breathing exercise intervention using Wilcoxon sign test.

A quasi-experimental study evaluating the effectiveness of Qing Fei Pai Du Tang (QFPDT), a traditional Chinese herbal formula, for treating joint pain in 30 long COVID patients diagnosed with cold-damp syndrome. Results showed an average VAS pain reduction of 3.1 points with 80% of participants experiencing significant pain relief and no serious adverse effects reported.

A case series of 83 long COVID patients (>6 months post-infection) who received medicinal leech therapy (MLT) applied on days 6 and 11 of treatment. Neuropsychological assessments showed improvements in cognitive function, autonomic symptoms, sleep quality, anxiety, and depression measures after the MLT procedures.

This RCT evaluates frequency-controlled ear acupuncture for treating COVID-19-related olfactory dysfunction, comparing acupuncture sessions to sham laser treatment in 40 patients. While it studies a treatment for a COVID-19 symptom, olfactory dysfunction during acute infection is not a long COVID focus—the paper does not address persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection, making it outside the long COVID scope.

Randomized trial of home-based pulmonary rehabilitation (HBPR) in 70 COVID-19 patients showing reduced anxiety and depression scores after 4 weeks compared to routine care. This study focuses on acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

This RCT evaluated an 8-week selected-exercise-rehabilitation (SER) program in COVID-19 survivors with fatigue and pulmonary damage, measuring fatigue, inflammatory markers, physical function, and mental health. The intervention group showed significant improvements across all measured variables compared to controls, supporting SER as a therapeutic approach for managing long-term post-COVID fatigue.

This open-label randomized controlled trial evaluated thiamine (vitamin B1) supplementation in 66 post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients, comparing treatment plus supportive care versus supportive care alone. Vitamin B1 significantly accelerated symptom resolution, with improvements in myalgia, anosmia, ageusia, fatigue, and sleep disturbances by week five, and doubled recovery rates by week seven compared to controls.

This study evaluated an 8-week water-based exercise program in 21 post-COVID-19 patients, measuring fatigue via the MFI-20 and quality of life via the EQ-5D-5L. The intervention was associated with maintenance of quality of life and fatigue levels, suggesting water-based exercise is a safe rehabilitation option for mild to moderate post-COVID recovery.

A pilot study examining eucalyptus essential oil aromatherapy in 15 post-COVID syndrome patients, evaluating effects on dyspnea, back pain, and anxiety using mMRC, VAS, and BAI scales. Results showed statistically significant improvements in all three symptoms following oil inhalation treatment.

A double-blinded pilot RCT (n=30 post-LSCS women) compared combined body weight, abdominal strengthening, and breathing exercises (Group B) versus breathing exercises with upper/lower limb strengthening (Group A) for post-COVID symptoms including fatigue, dyspnea, and arthromyalgia. Group B showed significantly greater improvements on ultrasonography, dynamometer, and sit-up tests.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated respiratory muscle training using an app-based device in 16 patients with persistent shortness of breath after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The intervention significantly improved respiratory symptoms (SGRQ score), subjective health, maximum ventilation, and exercise capacity in patients with initially low oxygen consumption values.

This study evaluates hypoxytherapy (controlled intermittent hypoxia exposure) as a treatment for respiratory dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients across three groups: healthy controls, untreated post-COVID patients, and post-COVID patients receiving hypoxytherapy. The hypoxytherapy group showed improvements in FVC, FEV1, and peak inspiratory capacity compared to untreated patients, suggesting potential benefits for pulmonary recovery in post-COVID rehabilitation.

Randomized controlled trial comparing aerobic/balance exercises plus relaxation (Group A, n=15) versus relaxation alone (Group B, n=15) in 30 post-COVID-19 patients with anxiety and dizziness over 4 weeks. Group A showed significantly greater reductions in anxiety and dizziness, with improved respiratory function (P < 0.001) compared to Group B.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial testing a synbiotic preparation (SIM01) in adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome in Hong Kong. The treatment alleviated some symptoms at 6 months follow-up.

A randomized controlled multicenter trial comparing exercise training rehabilitation to usual physical therapy in individuals with persistent dyspnea after COVID-19 ARDS. Exercise training was significantly more effective at reducing dyspnea at 90 days compared to usual PT.

Pilot study evaluating stellate ganglion block as a treatment for long COVID symptoms in 17 patients, measuring autonomic dysfunction, fatigue, anxiety, and PTSD symptoms before and after the procedure. Results showed significant improvements in fatigue severity and heart rate, with all patients reporting some degree of symptomatic improvement and no serious adverse events.

Open-label pilot study of dual sympathetic blocks (stellate ganglion blocks) in 20 PASC patients with dysautonomia and pain symptoms. Participants showed significant improvements in autonomic dysfunction (38.4% reduction, p=0.0016), pain interference (48.4% reduction, p<0.001), sleep quality, and fatigue by week four, with 88.2% reporting symptom relief and no adverse events.

The LINCOLN survey assessed the effects of L-Arginine + Vitamin C supplementation versus multivitamin controls on long-COVID symptoms in 1,390 COVID-19 survivors over 30 days. Patients receiving L-Arginine + Vitamin C showed significantly lower symptom scores and improved effort perception compared to the control group.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial evaluating photobiomodulation therapy (red LED light) for treating xerostomia (dry mouth) in 10 long COVID patients over 6 weeks. The intervention showed no significant superiority over placebo on primary outcomes, though some individual items showed improvement in the photobiomodulation group.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 RCTs examining the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation (in-person and telerehabilitation) on PASC outcomes. It finds PR significantly improves exercise capacity, fatigue, and quality of life compared to usual care, with telerehabilitation being equivalent to in-person modalities.

This paper reports findings from the STOP-PASC randomized controlled trial of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir versus placebo in adults with long COVID, analyzing patient-reported outcome trajectories over 15 weeks. Using latent class trajectory modeling, the authors identified distinct symptom trajectories across multiple PRO measures and found no overall treatment benefit from nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, emphasizing the clinical heterogeneity of long COVID and the need for validated, long COVID-specific outcome instruments.

This study evaluates add-on Ayurveda therapy versus standard care in oxygen-dependent diabetic COVID-19 patients over 60 days, measuring symptom resolution and inflammatory markers. While the paper mentions 'post-acute sequelae,' the population and focus are on acute/hospitalized COVID-19 patients (oxygen-dependent, on Remdesivir), not long COVID patients with persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection.

This RCT evaluates N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment in 63 COVID-19 patients over 6 months post-discharge, measuring patient-reported outcomes via the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire. NAC treatment showed significantly faster improvement in respiratory quality of life compared to placebo, but the study focuses on acute/post-acute COVID-19 recovery rather than long COVID as a distinct long-term condition.

This study evaluated 162 post-COVID syndrome patients treated with Mexidol (an antioxidant), measuring changes in neurological, psychological, and quality-of-life outcomes using validated scales. Treatment with Mexidol led to improvements in asthenia, anxiety, depression, and overall quality of life.

A social media analysis of 2,588 tweets from UK healthcare workers about long COVID in children and young people (January 2021-2022). The paper documents HCWs' perceptions and concerns about pediatric long COVID management but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This prospective cohort study examined how plant-based dietary practices influence COVID-19 outcomes including long COVID risk in Seventh-day Adventists compared to non-Adventists, and implemented a targeted educational nutrition intervention. Adventists showed significantly lower COVID-19 incidence and reduced long COVID risk, with the nutrition education intervention producing large effect sizes and sustained behavioral change in supplement and fortified food use.

A mixed-methods study surveying 135 long COVID patients and conducting 29 interviews to examine information accessibility, trust, and support experiences. The paper identifies information marginalization barriers and defensive coping strategies but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Mixed methods feasibility study of pacing interventions in non-hospitalised long COVID patients, part of the Therapies for Long COVID (TLC) trial. Participants reported pacing helped with motivation and activity planning, though concerns about complexity and time constraints were noted, indicating feasibility but requiring further research.

A cross-sectional mixed-methods study investigating the prevalence of oral manifestations of long COVID in 104 patients and examining healthcare professionals' views and experiences managing these conditions. The study found that 78% of respondents reported oral conditions, with changes in taste/smell (58%), dry mouth (48%), and mouth sores (45.7%) being most common, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A national survey of 1,320 Belgian long COVID patients assessing their unmet healthcare needs, symptom burden, and impact on quality of life and employment. The study identified gaps in health professional knowledge, diagnostic approaches, and interdisciplinary care coordination, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This paper analyzes and compares Long COVID definitions used across 34 European countries through a retrospective descriptive study with questionnaires. It finds significant variation in definitions and highlights the need for standardization to improve diagnostic processes and patient care, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This mixed-methods study evaluated a multi-component self-management platform (app, website, CRM messaging) designed to support long COVID-19 recovery in Hong Kong, using interviews and cross-sectional surveys to assess user intentions and barriers to adoption. The platform's features across six usability attributes (performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, information security, enjoyment) influenced >80% of participants' usage intentions, with digital access barriers most prominent for older users.

This mixed-methods study from the REACT cohort examines the prevalence and impact of long COVID among 123,463 healthcare workers and essential workers in England, finding higher rates in patient-facing HCWs (11%) and identifying occupational health challenges. The paper includes quantitative prevalence data and qualitative interviews exploring barriers to care and work-related impacts, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A mixed-methods study evaluating the acceptance and usefulness of mHealth telemonitoring in long COVID patients, examining patient perceptions of remote vital parameter monitoring via digital sensors and smartphone applications. The study addresses a gap in evidence regarding the value and feasibility of telemonitoring for long COVID management, unlike the clearer benefits demonstrated in acute COVID-19.

This retrospective study evaluated 195 COVID-19 ARDS survivors in NYC, finding 54% met Long COVID criteria, with Hispanic/Latinx patients facing greater barriers to rehabilitation and follow-up care. Qualitative interviews identified structural and healthcare-related barriers rooted in racism and poverty as key factors impacting post-COVID recovery.

A mixed-methods study surveying long COVID patients (n=126) and primary care practitioners (n=72) in Germany to explore their experiences with medical care and identify gaps in service provision. The study found uncertainty and a need for structured, coordinated healthcare pathways but did not test any treatment intervention.

This mixed-methods feasibility study evaluated a workplace-delivered multidisciplinary allied health service (ReCOV) for hospital staff with long COVID, with 23 participants receiving appointments across exercise physiology, occupational therapy, and neuropsychology over a median of 15 weeks. While participants valued the service's convenience and multidisciplinary approach, many perceived limited physical health improvement and desired longer treatment duration, suggesting the intervention was feasible to deliver but efficacy requires further confirmation.

This paper presents five empirical studies examining long-term consequences of COVID-19 in older adults across four countries, using a biopsychosocial framework. The studies investigate quality of life, fall risk, technology adoption, and technology-based interventions (body-mind and exercise programs) to mitigate pandemic-related health consequences.

A cross-sectional mixed-methods study examining how occupational physicians in Japan support employees with long COVID through interviews and questionnaires. The study describes current occupational health practices and support strategies but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or measure patient outcomes.

This paper reports findings from nationally representative surveys and focus groups exploring long COVID experiences in adults aged 50+, examining symptom burden, employment impact, and care needs. While it documents long COVID prevalence (27% among infected) and impacts (brain fog, fatigue, depression, anxiety), it does not study or evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A qualitative nested study within a randomized controlled trial examining patient experiences of supervised telerehabilitation and home-based respiratory muscle training (TSHB-RMT) for post-COVID-19 symptoms. Patients reported rapid perceived benefits from the intervention, though extended follow-up was needed to prevent program abandonment.

Mixed-methods study exploring barriers and facilitators of employment for workers with long COVID through interviews with occupational physicians and a questionnaire survey in Japan. Identifies 28 barriers/facilitators across 6 themes (company characteristics, workplace acceptance, work description, medical care, personal factors, symptoms) but does not test any intervention or treatment.

Longitudinal mixed-methods study examining the lived experience of long COVID in healthcare workers, including impact on quality of life, health services use, and work capacity. Primarily an observational cohort study documenting symptom trajectories and psychosocial burden without testing any specific intervention or treatment.

A mixed-methods study evaluating participant experience of a remotely delivered dance-based support programme for long COVID patients, involving 13 participants across 10 sessions. Participants reported perceived improvements in physical and mental health, increased confidence with movement, and overall satisfaction with the programme.

Mixed-methods study examining the impact of long COVID on UK healthcare workers' health, work patterns, and support received through online surveys (n=471) and qualitative interviews (n=50). Found that long COVID significantly affects work capacity with 90% reporting activity limitations, but this is an observational survey study with no treatment intervention evaluated.

NICO is a pilot study testing an asynchronous narrative-based therapeutic intervention for long COVID patients, measuring depression (PHQ-9) and anxiety (GAD-7) at baseline and 3 months. The intervention showed preliminary improvement in depression with 71% completion rate (12 of 17 participants), demonstrating feasibility as a flexible, scalable approach to mental health support.

topics: return to work|care utilization|activity limitations|occupational health
summary: This cross-sectional study examines care consultations and return-to-work experiences among 157 long COVID patients on Bonaire, Caribbean Netherlands, using logistic regression and qualitative analysis. While it identifies important occupational and healthcare needs, it is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention—patients were not given a specific therapy to evaluate.

A mixed methods study examining clinical characteristics and factors associated with long COVID among 1,359 patients attending post-acute COVID-19 (PAC-19) clinics in Zambia from August 2020 to January 2023. The study found that severe illness, prolonged hospitalization, and comorbidities were significantly associated with long COVID, with prevalence declining from 75.4% at first visit to 26.0% by fifth visit over approximately 7 weeks.

This study analyzes health care access and experiences during COVID-19 in a UK community-based cohort, with focus on socio-demographic inequalities and long COVID care. It finds that socially disadvantaged participants experienced worse access to care and poorer experiences specifically for long COVID, but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

Mixed-methods analysis of a new long-COVID clinic in Hertfordshire examining implementation barriers and facilitators through patient data analysis and healthcare professional interviews. Study describes the care pathway and patient needs but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This is a cross-sectional survey of 145 UK workers with post-COVID symptoms examining work ability and return-to-work experiences. While it documents that 90% experienced post-COVID symptoms and only 15% achieved full return-to-work, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention—it is a descriptive study of workplace accommodations and symptom impacts, not a treatment trial.

Mixed-method survey of 97 long COVID patients at a tertiary care clinic assessing symptom burden, functional impacts, and satisfaction with clinical services. Finds high symptom prevalence (fatigue 77%, brain fog 73%, exercise intolerance 73%) and identifies barriers to care such as scheduling delays and financial concerns, with recommendations for integrated patient-centered care.

Mixed-method study of 20 ICU patients assessing quality-of-life outcomes using WHO QOL BREF and qualitative interviews at 2 months post-discharge. While it documents long COVID sequelae, it is an observational assessment without any treatment intervention and does not meet inclusion criteria for a treatment trial screening.

This cross-sectional study surveyed 144 Brazilian patients with post-COVID syndrome via social media to understand how they navigate diagnosis and seek treatment in the context of contested illness and institutional dismissal. The paper focuses on patient activism, alternative expertise networks, and socioeconomic barriers to care rather than evaluating any intervention or treatment.

A nested intervention study evaluating a digital combined lifestyle intervention with motivational interviewing, counseling, and nutritional supplementation in 95 post-COVID patients. Results showed 74% compliance with individual sessions and patients reported perceived improvements in physical activity, dietary quality, and well-being with sustained changes post-intervention.

A mixed-methods cross-sectional study exploring people's experiences of COVID-19 illness during isolation and identifying perceptions of what would support recovery. The study synthesizes insights into recommendations for supporting people after COVID-19, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention, drug, or treatment.

Mixed-methods study examining health inequities in long COVID care and access barriers for disadvantaged populations across UK clinics and primary care. Identifies under-referral of marginalized groups and describes strategies implemented by LC clinics to improve inclusive service provision.

Multi-centre service evaluation surveying 269 long COVID patients across three UK services to assess symptoms, functional impact, recovery trajectories, and unmet care needs. Study documents high prevalence of fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and ongoing disability, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A mixed-method study auditing occupational therapy practice for post-acute COVID-19 patients in an Australian inpatient rehabilitation setting, analyzing 24 patient records and 10 interviews. Occupational therapists provided occupational engagement support, patient education, and discharge planning, with patients reporting improved occupational performance.

Mixed-methods study exploring cognitive symptoms in 25 UK long COVID patients through focus groups and self-report questionnaires. Identifies cognitive dysfunction as prevalent and proposes a framework for comprehensive rehabilitation targeting neural, individual, and lifestyle factors.

This paper presents a qualitative evaluation embedded in the REGAIN randomised controlled trial, which evaluated home-based online supervised group exercise and psychological support for post-COVID-19 condition compared to usual care. The study found that group sessions were valued by participants, with key themes including peer support, hope for progression, safe exercise environment, and the importance of being listened to and understood.

A prospective cohort study of 68 UK children and young people with persistent post-COVID-19 condition followed over 24 months, identifying two symptom subgroups (frequent vs. less frequent symptoms) and examining associated impairments and qualitative experiences. The study found that even children with fewer symptoms experience significant long-term anxiety and functional impact, highlighting the need for personalized management approaches.

This mixed-methods study explores barriers to healthcare access for long COVID among 471 NHS workers in Scotland through questionnaires and interviews. While it provides important qualitative insights into candidacy-related obstacles to care, it is not a treatment trial and does not evaluate any intervention.

UK-wide survey of 4,500 people with asthma assessing COVID-19 impacts and long COVID prevalence. Study found 56% of asthmatic COVID-19 patients reported long COVID with persistent breathing and asthma management issues, but did not test any treatment intervention.

This UK-wide survey of 3,290 long COVID patients documents the prevalence and characteristics of persistent symptoms 4+ weeks after acute COVID-19, with breathing problems, fatigue, and cognitive symptoms being most common. The study is descriptive and does not evaluate any treatment intervention, focusing instead on symptom patterns and patient experiences with healthcare.

topics: post-traumatic stress|quality of life|psychological impact|social stigma
summary: Qualitative study examining the lived experiences and quality of life of ICU survivors from critical COVID-19 in Wuhan using surveys and interviews. Identified themes of poor physical health, post-traumatic stress, social stigma, and family support but did not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 295 endurance athletes examines symptoms, barriers, and quality of life impacts during return to sport after COVID-19. The study documents high prevalence of persistent cardiopulmonary symptoms and fatigue but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This study evaluates a virtual peer support group intervention for UK health and social care staff with long COVID, using quantitative outcome measures (SWEMWBS and PHQ9) and qualitative thematic analysis. Results show improved wellbeing scores post-intervention and identified key themes including connectedness, reciprocity, and effective facilitation.

This paper describes the development and user-testing of a digital companion app designed to support long COVID patients with symptom monitoring, self-organization, and communication with healthcare providers. The study conducted surveys and interviews with long COVID patients and professionals to inform app design, but presents only a development/prototype study with no clinical outcomes or efficacy evaluation.

This paper describes the co-design process of Long COVID Companion, a voice-based digital health app for monitoring long COVID symptoms, involving both patients and healthcare professionals. The paper presents the development and design of the app but does not report efficacy or effectiveness data, as further studies are needed to evaluate its impact.

This mixed-methods study examines UK Long COVID policies affecting children and young people through policy document review and social media discourse analysis (12,650 posts). It identifies gaps in accountability, inclusiveness, and transparency but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This mixed-methods study examines how clinic-led onboarding and interaction practices influence patient engagement in the LWCR digital health program for long COVID care across seven clinics. The research identifies four key clinic practices associated with higher engagement (pre-assessment onboarding, proactive communication, patient education, experienced staff) but does not evaluate the efficacy of any specific treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional study with qualitative interviews examines how gender and parenting responsibilities affect social participation, quality of life, and mental health in 920 long COVID patients. The study documents associations between parenting tasks and impairments in family/domestic responsibilities, and finds higher anxiety in men with long COVID compared to women, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A pre-post feasibility study of teleyoga delivered via live-streamed sessions and digital app for 11 people with post-COVID condition over 7-12 weeks. The intervention was safe with low adherence but showed significant improvement in cognitive function (p=0.048) and self-reported benefits in breathing, relaxation, and stress reduction.

This study analyzes 1.38 million social media posts about long COVID across three pandemic phases to examine gaps between official health communications and patient narratives online. Rather than testing a treatment, it provides qualitative and quantitative analysis of patient experiences and public discourse, functioning as a secondary literature review of social media data rather than a primary clinical trial.

A qualitative study examining quality standards and variation in long COVID care delivery across 10 UK clinics through interviews, ethnography, and observational data. The study found that variation in services is often justified by patient complexity and comorbidities, and recommends supporting multidisciplinary team case-based learning rather than generic standardization.

This cross-sectional survey describes 112 specialized long COVID outpatient clinics in Germany and their diagnostic/treatment approaches, based on responses from 45 clinic directors. Treatment is predominantly personalized and symptom-oriented (respiratory vs neurocognitive) rather than standardized, with high perceived patient distress and clinician confidence in benefits, though greater standardization is recommended.

Mixed-methods study examining sleep and alcohol use experiences among Veterans with long COVID through chart reviews (n=57) and interviews (n=12). Finds that pre-existing sleep problems are exacerbated in long COVID, while alcohol use disorder is rare, and explores provider perspectives on delivering evidence-based care for these comorbidities.

A mixed-methods RCT protocol evaluating face-to-face rehabilitation (twice-weekly for 6 weeks, combining symptom-titrated exercise with self-management education) versus usual care in non-hospitalised long COVID patients, with embedded qualitative components to explore acceptability and healthcare inequalities. This is a protocol paper with no results yet (trial registered September 2024).

Cross-sectional and longitudinal study comparing cognitive function and psychological well-being in 121 adults with and without COVID-19, including 17 with long COVID symptoms. Found that COVID-19 survivors, especially those with long COVID, experience significant cognitive disruption (reduced processing speed, attention, memory) and higher depression/anxiety, but this is an observational assessment study without any treatment intervention.

This paper reviews the hypothesis that long COVID results from impaired cholinergic neurotransmission and evaluates low-dose transcutaneous nicotine (LDTN) as a treatment. It presents a case report with PET imaging showing improved cholinergic function after LDTN, plus survey data from 231 LDTN users reporting 73.5% symptom improvement.

Mixed-methods study characterizing the burden of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in 442 community-dwelling individuals through surveys and in-depth interviews. Found 30% experienced severe fatigue, persons with PASC had worse quality of life and mental health, and reported debilitating impacts on daily functioning.

This mixed-methods feasibility study tested a 4-week online mindful-walking intervention delivered via Facebook to 23 long COVID patients, with quantitative data collected via daily surveys and qualitative data from engagement metrics. Participants reported high feasibility scores and those who engaged in mindful walking showed improvements in positive affect, reduced negative affect, better perceived cognitive ability, and increased physical activity.

A mixed-method cross-sectional study assessing physical, mental, and social health status in 552 COVID-19 recovered patients across Nepal. The study documents symptom prevalence and functional impacts but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A multicentric prospective cohort study following 315 hospitalized COVID-19 patients for 1 year to assess long COVID prevalence and identify predictive factors. Found 16.5% prevalence with shortness of breath, cough, fatigue, and weight loss as significant predictors, but this is a passive observational follow-up without any intervention or treatment being tested.

A mixed-methods retrospective observational study examining Reddit activity of 7,544 users, finding that pre-pandemic activity on ME/CFS forums is the strongest predictor of participation in long COVID forums. The study explores motives for co-participation including mutual support, dual identification, and the possibility of shared pathophysiology between ME/CFS and long COVID.

A feasibility study of a complementary long COVID support service combining psycho-education and mind-body approaches (physiotherapy, craniosacral therapy) delivered in a UK community setting to 25 participants. The service showed positive changes in mental, physical, emotional, and spiritual wellbeing measured by the Warwick Holistic Health Questionnaire (33.7 to 39.5, n=16), with high participant satisfaction.

Mixed-methods evaluation of an ECHO tele-mentoring program designed to train medical officers in long COVID management across four Indian states, measuring changes in provider knowledge, competence, and patient satisfaction. Results showed significant improvements in MOs' knowledge and skills, with trained providers demonstrating increased confidence and adopting a comprehensive approach including mental health strategies, leading to high patient satisfaction.

Mixed-methods study evaluating a mobile app designed to improve self-management skills in 19 older adults with post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (PASC), measuring fatigue, cognitive problems, mood, and health-related quality of life. Findings indicate the app is relevant for PASC patients and support further development for this population.

Literature review and case study examining musculoskeletal symptoms in COVID-19 and post-COVID patients, with evaluation of physiotherapy interventions including exercises. Physical therapy, particularly exercise, significantly improved disability and function in a post-ICU long COVID patient.

A proof-of-concept study of the Hope Programme for Long COVID, an 8-week digital self-management intervention codesigned with people living with long COVID, combining peer support and positive psychology approaches. The uncontrolled study of 47 participants showed improvements in mental well-being and self-efficacy, with follow-up rates of 59.6%.

A multimethod study analyzing #longCOVID and #longhaulers conversations on Twitter (2,500 tweets) using text analysis and social network analysis to understand public discourse and lived experiences. Findings show long haulers emphasize symptoms and community-building, while general discussion frames focus on support and research, with networks being highly decentralized.

A mixed methods analysis of YouTube content discussing long COVID (post-COVID condition) symptoms, patient experiences, and information shared by medical professionals, news sources, and long haulers themselves. This is a qualitative content analysis study that does not test any treatment interventions.

A mixed-methods Twitter analysis examining healthcare workers' discourse and sentiment regarding post-COVID-19 condition in children and young people in the UK from January 2021-2022. The study analyzes 2,588 tweets to understand HCW perceptions and identifies themes including uncertainty, policies, vaccination, and management strategies, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper describes a situation analysis assessing post-COVID-19 patient needs and preferences in South Africa, followed by the design and piloting of an 8-week group intervention combining rehabilitation and mental health support. While outcome analysis is pending, the study demonstrates that patients found rehabilitation helpful and the intervention was feasible to deliver.

This mixed methods analysis examines patterns of electronic consultation (eConsult) cases submitted by primary care providers to long COVID specialists in Ontario between 2021-2022. The study documents common symptoms, question types, and response times but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A pilot study evaluating the feasibility of inspiratory muscle training as a home-based intervention for 16 patients with persistent dyspnoea after COVID-19. The intervention showed 73.7% adherence with no adverse events, and maximal inspiratory pressure improved from 84.7% to 111.3% of predicted values, though careful supervision and individualized training parameters were recommended.

Review article assessing mechanisms of CNS damage in HIV infection and examining how SARS-CoV-2 may contribute to neuropsychiatric pathology in HIV-infected patients. A small preliminary study of 146 HIV-infected patients found long-term neuropsychiatric manifestations post-COVID, but no specific intervention was tested.

This paper combines a literature review of obesity as a COVID-19 risk factor with a cross-sectional survey of COVID-19 patients in Latvia. It does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a trials meta-analysis.

Mixed-methods study examining how post-COVID-19 conditions affected sociocultural activities and quality of life in a Nepal district between 2022-2024. Found reduced motivation, economic disruption, and emotional strain, but identified cultural activities as protective factors for adaptation and recovery.

This study analyzes #longCOVID and #longhaulers conversations on Twitter using text and social network analysis to examine how long COVID is framed by users. It found that support and research frames dominate general discussions, while symptoms and community-building dominate patient perspectives, but no treatment interventions were tested or evaluated.

This study analyzes English-language tweets about long COVID from 2021 in Canada, the US, and Europe using topic modeling and sentiment analysis to understand public perceptions. It identifies five main topics including vaccination discussions, symptom duration, persistent symptoms, calls for treatment research, and symptom measurement, with findings showing mixed sentiments fluctuating with COVID-related news events.

Literature review combined with a single-center observational study comparing post-COVID syndrome prevalence and features in 203 healthcare workers versus 156 non-occupational controls followed for 60 days. Study documents higher rates of thermoregulation disorders, arrhythmias, and psychiatric symptoms in healthcare workers post-COVID but is primarily descriptive epidemiology without testing any intervention or treatment.

Mixed methods study examining how PASC status modifies the relationship between physical activity and perceived physical/mental health using an online survey (N=4316) and interviews (N=34). Findings show PASC participants report worse health outcomes with increased PA, with qualitative data highlighting post-exertional malaise and symptom worsening—this is an observational study, not a treatment trial.

Literature review of post-COVID syndrome in children and adolescents with a clinical case report of a 4-year-old boy treated with combination therapy including L-carnitine. The case demonstrates improvement in muscle weakness, fatigue, and overall well-being following L-carnitine treatment.

An intervention study evaluating a doctor-led blended therapy (stress-controlled training plus intensive cognitive behavioral therapy) in 46 post-COVID-19 patients with fatigue and sensorimotor instability. The study applied the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA) model to identify factors influencing health behavior and therapeutic outcomes, providing actionable recommendations for clinicians to improve patient engagement and symptom management.

This study surveyed 251 people with multiple sclerosis who had COVID-19 infection to identify post-COVID symptoms and test whether physiotherapy could help. Among respondents, 22% (76 people) experienced post-COVID symptoms lasting ≥12 weeks, with fatigue, dyspnea, and neurological deterioration being most common; a small pilot of 6 participants received individual physiotherapy with reported subjective relief.

This mixed-methods usability study evaluated occupational therapy telerehabilitation delivered via the Caspar Health system to 12 long COVID patients over a 6-week program in Hong Kong. Most participants found the system acceptable and reported perceived health benefits, with a median System Usability Scale score of 56.25 and willingness to continue or recommend the intervention.

This paper reviews clinical trials on long COVID listed in ClinicalTrials.gov and analyzes public sentiment about long COVID through Twitter data using emotion lexicon and regression methods. It does not conduct an original treatment trial but rather surveys existing trials and social media discourse.

This mixed-methods pilot study evaluated the acceptability and feasibility of an 8-week rehabilitation and self-management program for long COVID in South Africa, recruiting patients and staff from a tertiary hospital. Participants reported positive perceptions of the intervention and improved knowledge/confidence, though barriers included infrastructure, time, and language constraints.

Mixed-methods study examining long COVID symptoms and occupational status among 170 teachers in Israel using surveys and interviews. Found fatigue, weakness, and sleep difficulty as primary symptoms; sense of control and well-being predicted lower symptom levels.

Cross-sectional exploratory study assessing Romanian patients' perceptions of accessibility and quality of post-COVID-19 rehabilitation services, particularly for those with chronic conditions. Identifies barriers including lack of publicly funded services, cost, limited physician referral, and rural service scarcity, but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

This mixed-methods study evaluated a football club community trust exercise rehabilitation programme for post-COVID condition patients (n=7) over 12 weeks with 6-month follow-up using the RE-AIM framework. The programme produced significant improvements in physical function (6MWT distance, grip strength, MEP), quality of life, anxiety, and depression, with strong participant satisfaction.

This paper evaluates a 10-week virtual rehabilitation program (VRP) designed to provide early education and self-management techniques for long COVID patients. Mixed-methods analysis of 38 patient interviews and 17 healthcare professional surveys found the VRP was highly valued, digital delivery enabled self-management, but barriers to attendance included work/life balance and technology use.

A mixed methods exploratory study examining functioning and rehabilitation needs in 20 individuals with self-reported disability following COVID-19, using patient-reported outcomes, physical function tests, and focus groups. The study identified persistent symptoms (fatigue, concentration issues, breathing problems) and gaps in rehabilitation services, but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This paper describes a cross-sectional study of student self-perceptions and learning outcomes from organizing the Third Brazilian Congress on Clinical Evidence in COVID-19. It is an educational assessment, not a treatment trial, and should be excluded as it is primarily about pedagogy and student development rather than long COVID research or intervention testing.

This paper investigates the undiagnosed burden of ME/CFS in Latvia and its potential overlap with post-COVID syndrome, comparing self-reported data from ME/CFS patients, undiagnosed symptomatic individuals, and former COVID-19 patients. It is primarily an epidemiological and diagnostic burden assessment rather than an intervention trial, and does not evaluate any treatment.

A social network analysis of Twitter discourse on long COVID identifying key themes, influential users, and sentiment from 119,185 tweets collected over three months. The study examines how information about long COVID spreads on social media but does not test or evaluate any treatment interventions.

This study assessed cognitive functions and functional status in 32 COVID-infected individuals 3 months post-recovery, comparing differences by infection severity. While overall cognitive impairment was not significant on MMSE, subgroups differed in recent memory and functional domains, with qualitative follow-up at 6 months indicating subtle cognitive and psychological deficits that may be transient in nature.

This qualitative study examines the difficulties long COVID patients faced accessing and navigating the Belgian healthcare system through surveys, interviews, and forum discussions. The paper identifies shortcomings in clinical care (lack of empathy, unsystematic diagnosis, poor coordination) and recommends better provider education and interdisciplinary assessment—but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This is a narrative review and survey-based analysis describing the characteristics, symptoms, and mechanisms of long COVID in Belgian patients, based on literature review and a 1,320-person online survey. The paper concludes that treatment effectiveness is unknown and recommends a symptom-oriented multidisciplinary rehabilitation approach, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention.

A cross-sectional study of 98 post-COVID patients in Thailand examining factors associated with post-exertional malaise using questionnaires and interviews. Female sex, BMI, and COVID-19 severity were identified as predictors of PEM, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Mixed-method study examining return-to-work experiences and health-related quality of life among Filipino COVID-19 survivors with post-COVID condition through surveys and interviews. While focused on long COVID symptoms and rehabilitation, this is an observational study without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

This quasi-experimental study developed a decision-making logic model embedded in the iALERTS platform to stratify long COVID patients into risk categories based on demographic and clinical factors. The model identified fatigue, cough, cognitive dysfunction, and myalgia as most common persistent symptoms, with higher risk in females, older adults, those with obesity, unvaccinated individuals, and those with severe acute COVID.

Mixed-methods study investigating health consequences of long COVID among student teachers at Kasetsart University, with Phase 1 surveying 286 students and Phase 2 conducting interviews. The research identified seven categories of symptoms experienced by student teachers with long COVID but does not evaluate or test any interventions.

This pilot study evaluates iALERTS, a clinical decision support system designed to assist clinicians in identifying, stratifying, and managing long COVID patients. While the system showed high accuracy and user acceptance in a 120-patient pilot, it is a tool validation study rather than a treatment intervention trial.

Qualitative analysis of VA electronic health records examining how long COVID is clinically diagnosed and managed in a healthcare system. Identifies two dominant themes: clinical uncertainty in attribution of symptoms and care fragmentation in post-COVID patient management, highlighting the complexity of diagnosing and treating long COVID.

A prospective cohort study evaluating a multidisciplinary post-COVID outpatient clinic at a Swiss hospital, following 50 long COVID patients over 6 months with standardized questionnaires and qualitative interviews. Patients showed significant symptom improvement between weeks 4-8 and months 4-6, with most reporting satisfaction with the interprofessional coaching, though cognitive limitations worsened over time.

Qualitative study examining how social determinants of health (SDOH) influence recovery from COVID-19 through semistructured interviews with 24 patients and caregivers from a post-COVID clinic. Identifies three cross-cutting SDOH themes that positively or negatively affect recovery, including mobilization of social resources, disrupted social networks, and institutional mistrust.

A cross-sectional survey of 358 nurses in southern Santa Fe assessing health problems and their link to residual COVID-19. The study documents high prevalence of chronic fatigue (48.3%), distressing memories (34.6%), and concentration difficulty (36.8%), but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Qualitative grounded theory study exploring treatment preferences and expectations for long COVID cognitive impairments across age groups (young vs older adults). The study identifies age-specific intervention preferences but does not test or evaluate any actual treatment interventions.

Qualitative interview study (n=21) exploring long COVID patients' experiences with online support groups and their impact on health and wellbeing. Found that support groups provided community, validation, and self-efficacy benefits, but also some negative outcomes like increased fear.

This paper describes a methodology for engaging long COVID patients in research question prioritization within a learning health system, using a virtual patient panel to translate patient concerns into structured research questions. It is a methodological study focused on research design and patient involvement rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Mixed-methods study examining how long COVID patients use online and offline narratives to meet information and support needs, surveying 135 long-haulers and conducting 29 interviews. Findings show that reading and sharing personal stories about long COVID experiences is prevalent among patients, though the study does not evaluate any clinical intervention or treatment.

A 1-year follow-up study of participants from an 8-week exercise intervention trial for post-COVID-19 syndrome, examining facilitators and barriers to long-term exercise adherence through qualitative interviews and quantitative assessments. Key findings show that perceived need for further reconditioning is the strongest facilitator for continued exercise, while exhaustion is the strongest barrier, with group-based exercise being a critical factor for long-term adherence.

A qualitative analysis of COVID-19 patient experiences from Reddit posts (March-August 2020) examining early symptom reporting and disease characteristics. The study documents patient-reported symptoms including long-term impacts like post-viral fatigue, but is a secondary analysis of social media data without intervention testing or patient recruitment.

This mixed-methods study examines the information needs, seeking behaviors, and practices of long COVID patients, with focus on communication challenges and discrimination. The paper is a qualitative/information science study rather than a clinical treatment trial or observational study of interventions.

This qualitative mixed-methods study evaluates a VR-based physiotherapy prototype for long COVID patients through iterative co-creation with patients and physiotherapists. While the VR intervention was well-received, the paper reports on prototype development and requirements gathering rather than a formal clinical trial with quantitative outcomes.

A qualitative secondary analysis examining healthcare access barriers faced by 29 long COVID patients in the U.S. using Levesque et al.'s Conceptual Model of Healthcare Access. The study identifies issues including diagnostic delays, long waiting times, provider knowledge gaps, and financial costs, with findings intended to inform public health and clinical practice improvements.

A qualitative phenomenological philosophy analysis examining how affectivity and temporality shape the lived experience of post-COVID-19 condition in Swedish patients one year post-infection. The study identifies pre-intentional and intentional affective states but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring perspectives of 24 patients (predominantly Black, socioeconomically disadvantaged) 1 year after COVID-19 hospitalization, examining barriers and facilitators to recovery. Identifies persistent physical, cognitive, and psychological health deficits and highlights unmet mental health needs alongside inadequate holistic care.

Qualitative study of 23 Kenyans living with long COVID, exploring their lived experiences, symptom burden, and barriers to care. Findings highlight stigma, healthcare access limitations, and psychological impacts rather than evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study examining patient experiences navigating care for long COVID through interviews with 21 patients at a post-COVID recovery clinic. Findings highlight challenges in access to care, evaluation, and treatment, with patients reporting difficulties in symptom communication, frustration with normal test results, and appreciation for providers willing to try new approaches.

This qualitative study evaluated work capacity and life situation of 15 long COVID patients 12 months after completing medical rehabilitation (cardiac, pulmonary, or neurological). Patients and clinic staff identified work capacity restoration as a central goal, with most patients returning to work post-rehabilitation but using compensation strategies to maintain employment despite persistent impairments.

Qualitative study exploring the lived experiences and symptoms of 169 long COVID patients through open-ended survey responses. Identifies four themes: numerous/wearing symptoms, pervasive effects, difficulty with physical activity, and challenges in healthcare advocacy.

Qualitative interview study of 39 long COVID patients in VA clinical settings exploring how patients interpret and make sense of their post-COVID illness experience. Findings reveal challenges in disentangling COVID-19 effects from other health conditions and the role of clinical encounters in shaping patient understanding, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study examining how long COVID impacts employment and well-being through interviews with 21 patients at a post-COVID recovery clinic. Findings show patients struggle to work at pre-COVID capacity, face financial hardship, and experience emotional distress, with healthcare providers able to support through resource connection and accommodation facilitation.

This is a citizen science study that identifies long COVID research priorities through patient consultation and survey, rather than conducting a treatment trial. It establishes a framework for patient-centered research agendas but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Qualitative analysis of 152 COVID-19 survivors surveyed at 1 and 6 months post-discharge examining their long-term emotional and physical recovery experiences. Study identified five themes in post-acute recovery including persistent complications, premature aging, declined quality of life, and psychological impacts, but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This cross-sectional study used focus groups and surveys with 65 African American/Black, Hispanic/Latino, and Indigenous adults in Arizona to assess awareness and experiences with long COVID. While participants reported experiencing long COVID-consistent symptoms and mental health impacts, the study does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 80 Black adults with long COVID to understand barriers to care and inform equity-responsive care strategies. Study identifies challenges in diagnosis, physician awareness, and access to disability benefits but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study using 24 semi-structured interviews to characterize the variability in acute COVID-19 illness experience and ongoing recovery, including long COVID symptoms. Identifies key themes around symptom uncertainty, psychological distress, and information-seeking behavior but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Secondary analysis of qualitative data from a pilot study examining older and younger adults' experiences participating in 8 weekly virtually delivered Integrative Medical Group Visits (IMGV) for long COVID. Results support IMGV as a potentially feasible treatment approach for both age groups, with thematic analysis identifying three key themes around LC experiences, future outlook, and perceptions of the intervention.

Qualitative study examining experiences and perceptions of 8 long COVID patients who participated in an exercise-based respiratory physiotherapy program (INSPIRO2). Participants reported symptom improvement, reduced anxiety, recognition of their condition, and improved functionality through the intervention program.

Qualitative study examining psychosocial impacts of long COVID on 52 patients and 15 caregivers through interviews, identifying themes of disruption, stress/grief, and adaptive coping strategies. Recommends supportive rehabilitation approaches but does not test any specific intervention or treatment.

Qualitative narrative study of 37 Australian COVID-19 patients (6-10 months post-diagnosis) exploring recovery trajectories and social determinants of health through patient interviews. No intervention tested; descriptive analysis of recovery pathways and contextual factors.

This qualitative study describes challenges that long COVID patients face when returning to work and documents experiences of healthcare professionals providing vocational rehabilitation support. It provides recommendations for rehabilitation professionals but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment outcome.

Qualitative study exploring experiences of post-COVID-19 symptoms in 17 older adults (≥60 years) approximately 6 months after hospitalization, using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Participants reported persistent physical and cognitive symptoms (fatigue, brain fog, reduced fitness) alongside existential reflections about guilt, gratitude, and life perspective changes.

Medical students conducted longitudinal interviews and provided telehealth support to COVID-19 patients post-discharge from March-September 2020, following 64 consenting patients and identifying themes to improve transition of care. While the study addresses long COVID symptoms and their impact, it is primarily an educational intervention and quality improvement project focused on training medical students, not a treatment trial for patients.

Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews to characterize physical, cognitive, and mood symptoms in 8 long COVID patients. Findings emphasize diverse symptom presentations and individual impacts on daily functioning, work, and social life, concluding that personalized rehabilitation approaches are needed.

This mixed-methods study assessed cognitive and olfactory disturbances in COVID-19 convalescent patients over three follow-up visits, comparing those with and without olfactory hallucinations. The study found that olfactory hallucinations were associated with more pronounced depression and identified persistent anosmia as a predictor of parosmia, but did not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A qualitative phenomenological study describing the lived experiences of 34 long COVID patients with neuropsychological symptoms, including barriers they face and coping strategies they develop. The study identifies the need for psychological support integration and patient involvement in clinical practice design, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.
