Qualitative phenomenological study exploring the experiences and health/social impact of long COVID in 20 patients from the Basque Country more than a year after infection. Study identified three main themes: impacts on quality of life, areas for healthcare improvement, and comforting aspects, concluding that personalized multidisciplinary care approaches are needed.

This qualitative study analyzed perspectives of 13 long COVID patients who completed an 8-week virtual physical rehabilitation program with tailored exercises and education, nested within a larger RCT (n=132). Participants reported positive physical and emotional improvements including increased energy and mobility, though some faced challenges returning to work and maintaining exercise post-program.

This paper describes a body mapping workshop pilot (4 participants, June 2023) as a qualitative method for long COVID patients to communicate their symptom experiences to practitioners and support networks. It presents preliminary findings on the potential application of body mapping for patient advocacy and peer support, but reports no treatment outcomes or clinical trial results.

A qualitative grounded theory study of 66 Brazilians with long COVID exploring their symptom experiences and healthcare service access. The study identifies how persistent symptoms force lifestyle reorganization and reveals gaps in healthcare understanding and specialized services for long COVID patients.

This study validates the German version of the PROMIS 29+2 v2.1 questionnaire for measuring health-related quality of life in post-COVID patients through cognitive interviews with patients and experts. It identifies needed modifications to the questionnaire but does not test any treatment or intervention.

This paper explores general practitioners' barriers and experiences in managing long COVID patients in primary care settings in Malta. It is a qualitative study of healthcare provider perspectives, not a treatment trial or patient outcomes study.

A qualitative study exploring parents' experiences seeking healthcare for children with post-COVID-19 symptoms and the impact on family life through thematic analysis of 17 interviews. The study highlights healthcare system gaps in addressing long COVID in children but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This paper uses corpus-based critical discourse analysis to examine how long COVID patients describe experiences of medical gaslighting in online Reddit communities. It identifies seven types of gaslighting discourse (scapegoating, downplay, treatment refusal, etc.) driven by epistemic injustice and ideological barriers in doctor-patient relationships, rather than studying any treatment intervention.

Grounded theory study exploring experiences of people with POTS and health professionals who care for them through 44 in-depth interviews (19 patients, 25 health professionals). While associated with long COVID, this is a qualitative, observational study with no treatment intervention—it documents experiences and care gaps rather than testing or evaluating any specific treatment.

This study analyzes 31,892 Reddit posts from the r/covidlonghaulers subreddit to understand how long COVID patients seek information and support online, identifying 16 thematic clusters around symptoms, diagnostics, and coping strategies. While about long COVID patients, this is a qualitative content analysis of online discourse rather than a treatment trial or intervention study, making it a secondary/review-type analysis excluded from trial screening.

A sociological analysis of how patient-generated evidence and online mobilization transformed long COVID from an invisible condition into a recognized medical and public health concern. The paper examines the social and epistemic processes that legitimized long COVID as a disease entity but does not study any treatment intervention or clinical trial.

A qualitative study using journey mapping to document the experiences of 14 long COVID patients over three months, examining how social support and patient agency shape their disease trajectory. The study provides insights into daily challenges and coping strategies but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A reflexive thematic analysis of over 31,000 #longcovid tweets from May-August 2020 examining how Twitter users raised awareness of long COVID as a multi-system, cyclical condition. The study highlights the role of social consensus in overcoming stigma and driving real-world recognition of long COVID healthcare needs, rather than testing any treatment intervention.

This paper is a qualitative narrative inquiry analyzing storytelling and illness narratives from 114 long COVID patients in the UK, examining how patients used narratives to make their condition visible and advocate for care. It does not study any treatment intervention—instead it is a methodological analysis of patient narratives and their role in healthcare advocacy.

Qualitative study analyzing return-to-work experiences of 510 long COVID patients through thematic analysis of survey responses. Identifies key barriers (symptom fluctuation, workplace stigma, medical disbelief) and facilitators (job accommodations, medical provider support) to successful return to work.

Qualitative study analyzing the experiences of 39 children and adolescents with long COVID and their caregivers in the UK, exploring how the condition's limited social recognition creates barriers to support. The paper examines how societal misconceptions about COVID-19 severity and children's vulnerability contribute to the 'double invisibility' of pediatric long COVID.

Qualitative study examining how patient activists framed and named Long COVID through social media, and how this naming influenced perceptions among patients, clinicians, policymakers, and academics. No treatment intervention tested; primarily a sociological analysis of patient activism and diagnostic contestation.

Qualitative study examining lived experiences of ethnic minorities with long COVID in the UK through 31 semi-structured interviews conducted 2022-2023. Identifies structural violence and medical ambivalence as barriers to recognition and support, though some participants found alternative pathways through community and online resources.

Qualitative study examining the interembodied experiences of long COVID patients and their caregivers through in-depth interviews and case studies. Explores how chronic living with long COVID involves mutual interdependence between patients and carers across emotional, material, social, and biological dimensions.

A qualitative interview study of 20 long COVID patients exploring their illness experiences and interactions with healthcare and online communities. The study finds that patients experience uncertainty, healthcare dismissal, and gain validation through online community support—but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative analysis of patients' experiences negotiating healthcare recognition and access for long COVID symptoms across five countries during the early pandemic. Explores how patients established collective and individual candidacy for care, identifying patterns of validated, diverted, and rejected candidacy in healthcare encounters.

This is a collaborative autoethnographic study examining the emotional labour and experiences of researchers conducting a longitudinal mixed-methods study on long COVID in healthcare workers during the pandemic. It is not a treatment trial but rather a methodological/reflexive account of the research process itself, making it an editorial/commentary piece rather than a primary empirical study.

This is a qualitative interpretive meta-synthesis that synthesizes findings from existing qualitative literature to identify psychosocial interventions and coping strategies used by long COVID patients. It is a secondary analysis and synthesis of prior qualitative studies, not a primary empirical study of a treatment intervention.

Online survey of 1,191 long COVID patients in Germany evaluating their experiences with inpatient rehabilitation, with 733 providing qualitative feedback. Results show 50% experienced health deterioration from rehabilitation, with post-exertional malaise (PEM) being a major barrier; patients emphasized need for individualized pacing-focused treatment plans rather than standard rehabilitation protocols.

Qualitative study of 25 long COVID patients in Germany exploring how the condition affects social activities, medical support experiences, and emotional well-being. Finds inadequate medical care, prolonged specialist wait times, and significant social isolation, while identifying family support as a key resource.

Qualitative analysis of 264 long COVID patient reports examining barriers to healthcare access and medical recognition. Finds widespread lack of care infrastructure, insufficient provider knowledge, symptom dismissal, and harm from inappropriate treatments, particularly psychologizing approaches.

A qualitative study using focus groups with 23 long COVID patients to identify coping strategies they employ in daily life, such as pacing, energy management, physical activity, and lifestyle changes. The study documents patient-developed strategies for managing symptoms but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Qualitative study exploring experiences and satisfaction with care among 28 children and adolescents with post-COVID-19 condition and their parents in a Bavarian model project. While addressing a treatment context, this is a qualitative satisfaction survey rather than an intervention trial evaluating treatment efficacy or outcomes.

A qualitative study protocol exploring lived experiences of Long COVID among ethnically diverse populations in the UK using interviews and co-created artwork. The study aims to inform management and healthcare support, but presents only a study protocol with no results reported.

Qualitative study following 11 long COVID patients undergoing pneumological rehabilitation at three time points (post-rehabilitation, 6 months, and 12 months after) to assess occupational participation and work reintegration outcomes. Results identified cognitive, psychosocial, and physical limitations as barriers, with workplace flexibility, social support, and personality factors (acceptance) as key facilitators for successful return to work.

This paper reports on a sub-study embedded within the NIH RECOVER long COVID cohort, examining clinician perspectives on returning NT-proBNP heart failure biomarker results to study participants. It is a methodological study focused on return-of-results feasibility rather than testing a treatment intervention for long COVID patients.

A qualitative study exploring food consumption patterns and behavioral changes in 47 PASC patients with altered taste and smell. The paper identifies preferred food types and suggests early intervention but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This qualitative study describes the lived experiences of 35 COVID-19 survivors, documenting symptoms and impacts on health, relationships, and well-being. It does not test any treatment intervention but rather characterizes the patient experience of post-COVID condition through semi-structured interviews.

This quality improvement project uses qualitative interviews with 21 veterans with long COVID to explore their lived experiences, mental health needs, and barriers to treatment access. The study identifies themes around social isolation, functional impairment, and the need for psychotherapeutic interventions, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment.

Qualitative study using four focus groups to explore experiences of long COVID patients regarding medical care, therapeutic measures, and barriers within the German healthcare system. Presents patient perspectives on care gaps and systemic obstacles in managing long COVID.

A qualitative study exploring what long COVID support services should offer from the perspectives of 18 New Zealand patients with long COVID through semi-structured interviews. Identifies four themes (practical guidance, professional training/collaboration, personalized care, health system change) but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A qualitative study examining how UK residents made sense of chronic COVID-19 and reinfection risk through embodied knowledge and speculation about future vulnerabilities in 2021. The paper does not evaluate any treatment or intervention, focusing instead on experiential narratives and sense-making during the pandemic.

A qualitative narrative study exploring the lived experiences of four individuals with Long COVID through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Results identify six themes including symptom complexity, emotional impact, and healthcare navigation challenges, with recommendations for occupational therapy practice.

This paper explores coping strategies and self-management approaches used by people with long COVID who face inadequate healthcare support and prolonged symptom burden. Rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention, it describes how patients develop their own health-oriented self-management concepts in response to healthcare gaps.

Qualitative study examining post-COVID patients' experiences 12 months after completing cardiac, pulmonary, and neurological rehabilitation programs, along with rehabilitation staff perspectives. Findings highlight persistent symptoms, psychological distress, and evolving patient needs from physical to psychosomatic and social-medical dimensions, with recommendations for enhanced rehabilitation approaches.

This cross-sectional study analyzed Reddit posts from long COVID patients who reported using psilocybin, finding that 78.2% reported improvement in neuropsychiatric symptoms (fatigue, cognitive impairment, depression) with 77.9% reporting sustained improvement beyond the acute experience. The study documents perceived treatment effects from social media accounts rather than conducting a controlled trial.

Qualitative phenomenological study exploring lived experiences of 12 workers with long COVID and barriers/facilitators to workplace return using semi-structured interviews. Identifies individual, organizational, and contextual factors affecting work outcomes but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

topics: work ability|rehabilitation|qualitative|return to work|barriers and facilitators
summary: A qualitative interview study of 28 post-COVID-19 patients exploring facilitators and barriers to return-to-work, including individual, work-related, healthcare, and social factors. While about long COVID, it is a qualitative descriptive study without an intervention or treatment evaluation, focusing instead on lived experiences and contextual factors affecting work ability.

A phenomenological qualitative study exploring the subjective experiences and emotional impacts of persistent chemosensory dysfunction (loss of taste/smell) in 30 COVID-19 patients undergoing treatment. The study identifies themes of emotional discontent, sensory aversion, and perceptual disorientation, but does not evaluate treatment efficacy or outcomes.

A qualitative study exploring allied health workers' perspectives on resources needed for COVID-19 rehabilitation. Healthcare workers identify gaps in guidance for long COVID recovery trajectories and call for better accessible resources, but the study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment.

Qualitative descriptive study exploring the impact of long COVID on social and leisure well-being for 52 people with LC and 15 caregivers through interviews. Identifies themes around symptom burden limiting social engagement, loss of identity, and increased isolation, with recommendations for social- and leisure-targeted interventions in LC rehabilitation.

This paper analyzes Reddit posts from r/covidlonghaulers to characterize long COVID patient experiences and identify themes associated with symptom sentiment. It demonstrates the value of social media and digital technologies for understanding long COVID patient journeys rather than testing or evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring structural determinants of wellbeing for people with long COVID through interviews with 30 patients and 8 caregivers. The paper analyzes how social understanding of disability, ableist policies, and systemic factors impact psychological and social outcomes, finding that multilevel policy interventions are needed.

A qualitative sub-study of a randomized feasibility trial evaluating a 6-week supervised group telerehabilitation programme for hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Participants reported positive experiences with the intervention, highlighting the importance of group dynamics, instructor support, and online delivery in reducing social isolation and supporting recovery.

A qualitative study examining the experiences and challenges of 32 Canadian rehabilitation providers delivering care to long COVID patients, using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Identifies barriers to care (limited infrastructure, resource constraints), adaptive practice strategies, and key components of effective rehabilitation including individualized care planning, self-management, and inter-professional collaboration.

A longitudinal qualitative interview study of 19 long COVID patients over one year examining how they experience communicative resilience and make sense of their condition. The study documents temporal patterns of grief, patience, and hope but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A qualitative study of 65 narrative interviews examining how people with Long COVID experience episodic disability and navigate return-to-employment barriers in the UK. The paper analyzes the psychological and administrative burden of returning to work with fluctuating symptoms but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This study adapted and beta-tested reCOVer, a smartphone app designed to help long-COVID patients self-manage fatigue through activity pacing, goal-setting, and behavioral guidance. Eleven participants completed qualitative interviews over 7-10 days, reporting the app was helpful for awareness and behavior change, with suggestions for improvement before conducting a future pilot RCT.

Qualitative study exploring how occupational therapists in German-speaking countries manage long COVID patients through semi-structured interviews with seven practitioners. Describes OT strategies and treatment approaches but does not test or evaluate a specific intervention with measurable outcomes.

Qualitative study of vaccine perceptions among Black adults with long COVID using 15 semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Identifies five themes influencing vaccine decision-making, including safety concerns amplified by long COVID status and mistrust in medical systems.

Qualitative analysis of 1,043 Reddit posts from long COVID patients examining how they navigate medical encounters with normal test results. The study identifies themes around diagnostic uncertainty, treatment discordance, and credibility challenges but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A longitudinal qualitative interview study of 19 long COVID patients conducted over one year, exploring how uncertainty and liminality shape their experiences with the illness across medical, social, and personal domains. The study contributes to understanding chronic illness uncertainty but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Qualitative interview study examining German GPs' experiences managing post-COVID-19 syndrome patients, identifying care gaps and diagnostic challenges. Study documents clinical barriers and unmet needs rather than testing any intervention or treatment.

A reflective paper on 'Holding Breath', a co-creative sound project that explored collective listening and care in response to pandemic grief, collaborating with people living with long COVID. The work is a creative/methodological reflection rather than a treatment evaluation or empirical study.

Qualitative study of 30 long COVID patients across 6 countries examining self-tracking practices for symptom understanding and illness management. While participants found self-tracking valuable for empowerment and validation, this is a descriptive social science study without intervention testing, not a treatment trial.

Qualitative study using focus group interviews with post-COVID patients and rehabilitation physicians to explore experiences with interdisciplinary rehabilitation treatment. Findings show that patients experience progress with the biopsychosocial rehabilitation approach, learning to cope better and improving activities of daily living.

Qualitative study examining COVID-19 vaccination perspectives among 21 Long COVID patients receiving care at a post-COVID recovery clinic using deductive thematic analysis. Findings reveal diverse perspectives on vaccination ranging from acceptance to refusal, with concerns about vaccine side effects on Long COVID symptoms, but the study does not evaluate any treatment intervention or trial design.

This paper presents a framework for evaluating a virtual reality rehabilitation service designed for long COVID patients, focusing on user experiences and values rather than traditional cost-effectiveness metrics. It is a methodological study describing the development and assessment approach for the VR intervention, but does not report outcome data from an actual trial or patient cohort.

A qualitative focus group study exploring healthcare professionals' experiences treating long COVID patients and their views on healthcare service responses. The study identifies themes around uncertainty, care pathways, and the need for multi-level, personalized care but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This paper documents a rapid evaluation of Wales' Long COVID services using patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and experience measures (PREMs) conducted between September 2021 and December 2022. It is a reflective discussion of evaluation methodology and implementation challenges rather than a treatment trial, and thus is excluded as a secondary evaluation/service review without treatment intervention data.

A qualitative study examining long COVID's impact on healthcare workers' job performance in Spain through focus groups and interviews. Finds that long COVID significantly impairs work ability and identifies needs for workplace support and formal recognition.

Phenomenological qualitative study of 45 COVID-19 positive individuals exploring lived experiences, symptom presentations, and coping mechanisms. While mentions long haulers with lingering symptoms, this is a descriptive qualitative study without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Qualitative study exploring work ability and return-to-work experiences among 10 female professionals with long COVID through semi-structured interviews. Identifies key enablers (workplace flexibility, health care access, supportive colleagues) and barriers to sustaining work for long COVID patients.

Qualitative study exploring experiences of accessing care, diagnosis, and rehabilitation among 18 long-COVID patients in Denmark using semi-structured interviews and thematic framework analysis. Findings emphasize limited healthcare knowledge, uncertainty in diagnosis, and disparities in treatment experiences among ethnic minorities, but no intervention or treatment outcomes are evaluated.

Qualitative study of 134 long COVID patients in Belgium exploring barriers and experiences related to return to work, including clinical symptoms, workplace stigma, and gaps in social support. Study identifies occupational health considerations but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional survey of 145 long COVID workers identifies obstacles and enablers to returning to work, including fatigue, symptom-job interactions, and workplace policies. While it provides qualitative insights into work-related challenges, it does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

Qualitative longitudinal study examining resilience as an embodied social construction in people over 50 with Long COVID in the UK, using three in-depth case studies (2021-23) with different resilience trajectories. The paper argues resilience is rooted in narrative identity and life experiences rather than an intrinsic trait, highlighting the existential dimension of aging with Long COVID and the role of social support.

A qualitative study using Constructivist Grounded Theory to investigate how long COVID affects meaning in life through ten patient interviews. The study reveals that patients experience loss of prior understanding of life, social isolation, and loss of abilities, while also experiencing hope and acceptance.

Qualitative study documenting the lived experiences of 114 long COVID patients through interviews and focus groups, exploring their symptom narratives, healthcare access difficulties, and perspectives on service improvement. This is a qualitative descriptive study rather than a treatment trial—it assesses patient experiences and service quality rather than testing any intervention.

Qualitative analysis of 9,000 Facebook support group members documenting the impact of altered taste and smell on daily living, psychological well-being, eating, relationships, and sense of self in post-COVID patients. No treatment intervention is tested or evaluated; this is a descriptive study of symptom burden.

A qualitative study exploring factors that impact mental health and wellbeing in 21 people with long COVID through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Identifies five key themes including care experiences, lack of treatment options, disruption to daily life, illness uncertainty, and identity changes.

This paper mines Reddit posts from long COVID patients to identify and characterize self-reported symptoms, creating a symptom lexicon and comparing symptom distributions with published literature. It is an observational analysis of patient-reported data rather than a treatment trial, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

topics: social impact|quality of life|female long haulers
summary: Qualitative study examining how persistent COVID-19 symptoms impact the social lives of female long haulers through semi-structured interviews. The study documents challenges including physical limitations, social isolation, work-family conflicts, stigma, and job insecurity but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study characterizing the illness experience and recovery process in COVID-19 patients through in-depth interviews with 24 participants from the LIINC cohort. Does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, only describes patient experiences and psychological impact.

Narrative review synthesizing patient reports of internal tremors and vibration symptoms in people with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), collected from a patient advocacy group. The analysis identifies symptom characteristics, triggers, and patient experiences with the medical establishment, but explicitly notes no diagnosis or treatment is currently available.

Qualitative study exploring perceptions of Long COVID community rehabilitation services from patients, allied health professionals, and NHS staff across Scottish health boards. Identifies barriers and facilitators to accessing rehabilitation but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

A mixed-methods social media analysis of Twitter discourse by UK healthcare workers about Long COVID in children and young people from January 2021 to January 2022. The study identifies healthcare workers' perceptions and emotional responses but does not test or evaluate any treatment interventions.

A qualitative case-finding study exploring healthcare barriers and stigma experienced by people with probable long COVID in England. The study identifies epistemic injustice, self-doubt, and discrimination as key obstacles to care-seeking, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A qualitative interview study examining German general practitioners' experiences managing post-COVID-19 syndrome patients, their diagnostic and treatment challenges, and unmet care needs. The study documents GPs' roles in coordinating care but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A qualitative descriptive study of 40 long COVID patients exploring how the Episodic Disability Framework applies to their health-related challenges. The study characterizes disability as multidimensional and episodic with contextual factors and triggers, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A qualitative descriptive study of 40 adults with long COVID exploring their experiences with pacing as a self-management strategy to mitigate symptoms. The study identifies five key dimensions of pacing experiences including learning strategies, encountering challenges, and experiencing consequences of non-adherence.

A qualitative study exploring barriers and facilitators to accessing Long COVID care in England through interviews with 23 patients at post-COVID services. Findings highlight intersectional inequalities in care access, stigma, discrimination, and inadequate mental health provision for people with Long COVID.

Twitter sentiment analysis of 15,827 tweets about long COVID collected over 10 days in December 2021. Study finds negative sentiments dominate discussion of long COVID (44% negative) but positive sentiments increase when discussing treating long COVID (41% positive).

A qualitative interview study of 60 community-based participants with long COVID symptoms exploring how they experience, recognize, and manage persistent symptoms following COVID-19. The study found that many participants did not access clinical care or identify with the long COVID label, highlighting challenges in diagnosis, validation, and self-management within an under-resourced healthcare context.

Qualitative study using in-depth interviews with 20 long COVID patients to explore how the illness affects identity and sense of self. Findings show long-haulers experience biographical disruptions across three stages: misalignment with expectations, identity challenges, and reconciliation with uncertain prognosis.

A qualitative study exploring existential identity loss among 80 long COVID patients in the UK, examining how persistent symptoms disrupt narrative identity and continuity of self. The paper focuses on sociological and psychological dimensions of living with long COVID rather than testing or evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative interview study exploring barriers to long COVID diagnosis and life impacts among ethnically minoritized and marginalized communities in the UK. Identifies diagnostic odyssey, employment challenges, and health inequities but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study using narrative interviews with 15 young adults with long COVID to explore how their illness experiences differ from traditional biographical disruption models. The paper proposes 'biographical retrogression' as a more accurate framework for understanding the disruption young adults face, particularly given the timing of illness during crucial life trajectory formation.

An ethnographic study of UK long COVID clinics examining how multidisciplinary teams build working knowledge and practice. The paper analyzes clinical approaches (rehabilitation vs microscopic damage models) but does not study or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This study uses Q-methodology to explore how therapists and clients understand long COVID recovery, comparing perspectives on psychological and physiological pathways. While about long COVID, it is a qualitative exploration of perspectives on therapy rather than an evaluation of a specific treatment intervention or its outcomes.

Autoethnographic exploration of sharing vulnerability related to long COVID and gendered motherhood experiences in academia. Focuses on the emotional and relational processes of vulnerability disclosure rather than treatment outcomes or intervention testing.

Qualitative study examining the experiences of 13 doctors who are themselves long COVID patients, focusing on their clinical journey, access to care, and professional identity. The study documents themes of symptom management, healthcare navigation, and how experiencing long COVID influenced their clinical empathy, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This qualitative study examines how 33 people living with long COVID across three European countries use self-tracking practices to monitor their illness and make health management decisions. While the paper provides valuable insights into patient experiences and symptom management strategies, it is not a treatment intervention trial—it is a qualitative research study about patient behaviors and attitudes toward self-tracking data, and therefore falls outside the scope of clinical trials screening.

A qualitative analysis of 66 patient stories from an online COVID community exploring the physical and epistemic challenges of living with long COVID. The study highlights how patients face disbelief and stigma due to lack of objective medical indicators, emphasizing the importance of patient testimonies in understanding the condition.

A qualitative study collecting creative narratives from 28 long COVID patients to explore their lived experience of the condition. The thematic analysis identified five themes including identity loss, social impacts, symptom burden, healthcare interaction, and temporal disruption, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Qualitative study analyzing experiences of 26 long COVID patients enrolled in the LC-Optimal Health Programme (LC-OHP) intervention arm of an RCT. Participants reported fluctuating, burdensome symptoms impacting daily activities and mental health, with generally positive perceptions of the LC-OHP support program.

A qualitative study exploring barriers to healthcare access for long COVID patients and healthcare professionals in Bradford, UK through 40 patient and 12 HCP interviews. Findings show difficulties accessing primary care, inadequate support, lack of specialist services, and systemic barriers, with ethnic minorities facing additional challenges.

A qualitative study examining experiences of 32 long COVID patients who received a 4-week digital physiotherapy intervention via video. Participants perceived the intervention as helpful and appropriate for managing their health needs, with improvements suggested including video quality and face-to-face session options.

topics: healthcare access|patient perspectives|care pathways|barriers to care
summary: A qualitative study examining barriers and facilitators to healthcare access for long COVID patients through interviews with 8 patients and 8 healthcare practitioners. Findings identify gaps in care pathways, communication, and continuity of care, rather than evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring the lived experiences of 19 long COVID patients through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Documents patient journeys including symptom dismissal by healthcare professionals, lack of support, and psychological impacts, with gendered differences in experience.

This paper describes a coproduction project where children and young people worked as public advisors to develop health information materials about long COVID for younger audiences. The work involved 66 young people in designing videos and educational leaflets but did not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A coproduced qualitative study exploring healthcare access barriers and stigma experienced by people with probable long COVID in England through 23 interviews. Findings reveal epistemic injustice, self-doubt, healthcare hesitancy, and discrimination, with recommendations for improved signposting, listening time, and public health messaging.

A qualitative workshop paper discussing intersectional inequalities affecting long COVID prevalence, recognition, and care, identifying themes like healthcare access barriers, stigma, and systemic mistrust. This is a policy/research commentary rather than an intervention study or clinical trial.

This study uses photovoice methodology to document the experiences and capacity-building journey of long COVID patient experts participating in training at the Patient Engagement Studio. It is a qualitative research study on patient engagement in research rather than a clinical trial evaluating a treatment intervention.

A qualitative longitudinal study examining how NHS workers in Scotland experience barriers to healthcare access when seeking support for long COVID symptoms. Uses candidacy theory to identify multiple systemic and individual factors that restrict healthcare-seeking and receipt of treatment among healthcare workers with long COVID.

This qualitative study uses conversation analysis to examine how older adults with long COVID and doctors manage agenda-setting during outpatient consultations. It does not evaluate any treatment intervention, but rather analyzes communication patterns and clinical encounters.

A qualitative study evaluating consumer experience and acceptability of an Australian multidisciplinary Long COVID Recovery Clinic that incorporates personalized exercise prescription, respiratory/peripheral strengthening, and monitored cardiovascular training. 14 of 15 participants found the clinic acceptable and reported that supervised exercise, pacing, and peer support improved confidence and aided recovery alongside GP management.

A qualitative study examining long-term smell loss experiences in 11 COVID-19 patients with olfactory dysfunction lasting ≥3 months. Participants reported use of corticosteroid therapy and olfactory training but found limited solutions, with significant impacts on nutrition, hygiene, safety, and emotional well-being.

A qualitative comparative analysis examining how people experience and conceptualize 'recovery' from intensive care COVID-19 versus Long COVID through 93 interviews conducted in the UK. The study highlights differences in how Long COVID patients' illness experiences lack social legitimacy compared to ICU survivors, and emphasizes the importance of recognizing diverse recovery trajectories.

This is a qualitative study analyzing patient perceptions of a multimodal home-based rehabilitation program for post-acute COVID-19 delivered via telerehabilitation versus booklet control. It is a secondary qualitative analysis of participants from an underlying randomized pilot trial (NCT04794036), not a primary trial report, and thus excluded.

Qualitative study examining epistemic injustice experiences in long COVID patients participating in a peer support group intervention at a US academic medical centre. Peer support groups showed potential to counter epistemic injustice through recognition, solidarity, and information exchange, suggesting such programmes warrant further development as complex interventions for improving patient-centred care.

A collaborative autoethnographic study documenting one patient's personal journey of falling ill with and recovering from long COVID. While it provides valuable insights into the lived experience and advocates for patient-centered care, it is a qualitative narrative study without treatment intervention or clinical data.

This netnographic study examines how long COVID diagnoses are constructed and understood through social media forums and digital communities, analyzing patient narratives and knowledge production. It is excluded because it is a qualitative social science study of online discourse, not a treatment trial or clinical evaluation.

A qualitative study of 23 long COVID patients in Spain exploring their daily experiences, health information barriers, and quality of life through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. While the paper documents significant impacts on patients' lives, it does not evaluate any treatment or intervention—it is a descriptive study of patient experiences and healthcare system challenges.

A qualitative grounded theory study exploring the lived experience and perceived needs of 24 Brazilian adults with persistent respiratory symptoms of long COVID 12 months post-infection. The study highlights the complex psychosocial and functional impacts of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Qualitative study exploring how children, young people, parents, and professionals perceive and use long COVID diagnoses. Families value diagnosis for legitimizing symptoms and accessing support, while professionals focus on treatment according to individual needs.

A secondary analysis of 31 semi-structured interviews exploring how long COVID experiences among ethnic minorities are shaped by intersecting factors like gender and socio-economic status. The study identifies barriers to healthcare access and support, with findings emphasizing the need for intersectional understanding in clinical care.

A qualitative interview study of 60 people with long COVID nested in the REACT community study, exploring their experiences with persistent symptoms and challenges in accessing clinical care and support. The study documents self-management strategies and the impact of symptom burden on daily life, but conducts no intervention or treatment evaluation.

A qualitative study examining how Swedish experts understand and interpret post-COVID-19 condition as a diagnosis, exploring epistemological tensions around aetiology, patient demographics, and treatment approaches. The study identifies disagreements among experts about whether post-COVID is a unique condition requiring specialized care or a post-viral syndrome treatable in primary care, with implications for policy.

Qualitative interview study analyzing employment changes and workplace experiences among 60 long COVID patients in England. Identifies barriers and enablers to work sustainability, with findings centered on symptom management, organizational support, and adaptive accommodations rather than treatment evaluation.

This paper describes the community engagement model developed by the Boston COVID Recovery Cohort (BCRC), a consortium of RECOVER sites studying long COVID. It is a methodological reflection on research partnership approaches rather than a treatment intervention study, focusing on lessons learned from implementing community engagement in long COVID research.

Qualitative interview study exploring how people with long COVID perceive COVID-19 vaccines and how unexpected vaccine responses impact their trust in vaccination. The research identifies a gap between scientific and public health discourse on vaccine harms/benefits, leading to difficulties in maintaining vaccine trust among long COVID patients.

This paper uses Community-Based System Dynamics workshops to understand long COVID disparities in African American communities and develop health equity research methods. It does not study a specific treatment intervention but rather presents a methodological framework for community engagement and health system analysis.

A qualitative phenomenological study exploring the lived experiences of 27 older Chinese cancer patients with long COVID in Hong Kong through semi-structured interviews. The study documents their dual burden of cancer and long COVID symptoms and the role of nursing support in fostering resilience, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A descriptive phenomenological study examining how 14 post-COVID patients experience and perceive fatigue using interviews and the Chalder Fatigue Scale. The study identifies qualitative themes about fatigue's impact on daily life, dependency, and sociability, but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Qualitative study exploring patient experiences during COVID-19 hospitalization and post-discharge quality of life through semi-structured interviews with 10 patients. Identifies psychological distress and physical recovery challenges but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A qualitative interview study examining how 30 long COVID patients undergoing clinical treatment for persistent smell and taste dysfunction understand and cope with their condition. The study identifies coping strategies, emotional responses, and highlights the need for comprehensive physiological and psychological support approaches.

An exploratory qualitative interview study examining recovery experiences and rehabilitation needs of 20 COVID-19 critical illness survivors. The study identifies three key themes (traumatic experience, human connection, navigating systems) and emphasizes the importance of personalized, coordinated recovery pathways but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention.

Qualitative phenomenological study exploring lived experiences of 13 patients recovering from COVID-19-associated ICU acquired weakness through semi-structured interviews 4-8 months post-discharge. Identifies five recovery themes but is a descriptive qualitative analysis without intervention testing or outcome measurement.

A qualitative study characterizing the impact of long COVID on quality of life and symptom management approaches among 15 Black American adults using thematic analysis. The study identifies themes related to symptom impact on identity, self-management strategies, social determinants of health, and effects on relationships, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This paper describes the development of work-focused energy management coaching (jobcoaching) to support employed individuals with fatigue, based on qualitative analysis of focus groups and scientific literature. It presents a proposed intervention framework rather than trial results, making it a protocol or feasibility study without outcome data.

Qualitative phenomenological study exploring the lived experiences and recovery processes of 15 long COVID patients in Denmark through interviews and participant-generated photographs. Documents patients' struggles with reduced capacity, uncertainty, and psychosocial challenges while adapting to persistent post-COVID-19 condition, but provides no treatment intervention or outcome data.

A qualitative phenomenological study examining how a multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme affected 12 people with long-term cognitive effects of COVID-19. Participants reported improvements in coping strategies, daily routines, work capacity, and personal insight into managing cognitive challenges, fatigue, and headaches.

Qualitative study exploring the lived experience of long COVID patients (n=18) with focus on physical activity management through semi-structured interviews. Identifies four themes including physical/social isolation, information-seeking behavior, challenges managing fatigue and cognitive effects, and psychological adjustment to reduced functioning.

A qualitative descriptive study exploring how adults living with Long COVID experience disability as episodic in nature, characterized by fluctuations in symptom severity and health challenges over time. The study uses interviews and visual illustrations from 40 participants to document patterns of 'flare-ups' and 'crashes' and the unpredictability that intersects with disability experiences.

A qualitative study examining health system factors that shape access to long COVID care in Brazil's public healthcare system through interviews with 29 healthcare professionals. The study identifies multiple processes that invisibilise long COVID patients' candidacy for care but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A qualitative study using semistructured interviews with 18 long COVID patients exploring their lived experiences with physical activity, symptom management, and challenges resuming daily activities. The study identifies barriers to appropriate physical activity advice and the psychological impact of reduced physical function, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring the lived experiences of 12 long COVID patients through 16-week self-report diaries analyzed using thematic analysis. The study documents how long COVID impacts daily activities, quality of life, and personal identity, highlighting the need for integrated support mechanisms.

Qualitative study exploring how long COVID affects school experiences of 22 children/young people (ages 10-18) and 15 parents through narrative interviews. Identifies barriers to school attendance, impact on symptom management, and gaps in healthcare/education professional awareness, generating recommendations for supportive school responses.

A qualitative study of 25 parents whose children were hospitalized with COVID-19, exploring persistent physical, mental, and social health outcomes months after infection. Identified seven child-related themes including PTSD, social anxiety, and symptom severity on reinfection, plus four parent-specific themes about fear and support system challenges.

Qualitative descriptive study exploring perceptions and experiences of community rehabilitation for Long COVID among Scottish GPs and people with Long COVID through semistructured interviews. Identifies patient, GP, and service-level barriers to accessing rehabilitation and highlights the need for better promotion and understanding of rehabilitation's role in Long COVID management.

Qualitative descriptive study exploring barriers and facilitators to accessing long COVID community rehabilitation services in Scotland across 51 interviews with patients, allied health professionals, and NHS leaders. Identifies organizational challenges in service delivery and highlights the value of rehabilitation services when accessible, but provides no intervention outcomes or treatment efficacy data.

Qualitative study combining literature review with clinician and patient interviews to develop a conceptual model of long COVID symptoms and their impacts on daily life. Does not evaluate any treatment intervention—purely exploratory research on symptom phenotyping and patient-reported outcomes.

Qualitative interview study examining current Long COVID care practices in England through interviews with 21 patients and 15 healthcare professionals. Finds that Long COVID care is fragmented, patients face barriers in primary care, and specialized post-COVID services provide valuable validation and support.

Qualitative analysis of 140 long COVID patients from Survivor Corps describing experiences with internal tremors and vibrations as a prominent symptom. Study identifies 22 themes across 7 domains (symptom experience, onset, timing, triggers, baseline changes, healthcare experiences, and impact on livelihood) but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study using focus groups to identify the needs and challenges of 25 people with long COVID in the UK. Participants identified three key needs: accessible support systems (community groups, benefits, clinical services), research into physiology and treatments, and increased societal awareness and policy support.

A qualitative study exploring the lived experience of brain fog and neurocognitive symptoms in 50 long COVID patients through focus groups and email follow-up. While rich in descriptive findings about symptom burden and psychosocial impact, this is a qualitative descriptive study with no intervention or treatment component.

A qualitative study exploring physiotherapists' experiences treating long COVID patients in Canada through semi-structured interviews with 13 practitioners. Identifies key themes including disruption to the profession, learning curves, and evolving roles in long COVID rehabilitation.

Qualitative study using focus group interviews with 30 post-COVID patients to identify improvements to care delivery and health systems. Developed a conceptual framework for person-centered, multidisciplinary integrated care but did not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative evaluation of a digital health intervention (app + dashboard) for long COVID self-management using Normalisation Process Theory framework. Assesses implementation experiences among clinicians and healthcare professionals in community and secondary care settings, not a trial of treatment efficacy.

A qualitative cross-sectional study examining experiences of stigma and healthcare access among long COVID patients from Dutch, Turkish, and Moroccan ethnic backgrounds in the Netherlands. The study identifies barriers to care and self-stigma but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A qualitative study exploring the experiences of exercise professionals, physiotherapists, and long COVID patients in a novel online rehabilitation model combining exercise, education, and well-being support. The study found the model provided positive experiences for patients and job satisfaction for staff, with recommendations for team training and potential scaling to other populations.

A qualitative study of 13 pediatric long COVID patients' experiences with specialist clinic services in Southwest England. Findings emphasize the importance of validation, clinician expertise, peer support, proactive management involvement, and flexible appointment options, while identifying long waiting times as a barrier.

Qualitative study examining how long COVID impacts the working lives of 63 UK adults through narrative interviews and thematic analysis. Identifies barriers to employment including fatigue and brain fog, lack of employer awareness, and absence of supportive HR policies.

This qualitative study evaluates the usability and content validity of the ABCC-tool, a patient-reported outcome measure for post-COVID syndrome, through interviews with 19 post-COVID patients. The tool was found to be user-friendly and comprehensive, though the study does not test any therapeutic intervention.

Qualitative study exploring lived experiences of long COVID patients in North East England through interviews and Freedom of Information requests. Examines impacts on health, wellbeing, employment, and professional identity, finding widespread social isolation and inadequate workplace support.

This study uses discourse and media framing analysis to examine how long COVID has been represented in New Zealand radio broadcasts over 26 months. Rather than studying treatment or clinical outcomes, it analyzes media narratives and how long COVID is discursively constructed as 'real and important' versus 'not being addressed.'

Qualitative study exploring healthcare experiences of racially and ethnically minoritised people with Long COVID in the UK, using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis with 29 participants. Findings reveal systemic racism, dismissal, and lack of legitimisation in healthcare settings, with implications for improving care relationships and reducing health inequalities.

A qualitative study analyzing discussions in a private Facebook group for COVID-19 long-haulers, conducted through text analysis and interviews with community members. The paper examines how patients use social media for peer support and identifies primary discussion topics but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Qualitative research examining how long COVID patients and clinicians interact with personal tracking data and electronic health records within a specialized post-COVID clinic. The study identifies clinical workflow challenges and design opportunities for improving cross-provider collaboration, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This paper explores the co-design of pacing technologies for people with energy-limiting conditions including Long COVID and ME/CFS, using crip theory and asynchronous remote community co-design methods. While relevant to Long COVID, it is a methodological/design study rather than a treatment trial or evaluation, focusing on technology development processes rather than testing interventions for health outcomes.

This paper reports on the design and development of 'Living With Covid Recovery', a digital self-management app for long COVID patients, using user-centred HCI methods adapted for agile development. It focuses on methodological lessons from the design process and integration into clinical care pathways rather than reporting trial outcomes or treatment efficacy.

Qualitative study of how 21 long COVID patients use fitness tracking technologies for symptom management and pacing. Findings highlight design opportunities for tools supporting energy management, patient agency, and data sharing with healthcare providers.

A participatory design study exploring how mobile telemanipulator robots can be designed to support people with long COVID, grounded in disability and access studies. The paper presents design considerations and plans for future development but reports no clinical trial results or outcome data.

A design research paper exploring crip pacing technologies for energy-limiting conditions like long COVID and ME/CFS through co-design and research-through-design methods. The work proposes integrating jewelry-making techniques and wearable sensor data into therapeutic pacing tools, but presents no empirical trial or treatment evaluation.

This paper reports on a focus group discussion with occupational therapists about their experiences using energy management education (EME) protocol with post-COVID-19 fatigue patients. The study explicitly acknowledges that quantitative outcomes have not yet been measured and calls for further research, making it a protocol/feasibility study without results.

This qualitative study explores how mobile telemanipulator robots (MTRs) can be designed to support social inclusion for people with long COVID through participatory research with eight participants. The work presents design considerations for accessible robot systems but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment outcome.

The ErgoLoCo study evaluated acceptability of a telehealth-delivered occupational therapy intervention for long COVID patients through interviews with 13 participants and a focus group with 8 occupational therapists. Both occupational therapists and long COVID clients found the occupational therapy approach helpful, though participants receiving prerecorded videos emphasized the need for direct professional support to maximize effectiveness.

Qualitative interview study examining how long COVID affects caregiving responsibilities and experiences among people with long COVID and their caregivers in British Columbia. Findings highlight impacts of brain fog and exhaustion on household tasks, childcare, and emotional burden, with recommendations for health policy responses.

Qualitative study of 35 long COVID patients examining how the condition modifies social roles, with analysis of barriers (persistent symptoms, healthcare system gaps) and strengths (social networks, self-advocacy) by gender. While about long COVID, this is a non-interventional qualitative assessment with no treatment evaluation, making it ineligible for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

Qualitative substudy analyzing perceived social support in 330 posts from discussion forums of participants in a randomized clinical trial of an online group rehabilitation program for long COVID. Findings highlight the importance of peer support and identify gaps in formal healthcare support for long COVID patients.

This cross-sectional study examines how severe acute COVID-19 affects patients' dream experiences through structured interviews with 6 hospitalized patients. The study documents changes in dream frequency and content post-infection but does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for a treatment trials database.

Qualitative study exploring perspectives of nine rehabilitation professionals on long COVID rehabilitation and return-to-work interventions. Identifies education, gradual activation, and self-management as key interventions, but does not evaluate treatment outcomes in patients.

This is a qualitative sub-study of a completed RCT examining participants' perspectives on joining an 8-week virtual rehabilitation program for long COVID. The qualitative analysis reports on interviews with 13 intervention group participants, revealing themes around confidence in exercise, positive feelings about program assignment, and motivations for participation.

This sociology article examines how long COVID patients use self-tracking and online communities to challenge medical dismissal and generate lay knowledge about their condition. It is not a treatment intervention study but rather a qualitative analysis of patient practices and epistemic challenges.

This paper describes a telementoring ECHO program designed to educate healthcare providers about pediatric long COVID management through weekly tele-education sessions. While the program improved clinician knowledge and self-efficacy, it is not a patient treatment trial but rather an educational intervention for providers, and thus does not meet criteria for inclusion in the treatment trials meta-analysis.

This paper describes formative qualitative research (interviews and focus groups) to design a Long COVID care pathway and referral system through a learning health system approach. It presents no treatment intervention or clinical trial results, only insights from providers and community health workers to guide future implementation of care access.

Qualitative study exploring the lived experiences of patients with long-term cognitive sequelae after COVID-19 using in-depth interviews and interpretive analysis. The paper documents the psychological and social impacts of persistent symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study examining challenges faced by rehabilitation counselors and physicians when providing services to long COVID patients, particularly regarding return-to-work accommodations. Findings highlight workplace policy modifications and individualized service needs but do not test or evaluate a specific intervention.

A creative-relational qualitative inquiry exploring the lived experience of people with long COVID, particularly regarding physical activity. The study develops and shares a performance text as an advocacy and support resource, extending understanding beyond traditional evidence-based medicine approaches.

Qualitative study of 30 long COVID patients undergoing treatment for persistent chemosensory dysfunctions (taste/smell loss), examining how these disruptions affect social life, eating, and relationships. Findings highlight the importance of social support and healthcare recognition in managing these unique long COVID manifestations.

Qualitative study of 16 young people and parents with long COVID exploring lived experiences, symptom journeys, and access to care through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. The study identifies barriers to support and lack of available interventions but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment.

topics: patient experience|barriers to care|mental health|healthcare systems
summary: A qualitative study conducted by long COVID patients themselves exploring barriers and supports to recovery and return to health through focus groups and interviews with Canada-wide participants. The study identifies six themes including medical system challenges, mental health impacts, financial burden, and care/support resources, with recommendations for person-centered healthcare policy.

Qualitative study exploring patient experiences and acceptability of a rehabilitation program for post-COVID-19 symptoms through focus groups and interviews. Participants reported improvements in physical and mental symptoms and valued the supportive, shared learning environment of the program.

Qualitative study exploring long COVID patients' lived experiences and attitudes toward psychological approaches to their condition. Findings highlight patients' sense of disbelief and tension between psychological and medical explanations, suggesting that validating patient experiences may improve receptiveness to psychological support.

Qualitative study examining the financial and employment consequences of long COVID through in-depth interviews with 25 affected individuals. Explores gaps in unemployment, disability, and insurance policies rather than evaluating any medical intervention or treatment.

A qualitative study interviewing 12 long COVID patients to explore their psychological experiences and needs following hospitalization for COVID-19. Findings highlight severe psychological impacts and suggest the need for early psychological intervention, but this is a descriptive qualitative study without treatment testing.

Qualitative study exploring experiences of 18 long COVID patients from Danish, Turkish, and Moroccan backgrounds regarding access to care, diagnosis, and rehabilitation. Findings show systemic barriers to care and additional discriminatory obstacles faced by ethnic minority patients.

A qualitative study exploring menstrual health experiences among women and people who menstruate in Barcelona during COVID-19, including those with long COVID. The study found menstrual changes in some participants with long COVID and barriers to healthcare access, but did not test any interventions or treatments.

Qualitative phenomenological study exploring experiences of 19 Jordanian women regarding COVID-19 infection and vaccination effects on reproductive health. Study documents reported menstrual disturbances, sexual dysfunction, and pregnancy/breastfeeding concerns, but is excluded as it is purely descriptive qualitative research without treatment intervention or control comparison.

A longitudinal qualitative study following six COVID-19 critical care survivors and their relatives at 3 months and 1 year post-discharge, exploring recovery experiences and coping mechanisms. The study documents persistent long COVID symptoms and psychological impacts but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring how nurses in France contribute to managing post-COVID-19 condition patients across different healthcare settings. While addressing long COVID care organization, this is a descriptive study of nursing roles and care coordination rather than an intervention trial testing a specific treatment.

This qualitative study examines long COVID patients' experiences seeking healthcare by analyzing posts in two online forums (Mayo Clinic Connect and Reddit). The analysis identifies themes around time perception, symptom legitimacy, and responses to diagnostic dismissal, highlighting the importance of healthcare validation.

A qualitative narrative analysis of 8 Canadian long COVID patients' experiences seeking healthcare. The paper explores barriers to care and system-level challenges rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

topics: integrative medicine|group medical visits|symptom management|mental health
summary: Qualitative study evaluating a telehealth integrative medical group visit program (Nourish to Flourish) for long COVID patients, analyzing pre- and post-intervention interviews from 25 participants. Found that participants experienced unpredictable symptoms and barriers to conventional care, but benefited from group connection, shared experience, and integrative modalities including mindfulness, nutrition, and acupressure.

Qualitative study of 21 long COVID patients exploring emotional impacts and experiences of loss and grief related to their condition. While focusing on important psychosocial aspects of long COVID, this is a descriptive qualitative study that does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This narrative study evaluates patient experiences with the PaceMe app, a digital adaptive pacing intervention designed to help long COVID patients manage energy expenditure and prevent post-exertional malaise. Twenty-five participants completed two interviews over 3-6 months, with thematic analysis identifying key benefits including PEM management, support, validation, and improved sense of control.

Qualitative phenomenological study exploring meanings of recovery for 13 ICU survivors of COVID-19 through individual interviews. Findings emphasize patients' struggle for balance, need for social support, and inadequate follow-up care from healthcare professionals.

A qualitative interview study exploring the experiences of 13 post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients and 6 Dutch general practitioners regarding living with PCS and associated healthcare needs. The study identifies two patient phenotypes with different symptom patterns and healthcare requirements, emphasizing the importance of GP recognition and person-centred care approaches.

This qualitative study evaluated user experience and satisfaction with a respiratory telerehabilitation program among 17 older adults (≥65 years) with COPD or long COVID. Participants reported easy adaptation to the program, with key themes including access/continuity of care, communication with care team, and program experience (comfort, advantages, difficulties).

Qualitative descriptive study exploring older adults' and caregivers' experiences of long-term recovery from COVID-19 following inpatient geriatric rehabilitation in Ireland. Documents perceived long-term health effects and recovery enablers but does not test or evaluate a specific intervention.

A qualitative study exploring the lived experiences and psychosocial impact of long COVID in 16 children aged 9-18 through semi-structured interviews analyzed using thematic analysis. The study documents how children experience fatigue, loss of functioning, and gradual adaptation to living with long COVID, with findings emphasizing the importance of support from healthcare, school, and family.

A qualitative phenomenological study interviewing 56 long COVID patients 3 months post-hospitalization to understand their lived experiences, perceived needs, and difficulties. Findings confirm symptom persistence, psychological distress, and isolation, but do not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study examining emotional well-being, social support, and experiences of discrimination among 35 long COVID patients through interviews and focus groups. Findings show patients report low well-being, anxiety about the future, and discriminatory treatment in health care settings.

A nationwide cross-sectional survey of 991 US youth ages 14-24 assessing their experiences with and perspectives on long COVID. The study found that 32% of youth knew someone with long COVID symptoms and 50% expressed worry about long COVID, but the study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A qualitative phenomenological study exploring awareness and care-seeking behaviors for long COVID symptoms among COVID-19 survivors in Ethiopia. The study found significant awareness deficits about long COVID despite participants experiencing common symptoms, and documents various self-management and care-seeking approaches including medical care, remedies, spiritual solutions, and lifestyle modifications.

topics: unmet needs|healthcare access|quality of life|supportive care
summary: A qualitative study exploring the lived experiences of 24 long COVID patients and their unmet supportive needs across occupational, healthcare, and social domains. The paper identifies barriers to care, employment, and support, proposing a five-pronged policy approach but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring psychological distress experiences in COVID-19 patients during acute phase and post-recovery using content analysis of 34 interviews. The paper identifies sources of distress including disease uncertainty, quarantine anxiety, health system inefficiency, and stigma, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring self-generated coping strategies used by 18 long COVID patients to navigate everyday life, conducted through narrative interviews and reflexive thematic analysis. While valuable for understanding patient experiences and self-management approaches, this is a descriptive qualitative study that does not evaluate the effectiveness of any specific intervention or treatment.

A qualitative study examining how 48 German long COVID patients experienced COVID-19 vaccination and rehabilitation services through interviews and focus groups. While some participants found rehabilitation helpful, this is a descriptive qualitative assessment of existing healthcare utilization rather than an intervention trial testing treatment efficacy.

Qualitative study using focus groups with 99 Black and Latinx individuals experiencing long COVID symptoms to understand health and social impacts. Findings highlight disparities in long COVID awareness, healthcare access, and economic hardship among these communities, with recommendations for improved multilingual outreach and support.

Qualitative case study exploring how UK healthcare organizations developed and adapted post-discharge follow-up services for COVID-19 hospitalized patients using the Moments of Resilience framework. Findings show organizational responses were shaped by local need, funding, and systemic guidance, but the paper does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This is a qualitative study of 114 long COVID patients using interviews and focus groups to document lived experiences with the illness and healthcare access. It proposes quality principles for long COVID services but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

A qualitative study of 47 long COVID patients across 11 focus groups exploring their experiences with treatment, healthcare services, and mental health impacts. The study identifies systemic barriers to care and calls for improved long COVID-specific services and social support, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring Austrian GPs' experiences, knowledge, and attitudes toward long COVID management through 30 semistructured interviews conducted in 2022. Findings show GPs recognize long COVID but struggle with treatment, lack awareness of specific syndromes like post-exertional malaise and autonomic dysfunction, and call for better care pathways and specialist support.

This qualitative study conducted four focus groups with 23 long COVID patients to explore their experiences with medical care and barriers in the German healthcare system. The findings reveal that most patients perceived primary care as unhelpful, identified significant gaps in specialist access and awareness, and suggested improvements such as awareness campaigns and integrated care centers.

A longitudinal qualitative study examining healthcare experiences and system-level challenges for long COVID patients across UK primary, secondary, and specialist care settings. The study identifies barriers to care access and advocates for person-centered service delivery, but is a qualitative healthcare systems analysis rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This study uses nominal group technique to identify barriers and enablers to post-COVID follow-up care in Nigeria from healthcare provider perspectives. It is a qualitative health systems study, not a treatment trial, and should be excluded as a non-empirical assessment piece.

Qualitative study using interpretive description and thematic analysis to explore 56 long COVID patients' experiences accessing healthcare services and their barriers. Identifies key themes around symptom variability, service access challenges (stigma, logistics, testing), and factors affecting service quality, providing recommendations for health system improvement.

A qualitative analysis of 26 participants from a pilot feasibility trial evaluating group-based qigong (external and internal) for post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Approximately three-quarters of participants reported improvements in PASC symptoms (particularly fatigue, brain fog, and sleep quality) and 85% reported improved well-being, suggesting qigong may be a beneficial complementary therapy for managing PASC.

A phenomenological and netnographic study analyzing how 63 long COVID patients in France describe their symptoms across physical, cognitive, emotional, social, and behavioral dimensions using the Symptom Management Theory framework. The study documents the multidimensional impact of long COVID on daily life but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This qualitative study explores the impact of long COVID on UK healthcare workers, their families, managers, and workplace through semi-structured interviews with 42 participants across three groups. While it provides important insights into the lived experiences and support needs of affected HCWs, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.

Qualitative study of Canadian health and social service providers' experiences treating long COVID patients and their recommendations for service development. Documents personalized treatment approaches and gaps in evidence-based care, but does not test or evaluate a specific intervention.

A realist-informed qualitative study exploring how a structured out-patient long COVID rehabilitation intervention works through interviews with 12 patients, 1 focus group of health professionals, and 1 manager. The study refines the underlying programme theory, identifying identity transformation, person-centred rehabilitation, patient education, and peer support as key mechanisms, but is a qualitative methods paper analyzing an existing intervention rather than a trial testing intervention efficacy.

A qualitative study examining women's experiences seeking care at Long COVID clinics in the USA through semi-structured interviews with 30 patients. Identifies barriers to clinic access, gaps in provider knowledge, and need for improved care coordination, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative descriptive study exploring how 40 adults with Long COVID use pacing as a self-management strategy to mitigate symptoms across multiple life domains. Participants described pacing as a complex, challenging living strategy with benefits but limitations, requiring healthcare provider collaboration for implementation.

A qualitative interview study evaluating a community-based physical activity program for individuals with long COVID in Hertfordshire, UK, involving 8 service users and 3 health professionals. The study found that tailored physical activities and multidisciplinary collaboration provided benefits to some participants, though post-exertional malaise management and systemic barriers including stigma and disbelief remain significant challenges.
