Qualitative study examining how 35 long COVID patients in Spain used community resources (green spaces, public facilities, activities, associations) for self-directed rehabilitation. Patients reported improvements in physical and mental health through community resource use, with main barriers being symptoms and reinfection fear.

A qualitative analysis of 17 longitudinal health datasets on long COVID across nine high-income countries, examining data collection methods, populations, and outcomes. The study identifies gaps in comprehensive long-term data systems and notes that post-exertion malaise and patient-reported outcome measures are underrepresented in existing datasets.

This qualitative study examines how long COVID patients in Kenya access information and support through digital networks, comparing experiences of elite vs. non-elite patients. It is a social science analysis of patient networks and experiences rather than a treatment intervention study.

A qualitative study exploring stakeholder perspectives on WHO recommendations for using chest imaging to monitor COVID-19 pulmonary sequelae. While focused on long COVID monitoring, this is a guideline development study, not a treatment trial.

This qualitative grounded theory study explores treatment experiences, preferences, and expectations for cognitive impairments in long COVID among 23 Chinese young and older adults through semi-structured interviews. The study develops a theoretical framework showing age-specific differences in preferences (young adults favor non-pharmacological approaches; older adults prefer balanced pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies) but does not evaluate or test any actual treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring factors affecting mental health and well-being in 21 people with long COVID through semi-structured interviews. Identifies five themes including symptom burden, lack of treatment options, illness uncertainty, care experiences, and identity changes.

Qualitative study examining barriers and facilitators to healthcare access for long COVID patients in Austria through interviews with 15 experts and focus groups with 18 patients. Identifies systemic barriers including medical scepticism, specialist shortages, long waiting times, and financial constraints, with recommendations for improved care coordination and telemedicine.

Qualitative study examining workplace support and return-to-work experiences of 20 long COVID patients and 2 managers in the UK through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Identifies barriers (invisible symptoms, knowledge gaps, inflexible policies) and facilitators (phased return, work adjustments, occupational health) to supporting long COVID workers, highlighting the need for flexible, personalized RTW support.

Qualitative study using interpretive phenomenological analysis to explore the lived experiences of 18 long COVID patients referred to a primary care psychology service. Identifies key themes including uncertainty, mental/social impacts, self-advocacy, and coping mechanisms, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study examining how COVID-19 infection affects exercise participation and physical activity in 35 survivors at 7.74 months post-infection. Identifies themes of physical limitations (fatigue, dyspnea), reduced group exercise, increased exercise in some cases, and social support as factors influencing post-COVID exercise behavior.

This paper describes the development and content validation of a novel patient-reported outcome (PRO) instrument for measuring Long COVID/PASC symptoms through qualitative research with 30 patient interviews and clinician input. The study validates an 18-item measurement instrument but does not test any treatment or intervention—it is a measurement tool development study without clinical trial results.

Qualitative study documenting lived experiences of 25 long COVID patients with pain symptoms through focus groups, examining their healthcare interactions and treatment experiences. While addressing an important clinical gap, this is a descriptive qualitative study without testing any intervention or treatment, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

A qualitative study analyzing patient experiences and expectations when seeking long-COVID care in a primary care setting, using semi-structured interviews with 19 patients. The study identifies gaps between patient expectations and actual provider interactions, highlighting challenges in healthcare coordination and communication.

Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 in-depth interviews with long COVID patients exploring their lived experiences, symptoms, and psychosocial impacts. Study identified five major themes (decreased autonomy, decreased trust, worldview changes, social impacts, uncertainty) but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A critical discourse analysis of 103 UK media articles examining how long COVID in children and young people is characterized by parents, healthcare professionals, and the media itself. The study reveals that media characterizations contribute to epistemic injustice and barriers to care, with recommendations for journalists.

A phenomenological qualitative study of 19 long COVID patients describing symptom burden and impacts on work, relationships, and daily functioning. The study does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, instead providing descriptive insights on patient experiences and implications for primary care.

Pilot qualitative interview study exploring awareness and perceptions of Long COVID among 13 participants from the REACT community study, examining symptom attribution and understanding of the Long COVID term. Provides preliminary insights into varied patient experiences with persistent symptoms but conducts no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Qualitative analysis of 9,000 Facebook support group posts documenting the impact of post-COVID taste and smell alterations on daily life, psychological well-being, eating, and social engagement. This is a thematic analysis of user-generated text rather than a treatment trial or intervention study.

This study evaluated an 8-week inspiratory muscle training (IMT) rehabilitation program in 33 adults with post-COVID-19 condition through qualitative interviews. Participants reported perceived improvements in respiratory symptoms, exercise capacity, work capacity, and daily functioning, suggesting IMT may be beneficial as part of a holistic recovery approach.

Qualitative interview study examining expectations and experiences of 19 primary care patients seeking long COVID treatment. Identifies gaps between patient expectations (knowledgeable, attentive, collaborative care) and actual experiences (dismissal, fragmented care coordination, system barriers).

This qualitative study uses composite vignettes derived from thematic analysis of 47 semi-structured interviews with long COVID patients (6-11 months post-infection) to portray their lived experiences and recovery journeys. The analysis highlights psychological impacts, non-linear symptom recovery, variable healthcare access, and the broad impacts of long COVID on daily living, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A qualitative study of 10 COVID-19 patients in North Carolina examining their experiences from diagnosis through recovery, with particular focus on marginalized populations. The study identifies themes around testing, quarantine, medical care, and long-term recovery difficulties, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring the lived experiences of 47 adults with long COVID, focusing on mental health, quality of life, and coping strategies through focus groups stratified by pre-existing mental health conditions. Identified five key themes related to emotional impact, functional limitations, grief, stigmatization, and coping mechanisms, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Community-engaged qualitative study applying the Episodic Disability Framework to characterize the multi-dimensional and episodic health challenges experienced by 40 adults living with Long COVID across Canada, Ireland, UK, and US. The framework successfully conceptualizes disability in Long COVID but provides guidance for future measurement and rehabilitation approaches rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring why 20 hospitalized COVID-19 patients refused participation in a pulmonary rehabilitation program. Identified barriers including access difficulties, health problems, time constraints, and lack of perceived need for rehabilitation.

A qualitative study investigating general practitioners' and patients' perspectives on long COVID management in general practice through semi-structured interviews and questionnaires. The study identified themes around complex presentations, standardized care, and collaborative doctor-patient relationships, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Qualitative study interviewing 21 long COVID patients and 13 non-COVID controls about experiences returning to work during UK lockdown. Identifies barriers (fatigue, cognitive symptoms, lack of employer understanding) and recommends tailored return-to-work interventions, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment.

Qualitative study examining barriers to and facilitators of rehabilitation participation among COVID-19 ICU survivors with ARDS, stratified by socio-economic status. Finds that precarious socio-economic situations substantially impair access to rehabilitation through multiple social determinants.

This is a methodological study describing the creation of cordel literature (a Brazilian poetic form) as an educational technology for health promotion about post-COVID-19 syndrome. It does not study treatment outcomes or involve patient intervention—it is primarily an educational/awareness tool development study.

This is a focus group study that gathers patient feedback on a draft expectation management intervention for Long COVID as part of the SOMA.COV project. The study is a qualitative assessment of treatment acceptability and does not test the intervention itself; the actual RCT is planned separately.

A qualitative phenomenological study using unstructured interviews with 30 COVID-19 recovered patients to explore their post-recovery physical and mental health experiences. Findings describe persistent respiratory difficulties, cognitive impairments, psychological distress, and sleep disturbances, with recommendations for comprehensive post-recovery care but no intervention tested.

Qualitative study exploring the experiences of 18 long COVID patients accessing primary health care in New Zealand through narrative inquiry and thematic analysis. Findings reveal systemic gaps in primary care support, lack of staff training, and inadequate government investment, with no treatment intervention evaluated.

Qualitative study examining how 52 long COVID patients and 15 caregivers experience and cope with stressful life disruptions caused by the condition. Findings identify key themes of deviation from normalcy, stress and grief, and adaptive coping strategies, with implications for supportive rehabilitation approaches.

Qualitative study examining health needs and healthcare service utilization among 10 individuals with post-COVID-19 condition and their families in Brazil. Describes patterns of care access (public and private services) and identifies need for ongoing multidisciplinary rehabilitation and prevention of functional decline, but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention.

This paper describes experiences from a multicentre telemedicine study involving 373 long-COVID patients in Poland using the Aidmed wearable monitoring system. It is excluded because it is a qualitative analysis of telemedicine implementation methodology rather than a study of a specific treatment intervention with measurable patient outcomes.

Qualitative study of 9 cardiometabolic patients exploring their perception of lifestyle adaptations after COVID-19 infection. Found that long COVID symptoms (fatigue, muscle pain, blood pressure/glycemic dyscontrol) impacted daily routines but motivated some patients toward healthier lifestyle choices.

Qualitative study of 92 adult men in Brazil exploring their lived experience and discourse about long COVID symptoms and clinical complications using collective subject discourse analysis. Study documents respiratory, systemic, and psychological impacts of long COVID without evaluating any treatment or intervention.

This paper analyzes personal narratives of long COVID patients in media and social networks, examining how journalists and patients discursively construct the disease. It is a qualitative discourse analysis study, not a treatment intervention study.

Qualitative study exploring how nurses describe challenges and gaps in knowledge when caring for post-COVID-19 patients in an emergency unit. Findings highlight lack of institutional protocols, training, and knowledge about rehabilitation referrals, with nurses relying on experiential learning.

Qualitative study of 41 aged individuals with long COVID investigating their health needs and access to health services 18 months post-infection. Identifies healthcare demand patterns and heterogeneous service availability across public and private sectors, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A qualitative phenomenological study exploring the lived experience of 10 older adults with post-COVID-19 syndrome at a Brazilian reference center. The study documents psychological and physical impacts including insecurity, frustration, sadness, and impaired quality of life, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study examining care provided to 41 older Brazilian adults with long COVID symptoms persisting ~18 months post-infection, based on semi-structured interviews conducted 2022. Findings reveal episodic, reactive healthcare culture focused on curative rather than preventive approaches.

Qualitative study using in-depth interviews to explore how long COVID exacerbates social vulnerability among eight workers in Brazil, examining employment loss, inadequate social protections, and gender inequities. While the paper confirms long COVID's impact on vulnerable populations, it does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment.

Qualitative study collecting narratives from 5 long COVID patients about their lived experiences with the condition. Identifies themes around symptom uncertainty, mental health impacts, physical functioning, family effects, and identity changes, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This paper analyzes media and social media discourse on long COVID in Spanish digital media over 12 months using discourse analysis and social listening tools. It identifies communication patterns and develops recommendations for improving public health communication about long COVID, but does not study any treatment or intervention.

This paper analyzes how the Swedish Covid Association advocates for Long COVID patients using narrative policy framework, examining their advocacy strategies across multiple levels. It critiques how patient advocacy narratives may inadvertently reinforce ableist standards despite empowering individuals.

Qualitative study exploring how long COVID symptoms impact social life among 15 female long haulers through semi-structured interviews. Identifies impacts including physical limitations, financial hardship, social relationships, role conflicts, and stigma, with recommendations for tailored social support.

This qualitative study used broad consultation and Delphi consensus methods to identify research priorities for COVID-19 and long COVID in Brazil, involving researchers, health managers, and professionals. The resulting agenda consolidated 179 research lines, with long COVID, mental health, and immunosuppression as predominant themes, but it is a policy/guideline document rather than an empirical treatment trial.

This is a community health education intervention in Indonesia aimed at teaching elderly residents (posyandu members and local officials) about recognizing long COVID symptoms and performing rehabilitation exercises. The paper describes an educational event conducted on July 15, 2023, reporting that the intervention improved knowledge significantly, but this is an educational program description without a controlled design, no outcome measurement, and no empirical data collection—it is not a clinical trial.

Qualitative study using the Three Delays Model to assess obstacles to service recognition, access, and adequacy for people with long COVID through analysis of online mutual aid posts and lived experiences. Finds significant gaps in government service provision and identifies patients as primary sources of subject matter knowledge shaping policy.

This qualitative study uses directed content analysis to describe the experiences of 16 Iranian COVID-19 survivors, identifying intrapersonal, interpersonal, and extrapersonal stressors experienced during recovery. The paper focuses on phenomenological and psychological aspects of post-COVID recovery but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

Qualitative analysis of COVID-19 patient experiences from Reddit posts (March-August 2020), describing acute and post-viral symptoms reported by 1,296 tested-positive users. While mentions post-viral fatigue and long-term impacts, this is a passive observational study of social media data with no intervention or treatment evaluation—it characterizes patient experiences rather than testing interventions.

Qualitative multilevel study examining social and structural determinants of health affecting COVID-19 survivors, carepartners, and healthcare stakeholders in rural South Carolina through interviews and focus groups. Identifies themes around health challenges, care access gaps, equity needs, and systemic racism as barriers to recovery and chronic disease self-management.

Qualitative study exploring the roles and impacts of online peer support groups for long COVID patients in the UK through 11 semistructured interviews. Identifies that peer groups fill care gaps but often take on more responsibilities than they can manage, with recommendations for integrating peer support into broader care structures.

Thematic analysis of social media posts from patients with post-infectious olfactory dysfunction (parosmia, phantosmia) following COVID-19. The study identifies symptoms, triggers, and emotional impacts but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This is a literature review examining the challenges of involving long COVID patients in cocreative development of digital assistive technologies. It does not report outcomes from any treatment trial, but rather synthesizes lessons from the literature on participatory design methods.

This paper analyzes free-text responses from children and young people in the CLoCk cohort study to understand their experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic, using AI-powered text network analysis and manual sentiment coding. It is a secondary qualitative analysis of existing survey data from a long COVID study, not a treatment trial.

Qualitative interview study examining how German long COVID patients perceive state pandemic measures and media coverage during COVID-19. The study explores patient perspectives rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring how the COVID-19 pandemic influenced retirement decisions among Mexican university professors. While the paper mentions long-term COVID-19 effects as one factor affecting retirement, it is primarily a study of retirement decision-making and occupational stress, not long COVID research or treatment trials.

Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews to explore the illness experience of 17 Italian long COVID patients, examining symptomatology, loss of autonomy, social isolation, diagnostic challenges, and care access barriers. Concludes that intervention programs and multi-disciplinary rehabilitation are needed, but does not test or evaluate any treatment.

This paper discusses the design of post-COVID-19 patient care journeys and coordination strategies using digital health tools and hybrid care models in Brazil. It is a qualitative research article based on in-depth interviews with health leaders, not a treatment trial or outcome study.

A qualitative phenomenological study examining psychological resilience dynamics in 4 COVID-19 survivors experiencing long COVID symptoms (>60 days post-infection). The study identifies protective factors (adaptive thinking, emotional management, social support, spiritual factors) and risk factors (social stigma, long-term COVID impacts) influencing psychological resilience, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This paper describes virtual body mapping, an arts-based qualitative research methodology for exploring lived experiences of long COVID patients. It is a methodological guide focused on research design and process rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

A qualitative study using virtual body mapping with 19 long COVID patients to explore their lived experiences and embodied symptoms across three 2-hour sessions. The study documents patient narratives and coping strategies but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

This paper uses a three-round Delphi method to gather expert opinions from European physiotherapists on managing long COVID-19 patients and identifying appropriate assessments and treatments. Rather than testing a specific intervention, it develops consensus-based recommendations for physiotherapeutic management, making it a guideline/consensus study rather than a treatment trial.

A qualitative study of 11 general practice stakeholders exploring the challenges and experiences of diagnosing and managing long COVID in primary care settings. The paper identifies gaps in definitions, documentation, and screening tools but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a community health education program conducted in two Indonesian cities to increase public awareness about long COVID symptoms and vitamin use during the pandemic. The activity consisted of educational sessions and interactive dialogue with community members, with evaluation based on participant enthusiasm rather than clinical outcomes or treatment efficacy.

This study evaluated user experiences with the Untire mobile app for fatigue management in post-acute COVID-19 syndrome patients through semi-structured interviews. The app was perceived as supportive and easy to use, with particular utility for energy measurement and relaxation exercises.

Qualitative study exploring experiences of 56 people living with Long COVID accessing rehabilitation services in Alberta, Canada through semi-structured interviews. Identifies barriers and facilitators to rehabilitation access, highlighting need for accessible, multidisciplinary, flexible, person-centred approaches.

This paper analyzes Greek-language Twitter posts from 2022 to extract discussion topics and sentiment about long COVID. It is a social media sentiment analysis study, not a treatment trial, and should be excluded as it does not study interventions or treatments.

This qualitative interview study from the Progress-Projekt describes the development of an optimized care pathway for outpatient management of post-COVID patients in German primary care settings. The paper focuses on health system organization and clinical pathway design rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring lived experiences of 7 individuals with long-COVID-related communication and swallowing difficulties through semi-structured interviews. Identifies barriers to healthcare access and psychosocial impacts but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This paper discusses methodological challenges and proposes solutions for conducting daily computerized cognitive assessments in post-COVID patients. It is a protocol/methods paper proposing a study design rather than reporting results from an actual trial.

Qualitative investigation of COVID-19 experiences in 30 Nepalese residents using telephone interviews and purposive sampling. Study documents varied individual experiences and recovery timelines, with findings that most respondents reported post-COVID syndromes that gradually decreased over time.

This is an educational health promotion activity (PKM) delivered online in October 2021 to increase public knowledge about the role of medical rehabilitation in post-COVID-19 recovery. It was not a treatment study but rather a knowledge dissemination intervention with pre/post questionnaires showing gaps in understanding of rehabilitation for long COVID.

Qualitative study exploring how 15 long-hauler women use social media for support, information gathering, and health management. Identifies both benefits (reduced isolation, community connection) and challenges (misinformation, rumination) of social media use in long COVID patient communities.

This paper analyzes Greek-language Twitter posts about long COVID from 2022 using sentiment analysis and topic modelling, followed by ChatGPT interpretation and human expert labeling. It is a social media analysis study that does not evaluate any treatment interventions or clinical outcomes.

A qualitative study using focus group interviews to explore workplace factors that promote or hinder work ability and return to work among 19 individuals with long COVID. The study identifies key themes including communication/support, work adjustments, acceptance of limitations, and need for recovery time.

A qualitative study examining challenges faced by long COVID and post-vaccination affected individuals through the lens of virtual self-help groups, analyzing gaps in medical care, social security, and societal recognition. The work is a sociological analysis rather than a treatment trial, focusing on systemic failures and policy implications.

Qualitative thematic analysis exploring experiences of 5 long COVID patients, documenting symptoms (fatigue, smell/taste loss, breathing difficulty, anxiety) and recovery timelines. Study focuses on patient experiences and health monitoring needs rather than testing any intervention or treatment.

A social media analysis study using discourse analysis methods to explore how long COVID patients discuss mental health impacts and dietary supplement use on social platforms. The study does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention, but rather analyzes public perspectives and experiences.

Qualitative study exploring the psychological experiences of healthcare workers returning to work after acute COVID-19 infection. Does not focus on long COVID (persistent post-infection syndrome) and is not a treatment/intervention trial.

Qualitative study describing how a public hospital in Xi'an was designated as a COVID-19 rehabilitation center and implemented organizational changes to provide rehabilitation services to 583 discharged patients. The paper analyzes hospital management strategies and operational transformation rather than evaluating specific treatments or interventions for long COVID patients.

Qualitative study examining resilience resources and coping strategies used by female long COVID patients across individual, social, and health systems levels through 15 semi-structured interviews. Identifies cognitive, behavioral, spiritual, and social resources that support resilience but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Qualitative interview study examining perceived discrimination in fatigue across medical conditions and social domains, with intersectional analysis of 19 patients. Findings highlight discrimination in medical settings and structural barriers but do not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative interview study with 25 long COVID patients in Germany exploring how they perceive life restrictions and occupational impacts. Findings show severe symptom-related impairments in daily activities, work performance, and social contacts, highlighting need for workplace support and reintegration strategies.

This is a SWOT analysis and case study of two German long COVID care networks, examining how multidisciplinary and multispecialty healthcare approaches are organized and implemented. It describes network structure, collaboration experiences, and barriers rather than testing any specific treatment or intervention.

This mixed-methods study evaluated an 11-week multimodal integrative day clinic program (MICOM) for post-COVID syndrome patients, with qualitative interviews conducted with 20 intervention participants. Participants reported significant improvements in physical and mental symptoms, well-being, and self-efficacy, with sustained lifestyle changes in nutrition, stress management, and activity levels.

Qualitative study investigating lived experiences of COVID-19-positive frontline workers in Bangladesh during acute infection and early recovery. Focuses on workplace adaptation, isolation experiences, and psychological impacts during active infection, not post-COVID sequelae.

This study analyzes 1.35 million X (Twitter) posts from 2020-2023 using BERT-based topic modeling to characterize public discourse around long COVID. It identifies three themes (general discussions, skepticism, and adverse effects) but is a secondary analysis of social media data, not a primary research study or treatment trial.

This qualitative study evaluates a CDC-funded virtual learning program (LC&FIRP) that trained primary care providers in long COVID and ME/CFS management using an ECHO model with lived-experience experts. While relevant to long COVID, the study does not test a treatment or intervention for patients—it assesses provider education and training outcomes rather than patient clinical outcomes.

Qualitative study exploring the multidimensional aftermath of COVID-19 among 14 previously hospitalized patients in Bangladesh, examining physical health, financial, social, and psychological impacts. No treatment intervention is evaluated; this is a descriptive qualitative assessment of patient experiences and consequences.

A qualitative grounded theory study examining the lived experiences of 56 middle-aged and older Brazilian adults hospitalized with COVID-19 who developed long COVID symptoms. The study identifies themes around experiencing acute COVID, oscillating symptom severity, and identity reconstruction, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative interview study examining long COVID patients' experiences with persistent symptoms and impacts on daily life, mental health, and finances 15 months after initial interviews. Study demonstrates ongoing symptomatology and need for support resources but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring how children and families describe their experiences with long COVID, including diagnosis-seeking, symptom burden, and impacts on daily functioning. Analysis of 6 children and 5 caregiver interviews identified themes around diagnostic challenges, family/social impacts, and coping strategies, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study of 19 long COVID patients exploring subjective strategies for maintaining appetite in the context of chemosensory dysfunction. Identifies coping strategies focused on food texture, familiar foods, eating environment, and holistic well-being, but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment.

A qualitative study evaluating Energy Management Education (EME), a structured occupational therapy group intervention for long COVID-related fatigue. Six participants reported successfully implementing fatigue management strategies and experienced improved control over daily routines, with occupational therapists providing insights into the unique challenges of post-COVID fatigue management.

Qualitative descriptive study of 12 long COVID patients exploring their experiences with persistent taste and smell disorders, changes in daily life, and coping strategies. The study documents the significant impact of olfactory and gustatory dysfunction on quality of life but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A qualitative study of 7 participants with post-COVID condition who completed a 12-week exercise rehabilitation program delivered by a football club community trust. Participants reported improvements in exercise capacity, fatigue, breathlessness, physical function, quality of life, and emotional well-being.

This qualitative study examines healthcare provider perceptions of Alberta's provincial long COVID care pathway implementation across eight early-user sites. The research identifies themes around process perceptions, patient education awareness, and evolving knowledge challenges, but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring how social support influences long COVID patients' work and personal lives through semi-structured interviews with 21 patients. Findings show positive support from family and friends, but negative appraisal support from workplaces when others misunderstand the condition's scope and duration.

Qualitative study of 14 long COVID patients' experiences at a specialized outpatient clinic in Germany, examining care pathways and perceptions of clinical services. Findings highlight unmet expectations from prior care, positive experience at the specialist clinic, and need for optimized care models adapted to patients' limited resources.

Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 48 COVID-19 recovering patients to explore experiences and impact on physical activity levels. Identifies key challenges including symptom exacerbation upon return to PA, highlighting need for individualized support.

A qualitative study documenting patient experiences and understanding of post-COVID-19 syndrome through interviews with 230 patients two years post-infection, of whom 158 experienced the condition. The study describes the syndrome as characterized by interrelated physical and psychological symptoms but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This phenomenological study examines psychological experiences of COVID-19 patients during and after acute hospitalization in Hong Kong, identifying three themes: uncertainty during admission, adjustment post-discharge, and self-growth. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 psychological impacts during hospitalization, not long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions.

A co-produced intervention study that developed and tested a multidisciplinary rehabilitation program combining sport/exercise medicine and functional rehabilitation for long COVID patients in underserved UK communities. Ten participants were recruited with eight completing the intervention, showing feasibility of the approach for addressing fatigue, anxiety, and deconditioning in this population.

Qualitative study of 397 COVID-19 survivors interviewed at 6 months post-infection about their lived experience using metaphors. Findings show 62.5% expressed negative emotional orientations, with higher rates among females and older patients, highlighting long-term psychosocial burden of COVID-19 recovery.

Qualitative study exploring how persistent COVID-19 symptoms affect the social lives of 15 female long haulers through semi-structured interviews. Findings show long COVID negatively impacts physical functioning, economic stability, social relationships, and causes stigma, though social media provided some mitigation.

Qualitative study examining psychological experiences and health consequences of COVID-19 survivors hospitalized in ICU via semi-structured interviews with 15 participants. Found that 86.7% of participants moved to normal anxiety/depression values after discharge, but identifies long COVID as an important problem affecting physical and psychological health.

This qualitative study analyzes self-produced texts from long COVID patients on the Zhihu online Q&A community to explore illness experiences, adaptation, and life reconstruction in China. While relevant to long COVID, it is a qualitative analysis of patient narratives rather than a treatment intervention study, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

A qualitative thematic analysis of illness perceptions and recovery strategies in 24 post-COVID-19 patients (8 recovered, 16 non-recovered) 7-12 months after hospitalization. The study identifies patient perspectives on symptoms and coping mechanisms but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Qualitative study of 15 long COVID patients examining how brain fog and fatigue impact daily activities, work, and relationships through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Findings show cognitive and fatigue symptoms significantly impair functioning across multiple life domains and highlight the need for better clinical support.

Qualitative phenomenological study investigating perceptions of 27 long COVID patients in Spain regarding healthcare quality and support. Focuses on patient experiences and demands for improved healthcare systems rather than testing any specific treatment intervention.

A qualitative study exploring healthcare provider experiences delivering services to long COVID patients in Alberta. Findings emphasize the importance of education, symptom acknowledgement, and improving navigation to long COVID services, but this is a qualitative analysis of provider perspectives rather than a treatment intervention trial.

Qualitative study exploring health experiences of 14 post-COVID-19 condition patients through semi-structured interviews. Findings describe patients' experiences of loss (abilities, control) and revaluation, but this is descriptive qualitative research without any treatment intervention or control group.

Qualitative study exploring healthcare experiences and barriers to care among people from ethnic minority groups living with long COVID in the UK. Findings highlight gaps in awareness, negative healthcare encounters, discrimination, and the need for empathy and validation in clinical settings.

Qualitative study exploring the meaning and importance of Long COVID diagnosis from perspectives of affected young people, their parents, and healthcare professionals. Finds that diagnosis serves as validation and legitimization for families, while professionals focus on individualized treatment approaches.

Qualitative study describing how German general practitioners manage long COVID patients, their clinical approaches, and challenges. While focused on long COVID, this is a qualitative interview study of physician practices rather than a treatment trial or intervention study.

Qualitative study exploring the potential role of community pharmacists in supporting long COVID patients through interviews with patients and pharmacy staff. Study is incomplete with only 6 interviews completed at submission and results ongoing, making it a protocol paper without final results.

This qualitative study gathered perspectives from 8 Portuguese rehabilitation nurses on planning and implementing telerehabilitation programs for long COVID patients during transitional care. The study identifies key considerations and advantages for telerehabilitation but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention with patient outcomes.

Secondary qualitative analysis of women's experiences living with long COVID based on focus group data from 8 Scottish participants. Identifies themes around prolonged illness, care barriers, and coping mechanisms but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

A qualitative interview study exploring how Slovenian primary care physicians manage and perceive long COVID patients, identifying communication and trust as key factors. This is a qualitative study of physician experiences, not a treatment trial or intervention study.

This paper describes a cross-sectional survey of 26 long COVID patients' experiences, symptoms, healthcare utilization, and satisfaction with a patient-oriented knowledge-sharing session. It is excluded because it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention—it is a descriptive qualitative study of patient perspectives and needs.

This qualitative study explores patient experiences of the Long COVID-Optimal Health Programme (LC-OHP), a psychoeducational self-efficacy intervention, as part of a larger randomized controlled trial. Eleven participants who received the intervention reported benefits for physical health and mental wellbeing, with suggestions for program improvement.

A qualitative study exploring the lived experiences and care needs of children and young people with long COVID through interviews with patients, parents, and healthcare professionals. The study identifies key themes around living with long COVID, uncertainty surrounding the condition, and barriers to accessing appropriate support.

Qualitative study exploring the experiences of 24 people with long-COVID symptoms and their interactions with primary care, using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Findings emphasize the importance of GPs demonstrating empathy, understanding, and belief in patients' symptoms, with focus on support during recovery rather than treatment evaluation.

Qualitative analysis of 23 Russian Internet users' narratives about post-COVID-19 syndrome, examining health-preserving practices and behavioral strategies. Study documents symptoms, treatment-seeking behaviors, and patient experiences rather than testing a specific intervention or treatment outcome.

This paper reports structured interviews with 42 long COVID patients, 10 healthcare professionals, and 11 communication specialists to assess health information needs and communication gaps. It recommends institutional recognition, official digital platforms, and multidisciplinary collaboration but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Community health education initiative in Indonesia focusing on long COVID-19 awareness and stress management techniques (deep breathing exercises and relaxation training) for children. Demonstrated increased knowledge of stress management after educational intervention and relaxation training.

This qualitative descriptive study explores patients' experiences living with COVID-19 during the first pandemic wave through 15 semi-structured interviews in Canada. The paper highlights challenges in accessing care, persistent symptoms recognition, and the need for better healthcare provider responsiveness to long COVID patients, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper describes a health promotion counseling intervention (PDCA cycle method) delivered to 20 long COVID survivors in Indonesia to improve quality of life. The study is an uncontrolled descriptive case study evaluating knowledge gains from counseling, not a treatment trial with comparison groups or outcome measurement.

Qualitative phenomenological study exploring resilience experiences in 9 elderly long COVID survivors using interpretative phenomenology analysis. Identified five themes including trauma from critical COVID experience, grief, acceptance processes, and spiritual factors that support psychological resilience and recovery.

A qualitative phenomenological study exploring the lived experiences of 14 cancer patients with long COVID-19 in Zambia, examining disruptions to cancer treatment, psychological distress, and coping mechanisms. The study documents how long COVID exacerbates cancer care burden but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This phenomenological study examines perceptions of people living with long COVID regarding loss of instrumental activities of daily living function and reduced healthcare access. The paper is a qualitative study without treatment intervention or quantitative outcomes.

Qualitative study exploring experiences of healthcare workers who were hospitalized as COVID-19 patients at a private facility in South Africa. While some participants experienced long COVID and post-traumatic stress, this is a descriptive study of patient experiences without testing any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study using interpretative phenomenological analysis to explore how nine middle-aged women manage their long COVID symptoms and navigate healthcare experiences. Findings highlight patients' mistrust of health services, symptom ambiguity misattributed to anxiety, and recommendations for improved patient-centered care.

Qualitative case study examining how the COVID-19 pandemic affected South African healthcare workers' physical, psychological, social, and spiritual well-being. Reports long COVID among participants and describes development of a multifaceted wellness program, but provides no treatment intervention evaluation with measurable outcomes.

A phenomenological qualitative study examining physical and psychological effects of COVID-19 on 12 survivors in Pakistan using convenient sampling and thematic analysis. The study documents post-COVID symptom experiences, psychological impacts, and social stigma but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring the affective, cognitive, and psychological impacts of long COVID in six participants using ethnographic methodology and in-depth interviews. Found three main categories of impact: affective (sadness, fear, concern), cognitive (limited knowledge about the syndrome), and representation (significant changes in daily life).

This is a co-design study that developed an online 'Long COVID Education and Awareness Hub' through stakeholder workshops involving people with long COVID, caregivers, and healthcare providers. The work focuses on identifying care needs and knowledge translation rather than testing a specific treatment intervention or evaluating patient outcomes.

This paper evaluates a pilot group intervention (MACH Service) delivered by NHS Lothian that provided psychoeducation and peer support to hospitalized COVID-19 patients experiencing long COVID symptoms and psychological distress. The study reflects on successes and challenges of the intervention to inform future mental health interventions for this population.

This paper reports on interviews with 12 psychologists about their experiences treating adults with long COVID who have neurodiversity or intellectual disabilities. It identifies clinical considerations and recommends adaptations to long COVID treatments but does not study or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Qualitative study exploring health promotion behaviors and influencing factors in 15 long COVID patients using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Identifies barriers (limited cognition, low self-control) and enablers (family/peer support, medical guidance) to health promotion behavior.

This paper analyzes narrative reports and testimonies of people with post-COVID syndrome across digital spaces, social media, and everyday communication using qualitative/ethnographic methods. It examines how language is used to describe and communicate the post-COVID experience but does not study any treatment or intervention.

This paper describes a focus group study with rehabilitation nurses to design a tele-rehabilitation intervention framework for long COVID patients post-hospitalization. It is a protocol/design paper that proposes an intervention model without testing it on actual patients or reporting patient outcomes.

A qualitative study exploring how long COVID patients experience and manage physical activity limitations through semi-structured interviews with 17 participants in South Africa. The study identifies coping strategies and barriers to physical activity but does not test or evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A community health education intervention in Indonesia providing physical therapy assessment, management, and education to 18 long COVID patients aged 30-65. Pre/post-test results showed an 83.3% improvement in knowledge regarding the importance of physical activity for post-COVID health and quality of life.

Qualitative case study examining traditional Thai healing approaches (herbal medicine, massage, aromatherapy, meditation) for treating long COVID patients. No quantitative outcomes reported; focuses on documenting a healer's methods rather than evaluating treatment efficacy.

A qualitative interpretive description study exploring the lived experiences of 10 adults with pulmonary sequelae of long COVID through semi-structured interviews. The study identifies illness burden, emotional responses, and healthcare navigation challenges but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This is a community health education and screening intervention conducted in a coastal Indonesian district, providing respiratory health education, breathing exercises, and spirometry screening to COVID-19 survivors. The study reports improved knowledge about long COVID and vaccination, plus good respiratory health outcomes, but is an uncontrolled educational program without a control group and does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

A qualitative exploratory study of musculoskeletal pain experiences in 12 women with long COVID in South Africa using in-depth interviews. Identifies common pain presentations (back, neck, shoulder, headaches) and their impact on quality of life, with participants using pain medication, chiropractic treatment, and lifestyle changes for management.

Qualitative study examining herbal medicine use behaviors among 20 people in a Thai community for managing long COVID symptoms. Finds that participants have basic knowledge of herbal remedies obtained from online sources but lack accurate information, leading to incorrect and excessive use despite perceiving herbs as beneficial and affordable.

Qualitative grounded theory study exploring how younger and older UK adults experience and manage long COVID-related cognitive impairment, their coping strategies, and treatment preferences. Both age groups expressed urgent need for evidence-based interventions, with younger adults more proactive in seeking experimental therapies and older adults emphasizing pragmatic adaptation.

Qualitative study using narrative interviews and focus groups with 43 healthcare professionals with long COVID to inform service design and develop quality standards for long COVID care. Presents co-designed care pathway recommendations rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This study analyzes 10,670 English-language tweets about long COVID from March-April 2022 to characterize public sentiment and discussion topics. The analysis found comparable positive (19.90%) and negative (18.39%) sentiment, with dominant emotions being trust, fear, and sadness, but does not study any treatment or clinical intervention.

Case report of a single patient who developed secondary organizing pneumonia 40 days after mild COVID-19 infection recovery. The patient responded to corticosteroid therapy, highlighting a rare post-COVID pulmonary complication.

A case report describing a 5-week musculoskeletal physiotherapy intervention for a post-COVID-19 patient with physical sequelae. The patient showed substantial improvements in pain (10→3), muscle strength (2→4), joint range of motion (67%→100%), and functional balance tests.

This case report describes a rare delayed complication of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis (maxillary bony sequestration) in an immunocompetent patient, presenting 16 months after acute COVID-19 infection. While the patient experienced persistent symptoms, the paper is primarily about infectious disease complications rather than long COVID syndrome and does not study a treatment intervention.

Case report of a 21-year-old woman presenting with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) 4 months post-COVID-19 infection, featuring fever, mucocutaneous lesions, and refractory hypotension. The paper documents treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin and high-dose aspirin, highlighting MIS-A as a rare late complication of COVID-19 with similarities to Kawasaki disease.

Case report of a 39-year-old male with persistent dry mouth and dry eye lasting >3 months following COVID-19 infection, consistent with long COVID sequelae. Patient was treated with hydroxychloroquine and tear drops with symptom remission, suggesting sicca syndrome as a potential long COVID complication.

This is a single case report of a 33-year-old COVID-19 patient who developed insomnia and mental health impairment following ICU discharge. The paper describes acute post-ICU syndrome rather than long COVID, which requires persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection, and does not study a treatment intervention.

Case report of a single patient who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) as a post-viral complication following COVID-19 infection. The patient presented with rapidly progressive sensorimotor deterioration that was resistant to plasma exchange therapy, but this is a single case report rather than a long COVID treatment trial.

This paper presents a single case report of subacute thyroiditis occurring after COVID-19 infection, with review of its presentation and clinical outcome. It is a case report with no treatment intervention or control group, representing observational documentation of a post-COVID complication rather than a treatment trial.

A case report describing a pediatric patient with post-COVID hypertension and hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism. The paper highlights the importance of monitoring blood pressure and renal function in children recovering from COVID-19 but presents only a single case without treatment outcomes or comparative data.

A case report of a 63-year-old man who developed fatal Aspergillus endocarditis nine months after COVID-19-associated invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, treated with antifungal therapy (voriconazole) and surgical valve replacement. The case illustrates aspergillosis as a late consequence of COVID-19 requiring long-term follow-up and combined surgical and systemic antifungal management.

Case report of a 15-year-old with sickle cell disease who developed severe psychosis and cognitive impairment 4 weeks after COVID-19 infection, treated with antipsychotics and neuropsychiatric rehabilitation. Psychotic symptoms resolved after 3 weeks but mild cognitive impairment persisted for ~1 year, highlighting neuropsychiatric vulnerability in children with sickle cell disease post-COVID-19.

This case report describes a 26-year-old patient who developed sarcoidosis as a rare complication following COVID-19 infection, initially misdiagnosed as post-COVID fibrosis. The patient was successfully treated with inhaled and oral steroid therapy, achieving symptom relief and remission, illustrating the potential link between COVID-19 and autoimmune conditions.

This case report describes a patient with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome treated with aprepitant, a neurokinin 1 receptor antagonist. The authors suggest this case may warrant further investigation into the efficacy and safety of this drug class for managing long COVID symptoms.

Case report describing a 19-year-old woman who developed adult-onset Still's disease following SARS-CoV-2 infection, characterized by prolonged fever, joint pain, and inflammatory markers. The paper discusses the shared inflammatory features between AOSD and COVID-19 but does not study a treatment intervention or long COVID as its primary focus.

Case report of a 17-year-old with P-ANCA vasculitis developing two months after COVID-19 pneumonia, presenting with acute kidney injury and alveolar hemorrhage. Patient was treated with steroids, plasmapheresis, and cyclophosphamide, representing only the second pediatric case of this complication reported in the literature.

Case report of a hemodialyzed patient who developed tracheal stenosis as a complication of prolonged mechanical ventilation during acute COVID-19 ARDS. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 respiratory complications and post-intubation stenosis management, not long COVID syndrome.

This case report describes a 72-year-old woman with COVID-19 respiratory sequelae who underwent PET/CT imaging showing discordant uptake patterns. The paper presents a single clinical case with imaging findings but does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 68-year-old woman with tracheobronchial amyloidosis (TBA) following COVID-19 infection presenting with chronic cough. The paper documents a rare post-COVID complication and raises awareness about considering TBA as a differential diagnosis in patients with persistent respiratory symptoms after COVID-19, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing a rare complication of acute COVID-19 infection (Guillain-Barrè Syndrome with myelitis) in a single patient. The paper focuses on acute post-infectious neurological complications during active infection, not long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months later.

Case report of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (rare necrotizing lymphadenitis) occurring 1 month after COVID-19 recovery in a 24-year-old patient, with spontaneous resolution following supportive care. The paper documents a rare post-COVID complication but does not study long COVID as a primary focus and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a 42-year-old male who developed type I cryoglobulinemia with SARS-CoV-2 antibodies following COVID-19 infection, presenting with renal failure and malaise. The condition resolved spontaneously within three months, suggesting COVID-19-induced cryoglobulinemia is self-limiting.

Case report of a patient diagnosed with sarcoidosis following SARS-CoV-2 infection, exploring the potential link between COVID-19 and sarcoidosis development. The paper presents a single case without treatment intervention or comparative analysis.

A case report describing pulsed electromagnetic field treatment applied over 5 weeks (10 sessions) to a patient with post-COVID-19 fatigue syndrome. The patient showed improvements in fatigue, work ability, quality of life, and psychological well-being that were stable 6 weeks post-treatment.

Case report of a post-COVID-19 subacute cough in a middle-aged female patient, presenting diagnostic and management approaches for persistent cough following COVID-19. Discusses therapeutic options for refractory cough including diagnosis of underlying causes like upper airway cough syndrome, bronchial hyperresponsiveness, and gastroesophageal reflux.

Case report describing a single patient who developed neuropathic postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) as an autonomic neuropathy following COVID-19 infection. Discusses pathophysiologic mechanisms of orthostatic intolerance in long COVID but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

Case report of a 78-year-old COVID-19 patient with post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis treated with nintedanib in addition to methylprednisolone. The patient showed clinical improvement with nintedanib, demonstrating a potential therapeutic approach for managing post-COVID fibrosis, though further studies are needed.

Case report of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) diagnosed by bone marrow biopsy in an 81-year-old patient four weeks after COVID-19 recovery. The study documents a single case and mini-review of secondary HLH following COVID-19 infection without evaluating any treatment intervention.

This case report documents histopathological and functional recovery of lung tissue in a COVID-19 survivor who underwent lobectomy six months after critical illness requiring mechanical ventilation. Despite risk factors for fibrotic sequelae, the case shows complete pulmonary recovery, but represents only a single patient without treatment intervention.

Case report of a 49-year-old woman with Shapiro syndrome variant (paroxysmal hyperhidrosis and hypothermia) whose symptoms were exacerbated following SARS-CoV-2 infection, demonstrating long COVID-related autonomic manifestations. Treatment with increased clonidine dosing led to complete symptom resolution, providing clinical evidence for pharmacological management of post-COVID autonomic dysfunction.

A case report of a 45-year-old female with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) who experienced disease exacerbation following mild COVID-19 infection, with new heterotopic ossification and markedly elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines. The study documents post-COVID effects in FOP but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A one-year follow-up case report of a patient who developed secondary tension pneumothorax as a complication of acute COVID-19 pneumonia. The patient experienced post-acute fatigue and dyspnea for 3 months after treatment but fully resolved by one year with normal pulmonary function.

Case report of a pemphigus vulgaris patient who developed monomorphic flaccid bullae 40 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection, representing a post-COVID autoimmune manifestation. The patient responded well to treatment with prednisolone and methotrexate, with prednisolone successfully tapered during follow-up.

Case report of uveitis reactivation in a 43-year-old patient 13 years after initial onset, triggered by COVID-19 infection. While related to post-COVID manifestations, this is a single case report of an ocular complication rather than a treatment study for long COVID.

A case report documenting a 38-year-old woman who developed psychosis, HPA axis suppression, and long COVID-19 symptoms during dexamethasone treatment for acute COVID-19, with subsequent management using hydrocortisone replacement. The case illustrates a potential iatrogenic mechanism for long COVID symptoms through steroid-induced adrenal insufficiency.

Case report of a 15-year-old with myopericarditis occurring one month after COVID-19 infection, presenting with chest pain and ST-segment elevations on ECG. The paper describes diagnostic differentiation between myocardial infarction and myopericarditis as a cardiac complication of MIS-C, without evaluating any intervention or treatment.

Case report of maxillofacial osteomyelitis developing 6-8 months after COVID-19 acute infection in an Uzbek patient, demonstrating a delayed skeletal complication of COVID-19. The authors describe the protracted clinical course and treatment challenges associated with co-morbidities and metabolic/immune dysfunction.

This is a case report of a single patient with myasthenia gravis who presented with respiratory insufficiency after COVID-19 infection. While it discusses a post-COVID complication and treatment, it is a clinical case report (not a study of treatment efficacy) and does not focus on long COVID syndrome itself, but rather on a rare autoimmune complication.

Case report of a 36-year-old woman presenting with Kawasaki-like disease following COVID-19 infection, treated with pulse steroids, IVIG, and aspirin. This single case report does not constitute a treatment trial or systematic study of long COVID intervention outcomes.

A case report describing a 49-year-old male presenting with liver abscess and necrosis one month after severe COVID-19 pneumonia. The paper discusses potential pathophysiological mechanisms of liver damage in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 36-year-old patient who developed Wernicke's syndrome (thiamine deficiency) secondary to post-COVID nutritional intake and vomiting, presenting as bilateral blindness. The patient showed dramatic clinical resolution following high-dose IV thiamine supplementation, suggesting thiamine deficiency should be considered in acute-subacute vision loss with post-COVID nutritional complications.

This case report describes a 79-year-old male with post-COVID-19 hypoxemia and bilateral pneumonia who underwent pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) during a 28-day hospitalization and continued outpatient rehabilitation afterward. The patient achieved oxygen independence at 4 weeks post-rehabilitation initiation, demonstrating that early PR can prevent physical and emotional deterioration in post-COVID patients with hypoxemia.

Case report of a 34-year-old male with persistent hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia for 5+ months following COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical management with electrolyte replacement but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention or outcome.

A case report of a 27-year-old female with COVID-19 presenting with dilated cardiomyopathy and atrial/biventricular thrombi. The paper discusses coagulation abnormalities in COVID-19 and the need for post-recovery cardiac monitoring, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a single patient who developed acalculous cholecystitis 14 days after acute COVID-19 infection, hypothesizing a dysregulated immune response as the mechanism. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a clinical observation of a rare complication occurring post-COVID, not a treatment trial.

Case report of a 43-year-old female who developed acute transverse myelitis (ATM) with progression to quadriplegia ten days after COVID-19 infection. Despite treatment with steroids and plasmapheresis, she experienced complete neurological loss, illustrating a rare acute neurological complication of COVID-19 rather than a long COVID sequela.

Case report of a 52-year-old woman who developed post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis with declining lung function and underwent successful bilateral lung transplantation. The report demonstrates that lung transplantation is a viable treatment option for severe post-COVID-19 pulmonary complications.

A case report of a woman with fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome who experienced worsening symptoms following COVID-19 infection. The paper discusses the overlap between long COVID symptoms and central sensitivity syndrome but presents no treatment intervention or outcome data.

Case report of a woman who developed thyroiditis with hyperthyroidism 18 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with weight loss, tachycardia, and tremor. The paper discusses whether this was post-COVID thyroiditis or underlying autoimmune thyroiditis triggered by acute COVID infection, but does not study long COVID sequelae or treatment outcomes.

Case presentation of a 45-year-old man with fatigue, myalgia, cough, and hand stiffness occurring during the COVID-19 pandemic, progressing to interstitial lung disease. This is a single case report without treatment intervention or control group, describing a long COVID sequela but not evaluating any treatment.

A case report of a 50-year-old female with COVID-19-associated lymphocytic myocarditis presenting with persistent dyspnea, chest pain, and fatigue two weeks post-infection, found to have a pathogenic MYBPC3 variant predisposing to cardiomyopathy. The patient received multi-drug treatment including NSAIDs, furosemide, carvedilol, colchicine, and prednisone, with symptoms significantly improving over several months of continued treatment despite initial persistence.

Case report of occupational and physical therapy rehabilitation for a 61-year-old male with COVID-19-related Guillain-Barré Syndrome. Patient successfully regained independence in ambulation, strength, and self-care over 56 days of inpatient rehabilitation.

Case report of a 50-year-old nurse with persistent dysphonia and fatigue following COVID-19 infection, hypothesized to be psychogenic in origin. The patient received specialist examinations and psychological support but this is a descriptive case report without treatment evaluation or control group.

Case report of a 28-year-old woman with post-COVID chronic active myocarditis who received immunosuppressive therapy (prednisolone) with improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (21% to 45%) and reduced inflammatory markers. This is the first report evaluating immunosuppressive therapy efficacy in post-COVID myocarditis using both endomyocardial biopsy and cardiac MRI.

Case report of an 18-year-old female with recurrent psychotic episodes during COVID-19 recovery, presenting with disorganized speech, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Patient received antipsychotics, MECT, and combination hormone/antiviral therapy, with evidence of elevated IL-6/IL-10 and EEG/MRI abnormalities suggesting neuro-immuno-endocrine dysfunction.

Case report of a 41-year-old man with post-COVID myositis presenting with localized paraspinal and thigh muscle involvement despite normal creatine kinase levels. The patient was managed conservatively with analgesia and vitamin D, showing resolution without requiring immunosuppression.

A case report describing a single patient who developed focal seizures within a short timeframe after COVID-19 infection, presenting as a possible post-COVID inflammatory syndrome manifesting as new-onset focal epilepsy. The authors call for long-term follow-up studies to investigate whether COVID-19 infection increases the risk of developing epilepsy as a delayed manifestation, but this paper does not involve treatment intervention or control comparisons.

This case report describes a 62-year-old patient who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome during asymptomatic COVID-19 infection and received plasma exchange and immunoglobulin treatment. While the paper demonstrates a post-infectious neurological complication of acute COVID-19, it does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months after acute infection) and is a single case report rather than a systematic treatment trial.

Case report of a 17-year-old female with Parsonage-Turner Syndrome (idiopathic brachial plexopathy) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with severe shoulder pain and muscle inflammation. The paper documents imaging findings and excludes other etiologies, establishing a post-COVID neurological complication without testing any treatment or intervention.

A case report describing a 41-year-old female patient who developed Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) following acute COVID-19 infection, complicated by urinary dysfunction requiring catheterization and alpha-blocker therapy. While the paper documents treatment of a COVID-associated neurological complication, it focuses on acute/subacute COVID complications rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection), and as a single case report with no structured trial design, it does not meet inclusion criteria.

Case report of a 31-year-old male with SARS-CoV-2 infection presenting with chronic bilateral testicular pain followed by peripheral polyneuropathy two months later. Describes potential mechanisms including orchiepididymitis and systemic vasculitis but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

Case report of Sweet's syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis) occurring 3 weeks after severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection in a 51-year-old woman. The condition responded well to oral corticotherapy, suggesting it may represent a post-infectious skin manifestation rather than persistent long COVID sequelae.

Case report of a 58-year-old male who developed severe cardiomyopathy requiring heart transplant following COVID-19 infection and subsequent vaccination, with long COVID symptoms persisting over 8 months. While the paper documents a long COVID complication, it is a single case report without treatment intervention or control group, making it unsuitable for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

This case report describes the first durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation in a recovered COVID-19 patient who developed severe cardiomyopathy, acute myocardial infarction, and cardiogenic shock during acute infection. The patient underwent successful HeartMate 3 device placement and aneurysm repair, with successful discharge to rehabilitation, demonstrating LVAD as a feasible advanced therapy option for post-COVID cardiac complications.

This case report describes a single patient who developed Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) as a complication following severe COVID-19 with peripheral nerve injury in an ICU setting. The paper highlights the potential neurological sequelae and treatment approaches for this complication but does not evaluate a specific intervention or treatment for long COVID patients.

A case report of a young adult with chronic diarrhea and abdominal pain persisting 10 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, diagnosed with lymphocytic colitis. Treatment with budesonide achieved complete symptom resolution, suggesting a potential post-COVID GI complication.

This paper reports a single case of a patient who developed pulmonary fibrosis following successful treatment of COVID-19 pneumonia. It is a case report documenting an emerging complication of SARS-CoV-2 infection rather than a treatment study.

This is a single case report describing a post-COVID-19 myocarditis patient and the role of cardiac MRI in diagnosis. It is a descriptive case report with no treatment intervention or control group, making it ineligible for the treatment trial pipeline.

This case report describes Evans syndrome (concurrent immune-mediated thrombocytopenia and hemolytic anemia) as a late manifestation of COVID-19 in a 70-year-old male patient who presented with severe thrombocytopenia and hemolysis weeks after acute COVID-19 recovery. The patient received treatment with methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin but died two weeks after the hematological syndrome onset, highlighting Evans syndrome as a possible long-term complication of COVID-19 requiring early diagnosis and intervention.

Case report of a 5-year-old with acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) developing in the subacute phase of asymptomatic COVID-19. The paper documents imaging findings and serology results for a single pediatric case, not a long COVID study or treatment trial.

Case report describing autonomic dysfunction and POTS-like features in a long COVID patient with cardiovascular complications. This is a single case report without treatment intervention or control group.

This case report describes the first reported case of choroid plexitis caused by Burkholderia cepacia complex (BCC) occurring after severe COVID-19 in a 67-year-old woman. The patient recovered completely after prolonged multiantibiotic treatment, demonstrating a rare post-COVID neurological complication and its therapeutic management.

Autopsy report of a patient with COVID-19 and combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema, examining histopathological findings post-infection. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 pathology and lung fibrosis development during active infection rather than long COVID syndrome or treatment trials.

A case report of a 30-year-old male with cough-variant asthma whose symptoms were exacerbated by COVID-19 infection 12 months prior, with persistent dry cough lasting a year despite initial management. Long-term inhaled steroid therapy resulted in 50-60% symptom improvement, suggesting neuroinflammatory mechanisms may underlie post-COVID cough in asthmatic patients.

Case report of a 42-year-old man who developed persistent oligonecrozoospermia (low sperm count with abnormal morphology) following asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a literature review of COVID-19's effects on male reproductive health. The paper documents a single case with no treatment intervention, focusing on the condition itself rather than long COVID symptom persistence or therapeutic outcomes.

This study analyzes SARS-CoV-2 genomic mutations in an immunocompromised patient persistently infected for 4 months, examining viral evolution and drug resistance despite antiviral treatment. The research is a laboratory virology analysis rather than a clinical treatment trial, focusing on viral genome sequencing and mutation patterns rather than patient outcomes or therapeutic efficacy.

This case report describes Ayurvedic management of acute COVID-19 in a single patient, not long COVID. The paper focuses on acute infection treatment during the active phase, which falls outside the scope of long COVID research.

A case report describing a young man who developed chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) after mild COVID-19 infection, highlighting the association between COVID-19 and thrombotic complications. The paper presents clinical presentation and diagnostic findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 75-year-old COVID-19 patient with persistent oxygen dependency post-hospitalization who received Ayurvedic interventions (Rasasindura, Indukānta Ghṛita, and Suvarṇamālinīvasanta Rasa). The patient's oxygen saturation improved from 80-85% to 95% within 12 hours and oxygen support was discontinued by day 3, three weeks earlier than expected.

Case report of a 25-year-old man with post-COVID inflammatory syndrome (multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults) who presented with prolonged fever and conjunctivitis. Patient showed symptom improvement with treatment including colchicine, steroids, and intravenous immunoglobulin.

Case report of a 53-year-old patient who developed isolated ACTH deficiency and acute adrenal insufficiency after COVID-19, presenting with persistent fatigue, loss of appetite, and hyponatremia. Treatment with hydrocortisone successfully resolved symptoms, highlighting that adrenal insufficiency should be considered in differential diagnosis of prolonged post-COVID symptoms.

Case report of a 78-year-old patient with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A) following severe COVID-19, treated with high-dose methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin. The case emphasizes that MIS-A can occur in elderly patients and presents unique management challenges in this population.

Reports a fatal case of extensive gastrointestinal necrosis due to portal and mesenteric vein thrombosis occurring 6 weeks after acute COVID-19 onset. Highlights thrombotic complications as a concern during the post-acute phase of COVID-19, particularly when D-dimer levels remain elevated.

Case report of a patient with longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and MOG-IgG positivity following SARS-CoV-2 infection, representing a post-COVID neurological syndrome. The patient showed significant improvement with long-term oral corticosteroid therapy, suggesting a treatment approach for this post-COVID manifestation.

A case report of a patient with exacerbation of syringomyelia and syringobulbia symptoms following COVID-19 infection, presenting with chronic headache, pain, and neurological symptoms. Treatment with corticosteroids improved symptoms, with recurrence upon weaning and improvement upon reinitiation of the regimen.

Case report and mechanistic study of new-onset Peyronie's disease following COVID-19 infection, hypothesizing endothelial damage as the underlying cause. The study presents one patient case with comparative endothelial function testing against two control groups but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.
