This case report describes a 29-year-old patient with cholangiopathy as part of post-COVID syndrome, presenting with persistent abnormal liver tests despite treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid and cholestyramine. The case highlights the challenges of managing hepatobiliary complications in the post-COVID population.

A case report describing the use of low-field MRI (0.55 T) to visualize persistent pulmonary damage three months after COVID-19 pneumonia in a single patient. The study demonstrates that low-field MRI can detect ground-glass opacities and pulmonary changes consistent with CT, but is a diagnostic imaging case report with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

This paper reports a case of multiple sclerosis (MS) developing 2 months after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in a 36-year-old male, fulfilling diagnostic criteria for MS. It documents a potential post-COVID neurological complication but is a single case report without treatment intervention or outcome measurement.

A case report of a 34-year-old patient who developed acute limb ischemia with popliteal artery thrombosis 4 days after COVID-19 diagnosis, demonstrating prolonged hypercoagulability post-infection. The paper documents clinical management including embolectomies, anticoagulation therapy, and eventual bypass surgery, highlighting complications from post-COVID hypercoagulation.

Case report of a post-COVID-19 patient who developed opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome and encephalopathy associated with LGI-1 antibodies, treated with corticosteroids and antiepileptic medications. The patient showed clinical improvement with intravenous methylprednisolone and oral prednisolone tapering, demonstrating a steroid-responsive autoimmune neurological complication of long COVID.

Case report of a 42-year-old man who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) ten days after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with methylprednisolone and rituximab with complete clinical resolution. The paper reviews the literature on COVID-19-associated ADEM cases and discusses the post-infectious pathophysiology of this severe neurological complication.

A case report of a 72-year-old patient who developed post-COVID encephalitis 3 months after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with cognitive decline, parkinsonism, and brain MRI findings resembling SLIPPERS syndrome. While immunoglobulin therapy was attempted, this is a single case description documenting a rare neuro-inflammatory complication of long COVID rather than a systematic treatment trial.

A case report of a 69-year-old woman who developed atypical Guillain-Barré syndrome two weeks after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with severe axonal polyradiculoneuropathy requiring mechanical ventilation and corticosteroid therapy. The patient received rehabilitation management and achieved partial recovery, though persistent paraplegia remained after 2 years, highlighting Guillain-Barré syndrome as a potential disabling neurological complication of post-COVID infection.

Case report of a 78-year-old female presenting with oral lesions, dysgeusia, and odynophagia 15 days post-COVID-19, treated with topical medications including vitamin E, nystatin, acyclovir, and artificial saliva. Complete lesion repair was observed within 14 days of treatment.

Case report of a 2-year-old child with acute myeloid leukemia who developed post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) 4-6 weeks after COVID-19 infection while undergoing chemotherapy. Describes clinical presentation and management of a rare complication but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

A case report describing a long COVID patient who experienced cognitive issues, depression, and attempted suicide, illustrating neuropsychiatric complications of PASC. The paper presents a single clinical case without treatment intervention or systematic study design.

A case report describing acute onset of mania and psychosis in a patient with long COVID symptoms. The paper discusses potential etiological pathways and advocates for integrated multidisciplinary treatment but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention.

Case report of an 11-year-old with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) occurring 3 weeks after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection without respiratory symptoms. Patient received intravenous immunoglobulins and recovered well after 4 weeks of treatment.

Case report of a young man presenting with myopericarditis and multiple systemic arteriovenous thrombosis several weeks after acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents a rare manifestation of post-COVID syndrome but does not study any intervention or treatment.

A case report of a 72-year-old patient presenting with intermittent fever persisting over a month following COVID-19 pneumonia, diagnosed as long COVID after exclusion of other causes. This is a single case report describing clinical presentation and diagnostic workup rather than a systematic treatment study.

A longitudinal case report of a 26-year-old woman who developed severe psychotic symptoms days after recovery from mild COVID-19 infection, with no other identifiable etiologies. Treatment with quetiapine and lithium led to symptom resolution and functional recovery over nine months, suggesting COVID-19 can trigger new-onset psychosis as a long-term complication.

A case report describing a 33-year-old patient with post-COVID myocarditis presenting with chest pain and ST-segment elevation mimicking acute coronary syndrome. MRI imaging confirmed viral myocarditis diagnosis, highlighting diagnostic challenges in distinguishing post-COVID cardiac complications from acute coronary events.

A case report of left renal artery thrombosis occurring as a long-term complication after COVID-19 infection. The authors demonstrate successful treatment using interventional radiology to restore kidney vascularization.

A fatal case report of a 32-year-old man who developed ischemic stroke and pulmonary embolism 4 months after mild COVID-19 infection, attributed to post-COVID thromboembolic syndrome. The paper documents the clinical presentation and discusses potential mechanisms (coagulopathy, endothelial injury, immune dysregulation) but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

Case report of a 26-year-old woman who developed neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) with area postrema syndrome following COVID-19 infection, presenting with persistent nausea, vomiting, limb weakness, and urinary retention. Treatment with plasma exchange, pulse steroids, and intravenous immunoglobulin led to notable clinical improvement, demonstrating the therapeutic response to immunosuppressive interventions.

Case report of a 26-year-old woman with trigeminal neuritis following COVID-19 infection who responded well to corticosteroid treatment. Documents a neurological complication of COVID-19 with evidence of symptom persistence and treatment response.

Case report of a 45-day-old infant with pneumatocele-induced pneumothorax following probable maternal-fetal COVID-19 transmission during pregnancy. Describes radiologic findings and clinical course of a single neonate with post-infection pulmonary complications, not a treatment study.

Case report of a single rheumatoid arthritis patient on tofacitinib who developed a hypercoagulable state lasting ~6 months following COVID-19 infection. The paper documents d-dimer trends in this patient but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID symptoms.

Case report of a 70-year-old patient with post-COVID-19 organizing pneumonia successfully treated with prednisolone, with biopsy confirmation of pathology. Demonstrates corticosteroid efficacy for persistent respiratory dysfunction as a COVID-19 sequela.

Case report of a long COVID patient who developed progressive weakness, myalgias, and functional impairment following mild SARS-CoV-2 infection, with histopathological findings consistent with sclerosing lipogranuloma. Patient demonstrated significant symptom improvement with high-dose glucocorticoid treatment, suggesting COVID-19 as a possible trigger for autoimmune/inflammatory syndrome (ASIA).

A case report of a long COVID patient who experienced unexpected symptom improvement following COVID-19 vaccination, accompanied by discussion of long COVID diagnosis, treatment challenges, and clinical management in primary care. This is a single anecdotal case presented as a clinical narrative rather than a systematic study or trial.

Case report of a 61-year-old woman who developed dermatomyositis two months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with muscle weakness, rash, and inflammatory markers. The patient was treated with high-dose steroids with good clinical response, suggesting a potential post-COVID autoimmune manifestation.

This case report describes a patient who developed aortitis one month after acute COVID-19 infection, diagnosed via CT imaging and treated with high-dose corticosteroids. The patient experienced rapid clinical and biological improvement with prednisone 1 mg/kg/day, suggesting post-COVID aortitis as a rare vascular complication of COVID-19.

Case report of a 55-year-old woman who developed telogen effluvium (diffuse hair loss) three months after severe acute COVID-19 requiring ICU hospitalization and intubation. The patient received empirical supplementation with vitamin B12 and zinc, but this is a single case observation without control group or formal intervention trial structure.

Case report of a 30-year-old woman with post-COVID-19 bilateral retinal vasculitis who was initially worsened by corticosteroids but showed marked improvement following a 5-day course of Molnupiravir. The case demonstrates a potential direct therapeutic effect of the antiviral agent on post-COVID ocular complications, though larger clinical trials are needed for confirmation.

A case report of a single long COVID patient with persistent respiratory symptoms treated with Zofin, an amniotic fluid-derived extracellular vesicle product. Treatment was safe and showed improvements in respiratory function and oxygen saturation.

This paper reports a single case of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) developing two months post-COVID-19 in a normotensive patient who presented with dyspnea, cough, fatigue, and syncope. It documents a rare cardiovascular sequela but is a case report without treatment intervention or control groups.

Case report of cerebral phaeohyphomycosis caused by Neoscytalidium dimidiatum in a COVID-19 patient. Describes diagnosis and fatal outcome following delayed antifungal treatment, but does not study long COVID or any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 54-year-old male presenting with extensive purpura following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with differential diagnosis and clinical workup described. The patient recovered spontaneously with supportive care, supporting post-COVID vasculitis as a cutaneous manifestation of post-acute COVID-19 sequelae.

A case report describing remote patient monitoring (RPM) implementation for a patient with severe COVID-19 pneumonia during post-acute care at home discharge. The study demonstrates the potential of RPM technology to enable safer home-based monitoring and clinical follow-up for patients with prolonged post-COVID symptoms.

Case report of a 68-year-old patient with persistent cognitive impairment post-COVID-19, investigating anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid and brain spectroscopy findings suggestive of neuroinflammation. This is a single case report with no treatment intervention, only diagnostic/observational assessment.

Case report of a 56-year-old woman who developed anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (anti-GBM vasculitis) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with acute kidney injury and pulmonary hemorrhage. The patient received methylprednisolone, plasma exchanges, and cyclophosphamide, but progressed to end-stage renal disease.

A case report of a patient who experienced severe complications from recurrent SARS-CoV-2 infection, including acute respiratory distress syndrome and subsequent pulmonary hypertension. The paper documents clinical outcomes from reinfection but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic approach.

This paper describes a case of ANCA-associated vasculitis developing in a patient one month after mild COVID-19 infection, presenting with hemoptysis and acute renal failure. It is a single case report documenting a rare post-COVID complication, with no treatment intervention or study design applicable to clinical trial analysis.

A case report of a 46-year-old post-COVID patient with persistent dyspnea and dysphonia caused by paradoxical vocal fold movement, treated successfully with speech therapy referral. The paper demonstrates that paradoxical vocal fold movement is a treatable cause of post-COVID respiratory symptoms.

Case report of a 30-year-old long COVID patient presenting with hemoptysis caused by pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm, successfully treated with endovascular coil embolization. The patient also had pulmonary fibrosis and secondary infection, all of which were managed medically, allowing him to return to work.

Case report of a 16-year-old with long COVID presenting with digestive disorders and somatic symptoms masking anxiety-depressive features. Single case study with no treatment intervention or control group.

This paper describes the generation of an induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line derived from a long COVID patient's blood cells as a research tool. It is a methodological study establishing a cell line for future mechanistic research, not a treatment trial or intervention study.

This paper describes delayed thrombotic complications occurring in post-COVID-19 patients weeks to months after acute infection. It is excluded because it appears to be a case report or series documenting clinical observations rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

This paper describes critical illness cholangiopathy in long COVID patients through endoscopic evaluation and imaging findings. It documents a gastrointestinal complication observed in long-haulers without reporting any treatment intervention or comparative outcomes.

Case report of a 55-year-old male with post-COVID-19 Guillain-Barré syndrome treated with plasma exchange via filtration technique. Patient demonstrated clinical improvement in muscle strength and swallowing function following four plasma exchange sessions, with complete recovery of independent mobility at 6 weeks.

A case report of a long COVID patient who developed end-stage liver disease from post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy and underwent successful orthotopic liver transplantation. The patient maintained normal liver function 7 months post-transplant, establishing OLT as a potential treatment for this serious post-COVID complication.

Case report of a lung transplant recipient who developed COVID-19 with subsequent complications including thyroiditis and allograft rejection. The paper documents acute COVID-19 infection and its complications in an immunocompromised patient, not long COVID sequelae or treatment interventions for post-acute conditions.

A case report of a 61-year-old male who developed nasal polyposis following SARS-CoV-2 infection and was treated with mometasone furoate nasal spray, showing symptom improvement and polyp reduction. The study suggests post-COVID nasal polyposis may be a long COVID complication warranting further investigation into underlying mechanisms and treatment optimization.

A personal essay describing the author's long COVID experience, including onset, symptom progression, and impact on daily life. This is a first-person narrative account rather than a research study or clinical trial.

This case report documents a single patient who developed airborne allergic contact dermatitis to essential oils used during olfactory training for post-COVID-19 anosmia. It describes an adverse event associated with a common long COVID treatment intervention.

A geriatric case report of a 68-year-old female with post-COVID syndrome presenting with depression, anxiety, psychomotor slowing, and suicidal ideations 3 months after COVID-19 infection. Treatment with antidepressants and agomelatine resulted in improvements in heart rate, activity, and sleep patterns over 3 weeks, monitored via wearable devices and clinical scales.

This is a patient narrative/editorial describing one individual's experience with long COVID symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. It does not study a treatment intervention or present clinical trial data.

Case report of a patient who developed retropharyngeal abscess 3 weeks after COVID-19 infection, requiring multiple surgical washouts and multidisciplinary management. Highlights a rare infectious complication of post-COVID recovery rather than studying a specific treatment intervention.

A case report describing the experience of a young nurse in Dublin who developed long COVID symptoms after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection. The article is a personal narrative account rather than a systematic study and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a single case report of a 14-year-old girl with long COVID presenting persistent symptoms including chest pain, tachycardia, and fatigue 7 months post-infection, with detailed diagnostic workup findings. The paper documents clinical investigations and symptoms but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a single immunocompromised patient with long-term COVID-19 who developed 40 SARS-CoV-2 mutations over 318 days, including 12 mutations that escape CD8 T cell recognition. The study demonstrates viral evolution under immune pressure but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a single patient who developed secondary sclerosing cholangitis (SSC) as a complication following severe acute COVID-19 with ICU treatment. The paper documents the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and endoscopic management of this rare hepatic complication, but does not study long COVID or any intervention trial.

A case report of a 62-year-old patient with severe post-COVID neurological symptoms (ataxia, tremor, aphasia, concentration problems) treated with multimodal rehabilitation including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, psychological support, and off-label glucocorticoids and colchicine. The patient showed clear symptom reduction with this treatment approach, suggesting potential benefit of systematic rehabilitation and these pharmacological interventions in long COVID patients with neurological manifestations.

This paper describes clinical experience with interval hypoxia-hyperoxia training (IHHT/altitude training) as a therapeutic approach for post-COVID syndrome over a 2-year period at a German practice. The author reports using this method to restore individual regulatory capacity and improve functional performance in long COVID patients with prominent exhaustion symptoms.

A case report presenting two homeopathic remedies used to treat a complex long COVID patient. The paper describes the importance of correctly interpreting the healing process according to homeopathic principles to select appropriate treatment.

A personal narrative account of one patient's experience living with long COVID symptoms and their recovery journey. This is a first-person editorial/commentary piece rather than a research study with systematic data collection or treatment evaluation.

A case report series describing diverse neurologic complications of COVID-19 including strokes, neurovascular events, and post-COVID syndrome. The paper presents clinical cases rather than conducting a systematic study or testing interventions.

A case report characterizing respiratory function in long COVID patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). The paper illustrates functional respiratory abnormalities affecting lung, heart, circulation, and muscles in post-COVID syndrome but provides no treatment intervention or outcome data.

Case report of megestrol acetate treatment for post-COVID-19 fatigue in a cancer patient, showing dose-dependent improvement in quality of life. Authors call for larger randomized controlled trials to validate the approach.

A case report of a 9-year-old child who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) with prefrontal cortex involvement several weeks after COVID-19 infection. The patient presented with progressive weakness and was treated with standard ADEM management, achieving complete clinical recovery within 10 days.

Case report describing surgical therapy for major lung parenchymal damage (pulmonary cavities) as a serious long COVID complication. Reports surgical outcomes and reviews the literature on this rare but significant late complication of COVID-19 infection.

This case presentation describes the use of dupilumab (a biologic therapy) to treat severe chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) in a post-COVID syndrome patient. The paper documents the clinical outcomes of this specific intervention in addressing post-COVID-related sinus disease.

Case report of an 81-year-old male with portal vein thrombosis and acute-on-chronic cholecystitis potentially complicated by residual hypercoagulability from long COVID-19. Does not study a treatment intervention, only describes a clinical case and discusses diagnostic considerations.

Case report of a patient with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis who developed severe COVID-19 with acute respiratory deterioration and subsequent long COVID complications. This is a single case study with no treatment intervention evaluated, presenting clinical observations rather than a treatment trial.

Case report of a patient who developed cerebral venous thrombosis and massive brain hemorrhage four months after mild COVID-19 infection, attributed to post-infection hypercoagulability. This is a single case presentation describing a rare long COVID complication, not a treatment trial or systematic study of an intervention.

A case report of a 14-year-old pediatric patient who developed acute psychosis 2 weeks after COVID-19 infection, treated with chlorpromazine and showing improvement over 2 months. The paper documents clinical management of COVID-19-associated psychosis and suggests it represents post-viral sequelae warranting further investigation.

This case series reports successful treatment of a post-COVID-19 critical illness polyneuropathy patient complicated by positioning-related peripheral nerve injury using ultramicronized palmitoylethanolamide and luteolin for 6 months. The authors advocate for a larger clinical trial to validate this neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory therapy for post-COVID sequelae.

Case presentation of a 7-year-old child with atypical sensory Guillain-Barré syndrome developing after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with human immunoglobulin. The patient achieved complete resolution of neurological signs and symptoms following treatment.

A case report describing a single patient with Cryptococcus laurentii infection diagnosed in the post-COVID-19 phase. The paper focuses on a rare fungal opportunistic infection rather than long COVID management or treatment outcomes.

This paper reports a single case of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) occurring during convalescence from severe COVID-19, highlighting a delayed neurological manifestation of post-acute COVID-19. The case describes clinical presentation, imaging findings, and treatment with levetiracetam, but is a case report without intervention evaluation or control group.

Case report of a child with severe post-COVID-19 costochondritis (musculoskeletal chest inflammation) that was refractory to standard treatments (NSAIDs, steroids) but responded to colchicine therapy. The authors recommend colchicine as a treatment option for severe post-COVID-19 costochondritis in pediatric patients.

Case report of a 34-year-old man who developed severe rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury 3 weeks after COVID-19 infection, requiring hemodialysis. The patient showed clinical improvement after 2 weeks of dialysis, but this is a single case report documenting a complication rather than a treatment trial.

This case series reports rapid neurological improvements in a severe long COVID patient following a single perispinal etanercept injection, with measured benefits in fatigue, depression, cognition, and motor function sustained at 29 days. The authors propose perispinal etanercept as a promising treatment targeting neuroinflammation in long COVID and call for clinical trials.

Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with severe neuropathic corneal pain, tinnitus, and ageusia 7 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. Confocal microscopy revealed corneal microneuromas, documenting COVID-19 as a cause of neuropathic corneal pain.

A case report of physical therapy management for a 50-year-old woman with post-COVID fatigue, incorporating patient education and emotional health support over 20 biweekly sessions. The patient showed substantial improvements in exercise capacity (6MWD: 79.5→335 m), dyspnea, strength, and depression, allowing return to work.

Case report of a patient who developed central retinal vein occlusion eight months after COVID-19 pneumonia, presenting as a late thromboembolic complication. No treatment intervention is tested; this is a clinical observation of disease pathology rather than a treatment study.

Case report of a 42-year-old patient who developed a rare combination of acute cerebellitis, transverse myelitis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome two weeks after COVID-19 infection. The patient recovered well after corticosteroid treatment, achieving complete functional recovery (modified Rankin Scale score 0) by day seven of hospitalization.

Case report of focal myopericarditis occurring post-COVID infection in a recovered patient, presenting with ST elevation on ECG. The paper discusses cardiac complications after COVID-19 and the role of cardiac magnetic resonance and biomarkers in diagnosis, but does not study any treatment intervention.

A case study of a 55-year-old female with long COVID who received 16 manual therapy treatments aimed at aiding glymphatic drainage. The patient showed marked symptom improvement on the PFRS scale, with reductions in somatic symptoms, fatigue, and cognitive impairment.

Case report of a patient with bulimia nervosa who experienced COVID-19-related smell and taste disorders. The paper highlights the potential impact of long-term olfactory and gustatory dysfunction on eating disorder symptoms and suggests need for reassessment of ED treatment in affected patients.

Case report of post-acute physical therapy for a 56-year-old male recovering from critical COVID-19 requiring ICU admission and mechanical ventilation. The patient showed significant functional improvements (600% increase in chair stand test, 69.5% improvement in 6-minute walk distance) during 16 days of inpatient physical therapy, though exertional dyspnea remained limiting.

Case report of severe pigeon paramyxovirus 1 infection in a 66-year-old man with probable post-COVID-19 syndrome, complicated by residual SARS-CoV-2 detection. The case highlights increased risk of severe viral infection in immunocompromised long COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational case study evaluates acupuncture as a treatment for long-COVID syndrome in a single 46-year-old patient. The patient showed reduced symptoms and signs of long COVID following acupuncture treatment, supporting further research into acupuncture and Traditional Chinese Medicine modalities for long COVID.

A case report of a 50-year-old woman with post-COVID syndrome (8 months of fatigue, chest pressure, palpitations, and anosmia) who received 7 sessions of acupuncture combined with symptom-titrated physical activity. The patient's symptoms resolved after treatment and she resumed normal exercise, though the independent effects of acupuncture versus concurrent physical therapy remain unclear.

A case report describing a 73-year-old male patient with long COVID who underwent two prolonged water-only fasting interventions with subsequent refeeding. The patient achieved sustained improvements in long COVID symptoms following these interventions.

Case report evaluating transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) for post-COVID severe dyspnea in a single patient. One TEAS session relieved dyspnea with no recurrence at 6-month follow-up, suggesting TEAS may be a safe and effective treatment option.

This case report describes a long-haul COVID patient who practiced Tai Chi and Qigong 3-4 times weekly for 30 minutes and experienced improvements in resting heart rate, weight, and oxygen saturation (83% to 96%). The authors propose Tai Chi and Qigong as a low-cost, accessible intervention to improve lung function and quality of life in long COVID patients.

A detailed case report of a single patient with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 who developed anosmia, ageusia, and delayed-onset panic and depression, with neuropsychological testing before and after infection. The paper documents natural recovery of chemosensory and psychiatric symptoms over 8 months but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 45-year-old patient who survived severe COVID-19 with ARDS and cerebral microbleeds, followed longitudinally with neuropsychological testing at 4 weeks and 8 months post-extubation. While the case demonstrates cognitive recovery over time with improving outcomes, this is an uncontrolled single case report without any intervention or treatment being tested.

A case study of a 57-year-old male with severe COVID-19 (42 days on mechanical ventilation) evaluated ~15 months post-discharge for neurocognitive and psychological sequelae. Neuropsychological testing revealed declines in motor function, memory, executive function, and emotional dysregulation consistent with long-COVID post-intensive care syndrome, but no treatment intervention was tested.

A neuropsychological case study of a 14-year-old with long COVID presenting with cognitive deficits (attention, processing speed, memory) and emotional/physical symptoms, with brain MRI showing white matter lesions. The study documents clinical presentation and neuropsychological testing results but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 61-year-old woman who developed purulent pericarditis caused by methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus one month after COVID-19 pneumonia. The patient was treated with antibiotics (cloxacillin) for 6 weeks and fully recovered, suggesting a potential long-COVID cardiac complication.

Case report of a pregnant woman with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) who developed postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and orthostatic hypotension. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnostic evaluation but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This paper presents a case report of a 74-year-old patient who developed post-COVID myocarditis with progressive cardiac fibrosis and systolic dysfunction over 3 years following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The report documents clinical presentation, multimodal cardiac imaging findings, and pharmacological heart failure management, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

This paper proposes smartwatch-derived ECG metrics, specifically S-/R-wave amplitude ratio, as a non-invasive biomarker for tracking autonomic dysfunction in long COVID patients. The work focuses on diagnostic tool development and disease monitoring rather than testing a treatment intervention.

This paper describes a case of unilateral phrenic nerve palsy discovered via cardiopulmonary exercise testing in a 28-year-old woman with long-COVID-19 syndrome presenting with persistent exertional dyspnea. It is a single case report highlighting the importance of recognizing phrenic nerve involvement in unexplained dyspnea in long COVID patients, rather than a treatment study.

This case study describes an 80-year-old patient with post-COVID persistent atrial fibrillation-induced heart failure treated with empagliflozin added to optimized therapy over 9 months. Heart rate variability analysis demonstrated enhanced parasympathetic modulation and reduced sympathetic tone during treatment, with concurrent improvements in ejection fraction from 40% to 44%.

Case report of a 16-year-old COVID-19 survivor who developed dilated cardiomyopathy one month post-infection, presenting with fatigue and severely reduced ejection fraction (22%). The patient was treated with cardiac medications (ARB, beta-blocker, diuretics, anticoagulant, and metabolic modulator) and achieved stable recovery over three months.

Case report of a 31-year-old female with post-COVID PVC bigeminy (persistent palpitations and chest discomfort 3 months after acute infection) treated with electrophysiology study and catheter ablation. Ablation successfully eliminated the PVCs, demonstrating a treatment approach for this rare cardiac complication of long COVID.

Case report of a 40-year-old man who developed Mobitz type I atrioventricular block 8 weeks after asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, treated with NSAIDs and corticosteroids. At 3-month follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic with resolution of high-degree AVB, suggesting potential reversibility of COVID-19-related conduction abnormalities with anti-inflammatory therapy.

Case report of a 78-year-old woman who developed osteonecrosis of the knee one month after COVID-19 infection, with suspected association to hypercoagulability or corticosteroid use. Treatment included pain management and home exercises while awaiting surgical intervention.

A case report of a 61-year-old man who developed delayed-onset organizing pneumonia as a manifestation of post-acute COVID-19 syndrome following perioperative complications after lung lobectomy. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by a second course with cyclosporine A addition, achieving substantial radiological improvement by postoperative day 104.

Case report of a 15-year-old with PIMS-TS (pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2) presenting as terminal ileitis requiring surgical resection. While the patient had post-COVID inflammatory complications, this is a single case report of acute/subacute post-infection syndrome, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-to-months post-infection), and does not study a treatment intervention.

This paper reports a case study of a soldier in a deployed setting who developed multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) following SARS-CoV-2 infection. It is a single case report documenting clinical presentation and disease progression, not a treatment trial or systematic study of an intervention.

Descriptive case report documenting prolonged and late-onset symptoms of COVID-19, including dyspnea, fatigue, cough, dysosmia, and alopecia occurring weeks to months after symptom onset. No treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.

A case report of a 36-year-old long COVID patient treated with 10 sessions of Electro-Magnetic Brain Pulse (EMBP), a personalized transcranial magnetic stimulation protocol guided by EEG. The patient showed improvements in mood, anosmia, brain fog, and cognitive function (27% increase in cognitive test scores), with dyspnea decreasing by 11% and EEG shifts from delta to synchronized alpha waves.

Case report of a 67-year-old male with long-term COVID-19 who developed Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), diagnosed via BAL and immunofluorescence testing. Patient was treated with cotrimoxazole and supportive care with gradual resolution of hypoxia, highlighting the need to consider PCP in long COVID patients even without conventional risk factors.

A physician-patient perspective case discussion of Long COVID with autonomic dysfunction and ME/CFS, highlighting immunologic and mechanistic factors. Discusses complexities in patient care, public health education, and the need for more effective therapies, but does not report original research or treatment outcomes.

This case report describes the rehabilitation course of the first documented post-bilateral lung transplant patient for COVID-19 in the United States, a 28-year-old woman with severe long COVID requiring transplantation. Through interdisciplinary rehabilitation, the patient achieved significant functional improvements in strength, balance, endurance, and mobility, enabling safe discharge home.

A case report describing physical therapist management of a 37-year-old woman with post-COVID syndrome presenting with dyspnea, headaches, and cognitive fog. After 8 weeks of biweekly physical therapy including aerobic training, strengthening, and breathing techniques, the patient showed improvements in exercise capacity (6-minute walk distance increased by 199 m) and muscle strength, though cognitive and emotional symptoms persisted.

Case report of an 83-year-old patient with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viral isolation by culture 111 days post-acute infection, despite clinical recovery. Documents evidence of infectious virus in nasopharyngeal specimens and development of neutralizing antibodies, suggesting chronic infection may occur in long-haulers without active transmission.

This paper reports a single case of vocal fold paresis (right vocal cord paresis with incomplete abduction) occurring 11 weeks after COVID-19 infection in a 47-year-old female. The patient experienced gradual improvement without corticosteroid treatment, reaching complete remission in 4 weeks, highlighting a rare post-COVID neurological complication.

Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with intracranial microangiopathy and persistent myalgia 12 months post-infection. The authors describe MRI findings and discuss the possibility of overlooked microangiopathy cases in long COVID patients, but this is a single case presentation rather than a treatment intervention study.

Case report of a healthcare worker who developed severe myocarditis during acute COVID-19 infection (not long COVID). The patient was treated with high-dose prednisolone and recovered with normalization of cardiac function on follow-up imaging.

This brief journal article reports an association between diaphragmatic weakness, peripheral muscle weakness, and anosmia in long-COVID patients. It is a short communication/editorial piece rather than a primary research study with treatment outcomes.

This is a case report of a single patient who developed reactive arthritis and urticarial rash during acute COVID-19 infection (April 2020), treated with glucocorticoids with full resolution by two-month follow-up. The paper describes acute post-infectious complications of COVID-19 during active infection, not persistent long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months after acute illness.

A case report describing a single patient who developed self-limiting symmetrical polyarthritis five weeks after laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with oral prednisolone and NSAIDs, achieving remission within six weeks with normalized inflammatory markers.

Case report of a 16-year-old who developed reactive arthritis with rash and polyarthralgia 10 days after COVID-19 infection. Symptoms resolved spontaneously within 2 weeks with no treatment intervention studied.

Case report of a long COVID patient who developed multiple autoantibodies post-infection and received a trial of prednisolone therapy. The steroids showed no significant impact on symptoms or autoantibody titers, and the patient remained under long COVID clinical management with gradual improvement in autoantibody levels over two years.

Case report of aortic thrombosis with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies in a COVID-19 patient. Describes clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and anticoagulation management but does not study long COVID or any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 47-year-old female with long COVID syndrome who experienced recurrent ACE-inhibitor induced angioedema while taking lisinopril. The paper discusses the proposed mechanism linking SARS-CoV-2 ACE2 receptor downregulation to increased angioedema risk in ACE inhibitor users, based on a single patient case with symptom resolution after drug discontinuation.

Case report of a 61-year-old rheumatoid arthritis patient with persistent COVID-19 pneumonia lasting over 62 days despite initial treatment, complicated by Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Extended nirmatrelvir/ritonavir therapy resulted in significant clinical and radiological improvement, suggesting potential benefit of prolonged antiviral treatment in immunocompromised patients with chronic COVID-19.

Case report of a 13-year-old with post-COVID hypersomnolence and sleep disorders treated with a combination of methylphenidate and sodium oxybate. Treatment resulted in resolution of excessive daytime sleepiness and return to normal functioning.

Case report of a 16-year-old with post-COVID hypersomnia and excessive daytime sleepiness following two COVID-19 infections, characterized by reduced sleep latency on MSLT and elevated ESS scores. Patient was treated sequentially with Adderall (unsuccessful) and Modafinil (successful), with ESS score improving from 22 to 3 at follow-up, demonstrating treatment response in COVID-associated sleep disorder.

A case report of heterotopic ossification (abnormal bone formation) in the shoulder of a patient who required ICU mechanical ventilation during acute COVID-19 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation, imaging findings, and management with physiotherapy and NSAIDs, but does not study long COVID sequelae or test any intervention.

This case report describes a patient who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome involving bilateral facial nerves and lower extremities following COVID-19 infection. It is a single case report documenting a post-COVID neurological complication without any treatment intervention or controlled study design.

A case report of a 54-year-old male presenting with late-onset idiopathic hypersomnia two years after COVID-19 infection, with cognitive difficulties and normal diagnostic workup. The authors discuss potential mechanisms linking post-COVID syndrome to hypersomnia and review four previously reported cases of primary hypersomnias following COVID-19.

This case report describes a 17-year-old female with idiopathic hypersomnia whose condition progressed to narcolepsy type 1 with cataplexy following COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with sodium oxybate (Xywav) with reported improvement in daytime sleepiness and complete resolution of cataplexy symptoms.

Case report of a pregnant patient who developed acute motor axonal neuropathy (AMAN) following COVID-19 infection, resulting in premature delivery and prolonged recovery. This is a single case report documenting a post-COVID neurological complication without intervention or treatment evaluation.

Case report of a 12-year-old presenting with stroke and left ventricular apical thrombus during acute COVID-19 infection. Describes acute complications requiring surgical intervention; does not address long COVID or any treatment trial.

A case report of MIS-A development in a fully vaccinated patient four weeks after hospitalization for acute COVID-19 pneumonia. The patient presented with multi-organ inflammation, pulmonary embolism, and myocarditis, ultimately resulting in death despite treatment.

Case report of a 28-year-old female presenting with granulomatous pleuritis one year after COVID-19 infection, diagnosed via bronchoscopy and biopsy. The paper documents a rare post-COVID inflammatory complication but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a first-person narrative account by an emergency physician describing her experience with long COVID symptoms following a breakthrough infection. The piece is a personal clinical observation and editorial commentary published in Emergency Medicine News, not a research study testing or evaluating any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 21-year-old male with MIS-A (Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Adults) who developed bilateral cerebral strokes and adrenal hemorrhage, requiring intensive care and ultimately fatal. This is a single case report describing acute COVID-19 complications and post-infectious manifestations, not long COVID (which involves chronic symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

This case report describes physical therapy management of a 70-year-old long COVID patient using manual therapy techniques (suboccipital release, cervical paraspinal release, rib raising) combined with diaphragmatic breathing exercises to address autonomic nervous system dysfunction. After 11 sessions over 20 weeks, the patient demonstrated functional improvement and decreased symptoms of fatigue and shortness of breath.

A case report of a 31-year-old male who developed sicca syndrome (dry eyes and dry mouth) 3 months after COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with artificial tears, corticosteroid drops, and increased water intake, showing improvement within 15 days.

A case study of a 31-year-old physician with post-COVID auditory processing disorder and brain fog who underwent auditory training following the Buffalo Model. The patient showed improvement in hearing handicap scores and symptom resolution after 12 treatment sessions.

This paper describes a single case of Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Adults (MIS-A) occurring one month after COVID-19 infection, presenting with encephalopathy, multi-organ dysfunction, and cardiac/renal failure. While the patient had a prior COVID-19 infection, the clinical focus is on acute MIS-A presentation and management during the acute phase, not on long-term post-COVID symptoms or interventions for long COVID.

Case report of a 43-year-old female with long COVID treated with enoxaparin (low molecular weight heparin) at 20 mg/day subcutaneously for 8 weeks. Patient showed marked improvement in functional capacity (FUNCAP 3.3→5.07), activity levels, postexertional malaise, and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome with no adverse events, supporting further investigation of anticoagulation therapy for long COVID-related hypercoagulation and microclots.

Case report describing the beneficial effects of quetiapine treatment on sleep, anxiety, depression, and myalgia symptoms in a patient with post-COVID-19 condition. The study demonstrates symptomatic improvement with this antipsychotic medication in a long COVID patient.

Case report of posterior glottic stenosis as a complication following prolonged intubation in a COVID-19 patient during acute infection. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 respiratory management and intubation complications, not on long COVID or its treatment.

Case report of a 4-year-old child with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) associated with acute COVID-19, featuring Kawasaki-like shock and neurologic manifestations. The paper documents acute post-infectious complications during active infection rather than long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months after infection.

A case report describing a patient-centered management approach for post-COVID-19 dysautonomia symptoms during sports and exercise. The treatment regimen combined ivabradine and low-dose metoprolol on an exertional sliding scale, successfully managing symptoms to acceptable levels for work and recreation.

This case report describes exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation in a post-COVID-19 patient with pulmonary fibrosis who was oxygen-dependent following acute infection. The patient successfully discontinued oxygen supplementation and completed a 10-session rehabilitation program without activity limitations.

A case report of a 46-year-old woman who developed quadrantanopia from an occipital stroke weeks after COVID-19 infection, with elevated D-dimers suggesting thrombotic complications. The authors highlight the need to consider vascular-ischemic risks during long COVID recovery, particularly in patients with neurologic symptoms and elevated coagulation markers.

Case report of a 54-year-old male with post-COVID-19 syndrome treated with subanesthetic doses of local anesthetic injections (procaine) administered to the stellate ganglion, sphenopalatine ganglion, and clinically relevant points over 3 months. The patient achieved complete symptom resolution with significant improvement in SF-36 health survey scores across all domains.

Case report of a young patient with hyperadrenergic POTS secondary to long COVID who achieved complete remission with histamine blocker treatment. Documents clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and therapeutic response to pharmacological intervention in a long COVID patient with severe orthostatic intolerance.

Case report of a 68-year-old male with diffuse bladder calcification as a long-term sequela of severe COVID-19, presenting with persistent lower urinary tract symptoms. The patient underwent transurethral removal of mucosal calcification with lithotripsy, resulting in symptom improvement and no recurrence on follow-up.

A case report of a 43-year-old male who developed task-specific facial dystonia 2 weeks after COVID-19 infection, presenting with facial grimacing while chewing and spasms during nasal breathing. The patient showed significant symptom improvement following botulinum toxin injections to the affected facial muscles after failing conservative pharmacological treatments.

This paper reports on liraglutide (a GLP-1 agonist) as a treatment for post-COVID fatigue syndrome and executive function deficits in type 2 diabetic patients. The study presents clinical outcomes from cases treated with liraglutide for post-COVID symptoms.

A CARE-compliant case report of an 84-year-old female with post-COVID adjustment disorder treated with integrative personalized medicine care combining conventional Western drugs, herbal medicine, acupuncture, and moxibustion. Treatment resulted in significant improvements in depression, insomnia, palpitations, dyspepsia, and quality of life, with the patient able to taper off antidepressant medication.

Case report of a 67-year-old woman who developed chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) following COVID-19 infection and/or vaccination, with one relapse over 11 months. The patient was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and responded to treatment in both episodes.

A case report of an adolescent with long COVID-associated POTS who received weekly epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT) for 120 days and showed marked clinical improvement including reduced fatigue, improved orthostatic tolerance, and resumed normal activities. The case suggests EAT may offer a nonpharmacological treatment option by addressing chronic epipharyngeal inflammation underlying autonomic dysfunction in long COVID.

Case report of a 68-year-old female who developed systemic sclerosis with anti-Ro 52 and anti-centromere antibodies 1 month after COVID-19 infection, presenting with dyspnea, muscle weakness, and interstitial lung disease. Patient was treated with azathioprine and prednisolone and achieved clinical stability with monthly follow-ups.

This paper describes a case of an 80-year-old patient who developed platypnea-orthodeoxia syndrome (dyspnea and desaturation when upright) following moderate-severe COVID-19 infection. While it addresses a long COVID sequela, it is a single case report with no treatment intervention or control group, making it ineligible as a treatment trial.

Case report of a 15-year-old girl who developed Wernicke encephalopathy secondary to severe anosmia and dysgeusia following COVID-19 infection, resulting in malnutrition and thiamine deficiency. Treatment with parenteral thiamine replacement resulted in significant neurological improvement, highlighting an important long-term neurological sequela of COVID-19.

Case report of bilateral acute macular neuroretinopathy (AMN) occurring 3 weeks post-COVID-19 infection in a 24-year-old woman, with clear temporal relationship to acute infection. Patient was treated with oral prednisolone and showed improvement in central scotoma on follow-up, supporting a causal link between COVID-19 and AMN.

Case report of a pediatric patient with persistent abdominal pain and chronic colonic inflammation 3 months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, with detection of viral nucleocapsid protein in intestinal epithelium. The paper documents clinical manifestations and pathological findings but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A case series describing a 3-week pulmonary telerehabilitation program delivered to a postacute COVID-19 patient with persistent dyspnea and fatigue in Malawi. The patient showed clinically significant improvements in respiratory severity scores and functional status, including return to work.

This case report describes a 73-year-old male with Parkinson disease who developed severe and prolonged oropharyngeal dysphagia persisting 4 months after COVID-19 infection, despite receiving swallowing therapy. The authors speculate on neurological mechanisms linking COVID-19 to dysphagia and recommend clinical vigilance for aspiration risk in COVID-19 patients with Parkinson disease.

This case report describes a 30-year-old woman who developed post-COVID-19 Rasmussen encephalitis, a rare autoimmune neurological disorder causing unilateral brain inflammation and drug-resistant seizures. Although the case illustrates post-COVID neurological complications, it is a single case report describing clinical presentation and outcomes rather than a treatment trial or intervention study.

A case report of a 55-year-old patient with early-onset Alzheimer disease presenting with agitation during acute COVID-19 infection, treated with pharmacologic optimization (clonidine and prazosin). The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 symptom management rather than long COVID sequelae.

A nursing care article presenting a single case of a long COVID patient who developed Brugada syndrome post-cardiac arrest. The paper discusses assessment and care of this individual patient rather than evaluating a treatment intervention or conducting a systematic study.

This paper reports a case of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaws (MRONJ) in a post-COVID-19 patient treated with tocilizumab and dexamethasone. While the patient received tocilizumab during acute COVID-19 treatment, the focus is on a dental complication rather than long COVID intervention outcomes.

Single case report of a long COVID patient presenting with severe insomnia and reduced thalamic blood flow on SPECT imaging. This is a descriptive case study with no intervention or treatment evaluation, serving primarily as a clinical observation of neuroimaging findings rather than a treatment trial.

A case report describing a 48-year-old patient who developed persistent dysgeusia and hypoalgesia in the lower legs, hands, and cheeks 7 months after COVID-19 infection. The study documents clinical examination findings, quantitative sensory testing, and skin biopsy results showing reduced intraepidermal nerve fiber density, with partial symptom improvement at 5-month follow-up.

This piece describes a COVID-19 survivor's experience of illness and hospitalization in early 2020. It is a narrative account or editorial commentary rather than an empirical research study or treatment trial.

Case report of a 47-year-old man presenting with paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) 2 months post-COVID-19, followed by giant cell arteritis-like symptoms treated with high-dose steroids. The patient experienced rapid resolution of symptoms with steroid treatment, representing the first documented case implicating COVID-19 in both small and large vessel vasculitis in the ophthalmic setting.

This is a single-subject case report documenting changes in P-selectin-mediated leukocyte adhesion in a long-COVID patient before and after symptom resolution. The paper is mechanistic/observational research studying disease biology rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

Case report describing a patient who developed Peyronie's disease following COVID-19 infection, with evidence of endothelial dysfunction. The paper documents a potential long COVID sequela but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report and literature review of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with serositis and lymphopenia. Reviews 10 similar cases to identify common features but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 67-year-old woman who developed bilateral aspergillomas ten months after severe COVID-19 pneumonitis requiring mechanical ventilation. The paper raises awareness of aspergilloma as a long-term pulmonary complication in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 44-year-old man who developed bipolar disorder with manic and depressive episodes during acute COVID-19 infection, treated with mood stabilizers. Does not study long COVID (persistent post-infection syndrome) but rather acute psychiatric complications during active infection.

Case report of a patient who developed refractory status epilepticus 6 weeks after COVID-19 recovery, with elevated inflammatory markers and hippocampal atrophy. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a clinical observation of post-COVID neurological complications.

A case report documenting persistent cyanosis and thrombotic vasculopathy in a single patient's toes for 22 months following presumed SARS-CoV-2 exposure. Histopathology reveals capillary thrombosis and pernio-like inflammation, representing the first biopsy-confirmed case of long COVID-related toe pathology.

Case report of a 51-year-old female with Miller-Fisher syndrome (MFS) occurring two weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with IV immunoglobulin. While describing a post-infectious neurological complication, this is a single case report of an acute post-COVID neurological syndrome, not a long COVID study involving persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection.

This paper reports a case of a patient developing antibody-negative type 1 diabetes after COVID-19 recovery and presents in vitro experimental evidence that SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor binding domain binds to human islet cells. The work proposes a potential mechanism linking SARS-CoV-2 infection to type 1 diabetes but does not study long COVID (persistent post-COVID symptoms) or test any treatment intervention.

This case report describes a 70-year-old male patient who developed severe cerebellar ataxia 3 weeks after recovery from mild COVID-19. The patient responded well to pulse methylprednisolone therapy, demonstrating a treatment approach for post-infectious neurological complications following COVID-19.

A case report of a 58-year-old man who developed organizing pneumonia as a late complication 2 months after acute COVID-19 hospitalization, treated with prednisolone. The patient showed marked clinical and radiological improvement with corticosteroid therapy, suggesting corticosteroids may be effective for this post-COVID respiratory manifestation.

Case report of a young woman presenting with new-onset refractory status epilepticus (NORSE) as an early manifestation of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) following mild COVID-19 infection. The patient showed significant clinical recovery following treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin, expanding the known clinical spectrum of post-COVID-19 complications.

Case report of erythema gyratum repens (a rare skin condition) occurring after COVID-19 infection in a patient. The paper documents a dermatological manifestation but does not study long COVID or any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 25-year-old male who developed narcolepsy type II following COVID-19 infection, treated with intravenous high-dose corticosteroid pulse therapy (methylprednisolone). The patient experienced immediate and sustained remission of narcoleptic symptoms with normalized sleep latencies and improved alertness at 4-month follow-up, suggesting immunosuppressive therapy may be effective for post-COVID narcolepsy.

Case report of acute psychosis onset in a young patient following COVID-19 pneumonia, with EEG findings complicated by antipsychotic medication use. Describes a single case presentation rather than a treatment trial or systematic study.

This letter describes ultrastructural evidence of SARS-CoV-2 infection in hair follicles from a single patient with early-onset COVID-19 effluvium (hair loss occurring <30 days after acute infection). The study investigates the mechanism of post-COVID hair loss through microscopic examination rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Case report of a single patient who developed autoimmune hepatitis one month after acute COVID-19 infection. While the paper describes treatment with prednisone, it is a single case report of an acute post-infection complication, not a long COVID study (which requires persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection in a cohort of patients).

This case report describes a long COVID patient who developed post-surgical pyoderma gangrenosum after reduction mammoplasty and was successfully treated with infliximab, mycophenolic acid, and corticosteroids. The case highlights lingering systemic proinflammatory effects of COVID-19 that may increase risk of autoimmune complications following surgery.

Case report of a 14-year-old boy with long COVID presenting as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and post-exertional malaise. The patient showed clinical improvement with activity restriction and symptom management during hospitalization, suggesting activity restriction as a potential management strategy for severe ME/CFS exacerbation in long COVID patients.

A case report of a 27-year-old female presenting with persistent erythematous candidiasis and xerostomia as sequelae following SARS-CoV-2 infection, diagnosed 3 months post-infection. The patient received treatment with nystatin mouthwash and sialogogues, though candidiasis persisted during the 8-month follow-up, highlighting the challenge of managing post-COVID oral complications.

A case report of a post-acute COVID-19 patient with severe gastrointestinal symptoms who received a 2-month high-fiber nutritional formula designed to modulate gut microbiota. The intervention significantly alleviated symptoms including loss of appetite, palpitation, and anxiety, with corresponding improvements in serum lipid profile, insulin, and leptin levels, along with structural changes in the patient's gut microbiota.

A case report of a patient with mildly symptomatic COVID-19 who redeveloped symptoms and tested PCR-positive >4 weeks after initial infection, with negative antibody testing 2 months later. The case highlights potential reinfection and prolonged viral shedding patterns but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of an 11-year-old boy with PIMS-TS (Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome Temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2) treated with immunoglobulins, corticosteroids, and aspirin. This paper describes an acute post-viral inflammatory syndrome occurring during active/recent infection, not long COVID (which manifests weeks to months post-infection), and is a single case report rather than a systematic study.

This case report describes nucleocapsid protein accumulation in kidney tubular epithelium of a post-COVID-19 patient, suggesting persistent viral antigen after infection recovery. The study is a single case observation without intervention or treatment evaluation.

Case report of a 17-year-old with severe acute COVID-19 who developed petechial rash, peripheral neuropathy, and respiratory distress two months after discharge. Describes a single case observation of post-COVID manifestations without treatment intervention or comparative analysis.

Case report of a single patient who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents a rare neurological complication occurring during the acute infection phase rather than as a long COVID sequela.

A case report describing a 28-year-old woman with long COVID presenting with persistent breathlessness, fatigue, chest pain, cognitive deficits, and myalgia weeks after acute COVID-19 infection. The paper is a clinical case study with no treatment intervention or comparative data.

A case report describing delayed onset Guillain-Barré syndrome in a patient 53 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with progressive demyelinating neuropathy requiring ventilatory support. This is a single case observation with no treatment intervention, control group, or trial design.

Case report of a 45-year-old woman who developed severe acquired hypertriglyceridemia with reduced lipoprotein lipase activity following COVID-19 infection. Treatment with fibrates and dietary modification improved symptoms and triglyceride levels, with partial recovery of lipoprotein lipase activity at 5-month follow-up.

Case report of a 79-year-old woman with pre-existing idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis who experienced severe progression following COVID-19 infection. The paper documents the clinical course but does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a patient who developed acute-onset CIDP with three relapses following COVID-19 infection and ChAdOx1 vaccination. The paper documents clinical presentation and timeline but does not study a treatment intervention or outcomes in long COVID patients.

Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with cognitive impairment and executive dysfunction, diagnosed via neuropsychological testing. Patient showed response to empirical ADHD medication treatment with repeat testing 1 year later documenting continued executive functioning deficits.

Case report of a single long COVID patient presenting with persistent neurological and systemic symptoms 9 months post-infection, including elevated inflammatory markers and hypometabolism on PET imaging. The paper documents clinical presentation and diagnostic findings but does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report describing a woman presenting with cardiac conduction abnormalities (left bundle branch block, septal flash) and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome in the context of long COVID-19. The paper documents clinical findings and calls for future research but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment or intervention.

Case report of a 7-year-old girl who developed transient myasthenia gravis following recovery from MIS-C (multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children) associated with COVID-19. The patient responded to treatment with pyridostigmine, corticosteroids, and methotrexate, with complete resolution of ocular signs.

Case report of a woman with recurrent nodular episcleritis recurring nine times over 3 years following COVID-19 infection, attributed to long COVID after exclusion of other causes. No treatment trial or controlled intervention—documents clinical presentation and diagnostic workup only.

Case report of a woman presenting with encephalomyeloradiculitis during acute COVID-19 infection, featuring ascending weakness, sensory changes, and spinal cord demyelination. This describes an acute neurological complication occurring during active infection rather than long COVID sequelae weeks to months post-infection.

Case report describing a long COVID patient with persistent orthostatic tachycardia refractory to non-pharmacological management, successfully treated with ivabradine. The patient gradually improved her exercise tolerance and eventually discontinued ivabradine after several months.

This case report describes a patient with persistent post-COVID headache who was treated with botulinum toxin infiltration after poor response to pharmacological therapy. The patient showed improvement from VAS 8 to VAS 3 within one week of treatment, with sustained benefit at one month follow-up.

Case report of a 31-year-old female with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome presenting with parosmia, dysgeusia, and tongue feature changes that resolved completely after one month. Paper describes clinical presentation and natural resolution of symptoms without documenting any intervention or treatment.

This case study examines vascular and skeletal muscle function changes in a single participant during the presymptomatic phase of COVID-19 infection, finding widespread physiological impairment prior to symptom onset. The participant developed long COVID symptoms (fatigue, cough) 2.5 months post-diagnosis, but the paper does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 90-year-old patient who developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) with seizures one week after recovery from acute severe COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with supportive care and anticonvulsants, with resolution confirmed on follow-up MRI four months later.

Case report of a teenager who developed Graves' disease and psoriasis vulgaris after COVID-19 infection, suggesting long COVID can trigger autoimmune and dermatologic conditions. The paper documents clinical presentation and recommends including thyroid evaluation in long COVID syndrome assessment, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing visual snow-like symptoms and posterior uveitis in a patient following COVID-19 infection. Authors hypothesize COVID-19 may trigger transient autoimmune ocular inflammation, though the mechanism and treatment implications remain unclear.

A case report of COVID-induced pancytopenia that emerged months after acute infection, demonstrating a long COVID hematologic manifestation. The patient showed initial response to IVIG and steroids but developed persistent neutropenia, illustrating treatment outcomes in this long COVID complication.

A case report describing a 58-year-old woman presenting with illness anxiety disorder (IAD) alongside long COVID symptoms including cognitive deficits, breathlessness, fatigue, and anosmia. The paper discusses diagnostic challenges in differentiating between IAD and long COVID-19 but does not report outcomes from any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 26-year-old male presenting with acute lymphocytic myocarditis 1 month post-COVID-19 infection, characterized by fatigue, palpitations, and severely reduced left ventricular function. The patient received immunosuppressive therapy with steroids and azathioprine, showing partial improvement in cardiac function after 3 months.

This case report describes a 14-year-old boy who developed persistent, treatment-resistant immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) secondary to asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, with relapsing symptoms over 21 months despite immunosuppressive therapy. The case highlights long-term immune complications of COVID-19 and the need for better understanding of pathophysiology in post-COVID sequelae.

Case report of a patient with primary Sjögren's syndrome who developed persistent lung abnormalities (ground glass opacity, restrictive deficit) following acute COVID-19 pneumonia, with diagnostic uncertainty between COVID-19 sequelae and pSS-related ILD. The patient was monitored over 2 years with a 'wait and see' approach and showed spontaneous improvement, with almost complete radiologic resolution suggesting long-COVID lung manifestations.

Case report of a 75-year-old woman who developed polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) 2 weeks after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with severe musculoskeletal pain and stiffness in neck and shoulders. Patient was treated with prednisone 25 mg/day with progressive tapering and achieved complete recovery at 6-month follow-up, supporting PMR as a post-COVID autoimmune manifestation.

Case report describing the development and use of a low-cost 3D-printed respiratory muscle strength trainer device (RMSTD) for a long COVID patient with respiratory muscle weakness. The patient showed significant improvement, achieving full weaning from supplemental oxygen by day 5 and increasing 6-minute walk test distance from 290 to 390 meters after six weeks of outpatient therapy.

Case report of a 47-year-old female who developed Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) approximately 4-5 weeks after COVID-19 infection. The patient received various treatments including methylprednisolone and IVIG, but the paper is a single case report without control group or systematic evaluation of treatment efficacy, and CJD is a distinct prion disease rather than a long COVID sequela.

A case report documenting the 2-year course of a 16-year-old who developed OCD and psychosis following COVID-19 infection, with symptom worsening after reinfection. The patient's poor response to SSRIs, antipsychotics, and benzodiazepines is described, highlighting post-COVID neuropsychiatric sequelae as a diagnostic and treatment challenge.

Case report of a 14-year-old with MIS-C who developed primary adrenal insufficiency and autoimmune hypothyroidism following COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentation and treatment but does not study long COVID or test interventions for post-COVID syndrome.

This paper presents a single case study of a 62-year-old woman with cognitive and psychiatric complications 8 months after moderate/severe COVID-19 infection. The case describes neuropsychological assessment findings and differential diagnosis of dementia-like symptoms, but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a single long COVID patient with apathy who underwent neuropsychological assessment, neuroimaging, and high-density EEG compared to healthy controls. EEG revealed widespread oscillatory abnormalities including increased delta/beta activity and decreased alpha activity, suggesting dysfunction in cortical networks involved in motivation and emotion.

This case report describes the recovery trajectory of a severe COVID-19 survivor using occupational therapy interventions, focusing on improvements in mental health and social participation. The study demonstrates the potential therapeutic value of occupational therapy in supporting long-term functional and psychosocial recovery in post-COVID patients.

A case report describing a 44-year-old female who developed central adrenal insufficiency and diabetes insipidus following acute COVID-19 infection. This is a single case report documenting a rare endocrine manifestation of COVID-19, not a treatment study.

Case report of a pregnant woman presenting with bifacial weakness, paresthesia, and vestibulocochlear neuritis 6 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG) and intravenous steroids. The patient achieved complete recovery of facial palsy and hearing loss, with residual paresthesia at 2-week follow-up, demonstrating successful treatment of a post-COVID neurological manifestation.

Case report of a 50-year-old man who developed severe refractory diarrhea weeks after severe COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation, diagnosed as COVID-19-associated enterocolitis. Treatment with methylprednisolone pulse therapy resulted in marked symptom improvement, suggesting abnormal immune response in post-COVID-19 complications.

Case report of a 62-year-old man with progressive interstitial pulmonary fibrosis and dendriform ossification developing 3 months after mild COVID-19, requiring bilateral lung transplantation. Histological and molecular analysis revealed persistent SARS-CoV-2 in vascular endothelium and extensive remodeling, suggesting incomplete viral clearance as a pathophysiological mechanism in post-COVID lung disease.

This is a case report of a 53-year-old woman diagnosed with infective endocarditis four weeks after acute COVID-19 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation and treatment with antibiotics but does not focus on long COVID or study any intervention for long COVID patients.

This is a case report describing Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) in a COVID-19 patient in Tanzania. The paper does not address long COVID (post-acute sequelae) but rather an acute neurological complication during active infection, and presents a single case without treatment intervention or comparative data.

Case report of a patient who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) 43 days after severe COVID-19 infection, treated with intravenous immunoglobulin across four intervals. Describes clinical presentation, treatment course, and functional outcomes during rehabilitation.

Case report of a 40-year-old female who developed severe myocarditis with cardiogenic shock one month after mild COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and medical management (diuretics, inotropic support, glucocorticoids) but is a single case report with no treatment comparison or control group.

This case report describes a long COVID patient who developed proximal arterial thrombosis leading to transfemoral amputation during prolonged hospitalization, with subsequent multidisciplinary rehabilitation. The patient achieved functional independence gains using the Functional Independence Measure (84→96), demonstrating recovery despite severe post-COVID sequelae.

Case report of organizing pneumonia presenting as chronic cough following confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Describes a single case of post-COVID pulmonary sequelae without treatment outcomes or trial data.

Case report of a 34-year-old male who developed a pneumothorax 18 days after discharge from acute COVID-19 hospitalization during convalescence. Describes clinical presentation and emergency management but does not study a treatment intervention or evaluate outcomes across multiple patients.

Case report of a post-COVID patient presenting with exertional fatigue and presyncope, investigated using invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing (iCPET) which revealed exertional hyperammonemia and preload insufficiency. The patient improved with empiric rifaximin therapy, suggesting a potential novel mechanism of post-exertional fatigue related to metabolic dysregulation and bacterial overgrowth.

Case report of a 79-year-old male who developed interstitial lung disease five months after acute COVID-19 hospitalization, with imaging evidence of pulmonary fibrosis and elevated autoimmune markers. The paper discusses differential diagnosis between post-COVID fibrosis and exacerbation of pre-existing subclinical ILD, but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

A case report describing a patient who developed interstitial lung disease several months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with discussion of diagnostic challenges in identifying long COVID-related pulmonary complications. The paper presents a single clinical case without treatment intervention or comparison groups, serving primarily as a clinical vignette to highlight diagnostic considerations.

Case report of a patient who developed late-onset fibrosis more than 4 months after asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, initially with normal imaging at 2 weeks.
