The patient was treated with pirfenidone, corticosteroids, and pulmonary rehabilitation, showing significant radiological and clinical improvement by 7 months post-infection.

Case report of a patient with chronic hypersensitivity pneumonitis whose condition progressively worsened following severe COVID-19 infection and hospitalization. Describes long-term pulmonary sequelae but presents only a single case with no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

Case report of a long COVID patient with persistent dyspnea and cough evaluated using hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI to assess lung function and gas exchange. Imaging findings show patchy ventilation and reduced gas exchange consistent with mild obstructive disease, but this is a single case study without treatment intervention or control group.

Case report of a saddle pulmonary embolism in a patient 4 weeks after acute COVID-19 hospitalization. While it discusses VTE in the recovery phase of COVID-19, it is a single case report focused on acute post-discharge complications rather than long COVID syndrome or treatment of long COVID.

Case report of a 66-year-old man who developed acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP/Guillain-Barré syndrome) three weeks after acute COVID-19 infection, treated with IVIG and plasmapheresis. This is an acute COVID complication during the infection period, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection), and represents a single case report rather than a systematic study of a treatment intervention.

A case report describing post-viral pulmonary fibrosis development in a COVID-19 patient with initially mild symptoms, showing radiological and functional evidence of lung changes 10-12 weeks post-infection. The paper documents a single clinical case without treatment intervention or control group, presenting it as an unexpected complication of mild COVID-19.

A case report of a 71-year-old patient presenting with chronic eosinophilic pneumonia (CEP) 6 months after COVID-19 infection, suspected to be long COVID-related. The patient was treated with discontinuation of offending medications (pomalidomide) and oral prednisone, with clinical improvement following steroid therapy.

Case report of a 56-year-old male with severe COVID-19 pneumonia documenting radiological evolution of lung sequelae over 8 weeks post-infection, including ground glass opacities, bullae formation, pneumothorax, and pleural effusion with spontaneous resolution. The paper illustrates long-term pulmonary complications and imaging follow-up recommendations but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 64-year-old female with long COVID-related obstructive airway disease that improved when JAK inhibitor upadacitinib was paused but returned when switched to tofacitinib, suggesting a potential drug class effect. The paper documents a rare adverse outcome rather than testing a treatment intervention.

A case report describing a 62-year-old male with post-COVID syndrome who developed acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP) with multisystem complications including myocarditis, rhabdomyolysis, and cardiac arrest. The patient received IVIG therapy and plasmapheresis, showing improved neuromuscular strength but ultimately requiring prolonged hospitalization with tracheostomy.

A case report describing a 53-year-old woman who developed sarcoidosis with non-caseating granulomas following COVID-19 infection in July 2022. The paper documents the clinical progression and diagnostic workup but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a descriptive case without treatment outcomes.

Case report of a single adult patient presenting with Kawasaki-like disease following mild COVID-19 infection one month prior. The paper describes the clinical presentation and complications (peritonitis, myocarditis, hepatitis) but does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 43-year-old patient who developed acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis as a long-term sequela of COVID-19 pneumonia, presenting with progressive dyspnea and cough 2 months after initial infection. Patient was successfully treated with systemic corticosteroids, demonstrating clinical improvement and highlighting the importance of recognizing inflammatory lung complications in post-COVID recovery.

Case report of a 61-year-old patient who developed left hemidiaphragmatic paralysis following mild COVID-19 infection, presenting with progressive exertional dyspnea months after acute illness. Patient underwent left hemidiaphragmatic plication with significant improvement in symptoms, demonstrating surgical treatment of a rare long COVID manifestation.

A case study reporting the first documented case of prosopagnosia (face recognition impairment) and navigational deficits persisting 6+ months after COVID-19, along with survey data from 83 COVID-19 survivors indicating similar difficulties. The paper describes clinical assessment and symptomatology but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of acute-onset delusional parasitosis (Morgellons disease) in a young male following COVID-19 infection, associated with basal ganglia pathology. The authors discuss whether this represents a manifestation of neuro-COVID or a consequence of COVID-related misinformation (infodemic).

Case report of a 31-year-old male with severe pulmonary hypertension and fibrosis requiring bilateral lung transplant five months after acute COVID-19 infection. The explant analysis demonstrates chronic pulmonary vascular remodeling and organizing lung injury consistent with long-term COVID-19 sequelae.

A case report of a long COVID patient who developed pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with positive ANCA antibodies, treated with corticosteroids and Rituximab. The treatment resulted in improvement in renal function and systemic symptoms.

Case report of a 49-year-old long COVID patient presenting with pulmonary embolism after COVID-19 infection, treated conservatively with amantadine for a brief period. Effective conservative treatment with regression of thrombotic changes occurred over three months.

Case report of Adult Onset Still's Disease diagnosed in a patient 8 weeks after recovering from COVID-19, presenting with fever, rash, and arthritis. Patient was treated with corticosteroids with favorable outcome, highlighting the importance of differential diagnosis for post-COVID conditions.

Case report of serpiginous choroiditis (eye inflammation) presenting one month after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection in a previously healthy woman. While the case demonstrates a potential immunological link between COVID-19 and choroidal inflammation, this is a single case report rather than a long COVID study, as it focuses on an acute post-infection complication rather than persistent long COVID syndrome.

Case report of a 61-year-old patient with post-COVID inattention and fatigue treated with stimulant and antidepressant medications (Methylphenidate, Lisdexamfetamine, and Bupropion). The patient achieved symptom remission, suggesting potential benefit of ADHD-like syndrome treatment approach in post-COVID patients, though the authors acknowledge the need for further research to confirm findings.

Case report of a 23-year-old with long COVID who developed mixed cholestatic-hepatocellular liver injury after recreational kratom use for insomnia. The patient recovered after conservative management and liver function normalized at 3 months, highlighting kratom as a potential cause of acute liver injury in this population.

A case study of patient-led integrated cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for a 36-year-old male with long COVID and comorbid depression and anxiety, conducted over five months with 12 sessions. The patient showed reliable improvement in somatic symptoms, depression, anxiety, and quality of life.

Case report of a 24-year-old male who developed aquagenic syringeal keratoderma (ASK) 3 months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with palmar edema and white papules triggered by water exposure. Treatment with botulinum toxin injection led to sustained symptom resolution over 7 months, suggesting ASK may be a novel post-acute sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Case report of a severely immunized COVID-19 patient who developed progressive lung parenchyma damage over 2.5 months, culminating in massive pneumothorax and respiratory failure. The paper documents acute COVID-19 complications during the active infection phase, not long COVID sequelae.

Case report of a critically ill patient with acute COVID-19 who developed generalized myoclonus during the recovery phase of active infection. The patient responded to high-dose steroids, but the paper focuses on acute infection complications rather than post-COVID syndrome.

Case report of a patient with SARS-CoV-2 infection who developed Miller Fisher syndrome with autonomic dysfunction, confirmed anti-ganglioside antibodies, and treated with intravenous immunoglobulin. The paper documents excellent clinical response to IVIG treatment and reviews similar post-COVID Miller Fisher syndrome cases in the literature.

A case report describing a patient with post-COVID acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) affecting the cervicothoracic spinal cord and medulla, presenting with microhemorrhages and hemosiderin deposition. The patient received aggressive immunotherapy to control the inflammatory response.

Case report describing magnetic resonance neurography findings in 2 patients who developed severe peripheral neuropathies during recovery from COVID-19. The paper documents imaging findings and clinical presentation but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing a patient who developed psoriatic arthritis following COVID-19 infection, with review of literature on post-COVID rheumatologic manifestations. This is a single case report with no intervention or treatment evaluation, focusing on disease characterization rather than therapeutic outcomes.

Case report of a rheumatoid arthritis patient who developed multiple new-onset autoimmune diseases (autoimmune thyroiditis, LADA, pernicious anemia) following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper describes clinical manifestations of post-COVID autoimmune complications but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This paper describes a single case of a long COVID patient with SARS-CoV-2 RNA detected in cerebrospinal fluid, suggesting possible viral persistence in the central nervous system. While directly relevant to long COVID pathophysiology, it is a case report without a treatment intervention or control comparison, making it ineligible for the treatment trials analysis.

A case report of a 22-year-old healthcare worker with prolonged multi-systemic long COVID symptoms lasting 18 weeks and persistent SARS-CoV-2 detection for over 110 days. The paper documents clinical presentation and viral shedding duration but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case report of a patient with persistent dyspnea after COVID-19 infection, diagnosed with bilateral diaphragmatic paralysis. The patient was managed with CPAP support and showed symptomatic improvement at 1-year follow-up without specific interventions.

Case report of a 31-year-old woman with incontinentia pigmenti who developed severe COVID-19 and subsequent long COVID symptoms. The paper discusses the potential role of autoimmunity and interferon dysfunction in both conditions but presents only a single patient case without systematic treatment evaluation.

Case report of a 54-year-old man with functional movement disorder (repetitive head flexions) that developed 2 months after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, accompanied by cognitive impairment, headaches, fatigue, and psychiatric symptoms. Extensive neurological workup was normal, and symptoms persisted at 1-year follow-up, highlighting the neuropsychiatric manifestations and quality-of-life burden of long COVID.

Case report of a 51-year-old female with post-COVID-19 acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) presenting with multifocal neurologic symptoms. Early MRI evaluation and glucocorticoid-based treatment led to satisfactory clinical outcomes, demonstrating the importance of timely neurological evaluation and intervention in post-COVID neurological complications.

A case report describing a woman who developed abnormal uterine bleeding and premature ovarian insufficiency following COVID-19 infection, with suspected autoimmune-mediated mechanisms. The paper highlights post-viral endocrine dysfunction as a long COVID consequence but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.
Case report of taste impairment in a COVID-19 patient with pre-existing chronic smell loss during acute infection. Does not address long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

Case report of a young male who developed diabetes insipidus and myocarditis as late sequelae of COVID-19 infection. The patient recovered following treatment with desmopressin, demonstrating successful management of this rare post-COVID endocrine complication.

Case report of a 65-year-old COVID-19 patient who developed post-infectious encephalitis with delirium one week after discharge from severe pneumonia. Patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone and immunoglobulin therapy and recovered, demonstrating immunosuppressive therapy as an intervention for post-COVID neurological complications.

Case report of an infant with febrile status epilepticus and MIS-C (Multi-system Inflammatory Syndrome in Children) occurring 2-4 weeks post-COVID, presenting with bilateral brain MRI abnormalities. Patient improved with pulse steroids and IVIg, but this describes acute post-infectious MIS-C, not long COVID (chronic persistent symptoms months later).

Case report of a 12-year-old girl who developed Type 1 Diabetes and morphea (scleroderma) following mild COVID-19 infection, attributed to autoimmune activation during long COVID. The paper documents the clinical presentation and course but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report describing a single immunocompromised patient with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma who developed post-COVID interstitial lung disease (PC-ILD) with prolonged viral shedding. The paper documents the patient's clinical course and pathophysiology but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention or trial design.

Case report of a 73-year-old male who developed secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) 11 months after recovering from COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with dexamethasone, transfusions, filgrastim, and intravenous immunoglobulin but ultimately deteriorated and died, illustrating the severe complications and high mortality of delayed sHLH in post-acute COVID-19 patients.

Case report of a 69-year-old woman presenting with life-threatening ventricular tachycardia and aortitis in the weeks following mild COVID-19 infection, treated with radiofrequency ablation and long-term corticosteroids. While the case occurs in the post-COVID period, it focuses on acute multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A) rather than long COVID, which is characterized by persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection.

Case report of a patient with MOG antibody-positive optic neuritis that developed post-COVID-19, treated with methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin. While this describes a complication occurring after acute COVID-19 infection, it does not study long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months post-infection) but rather an acute/subacute post-infection neurological condition in a single case.

Case report of a non-severe COVID-19 patient who developed persistent thrombocytopenia (low platelet count) for several months after viral clearance, representing a long COVID sequela. The patient was treated with glucocorticoids (prednisone) with eventual improvement, highlighting immune system involvement in post-COVID complications.

Case report of a 77-year-old male who developed restless anal syndrome (a variant of restless legs syndrome) several weeks after COVID-19 recovery. The patient was successfully treated with clonazepam 1.5 mg per day, with resolution of symptoms.

A case report describing a 27-year-old runner who developed severe dysautonomia five weeks after mild COVID-19 infection, presenting with orthostatic intolerance, tachycardia, and post-exertional fatigue. The patient showed improvement over months with fluid/sodium intake, compression stockings, and a graduated exercise program.

A case report of a 62-year-old patient who developed subacute cerebellar ataxia one day after resolution of acute COVID-19 respiratory symptoms, with laboratory findings suggesting post-infectious immune-mediated etiology. The patient showed rapid improvement following high-dose methylprednisolone therapy, suggesting corticosteroids as a potential treatment for post-COVID neurological complications.

This case report describes a single patient with acute COVID-19 presenting with persistent dyspnea caused by an intrapulmonary right-to-left shunt (Acute Vascular Distress Syndrome). The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 pathophysiology and diagnosis during active infection, not long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

Case report of a 73-year-old female with post-COVID-19 encephalopathy presenting with cognitive decline, depression, and oral cenesthopathy 16 months post-infection. Treatment with Aripiprazole and Carbamazepine resulted in partial symptom improvement.

A case report of a 62-year-old patient with long COVID presenting with dyspnea and bilateral lung infiltrates who was found to have Tropheryma whipplei infection on lung biopsy. The patient recovered after treatment with intravenous ceftriaxone and oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, highlighting an infectious pathogen to consider in post-COVID lung disease.

A case report of a 47-year-old female with atypical Parsonage-Turner syndrome (brachial plexus neuritis) persisting for months after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting as unilateral chest pain and sensory loss. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnostic findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a case report of a single patient with lymphoma in remission who developed ARDS and severe hematologic complications after allogeneic HSCT, coincidentally occurring during a long-term COVID-19 infection, treated with ECMO support. The paper focuses on ECMO management in HSCT patients and does not study long COVID as the primary condition or investigate any treatment for long COVID itself.

Case report of a 51-year-old patient recovered from COVID-19 who experienced recurrent pulmonary embolism despite receiving direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) therapy. The case raises questions about DOAC efficacy in post-COVID thromboembolic complications.

This case report describes a 51-year-old patient who experienced multiple cerebral infarctions 11 months after mild COVID-19, attributed to persistent COVID-associated coagulopathy and a patent foramen ovale. The report documents a serious long-term complication of COVID-19 involving thromboembolism but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper reports a single case of a 21-year-old female with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome presenting with a right atrioventricular thrombus and pulmonary embolism, complicated by an underlying cardiac myxoma. The case illustrates potential thrombotic complications in the post-acute phase of COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 51-year-old male presenting with persistent dyspnea and widespread pulmonary embolism seven weeks after suspected COVID-19 infection. Documents a single case of long COVID-associated thrombotic complication treated with anticoagulation, highlighting PE as a potential long-term sequela.

Case report of a 9-year-old with bilateral anterior intermediate uveitis occurring 1 month after recovery from MIS-C, treated with topical difluprednate and immunosuppression. While this describes a post-viral complication and treatment, it is a single case report focused on an acute inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) rather than long COVID, which is characterized by chronic sequelae weeks to months after acute infection.

Case report of a 55-year-old woman who developed myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) following SARS-CoV-2 infection and recovered after multimodal treatment including dietary modifications, cognitive-behavioral interventions, conditioning exercises, and pharmacotherapy (amitriptyline and Kampo medicine). The paper presents therapeutic options for managing disabling symptoms in post-COVID ME/CFS patients.

Case report of a 34-year-old patient who developed penile Mondor disease (superficial vein thrombophlebitis) one month after COVID-19 infection, suggesting COVID-19 as a prothrombotic risk factor. The patient was treated pharmacologically and achieved complete recovery with clot dissolution confirmed on ultrasound.

Case report of a 9-year-old girl with abducens nerve palsy following COVID-19 infection, with improvement at 2-month follow-up. Discusses possible post-infectious immune-mediated mechanism but presents no treatment intervention or controlled study design.

A case report describing the use of dry and wet needling (trigger point injections) to treat myofascial pain in a long COVID patient. Both interventions showed good short- and long-term therapeutic effects in reducing the patient's myalgia symptoms.

A case report of a patient who developed ventricular tachycardia and cardiac fibrosis 6 months after mild COVID-19 infection. The case illustrates potential long-term cardiac involvement in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 29-year-old male who developed cavitary lung disease as a late complication months after COVID-19 recovery, initially unresponsive to conservative management. The patient ultimately required surgical intervention (lung decortication) with gradual improvement on combined medical and surgical therapy.

A case report of a long COVID patient who developed collagenous gastritis associated with Epstein-Barr virus reactivation following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The patient was treated with corticosteroids, proton pump inhibitors, and iron supplementation with improvement.

A case report of a 27-year-old male presenting with persistent hiccups 35 days post-COVID-19 (a post-acute sequela), successfully treated with chlorpromazine 25 mg. The case documents an atypical and rare manifestation of long COVID and its pharmacological management.

A case report of a 55-year-old long COVID patient treated with 60 sessions of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT), showing significant improvements in brain perfusion, cognitive function (particularly nonverbal memory and executive function), and cardiopulmonary capacity (34% increase in VO2 max, 44% improvement in forced vital capacity). The authors acknowledge this is a single case and call for prospective randomized controlled trials to validate the findings.

A case report of anesthetic management for transurethral prostate resection in a COVID-19 survivor with aortic dissection. The paper describes clinical presentation and surgical management of a single patient rather than a treatment trial or systematic evaluation of an intervention.

A case report of rehabilitation therapy in a severe acute COVID-19 patient who regained physical function after discharge. The paper focuses on acute-phase recovery and muscle rehabilitation during the immediate post-infection period, not long COVID or persistent post-acute sequelae.

Case report of a 73-year-old woman with gastric cancer who developed orthostatic hypotonia as a late sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection. Treatment with thiethylperazine maleate and nonpharmacological measures (postural changes, dietary modifications, fluid intake) resulted in sustained symptom relief.

This case report describes anesthesia management and airway procedures for a post-COVID-19 patient with severe tracheomalacia requiring surgical stenting. The patient was successfully treated with custom Y-shaped stent placement and discharged without significant long-term sequelae.

A case report of a 60-year-old long COVID patient with small airways disease treated with corticosteroids and pulmonary rehabilitation over 36 months. The study demonstrates progressive improvement in most parameters but persistent small airway abnormalities detected by forced oscillation technique and multiple breathing washout, emphasizing the importance of integrating these sensitive tests for detecting and monitoring small airways disease in post-acute COVID-19.

Case report of a single patient with persistent cognitive impairment and cerebrospinal fluid anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies six months after mild COVID-19. The study argues for neuropsychological testing in long COVID patients but presents no treatment intervention or comparative analysis.

Case report of a 16-year-old presenting with features of both multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) and adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) occurring 4 weeks post-SARS-CoV-2 exposure. While a post-infectious hyperinflammatory condition, this is a single case presentation of acute post-infectious syndrome rather than long COVID (which involves chronic persistent symptoms weeks to months after acute infection) and does not study a treatment intervention.

A case report describing successful treatment of prolonged COVID-19 in an immunocompromised patient (history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma) using extended combination therapy with remdesivir and nirmatrelvir/ritonavir outside standard guidelines. The combination therapy resolved symptoms and cleared viral load after initial monotherapy failure.

Case report of a 52-year-old man who developed acute mania with psychotic symptoms 20 days post-COVID-19 infection, successfully treated with olanzapine and sodium valproate. The paper highlights neuropsychiatric complications as a manifestation of long COVID and advocates for vigilant psychiatric assessment in COVID-19 survivors.

Case report of a 63-year-old male with pre-existing bipolar affective disorder who developed rapid mood cycling and neurological symptoms (tremor, numbness, unsteadiness) following COVID-19 infection. The authors document the temporal association and rule out lithium toxicity and other organic causes, but this is a single case observation without treatment evaluation or control group.

Case report of a 77-year-old post-COVID-19 patient presenting with vitamin B12 deficiency manifesting as pseudo-thrombotic microangiopathy, initially mimicking thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Treatment with high-dose intramuscular vitamin B12 resulted in rapid clinical and hematologic improvement with full recovery.

Case report of a 40-year-old female with long COVID presenting with neuropsychiatric symptoms, cognitive deficits, and depersonalization following SARS-CoV-2 infection and reinfection. Patient was treated with antipsychotics, antidementia therapy, and vasoactive medication, resulting in reduction of psychotic symptoms and initial improvement in cognitive functioning.

Case report of a 52-year-old woman who developed brief psychotic disorder (persecutory delusions and auditory hallucinations) 2 weeks after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper presents a single clinical case to illustrate potential psychiatric complications during acute COVID-19, not long COVID or a treatment intervention.

Case report of a 60-year-old man with severe post-COVID syndrome presenting with persistent dyspnea, fatigue, cognitive impairment, and moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms three months after acute infection. Treatment with vortioxetine 10mg resulted in significant improvement of fatigue, dyspnea, anxiety, and depressive symptoms, though cognitive deficits partially persisted.

A clinical case report of a 28-year-old patient who developed cognitive impairment (memory, attention, executive function) during the recovery phase after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper discusses possible mechanisms of post-COVID cognitive symptoms but presents no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Case report of a 48-year-old woman presenting with long COVID symptoms (fatigue, headaches, shortness of breath, neurological symptoms) complicated by depressive features, treated with Duloxetine. The paper discusses differential diagnosis between long COVID, major depressive disorder, and adjustment disorder, highlighting psychiatric manifestations as a key feature of persistent COVID.

Case report of a 30-year-old female who developed acute adrenal insufficiency 3 months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and elevated ACTH. The patient was successfully treated with corticosteroid and mineralocorticoid replacement therapy, suggesting autoimmune-mediated adrenal dysfunction as a late sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Case report of a 45-year-old male who developed new-onset diabetes mellitus during acute COVID-19 infection with subsequent recovery of normal glucose metabolism. The paper documents acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae.

Case report of a patient who developed new-onset diabetes mellitus 1.5 months after acute COVID-19 infection, with recovery after insulin therapy. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 and its immediate metabolic complications, not persistent long COVID symptoms or treatments for long COVID patients.

A case report describing a single patient who developed uncontrolled diabetes approximately 10 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, attributed to pancreatic B cell injury. The paper documents this long-term sequela of COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 48-year-old diabetic patient who developed Bell's palsy 4 months after asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with corticosteroids and acupuncture. The patient showed significant facial palsy improvement after 15 days and near-complete recovery by 6 months, supporting the use of corticosteroids and acupuncture for post-COVID neurological complications.

A case report of a vaccinated nurse who developed neurogenic orthostatic hypotension and postural orthostatic tachycardia following two COVID-19 infections, treated with midodrine (discontinued due to intolerance), hydration/salt management, and propranolol. The case illustrates long COVID's autonomic complications and response to pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions.

A case report of a 32-year-old female who developed subacute thyroiditis post-COVID-19 infection, initially presenting with thyrotoxicosis followed by hypothyroidism requiring levothyroxine treatment. The patient demonstrated clinical improvement with thyroid hormone replacement over a 3-month follow-up period.

Case report of a 34-year-old woman presenting with worsening shortness of breath two weeks after mild COVID-19, found to have anterior mediastinal mass suspicious for thymic hyperplasia that partially resolved over four months. Discusses thymic rebound hyperplasia as a potential post-COVID complication and its relationship to immune recovery, without testing any therapeutic intervention.

Case report of a patient who developed subacute thyroiditis 5 weeks after COVID-19 infection, presenting with fatigue, weakness, and palpitations. The paper describes clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and natural resolution over 9 weeks, but is a single case presentation without a treatment intervention or control group.

A case report of a 36-year-old woman with COVID-19-induced subacute thyroiditis (SAT) whose thyroid function abnormalities persisted for over a year, unusually prolonged compared to typical SAT. The patient was treated with propranolol and experienced gradual normalization of thyroid function by 17 months, suggesting thyroid involvement may represent a distinct manifestation of long COVID.

This case report describes a 46-year-old woman who developed eosinophilic granulomatous polyangiitis (EGPA) with peripheral neuropathy one year after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The patient was treated with oral steroids and Mepolizumab, and responded well to this immunosuppressive therapy.

This is a personal account/editorial piece about a pharmacy consultant's experience with long COVID symptoms months after initial infection. It does not present systematic treatment data, trial results, or structured research findings.

A case report of a patient with refractory headache and intracranial hypertension months after COVID-19 infection. The paper documents a single case presentation without treatment intervention or outcome measurement in a cohort.

Case report of a 28-year-old patient who developed MOG antibody-associated transverse myelitis six weeks after moderate COVID-19 infection, presenting with progressive paraparesis and spinal cord lesions. Treatment with systemic glucocorticoids and plasma exchange therapy resulted in significant symptom resolution and radiological improvement over 8 months of follow-up.

A case report of a 72-year-old male who experienced recurrent ischemic strokes within 8 weeks following COVID-19 infection despite respiratory symptom recovery. The paper documents multiple strokes of varying ages and proposes that the hyperinflammatory state persists after acute infection, potentially leading to late vascular complications.

A case report documenting a patient with stiff-person syndrome (SPS) that developed and severely worsened after mild COVID-19 infection, with video-documented clinical progression over 2-3 weeks. The patient received 3 monthly IVIG infusions and showed improvement, suggesting viral-triggered autoimmunity as a post-COVID sequela.

Case report of a 12-year-old girl with post-COVID-19 syndrome presenting with ischemic stroke and positive lupus anticoagulant. This is a single case report describing a neurological complication rather than a treatment study or systematic investigation.

A case report of a 17-month-old girl who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) 13 days after SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with upper extremity paresis and ataxia. She was treated with high-dose steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) with clinical improvement, followed by inpatient rehabilitation.

Case report describing treatment of severe post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) in a child with intravenous immune globulin (IVIG), addressing central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous system manifestations. The paper documents the clinical presentation and response to IVIG therapy in this pediatric long COVID patient.

Case report of a 47-year-old male with arginine-vasopressin deficiency and infundibulo-neurohypophysitis presenting 8 weeks after non-severe COVID-19, diagnosed via water deprivation test and MRI showing absent posterior pituitary bright spot. Patient was successfully treated with desmopressin therapy (0.2–0.8 mg/day), demonstrating a direct neuroendocrine treatment intervention for a rare long COVID manifestation.

A first-person narrative account by a theatre author describing her experience with long COVID symptoms including costochondritis, cardiac symptoms, and dyspnea over a one-year period. This is a personal essay/editorial rather than a research study with methodology or data analysis, and does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a patient who developed autoimmune type 1 diabetes following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper discusses potential mechanisms of COVID-induced diabetes and treatment approaches, but does not study long COVID or any intervention trial.

A case study of a 44-year-old woman with long COVID examining whether moderate- and vigorous-intensity aerobic and anaerobic exercise triggered dyspneic episodes. The study found that acute exercise did not trigger severe dyspnea, suggesting that exercise training may be feasible for long COVID patients with chronic respiratory symptoms.

Case report of a 67-year-old woman who experienced sudden hearing loss and tinnitus during acute COVID-19 pneumonia. She received corticosteroid therapy with partial improvement in hearing thresholds, but the paper focuses on acute infection complications rather than long COVID sequelae.

Case report of a woman who developed rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury one week after hospital discharge following severe COVID-19. The patient's muscle injury was attributed to post-viral myopathy secondary to COVID-19, highlighting late musculoskeletal complications as a potential sequela.

A case report of a 23-year-old man who developed acute psychotic symptoms (mania, delusions, hallucinations) one week after hospitalization for COVID-19 pneumonia. The patient was successfully treated with antipsychotic and mood stabilizer medications with complete symptom resolution within two weeks.

Case report of a 42-year-old man with non-critical COVID-19 who developed progressive pulmonary fibrosis weeks after initial infection, requiring high-flow oxygen and ICU admission. The patient showed clinical responsiveness to an extended course of corticosteroids, suggesting that post-acute pulmonary fibrosis may occur in milder COVID-19 cases, not just severe ARDS cases.

Case report of a patient who developed secondary sclerosing cholangitis following severe COVID-19, with progressive liver dysfunction and characteristic imaging/histological findings. The paper documents this rare post-COVID complication with no effective treatment beyond liver transplantation.

A case report of a long-haul COVID patient treated with therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), showing clinical improvement and reduced inflammatory markers with increased lymphocyte activity. The study suggests TPE may have therapeutic potential for treating long COVID symptoms.

Case report of a 69-year-old woman who developed giant cell arteritis (GCA) with arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (AAION) 2.5 weeks after COVID-19 infection. The authors discuss GCA as a potential post-COVID complication but provide no treatment trial data, only standard clinical management of a single patient case.

Case report of a kidney transplant recipient who experienced recurrence of C3 glomerulopathy following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents a rare complication of kidney disease in a transplant patient but does not study long COVID or any intervention for long COVID patients.

Case report of a 49-year-old man who developed pulmonary aspergilloma as a delayed complication 6 months after severe COVID-19 hospitalization and was successfully treated with robot-assisted lobectomy after failing antifungal therapy. The case illustrates that aspergilloma should be considered in post-COVID patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms and demonstrates minimally invasive surgery as a treatment option for antifungal-resistant post-COVID pulmonary fungal infections.

A case study of a 67-year-old patient with post-COVID-19 painless thyroiditis presenting with thyrotoxicosis symptoms 2 months after acute COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with beta blockers, methimazole, and corticosteroids, with significant symptom improvement and resolution of thyrotoxicosis.

This paper documents persistent cutaneous (skin) manifestations in COVID-19 long haulers, describing various skin symptoms occurring after acute infection recovery. It is a descriptive case report without any treatment intervention or control group.

Case report of a 73-year-old vaccinated patient who developed severe COVID-19 pneumonia with ARDS, opportunistic C. krusei infection, and secondary pulmonary arterial hypertension, treated with bosentan and antifungal therapy. Post-discharge follow-up documented persistent cardiopulmonary dysfunction consistent with post-COVID-19 syndrome.

This case report describes a 30-year-old woman with long COVID-associated anxiety, depression, insomnia, and mild cognitive impairment who received accelerated bilateral theta-burst transcranial magnetic stimulation (TBS) over 5 days. The patient showed improvements across depression, anxiety, sleep quality, and cognitive measures after 10 TBS sessions.

Case report of a 70-year-old woman who developed dual ANCA-positive vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis) following COVID-19 infection, presenting with sinusitis, cough, anemia, and renal dysfunction. The paper discusses post-infectious autoimmune phenomena triggered by SARS-CoV-2 but does not study long COVID or test any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 59-year-old patient with COVID-19 who developed bilateral lower limb weakness that persisted despite physical therapy, examining differential diagnoses for post-COVID neurological complications. The paper presents a clinical case to explore potential causes of weakness but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

A case report describing Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) occurring one month after COVID-19 infection in a 69-year-old female patient. The paper documents the presentation, diagnosis, and management of GBS as an acute COVID-19 complication rather than a long COVID sequela.

A case report of a health care worker who developed hyperventilation syndrome several weeks after mild COVID-19, presenting with severe dyspnea, palpitations, and anxiety. Multidisciplinary management including respiratory physiotherapy, psychotherapy, and anxiolytic medications led to significant symptom improvement and functional recovery.

Case report of a 62-year-old female who developed neurocognitive symptoms during acute COVID-19 infection in November 2020, treated with psychiatric care. The paper is not about long COVID as it focuses on acute infection symptoms rather than persistent post-COVID sequelae.

This case report documents a 73-year-old patient with post-COVID-19 chronic pruritus who experienced significant symptom relief following treatment with dupilumab (Dupixent), a monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signaling. The report suggests dupilumab as a potential therapeutic approach for COVID-19-associated chronic pruritus and highlights an immune-mediated mechanism underlying post-COVID dermatological symptoms.

A cautionary case report describing a patient misdiagnosed with long COVID via telemedicine when she actually had Graves' disease. The paper highlights diagnostic challenges and similarities in symptom presentation between long COVID and thyroid disease, emphasizing the need for in-person examination.

A case report describing a 73-year-old patient who developed severe complications (rib fractures, pleural effusion, diaphragmatic hernia) from uncontrolled cough 4 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, requiring surgical intervention. The paper documents an unusual presentation of post-COVID complications but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a long COVID patient with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), persistent antiphospholipid antibodies, and mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) who showed significant functional improvement with targeted therapy. Describes a 1-year clinical course with insights into immune mechanisms and treatment response in long COVID.

Case report describing rapid development of pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular failure in a patient with acute severe COVID-19 pneumonia treated with methylprednisolone and tocilizumab. Focuses on acute-phase complications during active infection rather than persistent long COVID sequelae.

A case report describing successful treatment of post-COVID-19 oropharyngeal dysphagia in a single patient using botulinum toxin type A injection after traditional swallowing therapy failed. The paper suggests that electrophysiologic assessment can guide treatment selection for neurogenic dysphagia caused by SARS-CoV-2 tropism to the nervous system.

A single-case study of a 39-year-old critically ill COVID-19 patient with persistent sinus tachycardia and ICU-acquired weakness during post-acute rehabilitation. Treatment with bisoprolol for heart rate control combined with cardiac rehabilitation principles improved functional independence and exercise capacity over 6 weeks.

A case study describing an emergency department nurse's COVID-19 hospitalization and subsequent post-discharge physical and mental health complications. The paper advocates for a bio-psycho-pharmaco-social approach to care and highlights inadequate follow-up of COVID-19 patients after ICU discharge, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

Case report of TB reactivation two years after severe COVID-19 in a patient treated with corticosteroids and anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibodies. While discussing immune suppression from COVID-19 treatment, this is a single case of acute infection complication, not a study of long COVID sequelae or a treatment intervention trial.

A longitudinal case study of one woman with long COVID examining cognitive-linguistic difficulties including memory problems, reduced verbal fluency, and brain fog over a 6-month period. While the patient showed some improvement, the study is a single uncontrolled case with no intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

This case report evaluates an individualized pulmonary rehabilitation program (breathing exercises, cycle training, neuromuscular electrical stimulation) in a 46-year-old male with post-COVID fibrosis over 8 weeks. The study reports small but promising improvements in respiratory function (FEV1, FVC, DLCO), exercise capacity (6MWD, shuttle walk tests), muscle strength, dyspnea, and fatigue.

A case report of a 70-year-old female who developed spinal cord infarction during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed by post-acute sequelae (PASC) including myalgias, neuropathic pain, and recurrent infections. The paper documents clinical complications and rehabilitation needs but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment.

Case report describing persistent tracheal hypersecretion (thick mucus) in a long COVID patient lasting 3 months post-infection. The paper identifies this as a previously unreported long-term symptom and proposes a pathophysiological mechanism involving goblet cell hyperstimulation, but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This paper reviews the emergence of asthma as a post-COVID complication, examining pathophysiological mechanisms including immunological dysregulation, airway inflammation, and epithelial damage. It includes a case study of a patient with asthmatic symptoms after COVID-19 recovery but is primarily a literature review rather than a controlled trial studying treatment outcomes.

Case report of a 55-year-old long COVID patient who developed recurrent thrombotic events (SMA thrombosis, splenic infarct, previous NSTEMI and stroke) despite therapeutic anticoagulation. Discusses mechanisms of post-COVID thrombotic complications and the need for vigilant monitoring in long COVID patients.

Case report of spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee in a young female patient following COVID-19 infection and steroid treatment. The paper discusses the potential link between COVID-19, steroid use, and bone necrosis, but is focused on acute/subacute orthopedic complications rather than long COVID syndrome.

This case report describes a single patient with long COVID presenting with cough and sore throat who was treated with Korean herbal medicines (Hyunggaeyungyo-tang and Saengmaek-san). The patient showed significant clinical improvement in symptoms as measured by visual analogue scale and Leicester Cough Questionnaire, suggesting potential therapeutic benefit of these herbal treatments for long COVID respiratory symptoms.

Case report of a 27-year-old woman who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) following COVID-19 infection, presenting with limb weakness and sensory changes. The patient showed rapid clinical improvement with intravenous corticosteroid therapy and immunoglobulin treatment combined with physiotherapy.

A personal narrative essay by a theatre scholar describing her own long COVID experience, including initial infection, symptom progression, and engagement with a post-COVID clinic. This is a first-person account rather than a research study and does not analyze treatment outcomes.

A case report of a 47-year-old patient with breakthrough long COVID after COVID-19 vaccination who experienced symptom resolution following nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment. The case raises questions about the potential role of antiviral therapies in long COVID pathogenesis and supports the need for clinical trials of antivirals in PASC.

Case report of a 43-year-old male who developed bilateral osteonecrosis of the femoral heads with concomitant septic arthritis 8 weeks after severe COVID-19 infection. The patient underwent bilateral two-staged total hip arthroplasty with successful outcomes at 3-year follow-up, demonstrating a rare musculoskeletal complication of post-acute COVID-19.

Case report of a 59-year-old male who developed secondary sclerosing cholangitis with persistent jaundice as a post-COVID complication following severe acute infection and multi-organ failure. Patient was treated with ursodiol which resulted in approximately 25% improvement in bilirubin levels, demonstrating a potential therapeutic approach for this rare post-COVID hepatic complication.

This is a single case report describing a patient who developed secondary sclerosing cholangitis (SSC-CIP) following critical COVID-19 illness requiring prolonged ICU stay and ECMO. The case documents clinical presentation, imaging findings, and long-term follow-up showing improvement, but does not constitute a treatment trial—it is descriptive documentation of a rare post-COVID complication.

This case report describes a 51-year-old female with COVID-19 pneumonia who developed a rare gastrosplenic fistula 2 weeks after discharge, attributed to COVID-19-related coagulopathy and splenic infarction. The patient was managed conservatively with percutaneous drainage, antibiotics, and anticoagulation with successful clinical outcome.

Case report of a 36-year-old man with post-COVID-19 immune dysregulation and EBV coinfection presenting with acute liver injury and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). The case illustrates a rare complication of post-COVID-19 and does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This case report describes a patient who developed small intestine bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with chronic diarrhea and bloating. The patient was successfully treated with Rifaximin and Neomycin antibiotics, with complete symptom resolution, illustrating a post-COVID complication and its management.

This case report describes cutaneous necrotizing vasculitis developing in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis after COVID-19 infection, treated with an IL-6 inhibitor. The paper focuses on the pathogenesis of vasculitis in RA rather than long COVID-specific symptoms or interventions for long COVID.

This case series presents a patient with long COVID who developed gastrointestinal symptoms attributed to mast cell activation, diagnosed via endoscopic biopsy showing elevated CD117+ mast cells. Treatment with famotidine and montelukast resulted in symptom resolution, suggesting mast cell disorders may be an underrecognized mechanism in post-COVID gastrointestinal manifestations.

Case report of a 47-year-old patient with post-COVID syndrome presenting with musculoskeletal pain and joint involvement treated with Chondroguard® (chondroprotective agent) via intramuscular injections followed by oral therapy. Treatment resulted in positive clinical dynamics with no adverse events reported during the observational period.

This paper presents a case report of a diabetic patient who developed dual fungal infections (Aspergillus and Mucor) with maxillary sinusitis as a post-COVID complication. It describes a single case observation rather than a treatment intervention study, making it ineligible for the trials meta-analysis.

A case report of a 48-year-old male with hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (veno-occlusive disease) following COVID-19 infection, presenting diagnostic challenges that mimicked hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. The patient was successfully treated with appropriate management, demonstrating a rare post-COVID complication with good long-term outcome.

Case report of a 54-year-old patient who developed a ruptured liver abscess following severe acute COVID-19 infection. The patient underwent percutaneous drainage for treatment, but this is a single case report documenting a complication of acute infection, not a long COVID study.

This case report describes a child who developed severe post-COVID myocarditis with ST-segment elevation and cardiogenic shock weeks after asymptomatic COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with heart failure therapy, anticoagulation, antiplatelet therapy, and corticosteroids, showing regression of clinical and laboratory symptoms with treatment.

Case report of a 27-year-old female who developed amenorrhea during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper discusses potential effects of acute COVID-19 on ovarian function but is not about long COVID or treatment interventions.

Case report of a 17-year-old with Takayasu's arteritis who developed ANCA-associated vasculitis with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage following COVID-19 infection. While post-COVID vasculitis is mentioned, the paper focuses on a rare autoimmune complication triggered by acute infection rather than long COVID management or treatment of persistent long COVID symptoms.

A case study objectively assessing neuromuscular fatigability in one long COVID patient 12+ months post-infection, comparing pre- and post-COVID measurements of muscle strength, endurance, and torque steadiness. The findings suggest fatigue may relate to cognitive impairment rather than intrinsic muscle dysfunction, but this single case report does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

A case report of a single COVID-19 patient describing electrophysiological and olfactometric evaluation of long-term olfactory dysfunction 8+ months post-infection. The study demonstrates peripheral electrophysiological signals but absent correlates in olfactory bulb and brain regions, with no treatment or intervention evaluated.

Case report of a patient in the post-COVID convalescence period presenting with myoclonus-ataxia syndrome, a novel neurological manifestation of COVID-19. The patient showed partial response to antimyoclonic drugs and full response to steroid therapy, suggesting immune-mediated pathophysiology.

This is a patient narrative piece featuring a French-Canadian teenager's personal experience with long COVID diagnosis and the challenges of navigating medical care. It is an editorial/opinion piece rather than a research study testing or evaluating a treatment intervention.
This is a patient testimony or editorial piece describing one person's experience with long COVID recovery over months. It does not present a systematic study, intervention, or trial data.

A case report documenting the clinical improvement of a 52-year-old male patient with post-COVID-19 syndrome (fatigue and headache) treated with Korean medicine including acupuncture and herbal remedies such as Sasammaekmoondong-tang. Treatment led to substantial improvements in fatigue (FSS score 48→18) and resolution of headache and insomnia symptoms.

This paper describes dyspnea and post-pulmonary embolism syndrome occurring after mild COVID-19 infection, documenting a complication of long COVID. It is a case series examining the prevalence and characteristics of these pulmonary sequelae in post-COVID patients without testing a specific intervention or treatment.

A case report documenting a 65-year-old man who developed multiple endocrine deficiencies (growth hormone, ACTH, and testosterone deficiency) following acute COVID-19, with clinical follow-up over 15 months showing partial recovery of some hormonal functions. The case demonstrates that prolonged endocrine dysfunction can occur as a long-term sequela of COVID-19 and may explain certain persistent post-COVID symptoms.

A teenager's personal narrative account of being diagnosed with long COVID and experiencing challenges with medical care. This is a first-person perspective piece rather than a systematic study or treatment evaluation.

This is a conference abstract presentation, not a full research study. It appears to be an editorial or comment on post-COVID complications in a patient with pre-existing thyroiditis, without presenting a treatment intervention or trial data.

Case report of a 62-year-old long COVID patient with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism treated with testosterone replacement therapy (TRT). TRT improved testosterone levels and hypogonadism-specific symptoms but showed minimal benefit for neuropsychiatric symptoms and quality of life, suggesting hypogonadism is one component of long-COVID syndrome rather than its primary cause.

Case report of a 1-year-4-month-old infant who developed multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) with coronary aneurysms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. While related to post-COVID sequelae, this is a single case report of acute post-infection inflammation rather than a long COVID treatment trial.

Case report of a 57-year-old female with post-COVID-19 syndrome presenting with persistent fatigue, cognitive impairment, anosmia, and other sequelae 4 months after acute COVID-19 hospitalization. The paper describes comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation management and emphasizes the need for early, individualized rehabilitation to prevent functional deterioration in post-COVID patients.

Case report of a 17-month-old with acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) occurring in the postinfectious stage after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with high-dose methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin. This is an acute/postinfectious neurologic complication during active disease recovery, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months later).

A case report of a 37-year-old patient who developed minimal change glomerulonephritis 6 months post-COVID-19 infection, presenting with proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome. The patient was treated with prednisolone and ramipril, achieving complete remission of symptoms and laboratory abnormalities within one month, with sustained improvement over two years of follow-up.

This paper reports a single case of myocardial infarction in a 28-year-old patient with long COVID-19, using coronary CT angiography with fat attenuation index technology to assess perivascular inflammation. The study demonstrates a potential cardiovascular complication of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or intervention efficacy.

A case report of a 57-year-old male with post-acute COVID-19 who received breathing exercises and chest physiotherapy twice daily during hospitalization. The patient showed improvement in shortness of breath by day 7 and was successfully weaned off non-invasive ventilation, demonstrating potential benefit of physical therapy for post-COVID respiratory symptoms.

Case report of a pregnant woman who developed post-infectious myocarditis with pulmonary hypertension two months after acute COVID-19 infection. Presents clinical findings and emphasizes the need for long-term monitoring of COVID-19 patients for post-acute complications, particularly in women planning pregnancy.

Clinical case report of an 11-year-old patient presenting with exanthema and ichthyosis following COVID-19 infection. The paper describes diagnostic findings and clinical presentation but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 61-year-old male with post-COVID-19 fatigue who developed acute pancreatitis with transient hyperzincaemia. The paper explores the metabolic and endocrine mechanisms underlying post-viral fatigue but presents only a single case without intervention or treatment evaluation.

Case report of recurrent cystitis management during post-COVID-19 recovery in an elderly patient. Treatment combined antiviral therapy and bacteriophage therapy to address both immune suppression and opportunistic infection.

This is a single case report of an 11-year-old child who developed post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) complicated by pulmonary embolism (PE) associated with hereditary thrombophilia. The paper describes the clinical presentation and management of this severe complication but does not study a treatment intervention or present any trial data.

Case report of a 73-year-old fully vaccinated woman who developed long COVID-19 following mild XBB.1.5 infection. The study demonstrates long COVID can occur after mild disease in vaccinated individuals without comorbidities, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Describes a clinical case of erythema infectiosum with Raynaud's phenomenon in a 9-year-old child with prior COVID-19 infection, analyzing the relationship between post-COVID syndrome and atypical skin manifestations. This is a single case report documenting comorbid pathological conditions without any treatment intervention or study design.

A case report of a patient with dilated cardiomyopathy who developed refractory arrhythmias and electrical storm during the post-acute COVID-19 period, treated with catheter ablation and antiarrhythmic therapy. The patient died from pulmonary embolism with autopsy-confirmed myocarditis; this is a single clinical case, not a treatment trial or systematic evaluation of an intervention.

Single-case study evaluating occupational therapy with cognitive strategies and metacognition for a long COVID patient over 9 sessions in a hospital setting. Patient demonstrated improved occupational performance and ability to create new habits and routines following the intervention.

A 1-year case report of gait biomechanics and physical therapy outcomes in a post-COVID-19 patient with severe motor impairment following intensive care, using 3D gait analysis and electromyography at three time points. The patient progressed from wheelchair-bound to independent walking with significant improvements in gait quality, muscle activation, and kinematic parameters.

A personal narrative account by a neuroscientist describing cognitive dysfunction, headache, fatigue, and sleepiness following mild COVID-19 infection. This is a first-person commentary on post-COVID symptoms rather than a systematic study or treatment intervention.

A longitudinal case report documenting auditory and vestibular dysfunction in a single patient following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study presents otoneurological findings including unilateral cochlear sensorineural hearing loss and progressive peripheral vestibular hypofunction over time.

Case report of a patient who developed proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposition (PGNMID) following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and treatment response with cyclophosphamide and bortezomib, but does not focus on long COVID sequelae or study treatment interventions for long COVID patients.

This case report describes a post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy patient presenting with persistent jaundice and biliary complications 10 months after acute COVID-19 infection. The patient underwent SpyGlass cholangioscopy as a diagnostic and therapeutic intervention to evaluate and manage the secondary sclerosing cholangitis condition.

This case report describes a 12-month interdisciplinary rehabilitation program for a 58-year-old long COVID patient, including physical, cognitive, and motor interventions. The patient showed improvements in neuropathic pain, muscle strength, gait, cognitive function, and quality of life, though some executive dysfunction persisted.

Case report of a 63-year-old male with post-COVID balance impairment treated with a four-month physiotherapy protocol combining pulmonary and neuro-physiotherapy with balance training. The patient showed good improvement in balance and regained functional independence.

A case report of a 29-year-old patient who developed peripheral facial paresis 14 days after COVID-19 infection onset, treated with corticotherapy, antiviral medication, vitamins, and facial gymnastics. The patient achieved complete remission of symptoms after 21 days of treatment.

This paper presents a clinical case of multiple cranial nerve neuropathy (affecting olfactory, trigeminal, facial, sublingual, and optic nerves) associated with post-COVID syndrome, with bilateral ocular involvement. The case describes staged rehabilitation measures to prevent visual acuity loss and restore function.

Case report of a patient presenting with concurrent post-COVID myocarditis and aortitis with aortic aneurysm 1 month after acute COVID-19, demonstrating autoimmune pathogenesis. Treatment with corticosteroids achieved myocarditis remission but aortic aneurysm progression required surgical intervention, and viral proteins were detected in tissue confirming chronic immune inflammation.

Clinical case report of new-onset bipolar affective disorder occurring in the post-COVID period in a patient with prior asymptomatic COVID-19. Discusses diagnostic challenges in recognizing bipolar disorder when depressive and anxiety syndromes predominate, and approaches to rational diagnosis and treatment.

This case report describes a patient with depression who developed lichen planus during the COVID-19 pandemic and experienced amplified itching in the post-COVID period, likely due to depressive cataesthetic hyperesthesia. Comprehensive psychosomatic treatment including psychocorrection alongside dermatotropic therapy resulted in normalized mood, reduced itching, and improved skin status and quality of life.

Describes a clinical case of post-COVID interstitial organizing pneumonia complicated by healthcare-associated infection in a 62-year-old patient. This is a single case report documenting a complication rather than a treatment intervention study.

Case report of an 18-year-old female with long COVID presenting with facial petechiae (mask phenomenon) several months after COVID-19 infection. The eruption resolved spontaneously within two weeks without treatment, representing a single clinical observation rather than a treatment trial or systematic study.

Case report of a patient with reversible cardiomyopathy and thrombotic complications following severe COVID-19, presenting with initial LVEF of 18% that improved to 60% over six months with rate control and intervention. The paper discusses COVID-19's potential role in modulating cardiovascular pathology in the long-term period but does not test or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This paper describes inflammatory and destructive lesions of the midface, nasal, and paranasal sinus bones as a long-term complication of COVID-19, presenting clinical examples. It is a descriptive case report/series with no treatment intervention tested.

A case study evaluating an 8-week exercise rehabilitation program in a 58-year-old long COVID patient, applying FITT-VP exercise prescription principles and CERT reporting standards. The intervention resulted in improvements across lung function, cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, functional status, fatigue, dyspnea, and depression.

Case report of Guillain-Barré Syndrome occurring during acute COVID-19 infection in a single patient, managed with supportive care. This paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae, as GBS occurred during active infection with positive COVID-19 testing.

Case report of a pregnant patient presenting with COVID-19-related cardiomyopathy (reduced ejection fraction of 38%) two months after acute infection. The paper describes clinical management considerations for pregnant patients with post-COVID cardiac complications but is a single case report without treatment intervention or comparative analysis.

This case report describes a 38-year-old male who developed post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy approximately 1 year after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and mechanical ventilation, presenting with persistent cholestasis and elevated liver enzymes. The patient underwent living donor liver transplantation with successful clinical recovery, demonstrating that transplantation may be an appropriate treatment for severe post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy.

A case report describing the application of xenon-oxygen inhalation therapy in a patient with respiratory failure and neuropsychiatric disorders persisting after acute COVID-19 infection. The treatment dramatically improved oxygen saturation and lung function, with proposed mechanisms involving restoration of surfactant function at the molecular level.

Single case report of a patient with acute COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury (suspected myocarditis or pericarditis) and persistent symptoms through 27 days post-infection. The paper focuses on acute-phase cardiac complications during active infection, not long COVID sequelae or treatment evaluation.

Case report of a 28-year-old female with post-COVID gastroparesis complicated by Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and anorexia nervosa who failed prokinetic therapy and required PEG-J tube feeding. Documents clinical management and outcomes of this severe long COVID gastrointestinal complication.

Case study evaluating the effectiveness of guided imagery therapy in an elderly patient with post-COVID-19 diabetes mellitus experiencing respiratory disorders. After 7 days of intervention, the patient showed improvements in blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate, with resolution of dyspnea symptoms.

Case report of a 71-year-old woman presenting with persistent gastroparesis and gastrointestinal dysmotility one month after COVID-19 infection, characterized by nausea, epigastric pain, early satiety, and constipation. Patient showed significant symptomatic improvement after treatment with metoclopramide, establishing COVID-19 as a potential etiology for post-infectious gastroparesis.

Case report of an 11-year-old child presenting with Miller Fischer syndrome and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) two months after COVID-19 exposure. The paper documents clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and neurological complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing a post-COVID-19 male patient who developed mild encephalopathy with reversible splenial lesion (MERS) presenting with neuropsychiatric and visual abnormalities. The patient's symptoms and MRI findings resolved spontaneously without immunosuppressive therapy, suggesting endotheliopathy as a mechanism of COVID-19 neurological complications.

This paper describes clinical cases of inflammatory and destructive lesions of the facial skeletal bones as long-term complications of COVID-19, including chronic osteomyelitis, sinusitis, and oroantral fistula. Patients received multicomponent inpatient therapy with documented improvement in general condition and local status, though underlying vascular and tissue regeneration issues remained.

Case report of a 49-year-old male who developed simultaneous bilateral avascular necrosis in four major joints (humeral and femoral heads) following high-dose corticosteroid treatment for severe COVID-19 pneumonia. The patient was treated with hyperbaric oxygen therapy, radiofrequency ablation, and nerve blocks, which provided significant pain relief, highlighting corticosteroid-induced musculoskeletal complications as a long COVID sequela.

Case report describing a patient who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) during acute COVID-19 infection, treated with intravenous immunoglobulin. The paper does not study long COVID or post-acute sequelae, but rather focuses on a rare neurological complication during the acute phase of infection.

Case report of post-poliomyelitis syndrome (PPS) in a patient with COVID-19, examining possible neuropathologic mechanisms linking SARS-CoV-2 to PPS manifestations. No treatment intervention or outcomes data presented; purely descriptive case documentation.

A clinical case report of a 40-year-old patient with post-COVID myoendocarditis and ventricular arrhythmias treated with propafenone, demonstrating management of cardiac complications weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The case illustrates cardiac complications in the post-COVID phase and describes the therapeutic approach and outcomes with antiarrhythmic medication.

This case report describes a post-COVID syndrome patient with reactivated chronic persistent Epstein-Barr virus infection and chronic nasopharyngotonsillitis of mixed etiology, presenting diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for this comorbid condition. The paper outlines modern laboratory diagnostics and principles of therapy for managing these overlapping conditions in a post-COVID context.

Case report of a 25-year-old woman who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) with sensory-dominant presentation 2 weeks after COVID-19 infection. The patient was treated with IV immunoglobulin and showed remarkable recovery, demonstrating a post-COVID neurological complication and its response to treatment.

Case report of a patient who developed concurrent Guillain-Barré syndrome and immune thrombocytopenic purpura one month after recovery from acute COVID-19, suggesting possible autoimmune sequelae of long COVID. The patient showed adequate response to treatment, illustrating a rare complication of post-acute COVID-19.

Case report of a 59-year-old male with bilateral optic nerve edema (papilledema) occurring after COVID-19 infection. Patient was treated with conservative and physiotherapy approaches, with OCT imaging documenting nerve fiber layer thickening and microcirculatory changes; the authors recommend screening, imaging protocols, and physiotherapeutic methods for post-COVID visual complications.

This case report describes a 46-year-old patient with severe COVID-19-related lung damage (80% involvement) treated with bovhyaluronidase azoxymer for 25 days in the post-COVID period. Clinical and radiological improvements were observed, including resolution of infiltrative changes and pneumofibrosis signs, suggesting potential therapeutic benefit of this immunomodulatory and antifibrosing agent in post-COVID recovery.

Case report of a 21-year-old woman who developed new-onset Tourette Syndrome after COVID-19 infection, presenting a rare neurological complication of long COVID. The patient improved with standard Tourette Syndrome treatments, contributing to the understanding of post-COVID neurological sequelae.

A case report of a 56-year-old male who developed atypical Takotsubo cardiomyopathy 12 days after recovery from acute COVID-19, presenting with chest pain and ultimately resulting in sudden death. The paper discusses potential mechanisms of late cardiac complications post-COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic strategy.

Describes a single case of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in an adult (MIS-A) presenting 3 weeks after COVID-19 infection with myocardial infarction and multi-organ dysfunction. While relevant to post-COVID sequelae, this is a single case report without treatment evaluation or control group.

Case report of a 41-year-old woman who developed seropositive rheumatoid arthritis one month after recovering from COVID-19 infection. The paper documents a single patient case without any treatment intervention or control group.

Case report of rehabilitation interventions in a 20-year-old female with acute post-COVID-19 symptoms and pre-existing intracranial pathology. The study describes a single patient's recovery with respiratory exercises over 4 weeks, but does not meet long COVID criteria as symptoms occurred only 5 weeks post-infection (acute phase) rather than persistent long COVID sequelae.

A case report describing a rare case of pulmonary artery thrombosis that developed two months after acute COVID-19 infection in a patient with severe pneumonia. The paper documents clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and management of this post-COVID complication, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or compare outcomes.

Case report of an 11-year-old girl with post-COVID interstitial lung disease presenting 4 months after acute infection with restrictive/obstructive lung function abnormality. Patient was treated with low-dose prednisolone for 6 weeks with clinical improvement noted.

Case report of a 42-year-old woman who developed post-COVID Guillain-Barré syndrome (AMSAN variant) with concurrent SIADH, successfully treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), fluid restriction, and tolvaptan. The case highlights a rare neurological complication of COVID-19 and demonstrates effective treatment management with both immunotherapy and pharmaceutical intervention for SIADH.

Case report of a 16-year-old girl who developed autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) 4 weeks after acute COVID-19 infection, presenting with jaundice, giddiness, and shortness of breath. The paper documents this rare post-COVID complication and its clinical presentation, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or trial.

Case report describing purpura fulminans as a rare post-COVID-19 complication in a pediatric patient. No treatment intervention is evaluated; this is a descriptive case presentation of a clinical manifestation.

Case report of a 16-year-old patient who developed Graves' disease following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper discusses thyroid dysfunction as a post-infection complication but does not study long COVID or test any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 3-year-old child presenting with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) with Kawasaki-like features following COVID-19 infection, treated with vasoactives, antibiotics, and supportive care. The paper discusses management approaches including the roles of aspirin and anticoagulants in MIS-C treatment.

Case report of a 12-year-old with nephrotic syndrome who developed cerebral venous thrombosis following COVID-19 infection, treated with anticoagulation therapy. The paper highlights the hypercoagulable state associated with COVID-19 as a risk factor for thrombotic complications in pediatric patients with comorbidities, but does not study long COVID or evaluate treatments for long COVID patients.

Case report describing penile gangrene as a rare vascular complication in a young patient during acute COVID-19 infection, attributed to COVID-related coagulopathy. The paper documents clinical presentation and outcome but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or compare outcomes across patient groups.

This is a case report describing a single case of multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS) in an adult occurring after COVID-19 infection, covering diagnostic approach and treatment. The paper adds limited clinical evidence as it presents only one case without systematic evaluation or outcome data.

This paper presents a case report of a 9-month-old child who developed esophageal achalasia following COVID-19 infection, combined with a literature review of the association between COVID-19 and achalasia.
