The patient showed clinical improvement with resolution of inflammation markers and symptom relief, highlighting cardiac complications in the long-COVID phase.

Case report of agranulocytosis developing after IVIG treatment in a patient with Guillain-Barré syndrome that occurred 5 weeks post-COVID-19 recovery. While the patient had recovered from acute COVID-19, the paper focuses on an acute neurological complication (GBS) and rare adverse event from treatment, not on long COVID syndrome or its treatment.

A case report of corneal graft rejection and posterior scleritis occurring five months after SARS-CoV-2 infection in a patient who received influenza vaccination, attributed to COVID-19-induced systemic autoinflammation. The patient was treated with naproxen, acyclovir, and immunomodulatory therapy; this is a single case report rather than a systematic treatment trial.

A case report of a patient who developed persistent immunosuppression and recurrent healthcare-associated multidrug-resistant infections following critical COVID-19 pneumonia. The paper discusses mechanisms linking post-COVID immunosuppression to secondary infections but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a 77-year-old patient who developed complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) with acute kidney injury two months after acute COVID-19 infection, treated with glucocorticoids, plasma exchange, and eculizumab. Despite treatment, the patient developed progressive kidney failure requiring hemodialysis, eventually stabilizing to chronic kidney disease stage 3b-4, demonstrating TMA as a rare long-term post-COVID complication.

This paper presents a detailed case study of a long-COVID patient with severe refractory cough, characterizing the condition longitudinally over 6 weeks using patient-reported outcomes and cough frequency monitoring. The authors discuss potential mechanisms and clinical management approaches for long-COVID cough with laryngeal hypersensitivity.

Case report of a 5-year-old child presenting with overlapping features of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) and secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a post-COVID-19 setting. Focuses on differential diagnosis and clinical features rather than long COVID syndrome or treatment outcomes.

A case report describing severe thrombocytopenia in a 79-year-old geriatric patient during post-COVID-19 recovery, resulting in bleeding complications and death. While relevant to long COVID sequelae, this is a single case report without treatment intervention or controlled comparison.

Case report of a 77-year-old patient who developed acute arterial and venous thromboembolism during post-COVID recovery despite anticoagulant therapy. The authors discuss endothelial injury and thrombogenic mechanisms in the post-COVID period and recommend combination anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy for high-risk patients.

A case report of a 28-year-old pregnant woman who developed post-COVID atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (p-aHUS) with thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury 28 days after COVID-19 infection, treated with plasmapheresis. The patient recovered completely following prompt plasma exchange treatment, demonstrating a successful therapeutic intervention for this rare post-COVID complication.

Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with worsening respiratory symptoms and radiological findings on chest X-ray. The paper discusses the utility of conventional chest imaging for detecting and monitoring lung abnormalities in long COVID progression, rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

A case report of a 60-year-old male with post-COVID-19 interstitial lung disease (ILD) presenting with severe chronic cough 4 months after acute infection. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone 32 mg/day and showed clinical improvement with near cessation of cough and radiological improvement in ground glass opacities after 2 weeks.

A case report of a 30-year-old woman with secondary infertility post-COVID-19 infection who was found to have a unicornuate uterus with fallopian tube blockage, treated successfully with fallopian tube cannulation resulting in spontaneous conception and live birth. The case suggests COVID-19 may cause fallopian tube blockage through ACE2 receptor expression as a long COVID sequela.

A case report documenting the use of hot fomentation therapy in a 35-year-old female with post-COVID dyspnea, showing improvements in pulmonary function test parameters including FVC, FEV1, FEF, and PEFR. The authors conclude that hot fomentation may be an effective complementary therapy for improving pulmonary function in post-COVID dyspnea patients.

This article describes integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine nursing interventions for a single patient with COVID-19 complicated by chronic cough. The case includes conventional nursing care combined with Chinese medicine techniques such as aromatherapy, herbal ointments, acupoint application, and music therapy to manage cough symptoms and improve quality of life.

Case report of a patient who developed bilateral pulmonary embolism 4.5 months after mild COVID-19 infection, with ongoing elevated D-dimer levels and exertional dyspnea. No treatment intervention is tested or evaluated; this is a passive clinical observation of a long COVID complication.

exclusion_reason: case_series with no control group and no systematic outcome measurement
summary: Case report of a 54-year-old patient with severe COVID-19 pneumonia who experienced recurrent hospital admissions and developed complications including sepsis, bronchitis, and drug-induced hyperglycemia. The paper documents the clinical course and multiple interventions (antibiotics, corticosteroids, oxygen support) but does not systematically evaluate treatment efficacy or outcomes.

Case report of a 40-year-old woman who developed dermatomyositis following long COVID with myalgia, weakness, and fatigue. Patient responded favorably to immunosuppressants, steroids, and intensive rehabilitation, achieving near-complete recovery.

This is a case report describing a single patient with Guillain-Barré syndrome following COVID-19 infection. While it documents a post-COVID complication, it does not study long COVID as defined (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Clinical case report of a patient with post-COVID gastrointestinal tract involvement presenting with diarrhea, vomiting, and progressive weight loss despite anti-coronavirus treatment. Describes diagnostic findings and treatment principles for GIT complications in the post-COVID period.

Case report of a 25-year-old female who developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with pulmonary fibrosis weeks after COVID-19 infection, requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Treatment with antivirals, chloroquine, antibiotics, and steroids resulted in good clinical outcome, highlighting emerging post-COVID complications and their management.

Case report of a 56-year-old diabetic male presenting with Adult Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-A) in the post-COVID phase, characterized by shock, heart failure, myopericarditis, and elevated inflammation markers. Treatment with IV immunoglobulin and steroids resulted in favorable clinical response, demonstrating immunomodulatory therapy as a potential intervention for post-COVID inflammatory complications.

A case report describing central pontine myelinolysis (CPM) as a complication in a post-COVID patient with hyponatremia correction. This is a single case report documenting a rare neurological complication rather than a treatment trial or systematic study.

A case report of a 48-year-old woman with long COVID-related neurocognitive dysfunction (brain fog) treated with EEG neurofeedback and goal-oriented cognitive training over 6 months. The patient showed improvement in long-term side effects and was able to return to work.

This case report describes a 62-year-old man who developed long COVID and Parkinson's disease following SARS-CoV-2 infection and received treatment with transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with art therapy. After 20 days of anodal tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex plus individual art therapy sessions, the patient showed improvement in long COVID and Parkinson's symptoms and returned to work.

Case report of a 42-year-old woman who developed ventricular arrhythmias 1-6 weeks after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection, documented with ECG and Holter monitoring showing spontaneous recovery by month 4. The paper advocates for long-term medical observation in non-hospitalized post-COVID patients but presents no treatment intervention or control group.

A case study of a visual artist with severe post-COVID-19 syndrome who received a 10-week comprehensive neurotherapy program combining neuropsychological rehabilitation, art therapy, and EEG-neurofeedback. The patient showed statistically significant reductions in anxiety, improvements in neurocognitive function, and was able to return to painting.

This case study describes a 67-year-old visual artist with long COVID (severe neuroCOVID following ICU admission and prolonged pharmacological coma) who received goal-oriented neuropsychological rehabilitation combined with EEG-neurofeedback. The patient showed marked improvement in neurocognitive dysfunctions and PTSD symptoms, with restoration of her ability to paint and improved quality of life.

Case study of a long COVID patient with persistent complications (fatigue, weakness, dizziness, diabetes, TIA) who underwent emergency carotid endarterectomy and endovascular stent placement (TCAR). SF-36 quality of life assessments showed significant improvement in physical function and overall HRQOL following surgical intervention.

Single-case study evaluating EEG neurofeedback training for dysexecutive syndrome in a long COVID patient who also underwent brain aneurysm surgery. The intervention significantly reduced executive dysfunction symptoms and improved quality of life, with improvements validated against normative databases.

This case study describes a 51-year-old visual artist who developed long neuro-COVID Parkinson's-like syndrome with motor and cognitive symptoms 4 months after acute COVID-19 infection. She received individualized neurotherapy combining EEG-Neurofeedback and art therapy, alongside dopaminergic and antidepressant medications, resulting in significant functional recovery and improved quality of life.

This is a detailed case report of a bilingual physician who developed semantic variant primary progressive aphasia (svPPA) 16 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with progressive cognitive and language decline over 2.5 years documented through neuropsychological testing and MRI. The paper is a single uncontrolled case study with no intervention or treatment evaluated, focused on describing the clinical and neuropathological presentation of long COVID-associated neurodegeneration rather than testing any therapeutic approach.

Case report describing spatial-visual memory disturbances in a 14-year-old girl following SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequent PANDAS syndrome diagnosis. The study documents neuropsychological assessment findings showing visuospatial dysfunction but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This case report describes rehabilitation outcomes for a single COVID-19 survivor who developed ARDS and ICU-acquired weakness during acute infection. While it documents a rehabilitation intervention, it is a case series (single case) with no control group and focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID sequelae.

Case report of a 53-year-old female patient who developed bilateral foot drop (peroneal and sciatic nerve damage) following severe COVID-19 with prolonged ICU admission. The paper describes clinical presentation and rehabilitation considerations but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a 62-year-old woman presenting with severe hypokalemia and muscular symptoms four months after COVID-19 diagnosis, attributed to post-COVID nephropathy with renal potassium losses. Treatment with intravenous potassium chloride, potassium-sparing diuretics, and supplementation achieved partial correction of serum potassium levels.

A case report of a 54-year-old male with post-COVID interstitial lung disease (ILD) treated with systemic corticosteroids (Prednisone 50 mg daily tapering to 10 mg maintenance). The patient showed significant clinical and functional improvement on PFTs and radiographic resolution of ground-glass opacities on follow-up HRCT.

Case report of a 13-year-old with multiple thromboses associated with COVID-19 during long-term follow-up, treated with cardiac surgery. Paper emphasizes unknown long-term effects of COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a clinical case description only.

A clinical observation describing the use of bioregulatory drugs in combination therapy for mixed-origin headaches in post-COVID patients with adaptation disorder. The treatment achieved significant pain reduction and improvement in anxiety and depression symptoms.

Case report of a young girl presenting with fever of unknown origin and cluster headache hypothesized to be associated with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), with dysregulation of the hypothalamus as the proposed mechanism. The patient showed clinical improvement following corticosteroid treatment.

A case study of a 62-year-old woman with severe post-acute COVID-19 who received an 8-week physiotherapeutic intervention combining pulmonary rehabilitation, aerobic and resistance training, and patient education. The patient showed substantial improvements in functional capacity (6MWT increased 750%, 30CST increased 380%), with complete resolution of dyspnea and fatigue and improved pulmonary function on spirometry.

Case report of a 63-year-old woman who developed multiple arterial thrombi 20 days after discharge from ICU for severe COVID-19 pneumonia and pulmonary embolism, requiring surgical and endovascular intervention. The case demonstrates persistent prothrombotic state post-COVID but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

This paper reports a single case of Horner's syndrome that developed in a 63-year-old male following COVID-19 hospitalization. While the neurological complication occurred after COVID-19, the paper focuses on diagnosis and management of Horner's syndrome rather than long COVID as a systemic condition, and does not study a treatment intervention.

A case report describing serial chest CT imaging findings in a patient who developed pulmonary fibrosis during recovery from severe COVID-19 pneumonia. The paper documents imaging features but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of an 80-year-old male who developed severe psychosis and attempted suicide following COVID-19 diagnosis, with symptoms persisting over six months. The paper documents the clinical presentation and discusses potential neuroinflammatory mechanisms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing a patient with post-COVID autoimmune-mediated encephalopathy associated with Caspr2 autoantibodies from a neurological division. The paper discusses neurological and neuromuscular manifestations of long COVID including autoimmune encephalopathies but does not present a treatment intervention or trial results.

This case report demonstrates a novel hyperpolarized xenon MRI protocol for assessing pulmonary physiology in long COVID patients, using unenriched xenon as a more accessible alternative to enriched xenon-129. The study shows successful dissolved phase imaging in two healthy subjects but presents preliminary findings without clinical outcomes or patient data.

This is a case report of an elderly female patient who developed acute coronary syndrome (heart attack) following acute COVID-19 infection, examining the thrombotic complications of active infection. The paper focuses on acute-phase cardiovascular complications rather than long COVID sequelae, and presents no treatment intervention or trial design.

Case report of a 36-year-old female with post-COVID-19 syndrome who experienced return of respiratory symptoms following reduction mammaplasty surgery. The paper describes a single clinical case and discusses the need for preoperative assessment in post-COVID patients, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

A case report of a 26-year-old woman with long COVID who presented with respiratory failure and was found to have a late pulmonary embolism over one year after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, despite being declared cured. The patient received antibiotic, anticoagulation, and supportive care but ultimately died, highlighting the risk of late thromboembolic complications in long COVID patients.

This is a clinical case report describing the experiences and prolonged symptoms of a 50-year-old male physician who developed severe COVID-19 in March 2020 and subsequently experienced long COVID with multiple system involvement including cognitive, psychiatric, neurological, and musculoskeletal manifestations. The paper is a qualitative case narrative rather than a systematic treatment evaluation or trial, focusing on patient experience and symptom documentation without evaluating a specific intervention or treatment outcome.

Case report describing a patient who developed new-onset psychosis and seizure disorder three months after COVID-19 infection. The paper presents clinical observations and calls for further research but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A case report of a 53-year-old female who developed Hashimoto's thyroiditis and severe autonomic dysfunction three months after acute COVID-19 infection. The authors recommend testing antithyroid antibodies in COVID-19 survivors and suggest early aggressive therapy for autonomic dysfunction, but present no treatment intervention or trial design.

A case report of a 55-year-old German male patient presenting with severe neuromuscular and psychological complications following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper describes the role of German long-COVID outpatient clinics in monitoring and providing comprehensive care for post-COVID patients, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

A case report of a 28-year-old man who developed acute ischemic stroke 2.5 months after COVID-19 infection, with underlying patent foramen ovale and congenital thrombophilia. The paper describes the clinical presentation and treatment outcome but is a single case report rather than a systematic study of a treatment intervention.

A case report describing diagnosis and surgical treatment of actinomycotic osteonecrosis of the maxilla in a post-COVID-19 patient. The patient received pentoxifylline, alpha tocopherol, and surgical debridement with fat pad closure, with no recurrence at 1-year follow-up.

A case study evaluating cardiorespiratory rehabilitation in a post-COVID-19 patient using physiotherapy intervention at a rehabilitation clinic. Results showed improvements in fatigue, dyspnea, cough, tremors, and respiratory/muscular function.

This case study describes an integrative management approach to post-COVID syndrome in a 42-year-old patient, combining antiviral drugs, respiratory supplements, nutrition, herbs, and lifestyle measures. The paper demonstrates the potential benefits of comprehensive multidisciplinary coordination in managing multiple post-COVID symptoms.

A clinical case report of a 32-year-old male who developed dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction (31%) following acute COVID-19 infection, presenting with post-COVID symptoms including cough, hemoptysis, and fatigue. The patient's condition improved with treatment and follow-up showed ejection fraction recovery to 53%, but represents a single case observation without control group or systematic treatment evaluation.

A case report of a 35-year-old woman with long COVID presenting with depression, exhaustion, recurrent fevers, and treatment-resistant skin boils that improved with high-dose lithium treatment (1.14 mmol/L serum level). The symptoms worsened when lithium levels were reduced to 0.8 mmol/L, suggesting lithium may be effective for post-COVID symptoms at higher concentrations.

Case report of a diabetic patient with severe acute COVID-19 managed in a hospital, discussing the management of COVID-19 in diabetic patients and associated complications. This paper focuses on acute COVID-19 infection and comorbidities, not long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

Case report of ozone therapy treatment for a severe acute COVID-19 pneumonia patient with pulmonary fibrosis. The paper documents radiologic regression and clinical improvement during and after hospitalization, but focuses on acute COVID-19 pneumonia rather than long COVID sequelae.

A case report of a long COVID patient with progressive neuroinflammation and demyelination, documenting a 14-month clinical course with imaging findings and elevated IL-18 cytokine levels. The patient received corticosteroid and planned rituximab immunotherapy, with elevated IL-18 identified as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for post-viral neuroinflammatory damage.

A case report of a single patient presenting with morphea (localized scleroderma) following two episodes of COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentation and laboratory findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or trial design.

Case report of a COVID-19 patient with recurring ventilator-associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia showing progressive antimicrobial resistance and T-cell activation. Documents immunological mechanisms in a post-acute COVID patient but is a single case report without treatment intervention or control group.

A case report of a 50-year-old man with long COVID presenting with PVCs and brain fog who received epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT), showing marked reduction in PVC burden on Holter monitoring and delayed improvement in cognitive function. The case suggests EAT may modulate autonomic dysfunction underlying both peripheral and central symptoms in long COVID.

This is a case report describing a single patient who developed acute myopericarditis 6-8 weeks after COVID-19 infection, presenting clinical and ECG findings. The paper documents a post-COVID cardiac complication but does not study any treatment or intervention.

Case report of a 37-year-old patient who developed bilateral pulmonary cavitary lesions in the weeks following severe COVID-19 pneumonia requiring hospitalization. The cavities resolved spontaneously over five months without intervention, illustrating a self-limited post-COVID pulmonary complication.

Case report of a patient who developed pericarditis with cardiac tamponade after acute COVID-19 resolution, presenting diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. The paper discusses management of pericardial disease as a late complication of COVID-19 but presents only a single case without intervention testing.

Case report of a single patient who developed multiple complications (deep vein thrombosis, endogenous endophthalmitis, empyema, post-inflammatory arthritis) in the 6 months following severe COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation. The paper documents the clinical presentation and timeline of these complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a patient presenting with STEMI three to four weeks after COVID-19 infection, illustrating thrombotic complications as a post-COVID sequela. No treatment intervention is tested or evaluated; this is a clinical observation of disease manifestation.

Case report of a 58-year-old COVID-19 patient who developed recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy and vocal cord paralysis two weeks after acute infection. The paper presents a single case with discussion of potential pathophysiology but does not study a treatment intervention.

Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with chest pain and breathlessness, subsequently diagnosed with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The paper highlights an association between long COVID syndrome and cardiac complications but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case report of a 38-year-old woman with post-COVID symptoms (fatigue, headaches, shortness of breath, brain fog) treated with enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP) therapy. Patient showed improvement in brain fog after one week and returned to pre-COVID health after five weeks of EECP treatment.

Case report of a 28-year-old male presenting with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) following acute COVID-19 infection, characterized by fever, rash, gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms. Patient recovered completely within 6 weeks after steroid therapy.

A case report of a 57-year-old female with long-COVID-associated POTS treated with enhanced external counterpulsation (EECP), showing improvements in fatigue, brain fog, functional capacity, and exercise tolerance after 15 sessions. This is the first reported use of EECP for COVID-19-associated POTS and demonstrates clinical utility warranting further investigation.

Case report of a 45-year-old male who developed reactive arthritis three weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with polyarthritis and elevated inflammatory markers. The patient was treated with oral corticosteroids, with symptom recurrence requiring a second course of therapy.

A case report describing saddle aortic embolism (lower abdominal aorta occlusion) occurring three days after discharge from severe COVID-19 pneumonia requiring mechanical ventilation. The patient was treated with emergency endovascular thrombectomy with symptom resolution, representing a rare post-acute sequela of COVID-19.

This paper presents a case report of a young female with a history of mild COVID-19 who developed acute pulmonary embolism with infarction five weeks post-infection, presenting with paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest. The case illustrates a serious thromboembolic sequela of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a patient who developed carotid artery thrombosis weeks after recovering from asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, presenting with stroke symptoms. The authors suggest COVID-19 infection-induced inflammation and hypercoagulability as risk factors for arterial thrombosis in the post-COVID period, and recommend prophylactic anticoagulation.

A case report of a 63-year-old male presenting with Guillain-Barré syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnosis but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or include quantitative outcome data.

This case report describes a 31-year-old patient who developed myopericarditis as a manifestation of long COVID syndrome two weeks after initial COVID-19 infection, confirmed by echocardiography, MRI, and cardiac scintigraphy. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by tapering prednisone, with gradual symptom resolution over one year.

Case report of acute transverse myelitis (ATM) occurring after COVID-19 infection in a female patient presenting with bilateral lower limb weakness and paresthesia. Patient was successfully treated with intravenous methylprednisolone, physical therapy, and bladder training with gradual improvement.

This paper reports a case of Lance-Adams syndrome (chronic post-hypoxic myoclonus) occurring as a delayed neurological complication of COVID-19 infection without preceding cardiac arrest. The authors discuss pathophysiological mechanisms linking COVID-19-induced hypoxia to myoclonus development and review various treatment strategies for managing this complication.

Case report of a post-COVID patient presenting with drug-refractory palpitations initially suspected as inappropriate sinus tachycardia, but confirmed as atrial tachycardia via electrophysiological study and successfully treated with ablation. Patient remained symptom-free at six-month follow-up without medication.

Case report of a patient with mild COVID-19 who developed ST-elevation myocardial infarction weeks later as a late complication. No treatment intervention was tested; this is a clinical observation of a complication without therapeutic evaluation.

Case report of an adult with acute Guillain-Barré syndrome following COVID-19 infection, accompanied by a literature review of 99 case reports, 38 reviews, and 2 meta-analyses examining the association between COVID-19 and GBS. The paper focuses on acute COVID-19 neurological complications rather than long COVID syndrome and is primarily a review rather than a treatment intervention study.

This case report describes a post-COVID-19 patient with MIS-A-like symptoms who clinically improved following tocilizumab and corticosteroid treatment. The paper demonstrates the therapeutic response to anti-inflammatory agents in a subset of long COVID patients with hyperinflammatory features.

An autobiographical case report by a healthcare worker describing her personal experience with COVID-19 and subsequent long COVID symptoms affecting physical and mental health. This is a first-person narrative account rather than a systematic study of treatment interventions.

Case report of a 26-year-old male with COVID-19-associated Miller Fisher syndrome presenting 10 weeks post-infection, treated with intravenous immunoglobulin. Most symptoms resolved within four days, with residual left-sided facial weakness at one-year follow-up.

Case report of a 28-year-old male with ischemic stroke involving the basilar artery following asymptomatic COVID-19 infection, with no other identifiable risk factors. Describes a rare thrombotic sequela of post-COVID status but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case report of a 20-year-old male who developed secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis eight weeks after COVID-19 infection, presenting with fatigue, fever, and abnormal lab findings. The paper documents clinical presentation and diagnosis of HLH as a post-COVID complication but does not describe any treatment intervention or outcomes.

A case report describing a 48-year-old woman who developed severe long-term sequelae including pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, and post-intubation tracheal stenosis following COVID-19 infection. The paper documents complications and discusses the role of cytokine storms but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

Case report of a patient who developed chronic demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) following COVID-19 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnosis of this rare autoimmune complication but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case report describes a middle-aged patient with remote COVID-19 infection who developed aortic thrombosis and ischemic stroke, treated with apixaban anticoagulation. The case illustrates a potential post-COVID hypercoagulable state and discusses anticoagulation management in this complication.

Case report describing recurrent pericarditis with pericardial effusion occurring more than one year after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection in a single patient. The case highlights that pericarditis can emerge as a delayed complication of COVID-19 with persistent symptoms extending beyond the first year post-infection.

Case report of a 33-year-old male presenting three weeks after COVID-19 recovery with proteinuric acute kidney injury found to be IgA nephropathy on renal biopsy. The paper describes a post-acute COVID complication but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 65-year-old post-COVID patient who developed methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia with widespread secondary infections including abscesses and cervical spine discitis/osteomyelitis. The case highlights potential post-COVID susceptibility to unusual secondary bacterial infections but provides no treatment intervention or outcome comparisons.

Case report of a 22-year-old woman with PANDAS who developed severe pneumonia and myocarditis one month after COVID-19 infection, responsive to high-dose steroids. While occurring post-COVID, the paper focuses on acute post-infectious complications rather than long COVID syndrome (persistent symptoms weeks to months later), and is a single case report without treatment intervention design.

Case report of a patient who developed Tietze's syndrome (inflammatory disorder of costal cartilages with chest pain) following asymptomatic COVID-19 infection. Treatment with anti-inflammatory medications and colchicine resulted in complete symptom resolution, demonstrating a potential post-COVID complication and its successful management.

A case series reporting successful resolution of persistent anosmia and dysgeusia in a long COVID patient treated with stellate ganglion block (SGB), a procedure that reduces sympathetic nervous system activity. The authors propose that SGB may address the autonomic dysregulation underlying smell and taste disturbances in long COVID.

Case report of a 30-year-old woman who developed relapsing immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) following COVID-19 infection, experiencing nine relapses over 10.5 months despite treatment with prednisone and IVIG. The study documents the clinical course and treatment response, highlighting ITP as a potential serious complication of COVID-19 infection requiring early therapeutic intervention.

Case report of an 89-year-old patient who developed neutropenia and myositis one month after acute COVID-19 infection, presenting with severe muscle pain and functional impairment. Treatment with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor and prednisolone was effective for managing the neutropenia and myositis complications.
Case report describing a single patient with myelitis during acute COVID-19 infection. Does not study long COVID (post-acute sequelae) or any treatment intervention.

Case report of a long-term care patient who developed bilateral deep vein thrombosis six weeks after COVID-19 recovery, with persistently elevated D-dimer levels. Describes clinical presentation and suggests that patients with elevated D-dimers post-COVID should be screened for thromboembolic complications.

A case report of bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis occurring 48 hours after mechanical ventilation for severe COVID-19, manifesting as a long COVID symptom. The patient underwent tracheostomy and experienced persistent vocal cord dysfunction for eight weeks, illustrating a rare post-viral neurological complication.

A case report of a 60-year-old male who developed bilateral hip avascular necrosis (AVN) requiring hip arthroplasty, 10 months following severe COVID-19 infection. The paper describes the clinical presentation and diagnostic workup but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a descriptive case report of a long COVID sequela.

Case report of a 73-year-old patient with post-COVID infection who developed secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) 11 months after initial COVID-19 infection, presenting with persistent fever, lethargy, and cognitive changes over 5 months. The patient was treated with dexamethasone and intravenous immune globulin (IVIG) but deteriorated and died, illustrating the severe complications and high mortality associated with secondary HLH in post-COVID patients.

Case report and literature review of new-onset myasthenia gravis (MG) as a rare post-COVID-19 sequela, presenting one patient case and summarizing 15 previously reported cases. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnostic findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or study outcomes.

Case report of a patient who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) during severe acute COVID-19 infection requiring mechanical ventilation. While the patient was treated with pulse steroids and immunoglobulins, this describes acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID (persistent post-infection symptoms weeks-months later).

summary: This case report documents the use of stellate ganglion block (SGB), a neuronal blocking procedure, to treat long COVID symptoms in a previously healthy patient. The patient experienced improvements in fatigue, post-exertional malaise, shortness of breath, and gastrointestinal symptoms, suggesting SGB may be a potential treatment for autonomic dysregulation in long COVID.

A case study of a 21-year-old long COVID patient with persistent cough treated with epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT), a Japanese treatment involving zinc chloride application. EAT performed weekly for three months eliminated residual SARS-CoV-2 RNA from the epipharyngeal mucosa, reduced inflammation, and decreased proinflammatory cytokine expression.

A case report describing a post-COVID-19 patient with multisystem inflammatory syndrome presenting with cardiomyopathy, hepatitis, and acute kidney injury who recovered with steroid treatment but developed persistent complications. The paper emphasizes the need for more research on long-term sequelae and pathophysiology of COVID-19 complications.

Case report of a post-COVID-19 patient presenting with osmotic demyelination syndrome (ODS) following hyponatremia correction, manifesting as central pontine myelinolysis and extrapontine myelinolysis. The paper describes clinical presentation, imaging findings, and differential diagnosis considerations but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

Case report of a 59-year-old woman who developed colonic strictures and intestinal obstruction following recovery from COVID-19 pneumonia, requiring surgical intervention. The paper documents a rare post-COVID gastrointestinal complication but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

A case report of a 39-year-old male with post-viral POTS treated with craniosacral therapy (compression of the fourth ventricle/CV4 technique). The treatment led to successful remission of the patient's symptoms, proposing craniosacral therapy as a management modality for post-COVID POTS.

Case report of an 80-year-old woman who developed acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) during acute COVID-19 pneumonia, not following it. The patient received steroids and plasma exchange but ultimately died, with no focus on long COVID or post-acute sequelae.

Case report of a 65-year-old man hospitalized with severe acute COVID-19 who subsequently developed Sjögren's syndrome. The paper discusses COVID-19 as a potential mediator of autoimmunity but focuses on acute infection and post-acute autoimmune sequelae, not long COVID symptom intervention or treatment.

Case report of a 67-year-old post-COVID patient who presented with acute cerebral infarction and saddle pulmonary embolism one month after COVID-19 infection and was treated with thrombolytics and mechanical thrombectomy. The report documents delayed thromboembolic complications and advocates for prophylactic antithrombotic therapy in high-risk post-COVID patients.

Case report of a single asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infected patient with prolonged viral shedding and persistent anosmia and ageusia symptoms. No intervention or treatment was evaluated; the study is a descriptive case follow-up without therapeutic evaluation.

A case report describing a 21-year-old male who developed new-onset ulcerative colitis one week after a second COVID-19 infection. The paper raises awareness of potential autoimmune gastrointestinal complications following COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a patient who developed transient premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) following COVID-19 infection, associated with anti-ovarian antibodies, and was treated with oral contraceptives and corticosteroids followed by IVF. The case suggests COVID-19 may transiently impact ovarian function through autoimmune mechanisms.

A case report describing brain fog as a neurological manifestation of long COVID, discussing potential pathogenic mechanisms including neuroinflammation and mast cell activation. This is a single case presentation with no treatment intervention or control group, therefore excluded from the trials analysis.

A three-year longitudinal case report of a 26-year-old medical student documenting the progression from acute COVID-19 infection through long COVID symptomology to near-total remission. The paper chronicles multiple treatment attempts and their outcomes in a single patient, contributing observational evidence on long COVID natural history and treatment response.

This paper describes a case of Tietze syndrome (costal joint inflammation) occurring in the post-COVID-19 period in a 38-year-old male. While it documents a potential post-COVID complication, it is a single case report without treatment intervention or controlled comparison, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.

Case report of a 66-year-old woman who developed shortness of breath seven weeks post-COVID infection, treated with prednisone, albuterol, and ipratropium with symptomatic relief. The paper documents a clinical presentation of post-COVID sequelae resembling acute asthma exacerbation and discusses potential mechanisms involving immune dysregulation.

Case report of a 47-year-old patient who developed dilated cardiomyopathy with left ventricular thrombus six months after COVID-19 infection. Describes clinical presentation and bedside echocardiography findings without evaluating a treatment intervention.

A single case report of an 81-year-old patient who developed secondary MRSA pneumonia and empyema weeks after acute COVID-19 pneumonia. While the infection occurred post-COVID discharge, the paper focuses on acute bacterial sepsis management rather than long COVID syndrome or any long COVID-specific intervention.

Case report of a 91-year-old female who developed chorea two weeks after mild COVID-19 infection. Describes a rare neurological manifestation of post-COVID syndrome without any treatment intervention or trial design.

A case report describing a 53-year-old woman who developed postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with discussion of post-COVID cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction mechanisms. The paper does not evaluate a treatment intervention but rather presents a clinical case and discusses management options in general terms without outcome data from a specific cohort or trial.

Case report of a patient who developed sterile osteomyelitis consistent with SAPHO syndrome 21 days post-COVID-19 infection, initially misdiagnosed as bacterial infection and treated with vancomycin. The case presents a potential post-COVID autoimmune complication and discusses diagnostic classification systems for SAPHO syndrome as a possible sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

This is a single case report of a 16-year-old presenting with severe neurological complications (reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome and stroke) two weeks after acute COVID-19 pneumonia. While it documents long COVID neurological sequelae, it is a case report of one patient receiving standard clinical care, not a treatment trial or intervention study.

This paper reports a case of pulmonary cryptococcosis developing as a complication of steroid treatment for post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis. It is a single case report describing an adverse outcome rather than a controlled study of an intervention.

A case report of a 42-year-old woman who developed bilateral avascular necrosis of the femoral head with symptom onset three months after COVID-19 infection. The authors suggest a potential link between COVID-19 and osteonecrosis but present only a single case without treatment intervention or comparative analysis.

This paper reports a single case of takotsubo cardiomyopathy in a post-COVID patient, documenting the clinical presentation and outcomes. It does not evaluate any treatment intervention, but rather describes an observed cardiac complication associated with long COVID.

Case report of a 60-year-old patient with COVID-19-associated autoimmune encephalitis who developed cognitive deficits and behavioral symptoms, treated with acute and chronic intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy over two years. The paper documents symptom improvement correlating with changes in immunological parameters and reviews the literature on IVIG treatment for long COVID neuropsychiatric sequelae.

This case report describes a single patient with cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP) presenting seven weeks after COVID-19 recovery, highlighting a potential pulmonary sequela of post-COVID syndrome. The paper is excluded because it is a case report of a single patient without an intervention or treatment being evaluated.

This is a pediatric case report of acute rheumatic fever (ARF) occurring one month after COVID-19 infection in a single patient, not a study of long COVID. The paper documents improvement after three months of treatment but does not study long COVID as a primary focus.

Case report of a COVID-19 patient who developed bilateral pneumothoraces from delayed rupture of pneumatoceles during acute infection. Describes the rare pathology and etiological hypotheses, not a long COVID study.

Case report of a 90-year-old patient who developed immune thrombocytopenia purpura (ITP) several weeks after COVID-19 infection, highlighting ITP as a potential post-infection complication. The patient received treatment for ITP with effective clinical outcomes, demonstrating the importance of monitoring for hematologic complications during the post-COVID period.

Case report of a 48-year-old female who developed MADSAM (Lewis-Sumner syndrome), a rare demyelinating neuropathy, following COVID-19 infection, presenting with asymmetric neurological symptoms including shortness of breath, fatigue, and motor/sensory deficits. Patient improved with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment, contributing to limited evidence on neurological complications and treatment response in long COVID.

Case report of myopericarditis presenting as a delayed cardiac complication in a young patient following COVID-19 infection, with elevated troponin and ECG changes. Demonstrates importance of identifying cardiac sequelae in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 50-year-old woman with post-COVID organizing pneumonia who developed subacute bacterial endocarditis with multiple splenic and liver abscesses, successfully treated with antibiotics. This is a single case report describing rare complications in an immunosuppressed patient rather than a treatment intervention study.

A case report of a 21-year-old male with post-acute COVID-19 encephalopathy presenting with psychotic symptoms, treated with antiviral and steroid pulse therapy. Brain imaging (SPECT and PET) revealed functional alterations in cerebellar and occipital regions that resolved over six months without psychopharmacotherapy.

Case report describing non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) occurring seven months after COVID-19 infection in a post-menopausal female. The authors discuss the plausibility of a link between COVID-19-associated coagulopathy and ophthalmologic complications but present no intervention or treatment outcomes.

This case report describes a 77-year-old patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia and persistent COVID-19 infection causing post-COVID pneumonia, who was successfully treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). The case emphasizes IVIG as a potential therapeutic intervention for post-COVID patients with hypogammaglobulinemia and provides a literature review on COVID-19 infection in CLL patients.

First case report of neurofeedback treatment for brain fog in a long COVID patient, using a Z-score neurofeedback technique targeting EEG abnormalities. Patient showed improvement in cognitive symptoms, pain, and anxiety with measurable changes in alpha and beta brain wave activity.

This case report describes a long COVID patient who developed aseptic osteonecrosis of the femoral head following high-dose corticosteroid therapy (dexamethasone) used to treat acute COVID-19, with onset occurring within three months. The study examines the relationship between corticosteroid exposure in COVID-19 treatment and the rapid development of this serious complication compared to non-COVID corticosteroid use.

This case report describes a 58-year-old patient who developed pulmonary inflammatory pseudotumors (PIPs) as a post-COVID-19 complication and was successfully treated with corticosteroid therapy. The paper documents the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and management of this rare post-viral inflammatory condition.

A case report describing bilateral avascular necrosis of the femoral head in a young male patient following COVID-19 infection without corticosteroid exposure. The paper documents a rare musculoskeletal complication of acute COVID-19 but does not study any treatment intervention or long COVID sequelae.

Case report of a female with post-COVID gastrointestinal symptoms (GERD-like presentation) for 18 months who was diagnosed with chronic pulmonary embolism. The patient's reflux symptoms resolved with anticoagulation therapy, highlighting the importance of considering PE in post-COVID GI presentations.

Case report of a 55-year-old woman who developed anti-synthetase syndrome (ASS) one month after COVID-19 infection, presenting with dyspnea, fever, rash, and interstitial pneumonia. The patient's condition improved with treatment including prednisolone, tacrolimus, and intravenous cyclophosphamide, highlighting ASS as a potential post-COVID autoimmune complication.

A case report of a 74-year-old patient who developed non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) five months after COVID-19 infection, resulting in acute respiratory distress syndrome and multi-organ failure. The case highlights potential long-term cardiovascular complications associated with past COVID-19 infection but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 24-year-old male who developed diabetic ketoacidosis and new-onset type 1 diabetes mellitus 12 weeks after COVID-19 infection, highlighting post-infectious autoimmune sequelae. The paper presents a single case without control group or intervention testing, serving as a clinical observation rather than a treatment trial.

Case report of a patient who developed post-COVID-vaccination syndrome with thrombosis and thrombocytopenia, later presenting with dysautonomia symptoms (POTS, tremor, postural instability) and elevated anti-GPCR autoantibodies. Therapeutic plasma exchange was used as treatment, resulting in clinical improvement of the neurological and autonomic symptoms.

This paper presents a case report of myasthenia gravis triggered by COVID-19 infection in a 30-year-old woman who developed a myasthenic crisis during hospitalization. The paper is primarily a case report with literature review of MG complications post-COVID, not a treatment trial or intervention study.

This case report describes an 83-year-old man who developed probable Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) several months after COVID-19 infection, with progressive cognitive decline and memory impairment. The paper documents the association between COVID-19 and neurodegenerative disease but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a patient who developed painless thyroiditis and new-onset atrial fibrillation following COVID-19 recovery. Describes a rare complication and clinical presentation but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A case report describing a 42-year-old male who developed bilateral facial paralysis from COVID-associated Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) five weeks post-infection, confirmed by CSF analysis. The patient received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) treatment with appropriate therapeutic response, demonstrating treatment of a rare neurological post-COVID complication.

A case report describing posterior circulation infarction in a 39-year-old patient three months after severe COVID-19. The paper discusses pathophysiology and anticoagulation therapy for COVID-related thrombotic complications but presents observational clinical findings rather than evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

A case report describing the multisystemic manifestations of long COVID in a 19-year-old female across cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, neurological, and musculoskeletal domains several months post-infection. The paper documents the patient's clinical experience and recovery process but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

A case report of axonal Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) occurring in a 46-year-old female following mild COVID-19 infection, describing diagnostic challenges and management. This is a single case report, not a treatment trial or comparative study.

A case report of an 81-year-old man who developed very-late-onset myasthenia gravis (MG) four months after COVID-19 pneumonia, presenting with dysarthria, dyspnea, diplopia, and oropharyngeal dysphagia. The patient was treated with pyridostigmine, methylprednisolone, and IVIG therapy, illustrating a rare neurological autoimmune complication of long COVID and the need for vigilance in managing post-viral autoimmune conditions.

Case report of a 59-year-old patient with post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A) and elevated suPAR levels treated with anakinra, an IL-1 receptor antagonist. The treatment effectively resolved MIS-A symptoms, suggesting interleukin-1 inhibitors may be beneficial for managing this potentially life-threatening post-COVID complication.

Case report of a 64-year-old patient with persistent lupus anticoagulant positivity and post-COVID-19 symptoms (fatigue, taste disturbance, numbness) lasting over 10 months following mild COVID-19 infection. The paper describes clinical findings and laboratory abnormalities but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

Case report describing a 37-year-old man who developed acquired angioedema following COVID-19 infection with no prior history of hereditary angioedema. The paper documents clinical presentation and recurrent angioedema episodes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or compare treatment outcomes.

Case report and literature review of new-onset Graves' disease following COVID-19 infection, analyzing 28 similar cases from 2020-2024 with varied onset times and severity. Does not present original treatment intervention data, functioning primarily as a clinical case presentation and literature synthesis.

A case report describing a 21-year-old woman who developed post-COVID-19 tenosynovitis following multiple COVID-19 infections, with pain in hand joints and upper extremities. Her condition improved with combined treatment approaches, highlighting the need for further research into long-term musculoskeletal complications of long COVID.

Case report of acute macular neuroretinopathy occurring one week after acute COVID-19 infection in a 24-year-old female. The paper documents the clinical presentation and imaging findings but explicitly states there is no evidence-based treatment and the patient was monitored without intervention.

A qualitative literature review examining a potential pathogenic pathway linking COVID-19 infection to secondary acute myeloid leukemia (AML), prompted by a case report of AML diagnosis following COVID-19. The authors draw parallels to virus-associated lymphomas but conduct no original research or treatment evaluation.

Case report of a woman who developed late-onset idiopathic generalized epilepsy with absence status epilepticus following mild COVID-19 infection. While the paper describes treatment with antiepileptic medications (levetiracetam, valproic acid, lamotrigine), it is a single case report documenting a potential neurological complication of acute COVID-19, not a study of long COVID treatment or intervention trial.

This case report describes a 31-year-old patient who developed autoimmune rhombencephalitis two weeks after COVID-19 infection and was treated with high-dose corticosteroids over four weeks, resulting in excellent clinical recovery. The findings support immunotherapy as a potential treatment for post-COVID-19 autoimmune neurological complications.

Secondary analysis of a case report examining qEEG neurofeedback treatment for COVID-19 brain fog in a single 34-year-old female patient. The treatment showed changes in brainwave patterns and patient-reported improvements in attention, memory, and anxiety, though findings are limited to one case and require validation in larger studies.

A case report of a 46-year-old COVID-19 survivor presenting with persistent dyspnea, fatigue, and chest pain four months post-infection, found to have myocardial fibrosis on cardiac imaging consistent with prior myocarditis. The patient was managed with antihypertensive treatment with good blood pressure control at follow-up.

A case report of a 57-year-old man with long COVID who received bioelectric meridian therapy (BMT) over six months and reported improvements in cognition, muscle power, sensation, and quality of life. The case illustrates potential benefits of integrative therapeutic approaches for managing post-COVID symptoms.

A case report describing a 46-year-old female with recurrent oropharyngeal lesions and systemic complications (pulmonary emboli, dysphagia, hemoptysis) occurring over five years following COVID-19 infection, attributed to atypical vasculitis, autoimmune condition, or infection. The paper documents clinical presentation and diagnostic challenges but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

This paper presents a single case report of rhabdomyolysis with discordant CK and myoglobin elevations occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection. While it documents a post-infection complication, it focuses on acute muscle injury mechanisms during the immediate post-infection period rather than long COVID (which requires persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection) and does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Case report of a 57-year-old man who developed vestibular neuritis following COVID-19 infection, with follow-up testing showing typical recovery patterns but persistent postural instability and orthostatic hypotension. The paper documents the time course of vestibular recovery but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a 31-year-old woman who developed heterotopic ossification in hip and knee joints after acute COVID-19 pneumonia requiring mechanical ventilation. Treatment with indomethacin and etidronate disodium resulted in clinical improvement, though the paper addresses acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID syndrome.

A case report describing a 58-year-old woman with post-COVID-19 autoimmune encephalitis who showed remarkable improvement after plasmapheresis treatment following failure of intravenous steroid therapy. The paper demonstrates the potential effectiveness of plasmapheresis as a treatment for severe post-COVID neurological complications.

A case report of an 11-year-old with posterior scleritis and serous retinal detachment occurring one year after COVID-19 infection, suggesting a potential delayed ocular manifestation. The patient was treated with topical corticosteroids and NSAIDs with complete symptom resolution, highlighting post-viral inflammatory responses affecting the eye.

Case report of a patient who developed inflammatory myopathy with dermatomyositis-MCTD overlap features following COVID-19 infection. Describes clinical presentation and highlights the importance of recognizing and treating post-COVID autoimmune complications.

A case report of an immunocompetent adult who developed post-COVID myoclonus-ataxia syndrome and showed rapid recovery with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) after minimal response to corticosteroids. The case highlights individualized treatment strategies for rare post-COVID neurological complications and the impact of healthcare barriers on treatment access.

This case report describes a 71-year-old woman who developed persistent urinary urgency following COVID-19 recovery and was successfully treated with oxybutynin. The paper reviews emerging evidence on COVID-associated cystitis as a long COVID sequela, discussing pathophysiologic mechanisms involving inflammatory cytokine release and viral receptor expression in the bladder.

This case report describes a 25-year-old woman with post-COVID-19 syndrome presenting with chest pain, dyspnea, and myocardial dysfunction, found to have MTHFR and prothrombin II gene mutations contributing to endothelial dysfunction. Treatment with anticoagulation (apixaban), aspirin, folic acid, B-complex vitamins, bisoprolol, and trimetazidine resulted in clinical improvement and reduced angina frequency at one-year follow-up.

A case report of a 78-year-old patient with atrial fibrillation who developed pulmonary emboli one month after recovering from acute COVID-19 pneumonia, despite warfarin anticoagulation. The case illustrates delayed thromboembolic complications in post-COVID patients and discusses the need for extended anticoagulation strategies, but does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Case report of a single patient who developed DRESS syndrome (drug-induced hypersensitivity) as an adverse reaction to pirfenidone, an anti-fibrotic medication prescribed for post-COVID-19 fibrosis. The patient improved with steroid tapering, illustrating an important safety concern for this treatment approach.

Case report of a 73-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes who developed executive dysfunction and cognitive impairment after COVID-19 infection, manifesting as inability to manage her insulin pump safely. The case describes clinical management and transition from CSII to MDI therapy, highlighting post-COVID functional decline in older adults with comorbidities.

A case report of a 45-year-old nurse with post-acute long COVID who underwent a tailor-made pulmonary rehabilitation program. The rehabilitation intervention showed improvement in functional capacity, quality of life, anxiety, and depression measured by ISWT, WHOQOL-BREF, and DASS-21.

A retrospective case study of a long COVID patient with autoimmune hepatitis markers who received lutein supplementation via extra virgin olive oil. After 12 months of dietary intervention, autoimmune hepatitis markers normalized and chronic fatigue and muscle pain improved.

A case report of a 44-year-old female with long COVID presenting with debilitating fatigue and neurologic symptoms, examining her complex medical history including EBV infection and chronic fatigue syndrome. The paper proposes treatment approaches to address the neurologic manifestations of post-acute SARS-CoV-2 sequelae.

This paper describes a case of long COVID syndrome presenting as toxic encephalopathy in a beta thalassemia patient, highlighting the synergistic effects of SARS-CoV-2-mediated neuroinflammation and ferritin overload. It is a single case report without treatment intervention or control group, thus excluded as a case study rather than a treatment trial.

A case study of a 50-year-old woman who developed idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) three months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with ecchymosis, petechiae, and thrombocytopenia. The paper describes clinical presentation, diagnostic findings (bone marrow examination, lab results), and provides a literature review on thrombocytopenia mechanisms in COVID-19, but does not evaluate or report outcomes of any treatment intervention.

Case report of a single patient with acute COVID-19 pneumonia who developed pulmonary embolism post-infection. This describes acute complications during active COVID-19 illness, not long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks/months after infection).

Case report of necrotizing fasciitis of the breast with leukemoid reaction in a female patient following COVID-19 infection in rural central India. Documents a rare post-COVID complication but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A case report describing intranasal ketamine treatment for a long COVID patient with severe depression and suicidality. The patient received 4 doses of intranasal ketamine and showed rapid improvement in depressive symptoms and complete resolution of suicidal ideation without major adverse events.

This case-control study examines cerebrospinal fluid markers of neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier disruption in long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms. The study is observational and does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-control study examines pathological features of COVID-19-related chronic bilateral dacryoadenitis by comparing lacrimal gland tissue from a patient with COVID-19 to a control patient without COVID-19. The findings show SARS-CoV-2-positive inflammatory cells and glandular damage in the COVID-19 case, suggesting chronic dacryoadenitis as a long COVID-associated ophthalmic aftereffect.

A retrospective case report describing the use of Clinical Emotional Freedom Techniques (EFT) to treat parosmia (distorted sense of smell) in a single long COVID patient over three sessions. The patient showed improvement in symptom tolerance and quality of life, enabling return to normal activities including eating and work.

Case-control study examining whether Paxlovid reduces the risk of long COVID smell and taste disorders in 846 patients (423 treated, 423 untreated). Results show that early Paxlovid intervention was significantly associated with lower rates of long-term olfactory/gustatory changes (p < 0.001), though acute symptoms initially were more common in the Paxlovid group.

Case report of a CKD patient who developed rapid renal function deterioration, hair loss, and wart remission following COVID-19 infection in December 2022. The patient progressed to uremic stage requiring peritoneal dialysis, with partial hair regrowth and stable renal function at 8-month follow-up.

A case report of an occupational health trainee with long COVID who developed and implemented a self-directed rehabilitation plan combining progressive physical fitness training with workplace adjustments. The case demonstrates that structured, individualized rehabilitation approaches can enable successful return-to-work for long COVID patients.

This retrospective case-control study compares autonomic, cerebrovascular, and neuropathic features in 9 PASC patients versus POTS and healthy controls. It characterizes multisystem involvement in long COVID but does not evaluate or test any intervention or treatment.

This case series describes a cognitive rehabilitation intervention delivered in a group setting to 6 long COVID patients with cognitive symptoms over 20 sessions. The study found high engagement (80% attendance) and qualitatively reports that group participation enhanced motivation through peer support and shared experiences.

A case report documenting post-COVID-19 multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A) and Bell's palsy in a young adult. The paper illustrates potential autoimmune complications in the early post-COVID period but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series of 3 long COVID patients with cognitive impairment (brain fog) undergoing FDG-PET imaging, revealing hypometabolic areas in the brainstem/pons. The study suggests locus coeruleus dysfunction may partly explain cognitive disorders but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series describes three patients with isolated dysphagia following COVID-19 infection who tested positive for anti-ganglioside antibodies, suggesting a possible autoimmune variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome. The paper reports clinical presentations and laboratory findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 32-year-old female who developed cerebral venous thrombosis 20 days after acute COVID-19 infection, presenting with acute dementia-like cognitive decline and headache. While the paper discusses treatment with anticoagulation, it is a single case report describing an acute COVID-19 complication, not a long COVID study or intervention trial.

Case report of a 17-year-old girl with telogen effluvium (hair loss) occurring 2-12 weeks after suspected COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentation and diagnostic findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a patient with severe COVID-19 who presented with symptoms mimicking cholangiocarcinoma after ERCP. The paper highlights the importance of considering post-COVID-19 syndrome in the differential diagnosis of biliary obstruction symptoms.

Two case reports of acute reactive arthritis occurring 15-20 days after COVID-19 infection, both resolving with NSAIDs and analgesics. This is a descriptive case series without treatment evaluation or control group, documenting a post-COVID sequela rather than studying a treatment intervention.

This is a case report describing the clinical presentation and multisystem manifestations of post-COVID syndrome in individual patient(s). It does not study a treatment intervention and lacks the structured data needed for the trials meta-analysis.

Case report describing a patient with Down syndrome who developed long COVID following acute COVID-19 hospitalization, highlighting increased vulnerability in this population. The paper documents clinical presentation and outcomes but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 41-year-old female with post-COVID-19 condition presenting with severe insomnia persisting 6 months after acute infection. This is a single case study with no treatment intervention or comparison group, making it unsuitable for meta-analysis of intervention trials.

A case report describing a long COVID patient treated with nitazoxanide and other antiviral medications, proposing that persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection may underlie long COVID symptoms. The author argues antivirals could be a potential treatment approach for long COVID patients globally.

Case report of a 41-year-old woman with long COVID who self-administered psilocybin and MDMA and reported significant symptomatic improvement. The authors note that long COVID lacks effective treatment options and call for future research into the safety and efficacy of psychedelic-assisted therapy.

This cross-sectional case series of 15 post-COVID patients examines the relationship between antinuclear antibodies and joint pain in post-COVID syndrome. The study investigates potential autoimmune mechanisms underlying musculoskeletal symptoms in long COVID.

Case series of 32 long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) followed for ~159 days, evaluating treatment approaches including β-blockers and psychiatric interventions. Results showed improvement in heart rate, performance status, and employment/education status in 94% of patients, attributed to treatment effects and spontaneous recovery.

A case series of 14 patients with biopsy-proven post-COVID myoendocarditis occurring 2-10 months after acute infection, characterized by SARS-CoV-2 persistence and elevated antiheart antibodies. Treatment with corticosteroids and chronic heart failure therapy resulted in improved left ventricular ejection fraction from 28% to 47%.

Case report of a 23-year-old woman presenting with depression and long COVID in whom idiopathic ventricular tachycardia was diagnosed. The paper describes a single clinical case with no intervention or treatment being studied.

This retrospective case series describes 44 patients initially suspected of having long COVID at a specialized outpatient clinic, of whom 30 were ultimately diagnosed with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 mimic conditions and 14 with alternative diseases. The study focuses on identifying differential diagnoses rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

Case report of a pediatric patient who developed cerebellar ataxia following COVID-19 recovery. This is a single case report, not a treatment trial, and therefore does not meet inclusion criteria for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

A case report describing a patient who developed new-onset sarcoidosis following long COVID. The paper speculates on potential links between sustained inflammation in long COVID and autoimmune conditions but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

This paper presents a clinical case report of a 63-year-old male with Good's syndrome who experienced severe COVID-19 infection and recurrent symptoms, combined with a systematic review of Good's syndrome cases globally. While the patient had recurrent COVID-19 symptoms, the paper is primarily focused on Good's syndrome diagnosis and management rather than long COVID as a distinct condition, and it is structured as a literature review rather than a treatment intervention study.

Case report of a post-COVID-19 myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in an immunocompetent patient that responded dramatically to intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) treatment. The patient showed significant neurological improvement within 17 days of receiving 5 days of IVIg therapy, with resolution of myoclonus and ataxia.

Multicenter case series of 27 Parkinson's disease patients with COVID-19, documenting post-COVID-19 syndrome prevalence and symptoms including motor worsening, cognitive disturbances, and fatigue. No intervention was tested; this is a descriptive case series characterizing long COVID manifestations in PD patients.

Retrospective case series of 13 long COVID patients with small fiber neuropathy (SFN), confirmed by skin biopsy in 6 cases, who developed new-onset paresthesias within 2 months post-infection. Nine patients received symptomatic neuropathy treatment with symptom control achieved in 7/9 (77.8%), suggesting SFN treatment is effective for this long COVID manifestation.

A case report describing a male patient with post-COVID-19 encephalopathy presenting with psychotic symptoms, delirium, and sexually inappropriate behavior. The paper documents clinical presentation, imaging findings, and theoretical discussion of autoimmune mechanisms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 55-year-old female with COVID-19 who developed severe and prolonged neuropsychiatric symptoms including delusion, psychomotor excitement, and encephalopathy despite mild respiratory infection. Patient showed improvement in consciousness and cytokine levels after steroid pulse therapy, though cognitive, motor, and fatigue symptoms persisted, demonstrating that mild COVID-19 can cause severe post-COVID neuropsychiatric sequelae treatable with corticosteroids.

This case report describes a 41-year-old woman who developed neurological manifestations and jugular vein thrombosis 24 hours after COVID-19 vaccination, three months post-SARS-CoV-2 infection. Laboratory findings suggest inflammatory immune components rather than vaccine-induced thrombotic thrombocytopenia, proposing thrombosis as a sequela of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

A case report of a 32-year-old woman with long COVID-related cognitive impairment treated with extended-release guanfacine, showing improvements in attention, working memory, and executive function over 6 months. The study demonstrates potential therapeutic benefit of guanfacine for cognitive dysfunction in long COVID patients.

Case report of a 53-year-old woman who developed trichotillomania (compulsive hair pulling) as a neuropsychiatric manifestation of long COVID, successfully treated with escitalopram. The patient showed significant improvement with gradual hair regrowth over approximately 3 months of hospitalization.

Case report of a 35-year-old patient who developed brain fog and cognitive impairment approximately 2 months after COVID-19 infection, presenting with concentration difficulties and work errors. The patient was monitored without medication and showed spontaneous improvement in cognitive function over 11 months post-infection.

Retrospective chart review of 29 children presenting to pulmonary clinic with persistent respiratory symptoms 1.3-6.7 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Study characterized respiratory sequelae including exertional dyspnea (96.6%), cough (51.7%), and exercise intolerance (48.3%), with normal spirometry but abnormal 6-minute walk test results in most tested children.

This pilot study assessed lung perfusion using 99mTc-MAA SPECT/CT imaging in 14 children with long COVID who had abnormal cardiopulmonary exercise testing results. Six of 14 children (42.8%) showed lung perfusion defects without structural CT abnormalities, suggesting endothelial dysfunction may occur in a subset of pediatric long COVID patients.

Post-mortem analysis of 27 patients who died after apparent COVID-19 recovery, revealing persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection in lung tissue despite negative PCR tests. Findings demonstrate viral persistence in specific cell types and lung pathology consistent with long COVID sequelae, though no treatment intervention was studied.

National survey and case series describing the occurrence and clinical features of long-COVID in Dutch children aged 2-18 years. Study identifies 89 suspected cases with fatigue, dyspnea, and concentration difficulties as primary complaints, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A case report of a 32-year-old woman with bipolar disorder who developed ME/CFS post-COVID and was treated with corticosteroids, demonstrating that high-potency glucocorticoid agents triggered psychiatric symptoms while lower-potency hydrocortisone provided safe therapeutic benefit. The case illustrates the importance of receptor selectivity in corticosteroid therapy for HPA axis dysfunction in patients with comorbid mood disorders.

This paper describes tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis (TINU) syndrome as a post-COVID-19 complication, explaining the pathophysiological mechanisms through ACE2 receptor expression in eye and kidney tissues. It is a descriptive/theoretical paper with no treatment intervention, results, or patient outcomes reported.

A case series describing five children who developed chronic lung disease following SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, with three patterns identified: post-ventilation CLD in infants, bronchiolitis obliterans, and adult-like post-COVID disease in an adolescent. The paper documents long-term fibrotic consequences through CT imaging but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

A case report of a child with post-COVID condition treated with interventions monitored by cardiopulmonary exercise testing and 24-hour Holter ECG. The study demonstrates the utility of these diagnostic tools in assessing treatment response and recovery in pediatric long COVID patients.

A case study of a long COVID patient with post-COVID pneumonitis treated with corticosteroids and pulmonary rehabilitation over 6-8 weeks. Treatment resulted in dramatic improvements in symptom severity, pulmonary function, and exercise capacity.
