This is a case report describing the diagnostic evaluation and treatment of chronic cough and atelectasis in a pediatric patient following COVID-19. While it documents a post-COVID respiratory complication, it focuses on acute post-infection sequelae (asthma-like symptoms) rather than long COVID syndrome, and presents a single case without systematic evaluation of long COVID patients.

Retrospective case series examining pulmonary function changes in 12 children with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease before and after COVID-19 infection, with assessments conducted 26-209 days post-infection. Most children had no or only transient pulmonary impairment, with only one displaying persistent post-COVID symptoms for 8 weeks.

This case series evaluates the combined effect of high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) and inspiratory muscle training (IMT) on respiratory sequelae in six long COVID patients over 5 weeks. The treatment appeared to enhance respiratory muscle strength, efficiency, and lung function.

A case series of 9 patients with post-acute COVID-19 symptoms who underwent 24 sessions of supervised pulmonary telerehabilitation. The intervention improved exercise capacity (6-minute walk test), VO2 peak, and respiratory function in most patients, with improvements in forced vital capacity and forced expiratory volume in several participants.

This case report describes a long COVID survivor who developed delayed-onset organizing pneumonia with sudden dyspnea weeks after being asymptomatic, treated successfully with steroids. The case demonstrates that post-COVID-19 syndrome can present with acute pulmonary complications responsive to corticosteroid therapy, highlighting a previously underrecognized manifestation of long COVID.

Case report of a 69-year-old female who developed bronchiectasis with Haemophilus influenzae colonisation following COVID-19 pneumonia. The paper documents a post-COVID respiratory sequela but is a single case report with no intervention or treatment being tested.

Case report of two post-COVID-19 pneumonia patients who experienced acute respiratory failure following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Both patients recovered with methylprednisolone therapy, highlighting a potential risk of vaccination timing in early post-COVID recovery.

Case report of a COVID-19 patient presenting with cardiac findings initially suspected to be trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity. The paper discusses myocardial involvement during acute COVID-19 hospitalization and cardiac monitoring during recovery, not a long COVID study.

This paper presents long-term neuroimaging follow-up of two cases of COVID-19-related leukoencephalopathy to evaluate neurologic symptoms and outcomes in critically ill patients. The cases demonstrate that leukoencephalomalacia on follow-up MRI may indicate irreversible white matter damage associated with more severe chronic neurologic deficits.

Two case reports of long COVID patients with organizing pneumonia diagnosed via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery. Case 1 responded well to corticosteroids and immunosuppressive agents, while case 2 required antifibrotic treatment (nintedanib) for partial response.

Case series describing three pediatric patients with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) in children 4-6 weeks post-COVID who showed reduced global longitudinal strain on echocardiography despite normal ejection fraction and absent cardiac symptoms. The authors suggest this finding may indicate subclinical myocardial injury but do not test any treatment intervention.

This retrospective case series of 7 pediatric patients with suspected long COVID used [18F]-FDG brain PET imaging to compare metabolic patterns with adult long COVID patients and age-matched controls. While the study demonstrates similar brain hypometabolism in children and adults with long COVID, it is a descriptive imaging study with no treatment or intervention evaluated.

A letter to the editor describing a single case of delayed bronchial artery pseudoaneurysm in a long COVID patient presenting with massive haemoptysis eight months post-infection. The patient was successfully treated with bronchial artery embolisation.

Case report describing a young patient with post-COVID syndrome treated with H.E.L.P. apheresis, a therapeutic approach for managing long-lasting post-COVID symptoms. The treatment reportedly enabled the patient to regain functional capacity and return to work and daily activities.

Descriptive case series of 6 long COVID patients with laryngeal sensory neuropathy, characterized through laryngeal electromyography and clinical examination. Documents physical and subjective symptoms including hoarseness, throat sensations, and voice fatigue as long-term complications of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Case report of two patients with long COVID presenting with cognitive complaints and brain fog, documented by abnormal FDG PET imaging showing hypometabolic regions in the cingulate cortex. No treatment intervention is evaluated; this is a clinical observation of imaging findings in long COVID patients.

Retrospective case series of 7 hospitalized COVID-19 patients with persistent cognitive deficits 12 months post-discharge, assessed via cognitive testing and brain PET/CT imaging. Found variable brain hypometabolism patterns and amyloid deposition in some patients, demonstrating long-term neurological effects of COVID-19.

This paper presents a literature-based case series of 27 patients with new-onset COVID-19-associated movement disorders (ataxia, myoclonus, tremor, parkinsonism), following up on outcomes weeks to months after symptom onset. The majority of patients recovered spontaneously within weeks or months, with only 22% showing persistence of movement disorders at follow-up.

This case series identifies long COVID symptoms (particularly dysphagia) in people with intellectual disabilities, highlighting diagnostic challenges and the risk of misdiagnosis in this population. The study uses the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale-modified to assess functional disability but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing two female patients who developed bilateral hand swelling weeks after mild COVID-19, with clinical and diagnostic findings suggesting a potential capillary leakage syndrome. The paper presents clinical observations and imaging findings but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This paper presents the Munich Berlin Symptom Questionnaires (MBSQs) as novel diagnostic tools for assessing ME/CFS case definitions in pediatric and adult patients with post-COVID-19 condition. It reports diagnostic and quality-of-life outcomes in ten young patients (aged 11-25) diagnosed with ME/CFS following SARS-CoV-2 infection, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a chronic migraine patient treated with erenumab who experienced worsening migraine attacks during acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents a single patient's response to infection and treatment adjustment, not a study of long COVID or its treatment.

This case report describes a young patient who developed focal seizures with impaired awareness as a long-term neurological complication following severe COVID-19 infection. The seizures responded to antiseizure therapy and were documented by EEG and neuroimaging, contributing evidence for SARS-CoV-2's potential to cause central nervous system involvement and chronic neurological sequelae.

This paper describes the detailed evaluation and treatment of an adolescent with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) presenting with progressive central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous system manifestations. It documents the clinical features and therapeutic approach for long COVID neurological complications in a pediatric patient.

This paper presents two case reports of longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) occurring 3-4 weeks after COVID-19 infection resolution, representing a rare post-COVID neurological complication. Both patients were treated with methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, and plasmapheresis, with clinical improvement noted.

A case series of 12 long COVID patients with persistent myalgia, pain, and fatigue undergoing electrophysiological assessment including sympathetic skin responses and quantitative EMG. Study found autonomic system involvement (reduced sympathetic activity) without evidence of myopathic changes.

A case series examining cutaneous phosphorylated α-synuclein in long COVID patients with postural tachycardia syndrome (POTS) using skin biopsies and autonomic testing. The study characterizes pathological markers in small fiber neuropathy associated with long COVID POTS but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper describes a single case report of a severe COVID-19 patient followed for 11+ months post-infection, documenting persistent respiratory symptoms, abnormal sleep patterns, and reproductive dysfunction. It is a descriptive case study without any treatment intervention or control group.

A case study of a 26-year-old woman with persistent post-COVID symptoms in whom clinical metagenomics revealed underlying Bartonella henselae infection, which was treated with clarithromycin. The case demonstrates the utility of clinical metagenomics in identifying hidden infections masquerading as long COVID symptoms.

Case series of 10 COVID-19 patients with prolonged symptom persistence weeks after initial infection. Symptoms resolved rapidly following hydroxychloroquine treatment, suggesting treatment responsiveness in long COVID cases.

This paper presents a theoretical mechanistic explanation and a clinical case of using xenon and oxygen gas mixture inhalation to treat post-COVID ventilation failure. The treatment relieved ventilation insufficiency symptoms and improved oxygen saturation and lung aeration in the reported case.

Retrospective case series of 12 COVID-19 patients with neurological complications (GBS, MFS, OMAS) treated between 2020-2022, analyzing clinical features and treatment outcomes. While some patients received immunomodulatory treatments, the paper focuses on acute/postinfectious neurological syndromes occurring during or shortly after active COVID-19 infection, not persistent long COVID symptoms weeks to months later.

Case report of a patient with subclinical COVID-19 who developed severe pulmonary embolism secondary to thrombosis after craniotomy surgery. The paper describes a single case observation of post-COVID hypercoagulability without testing any intervention or treatment.

This paper presents the APC-Model, a cognitive-behavioral framework for understanding and treating dysfunctional coping behaviors (overexertion vs. protective underactivity) in chronic fatigue associated with post-COVID. The authors illustrate the model's therapeutic application through a case study and provide clinical guidance for stabilizing activity levels and managing symptoms.

This paper presents four case studies of long COVID patients with sleep disturbances and fatigue syndrome, illustrating clinical presentations and treatment options. Multimodal individualized rehabilitation was found to reduce insomnia complaints and help patients return toward premorbid performance levels.

Retrospective study of 12 post-COVID patients who developed mucormycosis, examining the relationship between lymphocyte/CD4+ counts, diabetes, and fungal infection susceptibility. No treatment intervention was tested; the study documents risk factors and associated conditions in post-COVID recovery rather than evaluating a therapeutic approach.

This case series describes 12 patients who developed laryngotracheal stenosis (airway narrowing) 2-3 months after acute COVID-19, presenting histopathological findings and surgical reconstruction outcomes. The study reports clinical characteristics and management of this post-COVID complication with detailed pathological analysis of tissue biopsies.

Case series describing 4 young, asymptomatic post-COVID-19 patients who experienced delayed catastrophic thrombotic events (strokes, myocardial infarction, arterial thrombosis) 78 days post-infection. Reports clinical presentation and imaging findings but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a 69-year-old woman who developed hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) two weeks after COVID-19 recovery, presenting with hyperosmolar state and high inflammatory markers. Despite adequate treatment, the patient died, establishing HLH as a potential post-COVID complication requiring early recognition.

This paper reports the first case of a long COVID patient diagnosed with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) on PET imaging, presenting with new exertional chest pain and dyspnea after COVID-19 recovery. It raises CMD as a potential etiologic factor in long COVID syndrome but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This observational cohort study identifies persistent neurocognitive deficits in non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with 14 of the first 100 enrolled participants reporting cognitive issues lasting a median of 98 days post-infection. The study characterizes the nature and duration of cognitive symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case report of two patients who developed acute transverse myelitis 10 days after acute COVID-19 infection, treated with high-dose corticosteroids. Both patients showed rapid recovery, but this describes acute post-infectious complications during active infection rather than long COVID (weeks-to-months persistent symptoms).

Case series of five patients with post-COVID-19 myelopathy and myeloradiculopathy following mild-to-moderate acute infection, all with negative MRI findings. The paper documents clinical presentations and raises questions about pathophysiology but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper describes tracheal resection and reconstruction outcomes in 15 patients with post-intubation tracheal stenosis, 7 of whom had COVID-19-related intubation. The study found no significant differences in surgical outcomes between COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients, demonstrating that the procedure can be safely performed in both groups.

A case report of a dialysis patient with preexisting adrenal insufficiency who developed post-COVID-19 syndrome with persistent fatigue, requiring significantly increased corticosteroid dosages to manage hypotension and stabilize hemodynamics. The case illustrates the clinical challenge of managing adrenal insufficiency in the context of concomitant long COVID syndrome.

A case report of a hemodialysis patient who developed hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) during COVID-19 treatment, documented over one month post-infection onset. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by combination immunosuppressive therapy (prednisolone and cyclosporine) and survived, demonstrating HLH as a potential post-acute COVID-19 complication.

Case report of a 69-year-old male presenting with systemic and cerebral vasculitis as a post-acute COVID-19 manifestation, diagnosed 6 weeks after mild infection. Patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids and therapeutic plasma exchange, showing clinical response to intervention.

Case series of three post-COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms (seizures, insomnia, attention difficulties) treated with TNF-α inhibitor (Adalimumab). All patients showed dramatic improvement in symptoms following treatment, suggesting TNF inhibitors may be effective for post-COVID neuropsychiatric complications.

This case series followed 13 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors to assess respiratory function recovery at clinical recovery, 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months post-discharge. Patients showed significant improvement in FEV1, FVC, and FEV1/FVC ratios over the 12-month follow-up period, with residual restrictive pattern at 6 weeks resolving substantially by 12 months.

This case study uses electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to visualize lung ventilation patterns in a post-COVID patient with exertional dyspnea compared to a healthy control during treadmill exercise. The authors demonstrate that EIT can detect abnormal ventilation distribution and conclude it may be useful as a diagnostic tool, but this is a descriptive case report with no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Case report of two patients with LMNA p.R349W mutation who developed severe cardiovascular complications weeks after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection. Highlights elevated cardiac risk in lipodystrophy patients with underlying morbidities post-COVID, but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case report of a 60-year-old female who developed central diabetes insipidus with infundibuloneurohypophysitis 8 weeks after recovering from COVID-19 infection. The patient was successfully treated with oral desmopressin and showed prompt response with sustained improvement over 5+ months of follow-up.

A case report of a 44-year-old male with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) developing after COVID-19 recovery, initially misdiagnosed as post-COVID syndrome. The patient was successfully treated with left lung lavage in combination with conventional therapy, with significant clinical improvement during follow-up.

This is a narrative piece about nurses with long COVID sharing their personal experiences and recovery journeys. It is an editorial/opinion article rather than a research study and does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case report of a 32-year-old woman with long COVID presenting with persistent cardiac symptoms (chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea on exertion) and fatigue following overexertion during recovery. Treatment with acupuncture is described for managing her long COVID symptoms.

This paper proposes a 6-week immersive VR-based cognitive intervention for post-COVID-19 condition and presents initial results through a single case report of a 46-year-old female. The patient showed improvements in attention, executive functions, and processing speed, with reductions in perceived cognitive deficits and depression, though the paper is primarily a protocol paper with limited case data.

A case series describing eyelid myokymia (involuntary eyelid twitching) in 15 patients during or immediately after COVID-19 recovery. The study found that myokymia resolved within 3 months in most patients, with older age and longer hospitalization associated with slower recovery, but no intervention or treatment was tested.

Case report describing a 38-year-old man who developed long-term neurological symptoms (syncopes, paresis, vision loss, fatigue, dizziness) following BNT162b2 vaccination, with symptom exacerbation after subsequent COVID-19 infection. The paper discusses potential shared pathophysiology between vaccine adverse reactions and post-COVID syndrome but presents only a single clinical case without systematic evaluation of treatment or intervention outcomes.

This retrospective study identifies 13 cases of jaw osteonecrosis (post-COVID osteonecrosis of the jaw, PCONJ) occurring up to 21 months after severe COVID-19 in patients who received steroid treatment. The authors propose that a triad of post-COVID coagulopathy, steroid administration, and provocative dental treatment may contribute to this complication.

Case series of six patients with functional neurological disorders after COVID-19 infection or vaccination, combined with a literature review of reported cases. The paper describes clinical presentations and symptomatology but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

Case series describing four children presenting with prolonged fever and inflammatory shock-like states 1 month after COVID-19 infection, characterized by elevated cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α). The condition overlaps with Kawasaki Disease and Toxic Shock Syndrome, representing acute post-infectious inflammation rather than long COVID sequelae.

This pilot case series evaluates transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) as a treatment for neuropsychiatric symptoms in 23 long-COVID patients in Japan, primarily targeting chronic fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. Results show improvements in depression, fatigue, and cognitive function scores with no serious adverse events, supporting further investigation in randomized controlled trials.

Autopsy study of fatal COVID-19 cases (27-51 days post-admission) examining lung tissue remodeling patterns, showing basal epithelial cell hyperplasia and immune activation. This is a post-mortem pathological analysis without any treatment intervention or clinical trial design.

Case report describing two patients who developed avascular necrosis of the hip following COVID-19 treatment with corticosteroids. Discusses the pathological mechanisms and clinical management of this long COVID complication.

A case series documenting two cases of chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU) following COVID-19 infection and mRNA vaccination, with treatment outcomes. Both patients were managed with antihistamines (cetirizine), with one showing symptom improvement and the other experiencing persistent symptoms despite treatment.

Case report of a 3-year-old with Guillain-Barré syndrome occurring two weeks after COVID-19 infection, demonstrating a post-COVID neurological complication. Patient recovered favorably after intravenous immunoglobulin treatment, suggesting a causal link between COVID-19 and GBS development.

Case series reporting that plasma exchange improves cognitive function in long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome and autoimmune neurological dysfunction. Demonstrates potential therapeutic benefit of plasma exchange for a subset of long COVID patients with autoimmune features.

Monocentric observational study of 33 post-COVID-19 myocarditis patients examining ejection fraction recovery and prognostic factors at 3-month follow-up. While descriptive of disease evolution, this is a secondary analysis of cardiac outcomes in post-COVID patients rather than an evaluation of a specific treatment intervention.

Case report of six COVID-19 patients who developed post-intubation laryngeal injury (PI-LI) presenting with persistent dyspnea after recovery from acute infection. Four patients required surgical intervention; the paper highlights the need for otolaryngologists to assess the larynx in post-COVID patients presenting with dyspnea.

This paper presents a case report of rapidly progressing diabetic retinopathy following severe COVID-19 infection with long-COVID sequelae. It is a descriptive case study without intervention or treatment evaluation, focusing on the potential mechanism of accelerated retinal pathology due to hypoxia.

This paper describes pseudo-chilblain (pseudo-engelures) and other acute cutaneous manifestations in children during the early SARS-CoV-2 epidemic (April-June 2020). It documents clinical features and inflammatory markers in a case series but does not study long COVID (persistent post-acute sequelae) or test any intervention.

Case series reporting three index cases of severe long COVID patients who experienced complete remission of symptoms within days to a week following monoclonal antibody (casirivimab/imdevimab) infusions. The authors present clinical signals suggesting potential efficacy of MCA treatment for certain long COVID cases and discuss mechanistic implications for post-viral chronic conditions.

Case series of 9 severe COVID-19 patients assessing cognitive functioning 30+ days post-hospitalization for acute respiratory distress syndrome. Found cognitive decline in 33% of patients, with deficits correlated to ICU length of stay, but acknowledges results are preliminary and calls for larger future studies rather than presenting treatment intervention outcomes.

This case series reports on 4 patients with persistent post-COVID olfactory dysfunction unresponsive to medical therapy who underwent endoscopic sinus surgery to address olfactory cleft adhesions. All patients showed significant subjective improvement in olfaction within one week and objective test score improvements over subsequent months, suggesting surgical intervention may benefit carefully selected long-COVID patients with prolonged anosmia and CT-confirmed cleft obstruction.

Case series of five long COVID patients with visual dysfunction (blurred vision, diplopia, photophobia, near-point focus impairment) treated in acute and outpatient rehabilitation settings. All five patients showed confirmatory findings on comprehensive visual assessment, highlighting visual impairment as an underrecognized sequela of COVID-19 requiring systematic screening.

Retrospective case series examining autonomic function testing findings in 14 long-COVID patients with orthostatic intolerance using autonomic reflex screening and tilt table testing. Most patients (57%) showed symptoms without demonstrable orthostatic abnormalities, and only 3 met POTS criteria.

This paper describes the implementation of a multidisciplinary post-COVID clinic in a small rural community, detailing the roles of various healthcare providers (PM&R, physical therapy, speech therapy, respiratory therapy, psychology) in treating long COVID patients. It is a clinical implementation guide rather than a treatment evaluation study, with no comparative data or trial results.

A case series of 13 long COVID patients who received individualized multidisciplinary outpatient cognitive rehabilitation at Mayo Clinic, with assessments at admission and discharge using standardized instruments (MPAI-4, SWLS, PHQ-9, NSI-22). The study found no clear benefit in any of the outcome measures after cognitive therapy.

Retrospective chart review of 6 months of patients treated with bilateral stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) for long COVID symptoms, with self-reported outcomes on a 10-point scale. Patients reported significant reductions in fatigue, cognitive problems, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression, though taste and smell loss did not respond to treatment.

This paper presents a case series of 100 post-COVID syndrome patients and includes a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 articles (11,196 patients) examining symptom prevalence and clinical characteristics. No specific treatment intervention was tested; the study characterizes the disease presentation and confirms long-term antibody responses.

A case series evaluating the feasibility and tolerability of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) using intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) in four patients with post-COVID-19 condition. Active stimulation showed positive trends in cognitive interference, quality of life, and anxiety compared to sham, with no adverse events reported.

This paper reports 3 case histories of arterial thrombotic complications occurring weeks to months after COVID-19 recovery, describing delayed vascular events as long COVID manifestations. It is a descriptive case series without intervention or treatment evaluation, and functions as a clinical observation/review rather than a treatment trial.

A case series describing long-term complications of COVID-19 in 42 patients with rheumatic diseases, with 8 patients developing long-term consequences including lung involvement, neurological symptoms, and dermatitis 40+ days post-infection. The paper is excluded because it is observational documentation of complications without evaluation of any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective case series examines CD8 T-cell dysfunction in Long COVID and ME/CFS patients and evaluates treatment with a nebulized antioxidant/anti-pathogen agent. The study reports improved CD8 T-cell function and 54% reduction in symptom severity in 8 treated Long COVID/ME/CFS patients over 3-15 months with no serious adverse effects.

A pilot case series of 4 long COVID patients receiving transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with online cognitive training over 20 daily sessions. The intervention showed improvements across multiple neuropsychological domains, mood, anxiety, and PASC symptom scores, supporting further evaluation in a planned randomized controlled trial.

Case report of a 37-year-old man with post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome in adults (MIS-A) presenting one month after initial SARS-CoV-2 infection with cardiogenic shock and multiorgan failure. Treatment included corticosteroids, tocilizumab, plasma exchange, and mechanical circulatory support, though the patient ultimately died despite maximal intervention.

A clinical perspective paper presenting case reports to illustrate diagnostic approaches for respiratory symptoms in long COVID patients. Does not present original research, trial data, or treatment evaluation—primarily an educational commentary on diagnosis.

A case report of a 75-year-old severe COVID-19 survivor who developed diffuse pulmonary fibrosis and long-term oxygen dependence. The paper describes clinical presentation and risk factors but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series examining exercise capacity in 169 long COVID patients using cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) at baseline and 41 patients at 1-year follow-up. Found reduced peak oxygen uptake and abnormal oxygen uptake/workload slopes in subsets of patients, with no improvement at 1-year follow-up.

Case report of a long COVID patient presenting with insulin autoimmune syndrome, including excessive sweating, hypoglycemia, and high insulin levels with anti-insulin antibodies. Patient improved with azathioprine treatment and nutritional recommendations.

Case report of a lung transplant recipient who developed post-COVID complications including haemophagocytic lymphohistocytosis (HLH) and cholangiopathy following acute COVID-19 and subsequent transplantation. This is a single case describing clinical sequelae rather than a treatment trial or intervention study.

Case report of a 41-year-old woman who developed polyphagia and weight gain 6 months after acute COVID-19 infection, representing a rare post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. Patient was treated with psychotherapy and behavioral modifications with good outcomes.

Case report of a 28-year-old woman who developed prosopagnosia (face recognition impairment) following COVID-19, with survey data from 54 long COVID patients showing self-reported visual and navigational deficits. This is a descriptive case study without any treatment intervention, making it outside the scope of the intervention trials screening.

Case report of two Egyptian patients who developed optic neuritis 1.5-2 months after severe COVID-19 infection and hospitalization. Both patients presented with visual disturbances (monocular delayed perception and complete unilateral vision loss) with abnormal visual evoked potentials but no other neurological or ophthalmological findings.

Case report of a 35-year-old patient with post-COVID Guillain-Barré syndrome who experienced treatment-related fluctuation after intravenous immunoglobulin therapy but achieved complete recovery with repeat treatment. The study identifies clinical predictors of treatment-related fluctuation in post-COVID GBS and emphasizes importance of early recognition for proper management.

This paper describes a case of de novo seronegative inflammatory oligoarthritis occurring at the onset of acute COVID-19 infection in a single patient, with MRI findings of synovitis. The authors compare this presentation with two other similar cases but do not study long COVID (persistent post-acute symptoms weeks to months after infection) or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Three case reports of children aged 4-7 years presenting with seizures 2-4 weeks after COVID-19 recovery, with no prior epilepsy history. The paper describes clinical presentation and characteristics suggesting a predisposition for neurological complications post-COVID, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case series of three long COVID patients with persistent encephalopathy treated with therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), showing positive therapeutic effects. The authors propose that TPE warrants further evaluation through a prospective randomized trial.

Case report describing seizure as a post-COVID complication in a 71-year-old patient with hypertension and diabetes who developed seizures six days after recovery from acute COVID-19. The paper documents clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, and differential diagnosis but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A case report of a post-COVID-19 patient presenting with orthostatic cerebral hypoperfusion syndrome and small fiber neuropathy, initially misdiagnosed as Lyme Disease Syndrome. The patient showed recovery with symptomatic therapy and subsequent immunotherapy with intravenous immunoglobulins, suggesting potential benefit of early immunotherapy for post-COVID autoimmune complications.

Descriptive case series of 90 long COVID patients visiting an outpatient clinic in Japan, documenting clinical characteristics, symptoms, and examination findings. The study characterizes symptom prevalence (smell/taste disturbance, memory issues, fatigue) but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Case report of a 69-year-old woman who developed abrupt bilateral blindness three weeks after COVID-19 recovery due to COVID-19-related autoimmune demyelinating disorder. The patient was treated with immunosuppressive medications, which stabilized the demyelinating lesions and prevented further neurological deterioration.

A prospective case series of 8 hospitalized COVID-19 patients presenting with neuropathic pain during acute infection, treated with gabapentinoids and antidepressants. The study focuses on acute COVID-19 hospitalization rather than long COVID, as participants were assessed during acute illness and at 1-month follow-up, not weeks-to-months post-infection.

This study compared autonomic function tests in 6 participants pre- and post-SARS-CoV-2 infection to identify if the virus triggers or worsens dysautonomia. All participants demonstrated sympathetic cholinergic (sudomotor) dysfunction post-infection, with worsened or new-onset sudomotor abnormalities consistently observed, suggesting COVID-19 may trigger small-fiber neuropathy.

This case report describes the application of the Lightning Process, a positive psychology self-management program, to treat two long COVID patients in primary care. Both patients reported improvements in fatigue and physical/emotional symptoms post-treatment and at 3-month follow-up.

Case report of a 46-year-old woman with chronic COVID-19 pneumonia presenting with bilateral cavitary lung lesions and calcification, requiring bilateral lung transplantation. The paper describes the pathological findings and clinical course but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a case study of disease progression and surgical outcome.

This retrospective study compared plasma levels of von Willebrand factor and Factor VIII in 10 gynecologic patients with Long COVID versus 5 cancer controls, finding significantly elevated levels in all PASC/LC patients. The study identifies elevated VWF and Factor VIII as potential biomarkers of persistent microvascular inflammation in Long COVID, but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

This case series evaluates olfactory training with essential oils in 8 adult patients with post-COVID-19 smell dysfunction lasting 3+ months. Patients showed significant improvements in olfactory function and quality of life measures after a 30-day treatment protocol.

A retrospective case series evaluating N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplementation in 9 long COVID patients (3 NAC users vs 6 controls) from a gynecologic oncology clinic, with focus on dyspnea, brain fog, fatigue, and von Willebrand factor normalization. Results showed subjective improvement and vWF normalization in all 3 NAC users versus none in controls (Fisher's exact P = 0.0119), with authors calling for prospective randomized studies to confirm findings.

A case series of 4 patients with persistent acral lesions (COVID toes/chilblains) occurring weeks to months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed retrospectively for 3-10 months. The paper describes clinical features and course of these lesions as a potential distinct long COVID entity, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of a patient who developed severe pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) following COVID-19 infection, initially misdiagnosed as post-COVID syndrome. While the paper mentions post-COVID presentation, it is primarily about PAP diagnosis and treatment via lung lavage, not a study of long COVID interventions.

Case report of a follicular lymphoma patient with long COVID and persistent negative SARS-CoV-2 antibodies successfully treated with aggressive antiviral therapy. Describes clinical presentation and treatment response in an immunocompromised patient with atypical long COVID presentation.

This case report describes a 49-year-old patient who developed fulminant myocarditis one month after acute COVID-19 infection, with pathological evidence of severe lymphocytic infiltration and dermatomyositis-like features. The paper documents the clinical presentation and diagnostic findings of a single patient with post-acute COVID-19 myocarditis but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This case report describes an individualized multimodal treatment approach for pulmonary post-acute COVID-19 sequelae in a professional athlete, combining azithromycin, inhalation therapy, thermoplasty, and myoreflex physiotherapy. The patient achieved complete remission of symptoms and successfully returned to competitive athletics, qualifying for the 2024 Olympics.

Single-center retrospective study of 98 post-COVID patients treated for distinct respiratory sub-syndromes: interstitial lung disease (ILD) treated with mycophenolate mofetil and steroids, dyspnea-tachycardia syndrome treated with metoprolol, and undifferentiated mild symptoms. Treatment groups showed significant improvements in oxygen requirements and heart rate at 6-month follow-up.

A case report describing long-term post-COVID-19 rheumatoid and neurological manifestations in a single patient over 2 years, with symptom resolution after receiving a protein subunit vaccine booster. This is a single case report without a study design, control group, or intervention testing.

Three autopsy cases documenting severe hypercoagulopathy and vital organ damage (myocardial ischemia, pulmonary infarction, cerebral infarcts) in patients 1-6 months post-COVID-19 infection. The study demonstrates persistent thromboembolic complications in long COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This is a case series review of neurological manifestations of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at a Pakistani hospital, including encephalitis, cerebrovascular disease, and GBS. The paper focuses on acute complications during active infection rather than long COVID, and is a descriptive review of collected cases without treatment evaluation or intervention testing.

Case report of a long COVID patient with fatigue, post-exertional malaise, pain, and neurological symptoms who was treated with anticoagulatory and virustatic therapy. Circulating microaggregates detected in patient blood showed dissolution following treatment, correlating with clinical remission, suggesting microaggregates as a potential biomarker for post-COVID syndrome.

Case report of a long COVID-19 patient with B cell lymphoma who developed persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection despite antiviral treatment with Remdesivir, likely due to viral resistance mutations. The study documents a novel viral strain in an immunocompromised host and suggests such patients may serve as reservoirs for treatment-resistant variants.

Describes pulmonary pathological findings in 20 long COVID patients who underwent bilateral orthotopic lung transplantation, with analysis of fibrosis patterns and comparison to published literature. This is a retrospective pathology study of transplant outcomes rather than an intervention trial testing a treatment for long COVID.

This case series of five post-spike syndrome patients tested a therapeutic approach combining microbiome restoration (Bifidobacterium), ivermectin, and nattokinase to address vasculitis and systemic inflammation. All five patients showed notable symptom improvement, including resolution of fatigue, brain fog, and neuropathies.

Case report of a 58-year-old woman with persistent post-COVID syndrome featuring neurological complications, describing findings of persistent IgG anticardiolipin autoantibodies and eosinopenia one year after acute infection. The paper investigates potential autoimmune mechanisms in long COVID pathophysiology but does not test or evaluate a treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series describing two rare cases of systemic phaeohyphomycoses caused by Bipolaris species in post-COVID patients with uncontrolled diabetes. Both patients were successfully treated with antifungal therapy (amphotericin B, voriconazole, and itraconazole), highlighting the importance of timely diagnosis for appropriate management of invasive fungal infections as post-COVID sequelae.

Retrospective descriptive study of 100 patients presenting to a Post-COVID Cardiology Clinic with cardiovascular symptoms of long COVID, characterizing symptom phenotypes and clinical findings. While focused on long COVID cardiovascular manifestations, this is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention—patients were evaluated and treated clinically but not enrolled in a study testing a specific intervention.

Describes a case of prolonged COVID-19 in a vaccinated healthcare worker who experienced reinfection with the Gamma variant 387 days after initial infection. The case study discusses factors contributing to post-COVID syndrome including waning immunity, vaccine efficacy, and viral escape, but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

Case report of a 63-year-old woman with erythema nodosum persisting for over three months after COVID-19 infection, presenting as a rare skin manifestation of long COVID. Patient was successfully treated with high-dose steroids and NSAIDs after failing topical treatment.

A case report describing osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) applied to a 12-month long-COVID headache in a pediatric patient, with apparent resolution of symptoms. The authors suggest OMT may be a complementary non-pharmacological treatment option for long-COVID headache and call for further clinical trials to investigate efficacy.

This paper describes a clinical case of polyarthritis onset following COVID-19 infection, presenting clinical data, laboratory results, and therapeutic approaches. It discusses NETosis as a potential mechanism driving post-COVID-19 syndrome and articular symptoms in survivors.

A case report of a 74-year-old woman with prolonged COVID-19 related cough who developed rectus sheath hematoma and rectus abdominis rupture while on anticoagulation therapy, requiring emergency surgical repair. The paper describes a rare complication of long COVID cough rather than evaluating a treatment intervention.

A case report of a 43-year-old diabetic male who developed orbital apex syndrome caused by invasive aspergillosis following COVID-19 recovery, presenting with progressive vision loss and retro-orbital pain over 5 months. The patient received corticosteroid therapy and imaging-guided management, illustrating a rare but serious post-COVID infectious complication affecting the optic nerve.

This paper presents a case report of a long COVID patient with Lance Adams syndrome (post-hypoxic myoclonus) treated with globus pallidus internus-deep brain stimulation (Gpi-DBS), accompanied by a systematic review of eight prior studies on post-hypoxic myoclonus treated with DBS. Although the case report itself describes treatment outcomes, the systematic review component makes this primarily a review article rather than original trial data.

Retrospective cohort study of 59 long COVID patients treated with low-dose naltrexone (LDN), an anti-inflammatory immunomodulatory agent. LDN was associated with reduced symptom burden, improved fatigue, post-exertional malaise, sleep disturbances, and functional status, suggesting potential for rigorous RCT testing.

This case series describes 9 pediatric long-COVID patients diagnosed with persistent postural-perceptual dizziness (PPPD) and treated with vestibular physical therapy, SSRIs, and cognitive behavioral therapy. The majority of patients experienced symptom improvement and all showed improved activity levels and reduced dizziness handicap scores after treatment.

This paper analyzes intestinal biopsies from three cancer patients with severe inflammatory disorders following SARS-CoV-2 infection, finding persistent viral elements and inflammatory markers up to 49 days post-infection. While it documents post-COVID inflammatory complications, it focuses on a specific immunocompromised cancer population without studying any treatment intervention.

Case series describing 3 Swedish patients diagnosed with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome more than 3 months after COVID-19 infection. The paper presents clinical observations of this cardiovascular manifestation of long COVID but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series of 53 COVID-19 patients treated with levocetirizine and montelukast combination therapy during the first and second COVID-19 waves, with six-month follow-up data. The authors report no intubations or deaths in their cohort and suggest the combination may prevent progression to severe disease and mitigate long COVID symptoms, though a Phase 2 RCT is pending FDA approval to validate findings.

This case series examines orthostatic intolerance and exercise intolerance in recreational and competitive athletes with long COVID, highlighting diagnostic challenges and the role of graded exercise training. The study demonstrates the overlap between PASC and orthostatic dysfunction in athletic populations.

This case series reports on long COVID patients whose symptoms improved or resolved with exercise training, proposing exercise as a novel therapeutic strategy for managing long COVID syndrome. The authors suggest that cardiac deconditioning may underlie the clinical phenotype of long COVID.

Retrospective evaluation of 176 children and young people with post-COVID condition referred to a specialist tertiary service, documenting demographics, management approaches, and six-month outcomes. Over half of patients seen in specialist clinics showed functional improvement and increased school attendance at 6-month follow-up, though a subgroup experienced persistent symptoms.

Case report of a 35-year-old woman with cardiovascular disease presenting with long COVID-like symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination and infection. The case describes symptom progression and treatment with catheter ablation but does not evaluate a systematic treatment intervention or include a control group.

Case series of 3 older adults with pre-existing cognitive impairment who experienced worsening cognitive symptoms after COVID-19 recovery, evaluated with neuropsychological testing and neuroimaging. No treatment intervention was tested; paper describes clinical presentation and investigation of long-term cognitive consequences rather than evaluating a specific therapy.

This case series describes cardiovascular manifestations in five long COVID patients, identifying myocarditis confirmed by biopsy and electron microscopy showing mitochondrial vacuolations and myofilament degradation. The findings suggest a cellular mechanism linking SARS-CoV-2 infection to persistent cardiac complications, though the study involves no intervention or treatment evaluation.

Retrospective case series of 16 liver transplant patients with COVID-19 infection, assessing short and medium-term outcomes including post-COVID-19 syndrome presentation. While the paper documents post-COVID symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue) at 3-month follow-up, it does not study or evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is purely observational follow-up of COVID-19 outcomes in an immunocompromised population.

A case report of a 75-year-old long COVID patient with severe dyspnea and functional dependence who underwent a comprehensive cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program including respiratory muscle training. The patient showed rapid improvement in dyspnea, physical performance, pulmonary function, and activities of daily living following the rehabilitation intervention.

A case report describing a 79-year-old female with severe long COVID who developed persistent déjà vu and cognitive symptoms eight months after hospitalization. The patient's MRI revealed white matter microangiopathy and temporal lobe changes consistent with COVID-related neurological damage, treated symptomatically with antidepressants and anxiolytics rather than an experimental intervention.

Retrospective case series describing 18 patients with post-infectious neurological complications (PINCC) occurring 1-8 weeks after acute COVID-19 recovery, including CNS manifestations (cerebrovascular events, demyelination) and PNS manifestations (Guillain-Barré syndrome, neuropathies). No treatment intervention was tested or evaluated; the study is purely descriptive of clinical presentations and outcomes.

A single case report describing systemic manual therapy treatment for a 65-year-old patient with long COVID complications including polyneuropathy and organ failure following ICU hospitalization. The patient showed substantial improvements in functional measures (PIP score 52→11, QUICKDASH 68→16) and returned to work.

A 12-month case series evaluating safety and efficacy of autologous adipose-derived stromal vascular fraction (SVF) cells administered intravenously to 5 long COVID patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms. Four of five subjects showed improvements in cough, dyspnea, pulmonary function tests, and CT imaging, with benefits emerging as early as 1 month post-treatment, though the uncontrolled design prevents attribution of improvement to treatment versus natural recovery.

A longitudinal observational case series of 16 vaccinated kayak athletes examined cardiorespiratory fitness and time-trial performance before and after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study found significant decreases in peak oxygen uptake and impaired time-trial performance persisting two months after return to training, demonstrating post-COVID deconditioning in well-trained athletes.

Case series reporting three patients with post-COVID-19 interstitial lung disease presenting with severe hypoxemia who responded well to high-dose corticosteroid therapy. Demonstrates a potential treatment approach for a post-COVID pulmonary complication, though larger studies are needed to establish efficacy.

Case series describing neuropsychological assessments of two COVID-19 survivors with persistent cognitive complaints two months post-infection. Findings show dysexecutive syndrome and subjective cognitive disorder potentially related to subclinical hypoxic brain injury, but this is a descriptive case report without treatment intervention.

Retrospective study of 22 post-COVID-19 patients with acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (AIFR) describing clinical presentation and treatment outcomes. All patients received combined surgical debridement and antifungal medications, achieving a 72.7% survival rate, with meningitis as a significant predictor of fatal outcome.

Case series of two long COVID patients who developed de novo autoimmune disorders (Crohn's disease and ankylosing spondylitis) treated with TNF-α inhibitors, followed by subsequent development of post-COVID Parkinson's disease. Both patients showed substantial motor improvement with dopaminergic therapy, suggesting a pathogenic cascade linking viral-induced immune dysregulation to neurodegeneration.

This case series reports treatment of two long COVID patients with stellate ganglion block, a regional anesthetic procedure targeting cervical sympathetic chain activity. The authors propose that dysautonomia underlies long COVID symptoms and suggest stellate ganglion block as a novel therapeutic approach.

This case series describes six patients who developed endogenous fungal endophthalmitis (Candida or Aspergillus) following COVID-19 hospitalization and corticosteroid/antiviral treatment. While treatment with antivirals and antifungals was provided, the paper focuses on acute post-COVID complications during hospitalization recovery rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

Retrospective descriptive case series comparing antibody test results and clinical characteristics between patients with confirmed post-acute COVID-19 sequelae (true-PASC) and those with PASC-like symptoms without COVID-19 history (PASC-mimic). Findings show no significant clinical differences between groups, highlighting the need to exclude PASC-mimic conditions in future research.

Reports five cases of osteonecrosis of the femoral head in long COVID patients who received high-dose corticosteroid treatment during acute COVID-19 hospitalization. This is a case report documenting a potential adverse effect of treatment rather than an intervention trial evaluating a treatment for long COVID.

A case series evaluating Integrative Breathing Therapy (IBT) for post-COVID patients with dysfunctional breathing and associated symptoms like dyspnea, fatigue, and cognitive difficulties. All participants showed improvements in breathing parameters and symptom reduction after 6-12 weekly group telehealth sessions combined with individual sessions.

Retrospective case series describing neurological complications following acute COVID-19 infection in 7 patients, including thrombotic events, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and stroke. The paper focuses on acute and early post-infection complications rather than long COVID syndrome.

Describes a multidisciplinary COVID-19 Activity Rehabilitation Program at Mayo Clinic that evaluated and treated 100 patients with post-COVID syndrome, characterizing their symptoms, comorbidities, and functional impairment. Most patients required physical therapy, occupational therapy, or brain rehabilitation, with the majority showing no abnormalities on lab/imaging despite debilitating symptoms affecting return to work and daily activities.

A case series of 26 virologially confirmed long COVID patients presenting with prolonged or recurrent symptoms weeks after initial COVID-19 infection, seen at a post-COVID clinic from May-June 2020. The paper describes symptom patterns (neurological, cardiovascular, fatigue) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case-series study examined neurometabolic and structural brain changes in the hippocampus before and after COVID-19 infection in three elderly patients, two of whom had completed resistance training prior to infection and one in a non-training control condition. Findings suggest mild COVID-19 may be associated with neuroinflammation and altered glutamate levels, potentially explaining chronic neurological complaints in long COVID patients.

This paper describes neurological manifestations of long COVID, particularly cognitive dysfunction (executive, attentional, and memory impairment) observed in dozens of cases. Brain PET-FDG imaging shows hypometabolic zones in cingulate cortex, precuneus, temporal cortex, and brainstem, with variable patient outcomes dependent on the extent of cerebral hypometabolism.

Case series of 3 patients (ages 15-64) who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome during or 3 weeks after acute COVID-19 infection, treated with immunoglobulin with favorable outcomes. While it documents treatment of a COVID-related complication, this describes acute post-infection neurological syndrome, not persistent long COVID symptoms weeks-months later.

Retrospective study of 28 patients with ME/CFS following COVID-19 vaccination who received vitamin D replacement therapy, showing increases in serum vitamin D levels associated with symptom improvement. 82% of patients (23/28) no longer met ME/CFS diagnostic criteria after therapy, with sleep problems and autonomic symptoms showing the greatest improvement.

This case series describes two patients with postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC/long COVID) who received over-the-counter antihistamines and showed significant improvement in symptoms and functional ability. The authors propose histamine involvement in PASC pathogenesis and call for future studies to evaluate antihistamine efficacy in long COVID treatment.

Open-label case series of 12 long COVID patients with cognitive deficits treated with guanfacine (α2A-adrenoceptor agonist) and N-acetylcysteine (NAC). Treatment improved cognitive abilities in 8 of 12 patients, with reported improvements in working memory, concentration, and executive function; 4 patients discontinued due to adverse effects or unspecified reasons.

Cross-sectional study of 10 patients with demyelinating manifestations of the central and peripheral nervous system occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection, with mean onset 43 days post-infection. The study characterizes the neurological presentations (myelin, optic neuritis, brainstem syndrome, peripheral neuropathy) but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This case report describes steroid-induced avascular necrosis of the jaw in patients recovering from COVID-19, a post-COVID complication emerging at a tertiary care center in India. The paper is a descriptive case series without treatment evaluation or intervention testing.

Case series of 11 new pediatric patients with new-onset psychiatric symptoms (including psychosis) after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, followed for 1 year, combined with a review of 12 previously reported similar cases. Most patients received treatment and had good outcomes, with CSF analysis in some showing central immune responses.

This case report describes temporal changes in sputum rheological parameters in two patients with chronic cough following SARS-CoV-2 infection. While it documents post-COVID pathophysiology, it is a descriptive case series without an intervention or treatment being tested, making it unsuitable for a clinical trials meta-analysis.

A prospective observational study evaluating angina-like chest pain in long COVID patients using adenosine stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The paper presents preliminary results from the first 10 patients of the ANGI-Covid study, showing that 50% displayed microvascular dysfunction patterns, but the full protocol and broader results are still ongoing.

A case series of 15 post-COVID-19 patients with femoral head osteonecrosis treated with autologous bone marrow mononuclear cell transplantation. Treatment with autologous bone marrow progenitor cells reduced pain and improved Harris Hip Score in patients with this complication.

This is a personal testimony piece from two hospital caregivers describing their experiences with long COVID and its impact on their daily lives. It is an editorial/opinion piece rather than a research study with systematic data collection or treatment evaluation.

Retrospective case series of 23 patients with post-COVID reactive arthritis treated at a tertiary care center in India, documenting clinical profiles and treatment outcomes. Most patients responded well to NSAIDs and intra-articular steroids, with no relapses reported, though the study notes COVID-19's definitive role in arthritis etiology remains unproven.

This pilot study used whole-exome sequencing to investigate genetic factors in COVID orchitis (testicular pain), a symptom affecting 10-15% of long COVID patients. The authors identified a rare NACAD deletion in 3 brothers with orchitis and found decreased ACE2 levels, generating a hypothesis about genetic susceptibility to this complication.

This study describes characteristics of 4 long COVID patients listed for heart transplantation compared to 41 patients with other etiologies of advanced heart failure. It is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention—patients are being evaluated for transplantation as a last-resort treatment for refractory heart failure, not receiving an experimental or evaluable intervention.

This cross-sectional study describes postacute COVID-19 syndrome (long COVID) symptoms in maxillofacial surgeons in Brazil following their initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents the prevalence and nature of persistent symptoms in this healthcare worker population but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A serial single-case observational study evaluating cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) for severe post-COVID-19 fatigue in five adolescents. Three of five patients showed significant fatigue reduction at 12 weeks, with all five patients no longer severely fatigued post-CBT and improvements in physical functioning and school attendance.

An exploratory case-series study of 80 COVID-19 survivors in Brazil examined persistent gastrointestinal symptoms two years post-infection through clinical interviews and cytokine analysis. The study found that 30 participants reported ongoing GI symptoms with distinct inflammatory signatures, including elevated TNF-α and delayed IL-6 response, suggesting prolonged inflammatory dysregulation may underlie GI manifestations in long COVID.

A descriptive case series study of older adults from Peruvian Senior Centers who tested positive for COVID-19, followed up to four months to assess acute and persistent symptoms. Found a low frequency of long COVID (4.4%) in this population, with most experiencing one to three symptoms.

Case series reporting favorable clinical response to azithromycin treatment in three long COVID patients with neurological symptoms and cognitive impairment. Authors propose azithromycin as a potential intervention for post-COVID neuropsychiatric manifestations and recommend formal clinical trials.

Two case studies describing speech-language pathology treatment of dysfunctional breathing in long COVID patients with dyspnea and upper airway symptoms. Results show positive outcomes after comprehensive breathing retraining addressing multiple dimensions of dysfunctional breathing.

A case series of 13 long COVID patients who took extended courses (7.5-30 days) of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid) to evaluate symptom response. Some participants experienced meaningful symptom reduction while others reported no effect, suggesting potential benefits for a subset of long COVID patients but with variable responses.

This paper describes homeopathic treatment outcomes for COVID-19 acute symptoms, sequelae, and long COVID through 12 documented case reports. While it addresses long COVID treatment, it is an uncontrolled case series without a control group and lacks quantitative outcome data.

This case series describes six patients with retinal vascular anomalies (vasculitis, vein/artery occlusions) occurring 0-8 months after COVID-19 infection, suggesting ocular long-term effects of COVID-19. No treatment was administered; the study documents clinical manifestations and diagnostic findings only.

Diagnostic case series of 42 long COVID patients evaluated in a dedicated COVID-19 sleep clinic, identifying five sleep disorder syndromes including obstructive sleep apnea, chronic insomnia, hypersomnia, REM behavior disorder, and circadian phase delay. The study recommends comprehensive sleep evaluation for persistent severe sleep symptoms in PASC patients, providing diagnostic characterization and treatment recommendations.

Case report of two patients with Parsonage-Turner neuralgia (amyotrophic brachial neuritis) presenting with accessory nerve paralysis following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentation, imaging, and electromyography findings but does not involve treatment intervention or long COVID sequelae.

This paper describes a homeopathic treatment project for long COVID and post-acute COVID patients in Switzerland, presenting 8 case studies (4 vaccinated, 4 unvaccinated) treated with the Jus method and Natrium arsenicosum. All cases reportedly achieved health restoration, though the work lacks rigorous clinical design, control groups, and objective outcome measures.

This paper reports surgical outcomes for 11 post-COVID patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension treated via pulmonary endarterectomy, showing significant improvement in pulmonary vascular resistance and low operative mortality. It presents the first published series of post-COVID CTEPH patients undergoing this curative surgical intervention.

Two case reports demonstrating homeopathic treatment of COVID-19, long COVID, and vaccine-related symptoms. No quantitative outcomes or control group; editorial/case report format without systematic evaluation.

This paper presents 4 clinical cases of long COVID patients with anxiety and depression treated with herbal remedies (Silexan lavender oil, EGb 761 ginkgo extract, and SHR-5 rhodiola extract). The authors argue that phytotherapy has a clinically relevant role in managing psychiatric manifestations of long COVID, particularly subsyndromal anxiety and depression.

Describes neurological presentations in children with long COVID at Germany's first pediatric long COVID outpatient clinic in Jena, with systematic assessment using questionnaires and tests. Provides descriptive data on neurological symptoms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report describing three patients presenting with voice impairment (dysphonia/aphonia) following COVID-19 infection. No treatment intervention is described; this is a descriptive clinical observation of post-COVID symptoms.

Case report of two patients with heterotopic ossification (abnormal bone formation in soft tissues) following severe acute COVID-19 requiring mechanical ventilation. The paper describes radiological and nuclear medicine findings but does not evaluate any treatment intervention and focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID syndrome.

This case report describes two patients who developed longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) following acute COVID-19 infection. The paper documents the clinical presentation and timeline of neurological complications during the acute infection phase, not persistent long COVID sequelae.

This case series describes oral cavity manifestations of long COVID in 1,256 patients, including discoloration, ulceration, mycosis, and aphthous lesions occurring weeks to months post-infection. The authors document treatment responses (laser biostimulation, hygiene recommendations, specialist care) and spontaneous resolution patterns, with recommendations for monitoring and management strategies.

Ultrastructural analysis of quadriceps muscle biopsies from 8 severe COVID-19 patients reveals microangiopathic changes including endothelial damage, pinocytotic vesicles, and lamina thickening. The study documents pathological mechanisms underlying post-COVID muscle weakness but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective case series of seven long COVID patients with recurrent fever and autonomic dysfunction, including symptoms of tachycardia, blood pressure abnormalities, and electrolyte imbalances. Physical cooling and electrolyte correction with medication were effective treatments for managing autonomic dysfunction-related fever.

Retrospective case series describing clinical and OCT imaging features of retinitis in 17 patients with presumed post-COVID infection. The study documents retinal findings and imaging characteristics but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case series describing neurocognitive deficits in three severe COVID-19 patients during acute rehabilitation, with formal neuropsychological testing showing deficits in encoding and verbal fluency. While it demonstrates cognitive sequelae post-infection, it is a descriptive case series without intervention or treatment evaluation.

This retrospective case series evaluated whole-body hyperthermia (WBH) as part of a multimodal inpatient treatment approach for post-COVID syndrome patients. The study found significant improvements in fatigue (FACIT-F) and COVID-associated symptoms at 4-week follow-up, with 63% of patients rating WBH as effective, though the authors note results are preliminary and future RCTs are needed to isolate specific treatment effects.

A case series of two COVID-19 patients describing neuropsychological outcomes at 3–12 months post-illness, with one patient receiving formal cognitive remediation. Both patients showed cognitive recovery over follow-up despite some residual deficits and persistent emotional symptoms.

This case series describes the neuropsychological profile of 54 pediatric long COVID patients referred for testing, finding that approximately one-third showed objective weaknesses in sustained and divided attention. While the study identifies cognitive and emotional concerns in children with long COVID, it does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

Case series of 5 male patients with subacute thyroiditis presenting 12.8 weeks after COVID-19 infection, characterized by neck pain, fever, thyroid tenderness, and elevated thyroid hormones with suppressed TSH. All patients responded well to oral prednisolone therapy (average 6.8 mg/day for 2 months) and achieved full recovery to euthyroid state.

A case series of three older adults with cardiovascular risk factors who presented with cognitive symptoms 6-10 months after severe COVID-19 infection. Neuropsychological evaluations documented deficits in executive function, learning, recall, and mood, with all patients diagnosed with Mild Neurocognitive Disorder.

Retrospective clinical case series of 18 pediatric patients with long COVID who underwent neuropsychological evaluation at a multidisciplinary post-COVID clinic. Most patients had preexisting attention or mood/anxiety concerns, and over half performed below average on auditory attention measures, though the study cannot determine whether cognitive deficits are directly attributable to COVID-19 or to preexisting conditions.

This cross-sectional study assessed neurocognitive performance in 92 long COVID patients referred to a treatment program, using standardized neuropsychological tests. While patients showed specific cognitive impairments in processing speed and immediate recall, this is a descriptive assessment study without treatment evaluation or control group, functioning as a secondary analysis of an existing cohort.

Case report of two COVID-19 patients who developed pulmonary embolism days after discharge from initial hospitalization for non-severe pneumonia. Discusses VTE as a cardiovascular manifestation during acute COVID-19 infection, not long COVID.

A post-COVID-19 smell clinic assessed olfactory dysfunction in 20 long COVID patients using standardized tests (UPSIT, eODQ) and provided 4 months of smell retraining therapy. Initial results showed 40% experienced parosmia and 40% had rhinological symptoms, with outcomes to be evaluated after retraining completion.

A single-center registry study of 16 long COVID patients with chest pain who underwent endomyocardial biopsy to investigate histopathological causes of myocardial injury. Findings showed diffuse ischemic necrosis in 75% of patients, with some cases of lymphocytic myocarditis, thrombotic microangiopathy, and amyloidosis, but no active treatment intervention was evaluated.

This retrospective case series assessed medium-term outcomes in 200 severely ill COVID-19 survivors at 4-7 months post-infection. The study found persistent symptoms (breathlessness, fatigue, reduced mobility, pain) and abnormal lung function tests in a significant proportion of patients, with no sustained systemic inflammation despite ongoing symptoms.

Case series of 7 long COVID patients with postural tachycardia syndrome (PTS), describing clinical presentation, diagnostic testing, and treatment responses over ~152 days. Two of three severely symptomatic patients showed clinical improvement with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), suggesting potential therapeutic benefit for refractory PTS in post-COVID contexts.

This case series describes left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) measurements in 18 non-hospitalized COVID-19 survivors with persistent dyspnea weeks after infection resolution. The study documents subclinical myocardial dysfunction in these long COVID patients but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study investigated 11 consecutive long COVID patients with new-onset chest pain to determine if myocardial ischemia of non-obstructive origin could explain their symptoms, using intracoronary assessment of endothelial function and coronary flow reserve. Stratified medical treatment based on individual endotype patterns led to significant improvement in angina frequency and stability at follow-up.

Case series of three long COVID patients presenting with morphologically confirmed endocarditis 4-7 months post-infection, with both infective and non-bacterial variants identified. Treatment with corticosteroids, anticoagulants, and antibiotics was used, with SARS-CoV-2 RNA detected in myocardial biopsies and evidence of autoimmune mechanisms underlying the pathology.

Retrospective case report of four patients who experienced acute coronary syndromes (ST-elevation myocardial infarction) 47±32 days after recovering from acute COVID-19 infection. The study describes clinical presentations and angiographic findings but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention for long COVID.

Case report of two patients who developed neurogenic stuttering and cognitive impairment following long COVID-19 infection. Describes clinical presentation, neuropsychological findings, and natural recovery over 4-5 months without any intervention being tested.

This case series of 29 COVID-19 pneumonia survivors used cardiac and pulmonary ultrasound to detect long-term cardiopulmonary sequelae, finding high prevalence of ECG abnormalities, pericardial involvement, and diaphragmatic dysfunction. The study documents post-COVID complications but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of two young athletes with post-COVID-19 pericardial effusion identified during return-to-play screening, followed with serial imaging and cardiac testing. No intervention was given; this is a descriptive case series documenting natural history of the condition.

Case series of three long COVID patients who developed recurrent fungal urinary tract infections following COVID-19, presenting months after acute infection with various Candida and Aspergillus species. Treatment involved multiple antifungal regimens (micafungin, voriconazole, anidulafungin, caspofungin) with variable clinical outcomes, highlighting immune dysfunction and reduced antifungal penetration as key management challenges.

Retrospective case series of 6 lung transplant recipients with severe post-COVID-19 pulmonary disease followed for a median of 13 months post-transplantation. Five of six patients demonstrated excellent long-term outcomes with minimal post-transplant complications, demonstrating lung transplantation as a viable salvage treatment option for severe COVID-19-related lung fibrosis.

This paper describes clinical characteristics of 47 pediatric long COVID patients seen at the University of Minnesota Pediatric COVID Clinic, documenting symptom prevalence and demographics. It is a descriptive case series with no intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for a treatment trials meta-analysis.

Case series of 7 patients with COVID-19-associated collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (COVAN) from a UK renal centre, documenting patient demography, biopsy findings, and renal outcomes. While treatment outcomes are reported, this paper studies acute COVID-19 complications (renal disease during active infection), not long COVID sequelae.

This observational case series describes 8 patients who developed herpes simplex virus encephalitis (HSVE) within 6 weeks of COVID-19 infection, examining clinical presentation, imaging findings, and outcomes. All patients received intravenous acyclovir treatment with mostly complete recovery, suggesting that post-COVID immune dysregulation may increase susceptibility to secondary viral infections like HSVE.

topics: kidney function|acute kidney injury|critical illness outcomes
summary: This retrospective cohort study follows 13 COVID-19 survivors who required intensive care with acute kidney injury and continuous kidney replacement therapy, assessing kidney function recovery at 6 and 12 months post-ICU. While it demonstrates long-term organ dysfunction following acute COVID-19 critical illness, it does not address long COVID as a post-acute sequelae condition and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series describes 11 post-SARS-CoV-2 myocarditis cases identified in a military health system cohort, examining clinical characteristics, long-term outcomes, and potential recurrence after vaccination or reinfection. The study focuses on acute/early cardiac complications of COVID-19 rather than long COVID syndrome or persistent post-COVID conditions.

A case series of 10 adolescents with post-COVID-19 hypersomnolence treated with low-dose aripiprazole (0.5–2.0 mg). Low-dose aripiprazole effectively reduced total sleep duration and advanced wake-up times with no significant adverse effects reported.

Descriptive case series of 15 post-COVID myocarditis patients diagnosed 2-9 months after acute infection, characterized by cardiac MRI and/or endomyocardial biopsy findings. Study documents clinical features and viral persistence but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper describes the experience of a dedicated Cardio-COVID clinic that performed structured cardiac assessments (ECG, echocardiogram, CPET, CMR, etc.) on 76 long COVID patients with suspected cardiovascular sequelae between June 2020 and March 2021. While it is a legitimate long COVID paper documenting cardiovascular manifestations, it is excluded because it is a descriptive case series without treatment intervention—patients underwent diagnostic evaluation and assessment only, not a treatment or intervention trial.

Observational case series of 75 post-COVID-19 patients in Iraqi Kurdistan that documents the emergence of rheumatic autoimmune diseases (SLE, RA, antiphospholipid syndrome) following COVID-19 infection, with laboratory confirmation and disease severity assessments. The study describes manifestations and laboratory markers of post-COVID autoimmune conditions but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series describes 26 long COVID patients with new-onset sleep disorders evaluated at a dedicated clinic, including diagnoses of narcolepsy, hypersomnia, insomnia, and REM sleep behavior disorder.
