Patients received standard treatments (CPAP, stimulants, modafinil, sodium oxybate) with expected clinical responses, including one marked improvement with low-dose sodium valproate.

Case series of two teenagers who developed chronic insomnia 3-5 months after COVID-19 infection, with one patient showing insufficient sleep on actigraphy and both failing trials of multiple pharmacological treatments (melatonin, trazodone, hydroxyzine, gabapentin) and behavioral interventions. The report documents treatment attempts and responses in post-COVID sleep disturbance, highlighting the difficulty in managing pediatric long COVID-related insomnia.

Case report of 50 children admitted to Great Ormond Street Hospital with PIMS-TR COVID-19 (a post-acute inflammatory syndrome in children following COVID-19), describing physiotherapy assessment and treatment including muscle strengthening and mobility re-education. While the paper documents treatment outcomes (improvement in MMT8 and CMAS scores at 2-month follow-up), PIMS-TR is an acute post-infectious inflammatory syndrome distinct from long COVID and occurs primarily in the acute/subacute phase, not the persistent weeks-to-months post-infection period that defines long COVID.

Case series of three women with premature ovarian insufficiency following mild/asymptomatic COVID-19, attributed to autoimmune FSH receptor blockade. Two patients responded to corticosteroid treatment (prednisone 30 mg) with restoration of normal FSH levels and successful oocyte retrieval.

This case series evaluates whether Garmin wearable devices combined with pacing education help long COVID patients manage their symptoms through user testing with 11 individuals. Eight of nine participants reported the intervention helpful for symptom management, though the small sample size and lack of control group limit generalizability.

Case series describing Streptococcus pyogenes-related toxic shock syndrome occurring in the post-COVID period in pediatric patients. While temporally associated with COVID-19, the paper focuses on acute bacterial infection rather than long COVID sequelae and does not study treatment of long COVID.

Case series describing 3 children with post-COVID neurocognitive problems showing hypometabolism in the orbito-frontal cortex on PET imaging. The study is a descriptive case report without treatment intervention or control group, focused on imaging findings rather than clinical outcomes or interventions.

Retrospective case series of 26 long COVID patients with chronic chilblain-like lesions presenting to a rheumatology service between 2020-2022. Various treatments were trialed (NSAIDs, corticosteroids, sildenafil) with variable effectiveness, and symptom duration ranged from 2 months to over 2 years with seasonal variation.
A case series evaluating tricyclic antidepressants for treating neuropsychiatric symptoms in long COVID patients. Reports on treatment outcomes and clinical response in a series of cases.

Case series examining genetic variants associated with COVID orchitis (testicular pain) in 6 long COVID patients using whole-exome sequencing. Identified a rare NACAD deletion in 3 patients with orchitis and found decreased soluble ACE2 levels in affected men, suggesting a possible genetic mechanism for orchitis sequelae.

Retrospective case series of 5 pediatric patients with post-COVID-19 liver manifestations, including 2 infants with acute liver failure requiring transplantation and 3 children with hepatitis and cholestasis. Three children treated with steroids showed improvement in liver enzymes and successful weaning from treatment.

Case report of 2 patients with COVID-19-associated macular damage presenting with visual impairment shortly after acute infection. Both patients received corticosteroid therapy with partial visual improvement, but the study focuses on acute COVID complications rather than long COVID sequelae.

A case series of 44 long COVID patients who received outpatient physical therapy, with assessments at baseline, end of treatment, and 2 and 6 months follow-up using functional and quality-of-life measures. Physical functioning and health-related quality of life significantly improved over the 7-15 month follow-up period, with 55% showing meaningful improvement on physical performance and 45% on functional scales.

Retrospective review of 16 long COVID patients assessing cognitive impairment using Cambridge Brain Sciences computerized cognitive testing and concussion screening tools. Majority of patients (87%) showed signs of cognitive impairment, particularly in verbal processing, memory, and visuospatial processing, with cognitive fatigue as the predominant symptom profile.

Case report of two unusual post-COVID complications: diffuse panniculitis and inflammatory myositis, with clinical and FDG PET/CT imaging features. No treatment intervention or outcome measurement; descriptive imaging cases only.

Retrospective case series of 17 patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head following COVID-19 infection, with a mean interval of 6.5 months between infection and AVN presentation. Most patients presented with bilateral hip pain and were managed with conservative treatment, core decompression, or total hip replacement.

Follow-up study of 29 COVID-19 patients who received veno-venous ECMO support for acute respiratory distress syndrome, assessing functional and social recovery at 12 months post-discharge. While the paper documents recovery outcomes including 100% survival, return to work rate of 90%, and cardiopulmonary exercise capacity, it is a retrospective observational follow-up study that does not test or evaluate a specific intervention—it passively follows patients who received standard ECMO care.

Describes a pediatric multidisciplinary rehabilitation clinic model for long COVID patients and presents a case series of 9 pediatric patients with persistent symptoms including fatigue, headaches, brain fog, and cognitive difficulties. Most patients showed decreased quality-of-life scores and some demonstrated attention and mood concerns that improved through the multidisciplinary rehabilitation approach.

This case series evaluated 68 Ga-FAPI PET/CT imaging in 6 post-COVID-19 patients with suspected pulmonary fibrosis, comparing fibroblast activation protein uptake to 9 non-COVID controls. The study demonstrated enhanced imaging capability for detecting fibrotic changes but did not test any therapeutic intervention.

Case series of 4 COVID-19 patients with ARDS who received mechanical ventilation and rehabilitation therapy, with 6-month follow-up of exercise capacity via 6-minute walking distance test. Despite recovery of muscle strength and daily living activities, patients showed persistent decreased exercise capacity and oxygen desaturation during exertion at 6 months post-hospitalization.

Case report of 2 COVID-19 patients who developed rapid progressive dementia 5-10 months after prolonged infection with PET hypometabolism findings. Describes long-term neuropsychiatric complications but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A pilot study describing the adaptation of an interdisciplinary chronic pain rehabilitation program for youth with long COVID, focusing on return to school and activities of daily living. Three case examples demonstrate positive clinical changes in function through the rehabilitation approach.

A case series evaluating the Perrin technique (manual lymphatic drainage combined with self-massage and mobility exercises) as a treatment for long COVID in 20 patients. The intervention resulted in approximately 50% reduction in fatigue-related symptoms measured by the PFRS scale.

This case series evaluates repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in 5 long COVID patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms. While improvements in PROMIS scores for fatigue, depression, anxiety, and cognitive/social function were observed, they did not reach statistical significance, though 3 of 4 completing patients reported subjective improvement.

This case series evaluates the effect of a third dose of BNT162b2 vaccine in 20 long COVID patients who had experienced breakthrough infections. The study found significant reductions in inflammatory markers (CRP) and boosting of anti-S1 RBD IgG antibodies following the third vaccine dose.

Case-control study comparing P-selectin adhesion activity in one long-COVID patient versus one asymptomatic post-COVID patient using microfluidics and blood assays. While exploratory work on potential Long-COVID pathophysiology and mentions anti-P-selectin therapy as a possible treatment direction, the study does not actually test or evaluate a treatment intervention in patients.

Descriptive narrative study of 34 long COVID cases seen in general practice, with detailed clinical experience from 6 patients. SPECT imaging demonstrated cerebral perfusion disorders in 14 severe cases with partial improvement at 3-month follow-up, but no specific treatment was tested or evaluated.

This case series presents in-vivo PET imaging evidence of widespread neuroinflammation in two long COVID patients using [18F]DPA-714 PET scanning, with binding increases of 121% and 76% compared to matched healthy controls. The study demonstrates neuroinflammatory mechanisms in long COVID pathophysiology but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A retrospective case series of 16 long COVID patients with new-onset small fiber neuropathy, of whom 8 received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment with reported significant clinical improvement in neuropathic symptoms. Six patients tested positive for autoantibodies (TS-HDS or FGFR3) and invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing revealed neurovascular dysregulation consistent with ME/CFS.

This study investigated autoantibodies (AAbs) targeting neuronal receptors in 178 post-COVID patients and evaluated immunoadsorption (IA) as a treatment approach in two patients with elevated AAb levels. One patient showed substantial clinical remission after IA treatment but relapsed within 6 weeks with recurrent AAb elevation, suggesting AAbs may play a pathophysiologic role in post-COVID but require further investigation in randomized trials.

This paper combines a case report of five Swedish children with long COVID symptoms and a systematic literature review of pediatric long COVID. The systematic review found no existing publications on long COVID in children, while the case report documents symptoms lasting 6-8 months including fatigue, dyspnea, and cognitive difficulties.

This cross-sectional study characterizes new-onset chronic musculoskeletal pain in 18 long COVID patients using the ACR fibromyalgia diagnostic criteria. The study found that 72.2% of patients met diagnostic criteria for fibromyalgia, but it does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This retrospective cohort study examines COVID-19 severity, complications, and outcomes in 50 kidney transplant recipients followed for 6 months post-infection. While 58% developed chronic COVID-19 syndrome (long COVID), the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 infection outcomes rather than any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

A cross-sectional clinic-based study investigating post-COVID syndrome prevalence and characteristics in patients with underlying haematological disorders. The paper establishes a specialized clinic to identify and characterize how haematological disease patients are affected by persistent post-COVID symptoms.

A case series describing clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes of 16 patients with tardive COVID-19 pseudoperniosis (TCPP), a protracted acral skin manifestation of long COVID. Four patients achieved complete or near-complete resolution while others remained under active treatment, identifying potential risk factors and predisposing conditions.

This study compares penile corpus cavernosum tissue in patients 1 and 7 months post-COVID-19 infection versus uninfected controls, using immunohistochemistry and electron microscopy to detect residual SARS-CoV-2. While the study documents long COVID sequelae (erectile dysfunction), it is a tissue pathology/virology study without evaluating any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the trials pipeline.

This paper describes five long COVID patients with severe cardiovascular manifestations including sudden cardiac death, coronary atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and myocarditis, confirmed by endomyocardial biopsy. Electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial vacuolations and myofilament degradation in cardiomyocytes, with similar findings reproduced in SARS-CoV-2-infected mice, suggesting a cellular mechanism for long COVID-associated cardiac effects.

Case series of 3 children with newly diagnosed connective tissue diseases (SLE, neuropsychiatric SLE, mixed connective tissue disease) following COVID-19 infection, investigating autoimmune manifestations as immune-mediated post-COVID phenomena. No treatment evaluation or intervention testing is conducted; this is a descriptive report of disease diagnosis and mechanisms.

Cross-sectional study evaluating prevalence of low testosterone and impaired fertility markers in 143 male COVID-19 survivors at 8-12 weeks post-infection. Found 28.7% had low testosterone and 18.1% had Sertoli cell dysfunction, but these were not associated with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome.

Case reports of Parsonage-Turner syndrome (neuralgic amyotrophy) occurring in two patients following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation, electrophysiological findings, and imaging characteristics but does not study long COVID (chronic post-infection condition) or test any treatment intervention.

This retrospective multi-center case series describes seven patients with post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy who underwent liver transplantation between 2020-2022. Liver transplantation proved viable with acceptable outcomes, showing 86% patient and graft survival at median 11-month follow-up.

Case series describing telogen effluvium (hair shedding) occurring ~50 days after acute COVID-19 infection in 10 patients. Authors note this may represent a post-infection sequela but do not evaluate any treatment intervention for the condition.

A case series of six patients who developed Parkinson disease 4-7 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, all of whom received dopaminergic treatment with satisfactory response. The study hypothesizes that COVID-19 may unmask latent neurodegenerative processes through immune-mediated mechanisms.

This paper describes three case reports of migraine-like headaches in individuals with a history of mild COVID-19 infection to illustrate different phenotypes of persistent post-COVID headaches. It is a descriptive case series focused on clinical presentation and pathophysiology rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

Case report of two COVID-19 patients who developed chronic intracardiac thrombus as a long-term complication. Describes clinical presentation of a life-threatening cardiovascular sequela but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series of 31 patients with protracted headache after COVID-19 infection evaluated at a tertiary headache center, documenting characteristics and treatment outcomes. Most patients (74%) met criteria for migraine, with 65% developing chronic migraine post-COVID, and 72% of those started on preventive migraine medications reported improvement in headache frequency or severity.

Case series of 6 post-COVID patients with persistent oral ulcers showing immunohistochemical evidence of SARS-CoV-2 in oral epithelium despite negative RT-PCR. Describes pathological findings including epithelial ulceration and inflammatory infiltrate but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series examines accelerated androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss) occurring 220 days post-COVID-19 recovery and evaluates platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment in 9 patients. PRP injections over 4 sessions significantly improved hair loss metrics, with 55.5% of patients reporting the treatment as very effective.

Retrospective case series of 24 children with post-COVID-19 condition referred to a specialized clinic in Japan, documenting symptom profiles, duration, and treatments. Most patients (83.4%) showed symptom resolution or improvement with pain management and pacing-based counseling over a median 4.5-month follow-up.

This case series describes sicca symptoms (dry eye and dry mouth) in 22 patients recovering from severe COVID-19 at a Brazilian rehabilitation unit, finding high rates of Schirmer test positivity (72.7%) and reduced salivary flow (54.5%). The paper identifies oral dryness as a previously undescribed manifestation of post-COVID syndrome but does not test any treatment intervention.

Descriptive study of 16 consecutive patients with post-COVID-19 reactive arthritis presenting to rheumatology clinic, characterizing the clinical pattern of joint and periarticular involvement. Patients responded well to NSAIDs in 68.7% of cases, with corticosteroids and methotrexate used in select cases.

This cross-sectional study investigates the association between COVID-19 infection and new-onset rheumatoid arthritis (RA), examining ACPA seroprevalence and autoantibody characteristics in post-COVID patients. The findings suggest that RA onset after COVID-19 is likely coincidental rather than causally connected, with post-COVID RA patients resembling regular RA patients clinically and serologically.

Case series examining septal panniculitis (erythema nodosum) as a manifestation of COVID-19 in 21 patients, categorized by timing relative to infection (acute, ongoing symptomatic, and post-COVID syndrome). The study describes clinical features, laboratory findings, and imaging results but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Reports three cases of avascular necrosis of the femoral head developing after COVID-19 treatment with corticosteroids, occurring earlier than typical post-steroid AVN presentations. This case series documents a potential long COVID complication but does not evaluate any intervention for treating AVN or long COVID.

Case series reporting two children with vestibular migraine as a post-COVID-19 manifestation and describing their management. Highlights vestibular migraine as a novel symptom of long COVID in pediatric populations requiring prompt evaluation and treatment.

A case series describing two patients who developed osteonecrosis of the knee as a long COVID-19 sequela following corticosteroid treatment for acute COVID-19. The authors recommend early MRI diagnosis and bisphosphonate therapy as intervention for this long COVID manifestation.

A family practice case series of 55 long COVID patients characterized by extreme fatigue, brain fog, and multi-systemic symptoms, with 32 undergoing SPECT-CT imaging showing vascular encephalopathy. The study describes patient outcomes and clinical presentation but explicitly states 'there is no known verified treatment' and does not test any intervention.

This paper reports on inpatient rehabilitation for long COVID patients and its effects on exercise performance, lung function, and psychological parameters. However, the abstract presents only conclusions without reporting actual trial results or patient numbers, indicating this is likely a protocol or incomplete abstract rather than a full study with results.

This prospective case series of 48 long COVID patients with dysfunctional breathing describes symptoms, functional impact, and quality of life using standardized questionnaires and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Despite preserved pulmonary function, patients showed high symptom burden with dyspnea, hyperventilation, and palpitations being most common, with significantly reduced quality of life scores compared to reference values.

This case series describes six patients who developed or had exacerbated autoimmune phenomena following SARS-CoV-2 infection, discussing possible mechanisms underlying the association between autoimmunity and COVID-19. While the paper addresses post-infection complications, it focuses on acute autoimmune manifestations rather than long COVID's characteristic persistent symptoms, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Descriptive case series of three young COVID-19 convalescent patients presenting with long-term neuropsychological symptoms including inattention, executive dysfunction, and memory problems ('brain fog'). Reports neuropsychological test results and brain MRI findings but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

This case series of 5 long COVID patients uses invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing to characterize exercise limitation 1 year post-infection. The study finds that reduced aerobic capacity is attributable to impaired systemic oxygen extraction rather than central cardiopulmonary dysfunction.

Case series of 14 patients presenting with telogen effluvium (hair loss) occurring 1-3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study describes clinical patterns and proposes possible pathogenic mechanisms (pro-inflammatory cytokines, viral damage) but is observational without intervention and focuses on characterizing a symptom rather than testing a treatment.

This cross-sectional study describes cardiovascular manifestations in 71 patients referred to a cardiology clinic 4 months post-COVID-19, examining symptom prevalence and imaging abnormalities. The cohort presented with dyspnea, palpitations, and chest pain, with imaging revealing cardiomyopathy, ischemia, myocarditis, and orthostatic intolerance in subsets of patients.

Retrospective case series of 5 pediatric patients who developed liver injury following COVID-19 recovery, including 2 infants with acute liver failure requiring transplantation and 3 children with hepatitis responsive to steroid treatment. All patients underwent extensive workup excluding infectious and metabolic etiologies, supporting a potentially immune-mediated post-COVID-19 liver manifestation.

Case series describing three COVID-19 patients who developed post-ARDS pulmonary fibrosis with persistent dyspnea six months after acute infection. The paper documents clinical outcomes and management but contains no treatment intervention or control group, serving primarily as clinical documentation of a long COVID complication.

A three-year follow-up case study of two patients who developed autoimmune diseases (systemic lupus erythematosus and Hashimoto's thyroiditis) following COVID-19 infection and/or vaccination. The study highlights the connection between autoimmune disease manifestation and a family history of autoimmunity in the context of long-COVID symptoms and post-vaccination effects.

This case report describes two patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 cardiovascular syndrome (PASC-CVS) who were treated with Suxiao Jiuxin Pills, a traditional Chinese medicine preparation. Both patients experienced well-controlled cardiovascular symptoms including exercise intolerance, tachycardia, chest pain, and difficulty breathing following treatment.

This observational case series of 273 PASC patients identified 8 with chest pain who underwent acetylcholine provocation testing, finding that 5 had vasospastic angina responsive to calcium channel blockers and nitrates. The study suggests vasospastic angina should be considered as a potential cause of chest pain symptoms in long COVID patients and proposes diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

Describes a pediatric neurology post-COVID clinic infrastructure and clinical evaluation protocols for children with neurologic sequelae following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Reports cognitive impairments in 4 case patients months after acute infection but does not evaluate a treatment intervention.

Case series of 5 patients with residual lung injury following acute COVID-19 infection, examined via lung biopsy during the acute/early post-acute phase (18-30 days post-symptom onset). The paper documents histopathological findings (organizing pneumonia, interstitial pneumonia, diffuse alveolar damage) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series describing severe neurocognitive manifestations (pseudobulbar affect, cognitive impairment, mood/sleep disorders) in 3 healthy young individuals (aged 15-27) with COVID-19 lasting 2 weeks to 4 months. Patients were treated with medications including Clomipramine, Zolpidem, and Clonazepam with reported effectiveness.

An Integrative Medicine Center describes outcomes from a post-COVID-19 ME program treating 39 consecutive patients, with 12 completing baseline and follow-up SF-12 surveys showing modest improvements in both physical and mental component scores. The paper presents process improvement data and case studies demonstrating a standardized treatment approach for long COVID patients.

A retrospective case series analyzing self-reported long COVID symptoms from 1,008 individuals via a digital application, identifying 109 symptom categories and exploring demographic associations. The study found pain, neuropsychological issues, and fatigue as most prevalent, with symptom intensity varying by age, gender, ethnicity, education level, and deprivation—but it does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

Case series of 9 patients describing cystic lung disease as a long-term pulmonary complication following severe COVID-19 ARDS. The paper documents imaging findings and raises awareness of potential catastrophic respiratory sequelae but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Pilot study evaluating diagnostic imaging (renal sonography, flow cytometry, dynamic sonographic assessment) in 9 long COVID patients, 3 of whom received monoclonal antibody therapy. Demonstrates feasibility of point-of-care ultrasound assessment for detecting residual organ effects in long-haulers.

This study examined lung tissue from 10 long COVID patients with persistent pulmonary symptoms using transbronchial lung cryobiopsy to identify morphological and immunomolecular features. Three distinct histological patterns were identified (chronic fibrosing, acute/subacute injury, and vascular changes), each associated with different clinical and radiological presentations and potentially different pathogenic mechanisms.

Retrospective analysis of 317 long COVID patients referred to a UK clinic, characterizing demographics, symptoms, and clinical findings. 82% received rehabilitation and physiotherapy for fatigue and breathing disorders, with high prevalence of treatable comorbidities and abnormal oximetry.

A case series of three patients with indolent lymphoma treated with rituximab who developed long COVID-19 with complications including organizing pneumonia and chronic respiratory failure. The paper describes clinical presentations and outcomes but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention for long COVID.

Two PASC patients underwent pulmonary rehabilitation protocols guided by quantitative CT-based vascular density analysis (BV5%). Vascular redistribution was used to differentiate patient selection: one patient received corticosteroids due to cardiac concerns and improved significantly, while the other enrolled directly in rehabilitation and showed substantial improvement in VO2max.

Case series describing three cases of membranous nephropathy with double-negative crescentic glomerulonephritis occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with anti-CD20 agents. While the cases occurred in the post-COVID era, the paper focuses on rare renal autoimmune complications rather than long COVID syndrome as typically defined (persistent multi-system symptoms weeks to months post-infection).

Case report of two pediatric patients presenting with tender cervical lymphadenitis that progressed to multi-system inflammatory syndrome (MIS) in the acute post-COVID period. This is acute COVID sequelae (MIS), not long COVID, and is a case report without systematic evaluation of treatment efficacy.

Case series describing two adults with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A), a post-COVID cardiovascular complication, treated with IVIG, high-dose aspirin, and corticosteroids. Both patients showed resolution of cardiac dysfunction and acute illness following treatment.

This paper describes clinical, metabolic, and inflammatory features in 13 pediatric patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms occurring within one month of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study focuses on acute/subacute post-infection neuropsychiatric manifestations rather than long COVID (which requires symptom persistence weeks to months later) and is a retrospective descriptive analysis without treatment intervention.

Case series of 3 long COVID patients (2 autistic, 1 typically developing) treated with upadacitinib, a JAK1 inhibitor targeting type 1 interferon signaling. Treatment showed improvement in neuropsychiatric/encephalopathy-like symptoms and reduced monocyte cytokine activation.

This case series describes acute macular neuroretinopathy (AMN) occurring within one month of acute COVID-19 infection in 11 patients. While the symptoms appear shortly after acute infection, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 complications rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection) and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper describes a distinct long COVID phenotype characterized by exertional intolerance and dyspnea despite preserved lung function. The study appears to be a descriptive characterization of patient symptoms rather than a treatment intervention trial.

This study assessed small airway function in 20 Finnish COVID-19 survivors 3-6 months post-infection using spirometry, impulse oscillometry, and nitric oxide measurements. The findings showed no evidence of small airway obstruction, inflammation, or dysfunction in this cohort.

A retrospective case series examining histological changes in liver biopsies from 17 COVID-19 patients with 36-month follow-up. Findings show mild resolved hepatitis-like patterns with normal liver enzymes at follow-up, suggesting the liver is not a target of significant COVID-19 inflammatory damage.

A case series of 6 severe COVID-19 patients followed for 12 months, documenting persistent fatigue, cognitive deficits, and multidomain complaints. The paper describes clinical outcomes and symptom patterns but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series of 25 adolescents with functional respiratory disorders that developed after SARS-CoV-2 infection, characterized by thoracic dominant breathing and/or inducible laryngeal obstruction. All patients received reassurance and rebreathing training, with 5 followed-up patients showing normalization of breathing patterns within 3 months.

A case series of 5 long COVID patients treated with bright polychromatic light therapy (2000-4000 LUX) daily to address circadian dysfunction and sleep disturbance. Treatment restored sleep and unexpectedly improved depression, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms (brain fog) within 4-5 days, with improvements maintained for weeks to months without relapse.

Open-label case series reporting nicotine patch treatment for post-COVID-19 syndrome in multiple patients, with reported improvements ranging from substantial to complete remission within days. The study proposes that spike protein interference with nicotinic acetylcholine receptors contributes to long COVID symptoms and that nicotine agonism may reverse this effect.

This case series evaluates a manual therapy intervention (massage, mobility exercises, and thermal packs) for reducing fatigue in 20 long COVID patients. The treatment showed significant improvements in fatigue symptoms (45-52% reduction on the PFRS scale).

This case series evaluates methylprednisolone pulse therapy in 31 pediatric patients with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) occurring 2-6 weeks after COVID-19 infection. While the paper does study a treatment intervention, it focuses on acute post-infection inflammatory complications in children rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months post-infection), making it outside the long COVID scope.

A case series describing two pediatric patients who developed reactive arthritis during the acute phase of COVID-19 infection (second week post-infection). Both cases resolved with NSAIDs and rest over a two-month follow-up period.

A descriptive pilot study assessing immediate verbal learning performance in 17 post-ICU COVID-19 patients using the SCIP-S test. Found mild-moderate cognitive impairment in a subgroup (33.3%), with no treatment intervention applied.

This paper describes cognitive and psychiatric symptoms observed in post-acute COVID cases, including memory problems, poor concentration, and mental fatigue. It is a descriptive case series without any intervention or treatment being tested, making it ineligible for the intervention trials analysis.

A case series of 7 patients with persistent post-COVID olfactory dysfunction (hyposmia) treated with intranasal M2 macrophage conditioned medium for 28-30 days. Treatment improved olfactory perception and recognition at 6-12 month follow-up with high patient satisfaction and no safety concerns.

Case series describing four female patients who developed acute psychotic symptoms during COVID-19 recovery, diagnosed with brief psychotic disorder. The paper documents clinical presentations and proposes mechanisms but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case series of two long COVID patients with severe psychiatric manifestations (depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment) treated with esketamine (intravenous and intranasal). Both patients showed substantial clinical improvement and symptom remission within 6-8 weeks after esketamine treatment.

Cross-sectional and longitudinal study of 17 long COVID patients evaluated for peripheral neuropathy, with 59% showing objective test confirmation of small-fiber neuropathy. 65% of patients received immunotherapy treatment (corticosteroids and/or IV immunoglobulins), with longitudinal improvement averaging 52%.

This case series describes 6 patients who developed new-onset diabetes mellitus following acute COVID-19 infection, with clinical and biochemical data showing severe hyperglycemia at presentation and improvement over 2-4 months of follow-up. The paper focuses on acute/subacute post-infection metabolic complications rather than long COVID as a chronic syndrome, and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This paper describes cases of autoimmune encephalitis occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection, found in 3% of a laboratory cohort and 0.05% of COVID-19 patients. The study focuses on acute neurological complications during or immediately following COVID-19 infection, not long COVID sequelae.

Case report describing two patients who developed varicella-zoster virus (shingles) reactivation following COVID-19 infection or vaccination. The paper discusses potential mechanisms of VZV reactivation related to COVID-19-induced immunosuppression but does not study a treatment intervention for long COVID.

This paper characterizes the diagnostic and immunological features of post-COVID-19 POTS in children, examining how the condition presents in the pediatric population. It is a diagnostic/characterization study without an intervention or treatment component.

Case series reporting magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) findings in 3 patients with long-segment peripheral neuropathies following COVID-19 infection. This is a descriptive imaging study of post-COVID neuropathy manifestations with no intervention or treatment being tested.

Case series describing two patients who developed diffuse myoclonus and dystonia 3-4 weeks after COVID-19 infection, representing a potential post-infectious neurological complication. Both patients responded to immune-based therapy (IVIG and/or high-dose methylprednisolone), suggesting an immune-mediated mechanism.

This paper investigates the role of small fiber neuropathy in long COVID patients with neuropathic symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study appears to be a protocol or preliminary report with no treatment intervention being tested.

Reports initial outcomes of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) administered via telehealth to treat persisting symptoms in two patients with post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC). Demonstrates feasibility of remote neuromodulation intervention for long COVID symptom management.

This paper examines long-term outcomes of disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe COVID-19. As a conference abstract with no results reported, it appears to be a study protocol or preliminary announcement rather than a completed study.

This is a descriptive cross-sectional study documenting the frequency and types of post-acute COVID-19 sequelae symptoms observed in an outpatient neurology clinic. The paper characterizes PASC presentation patterns but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

A case series of 5 long COVID patients with cognitive deficits treated with EGb 761 (Ginkgo biloba extract) at 2×80 mg daily for up to 6 months. Treatment substantially improved or completely restored cognitive symptoms, concentration, attention deficits, and associated symptoms like fatigue and hyposmia with no detectable adverse effects.

Case report of 3 connective tissue disease patients who developed diffuse lymphadenopathy 3-4 weeks after mild COVID-19 resolution, treated with immunosuppressive therapy. No control group or systematic intervention trial—descriptive case series only.

This case report describes 3 female COVID-19 pneumonia patients who developed pulmonary fibrosis detected on follow-up CT imaging. The paper documents long-term respiratory sequelae but is a descriptive case series without treatment evaluation or control groups, making it ineligible for the intervention trials pipeline.

Case series describing three patients with interstitial lung disease-like radiological features attributed to long COVID, without prior acute COVID-19 infection. The paper demonstrates that long COVID can clinically and radiologically mimic ILD and should be considered as a differential diagnosis.

A case series of three non-diabetic long COVID patients who received evening carbohydrate supplementation to treat persistent night sweats. All three patients reported complete resolution of night sweats after one week of the dietary intervention.

A case series of 5 post-COVID patients who developed inflammatory arthritis (rheumatoid and reactive arthritis) weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Patients received various treatments including NSAIDs, corticosteroids, immunomodulators (golimumab), and DMARDs (methotrexate, leflunomide, hydroxychloroquine), demonstrating that COVID-19 can precipitate inflammatory joint disease requiring targeted treatment.

Case series of four long COVID patients who developed transient osteoporosis of the hip (TOH) 90-123 days post-infection and were treated with bisphosphonate therapy. Bisphosphonate treatment resulted in rapid pain relief, normalized MRI findings, and no progression to avascular necrosis.

Clinical observations of polymorbid long COVID patients presenting with multi-system involvement including pulmonary, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and neurological damage. The paper proposes treatment options for patients with immunoinflammatory syndrome and organ system complications.

Retrospective case series of 11 post-acute COVID-19 patients treated with Korean herbal medicine at a public health center in 2022. Korean medicine treatment was associated with significant improvements in cough and sore throat severity, with minimal adverse events reported.

This case series evaluates Tongtiao acupuncture-moxibustion therapy in 28 long COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction, treating them for 4 weeks with daily sessions. Results show significant improvements in olfactory test scores, TCM symptom scores, depression and anxiety scales, and increased serum cortisol levels post-treatment.

Case series describing two patients who developed biliary casts as a rare complication following severe COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentations, diagnostic findings, and ERCP treatment but does not evaluate an intervention or treatment protocol.

A single-case pilot study evaluating the feasibility and clinical utility of the Unified Protocol (UP), a transdiagnostic psychological intervention, in 12 long COVID patients with emotional disorders over 8 online sessions plus 6-month follow-up. Results showed high participant satisfaction and significant improvements in anxiety (67% of participants) and depression (75%) at post-assessment, with 67% of participants no longer meeting criteria for mental health diagnoses at follow-up.

Case series describing 3 patients who developed severe cholestasis during recovery from critical COVID-19, characterized by prolonged liver chemistry abnormalities and unique histologic features including cholangiocyte injury and hepatic microangiopathy. The paper identifies a novel post-COVID-19 cholangiopathy but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case report of two previously healthy patients who developed Crohn's disease within months after COVID-19 infection, suggesting COVID-19 may trigger IBD development in genetically predisposed individuals. The paper presents clinical presentations, diagnostic findings, and treatment responses but does not address long COVID or persistent post-COVID symptoms.

A cross-sectional case-series study of 366 COVID-19 positive UNRWA staff in Jordan documenting the clinical manifestations of acute COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome. The study found that 71.3% of participants continued to suffer from persistent symptoms including fatigue, shortness of breath, anxiety, and cognitive impairment, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series examines the development of type 1 diabetes mellitus in 15 children following COVID-19 infection, all presenting in diabetic ketoacidosis with elevated HbA1c and high SARS-CoV-2 antibodies. The study suggests SARS-CoV-2 may directly trigger diabetes development in children, even during asymptomatic infection, though the exact classification of post-COVID diabetes remains unclear.

Descriptive case series of 21 patients with erythema nodosum (EN) and joint symptoms occurring at different time points after COVID-19 infection (acute, ongoing symptomatic, and post-COVID syndrome stages). Reports clinical and laboratory features of EN as a post-infectious manifestation without testing any intervention or treatment.

A clinical review presenting case reports of patients initially misdiagnosed with post-COVID syndrome who actually had Alzheimer's disease, persistent postural-perceptual dizziness, chronic migraine, medication-overuse headache, or musculoskeletal pain. The paper emphasizes the importance of differential diagnosis rather than testing a specific treatment intervention.

Case report of two patients presenting with symptoms attributed to post-COVID syndrome but diagnosed with hereditary motor neuropathy (GARS1 mutation) and myasthenia gravis respectively. The paper demonstrates that prolonged neurological symptoms can be caused by underlying genetic or autoimmune conditions rather than persistent COVID-19 pathology.

This case series describes three pediatric patients who developed neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (NLUTD) following COVID-19 infection, with clinical features resembling Elsberg syndrome. The paper documents clinical manifestations and management strategies but does not evaluate or test any specific intervention or treatment.

Case series describing neurological rehabilitation approaches in post-COVID patients, with emphasis on differential diagnosis of fatigue, cognitive impairment, and psychosomatic comorbidities. Presents diagnostic protocols for identifying underlying causes of post-COVID symptoms in both hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients to guide targeted rehabilitation.

A case series of six long COVID patients treated with methylphenidate (5-20 mg) for post-COVID cognitive dysfunction, followed for 4-8 weeks. Three patients reported subjective improvement, with statistically significant improvements in Hopkins verbal learning test immediate and delayed recall and category-cued verbal fluency.

Case report of two pediatric patients presenting with unusual manifestations of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) following COVID-19 infection, including pericardial effusion with coronary artery dilation and cardiac tamponade. No treatment intervention is described; this is a descriptive case report documenting clinical presentations rather than evaluating a treatment.

Two case studies of COVID-19 patients with acute cardiac mechanical dysfunction assessed daily during the acute infection period. Findings show variable patterns of cardiac impairment during acute infection, not long COVID sequelae.

Case study of two long COVID patients (one native English speaker, one ESL) examining cognitive-linguistic impairments including brain fog, word-finding difficulty, and pragmatic/discourse difficulties months after acute infection. No treatment intervention tested; descriptive case analysis only.

This article discusses two case reports of functional neurological symptom disorder (conversion disorder), one following COVID-19 vaccination and one in the context of long COVID, using a psychodynamic lens to understand etiology and treatment. It is primarily a clinical commentary and case discussion rather than a treatment trial or outcomes study.

This case series examines histopathological changes in hippocampal tissue from 50 COVID-19 autopsies to understand the cellular basis of post-COVID brain fog and cognitive dysfunction. While it provides mechanistic insights into long COVID-related CNS damage, it is a descriptive autopsy study without any treatment intervention or clinical outcomes being tested.

Case series of 11 COVID-19 patients followed for 167 days with serial chest CT imaging to evaluate long-term radiological outcomes. Study focuses on acute infection recovery and lung healing patterns, not on long COVID syndrome or treatment of persistent post-COVID symptoms.

Two case studies of adults with long COVID treated with Icosapent Ethyl (an omega-3 fatty acid derivative). Both patients experienced resolution of long COVID symptoms following treatment, suggesting potential immunomodulatory effects warrant further investigation.

This case series describes clinical characteristics and persistent symptoms in 154 post-COVID-19 patients attending a private clinic in Erbil, Iraq. The study identifies associations between demographic factors (age, marital status, smoking) and severity of post-COVID symptoms, with hypertension as the most common comorbidity.

Case series describing postintubation tracheal stenosis as a complication in severe and non-severe COVID-19 patients, including those with long COVID. The paper discusses differential diagnosis and imaging considerations but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper presents two retrospective case reports of primary immunodeficiency patients who developed new autoimmune symptoms or worsening of existing autoimmune conditions following COVID-19 infection. It describes clinical observations but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Retrospective review of 273 PASC patients presenting to a cardiovascular outpatient unit, identifying 5 newly diagnosed cases of vasospastic angina as a potential cause of chest pain in long COVID. The study is a diagnostic characterization study rather than a treatment trial, and represents a secondary analysis of existing patient records without intervention.

A case series of 4 post-COVID patients who developed spontaneous pneumothorax weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, demonstrating this as a late COVID complication. Tube thoracostomy under video-assisted control was the treatment approach, with all patients recovering successfully.

A case series of 9 pediatric patients with long COVID presenting with persistent dizziness, describing diagnostic evaluation for postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and treatment outcomes with nonpharmacologic therapy and medications. Most patients experienced improvement in symptoms and quality of life with pharmacologic intervention, though nonpharmacologic therapy alone was ineffective.

This case series describes three COVID-19 patients who developed new-onset dysphonia (voice disorders) and documents their clinical presentation and outcomes. While it identifies dysphonia as a possible persistent manifestation of COVID-19, it presents only observational case reports without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

Case report and literature review of 66 published cases of pericarditis occurring 14-255 days after acute COVID-19 infection, with persistent symptoms for at least 6 months. Treatment with NSAIDs and colchicine was effective in most patients (48/54), though 12 required escalation to corticosteroids; only 6 patients had persistent symptoms despite therapy.

Case series of 18 patients with post-COVID-19 myocarditis (6.5 months post-infection) diagnosed by endomyocardial biopsy, with 28% presenting concurrent endocarditis (NBTE or IE). All patients received steroid therapy (methylprednisolone ~24 mg/day), with 10 monitored for 3+ months showing ejection fraction improvement to 44-46%.

This prospective case series evaluated the effects of a 25-session neurofunctional physiotherapy protocol on balance and functional outcomes in 10 long COVID patients with neuromuscular manifestations. The intervention produced statistically significant improvements in balance (Berg Balance Scale, p=0.034) and instrumental activities of daily living (p=0.026), though basic activities of daily living showed no significant gains.

Case series describing mitral valve chordal rupture occurring 3-5 weeks after mild SARS-CoV-2 infection in middle-aged men, likely related to post-viral endomyocarditis. The paper documents a cardiac complication of long COVID but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This cross-sectional case series assessed morbidity and frailty in 204 elderly post-COVID-19 patients using geriatric assessment tools, identifying cognitive impairment, multiple comorbidities, and functional limitations as independent factors associated with frailty. The study describes the health burden of post-COVID-19 in older adults but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Autopsy study examining pathomorphological changes and clinical laboratory parameters in 9 deceased patients with prior COVID-19 infection. Findings show unresolved viral pneumonia and diffuse alveolar damage in all cases, but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.

This prospective case series analyzes 13 patients with rhinoorbital mucormycosis occurring in the post-COVID syndrome, examining clinical presentation and pathomorphological features. The study identifies vascular and perineural changes in affected tissues that may explain the unique pathogenesis of fungal lesions in post-COVID patients and proposes treatment tactics for necrotic fungal lesions.

Histological study of lung biopsy specimens from 20 post-COVID syndrome patients showing interstitial pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis patterns. No treatment intervention tested; descriptive pathological analysis only.

This case series describes physiological and radiological findings in four COVID-19 patients assessed 60-90 days post-discharge, documenting persistent fatigue and interstitial lung abnormalities. While it is about long COVID, it is a descriptive case series without treatment intervention, making it an observational study rather than a treatment trial.

This paper describes a case series of 10 children with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), examining the neurological manifestations and differential diagnosis from musculoskeletal lesions during COVID-19. While GBS occurred post-COVID in some cases, the paper focuses on acute-phase complications and diagnostic differentiation rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months post-infection) or treatment of long COVID.

Case series of 2 patients presenting with transient spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee shortly after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated nonoperatively with complete symptom resolution. Highlights a potential post-COVID musculoskeletal complication and suggests conservative management should be preferred over aggressive surgical intervention.

This paper presents 4 clinical cases of ANCA vasculitis that developed approximately 3 months after COVID-19 infection, examining the autoimmune complications of post-COVID syndrome. The authors describe the clinical manifestations and autoantibody findings but do not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic outcome.

Case series describing acute psychotic episodes in COVID-19 patients during active infection, with treatment response to antipsychotics. This focuses on acute COVID-19 manifestations rather than long COVID sequelae.

Autopsy study examining histological changes in lung tissue from 19 deceased COVID-19 patients, focusing on post-COVID pathological findings. Identifies microcirculation disorders, thrombosis, and acute lung damage as key pathological features without testing any intervention.

This case series describes 11 COVID-19 patients treated with corticosteroids who subsequently developed osteonecrosis of the femoral head, with severity correlating to corticosteroid dose and duration. While it is a long COVID complication study, it is excluded because it does not study a treatment intervention—it is a descriptive case series reporting an adverse outcome rather than evaluating a therapeutic intervention for long COVID.

Two clinical case observations of acute ocular vascular pathology (retinovasculitis with retinal vein thrombosis and central retinal vein thrombosis) occurring 1.5-2.5 months after COVID-19 infection, treated with anti-inflammatory, anticoagulant, and supportive therapies. One case showed improvement with treatment, while the other developed secondary neovascular glaucoma with poor visual prognosis, with comorbid conditions (hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia) contributing to disease severity.

Case series of 350 patients (60% acute COVID, 20% respiratory long COVID, 20% neurological long COVID) treated with whole-organ photobiomodulation (PBM) using LED pads or scanning lasers. Reports symptom resolution including elimination of dyspnea, brain fog relief, and improved cognitive function, with 99.75% showing improvement and only 0.25% unresolved cases.

A case series of 8 post-acute COVID-19 patients presenting with episcleritis and sub-conjunctival haemorrhage 3-4 weeks after initial infection. Patients treated with topical steroids and ganciclovir showed improvement/recovery within 10 days, demonstrating ocular manifestations as post-acute COVID-19 sequelae.

This paper reports 4 cases of long COVID patients treated with nirmatrelvir at different time points post-infection, showing variable outcomes including symptom improvement in some cases and symptomatic rebound in others. The authors argue for the need for systematic studies of antiviral therapy as a potential treatment for long COVID.

This case series describes fungal sinusitis (primarily mucormycosis and aspergillosis) occurring in 10 patients during the acute post-COVID period (April-June 2021). While these are infectious complications in recently infected patients, the paper is not about long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks-months after infection) but rather acute complications occurring immediately post-infection in hospitalized or recently infected patients.

Retrospective case-series evaluating health-related quality of life and disability in 45 COVID-19 survivors of critical illness, assessed 30-90 days post-discharge using EQ-5D-5L and WHODAS 2.0 instruments. Found that 64% had moderate to extreme problems in mobility, self-care, activities, pain/discomfort, or anxiety/depression; concludes organized follow-up is needed to improve outcomes.

A literature review summarizing 25 published clinical cases of acute arthritis associated with COVID-19 from 2020-2021, analyzing patient demographics and joint involvement patterns. The paper discusses post-infectious arthritis as an immune-mediated sequela of COVID-19 and treatment approaches, but does not present original research or test a specific intervention.

This cross-sectional study evaluated long-term effects of COVID-19 in 109 adolescent patients diagnosed with non-severe disease, using telephone follow-up at a median of 121.6 days post-diagnosis. Five patients (4.6%) reported persistent symptoms including myalgia, fatigue, cough, chest pain, palpitations, sleep disorders, or psychiatric problems, suggesting that long COVID can occur in otherwise healthy adolescents following mild infection.

Case series of 3 patients with pulmonary cavities as a late COVID-19 complication treated with surgical intervention (VATS lobectomy or thoracotomy). All patients recovered successfully post-operatively, with a literature review of 12 additional publications identifying surgical therapy as an effective treatment option for severe pulmonary cavity complications in long COVID patients.

This case series describes 11 male patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) following COVID-19 infection, exploring the potential association between post-COVID-19 infection and AVN occurrence. The study suggests hypercoagulability, inflammation, and corticosteroid exposure during COVID-19 treatment may accelerate AVN progression, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention for AVN or long COVID.

An uncontrolled case series evaluating maraviroc (CCR5 antagonist) plus pravastatin in 18 long COVID patients over 6-12 weeks. Treatment showed significant improvements in neurological, autonomic, respiratory, cardiac, and fatigue symptoms with correlating decreases in vascular biomarkers (sCD40L, VEGF).

A case series of three post-COVID syndrome patients who received monitored aerobic exercise combined with supplemental oxygen therapy over 22 sessions. All patients showed ~54% improvement in exercise tolerance, normalized heart rate/blood pressure response, and remission or improvement of symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, and post-exertional malaise.

This case report describes two patients with prolonged dyspnea and reduced effort capacity lasting 4-5 months following acute COVID-19 infection, diagnosed with post-acute COVID-19 syndrome. The patients were passively followed for 6 months without any intervention, and symptoms improved spontaneously over time.

This study detects residual SARS-CoV-2 viral antigen and RNA in tissue samples (appendix and breast) from 2 long COVID patients 175-462 days post-infection using immunohistochemistry and RNAscope. The findings suggest ongoing viral replication in tissue reservoirs, contributing to understanding of long COVID pathophysiology rather than testing any intervention.

A case series of three long COVID patients treated with graduated treadmill exercise combined with supplemental oxygen twice weekly for 22 sessions. All patients showed ~54% improvement in exercise tolerance, improved autonomic function, and remission or improvement of dyspnea, fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and other PASC symptoms.

This case series reports on three long COVID patients treated with stellate ganglion block (SGB), a local anesthetic procedure targeting sympathetic nerves. All three patients showed significant improvement in fatigue, brain fog, and smell/taste dysfunction, suggesting dysautonomia as a key mechanism in long COVID and SGB as a potential therapeutic intervention.

Case series of 13 long COVID patients who took extended courses (7.5-30 days) of oral nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (Paxlovid), documenting symptom changes before, during, and after treatment. Results were mixed, with some participants experiencing meaningful symptom reduction while others saw no benefit or experienced adverse effects.

Two case reports of immunocompromised patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome and interstitial inflammation who failed conventional therapies (molnupiravir, Paxlovid, corticosteroids) but responded to low-dose ruxolitinib salvage therapy. Ruxolitinib relieved persistent hypoxemia and resolved interstitial inflammation within 1-2 months.

A cross-sectional study of 30 patients admitted within 4 weeks of acute post-COVID sequelae, examining clinical presentations and prognostic factors following acute infection during the first COVID wave in India. The paper characterizes severe post-COVID manifestations and identifies factors associated with poor clinical outcomes.

Autopsy study examining β-amyloid deposits in brains of COVID-19 patients, with speculation about potential role in post-COVID cognitive impairment. Study describes pathological findings in deceased patients rather than evaluating any treatment intervention.

This case series describes 18 young men with asymptomatic COVID-19 who presented with acute ischemic stroke in the convalescent phase, with median time from positive serology to stroke of 54.5 days. The study documents the clinical and imaging characteristics of these stroke cases but does not evaluate any treatment intervention—it is a descriptive observational case series of a late COVID-19 complication.

Case series of 9 post-COVID-19 patients with pulmonary embolism, predominantly affecting females, presenting with breathlessness and chest pain. One-year follow-up showed mostly normal lab results but persistent elevated thrombotic risk and reduced quality of life scores, highlighting the need for monitoring and mental health support.

Retrospective case series of 30 long COVID patients evaluated in an outpatient psychiatric department, describing sociodemographic characteristics, psychiatric diagnoses, and treatment outcomes. Patients received psychotherapy, medication (modafinil, antidepressants), and cognitive rehabilitation targeting neuropsychiatric sequelae including depression, anxiety, fatigue, and cognitive impairment.

This case series examines the prevalence and characteristics of rheumatoid-associated autoantibodies in acute COVID-19 patients, finding such antibodies in 20% of patients with varying levels by disease severity. The study focuses on acute infection dynamics and autoimmune responses during active COVID-19, not long COVID or any treatment intervention.

Case reports of two COVID-19 patients who developed early lung fibrosis during acute hospitalization, with radiological worsening despite clinical improvement. The paper highlights the need for long-term follow-up but does not test or evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Clinical case report describing multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) that develops in children 2-6 weeks after acute COVID-19 infection. The paper presents clinical cases and discusses possible variants and outcomes but contains no treatment intervention or trial data.

Case series of 4 patients describing ophthalmic inflammatory complications associated with COVID-19 infection, including manifestations in both acute and post-COVID periods (2-5 months after infection). Reports clinical features and treatments of eye damage including keratitis, iridocyclitis, dacryoadenitis, and episcleritis.

Clinical case series describing dyspnea presentations in elderly patients with late post-COVID-19 syndrome, analyzing different mechanisms of lung tissue damage (fibrotic vs non-fibrotic) and risk factors for progression. No treatment intervention is tested or evaluated; this is a descriptive observational analysis of clinical presentations and pathological mechanisms.

A pilot case series evaluating photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) as a treatment for olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in 6 long COVID patients. The study found statistically significant improvements in smell and taste function, with improvements sustained at 6-month follow-up and associated quality-of-life gains.

This case series describes 9-month follow-up of pediatric long COVID patients using lung ultrasound and respiratory testing at a university pediatrics department. The study found that pathological lung ultrasound signs resolved in 6-9 months despite early improvement in respiratory symptoms, highlighting the need for customized pediatric long COVID follow-up protocols.

This case series reports three post-COVID-19 patients with thromboembolism complications and discusses post-discharge anticoagulation prophylaxis. The cases highlight the clinical dilemma of balancing thromboembolism prevention against bleeding risk in recovered COVID-19 patients.

This article describes the clinical presentation and pathophysiological mechanisms of post-COVID-19 syndrome through comprehensive biochemical and immunological screening of three clinical cases. It characterizes organ dysfunction patterns, metabolic disorders, and immunological dysfunction in post-COVID patients but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic approach.

A case series of 14 patients describing new or worsening rheumatic manifestations following SARS-CoV-2 infection, including rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, reactive arthritis, and post-COVID syndrome. Patients received various treatments (DMARDs, prednisone, NSAIDs, lifestyle modifications) with variable symptomatic improvement at follow-up.

A case series of 15 long COVID patients treated with individualized homeopathic therapy, documenting symptom improvements. 93.3% of patients experienced improvement to complete healing within a median of 37 days, as assessed by modified Naranjo criteria.

A case series of 7 long COVID patients (6 with headaches, 1 with back pain) who received replacement therapy with melatonin, L-arginine, and L-carnitine after documented deficiencies. All patients experienced pain relief within 10 days, with normalized biomarker levels at one month follow-up.

A retrospective case series of 20 post-COVID-19 patients with acute invasive fungal rhinosinusitis (AIFR) treated with IV amphotericin B and surgical debridement. Combined antifungal therapy with local tissue debridement achieved a 15% mortality rate, demonstrating improved prognosis for this serious post-COVID fungal complication.

A single-center retrospective chart review of 12 patients who underwent bilateral lung transplantation for COVID-19 related lung disease between January 2021 and June 2023, including cases of COVID-19 ARDS, post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis (PCPF), and SARS-CoV-2 induced interstitial lung disease exacerbation. Median survival ranged from 12.6 months for PCPF to 20.5 months for IPF cases, with 91% 3-month survival and 8 patients alive over 1-year post-transplant, demonstrating promising short- and long-term outcomes despite significant morbidity.

This case series describes 3 patients who developed osteomyelitis of the maxillofacial region post-COVID-19 and received surgical intervention. The authors highlight risk factors for these infections and emphasize early diagnosis for improved surgical outcomes.

Retrospective case series of 15 long COVID patients treated with Korean medicine (herbal remedies, acupuncture, cupping) at a Korean medicine hospital from January 2021 to April 2022. Treatment showed improvements in cough, dyspnea, fatigue, and quality of life measures (NRS, mMRC, LCQ, QOL-VAS, PCFS) with mild adverse events.

Six long COVID patients (>30 days of symptoms) received hyperbaric oxygen therapy and were assessed using ImPACT questionnaire, muscle/joint pain scale, and modified Borg dyspnea scale. All patients showed symptom improvement to pre-infection levels or better, suggesting HBO2 may improve symptom scores and quality of life, though authors call for larger randomized studies.

A case series describing five long COVID patients with pulmonary fibrosis who received pirfenidone, a drug used for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The addition of pirfenidone showed marked improvement in symptoms and radiological findings in these patients.

A case series of 21 long COVID patients completing a 12-week plank-based strength training programme targeting trunk and pelvic muscles. The intervention significantly improved muscle activation in core muscles and reduced fatigue across multiple domains.

Retrospective chart review of 29 pediatric patients with persistent respiratory symptoms 1-6 months post-COVID-19 infection seen at a pulmonary clinic. Study describes symptom prevalence and functional findings (6MWT, lung function) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective case series of 33 post-acute COVID-19 patients from a Spanish family medicine office describing clinical-epidemiological characteristics and comorbidities. Main findings include persistent general and respiratory symptoms in 36% and 32% of patients respectively, with 14 new diagnoses during post-acute follow-up including cardiovascular and metabolic complications.

A Czech multicentric observational study of 39 children with persistent respiratory symptoms more than 12 weeks after COVID-19. Most children had exercise-induced dyspnoea and cough, with abnormal lung function in <15% and abnormal imaging in <20%, and identified four clinical subgroups with median symptom remission of 4 months.

Case series of 28 long COVID patients presenting with telogen effluvium and alopecia areata, documenting hair loss beginning one month after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Study reports symptom characteristics but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

Literature review on multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS) occurring after COVID-19 recovery, with emphasis on gastroenterological manifestations that can mimic acute abdominal conditions. Presents two case reports of MIS-A from a single institution to raise awareness and reduce morbidity/mortality.

Case series of four young COVID-19 patients who developed pulmonary embolism 2-4 weeks after hospital discharge, with markedly elevated D-dimer levels. Describes a post-discharge thrombotic complication of COVID-19 but does not test or evaluate any intervention.

This case series evaluates the safety and efficacy of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (hBM-MSC EVs) as a novel therapeutic intervention for long COVID patients. The study leverages the immunomodulatory and regenerative properties of stem cell vesicles to address the persistent symptoms of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC).

This case series describes three post-COVID-19 patients with olfactory and gustatory dysfunction treated with photobiomodulation therapy using red and infrared lasers. Two patients achieved complete olfactory recovery, with one also recovering full taste function, while the third showed partial improvement in both senses over a 6-month to 1-year follow-up period.

Reports three cases of acute COVID-19 patients with persistent respiratory symptoms treated with anisodamine hydrobromide, showing symptomatic improvement. This paper focuses on acute COVID-19 infection management, not long COVID sequelae occurring weeks to months post-infection.

This study evaluates Calcarea Carbonicum 200C homeopathic treatment in 20 post-COVID patients with persistent symptoms, finding a statistically significant 52% decrease in IgG levels after treatment and confirming the molecular composition of the remedy via FTIR spectroscopy. The authors acknowledge limitations (lack of control group, small sample size) and call for larger randomized controlled trials to validate these preliminary findings.

Observational study of 10 patients with telogen effluvium (hair loss) following COVID-19 infection, compared with 28 cases from literature review. While the paper documents a post-COVID symptom, it does not study or evaluate any treatment intervention for the condition.

Case series of 29 patients with rhino-orbital mucormycosis (ROM) that developed 20-40 days after COVID-19, presenting ocular and orbital symptoms. While occurring post-COVID, this paper focuses on acute fungal complications rather than long COVID syndrome and does not evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Case report describing two instances of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) that developed following COVID-19 infection, proposing COVID-19 as a potential trigger for AIH debut. The paper documents clinical presentations but does not evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

Case series and literature review examining joint manifestations (myalgia, arthralgia, arthritis) in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients during the second year of the pandemic. Discusses clinical presentations and reviews existing literature on joint complications after SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Case series of patients with psoriasis exacerbated or onset after COVID-19 infection, treated at a Moscow dermatology clinic from 2021-2023. Reports on plasmapheresis and other individualized treatment approaches for post-COVID syndrome with dermatological manifestations.

A case series describing the application of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy in 2 long COVID patients with ARDS complications. After 5 days of HFNC therapy, patients showed improvements in respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, ROX index, and blood gas parameters.
Case series evaluating acupuncture treatment for long COVID patients, focusing on fatigue and mood disturbances. Reports improvement in patient symptoms after 1-4 acupuncture sessions.

A cross-sectional case-series study of 300 COVID-19 patients attending a private GP clinic in Amman, Jordan, documenting the clinical manifestations of acute COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 symptoms. The study found 28% prevalence of long COVID with fatigue, shortness of breath, anxiety, and cognitive symptoms as the most common long-term effects, but did not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Prospective case series of 8 chronic COVID-19 patients assessing cognitive function and brain metabolism via Montreal Cognitive Assessment and 18F-FDG PET imaging at subacute and chronic stages (~6 months post-symptom onset). Study documents significant recovery in frontoparietal hypometabolism and cognitive performance over time, though residual impairment remains, but does not evaluate any specific intervention or treatment.

This case series describes 122 post-COVID-19 syndrome patients discharged from ICUs who enrolled in a chronic care program (Remeo®) in Colombia, where they received physical therapy, occupational therapy, respiratory therapy, and psychological support. The program delivered over 9,500 interventions in the first four months, demonstrating chronic care as a viable option for facilitating recovery and reducing ICU burden.

This case series reports 17 long COVID patients treated with H.E.L.P. apheresis (an extracorporeal blood purification procedure) to remove microclots and inflammatory mediators. Of the 17 patients, 16 experienced immediate improvement and 12 achieved near-full recovery, with 15 maintaining improvements at 6-10 month follow-up.

This case report describes two patients who developed hypomanic episodes following acute COVID-19 pneumonia, with normal investigations and age-related neuroimaging findings. The authors suggest psychiatric symptoms may result from psychosocial stressors and COVID-19-induced brain vulnerability, but this is not a long COVID study as it focuses on acute post-infection psychiatric manifestations rather than persistent symptoms weeks to months later.

Case series reporting two acute COVID-19 ARDS patients who developed Tapia syndrome (cranial nerve compression injury) as a complication of prone positioning during mechanical ventilation. The paper describes the acute ICU complication and neurologic sequelae but does not study long COVID or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Two case reports describing MRI findings of post-COVID myocardial damage in patients with cardiovascular complications. The paper presents imaging syndromes of focal infarction and diffuse inflammatory lesion without testing any treatment or intervention.

A case series describing two long COVID patients with arthralgias, anginal chest pain, and sub-endocardial ischemia who showed symptom improvement following baricitinib treatment. The report demonstrates potential therapeutic benefit of JAK inhibition for long COVID-associated cardiovascular manifestations.

This paper describes CT imaging findings in 120 patients with long-term COVID-19 pneumonia over 6-12 months of follow-up, presenting two clinical cases. It documents structural lung changes and their progression/regression but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is purely observational imaging documentation.

This study examines nine cases of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), six of which were associated with prior COVID-19 infection, comparing disease severity and course between COVID-associated and non-COVID GBS. The findings show that COVID-associated GBS develops more frequently in men over 50 and presents with greater severity, including axonal lesions and prolonged recovery.

Case series and systematic review of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) triggered by COVID-19 infection in genetically predisposed individuals. Reports three cases and reviews literature suggesting RA may be induced post-COVID, but does not study any treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of 1,500 case histories from a Russian neurological clinic examining clinical and epidemiological characteristics of neurological variants of post-COVID syndrome from July 2020 to February 2022. Identified 30 patients with confirmed COVID-19 and neurological conditions, predominantly affecting the central nervous system (74%) with encephalopathies, followed by peripheral nervous system involvement (23%) including Guillain-Barré syndrome.

Case series of 16 patients who developed acute polyneuropathy 11-63 days after COVID-19 infection, with electroneuromyography showing various neuropathy patterns. Study documents the clinical manifestations and neurological sequelae but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series describes ten patients with post-COVID-19 respiratory dysfunction (ventilatory and diffusional disorders) and evaluates the effectiveness of inhalation therapy, including bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids. The study demonstrates that Bufomix Easyhailer® showed good efficacy and safety in managing post-COVID respiratory complications.

Clinical case series describing pulmonary interstitial lung abnormalities in post-COVID-19 patients, with analysis of pathogenic mechanisms shared with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Treatment according to standard recommendations showed positive clinical effects in the presented cases.

This prospective observational study describes 10 COVID-19 patients with severe disease and post-infection mental symptoms treated with fluoxetine and paroxetine, reporting progressive reduction in illness severity and anxiety.
