However, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 severity and stress-related mental health effects during active infection, not persistent symptoms weeks/months after infection (long COVID/PASC).

This clinical trial compared TCM (Traditional Chinese Medicine) treatment outcomes between seniors (>45 years) and younger adults (<44 years) with COVID-19, examining effects on pre-existing conditions, complications, and post-syndromes. Results indicated that TCM treatment could stabilize pre-existing diseases, manage complications, and prevent post-syndrome occurrence in COVID-19 patients.

Case series describing two female patients who developed subacute thyroiditis 6 weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting with neck pain, fever, and fatigue. Both patients received corticosteroid and beta-blocker treatment with complete resolution of symptoms within 3 weeks, establishing post-COVID-19 thyroiditis as a treatable complication.

Case series of five children who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) following COVID-19 infection, presenting neurological manifestations during the pandemic's second wave. All patients responded well to intravenous immunoglobulin treatment without residual weakness.

This retrospective study of 70 patients with post-COVID-19 herpetic keratitis compares clinical features between primary and recurrent cases and assesses viral serology levels. The study documents increased frequency of stromal forms and bilateral lesions in post-COVID patients, particularly those with severe initial infection, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of 10 patients with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) diagnosed within 30 days of COVID-19 infection, evaluating clinical, electrophysiological, and treatment characteristics. While GBS is a post-COVID neurological complication, this paper focuses on acute post-infectious syndrome rather than long COVID (persistent symptoms weeks to months after acute infection).

Observational case series describing salivary gland complications in 17 patients 3-4 weeks after COVID-19 recovery, including xerostomia, taste loss, and reduced parotid secretion. No intervention or treatment was evaluated; this is a descriptive clinical documentation of residual phenomena rather than a treatment study.

Two case reports evaluating non-invasive brain microcurrent stimulation (NIBS) therapy in long-COVID patients with cognitive and visual impairment. Treatment produced marked improvements in cognition and partial reversal of visual field loss within 3-4 days, with restoration of vascular autoregulation measured by retinal dynamic vascular analysis.

Case report of two patients with post-COVID-19 osteomyelitis of the mandible in otherwise healthy individuals. Describes clinical, histologic, and radiographic presentations and discusses pathophysiology but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

This paper describes clinical observations of remote complications from the disappearing lung syndrome in post-COVID patients who were previously treated for COVID-19 pneumonia at a Ukrainian institute. It is a retrospective case study documenting radiological manifestations (emphysema, cysts, pneumothorax) but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or therapeutic approach.

Case series describing COVID-19 outcomes in 13 peritoneal dialysis patients during the acute phase of the pandemic (March 2020–January 2021). While 81.8% reported persisting symptoms beyond one month, the study focuses on acute COVID-19 severity and complications in a chronic kidney disease population, not on long COVID as a condition of interest.

Two case reports of persistent dyspnea in patients recovering from COVID-19, describing clinical presentation and symptomatic management strategies. Discusses pathogenesis and management approaches for common long COVID symptoms.

An uncontrolled case series evaluating electro-acupuncture treatment for post-COVID menstrual irregularities in 40 patients across 12 weekly sessions. Results showed 82.5% effectiveness with 33 of 40 patients achieving clinical cure and improved quality of life.

This case series reports outcomes of electroacupuncture treatment for long COVID brain fog in 57 patients in Eastern Canada, using specific acupoints (DU20, DU24, EX-HN1) for 12 treatments over 4 weeks. The study reports an 84.2% effectiveness rate with improvements in memory, concentration, and attention, though it lacks a control group and uses subjective outcome measures.

Retrospective cohort study of nine long COVID patients with persistent headaches treated with calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibodies. Treatment resulted in significant reductions in monthly headache days, severity scores, and quality of life impairment.

A consecutive series study of 311 Nepali men with documented COVID-19 infection, contacted 3-4 months post-diagnosis to assess symptom persistence. At 3.5 months, 25.7% reported incomplete recovery with fatigue (17.4%), pain (12.4%), and cognitive issues (10.8%) being most common; recovery continued with only 4.4% unrecovered by 9 months.

This case series describes five pediatric patients who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a literature review of post-COVID neurological complications. The paper documents clinical presentations and outcomes but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case series describing neuro-ophthalmological manifestations of COVID-19, including optic neuropathy in the post-COVID recovery phase. No treatment intervention is evaluated; the paper documents clinical presentations and sequelae.

Case report of two COVID-19 patients who developed pulmonary fibrosis with restrictive lung disease during post-acute follow-up. No treatment intervention is tested; this is a descriptive case series documenting a long COVID complication.

Case series describing chest CT imaging features of pulmonary sequelae in four COVID-19 patients, including pulmonary fibrosis and organizing pneumonia patterns with persistent dyspnea. No treatment intervention is tested or evaluated; this is a descriptive imaging study of long COVID complications.

A non-randomized controlled study evaluating a 4-week interdisciplinary telehealth intervention combining physical therapy and speech therapy for long COVID patients experiencing fatigue, breathlessness, and vocal fatigue. The study found positive outcomes in pulse oximetry and modified Borg scale readings after the treatment period of manual stretching and self-directed exercises.

Describes the acute and long-term cardiovascular, metabolic, and systemic consequences of COVID-19 based on case observations. Does not test or evaluate any specific intervention, and appears to be a narrative review of clinical manifestations rather than a treatment trial.

Case series describing four patients who developed spontaneous secondary pneumothorax during the post-COVID period, presenting with sudden respiratory distress and hypoxia. The authors discuss potential etiologies including persistent inflammation and ischemic damage, and propose future research to identify causal associations with prior COVID-19 treatments.

Clinical case series of 31 pediatric multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C) cases and 23 systemic connective tissue disease cases associated with COVID-19, plus 29 cases of exacerbated pre-existing connective tissue disease following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study describes clinical presentations and emphasizes the importance of timely anti-inflammatory treatment tailored to individual patients.

This paper presents two clinical cases of post-COVID syndrome manifesting as gastrointestinal dysfunction—dyspeptic disorders in one patient and diarrhea with colonic polyp growth in another, occurring weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents clinical observations and discusses potential relationships between COVID-19 infection and GI pathology but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

Case report describing the detection of residual SARS-CoV-2 antigen and RNA in tissue samples from two long COVID patients 163 and 426 days post-symptom onset. The study found viral nucleocapsid protein in appendix, skin, and breast tissues colocalized with immune cells, supporting the hypothesis that the gastrointestinal tract may serve as a viral reservoir.

Case series describing four patients with neurological complications (radiculitis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, myelitis) following SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination, all positive for anti-ACE2 antibodies. The paper is excluded because it presents observational case descriptions without testing any intervention or treatment.

This early-phase prospective trial evaluated the safety, tolerability, and effects of tolerability-adapted exercise therapy in three patients with severe COVID-19, delivered remotely over 30 weeks with escalated aerobic doses. Exercise therapy was safe and well-tolerated, with improvements in exercise capacity and quality of life, along with marked alterations in immune and protein phenotypes related to post-COVID condition.

Case series of 9 long COVID patients treated with high-dose immunoglobulin therapy for 3 months. Six patients completed treatment and all showed significant to remarkable clinical improvement in pulmonary, neurological, and cardiological symptoms.

An open-label case series evaluating antiviral therapy (IMC-2 alone or combined with Paxlovid) in 24 long COVID patients over 120 days. Both groups showed fatigue reduction, with the combined antiviral group demonstrating statistically significant improvements in fatigue, brain fog, and dysautonomia that persisted at follow-up.

Case report describing five patients who developed or experienced worsening of autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, Graves disease, thyroiditis) following COVID-19 infection. No treatment intervention was tested; the paper documents disease manifestations and immune responses triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection.

A case series of 5 long COVID patients with post-infectious neurological syndromes (PINS) who underwent intensive neurorehabilitation, with clinical and electrophysiological assessments at baseline and 3/6-month follow-ups. Results showed variable functional recovery, with myelitis cases improving more substantially than polyradiculoneuropathy cases.

Autopsy study examining microglial and macrophage activation in COVID-19 deceased patients using immunohistochemical analysis. Findings show pronounced activation in white matter, brain stem, and cerebellar areas, with reduced but detectable activation in post-COVID patients, potentially explaining long COVID syndrome mechanisms.

Case report of two post-COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction treated with traditional acupuncture at the LI20 point. Acupuncture provided short-term symptom relief lasting 2-4 days, with improvement duration increasing with repeated treatments.

This paper reports clinical presentations of 100 patients attending a post-COVID-19 syndrome neurology outpatient clinic, assessing cognitive impairment, fatigue, headache, and other neurological sequelae. While it characterizes long COVID phenotypes, it is a descriptive cross-sectional study with no treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

Open-label case series of 18 long COVID patients treated with the CCR5 antagonist maraviroc and pravastatin targeting the monocytic-endothelial-platelet axis. Six to twelve weeks of combination therapy produced significant clinical improvements in neurological, autonomic, respiratory, cardiac, and fatigue symptoms with corresponding decreases in vascular markers sCD40L and VEGF.

A retrospective chart review of 16 long COVID patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) seen at a tertiary care center, examining clinical presentation, autonomic testing results, and symptom burden. The study documents high prevalence of palpitations and fatigue in post-COVID POTS patients but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This paper reports 4 case studies of post-COVID central hypersomnia (excessive daytime sleepiness) identified among 530 long COVID patients, with objective sleep examination data. Three cases showed favorable response to methylphenidate treatment, and one resolved spontaneously, highlighting post-COVID hypersomnia as a treatable manifestation.

Case report of three long COVID patients with persistent gastrointestinal symptoms (epigastric pain and diarrhea) treated with celiac plexus block, a procedure targeting the autonomic nervous system. The authors report successful symptom improvement, extending previous findings on nerve block interventions for long COVID symptoms.

A case series of 14 long COVID patients who underwent medically supervised long-term fasting (6-16 days) using the Buchinger Wilhelmi protocol. Thirteen patients reported improvement in overall health and multiple symptoms (fatigue, breathlessness, muscle/joint pain, cognitive impairment, smell/taste disorders), with reduced body weight and cardiometabolic risk factors.

Case series describing two CLL patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-COVID-19 condition treated with casirivimab/imdevimab monoclonal antibodies. Both patients experienced rapid viral clearance and resolution of post-COVID symptoms following treatment, suggesting passive anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody therapy as a potential therapeutic option for persistent infection.

Case report of two sisters with post-COVID neurocognitive decline and bilateral mesial-temporal hypometabolism documented by brain imaging. This is a descriptive case report with no treatment intervention or control group, focusing on clinical presentation and diagnostic findings rather than treatment evaluation.

This pharmacovigilance analysis reviews 44 case reports of off-label use of Pelargonium sidoides root extract (EPs 7630) for treatment of COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 syndrome. All 28 cases reporting treatment outcomes showed patient improvement with no unexpected adverse reactions.

This case series of six long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea examines the role of dysfunctional breathing using hyperventilation provocation tests (HVPT). Findings suggest underlying post-COVID respiratory dysregulation but no treatment intervention is tested or evaluated.

Case series of three patients with jaw osteomyelitis during or after COVID-19 infection, including surgical and antibiotic management. While one patient is described as post-COVID, the paper focuses on a specific opportunistic infection complication rather than long COVID syndrome or treatment of long COVID symptoms.

This case series describes contactless sensor monitoring of three COVID-19 patients in an assisted living facility over 3 months to track respiratory and behavioral phenotypes during recovery. The study found persistent sleep and motor abnormalities months after viral clearance, demonstrating proof-of-concept for passive monitoring as a research tool, but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

A case series of 7 post-COVID patients undergoing a comprehensive rehabilitation program that included whole-body cryostimulation (WBC) as an adjuvant therapy. All patients showed improvements in symptoms including dyspnea, fatigue, pain, and sleep quality, though the isolated contribution of WBC versus other program components (physiotherapy, nutrition, psychology) could not be determined.

This paper combines a literature review of 25 studies with a case series examining MRI findings of olfactory bulb reduction in long COVID patients with persistent smell dysfunction. The work presents imaging evidence of structural changes but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series of 5 pediatric long COVID patients presenting with neuropsychiatric symptoms (abnormal movements, anxiety, emotional dysregulation) weeks to months post-infection. Patients received pharmacological treatment and cognitive behavioral therapy, with the authors noting a multifactorial etiology involving systemic/brain inflammation and environmental stress.

A retrospective case series describing three young male patients who developed cardiac arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia) in the post-acute phase of COVID-19 infection. The paper documents clinical presentations of new-onset rhythm disturbances but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series describing resolution of chronic gastrointestinal symptoms in two pediatric long COVID patients treated with high-dose oral lactoferrin. The paper reviews lactoferrin's anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties and proposes it as a potential treatment strategy for post-COVID gastrointestinal complications.

A case series of 23 post-COVID patients with cognitive impairment who received neuroprotective agents (Citicoline, Piracetam, Memantine) and underwent neuropsychological and neuroimaging assessments. After 3 months of treatment, both groups showed positive results on neuropsychological testing, suggesting potential benefit of pro-cognitive agents for cognitive recovery in post-COVID patients.

First study assessing clinical management of severe isolated dysphonia in post-COVID-19 syndrome, examining 6 patients with instrumental laryngeal assessment before and after treatment. Treatment with systemic steroids, hyaluronic acid inhalations, and reflux protective agents resulted in improvement in vocal fold function and patient-reported voice quality.

Retrospective analysis of 38 critically ill COVID-19 patients admitted to ICU with ARDS, assessing long-term activities of daily living (ADLs) at hospital discharge and one year post-discharge using the Barthel index and Karnofsky Performance Status scales. Patients showed significant functional recovery at one-year follow-up, with complete ADL recovery in most patients, but this is an observational cohort study without an intervention or treatment being tested.

This paper describes liver histopathology findings in 10 severe COVID-19 survivors with persistent cholestasis, examining bile duct anomalies and fibrosis patterns. It is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention or control group, documenting the natural disease course rather than testing a therapeutic approach.

Two case reports of long COVID patients with persistent cough, breathlessness, and fatigue treated with manual lymph drainage (MLD) using the Dr Vodder method over six weekly 45-minute sessions. Both patients showed improvement in respiratory function, oxygen saturation, dyspnea, and fatigue measures by the third treatment, with further gains at three-month follow-up.

A case series of 16 post-COVID patients (8 with PCS, 8 with PVS) treated with statins plus ARBs for 6 weeks, with HDL proteome analysis via mass spectrometry and inflammatory markers assessed in endothelial cells. Treatment improved clinical symptoms and reduced inflammatory potential of the HDL proteome, identifying specific protein alterations and metabolic pathways involved in disease pathogenesis.

This case series presents two patients with long COVID-related vertebral algic syndrome and radiculopathy that worsened after SARS-CoV-2 infection and were resistant to conservative treatment. Both patients underwent spinal surgery with radicular decompression, resulting in significant pain relief and neurological improvement.

This case series describes histopathological and immunohistochemical findings in six long COVID patients with cutaneous neuropathic symptoms, revealing hypertrophy of nerve endings and disturbances in dermal neuronal fibers. While it provides pathological evidence of nerve involvement, it is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention or comparison group.

This case series describes clinical management outcomes of new-onset atrial fibrillation in 23 COVID-19 patients evaluated at a tertiary cardiac center after hospital discharge. The focus is on acute COVID-related cardiac complications rather than long COVID, and management did not differ from standard arrhythmia practice.

Preliminary case study of 3 long-COVID patients using telemonitoring devices to track vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature) over 10-day periods. The study presents initial findings of detected cardiorespiratory abnormalities but lacks a complete trial design with structured outcomes and control group.

This retrospective case series describes clinicopathologic features of Acute Fibrinous and Organizing Pneumonia (AFOP) nodules in post-COVID-19 patients, finding a 55% association with prior COVID-19 infection. The study focuses on diagnostic imaging and histopathological characterization to distinguish these nodules from malignancy, not on testing or evaluating any treatment intervention.

A retrospective case series of three long COVID patients presenting with myocarditis-related heart failure of varying severity. All three patients showed cardiac function improvement with optimal medical treatment, demonstrating that myocarditis is a treatable but serious complication of long COVID.

This case series evaluates cardiac and pulmonary involvement in 29 patients recovered from COVID-19 pneumonia using echocardiography, lung ultrasound, and ECG. The study documents persistent cardiopulmonary abnormalities but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective analysis of 12 post-acute COVID-19 patients in a rehabilitation unit evaluating neuropsychological patterns and their correlation with functional outcomes. Study found subclinical cognitive alterations (dysexecutive disorders) in 4% of recovering patients, with correlations between verbal memory/frontal functions and degree of functional impairment.

Case report of two relatives (age 14 and mother) presenting with spontaneous pneumomediastinum, thymic hyperplasia, myasthenic-like symptoms, and long COVID features following COVID-19 infection/vaccination. No treatment intervention evaluated; primarily a clinical observation with literature review.

Case series of three autism spectrum disorder patients who developed or experienced worsening neuropsychiatric symptoms following COVID-19 infection and long COVID. Reports immune activation markers (inflammatory and counter-regulatory cytokines) in peripheral blood monocytes and describes treatment challenges in managing post-COVID neuropsychiatric symptoms in ASD populations.

This case series describes 19 post-COVID and post-vaccination syndrome patients with undifferentiated arthritis and suspected small fiber neuropathy, comparing clinical and pathological features in 8 skin-biopsy-confirmed neuropathy cases versus 10 neuropathy-negative controls. Over 12 months of follow-up, treated patients showed significant improvements in joint inflammation, fatigue, motor impairment, and neurological symptoms, though skin biopsy findings did not fully normalize.

This paper presents two clinical case reports of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) with severe manifestations following COVID-19 exposure, focusing on diagnostic and clinical management challenges. It describes inflammatory involvement across gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, nervous, and respiratory systems but does not evaluate any specific treatment or intervention.

Describes a subgroup of long COVID patients with organizing pneumonia following COVID-19 who were effectively treated with systemic glucocorticoids. Provides a management algorithm for early diagnosis and treatment of post-COVID lung disease.

Case series of 10 patients with avascular necrosis and bone degeneration occurring immediately after acute COVID-19 infection. Paper describes clinical observations and steroid treatment response but is focused on acute infection complications, not persistent long COVID symptoms.

Case series of two immunocompromised patients with prolonged COVID-19 infection treated with convalescent plasma (CP). Both patients showed rapid clinical and virological recovery with symptom resolution after CP administration.

Two case presentations of paroxysmal finger hematoma (Achenbach's syndrome) occurring after COVID-19 recovery, hypothesizing SARS-CoV-2 as a triggering factor in microvascular pathology. Authors recommend Iloprost (synthetic prostacyclin receptor agonist) as first-line conservative treatment for this post-COVID vascular complication.

Case series of four patients who developed hemorrhagic cardiac tamponade in the recovery phase following COVID-19, with onset weeks to months after acute infection. Three cases required pericardiocentesis and anti-inflammatory treatment, with three patients discharged and one fatal outcome; histopathology showed fibrous pericarditis with inflammatory infiltrate.

Case report of two immunocompromised transplant recipients with chronic COVID-19 treated with remdesivir, documenting transient RNA-dependent RNA polymerase mutations during treatment. The study provides evidence of potential remdesivir resistance development and suggests monitoring for viral resistance mutations in vulnerable populations receiving prolonged antiviral therapy.

An uncontrolled case series evaluating hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) in 5 long COVID patients with various comorbidities, assessing changes in oxidative stress and inflammation biomarkers via saliva and urine samples. Results showed reduced ROS production, lipid peroxidation, DNA damage, and inflammation markers post-treatment, particularly in athletes.

A case series of 12 long COVID patients undergoing 12-week synchronous telerehabilitation combining therapeutic education, physical, and respiratory rehabilitation. The intervention resulted in significant improvements in fatigue, aerobic capacity, and limb/respiratory strength, though dyspnea showed no improvement.

This paper describes a new clinical phenotype of post-COVID syndrome combining fibromyalgia and joint hypermobility, presenting three case examples. Rather than testing a treatment, it identifies a disease pattern and hypothesizes that local connective tissue damage in hypermobile patients, triggered by COVID-19, may lead to fibromyalgia syndrome.

Retrospective case series of 15 patients with post-COVID Guillain-Barré syndrome at a Croatian hospital in 2021, examining clinical presentation and treatment outcomes. Treatment with IVIG and/or plasma exchange resulted in improvement in 13 of 15 patients, with most patients having recovered from the acute COVID-19 infection prior to GBS onset.

This paper studies anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgA antibody responses in 88 COVID-19 patients during acute infection and early recovery (4-41 days post-infection). While it mentions one patient with persistent symptoms seven months post-infection, the paper is primarily an immunological investigation of acute-phase IgA responses and does not study long COVID as its main focus or test any interventions for long COVID patients.

Case series describing two post-COVID patients who developed sacroiliitis with longitudinal MRI follow-up over nearly one year. Inflammatory back pain improved with NSAID therapy, though MRI findings remained positive.

This case series describes eight non-HIV patients who developed cerebral cryptococcosis associated with CD4+ T lymphocytopenia weeks to months after mild COVID-19 infection. The paper is a descriptive case series without any treatment intervention—it documents a post-COVID complication and natural disease outcomes, making it ineligible for the treatment trial extraction pipeline.

This paper examines the role of anticoagulants (particularly low-molecular-weight heparin and direct oral anticoagulants) in treating thrombosis and inflammatory complications in both acute COVID-19 and Long-COVID-19 patients. The authors present two clinical cases—one acute COVID-19 patient with disseminated intravascular coagulation and one Long-COVID patient with persistent cardiovascular risk—to illustrate the therapeutic potential of anticoagulant therapy.

A case series of 7 long COVID patients who developed pericarditis after SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with colchicine, NSAIDs/ASA, or glucocorticoids. Four patients initially unresponsive to conventional therapy achieved recovery with glucocorticoids, suggesting ongoing pericardial inflammation may be a treatable long COVID manifestation.

This is a postmortem neuropathological study of macaque brains following SARS-CoV-2 infection, examining brain inflammation and α-synuclein aggregates. The paper does not study long COVID patients or test any treatments; it is a preclinical animal model study investigating potential neurological mechanisms that could occur after infection.

This study evaluates xenon therapy as a treatment for mental disorders in patients with post-COVID syndrome. The paper presents a case series of post-COVID patients receiving xenon therapy for psychiatric symptoms.

This paper presents clinical cases describing dermatological manifestations of COVID-19 and post-COVID syndrome across different patient age groups and infection periods. It is descriptive/observational case reporting without any treatment intervention, so it does not qualify as a treatment trial.

Case series of 3 long COVID patients with parosmia (olfactory distortion) treated with saline nasal irrigation and olfactory training over 3 months. One patient showed symptom resolution while two showed no response, suggesting the intervention has variable efficacy in this patient population.

This case series describes 154 long COVID patients who developed intracranial abscesses and received neurosurgical intervention at Gandhi Medical College in 2022. It reviews the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and surgical management of this severe neurological complication following COVID-19 infection.

A descriptive case series documenting the clinical presentation of long COVID patients from a tertiary care hospital in Arunachal Pradesh, India. The study describes symptom profiles including fatigue, headache, attention deficit, hair loss, dyspnea, myalgia, and arthralgia but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Retrospective cross-sectional study examining interstitial lung disease (ILD) as a post-COVID-19 complication in 15 patients, exploring pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and radiological patterns. No treatment intervention was tested; this is descriptive/observational research on disease characterization.

A case series of four long COVID patients with dyspnea and fatigue who received face-to-face pulmonary rehabilitation at a tertiary care center. The study presents physiotherapy as an integral intervention for improving functional status and quality of life in post-COVID patients.

Case series describing new-onset hypertension in eight post-COVID patients within four weeks of recovery from COVID-19. The study documents the clinical presentation and proposes a mechanism via ACE2 and RAAS dysregulation but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series describing three cases of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) occurring post-COVID-19 infection or vaccination, with treatment outcomes following IV immunoglobulin therapy. The paper focuses on the acute neurological complication (GBS) temporally associated with COVID-19, not on long COVID sequelae.

This case series documents cardiac dysautonomia as a post-COVID-19 sequela in long COVID patients, describing clinical presentations and diagnostic criteria. The paper reports that patients following non-pharmacological interventions (cardiovascular exercise, increased water intake, BMI control) showed improvement, while non-adherent patients did not.

This case series describes transbronchial biopsy findings in six long COVID patients with persistent dyspnea 4-15 months post-discharge, demonstrating peribronchial remodeling and interstitial pulmonary fibrosis. The study does not evaluate a treatment intervention but rather characterizes pathological findings, and the authors note that the clinical utility, indications, and timing of lung biopsy in long COVID remain to be clarified.

Autopsy study of 96 deceased patients examining morphological lung changes in post-COVID-19 syndrome, comparing findings across three groups stratified by acute COVID-19 severity. Found pneumosclerosis, immune infiltration, and emphysematous changes that correlated with acute infection severity, providing pathological basis for understanding respiratory manifestations.

This cross-sectional study describes brain abnormalities detected via MRI in 21 post-COVID patients with cognitive decline, memory loss, dizziness, anxiety, and chronic headaches, all assessed at least 1 year after acute COVID-19 infection. The findings show neurodegeneration in all patients and support further research into the link between post-COVID symptoms and accelerated neurodegeneration.

Retrospective case series of 25 COVID-19 patients who developed laryngotracheal stenosis (LTE) post-intubation, describing demographic characteristics, risk factors, and management outcomes. Balloon dilation and tracheostomy were the primary interventions used to manage airway stenosis complications in these long-term COVID sequelae cases.

This retrospective case series analyzes 10 long COVID patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) of the hip joint following COVID-19 infection. Patients responded well to anti-inflammatory drugs and supportive therapy, suggesting a treatment approach for this post-COVID musculoskeletal complication.

Two case reports of diaphragmatic dysfunction and myasthenia gravis following COVID-19 infection, diagnosed through imaging and neurophysiological testing. Both patients showed clinical improvement after treatment, demonstrating a rare post-COVID neurological complication.

Case series of four neurosurgical patients with long COVID-19 who experienced resolution or improvement of symptoms after treatment with acyclovir. Presents a novel theory on long COVID pathophysiology and proposes acyclovir as a potential therapeutic intervention warranting further study.

This paper presents a case series of osteonecrosis of the femoral head occurring 132.8 days post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, primarily in patients who received corticosteroid therapy. While it documents a post-COVID complication, it does not evaluate or test any intervention—it is purely observational/descriptive and therefore not a treatment trial.

This paper discusses angioedema as a non-respiratory post-COVID symptom, reviewing reported cases in medical literature and presenting a case study. It is a descriptive case report/editorial without treatment intervention or controlled study design.

Case report of two long COVID patients who developed avascular necrosis of the hip following high-dose corticosteroid treatment for acute COVID-19. The paper describes clinical presentations and imaging findings but does not evaluate or test any intervention for treating long COVID.

This case report describes three elderly Brazilian women who developed urinary incontinence (mixed or stress type) following COVID-19 recovery, attributed to post-COVID muscle weakness. All three patients showed clinical improvement with physiotherapy treatment, highlighting a potential long COVID-related pelvic floor dysfunction requiring further investigation.

A prospective case series of 11 long COVID patients with olfactory dysfunction followed for 12 months, all receiving combined traditional Chinese and Western medicine treatment. Most patients (81.8%) recovered completely by 12-month follow-up, with majority of improvement occurring within the first 2 weeks.

Retrospective analysis of 10 COVID-19 patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head post-infection, with elevated IgG antibodies and documented correlation to disease severity. Patients responded well to anti-inflammatory drugs and supportive therapy, suggesting steroid use and microembolism as potential mechanisms of bone necrosis.

Case series of 3 critically ill COVID-19 patients describing augmentative and alternative communication interventions provided by speech-language pathologists during acute hospitalization and recovery. All patients demonstrated progressive gains in communication ability through multimodal interventions including communication boards, video interpretation, and tracheostomy speaking strategies.

A case series of 8 COVID-19 patients who developed venous insufficiency post-discharge, presenting with leg pain, swelling, edema, and reflux in deep veins. The authors recommend strengthened calf muscle exercises combined with venoactive medications as treatment, suggesting conservative management may prevent progression to chronic venous insufficiency.

Case series of two women with long COVID-related hair loss treated with Ninjin'yoeito (a traditional Japanese herbal medicine). Both patients showed halting of hair loss by one month and regrowth by two months, with improvement in mood symptoms associated with hair loss.

This retrospective case series describes the clinical trajectories of 13 pregnant women admitted to ICU with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) during acute COVID-19 infection in 2020-2023. While some patients reported reduced health 15 months later, the paper focuses on acute COVID-19 management during pregnancy, not on long COVID as a persistent condition or treatment of long COVID.

This paper presents a case series of four post-COVID patients with autoimmune vasculitis and sarcoidosis, describing clinical presentations and pathophysiological mechanisms. It is excluded because it combines case presentations with a review of immunological sequelae rather than studying a specific treatment intervention.

This paper presents two case reports with imaging findings (PET/CT) comparing an asymptomatic patient and a patient who developed long COVID following SARS-CoV-2 infection. It is descriptive/observational with no treatment intervention and does not meet eligibility criteria for a treatment trial meta-analysis.

This case series reports two patients with post-COVID-19 diaphragmatic paralysis who were treated with robot-assisted thoracoscopic plication of the diaphragm reinforced with acellular dermal matrix. Both patients experienced significant improvement in dyspnea and fatigue following the surgical intervention.

This case series evaluated a 6-week pulmonary rehabilitation protocol in 9 post-COVID-19 patients, measuring changes in pulmonary function, respiratory muscle strength, and diaphragm/quadriceps thickness via ultrasound. The rehabilitation program improved peak expiratory flow (26%), FVC (7%), FEV1 (10%), respiratory muscle parameters, and muscle thickness, with reduced echo intensity in quadriceps.

Case series of three severe COVID-19 patients with CT and pulmonary function testing at 4 weeks and 5-month follow-up to assess residual lung changes and fibrosis. Authors discuss need for long-term follow-up studies and mention potential use of corticosteroids and antifibrotic agents, but no actual treatment intervention is reported.

Case series describing three patients who developed functional movement disorders (FMDs) following COVID-19 infection, presenting with fatigue, weakness, and involuntary jerks. The paper documents clinical presentations of this neuropsychiatric complication but does not evaluate or test any treatment intervention.

Case series of 5 post-COVID-19 patients with bilateral bronchopleural fistula who underwent surgical repair, with perioperative anaesthesia management strategies. Erector spinae plane blocks were found to be a safer alternative to general anaesthesia for managing these patients during fistula repair.

This paper presents two case reports of Achilles tendinopathy, one occurring 8 weeks after COVID-19 infection and another following COVID-19 vaccination. While it documents musculoskeletal complications associated with COVID-19, it is a descriptive case series without treatment intervention or outcome evaluation, making it ineligible for the clinical trials meta-analysis.

A case series of 107 long COVID patients examined the prevalence of vitamin D3 deficiency and the effects of treatment over 6 months. The study found high rates of vitamin D3 deficiency at baseline (84.1%) that significantly improved after treatment, suggesting vitamin D3 supplementation may benefit long COVID symptom recovery.

This case series describes three children who developed Guillain–Barré Syndrome (GBS) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and methylprednisolone. While it documents a post-COVID neurological complication and its treatment, the paper focuses on acute GBS manifestation rather than long COVID syndrome itself, as GBS is a distinct post-infectious autoimmune condition rather than the characteristic persistent symptoms of long COVID.

Three pediatric cases of unilateral acute parotitis occurring weeks after COVID-19 infection, presenting as a post-COVID immune-mediated manifestation. All cases resolved rapidly with systemic steroid therapy, supporting an immune-mediated mechanism.

A case series of 5 long COVID patients with neurological complications (stroke, encephalitis, polyneuropathy, movement disorders) who received rehabilitation at a tertiary care center. Patients showed significant functional and cognitive recovery with improved mobility and quality of life, though residual fatigue and motor impairments persisted at 2-year follow-up.

A descriptive case series of 313 long COVID patients seen at a dedicated outpatient clinic in Italy from 2021-2023, documenting clinical presentations, specialist referrals, and prescribed treatments. The study demonstrates the multisystem nature of long COVID and emphasizes the importance of differential diagnosis and structured clinical management.

This study investigates the persistence of SARS-CoV-2 virus and antigens in tissue samples from 2 long COVID patients 163-462 days after infection, using immunohistological and multiplex immunochemistry techniques. The findings demonstrate residual viral nucleocapsid protein and evidence of ongoing viral replication in appendix and breast tissue, suggesting the gastrointestinal tract may function as a viral reservoir.

This paper reports two case studies of septic hip arthritis caused by Aspergillus species in post-COVID-19 patients who were immunosuppressed by corticosteroid treatment. While set in the COVID-19 era, it does not address long COVID or its treatment; rather, it documents a rare fungal complication.

Retrospective audit of 12 long COVID patients treated with the lightning process intervention, examining benefits and harms. 11/12 participants reported being 85% back to normal or more, with none reporting harm from the intervention, suggesting it is a promising and safe treatment option.

This case series describes seven patients with post-COVID neurological complications (facial palsy, lateral rectus palsy, cerebellar ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, stroke) occurring within 2 weeks after acute COVID recovery. The paper hypothesizes an antibody-mediated mechanism but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

A case series describing 3 patients who developed Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) during or shortly after acute COVID-19 infection. The paper discusses the potential immunological mechanisms linking COVID-19 to GBS but does not study a treatment intervention.

A case-series study of 51 post-COVID patients with behavioral and mental disorders who received 14 sessions of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT). HBOT significantly reduced anxiety, depression, and stress scores, improved quality of life, restored cerebral blood flow, and increased antioxidant capacity.

A case series describing four patients with Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS) occurring after COVID-19 infection, discussing the hypothesized immune-mediated pathogenesis. The paper presents clinical cases and reviews the literature on post-COVID neurological complications but does not report treatment outcomes or interventions tested.

A case series describing 5 patients with acute severe neurological syndromes (parkinsonism, status epilepticus, ataxia) during long COVID infection. The paper documents clinical and radiological features but does not evaluate any treatment or intervention.

A retrospective case series of 10 COVID-19 patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) of the hip as a post-infection complication. Patients responded positively to supportive therapy and anti-inflammatory drugs, suggesting a treatment response in this post-COVID musculoskeletal condition.

Case series examining long COVID-19 outcomes in multiple sclerosis patients treated with rituximab and the therapeutic effects of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Results showed IVIG improved respiratory symptoms, fever, immune parameters, and C-reactive protein levels in this immunocompromised population.

This paper reports two case studies of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) with severe gastrointestinal complications including appendicular and ileal perforation. While MIS-C can occur post-COVID, the paper focuses on acute, severe complications during the acute inflammatory phase rather than persistent long COVID sequelae, and does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

A longitudinal case series documenting persistent anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgM antibodies in two patients 8+ months post-COVID-19, demonstrating unusual serological findings. The study does not evaluate any treatment intervention, making it ineligible for the clinical trials pipeline.

This study evaluated the efficacy of off-label pirfenidone (an anti-fibrotic agent) in 15 long COVID patients with post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis who had persistent respiratory symptoms ≥12 weeks after acute infection. Treatment for 12 weeks resulted in statistically significant improvements in pulmonary function tests (FVC, FEV1, DLCO), 6-minute walking distance, and room air saturation levels, with earlier treatment initiation associated with better clinical outcomes.

Case series of 11 post-COVID-19 patients with phantosmia (distorted smell sensation) treated with combined olfactory training, nasal irrigation with budesonide, and oral prednisolone over 3 months. Patients reported self-perceived improvement in phantosmia symptoms, though the study lacked an untreated control group for comparison.

A case series describing four patients who developed pemphigus vulgaris (PV), an autoimmune mucocutaneous disease, following SARS-CoV-2 infection, treated with corticosteroids and immunomodulators. The paper focuses on a rare post-COVID autoimmune complication rather than long COVID's characteristic persistent symptoms (fatigue, post-exertional malaise, cognitive dysfunction).

Case report of two COVID-19 patients who developed laryngotracheal stenosis following prolonged intubation for severe pneumonia. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnosis of this complication but does not study a treatment intervention or long COVID syndrome.

This cross-sectional study evaluates clinical characteristics and plasma cortisol concentrations across healthy controls, acute COVID-19 patients at various stages, and post-COVID syndrome patients. While it documents higher cortisol levels in post-COVID patients, it is a descriptive observational study without any treatment intervention or control design, making it ineligible for the intervention trials meta-analysis.

A case series of 2 patients with spinal cord infarction attributed to acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, presenting diagnostic and rehabilitation challenges. While both patients developed post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), the paper describes clinical presentations and outcomes rather than evaluating any specific treatment intervention.

Case series reporting two novel cases of new-onset autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) in post-COVID patients. The paper describes this previously unreported autoimmune complication of long COVID and calls for further research to understand the association.

Case report of two long COVID patients presenting with fibromyalgia syndrome, characterized by generalized musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and neurological symptoms. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnostic criteria but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment outcomes.

A case series describing 3 patients who developed ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction in the post-COVID recovery phase, sharing features of hypercoagulability and elevated thrombotic markers. The study documents thrombogenic complications persisting after COVID-19 recovery but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series of 21 COVID-19 patients with severe gastrointestinal and hepatic manifestations including enterocolitis, peritonitis, and colonic necrosis. Describes clinical presentation and outcomes of acute digestive complications during active COVID-19 infection rather than post-COVID sequelae or treatment evaluation.

Observational study examining post-COVID syndrome prevalence and characteristics in 45 patients with rheumatic diseases, finding PCS in 20% of cases with varying severity by disease type. Reports clinical outcomes and disease relapses but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case reports of 3 patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) of bones 4-6 months after COVID-19 with bilateral lung disease. The paper discusses pathogenic mechanisms of AVN in post-COVID syndrome and treatment approaches, but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment.

This study investigates the presence of autoantibodies in post-COVID-19 patients by testing 24 convalescent patients' sera 3 and 9 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection and comparing with their pre-infection ANA results. The findings show that 41.66% of patients had positive IIF-ANA at 3 months, with 3 cases (12.5%) showing changes in ANA status post-infection, suggesting SARS-CoV-2 may trigger autoimmunity.

Case report of two long COVID patients presenting with persistent dyspnea and palpitations months after viral pneumonia clearance, diagnosed with viral myocarditis via cardiac MRI. This is a descriptive case series without treatment evaluation or intervention data.

This paper describes the use of medical leeches as a treatment for post-COVID syndrome, presenting the author's "System Method of Leeching" in cases where intoxication was a dominant clinical feature. The study reports on outcomes from patients with various pathologies including COVID-19 post-COVID syndrome treated with this therapeutic approach.

This paper reviews clinical cases of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) manifesting after COVID-19 infection and discusses COVID-19 as a potential trigger. It presents a descriptive case series with literature review but does not study or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

This study evaluates psychotherapy and cognitive restructuring interventions in 20 geriatric long COVID survivors experiencing psychological and physiological post-COVID complications. Pre-post testing using the WHO-5 wellbeing scale showed significant improvements in psychological symptoms including stress, depression, anxiety, and emotional regulation.

This case series describes four adults presenting with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-A) in the convalescent phase following COVID-19 infection, characterized by severe systemic inflammation and multiple organ dysfunction. The paper documents clinical presentations, laboratory findings, treatment strategies, and clinical outcomes of MIS-A cases, highlighting this as a distinct post-COVID complication requiring prompt recognition and management.

Retrospective case series of 10 long COVID patients treated with systemic or inhaled corticosteroids based on pulmonary phenotype (LC-ILD vs LC-OAD). LC-ILD patients showed improvement in hypoxia, exertional desaturation, and 6-minute walk distance with oral steroids; LC-OAD patients responded well to inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators.

Case report of two patients presenting with sudden sensorineural hearing loss following COVID-19 infection. The study documents the clinical presentation and highlights the association between SSNHL and post-COVID-19 sequelae for improved clinical awareness.

Reports use of Chinese herbal medicine to treat COVID-19 patients via telemedicine consultations, including post-viral syndromes. No structured data, outcomes, or patient numbers reported; appears to be a clinical observation summary rather than a formal trial.

This case series describes nerve conduction study findings in 18 post-COVID-19 patients with neuropathic symptoms, identifying various types of peripheral neuropathy including Guillain-Barré Syndrome variants. The study is observational and diagnostic in nature, characterizing neurological sequelae rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

A case series testing carbohydrate supplementation before bedtime in three long COVID patients with persistent night sweats. All three patients reported complete resolution of night sweats after one week of intervention, suggesting dietary carbohydrates may be an effective non-pharmaceutical treatment for this symptom.

A case series investigating whether evening carbohydrate supplementation reduces persistent night sweats in three long COVID patients. All three patients reported complete resolution of night sweats after one week of the dietary intervention.

Post-mortem electron microscopic study examining myocardial tissue changes in COVID-19 patients diagnosed with post-COVID myocarditis. Documents viral damage, edema, thrombus formation, and cardiomyocyte necrosis at the submicroscopic level without testing any intervention.

This paper presents two clinical cases of long COVID in children and reviews the literature on immune dysregulation and autoimmunity as pathogenic mechanisms. It does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention, making it a literature review with case illustrations rather than a treatment trial.

A case series describing six patients who developed active tuberculosis following COVID-19 infection, hypothesizing that COVID-19-induced CD4+ T-cell depletion may have reactivated latent TB. This is an observational case report without any treatment intervention being tested or evaluated.

This paper analyzes 30 clinical cases of mental disorders associated with post-COVID-19 syndrome, identifying four clinical variants: asthenic, anxiety-phobic, depressive, and insomnia. The authors describe an integrated therapeutic approach combining medications to improve brain metabolism and hemodynamics, antidepressant and anti-anxiety psychopharmacotherapy, and psychotherapeutic correction for post-COVID mental health sequelae.

Reports two cases of long COVID/PASC patients with dramatic symptom responses to rintatolimid and galantamine, with symptom recurrence upon drug withdrawal. Proposes a personalized medicine approach to CFS/ME and long COVID treatment, suggesting these conditions may respond to individualized pharmacological intervention.

Prospective observational case series of 20 young patients who developed bilateral avascular necrosis of the hip following high-dose steroid therapy for COVID-19 and underwent bilateral total hip replacement. Bilateral pericapsular end nerve blocks provided effective postoperative analgesia (85% with VAS<2) and enabled early mobilization within 12 hours in 88% of patients.

Retrospective observational study characterizing mononeuritis multiplex as a late neuromuscular complication in 9 severe COVID-19 survivors, presenting clinical, laboratorial, and neurophysiological findings. Study describes the natural history and pathophysiology of the condition but does not evaluate any intervention or treatment outcomes.

A case series describing three patients with persistent hypoxia and interstitial lung disease following COVID-19, documenting their clinical course, complications, and treatment outcomes. The paper presents management experience and follow-up results in long COVID patients with pulmonary manifestations.

Four case reports of long COVID patients with persistent loss of smell and taste treated with osteopathic cranial manipulative medicine. Treatment resulted in rapid symptom resolution in all cases after symptoms had persisted for over a year.

A 12-month follow-up study of 8 pregnant women with PASC examining neuropsychiatric symptoms through cognitive testing, sleep assessments, and psychiatric inventories. The authors note the study is still ongoing with a small sample size and conclude that more research is needed to validate findings, indicating this is a preliminary protocol stage rather than a completed trial.

This paper presents clinical case illustrations of long COVID patient management in primary care, describing the heterogeneous symptoms and multidisciplinary approach used in outpatient settings. It is an editorial/opinion piece based on clinical cases rather than a systematic treatment trial or research study.

This case series reports treatment outcomes for nine long COVID patients using homoeopathic remedies, with seven cases of acute post-COVID condition and two with chronic sequelae. All patients had failed to improve with conventional care, and homoeopathic treatment demonstrated symptom relief, particularly with Bryonia Alba and other remedies.

An open-label case series evaluating dobesilate (an anti-FGF and anti-VEGF agent) in 13 long COVID patients, hypothesizing benefit based on vascular and inflammatory mechanisms. The authors report clinical efficacy with symptom improvement following 15 days of treatment.

This case series evaluates Ayurvedic treatment for post-COVID multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS) in patients experiencing post-recovery complications. The authors report that Ayurvedic anti-inflammatory medicines reduced symptoms and biochemical inflammatory markers in their patient cohort.

A case series of two post-COVID Guillain-Barré syndrome patients with severe disease course, examining olfactory function through subjective and objective testing including olfactory event-related potentials. Both patients recovered despite severe GBS, but this is a descriptive case report without intervention or control group, making it ineligible for the treatment trials analysis.

Case report describing two young adults who developed ischemic vasculitis and neuropsychiatric symptoms 1-2 months after acute COVID-19 infection, confirmed by CT and angiography imaging. Neurological therapy led to improvement of symptoms in both cases.

A case series analyzing psychiatric manifestations in 5 COVID-19 patients (1 acute phase, 4 post-COVID). All patients received treatment and were monitored with psychological scales, showing improvement in conditions including delirium, neurocognitive disorder, depression, panic disorder, and psychosis.

This pilot study examined penile tissue from COVID-19 patients with post-infection erectile dysfunction compared to controls without COVID-19 history, finding viral particles and reduced endothelial function markers in affected tissue. The study is pathological/mechanistic in nature and does not evaluate any treatment intervention for long COVID.

Retrospective observational study of 5 critically ill COVID-19 patients who developed delayed respiratory deterioration weeks after acute infection, treated with glucocorticoids and/or IVIG. While the paper describes a post-COVID inflammatory syndrome and its treatment response, it focuses on acute hospitalization complications rather than long COVID syndrome with persistent symptoms weeks to months after infection.

This paper presents clinical case reports of thrombotic complications in children following COVID-19 infection, including cases with congenital heart defects and thrombosis of limb veins and cerebral vessels. It focuses on describing complications rather than evaluating a specific treatment intervention.

Case series presenting two new cases of ataxia-myoclonus syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with review of 16 total reported cases. Patients treated with intravenous immunoglobulins and/or steroids showed significant improvement within 1-8 weeks, suggesting immune-mediated pathogenesis and potential therapeutic benefit of immunological treatment.

Observational case series describing 14 long COVID patients who developed postural tachycardia syndrome (PoTS) with autonomic nervous system abnormalities. The paper characterizes clinical presentation and recommends diagnostic screening and clinical training, but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series describing bilateral vocal fold paralysis as a potential neuro-invasive manifestation in COVID-19 patients. Reports clinical presentation and discusses plausibility of SARS-CoV-2 as an etiology, but presents no treatment intervention or outcomes data.

Case report describing three older adults with pre-existing cognitive impairment who experienced worsening neurocognitive symptoms during the convalescent phase of COVID-19. The report documents clinical characteristics, neuropsychological testing results, and neuroimaging findings, hypothesizing that persistent inflammatory/immune responses contribute to post-acute cognitive decline.

A case series describing post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection in three family members, with multi-system manifestations including neuropsychiatric, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and dermatologic symptoms persisting over one year. The paper documents clinical features and recommends management strategies but does not evaluate or test any specific treatment intervention.

topics: olfactory dysfunction|gustatory dysfunction|long COVID sequelae|Kampo medicine|symptom persistence
summary: A case series of 33 hospital staff members with COVID-19 examining the course of gustatory and olfactory dysfunction, finding these symptoms persisted in 21% at 2 months and 18% at 4 months post-onset. The authors administered Kampo medicines as a treatment intervention for the persistent dysfunction and recommend olfactory training for future management.

A prospective case series of 27 long COVID patients in a Spanish general medicine clinic from 2020-2022, characterizing demographic and clinical features. The study documents symptom prevalence (respiratory 27%, ENT 20%, neurological 18%) but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This case series describes 7 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent cholestatic liver injury and secondary sclerosing cholangitis, characterized by markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase and imaging/histologic evidence of biliary damage months after acute infection. The study is a retrospective pathology review documenting a long-term sequela of severe COVID-19 but does not evaluate any treatment intervention.

Case series describing bilateral avascular necrosis of the femoral head in COVID-19 survivors, potentially related to corticosteroid use during acute infection. The paper documents a post-COVID complication but does not test or evaluate any treatment intervention.

This paper presents a case series of patients with myocardial inflammation after COVID-19 infection, accompanied by a comprehensive literature review of myocarditis and pericarditis complications. It is primarily a review article with case illustrations rather than a treatment trial, and does not evaluate any specific intervention or therapy.

This case series describes upper airway obstruction due to subglottic stenosis in two long COVID patients with a history of prolonged intubation during acute COVID-19. The authors discuss the clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and recommend early tracheostomy as a management strategy for intubation-related complications in PASC.

A qualitative multiple-case study examining symptom management experiences of six patients with post-COVID-19 syndrome through interviews and surveys. Identifies three patterns of symptom management (self-management, treatment focus, lethargy) and highlights the need for structured nursing intervention programs.

Case series describing quality of life and symptom changes in 36 long COVID patients following COVID-19 vaccination (Pfizer or Oxford-AstraZeneca). Found 23% of symptoms improved, 72% unchanged, and no significant worsening in quality-of-life metrics 1 month post-vaccination.

Case report describing secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) in two post-COVID-19 patients diagnosed using the H-score. The paper highlights an unusual immune dysregulation complication occurring after COVID-19 recovery rather than testing a treatment intervention.

Case report describing three children who developed Alice in Wonderland Syndrome (visual distortions) during or shortly after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents self-limited symptoms that resolved within days without treatment, focusing on the acute phase of COVID-19 rather than long-term sequelae.

Reports two cases of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) occurring approximately eight weeks after acute COVID-19 infection, representing an unusually delayed post-infectious neurological complication. Both cases responded to intravenous immunoglobulin therapy, demonstrating a successful treatment outcome for COVID-19-associated GBS.

This case series reports restoration of taste and smell in two COVID-19 patients following a single 1000 mg dose of turmeric supplement. The authors propose turmeric as a potential treatment for COVID-19-induced anosmia and ageusia.

Descriptive case series of 87 Japanese patients presenting to a COVID-19 aftercare clinic with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19, documenting symptom patterns and clinical characteristics. The study describes patient presentations and symptom evolution but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention.

Case report of two elderly COVID-19 survivors who died from post-COVID complications including malnutrition and nosocomial pneumonia. The paper advocates for rehabilitation programs but does not study or evaluate a specific treatment intervention.

Case report of two severe COVID-19 patients who developed chronic pulmonary aspergillosis during convalescence and were treated with oral itraconazole. This study focuses on acute/post-acute COVID complications in hospitalized patients, not long COVID syndrome.

Case series of three patients who developed new-onset insulin-dependent diabetes during acute COVID-19 infection, presenting with diabetic ketoacidosis. While patients remained insulin-dependent months post-recovery, the paper does not study a treatment intervention and focuses on a complication occurring during acute infection rather than long COVID sequelae.

Retrospective case series of 8 patients (4 children, 4 adults) with multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS) treated with IVIG, steroids, and immunomodulatory medications at Walter Reed. Most patients achieved full symptomatic resolution within 1-2 months, though some experienced persistent deconditioning or dyspnea at 6-month follow-up.

Case series describing sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSNHL) as a rare sequela occurring after complete recovery from COVID-19 in four patients, all with unexplained unilateral left ear involvement. The authors review literature on this presentation and call for further research to understand the persistence of this symptom in COVID-19 survivors.

Case series of four long-haul COVID patients treated with off-label acyclovir, focusing on neurological symptoms including encephalopathy. Treatment reportedly resolved symptoms and reduced IgG/IgM titers.

Retrospective descriptive study of 15 patients who developed lung cavitation during COVID-19 recovery, documenting clinical and radiological characteristics. Study describes imaging findings in severe COVID-19 sequelae but does not test or evaluate any intervention or treatment.

A case series describing four long COVID patients who experienced new-onset alcohol sensitivity following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The paper documents clinical observations without testing any treatment intervention or control group comparison.

Case report of two patients who developed inflammatory arthritis following COVID-19 infection and were treated with upadacitinib, a JAK inhibitor. Both patients showed clinically meaningful responses to treatment.

topics: olfactory dysfunction|taste dysfunction|stellate ganglion block|symptom management
summary: This case series evaluates stellate ganglion block (SGB) as a treatment for olfactory and gustatory dysfunction in six long COVID patients. Five of six patients reported improvements in smell and taste after undergoing bilateral SGB procedures, suggesting SGB may be a promising therapeutic intervention for these persistent COVID-19 sequelae.

This case series presents five patients with post-COVID syndrome (PCS) who received amifampridine treatment for fatigue symptoms, with two patients participating in double-blind discontinuation trials. All five patients showed normalization of sleep needs and improved functional outcomes, returning to normal activities after treatment.

Case-based comparison of small fiber neuropathy occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection versus vaccination, discussing immune dysregulation mechanisms. Presents two case presentations without quantitative treatment outcomes or systematic data collection.

This case series describes six post-COVID-19 patients who developed abdominal cocoon syndrome (encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis), a rare condition characterized by fibrous membrane envelopment of the small bowel. The paper reports surgical findings and histopathological confirmation but does not study a treatment intervention—it only documents a rare post-infectious complication without testing or evaluating any therapeutic approach.

Case series describing three patients who developed avascular necrosis (AVN) following COVID-19 hospitalization and corticosteroid treatment. The paper documents the clinical presentation, management via core decompression, and discusses the association between COVID-19, corticosteroid use, and AVN as a potential long-term complication.

Case report of two patients who developed Wallenberg syndrome with dysphagia following COVID-19 infection. The paper describes clinical presentation and diagnostic approach but does not evaluate any treatment intervention or outcomes.

This cross-sectional study characterizes 31 long COVID patients with persistent taste impairment (CRLTTI), evaluating taste perception across four taste modalities and self-reported smell. The study found that taste disturbances persisted for an average of 10.8 months, affected different taste types unequally, and was more common in women and unvaccinated participants, but is excluded because it is observational without any intervention or treatment evaluation.

A case series of seven long COVID patients with pre-existing migraine disorder who experienced worsening headache frequency, intensity, and medication efficacy following SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study evaluates treatment responses including standard migraine therapies (Botox and anti-CGRP agents) and medication regimen changes in this population.

A case series of three long COVID patients treated with pemivibart, a monoclonal antibody, showing rapid symptomatic improvement in fatigue, postexertional malaise, dysautonomia, and cognitive dysfunction. The authors report variable duration of benefit (1-6 weeks) and call for controlled studies to evaluate efficacy in larger populations.

Case series of 6 long COVID patients presenting with joint manifestations including arthritis, arthralgia, and reactive arthritis following SARS-CoV-2 infection. NSAIDs and steroids were found beneficial in managing the symptoms, providing clinical observations on post-COVID musculoskeletal complications.

This case series describes three patients who developed Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome (periorbital headache with ophthalmoplegia caused by orbital inflammation) following COVID-19 infection. All three patients showed clinical improvement in cranial nerve function and symptom relief following steroid therapy.

This is the first evaluation of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) for long COVID treatment, testing 10 sessions in 10 consecutive patients. Results showed statistically significant improvements in fatigue, global cognition, executive function, attention, information processing, and verbal function.

Describes a series of long COVID patients with autonomic dysfunction symptoms (breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, orthostatic intolerance) and proposes an underlying mechanism of virus- or immune-mediated autonomic nervous system disruption. Provides clinical recognition and supportive management strategies rather than testing a specific intervention.

A single-centre UK case series surveying acute and chronic gastrointestinal symptoms in COVID-19 patients with 6-month follow-up. Found that 43.8% of patients experienced gastrointestinal symptoms at 6 months, suggesting a potential post-COVID-19 IBS phenotype.

Case series describing four patients who developed lung cavitation post-COVID-19 infection, with three cases also presenting sino-orbital mucormycosis. The paper documents clinical presentations and outcomes but does not evaluate any specific treatment intervention—it is a descriptive case series of complications rather than a treatment trial.
